title: fln-unsafe-abi: three membrane defects — safe scalar accessors unbounded, cold dec-ref skips the shadow, MT storm precondition unasserted
description:
Type: bug
Priority: 1
Title: fln-unsafe-abi: three membrane defects — safe scalar accessors unbounded, cold dec-ref skips the shadow, MT storm precondition unasserted

AbiReview's three findings over the ABI twin, each verified line-by-line against
the code and the vendored pin before fixing:

1. Obj::ctor_scalar_u64 / ctor_scalar_set_u64 (handle.rs) asserted ONLY the tag
   — the safe accessors read/write a u64 at any caller-supplied byte offset with
   no upper bound at any layer (the raw layer debug-asserts only the lower
   bound). A safe method permitting an out-of-bounds read or write is a
   soundness hole in the membrane. Root fix: the full law is asserted at the
   safe surface — scalar accesses must land in [other*8, cs_sz - 8) measured
   from obj_cptr, exactly the layout the shared engine already enforces.
2. rc::dec_ref_cold (FLN-UL-0043) was the only RC entry point that skipped
   shadow::check_rc_target — every sibling (inc_ref_n, dec_ref, dec_child)
   checks first. A double-release or foreign pointer through the cold path
   recorded nothing and proceeded to del_core on freed state — the exact UB the
   debug ownership shadow exists to catch. Root fix: the same check first, and
   on a failed check release nothing.
3. Obj::stress_mt spawned scoped RC storms with only an is_scalar assert:
   racing the RC of a single-threaded (rc > 0) object is upstream's UB,
   mirrored or not. The MT-or-persistent precondition (rc <= 0) is now asserted
   with the value named.

Regression cells: shadow_kills_cold_double_release (the cold path detects and
skips like every sibling), ctor_scalar_bounds_refuse_every_escape (control
reads/writes inside the area, four escapes refused each way),
stress_mt_refuses_a_single_threaded_object (the refusal names the
precondition).
close_reason: All three membrane laws landed and verified: full scalar-area bounds at the safe surface, cold dec-ref shadow check, asserted MT storm precondition. Three regression cells (cold double release, bounds escapes both ways, ST storm refusal). Boundary covenant kept end-to-end (FLN-BX-0067). 48cf915b, 3d90f0ea.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
JUDGEMENT (close walk) — three membrane laws, each verified against the code and the vendored pin before fixed, each celled.

1. THE SOUNDNESS ONE (P1): the safe scalar accessors
Obj::ctor_scalar_u64 / ctor_scalar_set_u64 asserted only the tag. A
caller-supplied byte offset of ANY value read or wrote out of the object — the
raw layer debug-asserts only the lower bound (offset >= other*8), and nothing
bounded above at any layer. A safe method that can read or write out of bounds
for some input is not a safe method. The full law is now asserted at the safe
surface: a scalar access must land in [other*8, cs_sz - 8) measured from
obj_cptr — exactly the layout the shared engine already enforces — and the
accessor docs now state the offset convention the raw layer actually uses
(from obj_cptr, not "from the slot base", which contradicted it). The cell
proves both directions: in-area reads and writes at the area's two ends round-
trip, and four escapes (0, past-end, far, near-MAX) are each refused both ways.
2. THE SHADOW HOLE: rc::dec_ref_cold (FLN-UL-0043) was the only RC entry point
that skipped shadow::check_rc_target; inc_ref_n, dec_ref, and dec_child all
check first. A double-release or a foreign pointer through the cold path
recorded nothing and proceeded to del_core on freed state — the exact UB the
debug ownership shadow exists to catch. The cold path now checks first and
releases nothing on a failed check, exactly its siblings' discipline; the call
from dec_ref (already checked) is idempotent. The probe mirrors
probe_double_release through the cold path directly, and the shadow records the
DoubleRelease like it does for every sibling.
3. THE UNASSERTED PRECONDITION: Obj::stress_mt spawned scoped RC storms with
only an is_scalar assert. Racing the RC of a single-threaded (rc > 0) object is
upstream's UB, mirrored or not — the precondition the atomic traffic requires
is rc <= 0 (MT or persistent), and it is now asserted with the value named in
the refusal. The Miri concurrency guard's discipline is untouched: its storms
run on MT objects, which the precondition permits. The cell proves an ST
object's refusal names the precondition.

The boundary covenant was kept end-to-end: the new pub probe carries its
reviewed row (FLN-BX-0067), with the duplicate-id stumble (0053 was taken) fixed
to 0067 and re-verified 18/18. KERNEL_CONTRACT_OWNERSHIP was regenerated for the
bead (421 records). UBS v5.3.7: zero new criticals over baseline.

title: fln-checker seed constructor expectations encode parameter binders Default where the pin encodes Implicit
description: The council path of `fln check-olean` (K1 + `fln-checker` independent implementation) halted on the real pinned `Init.Prelude.olean` (leanprover/lean4 v4.32.0, `8c9756b2`) at declaration batch item 1: `fln-checker rejected the inductive block: ConstructorShape { name: And.intro }` while K1 accepted the same block. Root cause found by decoding the pinned artifact with `fln olean inspect --constants`: the pin encodes `ctor And.intro` as `(Πi#Sort{0}, (Πi#Sort{0}, (Π##1, (Π##1, ((And #3) #2)))))` — implicit (`i#`) parameter binders for `a b : Prop`, default field binders. The checker's `and_constructor_type` (crates/fln-checker/src/admit.rs) built the expected constructor type with `BinderStyle::Default` for both parameters, and `compare_inductive_expression` passes `compare_binder_styles = true`, so `Default != Implicit` rejected the block. The same defect pattern existed in `or_constructor_type`, `sum_constructor_type`, `prod_constructor_type`, `option_constructor_type`, and `list_constructor_type` (all seed constructor-type builders with parameters). `expected_equality_constructor_type` (Eq.refl) already used `Implicit` correctly, as did every recursor-type builder. Binder names are not compared by `structural_expression_equal`; only styles and structure. Synthetic fixtures in crates/fln-checker/tests/admit.rs (`init_and_entries`, `init_or_entries`, `init_sum_entries`, `init_prod_entries`, `init_option_entries`, `init_list_entries`) carried the mirrored `BinderInfo::Default` bug, which is why the suite was green while the real artifact diverged. Fix applied 2026-08-29: all six source builders changed to `BinderStyle::Implicit` for parameter binders and all six fixtures changed to `BinderInfo::Implicit` for the constructor-type parameter Pis (inductive-type expectations unchanged — the pin encodes inductive parameter binders as Default, consistent with the observed error path reaching the constructor check). Full `cargo test -p fln-checker` after the fix: 469 passed, 0 failed across 10 targets (13 lib, 328 admit, 32 defeq, 46 infer, and the rest), run via `rch exec` local fallback at the shared CARGO_TARGET_DIR.
close_reason: Root cause confirmed against real pinned bytes; fix landed and verified: suite green (330 admit tests), real pinned Init.Prelude council passes items 1-10 (was item 1). Remaining item 11 Eq.rec rule-rhs encoding tracked under fln-51y8 with typed fail-closed deferral. Judgment: bead-comment:fln-0eq8:2800.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
Judgment at close (2026-08-30; code landed at 3afeb7eb, 6f3f44ae, and b9473558):

Root cause confirmed against real pinned bytes, not inferred: `fln olean inspect --constants` renders the pin's constructor parameter binders Implicit (`Πi#`) while every seed constructor/recursor expectation builder in `crates/fln-checker/src/admit.rs` asserted `BinderStyle::Default`, and `compare_inductive_expression` compares binder styles. The six affected builders: `and_constructor_type`, `or_constructor_type`, `sum_constructor_type`, `prod_constructor_type`, `option_constructor_type`, `list_constructor_type` (parameter binders), plus `empty_recursor_type` (motive was Implicit where the pin binds Default — confirmed on `False.rec`/`Empty.recOn` rows). The mirrored defect in the synthetic fixtures (`init_and_entries`, `init_or_entries`, `init_sum_entries`, `init_prod_entries`, `init_option_entries`, `init_list_entries`, `init_empty_entries`, `init_false_entries` in `crates/fln-checker/tests/admit.rs`) is why the suite was green while the real artifact diverged: fixtures matched the bug, not the pin.

Evidence: after the fix, `cargo test -p fln-checker` is green (330 admit tests including the pin-shaped fixtures and two new Init.Eq block tests; full package green across all targets), and the real pinned `Init.Prelude.olean` (v4.32.0 @ 8c9756b2) council run advances from halting at declaration batch item 1 (`And.intro`) to passing items 1-10 end to end through K1 plus fln-checker.

Not claimed: the full-Prelude council pass. Item 11 (the `Eq` block) exposed a further gap — the pin's `Eq.rec` iota rule rhs uses a richer encoding (hygienic internal binders, distinct level context) than reconstructed; that unit belongs to fln-51y8 and currently defers typed and fail-closed (`ResultUniverse`), never rejecting the real block. Claim type bounded_model: one host, one pin, one artifact, run via `rch exec` local/remote fallback at the shared target dir.

title: Verification manifest: unresolvable citations are 86% AUTHORING defects and 7% rot; artifact validation EXISTS and is gated on an unadopted registry, not missing
description:
Of 403 artifact strings across 150 coverage rows in ci/VERIFICATION_MANIFEST.jsonl, exactly 14 are ever resolved by any check, and 167 cannot be resolved to a durable referent at all. The validator requires the artifacts array to be a non-empty, sorted, duplicate-free string array (scripts/evidence.py:4078 require_manifest_string_array) and validates its SHAPE only. It never requires an entry to DENOTE anything. The single place record["artifacts"] is dereferenced is scripts/evidence.py:4583, the iumd closure citation, which resolves only bead-comment: entries. So "artifacts": ["x"] is a valid judgement row.

MEASURED AT d5ecb966, read-only, scripts retained at /data/tmp/claude-1000/cc3-audit-artifacts.py, cc3-audit-depth.py, cc3-audit-tally.py.
  190 exists and tracked in git
  122 ROOTLESS leaf name (run.ndjson, bundle.complete.json, manifest.json, human.log) - no root stated anywhere in the row
   20 prose/opaque token (bead:<id>:<slug>) - denotes no file by design
   20 GLOB (env-snapshots/*/run.ndjson) - a pattern, not a referent
   14 bead-comment citation - the only class ever checked
   13 repo path that NEVER EXISTED on any ref
   12 commit sha reachable from main
    9 commit sha UNREACHABLE from main (vdi4)
    2 present but untracked, absent in a fresh clone (2ya9/krb0)
    1 under target/, ephemeral (povo)

WHY THIS IS NOT povo OR vdi4. Those two cover 10 of the 167 and are about referents that EXISTED and were destroyed - povo an orchestrator tick deleting a run dir, vdi4 filter-branch rewriting the address space. The other 157 never denoted anything resolvable in the first place. That is the bkw6 empty-referent shape, sitting inside the one artifact whose job is holding claims to their evidence.

SHARPEST EXAMPLE: ci/VERIFICATION_MANIFEST.jsonl line 4, bead fln-23cz, cites crates/fln-syntax/src/syntax.rs. git log --all on that path is empty and there is no delete record: not a rename, not a deletion, the file was never in the repository. franken_lean-tkr2 cites the same non-path. Also fln-pu6i line 58 (crates/fln-verdict/tests/CERTIFICATE_GOLDENS_PROVENANCE.md) and fln-q3u4 line 59 (tribunal/epoch-lab/MANIFEST.txt).

PROPOSED MECHANISM, the bkw6 move: classify every artifacts entry by referent kind, require each to resolve in its own kind or be listed in a declared allowance, and assert the allowance SIZE in BOTH directions so a repair shrinks it and a regression grows it.

SIX TRAPS THAT WOULD MAKE THE CHECK VACUOUS.
1. Do not resolve a rootless leaf against a run dir the checker picks. Resolving run.ndjson against any existing run directory passes all 122 while proving nothing. The root must be stated in the ROW; supplying it in the checker is the defect, mechanised.
2. A glob that matches is still not a referent - it does not say which file the claim rests on. Unresolvable regardless of what it matches today.
3. For commits, existence is not the test, reachability from main is. refs/original makes every dead anchor resolve locally, so cat-file -e passes in this clone and strands a fresh one. The 9/21 above used merge-base --is-ancestor.
4. A scan returning zero unresolvable citations is a BROKEN SCAN, not a clean tree. Plant a decoy row with a known-bad citation and require the scan to find it.
5. The allowance must shrink in both directions: one-way membership plus a floor. Equality and reverse-membership are walls that redden a correct repair.
6. Do not start the allowance at 167 and call it done. That converts an unmeasured population into a frozen one, which is 3s8w's complaint about the 105 date-exempt rows.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH. No row is claimed false: an unresolvable citation means the evidence cannot be CHECKED, not that the work was not done. Counts are one measurement at one commit on one clone, class bounded_model. The never-existed classification is only as good as git log --all; a path that lived only on a dropped branch would misclassify. The 190 tracked paths are verified only to RESOLVE - whether the file says what the row claims is a separate and much harder join. The "asserts a scanner ran without proving it ran" angle is unexamined, not clean.
close_reason: Repairability answered, price measured, ruling reached, binding built and proved to fire. Declaring is not repairing: the 17 third-state rows remain unrepairable and are routed, not resolved.

comments.text:
THE PARTITION BY CAUSE, AND THE VALIDATOR HALF SETTLED. cc_3 at 0a1b1a66 (join measured) and
re-derived at HEAD for this comment. Two findings; the second changes what the repair IS.

=== PART 1: 167 IS A POPULATION, NOT A DEFECT, UNTIL THE KINDS ARE SEPARATED ===

Of 180 unresolvable citations at this commit, partitioned by CAUSE, conservation exact:

  NEVER DENOTED    155  (86%)  120 rootless leaves + 20 globs + 15 never-in-history
  ROTTED            12  ( 7%)    9 commit-unreachable (vdi4) + 3 pruned run dirs (povo)
  AT RISK            4         under target/, present today, ephemeral by construction (povo)
  HOST-DEPENDENT     9  ( 5%)  present but untracked; absent in a fresh clone (2ya9/krb0)
                   ----
                    180

THE TWO KINDS HAVE DIFFERENT REPAIRS AND DIFFERENT OWNERS, which is why a single count over both
is the denominator error this swarm has paid for twice today.

  ROTTED means the referent EXISTED and the address stopped reaching it. The repair is DURABILITY:
  povo's tracked-ness criterion for paths, vdi4's main-reachability for commit anchors. Both are
  about keeping a real referent addressable. Together they cover TWELVE of 180.

  NEVER DENOTED means no referent was ever addressable FROM THE ROW. A rootless leaf
  (`run.ndjson`) states no root, so there is nothing to keep; a glob names a pattern, so it does
  not say which file the claim rests on; and 15 paths were never in history under `git log --all`.
  The repair is a CITATION GRAMMAR that requires a stated root, and it is this bead's own. It

UBS-TRIAGE/1 — `panic! macro(s) present`, CRITICAL, class-level, known-false for this file

Filed by cc_3 (pane 4) for the third-state decomposition repair landing in
`crates/fln-conformance/tests/artifact_referent_census.rs`. This bead owns that file and
that population, so the triage lives here.

## THE RUN

- owning bead / class: `fln-0rxm` / `panic! macro(s) present` — remediation text
  `Avoid panic! in library code`. Severity CRITICAL. It is the file's ONLY critical class in

- exact command:
  `ubs crates/fln-conformance/tests/artifact_referent_census.rs ci/VERIFICATION_MANIFEST.jsonl`
- UBS version: **v5.3.7**. See the correction at the end — the sha `ubs --version` prints in
  parentheses is NOT UBS's version.
- HEAD: `cd3e203e`. Porcelain at the run: 7 modified files — 2 mine (the two inputs), 2 the
  standing `franken_lean-h4o1` orphans (`crates/fln-syntax/tests/golden_vellum.rs`,
  `scripts/evidence.py`), 3 a peer's in-flight edits (`AGENTS.md`,
  `scripts/git-hooks/pre-commit`, `scripts/git-hooks/test_projection_guard.sh`).
- inputs and sha256:
  - `crates/fln-conformance/tests/artifact_referent_census.rs`
    `e03b849ec62099ab20ef3933525b8eb64af51653b12ffad2027a8ab52d14f6ab`
  - `ci/VERIFICATION_MANIFEST.jsonl`
    `5ce87b534c6acb7308f4bb90180307c2815b4844a96e8910b6af426d61ec27c3`
- exit code: **1**, read from the process.
- expected/observed scanner: rust. Positive execution evidence, quoted: `Finished rust (7s)`
  and `Files scanned:    1`.
- intended vs accounted supported inputs: **1 intended, 1 accounted**. The `.jsonl` is in no
  language UBS supports, so for that input alone the mode is
  `not_applicable_no_supported_inputs`, which is an explicit non-pass carrying zero scanner

- terminal mode: **`completed_findings`**. The scanner ran, every supported input is
  accounted for, totals are consistent, and findings are present.
- totals reported: Critical **12**, Warning **46**, Info **10**.

## THE CONTROL, AND WHY THE RAW 12 MEANS NOTHING WITHOUT IT

A count on a Tribunal guard file is uninterpretable without a same-path content baseline, so
one was taken with cwd and the RELATIVE path held fixed and ONLY the content varied — HEAD's
blob of the same path versus mine, restored afterwards and verified byte-identical by sha256.
The two cells were asserted DISTINCT by sha256 before their counts were compared, because a
delta against a control not proved distinct is a comparison of a thing with itself:

```
baseline (HEAD blob, sha 0a169a46...)  rc=1  files_scanned=1  critical=9   warning=29
mine     (sha e03b849e...)             rc=1  files_scanned=1  critical=12  warning=46
```

So **9 of the 12 are pre-existing at HEAD in this same file** and 3 are mine.

## WHAT THE THREE ARE — AND THE ATTRIBUTION I GOT WRONG FIRST

The class counts **physical lines** of a `panic!` invocation, not logical sites. My +3 is
**one** site spanning three lines after rustfmt:

```
                panic!(
                    "no third-state row is blocked solely by {kind:?} — the plant has no subject"
                )
```

in `a_third_state_row_moving_between_blocking_kinds_is_caught_though_the_total_is_unmoved`.

**My first attribution was wrong and the correction is the useful half.** I derived the +3 by
grepping for `panic!`, `.expect(` and `unwrap_or_else`, which found exactly three new
constructs and read as a clean explanation. I then removed one of them — an
`.expect("length checked")`, replaced by a slice pattern that carries the exactly-one
guarantee in the type instead — and re-ran: **criticals stayed at 12** while warnings moved
47 to 46. The `expect` had been a WARNING all along. A count inferred from a grep is not the
tool's count, and it agreed with the tool's total by coincidence. The attribution above is
taken from the tool's own records.

(The simplification was kept: it is better code on its own merits. It was not made to move a
count, and it did not move the one it was wrongly credited with.)

## CLASSIFICATION: KNOWN-FALSE

The class's own remediation text scopes itself to **library code**. This file is a
`crates/*/tests/*.rs` test target: `panic!` is not a failure path here, it is the refusal
mechanism of a guard. The specific site is an **anti-vacuity refusal** — it refuses a mutant
plant that has no subject rather than reporting a kill against an empty population, which is
this repository's own standing rule. Removing it would convert a refusal into a silent pass,
i.e. it would install the exact defect the file exists to detect. No `ubs:ignore`, no
`.ubsignore`, no category skip and no source contortion was added.

## GRANULARITY: `class-level`, NOT `site-level`

Per `fln-7vzi`, UBS's rust findings model is per-CLASS at v5.3.7: criticals emit one record
carrying a class total plus a **capped** sample list, and no per-site object exists in any
format. Both cells here emit exactly **5** sample sites against totals of 9 and 12, which
demonstrates the cap directly. **A count taken from that list is a floor, not a census.** The
per-site clause of UBS-TRIAGE/1 is therefore unsatisfiable at this version by construction,
and this record is typed `class-level`. Enumeration is unavailable; it is named as such
rather than silently skipped.

Three required fields have **no referent for this class** and are recorded as not-applicable
rather than omitted: "both operands", "both semantic roles" and the changed-hunk intersection
of an operand pair. Those are fields of the `==` comparison class (`fln-lyc8`); a
panic-presence class has no operands.

Class-level reconciliation: 12 reported = 9 baseline + 3 mine; 3 mine = 1 logical site x 3
physical lines; 1 logical site is enumerated above in full. Reported and enumerated agree.

## A CORRECTION ABOUT THE VERSION FIELD ITSELF

UBS-TRIAGE/1 requires the UBS version, and the obvious place to read it misreports it.
`ubs --version` prints `UBS Meta-Runner v5.3.7 (git <sha>)`, and **that sha is the HEAD of the
CURRENT DIRECTORY's repository, not UBS's own revision.** Measured in three cells, one
variable each: run inside `franken_lean` it printed `(git cd3e203e)`, which is franken_lean's
HEAD; run inside `/data/projects/001-pages`, whose HEAD is `0279fb0f`, it printed
`(git 0279fb0)`; run in a directory that is not a repository at all it printed **no sha**,
which is the negative control that stops the first two agreeing vacuously. It also appears in
the finding permalinks, as `github.com/Dicklesworthstone/franken_lean/blob/<that sha>/...`.

The cost if uncorrected is specific: two triage comments quoting different parenthesised shas
read as two different UBS versions when they may be one version at two commits — and
AGENTS.md makes the recorded version load-bearing, since a version bump is declared to expire
every `class-level` claim. Record `v5.3.7` and record the repository HEAD separately, as this
comment does.

## WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH

One host, one instant, class `bounded_model`. UBS lives outside this repository, so nothing
here can hold its version, its class model or its cap, and a version bump expires this claim
by AGENTS.md's own rule — re-measure the format matrix before reusing it. "Pre-existing"
establishes attribution for the 9, never safety: this record does not adjudicate them, it
only separates them from mine. The baseline is one pair of runs on one host. And the
known-false judgement is about this class in THIS file; it says nothing about `panic!` in any
non-test target, where the class's own advice stands unchallenged.

NAMED TRAP: a search returning nothing is evidence of absence ONLY when the search is known capable of finding the thing

Filed by cc_3 (pane 4) on the sequencer's instruction, because this shape hit **twice inside
one hour on 2026-07-27** and a route reaches one pane while a bead reaches whoever next opens
the work. Recorded here rather than only in
`route-cc_3-to-cc_1-amv-landed-86d87486-and-your-grep-could-not-see-a-fourth-site.md`.

> **A search returning nothing is evidence of absence ONLY when the search is known capable
> of finding the thing.**

The failure is not that the search is wrong. It runs, it is well-formed, it returns a
well-formed answer, and the answer means *you are safe to proceed*. Nothing distinguishes it
from a true negative at the moment you read it.

## INSTANCE 1 — a grep for a COUNT cannot find a DECOMPOSITION of that count

Landed at `86d87486`. A routed repair moved `THIRD_STATE_ROWS` 17 -> 14 in
`crates/fln-conformance/tests/artifact_referent_census.rs`, and enumerated the prose sites
needing to move with:

```
grep -nE '\b(17|18)\b' crates/fln-conformance/tests/artifact_referent_census.rs
```

Four sites, correctly reported; I reproduced the grep verbatim and it returns exactly what
was claimed. **A fifth site was invisible to it by construction:**

```
//! **single** kind — 10 rootless-leaf-only, 4 glob-only, 3 never-existed-only — because they
```

That sentence decomposes the same 17 and therefore carries 10, 4 and 3 — **neither 17 nor
18**. Measured: all three rows the repair moved were rootless-leaf-only, so the decomposition
went 10/4/3 -> 7/4/3. Applying the enumeration as derived would have landed
`10 rootless-leaf-only` describing a measured population of 7, still summing to 17 in a
paragraph whose headline now read 14, with nothing in the repository able to say so.

The only other statement of that decomposition is immutable comment
`bead-comment:fln-0rxm:1502`, which can be annotated and never repaired.

**Nobody was careless.** Enumerating by the number is the obvious method, it is complete for
every site that *states* the number, and the class it misses is exactly the class that
restates the number in another form.

## INSTANCE 2 — my own, within the hour, while working on instance 1

Probing the anchor guard for a measured value, I ran:

```
... | grep -E 'VERIFICATION_MANIFEST: declared'
```

The guard's actual text is `ci/VERIFICATION_MANIFEST.jsonl: declared 1, measured 17`. I had
dropped `.jsonl`. The grep returned **nothing**, and nothing is what a *passing* probe also
looks like — I had run the same probe minutes earlier expecting a violation line. I briefly
read it as "the repair lowered the count to at or below 1", which is absurd on its face and
was still the reading that arrived first. Re-run with a pattern that could match, the answer
was `measured 12`.

**Instance 2 is the more useful one**, because instance 1 was somebody else's method and this
one was mine, made *while writing up instance 1*, with the lesson fully in mind. Knowing the
rule does not protect you; only giving the search a positive control does.

## HOW TO APPLY IT

- **Enumerate by SUBJECT, not by the value.** For a count, search the noun
  (`third-state`, `rootless-leaf-only`, `commit_unreachable`) as well as the digits, and read
  the whole paragraph around every hit. That is how instance 1's fifth site was found and how
  the twin repair's out-of-scope survivors were found.
- **Give every negative a positive control** — run the search against something you know it
  must match, in the same invocation. A grep whose pattern has never matched anything is not
  a measurement.
- **A zero is a claim.** This repository already refuses derived zeros as broken scans in
  `commit_anchor_reachability` (`a_derived_zero_is_refused_as_a_broken_scan`) and in the
  census (`an_empty_or_shallow_scan_is_refused_rather_than_reported_clean`). The same
  scepticism belongs on an ad-hoc grep, where nothing enforces it.
- Related shapes already recorded in this repository: a filter that `continue`s on what it
  cannot parse silently redefines its denominator; a character class that excluded a digit
  reported `kernel_replay.sh` as governing zero paths; `grep -rln <path> scripts/*.sh` returns
  nothing for files governed by seven arrays. **All four are the same defect** — a scan that
  cannot see the thing, reporting its blindness as absence.

## WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH

Nothing mechanises it: no check anywhere requires a search to carry a positive control, and
this comment does not create one. Two instances at one host on one day, class
`bounded_model`. It also does not say the enumerations were wrong — instance 1's four sites
were all real and all needed to move; the defect is the *completeness* claim resting on them,
which is a different predicate from the one the search answered.

title: fln-core: Level.normalize is not idempotent — universe defeq must not depend on normalization count
description:
REPRODUCER (exact, no setup):

    let v = Level::param(Name::str(Name::anonymous(), "v"));
    let m = Level::mvar(LMVarId(Name::str(Name::anonymous(), "m")));
    let u = Level::imax(v, m.succ()).succ();          // (imax v (m+1)) + 1

    u.normalize()              == (max v (m+1)) + 1   // first pass
    u.normalize().normalize()  == max (v+1) (m+2)     // second pass, DIFFERENT
    u.normalize().normalize().normalize() == max (v+1) (m+2)   // settles here

The first pass collapses imax to max (the right argument is a succ, so it cannot be zero) but leaves the outer offset outside the max; the second pass distributes it. Non-idempotence is one step, not an oscillation.

THIS IS NOT A DIVERGENCE FROM THE PIN. The same input was run through the pinned Reference binary (v4.32.0, commit 8c9756b28d64dab099da31a4c09229a9e6a2ef35) and it prints:
    u             = (imax v (m + 1)) + 1
    u.normalize   = (max v (m + 1)) + 1
    u.normalize^2 = max (v + 1) (m + 2)
    idempotent    = false
So fln-core is faithful, and the two-pass behaviour is pinned by crates/fln-core/src/level.rs::tests::normalize_is_not_idempotent_and_the_pin_agrees (landed in 3397b9a).

WHY IT IS FILED AS A BUG ANYWAY — the hazard is downstream. Level.isEquiv is defined as syntactic equality of normal forms (u == v || u.normalize == v.normalize). If a consumer can reach the same universe having normalized a different number of times — because of a cache hit, a memo table, a different traversal order, or a different thread interleaving — then isEquiv can answer differently for the same pair of universes in the same environment. That is a schedule-dependent verdict, which is exactly what FL-INV-01 forbids, and universe defeq feeds the kernel judgment inventory (KR-6xx constructor-field universes, KR-602/700 machinery).

WHAT TO DETERMINE (the analysis this bead is really asking for):
1. Can any consumer path normalize a level a variable number of times? Audit fln-kernel's universe comparison and any caching of normalized levels, plus fln-env if normalized levels are ever stored.
2. If yes, decide the contract in fln-core: either expose a fixpoint helper (normalize-to-fixpoint, documented as NOT the pin's normalize and therefore not usable where faithful output bytes are compared), or state as an invariant that consumers compare only once-normalized levels and enforce it at the boundary.
3. Either way, the pin's one-pass normalize must remain available unchanged for faithful-mode output and for the core_observables oracle rows, which compare normalize().hash() against the Reference.

OWNERSHIP: the consumer is fln-kernel (cc_2 domain) but the primitive and its contract live in fln-core, so this is cc_3's unless the analysis in (1) finds the exposure is purely in kernel caching. Do not 'fix' normalize to be idempotent: that would diverge from the pin and break the faithful-mode rows. Any change to normalize itself needs a Behavior Note (D23).
notes:
cc_3 ANALYSIS AND RESOLUTION, commit 1fc50b9.

CONSUMER MAP (the question this bead led with):
* Level::normalize — called only inside fln-core/src/level.rs (collect_max_args, is_equiv, is_geq). No other crate calls it.
* Level::is_equiv — called by fln-kernel in exactly four places: lib.rs:301, tc.rs:885, tc.rs:1213, tc.rs:1878. All four are `level.is_equiv(&Level::zero())`, the Prop check.
* Nothing outside fln-core stores, digests, or keys on a normalized level. The canonical encoder writes the level's own structure (LEVEL_ZERO/SUCC/MAX/IMAX/PARAM/MVAR tags), not its normal form, and Level::hash is the data word of the value as built. NOT the witness-collision escalation class: no cache key or digest is computed over a non-canonical normal form anywhere today.

THE KERNEL IS STRUCTURALLY IMMUNE, and this is an argument rather than a sample. Non-idempotence requires exactly succ^k(imax a (succ b)) with k >= 1. Its one-pass form always carries that outer offset, so it is never zero, so no level can need a second pass to be recognised as Prop. The four kernel sites only ever ask 'is this zero'. cc_2: no action needed on 8ce or elsewhere — but if fln-kernel ever caches or stores a normalized level for later comparison, use Level::normalize_fixpoint, not normalize.

THE HAZARD IS REAL, LATENT, AND REACHABLE WITH PARAMETERS ALONE (no metavariable, so the shape occurs in ordinary kernel-checked universes, not just mid-elaboration). For x = succ(imax v (succ u)) and y = x.normalize().normalize(): is_equiv(x, y) = false, is_equiv(x.normalize(), y) = true. Two callers holding the same universe get different answers because one normalized first — an answer decided by history rather than content, which is the FL-INV-01 failure mode.

RESOLUTION — AND A DELIBERATE DEVIATION FROM THE INSTRUCTION, stated plainly: making Level::normalize idempotent would be WRONG here. The pinned Reference is non-idempotent in exactly this way, byte for byte (verified: same two forms, and it reports idempotent = false itself). Level.normalize is public Meta API that user metaprograms call, so changing it diverges from the pin on a compatibility surface, breaks faithful mode by construction, and invalidates the L2 oracle row that compares normalize().hash() against the Reference. That is a D23 Behavior-Note decision, not a bug fix. normalize therefore stays bit-faithful and gains a doc note naming the shape class.

What landed instead: Level::normalize_fixpoint — iterate normalize to a fixpoint, documented as ours and explicitly NOT the pin's, for any consumer that stores, keys, digests, or caches a normalized level. Bounded (NORMALIZE_FIXPOINT_PASSES = 8) because a non-converging fixpoint must be a typed outcome and not a hang (FL-INV-07); two passes suffice for every shape observed.

TESTS: pre_normalization_changes_an_is_equiv_verdict pins the hazard with params only; normalize_fixpoint_converges_and_is_idempotent generates levels including the non-idempotent class ON PURPOSE and asserts the fixpoint is stable, idempotent, unaffected by pre-normalization, reached within two passes, and coarser than isEquiv in the only direction that holds.

METHOD NOTE worth carrying: my first exposure search covered 80,000 generated pairs and reported ZERO exposure on all four predicates — because the generator never built the shape. It was a false negative, caught only by checking the search against the known counterexample. The committed test now validates itself against that counterexample first and fails if the corpus never produces a non-idempotent level.
close_reason: Analysed and resolved in 1fc50b9. No live defect: every consumer is mapped, no cache key or digest is taken over a normalized level, and the kernel's four is_equiv(_, zero) Prop checks are structurally immune because the non-idempotent class always carries an outer offset and so never normalizes to zero. The latent hazard is real and reachable with parameters alone, and is now pinned by a test. normalize stays bit-faithful to the pin — which is itself non-idempotent, so making it idempotent would be a divergence on a Meta API surface and a D23 Behavior-Note decision, not a fix — and consumers that need a canonical form get Level::normalize_fixpoint, bounded per FL-INV-07 and property-tested for stability, idempotence, and independence from how many times the caller normalized.

title: W1: Typed operation outcomes and diagnostic-cause taxonomy core — FL-INV-07
description:
## Description

Define the versioned fln-core operation-outcome algebra separately from diagnostic causes. Every authoritative operation returns exactly one of: Complete with its domain result (including a legitimate rejection only where that domain defines one); Inconclusive with explicit cancellation, resource, unavailable-dependency, or incomplete-authority reason plus budget/usage facts and authority=false; or InternalFault with invariant, causal, and evidence facts. No generic conversion may map Inconclusive or InternalFault to acceptance, rejection, cacheable negative result, normal user error, or successful absence.

Define the stable diagnostic-cause vocabulary required across the product: SyntaxFailure, MacroFailure, ElaborationFailure, kernel rejection cause, ArtifactCorrupt, ArtifactEpochMismatch, AbiViolation, CapabilityDenied, PluginCrashed, BuildFailure, ProtocolFailure, ReplayDivergence, and InternalInvariantViolation, with structured cause chains, source identity/byte spans, related spans, severity, resources, evidence references, bounded details, and explicit truncation. Outcome authority and diagnostic cause are orthogonal: a resource refusal is an Inconclusive outcome carrying a cause, not a rejected theorem or malformed user program.

Own values, pure compatibility rules, and safe versioned serialization only. Unknown versions/variants and malformed/truncated encodings fail typed at the boundary. Authoritative internal matches are exhaustive with no wildcard/catch-all that silently swallows a new variant. Panics remain invariant failures and never become user diagnostics. Renderer and transcript conformance are downstream.

## Acceptance Criteria

Named suites operation_outcome_authority_model, outcome_cause_orthogonality, diagnostic_schema_versioning, bounded_diagnostic_payloads, and outcome_serialization_no_mock_e2e cover every complete/inconclusive/internal-fault branch, every diagnostic cause, nested cause/evidence/resource fields, old/current/unknown versions, malformed and adversarial payloads, bounded truncation, cache/publication authority, cancellation, and clean retry. Property/model tests prove no non-authoritative result crosses acceptance/rejection/cache/promotion joins. Mutations for Inconclusive-to-rejection, InternalFault-to-user-error, cancellation-to-empty-success, missing authority=false, cacheable resource failure, unknown-version default, wildcard swallow, unmarked truncation, dropped cause/evidence, and panic-on-malformed-input are all killed for the intended reason. A real no-mock E2E serializes outcomes across representative crate/process boundaries, injects each failure class, validates strict human plus semantic NDJSON projections, restores, retries, and ends with exact clean state. Logs bind schema/version, operation/domain, outcome/authority, cause chain, budget/usage, evidence/root, expected/actual, truncation, cleanup, and final state; telemetry cannot alter semantic identity.

Property/model tests prove no non-authoritative result crosses acceptance/rejection/cache/promotion joins. Mutations for Inconclusive-to-rejection, InternalFault-to-user-error, cancellation-to-empty-success, missing authority=false, cacheable resource failure, unknown-version default, wildcard swallow, unmarked truncation, dropped cause/evidence, and panic-on-malformed-input are all killed for the intended reason. A real no-mock E2E serializes outcomes across representative crate/process boundaries, injects each failure class, validates strict human plus semantic NDJSON projections, restores, retries, and ends with exact clean state. Logs bind schema/version, operation/domain, outcome/authority, cause chain, budget/usage, evidence/root, expected/actual, truncation, cleanup, and final state; telemetry cannot alter semantic identity.
close_reason:
The core algebra landed in 73039d4. fln_core::outcome defines Outcome<T> with exactly three arms: Complete(T) carrying the domain's own result (a legitimate rejection lives INSIDE T where the domain defines one), Inconclusive with a typed cause (cancelled / resource-exhausted with allowed+observed facts / dependency-unavailable / authority-incomplete), and InternalFault with invariant, detail and evidence.

The orthogonality the bead insists on is enforced and pinned: the cause vocabulary already existed in diag::ErrorValue (14 variants, bead fln-rk6), so this adds the missing AXIS rather than a sixth taxonomy. outcome_cause_orthogonality asserts it in both directions -- a rejection-classed cause can sit on a non-authoritative outcome, and an inconclusive-classed cause on an authoritative one, because reporting that a kernel run was inconclusive is itself a completed operation.

Non-cacheability is structural rather than per-crate convention: cache_admission() refuses every non-authoritative arm, admission is proven to be the same predicate as authority over a population covering every shape, and the only extraction path is into_complete() returning Result<T, NonAuthoritative>, so a caller cannot spell 'treat not-knowing as an answer' with an Option, a Default, a From, or an unwrap_or. Bounded details mark their truncation and cut on character boundaries; unknown schema versions classify as Unsupported{seen} rather than defaulting.

fln-core kept rank 0: [dependencies] is still empty and ci/WORKSPACE_GRAPH.txt still shows no outgoing edge for fln-core. No byte codec was added here because canonical serialization lives in fln-hash, which depends on this crate -- the compatibility rules are stated in the core and the encoder that obeys them is downstream.

Suites: operation_outcome_authority_model, outcome_cause_orthogonality, plus mapping-cannot-manufacture-authority, per-cause fact retention, bounded truncation, typed unknown-version refusal, and the cache-join model check. cargo test -p fln-core 5 targets 0 failures; clippy -D warnings 0; fmt clean; ubs 0.

SCOPED OUT AND FILED, not silently dropped: the versioned byte codec and the outcome_serialization_no_mock_e2e suite need a downstream encoder plus a scripts/ lane (another pane's tree), and adoption by the crates that hand-rolled their own lattices is filed as franken_lean-1fxz (fln-kernel, cc_2), fln-um4a (fln-env, cc_1) and fln-8gz3 (fln-hash, mine), each blocked on this bead. Until those land, the five lattices still exist alongside the core type -- the core is now the single definition, but it is not yet the single implementation.

comments.author: cc_3
comments.text:
DESIGN FINDING FROM THE FIRST REAL ADOPTION ATTEMPT (cc_3, fln-hash, bead fln-8gz3, commit 5298ab5). Filed here rather than fixed, because these are the core type's gaps and widening it from inside one adopting crate is exactly the thing the adoption beads were split out to avoid.

fln-8gz3 folds canon::Decoded into Outcome<Result<T, CanonError>>. Two arms fold with no core change and I verified that: Decoded::Value -> Complete(Ok(..)), Decoded::Malformed -> Complete(Err(..)), since malformed bytes are a real domain verdict and belong inside the authoritative arm. The third arm cannot fold today.

GAP 1 — BLOCKING. THE RESOURCE VOCABULARY DOES NOT COVER A BUDGETED DECODE. InconclusiveCause::ResourceExhausted requires a ResourceUsage, which requires a ResourceReason — the D8 diagnostic taxonomy, declared closed at version 1. Its four entries are Heartbeats{consumed,limit}, RecursionDepth{limit}, Cancelled, Memory{limit_bytes}. A budgeted canonical decode stops on neither: its BudgetLimit values are InputBytes (bytes consumed from input) and ProducedNodes (values built — deliberately a count of WORK, not nesting). Nothing in the taxonomy names either, and both available mappings publish a false diagnostic:
  * Memory{limit_bytes} for InputBytes => a renderer prints 'memory budget exhausted' for a decode stopped by an input-byte cap. D8 diagnostics are a compatibility surface, so that is a false published claim.
  * RecursionDepth for ProducedNodes => strictly worse. The produced-node meter exists BECAUSE a depth cap would refuse legitimately deep terms, which franken_lean-fnj forbids; reporting it as a depth limit reintroduces the claim that bead exists to deny.
So the honest options are (a) extend the D8 taxonomy with a byte/work budget reason, or (b) leave Decoded standing. I took neither unilaterally.

WHAT OPTION (a) ACTUALLY COSTS — I priced it by planting ResourceReason::InputBudget rather than guessing, and it is more than a taxonomy arm:
  * fln-core's own renderer (diag.rs:172, ErrorValue::KernelInconclusive) breaks first.
  * crates/fln-hash/src/canon.rs:1249 write_resource breaks — that is the fln.canon.diag WIRE encoder, byte tags RES_HEARTBEATS=0 .. RES_MEMORY=3. A new reason adds a wire tag, so it CHANGES A REGISTERED DURABLE FORMAT and requires bumping SCHEMA_DIAG's version, which the SCHEMA_REGISTRY join (franken_lean-rps, f5a3944) now enforces in both directions.
  * Plus every other exhaustive match in the workspace, in other panes' crates.
That is a reviewed, spec-level, cross-pane change with a durable-format version bump attached. It is not P3-sized and it is not fln-hash's to make.

GAP 2 — NO LOCALIZATION AXIS. canon's Exhausted carries , the byte offset the decode reached. ResourceUsage has no field for it. It is NOT needed to size a retry (allowed/observed do that), but it is what makes the stop diagnosable, so dropping it silently would lose information the current type keeps. Options: an optional bounded progress/at on ResourceUsage, or carry it in Inconclusive.diagnostic. Worth deciding once in the core rather than five times in the adopters — note the same question will arise for every other lattice, and 'where it stopped' will be a declaration name or a module for some of them, not a byte offset, which argues for a bounded-text progress field rather than a usize.

GAP 3 — ONE FACT, TWO HOMES. ResourceUsage{reason, allowed, observed} duplicates what ResourceReason::Heartbeats{consumed, limit} already carries. Two representations of one fact can disagree, and is_genuine_exhaustion() only checks the outer pair, so a Heartbeats reason whose inner limit contradicts the outer allowed passes. Either the inner limits come out of ResourceReason, or is_genuine_exhaustion() cross-checks them.

HELD AS A TRIGGER, NOT A NOTE: canon.rs now matches ResourceReason and BudgetLimit exhaustively in the_outcome_adoption_blocker_is_a_missing_resource_vocabulary, so any variant added to either fails to compile there with the reasoning attached — whoever revises the taxonomy is told that fln-8gz3 is waiting on it and what to check. Verified by planting: the trigger fires at canon.rs:2986. Decoded itself is untouched, so no hybrid state exists for new call sites to be written against while this is open.

comments.text:
CORRECTION to my previous comment (cc_3), GAP 2. One word was lost from the durable record: the text reads "canon's Exhausted carries , the byte offset the decode reached" and should read "canon's Exhausted carries **at**, the byte offset the decode reached". The field name is Exhausted.at, declared in crates/fln-hash/src/canon.rs as "pub at: usize" with the doc comment "Byte offset the decode had reached". The finding is unchanged: ResourceUsage has no field for it, dropping it silently would lose information the current type keeps, and the right fix is probably a bounded-text progress field rather than a usize, because for other adopters "where it stopped" will be a declaration name or a module rather than a byte offset.

Cause, recorded because it can corrupt any bead record and is invisible afterwards: I passed the comment through a double-quoted shell argument, and the field name was wrapped in backticks for markdown. zsh read the backticks as a command substitution, ran "at", got "Command 'at' not found", and substituted empty. The comment was stored already damaged. Nothing else in that comment or in the fln-8gz3 comment was affected — I scanned both. Pass bead comment bodies through a file rather than an inline double-quoted string when the text contains backticks.

comments.author: cc_3
comments.text:
DECISION RECORDED (cc_3, commit fbe3c95, bead fln-um4a): the non-answer arms of Outcome carry NO domain payload, and that is now a decision with a compile-time guard rather than an accident of the first draft.

Three adopters have now reached this type, and the pattern in the answers is worth having in one place:

* fln-8gz3 and fln-49c needed a missing VARIANT — a resource reason for a data-structure budget. franken_lean-vui8 added the structural-budget axis and both proceeded. One extension, two callers.
* fln-um4a appeared to need a missing SHAPE — a slot for a partial result on a stop. It did not. Four of the five arms in fln-env's ClosureStatus are not non-answers at all: Incomplete{missing} and Invalid{reason} are completed traversals reporting a verdict, so they belong inside Complete(..). What remained on a genuine stop was two scalar reasons that ResourceUsage and progress already carry.

The generalizable lesson, for the two adoption beads still open: when a caller seems to need a payload on Inconclusive, first ask of every arm of its existing lattice "did the operation FINISH?". A surprising number of arms that look like failures are completed runs reporting a negative or qualified verdict, and those belong in the authoritative arm — the same reclassification that put a decoder's "malformed" inside Complete(Err(..)) rather than beside it. The payload usually wants to be in Complete, not in Inconclusive.

WHAT THE DECISION IS AND WHAT WOULD REOPEN IT is documented on Inconclusive itself, at the point of temptation, with the reasoning: a payload on that arm is the FL-INV-07 footgun the module exists to remove, the need is rarer than it looks, and the cost falls on every signature in the program. Reopening needs a caller that must RESUME from partial progress — where the partial value is an input to a later operation rather than material for diagnosis — and even then a domain resume-token is the likelier answer than a payload on the authority type.

THE GUARD: Outcome::non_answer_for re-types a non-answer for a different domain result. It compiles only because the arm holds no domain content, so it is the witness as well as a convenience — planting a T payload on the arm fails inside it with E0061 at both reconstruction sites. Deleting the decision requires deleting the function.

title: Tribunal: oracle outcome authority and the typed normalizer model (oracle_outcome_authority, typed_normalizer_model)
description:
Second slice carved out of fln-euo by cc_2 on 2026-07-25, after fln-q3u4 (the revision chain). Everything still open in the epic - Parity rows, G0 decisions, the reachability scan - cites these vocabularies, so they are the next load-bearing thing.

THE HIGHEST-RISK RULE IN THE EPIC IS IN THIS SLICE. A Reference timeout, cancellation, resource refusal, unavailable platform, or crash is Inconclusive or InternalFault - NEVER a semantic reject, and NEVER a FrankenLean divergence. Getting it wrong makes the Tribunal manufacture divergences that do not exist, which is worse than missing real ones because it burns the oracle's credibility: once the rig cries wolf, every real finding is discounted. This is the same law as the one already enforced in crates/fln-kernel/tests/reference_differential.rs, where a non-answer from either side is unscorable and fails rather than passing - this is the other end of the same pipe.

VOCABULARY DECISIONS, recorded before implementation. Each is a SEPARATE closed enum with no From/Into between them, because the failure mode the epic names is conflation - an L-level standing in for a claim state is how an unearned claim gets laundered:
* OracleKind - which oracle produced the observation.
* OracleAuthority - whether its word can settle a question or only inform one.
* ProcessOutcome - what the process did: Completed{exit} versus Timeout, Cancelled, ResourceRefused, PlatformUnavailable, Crashed. ONLY Completed can carry a semantic verdict.
* ComparisonClass - how two observations were compared.
* NormalizerId plus version - which normalizer, at which version, touched the bytes.
* ClaimType (D7) - invariant, proof, bounded_model, statistical, slo, benchmark.
* EvidenceKind and EvidenceState - what the evidence is, and what state it is in.
* LLevel - L0..L4 compatibility level.
* Mode - faithful, sound, frontier.
* DeterminismClass - D0..D4.
* Freshness.
* Platform.
Twelve vocabularies, twelve types. No shared integer, no stringly-typed field, no conversion helper that would let one be read as another.

NORMALIZER OBLIGATIONS, as provable properties rather than prose: total, bounded, deterministic, idempotent, versioned, preserving distinct semantic errors and ordered diagnostics, and unable to expand adversarial input beyond budget. Idempotence and non-expansion are the two most likely to be quietly false, so they get property tests over generated adversarial inputs rather than assertions.

MUTANTS THE EPIC NAMES FOR THIS SLICE, each needing a discriminating kill: oracle crash read as reject, normalizer expansion past budget, an error normalized away, and claim/L-level conflation.

Lives beside fln-q3u4 in the tribunal/epoch-lab nested workspace. Lane registration stays on fln-giap rather than reaching into scripts/.
close_reason: Delivered in 1bd0093: both suites green, authority rule structural, all four named mutants killed. Coverage statement in the final comment; claim type bounded_model, evidence state observed not proven.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
BUILT. cc_2, 2026-07-25. tribunal/epoch-lab/src/oracle.rs + src/normalize.rs, suites tests/oracle_outcome_authority.rs (16 tests) and tests/typed_normalizer_model.rs (14 tests), plus 5 in-crate structural tests. 45 tests green in the crate; fmt clean; clippy --all-targets -D warnings clean; ubs run and triaged.

THE AUTHORITY RULE IS STRUCTURAL, NOT DOCUMENTARY. ProcessOutcome::completed_exit() is the only route to an exit status and it returns None for every non-completing arm, so a caller cannot read a verdict out of a crash without going through a function that hands it None. Observation::verdict() then maps None to NoAnswer, and score() checks the oracle's non-answer BEFORE it consults our verdict at all, so there is no code path where a crash is paired with anything. Scored::is_divergence() is false for Unscorable by construction.

SYMMETRY, DELIBERATE. Our own Inconclusive is equally unscorable - there is no asymmetry where our silence counts as agreement. Same law both ends of the pipe.

OVER-CORRECTION GUARD. Every property above is satisfiable by never producing a rejection at all, which would make the rig blind instead of noisy. a_completed_nonzero_exit_is_a_real_reject and only_two_answered_sides_can_produce_a_divergence pin the other side: a completed run that says no means no, we-reject/they-accept is Restrictive (the only direction D23 can ever carve out) and we-accept/they-reject is UnsoundlyPermissive (never carve-out-able).

CRASH IS INCONCLUSIVE, NOT INTERNALFAULT. Recorded because it is a real decision, not an accident. The Reference dying is a fact about the Reference; InternalFault is reserved for OUR accounting contradicting itself and is reachable only through NonAuthoritative::internal_fault. Collapsing the two would lose the only signal that says which side to go and fix.

NO PANICKING CONSTRUCT IN EITHER NEW MODULE. verdict() originally used .expect() on a provably unreachable arm. In a crate whose entire subject is FL-INV-07 that is the wrong shape, so the arm now returns a typed InternalFault ("outcome classified as both completed and non-completed") instead. If the two classifiers ever disagree, that IS our accounting contradicting itself, which is precisely what InternalFault means - and it is unscorable, exactly like every other way of not having an answer.

NON-EXPANSION IS TRUE BY CONSTRUCTION, NOT CLAMPED AFTER THE FACT. Two structural rules: (1) every rewrite rule declares min_match >= placeholder.len(), the scanner refuses a shorter match, and a test walks the rule table checking the relation - so every individual rewrite is non-expanding; (2) invalid UTF-8 is replaced ONE BYTE PER BAD BYTE with '?', never with U+FFFD. String::from_utf8_lossy turns one bad byte into three, which is an expansion the adversary controls by choosing how many bad bytes to send. With both, output.len() <= input.len() BEFORE the budget is consulted, so the budget only bites on inputs that were already over it.

VALID MULTI-BYTE UTF-8 IS COPIED VERBATIM. Lean diagnostics are full of real Unicode and it is semantic - "expected a != b" and "expected a <= b" differ in exactly one multi-byte character. Folding Unicode to a byte would be an error normalized away while remaining perfectly bounded.

IDEMPOTENCE SCOPE, PINNED. Idempotence is a property of the normalized TEXT. Normalized::truncated deliberately does not participate: it records what happened to the input that produced this value, and re-normalizing an already-clamped text clamps nothing, so the flag is false the second time. That is correct, it is asserted directly in idempotence_survives_every_clamp_boundary, and it is written down so nobody later "fixes" the flag into stickiness and quietly turns it into a comparison field.

VERSIONING HAS TEETH. compare() refuses across NormalizerId or NormalizerVersion with a typed CompareError::NormalizerMismatch rather than resolving it. Without a refusal, "versioned" means a field nobody reads and a rule-table change silently reinterprets every normalized value ever recorded. AcceptanceOnly comparison is vacuously true by design and says so: the class declares the diagnostic was not part of the comparison, so reporting a text difference under it would be a claim about something that was never checked.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
MUTATION CAMPAIGN, all four mutants the epic names for this slice. Each was planted, run, and killed; sources restored and verified byte-identical by sha256 against a pre-campaign snapshot (oracle.rs 4be1ee54f304e27cb758f3e6367ebb97a40913374a4f76e9d443897e47d413fe, normalize.rs 0513a8c84428255906bbfe35f0b5e4a15b5d7000917e615e4871b56a168d94fc). No production logic was changed to make any test pass.

1. ORACLE CRASH READ AS REJECT. Edit: completed_exit() returns Some(1) for Crashed. Killed by 5 tests. The one that matters most is a_non_answer_from_the_oracle_is_never_a_divergence_whatever_we_said - a crash paired with our Accepted became UnsoundlyPermissive, which is the manufactured divergence itself, not merely a misclassification. The sharpest kill message came from a_crash_is_never_a_reject_even_when_its_stderr_says_error, which feeds a SIGSEGV whose stderr already contains "error: unknown identifier": a crashing Reference can print a diagnostic before it dies, so "the text looks like a rejection" is exactly the wrong signal to key on. The process outcome decides; the text never does.

2. CLAIM/L-LEVEL CONFLATION. Edit: EvidenceRow::justifies() also accepts a row whose level is L4. Killed by justifies_does_not_read_the_l_level ("justifies(Invariant) moved with the L-level (claim Invariant, state Targeted, level L4)") and by an_unestablished_evidence_state_justifies_nothing_and_reports_no_level ("a Targeted Invariant row justified a Invariant claim") - the laundering path named in the message. The guard is symmetric: compatibility_level_does_not_read_the_claim_type holds the other direction, because a strong claim type must not confer a compatibility level either. The claim-strength rank is a PRIVATE free function, never a method and never public, so no caller outside the module can obtain an integer from a ClaimType and compare it against an L-level or a determinism class.

3. NORMALIZER EXPANSION PAST BUDGET. Edit: hex-address rule min_match 8 -> 3. Killed by output_is_never_longer_than_input, output_never_exceeds_the_budget, and ten_thousand_short_tokens_cannot_inflate_the_output, which measured the amplification rather than arguing about it: 40000 bytes in, 70000 bytes out. Also killed at the source by the structural test every_rule_declares_a_minimum_at_least_its_placeholder_length. Note this mutant is perfectly idempotent and preserves every semantic distinction - only the size properties noticed.

4. AN ERROR NORMALIZED AWAY. Edit: rewrite()'s valid-UTF-8 arm emits one '?' instead of copying the sequence. Killed by distinct_semantic_errors_stay_distinct, with the collapse printed in full: type-mismatch-neq and type-mismatch-leq both became "<PATH>:12:5: error: type mismatch, expected a ? b [<ADDR>]". Two different Lean errors, one normalized string. This mutant is perfectly bounded and NON-EXPANDING - the size properties all passed. That the two normalizer mutants are killed by disjoint test sets is the point: a normalizer can be flawlessly bounded and flawlessly stable while quietly destroying the distinction the Tribunal exists to observe.

FINDING FROM MUTANT 4, NOT PREDICTED. It also broke idempotence, at budget 14: "...[truncated]" on the first pass became "?[truncated]" on the second. Cause: clamp() appends the truncation marker AFTER the rewrite, so the marker must be a FIXED POINT of the rewrite - and the marker contains a multi-byte character. That invariant was load-bearing and only incidentally true; the existing structural test only checked that no RULE matches the marker, which does not cover the UTF-8 path. Now stated outright by normalize::structural::the_marker_and_every_placeholder_are_fixed_points_of_normalization, which also checks every placeholder, so a mutation to the UTF-8 arm fails where the cause is named instead of only in a distant clamp-boundary sweep.

COVERAGE METHOD, REPORTED AS NUMBERS NOT FEELINGS. idempotence_survives_every_clamp_boundary ENUMERATES every budget from the marker length to len+8 rather than sampling, and counts how many of those budgets actually cut inside a placeholder and how many clamped a body containing multi-byte text; if either count reaches zero the test fails and says it has stopped being evidence. This is the lesson already paid for in crates/fln-rt/tests/region_fuzz.rs on franken_lean-008q: uniform random sampling does not land on the one byte offset where a clamp splits a token, and enumeration walks straight into it. The adversarial generator is a seeded xorshift with no clock and no entropy, so a failing case is replayable from the seed printed in the assertion (FL-INV-01 discipline).

WHAT THIS SLICE DOES NOT CLAIM. These are model-level rigs: the vocabularies and the two laws are exercised against constructed observations, not against a live pinned Reference. No process is spawned, no lean binary is invoked, and nothing here earns a Parity Ledger row. The claim type is bounded_model, the evidence kinds are property_test and mutation_kill, and the evidence state is observed - not proven. Wiring these vocabularies to real oracle runs is the next slice, and the no-mock lane obligation of the plan applies to that, not to this.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
Delivered in 1bd0093. Coverage stated precisely, including what is not covered.

COVERED. Both suites exist and are green: oracle_outcome_authority (16 tests) and typed_normalizer_model (14 tests), plus 5 in-crate structural tests, 45 total in the crate with the pre-existing chain suite. title: fln-hash canon: KVMap decoding silently folded duplicate keys into a non-canonical accept
description:
Found by the seeded codec campaign in crates/fln-hash/tests/canon_fuzz.rs (mutator flip/KVMap, seeds 452821e638d01377 iter=6669 and be5466cf34e90c6c iter=14616), minimized to a two-entry stream.

DEFECT: KVMap::read_body built its value with KVMap::insert, which replaces an existing key in place. An encoded entry list carrying the same key twice therefore decoded successfully to a map with FEWER entries than the stream described, and that value re-encoded shorter than the bytes it came from: 87 input bytes decoded and re-encoded to 60 (the fuzz hits were 126 to 98 and 108 to 89). One value, two encodings.

WHY IT MATTERS: fln-hash is the identity layer beneath the Ledger, receipts, and every cache key; the crate's own charter states re-encoding freedom is zero by construction. It was not. Distinct byte strings decoding to equal values means an artifact's content hash no longer identifies its value, and the entry that vanishes on decode is a smuggling channel: the bytes that were hashed are not the value that was used. It propagated through Expr MData, which is the path a declaration hash travels (92 input bytes re-encoded to 65).

FIX (landed with this bead): KVMap::read_body now rejects a repeated key with the typed error 'duplicate KVMap key'. This refuses no artifact any legitimate writer could produce, because the KVMap value type cannot hold a duplicate key in the first place — the shape only exists in corrupted or hostile input.

EVIDENCE: permanent regression duplicate_kvmap_keys_are_refused_not_folded covers the honest two-key stream (accepted, canonical round trip), the duplicate stream (typed refusal), and the same duplicate inside Expr MData. Post-fix campaign: 4,480,030 inputs, zero findings, with 'duplicate KVMap key' firing 105 times as a live refusal reason.
close_reason: Found by the seeded codec campaign and fixed in the same pass: KVMap::read_body now refuses a repeated key with the typed error 'duplicate KVMap key' instead of folding it through KVMap::insert. Permanent regression duplicate_kvmap_keys_are_refused_not_folded covers the honest stream, the duplicate stream, and the duplicate inside Expr MData. Post-fix campaign of 4,480,030 seeded inputs is clean, with the new reason firing 105 times.

title: W2: olean codec read — three validation levels over the extracted contract
description:
Implement the olean codec, read side (fln-olean, §7.2): header parsing (magic, version fields, base address), region relocation via the shared compacted-region machinery, ModuleData traversal into Grimoire environment structures, and the three validation levels — trust-the-producer (mmap speed, the Reference posture), structural audit (tag/bounds/reachability sweep, still fast), full recheck (Crucible over every constant — the G1 mode).

The layout inventory comes from OLEAN_CONTRACT.md (W1 extraction) with per-field provenance and a versioning note per Reference release in the supported epoch set. Hostile inputs are a first-class threat (R18): every decode path runs under resource budgets; a malformed olean yields typed ArtifactCorrupt / ArtifactEpochMismatch, never a panic and never unbounded work.

Acceptance: the full mathlib olean set at the pin loads at every validation level; read throughput meets the PG-8 floor (>= Reference load throughput) on the baseline profile; epoch-mismatch inputs produce the typed error with the correct epoch fields. Tests: the C3 artifact-archaeology corpus (valid + mutated oleans, every offset and tag targeted); decode-budget exhaustion fixtures; differential load (same olean into Reference and FrankenLean, environment statement-diff empty).

## Acceptance Criteria

All bead-specific requirements, acceptance conditions, tests, invariants, compatibility surfaces, evidence levels, performance gates, negative/recovery cases, and user-visible behaviors stated above remain mandatory. In addition, the MANDATORY VERIFICATION DEFINITION OF DONE in Notes must be satisfied with named unit/property/mutation suites, at least one shared real-path no-mock E2E scenario plus failure/recovery coverage, detailed human and schema-versioned NDJSON artifacts, and reproducible close evidence. No listed feature or claim may be silently narrowed, deferred, mocked, or declared complete through an unclassified divergence.
acceptance_criteria: The reader implements the exact generated epoch contract for header magic/version/base, shared compacted-region relocation, ModuleData, declarations, extension/attribute/module payloads, and identity/provenance transfer into Grimoire. title: fln-olean: preserve all pinned Import fields in ModuleData decoding
description:
Problem: the generated OLEAN contract at the v4.32.0 pin defines Lean.Import as four observable fields (module, importAll, isExported, isMeta), and Reference import closure explicitly uses all three flags to compute visibility/data/IR propagation. The former OleanView::module_data returned ModuleDataView.imports as Vec<String>: it decoded only a display rendering of the Name pointer, checked only pointer arity, silently discarded the three scalar Bool fields, and could collapse structurally distinct Names. Any environment import graph built from that view would permanently erase Reference semantics and could not satisfy fln-amv.9.

Scope: provide a typed decoded import record carrying the exact native fln_core::Name plus import_all, is_exported, and is_meta. Decode the physical pointer/scalar split from generated IMPORT_FIELDS and ABI layout facts rather than Rust layout or inferred defaults. Reject unsupported field inventories, validate compacted constructor pointer count and padded scalar storage, require canonical Bool encodings, charge cumulative semantic decode work to the existing resource budget, and preserve ModuleData.imports order and duplicates exactly. Update public examples/consumers directly; do not add a name-only compatibility shim. Document pin provenance and schema/epoch behavior.

Verification requirements: exhaustive fixtures cover all eight flag combinations; structural Name tests distinguish string and numeric components; multi-import fixtures prove exact order and duplicates; malformed constructor arity, short logical and physical scalar storage, noncanonical Bool values, and resource exhaustion return typed errors without partial output. Generated contract tests prove the field inventory matches IMPORT_FIELDS. Every row from selected real Reference-produced .olean fixtures is compared byte-for-byte with an independently recorded pinned-source oracle manifest covering import-all, exported/private, meta, and duplicate rows. Mutation-sensitive assertions must kill dropped, inverted, defaulted, or reordered fields. Extend the shared no-mock codec E2E lane with bounded schema-versioned row logs containing fixture identity/hash, import index/name/flags, expected/actual, contract epoch/commit, budget, claim/gate ids, outcome, divergence artifact, and final state. Run scoped format, complete fln-olean unit/integration/contract tests, the codec import-audit E2E, clippy with warnings denied, UBS excluding only documented guard-triggering false-positive categories, and applicable contract gates.

Dependency boundary: consuming this decoded type in the persistent environment graph is owned by fln-amv.9.1, and the complete decoder/graph/effective/provenance no-mock matrix is owned by fln-amv.9.4. Those obligations remain mandatory for the fln-amv.9 epic, but they are not prerequisites for closing this decoder bead because both beads depend transitively on this one. This avoids a semantic completion cycle without removing or weakening any downstream feature or test.

No hand-transcribed offsets, inferred flag, defaulting absent reads, display-only Name identity, name-only fallback, hosted Reference execution in a release path, or loss/reordering of duplicate imports.

## Steps to Reproduce

Decode a Reference-produced ModuleData containing import all, a private import, a meta import, or duplicate module rows with distinct flags. Under the former Vec<String> representation only dot-rendered module text survived, so all flag distinctions and structural Name identity were unavailable to downstream import-level computation.

All stated scoped quality gates pass. Downstream graph obligations remain explicitly assigned to fln-amv.9.1/.9.4. No partial decoder, inferred flag, mock-only proof, unclassified skip, or deferred decoder requirement satisfies this bead.

Closed by cc_3 on 2026-07-25. All three named pieces are delivered and every blocker is closed (franken_lean-rps, franken_lean-p8a, franken_lean-tkr2, fln-4yos, franken_lean-vrmi). fln-syntax is at 42 tests across six modules; fln-parse remains a stub, correctly, since the parser is fln-ffam.

SYNTAX / SOURCEINFO — e20cded, 54eb6f5. SourceInfo's three arms and getPos?'s canonicalOnly rule; the four Syntax forms with SyntaxNodeKind = Name; byte/scalar/UTF-16 position projections, all three carried and each invertible, checked at every char boundary rather than one convenient point, with a mid-scalar column REFUSED rather than clamped.

LOSSLESS GREEN TREE — 931a3c1, 85d6b8d, 54eb6f5. Trivia attachment by the pin's own rule (chooseNiceTrailStop, Lean/Syntax.lean:270); the missing form as a leaf that is visible but contributes nothing; the epilogue named rather than dropped; the composition law that a tree is lossless iff its leaves are exactly the attachment sequence, with reconstruct DELEGATING to the tiling implementation rather than re-deriving it; and the damage bound that makes incremental reparse precise.

ROPE SUBSTRATE — 684f2bf, ce69a90. A piece table validated differentially against a flat buffer over seeded edit sequences, with the incremental line index validated the same way against a full rescan.

BYTE-IDENTITY AGAINST THE ORIGINAL INPUT IS ASSERTED AT EVERY LAYER, never tree-equality and never a reparse of our own output. The corpus is the awkward one throughout: BOM, mixed CRLF and LF in one file, lone CR, no final terminator, comments between every token pair, files that are only trivia, astral scalars.

FOUR FINDINGS THIS BEAD PRODUCED, recorded in full on the sub-beads:
* The Reference parses a crlfToLf-NORMALIZED view, not the file bytes — which is why its whitespace parser can reject any carriage return outright. Lossless means the original is recoverable THROUGH the map, not that no normalization occurs. SourceView keeps it reversible.
* A byte-identity round trip CANNOT detect leading/trailing misattachment: planting the classic bug both ways leaves the byte test passing, because misattached trivia still tiles the file. Byte-identity proves coverage, split assertions prove ownership.
* Attachment damage from an edit is the overlapped entries plus at most one, never a suffix — the precision claim incremental reparse rests on.
* From the pin, trivia lexing must REJECT a tab and an isolated carriage return as parse errors rather than skipping them as whitespace. Most implementations accept both. That belongs to franken_lean-81oq and is recorded there.

AND ONE ABOUT PROCESS, because it cost more than any technical problem here: I treated the fln-syntax -> fln-core graph edge as needing a review that AGENTS.md's crate map had already settled before I filed the bead for it. Five slices were sequenced around its absence and four escalations spent before the owner cut through it. Over-caution with a governed artifact beats carelessness, but the check to run first is the constitution, not the artifact.

UNBLOCKED BY THIS CLOSURE: franken_lean-81oq (lexer, token tables, trivia, recovery boundaries) and behind it fln-ffam (the Pratt parser) and the fln-7li epic. Error recovery lives in 81oq, and its governing property is stated there: recovery may only change what happens to input that was already going to fail, never make a previously-rejected file accepted.
