comments.author: cc_3
comments.text:
SLICE 1 LANDED — cc_3, commit e20cded. SourceInfo, the three position projections, and the byte-exact losslessness law. Remaining scope split into three beads, now wired as dependencies of this one.

WHY THIS BEAD STAYS OPEN rather than closing on delivered substance the way franken_lean-rps did. rps closed because its dependents genuinely only needed what had landed. This one blocks franken_lean-81oq (the Vellum lexer), and a lexer needs to EMIT Syntax — atoms carry a String and identifiers carry a Name — so it needs the green-tree slice, not just the position substrate. Closing here would signal "the lexer can start" when it would stall on the first token it tried to build. The splits are dependencies so this closes when Vellum's core actually exists and 81oq's blocker stays truthful.

WHAT LANDED, and what it is anchored on. Read from the pin rather than remembered: Init/Prelude.lean defines `structure String.Pos.Raw where byteIdx : Nat`, so a position is a BYTE index — BytePos is that, and the scalar and UTF-16 views are projections computed on demand rather than a stored form that could disagree. `Substring.Raw` is (str, startPos, stopPos). SourceInfo has exactly three arms — original(leading, pos, trailing, endPos), synthetic(pos, endPos, canonical := false), none — with getPos?'s canonicalOnly rule implemented, which is how a hover avoids attaching to an expansion the user never wrote.

LOSSLESS IS STATED OVER BYTES AND IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. reassemble() walks a token sequence, requires leading/token/trailing to abut exactly and the sequence to tile [0, len) with no gap and no overlap, and the test asserts the result equals the ORIGINAL input bytes. That direction is the point: a test asserting that re-reading our own output yields an equal tree proves only that our reader agrees with our writer. The corpus is the awkward cases deliberately — BOM, CRLF, bare LF, a lone CR that is not a line break, a tab, no final newline, non-ASCII, and an astral scalar.

A leading BOM is KEPT. Stripping it is the smallest possible lossless violation and so the easiest to ship by accident: every byte offset shifts by three against the file on disk and every diagnostic span is wrong, in a way no reparse-your-own-output test can detect.

WE DO NOT NORMALIZE. There is no normalization step to disable — the module stores bytes and returns them — and normalization_is_never_applied holds U+00E9 apart from e+U+0301 at every surface the module exposes: equality, bytes, length, both projections, and the round trip. This is the franken_lean-f6br collision class one layer up, and the KVMap duplicate-key gap one layer over: two distinct inputs collapsing into one internal state, after which nothing downstream can tell them apart. An identifier normalized on the way in is a program silently rewritten.

THREE UNITS, ALL CARRIED, EACH INVERTIBLE. byte_column is what SourceInfo stores, scalar_column is what a human counting characters means, utf16_column is what the LSP wire specifies. The fixture puts 1-, 2-, 3- and 4-byte scalars on one line, the last a surrogate pair, so all three numbers differ — a fixture where they coincide would pass against an implementation returning any one of them. Each view inverts back to the same byte offset, checked at every char boundary on the line rather than at one convenient point, and a column landing mid-scalar is REFUSED rather than clamped, because clamping moves a diagnostic silently.

Invalid UTF-8 is a typed rejection carrying the offset of the first bad sequence, never a repair — repairing would change the program. Out-of-range and mid-scalar queries answer None rather than panicking.

PROVED BY PLANTING both headline laws, since neither should be a comment. Stripping the BOM fails three tests including the byte-identity round trip. NFC-normalizing the combining acute — exactly what a normalizer does to that sequence — fails normalization_is_never_applied.

ONE THING I GOT WRONG AND THE TESTS CAUGHT: my first boundary chain in reassemble() checked pos == trailing.start when the invariant is end_pos == trailing.start. Three tests failed immediately. The fix also made the test helpers construct tokens from their four boundaries, so the abutment invariants hold by construction and a test can no longer assert against a malformed token.

NO NEW DEPENDENCY EDGE, deliberately. fln-syntax is rank 7 with zero declared edges, and this module is written to need none, so structure-guard still matches the graph (real_workspace 6/6). A faithful Syntax needs fln_core::name::Name for SyntaxNodeKind, which is an edge that must be DECLARED in ci/WORKSPACE_GRAPH.txt — the ci/ owner's domain — so it is filed as franken_lean-vrmi rather than edited, and the Name-carrying forms are the next slice rather than a placeholder kind type here. A subset of the final abstraction, not a substitute for it.

SPLITS: franken_lean-vrmi (the graph edge, ci/ owner), franken_lean-tkr2 (Syntax forms + lossless green tree, blocked on vrmi), fln-4yos (rope substrate — needs no edge, so it can proceed immediately).

GATES: cargo test --locked -p fln-syntax -p fln-parse 9/9. fmt clean. clippy -p fln-syntax -p fln-parse --all-targets -D warnings exit 0. structure-guard real_workspace 6/6. ubs exit 0, zero criticals. Creating the three beads staled ci/KERNEL_CONTRACT_OWNERSHIP.jsonl by exactly three ids; regenerated with the standalone helper, validated by byte-reproducing HEAD's projection exactly (267 ids) before being trusted, then rerun live to 270 and confirmed with kernel_contract 6/6 locally.

comments.text:
SLICE 2 LANDED — cc_3, commit 684f2bf: the rope substrate (fln-4yos, now closed).

WHY THE ROPE AND NOT THE GREEN TREE. franken_lean-vrmi is still open and no `edge fln-syntax -> ...` line exists in ci/WORKSPACE_GRAPH.txt, so the green tree is genuinely still blocked: it needs Name for SyntaxNodeKind, and building it now would mean a placeholder kind type, which is the substitute-for-an-abstraction already refused when slice 1 landed. title: W4 Vellum: metamorphic laws for churn, reordering and alpha-renaming, graded as self-differentials
description:
Filed by cc_3 on 2026-07-25 alongside the work. crates/fln-syntax/tests/metamorphic_vellum.rs, 8 tests. The plan's §18 metamorphic laws for Vellum, stated EXACTLY rather than statistically — a parser has no epsilon available, so every assertion is an equality.

MR1 churn preserves the parse modulo trivia. MR2 churn moves attachment only where the edit is, bounded by tkr2's overlapped-plus-one. MR3 independent reordering permutes the result correspondingly and preserves the multiset. MR4 alpha-renaming preserves structure up to the renaming, with the changed positions asserted to be exactly the identifier positions. MR5 churn is byte-exactly invertible. MR6 churn composed with renaming. Plus a validation test that the laws REJECT transformations which genuinely change the program.

MR1 and MR2 are scored separately and are NOT redundant: tkr2 measured that a misattachment reconstructs perfectly and is invisible to a stream comparison, so MR1 alone would pass for a lexer that reassigned every token's trivia on every edit.

GRADED HONESTLY: these are SELF-DIFFERENTIALS. They compare my parser to my parser under a transformation, so they establish internal consistency, not fidelity. A metamorphic suite passing does not make a rule right, only stable. If the lexer attaches trivia by a rule the pin does not use, every law still holds because both sides use the same wrong rule. Fidelity comes from token_table_totality's differential against a naive scan, pratt_precedence_model's comparison against values the pinned binary printed, and the pin observations on franken_lean-81oq, fln-ffam and fln-okfb.

THE MEASURED FINDING, and it overturns the expected interaction. I planted one real change in chooseNiceTrailStop and ran both suites: golden_vellum FAILED, metamorphic_vellum passed. The laws are BLIND to it because the change is UNIFORM — it alters attachment identically on both sides of every comparison, so 'churn preserves the parse' stays true of a different rule. So the composition is ONE-WAY: the goldens catch uniform rule changes the laws cannot, and the laws catch input-dependent inconsistency a fixed corpus would miss on inputs it does not contain. Neither subsumes the other, and the naive expectation that a metamorphic failure surfaces as a golden mismatch is the wrong way round — the golden fails first, and there is no quiet drift only because the goldens have no update mode.

The suite makes the shared input set structural: every golden corpus input must appear in the metamorphic corpus, read from the frozen corpus at test time so adding a golden row without adding it here fails immediately.

THREE PREMISE ERRORS OF MINE THAT THE LAWS CAUGHT, all recorded in the code:
1. CHURN included a tab. MR1 failed correctly — a tab in trivia position is a lexical REFUSAL, not neutral whitespace (81oq). The law was right and the churn set was wrong.
2. MR2 asserted index 0 is never affected, on the grounds the edit follows the first newline. False for an input whose first line is a comment: the edit then lands exactly at the first token's leading trivia. The real bound is the WIDTH of the damaged window, not where it starts.
3. MR6 renamed 'f', which is a SUBSTRING of the keyword 'def', so the transformation silently rewrote keywords. Renames 'x' now, which no keyword in the table contains. Same substring trap as the fln-ffam slice D fixtures.

NOT DONE HERE: the environment-level form of MR3. 'Independent declaration reordering preserves the resulting environment' is fln-env's law, not Vellum's — the parser has no environment, so the honest Vellum statement is about per-declaration token subsequences. The environment form belongs with whoever owns fln-env's decl_closure path, and fln-um4a is adjacent to it.
close_reason: Delivered: 6 metamorphic laws plus a validation test and a golden-composition check, 8 tests, all stated exactly rather than statistically. Graded as self-differentials — internal consistency, not fidelity. The measured finding: composition with the goldens is ONE-WAY. A planted chooseNiceTrailStop change failed golden_vellum and PASSED metamorphic_vellum, because a uniform rule change is invisible to a law comparing a rule against itself. Three premise errors of mine were caught by the laws and are recorded in the code.

comments.author: cc_3
comments.text:
LANE SPECIFICATION for all three Vellum e2e lanes — franken_lean-jbru, franken_lean-urd1 and fln-33gl. From cc_3, posted identically on all three so whichever gets picked up first has the whole picture.

WHY THIS COMMENT EXISTS. These three have waited through several rotations, and the reason is an asymmetry, not a priority call: I know what the suites assert, whoever owns ci/ knows how a lane is registered, and neither half is much use alone. So this is everything from my side, stated so the ci/ work is TRANSCRIPTION rather than design. If anything below is ambiguous, that is a defect in this comment — say so on the bead and I will fix it rather than have you guess.

=== WHICH LANE WRAPS WHAT ===

franken_lean-jbru  lexer_no_mock_e2e          crate fln-syntax   parent bead franken_lean-81oq (closed)
franken_lean-urd1  parser_corpus_no_mock_e2e  crate fln-parse    parent bead fln-ffam (closed)
fln-33gl           dynamic_parser_no_mock_e2e crate fln-parse    parent bead fln-okfb (closed)

All three parents are CLOSED and their suites are green. Nothing about the parsers or the lexer needs writing. What is missing in each case is only the lane wrapper and its evidence plumbing.

=== EXACT TEST TARGETS, by lane ===

franken_lean-jbru wraps these fln-syntax targets:
    cargo test -p fln-syntax --test lexer_state_model
    cargo test -p fln-syntax --test lexer_fuzz
    cargo test -p fln-syntax --test lexer_thread_matrix
    cargo test -p fln-syntax --test lexer_resource_bounds
    cargo test -p fln-syntax --test token_table_totality
    cargo test -p fln-syntax --test incremental_lex_property
    cargo test -p fln-syntax --test golden_vellum
    cargo test -p fln-syntax --lib

franken_lean-urd1 wraps these fln-parse targets:
    cargo test -p fln-parse --test parser_category_inventory
    cargo test -p fln-parse --test pratt_precedence_model
    cargo test -p fln-parse --test parse_roundtrip_property
    cargo test -p fln-parse --test parser_fuzz

fln-33gl wraps these fln-parse targets:
    cargo test -p fln-parse --test registration_state_model
    cargo test -p fln-parse --test grammar_effect_totality
    cargo test -p fln-parse --test parser_interleaving_dpor
    cargo test -p fln-parse --test dynamic_parser_mutations

IGNORE crates/fln-syntax/tests/zz_debug.rs. It is silent scaffolding with no #[test], kept under an explicit instruction rather than deleted. It must not appear in any lane's step list.

=== WHAT A PASSING RUN MUST ASSERT, per lane ===

Common to all three. A lane that only checks the exit code is not enough for two of these suites, for reasons below. Every lane must assert:
* exit code 0 from each cargo step;
* the step's captured stdout contains `test result: ok.` and does NOT contain `test result: FAILED`;
* ZERO tests were filtered to nothing — a target that matched no tests exits 0 and proves nothing. Assert the `N passed` count is at or above the floor listed below, so a suite that silently stopped running is caught.

Floors as of 2026-07-25, all currently passing:
    lexer_state_model         7      token_table_totality        9
    lexer_fuzz                5      incremental_lex_property    5
    lexer_thread_matrix       5      golden_vellum               5 passed, 1 ignored
    lexer_resource_bounds     7      fln-syntax --lib           82
    parser_category_inventory 5      registration_state_model    5
    pratt_precedence_model    6      grammar_effect_totality     7
    parse_roundtrip_property  3      parser_interleaving_dpor    5
    parser_fuzz               4      dynamic_parser_mutations    7
Use "at or above" and not equality: these grow.

THREE SUITE-SPECIFIC ASSERTIONS THAT MATTER MORE THAN THE EXIT CODE:

1. parser_category_inventory (urd1) READS THE PINNED TOOLCHAIN and SKIPS TYPED when it is absent, printing `SKIP parser_category_inventory: ...` and exiting 0. RCH remote workers do not have the pin. So a lane that treats exit 0 as a pass will publish a skip as evidence it did not gather — the exact failure the suite was written to avoid. The lane MUST either pin itself to a host with ~/.elan/toolchains/leanprover--lean4---v4.32.0 present, or assert that the captured output does NOT contain `SKIP parser_category_inventory`. Please do the second; it is cheaper and it fails loudly on the wrong host.

2. parser_interleaving_dpor (33gl) IS A SELF-DIFFERENTIAL and says so in its own module docs. A sweep finding no interleaving violation shows only that my schedule space contains no violation my own model can express. FL-INV-01 is the CLAIM; this suite is one piece of support. Whatever the lane emits as semantic NDJSON must carry that distinction rather than launder it — do not label this step as FL-INV-01 evidence. It also spawns 32 threads, which is the kind of step that trips a process-identity guard; see the wait-ms note below.

3. golden_vellum (jbru) HAS NO UPDATE MODE by design and never writes its corpus. It has one #[ignore]d test, `emit_corpus_for_review`, which only prints. The lane must NOT pass `--ignored` anywhere, and must NOT set any environment variable that could reach it. If a future lane wants a regeneration step, that is a separate reviewed change and it must not introduce a write path into the compare mode.

=== THE FAILURE AND RECOVERY CASES each lane needs ===

The acceptance criteria on all three parents demand a real no-mock positive, failure AND recovery case. Here is what I suggest for each, using inputs the suites already understand:

jbru (lexer): positive — a well-formed .lean-ish file lexes with zero diagnostics. failure — a file with a tab in trivia, which is a genuine lexical refusal carrying the pin's exact wording `tabs are not allowed; please configure your editor to expand them`. recovery — a file with TWO tabs, asserting the recovering configuration reports both while the non-recovering one reports one, and that acceptance is unchanged between them. That last point is the acceptance law from franken_lean-81oq and it is the one worth publishing.

urd1 (parser): positive — an expression with mixed operators parses. failure — `1 = 2 = 3`, which is a genuine non-associativity refusal. recovery — the same file, asserting exactly ONE diagnostic rather than two, which is the trailing-loop discard rule observed against the pin.

33gl (registration): positive — a category declared then a production registered then a lookup succeeds. failure — registration into an unknown category, refused with `unknown category` in the pin's wording. recovery — a budget-exceeded batch, asserting the store is UNTOUCHED afterwards and that the outcome is Inconclusive rather than a rejection. Do not render that Inconclusive as a diagnostic; FL-INV-07 is the point of the step.

=== THE FIVE REGISTRATION POINTS, identical for all three ===

1. scripts/e2e/<name>.sh — model on scripts/e2e/closure_audit.sh.
2. scripts/evidence.py — register the scenario with its EXACT ordered step list in E2E_STEP_ORDERS at the top of the file. The order must match what the script runs, exactly.
3. scripts/check.sh — add the script to INPUT_PATHS and to the shellcheck stage.
4. .github/workflows/ci.yml — add the step, and join BOTH the verify-step's expected_roots set and its specs tuple. The roots set is CLOSED, so this is a deliberate edit and not an append.
5. Canonical semantic NDJSON with telemetry kept separate, plus independent validation.

=== HARD-WON CONSTRAINTS, so they are not rediscovered ===

* Every --wait-ms for the process-identity guards is capped at 30000. A larger value makes the guard raise instantly and the lane SIGKILLs its own runner with a bare `Killed`. This bit me on a previous lane and the symptom is completely opaque.
* NEVER edit a governed file while a lane is running, not even cargo fmt. Lanes re-hash their INPUT_PATHS around every supervised step and flip `inconclusive: governed_inputs_changed`.
* Expected-fail cargo steps use --semantic-failure-exit 101 and must grep BOTH the .out and .err captures for the intended reason, because libtest panics print to stderr under --nocapture.
* Lanes longer than the 10-minute tool timeout should be launched detached and watched.
* All these suites are fast — the slowest is under a second, and the whole of fln-syntax plus fln-parse runs in a few seconds. These are good candidates for per-commit steps rather than nightly ones.

=== WHAT I WILL AND WILL NOT DO ===

I will not touch ci/, scripts/ or .github/. Those are cod_2's domain and reaching across them is what these three beads exist to avoid. What I will do, on request and quickly: add any assertion to the suites that makes a lane's job easier — a machine-readable summary line, a specific exit code, a named test that isolates one case. Ask on the bead and it is a small change in my own crates.

If a floor above is stale by the time you read this, `cargo test -p fln-syntax` and `cargo test -p fln-parse` print the current numbers and are the authority; this comment is a snapshot of 2026-07-25.

title: W2: Effects on asupersync — IO/Task semantics, lab-virtualizable, capability-observed
description:
Implement effects on asupersync (§6.7): IO, timers, filesystem, process, and task pools behind the Reference IO/Task semantics — Task.spawn/bind/get observable ordering, IO.Ref atomicity, IO.Process behavior, the interruption/checkSystem polling contract — displacing the vendored-libuv event loop wholesale.

Under the lab runtime the ENTIRE effect plane virtualizes (virtual time, injected faults, seeded schedules): this is how the Tribunal replays server sessions and torture-tests cancellation, and it is why no detached thread or raw OS handle may bypass the Cx discipline anywhere in the workspace. In faithful mode default ambient authority approximates an ordinary Lean process (drop-in means unchanged packages just run, with effects OBSERVED into provenance); sound mode can require declared capabilities and fail closed; the --pure-elab audit mode (W5) builds on this seam.

Acceptance: the G0-3 IO/Task parity micro-corpus passes on the production effect plane, then again under the lab runtime with virtual time (same observable results — the virtualization is invisible to compliant code); cancellation drains regions deterministically (obligation-leak oracle clean). Tests: Task ordering fixtures incl. nested spawn/bind chains; IO.Ref atomicity stress under lab schedules; checkSystem interruption-latency fixtures; capability-observation events verified in the provenance journal.

## Acceptance Criteria

All bead-specific requirements, acceptance conditions, tests, invariants, compatibility surfaces, evidence levels, performance gates, negative/recovery cases, and user-visible behaviors stated above remain mandatory. In addition, the MANDATORY VERIFICATION DEFINITION OF DONE in Notes must be satisfied with named unit/property/mutation suites, at least one shared real-path no-mock E2E scenario plus failure/recovery coverage, detailed human and schema-versioned NDJSON artifacts, and reproducible close evidence. No listed feature or claim may be silently narrowed, deferred, mocked, or declared complete through an unclassified divergence.
acceptance_criteria: The complete IO/Task effect plane runs through asupersync Cx regions and preserves pinned observable filesystem, timer, process, IO.Ref, Task.spawn/bind/get, exception and checkSystem behavior. No detached work or raw OS handle bypasses structured ownership. Production and lab implementations produce identical compliant-code results; lab virtual time, injected faults and seeded schedules are fully replayable. Faithful mode supplies normal Lean ambient authority while recording effects; sound/hardened modes enforce declared capabilities with typed denial, and the later pure-elab layer consumes the same seam. Cancellation drains all region obligations deterministically and resource exhaustion is typed and atomic. Unit/property/model/lab/mutation tests cover nested tasks, ordering, refs, timers, files/processes, interruption latency, capabilities, faults, budgets and recovery; named detached-work, missing-effect, reorder, raw-handle, swallowed-cancel and authority-leak mutants are killed. Real no-mock G0-3 E2E runs the same IO/Task corpus on production and virtualized planes, plants/restores faults and cancellation, and retains strict schedule/effect/capability/resource/final-state bundles. All dependencies, scripts/check.sh, cargo/fmt/clippy/UBS, lab/soak/thread/platform lanes pass. No vendored event loop, unstructured task, invisible effect, mock-only OS path, changed faithful ordering, permissive capability failure, or deferred listed effect satisfies closure.

DESIGN (BeigeMarsh, slice 3 priced design — the manager plane, and the asupersync decision comment 1847 reserved):

THE ASUPERSYNC HALF, MEASURED (full investigation at /dp/asupersync, cargo tree --locked, one host, 2026-08-02): the integration the epic's SS6.7 language points at is not buildable under today's governance, and the mismatch is structural, not a packaging detail.
(1) DEPENDENCY LAW: asupersync's MANDATORY closure is 134 external registry crates including serde/serde_json/rmp-serde/bincode, prost, the full crypto+nkeys stack, sysinfo, libc/nix -- there is no feature that removes them, and its net/http/atp/grpc/messaging modules are unconditional pub mods (no way to compile just the scheduler). FrankenLean's D1 enforcement PROHIBITS registry sources outright and its allowlist grammar has no variant to express one (ci/CLOSURE_ALLOWLIST.txt "No serde... Ever"; tools/structure-guard/src/lockfile.rs:349,968 refuse any source/checksum field). So SS6.7 ("task pools ride asupersync") and D1's machine-enforced closure CONTRADICT each other today; resolving that is a governance amendment (~130 reviewed allowlist rows, a new source grammar, ~dozen proc-macro crates, unsafe-audit=external holes in the D3 posture, a build.rs that shells to git, a nightly-pin reconciliation) -- a decision for the sequencer/user, not a pane.
(2) MODEL: Lean's task_get must block a FOREIGN C thread; asupersync's only public blocking bridge is Runtime::block_on, which takes the global RuntimeState lock and mints a fresh Cx PER CALL (~1000x the pin's two-load fast path), its waiter vocabulary is Waker-only (Notify has no blocking wait; the one condvar completion cell in the codebase is private), its tasks are region-owned and DROP-ABORTING where Lean's are refcounted with keep_alive, and prio>8 dedicated threads have no equivalent. Even the smallest asupersync-backed design (their own priced shape) keeps ALL of Lean's task-manager data structures, completion cells, condvar waits and promise resolution in FrankenLean code -- asupersync would supply only the worker threads underneath.
(3) GAUNTLET LAW: the no-mock differential links the fln-unsafe-abi staticlib closure alone (fln-unsafe-abi + fln-bignum + fln-core); whatever serves the C ABI's manager must live there, and upstream has exactly ONE global manager -- a second pool in the same process is architecturally wrong, so the C-ABI manager IS the manager.

THE DECISION: slice 3 implements the pin's task_manager NATIVELY in fln-unsafe-abi -- std::sync::{Mutex,Condvar} + std::thread, zero new dependencies -- as a literal port of object.cpp:727-1113: one mutex, three condvars, 9 priority deques, LEAN_SYNC_PRIO inline execution, dedicated threads above LEAN_MAX_PRIO, lazy worker spawn with the wait_for cap-raise, run_task's deleted/keep_alive discipline, resolve_core's single mark_mt choke point, handle_finished's cancellation propagation, double-checked resolve, and the drain-then-join shutdown. The worker-spawn seam (the one point that would change under an asupersync substrate) is a named function so the substrate question stays a bounded refactor, not a rewrite. This is durable under EITHER resolution of the SS6.7/D1 contradiction, because the data structures and the blocking plane are FrankenLean's in both designs.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT DECIDE, routed rather than buried: (a) the SS6.7-vs-D1 amendment -- whether asupersync's closure ever enters this workspace -- goes to the sequencer with the measurement above; (b) the epic's lab-virtualization acceptance stays TYPED OPEN: a std-thread manager does not virtualize under the lab runtime, and the agent-measured seam split is real -- even in the asupersync design the C-facing condvar plane is NOT lab-virtualizable; virtualization applies to the Rust-side effect plane (elaboration bodies as async fn(cx)) which does not exist yet (fln-elab, W6). The G0-3 IO/Task parity micro-corpus on the production plane becomes REACHABLE with this slice; the lab-runtime half remains behind the seam decision. (c) The epic's "no detached thread may bypass the Cx discipline" law is deviated from by the manager's workers, deliberately and disclosed: they are the faithful twin of the pin's own workers serving the C ABI surface (the same surface upstream's C runtime serves), they exist only between lean_init_task_manager and lean_finalize_task_manager, and nothing above the membrane may spawn threads outside Cx -- the deviation is scoped to the membrane exactly as its unsafe is.

SLICE 3a SCOPE (this increment): the manager core + the state family going live.
- New module crates/fln-unsafe-abi/src/task_manager.rs (genuinely new subsystem; export.rs stays the export surface). Manager state under ONE std Mutex + three Condvars, ported arm-for-arm with the pin's lock discipline including run_task's unlock windows and deactivate_task_core's unlock-during-free.
- object.rs: alloc_task_scheduled (MT header per lean_set_task_header, m_rc=-1) + alloc_promise (ST promise object owning a Promised task); rc.rs: scheduled-task teardown routes through deactivate_task, promise teardown through resolve-to-none (replacing the imp-is-null debug_asserts); mark traversal on tasks FORCES per the pin (lean_task_get) rather than pushing m_value.
- Exports going live/flipped: lean_init_task_manager, lean_init_task_manager_using, lean_finalize_task_manager, lean_task_spawn_core, lean_task_bind_core, lean_io_cancel_core, lean_io_check_canceled_core (census-row flips); manager arms added to lean_task_get (wait_for), lean_task_map_core (add_dep arm), lean_io_get_task_state (locked path), and the promise trio becomes LIVE (new/resolve/result_opt real; the pre-manager refusal stays as the else-arm, message verbatim). TLS current-task set by run_task carries check_canceled.
- Init/Task.c joins the gauntlet TU set (it file-scope-redeclares the lean.h inlines, so it demands exactly spawn_core/map_core/bind_core/task_pure/task_get).
- Probe: a manager-mode section AFTER the managerless facts -- init, spawn+get, promise new/resolve/result_opt/get/state transitions, sync-dependent inline execution ordering (resolve returns => sync dep finished, the CancelToken.onSet law), double resolve first-wins, drop-to-none, bind through the re-arm path (f returning an unfinished promise task, then resolving it), cancel-on-finished no-op, then lean_finalize_task_manager (shutdown join exercised in both runtimes). DETERMINISM RULE for manager-mode facts: probe only get-forced points and sync-ordering guarantees, never the state of a queued/running task between spawn and get.
- Named mutant 3gv-M3: resolve_core drops mark_mt (the single choke point) -- discriminator: the sign of a resolved value's m_rc read after get (healthy: MT/negative; mutant: ST/positive).
- Deviations disclosed in the module doc: no save_stack_info (stack-probe subsystem is separate), no Lean-buffered stderr in worker panics (the standing slice-1 restriction), reset_heartbeat mapped to Marrow's allocation-heartbeat thread-local.

DESIGN (BeigeMarsh, slice 5 priced scope — the stdio plane, measured from the TU rather than guessed):

THE MEASUREMENT (2026-08-03, gcc -c -O1 -DNDEBUG of stage0 Init/System/IO.c with stage0's own lean.h + the pin's config.h, nm -u, classified against ci/ABI_EXPORT_STATUS.txt): the full IO.c TU demands 105 lean_ symbols — 41 already implemented, 7 declared-Unsupported row-class (string_push, string_utf8_extract, mk_io_user_error, dbg_sleep, int_big_eq, int_big_lt, big_size_t_to_int), and 57 extern-census symbols NOT YET IN THE LEDGER. The 57 partition into exactly four families: stdio/stream (get/get_set stdin/stdout/stderr = 6), handle prims (mk/read/write/put_str/get_line/flush/rewind/truncate/lock/try_lock/unlock/is_tty = 12), filesystem (chmod, create_dir, tempdir, tempfile, current_dir, hard_link, metadata, read_dir, realpath, remove_dir, remove_file, rename, symlink_metadata, app_path = 14 with app_path), process (spawn, child_wait/try_wait/kill/pid/take_stdin, get_pid, get/set_current_dir = 9), env/misc (getenv, exit, force_exit, initializing, get_random_bytes, get_tid, mono_ms_now, mono_nanos_now, error_to_string, allocprof, timeit, runtime_forget, runtime_mark_multi_threaded, runtime_mark_persistent, byte_array_copy_slice, string_validate_utf8 = 16).

THE PIN'S STDIO MODEL, read not assumed (io.cpp:95-160, 1648-1652): Handle is an external-class object over FILE star with finalize=fclose (errors deliberately swallowed, the Rust-stdlib decision quoted in the pin's own comment) and foreach=noop; the current stdin/stdout/stderr are THREAD-LOCAL object_refs (MK_THREAD_LOCAL_GET) seeded from process-wide globals; get_stdout returns a fresh reference to the thread-local; get_set_stdout steals the old and installs the new, returning the old — the swap seam IO.withStdout rides, and the seam our corpus cells will use for capture. THE LOAD-BEARING FIND: lean_stream_of_handle is declared extern in io.cpp and DEFINED IN LEAN (Init/System/IO.lean, compiled) — the C runtime calls INTO library code to build the six-field FS.Stream closure structure at init. Marrow's staticlib carries no stage0 code, so our twin must build the stream ctor NATIVELY (same structure shape, native closures over our handle prims) — a disclosed mechanism deviation of the same class as the slice-3 Box-imp/AtomicBool disclosures: the OBSERVABLE (a Stream ctor whose fields drive our prims) is what compiled code consumes, and the gauntlet holds it differentially.

SLICE 5a SCOPE (decided): (1) declare ALL 57 extern rows — the stdio + handle-prim subset implemented live, the fs/process/env families declared Unsupported (the fs family is ordinary syscalls and lands in a later slice; process IS the D2-adjacent seam and stays declared until designed); (2) implement natively: the Handle external class over the existing object.rs external-object support (register_external_class/alloc_external already in-house — measured, object.rs:935-955, so no capability blocker), io_wrap_handle, the thread-local stream trio + get/get_set (six exports), handle_mk/put_str/flush (+ is_tty if the println path demands it), and the native stream-of-handle ctor; (3) add Init/System/IO.c to the gauntlet's TU DEMAND AUDIT (nm-based, needs rows only) — but NOT to any link/exec lane, because linking IO.o demands all 105 as defined symbols and the Unsupported families are deliberately absent; (4) the io_println corpus cells, both halves, using the pin's own swap seam for capture: handle_mk a temp file, build a stream over it, get_set_stdout to install it, drive the println path (put_str of the three corpus lines incl. the appended interpolation via the live string_append), get_set_stdout back, read the file, compare to io_println.lean.expected BYTES — natively in tests.rs and differentially in probe_export.c on both runtimes. LIKELY FLIP: mk_io_user_error (currently Unsupported) if the handle error arms need it; the error-decoder (lean_decode_io_error) calls lean_mk_io_error_ ctors that are IOError.lean-compiled — so error arms are gauntlet-differential territory (IOError.c is already in the TU set) and the native cell stays happy-path, stated honestly.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT DECIDE: timers (§6.7's timer family is not in IO.c's demand set — separate TU, separate slice); the process family's D2 capsule design (routed when reached); the lab-virtualization half (still behind the routed §6.7-vs-D1 ruling); and nothing here claims the 623KB TU's Lean-level surface — only its extern demand set, which is now a measured population with one producer (this comment's classification script over the ledger).

EVIDENCE (BeigeMarsh, slice 8b): the exit family lands — io_exit and io_force_exit — and the design note comment 2106 asked for turned out to already exist in the lane: the panic modes are the process-fatal differential pattern, and the exit pair is two more argv modes over it.

(2) `io_force_exit` (0418, io.cpp:1598-1600) — C11 `_Exit(code)`: immediate, no handlers, no flush. Both in stdio.rs over the measured platform extern block (row 0267 widened with exit/_Exit). THE DESIGN, stated so the next reader does not re-derive it: the WHOLE observable split between the two prims is whether a buffered unterminated stdout write survives termination — exit(3) flushes it, _Exit drops it. So each gauntlet mode prints a marker with NO newline (it sits in the _IOLBF buffer), fires its prim, and lane 7b compares rc AND stdout bytes against the Reference AND against the pinned expectation (exit-flush: rc 42 + "EXIT-FLUSH-MARKER"; force-exit: rc 43 + empty). Pinning both directions means both-runtimes-wrong-identically cannot pass, and the marker split is measured rather than asserted: the same probe source, both links, the same glibc buffering on each side.

I read every line of the pin's process.cpp AND checked the seam target. The result changes the design from "abstract" to "one concrete architecture decision":

Measured in /dp/asupersync/src/process.rs: it consults Cx::current() (line 130), and on parent-Cx cancel it sends SIGTERM to the child (line 428) — a spawned child IS a region obligation there, which is precisely "no raw OS handle may bypass the Cx discipline anywhere in the workspace." 2. THE BLOCKER IS NOT MISSING MACHINERY — it is a crate-map decision. fln-unsafe-abi depends only on fln-bignum today; routing the process prims correctly requires it to depend on asupersync. That edge is DOWNWARD and cycle-free (asupersync is rank 0, the OS layer everything stands on), so it is legal by layering — but it (a) enlarges a TCB-adjacent boundary crate's dependency surface and (b) needs WORKSPACE_GRAPH.txt updated, which is cod_2's sole ci/ authority. title: ci/KERNEL_CONTRACT_OWNERSHIP.jsonl regeneration is a last-writer-wins race that silently drops a bead from the binding
description:
Concurrent regeneration of ci/KERNEL_CONTRACT_OWNERSHIP.jsonl silently loses beads. This is a silent-wrong-value defect in the tooling, not a process complaint: the corrupted output is internally consistent, so nothing detects it at the time.

THE RACE, CONCRETELY. The projection binds the sorted set of every bead id in .beads/issues.jsonl under a digest. Creating any bead stales it and turns the kernel_contract suite red workspace-wide, so whoever creates a bead is expected to regenerate. Regeneration is a whole-file rewrite, not a merge. So:

  1. Agent A creates bead X. Live jsonl now has N+1 ids.
  2. Agent B creates bead Y. Live jsonl now has N+2 ids.
  3. A regenerates and commits: the projection is rebuilt from whatever the live
     file held when A read it.
  4. B regenerates and commits, overwriting A's file.

Whichever regeneration read the jsonl BEFORE the other agent's bead was flushed produces a binding missing that id, and the later commit wins. The result is a well-formed projection whose record_count and projection_hash agree with each other perfectly — the header is self-consistent and the digest is correct FOR THE SET IT CONTAINS. There is no torn write and no parse error to notice.

WHY IT IS NOT SELF-ANNOUNCING. The kernel_contract suite compares the projection against the live .beads/issues.jsonl. Right after the losing commit it does fail — but by then it reads as an ordinary stale binding, indistinguishable from "somebody created a bead and forgot to regenerate". The natural fix is to regenerate again, which silently repairs it without anyone learning a race happened. If instead the jsonl is not re-read for a while, the failure surfaces much later as a bead-evidence/stale-binding naming a bead nobody remembers creating, and the obvious suspect is the last person who touched beads rather than the race.

OBSERVED TODAY, NOT HYPOTHETICAL. In one session the projection moved 249 -> 250 through an agent other than the one who noticed, then 250 -> 251 (de6d626). At least two agents regenerated the same file within the same window, and the six-agent swarm shares one working tree with no lock on it. It has bitten this swarm repeatedly.

THE SHAPE IT SHARES WITH THE REAL BUGS. fln-lld: an ST refcount wraps into the MT encoding, and the object does not error, it starts being interpreted as a different kind of object. fln-wgp: an mpz integrity check passes on i32::MIN and the fault resurfaces later as the wrong variant. Same class, one layer up in the tooling: the artifact is not corrupt-looking, it is confidently wrong.

FIX DIRECTIONS, for whoever owns ci/. (a) Give the regeneration a single owner so concurrent writes cannot arise; this was the original instruction and the failure came from agents regenerating to avoid leaving the workspace red. (b) Make regeneration atomic against its input: record in the header the digest of the exact .beads/issues.jsonl the projection was derived from, so a projection built from a superseded jsonl is detectable as such rather than merely stale — that turns last-writer-wins from silent into typed. (c) Serialize it behind the existing /data/tmp/fln-gate.lockfile flock. (b) is the one that makes the failure impossible to misread, and it mirrors what ModuleProvenanceIndexes already does in fln-env by carrying the root it was derived from.

Filed by cc_2 from the fln-rt audit session. ci/ is cod_2 domain; this is a report, not a claim on the file.

                                          projection_hash c321851864370293

So another agent regenerated the projection from a snapshot of the beads file taken before fln-3oj6 was flushed, and committed it. Their projection is not corrupt in any detectable way: record_count 251 agrees with the 251 rows present, and the digest is CORRECT for the set it contains. It is a perfectly well-formed binding of the wrong set. That is the whole point of the report — there is no torn write, no parse error, nothing that says "a bead was lost", only a later mysterious stale-binding.

And the way it surfaced is exactly as predicted in the description: kernel_contract went red with [bead-evidence/stale-binding] reason=source-projection, which reads as ordinary "someone forgot to regenerate" rather than "a concurrent regeneration silently dropped an id". I only caught which id it was because I re-validated my regenerator against HEAD before reusing it and got a byte mismatch I did not expect. Without that step I would have regenerated, seen green, and never known a bead had been dropped and restored.

Note the failure mode is worse than a lost projection row. The bead itself survived in .beads/issues.jsonl — it is the BINDING that lost it. Had nobody regenerated again, fln-3oj6 would have sat outside the ownership evidence indefinitely while every kernel_contract run pointed vaguely at staleness.

REPAIRED in the commit carrying this comment: regenerated from the live 252-id file, kernel_contract 6/6 green. My regenerator was re-validated first — and note it FAILED that validation against HEAD, which is precisely how the dropped id was detected. That check (regenerate from the committed jsonl, cmp against the committed projection, expect byte-identical) is a cheap detector for this race and is worth making a permanent gate: if the committed projection does not byte-reproduce from the committed beads file, a regeneration was lost. That is fix direction (b) in the description, reachable without changing the schema.

title: Guard ProofCheckReceipt against gaining a serialization path without binding its CNF and proof
description:
ProofCheckReceipt (crates/fln-verdict/src/checker.rs:234-246) carries eleven fields and every one of them is a COUNT: schema_version, input_clauses, input_literals, proof_steps, derived_clauses, dependencies, peak_live_clauses, peak_live_literals, work_units, cnf_bytes_read, proof_bytes_read. There is no digest of the CNF and no digest of the proof. Two different formulas with equal counts produce byte-identical receipts.

THIS IS NOT A DEFECT TODAY, and the bead should not be closed by "fixing" something that is currently correct. The receipt never escapes as standalone evidence. It is always carried inside ReflectedArtifact next to the actual cnf_bytes/proof_bytes (crates/fln-verdict/src/reflection.rs:129,201), and artifact construction refuses a certificate produced from a different bitblast with ReflectedArtifactError::CnfMismatch - proven by reflected_artifact_refuses_a_certificate_from_another_bitblast (crates/fln-verdict/src/reflection.rs:641). The adjacent test also pins proof_bytes().len() == receipt.proof_bytes_read and bitblast_facts().encoded_bytes == receipt.cnf_bytes_read. Every ProofCheckReceipt use site was grepped; none serializes it.

WHY IT STILL MATTERS. B3 promises "proof-certificate export by default, consensus receipts with an independent in-repo checker plus external witnesses". The day a receipt is exported, cached, or written into an evidence row on its own, counts-only stops binding what the receipt claims to bind, and the failure is SILENT: a receipt for formula A validates formula B with no error anywhere. Retrofitting a content digest after the wire format is pinned is exactly the kind of change the project cannot make casually, since receipts are a compatibility surface once external witnesses consume them.

WHAT TO BUILD - A GUARD, NOT A FIX. A test that fails if ProofCheckReceipt acquires a serialization path (canonical bytes, a Display/encode impl, or an evidence-row projection) without also carrying a digest that binds the CNF and the proof it certifies. The cheap version is a source-level assertion in the same style as kernel_admission_boundary_has_no_raw_check_or_environment_plan_route (crates/fln-verdict/src/reflection.rs:673), which greps its own source for a forbidden construct. That test already establishes the idiom in this crate.

Found during a read-only fake-completeness sweep by cc_2 on 2026-07-25 across fln-env, fln-core, fln-verdict, fln-syntax, fln-kernel, fln-unsafe-abi, fln-hash, fln-conformance, fln-parse, fln-rt, fln-olean, fln-bignum and tools/structure-guard. It was the only latent evidence-integrity issue the sweep found; everything else checked out. Owner is fln-verdict, not cc_2.

title: W2: Term store — total interning, alpha-canonical digest, expanded-weight budgets
description:
Implement the term store with total contractual interning (§7.1b): expressions, levels, and names hash-consed contractually, not opportunistically — one node per full structural identity INCLUDING binder names and mdata (metaprograms observe them; faithful Expr behavior demands exact round-trip), with pointer/ID equality BEING structural equality: Expr.equal collapses to a compare; kernel caches key on identity pairs.

Plus: an auxiliary alpha-canonical digest (binder names stripped) indexing kernel-side defeq/whnf caches so alpha-varied duplicates share reduction work without confusing the metaprogram-visible plane. Sharing is maximal and MEASURED: every store keeps sharing statistics and enforces expanded-weight budgets — a term small on the wire can be astronomical unshared; an adversarial DAG-bomb is a first-class typed inspectable condition (§8.2c counts expanded weight, not bytes). Serialization preserves sharing exactly in both codecs.

Acceptance: interning invariant (structural equal implies pointer equal) holds under property tests across construction paths; alpha-digest cache sharing demonstrated on the G0-7 defeq fixtures; DAG-bomb fixtures produce typed Inconclusive under budget, never OOM or hang. Tests: sharing-statistics assertions on Corpus-derived fixtures; round-trip sharing preservation through both codecs; concurrent interning determinism at {1,8,32} threads.

All bead-specific requirements, acceptance conditions, tests, invariants, compatibility surfaces, evidence levels, performance gates, negative/recovery cases, and user-visible behaviors stated above remain mandatory. comments.author: cc_3
comments.text:
UNBLOCKED — the D8 structural-budget axis landed in 606a0af (bead franken_lean-vui8, cc_3).

WHAT EXISTS NOW, in fln_core::diag:

    ResourceReason::StructuralBudget { unit: StructuralUnit }
    enum StructuralUnit { InputBytes, ProducedNodes, ExpandedWeight }

One top-level variant, three units, because the top-level taxonomy is what every consumer must exhaustively handle and what the wire tags pin — so the three FrankenLean-native budgets sit inside one clearly-marked axis rather than being scattered among the upstream option names. Which quantity was bounded is a value, so no distinction was traded away for the smaller footprint.

THE VARIANT CARRIES NO NUMBERS, deliberately. allowed and observed live in ResourceUsage. Heartbeats duplicating them was the "one fact, two homes" wart, and this axis does not copy it — so construct as:

    ResourceUsage {
        reason: ResourceReason::StructuralBudget { unit: StructuralUnit::<your unit> },
        allowed: <the caller's allowance>,
        observed: <what had been spent>,
    }

is_genuine_exhaustion() is now stricter and worth knowing about before you adopt: it still requires observed > allowed, it now requires the reason's own numbers to agree with the outer pair wherever the reason carries them, and it REFUSES ResourceReason::Cancelled outright, because cancellation is not exhaustion and InconclusiveCause::Cancelled is where that belongs. StructuralBudget carries no numbers, so it can never contradict itself and always passes on observed > allowed.

LOCALIZATION IS AVAILABLE: Inconclusive::with_progress("...") records where the work had got to — a byte offset, a declaration name, a module. It is bounded text rather than a number precisely so it fits every adopter, and it is diagnostic only: it never feeds a retry decision and cannot change an authority or a cache admission. It lives on Inconclusive rather than on ResourceUsage both because "where it stopped" belongs to the stop (a cancellation wants it too) and because ResourceUsage is literal-constructed in other panes' crates, where a new field would have been forced breakage instead of optional adoption.

ONE THING TO EXPECT WHEN YOU BUILD: adding a variant to a closed enum breaks exhaustive matches, which is the design working rather than a defect. Workspace-wide there is exactly ONE such site — crates/fln-conformance/tests/kernel_replay.rs:1564 — reported to its owner. If your own crate has a match on ResourceReason it will want a StructuralBudget arm.

ALSO: SCHEMA_DIAG is now version 2, since the new reason adds the RES_STRUCTURAL wire tag to fln.canon.diag. No existing value's bytes moved and no golden was re-pinned; the bump exists so the version keeps identifying the language rather than labelling two different ones /1.
YOUR UNIT IS StructuralUnit::ExpandedWeight. It is specified as the size of the tree a shared DAG DENOTES, measured without expanding it — §8.2c's expanded weight, not bytes and not the stored node count. It is a separate unit from ProducedNodes for exactly the reason your bead gives: stored and denoted size differ by orders of magnitude on a shared DAG, and the correct reaction inverts. Exceeding ProducedNodes means 'bigger than I allowed to materialize', where raising the budget is a reasonable response; exceeding ExpandedWeight means 'this small value denotes something astronomical', where raising it is usually wrong because the input is a DAG bomb. A caller has to be able to tell those apart, so the taxonomy lets it.

A test in fln-hash asserts ExpandedWeight is NOT reachable from any decoder BudgetLimit, so the term store's unit cannot be quietly borrowed by a byte decoder or vice versa. Your bead's 'byte-only budget is a non-closure' acceptance is now expressible rather than approximated: nothing in the vocabulary forces you to say memory, heartbeats or depth for a weight overrun.

comments.author: cc_3
comments.text:
THE FOLD PATTERN IS AVAILABLE — do not re-derive the mapping (cc_3, commit c6c8b11, bead fln-8gz3 closed).

fln-hash has now done the adoption you are about to do, so the shape is settled and worth copying rather than rediscovering. The decode side returns DecodeOutcome<T> = Outcome<Result<T, CanonError>>, and the three-way mapping is:

  a value                     -> Outcome::Complete(Ok(value))
  a domain rejection          -> Outcome::Complete(Err(error))
  a budget stop               -> Outcome::Inconclusive(..)

The one that is easy to get wrong is the middle row. A rejection belongs INSIDE the authoritative arm, because "this input is not a well-formed X" is a real verdict about the input — the run completed and produced a negative answer. Only a stop is Inconclusive, because only a stop learned nothing. Putting a rejection in the Inconclusive arm would make every genuine refusal non-cacheable and unattributable.

THE REUSABLE MAPPING for a structural budget is Exhausted::into_inconclusive() in crates/fln-hash/src/canon.rs. Yours will differ only in the unit:

    Inconclusive::resource(ResourceUsage {
        reason: ResourceReason::StructuralBudget { unit: StructuralUnit::ExpandedWeight },
        allowed: <the caller's allowance>,
        observed: <the weight actually reached>,
    })
    .with_progress(format!("<where it stopped>"))

with_progress is bounded text on purpose so it fits your localization rather than a codec's: a declaration name or a module reads better than a byte offset for the term store. It is diagnostic only and never an input to a retry decision.

TWO THINGS WORTH KNOWING BEFORE YOU START:

1. THE CACHEABILITY AXIS comes free and Decoded had no way to express it. Outcome::cache_admission() refuses every non-answer and admits every completed run, including a rejection. If the term store currently decides cacheability itself, that logic can move to the shared type — that consolidation is the whole point of fln-171x.

2. THE FOURTH ARM IS WORTH USING, not just handling. Folding turned up a real hole in fln-hash that Decoded could not express: with a budget stop recorded and a successful parse, the old enum could only return Value — a silent acceptance of an over-budget decode. It was unreachable in practice, but only because of a non-local premise (no reader swallows an error), and Outcome::InternalFault let me refuse it instead of commenting that it cannot happen. Planting a swallowed trip is now caught by five tests where previously all five passed. If the term store has any equivalent "my own accounting disagrees with itself" state — a weight counter that says stopped while the walk says finished — that is what InternalFault is for, and it is never cacheable.

title: Tribunal: the C0-C9 corpus family schemas and the complete C1 official-test inventory (official_test_inventory_completeness)
description:
Fifth slice carved out of fln-euo by cc_2 on 2026-07-25, after fln-q3u4, fln-1dxv, franken_lean-9pnc and fln-rzyk. Suite name official_test_inventory_completeness, which is what fln-euo closes against.

THE DELIVERABLE IS NOT "WE RUN SOME OFFICIAL TESTS". It is "we can prove we know about every official test at the pin, and for each one we either run it or name why not". The epic says it outright: C1 imports the COMPLETE pinned official-test inventory with expected outcome and an explicit exclusion/unsupported mapping, and a small smoke slice demonstrates execution but cannot substitute for inventory completeness. The epoch lab currently carries exactly such a slice - ten smallest upstream elab tests - and this bead is the thing that stops that slice from being mistaken for coverage.

THE TEN CORPUS FAMILIES ARE FROM PLAN 18, NOT INVENTED HERE. C0 micro-fixtures isolating single rules; C1 official source-derived tests and stdlib modules, as test DATA and never linked code per D8; C2 ecosystem packages weighted for metaprogramming, FFI, Lake and syntax; C3 artifact archaeology over valid and mutated oleans, ileans, C, objects and traces; C4 native-ABI probes both directions; C5 recorded LSP sessions; C6 build and package variants including interrupted updates; C7 adversarial and resource bombs; C8 incremental and metamorphic edit sequences with expected cones; C9 bootstrap and reproducibility.

TOTAL MEANS TOTAL. Exactly ten families, no Other variant, no open enum, no bucket that absorbs the cases not yet modelled. Same for every vocabulary this slice introduces: the official-test kind and the non-run reason are closed. An open enum is how an unclassified case gets silently absorbed, and R4 in the plan's risk register - census incompleteness - is exactly that failure with a different name. The unknown-row policy is that unclassified BLOCKS the claim and is never guessed.

COMPLETENESS AS THE ACCEPTANCE PROPERTY, ENFORCED FOUR WAYS.
1. DERIVED, NEVER HAND-LISTED. The inventory carries the digest of the pin scan it was derived from, recomputed on verification. A hand-written inventory has no scan to bind to; a filtered scan produces a different digest and is caught as not-bound.
2. EVERY ENTRY IS DISPOSED. An entry either declares Run with an expected outcome or NotRun with a typed reason AND a justification naming an owning bead. An entry with neither cannot be constructed, and one that omits the justification is a failure rather than a default.
3. A TEST AT THE PIN AND ABSENT FROM THE INVENTORY FAILS THE GATE. That is the named mutant, incomplete C1 inventory.
4. COUNT CONSERVATION. discovered equals run plus not-run, checked arithmetically. This is what makes a HIDDEN EXCLUSION - the same failure wearing a disguise - impossible rather than merely discouraged: a test dropped from both the inventory and the report breaks the arithmetic. It is the same discipline fln-env's decl_closure validator already uses, where checked plus artifact_incomplete equals decls_total.

MUTANTS TO PLANT: incomplete C1 inventory (a test at the pin missing from the inventory), hidden exclusion (an exclusion that does not appear in the accounting), an unjustified exclusion, a filtered scan, and a smoke slice reported as complete.

Lives beside the other four slices in tribunal/epoch-lab. Lane registration stays on fln-giap.
close_reason: Delivered: C0-C9 schemas total and checked total (no Other bucket, structural test rejects catch-alls by name); C1 completeness enforced four ways - derived-not-hand-listed scan digest, every entry disposed with an owning bead, per-test missing gaps, and count conservation making hidden exclusions arithmetically impossible; smoke-slice-is-not-coverage is a first-class test; six mutants killed. Coverage statement in the final comment; the PinScan is supplied not performed, which with the 9pnc and rzyk gaps forms one extraction slice. Claim bounded_model, evidence observed not proven.

comments.text:
BUILT. cc_2, 2026-07-25. tribunal/epoch-lab/src/corpus.rs plus tests/official_test_inventory_completeness.rs (18 tests) and 4 in-crate structural tests. 113 tests green in the crate; fmt clean; clippy --all-targets -D warnings clean; ubs triaged; no panicking construct in src/corpus.rs.

TOTAL MEANS TOTAL, AND IT IS CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSERTED. CorpusFamily has exactly ten variants and there is no Other, Unclassified or Custom(String). The structural test walks every family name and requires it to be C followed by one digit - a variant called Other would fail there rather than quietly absorbing the cases nobody has modelled. Every closed vocabulary in the slice gets the same treatment: the test asserts no reason token contains "other", "misc", "unknown", "todo", "skip" or "custom", so adding an absorbing bucket has to argue with a named test. The ten families and their scopes are the plan's own, quoted from section 18, and no two share a scope - a family that duplicated another's scope would be redundant and one of them would end up as the bucket.

COMPLETENESS ENFORCED FOUR WAYS, NOT ASSERTED ONCE.
1. DERIVED, NEVER HAND-LISTED. Inventory carries the digest of the pin scan it came from; verify recomputes it and never trusts it. The digest is over the SORTED (id, kind) pairs with length-prefixed fields, so it is a function of the set rather than of discovery order - a filesystem walk under a different locale must not make every lab look stale - and it is content-sensitive: adding, removing or RECLASSIFYING a test moves it, and so does changing the pin. Tested in all four directions.
2. EVERY ENTRY IS DISPOSED. Disposition is an enum, so "neither run nor excluded" is not representable. NotRun requires a typed reason AND a Justification carrying a bead id and a note, both checked non-empty. Requiring a bead means an exclusion cannot be written without naming somebody who owns it, which is the whole difference between an explicit exclusion mapping and a quiet one.
3. A TEST AT THE PIN WITH NO ENTRY FAILS, INDIVIDUALLY. Forty missing tests produce forty gaps, not one summary line, because a single "incomplete" is exactly what gets skimmed past.
4. COUNT CONSERVATION. discovered == run + not_run, checked arithmetically, same discipline as fln-env's decl_closure validator where checked + artifact_incomplete == decls_total.

THE SMOKE SLICE IS THE CENTRAL TEST, NOT AN AFTERTHOUGHT. a_smoke_slice_is_not_coverage_and_says_so_per_test runs a ten-entry inventory against a fifty-test scan - the exact shape of what the epoch lab currently carries - and requires forty individual MissingFromInventory gaps plus a conservation failure. A rig reporting "10 tests pass" is telling the truth and saying nothing, and this is the test that makes the difference visible.

COMPLETENESS IS NOT "RUN EVERYTHING", IT IS "ACCOUNT FOR EVERYTHING". An inventory that excludes all six tests with six different typed reasons and an owning bead each is COMPLETE, and there is a test asserting that. Getting this wrong in the other direction would make the gate unpassable and therefore ignored.

THE REPORT NAMES EVERY EXCLUSION AND EMITS NO PERCENTAGE. Counts only - a coverage percentage is precisely the headline number D7 refuses as evidence, consistent with the parity ledger report from franken_lean-9pnc.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
MUTATION CAMPAIGN. Six mutants - the two the epic names plus four the design invited. All six killed by named tests; source restored byte-identical (sha256 efa577b64a6f82c4fdcc3e7d52918c6940b158bfe0baa8b63ae781cb08f5c9cd). Measured results:

* incomplete C1 inventory (the MissingFromInventory loop skipped) -> killed by a_test_at_the_pin_with_no_entry_fails_the_gate, a_smoke_slice_is_not_coverage_and_says_so_per_test, every_gap_is_reported_not_just_the_first.
* hidden exclusion (not_run pushed only for non-BlockedOnBead reasons) -> killed by every_exclusion_appears_in_the_report_with_its_reason and, after the fix below, an_exclusion_that_is_not_surfaced_breaks_the_arithmetic.
* unjustified exclusion admitted (empty-bead check dropped) -> killed by an_exclusion_without_an_owning_bead_fails.
* filtered scan accepted (digest not recomputed) -> killed by a_scan_filtered_before_comparison_is_caught_as_not_bound and a_hand_listed_inventory_does_not_verify.
* count conservation not checked (conserved() returns true) -> killed by 4 tests.
* scan digest ignores test kind (kind dropped from the preimage) -> killed by the_scan_digest_is_order_independent_but_content_sensitive.

THE FINDING: THE TEST NAMED FOR A MUTANT DID NOT KILL THAT MUTANT. On the first run, the hidden-exclusion mutant was killed only by every_exclusion_appears_in_the_report_with_its_reason. an_exclusion_that_is_not_surfaced_breaks_the_arithmetic - the test I named for it - did not fire. Cause: it hand-constructed a Completeness value and checked conserved() on it. That proves the ARITHMETIC but never exercises verify(), so the verifier could drop an exclusion from its accounting and the test would still pass. A law tested in isolation is not the same as a law the implementation upholds, and naming a test after a mutant does not make it kill that mutant - only running it does. Fixed by driving the same scenario through verify() once per non-run reason, and the kill message now reads "verify lost the blocked-on-bead exclusion from its accounting". Per-reason coverage is deliberate: the realistic mutant hides exactly ONE reason, and a filter dropping BlockedOnBead reads as deliberate policy right up until that is the only thing being deferred.

The general lesson is the same one this session has produced twice before, in a third disguise. On fln-1dxv the marker's fixed-point invariant was load-bearing but only incidentally true. On fln-rzyk two redundant guards were indistinguishable and one became invisible to the campaign. Here a test asserted a property of a value instead of a property of the function. In all three cases the code was right and the EVIDENCE was weaker than it looked, and in all three the mutation campaign was the only thing that noticed.

WHAT THIS SLICE DOES NOT CLAIM. The PinScan is SUPPLIED, not performed. Nothing here walks the pinned toolchain's tests/ tree, so the scan's OWN completeness - that it actually looked, and looked everywhere - is not established by this layer. That is the load-bearing gap and it is the same shape as the supplied-Inventory gap on fln-rzyk and the unverified-fixture-digest gap on franken_lean-9pnc: the model refuses what it is shown, and showing it the truth is the extraction slice's job. an_empty_pin_scan_is_not_a_free_pass pins the consequence explicitly - an empty scan is vacuously covered by an empty inventory, which is arithmetically correct and exactly why scan completeness must be established elsewhere. Two smaller gaps: the OfficialTestKind taxonomy is asserted from upstream's directory layout and has not been checked against the pin's actual tree; and expected outcomes are declared, not observed, so nothing yet confirms that a test marked Accepts does accept at the pin. Claim type bounded_model, evidence kinds property_test and mutation_kill, evidence state OBSERVED not proven, backing not real-reference. By franken_lean-9pnc's own rules this slice would not close an L-level above L0.

Lane registration for the now-six epoch-lab test targets stays on fln-giap.

title: W8: Lake surface — lakefile.lean on Golem, dual rebuild decisions, transactional resolution
description:
Implement the Lake surface (fln-lake, §13.3): lake CLI-compatible — lakefile.lean EXECUTES on Golem (the configuration DSL is just Lean; user code, so Golem executing it IS the compatibility mechanism), lakefile.toml takes the fast path, targets/facets map onto Ledger queries, require fetches via the D2 git tool through the shared subprocess capsule, lean-toolchain and elan layout honored so elan multiplexes FrankenLean toolchains transparently. Exit codes, --json, and the query surface match the pin.

The behavior upgrade is sound-mode and Behavior-Noted (BN-03): decl-granular no-op detection, with --faithful-invalidation restoring file-cone behavior for byte-for-byte CI reproduction studies. Internally TWO rebuild decisions are computed every time: the Reference decision (what the pin Lake would rebuild — faithful mode never omits an output upstream would produce, though it may satisfy it from a valid Ledger record and still project expected files/traces) and the native decision (which demand nodes actually changed); fln build explain <target> shows both, the delta, changed input identities, opaque barriers, and cache outcomes. Dependency resolution is transactional (a failed fetch never leaves a half-rewritten manifest presented as complete) and emits a resolution receipt; hermeticity is reported on the H0-H4 ladder, never overclaimed.

This bead also OWNS open question OQ-9: whether a native git-protocol client eventually replaces the D2 git tool, or git stays a permanent optional external — resolved here with the decision recorded in the plan decision log (the default posture is permanent D2 status, matching upstream Lake own contract; a native client is only justified if the closed-universe benefit outweighs the protocol-maintenance cost).

Acceptance: real Lake projects (incl. mathlib layout) configure and build unmodified; the Lake transcript corpus (C6) diffs clean on CLI surfaces; fln build explain output validated on fixture edits; OQ-9 decision recorded. Tests: lakefile.lean execution differentials; interrupted-fetch drills (C6 interrupted updates); manifest-atomicity fault drills; exit-code/JSON transcript fixtures.

## Acceptance Criteria

All bead-specific requirements, acceptance conditions, tests, invariants, compatibility surfaces, evidence levels, performance gates, negative/recovery cases, and user-visible behaviors stated above remain mandatory. In addition, the MANDATORY VERIFICATION DEFINITION OF DONE in Notes must be satisfied with named unit/property/mutation suites, at least one shared real-path no-mock E2E scenario plus failure/recovery coverage, detailed human and schema-versioned NDJSON artifacts, and reproducible close evidence. No listed feature or claim may be silently narrowed, deferred, mocked, or declared complete through an unclassified divergence.
design: Dependency topology: Lake needs the concrete G2-proven Golem execution stack, initialization/effect receipts, D2 subprocess capsule, and Ledger records/CAS. It does not consume a separate artifact from the W5 aggregation epic. G4 directly requires this real Lake surface; full W8 and later front-door/distribution work also consume it. This permits lakefile.lean and mathlib build validation as soon as the production runtime exists without dropping native_decide, VM, or wider W5 obligations from their own owners.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Provide pin-compatible lake CLI personalities, exit codes, JSON/query surfaces, target/facet behavior, lean-toolchain and elan layout. Execute lakefile.lean as real user code on Golem; support lakefile.toml fast paths; perform require fetches only through the fully provenanced D2 git subprocess capsule.
2. Compute and persist both the pinned Reference rebuild decision and native demand-node decision for every build. Faithful mode never omits an output or observable trace the Reference decision requires, while native mode may satisfy it from valid Ledger records; --faithful-invalidation restores file-cone behavior. fln build explain reports both decisions, their delta, changed identities, opaque barriers, and cache outcomes with stable machine schema.
3. Dependency resolution and manifest/lock updates are transactional and failure-atomic, with resolution receipts. Interrupted fetch, cancellation, disk/process faults, malformed manifests, and unavailable optional git leave no half-complete state presented as success. Hermeticity is reported only at evidenced H0-H4. OQ-9 is explicitly decided and entered in the plan decision log.
4. Named unit/property/differential/fault/mutation suites cover lakefile execution, TOML parity, target/facet mapping, elan discovery, transcript/exit/JSON compatibility, dual decisions, explain reasons, transaction atomicity, receipt binding, and restart recovery. Silent external fallback, omitted Reference work, stale-hit, partial-manifest, and false-hermeticity mutants must be killed.
5. A shared no-mock E2E lane configures and builds unmodified real Lake projects including mathlib layout, executes a lakefile on Golem, exercises cache hit and leaf edit with both decisions, uses the real sanctioned git fetch path, interrupts each promotion/update phase, restarts, and verifies exact final filesystem/database/manifest state. Human logs plus schema-versioned NDJSON include run/project/target/facet/demand/transaction/receipt ids, bead/claim/gate rows, redacted argv/cwd, pins/build/mode/profile/platform/thread/seed/cache/network/tool facts, canonical manifest/input/output/logical roots, both decisions/reasons, expected/actual exit and artifacts, timings/resources/status, cleanup, and final state.
6. C6 transcripts diff clean and reproducible evidence archives receipts, manifests, fault matrices, mutant outcomes, build-explain outputs, and tests/E2E bundles. Mocked fetches or lakefile execution cannot close compatibility, recovery, or hermeticity claims.

REVIEW AMENDMENT — Reference rebuild decisions are natively reproduced from the pinned algorithm and fixtures; release code never invokes the Reference. D4/external-effect tasks cannot be skipped merely because output bytes exist unless the effect contract proves replayability; faithful traces cannot fabricate side effects. Hermeticity and cache authority are separate. CLI/config/lakefile execution, demand graph and dual decisions/build-explain, and transactional git resolution/manifest/hermeticity each remain independently testable. Named suites: lake_cli_contract, dual_rebuild_decision_model, resolution_transaction_recovery, lake_real_project_e2e.

W6-W8 EVIDENCE CONTRACT — canonical schema-versioned semantic NDJSON is validated independently; telemetry remains separate and non-authoritative. Unknown schema, missing/duplicate ids, broken order/linkage, unbound artifacts, truncation, merged streams, or cleanup/final-state mismatch fail. Cancellation/exhaustion/InternalFault never enters cache, negative storage, admission, publication, or promotion. Productive 1/8/32 evidence proves useful work and deterministic reduction. Named unit/model/property/mutation/fuzz suites and real no-mock positive/failure/recovery E2E are mandatory.
notes:
