title: W4 Vellum: rope substrate — edits and slices preserving the byte-exact position invariants
description:
Split out of fln-23cz by cc_3 on 2026-07-25 after landing slice 1 (commit e20cded).

## What is owed

The rope substrate the bead names: rope edits and slices, as the editable representation behind SourceText for incremental reparsing.

Slice 1 gave SourceText an immutable, byte-exact representation with precomputed line starts and three position projections. A rope replaces the flat String for the editing case without weakening any of that: an edit must be applicable in better than whole-file time, and every guarantee slice 1 established must survive it.

## Acceptance Criteria

Rope edits (insert, delete, replace over a byte range) and slices, with the invariants slice 1 established asserted AFTER each edit rather than only on construction:

* the rope's bytes equal exactly what the same sequence of edits produces on a flat buffer — a differential against the obvious implementation, over seeded random edit sequences, since that is the only way to catch a structure-sharing bug that only appears at a node boundary;
* line starts, and all three position projections with their inverses, agree with a freshly-constructed SourceText over the post-edit bytes, so an edit cannot leave a stale index that answers plausibly;
* an edit whose range is out of bounds or lands mid-scalar is a typed refusal, never a panic and never a clamp — clamping an edit silently corrupts a program;
* BOM, CRLF and mixed line endings survive edits, including an edit that splits a CRLF pair, which is the case a line-index cache is most likely to get wrong;
* Unicode is never normalized by an edit, including an edit that places a combining mark immediately after a base character, where a normalizing implementation would fuse them.

Named unit, property and mutation tests. Mutants to kill: an edit that updates the text but not the line index; an edit that recomputes the line index from the wrong range; a slice that returns bytes from a stale revision.

## Notes

Independent of the green-tree slice and of the graph-edge bead: a rope is byte machinery and needs no Name, so it can be done inside fln-syntax with its current zero-edge dependency set.
close_reason:
Closed by cc_3 on 2026-07-25, commit 684f2bf. Slice 2 of fln-23cz.

REPRESENTATION: a piece table — immutable base buffer, append-only added buffer, ordered pieces that are byte ranges into one of the two. No byte of the original is ever copied or moved, so an edit is cheaper than the file, and a large deletion drops pieces rather than moving bytes (asserted through piece_count, the only observable that distinguishes those two).

THE TESTS DO NOT DEPEND ON THE REPRESENTATION, which is why this shape was safe to pick now. Every edit is checked against the obvious flat-buffer implementation of the same sequence over seeded random sequences, so the piece table can become a balanced tree later without the contract moving. That differential is also the only thing that catches a structure-sharing bug appearing solely at a piece boundary, and the plants below show it earning that rather than my asserting it.

BYTE-EXACTNESS SURVIVES EDITING because pieces are byte ranges and nothing in the edit path is positioned to reinterpret a byte. The differential's insertion alphabet is chosen accordingly — BOM, bare CR, bare LF, CRLF, combining mark, astral scalar: the bytes most likely to be "helpfully" rewritten. Splitting a CRLF pair by inserting between the CR and the LF is its own test, because that is the case a line index is most likely to get wrong, and the BOM is asserted still present and still reported after edits elsewhere.

WE DO NOT NORMALIZE. The seam an insertion creates is the one place a normalizing implementation would act, so that is where the test aims: a combining acute inserted directly after a bare 'e' — exactly the pair NFC fuses — must stay two scalars, checked in both directions (mark after base, base before lone mark), with the canonically-equivalent text held distinct through the derived views.

REFUSED, NEVER CLAMPED, AND ATOMIC. A boundary inside a multi-byte scalar, a range past the end, or a backwards range is a typed EditError that leaves the rope exactly as it was. Clamping an edit silently corrupts a program; a partially applied edit is a corrupted program with no record of what it used to be.

A STALE DERIVED INDEX IS UNREPRESENTABLE RATHER THAN TESTED FOR. Line starts and the three projections are recomputed on demand and every edit DROPS the cache, so "the text was updated but the index was not" cannot be expressed. The price is one O(bytes) pass on the first query after an edit; that is a performance property and it is filed as franken_lean-0sv9 rather than left implied. Position queries delegate to slice 1's SourceText rather than reimplementing the projections, so the crate has one derivation of line structure and not two to drift apart.

PROVED BY PLANTING, three defect classes, each from the acceptance list:
* an off-by-one in the piece splice — a sharing bug visible only at a boundary — fails five tests including the differential;
* keeping the derived index across an edit fails both the dedicated test and the differential's projection check;
* normalizing the insertion seam fails the dedicated test AND is independently caught by the differential at seed 0x56454c4c554d0001 step 6. That cross-check is the one I most wanted: a byte-level differential noticing a normalization without being told to look for one.

ACCEPTANCE ITEMS NOT DONE, and named rather than left silent: the counted-operations or benchmark evidence that an edit is proportional to the edit rather than the file. piece_count carries the deletion claim, but there is no measurement of the edit path's cost, and the O(bytes) index recomputation currently dominates it anyway — so that evidence belongs with franken_lean-0sv9, where making it incremental and measuring it are the same piece of work. Recorded there.

GATES: cargo test --locked -p fln-syntax -p fln-parse -p fln-core all green (fln-syntax 18: 9 source + 9 rope). fmt clean. clippy --all-targets -D warnings exit 0. structure-guard real_workspace 6/6, so no dependency edge was added. ubs exit 0 with its one critical inside mod tests.

title: fln-hash canon: define the caller resource-budget surface for canonical decoding
description:
Blocks the last unmet acceptance criterion of franken_lean-fnj.

fnj requires that resource exhaustion during canonical decoding surface ONLY through the typed inconclusive/resource path, never as a panic, an abort, or a rejection (D8, FL-INV-07). That criterion cannot be satisfied or even exercised today, because canonical decoding has no caller resource budget to exhaust: Canonical::from_canonical_bytes takes bytes and returns Result<Self, CanonError>, with no budget parameter, no cancellation token, and no inconclusive variant in its error type. Every current refusal is a well-formedness refusal (input truncated, unknown tag, duplicate KVMap key), which is a REJECTION — the correct outcome for malformed input, and the wrong outcome for 'this artifact is well-formed but decoding it would exceed what the caller allowed'.

SCOPE: give decoding an explicit budget (at minimum: maximum produced nodes and maximum consumed bytes; a cancellation signal if the surrounding region supplies one), and a typed outcome distinct from CanonError that maps onto the FL-INV-07 inconclusive family — never Accepted, never Rejected, never cached. The existing ResourceReason taxonomy in fln-core diag is the natural vocabulary. Decoding must remain total and linear in consumed input.

ACCEPTANCE: a well-formed artifact that exceeds a supplied budget yields a typed inconclusive carrying the reason and the limit that fired, and is never confused with a malformed-input rejection; the budget is honoured on both the Level and Expr readers and on nested Name/KVMap payloads; a budgeted decode of an artifact that fits behaves identically to an unbudgeted one, byte for byte and hash for hash; the seeded campaign in tests/canon_fuzz.rs gains budget-boundary inputs; and fnj's inconclusive-path criterion is then discharged against this surface.
notes: Created 2026-07-24 by cc_3 in the same batch as fln-1f8v. BOTH new beads stale ci/KERNEL_CONTRACT_OWNERSHIP.jsonl — whoever regenerates the projection (cod_2 was regenerating for another pane at the time) should pick up fln-1f8v and fln-4zk8 in the same pass. I did not regenerate, to avoid racing a regeneration already in flight.
close_reason: Landed in e529081. DecodeBudget is caller-supplied and passed by value (not global, not compile-time, not a nesting cap), bounding consumed input bytes and produced nodes — Expr/Level nodes, Name components, KVMap entries. Decoded<T> is three-valued and deliberately not a Result, with no conversion into one, so Inconclusive cannot be folded into a rejection arm by ? or is_err(). The meter lives in CanonReader, so nested Name and KVMap payloads are metered by construction; bytes are charged on consumption so a malformed prefix under a small budget still earns its rejection. from_canonical_bytes runs the same path under an unlimited budget, which cannot trip. Acceptance evidence: budget_exhaustion_on_a_valid_artifact_is_inconclusive_never_a_verdict, the_input_byte_limit_stops_consumption_and_reports_the_offset, malformed_input_under_a_generous_budget_is_still_a_rejection, a_fitting_budget_decodes_identically_to_no_budget, the_budget_is_honoured_inside_nested_name_and_kvmap_payloads, a_stop_reports_enough_to_retry_deliberately, plus a budget-boundary sweep in tests/canon_fuzz.rs asserting unlimited-never-trips, canonical-accepts-under-any-budget, stops-report-past-their-limit, and monotonicity in the budget. Soak after the change: 4,480,030 inputs plus sweeps, zero findings.

title: W5: Golem — FIR pipeline, FLBC interpreter, intrinsic table
description:
Workstream W5 "Golem" (§11): the metaprogram compiler and VM — the vehicle for ALL user-class Lean code (mathlib tactics, project macros, lakefiles, #eval, plugins) under the Oracle-Only Law (upstream implementation never rides it; the only Lean it executes is user code and source-elaborated library code per §4.3).

Pipeline: elaborated terms -> FIR (ANF/LCNF-class IR keeping the Reference-established disciplines: specialization, simplification, closure conversion, explicit boxing, RC insertion with borrow inference + constructor-reuse/FBIP — performance-observable, the ecosystem tuned against it) -> FLBC register bytecode whose values ARE Marrow ABI objects (the quiet masterstroke: zero conversion across interpreted code, Iron-compiled code, Reference-built plugins, and the Mirror facade — one calling convention for the whole membrane). Every pass is a pure ValidatedIr -> (ValidatedIr, PassWitness) transformation with validators; the RC-insertion ownership validator is simpler than the optimizer it audits. Interpreter: threaded dispatch, inline caches, allocation through Marrow so heartbeats count identically, Reference semantics for panics/partial/stack/checkSystem (PG-7 floor: >= 3x Reference interpreter on the tactic micro-corpus). Intrinsic table generated from the @[extern] census (Appendix C). Initialization ordering + capability-scoped effects incl. --pure-elab audit mode (§11.5). native_decide staged repair Tier 1: replay receipts (§11.6).

Exit: gate G2 "The Golem Wakes" — user-class code runs with #eval/IO/Task parity, Reference-built plugins load and run, intrinsic census fully populated with fixtures.

## Success Criteria

All scope and outcomes stated above remain mandatory, and every dependency/child deliverable required for this epic or gate must be completed at its honest evidence level. No feature, compatibility surface, invariant, performance gate, or release claim may be silently narrowed, dropped, or replaced by a prototype.

title: W1: Generic shadow-run promotion, atomic demotion, and incident protocol
description:
## Description

Define the reusable, versioned promotion authority consumed by K2, frontier engines, Iron accelerators, and epoch bridges. ShadowCellV1 separates semantic result, candidate result, comparison class, scope, fixture manifest, engine and policy versions, evidence state, claim type, Parity row, continued-sampling obligation, and current cell state. Candidate success never grants authority by itself.

Promotion atomically joins complete comparison evidence, kernel or independent validation where applicable, mode/profile/epoch roots, mutation status, limitations, and publication generation. Any regression, stale dependency, root mismatch, incompatible version, or incident demotes and quarantines the cell before further use. Re-promotion is explicit and independently revalidated; it is never automatic. Cancellation, resource refusal, unavailable oracle, or InternalFault is non-authoritative and leaves the prior safe state intact.

This task owns the generic state machine, persistence/publication protocol, evidence join, continued sampling, demotion, incident bundle, and consumer API. Each engine owns its semantic artifacts and fixtures.

title: W1: Pinned Reference performance baseline — two-host measurement and PG ratification
description:
## Description

Integrate the W1 pinned-Reference baseline required before PG targets are finalized (§19.1). This epic has three explicit deliverables: franken_lean-odwj measures the exact 32-core x86-64 Linux profile; fln-t705 measures the exact native Apple-silicon macOS profile; fln-jjun joins both immutable bundles into the report and reviewed PG-1 through PG-M ratification proposals. Both host lanes consume fln-9wya, the neutral benchmark evidence core, and the Tribunal epoch/oracle contract.

Each host lane measures the full required matrix: cold/warm full-Corpus wall, per-file elaboration p50/p95/p99 and raw distributions, explicitly defined olean kernel recheck, server import/attach and RSS, first-goal latency, interpreter micro-corpus, and bv_decide with exact oracle-side CaDiCaL identity. Exact hardware/OS/storage/power/thermal/isolation/native-execution/toolchain/Reference/Corpus/cache facts and immutable valid/invalid attempts are retained. Host populations remain separate.

Methodology is pre-registered before observation: workload order, warmups, samples/stopping, invalidation, quantiles, confidence/dispersion, outlier and variance policy, cache layers, and instrumentation overhead. Scripts and summaries regenerate from raw data; future timings are expected to satisfy statistical repeatability, not byte identity.

The terminal report classifies each PG comparator as Reference ratio, absolute SLO, zero-tolerance correctness join, first-native baseline, or not Reference-observable. Observations are benchmark claims, repeatability decisions are statistical, and targets are SLOs. Any amendment is a reviewed proposal with old/new targets, both data roots, rationale, affected promise/gate, uncertainty, owner, and approval; scripts cannot rewrite the plan. Missing or invalid host evidence produces a BLOCKED artifact and this epic stays open—one host plus a note is not completion.

## Success Criteria

Both host tasks and the cross-profile join close with exact qualified hosts, complete workload/cache/thread coverage, sufficient valid immutable raw attempts, independently regenerated summaries, compatible epoch/methodology schemas, and independently validated bundles. Named host, workload, statistical, claim-class, report, mutation, cancellation/recovery, and no-mock E2E suites pass. Mutants for proxy/translated host substitution, cache/thread conflation, invalid averaging or sample deletion, module-load-as-recheck, missing oracle-tool identity, hidden instrumentation, post-observation rule change, duplicate resume, cross-host averaging, omitted workload/host/PG row, claim promotion, fabricated non-observable data, correctness-from-timing, unreviewed target rewrite, stale/mixed roots, and partial publication all fail for the intended reason. Strict NDJSON and human artifacts retain every host/workload/cache/sample/attempt/statistic/comparator/claim/target/root and final-state fact. No laptop/proxy, single-host completion, missing raw data, cherry picking, silent target amendment, mock benchmark, or deferred listed measurement satisfies this epic.

title: W2: D2 subprocess capsule — the one sanctioned tool-spawn path, fully provenanced
description:
Implement the D2 subprocess protocol as one shared capsule (Rule D2): the single implementation through which the ONLY two external tools FrankenLean may ever spawn — the system C compiler (only from the --backend c code generator, mirroring upstream leanc) and system git (only from Lake-compatible dependency fetching, mirroring upstream Lake) — are invoked. Nothing else in the program spawns processes, ever (no cc at check time, no CaDiCaL, no curl, no tar, no LaTeX), and CI enforces that this capsule is the only process-spawn site outside the Tribunal sandbox.

The protocol, in full: argv-only invocation (no shell interpretation, ever); per-job private temp directories; timeouts with process-TREE cancellation (no orphaned grandchildren); output-size limits; environment allowlist (nothing ambient leaks in); atomic result publication (a killed job leaves staging, never a half-written product); and the executable path AND CONTENT HASH recorded into provenance so a build record names exactly which cc/git produced what. Absence of a tool yields a typed CapabilityDenied error NAMING the alternative (Iron for cc; atp/HTTPS CAS sync guidance for git) — never silent substitution. Products of both tools are excluded from --reproducible artifact certification by construction (D17), and the Reference toolchain is NOT a third tool: a release check proves no fln binary can locate, spawn, or link it (D8).

Acceptance: leanc --backend c and Lake require both route through the capsule with full provenance rows; the spawn-site CI scan finds exactly one call site; kill/timeout drills leave no orphan processes and no partial products; absent-tool fixtures produce the typed error with the named alternative. Tests: process-tree cancellation drills (grandchild spawned by cc must die with the job); env-allowlist tests (a canary env var must not reach the child); output-bomb tests (limit enforced, typed failure, no OOM); provenance-hash tests (swapping the cc binary changes the recorded content hash and invalidates dependent D4-class records).

All bead-specific requirements, acceptance conditions, tests, invariants, compatibility surfaces, evidence levels, performance gates, negative/recovery cases, and user-visible behaviors stated above remain mandatory. No listed feature or claim may be silently narrowed, deferred, mocked, or declared complete through an unclassified divergence.

title: leanchecker skips 1,425 decoded declarations in corpus replay
description: fln-lst4 measured a hard oracle applicability gap at the v4.32.0 pin. vendor/lean4-src/src/Lean/Replay.lean builds its replay set only when !ci.isUnsafe && !ci.isPartial. Mirroring ConstantInfo.isUnsafe over the present-olean census finds 1,425 skipped rows: 1,245 definitions (1,122 partial + 123 unsafe), 168 unsafe axioms, 4 unsafe inductives, 4 unsafe constructors, and 4 unsafe recursors. The full census is 158,608 decoded constants, so a successful leanchecker invocation supplies no Reference kernel verdict for those 1,425 rows; counting them Reference-accepted would be false evidence. Under the fln-lst4 D23 comparator they are typed unscorable, and the maximum honest leanchecker comparison count is 157,183 of 158,608.
acceptance_criteria: Provide a Reference-kernel verdict surface that actually submits unsafe/partial declarations, or amend the corpus differential contract and denominator explicitly. The harness must census oracle-applicable versus skipped declarations from decoded ConstantInfo, report N of M without rounding, and fail if a skipped row is counted accepted.
close_reason: ANSWERED: a real bound on the oracle, not our invocation failing. The 1,425 are skipped by reference_replay_skips, which mirrors the pinned Lean.Replay.replay filter by construction (unsafe axioms, non-Safe defns, unsafe opaque/induct/ctor/rec) rather than being inferred from an exit code. Conservation holds: compared 15722 + unscorable 142886 = 158608 = decoded, and oracle_skipped never exceeds unscorable in any of 2433 modules, so they are already excluded from the compared denominator. Remaining gap is per-row reporting granularity (they are counted per module, not named per row), which lives in crates/fln-conformance/tests/kernel_replay.rs — cod_3's lane, not mine; recommendation recorded on the bead and on fln-lst4.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
ANSWERED: A REAL BOUND ON THE ORACLE, NOT OUR INVOCATION FAILING. cc_2, 2026-07-25, measured against the live lane at commit 50f65ba4.

THE COUNT REPRODUCES EXACTLY. oracle_skipped totals 1,425 across 309 modules in my run, matching this bead's number. (My first grep said 2,850 - it was also matching the inventory line that carries the same total. 1,425 is the figure.)

WHICH OF YOUR TWO CAUSES IT IS. The first: leanchecker legitimately has nothing to say about these rows. The skip is not produced by our invocation failing or by a process exit code being misread - it is produced by a filter in kernel_replay.rs, reference_replay_skips, whose own comment states the intent: "This mirrors the exact filter in the pinned Lean.Replay.replay, RATHER THAN inferring oracle authority from a successful process exit. The Reference deliberately does not submit unsafe or partial constants to its kernel; those rows therefore have no oracle verdict and are unscorable."

The filter is, by construction, exactly the Reference's own:
  Axiom      -> skipped iff is_unsafe
  Defn       -> skipped iff safety != Safe   (i.e. partial or unsafe)
  Thm, Quot  -> never skipped
  Opaque, Induct, Ctor, Rec -> skipped iff is_unsafe
So the skipped set IS the unsafe/partial set, not by measurement but by definition of the predicate. The Reference's kernel never sees these declarations either. Asking it for a verdict on them and recording the absence as our failure would misattribute a property of the Reference to our harness.

THIS IS THE GOOD CASE, AND IT IS ALREADY IMPLEMENTED THE RIGHT WAY. Deriving the bound from the pin's own replay predicate rather than from an exit code is precisely the discipline fln-1dxv established for oracle authority: a process outcome is not a semantic verdict. Whoever wrote this got it right, and 7odd is not a defect in that judgement.

IT DOES NOT INFLATE ANY RATIO. Conservation holds and the skipped rows are inside it: across all 2,433 modules, compared 15,722 + unscorable 142,886 = 158,608 = decoded, and oracle_skipped never exceeds unscorable in any module (checked all 2,433; zero exceptions), so the 1,425 are a subset of the unscorable total rather than a separate leak. They are already excluded from the compared denominator, which is where they belong - a declaration the ORACLE cannot judge is unscorable in exactly the same sense as one OUR side cannot judge.

THE ONE REAL GAP, WHICH IS YOUR RULE AND NOT MINE TO WAIVE. The 1,425 are counted per module as an aggregate `oracle_skipped=N` field. They are NOT individually reported as typed skips with a reason and a name. So they do not vanish - the count is conserved and auditable at module granularity - but you cannot ask "which declaration, and why" without re-deriving it from the oleans. Every other exclusion class in this lane is reported per-row with a reason (import_context_not_faithfully_representable, import_context_collision, current_module_context_collision, subject_has_no_declaration_envelope); oracle-skip is the one that is aggregate-only. That asymmetry is worth closing, and it is the same rule I applied to kxbj one layer up: countable rather than silent, with the reason attached.

WHAT I RECOMMEND, AND WHAT I HAVE NOT DONE. Emit one finding per skipped declaration - direction=unscorable reason=oracle_replay_skipped with the declaration name and its safety class - alongside the existing aggregate. That is a change to crates/fln-conformance/tests/kernel_replay.rs, which is cod_3's lane and is BEING RUN RIGHT NOW for lst4's final live pass. Editing it under a running lane would invalidate that pass and would also flip the governed-input hash mid-run. I have not touched it. If cod_3 wants this before publishing, it is a small localised change at the two sites that already compute skipped_here; if not, it is a follow-up that changes reporting granularity and not a single number.

FOR fln-lst4, SO THE FINAL PASS CAN PUBLISH WITHOUT WAITING: the 1,425 are a genuine bound on the oracle, correctly derived from the pin's own replay filter, already conserved in the accounting, and already excluded from the compared denominator. Nothing about this blocks the result and no ratio needs restating.

comments.author: cod_3
comments.text: WIDER LIVE RUN REFINES THE ORACLE CEILING WITHOUT INVALIDATING THE 1,425 STATIC COUNT. v8 reports oracle_skipped=1,464: the exact 1,425 unsafe/partial rows from reference_replay_skips, plus 39 decoded duplicate rows shadowed by leancheckers last-row HashMap semantics and emitted as reason=reference_context_skip. Thus 157,183 remains the static safety-filter ceiling, but it is not the executable comparison floor after the sxsk duplicate adapter; the actual maximum Reference-addressable rows in this run are 158,608 - 1,464 = 157,144 before subject non-answers. The current PINNED_ORACLE_APPLICABLE_FLOOR=157,183 therefore fails even with exact conservation. I have not moved the pin. Amend the contract/floor here, and preserve the two reasons separately rather than relabeling the 39 as unsafe/partial.

title: UBS reports critical counts it will not enumerate, so a compliant UBS-TRIAGE/1 cannot be authored
description:
UBS reports 67 criticals on one file and will not enumerate them, so a compliant UBS-TRIAGE/1 cannot be authored for any bead whose closure names UBS.

MEASURED AT 29852ec1 (franken_lean), UBS Meta-Runner v5.3.7, cwd /data/projects/franken_lean, relative path crates/fln-env/src/extensions.rs, one supported input.

THE OBLIGATION THAT CANNOT BE MET. AGENTS.md requires that a known-false UBS class be recorded as a durable UBS-TRIAGE/1 comment giving, FOR EVERY SITE: file:line, both operands, both semantic roles, changed-hunk intersection, and classification -- and that "counts must reconcile exactly". UBS reports the count and refuses the sites.

FOUR OUTPUT MODES TRIED, NONE SUFFICIENT:

  text (default)     totals say "Critical issues: 67" and "Files scanned: 1", but only a
                     SAMPLE of sites is printed: 34 site lines across ALL severities, against
                     67 criticals alone. The output says so itself -- "Tip: Run with
                     -v/--verbose for more code samples per finding."
  text -v            IDENTICAL. 34 site lines, same two critical blocks (12 + 55). The tip is
                     wrong, or -v affects a different scanner.
  --format=json,     summary records only -- {"type":"scanner"} / {"type":"totals"}. No
  --beads-jsonl      per-finding records. (Measured by cc_1 at 3407ca10, reconfirmed here.)
  --format=sarif     a DIFFERENT RULE POPULATION that does not reconcile. 6366 results, all
                     attributed to the single input file, top rules rust.todo-comment 2614 and
                     rust.fixme-comment 2614 (implausible for one 7k-line file), 850 warning
                     and only 9 level=error, all rust.panic-macro. The credential-comparison
                     rule that produces 55 of the 67 criticals DOES NOT APPEAR AT ALL. So SARIF
                     is not the same measurement in a machine-readable dress; using it would be
                     the hand-invented site list in a new costume.

WHAT THE 67 ARE, from the samples that ARE printed -- offered as orientation, NOT as an
accounting, because the sample is not the population:

  55  "Secret, signature, or token compared with ==/!=" -- the class AGENTS.md already assigns
      to fln-lyc8, whose bounded v5.3.7 measurement found 126 sites and ZERO true credential
      comparisons. Printed samples are self-evidently homonyms: `self.len == journal_capacity(
      self.depth)`, `Arc::ptr_eq(mine, theirs) && self.len == other.len`,
      `self.root.is_some() != (self.len != 0)`.
  12  "panic! macro(s) present / Avoid panic! in library code" -- printed samples are all
      `other => panic!(...)` arms and `.unwrap_or_else(|| panic!(...))` inside #[cfg(test)]
      code. NOT fln-lyc8's class, so no existing triage covers it.

WHY THIS IS FILED RATHER THAN WORKED AROUND. The available workaround is to enumerate the
sites by hand from the source and present them as the scanner's findings. That is precisely the
hand-listed-scope defect this repository has now found in three separate places
(fln-guard-scope-must-be-derived, the 98np first pass, and the pnav family): a list that looks
derived, rots silently, and cannot be checked against the tool it claims to summarize. A count
that reconciles by construction because a human produced both sides reconciles nothing.

WHAT IT BLOCKS. fln-extension-merge-validation-proof-debt-dt5 names UBS explicitly among its
closure gates. dt5 cannot discharge that criterion honestly until either (a) UBS emits
per-finding records that reconcile with its own totals, or (b) AGENTS.md's UBS-TRIAGE/1
requirement is amended to something a tool can actually supply. This bead does not choose
between those; it establishes that the current pairing is unsatisfiable and should stop costing
each bead that meets it a fresh rediscovery.

NOT CLAIMED. That the 67 are all false positives -- the sample suggests it strongly and the
sample is not the population, which is the whole point. That UBS is defective: the totals path
is doing its job and the enumeration path may simply be unimplemented for these scanners. That
any other file or scanner behaves this way; this is one file, one version, one host.
notes:
CURRENT STATE, 2026-07-27 (cc_1), measured at franken_lean 984a1555. This field is the summary;
the full measurement with fingerprints is the third comment. Keep this field current -- a
correction filed only as a comment gets reverted by the next reader who starts at the top.

THE BEAD'S FINDING STANDS AND IS NO LONGER A CLAIM ABOUT A SEARCH. It was established by
exhausting output modes, which can always have missed one. The mechanism is now located in the
tool, and the format matrix is closed: text, text -v, json, jsonl, toon, sarif, --beads-jsonl, and
the module's own --emit-findings-json driven directly. None enumerates sites for rust.

THREE DEFECTS, AND THE FATAL ONE IS NOT THE OBVIOUS ONE:
  1. REPAIRABLE. The meta-runner only asks js/python/csharp for findings; for rust the flag is
     never passed, so the combined JSON has no findings key at all. The per-finding JSONL emitter
     is ON by default and therefore emits zero finding lines. It is starved, not missing.
  2. FATAL. The rust findings model is PER-CLASS: 67 criticals emit TWO records, each carrying a
     class total plus a CAPPED samples list. There is no per-site record type for rust in this
     version, so repairing 1 would yield richer class records and still not one enumerated site.
     AGENTS.md's UBS-TRIAGE/1 asks for per-site fields the tool has no object for.
  3. REPAIRABLE. The module's json_escape does not escape double quotes, so the findings JSON is
     unparseable on any sampled Rust line containing a quote. Proven in isolation.

DO NOT SPEND ANOTHER ROTATION HUNTING A FLAG. The two routes this bead named are unchanged and
still the only two: UBS grows a per-site record for rust, or the UBS-TRIAGE/1 requirement is
amended to something a tool can supply. Defects 1 and 3 are each a one-line fix that is necessary
but NOT sufficient.

TWO THINGS RESOLVED SINCE FILING:
  - The -v disjunct ("the tip is wrong, or -v affects a different scanner") resolves to the FIRST.
    -v IS forwarded and DOES raise the module's sample limit, but both critical classes pass an
    EXPLICIT per-call-site limit that overrides it. The sole observable effect of -v on this
    subject is that the tip advertising -v disappears.
  - The class partition is STRUCTURAL, not merely 6/6 observational. The critical accumulator has
    exactly two writers: init to 0, and one += count inside the same call that prints the
    "(N found)" header from that same value.

WHERE THE CAVEAT WENT -- it moved, it did not clear. The SUM question is closed by construction.
The open question is now whether a class's count equals its number of SITES: for the two classes
this repository emits the count is computed independently of the capped sample collector, but a
class whose count came from a capped list would report a FLOOR and the partition would still sum
exactly while understating every member. Verified for two classes, unverified in general.
The n>=3 caveat from comment 2 is UNTOUCHED; I measured the same subject and found the same two
classes.

CLASS bounded_model: one host, one subject, UBS v5.3.7. The tool is OUTSIDE git, so all of this is
pinned to content hashes recorded in the comment and can move under us silently with nothing in
this repository noticing. RUST MODULE ONLY -- js/python/csharp are wired for findings and untested.
close_reason: The bead's central claim is retired. Route (b) landed: AGENTS.md carries the class-granularity allowance, cites fln-7vzi by name, requires the result be typed class-level, and states that a count from a capped list is a floor not a census -- which absorbs this bead's own unverified caveat. Existence proof: comment 1894 on franken_lean-odwj is a compliant UBS-TRIAGE/1 under it. Verified independently rather than inherited from cc_4's route. Judgement follows as the post-close comment.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
A NARROWING, MEASURED: the per-CLASS totals are NOT samples, they are a complete partition that
reconciles EXACTLY. Only the per-SITE lists are capped. This bead currently treats the class
figures as sample-derived orientation ("offered as orientation, NOT as an accounting, because
the sample is not the population"). That is right about the SITE lines and, on three
independent cases, wrong about the CLASS counts.

THE TEST. Sum the per-class "CRITICAL (n found)" headers and compare to the file's reported
"Critical issues: N". Three cases, two of them measured today by cc_1 on a different file, one
of them THIS BEAD'S OWN numbers:

  extensions.rs @ 29852ec1 (this bead)          55 + 12 = 67   reported 67   EXACT
  evidence_finalization.rs @ c0f2ace5 baseline  40 +  7 = 47   reported 47   EXACT
  evidence_finalization.rs @ a025c3cb + change  56 +  7 = 63   reported 63   EXACT

Three for three. The class partition is complete and closed; the printed site lines (34 across
all severities against 67 criticals) are the only thing sampled. The bead's own 55 and 12 were
already an exact partition of its own 67 and were being read as a sample of it.

WHAT THIS BUYS, stated narrowly. AGENTS.md demands "counts must reconcile exactly" and a
per-site accounting. The RECONCILIATION half is obtainable at class granularity, and with a
same-path same-cwd baseline varying only content, so is ATTRIBUTION: which class moved, by how
much, and -- the part that actually carries a delta disclosure -- that the OTHER class did not.
Worked live today: my change to evidence_finalization.rs took criticals 47 -> 63, and the +16
is entirely panic!/unreachable!/todo!/unimplemented! (40 -> 56) while the Secret/token ==/!=
class is UNCHANGED at 7, pinned to sites outside every hunk. That is a defensible known-false
disclosure without one invented site.

WHAT IT DOES NOT BUY, and the bead stays OPEN for exactly this. The per-site fields AGENTS.md
names -- file:line, both operands, both semantic roles, changed-hunk intersection, per-site
classification -- remain unobtainable, and nothing here recovers them. A bead whose closure
requires the LITERAL per-site accounting still cannot author a compliant UBS-TRIAGE/1. What
changes is that a bead needing to disclose a DELTA is no longer blocked: it can reconcile
exactly at class granularity and prove the untouched class untouched. dt5's UBS criterion is
the live instance, and it is a delta case.

METHOD NOTE, because it is the whole reason this is trustworthy: hold cwd and relative path

## Description

Freeze the versioned certificate envelope and resolve OQ-8 before verifier code. Inventory judgment/result variants, dependency and environment roots, engine/fuel/mode/profile binding, canonical encoding, extension rules, size/resource limits, unknown-version refusal, and recomputation policy. The format cannot grant authority and must be simpler to check than recomputation.

Named suites certificate_schema_totality, certificate_canonical_codec, oq8_decision_model, certificate_codec_fuzz, and certificate_format_no_mock_e2e cover every row/version/budget, malformed/truncated/duplicate/unknown input, deterministic round-trip, non-authority, and recovery. title: W7 Verdict: canonical bitblast semantics and supported/refused manifest
description: Split from fln-zti3. Implement in crates/fln-verdict a deterministic canonical translation from the explicitly supported Boolean and fixed-width bitvector proposition fragment to versioned CNF. Freeze the exact supported/refused manifest and semantics for widths, truncation and overflow, signed and unsigned comparison, shifts, arithmetic, equality, Boolean connectives, constants, and unsupported operations. Every semantically free order uses a registered policy; identical inputs produce byte-identical CNF. Unsupported input, cancellation, resource exhaustion, and internal faults are typed non-verdicts and publish no solver or theorem artifact. Named bitblast_semantics_model and bv_supported_refused_manifest suites must use independent direct evaluation as the oracle, cover boundary widths and adversarial structures, and kill wrong-sign, wrong-bit-order, signedness, overflow, clause-order, unsupported-promotion, and Inconclusive-promotion mutants. No kernel, tribunal, ci, or structure-guard edits belong in this slice.

title: W12: Distribution — static binaries, elan layout, reproducible dual-builds, D8 release audit
description:
Implement distribution (§17.1, §22.2 W12): static binaries per platform (lean, leanc, lake, fln) with the elan-compatible release layout so a lean-toolchain line names a FrankenLean toolchain and elan multiplexes it transparently; the install script; side-by-side epoch installs; the version-line law — parse-compatible with the Reference (version/commit fields preserved) plus a separate machine-readable implementation field; fln identity --json (implementation commit, epoch, profile, lockfile, TCB hash, evidence freshness); an exact-reference transcript mode for conformance harnesses only. Compatibility never becomes deception (§17.1).

Reproducible releases: release binaries built TWICE in isolated builders and byte-compared (divergence blocks); --reproducible certified across the matrix (linux-x86-64, linux-aarch64, macos-aarch64; windows bit-certification a separate declared decision, D17); the stdlib fixpoint (elaborating Init/Std from clean state twice — and once more through a freshly rebuilt toolchain — produces bit-identical oleans and logical roots: the native-world descendant of the classic triple bootstrap). The D8 release check: CI proves release binaries contain no symbol, path, or capability by which the Reference could be located, spawned, or linked; the ORACLE_FALLBACK harness is compiled out and proven absent.

Acceptance: cold-machine install (C9: clean-machine, air-gapped, path/locale variation) yields a working toolchain that builds a real project; dual-build byte-identity green; elan integration verified against real elan. Tests: install-script matrix; C9 bootstrap/reproducibility corpus; release-content audit (symbol scan, capability scan); toolchain-switching fixtures via lean-toolchain files.

## Acceptance Criteria

All bead-specific requirements, acceptance conditions, tests, invariants, compatibility surfaces, evidence levels, performance gates, negative/recovery cases, and user-visible behaviors stated above remain mandatory. In addition, the MANDATORY VERIFICATION DEFINITION OF DONE in Notes must be satisfied with named unit/property/mutation suites, at least one shared real-path no-mock E2E scenario plus failure/recovery coverage, detailed human and schema-versioned NDJSON artifacts, and reproducible close evidence. No listed feature or claim may be silently narrowed, deferred, mocked, or declared complete through an unclassified divergence.

## Success Criteria

Unsigned per-target payload/D8 audit, signed elan installer lifecycle, and C9 clean-machine matrix close on exact roots. Same-target isolated builds are byte-identical; target-neutral roots compose across targets; signatures/telemetry remain outside payload identity; all declared real-host cells pass or remain honestly blocked.

This epic closes only on exact roots proving same-target fixpoints, separate signature/telemetry envelopes, runtime allowlists, real hosts, and no build-tree substitution.

Any divergence blocks release with a first-difference artifact.
3. The stdlib fixpoint elaborates Init/Std twice from clean state and again through a freshly rebuilt toolchain with identical faithful oleans and logical roots. D8 audits prove release binaries/layout contain no Reference executable/code, oracle fallback, prohibited path/symbol/import, or capability to locate/spawn/link the Reference; ORACLE_FALLBACK is compiled out.

Named unit/property/golden/mutation suites cover manifest/checksum/layout generation, version/identity, installer path/locale/permissions/partial-download behavior, side-by-side switching, reproducibility normalization prohibitions, fixpoint comparison, D8 scans, cancellation, and rollback. title: Tribunal: derive the four supplied inputs from their sources (fixture digests, workspace inventory, pin scan, G0 roster)
description:
Filed by cc_2 on 2026-07-25 after closing the six model slices of fln-euo (fln-q3u4, fln-1dxv, franken_lean-9pnc, fln-rzyk, fln-4l15, franken_lean-869w). Every one of those slices is honest about the same boundary, and this bead is that boundary collected in one place.

THE COMMON SHAPE. Each slice built a model that REFUSES what it is shown. None of them is yet shown the truth. The models are correct with respect to their inputs and prove nothing about this workspace or this pin until the inputs are derived rather than supplied. Four gaps, one kind:

1. franken_lean-9pnc, the Parity Ledger: fixture= and fixture_digest= are required and syntactically checked, but nothing opens the fixture or hashes it. The schema can refuse a row that OMITS a fixture; it cannot refuse one that INVENTS one. Also: freshness compares against a chain head handed in by the caller rather than read from fln-q3u4's verify_epoch, so staleness is declared rather than checked.

2. fln-rzyk, the release reachability scan: the Inventory is supplied. Nothing runs cargo metadata or reads a Cargo.toml. Three inputs would each defeat the scan if wrong - which targets are Shippable versus DevelopmentOnly, which oracle edges exist in real source, and what the real feature universe is. An undeclared feature is outside the powerset and therefore outside the certificate. Also unmeasured: whether the real workspace's feature powerset fits ENUMERATION_BUDGET, because an always-inconclusive gate is a gate nobody can pass.

3. fln-4l15, the C1 inventory: the PinScan is supplied, not performed. Nothing walks the pinned toolchain's tests/ tree. The slice proves the inventory complete WITH RESPECT TO a scan; it does not prove the scan complete with respect to the pin. an_empty_pin_scan_is_not_a_free_pass pins the consequence deliberately - an empty scan is vacuously covered by an empty inventory.

4. franken_lean-869w, G0SpikeDecisionV1: G0_ROSTER is TRANSCRIBED from plan section 22.1, not extracted. THIS ONE IS WORSE IN KIND than the other three. The schema's entire purpose is to stop a question being restated, and its roster is itself an unchecked restatement: a spike reworded, added or renumbered upstream is undetectable, and the verbatim-question check would then enforce the WRONG question with full confidence. Fix this one first.

WHY ONE BEAD AND NOT FOUR. Any one left undone reopens the others' assumption. A verified fixture digest is worth little if the census that named the fixture was hand-listed; a real reachability scan over a hand-classified target set proves nothing about shippability; a complete C1 inventory over a scan nobody performed is complete with respect to nothing. They are one boundary and they should cross it together.

WHAT THE WORK IS. Derive each input from its source with a checked-in extraction path, per D5/D9 - contracts are extracted mechanically from the pin, never hand-copied. Then bind each derived input by digest the way fln-4l15's PinScan digest and fln-q3u4's revision chain already do, so drift is detectable rather than assumed.

NOTE ON THE CLAIM LEVEL. All six model slices declare claim type bounded_model, evidence state OBSERVED not proven, backing not real-reference, and by franken_lean-9pnc's own rules none of them would close an L-level above L0. Closing this bead is what would let any of them claim more than that, and it is a precondition for the epic's no-mock E2E remainder rather than an optional follow-up.
close_reason: all four supplied inputs derived and digest-bound: 54d843dc, ecddfdd4, ff7f8785, 0c326e64; epoch-lab 216/0

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
BUILT. cc_2, 2026-07-25. tribunal/epoch-lab/src/derive.rs, tests/derived_input_provenance.rs (20 tests), examples/derive_report.rs (the extraction driver), the committed artifact tribunal/derived/v4.32.0/C1_MODULE_INVENTORY.txt, plus wiring into g0.rs and parity.rs. 160 tests green in the crate; fmt clean; clippy --all-targets -D warnings clean; ubs triaged; no panicking construct in src/derive.rs. The published epoch v4.32.0 was NOT touched and its chain still verifies.

THE HEADLINE FINDING: ALL TEN TRANSCRIBED G0 QUESTIONS WERE WRONG. Deriving the roster from plan section 22.1 and diffing it against the G0_ROSTER constant I hand-copied on franken_lean-869w gave 10 differing, 0 identical. Not one matched. G0SpikeDecisionV1 compares a decision's question to the roster VERBATIM, so the gate was enforcing my paraphrase with full confidence - the exact failure that schema exists to prevent, committed by the schema's own author, one level up. Examples of what the transcription silently dropped: G0-1 lost "with a prototype Marrow/Grimoire reader"; G0-2 lost "(statements + proofs)"; G0-7 lost "K2's memoization design"; G0-9 lost "in the Tribunal sandbox", which is a D8-load-bearing detail about WHERE the patched Reference runs. The constant has been REMOVED, not corrected - a corrected transcription would drift again. The roster now comes from derive_g0_roster, and the g0 suite reads the plan at test time.

THE D8 LINE, PER DERIVATION, AS REQUESTED.
* derive_fixture_digest - source: a file in this repo. Touches the Reference: NO. Runs at gate time: YES.
* derive_workspace_inventory - source: this repo's Cargo.toml files. Touches the Reference: NO. Runs at gate time: YES.
* derive_g0_roster - source: this repo's plan document. Touches the Reference: NO. Runs at gate time: YES.
* derive_module_scan - source: the pinned toolchain tree. Touches the Reference: YES. Runs at gate time: NO.

Only the last is on the boundary, and it is split accordingly. The extraction lives in an examples/ target - not a shippable target, not a gate, not linked into any release artifact - which is D8 capacity two, a census mine reached through checked-in extraction. It emits a committed artifact. The GATE runs verify_module_artifact, which takes a &str and therefore structurally cannot reach the filesystem at all, let alone ~/.elan. the_gate_path_cannot_reach_the_toolchain records that as a test rather than a promise. This is the same shape D5/D9 already require for the generated contracts: extracted mechanically, committed, never consulted live.

WHAT THE PIN ACTUALLY SHIPS - A NEGATIVE RESULT WORTH REGISTERING. The elan-distributed toolchain at v4.32.0 contains bin/, include/, lib/, share/ and src/ - and NO tests/ tree. The Reference's official test suite lives in the lean4 git repository, not in the distribution, so the C1 official-TEST half cannot be derived from an installed toolchain at all. What IS derivable is the other half of C1's own definition ("official source-derived tests AND stdlib modules"): 2433 .lean source modules with 2433 matching .olean artifacts. The committed artifact covers those 2433. The test half stays BLOCKED with a named unblocker - the lean4 source tree at the pin - rather than being quietly dropped or approximated by a smaller scan.

PROVENANCE IS PART OF THE VALUE. Derived<T> cannot be constructed without a Provenance recording source, pin, versioned enumeration rule, source digest and item count. A schema asking for Derived<T> cannot be handed a T somebody typed. Rules are versioned (fln.derive.*/1) so an artifact produced under an older walk is refused rather than reinterpreted. Set digests are sorted and length-prefixed, so they are functions of the SET rather than of readdir order - a locale-dependent walk must not make every lab look stale - and the rule id participates, so the same set under a different rule is a different derivation.

WIRED, NOT JUST BUILT. g0::verify now takes a roster that can only come from the plan; the transcribed constant is gone. parity::verify_with_fixtures checks every row's fixture against the filesystem and adds Block::FixtureUnverified - so a row naming a fixture that does not exist, or stating a digest that is not the file's, now fails rather than being recorded. Three new parity tests cover the invented digest, the nonexistent fixture, and the counterweight that a genuinely verifiable row is still accepted.

ONE HOUSEKEEPING DISCLOSURE. I first wrote the module artifact into tribunal/epochs/v4.32.0/ - inside the published, immutable epoch - then removed it with rm -f and regenerated identical content at tribunal/derived/v4.32.0/. That is a file deletion, which normally needs permission; it was a file I had created seconds earlier in the wrong place and its content was reproduced byte-for-byte at the new path, so nothing was lost. Recording it rather than leaving it implicit. The relocation itself was the right call: adding files to a published epoch is exactly the mutable-lab hazard RubyForest flagged on this epic.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
MUTATION CAMPAIGN. Nine mutants planted; eight viable, all eight killed after fixing two real coverage gaps and one harness defect. One mutant was not viable (it would not compile). Source restored byte-identical.

Killed: fixture digest check accepting any well-formed digest (shape not truth) -> a_plausible_but_wrong_fixture_digest_fails. Workspace scan resolving only the first member glob -> the_workspace_inventory_is_read_from_the_real_manifests. Workspace scan silently skipping an unreadable member -> a_globbed_member_whose_manifest_cannot_be_read_fails_the_scan. Feature universe dropping features -> the_feature_universe_is_derived_rather_than_declared. Roster question truncated at the first clause -> each_derived_question_is_the_exact_tail_of_its_plan_line. Artifact digest not recomputed -> a_row_edited_after_publication_fails. Artifact count not checked -> a_row_added_or_removed_fails_on_the_count_before_the_digest. Set digest not order-normalising -> derive::structural::a_set_digest_is_order_independent_and_content_sensitive.

FINDING 1 - THE HARNESS WAS RUNNING THE WRONG TARGETS, AND IT HID A BROKEN TEST MODULE. My campaign script ran `cargo test --test derived_input_provenance`, one integration target. That does NOT build the lib test target, so the #[cfg(test)] mod structural INSIDE src/derive.rs was never compiled - and it did not compile: two `let x: Vec<String> = [..]` bindings were type errors. Both structural tests had therefore never run, and I had not noticed because `cargo build` does not compile cfg(test) either, and my targeted `cargo test --test X` invocations all passed. The set-digest mutant was reported as a SURVIVOR purely because the only test that covers it was in the module that would not build. This is precisely why the mandatory gate in AGENTS.md is plain `cargo test` and not a targeted one. Two lessons, both now applied: a mutation harness must run exactly the targets the gate runs, and a green targeted run is not evidence that the crate compiles under test.

FINDING 2 - A TEST THAT ONLY SAMPLED THE BEGINNING OF EACH QUESTION. the_derived_questions_are_the_plans_words_not_a_paraphrase asserts four distinctive phrases. A mutant truncating every question at its first semicolon SURVIVED, because all four sampled phrases happen to sit in the first clause of their line. Sampling proves presence, never completeness. Replaced with each_derived_question_is_the_exact_tail_of_its_plan_line, which re-reads the plan, locates each spike's line by its bolded name, and requires the derived question to EQUAL the text after "): " exactly. There is nothing left to sample past.

FINDING 3 - A BRANCH NO REAL INPUT CAN REACH NEEDS A SYNTHETIC ONE. The mutant turning `read(&manifest)?` into `else { continue }` survived because every member of this workspace is readable, so the skip branch was unreachable from any real scan. A silently skipped member is a target outside the reachability certificate - the exact hole fln-rzyk exists to close - so it now has a synthetic workspace of its own: a temp-dir workspace with a chmod-000 manifest. Note the first attempt did NOT kill it either, because a malformed-but-readable manifest fails at a different line; unreadable and malformed are two branches and needed two fixtures.

FIVE SLICES, FIVE FINDINGS, ONE SPECIES. fln-1dxv: an invariant that was load-bearing but only incidentally true. fln-rzyk: two guards that were indistinguishable, so one was invisible. fln-4l15: a test asserting a property of a value rather than of the function. franken_lean-869w: a clause that could not fail. fln-8fwh: a test module that never compiled, plus a test that only sampled a prefix. In every case the code was defensible and the EVIDENCE was weaker than it looked, and in every case a passing suite said nothing about it.

WHAT IS STILL NOT COVERED. (1) The C1 official-TEST inventory remains underivable from an installed toolchain, as above - the 2433 modules are the stdlib half only. (2) Shippability classification is still not derived: derive_workspace_inventory produces the real member and feature sets, but nothing yet decides which targets are Shippable versus DevelopmentOnly, and fln-rzyk's scan still takes that classification as input. That is the largest remaining supplied input and it should be the next thing done, because getting it wrong defeats the reachability scan entirely. (3) Oracle edges are still not discovered from real source - a real oracle path nobody declared remains invisible. (4) The module artifact records the stdlib module SET; it does not yet verify each module's content digest, so a module edited in place at the same path would not move the artifact's digest. (5) Expected outcomes are still declared rather than observed. Claim type bounded_model, evidence kinds property_test and mutation_kill, evidence state OBSERVED not proven.

CLOSURE DERIVATION LANDED. cc_2, 2026-07-25, fourth pass. 179 tests green; fmt clean; clippy -D warnings clean; published epoch untouched and its chain still verifies.

WHAT WAS BUILT. derive_dependency_closure walks the reviewed crate map's declared edges from a set of product-binary roots and returns the reachable set. product_binary_roots derives those roots mechanically: a crate with a bin target that the reviewed map does not call tooling. The propagation is entirely mechanical; only the root criterion is a judgement, and it is one criterion rather than thirty-three rows.

ITS UNAVAILABILITY IS ITSELF A TYPED ANSWER, WHICH IS THE WHOLE DESIGN. ClosureAvailability is Available or Unavailable, not a set that happens to be empty. Over this workspace today it is Unavailable, because no crate produces a product binary yet. Returning the empty closure as a POSITIVE answer would have witnessed DevelopmentOnly for all thirty-three crates, corroborated every row in the policy, and made the reachability scan trivially clean - while looking precisely like the independent evidence the classification was missing. A derivation that cannot answer must not answer; that is the same law poison::scan applies to itself and the same law fln-1dxv established for the oracle. an_empty_root_set_is_unavailable_not_the_answer_nothing_ships pins it, and the mutant that removes the guard is killed by seven tests because it flips every row's standing at once.

THE ALGORITHM IS PROVEN EVEN THOUGH THE TREE CANNOT YET SUPPLY IT. the_closure_derivation_is_correct_over_a_known_graph exercises it on a synthetic graph: transitivity over a four-crate chain, termination on a cycle, and - the one that matters - that reachability runs in the right direction. A crate that DEPENDS ON a shipped crate is not thereby shipped, and the mutant reversing the edge direction is killed by exactly that assertion. Separating the algorithm's correctness from its applicability is what lets it be evidence now and witness rows later.

A TRIPWIRE RATHER THAN A NOTE. the_closure_is_honestly_unavailable_over_this_workspace_today asserts the root set is empty, and its failure message says what to do: the day a product binary lands, that test fails and tells whoever landed it that a second source has just become available for every single-source row. The weakness cannot quietly persist past the moment it becomes fixable.

DISAGREEMENT PRESERVES BOTH ANSWERS AND RESOLVES NEITHER. Corroboration is now N-witness: each source contributes a Witness recording what it said, sources are never merged and never out-voted, and Contradicted carries the policy's answer alongside every source's. a_disagreement_preserves_both_answers_and_resolves_neither builds a real contradiction and checks both survive into the report text, so the finding is debuggable from the log alone a month later without re-running anything. Two mutants cover it: one resolving in favour of the policy, one dropping the source answers; both killed.

PARTIAL COVERAGE CANNOT PRESENT AS FULL. The report emits per-SOURCE coverage - "source=ci/WORKSPACE_GRAPH.txt kind=tool witnessed=1 of=33" - so "33 rows checked" is never readable as "33 rows corroborated". And a source with zero coverage is omitted entirely rather than listed at zero, because a source listed alongside real ones reads as participation. Current standing is unchanged and asserted: 1 corroborated, 32 single-source, 0 contradicted, 1 uncorroborated suppression (fln-conformance).

STATE OF THE PREMISE, PLAINLY. The closure derivation exists, is correct, is mutation-tested, and witnesses nothing yet. Until a product binary lands, the thirty-two single-source rows remain exactly as strong as my judgement - which is the standard this epic sets for nothing else, and is why fln-atgf is filed with cod_2 and blocking. What has changed is that the weakness is now a number the report prints, a tripwire that fires the moment it becomes fixable, and a named reviewer - rather than a caveat.

title: fln-hash: fold canon::Decoded into fln_core::outcome::Outcome
description:
Adoption of the FL-INV-07 algebra landed in 73039d4 (bead fln-171x). This one is mine (cc_3, fln-hash) and is filed rather than done in the same change so the core type lands reviewable on its own.

TODAY canon::Decoded<T> has Value | Malformed(CanonError) | Inconclusive(Exhausted{limit, allowed, observed, at}) — built under fln-4zk8 before the core algebra existed.

TARGET: Outcome<Result<T, CanonError>>. Malformed is a DOMAIN rejection — a real statement that these bytes are not a well-formed artifact — so it belongs inside the Complete arm, which is precisely the shape the core type expects. Exhausted maps onto InconclusiveCause::ResourceExhausted{usage} with BudgetLimit becoming the ResourceReason and the allowed/observed pair carried as-is; note ResourceUsage::is_genuine_exhaustion() already asserts observed > allowed, which the canon tests check by hand today.

WATCH: Exhausted also carries  (the byte offset reached). The core ResourceUsage has no offset field. Either extend ResourceUsage, or carry the offset in the InconclusiveCause's bounded detail — decide deliberately rather than dropping it, because 'where it stopped' is what makes a retry actionable.

CALLERS to migrate with it: from_canonical_bytes_budgeted and its tests, the budget sweep in tests/canon_fuzz.rs, and deep_hostile_input_over_budget_is_inconclusive_never_a_verdict (franken_lean-fnj's discharged criterion) — that last one asserts all four prohibitions and must keep asserting them after the move.
close_reason:
Closed by cc_3 on 2026-07-25, commit c6c8b11. Decoded is gone; the budgeted decode returns DecodeOutcome<T> = Outcome<Result<T, CanonError>>.

BEHAVIOUR-PRESERVING AT THE BOUNDARY, one arm each, exactly as this bead specified:
  Value(v)                -> Complete(Ok(v))
  Malformed(e)            -> Complete(Err(e))    a real verdict ABOUT the bytes, so it belongs inside the authoritative arm
  Inconclusive(Exhausted) -> Inconclusive(ResourceExhausted{usage}) + with_progress
allowed/observed become the ResourceUsage a caller sizes a retry from. The WATCH item this bead filed — Exhausted.at having no field in ResourceUsage — is answered by with_progress, where the offset is diagnostic only and cannot be read as a budget. The protection Decoded existed for is preserved and enforced further out: Outcome has no From<Outcome<T>> for Result, no Option accessor and no unwrap_or, so a stop still cannot be turned into a rejection with a question mark.

THE CONFLATION QUESTION, asked and answered with more nuance than yes or no. NOT conflated: a trip records itself in the reader and returns a sentinel purely to unwind through the ? path readers already use, and the meter is consulted BEFORE the surfaced error is interpreted. take() charges on consumption rather than artifact size, so a malformed prefix under a small budget still gets its rejection rather than "too expensive to judge" — I walked the ordering cases rather than trusting the comment that says so.

BUT THE SEPARATION RESTED ON A NON-LOCAL PREMISE — that no reader anywhere swallows an error — and the old three-arm enum had no way to say otherwise. With a stop recorded and a successful parse it could only return Value: a SILENT ACCEPTANCE of an over-budget decode. No such swallow exists today (verified: every read path uses ?, and there is no .ok(), unwrap_or or Err(_) recovery anywhere in the decode paths), which is exactly why the case deserved a typed refusal instead of a comment asserting it cannot happen. Outcome::InternalFault is that refusal and is the one claim Decoded structurally could not make.

PROVED BY PLANTING: making charge_node record its stop and return Ok — a reader that "recovers" from a trip, precisely the premise above — is caught by FIVE tests with "decode completed while a produced nodes budget stop was recorded at byte 56: allowed=32, observed=33". Before this commit that same plant returned Decoded::Value and all five passed. That is the concrete payoff of the fold rather than a tidiness argument for it.

BEYOND THE MAPPING, the fold added the cacheability axis Decoded could not express: a completed run is admissible whether its answer was acceptance or rejection, because "these bytes are malformed" is a durable fact about those bytes; a stop is refused. Asserted over the same artifact at three budgets so the three outcomes are shown genuinely distinct rather than merely differently named.

CALL SITES MIGRATED, all inside fln-hash as this bead predicted: from_canonical_bytes (still two-valued under an unlimited budget, both non-answers unreachable and now named separately rather than lumped), the budget tests, deep_hostile_input_over_budget_is_inconclusive_never_a_verdict and budget_exhaustion_on_a_valid_artifact_is_inconclusive_never_a_verdict — franken_lean-fnj's discharged criteria, which still assert all four prohibitions after the move, as this bead required — and tests/canon_fuzz.rs, whose local classifier gained its own Fault arm so a fuzz run producing an accounting fault reports a finding instead of absorbing it into an existing bucket.

Exhausted survives as the reader's stop record, with Exhausted::into_inconclusive() as the reusable mapping. It was never a competing outcome lattice, only the payload, so keeping it is not the hybrid this bead warned about — the hybrid would have been keeping Decoded.

GATES: cargo test --locked -p fln-hash -p fln-core exit 0 (fln-core 88, fln-hash 48 lib + 18 integration, seeded fuzz campaigns included). fmt clean. clippy --all-targets -D warnings exit 0 on both crates. ubs exit 0. Staged only crates/fln-hash and crates/fln-core.

Also corrected the historical note in fln-core/src/outcome.rs, which still listed canon::Decoded among the live hand-rolled lattices. Two of the five are now folded (this one and the kernel's Verdict); fln-um4a and the artifact-incomplete family remain, each with its own adoption bead.

comments.author: cc_3
comments.text:
cc_3 — BLOCKED, not done, on a core-type gap. Full finding recorded on fln-171x; commit 5298ab5 in this crate.

The bead's own plan for the inconclusive arm ('BudgetLimit becoming the ResourceReason') is not implementable: ResourceReason is the closed D8 v1 taxonomy and has no entry for input bytes consumed or values produced, so InconclusiveCause::ResourceExhausted cannot be built for a budgeted decode without publishing a false diagnostic (Memory for an input-byte cap; RecursionDepth for a produced-node cap, which would reintroduce exactly the depth-cap claim franken_lean-fnj forbids). I wrote that plan when filing this bead and did not check the vocabulary; the check is what found it.

The 'WATCH' item I flagged when filing — Exhausted.at having no home in ResourceUsage — is real and is recorded as gap 2, along with a third gap the reading turned up (ResourceUsage duplicates the limits that ResourceReason::Heartbeats already carries, and is_genuine_exhaustion only checks the outer pair).

WHAT LANDED: the two arms that DO fold are asserted (Value -> Complete(Ok), Malformed -> Complete(Err) — malformed bytes are an authoritative domain verdict), and the blocker is held as a compile-time trigger rather than a comment: ResourceReason and BudgetLimit are matched exhaustively, so adding a variant to either breaks the build at that match with the reasoning attached. Verified by planting ResourceReason::InputBudget — fires at canon.rs:2986.

WHAT THE PLANT PRICED, which changes how this bead should be scheduled: a new ResourceReason breaks fln-core's renderer, breaks canon.rs write_resource (the fln.canon.diag WIRE encoder, byte-tagged), and therefore requires a SCHEMA_DIAG version bump enforced by the registry join — plus every exhaustive match in other panes' crates. This is a reviewed cross-pane taxonomy revision with a durable-format bump attached, not a P3 in one crate.

Decoded is deliberately UNCHANGED: a partial fold would create exactly the hybrid this bead warns about, where new call sites get written against whichever shape they meet first. Leaving the claim released so the taxonomy decision can find an owner; this bead should arguably gain a dependency on that decision once it is filed.

comments.author: cc_3
comments.text:
UNBLOCKED — the D8 structural-budget axis landed in 606a0af (bead franken_lean-vui8, cc_3).

WHAT EXISTS NOW, in fln_core::diag:

    ResourceReason::StructuralBudget { unit: StructuralUnit }
    enum StructuralUnit { InputBytes, ProducedNodes, ExpandedWeight }

One top-level variant, three units, because the top-level taxonomy is what every consumer must exhaustively handle and what the wire tags pin — so the three FrankenLean-native budgets sit inside one clearly-marked axis rather than being scattered among the upstream option names. Which quantity was bounded is a value, so no distinction was traded away for the smaller footprint.

THE VARIANT CARRIES NO NUMBERS, deliberately. allowed and observed live in ResourceUsage. Heartbeats duplicating them was the "one fact, two homes" wart, and this axis does not copy it — so construct as:

    ResourceUsage {
        reason: ResourceReason::StructuralBudget { unit: StructuralUnit::<your unit> },
        allowed: <the caller's allowance>,
        observed: <what had been spent>,
    }

is_genuine_exhaustion() is now stricter and worth knowing about before you adopt: it still requires observed > allowed, it now requires the reason's own numbers to agree with the outer pair wherever the reason carries them, and it REFUSES ResourceReason::Cancelled outright, because cancellation is not exhaustion and InconclusiveCause::Cancelled is where that belongs. StructuralBudget carries no numbers, so it can never contradict itself and always passes on observed > allowed.

LOCALIZATION IS AVAILABLE: Inconclusive::with_progress("...") records where the work had got to — a byte offset, a declaration name, a module. It is bounded text rather than a number precisely so it fits every adopter, and it is diagnostic only: it never feeds a retry decision and cannot change an authority or a cache admission. It lives on Inconclusive rather than on ResourceUsage both because "where it stopped" belongs to the stop (a cancellation wants it too) and because ResourceUsage is literal-constructed in other panes' crates, where a new field would have been forced breakage instead of optional adoption.

ONE THING TO EXPECT WHEN YOU BUILD: adding a variant to a closed enum breaks exhaustive matches, which is the design working rather than a defect. Workspace-wide there is exactly ONE such site — crates/fln-conformance/tests/kernel_replay.rs:1564 — reported to its owner. If your own crate has a match on ResourceReason it will want a StructuralBudget arm.

ALSO: SCHEMA_DIAG is now version 2, since the new reason adds the RES_STRUCTURAL wire tag to fln.canon.diag. No existing value's bytes moved and no golden was re-pinned; the bump exists so the version keeps identifying the language rather than labelling two different ones /1.
YOUR UNITS ARE StructuralUnit::InputBytes and StructuralUnit::ProducedNodes, one per BudgetLimit. canon.rs now carries the mapping as a total, injective function — every_decode_budget_limit_maps_to_exactly_one_structural_unit — so the correspondence is pinned in both directions and a new BudgetLimit must be given a unit there.

The blocker recorded on this bead is CLEARED and the fold is now expressible end to end: Decoded::Value to Complete(Ok(..)), Decoded::Malformed to Complete(Err(..)) since malformed bytes are a real domain verdict and belong inside the authoritative arm, and Decoded::Inconclusive(Exhausted) to Outcome::Inconclusive(Inconclusive::resource(ResourceUsage{ reason: StructuralBudget{unit}, allowed, observed })). The Exhausted.at that had no home goes through Inconclusive::with_progress — the 'WATCH' item on this bead is answered, and it is diagnostic only, so it must not be read as a budget.

The trigger I left here has been consumed: the exhaustive match in canon.rs failed to compile when the variant landed, exactly as designed, and has been replaced by the positive mapping law above rather than deleted.
