title: W1: Workspace scaffolding — §21 crate map, pinned nightly, unsafe-ledger CI, layering checks
description:
Scaffold the cargo workspace per the cycle-free crate map (§21): every fln-* crate stubbed with its one-line charter as crate-level docs — fln-core, fln-hash, fln-bignum, fln-libm, fln-rt, fln-unsafe-abi, fln-unsafe-region, fln-env, fln-olean, fln-kernel, fln-checker, fln-parse, fln-syntax, fln-elab, fln-comp, fln-vm, fln-unsafe-jit (feature iron), fln-anvil, fln-verdict, fln-ledger, fln-lake, fln-server, fln-trace, fln-hound, fln-doc, fln-mcp, fln-tui, fln-cli, fln (library facade), fln-conformance, fln-wasm — plus vendor/lean4-src at the pin (three D8 roles only, Apache-2.0 notices carried, never linked).

Structural enforcement from day one: rust-toolchain.toml pinning the exact nightly (no or-later); #![forbid(unsafe_code)] at every ordinary crate root; the three fln-unsafe-* boundary crates with #![deny(unsafe_code)] roots and the unsafe-boundary ledger file (path, invariant, evidence, safe fallback, no-claim boundary per row); CI checks that (a) walk the dependency graph and fail on any edge violating the strictly-downward §5 layering or the D3 structural laws (no fln-unsafe-* crate depends on fln-kernel/fln-checker; no unsafe crate exports a type launderable into a checked declaration), (b) reject any unledgered unsafe site, (c) enforce the fln-kernel line-count covenant once the crate has content.

Acceptance: cargo check --all-targets green on the stubbed workspace from a cold checkout; the layering CI check demonstrably fails on a seeded illegal edge (add a test-only violation in CI to prove detection, then remove); the unsafe-ledger check fails on a seeded unledgered allow site. Tests: the CI checks themselves plus a workspace-graph snapshot test that any new crate or edge must be explicitly acknowledged in a reviewed file.

## Acceptance Criteria

All bead-specific requirements, acceptance conditions, tests, invariants, compatibility surfaces, evidence levels, performance gates, negative/recovery cases, and user-visible behaviors stated above remain mandatory. In addition, the MANDATORY VERIFICATION DEFINITION OF DONE in Notes must be satisfied with named unit/property/mutation suites, at least one shared real-path no-mock E2E scenario plus failure/recovery coverage, detailed human and schema-versioned NDJSON artifacts, and reproducible close evidence. No listed feature or claim may be silently narrowed, deferred, mocked, or declared complete through an unclassified divergence.
design:
REVIEW AMENDMENT — close repository-configuration and bootstrap gaps in the structural contract. Until an explicit reviewed Cargo-config contract exists, both .cargo/config.toml and legacy .cargo/config are forbidden because they can inject lint caps, compiler wrappers, linkers/runners, and source replacement outside Cargo.toml/WORKSPACE_GRAPH. The exact nightly is validated structurally as one [toolchain] table with one dated channel and recognized typed keys only; path, decoy-section, duplicate, and unknown-key forms fail closed. CI performs the same SUITE.lock↔rust-toolchain validation with a bootstrapping parser before repository-selected rustc executes, installs the explicit lock channel, and verifies the compiler commit. Seed both Cargo-config filenames and malformed/ambiguous toolchain shapes; retain the layering, unsafe-ledger, closure, line-covenant, and no-mock evidence requirements.

REVIEW AMENDMENT — seal ambient compiler configuration. Source lint posture is not sufficient if lint caps, wrappers, alternate toolchains, ancestor/Cargo-home configuration, or target-specific flags can change the effective compiler. Every authoritative gate invokes the exact locked cargo/rustc and either rejects or excludes every ambient configuration channel. Isolation must preserve user state and shared caches through per-run homes/targets or validated read-only inputs. Effective compiler identity and admitted environment are evidence facts. Source-level unsafe-ledger scanning remains an independent defense.

REVIEW AMENDMENT — make the governed structural authority complete and outcome-typed. The universe is every Cargo workspace member and every Rust-bearing target reachable under any supported host/target, feature, profile, tool, build, test, example, bench, proc-macro, build-script, generated-code, or macro-expanded invocation. Every package and target has exactly one reviewed class and charter. Hidden nested workspaces, unclassified members/targets, default-members or exclude tricks, manifest-path/symlink escapes, auxiliary targets substituting for a missing primary product, and generated/macro logic outside the authority census fail closed.

No repository-local Cargo config or legacy rust-toolchain file may exist at any depth from which a supported command can discover it. Authoritative root, locked toolchain, isolated configuration inputs, and validated environment are explicit. Unreadable/non-UTF-8 governed input, incomplete traversal, source-root change, cancellation, resource exhaustion, or ambiguous compiler/invocation identity yields typed Inconclusive/InternalFault and never a clean result.

The kernel covenant cannot be evaded by generated, included, proc-macro, declarative-macro, target-only, test-only, or tool code that contributes checking authority. Such project-authored logic is either forbidden or inventoried and counted under a reviewed expanded-authority rule with an exact source/generated mapping. This is a plan-space clarification only; CopperHare retains implementation ownership.
acceptance_criteria: All original workspace, crate-map, toolchain, unsafe-ledger, layering, line-covenant, seeded-failure, and cold cargo-check requirements remain binding. Named suite structure_authority_model covers every package/target/feature/profile/host-target lane, nested Cargo configuration, legacy toolchain files, duplicate roots/keys, hidden targets/workspaces, default-members/exclude and manifest/symlink escapes, cfg/feature/target-only edges, unreadable inputs, concurrent root changes, incomplete scans, ambiguous compiler/root identity, ambient configuration, and expanded generated/macro kernel authority. Mutants include omitted auxiliary target, partial scan promoted to pass, hidden generated kernel logic, dropped read failure, fake compiler/root, and each configuration escape. The no-mock structure E2E runs from repository root and a representative crate/tool directory, plants each violation in an isolated candidate, proves typed refusal, restores exact inputs, and ends clean. Strict NDJSON adds package/target/feature/target-triple class, traversal completeness, pre/post governed roots, effective compiler identity, admitted environment, authority-count rule, outcome/authority, cleanup, and final state. Ownership remains with CopperHare; this review does not claim implementation progress.
notes:
MANDATORY VERIFICATION DEFINITION OF DONE (inherits franken_lean-rur; additive to this bead's own Tests/Acceptance):
1. Unit coverage: deterministic happy-path, boundary, malformed-input, resource-exhaustion, cancellation, and failure-atomicity cases for every new public behavior; property/metamorphic and mutation-kill tests wherever an invariant or equivalence is claimed.
2. E2E coverage: add or extend at least one shared scripts/e2e scenario for the real user-visible path, plus a negative/recovery scenario. Release-level evidence uses the no-mock lane (real Reference binary/artifact/filesystem/editor/process/host as applicable). A mock may support a unit test but may not close an L-level, PG gate, or public claim.
3. Detailed logs: emit both concise human logs and schema-versioned NDJSON with run/scenario/step ids; bead, claim, invariant, Parity-Ledger row, and gate ids; exact command/argv with secrets redacted; cwd; epoch/mode/profile/platform/thread-count/seed/cache-state/host facts; canonical input hashes; expected vs actual; monotonic start/end/duration; resource and budget facts; exit status/signal; stdout/stderr artifact references; receipt/logical roots; first-divergence data; cleanup and asserted final state. Never swallow stderr, never leak secrets, and bound adversarial log volume.
4. CI/closeout: archive logs, fixtures, repro bundles, and evidence manifests; failures must be diagnosable from artifacts alone. Run scripts/check.sh, cargo test, the bead-specific unit/property suites, relevant Tribunal differential/mutation/fault lanes, and the shared E2E scenario. The close evidence names every test/scenario id and artifact location; skips require a typed, logged, honest L-level limitation and may not satisfy the skipped claim.

Adversarial review of tools/structure-guard (Claude Fable session, via a dedicated review subagent, 2026-07-22). Reporting rather than editing since CopperHare is actively in this crate. The tool is very well-hardened — the subagent tried every smuggling class from the brief and confirmed SOLID: target-cfg/sub-table/dotted-key/renamed(package=)/workspace-inherited deps all fail closed to FLN-STRUCT-016; dev- and build-dependencies ARE collected and subject to layering+D3 (the 'hide an upward edge in dev-deps' attack is closed); equal-rank edges rejected (fr<=tr); D3 transitive BFS uses the full edge set; root-lint spoofing defeated (cfg_attr/nested-mod/string/macro decoys); unsafe-ledger scan walks the filesystem (not a hardcoded list) incl. tests/examples/benches/build.rs and ignores UNSAFE-LEDGER: inside string literals; symlink escapes flagged; all governance parsers fail closed on missing-schema/decoy-section/dup-key/short-hash; exit-code/report integrity correct (every finding->exit 1, no dedup drop, no severity downgrade). FINDINGS:
1) MEDIUM (real gap): audit_repository_cargo_config (checks.rs:166-186) checks ONLY <root>/.cargo/config.toml and <root>/.cargo/config. Nothing scans nested .cargo/ dirs. A regular file at crates/fln-kernel/.cargo/config.toml (or crates/.cargo/, tools/*/.cargo/) is invisible — yet cargo merges config from the invocation dir upward, so any per-crate 'cd crates/X && cargo ...' step picks up an injected rustc-wrapper/runner/linker/[source]-replacement OUTSIDE the reviewed graph. Contradicts the check's own doc comment. Fix: reuse the existing crates/+tools/ walk (already done in scan_symlinks) to emit FLN-STRUCT-016 for any .cargo/config(.toml) at any depth, not just root.
2) LOW-MED: a single non-UTF-8/unreadable governed .rs or manifest makes fs::read_to_string(...)? propagate to a whole-run exit 2, masking all other findings (griefing/diagnosability). Manifest PARSE errors are already localized to FLN-STRUCT-016; do the same for unreadable/non-UTF-8 source files instead of ?-to-exit-2.
3) LOW: legacy plain 'rust-toolchain' (no .toml) is never audited though the tool forbids the legacy .cargo/config filename by the same reasoning (defense-in-depth; rustup prefers .toml when both exist).
4) LOW: suite-dep only required to be is_some() path dep; not checked against the SUITE.lock path= (code comments 'SUITE.lock pending' — documented limitation).
5) LOW: LOC covenant (FLN-STRUCT-015) counts written lines; a macro_rules! in fln-kernel can expand under the 12k cap (inherent line-counter limit).
6) INFO: AllowSite doc says same-line marker allowed but scan_allow_sites only inspects lines above (fails closed/over-strict — doc/behavior mismatch).
Bottom line: no 'unsafe/upward edge ships green' hole; #1 is the one worth fixing promptly.

title: W1/W10/W12: Certified platform and target support decision contract
description:
## Description

Define the single versioned platform-support decision consumed by codegen, plugin doors, distribution, epoch ratchet, and G6. Distinguish build host, target triple/features, object/runtime ABI, functional support, execution support, C4 plugin support, certified reproducibility, browser tier, installer availability, and R4 declaration. Resolve D17 Windows explicitly rather than allowing build success or functional CI to imply certification.

Every matrix cell binds exact toolchain/closure, target/profile/mode, owner, required real host, support/evidence state, exclusions, runtime allowlist, artifact class, and promotion criteria. Unknown or missing cells fail closed; one host cannot proxy another.

## Acceptance Criteria

Named suites platform_cell_schema, target_runtime_allowlist, support_level_lattice, d17_windows_decision, matrix_promotion_model, and platform_real_host_no_mock_e2e cover Linux, macOS, Windows, browser, supported/unsupported targets, cross compilation versus execution, plugins, installers, reproducibility, transitions, cancellation, and stale evidence. Mutants conflate host/target, functional/certified, C4/R4, static/runtime-allowlisted, or browser/native; omit cells; alias host proof; or promote from mock/cross-build only; all fail. Canonical semantic decisions are separate from host/performance telemetry and every promoted cell cites real evidence.

title: W2: Owned allocator — size-classed, heartbeat hook, membrane discipline
description:
Implement the owned allocator (§6.3): size-classed, mimalloc-tradition (thread-local pages, size-class bins, deferred frees) — owned rather than off-the-shelf because allocation behavior is SEMANTICALLY visible through heartbeat accounting (fuel parity, §4.2/§8.5) and performance-visible everywhere.

The heartbeat hook lives here: one counting law, calibrated by spike G0-6, shared by both kernel engines and Golem (allocation through Marrow so heartbeats count identically across interpreted and native paths). The allocator must also serve the CompatHeap discipline (§6.1b): membrane-only allocation and free, so foreign code observes exactly the Reference allocation contract at the ABI.

Acceptance: fuel-parity fixtures from G0-6 stay green when running over the real allocator; allocation-heavy corpus benchmarks show no pathological regression vs the baseline report envelope; zero leaks over the PG-6 four-hour soak profile (measured under the lab runtime with the leak oracle). Tests: size-class boundary unit tests; concurrent alloc/free stress under the asupersync lab with seed replay; heartbeat-count determinism test at thread counts {1, 8, 32} (same input, same tick totals — FL-INV-01 applies to fuel too).

## Acceptance Criteria

All bead-specific requirements, acceptance conditions, tests, invariants, compatibility surfaces, evidence levels, performance gates, negative/recovery cases, and user-visible behaviors stated above remain mandatory. In addition, the MANDATORY VERIFICATION DEFINITION OF DONE in Notes must be satisfied with named unit/property/mutation suites, at least one shared real-path no-mock E2E scenario plus failure/recovery coverage, detailed human and schema-versioned NDJSON artifacts, and reproducible close evidence. No listed feature or claim may be silently narrowed, deferred, mocked, or declared complete through an unclassified divergence.
acceptance_criteria: The owned size-classed allocator implements thread-local pages, bins and deferred frees for every Marrow allocation class while preserving the CompatHeap membrane and exact foreign allocation/free contract. One calibrated heartbeat hook is shared by K1/K2 and Golem; charge totals and timeout behavior match the ratified G0-6 class and are deterministic at 1/8/32 threads. Allocation/free never bypasses typed heap ownership, and cancellation/resource/fault paths reclaim or retain only explicitly owned objects. Unit/property/model/lab/mutation tests cover every size/alignment/class boundary, reuse/deferred free, concurrent allocation, foreign/incorrect heap, exact budget/tick boundaries, fragmentation, cancellation and replay; named missed/double charge, wrong class, lost free, cross-heap, nondeterministic tick and leak mutants are killed. Real no-mock allocation-heavy Corpus/plugin/VM E2E exercises production ABI paths and seeded lab schedules, plants/restores faults, and retains strict class/tick/allocation/leak/root/final-state bundles. PG-6 four-hour soak has zero leaks and performance remains within the baseline envelope with raw evidence. All dependencies, scripts/check.sh, cargo/fmt/clippy/UBS, ownership/lab/thread/soak/platform lanes pass. No off-the-shelf opaque allocator, uncalibrated clock/timing proxy, raw bypass, hidden cross-heap free, leak waiver, schedule-dependent fuel, or deferred listed allocation behavior satisfies closure.
notes:
MANDATORY VERIFICATION DEFINITION OF DONE (inherits franken_lean-rur; additive to this bead's own Tests/Acceptance):
1. Unit coverage: deterministic happy-path, boundary, malformed-input, resource-exhaustion, cancellation, and failure-atomicity cases for every new public behavior; property/metamorphic and mutation-kill tests wherever an invariant or equivalence is claimed.
2. E2E coverage: add or extend at least one shared scripts/e2e scenario for the real user-visible path, plus a negative/recovery scenario. Release-level evidence uses the no-mock lane (real Reference binary/artifact/filesystem/editor/process/host as applicable). A mock may support a unit test but may not close an L-level, PG gate, or public claim.
3. Detailed logs: emit both concise human logs and schema-versioned NDJSON with run/scenario/step ids; bead, claim, invariant, Parity-Ledger row, and gate ids; exact command/argv with secrets redacted; cwd; epoch/mode/profile/platform/thread-count/seed/cache-state/host facts; canonical input hashes; expected vs actual; monotonic start/end/duration; resource and budget facts; exit status/signal; stdout/stderr artifact references; receipt/logical roots; first-divergence data; cleanup and asserted final state. Never swallow stderr, never leak secrets, and bound adversarial log volume.
4. CI/closeout: archive logs, fixtures, repro bundles, and evidence manifests; failures must be diagnosable from artifacts alone. Run scripts/check.sh, cargo test, the bead-specific unit/property suites, relevant Tribunal differential/mutation/fault lanes, and the shared E2E scenario. The close evidence names every test/scenario id and artifact location; skips require a typed, logged, honest L-level limitation and may not satisfy the skipped claim.

title: Corpus census is produced at one thread count; FL-INV-01 matrix evidence covers only the Prelude
description:
The FL-INV-01 thread-matrix evidence and the corpus census are produced by two DIFFERENT tests over two different input sets, and only the smaller one is matrix-verified.

WHERE THE MATRIX EVIDENCE ACTUALLY IS. crates/fln-conformance/tests/kernel_replay.rs:3167-3252, inside prelude_replays_through_the_kernel (line 2927). It checks the same prepared units at {1, 8, 32} workers over a shared racing cursor and asserts the merged verdict stream is byte-identical at every width, failing with "FL-INV-01 violation: verdict stream diverged across the thread matrix". That test is correct and its construction is sound. Its input is the PRELUDE.

WHERE THE CENSUS COMES FROM. pinned_present_olean_kernel_differential (line 2613, ignored pending fln-7odd), which at line 2803 selects its width by a size heuristic:

    let threads = if prep.items.len() < 64 { 1 } else { 8 };

So the corpus census - the artifact behind the 15,722-compared figure and everything derived from it - is produced at a SINGLE thread count, chosen per module, and is never run across the matrix. Its schedule-independence is inferred from the Prelude matrix on different inputs rather than demonstrated on the corpus itself.

WHY THIS IS WORTH CLOSING RATHER THAN SHRUGGING AT. The inference is reasonable: the kernel is pure, each unit's inputs are fixed by prepare_replay, and the merge is deterministic by construction (index-addressed OnceLock slots, canonical-order merge, BTreeMap for rejection classes, sum and max for the aggregates, and duration_us explicitly marked timing_used_as_gate:false). I checked all of that and found no schedule-dependence. But "we reason it must be schedule-independent" is a different claim class from "we ran it at three widths and the digest was identical", and on this project that distinction is the entire point - D7 says a weaker class may never justify a stronger one. The corpus is also the input most likely to contain the pathological case the Prelude does not: it is 158,608 decoded declarations against a few thousand.

The heuristic is a second, smaller wrinkle: because width depends on prep.items.len(), two modules of different sizes run at different widths, so the census is not even produced at ONE consistent width across the run.

WHAT TO DO, cheapest first. Either (a) run the corpus differential across {1, 8, 32} and compare stream digests as the Prelude test does - expensive but it is the real evidence, and it could be a nightly rather than per-commit lane; or (b) if that cost is not acceptable, say so explicitly where the census is reported: record that corpus schedule-independence is INFERRED from the Prelude matrix plus the purity and merge-determinism argument, not measured on the corpus. Option (b) costs nothing and stops the stronger claim from being read into the number.

Found during a read-only concurrency sweep by cc_2 on 2026-07-25, looking for FL-INV-01 breakers. The sweep found no actual schedule-dependence in the merge path; this is an evidence-scope gap, not a defect. Owner is the conformance/corpus lane, not cc_2.
close_reason: Option (b) landed in 66e56721: census reports schedule_independence=inferred_not_measured inline, module doc scopes the matrix to the Prelude, width heuristic marked not-a-matrix. Option (a) (corpus run across {1,8,32}) deliberately NOT done and recorded in the closure comment and coverage row.

comments.author: PeachBass
comments.text:
PRIORITY RAISED P3 -> P1 by the orchestrator, with reasoning, because the filer under-rated their own finding.

The finder is right that this is an evidence-scope gap and not a defect, and right that no schedule-dependence was found in the merge path. Both of those argue against calling it a bug. Neither argues for P3.

What sets the priority here is not the size of the fix but WHICH claim is unsupported. FL-INV-01 is constitutional on this project: doctrine item 6 states determinism is a contract, PG-5 gates bit-identical environments, diagnostics and artifacts across {1, 8, 32} threads PER COMMIT, and the doctrine says plainly that no subsystem ships against an unenforced invariant. The finding establishes that the matrix evidence covers the Prelude while the corpus census - the artifact behind the headline comparison figure - is produced at a single width chosen by a size heuristic, and is therefore not matrix-verified at all.

That is precisely the D7 failure shape the project exists to prevent: a weaker claim class standing in for a stronger one. "We reason it must be schedule-independent" is bounded_model at best; "we ran it at three widths and the digest was identical" is the invariant claim PG-5 actually requires. D7 says a weaker class may never enforce or justify a stronger one.

It also directly qualifies the most-quoted number this project has. The corpus differential result - 15,722 compared, 9.9 percent of 158,608 decoded, zero unsoundly-permissive - now carries an INFERRED rather than measured schedule-independence. Anyone restating that figure as evidence of deterministic corpus checking would be overclaiming, and would not know it.

SEQUENCING, which is why this is P1 and not P0. Option (b) costs nothing and should land immediately: state at the point the census is reported that corpus schedule-independence is inferred from the Prelude matrix plus the purity and merge-determinism argument, not measured on the corpus. That closes the overclaim today. Option (a), running the corpus differential across {1, 8, 32} and comparing stream digests, is the real evidence and can be a nightly lane rather than per-commit.

Do (b) first. Do not let (a)'s cost delay (b), because until (b) lands the stronger claim is readable into the number.

Second wrinkle worth not losing: the width heuristic at kernel_replay.rs:2803 means two modules of different sizes run at different widths, so the census is not produced at one consistent width either. Whoever takes (a) should pin the width explicitly rather than leaving it size-dependent.

comments.text:

WHAT I AM NOT DOING: option (a), the full {1, 8, 32} corpus run. The orchestrator has ruled that a nightly lane whose cost must not delay (b), and it stays open for whoever takes it. If you want (a) it is yours; I am not claiming it.

WHY IT CANNOT WAIT FOR A HANDOFF: until the wording lands, the corpus differential figure - 15,722 compared, 9.9 percent of 158,608 decoded - reads as evidence of deterministic corpus checking, and PG-5 requires a measured invariant where today there is only a reasoned argument. That is the D7 shape the project exists to prevent, so the fix is to stop the overclaim being readable, today.

I wrote the containment analysis on this file for kxbj and know the merge path, which is why I took it rather than queueing it behind you. Revert or reword freely afterwards - the claim-class correction is the point, not my phrasing.

title: W1: Benchmark evidence core — host profiles, raw attempts, statistics, and bundle validation
description:
## Description

Build the neutral benchmark-evidence substrate shared by Reference baselines and FrankenLean performance gates. It owns versioned host-profile qualification, workload/sample-plan manifests, immutable raw-attempt records, cache-state vocabulary, statistical calculations, semantic-versus-telemetry separation, bundle rendering/validation, and failure-atomic publication. It does not own target values, PG policy, Reference observations, or a subsystem bench adapter.

A host profile binds CPU SKU/topology and enabled cores/SMT, RAM, storage/filesystem, OS/kernel, power governor, thermal policy and sensors, virtualization/translation state, toolchain/binary hashes, target/profile/features, and clock/counter capabilities. A workload freezes inputs/order, warmup, sample count or stopping rule, invalidation rule, quantile algorithm, confidence interval, outlier policy, variance decision, cache layers, and resource bounds before results are observed. Cache state independently records filesystem/page cache, Reference or candidate artifact cache, build cache, imported-module residency, and warm daemon state.

Every attempt is immutable and typed valid, invalid-host, cancelled, resource-refused, target-failed, infrastructure-fault, or insufficient-sample. Invalid attempts never disappear or enter aggregates; resume cannot duplicate samples. Raw data, statistical summaries, and rendered reports share one content-addressed root chain. Benchmark observations are D7 benchmark evidence, repeatability/variance decisions are statistical, and targets are SLOs; none becomes PROVEN or a correctness result.

Canonical semantic records contain identities, sample plan, raw measurements in declared units, validity decisions, statistical result, and roots. Wall-clock collection metadata, timestamps, host/PID/absolute-path details, and profiling counters that are not comparison inputs remain bounded linked telemetry. Candidate publication occurs only after independent schema/statistics/root validation and unchanged input roots.

## Acceptance Criteria

Named suites benchmark_host_profile_model, benchmark_attempt_state_machine, cache_state_lattice, statistical_reference_vectors, benchmark_bundle_validator, and benchmark_core_no_mock_e2e cover all host/cache/workload/attempt states, exact quantile/confidence/dispersion algorithms, pre-registration, invalid exclusion, resume/deduplication, cancellation/fault/nonpublication, semantic/telemetry separation, and independent regeneration. Mutations for invalid sample averaging, dropped attempt, duplicate resume sample, post-observation stopping change, cache conflation, host-profile substitution, naked point-estimate gate, benchmark-as-proof promotion, telemetry in semantic root, silent raw edit, stale summary, partial publication, and profiler contamination are killed. The no-mock E2E runs a small real benchmark under a qualified local profile, plants valid/invalid/cancelled/insufficient attempts, recomputes the summary from raw data, detects tampering, restores, retries, and independently validates the final immutable bundle. Strict NDJSON records schema/workload/host/cache/sample/attempt ids, exact units and measurements, validity/reason, statistical method/result, pre/post roots, expected/actual, resources, publication authority, cleanup, and final state. Reference baselines and PG policy remain downstream owners.

title: W1: Performance-gate harness — bench binaries, baselines, tail gates, flame artifacts
description:
## Description

Build the single versioned performance-gate registry, evaluator, and evidence join for PG-1, PG-2, PG-3, PG-4, PG-5, PG-6, PG-7, PG-8, PG-9, PG-K, PG-10, PG-L, PG-1b, and PG-M. W1 closes this task on the complete registry/common evaluator/validators, one real end-to-end gate, and an exact owner/activation entry for every remaining production adapter. Each downstream gate owner remains unable to close until its real adapter is active and green; no PG feature is dropped or waived because its subsystem is not yet implemented.

Every PG row freezes stable id/owner, workload/corpus, profile/mode/platform/host, threads, cache state, metric/unit/direction, comparator kind, absolute target, regression threshold, minimum valid samples, baseline id/root, statistical method/uncertainty, freshness, convergence gate, rollback owner, activation state, and required correctness evidence. Absolute convergence targets and regression thresholds are separate: an alert-only two-release regression policy cannot postpone an explicit gate target.

Performance and correctness form a two-key join. PG-5 semantic bit identity comes from TD9/invariant evidence; PG-8 byte round-trip, PG-9 agreement, PG-M fidelity, kernel verdicts, and analogous semantics come from their authoritative rigs. A fast benchmark cannot override missing/failed/stale/Inconclusive correctness evidence. TD9 owns the semantic 1/8/32 matrix; this task measures scaling/overhead and joins evidence.

Use paired/interleaved same-host baseline/candidate runs under fln-9wya’s predeclared sample rules, robust dispersion/confidence bounds, immutable attempt-complete reporting, and independent bundle validation. Cancellation, candidate crash, insufficient samples, profiler failure, resource refusal, or infrastructure fault is typed non-passing. Profiling occurs in a separate diagnostic rerun after a regression; its overhead never contaminates authoritative samples. Profilers/renderers must be owned or explicitly platform-contracted within D1; an undeclared external flamegraph tool is forbidden. A {96}+ lane requires a declared qualified high-core host, not oversubscription.

title: fln-olean: six verified hostile-input defects — cyclic decode OOM, unchecked multiplies, base+offset overflow, walk/audit disagreement
description:
Type: bug
Priority: 1
Title: fln-olean: six verified hostile-input defects — cyclic decode OOM, unchecked multiplies, base+offset overflow, walk/audit disagreement

OleanReview's six findings, each verified line-by-line against the code before
any fix (class: hostile .olean input → panic/OOM/validator-disagreement, all
FL-INV-07 violations — malformed input must never panic):

1. decl.rs decode_expr/decode_level: charge() runs only when a node BUILDS; a
   cyclic graph (A's child B, B's child A) never builds, the stack grows
   unbounded, the budget never trips → OOM on any profile. Root fix: enforce
   the writer's post-order law (child offset strictly below parent, the law
   fln-rt/region.rs:9 already documents), making cycles structurally
   impossible.
2. rebuild.rs:193 `checked_sub(size)? * 8`, :205 `let payload = size * elem;`
   (evaluated BEFORE any bounds check — wraps to 0 → silent accept in release),
   :211 `checked_sub(size)? * elem` — the eb1de0d0 campaign converted the
   subtractions and left the multiplies; debug panics, release wraps silently.
   No mutant ever exercised a multiply (the receipt confirms).
3. region.rs:395 shared_audit passes `base_addr + header` unchecked;
   rebuild.rs:112 `encode_ptr = base + file_off` unchecked; base_addr is only
   alignment-checked in parse_olean_envelope. One envelope law —
   base_addr.checked_add(file_len) must not overflow — plus checked_add per site.
4. shared_fault error mapper: `shift + offset + wanted` overflows while
   CONSTRUCTING the typed error on attacker-influenced wanted.
5. walk() scalar-array branch charges `size` bytes, ignoring the element size
   and skipping the capacity check the TAG_ARRAY branch above it has; ctor
   scalar tails (cs_sz) are discarded unchecked. A payload extending past EOF
   passes walk clean — a false valid verdict the shared audit rejects.
6. check_mpz is weaker than the shared engine: no limbs≥1, no alloc≥|size|,
   no inline-limb-block law — an mpz can point its limbs into another object
   and decode foreign bytes as a number.
7. decl.rs Level arity guard covers succ/max/imax but not param/mvar (tag 4/5),
   whose `other` then indexes the stored Data word at off+8+8*other — reads
   past the object (typed only when cross_check is enabled, and cross_check is
   a pub field that can be disabled).

Acceptance: hostile fixtures per finding (cyclic expr/level, capacity high-bit
flip, wrap-around base_addr, over-EOF scalar array, foreign-limb mpz,
param/mvar arity), each refused typed with its reason named; the 2433-file
corpus sweep still passes byte-identical (proving the post-order law holds on
the real corpus); clippy/fmt/ubs clean.

description:

Key contracts are cumulative and non-negotiable. Mathlib custom extensions round-trip as region data without executing upstream implementation code. title: fln-env: include opaque mutual-block membership in declaration content digests
description:
Problem: Environment::decl_content_digest encodes the mutual-block member list for definitions, theorems, inductives, and recursors, but omits OpaqueVal.all. Two opaque declarations that differ only in their mutual-block membership can therefore receive the same declaration content digest and contaminate Ledger/CAS identity and logical environment roots. Scope: encode OpaqueVal.all with the same canonical length-plus-ordered-name representation as every other all-bearing ConstantInfo variant. Preserve all existing digest fields and ordering. Verification requirements: (1) unit regression proves solo versus grouped opaque membership produces distinct digests; (2) one table-driven regression covers every current all-bearing variant: Defn, Thm, Opaque, Induct, and Rec; (3) environment logical-root coverage proves the corrected declaration digest propagates to snapshot identity; (4) the existing environment snapshot E2E lane is extended or explicitly demonstrated to emit detailed, versioned, line-oriented scenario logs containing case, expected digest relation, actual digest relation, and final result; (5) cargo fmt, fln-env unit tests, fln-env clippy with warnings denied, and UBS pass. No compatibility shim and no unrelated codec changes.

## Steps to Reproduce

Create otherwise-identical Opaque declarations whose `all` lists differ in length, order, or member name. Before the fix, `Environment::decl_content_digest` and the resulting logical roots are equal because `OpaqueVal.all` is never encoded.

comments.text:
REUSES fln-amv.12'S TAGGING CONVENTION — do not invent a second one (PeachBass/cc_1, 2026-07-25).

This bead and fln-amv.12 are the same question from two sides: amv.12 fixes what a declaration digest must NOT bind implicitly (Rust discriminants), this one fixes what it MUST bind explicitly. Three tagging disciplines in one crate is how the next f6br-class collision gets built, so the convention below is shared, established on amv.12, and should be applied here rather than re-derived.

THE CONVENTION, six points:
  1. Every enum reaching an identity digest gets an explicit const fn tag with an EXHAUSTIVE match. Never `as u8`, never repr, never Debug text.
  2. Guard that helper with #[forbid(clippy::as_conversions)] so a cast cannot be reintroduced silently. This is a compile-time guard and is stronger than any test.
  3. Freeze a golden PER VARIANT, not just pairwise distinctness. Distinctness survives a coordinated renumbering of every tag; a golden does not.
  4. Keep an independent model of the WRONG encoder and assert the canonical digest DIFFERS from it (amv.12 uses DeclarationTagDigestModel::CastAfterSourceReorder). Both directions or the test proves nothing — the rule that caught root.rs lying and that the alpha-canonical digest needed.
  5. DERIVE the test matrix from an exhaustive match, never a hand-written array. This is the hole amv.12's own guard exposed: a new variant was forced to get a TAG but not into the test matrix, so it would ship with no golden, no distinctness coverage and no E2E row. Use the succ-chain idiom (const fn next(v) -> Option<v> with an exhaustive match) so the chain both forces registration and generates the matrix, plus a frozen length assertion so shortening the chain also fails.
  6. State the three-way expectation explicitly: reorder = NO digest change (tags bind names, not positions), add = compile error, retag = golden failure. "A test that fails on reorder" is the natural phrasing and it asserts the bug.

VERIFIED STATE OF THIS BEAD'S SUBSTANCE (checked 2026-07-25, do not re-implement): the fln-env fix is already present — see fln-amv.14's closure and commits fe4a825 / d6126b9. What was missing was lane-consumable evidence, and that landed: fln.e2e.declaration-membership/1 for fln-amv.1 (41 records: 35 matrix rows over five all-bearing kinds x seven membership boundaries, 5 defect rows, 1 summary) and fln.e2e.extension-descriptor-matrix/1 for fln-amv.2 (25 records: all twelve merge x checkpoint x provenance combinations, 12 defect rows, 1 summary). Complete field lists are in fln-amv.14's comments. So the likely remaining work here is an acceptance-criteria review against evidence that already exists, not implementation — check before building.

CONCURRENCY POSTURE, since cc_2's Marrow audit just closed two ownership-transition bugs: the identity paths in fln-env are pure functions over immutable values, with no shared mutable state to race. The admission plan deliberately does NOT assume a single writer — it revalidates its base binding before publishing and reports PlanSuperseded when the lineage moved. If work on this bead introduces any cached or memoised identity, state its writer assumption explicitly rather than leaving it implicit.

title: fln-env: canonicalize full-hash collision buckets for schedule-independent iteration
description:
Problem: PMap iteration is insertion-order independent only for non-colliding hashes. Distinct keys with the same complete 64-bit key_hash are appended to a leaf bucket, so bucket iteration, Debug output, and any future environment enumeration depend on insertion/scheduling order. This violates FL-INV-01 under adversarial Name collisions even though LogicalRootBuilder currently masks the defect by sorting again. Scope: give PKey a deterministic total tie-break consistent with Eq and maintain every full-hash collision bucket in canonical key order during insert/overwrite/remove; do not sort the entire map at iteration time or rely on randomized hashing. For Name, use the pinned Name.cmp order after its stack-safety prerequisite is complete. Document the CGSE policy and complexity for large collision buckets. Verification requirements: permutation/property tests use many distinct constant-hash keys and prove identical iteration/Debug/equality after insert, overwrite, remove, fork, and reinsert; mixed near-collision tries exercise every hash chunk and the final partial chunk; a schedule matrix constructs the same environment in several thread partitions and compares enumerations and roots; deep valid names remain bounded once the Name-order prerequisite lands. Extend the shared environment E2E lane with versioned detailed logs containing collision cardinality, insertion schedule, canonical key order, expected/actual enumeration and roots, operation counts, resources, and final state. Run fmt, all fln-env tests, clippy -D warnings, UBS, and parent gates. No iteration-time global sort, address-based tie-break, randomized seed, or collision rejection.

## Steps to Reproduce

Insert the same set of distinct constant-hash keys in forward and reverse order, then compare `PMap::iter` and Debug output. The current collision leaf retains insertion order, so the two enumerations differ.

## Acceptance Criteria

Every scope, behavior, verification requirement, dependency, and prohibited shortcut above is mandatory. Closure requires the named deterministic unit/property/model coverage, the shared real-path E2E success plus negative/recovery scenario with detailed schema-versioned logs, all stated performance or evidence proofs, and green fmt/test/clippy/UBS and parent gates. No unclassified skip, mock-only evidence, partial implementation, or deferred listed feature satisfies this bead.
acceptance_criteria: 1. PKey exposes a deterministic total tie-break consistent with Eq, and every complete-primary-hash collision bucket is maintained in canonical key order across distinct insert, overwrite, remove, fork, reinsert, collapse, equality, iteration, and Debug behavior. No global iteration-time sort, randomized seed, address tie-break, or valid collision rejection is permitted. 2. Named unit/property/model tests compare many distinct constant-hash keys against an independent ordered model across forward, reverse, randomized, and all removal/reinsertion permutations; mixed near-collision tries exercise every hash chunk including the final partial chunk; exact-key overwrites preserve cardinality and canonical order. Named append-order, wrong-tie-break, missed-overwrite, and removal-order mutants are each killed. 3. Environment construction at thread partitions 1, 8, and 32 and repeated identical runs produces byte-identical canonical enumeration, Debug/equality observables, logical roots, operation counters, and semantic records. Deep valid Name keys use the pinned Name order without host-recursive comparison. Total resident storage for N exact colliding entries is necessarily linear in N. fln-amv.13 owns sublinear lookup and sublinear fresh/copied-node work per update where its representation permits, nonquadratic family construction, and exact resource accounting; no compression, coalescing, or valid-collision loss is permitted. 4. The shared real-path no-mock environment E2E includes positive collision construction, a planted append-order mutant with the exact expected semantic failure, byte-exact restoration, and clean recovery. It emits strict schema-versioned line-oriented records containing bead/invariant/claim IDs, collision cardinality, schedule and thread, canonical expected/actual order, expected/actual roots, operation/resource facts, input and final hashes, exit/signal, separate stdout/stderr artifacts, cleanup, and final state. Its validator rejects missing/extra fields, stale inputs, wrong or unrelated failures, merged streams, surviving mutants, and incomplete bundles. 5. cargo fmt --check, all fln-env tests, warnings-denied Clippy, UBS on changed files, evidence-validator self-tests, the focused positive-mutation-recovery E2E, scripts/check.sh, and currently runnable parent gates are green with independently valid retained bundles. Final outer environment-schema migration remains explicitly owned by fln-amv.14.
close_reason: Canonical full-hash collision buckets and strict bounded-model E2E/validator/CI proof are complete with green exact parent gates; legacy outer-parent evidence debt remains tracked in fln-amv.14.

title: fln-env: integrate atomic three-way environment merge across all semantic state
description:
Final child integration for fln-env: component APIs can merge individual structures, but speculative branches need one atomic three-way merge across the combined committed state. After every dependency lands, implement a typed merge of base, ours, and theirs containing Environment declarations/extensions, attribute state, module graph, canonical provenance manifest, actual payload-bearing contribution state, and both provenance index directions. A plain Environment-only merge is insufficient.

The lifecycle child of fln-amv.9.3 produces the exact ProvenanceMergePlan. Global merge must consume and immediately revalidate that plan against base/ours/theirs logical roots, provenance roots, schema/epoch, actual declaration and extension values, ranges, contributor identities, and resource envelope before any publication. It must not independently reconstruct a second provenance truth. A stale, mismatched, incomplete, or value-collision plan is a typed atomic refusal. The final commit publishes Environment plus graph/provenance/index state together, or publishes nothing.

Constants added on disjoint names combine; identical same-name additions are idempotent only after actual ConstantInfo equality, not digest equality; different same-name declarations and equal-digest unequal-value cases conflict with both origins and canonical identities. Extension registration/journals follow declared merge and checkpoint laws, including new-on-one-side, identical-new-on-both, AppendOrdered precedence, SetUnion semantic-view/raw-journal law, descriptor/ancestry/range mismatch, opaque provenance, and review-required conflicts. Attribute state follows its pinned contract. Import topology, actual module contributions, completeness grades, contributor indexes, and invalidation roots follow the revalidated provenance plan. Missing or partial input remains explicitly graded and never becomes verified completeness or rejection.

Aggregate every independent conflict in frozen category then canonical Name/module/range order rather than stopping at map traversal order. Define deterministic ours/theirs precedence only where AppendOrdered makes it observable. Before allocating conflict/output collections, enforce independent limits for declarations, extension rows/bytes, attribute rows, modules/import rows, provenance/index rows, names/depth, conflicts/witness bytes, total output bytes, and merge work. Cancellation is observed at fixed deterministic boundaries. Exhaustion or cancellation returns Inconclusive with usage facts and no authoritative partial environment; InternalFault covers inconsistent validated-state/index/plan invariants. Neither outcome is cached as accept/reject.

Root behavior is explicit and checked twice, before and after publication construction. Metadata-only module/provenance changes do not affect logical_root. Merged declarations, extension deltas, attributes when contractually logical, and options affect logical_root exactly through their canonical builders. Provenance root covers topology/ownership/evidence/completeness and remains separate. Operational metadata affects neither. The result reports base/ours/theirs/final logical and provenance roots plus transition reasons, and preserves structural sharing for every unchanged trie, journal chunk, module record, contribution array, index branch, and payload Arc.

Verification uses independent Vec/BTreeMap models for every component and the combined commit. Random fork/edit/merge tests and exhaustive tables cover no-op, one-sided, disjoint, identical, conflicting, opaque/partial/missing, all extension policies, attributes, topology, actual contributions, equal-digest collisions, stale plans/roots/bases, multi-conflict aggregation, every exact resource boundary, cancellation point, Inconclusive recovery, and InternalFault nonpublication. Branch permutations, insertion orders, and thread partitions yield byte-identical authoritative products, diagnostics, roots, and provenance plans. Failure-atomicity and allocation/pointer instrumentation prove unchanged state remains shared. Named mutants drop a declaration, extension, attribute, module, forward/reverse provenance row, plan revalidation, conflict category, completeness grade, root transition, or sharing edge.

Extend the shared no-mock environment E2E lane with a real multi-module branch/merge/failure/recovery scenario and detailed schema-versioned line logs containing snapshot/plan ids, base/ours/theirs roots, actual branch edits and origins, merge policy, ordered conflicts, contribution/index/range facts, completeness and authority grade, logical/provenance transition reasons, sharing/allocation/resource facts, publication/cacheability flags, expected/actual result, recovery action, and final state. Run fmt, all fln-env and fln-hash/domain tests, clippy with warnings denied, UBS, every component scenario, and parent gates.

No last-writer-wins declaration overwrite, digest-only equality, dropped extension/attribute/module/provenance state, stale merge plan, independently rebuilt provenance truth, partial success, authoritative inconclusive result, hidden logical-root change, or traversal-order diagnostic drift.

## Acceptance Criteria

The global three-way merge must consume and revalidate the provenance lifecycle plan and atomically publish the entire combined committed state across declarations, extensions, attributes, module graph, actual payload contributions, completeness, and both index directions. Every success/conflict/stale/collision/resource/cancellation/internal-fault/root-transition/sharing case, independent combined model, permutation/thread matrix, named mutant, detailed real E2E positive-negative-recovery log, fln-env/fln-hash/domain test, fmt, clippy, UBS, component gate, and parent gate above is mandatory. Environment-only merge, partial publication, or deferred semantic state fails closure.
design: Dependency topology: global merge consumes the concrete module integration output of fln-amv.9.4 plus attribute state and every other component contract. It does not consume an implementation artifact from the fln-amv.9 aggregation epic. The fln-amv parent separately joins both fln-amv.9 epic closure and this global merge, so the complete module acceptance matrix remains mandatory while module-epic bookkeeping and merge implementation can close in parallel. No component proof is weakened or bypassed by this topology.
acceptance_criteria:
The global merge consumes and revalidates the exact provenance plan, then atomically publishes the complete Environment plus attribute/module/provenance/payload/index state with correct separate roots and structural sharing. Named unit suites and independent Vec/BTreeMap model/property tests cover no-op, one-sided, disjoint, identical, every conflict/collision/extension/attribute/topology/completeness case, each exact resource boundary, cancellation/InternalFault nonpublication, root transitions, and allocation/pointer sharing; exhaustive permutation/thread matrices and every named mutant in the description are mandatory. The shared real multi-module no-mock E2E covers positive merge, aggregated conflict/stale-plan/value-collision refusal, resource/cancellation Inconclusive, byte-exact restoration, and later clean publication. Schema-versioned NDJSON carries run/scenario/step/snapshot/plan ids, all roots and origins, policies/conflicts, contribution/index/range/completeness/authority, sharing/resources/cacheability, expected/actual, cleanup, and final state. Separate bounded stdout/stderr artifacts, exact input/output hashes, commands, process results, mutation identity, and first divergence are inventoried in a committed manifest; strict validation rejects missing/extra/stale/swapped/merged-stream/wrong-mutant/surviving-mutant evidence and the retained bundle validates independently. All fln-env/fln-hash/domain tests, fmt, clippy with warnings denied, UBS, component gates, and parent gates must be green. No Environment-only merge, digest-only equality, partial publication, traversal-order drift, or deferred semantic state satisfies closure.

Plan-space precision addendum: conflict completeness is outcome-qualified. CompleteConflict contains the complete canonically ordered conflict set after a full bounded scan. If conflict-count, witness-byte, total-work, allocation, or cancellation limits prevent proving completeness, the result is typed Inconclusive with complete=false and at most a deterministic bounded diagnostic prefix. That prefix has authority=false, is non-cacheable, is never rendered as the full set or as rejection, and cannot drive publication. Frozen observed-outcome precedence is InternalFault, then Inconclusive/Cancelled, then complete aggregated Conflict, then publication.

Global merge consumes versioned immutable child plans from declaration admission, bounded collision handling, extension/history validation, attributes, and module provenance. All plans bind the same base/ours/theirs roots, schema/epoch, governed inputs, outcome facts, and reservations. The combined plan revalidates them, sums each child usage exactly once, and never reconstructs child canonical bytes, digests, collision order, prefix truth, attribute order, provenance truth, or component conflicts. Preflight reserves every claimed input-sized output/conflict/index collection through genuinely fallible calls where supported. After final root/cancellation/plan revalidation, one publication phase exposes all semantic planes together; no new failure or cancellation checkpoint and no unreserved input-sized allocation exists after publication begins. Arbitrary global allocator abort remains outside the in-process recovery claim unless all paths are demonstrably fallible.

For SetUnion, ours_suffix and theirs_suffix are the exact ordered raw sequences after the validated base prefix. Compare the complete suffix blocks by collision-safe canonical ExtensionEntry encoding and publish base_raw plus lesser_suffix_block plus greater_suffix_block. Never sort/interleave entries inside a block or remove raw duplicates; equal blocks are both retained. The semantic view is stable first occurrence by exact payload bytes over that final raw sequence. Payload-equal rows with different provenance remain distinct raw evidence. Hashes accelerate but never decide equality/order without an exact collision tie-break.

fln-amv.11 owns composition seams and aggregate dimensions, not duplicate child campaigns: checked usage roll-up, stale/substituted/cross-root child plans, complete cross-plane conflict aggregation, total output/conflict budgets, late cancellation before publication, all-or-nothing publication, and one representative refusal per child outcome class. Named mutants double-count or omit child work; substitute a declaration or plan; accept a stale root; truncate conflicts while marking complete; reorder/deduplicate SetUnion suffix contents; allocate or cancel after publication begins; cache Inconclusive; or publish one semantic plane early. Productive 1/8/32 schedules use fixed seeds, controlled interleavings, and replayable minimized failures.

Evidence ownership is nonduplicative: fln-amv.14 owns lifecycle/envelope validation and child composition mechanics; semantic children own their bundles; this bead owns the real global merge positive/complete-conflict/Inconclusive/nonpublication/recovery scenario and records exactly one validated digest reference per child bundle. Missing, duplicate, stale, cross-input, or contradictory references fail; one aggregate green bar cannot substitute for a child proof.

title: fln-env: replace implicit Rust discriminants in declaration identity
description:
Problem: Environment::decl_content_digest encodes DefinitionSafety and QuotKind with `as u8`, binding durable declaration/CAS identity to implicit Rust source-order discriminants. Reordering an enum, inserting a variant, or changing representation can silently rewrite logical roots without an epoch/schema decision, and new variants do not force the identity code to choose a stable tag deliberately. Scope: replace both casts with exhaustive explicit canonical tag matches, document the stable mapping as part of Domain::DeclContent, and keep every other field and byte order unchanged. Any future variant must fail compilation here until assigned an intentional schema value. Verification requirements: table-driven unit tests cover all DefinitionSafety and QuotKind variants, prove pairwise distinct content digests and stable repeated roots, and include fixed canonical tag expectations independent of enum declaration order; a deliberate cast-based encoder must be detected by the test or policy check. Existing declaration-field, logical-root, insertion-order, and thread determinism tests remain green. Extend the shared environment E2E lane with detailed versioned records containing variant, schema tag, expected/actual digest and root, epoch, and final result. Run fmt, all fln-env tests, clippy -D warnings, UBS, and parent gates. No repr-based workaround, debug-string encoding, or silent renumbering.

## Steps to Reproduce

Observe that declaration identity writes `DefinitionSafety` and `QuotKind` with `as u8`. Reordering either Rust enum changes durable digests despite no explicit identity-schema edit; the fixed-tag regression demonstrates the intended stable mapping.

## Acceptance Criteria

Every scope, behavior, verification requirement, dependency, and prohibited shortcut above is mandatory. Closure requires the named deterministic unit/property/model coverage, the shared real-path E2E success plus negative/recovery scenario with detailed schema-versioned logs, all stated performance or evidence proofs, and green fmt/test/clippy/UBS and parent gates. No unclassified skip, mock-only evidence, partial implementation, or deferred listed feature satisfies this bead.
acceptance_criteria: DefinitionSafety identity tags are exhaustively and explicitly frozen as Unsafe=0, Safe=1, Partial=2; QuotKind tags are Type=0, Ctor=1, Lift=2, Ind=3. Domain::DeclContent writes those canonical tags without enum casts, repr dependence, debug text, or any change to adjacent field order or bytes; adding a new variant fails compilation until assigned a reviewed schema tag. Table-driven unit tests assert the exact seven-row tag table, independently model the complete Definition and Quotient declaration streams, prove pairwise-distinct declaration digests across every variant, stable repeated digests and logical roots, exact LogicalRootBuilder propagation, and unchanged declaration-field and insertion-order laws. A compiler-enforced cast policy plus named source-order, omitted-tag, debug-text, adjacent-field, wrong-domain, and failed-root-propagation models kill the relevant single-defect mutations without pretending that current equal Rust ordinals can behaviorally distinguish a cast. Each of 1, 8, and 32 productive workers independently builds and hashes the complete seven-declaration environment from a distinct full permutation; unit evidence asserts full Environment equality, per-name digest equality, explicit aggregate-root equality, and detailed versioned rows while classifying this honestly as bounded component evidence rather than full PG-5 closure. The tag mapping is a const exhaustive finite match contributing exactly one canonical byte, with no input-sized iteration, helper-owned allocation, or independent cancellation point, so it introduces no new resource dimension or separate limit. The independent stream model proves the surrounding DeclContent layout and byte count are unchanged. Typed input-sized declaration hashing/admission budgets do not exist in the current API and are therefore not falsely claimed here; that preserved functionality is owned explicitly by franken_lean-j8h and remains a W2 parent blocker, while fln-amv.14 owns runner-level resource and artifact facts. The shared real Environment E2E emits schema-versioned records for every variant with epoch/profile, tag, canonical input hash, expected and actual digest/root relation, process result, resource facts, cleanup, and final state; strict validation rejects unknown, duplicate, stale, missing, or reordered cases and proves negative detection plus clean recovery. Separate bounded stream artifacts, exact input/output hashes, and the artifact manifest are retained and validate independently. cargo fmt --check, all fln-env tests, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, UBS, scripts/check.sh, and every currently runnable environment integration lane pass. No unclassified skip, mock-only proof, silent renumbering, partial matrix, enum reorder/repr workaround, nonexistent resource claim, or deferred listed identity behavior satisfies closure.

comments.text:
CLAIMED, AND THE WORK IS ALREADY IN PLACE — WHAT REMAINS IS PROVING THE GUARD FIRES (PeachBass/cc_1, 2026-07-25).

WHAT THIS BEAD ASKS FOR IS PRESENT, verified by reading crates/fln-env/src/environment.rs:
* definition_safety_tag and quot_kind_tag are exhaustive explicit const matches (lines 32-46). No implicit discriminant reaches a digest.
* Both carry #[forbid(clippy::as_conversions)], so a cast cannot be reintroduced without failing the build. That is a stronger guard than a test — it is a compile-time one.
* Zero real `as u8` casts remain in the file. The single grep hit is inside a COMMENT in the E2E producer, quoting the defect this bead exists to prevent.
* DeclarationTagDigestModel::CastAfterSourceReorder already models a cast-based encoder and is used at two sites (around lines 1563 and 1603).
* Frozen goldens exist per case: golden_stream_bytes, golden_stream_hash, golden_digest, golden_root on DeclarationTagCase.
* E2E evidence landed this session in fe4a825 — fln.e2e.declaration-tag-matrix/1 asserts canonical_tag == production_tag on every one of the seven cases and pins the stream hashes and digests.

WHAT THE GUARD ACTUALLY HAS TO BE, stated because it is easy to get backwards and a future reader will need it:
  * A genuine enum REORDER must produce NO digest change. The tags bind variant NAMES, not positions, so reordering is a no-op and nothing should fail. A test that failed on reorder would be asserting the bug.
  * An ADDED variant must fail to COMPILE, via the exhaustive match. It does.
  * A CHANGED TAG VALUE must fail the frozen goldens. This is the case that makes the tags durable rather than decorative, and it is the one I have not yet proven.

BLOCKED ON A PEER BUILD BREAK, not on design. crates/fln-hash/src/lib.rs:28 declares `pub mod benchmark;` with no such file (cod_1, under fln-9wya, in cc_3's crate; the orchestrator has told it to relocate and it is being reverted). fln-env depends on fln-hash, so nothing in this crate compiles and no test can run. I am not investigating or touching it, per instruction.

THE EXACT REMAINING STEP, one command once the tree builds:
  1. Seed: in environment.rs, change `DefinitionSafety::Safe => 1` to `=> 5` in definition_safety_tag.
  2. Run: cargo test --locked -p fln-env --lib
  3. Expect: the frozen-golden assertions fail (golden_digest and golden_root for the definition_safety/safe case, and the E2E producer's canonical_tag == production_tag assertion).
  4. Revert the seed and confirm green.
If they fail, this bead is closeable on existing evidence. If they DO NOT fail, that is a real finding — the goldens are not binding what they claim, and this bead becomes implementation work after all.
I attempted exactly this and reverted my seed the moment the build error appeared, rather than leave a deliberately wrong identity tag in a shared tree. git diff on crates/fln-env is empty; nothing of mine is in flight.

THE TAGGING DISCIPLINE THIS ESTABLISHES, for fln-amv.1 and fln-amv.2 to REUSE rather than each inventing its own — amv.12 is "what a digest must not bind implicitly" and those two are "what a digest must bind"; same question from two directions:
  1. Every enum reaching an identity digest gets an explicit const fn tag with an exhaustive match. Never `as u8`, never repr, never debug text.
  2. Guard the helper with #[forbid(clippy::as_conversions)] so the cast cannot come back silently.
  3. Freeze a golden per variant, not just a pairwise-distinctness check. Distinctness survives a coordinated renumbering; a golden does not.
  4. Keep an independent model of the WRONG encoder (CastAfterSourceReorder here) and assert the canonical digest differs from it — the both-directions rule that caught root.rs lying and that my alpha-digest work needed.
  5. State the three-way expectation explicitly (reorder = no change, add = compile error, retag = golden failure), because "add a test that fails on reorder" is the natural phrasing and it is wrong.

PROVEN BY CONSTRUCTION: an ADDED VARIANT fails to COMPILE. definition_safety_tag and quot_kind_tag are exhaustive const matches, so a new variant cannot reach a digest without someone assigning it a tag. That is stronger than a test.

CORRECT EXPECTATION FOR A REORDER, stated because the natural phrasing of this bead inverts it: a genuine enum reorder must produce NO digest change. The tags bind variant NAMES, not positions. A test that failed on reorder would be asserting the bug. The three-way guard is: reorder = no change, add = compile error, retag = golden failure. All three now hold.

THE HOLE THE PROOF FOUND — the class-level guard is incomplete. DeclarationTagCase::ALL is a HAND-MAINTAINED const array of 7 (environment.rs:514) and it is what the golden matrix, the mutant tests and the E2E producer all iterate. So a new variant is forced to get a TAG (the exhaustive match) but is NOT forced into the TEST MATRIX. Someone adding DefinitionSafety::Foo fixes the compile error in definition_safety_tag, ships, and the new variant has no golden, no pairwise-distinctness coverage, no E2E row, and no mutant — silently untested identity, which is this bead's own failure mode one level up.

That is exactly the "assert the full tag-to-variant mapping in one place so adding a variant without registering its tag fails" idea, and the current code does it for tags but not for coverage. The fix is small and I did not land it because I am out of working context to write and verify it properly: derive the matrix from an exhaustive match rather than a literal array, so the ONE place that must change on a new variant is the same place that fails to compile. Concretely, replace the hand-written ALL with a builder whose match over each enum is exhaustive, and assert ALL.len() equals the derived length. Then adding a variant breaks compilation until it is both tagged and covered.

I am NOT closing this bead on that basis. The two guards it names are proven, but the coverage hole means "add a variant" is only half-guarded, and closing would record a durability claim stronger than what holds.

THE TAGGING DISCIPLINE, for fln-amv.1 and fln-amv.2 to REUSE rather than each inventing one. amv.12 is what a digest must NOT bind implicitly; amv.1 (opaque mutual-block membership) and amv.2 (extension contracts in logical roots) are what a digest MUST bind. Same question from two sides, so one convention:
  1. Every enum reaching an identity digest gets an explicit const fn tag with an exhaustive match. Never `as u8`, never repr, never debug text.
  2. Guard the helper with #[forbid(clippy::as_conversions)] so a cast cannot return silently.
  3. Freeze a golden PER VARIANT, not just pairwise distinctness — distinctness survives a coordinated renumbering, a golden does not.
  4. Keep an independent model of the WRONG encoder and assert the canonical differs from it (CastAfterSourceReorder here). Both directions, the rule that caught root.rs lying.
  5. DERIVE the test matrix from an exhaustive match, never a hand-written array — this is the hole above, and amv.1/.2 will hit it the moment their variant sets grow.
  6. State the three-way expectation explicitly, because "a test that fails on reorder" asserts the bug.

PRECISION ON WHAT IS AND IS NOT COVERED, PLUS THE FIX DESIGN AND A CONCURRENCY STATEMENT (PeachBass/cc_1, 2026-07-25).

ALL THREE CASES ARE COVERED. I described this as "two of three" and that was imprecise, so to be exact:
  * REORDER -> no digest change. COVERED, and covered by DESIGN rather than by a test: the tags bind variant NAMES via an explicit match, so moving variants in the source cannot move a digest. There is nothing to assert here; a test that went red on reorder would be asserting the bug.
  * ADD a variant -> compile error. COVERED by the exhaustive const match in definition_safety_tag / quot_kind_tag. A new variant cannot reach a digest untagged.
  * RETAG (change a value) -> golden failure. COVERED and now PROVEN: seeding Safe 1 -> 5 turns three tests red, including the E2E producer. Reverted; tree clean.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY OUTSTANDING is not a fourth case but a COMPLETENESS GAP INSIDE THE ADD CASE. A new variant is forced to get a tag; it is NOT forced into DeclarationTagCase::ALL, the hand-written array of 7 at environment.rs:514 that the goldens, the pairwise-distinctness check, the mutant tests and the E2E producer all iterate. So the variant ships tagged but with no golden, no distinctness coverage, no E2E row and no mutant. Its identity is untested, which is this bead's own failure mode one level up — hence not closing on it.

THE FIX, designed so it is transcription rather than invention. Rust has no enum reflection, so the forcing function has to be an exhaustive match that GENERATES the matrix instead of one that merely validates it. The succ-chain idiom does this:

    const fn next_safety(s: DefinitionSafety) -> Option<DefinitionSafety> {
        match s {
            DefinitionSafety::Unsafe => Some(DefinitionSafety::Safe),
            DefinitionSafety::Safe   => Some(DefinitionSafety::Partial),
            DefinitionSafety::Partial => None,
        }
    }

Adding a variant fails to compile here until the author places it in the chain, and the chain is what BUILDS DeclarationTagCase::ALL — so tagging and covering become the same edit. Same shape for QuotKind. Keep an assertion that the generated length equals a frozen constant (7 today), so deliberately shortening the chain — the one way to satisfy the match while dropping a variant, e.g. writing `Foo => None` and orphaning Partial — still fails. That closes the loop: match forces registration, frozen count forces the chain to stay complete.

I have not landed it. It replaces a const array five test sites depend on, and I do not have the working context left to make that change and verify it properly. Recording the design so the next pane transcribes rather than re-derives.

CONCURRENCY, prompted by cc_2's Marrow audit closing a tri-state RC data race and a staging collision in region publication — both ownership-transition bugs. Stating fln-env's position explicitly rather than leaving it implicit:
  * The declaration-identity tag path is PURE. definition_safety_tag / quot_kind_tag are const fns over a value; decl_content_digest reads an immutable ConstantInfo. No shared mutable state, no ownership transition, nothing to race. declaration_identity_tag_is_stable_across_1_8_32_concurrent_complete_builds already exercises it at 1/8/32 workers and asserts one root.
  * The admission plan does NOT assume a single writer, deliberately. PreparedAdmission::commit revalidates the base binding immediately before publishing and returns ModuleGraphInconclusive::PlanSuperseded when the lineage moved underneath it (franken_lean-6sf3, commit 39b6465). That is precisely the ownership-transition case cc_2 hit, handled by detection rather than by assuming exclusivity.
  * The one place a single-writer assumption WOULD need stating is the term store's interner, which does not exist yet (franken_lean-oh1j). Whoever builds it should say explicitly whether interning is single-writer or shared, because "pointer equality IS structural equality" is exactly the invariant a concurrent inserter can break — two threads interning the same term concurrently must not produce two nodes. Noted on that bead.

THE SHARED TAGGING CONVENTION for fln-amv.1 and fln-amv.2 is in my previous comment (six points). Both beads should say they REUSE it rather than inventing their own: amv.12 fixes what a digest must not bind implicitly, amv.1 and amv.2 fix what it must bind explicitly, and three tagging disciplines in one crate is how the next f6br-class collision gets built.

title: fln-env: make adversarial full-hash collision handling resource-bounded
description:
Problem: a PMap full-hash collision leaf is a Vec. Looking up/removing a key is linear in collision cardinality, and persistent insertion clones the entire bucket, so constructing N distinct same-hash names is quadratic in comparisons and copied entries. Canonicalizing order in fln-amv.10 fixes determinism but not this denial-of-service/resource-accounting surface. Scope: after the canonical tie-break contract lands, replace large collision buckets with an immutable deterministic secondary structure or tiered representation that gives bounded/sublinear lookup and avoids whole-bucket copying per update while preserving O(1) snapshots, exact Eq semantics, canonical iteration, and small-bucket efficiency. Define promotion/demotion thresholds, secondary key identity, collision-of-secondary-key behavior, allocation/expanded-weight budgets, typed resource exhaustion, and structural-sharing rules; never reject a valid declaration merely because hashes collide. Verification requirements: model/property tests cover promotion, overwrite, remove, collapse, fork, equality, and iteration against BTreeMap for random and all-colliding keys; operation/allocation counters demonstrate non-quadratic 1k/10k collision-family construction and bounded snapshot cost; budget boundaries yield typed inconclusive/resource outcomes where the owning API provides budgets; deterministic permutations and thread partitions stay identical. Extend the shared environment E2E lane with detailed schema-versioned logs containing collision cardinality, representation tier, comparisons, allocations/shared nodes, budget, expected/actual order and roots, resources, and final state. Run fmt, all fln-env tests, clippy -D warnings, UBS, and every currently runnable environment integration check that does not require unfinished sibling slices; final fln-amv.11 and W2 aggregation remains downstream. No randomized secondary hash, collision rejection, global mutable table, or timing-only performance claim.

## Steps to Reproduce

Insert increasing families of distinct keys whose `key_hash` is identical while counting comparisons and copied bucket entries. The Vec collision leaf performs linear lookup and whole-bucket cloning per persistent update, yielding quadratic construction.

## Acceptance Criteria

Every scope, behavior, verification requirement, dependency, and prohibited shortcut above is mandatory. Closure requires the named deterministic unit/property/model coverage, the shared real-path E2E success plus negative/recovery scenario with detailed schema-versioned logs, all stated performance or evidence proofs, and green fmt/test/clippy/UBS and parent gates. No unclassified skip, mock-only evidence, partial implementation, or deferred listed feature satisfies this bead.
acceptance_criteria: Collision buckets use the deterministic tiered persistent representation without changing key, value, equality, or canonical iteration semantics: inline sorted storage contains at most 8 entries, the ninth distinct exact secondary key promotes, removal back to 8 demotes, and secondary identity is exact PKey ordering with no randomized or probabilistic hash. Insert, overwrite, lookup, remove, collapse, clone, fork, equality, and canonical iteration match independent BTreeMap and simple-vector models for ordinary, random, all-primary-colliding, and exact-key cases. Arc path-copying preserves O(1) snapshots and shares every unchanged map and collision node. Allocation, comparison, collision-cardinality, expanded-weight, and fresh-node budgets are preflighted deterministically; zero, one-under, exact, one-over, refusal, and recovery budget cases return typed nonpublication outcomes, never rejection or partial mutation, and exact expanded-weight totals cannot saturate or wrap into acceptance. Where the owning Environment operation exposes cancellation or InternalFault, its integration tests must prove the same nonpublication and recovery law without forcing cancellation state into the pure PMap API. Exact 1k and 10k all-collision construction and lookup counters prove the registered logarithmic or subquadratic bounds against the legacy N times N-minus-1 over 2 copy baseline, while timing is recorded only as diagnostic evidence. Deterministic insertion permutations, removals, thread partitions 1, 8, and 32, repeated runs, and platform lanes produce byte-identical canonical order, environment roots, recovery roots, diagnostics, and counters. Unit and property tests cover both promotion boundaries, overwrite without cardinality growth, every AVL rotation shape, demotion, root collapse, snapshot isolation, equality across tiers, clone and drop behavior, budget refusal atomicity, exact-bound recovery, and adversarial comparison or allocation accounting; named mutants that disable promotion or sharing, alter ordering, skip budget charging, saturate weight, lose refusal atomicity, or accept a wrong key are killed. The shared environment E2E emits exactly the disjoint fln.e2e.environment-resource-collision version 1 records for 1, 8, and 32 threads, with positive, planted inline-threshold mutant, exact byte-restoration, and clean recovery phases. Strict validation checks the complete field set and exact identities, orders, roots, cardinalities, tier and threshold facts, per-worker schedules, comparison and allocation bounds, shared and fresh nodes, budgets and resources, monotonic timings excluded from the gate, separate stdout and stderr artifacts, process result, cleanup, and final state; it rejects extra or missing fields, stale roots, over-bound counters, false atomicity, duplicate or malformed schedules, compile failures, unrelated or wrong assertions, merged streams, missing mutant marker, and surviving mutants. Retained manifest-backed bundles validate independently. scripts/check.sh, fmt, cargo check and test, all fln-env and relevant fln-hash or domain suites, clippy with warnings denied, UBS, the focused E2E positive-mutation-recovery lane and all currently runnable environment integration checks that do not require unfinished sibling slices are green with artifact paths recorded. Final fln-amv.11 and W2 aggregation remains downstream and is not a circular prerequisite for this child. No vector-sized update cloning, randomized secondary identity, timing-only claim, valid-key rejection, global mutable table, hidden Inconclusive promotion, mock-only evidence, unclassified skip, or deferred listed feature satisfies closure.
