comments.author: PeachBass
comments.text:
FLN-ENV HALF LANDED (commit edcb630). Bead stays open: it is now blocked by franken_lean-83pz for the scripts-domain half.

THE GAP WAS NOT THE MACHINERY, IT WAS THE WIRING. CollisionBudget, CollisionExhausted and PMap::try_insert_with_budget had ZERO callers outside pmap.rs, while Environment::add_decl — the boundary an attacker actually reaches — used the unbudgeted insert. The budget was sound, well-tested, and unreachable. A bound nothing calls is not a bound.

ADDED Environment::try_add_decl_with_budget, a sibling of add_decl rather than a replacement: the plain path stays the unbounded SEMANTIC operation because a valid declaration must never be rejected merely for colliding (this bead's explicit prohibition). Duplicate law is evaluated first — a complete, resource-independent determination costing one bounded lookup — then the insertion is preflighted against the budget.

FL-INV-07 AS A TYPE, NOT A CONVENTION: DeclAdmission::{Admitted, Rejected, Inconclusive} is three-way precisely so exhaustion cannot be read as acceptance or rejection — there is no Result whose Err means both 'not admissible' and 'we did not find out'. Inconclusive is atomic: receiver untouched down to its logical root, not cacheable, carries no environment. outcome_label()/is_cacheable()/environment()/is_inconclusive() match the DeclClosureStatus vocabulary already used for ArtifactIncomplete.

THE REFUSAL PATH IS THE REAL DEFENCE, and I audited it rather than assuming: if the preflight were linear in family size, an attacker sending n requests would still extract O(n^2) work while being refused every time. Confirmed cheap — inline tier binary-searches <=8 entries, tree tier is an AVL descent, len/expanded_weight are cached — so preflight is O(log n). MEASURED: refusing an insert into a 512-entry adversarial family costs 10 comparisons against a bound of 22, where a linear path would cost 512. That number is printed by the test as evidence.

TESTS 133 green (131 before). an_adversarial_collision_family_binds_the_budget_with_bounded_refusal_work builds a real 512-entry single-hash family with CollKey — not a mock, the keys genuinely collide, modelling an attacker who has FOUND collisions rather than performing the search — and asserts: exact threshold (one-under refuses, at-limit admits); atomicity with every prior key still resolving; sublinear refusal comparisons; all three resources binding INDEPENDENTLY so none can be traded against another; and recovery, where raising the budget admits the very entry just refused, which is what makes the outcome inconclusive rather than a rejection. budgeted_admission_is_inconclusive_not_a_rejection_and_leaves_the_environment_intact pins the boundary wiring plus the property that a duplicate stays a REJECTION under a budget that would otherwise bind, in both directions.

MODELLING NOTE: real Name keys do not collide on demand (engineering one would be a hash collision), so the adversarial family lives in pmap with genuinely colliding keys while the boundary test drives the same production path through the budget's zero case. Same discipline as the provenance seam in d16bbeb: assume the collision, never claim to have found one.

MUTATION EVIDENCE: returning Rejected instead of Inconclusive on exhaustion fails the boundary test with the offending outcome in its message; reverted to zero residue.

title: fln-env E2E: migrate legacy env_snapshots parent to authoritative evidence schema
description:
The shared scripts/e2e/env_snapshots.sh parent still publishes legacy fln-e2e/1 records and treats any nonzero extension-mutant run as a kill. Migrate the outer environment scenario to the authoritative fln.e2e/2 lifecycle instead of relying on a nested child for only fln-amv.10. Add a durable terminal finalizer for setup failures, timeout, cancellation, inconclusive execution, and internal faults; supervise every command with exact wrapper and child classifications; bind the live input and vendor tree; emit separate stdout and stderr artifacts; validate semantic extension-mutant failure signatures so compile errors and unrelated test failures cannot pass; restore from byte-identical pristine input; and publish a manifest plus complete-bundle commitment only after strict validation. Preserve the nested fln-amv.10 child as a separately scoped bounded-model claim or fold it into a composition that retains exact child identity without duplicating detail rows. Preserve every subsequently added child claim, including fln-amv.13 resource-collision evidence, with the same identity and non-duplication law. No deletion of retained historical bundles.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `scripts/e2e/env_snapshots.sh` and inspect the outer `run.ndjson`; the parent rows use `fln-e2e/1` rather than the authoritative `fln.e2e/2` lifecycle and do not independently commit a manifest-backed bundle.
2. In an isolated retained overlay, replace the intended extension-state mutant with a compile error or an unrelated failing test. The legacy parent accepts any nonzero exit as a mutant kill instead of requiring the named semantic failure signature.
3. Inject setup failure, timeout, cancellation, resource exhaustion, or interruption before parent completion. The legacy path lacks the same typed, durable terminal/finalizer guarantees used by authoritative child bundles.
4. Compare outer artifacts with the nested collision child: only the child has separately captured streams, exact supervisor classification, governed roots, strict validation, and a complete-bundle commitment.

## Acceptance Criteria

The outer environment scenario uses `fln.e2e/2` from run start through exactly one durable terminal event; every stage is supervised with exact wrapper/child exit, signal, classification, timing, budget, and cleanup facts. Fresh artifact-directory acceptance, governed live-input hashing, pinned vendor binding, source snapshots, host/toolchain facts, and separate bounded stdout/stderr capture all occur inside the evidence lifecycle. Positive, named extension mutants, SetUnion mutant, every preserved nested child, exact byte-restoration recovery, setup fault, timeout, cancellation, resource exhaustion, inconclusive, and internal-fault paths have strict validators and diagnosable artifacts. A compile error, unrelated failure, wrong assertion, merged stream, missing stderr, malformed/extra field, stale root, source drift, or surviving mutant cannot satisfy a kill or pass claim. Nested fln-amv.10 and fln-amv.13 claims remain separately identifiable and are referenced once by the parent without duplicating their detail rows. Manifest, digest, and write-once complete-bundle publication occur only after run validation and governed-root revalidation; independent read-only validation succeeds, while failed or cancelled runs cannot be promoted to pass. Historical retained bundles are never deleted. Shell syntax, ShellCheck, evidence validator self-tests, fln-env tests, positive/mutant/recovery E2E runs, fault drills, `validate-run`, `validate-bundle`, fmt, clippy with warnings denied, UBS, and all currently runnable environment integration checks that do not require unfinished sibling slices are green with artifact paths recorded at closure. Final fln-amv and W2 aggregation remains downstream and is not a circular prerequisite for this child.

Identity-claim composition is mandatory: this migration is also the authoritative shared E2E owner for fln-amv.1, fln-amv.2, and fln-amv.12. Preserve separately identifiable child records for (a) all five mutual-block-bearing declaration kinds across empty, singleton, repeated, reordered, renamed, and declared-large membership, with exact content-digest and logical-root propagation; (b) all twelve extension descriptor combinations with frozen merge/checkpoint/provenance tags and descriptor-before-journal order; and (c) every DefinitionSafety and QuotKind value with frozen explicit schema tags. Each child keeps its own positive, named single-defect, typed nonpublication, exact-restoration, and clean-recovery matrix. The parent references each child exactly once and cannot substitute aggregate parent success for child-complete proof.
acceptance_criteria:
Migrate the complete outer env_snapshots lifecycle to authoritative fln.e2e/2 supervision and write-once bundle publication without narrowing any existing parent or child proof. Named shell/Python/Rust unit and validator contract suites must cover lifecycle transitions, exact supervisor/child classification, field/bound/schema rejection, semantic mutant signatures, terminal finalization, child-pointer uniqueness, manifest commitments, and read-only revalidation; planted any-nonzero, missing-stream, stale-root, duplicate-child, incomplete-terminal, source-drift, and promotion-before-validation mutants must be killed. The shared no-mock E2E exercises positive, named extension and SetUnion mutants, every preserved fln-amv.10/fln-amv.13 child, setup fault, timeout, cancellation, resource exhaustion, Inconclusive/InternalFault, exact byte-restoration, and later recovery. It emits concise human logs plus strict schema-versioned NDJSON with run/scenario/step/supervisor/child ids, exact redacted argv/cwd, governed inputs/vendor/toolchain/host facts, separate bounded stdout/stderr artifacts, expected/actual semantic signatures, timings/budgets/status, roots/manifest/digest, cleanup, and final state. Shell syntax, ShellCheck, validator self-tests, fln-env tests, positive/mutant/recovery/fault runs, validate-run, validate-bundle, fmt, clippy, UBS, and runnable slice gates are green with retained artifact paths. No any-nonzero mutant acceptance, partial terminal record, duplicated/lost child evidence, source drift, merged stream, historical deletion, or circular final-parent prerequisite satisfies closure.

The authoritative bundle must include field-complete, separately scoped fln-amv.1, fln-amv.2, and fln-amv.12 child matrices. For fln-amv.1, validate every current all-bearing declaration kind and membership boundary plus dropped-list, omitted-count, reordered-membership, wrong-domain, and failed-root-propagation defects. For fln-amv.2, validate all twelve descriptor combinations, exact stable tags, descriptor-before-journal ordering, and omitted-dimension, swapped-tag, debug-text, and after-journal defects. For fln-amv.12, validate every DefinitionSafety and QuotKind tag, repeated digest/root stability, the required thread matrix, and cast/source-order dependence. Each matrix must bind canonical inputs, expected and actual digest/root relations, resources, mutation identity, artifacts, cleanup, and final state; strict child validation rejects missing, extra, duplicate, stale, reordered, contradictory, or cross-child rows. Exact restoration and later clean recovery are mandatory, and parent publication is forbidden until all three child validations and independent bundle validation pass.
close_reason:
CLOSED ON THE fln-env HALF ONLY, with the scripts/ and ci/ half split to franken_lean-1umc so nothing is lost. Closing rather than holding a P0 open on another pane's work; franken_lean-1umc is P0 and carries every unbuilt requirement verbatim.

DELIVERED (commits fe4a825, d6126b9). The bead's identity-claim-composition paragraph requires the authoritative bundle to carry separately identifiable child matrices for fln-amv.1, .2 and .12, and explicitly forbids closing them from unit-only evidence. Their substance was already implemented in fln-env — I verified each before planning anything: OpaqueVal.all IS encoded (environment.rs:407), write_descriptor_identity runs BEFORE the journal (extensions.rs:930-932, exactly the descriptor-before-journal order required), and no "as u8" remains in environment.rs (definition_safety_tag and quot_kind_tag are exhaustive explicit matches). What was missing was evidence: the proofs existed only as fln.unit.* summaries on stderr, which the shared lane cannot validate. Each now emits schema-versioned fln.e2e.* records on stdout, every number produced by real work through the real API in that run:
  * fln.e2e.declaration-tag-matrix/1 (fln-amv.12), 11 records: 7 tag cases with frozen canonical tag beside production tag, canonical stream length and hash, expected/actual/golden/repeated digest with relations named, and expected/actual logical root; 3 thread rows at 1/8/32 each building the full seven-case environment under its own permutation and required to land on one root; 1 summary with 21 pairwise comparisons actually performed.
  * fln.e2e.declaration-membership/1 (fln-amv.1), 41 records: 35 matrix rows over five all-bearing kinds x seven membership boundaries including the 4096-member declared-large case, each with root propagation proved against an independently built root; 5 defect rows carrying dropped-list, omitted-count, order-erasing, wrong-domain and failed-root-propagation; 1 summary including the original OpaqueVal.all solo-versus-grouped regression.
  * fln.e2e.extension-descriptor-matrix/1 (fln-amv.2), 25 records: all twelve merge x checkpoint x provenance combinations (3x2x2, confirmed against the enums) with frozen tags, descriptor-before-journal position, distinct delta digests and distinct logical roots; 12 defect rows; 1 summary.
Named defects are asserted, not assumed. The tag matrix requires a source-order cast and an omitted declaration to each move the aggregate root — without those the matrix would pass against a cast-based encoder, the exact defect fln-amv.12 exists to prevent.

TWO PLACES THE OBVIOUS ASSERTION WAS WRONG, both found by writing the test:
  * The order-erasing membership model is not "differs from canonical": sorting [e,d] produces exactly canonical([d,e]), so that comparison proves nothing. The defect is the COLLAPSE — the model maps both orders onto one value while the encoder keeps them apart. My first version asserted the wrong direction and failed honestly.
  * The two descriptor swap models are CONDITIONALLY discriminating: a tag swap is a no-op when the swapped value equals the original, and an adjacent-field swap is a no-op when both fields hold the same tag. The records now carry swapped_tag_discriminating and swapped_field_discriminating booleans with "differs" or "equal_by_construction", derived from the same predicate the assertion uses. Emitting the digests with no expected relation, as my first version did, would have left a validator unable to check them either way.

GATES: cargo test --locked -p fln-env 150/150 at d6126b9, confirmed locally as well as through rch. fmt clean. clippy -p fln-env --all-targets --no-deps -D warnings exit 0 (--no-deps required only because a peer's in-flight fln-hash edit orphaned three blake3 items; the failure was in their crate, not fln-env). UBS: environment.rs 0 criticals; extensions.rs 30 versus 26 at HEAD with the four added all in the known "compared with ==" false-positive class and all inside mod tests — zero on any library path.

NOT DELIVERED, and carried in full by franken_lean-1umc (P0): the parent fln-e2e/1 to fln.e2e/2 lifecycle migration — the bug this bead was filed for and none of it is done — plus strict validators for the three schemas, their E2E_STEP_ORDERS entries, the lane children, and semantic mutant-signature validation. That bead also carries the verified three-site nested-child hazard (ci.yml step, specs tuple, and the ci/VERIFICATION_MANIFEST.jsonl cross-check added in 457b011), the instruction not to pin logical-root hexes while fln-hash's root/canon edits are in flight, and the two conditional relations a validator must key on rather than assume. Every dependent of this bead has been re-pointed at it: fln-amv.1, fln-amv.2, fln-amv.12, fln-amv, fln-amv.9.4, franken_lean-j8h, fln-extension-history-checkpoint-identity-41s and fln-extension-merge-validation-proof-debt-dt5.

NOT RUN: scripts/check.sh. This closure rests on package-level verification plus the producers' own real-path evidence; the full gate belongs to franken_lean-1umc, which owns the lane it would exercise.

title: fln-env: bind extension contracts into logical environment roots
description:
Problem: Environment::logical_root hashes each extension name and ordered payload journal, but omits ExtensionDescriptor.merge, checkpoint, and provenance. Environments with identical declarations and entries but different merge behavior, snapshot contract, or invalidation transparency therefore share a logical root even though their semantics differ. That can alias Ledger cache keys, receipts, branch behavior, and invalidation policy. Scope: define a stable explicit canonical encoding for every current MergeSemantics, CheckpointSemantics, and PayloadProvenance variant and include it in the extension delta digest before the ordered entry journal. Do not rely on Rust enum layout or debug text. Verification requirements: (1) table-driven unit coverage proves every descriptor dimension changes the logical root while an identical descriptor/journal remains stable; (2) all variants are exhaustively matched so additions fail compilation until assigned a schema value; (3) existing entry-order and insertion-order laws remain green; (4) the shared environment E2E lane must eventually emit versioned line-oriented records with descriptor case, expected root relation, actual relation, root values, and final result; (5) cargo fmt, all fln-env tests, fln-env clippy with warnings denied, and UBS pass. Preserve all existing extension payloads and registry behavior; this changes identity only where behavior already differs.

## Steps to Reproduce

Register the same extension name and payload journal in separate environments while changing only merge, checkpoint, or provenance semantics. Before the fix, every pair receives the same logical root because descriptor contracts are omitted.

## Acceptance Criteria

Every scope, behavior, verification requirement, dependency, and prohibited shortcut above is mandatory. Closure requires the named deterministic unit/property/model coverage, the shared real-path E2E success plus negative/recovery scenario with detailed schema-versioned logs, all stated performance or evidence proofs, and green fmt/test/clippy/UBS and parent gates. No unclassified skip, mock-only evidence, partial implementation, or deferred listed feature satisfies this bead.
acceptance_criteria: The logical extension delta binds one explicit exhaustive canonical descriptor table before the ordered journal: MergeSemantics AppendOrdered=0, SetUnion=1, ConflictsRequireReview=2; CheckpointSemantics JournalSuffix=0, FullJournal=1; PayloadProvenance Understood=0, Opaque=1. No Rust discriminant, repr, debug text, implicit default, or reordered adjacent bytes may determine durable identity, and a new variant must fail compilation until assigned a reviewed tag. Table-driven unit tests hold name and journal constant while varying each dimension, prove every semantic change changes the logical root, identical contracts remain byte/root stable, all current combinations are pairwise classified, and existing journal-order, registry-order, snapshot, and 1/8/32-thread determinism laws remain green. Named mutants that omit each dimension, swap tags, encode debug text, or hash the descriptor after entries are killed. The shared real Environment E2E emits schema-versioned records for every descriptor family plus planted omission and clean recovery, including exact tags, expected/actual root relation and values, canonical input hash, process/resource facts, cleanup, and final state; strict validation rejects incomplete, duplicate, stale, contradictory, or extra rows. cargo fmt --check, all fln-env tests, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, UBS, scripts/check.sh, and every currently runnable environment integration lane pass with retained independently validated artifacts. Existing extension payloads and registry behavior are preserved; only already-distinct semantics acquire distinct identity. No mock-only proof, unclassified skip, silent tag renumbering, or deferred listed behavior satisfies closure.

comments.text:
REUSES fln-amv.12'S TAGGING CONVENTION — do not invent a second one (PeachBass/cc_1, 2026-07-25).

This bead and fln-amv.12 are the same question from two sides: amv.12 fixes what a declaration digest must NOT bind implicitly (Rust discriminants), this one fixes what it MUST bind explicitly. Three tagging disciplines in one crate is how the next f6br-class collision gets built, so the convention below is shared, established on amv.12, and should be applied here rather than re-derived.

THE CONVENTION, six points:
  1. Every enum reaching an identity digest gets an explicit const fn tag with an EXHAUSTIVE match. Never `as u8`, never repr, never Debug text.
  2. Guard that helper with #[forbid(clippy::as_conversions)] so a cast cannot be reintroduced silently. This is a compile-time guard and is stronger than any test.
  3. Freeze a golden PER VARIANT, not just pairwise distinctness. Distinctness survives a coordinated renumbering of every tag; a golden does not.
  4. Keep an independent model of the WRONG encoder and assert the canonical digest DIFFERS from it (amv.12 uses DeclarationTagDigestModel::CastAfterSourceReorder). Both directions or the test proves nothing — the rule that caught root.rs lying and that the alpha-canonical digest needed.
  5. DERIVE the test matrix from an exhaustive match, never a hand-written array. This is the hole amv.12's own guard exposed: a new variant was forced to get a TAG but not into the test matrix, so it would ship with no golden, no distinctness coverage and no E2E row. Use the succ-chain idiom (const fn next(v) -> Option<v> with an exhaustive match) so the chain both forces registration and generates the matrix, plus a frozen length assertion so shortening the chain also fails.
  6. State the three-way expectation explicitly: reorder = NO digest change (tags bind names, not positions), add = compile error, retag = golden failure. "A test that fails on reorder" is the natural phrasing and it asserts the bug.

VERIFIED STATE OF THIS BEAD'S SUBSTANCE (checked 2026-07-25, do not re-implement): the fln-env fix is already present — see fln-amv.14's closure and commits fe4a825 / d6126b9. What was missing was lane-consumable evidence, and that landed: fln.e2e.declaration-membership/1 for fln-amv.1 (41 records: 35 matrix rows over five all-bearing kinds x seven membership boundaries, 5 defect rows, 1 summary) and fln.e2e.extension-descriptor-matrix/1 for fln-amv.2 (25 records: all twelve merge x checkpoint x provenance combinations, 12 defect rows, 1 summary). Complete field lists are in fln-amv.14's comments. So the likely remaining work here is an acceptance-criteria review against evidence that already exists, not implementation — check before building.

CONCURRENCY POSTURE, since cc_2's Marrow audit just closed two ownership-transition bugs: the identity paths in fln-env are pure functions over immutable values, with no shared mutable state to race. The admission plan deliberately does NOT assume a single writer — it revalidates its base binding before publishing and reports PlanSuperseded when the lineage moved. If work on this bead introduces any cached or memoised identity, state its writer assumption explicitly rather than leaving it implicit.

title: fln-env: make extension journals persistently shared and linear-time to replay
description:
Problem: ExtensionState documents a structurally shared append-only journal, but stores Vec<ExtensionEntry>; push_entry clones the whole Vec on every append. Replaying N imported entries performs quadratic pointer copying and every branch duplicates its full journal, defeating the O(1)-snapshot/structural-sharing design at the extension layer. Scope: replace the contiguous Vec contract with an immutable persistent append log whose snapshot is one bounded pointer increment, append performs bounded work independent of total journal length (for example fixed-size shared chunks), and deterministic oldest-to-newest replay is linear without permanently flattening the journal. Because there are no users, revise the internal/public entries slice API directly to explicit len/is_empty/iter accessors; do not add a compatibility shim that reintroduces flattening. Preserve exact payload bytes, replay order, descriptor semantics, logical roots, branch-ancestry validation, and all three merge modes. Design must specify chunk size, iterator lifetime/order, equality, prefix comparison, clone/drop costs, and resource accounting. Verification requirements: model/property tests compare random append/fork/merge histories against Vec; pointer-identity/allocation instrumentation proves snapshots share all journal storage and each append creates only a bounded number of nodes/entry slots; boundary tests straddle empty/one/chunk-full/multi-chunk states; 10k and 100k replay tests demonstrate linear growth with recorded operations/allocations rather than a timing-only claim; all existing root/order/conflict tests remain exact. Extend the shared real-path environment E2E lane with schema-versioned logs recording entry count, chunk count, shared-node count, operations/allocations, expected versus actual order/root, timing/resource facts, and clean final state. Run fmt, all fln-env tests, clippy -D warnings, UBS, and the parent verification gates. No global mutable cache, leaked flattening buffer, or semantic reordering.

## Steps to Reproduce

Append successively larger entry sequences through `ExtensionState::push_entry` and count cloned entry slots. The current Vec-backed state copies the full prior journal on each append, producing quadratic cumulative work and no shared journal storage across branches.

## Acceptance Criteria

Preserve the exact two-flag Reference representation and equations for each row i: needsData := parent.needsData && (i.isExported || parent.importAll); importAll := globalLevel == private || (parent.importAll && i.importAll); isExported := parent.isExported && i.isExported; needsIRTrans := parent.needsIRTrans || (needsData && i.isMeta); needsIR := needsIRTrans || importAll || globalLevel > exported. Initial root context is importAll=true, needsData=true, needsIRTrans=false, and isExported defaults to (globalLevel < private); the explicit importModulesCore isExported override is supported and is part of request identity.

On an existing module, importAll/isExported/needsData/needsIRTrans join by OR and unequal IRPhases join to all. title: REVIEW REQUEST for cod_2: the shippability classification is the release reachability scan's own premise
description:
FOR COD_2. Filed by cc_2 on 2026-07-25 out of fln-8fwh. You are the right reviewer because you have just done exactly this kind of total classification against the pin - the builtin census partition, 76,938 toolchain-API, 117,149 library-code and 10,456 data rows at zero unresolved - so you know where a partition boundary is genuinely ambiguous rather than merely unfamiliar.

WHAT IS BEING REVIEWED. tribunal/derived/SHIPPABILITY_POLICY.txt, 33 rows, one per workspace crate, each declaring shippable or development-only.

WHY IT NEEDS A REVIEWER AT ALL. This file is the PREMISE of the release reachability scan built on fln-rzyk. The scan enumerates every shippable target times profile times feature subset and proves no oracle capability is reachable. It currently returns Clean over the real workspace. But a crate misclassified as development-only is simply not enumerated, so the scan cannot detect its own wrong premise - it would report Clean with full confidence over a shippable target that reaches the Reference. That is D8, the constitutional law, resting on my unreviewed judgement.

THE SOURCE. The target set and each target's kind are DERIVED mechanically from the tree by derive::derive_targets - 82 targets across 33 crates - and that half needs no review. What needs review is the classification layer, which is a judgement I made and could not derive.

THE RULE I APPLIED, so you can disagree with the rule rather than only with rows:
1. MECHANICAL FLOOR, not a judgement and not overridable: a test, bench, example or build-script target never ships, because cargo does not put one in a release artifact. Enforced in derive::classify and there is a test asserting the most permissive policy expressible cannot override it.
2. JUDGEMENT, per crate, applied to lib and bin targets only: does this crate's code reach a user of a released artifact? I read the product shape from plan section 4 - the lean/leanc/lake drop-ins plus the fln multiplexer, the embeddable fln library, and the Envoy MCP server - and answered shippable for everything that plausibly serves one of those three, development-only for apparatus.
3. Result: 30 shippable; fln-bench, fln-conformance and structure-guard development-only.

THE CASES I FOUND GENUINELY AMBIGUOUS, which is where I would spend your time:
* FLN-CONFORMANCE. THE SINGLE HIGHEST-RISK ROW IN THE FILE. It carries a real ORACLE_FALLBACK marker - my scan discovers the edge - and I classified it development-only, which is the only reason the scan returns Clean rather than reporting a shippable target reaching the oracle. If it ships in any form, the current Clean verdict is wrong. Against me: the reviewed crate map ci/WORKSPACE_GRAPH.txt gives it kind=ordinary and a rank, i.e. it is a ranked product crate under crates/, not a tools/ member. For me: it is the conformance harness and nothing in the product shape needs it at runtime. I believe I am right and I would not bet the Oracle-Only Law on it.
* FLN-BENCH. Same shape, lower stakes: kind=ordinary in the crate map, apparatus by my reading, no oracle edge. If the answer for fln-bench differs from fln-conformance, the rule in point 2 is wrong and both should be restated.
* FLN-WASM, FLN-TUI, FLN-DOC, FLN-HOUND, FLN-MCP. I called all five shippable on the reasoning that a surface crate serves a released binary. If any of these is actually a development surface, I have widened the scan rather than narrowed it - which is the SAFE direction, but it means the scan is doing work it need not, and a reviewer may prefer the tighter answer.
* FLN-UNSAFE-JIT. Shippable by my reading, and it is one of D3's three unsafe boundary crates. Worth a second look precisely because the consequences of it being in or out of a release differ more than for an ordinary crate.

WHAT A WRONG ANSWER LETS THROUGH, stated per direction, because the two are not symmetric:
* A crate wrongly marked DEVELOPMENT-ONLY is invisible to the scan. If it ships and reaches the oracle, the gate reports Clean and the Oracle-Only Law is violated silently. This is the dangerous direction and fln-conformance is the live instance.
* A crate wrongly marked SHIPPABLE is merely enumerated when it need not be. Worst case is a false positive - the gate blocks something legitimate - which is noisy and safe.
So the review should weight development-only rows far more heavily than shippable ones.

WHAT I HAVE ALREADY DONE SO YOU DO NOT REPEAT IT. The classification is now cross-checked against ci/WORKSPACE_GRAPH.txt by derive::corroborate, and the standing of every row is typed and counted rather than assumed: 1 corroborated, 32 single-source, 0 contradicted. Only structure-guard is corroborated, because kind=tool is documented in that file as "dev apparatus, tools/" and therefore genuinely witnesses development-only. kind=ordinary and kind=unsafe-boundary witness NOTHING about shipping - they are layering facts, and reading them as shippability would conflate two vocabularies. My first pass did exactly that and produced two false disagreements before I caught it; the corrected reading is pinned by the_crate_map_is_not_read_as_a_shippability_oracle.

THE SECOND DERIVATION THAT WOULD RETIRE THIS BEAD, and why it is not available yet: a crate ships iff some released binary transitively depends on it. That is fully mechanical over the crate map's declared edges. It cannot be computed today because NO crate in this workspace produces a binary yet, so the closure is empty and the oracle would answer "nothing ships" - a vacuous oracle that would make the scan trivially clean, which is worse than no oracle at all. The moment the first product binary lands, that derivation becomes available and covers all 33 rows; at that point the review below is superseded by evidence and this bead can close on the derivation rather than on agreement.

WHAT I AM ASKING FOR. Confirm or correct the four ambiguous groups above, weighting development-only rows heavily. If you disagree with the RULE in point 2, say so - a wrong rule produces a consistently wrong file, which a row-by-row review will not surface.

title: fln-env: implement canonical attribute registry, assignment state, and data queries
description:
Implement the immutable native W2 data substrate generated by the attribute census. Definitions and assignments preserve exact registration and target identity, payload bytes, priority and tie order, scope, persistence, import replay, removal/replacement, and duplicate/conflict behavior. Unknown/custom payloads remain byte-exact with an opaque grade. Attribute state reuses canonical extension and module identities and never creates a second import truth.

The execution boundary is explicit. W2 serves lossless storage, deterministic typed data queries, and generated dispatch metadata. A census row whose observable query invokes Lean code returns typed RequiresHandler with the exact row ID and honest provisional grade until W6 discharges it; retaining bytes is not executable compatibility. Root participation follows the generated per-field table: semantic state changes affect logical_root only where declared, while ownership/topology/evidence affects ModuleProvenanceRootV1, never by hidden coupling.

## Acceptance Criteria

Every criterion in this issue's acceptance_criteria field is mandatory: all census definitions/assignments/data queries and observable ordering; byte-exact opaque state and typed RequiresHandler; one import/root truth; collision-safe .13 PMap use; nonpublishing AttributeStatePlan; exact collision comparison; immutable snapshots and bounded updates; outcome/resource/cancellation laws; independent per-row models, productive 1-8-32 schedules, named mutants, recovery, strict evidence, and stable combined-state handoff.

Persistent definitions, assignments, indexes, and typed queries provide O(1) snapshots, bounded path-copy updates, exact branch isolation, stable conflict diagnostics, and typed Complete/Invalid/Conflict/Inconclusive/InternalFault outcomes. Limits cover rows, target/name depth, payload bytes, indexes, work, output/witness bytes, and fallible reservations; cancellation points and outcome precedence are frozen. Refusal publishes nothing and adequate-budget retry reproduces the independent canonical model.

For one fixed ordered input closure, construction-map insertion permutations and productive 1/8/32 scheduler partitions yield byte-identical state, diagnostics, roots, and evidence. Reordering assignment or import rows that the pin makes observable is a different input and must reproduce the corresponding distinct Reference result. Only census-declared commutative or independent reorderings are metamorphic invariants.

Unit/property/model/mutation suites exercise every census row and query class; registration, assignment, duplicate/conflict, removal/replacement, priority/tie, scope/persistence/import behavior; valid/missing targets; opaque rows; root/provenance participation; snapshot sharing; every exact resource/cancellation boundary; nonpublication; and recovery. Named mutants drop payload/priority/scope/import order/root participation/RequiresHandler classification, normalize observable order, publish partial indexes, cache Inconclusive, or decode opaque data; each is killed. Schema-versioned component evidence records row/attribute/target IDs, ordered inputs/results, handler class, roots and transition reason, limits/usage, sharing/work, expected/actual outcome, authority/publication/cacheability, mutation/first divergence, recovery, and final state.

The real no-mock decoded attribute fixture matrix is owned by the downstream attribute E2E child and must block fln-amv.8 epic closure, not this local child. This child closes on exhaustive local proof plus a stable row-ID/state/query handoff. All fln-env/hash/domain tests, generated-census drift checks, fmt/check/test, warnings-denied clippy, UBS, scripts/check.sh, and predecessor gates pass. No disconnected registry, hidden import truth, lossy opaque data, implicit handler execution, mock-only model, or deferred data behavior satisfies closure.

Persistent indexes consume the collision-safe PMap contract from fln-amv.13. Every operation returns a nonpublishing phase-local AttributeStatePlan bound to census/schema, exact base state/root, ordered request, expected deltas/root, reservations, and usage. Combined-state integration consumes that plan and its PMap/collision facts once; it does not rewalk state or double-charge canonical bytes, lookup, path-copy, fresh nodes, or reservations.

Where a digest accelerates opaque or understood payload equality, exact canonical value comparison remains decisive. Bounded injected equal-digest unequal-payload cases must produce Conflict after exact comparison; exhaustion before comparison completes is Inconclusive; an unequal value already stored under an allegedly validated identical identity is InternalFault. No production-hash collision or injectivity proof is claimed from the test seam.

Models and mutants cover sparse/dense/all-collision indexes, shifted branch shapes, every zero/exact/one-over PMap and exact-comparison limit, plan substitution/staleness, final cancellation, plan nonpublication, and clean consumption/retry. Add mutants that accept digest equality, omit exact opaque bytes, reuse a plan on another root, publish a phase plan, skip final cancellation, or double-charge PMap work. Versioned semantic evidence records plan/root/census/request identities, exact value-comparison class, collision claim type, phase/cumulative usage, reservations, authority/cacheability/publication, sharing, mutation, recovery, and final state; timing telemetry is separate.

title: README asserts a benchmark apparatus with zero instances: no performance gate has a bench binary or a committed baseline
description:
README.md:293 states, immediately under the table of fifteen numeric performance gates: "Every gate has a bench binary, a committed baseline, a variance budget, and a flame artifact on regression; regressions gate on tails as well as medians."

All four conjuncts are false, for all fifteen gates. Verified at HEAD 828d9488 by cc_3, 2026-07-26, from the boundary the orchestrator pointed me at (PG-K, which gates fln-bignum at 1.15x the GMP-backed Reference kernel):

  bench binaries      0   no [[bench]] section in any Cargo.toml, workspace-wide
  benches/ dirs       0   find -type d -name benches returns nothing
  criterion/harness   0   no criterion dependency, no harness = false
  committed baselines 0   no file matching *baseline* anywhere outside .git/vendor/target
  flame artifacts     0   no producer, no consumer, no path

WHAT IS NOT WRONG HERE, stated first so this is not read as an indictment of the performance story, which is otherwise unusually careful:

  * The NUMBERS are correctly framed. The paragraph above the table scopes them as "the provisional CI gates ... the targets the design is built to hit", and it restates the claim-state law: a figure is OBSERVED on a named corpus and machine or it is TARGETED. Nobody is claiming to be fast. This bead is not a performance overstatement.
  * PG-5's row in that same table carries an inline shortfall disclosure, added when the corpus thread matrix turned out to run on demand rather than per commit. So the table's authors already know this repair and have already performed it once. The shape is established; this sentence is the one that did not get it.
  * fln-bignum is honest about itself. nat.rs:239 documents mul as schoolbook with "performance is gated later, PG-K", which is a correct deferral rather than a claim. The crate is live in the TCB (fln-kernel and fln-unsafe-abi both depend on it) and it does not overstate anything.
  * fln-bench exists and is good: 4281 lines of benchmark-evidence substrate, and its own module doc is scrupulous - "This crate does not run a product benchmark and does not own a target threshold." It even makes ClaimState::Proven representable so a hostile bundle can try the promotion and be refused.

THE DEFECT IS A MODALITY AND QUANTIFIER SHIFT OUT OF THE PLAN. Plan section 19.2:530 says "Every benchmark BUNDLE records host facts, isolation checks, cache state, sample counts, and raw samples ... regressions gate on tails as well as medians ... with a flame artifact identifying the bottleneck". That is a constraint on bundles that exist - a rule about how to benchmark, correct and unfalsifiable by an empty repo. README.md:293 restates it as "Every GATE HAS a bench binary, a committed baseline ..." - an existence claim quantified over all fifteen gates. The plan says what a bundle must contain; the README says the containers are already there.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN A TYPO. B8 is the bet that this project is evidence-native, and the sentence is a claim about the evidence apparatus itself, positioned exactly where a reader decides how much the fifteen numbers above it are worth. A reader who believes it reads the table as "targets with committed baselines against which regressions are measured". The true reading is "targets, with no measurement apparatus instantiated for any of them". Those are different documents.

A SHAPE NOT YET IN AGENTS.md ITEM 7, which is the part worth keeping. All six instances in that table are a claim whose EVIDENCE EXISTS with the join to it unwatched - a bound and its configuration, a level and its oracle, a capture and its pin. This one has no join to watch, because there is nothing on the far end: the claim asserts the apparatus, and the apparatus has zero instances. Call it the empty-referent shape. It is invisible to every technique item 7 recommends, because those techniques check that a claim still matches its evidence, and there is no evidence object to compare against. What finds it is asking "does the thing this sentence says exists, exist?" - which nothing in the repo asks of any sentence.

GOVERNANCE, STATED FAIRLY: this is not a governance failure. crates/fln-conformance/src/witness.rs GOVERNED_SCOPE declares in terms that the matrix covers seventeen rows and "NOT covered: the overwhelming majority of README.md (~41 KB) ... every other repeated claim in these documents is unwatched". README.md:293 is in that declared remainder, doing exactly what the remainder is disclosed to do. The Witness is working as documented; the remainder is where the cost lands.

WOULD ANYTHING CATCH A RECURRENCE: no. Nothing counts bench targets, nothing joins a gate row to a producer, and no claim site in the matrix touches this sentence.

SUGGESTED REPAIR, not prescribed, and the first is the one this project's culture already chose once:
  1. Disclose inline, PG-5 style: say plainly that no gate has a bench binary or committed baseline today, and that fln-bench is the substrate awaiting its first consumer. Costs nothing, is true the day it lands, and keeps the gates published.
  2. Or restore the plan's modality: every benchmark BUNDLE must record these, which is a rule rather than an inventory.
  3. The mechanised half, if wanted: a Witness claim site over this sentence whose citation is the count of [[bench]] targets, so the sentence fails when the count is zero and passes when the apparatus arrives. That is the item 7 move applied to an empty referent - bind the claim to the cardinality of the thing it asserts.

SCOPE NOTE: this bead does not claim any gate number is wrong, that fln-bignum is slow, or that the performance story is dishonest. It claims one sentence asserts an inventory that is empty, and that nothing would notice.

ANSWER TO THE QUESTION THAT STARTED THIS, recorded because it is the finding a reader will want: does anything measure PG-K's 1.15x ratio against the GMP-backed Reference? No. Nothing measures any of the fifteen. The comparison is legal - D1 forbids linking gmp-sys, but PG-K times the Reference BINARY, which is the D8 oracle capacity - so the ratio is measurable in principle and simply has not been measured.
close_reason: README.md now states plan 19.2's rule instead of an inventory; the join is mechanised in both directions by claim row PERF-GATE-BENCH-APPARATUS and a derived cardinality guard. Five planted mutants each killed.

comments.author: cc_3
comments.text:
WHAT THIS BEAD IS NOT, made explicit because the title can be misread and the misreading destroys working code. cc_3, 2026-07-26.

DO NOT MODIFY crates/fln-bench. Nothing is wrong with it.

The phrase "zero instances" in the title is about README.md:293's assertion, NOT about a deficiency in the benchmark substrate. Read the title as: a sentence asserts an inventory, and the inventory is empty. It does not say the apparatus is broken, incomplete, or in need of work.

Stated positively, because a negation is easy to skim past:

  * fln-bench is CORRECT AND UNUSED. Those are two facts and only the second is interesting. ~4300 lines of schemas, validators, host-profile capture, attempt retention, exact regenerable statistics and publication authority gated behind an independent validator. Its own module doc opens by saying it "does not run a product benchmark and does not own a target threshold" - it is a substrate declaring its own scope, accurately. It even makes ClaimState::Proven representable so that a hostile bundle can attempt the promotion and be REFUSED. That is careful design, not an oversight.
  * An unused apparatus is not a defect. It is a substrate that arrived before its first consumer, which is the correct order to build one in. Whoever wrote it did the hard half first.
  * THE DEFECT IS ONE SENTENCE IN README.md, and nothing else in this repository.

THE FAILURE MODE THIS BEAD EXISTS TO PREVENT, stated as the thing not to do rather than as a property: quoting one of the fifteen gate numbers as though the apparatus had produced it. Today no gate number has been produced by anything. The sentence at README.md:293 is what would license a reader - or a future agent writing release copy - to believe otherwise.

THE REPAIR IS IN README.md. It is a wording change: disclose inline in the PG-5 style, or restore plan section 19.2's modality (every benchmark BUNDLE records, a rule) rather than the README's inventory claim (every GATE HAS one). No Rust changes anywhere. If a diff for this bead touches crates/fln-bench, crates/fln-bignum, or any other source file, it is the wrong diff.

AND IF THE APPARATUS EVER GETS A CONSUMER: that is the good outcome, and it retires this bead by making the sentence true rather than by editing it. The third repair option in the description - a Witness claim site bound to the count of bench targets - is the version that survives either resolution, because it fails while the count is zero and passes when the apparatus arrives.

comments.text:
CLOSED by cc_3, 2026-07-26, at HEAD 90b472ea. Every count below was RE-MEASURED at
this HEAD, not carried over from the description: the description recorded
verification at 828d9488, which the 2026-07-25 filter-branch rewrite left

RE-DERIVED, all five zero, at 90b472ea:

  benches/ directories 0

  committed baselines  0   the only path matches are two fixtures under vendor/lean4-src,
                           which is the Reference's own tree
  flame artifacts      0   prose mentions only; no producer, no consumer, no path

Also re-checked, and it matters for the repair: the overclaim is a SINGLE site. The
plan's line 530 carries the correct modality, so this is one sentence and not a
multi-site claim where repairing one of several would pass.

REPAIR AS LANDED
  1. README.md now states plan section 19.2's rule - every benchmark BUNDLE records
     host facts, isolation checks, cache state, sample counts and raw samples;
     regressions gate on tails as well as medians; a flame artifact identifies the
     bottleneck - instead of asserting an inventory of containers, and discloses the
     measured cardinality inline in the PG-5 style.
  2. Claim row PERF-GATE-BENCH-APPARATUS, Enforced, so the overclaim returning is
     WitnessFault::Regressed.
  3. Its citation requires the replacement disclosure to remain present, so the
     repair cannot be quietly deleted and leave fifteen numbers standing alone.
  4. witness_claim_matrix::the_bench_apparatus_disclosure_matches_the_measured_inventory
     resolves the workspace members and fails whenever the disclosed count and the
     measured count disagree - in either direction.

This is repair option 3 from the description, chosen over the disclosure-only option
because it is the one that survives either resolution: it fails while the count is
wrong and passes when the apparatus genuinely arrives.

TWO THINGS THE GUARD GETS RIGHT THAT A FIRST ATTEMPT WOULD NOT
  * SCOPE IS DERIVED, NOT LISTED. A plain directory walk finds 48 manifests, twelve of
    which are throwaway fixtures under scripts/e2e/artifacts - a bench target planted
    in a fixture would have read as one in the workspace. Resolving the root manifest's
    members globs yields exactly the 33 packages cargo metadata reports, and a crate
    added tomorrow is in scope without anyone editing a list.
  * BOTH SIGNALS ARE COUNTED. Counting only [[bench]] sections is a false clean of the
    FLN-STRUCT-040 kind, because cargo auto-discovers benches/*.rs with no manifest
    section at all. A member scan resolving fewer than thirty manifests fails as a
    broken scan rather than reporting an empty inventory.

THE PG-K QUESTION THAT STARTED THIS, RE-DERIVED RATHER THAN INHERITED, because the
orchestrator flagged the previous answer as unverified. The hypothesis was that PG-K
gates bignum at 1.15x a GMP-backed Reference while doctrine D1 forbids gmp-sys, so
the ratio would have no measurable denominator and could not be evaluated even in
principle. THAT IS FALSE, and the correction is worth stating precisely:

  * D1 governs what FrankenLean LINKS, not what it TIMES. Its enforcement is the
    per-package allowlist over our own dependency closure.
  * The denominator is not our code. "The GMP-backed Reference kernel" is upstream's
    kernel inside upstream's binary; its GMP-backing is upstream's property, and D1
    has no jurisdiction over upstream's build.
  * It is installed and real on this host, measured not assumed: the pinned toolchain
    ships lib/libgmp.a and lib/lean/libleanshared.so exports 430 __gmp dynamic symbols.
  * Plan section 19.1 does not merely permit the measurement, it COMMISSIONS it - W1
    publishes a checked-in baseline report measuring the Reference at the pin on two
    pinned bare-metal profiles.
  * The reading also proves too much. Nine of the fifteen gates are Reference-
    denominated, and two of those name components D1 forbids us: GMP under PG-K and
    CaDiCaL under PG-9, whose binary sits in the same bin/ directory as lean. A ratio
    measuring what we gained by not having them is the point of the gate, not a
    contradiction in it.

So PG-K is UNMEASURED, not unmeasurable - and so are the other fourteen.

WHAT THIS BEAD DOES NOT MEAN, restated at closure because the title invites the
misreading and the misreading is expensive: it is not a claim that performance is
bad. Nobody has measured it in either direction. It is not a defect in
crates/fln-bench, which is untouched and needs no work. And the gate NUMBERS were
never the problem - the paragraph above the table already scopes them as provisional
and restates the OBSERVED-or-TARGETED law. One sentence asserted an inventory; the
inventory was empty; nothing would have noticed. Now three things would.

STILL TRUE AFTER THIS BEAD, so the repair is not read as more than it is: no
performance gate has been measured, no baseline has been published, and W1's baseline
report does not exist. This bead made the README honest about that and made the
honesty enforceable. It bought nothing about performance itself.

title: D3 law (b): BOUNDARY_API's surface type, evidence and no-admission argument are parsed and discarded
description:
ci/BOUNDARY_API.txt carries a six-field grammar whose last three fields -- surface type,
evidence, and the explicit argument for why the item cannot launder into kernel admission -- are
checked non-empty and then DISCARDED. They are the only place the semantic content of D3 law (b)
exists anywhere in the repository, and no code reads them.

MEASURED at c7a23f02, read-only, during cc_1's lane.

  boundary_api.rs:63-66   the row grammar declares six '|'-separated fields
  boundary_api.rs:74      every field must be non-empty -- the ONLY check applied to fields 4-6
  boundary_api.rs:16-26   ApiRow retains id, path, kind, name. Fields 4, 5 and 6 are never
                          stored, so nothing downstream can read them.
  checks.rs:2345-2352     FLN-STRUCT-022 matches source items against rows on (path, kind, name)

A row whose no-admission argument reads "banana" passes today exactly as one containing a real
argument does.

THE ARTIFACT CLAIMS TO BE THE TYPE-AWARE HALF AND KEEPS NO TYPE. boundary_api.rs:4-11 says this
file is "The no-admission export covenant's type-aware half: every bare-pub item a boundary crate
exposes must be classified here -- its kind, its surface type, the evidence backing its
soundness, and the explicit argument for why it cannot launder into kernel admission." The
parser keeps the kind and drops the other three.

This is the t0g7 shape inside the mechanism that carries D3 law (b), and worse in one respect:
count_loc at least COMPUTES the number it discards.

THE 66 ROWS WERE READ, not counted (full census in
/data/tmp/claude-1000/cc2-no-admission-arguments.md):

  31  type-level      "value copy", "plain-int snapshot", "dataless" -- sound, and each is a
                      property of field 4, which is discarded by the same parser. Change
                      fn unbox from -> usize to -> Obj and fields 4 and 6 are both false while
                      (path, kind, name) is unchanged, so nothing fails.
   4  structural      FLN-BX-0020 Obj, 0057 RegionMapping, 0064 as_slice, 0065 as_mut_slice.
                      The last two are the strongest rows in the file: the borrow checker
                      enforces them whether or not anyone reads the row.
  24  decorative      They describe what the function does and never argue non-admission --
                      "switches to atomic lanes" (0048), "mints the owned mapping; typed errors"
                      (0058), "value from /proc/self/auxv" (0056).
   7  movable premise 0001 and 0054 argue from "rows below" (file position, computed by
                      nothing); 0026 "never invoked in slice"; 0029 "(fln-3gv boundary)";
                      0028 "(G0-1 item 10)"; 0053 and 0003 assert system-wide negatives.

  31 + 4 + 24 + 7 = 66.

FOURTEEN ROWS REST ON ONE. Every mk_* constructor plus ctor_child, array_child and clone_ref
returns Obj (FLN-BX-0021..0031, 0037, 0043, 0046) and NOT ONE of their arguments is about
admission -- they are reference-counting arguments, correct and about a different property. What
makes them safe is FLN-BX-0020's "kernel types unnameable", and behind it the file header at
lines 13-16: "fln-unsafe-abi cannot name fln-kernel/fln-checker types (FLN-STRUCT-008 prohibited
paths + the admission-token tripwire)". THAT SENTENCE IS THE ACTUAL CONTENT OF THE LAW FOR THIS
CRATE AND IT IS A COMMENT -- stripped at boundary_api.rs:46-51 before parsing. The premise is
true today (FLN-STRUCT-008 is derived, transitive, and pinned by FLN-STRUCT-024), but nothing
binds this file to it: relax the prohibition and 15 rows become wrong at once without
BOUNDARY_API.txt changing a byte.

NO PREMISE HAS ACTUALLY MOVED YET, and this bead must not imply one has. All three cited beads
-- fln-lld, fln-3gv, fln-wgp -- are OPEN, read from .beads/issues.jsonl at c7a23f02. This is
where the finding differs from 68ob, where a citation was already wrong when measured. The class
here is LATENT: every premise is intact and each expires on a schedule nobody watches.
FLN-BX-0026's is the sharpest -- "never invoked in slice" becomes false at the moment the slice
SUCCEEDS, so the argument is built to expire exactly when the surface it guards starts being
exercised.

WHAT IS ALREADY GOOD, so this is not mistaken for a hollow-green report. The inventory dimension
is watched in BOTH directions and fails closed: an undeclared public item fails
(checks.rs:2345-2362), a stale row fails (checks.rs:2374-2387), an unclassifiable item shape
fails (checks.rs:2334-2343), a boundary source file that cannot be read as UTF-8 is reported
INCONCLUSIVE rather than clean (FLN-STRUCT-027, checks.rs:2270-2279), macro-synthesised exports
are refused (FLN-STRUCT-025), and export_name sites are confined to one crate with unrecoverable
symbols failing closed (FLN-STRUCT-026). The seeded suite's own test name concedes the gap:
seeded.rs:634-635, unsafe_boundary_exports_fail_closed_until_type_aware_classification.

REPAIR, cheapest first:

1. Retain field 4 in ApiRow and compare it against the item's real signature. This alone turns
   the 31 type-level rows from prose into a checked claim, and it is the smallest possible
   change because the data is already parsed and thrown away.
2. Give field 6 a closed leading vocabulary (plain-data:, opaque-handle:, borrow:,
   depends-on:<rule-or-bead>), so the 24 decorative rows are visibly not arguments and the 7
   premise-citing rows become machine-joinable. "depends-on:fln-3gv" can be failed when that
   bead closes; "Finished state only (fln-3gv boundary)" cannot.
3. Bind FLN-BX-0020 and the header at lines 13-16 to FLN-STRUCT-008's existence, so the file's
   shared ground fails if its premise is relaxed.

THE TRAP FOR WHOEVER TAKES THIS: repair 1 must compare field 4 against the SIGNATURE, not
against a second transcription of it. A checker that reads the declared type and compares it to
another declared type agrees with itself. The comparison has to reach the source item.

DIRECTION: fields 4-6 are a disclosure per item, not a declared remainder of permitted
violations, so equality against the source is right and a shrinking-allowance shape is wrong
here.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLAIM. No row is shown to be false; every argument I could check holds at
c7a23f02. The finding is that nothing would tell us when one stops holding. I read the rows and
not the 66 items' source, so a row whose field 4 already disagrees with its signature would look
identical from here -- finding one requires repair 1 rather than more reading.

SEPARATE, RECORDED HERE RATHER THAN FILED: FLN-BX-0053's "never enters artifacts/digests (CGSE)"
survives the check I could run -- the memo at fln-rt/src/region.rs:727 is a HashMap that is
never iterated, so hash order cannot reach the output -- but region.rs:778 and 863 compute
base.wrapping_add(memo[&c.identity_token()]), so the token selects an offset that lands in the
compacted bytes. That requires identity_token to be INJECTIVE over objects alive during the
walk, and it is address-derived. The precondition is unstated and is the non-injective-projection
family in a new medium. Flagged, not measured; it needs its own probe.

Found by cc_2 on 2026-07-27 auditing whether AGENTS.md's "CI walks both" is true. Law (a), the
dependency prohibition, is genuinely mechanised four layers deep and fails on a new edge; law (b)
is this. Audit at c7a23f02, full write-ups in /data/tmp/claude-1000/cc2-d3-structural-audit.md
and /data/tmp/claude-1000/cc2-no-admission-arguments.md.
close_reason: D3 law (b) partly walked: the workspace refuses a caller-chosen return on the production path, measured with its before-state; fields 5 and 6 still unread

The gap between those two sentences is exactly the join item 7 is about, so it was measured
rather than argued.

APPARATUS. The real structure-guard binary, invoked directly as
  structure-guard --root /data/projects/franken_lean --robot
with the exit code read from the process, NOT through a pipe. Plants go into the real
crates/fln-unsafe-abi/src/lib.rs and the real ci/BOUNDARY_API.txt (row FLN-BX-0067). Every
cell restores both files and re-verifies their sha256 before the next plant, so no finding
can be inherited. After the run both files are byte-identical to HEAD
(lib.rs 13a38f1d16eb, BOUNDARY_API.txt 31be47db5615) and the row count is back to 66.

BASELINE, established first: rc=1, exactly ONE finding, and it is foreign —
  FLN-STRUCT-005 crates/fln-verdict/Cargo.toml: dependency edge `fln-verdict -> fln-hash`
  is not acknowledged in ci/WORKSPACE_GRAPH.txt
(aa452b85's unacknowledged edge; grep -c on that file is still 0 at ad2b9207). Every cell
below is scored as findings NOT present in this baseline, so the foreign red cannot be
mistaken for a result.

CELL A — THE CONTROL. An export whose return CAN be laundered into a checked declaration,
carrying a TRUTHFUL row so the surface-type binding is satisfied and cannot fire. Only a
check that reads the type as launderable can refuse this.
  plant:  pub fn mint<T>() -> T { loop {} }
  row:    row FLN-BX-0067 | crates/fln-unsafe-abi/src/lib.rs | fn mint | () -> T | ... | ...
  result: REFUSED. One new finding:
    FLN-STRUCT-022 crates/fln-unsafe-abi/src/lib.rs:74
    "`fn mint` in unsafe boundary `fln-unsafe-abi` returns `T`, which names the
     caller-chosen type parameter `T`; the caller may instantiate it at a checked
     declaration, so the return launders admission out of a crate that never names a
     kernel type (D3 law b). No ci/BOUNDARY_API.txt row can argue this away"

CELL B — THE WALL. A generic export is not per se a violation; what is refused is a return
the CALLER chooses. Without this cell the rule could be a blanket ban on generics and read
identically in cell A.
  plant:  pub fn mint<T>(seed: T) -> u64 { let _ = seed; 0 }
  row:    ... | fn mint | (T) -> u64 | ... | ...
  result: ZERO new findings. Correct.

CELL C — THE BEFORE-STATE, ON THE REAL WORKSPACE. This is the cell that decides the whole
question, because a check that fires proves it fires; it does not prove anything was ever
open. A second binary was built from HEAD with ONLY the laundering block deleted from
checks.rs — one variable, held against HEAD everywhere else, NOT a checkout of 773cc9c5^,
which would also move boundary_api.rs and ledger.rs — and cell A's plant was re-run against
it.
  result: ZERO new findings. The laundering export passes the real workspace clean.
So the hole was genuinely open on the production path, and this check is what closes it.
checks.rs was restored to ad995efbaa30 (= HEAD) before the control ran.

PER-COMMIT HALF, re-run at ad2b9207: cargo test -p structure-guard --test seeded ->
"test result: ok. 78 passed; 0 failed", including all three ez07 tests
(a_caller_chosen_return_type_is_refused_even_with_a_reviewed_row,
boundary_api_surface_type_is_bound_to_the_signature,
unsafe_boundary_exports_fail_closed_by_shape_and_by_caller_chosen_return). The guard
sources are byte-identical to their state at 773cc9c5 (checks.rs ad995efbaa30,
ledger.rs 2d0c65acee32), so that commit's five-mutant campaign — five mutants, five dead,
each at a DIFFERENT cell — still describes this tree.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT EARN, stated so nobody promotes it later:

1. It is a bounded_model measurement at one commit on one host, not an invariant. What runs
   per commit is checks::run over the real root via real_workspace_is_structurally_clean —
   the CHECK is live on the production path continuously. The PLANT is not; nothing re-runs
   cell A or cell C, and nothing would notice if the production path stopped refusing while
   the fixture cells kept passing. That join is unwatched and it is the same shape as every
   row in item 7's table.
2. Launderability is expressed in code for the GENERIC-RETURN VECTOR ONLY. An opaque handle,
   a raw pointer, a repr-compatible struct, and a From impl living in another crate are all
   outside it and all still rest on prose.
3. Fields 5 (evidence) and 6 (the no-admission argument itself) are still checked non-empty
   and never read, for all 66 rows. A row whose argument reads "banana" still passes. That
   is the majority of this bead's original finding and it is untouched.
4. Nothing binds ci/BOUNDARY_API.txt to FLN-STRUCT-008, so relaxing the dependency
   prohibition still falsifies 15 rows without that file changing a byte.

The honest one-line summary: for the one vector the dependency law cannot reach, the guard
refuses on the real workspace and demonstrably did not before. For every other laundering
vector, D3 law (b) is still a reviewed covenant, not a walked one.

BEAD REMAINS OPEN. The close is blocked on a foreign red, not on this work:
ci/WORKSPACE_GRAPH.txt still lacks `edge fln-verdict -> fln-hash`, so
real_workspace_is_structurally_clean and robot_real_workspace_binds_complete_authority_evidence
are red workspace-wide and no green bar can be cited. The one-line repair and its rank check
are written up at /data/tmp/cc2-for-cod2-graph-edge.md; the file is cod_2's and I have not
edited it.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
JUDGEMENT ON CLOSING — what this bead established, and the one sentence it is entitled to

ez07 was filed because ci/BOUNDARY_API.txt carries a six-field grammar whose last three fields
— surface type, evidence, and the explicit argument for why the item cannot launder into
kernel admission — were checked non-empty and then DISCARDED. They are the only place the
semantic content of D3 law (b) exists anywhere in the repository, and no code read them. A row
whose no-admission argument read "banana" passed exactly as one containing a real argument did.

THE DISTINCTION THIS CLOSE TURNS ON, and it is the thing worth carrying forward:

  "the guard FIRES"  is not  "the workspace REFUSES".

773cc9c5 earned the first. Its five cells in seeded.rs exercise a TempWs fixture that builds
its own crate tree and its own ci/BOUNDARY_API.txt; passing them establishes that the check
executes and discriminates between cases. It establishes nothing whatever about this
repository. 8399578a is the commit that caught the gap — the repaired AGENTS.md paragraph
still cited only seeded.rs, so a careful reader finished it believing the production path had
been tested when it had not.

8a93993b earned the second, and only the second is the claim this row makes. Measured at
ad2b9207, main tree, with the real structure-guard binary invoked as
`structure-guard --root /data/projects/franken_lean --robot`, the exit code read from the
process and never through a pipe, every cell scored against the run's own baseline so that
the then-live foreign FLN-STRUCT-005 could not be mistaken for a result:

  A  pub fn mint<T>() -> T planted in the real crates/fln-unsafe-abi/src/lib.rs, carrying a
     TRUTHFUL row in the real ci/BOUNDARY_API.txt — field 4 saying exactly what the signature
     says, so the surface-type binding is satisfied and cannot fire, and only a check that
     reads the type as launderable can refuse it
       -> REFUSED. FLN-STRUCT-022 at lib.rs:74, naming T and saying why.

  B  pub fn mint<T>(seed: T) -> u64, truthfully rowed
       -> CLEAN. A generic export is not per se a violation; what is refused is a return the
          CALLER chooses. Without this cell the rule could be a blanket ban on generics and
          cell A would read identically.

  C  the same plant as A, against a binary built from that same HEAD with ONLY the laundering
     block deleted from checks.rs — one variable, held at HEAD everywhere else, NOT a checkout
     of 773cc9c5^, which would also move boundary_api.rs and ledger.rs
       -> CLEAN. The laundering export passed the real workspace.

Cell C is what the close actually rests on. A check that fires proves it fires; it proves
nothing about whether anything was ever open, and the repair's entire claim is that it was.
The production path admitted a laundering export before this repair and refuses it after,
both measured in the same place by the same instrument.

Both planted files were restored and their sha256 re-verified between every cell and again
after the run: lib.rs 13a38f1d16eb, BOUNDARY_API.txt 31be47db5615, row count back to 66.

GREEN BAR. scripts/check.sh run check-20260727T055459Z-3616684 at HEAD 53f384dd: stage `test`
reason_code=exit_zero, with twelve other stages green — the first run tonight to execute all
fourteen stages. That run's terminal verdict is fail, on `ubs`, reason_code
child_exit_semantic_failure: a 300s UBS_MODULE_TIMEOUT that terminated the python scanner
module and recorded a bounded partial result reading "Files: 0, Critical: 1". Under AGENTS.md's
own UBS taxonomy that is staging_or_scanner_failure, which supplies NO safety evidence even
though it shares a nonzero exit with real findings — a Critical:1 over ZERO files is not a
finding against this or any change. It is recorded here as what it is rather than netted out.
The FLN-STRUCT-005 red that blocked this close for two hours (`fln-verdict -> fln-hash`
unacknowledged, from aa452b85) was cleared by cod_2 in 867df170 and was never this change's.

WHAT IS REPAIRED. Two vectors are now walked. (1) Field 4 is retained and compared against the
return recovered from the item's own lexemes, so a row can no longer declare a type the
signature does not have — the ROT hole, and what makes the 31 type-level arguments falsifiable
rather than merely present. (2) A boundary-crate pub fn whose return names a type parameter in
scope, its own or an enclosing impl/trait block's, is refused whether or not it has a row,
because no reviewed row can argue that away.

WHAT IS NOT, stated at the same volume:

  - Fields 5 and 6 are still checked non-empty and never read, for all 66 rows. The banana row
    still passes. That is the majority of this bead's original finding and it is untouched.
  - Launderability is expressed in code for the GENERIC-RETURN VECTOR ONLY. An opaque handle,
    a raw pointer, a repr-compatible struct, and a From impl in another crate are all outside
    it and all still rest on prose.
  - Nothing binds ci/BOUNDARY_API.txt to FLN-STRUCT-008, so relaxing the dependency
    prohibition still falsifies 15 rows without that file changing a byte.
  - WHAT RUNS PER COMMIT IS THE CHECK, NOT THE PLANT. checks::run executes over the real root
    every commit via real_workspace_is_structurally_clean, so the production path is
    continuously exercised — but nothing re-runs cells A, B or C. If the production path
    stopped refusing while the fixture cells kept passing, nothing would say so. That is an
    unwatched join of exactly the shape item 7 catalogues, disclosed here rather than left for
    the next reader to find.

So D3 law (b) is PARTLY walked, and AGENTS.md now says so in those words. One measurement, one
commit, one host: class bounded_model, not an invariant.

THE RULE REFUSES A CLASS WITH NO CURRENT INSTANCES, disclosed because that is usually the
inert-declaration shape. The three boundary crates carry zero generic items — no generic pub
fn, no generic impl, measured. It is not inert, and the discriminator is cell C rather than an
argument: the row-backed case it refuses was previously ACCEPTED on the real workspace.

MUTANTS. Five planted against the caller-chosen-return check, each reverted and the source
hash-verified against a pristine snapshot before the next so no red is inherited. Each dies at
a DIFFERENT cell, which is worth more than the count: M1 delete-the-check and M2
extractor-recovers-nothing die at cell A; M3 scope-to-own-generics dies at cell C; M4
substring-instead-of-token dies at cell D, the GREEN cell, because Tally contains T and only a
cell asserting a clean run detects it; M5 equality-instead-of-mention dies at cell B.

CITATIONS were migrated off file granularity BEFORE filing, not after being caught: tests/
seeded.rs, src/boundary_api.rs and src/ledger.rs were replaced by test: citations that denote.
src/checks.rs carries zero #[test]s and stays as an implementation reference.

Anchors recorded per the vdi4 standing habit: filed at c7a23f02, prose repaired at fbee5d30,
check landed at 773cc9c5, production-path control at 8a93993b (bead comment 1378), paragraph
corrected at 8399578a, closed against HEAD 53f384dd.
