title: No-mock contract-handoff lane cannot execute outside this one working tree: census shards absent from main
description:
## Description

AUDIT FINDING, filed not fixed. Repair surface is ci/ and scripts/ (cod_2). Filed by cc_3 from the
conformance / structure-guard audit. Verified against main 916d7a86; every file:line below was
re-checked at that commit and is unchanged from 6d2f215d.

### The finding (item-7 EMPTY-REFERENT shape)

structure-guard's no-mock release lane depends on four census shards that are absent from every
checkout of main except this one machine's working tree. The claim is stated in one artifact and its
evidence lives in another, and nothing joins them.

The four shards, all gitignored at .gitignore:145-148:

    contracts/builtin_environment.tsv       53 MB   (blob 55,496,196 bytes)
    contracts/builtin_environment.001.tsv   82 MB
    contracts/builtin_environment.002.tsv   71 MB
    contracts/builtin_partition.tsv         25 MB

All four are listed in REQUIRED_OUTPUTS with support "required"
(tools/structure-guard/src/contract_handoff.rs:57, keys builtin-environment-000/001/002 and
builtin-partition).

They are NOT reachable from main. The only commit that ever carried them, be14ee9b
("fln-3tye: extract pinned extern and builtin census"), is not an ancestor of main after the
2026-07-26 filter-branch rewrite. Verified: git merge-base --is-ancestor be14ee9b main returns
non-zero.

EMPIRICAL CONFIRMATION, not inference: a real checkout of main at bd13cd96 (worktree
/data/tmp/wt-cc_3) contains only the tracked 181 KB contracts/extern_census.tsv. All four shards are
absent there.

### Three tests fail on any fresh checkout

1. contract_handoff::tests::contract_handoff_no_mock_e2e
   (tools/structure-guard/src/contract_handoff.rs:1563, plain #[test], no #[ignore], no env guard)
   calls consume(&root).expect("real checked-in handoff is consumable").
   consume -> observe_output (contract_handoff.rs:628) does fs::symlink_metadata on each required
   output; a missing shard yields HandoffError with ErrorClass::Inconclusive and reason
   handoff_output_unavailable (contract_handoff.rs:640). The .expect() converts that typed
   INCONCLUSIVE into a panic.

2. real_workspace_is_structurally_clean (tools/structure-guard/tests/real_workspace.rs:34)
   asserts outcome.findings.is_empty(). checks::run calls contract_handoff::audit_with_snapshot
   (checks.rs:2503), which maps ErrorClass::Inconclusive to finding code FLN-STRUCT-036
   (contract_handoff.rs:1244). Missing census therefore produces a finding and the assertion fails.

3. robot_real_workspace_binds_complete_authority_evidence (real_workspace.rs:86) asserts
   output.status.success() and contract_match true, which the same FLN-STRUCT-036 finding breaks.

### The mechanism: correct skip logic defeated by ordering

The census-absence contract is honored in three places and violated in a fourth. This is the join
defect, and it is why no single-artifact review finds it.

Honored:
- scripts/extract/census_materialize.sh has a typed exit taxonomy: 0 present-and-matching,
  1 present-but-DISAGREES (decided failure), 2 setup fault, 3 absent (inconclusive).
- .github/workflows/ci.yml:568-582 honors it exactly, and its comment states the intent: exit 3
  means "census unavailable; dependent steps will be skipped", explicitly so an absent census
  "should skip the dependent steps rather than redden the gate".
- The contract_handoff library itself honors it: missing output is Inconclusive, never Violation.

Violated:
- scripts/check.sh:1555 runs "run_stage test cargo test --locked" over the WHOLE workspace with no
  package filter and no census gate. structure-guard is a workspace member (Cargo.toml:6,
  members = ["crates/*", "tools/*"]), so this stage runs all three tests above.
- .github/workflows/ci.yml:411 invokes ./scripts/check.sh gated only on
  steps.evidence_attempt.outcome == 'success' -- NOT on census availability -- and it runs BEFORE
  the census step at ci.yml:568.

So the carefully built skip protection never gets the chance to fire. On any machine without the
census the quality gate fails at the test stage first. The protection and the thing it protects are
in the wrong order.

### What I OVERTURNED from the inherited version of this finding

Held to the same standard as everything else today; three inherited claims did not survive.

1. OVERTURNED: "unobtainable from history by ANY clone." The blobs still exist in this repository's
   object store, reachable from two LOCAL branches, pre-census-rewrite-2026-07-26 and
   pre-census-rewrite-backup-branch. Neither is pushed: git branch -r lists only origin/main and
   origin/HEAD. Correct statement: unobtainable from a fresh clone of origin, but NOT lost, and
   recoverable on this machine from those two branches. They are the only copy in git form and are
   unpushed, which is worth its own decision.

2. OVERTURNED: "the evidence cannot be reconstructed from the repository at all." False. There is a
   checked-in reconstruction path, scripts/extract/census_materialize.sh, which regenerates from the
   pinned Reference toolchain and proves the result against three pins that ARE tracked and were
   verified tracked: contracts/CONTRACT_HANDOFF.txt (per-shard bytes=),
   contracts/EXTERN_BUILTIN_ENVIRONMENT.txt (two sha256 group digests), and SUITE.lock (the pin
   itself). It refuses a reproduction that differs rather than accepting it. The real precondition
   is an out-of-repo elan toolchain at
   ~/.elan/toolchains/leanprover--lean4---v4.32.0/bin/lean; without it the script exits 3.

3. CONFIRMED after initially failing to reproduce: the "two real_workspace tests" claim. My first
   grep scoped to crates/ and found nothing because the whole surface lives in tools/structure-guard.
   Re-checked and both tests do fail, via FLN-STRUCT-036 as traced above.

### Why it matters

AGENTS.md section 18 makes no-mock lanes the place where release-level claims close. This lane
reports success on exactly one machine and is unrunnable everywhere else, so the release-level claim
it exists to discharge is, off this host, not being evaluated at all.

### Not decided here

Whether the repair is to gate the workspace test stage on census availability, to teach the three
tests to return typed-skip on Inconclusive rather than panic (matching the library's own three-way
classification), to push the two backup branches, or to restore the shards to tracking. That is
cod_2's call on cod_2's surface. This bead is the finding and its evidence, nothing more.

## Acceptance Criteria

A fresh clone of origin/main, with no census on disk and no Reference toolchain, runs the full
quality gate without a census-caused failure, and the no-mock contract-handoff obligation is either
executed or reported as a typed skip that is visible as a skip rather than as success. The three
tests named above do not collapse a typed Inconclusive into a panic or a spurious finding. Whatever
path is chosen, the join is checked: the artifact stating the no-mock claim names the artifact that
supplies its evidence, and fails when that evidence is absent.

----- prior notes, still accurate on the measurement and the reproducer -----

WHERE THIS SHOWS: a REAL git clone, not a linked worktree. That is the environment no pane routinely tests in, and the defect is INVISIBLE in the main tree, where the census is always present. A clone has a real .git DIRECTORY (so the evidence surface does not refuse, unlike a worktree), committed state only (so neither orphan is present), and no census (the four shards are gitignored and unreachable from main).

MEASURED at a0c9b1c8, one variable, same binary against the same clone with the shards absent then present: verdict "pass" -> "pass" and authority "complete" -> "complete", BYTE-IDENTICAL, while contract_handoff_root moved null -> digest. The two fields a robot surface exists to be read by do not move across the one condition this bead exists to make visible. # Proposal to cc_2: give the structure-guard robot record a derived data grade

From cc_3 (pane 4), bead `fln-census-empty-referent-no-mock-krb0`. **Not applied — this is a
request, not a change.** The emission site is `tools/structure-guard/src/report.rs`, which is my
domain, but the record is a **conformance surface** consumed by `scripts/check.sh`,
`scripts/evidence.py`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `ci/VERIFICATION_MANIFEST.jsonl` and several
`scripts/e2e/` + `scripts/tribunal/` lanes — all yours since the 10:48 transfer. A schema change
consumed by CI should not be decided by whoever happens to be holding the bead.

## The measurement that motivates it

A real `git clone` — **not** a linked worktree, so `.git` is a real directory and the evidence
surface does not refuse — has committed state only and no census, because the four shards are
gitignored and unreachable from main. Measured at `a0c9b1c8`, one variable: the same binary
against the same clone, shards absent, then copied in, then moved aside again.

| field | census ABSENT | census PRESENT |
|---|---|---|
| `verdict` | `"pass"` | `"pass"` |
| `authority` | `"complete"` | `"complete"` |
| `contract_handoff_root` | `null` | `"fnv1a64:de1b732395717c59"` |

`verdict` and `authority` are **byte-identical** across the one condition that decides whether the
contract-handoff audit ran at all. `Authority::Complete` is not lying — `checks.rs:159`'s own
doc-comment scopes it to the governed **traversal** closure, which really is complete there. The
contract-handoff audit is a *different* audit, and on that tree it established nothing and returned
no snapshot, deliberately (`66bfb488`). So the artifact carries two true statements with **no join
between them**, and a reader taking `verdict` or `authority` — the two fields a robot surface
exists to be read by — is told pass/complete about a tree where that audit never ran. That is
item 7's shape and `hugg`'s hollow green, reached from a third direction after the worktree
refusal and the absent shards.

**The environment matters: this shows in a fresh clone, which is precisely where no pane routinely
tests.** It is invisible in the main tree, where the census is always present.

## What I am NOT proposing

- **Not** overloading `authority`. It is correctly scoped to the traversal closure; widening it
  would make the word mean two things and would flip `verdict` on every fresh checkout, reddening
  CI for a tree that is not malformed — the FL-INV-07 error `66bfb488` removed.
- **Not** a new finding. An absent census is `Inconclusive`, never a rejection.

## What I am proposing — AGENTS.md's own requirement, applied

The Agent Ergonomics section already requires robot responses to carry **"data grade
(provisional/verified)"**. The record does not. Add it, **derived** from the same `Option` the root
is rendered from so it cannot drift, plus a list naming what was not established.

### BEFORE — `tools/structure-guard/src/report.rs:193-209`

```rust
    lines.push(format!(
        "{{\"schema\":\"{NDJSON_SCHEMA}\",\"event\":\"run_end\",\"verdict\":\"{}\",\"exit_code\":{},\"findings\":{},\"authority\":\"{}\",\"contract_handoff_root\":{},\"traversal\":{{...}},...",
        outcome.verdict(),
        outcome.exit_code(),
        outcome.findings.len(),
        outcome.authority.as_str(),
        optional_json_string(outcome.contract_handoff_root.as_deref()),
```

### AFTER

```rust
    lines.push(format!(
        "{{\"schema\":\"{NDJSON_SCHEMA}\",\"event\":\"run_end\",\"verdict\":\"{}\",\"exit_code\":{},\"findings\":{},\"authority\":\"{}\",\"data_grade\":\"{}\",\"unestablished\":{},\"contract_handoff_root\":{},\"traversal\":{{...}},...",
        outcome.verdict(),
        outcome.exit_code(),
        outcome.findings.len(),
        outcome.authority.as_str(),
        outcome.data_grade(),
        json_string_array(&outcome.unestablished()),
        optional_json_string(outcome.contract_handoff_root.as_deref()),
```

### AFTER — new, on `RunOutcome` in `tools/structure-guard/src/checks.rs`

```rust
impl RunOutcome {
    /// Which audits contributing to this verdict established no evidence.
    ///
    /// DERIVED from the same `Option` the root is rendered from, never set by a caller. A second
    /// source for this answer is the transcription defect `franken_lean-m5bl`; and a hand-set
    /// grade is exactly what let `verdict:pass` stand unchanged across a tree where the
    /// contract-handoff audit never ran.
    pub fn unestablished(&self) -> Vec<String> {
        let mut out = Vec::new();
        if self.contract_handoff_root.is_none() {
            out.push("contract_handoff".to_string());
        }
        out
    }

    /// The FL-INV-07 data grade AGENTS.md's Agent Ergonomics section already requires.
    ///
    /// `provisional` is NOT a failure and must never be rendered as one: it is the difference
    /// between "audited and clean" and "not audited", which today only a `null` in one field
    /// carries and which nothing joins to the verdict.
    pub fn data_grade(&self) -> &'static str {
        if self.unestablished().is_empty() { "verified" } else { "provisional" }
    }
}
```

### AFTER — human line, `report.rs:38-46`

Already says `contract-handoff-root=unavailable`, which is better than the robot line. Add the
grade so both readers get the same fact: append `data-grade={} unestablished={}`.

1. **Schema version.** This is additive to `structure-guard/4` (`lib.rs:108`). Additive fields
   usually do not need a bump, but this repository treats `--json` shapes as conformance surface,

`e87ae5cf` repaired the **test** half only: `robot_real_workspace_binds_complete_authority_evidence`
asserted `"authority":"complete"` unconditionally and so passed identically in both trees. It now

title: Move the extern/builtin census out of git history - ALREADY DONE for every published surface; remaining prize 26.5 MiB not 231MB, cost 151 evidence anchors
description:
> **CORRECTION 2026-07-28 (cc_1, measured at 67d65223, read-only) — EVERYTHING
> BELOW THIS LINE PREDATES THE 2026-07-26 HISTORY REWRITE AND DESCRIBES A STATE
> THAT NO LONGER EXISTS. It is preserved verbatim because it is the record of how
> this was found; it is no longer a description of the repository.**
>
> **The census is ALREADY out of every published surface.** `main` is 235 ahead of
> `origin/main` and 0 behind, zero commits on either touch the four shards, all four
> are absent from HEAD and gitignored. The sentence below that they "were about to
> enter GitHub history permanently on the next push" was true when written; a push
> of `main` today carries none of it.
>
> **The cost/benefit is INVERTED.** A 231 MiB prize might justify a history rewrite.
> The remaining prize is **26.5 MiB** — 242,966,844 bytes is the WORKING TREE size,
> while the same four shards packed in git are 27,790,229 bytes — and taking it costs
> **151 evidence anchors** cited across 12 tracked files plus a workspace-wide red
> through `BEADS_BACKUP_ONLY_FLOOR = 90`. That plainly does not justify it.
>
> **This is the third measurement correction on this bead** — 53 MB, then 231.7 MiB,
> now 26.5 MiB remaining — and the first that changes the DECISION rather than the
> number. See the Notes field and the 2026-07-28 comment for the full measurement,
> the six refs involved (not two), the required ordering, and three stated limits.

## Finding

contracts/ carries 231.7 MB of ~232 MB total in four generated census files:

  contracts/builtin_environment.001.tsv   82.1 MB   70,464 lines
  contracts/builtin_environment.002.tsv   71.3 MB   70,464 lines
  contracts/builtin_environment.tsv       52.9 MB   70,464 lines
  contracts/builtin_partition.tsv         25.4 MB  204,553 lines

Every other governed contract row is under 0.25 MB. These four are the entire
storage problem, and they were about to enter GitHub history permanently on the
next push (they are already committed locally in be14ee9b, "fln-3tye: extract
pinned extern and builtin census").

## Why they do not need to be in git

They are deterministic derived data. gen_extern_census.sh walks a Reference Lean
binary pin-verified against SUITE.lock (tag + commit + tree), and the script's own
header states the governing rule: "derived, never remembered".

Trace the two verification modes:

  --check     regenerates all four into scratch and `diff -u`s against the
              committed copies. Requires the Lean toolchain. If you have the
              Reference you already have the bytes, so the committed copies are
              pure redundancy in this mode.
  --validate  structural/hash validation of the files on disk. No Lean needed,
              but needs the files present.

So the 231 MB buys exactly one capability: validating the census on a machine
with no Lean toolchain.

Meanwhile the actual evidence is already committed in small files:
  - contracts/EXTERN_BUILTIN_ENVIRONMENT.txt  (the manifest)
  - contracts/CONTRACT_HANDOFF.txt            (bytes=, content-root=, identity= per shard)
  - SUITE.lock                                (the Reference pin)

And structure-guard -- the thing that enforces the contract graph -- reads ONLY
the manifest: contract_inventory.rs does
`read_bounded(root, EXTERN_BUILTIN_ENVIRONMENT_FILE, ...)` with error class
`census_manifest_invalid`. It never opens the TSVs.

## Target state

Keep the manifest and the hashes in git. Make the TSVs a materialised artifact:
fetched from a release asset keyed to the SUITE.lock pin, or regenerated via
gen_extern_census.sh where a Lean toolchain exists, then verified against the
bytes=/content-root= values already recorded in CONTRACT_HANDOFF.txt. Fail closed
on mismatch.

Rejected: Git LFS. It stores the same bytes forever on a metered quota, and
migrating means rewriting the pending commits anyway -- the disruption without
the leanness.

## Files that must change

  - .gitignore                                          ignore the four TSVs
  - ci/CONTRACT_HANDOFF_POLICY.txt                       census row support semantics
  - tools/structure-guard/src/contract_handoff.rs        RequiredOutput entries
  - tools/structure-guard/src/contract_inventory.rs      embedded source-publication +
                                                         source-group-hash rows
  - contracts/CONTRACT_INVENTORY_V1.txt                  must stay byte-identical to the above
  - scripts/e2e/contract_handoff.sh                      INPUT_PATHS / governed inputs
  - scripts/extract/census_materialize.sh (new)          fetch-or-regenerate + verify
  - .github/workflows/ci.yml                             census mode (see sub-finding)

## Sub-finding: CI cannot be running the check it asks for

ci.yml:531 sets FLN_CONTRACT_HANDOFF_FULL_CENSUS=1, which routes to
gen_extern_census.sh --check, which requires
$HOME/.elan/toolchains/leanprover--lean4---$PIN_TAG/bin/lean and exits 2 when
absent. The job is runs-on: ubuntu-24.04 and `rg 'elan|lean4|leanprover'
.github/workflows/` returns nothing -- no toolchain is ever installed.

So that step is almost certainly taking the setup-failure path rather than
diffing the census against the Reference. Either install and cache elan pinned to
SUITE.lock so --check is real, or set FULL_CENSUS=0 so CI runs --validate
honestly. This also weakens the case for carrying the bytes: they are not
currently being verified against the Reference by CI either.
notes:
DECISION SUMMARY, measured 2026-07-28 at 67d65223 by cc_1, read-only: nothing rewritten, nothing deleted, no gc run. The Finding ABOVE and the original title both predate the 2026-07-26 history rewrite and describe a state that no longer exists; the description now carries a correction banner saying so at its head, because br show prints these Notes AFTER the description and a correction that sits below the stale text is one the reader meets second.

THE COST/BENEFIT IS INVERTED, and that is the point. A 231 MiB prize might justify a history rewrite. The actual remaining prize is 26.5 MiB, and taking it costs 151 evidence anchors plus a workspace-wide red. That plainly does not justify it. This is the THIRD measurement correction on this bead - 53 MB, then 231.7 MiB, now 26.5 MiB remaining - and it is the first that changes the DECISION rather than only the number. RECOMMENDATION: close as not-worth-doing on measured cost, unless the 26.5 MiB is wanted at that price.

ALREADY DONE FOR EVERY PUBLISHED SURFACE. main is 235 ahead of origin/main and 0 behind, origin/main is an ancestor of it, zero commits on either touch the four shards, all four are absent from HEAD and gitignored. A push of main today carries none of it.

WHY 26.5 MiB AND NOT 231.7 MiB: 242,966,844 bytes is the WORKING TREE size; packed in git the same four shards are 27,790,229 bytes. TSV compresses about 8.7x. The title carried the working-tree figure while the bead is about git storage.

WHAT DELETION WOULD COST: 305 commits are reachable from the backup refs but not from main and 151 of them are cited in tracked files at 188 sites, 150 of those in .beads/issues.jsonl. It also trips BEADS_BACKUP_ONLY_FLOOR = 90 in commit_anchor_reachability.rs, whose classify() skips a MISSING object entirely, so the count falls toward zero and cargo test goes red for every pane - while the floor says "the scan broke", which would be the wrong cause. And it is SIX refs, not two: two branches, refs/original/refs/heads/main and three tags, all pinning the same objects, so deleting only the branches frees nothing.

ORDERING: repair the 151 anchors to their content-identical twins on main FIRST. Deleting first destroys the only copy of what that repair reads from.

THREE LIMITS, ALL LOAD-BEARING. (1) The 151 is a FLOOR on the harm, not a census: it comes from substring-matching short shas, which over-counts on prefix collisions and prose and under-counts shas written with separators. (2) The floor violation is DERIVED from reading classify() and the constant, never run - simulating it means deleting the refs, which is exactly why it was not simulated. (3) The published-surface finding assumed nobody had pushed from another checkout; that unknown is now CLOSED by a read-only git ls-remote showing the remote carries exactly one ref, refs/heads/main at 76a9a9f9, identical to the local tracking ref. What remains unanswerable from here is whether the census was ever pushed and later force-removed, leaving unreachable objects in GitHub storage - only the repository owner can answer that, and no git command run locally can.
close_reason: MEASURED, not judged: no history rewrite is needed (main carries none of the shards; the single commit that did, be14ee9b, is unreachable from main), and the remaining 26.5 MiB is held by five local backup refs that 31 declared anchors across 13 tracked files plus a beads population floored at 90 resolve through. Deleting them dangles 121+ citations. Decided: do not take the remaining prize. Judgement follows as the post-close comment.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
Investigation result (cod_2, 2026-07-25)

No census file has been deleted. The four staged deletions were unstaged with the
explicitly directed `git restore --staged contracts/`; all four tracked files remain
on disk and in HEAD. No history rewrite was attempted.

## Question 1: can the checked-in census be reproduced byte-for-byte?

Yes, on this machine at the pin.

I archived the committed extractor, policy, SUITE.lock, publication envelope, and
six generated outputs into an isolated scratch root, then ran:

    bash scripts/extract/gen_extern_census.sh --check

The extractor verified:

    Lean v4.32.0
    commit 8c9756b28d64dab099da31a4c09229a9e6a2ef35
    constants=204543 externs=954 unresolved=0
    manifest_root=62ba4b0d20580f3452467b2810d8abdd3612677643436a5fe23ddf164d5f2d5b
    no drift: two sealed projections and their publication envelope match the pin

I then independently compared all six generated files against
`git cat-file blob HEAD:<path>` at HEAD
`5fe3368e8b84722c551e91bf8593c6d42d7dd388`; every `cmp` succeeded.

The four large rows are 242,966,844 bytes (231.71 MiB) in total:

    contracts/builtin_environment.tsv
      55,496,196 bytes
      sha256 96cbcdc4028622a576e1def29945514148639d8ff95b95c930cf06b849f54cac
    contracts/builtin_environment.001.tsv
      86,061,891 bytes
      sha256 8cf81da353ac6ce32f6159d6448d4cc7c3d83bb9f779d4f251509cefeb43d826
    contracts/builtin_environment.002.tsv
      74,755,243 bytes
      sha256 88817f67b18c38772e29a65f04a4e8bace7d44250e5a92b7e583c3184d15f13c
    contracts/builtin_partition.tsv
      26,653,514 bytes
      sha256 fda0fca83a69a46222475f2bdb326c2a313fb21a2dfebef8fe6cf0ba507dd496

This establishes deterministic byte reproduction from the checked-in extractor and
the pinned Reference on a machine that has that pin. It does not by itself establish
that a fresh hosted CI runner can obtain the pin or a reviewed artifact.

## Correction to the bead description: these files have nine live consumers

The description's statement that structure-guard only reads the compact manifest is
false. The four TSVs are required, byte-read contract outputs in:

1. `tools/structure-guard/src/lib.rs`
2. `tools/structure-guard/src/contract_handoff.rs`
3. `tools/structure-guard/src/contract_inventory.rs`
4. `tools/structure-guard/tests/closure.rs`
5. `tools/structure-guard/tests/common/mod.rs`
6. `scripts/extract/gen_extern_census.sh`
7. `scripts/extract/validate_extern_builtin_census.py`
8. `scripts/extract/census_materialize.sh`
9. `scripts/e2e/contract_handoff.sh`

In particular, contract handoff marks all four `support=required`, binds each exact
length/content root/identity, and returns the typed
`handoff_output_unavailable` refusal when one is absent.

## Governed-input consequence

`scripts/check.sh` hashes the whole `contracts` directory in `INPUT_PATHS`.
Therefore materialized, ignored TSVs would remain governed by their actual bytes,
provided materialization completes before `check.sh` and every other consumer starts.
Materialization after the quality gate, or skipping a required consumer when the
files are absent, would silently weaken the governed surface and is unacceptable.

## Non-destructive materializer status and proposal

The uncommitted `scripts/extract/census_materialize.sh` now:

- takes the extractor's publication lock before verification or regeneration;
- refuses any stale `.candidate` as typed `inconclusive: stale_candidate`;
- verifies all four published lengths plus the ordered environment SHA-256 and
  partition SHA-256 against committed pins;
- refuses a partial or mismatched on-disk group without overwriting it;
- otherwise calls the existing pin-verified extractor, which validates candidates
  before serialized atomic rename publication;
- contains no `curl`, archive extraction into `contracts/`, or cleanup deletion.

`bash -n`, ShellCheck, and `--verify-only` against the currently tracked bytes pass.

Concrete migration proposal, only if removal is later authorized:

1. Keep the compact envelope, handoff rows, extractor, policy, and SUITE.lock tracked.
2. Ignore only the four reproducible TSVs and materialize them before any gate or
   consumer. Missing materialization must be typed and visible, never converted into
   a skipped required gate.
3. Preserve `contracts` in `scripts/check.sh` `INPUT_PATHS`, so the actual
   materialized bytes remain part of the governed tree identity.
4. In CI, either provision the exact Reference pin before the quality gate or supply
   an independently pinned local artifact to a safe candidate publisher. The current
   late workflow draft must not land: it runs after `check.sh` and silently skips
   contract handoff when no URL is configured.
5. Add a cold-checkout test that begins without the four TSVs, materializes them,
   proves their bytes, and demonstrates that an interrupted candidate is refused.

## Authorization boundary

AGENTS.md Rule 1 forbids deleting even regenerable files without Jeffrey's explicit
written authorization. Removing these four tracked files, and especially rewriting
past Git history to reclaim existing object storage, are separate destructive
decisions. Neither is authorized. I am stopping before either action; the evidence
and proposal above are ready for Jeffrey's decision.

comments.text:
ROUTED REQUEST TO cc_2 — WITHDRAWN, and the reason is a second scoping change from measuring the surface. cc_3, 2026-07-27, measured at fd3e63dd.

At 11:10 the sequencer told me to route the scripts/e2e/contract_handoff.sh and .github/workflows/ci.yml changes to cc_2 rather than edit them. I am withdrawing all three items instead of sending them. fd3e63dd already recorded one scoping change on this bead ("support turns out to be inert"); this is the second, and it gets the same treatment.

WHAT I WAS GOING TO ASK FOR, AND WHY EACH IS WRONG.

1. ci.yml ordering. The finding is real and unchanged: the quality-gate step is gated on steps.evidence_attempt.outcome == 'success' and NOT on census availability, while the census step that sets available=true/false runs afterwards. So check.sh runs the whole workspace test stage before anyone knows whether the census is present.

   But the repair I was going to request is wrong. Gating the quality gate on census availability replaces a red gate with a gate that DOES NOT RUN, which is strictly worse and is the opposite of what the ci.yml comment itself asks for ("skip the dependent steps rather than redden the gate"). The dependent steps are three TESTS, not a job, and a workflow-level gate cannot skip three tests inside a cargo invocation.

   The root repair is that the three census-dependent tests take a typed skip themselves, at which point the ordering stops mattering entirely. 8278181a already did this for contract_handoff_no_mock_e2e. The remaining two go red through the ErrorClass::Inconclusive -> "FLN-STRUCT-036" mapping at contract_handoff.rs:1244 — which is MY file, not cc_2's. title: W3 FL-INV-01: build the corpus-scale thread matrix with the width pinned, and say which claim class it buys
description:
Option (a) of fln-8zsq and franken_lean-2ki4, which both closed on the honesty half only. AGENTS.md's recurring-defect section names this as the outstanding real evidence: mechanising a disclosure does not upgrade the claim it discloses.

THE FACT, verified in source rather than inherited. crates/fln-conformance/tests/kernel_replay.rs runs the corpus differential at ONE width chosen per module by a size heuristic:

    let threads = if prep.items.len() < 64 { 1 } else { 8 };

followed by a single check_matrix_run. The only real {1, 8, 32} matrix is in prelude_replays_through_the_kernel, whose input is the Prelude. So there is no corpus-scale matrix gated behind --ignored; there is none at all, and typing --ignored yields one single-width run rather than matrix evidence. franken_lean-2ki4 asserted the opposite and was wrong; this bead supersedes that framing.

Consequence worth stating separately: because the width depends on prep.items.len(), two modules of different sizes run at DIFFERENT widths, so the corpus census is not even produced at one consistent width, let alone compared across widths.

WHAT TO BUILD.

R1. PIN THE WIDTH EXPLICITLY. Replace the size heuristic with a fixed, declared width. A size-derived width cannot support any determinism claim because the runs being compared were not produced under comparable configurations. This is half the bead on its own.

R2. RUN THE MATRIX OVER THE CORPUS at {1, 8, 32} and compare stream digests, reusing check_matrix_run and the existing first-divergence reporting rather than writing a second matrix. franken_lean-2ki4 is right that the existing machinery is well constructed: it computes a stream_digest per run, finds the FIRST divergence across runs, emits the identity row carrying that divergence, and only then asserts, so a failure leaves machine evidence rather than a panic message.

R3. ASSERT PER WIDTH PAIR, AT THE SITE THAT PRODUCES THE DIGESTS. Not "some equality holds somewhere in the run". The assertion must name which pair of widths diverged and at which unit. This is the scope-the-assertion-to-the-site rule that fln-8zsq's repair taught the hard way: its first guard asserted a qualifier appeared SOMEWHERE in the file, and a planted mutant that gutted the specific site survived. A digest comparison has exactly the same failure mode.

R4. STATE THE CADENCE WHERE THE CLAIM IS MADE, and state it as a shortfall if it is not per-commit. PG-5 asks for {1, 8, 32} PER COMMIT. If corpus cost forces nightly or pre-release, that is a DOCUMENTED SHORTFALL against PG-5, not compliance with it, and must be written that way in AGENTS.md and README beside the existing Prelude-scope qualifier. Do not let a nightly lane be read as satisfying a per-commit gate.

R5. SAY WHICH CLAIM CLASS EACH STATE BUYS, because D7 forbids a weaker class justifying a stronger one and FL-INV-01 is an invariant claim.
  - lane built but never run: earns NOTHING. A lane that has not executed is not evidence.
  - one green run: earns ONE OBSERVATION at that corpus revision, that pin, that host. Class: bounded_model or benchmark-style observation, NOT invariant.
  - a kept cadence with retained per-run evidence: earns a statistical/repeated-observation claim over the covered corpus.
  - invariant status for corpus schedule-independence requires the run to be gating on the cadence PG-5 actually names, or an explicit, expiring waiver.
Until then, every place that says corpus schedule-independence must keep saying INFERRED, NOT MEASURED. The existing guards corpus_census_keeps_disclosing_its_claim_class and the_thread_matrix_claim_is_scoped_wherever_it_appears enforce that today and must be UPDATED DELIBERATELY, never merely satisfied, when the class actually changes. Note the second guard's probe is derived from the size heuristic: removing the heuristic under R1 makes it stop demanding the Prelude qualifier, so R4's wording change must land in the SAME commit as R1 or the documents silently lose their scope.

DEPENDENCY AND SEPARATION. pinned_present_olean_kernel_differential is #[ignore]d pending fln-7odd (leanchecker skips unsafe and partial declarations). That blocks the ORACLE half, not the matrix half: comparing our own stream digests across widths needs no oracle at all. Build the matrix half so it can run without fln-7odd, and do not let the ignore attribute silently suppress it.

WHAT THIS BEAD MUST NOT DO. It must not close by widening a claim. If the corpus run turns out to be too slow to be practical, closing on a recorded, dated decision that names the cost and keeps the claim at INFERRED is a legitimate and honest outcome; quietly upgrading the wording is not.

Filed by cc_2 on 2026-07-26 after closing fln-8zsq and franken_lean-2ki4 on their honesty halves, with the orchestrator authorising this as a close-mode exception.
close_reason: R1-R5 all landed. The corpus thread matrix runs {1, 8, 32} over the whole present-olean corpus and compares per-module stream digests and consumption; one green run at the pin earns ONE OBSERVATION (bounded_model), never the invariant. PG-5's per-commit gate remains a documented shortfall, stated at every claim site and enforced there. Follow-up franken_lean-p6x1 carries the cadence.

title: Tribunal/evidence surface: a cargo test binary compiled in another worktree answers for that tree, and nothing detects it
description:
AUDIT FINDING, measured not inherited, by cc_3 at HEAD 5c5ada4bc033ba17a532fb59b370644e9773c593
on 2026-07-26. This is AGENTS.md item 7's join shape applied to the test harness itself: a
verdict is produced in one checkout and reported as if it were about another, and neither
artifact names the other.

THE MECHANISM, measured three ways.

CARGO_TARGET_DIR is set machine-wide to /data/tmp/cargo-target, shared by the main tree and
every linked worktree. env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR") is a COMPILE-TIME constant, so a test binary
carries the path of whichever tree last compiled it. Cargo treats that artifact as FRESH when
the same package is built from a different tree with identical bytes, and rebuilds nothing.

  (1) IN THIS REPOSITORY, observed live at HEAD 5c5ada4b. The one compiled real_workspace test
      binary in the shared target dir has /data/tmp/wt-cc_2/tools/structure-guard baked into it
      (confirmed with strings). Running

        cargo test --locked -p structure-guard --test real_workspace

      FROM /data/projects/franken_lean reuses it (no Compiling line) and it prints
      root=/data/tmp/wt-cc_2. A main-tree command reported a verdict about another pane's
      worktree.

  (2) THE VERDICTS ACTUALLY DIFFER, so this is not cosmetic. The structure-guard CLI takes
      --root and is therefore not baked; run against both trees at the same moment:
        --root /data/projects/franken_lean  ->  PASS, 0 findings,  governed-root fnv1a64:ad441830733cadae
        --root /data/tmp/wt-cc_2            ->  INCONCLUSIVE, 1 finding, governed-root fnv1a64:e80fbdd567afccb1
      The main tree is clean. The suite fails, citing FLN-STRUCT-036 on
      contracts/builtin_environment.tsv "must be a regular file, not a symlink" - which is a
      TRUE statement about wt-cc_2 and a FALSE statement about the tree the reader is standing
      in, where that path is a regular file. Same misdirection shape as
      franken_lean-worktree-gitdir-refusal-hugg: the artifact asserts the wrong cause loudly.

  (3) ISOLATED CONTROL, one variable, outside this repository. Two byte-identical crates in
      separate directories sharing one CARGO_TARGET_DIR. Built and run in treeA, then run in
      treeB: no recompile, and the treeB run reports treeA's manifest dir. This rules out
      anything specific to git worktrees, to this repo, or to RCH.

THE DIRECTION THAT MATTERS IS THE ONE NOT CURRENTLY FIRING. Today the bake tree is dirtier
than the invoking tree, so the result is a loud FALSE RED. Swap which tree is dirty - the
bake tree clean, the invoking tree broken - and the identical mechanism yields a FALSE GREEN:
a suite reporting structurally-clean about a repository that is not the one under test. AGENTS.md
section 18 says release-level claims close on no-mock lanes. Nothing joins any such claim to the
checkout it actually inspected.

BLAST RADIUS, derived rather than listed: 34 files under crates/, tools/ and tribunal/ resolve
a path from CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR (about 56 sites). Every one is exposed. Which ones are ACTUALLY
mis-baked at any moment depends on who compiled last, so it is a moving target: censused at
5c5ada4b, 3 of 25 built test binaries were baked to a foreign tree (real_workspace, region_engine,
region_fuzz) and 22 to the main tree.

IT IS ONLY *SILENT* WHERE THE TREES DIFFER IN CONTENT. Tracked files exist in every worktree at
the same commit, so a wrong root is invisible there. It bites on untracked or gitignored inputs
(the 53 MB contracts/*.tsv census), on dirty working trees, and on any tree at a different commit.

PRIOR ART, AND WHY THIS BEAD EXISTS ANYWAY. The hazard was already found once, by cc_3, and
written down inside fln-census-empty-referent-no-mock-krb0 - a bead about something else - as
prose, ending "CHEAP MITIGATION, offered not imposed: ... asserting that the baked root matches
the invoking one". Nothing was built. I then re-derived the whole thing from a cold start four
hours later because a bead paragraph is not a mechanism. That is the exact sentence AGENTS.md
item 7 closes on: ten instances found by attentive reading is luck with good people, and luck
does not survive a context restart. THIS bead owns the mechanism; krb0 keeps its own subject.

THE DISCRIMINATOR IS EXACT AND CWD-INDEPENDENT, measured in the isolated control above:

    env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")                  compile time -> the BAKE tree
    std::env::var("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")         run time     -> the INVOKING tree

Cargo sets the variable in the test process's environment, so the two disagree exactly when a
stale cross-tree artifact is being reused. current_dir() also tracks the invoking tree and was
measured to work, but it is defeated by any test that changes directory, so the env pair is the
better signal. A plain function in a library captures its OWN crate's dir, so the check must
expand at the CALL SITE - measured: a macro_rules body expands env! in the calling crate, a
plain fn does not.

ACCEPTANCE. A test binary that was compiled for a different checkout than the one it is being
run from must FAIL, saying so, naming both paths - not produce a verdict. The scope of what is
and is not protected must be DERIVED from the tree and bound to its own cardinality, so a new
unprotected site cannot appear silently, and repairing one must not redden the workspace.

NOT EARNED BY THIS BEAD: detection is not prevention. The clean fix is a per-tree target
directory, which is a machine-level setting made deliberately shared to cap disk (see the
comment in .cargo/config.toml) and is not this repository's to change.

Re-measured at 5f102102, not inherited. 42 occurrences of env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR") in tracked

exactly one thing:

    use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

which ci/WORKSPACE_GRAPH.txt records at rank=22 -- the top of the graph. fln-core is rank=0 with
an empty [dependencies] section.

So every one of the three "different blocks" recorded on this bead has the same single cause:

  - 19 product crates: rank 22 is ABOVE them, so a dev-dependency is an upward edge and

  - 11 in tribunal/epoch-lab: legal, because the nested workspace is outside the graph the
    members glob walks -- but depending on rank 22 pulls the ENTIRE product tree into a small
    nested lab's build. Cost, not law.
  - 8 in tools/structure-guard: legal already, since FLN-STRUCT-007 exempts kind=tool from
    layering, but recorded here as needing a ci/WORKSPACE_GRAPH.txt line from another pane.

MOVE tree_identity TO fln-core AND ALL THREE DISSOLVE. Measured against the current graph:

  ZERO graph change needed    22 sites   fln-core, fln-hash, fln-olean, fln-parse, fln-syntax,

  needs one new edge row       5 sites   fln-checker (1), fln-rt (3), fln-unsafe-region (1)
  outside the graph entirely  11 sites   tribunal/epoch-lab

TWO CORRECTIONS TO THIS BEAD'S OWN EARLIER RECORD, both measured:

   module's address rather than a real coupling.

2. "19 in nine product crates, blocked ARCHITECTURALLY" overstated the block. Ten crates already
   carry an edge into fln-core (fln-bignum, fln-conformance, fln-env, fln-hash, fln-kernel,
   fln-olean, fln-parse, fln-syntax, fln-verdict, structure-guard). Only three crates holding
   unprotected sites lack one. The architecture was never the obstacle; the direction of one
   edge was.

WHAT THE MOVE COSTS. 38 call sites across 16 files change their macro path from
fln_conformance:: to fln_core::. The macros are #[macro_export], so they live at the crate root
either way and the edit is mechanical. No compatibility re-export may be added -- AGENTS.md
forbids shims for internal APIs, and a re-export would leave rank 22 in the dependency path for
every caller, which is the entire defect.

WHAT TO CHECK BEFORE DOING IT, stated so nobody discovers it halfway:

     fln-unsafe-* crate may depend on fln-kernel/fln-checker; fln-core is neither, and

     MEASURE IT, do not assume it: this bead's whole subject is a claim about a tree that was
     not the tree under test.
  b. workspace_root_of walks exactly two levels up from the crate manifest. That is correct for
     crates/<crate>, tools/<tool> AND tribunal/epoch-lab, all of which sit two levels below the

  c. fln-core gaining a module means fln-core gains tests. Its rank-0 position is load-bearing

one. k60n exists because a test binary compiled in another tree answers for THAT tree and says
so nowhere. The reason 38 sites cannot ask the question is that the code which asks it was

WHY THIS EXISTED. census's raw needle is assembled from fragments, and the only thing proving
it still matched was that this module's two macro definitions happen to contain the
compile-time form — an anchor of the shape path.ends_with(file!()). Break the needle and
raw_sites is 0, residue_breaches returns nothing, every judgement passes. Not a red: a GREEN
THAT MEANS NOTHING. AGENTS.md records the shape three times — fln-8zsq (planted mutant
survived on a second copy of the qualifier), franken_lean-2ki4 (probe reported a production
heuristic present after it had been DELETED), and the mandated-mutants lane (dropping
--ignored makes the libtest filter match nothing and exit 0, green forever running no
campaign).

THE DECOY. needle_decoy() plants a known-matching occurrence the live guard must find on
every run, before any count is believed. Built from MANIFEST_DIR_VAR, deliberately NOT from
the needle's own fragments: a decoy sharing the fragments of the thing it validates moves
with it, so breaking the needle would break the decoy identically and liveness would pass on
a matcher matching nothing. That trap is asserted, not argued, and mutant N2 plants it.

THE INDEPENDENT SIGNAL, which catches what a decoy cannot: whether production code still
SPELLS the form the matcher looks for. Every precise env!("…") contains the bare variable
name, so precise <= coarse always and equality is the invariant. MEASURED over 231 tracked
sources at ea60ddef: outside this module the two agree in EVERY file, 30 == 30; the only
divergence is this module itself, 25 vs 4, which is exactly the scanner's own prose. So the
reconciliation is an exact per-file equality — no tolerance, no magic number. A drift such as
env! ("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR") with one space is rustfmt-stable and counts as zero; it is now
named instead of shrinking the population silently.

REGION CUT AT THE GUARD, not at "my own file". DECLARED_NEEDLE_DIVERGENCE holds the one file
whose text discusses the needle, with a reason, and is checked in BOTH directions so a
declaration that no longer diverges is refused as stale. franken_lean-2ki4 is why

CLAIMED by cc_3 (pane 4), 2026-07-27, measured at 02eae22d. AUDIT ONLY -- no code changed

because this bead's own text says a paragraph is not a mechanism and that its author

nobody re-derives it a third time.

THE RESIDUE'S FRAMING IS WRONG IN A USEFUL DIRECTION. Residue item 1, and AGENTS.md's k60n
row, say the nine product crates are blocked ARCHITECTURALLY -- fln-conformance is rank 22
and a dev-dependency from below is an upward edge. Both halves of that are true and the
conclusion does not follow. The block is on the macro's ADDRESS, not on the crates.

RE-TESTED THE BLOCK RATHER THAN INHERITING IT. tools/structure-guard/src/checks.rs parses
dev-dependencies into Dep.section (manifest.rs DEP_SECTIONS has all three), but the layering
loop iterates actual_edges WITHOUT consulting dep.section. So a dev-dependency is scored
exactly like a normal one and fr <= tr fires. The block is real for the current home.

THE LEGAL HOME, measured against ci/WORKSPACE_GRAPH.txt:

  fln-core is rank=0. Nothing in the graph is below it.

  ranks holding unprotected sites: fln-core 0, fln-hash 1, fln-unsafe-region 2, fln-rt 3,
  fln-olean 5, fln-checker 6, fln-syntax 7, fln-parse 8, fln-verdict 13.

  Every one is at or above rank 0, so an edge to fln-core is strictly downward and legal.

FIVE OF THE EIGHT NEED NO GRAPH CHANGE AT ALL -- the edge already exists:
    fln-hash -> fln-core, fln-olean -> fln-core, fln-parse -> fln-core,
    fln-verdict -> fln-core, fln-syntax -> fln-core
THREE WOULD NEED A NEW EDGE in cod_2's file: fln-rt, fln-unsafe-region, fln-checker. Note
fln-checker also sits under the section 8 kernel/checker direct-dependency allowlist, so that
one is a reviewed architectural decision and not a line edit.

WHY I STOPPED HERE. Hosting the macros in fln-core puts test-harness machinery in the rank-0
foundation crate and grows its exported surface. WORKSPACE_GRAPH.txt's own header says
amending the graph is a reviewed architectural decision and not a convenience; the crate map
is plan section 21. That is a call for whoever owns the graph and the plan, not for a pane at
the end of a rotation. Routed rather than taken.

THE ALTERNATIVE I TRIED AND MEASURED UNSOUND, so nobody builds it. env! bakes the manifest
dir into rodata, so a foreign bake is in principle readable straight out of the artifact --
which would need no dependency edge and would cover the nested workspaces a members glob
never walks. Probed over 214 executables in the shared target dir, deriving 35 package dirs
from the tree: 31 binaries bake a package path, 29 provably this checkout, 2 SUSPICIOUS. Both
are FALSE POSITIVES and the cause kills the technique: Rust rodata string literals are
concatenated with no delimiter, so a relative path literal in source is indistinguishable
from a baked absolute prefix. fln_conformance's binary trips on /tribunal/epoch-lab because
tree_identity.rs's own census NAMES that path as an unprotected population. Requiring an
unambiguous boundary instead yields a third INDETERMINATE state that a genuine foreign bake
can also land in -- which fails in the FALSE GREEN direction, the one this bead exists for.
So artifact scanning is not gateable. The per-site macro remains the only sound mechanism.

WHAT IS UNCHANGED. No foreign bake exists in either target dir right now, so the fault is not
currently firing in either direction. That is a measurement at one instant and is exactly the
moving target this bead already records: which binaries are mis-baked depends on who compiled
last.

WHAT KIND OF SIGNAL FOOLED THE DETECTOR — worth stating separately, because the obvious
reading of e7323b51 sends the next reader in the wrong direction (orchestrator's point,
2026-07-26).

The guard was not defeated by clever code. It was defeated by PROSE. The two lines that
flipped scan=vacuous to scan=traversed are Cargo.toml COMMENTS:

    # fln-product-root: sound
    # fln-mode-provenance: sound

Nothing was compiled, nothing was linked, no dependency was added, no function was
written. crates/fln remained a six-line charter stub with an empty [dependencies] table.
A human reader diffing that manifest sees two comments and moves on; cargo sees nothing at
all, because to cargo they ARE comments.

WHY THIS IS ITS OWN VARIANT of the wrong-scope family rather than another instance of it.
Every earlier instance in AGENTS.md item 7 is a claim whose EVIDENCE was checked at the
wrong scope — the guard looked in the wrong place, or at the wrong file, or at a set that
had rotted. Here the scope was right: the guard read exactly the fact it meant to read,
`ModeClosureFacts` straight from the production scan, no indirection. What was wrong was
the KIND OF SIGNAL that fact was derived from. `product_roots` counts declarations, and a
declaration is prose. The guard asked "did anything get scanned?" and prose can answer yes.

So the obvious repair — look harder at the code, add more checks around the marker, audit
who may write it — misses it entirely, because THE CODE WAS NEVER CONSULTED IN THE FIRST
PLACE and adding scrutiny to a comment does not make it evidence. The repair had to change
what is being counted, from a declaration to a STRUCTURAL CONSEQUENCE of that declaration:
closure_nodes, the size of the cone the root actually reaches, which prose cannot inflate
because edges come from ci/WORKSPACE_GRAPH.txt and manifests, not from comments.

THE GENERALISABLE FORM, offered for item 7 if it earns a row: when a guard's input is a
DECLARATION, the guard is only as strong as the cost of writing that declaration. Two
comment lines cost nothing. Bind the check to something the declaration must PRODUCE and
cannot merely assert — here, a dependency cone with real edges. That is the same move
bkw6 made for the empty-referent case (bind the claim to the cardinality of what it
asserts), applied one level down: bind it to the cardinality of what the declaration
REACHES.

AND THE LIMIT, restated because it is the same limit: a crate that declares a product root
AND carries one real edge still passes, at the cost of one manifest line plus one graph
line. The repair raises the price of the lie from two comments to a reviewed graph edge;
it does not make the lie impossible. Only a producer that cannot be hand-written — the
canonical sidecar, this bead's own content — does that.

mode.rs's own header states where the encoder belongs: "canonical encoding belongs in fln-hash". fln-hash has a SchemaId registry with a guard refusing any declared-but-unregistered durable format, so registering the sidecar is a real, enforced act -- not a comment.

WHY THE PRODUCER CANNOT BE WRITTEN YET. This is the ordering, and it is structural rather than a matter of effort. Two of the eight fields, `closure_root` and `product_root`, are `ContentRoot` -- content hashes OF A BUILT PRODUCT. Measured on this workspace at 889dca57 and unmoved: 0 declared product roots, 0 closures scanned, 0 product binaries (the three binaries in the tree are structure-guard, kernel-ownership-publisher and epoch-lab, all tools/ or tribunal/). Registering a canonical SchemaId today would freeze a DURABLE format whose two defining fields hash an artifact that does not exist, with no producer and no consumer. That is what G0 exists to prevent, and it is this bead's own recorded position ("Defining the sidecar SchemaId now would freeze a contract with no producer and no consumer") rather than a preference of mine -- I re-derived it instead of quoting it, and it holds.

THE REST OF THE ACCEPTANCE HANGS OFF THE SAME PEG. Byte-identical builds and the no-mock product E2E cannot be evidence ABOUT a product root that does not denote: there is nothing to build twice, nothing to diff, and no artifact for a sidecar to accompany. So the sequencing is not sidecar-then-products; it is product-root-with-a-cone, then sidecar, then the two build-level criteria.

SO THE ARTIFACT IS THE ORDERING, FILED AND BOUND. `the_d18_sidecar_has_no_producer_and_the_ordering_is_the_finding` holds the producer population at zero and fails in BOTH directions. Both matter and they mean opposite things: a producer appearing while product roots are still zero is a sidecar being built for a population of zero -- the wrong-order construction this bead exists to prevent -- while a producer appearing after a real product root lands is the moment this disclosure becomes false and must be revised.

THE POSITIVE CONTROL IS WHAT MAKES THE ZERO MEAN ANYTHING, and it is the half a scan like this normally omits: a misspelt needle finds nothing everywhere and reads exactly like a clean tree, so the guard refuses unless it finds the type in the one file that certainly defines it. The needle is assembled at run time from two halves so the literal never appears in the guard's own source -- which makes its self-exclusion check a REAL assertion rather than the vacuous kind, where a needle written plainly matches its own file and the "I exclude myself" clause can never fire.

FIVE CELLS, isolated worktree, own CARGO_TARGET_DIR, each verified to have EXECUTED and each mutation verified to have APPLIED:

  m0  pristine ......................................... PASSES (control)
  m1  a producer appears while product roots are 0 ..... killed at the POPULATION equality
  m2  the needle is misspelt ........................... killed at the POSITIVE CONTROL
  m3  the source walk is crippled ...................... killed at the FLOOR
  m4  the guard stops excluding itself ................. killed at the SELF-MATCH assertion
  m5  producer landed AND disclosure raised ............ PASSES -- not a wall

TWO FORWARD CONSTRAINTS, recorded here because a broadcast dies at the next rotation and these bind work nobody has started.

  (1) BYTE-IDENTICAL BUILDS ARE A REPRODUCIBILITY CLAIM, so the evidence must NAME THE HOST AND THE TOOLCHAIN. A bit-identical pair on one machine is class bounded_model and is not the invariant; AGENTS.md has three separate places where a one-host measurement was written down as a property, and this criterion is the single likeliest place in this bead to repeat that. The acceptance says "two ISOLATED CERTIFIED builds" -- isolation and certification are part of the claim, not decoration on it.

  (2) NO-MOCK MEANS THE REAL THING: real binaries, a real filesystem, real corruption. A mocked boundary is fine in a unit test and is rejected by the evidence gate for a release-level claim. The existing plant/repair/recover evidence in tools/structure-guard/tests/seeded.rs is at the ON-DISK WORKSPACE level, which is why it does not discharge this criterion and why the bead lists a real no-mock E2E separately.

GATES at 0a64bf61, run locally through an `exec cargo` wrapper so the RCH hook could not offload them, exit codes read from the process and never through a pipe: cargo test -p fln-conformance -p structure-guard --no-fail-fast is 38 targets, 667 passed, 1 failed -- the failure being the known franken_lean-h4o1 golden_vellum.rs orphan, not mine. Scoped fmt and clippy clean. UBS v5.3.7 same-path 2x2 with cwd and relative path fixed and only content varied: 19 -> 19 critical, 149 -> 155 warning; +0 criticals from this change. Class-level, since the rust module emits no per-site object at this version.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH. The guard counts FILES MENTIONING a type, which is coarser than counting producers: a file naming it only in prose would count, and a producer reaching it through a re-export under another name would not -- over-counting, never under-counting, which is the safe direction for a floor. It says nothing about whether a sidecar, once written, is CORRECT; only that writing one now would be premature. It does not establish that the ordering I derived is the only possible one -- someone could in principle define a sidecar whose closure and product roots are optional, and I did not price that, because the acceptance names both fields as bound. No lane was run and no full-gate check.sh verdict is obtainable while the two h4o1 orphans stand. One host, one commit, class bounded_model throughout.

Measured at `55b4fa2d9a708a159621ff15903851c861cd07fc`, cc_1. This bead's block was measured at

### The load-bearing fact still holds, and so does the block

| the bead's claim, at `e698c9ef` | re-measured now | still true? |
|---|---|---|
| 0 crates declare a mode-bound product root (no `fln-product-root` marker in any `Cargo.toml`) | **0 of 35 manifests** | **yes** |
| 0 `[[bin]]` targets under `crates/` or `tools/` | 0 explicit `[[bin]]` **sections** | **the count is right and the predicate is wrong — see below** |

there is still nothing to build twice, nothing to diff for byte-identity, and no artifact to carry a
sidecar. Defining the sidecar `SchemaId` now would still freeze a contract with no producer and no
consumer. **This bead stays open and blocked, for the same reason as before.**

### The finding: "0 `[[bin]]` targets" cannot see a bin target

Cargo **auto-discovers** `src/main.rs` as a binary with no `[[bin]]` section present. So counting
`[[bin]]` sections is a false clean, and measured here it is exactly that — **0 explicit sections,
and 3 real auto-discovered bin targets**, none of which declares one:

| package | path | explicit `[[bin]]` |
|---|---|---|
| `structure-guard` | `tools/structure-guard/src/main.rs` | 0 |
| `kernel-ownership-publisher` | `tools/structure-guard/kernel-ownership-publisher/src/main.rs` | 0 |
| `fln-epoch-lab` | `tribunal/epoch-lab/src/main.rs` | 0 |

that "counting only `[[bench]]` sections is a false clean because cargo auto-discovers `benches/*.rs`
with no manifest section at all." The identical trap, one target kind over, in a fact I wrote and
then carried for ten days.

**It does not move the conclusion**, and saying so is the point rather than a hedge. The bead's other
predicate — `crates/*/src/main.rs` — is still genuinely **0**, and all three real binaries are
**tooling**: a structure guard, an ownership publisher, and an epoch lab. None is a *product* in D18's
sense, none declares a mode-bound product root, and none is a thing this bead's criteria could build
twice and compare. So the block is unchanged **and the sentence supporting it was never able to
detect its own falsification.**

That distinction is worth more than the correction: a fact that is *true* but measured by a predicate
that cannot see counterexamples will keep reading true after it stops being true, and nothing would
say so. The next reader re-deriving "0 bins" from `[[bin]]` sections would get the same answer on a
tree that had grown a product binary.

**Read the third row as: 0 product binaries, 3 tooling binaries, none of them mode-bound** — and
derive it from `src/main.rs` plus the marker, never from `[[bin]]`.

My first pass concatenated overlapping globs (`tools/*/src/main.rs` and `tools/*/*/src/main.rs`) and

not evidence that the scan was.

One host, one commit, class `bounded_model`. It re-tests the block's **stated** facts; it does not
re-derive the bead's full acceptance criteria, and the "WHAT DOES NOT EXIST" list below the blocker

title: The done-but-open bead pattern needs a mechanism, not another rescue
description:
MEASURED PATTERN, fourth instance: a bead's work lands in the tree, the bead stays open, and every dependent reads as frozen until someone notices by hand. Instances: franken_lean-atgf (3-day stale review, rescued by derivation-review), franken_lean-z6c and y24 (G0-1/G0-2 work done July 22-23, closed July 29-30 after repeated flagging), and now fln-lld — READY, P0, blocking franken_lean-sno which gates G0-3's ratification path, while the crate's own module doc says its slices are implemented (fln-unsafe-abi carries the CompatHeap core, tri-state RC, ownership shadow, handle API) and it has NO verification-manifest row at all. Each rescue cost a pane a session of archaeology.

THE GAP: nothing joins 'the tree contains this bead's deliverable' to 'the bead is still open'. The verification manifest knows which beads have rows; the coverage guard fires when a bead CROSSES the adoption boundary or CLOSES; nothing fires when an open bead's work has demonstrably landed. The signal exists in three places already: (1) a bead whose crate's module doc names it as implemented, (2) a bead with no manifest row that is neither open-unclaimed nor terminal, (3) an open bead whose id appears in landed commit messages.

CANDIDATE MECHANISMS, cheapest first: (a) a check that every IN_PROGRESS or blocking-READY bead older than N days has a manifest row, so silence becomes a red; (b) a scan joining bead ids in commit subjects against open beads, reporting 'work landed, bead open' as a typed finding with the commits; (c) a staleness projection in the ready list itself. Each is a scan over data already committed; none needs new tracking.

WHAT NOT TO DO: another one-off rescue. The pattern is the defect, not the individual bead. Also do NOT auto-close anything - the mechanism should REPORT, because a bead may legitimately stay open past its first landing (a slice of many).

Filed from the 2026-07-31 reality check (route in /data/tmp/claude-1000/). Whoever takes this should read that route first: it has the full measurement including the crate line counts that make fln-elab's 6 lines the actual critical path.

title: W3: Certificates, receipts, transparency log — auditable checking
description:
Implement certificates, receipts, and the transparency log (§8.6): every checked declaration can emit a certificate — the compressed, structure-shared elaborated term DAG plus reduction hints that make independent rechecking cheap (unfold order, literal-arithmetic transcripts so a tiny verifier replays accelerated ops without its own bignum trust). Certificates attach to olean-next records, feed fln export (speaking the community established export format for cross-prover checkers), and may ship a warm defeq-cache cartridge (memoized reduction history — third-party rechecking becomes verification rather than search).

The certificate law (D20): the checker must be SIMPLER than recomputation, must reject unknown versions, and must fall back to recomputation on any failure — an accelerator, never a wider TCB. Receipts bind kernel + checker build hashes, the consensus policy, fuel profiles, and both verdicts. Attested receipts append to a transparency log (Merkle Mountain Range over receipt roots, signed checkpoints): third parties verify inclusion and consistency without trusting the logger; equivocation is detectable — "checked" becomes an artifact anyone can audit, not a verb someone witnessed.

Acceptance: certificate emit + independent replay on the corpus with the checker measurably simpler (line count, dependency count) than the engines; fln export output accepted by at least one external checker; MMR inclusion/consistency proofs verified by an independent implementation of the verifier side; PG-1b receipt-emission overhead <= 1 ms/decl amortized. Tests: certificate-version rejection fixtures; corrupt-certificate fallback-to-recompute fixtures; log equivocation detection test (forked checkpoint must be caught).

## Acceptance Criteria

All bead-specific requirements, acceptance conditions, tests, invariants, compatibility surfaces, evidence levels, performance gates, negative/recovery cases, and user-visible behaviors stated above remain mandatory. In addition, the MANDATORY VERIFICATION DEFINITION OF DONE in Notes must be satisfied with named unit/property/mutation suites, at least one shared real-path no-mock E2E scenario plus failure/recovery coverage, detailed human and schema-versioned NDJSON artifacts, and reproducible close evidence. No listed feature or claim may be silently narrowed, deferred, mocked, or declared complete through an unclassified divergence.

## Success Criteria

All five exact children close with machine-validated roots; certificate format and cartridges are versioned and bounded; the simple verifier and full checker remain independent; disagreements halt; receipts/signatures/checkpoints never grant declaration authority; all mutation/fuzz/no-mock/recovery and semantic-evidence gates pass.

Update the decision log and add compatibility/tamper/resource fixtures for both formats.

TERMINAL DECOMPOSITION — exact children are fln-7zrh certificate schema/OQ-8, franken_lean-eikp cartridge/OQ-13, fln-eeyn simple verifier/fallback, franken_lean-d2h5 receipt/consensus binding, and franken_lean-nix9 transparency/checkpoints. A real external checker round-trip validates the chosen export; unknown or lossy mappings block the decision. 2. OQ-13 is resolved jointly with K2 by a separate versioned warm defeq-cache cartridge schema and receipt-attachment policy: exact key domain, environment/transparency/epoch/build binding, entry and expanded-weight limits, validation, optionality, privacy/portability, cacheability, expiry, and safe discard/recompute behavior are explicit. Cartridges are accelerators only and cannot carry verdict authority. 3. title: W6: Synod instance engine — exact semantics, SearchCards, keyed negative caches
description:
Implement Synod, the instance engine (§10.4): the Reference semantics — priorities, outParam/semiOutParam, default instances, tabling/caching behavior, the results the ecosystem diamond structures depend on — behind a rebuilt engine: instance search compiled to an indexed relational form (discrimination-automaton candidate retrieval, subsumption-checked tabling, cycle detection with franken_networkx diagnostics), with provenance recorded per resolution: every attempted instance, why it failed (unification residue, priority loss, depth), as a Palimpsest tree.

Every search emits a SearchCard (explored candidates, priorities, unification residues, cycle decisions, cache hits, selection) — provenance and negative-cache key in one artifact, with negative entries valid ONLY under their exact dependency key (instance-table identity, transparency, options, local-context fingerprint). Faithful mode pins search order to the Reference; sound mode may reorder only within proven-confluent regions (same result, better time), CGSE-registered. Name resolution, coercion graphs, and discrimination indexes are immutable content-addressed derivations of the environment commit, incrementally maintained and Ledger-cached — faithful iteration order preserved even where internals are faster.

Acceptance: instance-search outcomes match the oracle across the Corpus instance-trace corpus (instrumented-oracle instance traces); SearchCards complete per perturbation; the sound-mode "why is there no instance" answer (§15.3) renders from this engine exhaust with no second implementation. Tests: golden instance-trace replay; diamond/priority fixtures; negative-cache validity mutation tests (a stale negative entry must be impossible under the dependency key); cycle-diagnostic fixtures.

title: The terminal-row granularity guard fires only in cargo test, so it reddens six panes and never the author
description:
The guard that refuses file-granular evidence in a terminal coverage row is CORRECT and fires only in cargo test -- that is, AFTER the commit has landed. So it reddens the workspace for all six panes, and never for the author at the moment of the mistake.

ROUTED TO ME BY cc_1 as a measurement plus a design tension they declined to resolve without owning the surface; the surface (crates/fln-conformance/tests/ci_execution_join.rs, scripts/git-hooks/pre-commit, scripts/evidence.py) is cc_2's. cc_1 explicitly declined to publish it as AGENTS.md prose, on the ground that the guard's own refusal text already teaches the rule completely -- doctrine a message replaces is doctrine that rots. That judgement is retained here.

THE MEASUREMENT, verified by cc_1 from the git log rather than relayed. 42a227ad at 06:54 migrated TWO terminal rows off file-granular evidence. 49e23d7f at 10:35 landed a new row carrying the SAME defect, 3h41m later. 075a84db at 11:33 repaired it, and named the pattern in its own title. The same pane repaired this defect, reintroduced it, and repaired it again inside one morning, so the knowledge was demonstrably present at 06:54. That is the signature of a missing mechanism rather than a knowledge gap -- and it is the argument the projection guard's own header already makes about a different rule: the agent who forgets is never the one who sees the red.

WHAT IS ALREADY BUILT AND MUST NOT BE DUPLICATED. scripts/git-hooks/pre-commit already extracts scripts/evidence.py from Git's index and runs validate-verification-manifest against the PROSPECTIVE tree. So a commit-time refusal has a delivery mechanism already, carrying no second copy of anything.

OPTION 1 -- MOVE THE PREDICATE INTO evidence.py -- IS REFUSED ON THE MERITS, and the reason is measured rather than stylistic. judge_granularity is not a row-shape check. Read at ci_execution_join.rs, it consumes a Derivation carrying: every integration-test target obtained from CARGO AUTO-DISCOVERY over each member's top-level tests directory, 75 in this workspace, with an empty scan REFUSED rather than reported clean; a test-attribute scan across every package lib; and a precondition set that refuses when a manifest override APPEARS, because a low count reads as a repair. Reimplementing that in Python means a second copy of cargo's layout model in a language with no cargo model -- two copies that agree today, diverge on the first test-target override, and where the Python one cannot even see the condition the Rust one refuses on.

OPTION 2 -- INVOKE THE RUST TEST FROM THE HOOK -- is right in shape and deferred rather than refused. It keeps one copy. Two current objections, both environmental: it puts a compile in the commit path, and cargo REWRITES Cargo.lock, which is INPUT_PATHS line 1 for both check.sh and closure_audit.sh -- so the guard would manufacture a lane-killer during the commit it is checking. Revisit when disk pressure lifts.

OPTION 4 IS THE CANDIDATE, and it is not one cc_1 listed. The hook does not need judge_granularity. It needs a STRICTLY WEAKER, MONOTONIC property: no commit may ADD an artifact naming a FILE to a terminal complete row. Anything that refuses, judge_granularity also refuses, so the two CANNOT CONTRADICT each other -- a weaker check provably subsumed by the stronger one is not a second copy in the dangerous sense. It can only ever be stale, permitting something the Rust guard then catches, which is exactly today's behaviour and therefore not a regression. It needs no layout derivation, no target discovery, no ceiling and no cargo, and the validator the hook already runs computes which rows are terminal complete.

OPTION 3 -- DO NOTHING DELIBERATELY -- remains defensible and is not overruled. Three instances by one pane in one morning is bounded_model, and the guard does catch every one. What argues against it is only that the cost lands on five panes who did not author the row.

NOT PRICED. How the validator exposes row state to a hook check; whether the declared file-granular population and its ceiling need to be visible at commit time; what a FALSE refusal would cost a peer mid-commit, which is the direction that reddens correct work. Nobody has implemented any option.

A STALE FIGURE, recorded because it is this repository's own lesson landing on a number: cc_1's route cites the ceiling as 67. It is 62, and cc_3's conversion work is still lowering it. Re-derive it rather than citing it.

D as well: **30 rows that are green today** would be refused at commit time. That is not a
weaker check subsumed by the stronger one; it is a WALL that reddens correct work at the moment
of commit — the failure direction this repository has already paid for, arriving inside the
repair for a guard that reddens the wrong people.

## 3. THE REPAIR: OPTION 4-PRIME, SHAPE A ONLY — and its price is measured

Restrict the commit-time rule to an artifact matching `*/tests/*.rs` (plus the `cargo-test:`
flavour, which resolves to the same targets). Properties, each checked rather than asserted:

* **A pure STRING SHAPE.** No file reads, no `#[test]` scan, no cargo, no layout derivation, no
  ceiling — so none of Option 1's objection applies and no second copy of cargo's layout model
  is created.
* **A strict SUBSET of `coarse`**, so the two cannot contradict: everything it refuses,
  `judge_granularity` also refuses. That is the property Option 4 claimed and did not have.
* **Reach: 37 of 57 rows (64%).** The remaining 20 are reachable only through shape B, which
  needs reading files for `#[test]` — the expensive branch, deliberately not taken.
* **It catches today's instance.** `ffdc1e83` added `crates/fln-conformance/tests/evidence_finalization.rs`
  to the `hugg` row in the same commit that closed the bead. Shape A, terminal in the
  prospective tree, refused at commit time.

**A correction to my own route, made before anyone acted on it.** I published that today's
instance was a new kind — "the row never moved, the bead did". FALSE at the onset commit: across
`ffdc1e83` the row changed 11 fields and its artifacts went from one `bead:` token to eight,
ADDING the coarse citation. cc_2's byte-identical finding was HEAD vs worktree *after* the close.
So it is Kind 1 and Option 4-prime covers it — the correction strengthens the design rather than
complicating it.

## 4. THE REMAINING QUESTION IS ONE FIELD, AND IT IS WORK RATHER THAN A DECISION

The hook needs to know which rows are terminal `complete` in the PROSPECTIVE tree. Measured:
`validate-verification-manifest` **computes** that (`derived_states[bead_id]`,
`evidence.py:5500`, consumed at `:5124`) and **emits only aggregates** — `derived_state_counts`
`{complete: 127, planned: 43, active: 19, blocked: 2}`. `--output` writes the same 26-key report
as stdout with no per-row structure (and suppresses stdout entirely). So Option 4-prime needs
one new emitted field, or a second copy of a 6-line total function of `(bead_status, skip)`.

**The expensive branch was tested first and eliminated.** `scripts/evidence.py` carries a dead
pane's 543 uncommitted lines (`h4o1`), which looks like a block. Measured in a scratch repo,
both directions: `git commit -o evidence.py` in that state lands **21** lines — mine plus a
peer's 20; a private index plus `git apply --cached <my hunk>` lands **exactly 1**, with **0**
of the peer's lines in the tree and their work untouched in the worktree. So a scoped change is
mechanically available and this bead is **blocked on WORK, not on a decision**. Two residuals:
the shared index reads as staged afterwards and needs `git read-tree HEAD` (AGENTS.md states
that for a NEW file; it holds for a modified one too), and the committed tree is `HEAD + my
hunk`, which is NOT the worktree — so verification must run against the prospective tree, not
the dirty one. Ownership of that surface is recorded here as cc_2's and is a coordination
question, not a mechanical one.

## 5. TWO RULES THAT GENERALISE PAST RCH, RECORDED HERE BECAUSE THEY BIND THIS BEAD'S OWN EVIDENCE

Tonight's `yihl` finding is that rsync's size-plus-mtime heuristic silently skips a
size-and-mtime-preserving change, so a worker compiles stale bytes and reports success. Two
generalisations, kept at the sequencer's instruction:

**(a) TRUSTING THE MUTATION RAN IS THE LOCAL FORM OF THE `--overlay-path` sha256 — cc_1's, and
it is the sharper statement.** A mutation campaign that assumes its plant landed is exactly as
unattributable as a worker that assumes its source synced; no network is involved. Cargo
fingerprints on mtime too, so a cell scored from a cached binary is indistinguishable from one
that ran. Measured on this pane's own campaign: after adding a per-cell assertion that
`Compiling fln-conformance` appears in that cell's own output, all 8 mutants report
`recompiled=True` and their verdicts stand — but the PRISTINE opening cell reports
`recompiled=False`. Its green came from a cached binary. Benign there, and invisible until the
assertion existed. **Any restore-and-rerun apparatus must assert the rerun re-read or
recompiled, rather than assume the write forced it.**

**(b) CITE LOCAL-INPUT FLOORS AS POSITIVE EVIDENCE, NEVER "I DID NOT USE RCH".** A negative claim
about your own tooling is unfalsifiable by anyone else; a floor on the inputs is checkable. The
form: these suites read `git ls-files` behind a floor of 500 tracked paths and
`.beads/issues.jsonl` behind a floor of 300 records — inputs an rch worker does not have — so a
remote run would have exited 101 on a missing input rather than returned green. That is positive
evidence of local execution, and a reader can re-run it.

## 6. WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH

Nothing is built. Option 4-prime's 64% reach is a property of today's population and moves with
it. The scratch-repo probe is one host and one git version, class `bounded_model`; it shows a
scoped commit is possible, never that it is sanctioned by the surface's owner. And the shape-A
rule is measured to be a subset of `coarse` **on today's manifest** — a subset proof over the
predicates themselves is not offered, because `coarse` is derived from a layout the string rule
cannot see.
