title: fln-env: close extension merge validation mutation-proof debt before atomic integration
description:
Closed beads fln-amv.3 and fln-amv.4 established useful baseline behavior and real refusal/recovery records, but their closure evidence does not demonstrate the named mutation matrix required by their acceptance criteria. Preserve those closures and add the missing proof before global Environment integration.

Freeze the extension merge pipeline in this order: bounded descriptor admission and complete descriptor-difference construction; exact branch-ancestry validation; merge-policy dispatch; output construction; publication. Descriptor refusal must inspect zero journal entries, clone zero payloads, select no policy, and expose no product or root. An ancestry refusal must stop at its deterministic exact comparison boundary and expose no product or root. Diagnostics report every simultaneous mismatch in canonical branch-then-field order and both branch-history facts in stable ours-then-theirs order.

The SetUnion raw-order law is exact. After validating the common base, compare the complete ours and theirs suffix sequences by collision-safe canonical ExtensionEntry encoding, then append base_raw plus the lesser suffix block plus the greater suffix block. Never sort or interleave entries inside a suffix block and never remove raw duplicates. Equal suffix blocks are both retained. The semantic view is the stable first-occurrence projection by exact payload bytes over the resulting raw sequence; provenance remains byte-exact. Hashes may accelerate comparison but may not decide equality or ordering without an exact tie-break.

This bead owns the missing semantic mutation bundle and its authoritative child evidence. It does not duplicate the baseline implementation of fln-amv.3/.4 or the global multi-plane publication owned by fln-amv.11.

## Steps to Reproduce

Compare the closed fln-amv.3/.4 evidence and named test inventory against their required mutation matrix. Baseline descriptor and ancestry refusal/recovery passes, but no discriminating compiled kill is identified for each skipped descriptor field, deferred validation, premature policy selection, payload clone, partial product publication, length-only/one-branch/unordered ancestry, or merge-after-refusal mutant. Run the final 41s history seam with those independently selectable mutants; the current proof debt is reproduced whenever a mutant survives, fails only to compile, or is counted by an unrelated failure.

## Acceptance Criteria

Every criterion in this issue's acceptance_criteria field is mandatory, including the final 41s comparison-plan dependency, complete stage/diagnostic/allocation proof, exact SetUnion suffix-block law, named discriminating kills, unit/model/productive 1-8-32 coverage, real Environment refusal/restoration/recovery, and strict independently revalidatable evidence.
acceptance_criteria:
Independently selectable, compiling semantic mutants skip each descriptor field (name, merge, checkpoint, provenance); defer descriptor validation until journal traversal; select a merge policy before validation; clone payloads during refusal; expose a partial product/root; skip ancestry validation; check only length; check only ours; check only theirs; compare entries unordered; or continue merging after refusal. The unmutated baseline passes and a specifically named assertion fails for the intended divergence for every mutant; compile failures, unrelated failures, and generic nonzero results do not count as kills.

Descriptor inputs have explicit name-depth, canonical-byte, diagnostic, work, and cancellation limits. Complete mismatch aggregation is authoritative only after bounded completion; exhaustion or cancellation is typed Inconclusive with authority=false and no product. Exact operation/allocation facts prove descriptor refusal performs zero journal comparisons, payload clones, policy dispatches, or product publications. Ancestry facts identify exact compared entries/bytes, both side lengths and first divergences, and stop before policy/output work. Inputs, roots, sharing, and cache state remain unchanged after every refusal; adequate-budget retry succeeds.

Unit tables and independent generated models cover single and simultaneous descriptor differences on either/both branches, every invalid prefix class on either/both branches, empty/boundary/large journals, all merge policies, repeated refusal, restoration, and recovery. SetUnion cases include one suffix prefixing the other, equal and empty blocks, duplicates in base/each suffix/across suffixes, payload-equal entries with differing provenance, branch permutation, and injected hash collisions. Productive 1/8/32 worker matrices process distinct cases and yield identical canonical diagnostics, roots, work facts, and minimized replayable counterexamples for one fixed input closure.

The real Environment lane runs at least one descriptor-order or premature-publication mutant and one ancestry mutant, restores governed bytes exactly, and then completes a clean recovery. Strict schema-versioned NDJSON records run/scenario/step and bead/claim/invariant IDs; governed source/input hashes; mutation ID and targeted assertion; pipeline stage; descriptor and prefix facts; limits/usage; work/allocation counters; expected/actual outcome; authority/publication/cacheability; before/after roots; first divergence; bounded artifact references; cleanup; and final state. Validation rejects missing, extra, duplicate, stale, reordered, wrong-mutant, unrelated-failure, merged-stream, surviving-mutant, or incomplete evidence; the retained child bundle revalidates independently. All fln-env tests, focused mutation/model suites, the authoritative environment lane, fmt, check, warnings-denied clippy, UBS, scripts/check.sh, and predecessor gates pass. No baseline-only green bar, digest-only equality, raw-entry reordering/deduplication, partial publication, mock-only proof, or deferred named mutant satisfies closure.

The collision-safe history comparison contract is imported from fln-extension-history-checkpoint-identity-41s. This bead consumes that bead's exact comparison plan, checkpoint facts, and logical usage once; it neither redefines digest equality nor rewalks/recharges the history. Its distinct ownership is pipeline stage order, refusal work/allocation, complete diagnostics, raw suffix-block ordering, nonpublication, and the mutation evidence proving those laws. Every ancestry/order mutant must run against the final 41s exact-history API, including injected equal-digest unequal-history inputs, so it cannot accidentally certify the superseded hash-only seam. Evidence references the 41s child bundle by one validated digest and adds only this bead's stage/order/allocation/publication rows.

This bead's matrix is about the VALIDATION PIPELINE - descriptor admission, difference construction, ancestry validation, policy dispatch, output construction, publication - and about what the pipeline DOES on a refusal. A digest that discriminates says nothing about whether a validator skipped a field, cloned a payload, or published a partial product.   * select a merge policy before validation
  * clone payloads during refusal
  * expose a partial product/root
  * skip ancestry validation
  * check only length
  * check only ours
  * check only theirs

"partial_product" matches once, at :4634 - but it is the NDJSON field partial_product_published:false inside the fln-amv.6 set-union E2E producer. That is an ASSERTION THAT IT DID NOT HAPPEN, emitted on the clean path. It is not a mutant that makes it happen and gets killed. An evidence field named after a defect is the easiest thing in this tree to mistake for coverage of that defect.

WHY THE SUITE STILL LOOKS COMPLETE, which is the honest part. The pipeline PROPERTIES are covered by behaviour tests, and good ones: equal_length_and_equal_digest_unequal_histories_are_refused (:5248) is exactly the check-only-length and check-only-digest discriminator, capture_refuses_a_base_that_only_matches_the_prefix_digest (:6394) is an ancestry-prefix discriminator, mismatched_descriptors_are_typed_conflicts_on_either_branch (:4856) covers either-branch mismatch, and set_union_keeps_raw_replay_lossless_and_projects_exact_semantics (:4027) covers the raw-order law. That is precisely what this bead says does not count, and it is right to say so. A behaviour test asserts the implementation produces the correct outcome TODAY. A mutant asserts that a specific WRONG implementation would be CAUGHT - and the bead's own wording is that "compile failures, unrelated failures, and generic nonzero results do not count as kills". The remaining ten are prose in a bead - which is this project's item-7 shape yet again, a claim whose evidence lives in a different artifact from the claim, and in this case in no artifact at all.

CORRECTION TO MY OWN MEASUREMENT, same session, before anyone builds on it. My note above says the surviving expose_partial_product mutant means a merge "publishes a merge outcome where the pipeline must refuse". THAT OVERSTATES IT AND I AM WITHDRAWING IT. The measurement (11 killed, 1 survived, arm never reached) stands; the interpretation of the survivor was wrong, and I found it by checking who calls the projection instead of trusting my own reading.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE. project_set_union_entries has TWO callers, not one:
  * ExtensionState::merge (:2139)
  * ExtensionState::semantic_projection (:1535), a PUBLIC method

Through merge, the projection's Inconclusive arm CANNOT FIRE. merge already runs set_union_cached_limit_refusal on the same limits and the same raw_entries/raw_payload_bytes, and set_union_entry_limit_refusal over ours ++ theirs-suffix. The projection then re-tests exactly those two conditions over first ++ second-suffix, which is the SAME MULTISET in a possibly swapped branch order - and both conditions are order-independent (a maximum and two totals). So every condition the projection can refuse on has already been refused on upstream.

That is why the mutant survived: on the merge path it is an EQUIVALENT MUTANT, not an uncovered defect. No merge outcome is wrong, and no partial product can be published through merge. Reporting a surviving equivalent mutant as a live defect is precisely the "counted by an unrelated failure" error this bead's own criteria forbid, in the other direction.

WHAT THE SURVIVOR DOES REVEAL, and both halves are real:

1. A CHECK THAT CANNOT FIRE. The projection's own limit checks are dead on the merge path. This codebase already has the law, in this same crate's sibling: "A check that cannot fire is not defence in depth, it is an untruthful contract" (environment.rs:265, written for commit's duplicate-name ordering). The merge path currently carries exactly that shape - a second refusal stage whose conditions the first stage has already decided. Either the upstream checks are the contract and the projection's are redundant, or the projection's are the contract and merge should not pre-empt them; today the code asserts both and only one can be true.

2. A PUBLIC REFUSAL PATH WITH NO TEST. semantic_projection(limits) reaches that arm with no pre-checks at all, so it IS reachable in production - just not through merge. The panic probe proves no test in the suite reaches it by ANY route, so the public method's refusal path is entirely unexercised. That is a genuine coverage hole and it is the one worth closing.

REVISED WORK ORDER for whoever takes this:
  (a) Drive semantic_projection to Inconclusive directly and assert the typed refusal, no product, unchanged state. That closes the real hole.
  (b) Decide the duplication in (1) deliberately rather than leaving both. If merge's pre-checks stay, the projection arm is unreachable there and should say so, or the pre-checks should go and let the projection be the single refusal authority. This is a small design decision, not a test.
  (c) Record the eleven mutant->killer pairings so the kills cannot be refactored away silently.
  (d) Seeds and lane wiring remain scripts/ and cod_2's.

METHOD NOTE, because it is the reusable part: the survivor was only interpretable after asking who else calls the mutated function. A surviving mutant has three explanations - missing test, unreachable code, or equivalent mutant - and they demand opposite responses. Reporting one as another is how a mutation campaign produces confident wrong conclusions.

WHAT I SAID IN THE COMMENT ABOVE (landed ce3c21d0): that my worktree ubs run was "measured
in the wrong tree" and that ubs "does not inherit the worktree escape hatch". BOTH ARE
FALSE. cc_2's measurement (175e0ad1) establishes that ubs roots its shadow workspace at
CWD and fails only when an argument resolves outside it. My runs were `cd` into the tree
followed by a RELATIVE path, which is the valid shape. So the run was admissible, and the
main-tree re-measurement in that comment is a confirmation rather than a repair.

I DID NOT INHERIT THAT. I ran the full 2x2 myself, on BYTE-IDENTICAL content -- sha256 of
crates/fln-env/src/extensions.rs is one value across the main tree and the worktree at
990ed26d, so content is held fixed and only cwd and path shape vary:

  cwd=worktree, RELATIVE path            works   Critical 56
  cwd=main,     RELATIVE path            works   Critical 56
  cwd=main,     ABSOLUTE into worktree   FAILS   "Failed to prepare files workspace"
  cwd=worktree, ABSOLUTE into main       FAILS   "Failed to prepare files workspace"

THE FOURTH CELL IS THE ONE WORTH ADDING, because it kills the remaining wrong framing. It
is a worktree cwd pointing at the MAIN tree, and it still fails. So this is not "worktrees
are degraded" and not "the main tree is safe" -- it is cwd-relative resolution, symmetric,
and neither tree is privileged. Identical bytes also give identical counts (56 both), which
independently confirms the caveat that cross-tree count differences are CONTENT differences,
not tool inconsistency.

THE HAZARD NOBODY HAS STATED, AND IT IS THE REAL FINDING HERE: **ALL FOUR CELLS EXIT 1.**
The two working runs exit 1 because this file has findings; the two broken runs exit 1
because staging failed. So on any file that has findings, THE EXIT CODE CANNOT DISTINGUISH
"ubs ran and found things" FROM "ubs never ran". I measured the discriminating case too:
a finding-free file (crates/fln-env/src/lib.rs, crates/fln-core/src/lib.rs) exits 0 on a
working run. So exit status discriminates ONLY on clean files -- which are exactly the ones
where you would not look. On a file with a known finding profile, like this one, an
automated gate reading `$?` alone would score a never-executed scan as a normal
findings-present run.

THE CHECK THAT ACTUALLY WORKS: grep the output for "Failed to prepare files workspace"
before believing any ubs result, and never treat nonzero as "scanned, has findings".

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THIS BEAD'S RECORD. The numbers stand and are unchanged: 53 -> 56
critical, the whole delta being the one "Secret, signature, or token compared with ==/!="
false-positive rule, exit 1 before and after, on same-path same-bytes runs. What changes is
that ce3c21d0's framing conceded a defect that did not exist. I am leaving that comment in
place rather than pretending it was not written -- it is immutable, and a correction chain
that hides its own middle step teaches nothing.

THE LESSON I AM TAKING, since it is the third provenance correction on my evidence today
and the first one where I was wrong in the CAUTIOUS direction: conceding a fault to a rule
you have not measured is the same error as claiming a green you have not measured. Both
put an unverified statement into an immutable record. "Measure, do not inherit" has no
exception for corrections, and I applied the rule to my greens today but not to my
apologies.

| clause | cell in `crates/fln-env/src/extensions.rs` | the assertion that fails |

| C4 stops before policy/output work | `the_ancestry_stage_cannot_see_a_policy_because_it_cannot_see_a_field` | **the strongest form in the paragraph: it is not an assertion at all but a compile-time constraint** — the stage is generic over a subject whose bounds do not expose the policy field, so policy work is inexpressible rather than merely unperformed. `ancestry_facts_carry_only_plain_counts_so_neither_arm_can_hold_a_product` is the output half |

absence. A cited cell that exists but is ignored is not per-commit evidence, which is why this was
measured from the run list rather than from the source.

Reading the criteria beside the cell names, C3 says descriptor refusal performs **zero** payload

checkpoints.

claims and what discharges it, and a criterion that undersells its discharge is a finding of that

**One paragraph of five**, so nothing here bears on paragraphs 1, 3, 4 or 5, and dt5 stays open.

because a close resting on fourteen unmeasured bindings would be this bead's own defect.

that the fourteen cells run — never that any of them would fail for the reason stated beside it.

## Acceptance paragraph 3 of 5: every enumerated member has a cell, and the bindings here are a different KIND from paragraph 2's

headline is not that they are all covered — it is *how*.

Comment 2062 disclosed that paragraph 2's fourteen bindings are candidate bindings "at the strength
of a careful read", because no gut campaign was run. **Paragraph 3 is not in that position, and the
difference is structural rather than a matter of my confidence.** Four of its cells do not assert a
fact about a population — they *derive* the population and compare set-to-set in both directions,
so a member that stops being covered fails without anyone re-reading anything:

  bound to that product. A new descriptor field enlarges the table automatically; a field dropped
  from the dimension fails the count.
- `the_prefix_class_model_covers_every_class_on_either_and_both_branches` asserts
  `classes_as_ours == realizable` and `classes_as_theirs == realizable` — exact set equality, both
  directions, against a **computed** `realizable_prefix_classes(base_len, MAX_BRANCH_LEN)` rather
  than a hand-list. "Every invalid prefix class" is therefore bound to the classes that can exist,
  which is the only honest denominator; an unrealizable class demanded would be a wall, and a
  realizable one missed is a failure.
- `the_set_union_case_table_covers_every_named_shape_by_computed_predicate` computes each case's
  shapes from **the case's own data** (`set_union_case_coverage`), then asserts
  `observed == declared` where `declared` comes from `SetUnionCoverage::all()`. That `all()` is a
  succ-chain walk which panics if the chain yields more values than `COUNT` ("a variant is
  double-counted or the chain cycles") and asserts equality if fewer — **so `COUNT` cannot lie about
  the enum**. A case edited until it no longer exhibits a shape drops that shape and reddens.
- `merge_validation_is_canonical_across_1_8_32_productive_workers` — see below; its control is the
  best single assertion in the paragraph.

### The three sentences, member by member

**S1 — unit tables and independent generated models.** Single and simultaneous descriptor
differences on either/both branches: `the_descriptor_difference_table_is_exhaustive_over_fields_and_branches`.
Every invalid prefix class on either/both branches: `the_prefix_class_model_covers_every_class_on_either_and_both_branches`,
with `model_common_prefix` / `model_prefix_verdict` / `prefix_class` as the independent model — a
second implementation in the test module, which is what makes "independent" true rather than
decorative. Empty/boundary/large journals: `the_journal_size_table_spans_empty_boundary_and_large_journals`
(the same cell paragraph 2 leans on for the diagnostic bound). All merge policies, repeated
refusal, restoration and recovery: `a_descriptor_refusal_is_recoverable_under_every_merge_policy`
iterates `MergeSemantics::all()` and runs the whole sequence — refuse, repair **only** the
descriptor, refuse again at the ancestry stage, repair fully, recover — closing with "none of the
refused attempts may have touched the base", an assertion that spans *every* refusal in the
sequence and is therefore the repeated-refusal binding rather than a single-refusal one.
`suffix_checkpoints_round_trip_empty_nested_and_repeated_restores` and
`suffix_capture_refuses_every_invalid_base_atomically` carry the restoration half.

**S2 — SetUnion cases.** All nine shapes the criteria name are members of `SetUnionCoverage` and
each is computed by a predicate over the case: one suffix prefixing the other, equal blocks, empty
blocks, duplicates in base, duplicates within a suffix, duplicates across suffixes, payload-equal
entries with differing provenance, branch permutation, injected hash collisions. Two details worth
keeping. The provenance predicate carries a comment resolving the criteria's own wording —
provenance in the raw sequence is **position**, computed over the *product* rather than the inputs,
which is what makes it a different claim from the cross-suffix one. And the collision is
**verified rather than assumed**: `collision_verified` gates the coverage insert, so a fixture that
stopped colliding would remove its own coverage instead of silently passing.

**S3 — the 1/8/32 worker matrix.** `merge_validation_is_canonical_across_1_8_32_productive_workers`.
It asserts `factorial(scenario_count) >= 32` so distinct permutations exist at all; then
`orders.len() == worker_count` for the criteria's "process **distinct** cases"; then
`canonical_digest == expected_digest` and `canonical == expected` at every worker count, and
`distinct.len() == 1` across the three.

### The single assertion I would point a reviewer at

```
assert_eq!(processing_digests.len(), worker_count,
    "distinct orders must produce distinct processing-order digests, or the \
     canonical agreement below is measuring the sort rather than the schedule");
```

Every worker sorts its records before digesting, so **canonical agreement across workers is
satisfiable by a matrix that never varied the schedule at all** — the vacuity this whole cell would
otherwise have. That assertion is the control which excludes it, and it is stated as the thing that
must NOT be true. It is the paragraph's strongest evidence and nothing in the criteria asked for it.

The canonical comparison's message says "diagnostics, roots, work facts and minimized

Two exact cardinalities rather than floors, both of which would fail on drift: seven of the nine
scenarios refuse and so carry a minimized counterexample while two carry none; and every

All **12** cited cells appear in the `fln-env` lib run list (318 tests); a planted decoy resolves to

measurement — the only intervening commit is `01df59a5`, my own beads-only one — and the list was
re-derived rather than reused on that reasoning.

### What this does not earn

**Three paragraphs of five audited; 1, 4 and 5 remain and dt5 stays open.**

The strength claim above is **about the mechanisms, not about my having attacked them.** No gut
campaign was run here either. What is different from paragraph 2 is that four of these cells fail
on population drift *by construction* — a derived set compared both ways cannot quietly stop
covering a member — so their bindings do not rest on my reading in the way paragraph 2's fourteen

## Acceptance paragraph 1 of 5: the mutation record is the strongest mechanism in this bead — and the audit found a stale claim inside it, now repaired at `f2092fb8`

Measured at `f2092fb88d29688a835af2aae485661b65db763a`, cc_1. **All five paragraphs are now audited
(1, 2, 3, 4, 5). This still closes nothing, and the reason is paragraph 4.** Same method throughout.

### The fourteen are exactly the fourteen

Paragraph 1 enumerates four descriptor-field skips (name, merge, checkpoint, provenance) plus ten
others. `CRITERIA_NAMED_MUTANTS` in `extensions.rs` declares **14**, and they correspond one for
one, in order: `descriptor_skip_name`, `descriptor_skip_merge`, `descriptor_skip_checkpoint`,
`descriptor_skip_provenance`, `descriptor_validation_deferred`, `policy_before_validation`,
`clone_payloads_during_refusal`, `expose_partial_product`, `ancestry_skipped`,
`ancestry_only_length`, `ancestry_only_ours`, `ancestry_only_theirs`, `compare_entries_unordered`,
`continue_after_refusal`.

`the_merge_validation_mutation_record_is_complete_and_classified` holds the join:
`MERGE_VALIDATION_MUTANTS` against `CRITERIA_NAMED_MUTANTS` by **set equality in both directions**,
with a duplicate check on **each** side — because a duplicated name on either side hides a missing
one and a set comparison alone would not see it. Its own comment records why one direction is not
enough: subset-only would readmit the measured 12-of-14 state, superset-only would let an entry sit
under a name no criterion names.

### The requirement's second sentence is not satisfied for 2 of the 14 — and both times because the code is STRONGER

"A specifically named assertion fails for the intended divergence for **every** mutant." Measured,
the record is **12 killed + 1 equivalent + 1 structurally prevented + 0 uncovered = 14**, under a
conservation identity asserting exactly that sum against `CRITERIA_NAMED_MUTANTS.len()`.

Two members therefore have no failing named assertion, and neither is a gap:

- one is `EquivalentBecause` — the mutation cannot change observable behaviour, so no test can kill
  it and none should be written. The record's own words: filing an equivalent mutant as a gap
  "creates debt that can never be discharged, because the test it asks for cannot exist."
- `clone_payloads_during_refusal` is `StructurallyPrevented`. It was **measured surviving the full
  suite at 239/239** — the returned conflict is byte-identical and nothing observed the copying —
  and was then repaired by making stage 1 generic in its subject with only `Clone + Eq` in scope, so
  the mutation body does not compile against an opaque `D`.

That second one makes paragraph 1's opening literally unsatisfiable for that member: the criteria
demand *compiling* mutants, and the repair's whole content is that this one **cannot be written**.
**This is the third instance of the same directional finding** — comment 2062 (no diagnostic limit,
because the diagnostic is constant-size by construction), comment 2063 (a tenth SetUnion shape the
criteria do not name), and now this. It is the sharpest of the three: the other two understate the
discharge, this one is unsatisfiable *as written* because a repair landed that made it so. An
unkillable-by-construction mutant beats a killed one, and the criteria have no way to say so.

### The single mechanism I would carry to another bead

`MutantOutcome::KilledBy(fn())` holds the killer as a **function item, not its name as a string** —
and `assert_classification_is_well_formed` *reads* it (`let _killer: fn() = *killer;`), so the
reference is a use. Renaming or deleting a killer is then a **compile error** rather than a silently
stale record. That is the "specifically named assertion" requirement mechanised at the only point
where it cannot rot.

The same function is extracted from the loop deliberately, so it can be applied to **constructed**
variants: the record holds no `SurvivedUncovered` entry today, so checking these rules only against
the live table would leave that arm's discipline unexercised — a repaired population's guard going
decorative, caught in advance rather than after. Every classification must carry its *argument*: an
equivalence's reason over 80 characters, a survivor's `measured` over 80 **and** its `obligation`
over 40, a prevention **both** `by` and `still_unproven`. "It survived" is not a classification.

And `uncovered == 0` is a wall on purpose: a survivor found by a later campaign must redden the
build until it is recorded deliberately with its obligation named.

### The finding — and it is the most direct evidence this bead could produce for its own subject

The prevention entry's `still_unproven` field exists precisely so a structural repair is not "quoted
as a clean win". Its item (c) read: *"what remains open there is the walk's COST, which is
unbounded."*

**That was true when written at `8f539b85`, and was falsified by the very next commit.** `9m74`
bounded and cancelled every merge stage at `5b6158ad`, charging the ancestry walk the same
`ProofBudget` its checkpoint sibling already paid.

Why nothing caught it is the part worth keeping. **`9m74` did exactly the right thing**: it had
written its disclosure as a test a correct repair would redden, and in that same commit the test
duly flipped to `the_ancestry_walk_is_bounded_like_its_checkpoint_sibling`. That mechanism protected
`9m74`'s sentence and **could not** protect this one, because the fact had **two homes and only one
join**. Verified rather than inferred: the flipped test exists at `extensions.rs:9687` and runs,
the ancestry budget cells run, and `extensions.rs` moved four more times since `5b6158ad` —
**twice under this very bead** — with the stale half surviving every one.

So the field whose existence is mandated so a residue gets stated does not require that residue to
stay **true**. A rule that forces you to write the remainder down buys nothing about whether the
remainder is still there.

Repaired at **`f2092fb8`**, corrected rather than deleted, because deleting it hides that the claim
moved. Gates at `ed3215ca` plus the patch, gate probed FREE: `fmt --check` 0, `clippy -D warnings`
0, `cargo test -p fln-env --no-fail-fast` **318 passed / 0 failed**. UBS terminal mode
`completed_findings`, exit 1, and **attributed** rather than reported — same path, same cwd, varying
only content: HEAD baseline **12 critical / 1284 warning / 899 info**, with the patch **12 / 1284 /
899**, delta **zero**, all findings pre-existing, restoration verified byte-identical by sha256.

### The remaining clauses

*"The unmutated baseline passes"* has **no cell, correctly.** It is discharged by the package suite
itself — 318 passed, 0 failed — and a test asserting that the other tests pass would be circular. I
looked for a producer and am recording that the right answer is that there should not be one.

*"Compile failures, unrelated failures, and generic nonzero results do not count as kills"* is
enforced at the **lane**, not in the record: `intended_failure_signature_missing` greps the run's
captures for the intended divergence signature, and `mutant_survived_or_wrong_exit` separates a
survivor from a wrong exit. This is the same two-producer split comment 2064 records for S3 — the
record says *which* assertion kills, the lane says it failed *for the right reason*.

### Where dt5 stands, with all five paragraphs audited

| paragraph | state |
|---|---|
| 1 — mutants | discharged; 12 killed + 1 equivalent + 1 prevented, one stale claim found and repaired |
| 2 — limits, facts, restoration | discharged; bindings at the strength of a careful read, no gut campaign |
| 3 — coverage tables and the 1/8/32 matrix | discharged; four cells derive their population and compare both ways |
| 4 — the real Environment lane | **S1 discharged but its RUN is stale; S2 unresolved; S4 NOT SATISFIED** |
| 5 — the negative closure clause | binds the closing judgement, not the code |

**dt5 does not close today, and the blocker is one thing:** there is no green `scripts/check.sh`,
which paragraph 4 requires by name. That is routed and is not dischargeable by me alone — a
`check.sh` run freezes the repository for every pane — and it is the same single outstanding
criterion `8o3o` records.

### What this does not earn

The audit is now complete in **coverage** and not in **strength**. No gut campaign was run for any
paragraph; paragraphs 1 and 3 rest on mechanisms that fail on drift by construction, paragraph 2 on
readings. The repair at `f2092fb8` fixes one stale claim **found by hand** — nothing scans for the
others, and the defect it instances (one fact, two homes, one join) has no mechanism here. Its
population in this file is unmeasured, which is a stated gap and the obvious next slice.

One host, one commit, class `bounded_model`.

## The stale-claim population is now MEASURED — 5 of 36, one was stale, and the tractable guard would NOT have caught it

Measured at `bb0810df0be4f985c05250e3cd63b77f7d5cd1f9`, cc_1. Comment 2065 ended by naming this as
the obvious next slice: the defect `f2092fb8` repaired — a prose claim whose producer moved — had an
**unmeasured population**. It is measured now.

### The population

| | |
|---|---|
| registry entries across `REFUSAL_FACT_MUTANTS`, `MERGE_ENVELOPE_MUTANTS`, `MERGE_VALIDATION_MUTANTS` | **36** |
| entries whose outcome is `KilledBy(fn())` — **compile-bound**, cannot go stale silently | **31** |
| entries carrying **unbound prose arguments** | **5** |
| of those 5: found stale and repaired at `f2092fb8` | **1** |
| of those 5: audited against HEAD today and clean | **4** |

The 31 need no audit and that is the mechanism working: the killer is held as a function item and
the well-formedness check reads it, so a rename or deletion is a compile error. **The auditable
surface is 5, not 36** — which is why this was worth doing by hand rather than deferring for a tool.

### The four, each checked against a named referent rather than read for plausibility

- **`stage_one_specialised_back_to_descriptors`** — cites `_DESCRIPTOR_ADMISSION_STAYS_JOURNAL_FREE`
  as the site that stops compiling. Present, 5 occurrences. `CountedSubject` present.
- **`descriptor_grows_a_fifth_field`** — claims the allocation test destructures `ExtensionDescriptor`
  **totally with no rest pattern**, so a fifth field is `E0027` rather than a field quietly left out
  of the account. Verified twice over: `ExtensionDescriptor` still has exactly **four** fields
  (`name`, `merge`, `checkpoint`, `provenance`), so "a fifth" is still the right counterfactual; and
  the destructuring at `extensions.rs:9283` still names all four with no `..`.
- **`ancestry_stage_specialised_back_to_entries`** — `walk_branch_ancestry`,
  `validate_branch_ancestry` and `CountedEntry` all present. **And it already carries the `9m74`
  correction** in its own `still_unproven`: "the stage was unbounded when this row was written and is
  now charged against the same ProofBudget its checkpoint-path sibling takes".
- **`expose_partial_product`** — the only `EquivalentBecause`. Names `semantic_projection`
  (`extensions.rs:2055`) as the other caller and
  `semantic_projection_refuses_typed_on_every_resource_and_exposes_no_view` as the covering test.
  Both resolve, and the test **runs**; a planted decoy resolves to nothing, so the scan can report
  absence.

### The sharpening, and it is worth more than the original finding

`ancestry_stage_specialised_back_to_entries` and `clone_payloads_during_refusal` asserted the **same
fact** about the ancestry walk's boundedness. When `9m74` landed, **one was updated and the other
was not.**

That rules out the cheap explanation. It was not that the author didn't know the walk had been
bounded — they demonstrably did, and corrected one site in the same file. It was that the fact had a
**second copy nobody enumerated**. "One fact, two homes, one join" is not a story about attention;
it is a story about *not having the list*. Producing the list is exactly what this comment does, and
it took one pass now that the question was asked.

### The part that decides whether to build a guard, and it points the other way

The obvious mechanism is this repository's own citation-registry technique: require every identifier
a prose argument names to resolve, and every test it names to run. It is cheap, it is proven here
twice already, and I have just run it by hand over all five.

**It would not have caught the defect I found.** `clone_payloads_during_refusal`'s stale clause read
"what remains open there is the walk's COST, which is unbounded". It **named no identifier at all**.
Every referent in that entry resolved perfectly, before and after the repair. A referent-resolution
guard over this population would have been green through the entire period the claim was false.

So the checkable sub-shape and the observed defect are **disjoint**, and building the guard now
would produce a green that means nothing about the class that actually bit. Worse, with all five
currently clean it would be a repaired population's guard — decorative on a healthy tree, catching
nothing until a decoy is planted in it.

**Recorded as a decision, not a deferral:** the referent guard is *not* the repair for this defect,
and adopting it would let a future reader believe the class is covered. What would actually cover it
is a join from each prose claim to a producer that fails when the claim becomes false — which for
"the walk is unbounded" is precisely the disclosure-test shape `9m74` used and which worked, for the
one copy it knew about. The honest generalisation is therefore **not** a scanner: it is that a
disclosure test must be written for the *fact*, and every restatement of that fact must point at it
rather than repeat it.

### What this does not earn

The population is **this file's three registries only**. Prose claims elsewhere in `extensions.rs` —
module docs, cell doc-comments, assertion messages — are not counted here, and paragraph 3's audit
already found one assertion message making a load-bearing claim (which was checked and held). So 5
is a floor for the *registry* surface, not a census of the file.

Four entries were audited by **resolving the referents they name**; that establishes the citations
denote, never that each argument is sound. `expose_partial_product`'s equivalence — that merge
pre-tests both refusal conditions over the same multiset so the projection's Inconclusive arm cannot
fire on that path — is a semantic claim I did not re-derive.

One host, one commit, class `bounded_model`. Nothing here runs per commit; this is a measurement
plus a decision against the tool that looked obvious.

## The narrowed-denominator hypothesis I disclosed three times is WRONG — measured, 3 semantic kills and 1 structural prevention, 0 survivors

Campaign base `c9a84a89629163364bb1a169a159fa692f02b307`, recorded at
`36037ea3a2d914e12e2839964d38211e7fa97f56`, cc_1.

Comments 2062, 2063 and 2065 each closed by disclosing that **no gut campaign was run**, and 2063
went further and named the specific vector it thought would matter:

> the interesting mutant against the four derived cells is not a deleted assertion but a **narrowed
> denominator** — a `realizable_prefix_classes` that returns fewer classes, or a `COUNT` moved with
> its enum — both of which shrink the population and the equality still holds.

That is a claim about my own praise, so it is measured here rather than repeated. **It does not
hold.** Every form of it I could write either dies at the named cell or fails to compile.

### Method

An isolated `git worktree` at the campaign base with its own `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`, so no pane ever
saw a mutated tree and no nested build contended for the shared target directory. Each mutant
applied **alone** by exact byte-pair replacement, **refused unless its anchor occurs exactly once**,
the whole `fln-env` lib suite run with `--no-fail-fast`, then the source restored and verified by
sha256 before the next plant. The unmutated baseline was run first and was **green** — without that,
no kill below would be attributable.

### Results

| mutant | what it narrows | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `narrow_realizable_prefix_classes` | the **computed denominator** the equality is taken against — `PrefixKind::all()` truncated to one kind | **killed** by `the_prefix_class_model_covers_every_class_on_either_and_both_branches`, and by that cell **alone** |
| `silence_one_setunion_coverage_predicate` | the **observed** set — one shape's predicate made unreachable, the declared enum untouched | **killed** by `the_set_union_case_table_covers_every_named_shape_by_computed_predicate`, alone |
| `shrink_the_descriptor_field_dimension` | the power set **and** the cardinality assertion **together** — `DESCRIPTOR_FIELD_COUNT` 4 → 3, the sharpest form of the hypothesis | **COMPILE FAILURE**, `E0308`. Not a kill, and this bead's own criteria say so |
| `give_every_worker_the_same_order` | the 1/8/32 matrix's schedule variety — every worker handed the identity permutation | **killed** by `merge_validation_is_canonical_across_1_8_32_productive_workers`, alone |

**3 semantic kills, 1 structurally prevented, 0 survivors.** Each kill was by **exactly one** cell —
the independent-gut discipline this repository asks for — so no mutant rode a neighbour's assertion.

### Why the hypothesis failed, which is more useful than that it failed

It assumed the two sides of the equality could be narrowed **independently**. They cannot, and for
two different reasons:

- Where the denominator is **computed from a model** (`realizable_prefix_classes`), narrowing it
  leaves the *observed* side unchanged, so the equality breaks immediately. The both-directions
  comparison is what does this: a subset-only check would have passed.
- Where the denominator is a **declared constant**, `DESCRIPTOR_FIELD_COUNT` is not merely compared
  against — it is the **length of an array type**, `[DescriptorField; DESCRIPTOR_FIELD_COUNT]`. So
  moving it does not produce a smaller-but-consistent world; it produces a type error. That is
  strictly stronger than a test, and it is the same mechanism `CaseDimension::all()` uses when it
  refuses a succ chain longer or shorter than `COUNT`.

So the "move the `COUNT` with its enum" half of my caveat was not a gap in the tests; it was a case
the **type system** already closed, and I mistook an unexercised vector for an unguarded one.

### The classification, and it cannot go where the house pattern would put it

By this bead's own taxonomy the third mutant is `StructurallyPrevented`: measured, named site,
compile failure rather than a green suite — and **a compile failure is not a kill**, which paragraph
1 states explicitly.

**It cannot be added to `MERGE_VALIDATION_MUTANTS`, and that is the closure property working rather
than an obstacle.** That registry is closed in *both directions* against `CRITERIA_NAMED_MUTANTS`,
so an entry under a name no criterion names would fail
`the_merge_validation_mutation_record_is_complete_and_classified` at its `unnamed` assertion. The
record's own doc-comment already anticipates exactly this — it is why `REFUSAL_FACT_MUTANTS` is a
second table rather than four more rows in the first: folding them in "would trade a checked
property for a longer list". These four target the *coverage tables* rather than the pipeline
stages, so they belong to neither existing registry, and they are recorded here.

### What this changes for dt5

Paragraph 3's discharge is upgraded from **"derived mechanisms, unattacked"** to **"derived
mechanisms, attacked at the vector their own author judged most dangerous, and unbroken"**. That is
the caveat comments 2062/2063/2065 carried, now discharged for paragraph 3.

It is **not** discharged for paragraph 2, whose fourteen bindings remain readings, and this campaign
did not touch them.

### What this does not earn

**Four mutants is not a campaign over the paragraph.** It tests one named hypothesis at four sites,
chosen because I had published that hypothesis — not a systematic sweep of paragraph 3's twelve
cells. A survivor elsewhere in those cells is entirely possible and is not excluded by this.

The three kills establish each cell fails **when its population is narrowed**; they say nothing
about whether the cell's *argument* is sound, which is the limit every layer of this audit has had.

One host, one commit, class `bounded_model`, and a mutation result is a measurement at the campaign
base — `c9a84a89` — not a property of every future tree, which is exactly why the base is named here
rather than left as "at HEAD".

**Disclosed housekeeping:** the campaign worktree at `/data/tmp/cc1-dt5-mut` and its target
directory are left in place rather than removed, because this repository's first rule forbids me
deleting anything without express permission. Its source is restored byte-exactly and both trees are
clean; say the word and I will remove the worktree registration.

Campaign base `c9a84a89629163364bb1a169a159fa692f02b307` (verified still describing `extensions.rs`
at this HEAD), recorded at `ea37e786ab00675a04f73c42f0dcc365ecbbe34c`, cc_1.

Comment 2062 disclosed that paragraph 2's fourteen bindings are candidate bindings "at the strength
of a careful read". Comment 2067 closed that caveat for paragraph 3 and said plainly it remained
live for paragraph 2. This closes it, with the same discipline: four **production** defects, each
forbidden by a distinct paragraph-2 clause, planted one at a time in the isolated worktree, anchor
required to occur exactly once, whole suite per plant, byte-exact restore verified by sha256, green
baseline first.

### Results — 4 planted, 4 semantic kills, 0 survivors, 0 compile failures

| mutant | clause it violates | killed by |
|---|---|---|
| `numeric_components_charged_nothing` — a numeric name component costs 0 | C1 canonical-byte limit | `numeric_name_components_are_charged_their_comparison_width`, alone |
| `budget_resets_per_name_instead_of_totalling` — the spend stops accumulating | C1 name-depth limit / totality | **seven** cells, including `the_descriptor_budget_is_a_total_across_all_three_subjects` |

### The finding: my audit named ONE cell per clause, and the discharge is a SET

Comment 2062's method was "name the cell that discharges it **and** the assertion inside that cell
that would fail". Two results say that framing was too narrow, and both are corrections to my own
work rather than to the code:

**The canonical-byte clause is discharged by a cell my audit never named.** I bound C1's
canonical-byte limb to `the_descriptor_byte_dimension_is_not_the_canonical_encoding_length`. The
mutant that actually stops the byte dimension bounding anything — making numeric components free —

**A cell pins more than its name advertises.** `byte_allowance_off_by_one` moves the *byte*

Together these say the honest form of comment 2062's table is **clause → set of cells**, not clause

than as a caveat.

`budget_resets_per_name_instead_of_totalling` fired **seven** cells. Under the independent-gut

shape and not evidence that any cell is over-broad. The three narrow mutants each died at exactly
one cell, which is the property that discipline actually asks for. I am recording the seven rather
than only the intended killer, because a campaign that reports just the expected name cannot tell a
precise kill from a coarse one.

### Both rounds together

**8 mutants planted, 7 semantic kills, 1 structural prevention, 0 survivors.** Round 1 (comment
2067) attacked paragraph 3's derived cells at the narrowed-denominator vector I had published as
most dangerous; round 2 attacks paragraph 2's readings at four production sites. Every kill names
its cell, and the one non-kill is a compile failure that this bead's criteria explicitly refuse to

### What this does not earn

**Four mutants over five clauses is not a sweep.** Paragraph 2's C3 (zero journal comparisons /

The kills establish each cell fails when the property it names is broken. They still say nothing

One host, class `bounded_model`, and a mutation result is a measurement **at the campaign base**,

## Round 3: the LYING INSTRUMENT is caught, the harness is validated against the record's own claim, and one of my predictions was wrong

Campaign base `c9a84a89629163364bb1a169a159fa692f02b307`, recorded at
`5d42aa0b108b293ff16f6297f0a13eec0c2b5374`, cc_1.

Comment 2069 disclosed that paragraph 2's C3, C4 and C5 were **not** attacked. This round attacks
them and adds the control the first two rounds lacked.

### The mutant that mattered: an instrument that measures nothing

C3's clause is *"exact operation/allocation facts prove descriptor refusal performs zero journal
comparisons, payload clones, policy dispatches, or product publications"*, and every one of those
zeros is read through an instrumented subject. **A counter that never counts satisfies all four
vacuously.** If nothing catches that, C3's discharge is hollow — which would be a far worse finding
than a missing test, because the suite would be green while measuring nothing.

Planted: `ops.clones += 1` → `ops.clones += 0`.

**Killed, by two cells** — `descriptor_refusal_performs_exactly_three_subject_clones_and_nothing_else`
and **`the_subject_tally_moves_when_the_stage_does_more_work`**.

That second cell is a **dedicated anti-vacuity guard whose entire purpose is to refuse an instrument
that does not move**, it runs per commit, and **I did not name it anywhere in the paragraph-2 audit**.
So C3 is not hollow, and the protection is deliberate rather than incidental: the zero-assertions are
paired with a cell that requires the same counter to *rise* when the stage does more work. That is
the exact shape this repository prescribes for a zeroed measurement, present here before I went
looking for it.

### The harness is now validated against a claim I did not author

Rounds 1 and 2 measured mutants against **my own predictions**, which is weaker than it looks: a
harness that silently ran nothing would agree with a wrong prediction as readily as a right one. So
this round reproduces a **criteria-named** mutant whose killer the repository already records —
`ancestry_only_ours`, recorded `KilledBy(invalid_branch_history_is_a_typed_conflict)`.

Planted by deleting the `&& facts.theirs.verdict == BranchAncestry::Descends` conjunct. **Killed by
five cells, and `invalid_branch_history_is_a_typed_conflict` is among them** — the record's own claim
reproduced independently. Every kill reported in rounds 1 and 2 now rests on a harness that has been
checked against an external claim, not only against me.

### My prediction was wrong about which cell kills the over-report, and C4's exactness cell is still UNTESTED

Planted: the ancestry walk charges `+2` per compared entry instead of `+1`, so it reports more than
it compared. I predicted `ancestry_refusal_compares_exactly_the_entries_it_reports`.

**It died at three cells and that was not one of them** — `the_ancestry_budget_spans_both_branch_walks`,
`the_ancestry_walk_is_bounded_like_its_checkpoint_sibling`, and
`an_ancestry_stop_outranks_a_divergence_it_never_reached`. The mutation perturbs the **budget spend**,
and the exactness cell reaches the walk through its *unbounded* path, which charges no budget — so
the mutant never touches the code path that cell measures.

The honest consequence: **C4's exactness clause was not attacked by this round.** The mutant died, but
it died somewhere else, and reporting this as "C4 covered" would be exactly the substitution this bead
exists to catch — a kill counted against a clause it never reached. Recorded as an open vector, and
the mutant that would test it must perturb the unbounded path.

### Where the campaign stands across all three rounds

| | |
|---|---|
| mutants planted | **11** |
| semantic kills | **10** |
| structurally prevented (compile failure — **not** a kill by this bead's criteria) | **1** |
| **survivors** | **0** |

### The recurring result, now three times over

Every round has produced the same correction to my own audit: **the discharge is a set of cells, and

## "No green describes this tree" is now a MEASUREMENT — 18 of 67 governed entries have moved, and I did not reimplement the hasher to prove it

Measured at `a1f66a6c2708407b797c62c2d0185496627ad8ba`, cc_1. Comment 2075 corrected the false "there
is no green" and deliberately left one thing as an **inference**: that none of the twenty greens
describes this tree. That inference is discharged here.

### Why I did not compute today's `input_root`, which was the obvious move

`check.sh` does not hash the repository in place. `GOVERNED_ROOT` starts as `$REPO` and is
**re-pointed to a materialized artifact directory** (`scripts/check.sh:965`), which is then hashed by
`evidence.py hash-tree` with two sets of context arguments. Reproducing that by hand means
reimplementing the materialization *and* the context binding, and this repository has already
measured what that costs: `povo`'s population was reported as **154** by a hand-rolled scan and
**430** by the real classifier driven with a hand-built authority, against a true **276**. Same
inputs, wrong instrument, confident answer, twice.

So I did not build a second hasher.

### The weaker claim is sufficient, and it needs no hasher at all

A content root over a set is a function of that set's bytes. **If one governed member's bytes differ,
no earlier root over that set can equal today's — whatever the hasher does.** That is provable with
`git` alone, which is the right instrument because it is the one that already knows the bytes.

Comparing `HEAD` at the newest green's wall time (`7a601011`, 2026-08-04T03:57Z) against now
(`a1f66a6c`):

| | |
|---|---|
| `check.sh` `INPUT_PATHS` entries | **67** |
| tracked paths changed between the two commits | **91** |
| **governed entries whose content changed** | **18 of 67** |

The decisive single member, since one is enough:

```
.beads/issues.jsonl   blob 6cb140cd…  ->  04185ac2…   DIFFERS
```

**Control, because a comparison that cannot report "same" proves nothing:** the same probe run
`HEAD` against `HEAD` on a governed file reports `DIFFERS=False`.

### Two of the eighteen are the lane's own producers, which sharpens the conclusion

Among the changed entries are **`scripts/check.sh` itself and `scripts/evidence.py`** — the script
that defines the governed set and the program that hashes it. `crates` moved by 52 paths, `ci` by 6,
`tools` by 4, `tribunal` by 3, `contracts` by 3.

So the newest green is not merely stale about the tree's *contents*: it was produced by a **different
version of the gate**. Even a hypothetical byte-identical content root would not make it a green for
today's `check.sh`, because today's `check.sh` is not the one that ran.

### What this settles for dt5, and what it does not

**Settled:** none of the twenty greens can serve paragraph 4. Not because they are unattributable —
comment 2075 corrected that; each binds a real `input_root` — but because **every one of them hashed
a governed set that has since demonstrably changed**, and because all twenty were run for
`franken_lean-rur` rather than for this bead.

**Unchanged:** the ask. One `check.sh` run bound to dt5, at a governed input state containing dt5's
evidence. Not mine to launch, and the same run discharges `8o3o`.

**What this does not earn.** It proves *inequality*, never *equality*: it establishes that no green
matches, and would say nothing about which green matched if one did. It compares the two commits'
**tracked** content, so an untracked governed input — the census shards `ci/` work has hit before —
is outside it. The 18 is a count of **entries**, and entries are not paths: `crates` is one entry
covering 52 changed files, so the figure understates the movement by design and is the conservative
direction for this argument. And it says nothing about whether a green run *for* dt5 would pass;
that is what running it is for.

title: DECIDE: extend the Parity Ledger row or supersede it — it cannot express a divergence, an oracle-silent symbol, or an unassessed one
description:
DECISION BEAD, NOT A FIX BEAD. Filed by cc_2 on 2026-07-25 out of franken_lean-9pnc, which stays CLOSED and correctly so - it delivered what it promised and its refusals are sound. This is a defect found by USING it, and the choice below is upstream of any code.

THE DEFECT, PROVEN BY FOUR TESTS IN parity_row_authority.rs (commit 195807a9), not asserted. I tried to encode the project's strongest corpus result in the schema. Four row kinds; ONE expressible.
* AGREEING SYMBOL - works. This is the case the schema was designed around.
* RESTRICTIVE DIVERGENCE - refused. Ours and theirs necessarily differ, so byte-identical blocks it as root-mismatch, and no ComparisonClass means "compared, and they disagreed" - all four assert an act of comparing that concluded in agreement. franken_lean-d17i's unclassified divergences cannot be written down at all.
* ORACLE-SILENT SYMBOL - not expressible, and the nearest encoding LIES. fln-7odd's 1,425 declarations are ones leanchecker legitimately cannot judge. acceptance-only with both roots absent PASSES the verifier while asserting "we compared acceptance and agreed" when the oracle never spoke.
* UNASSESSED SYMBOL - not expressible, and this is the largest by volume. 142,886 of 158,608 decoded were never compared. The schema offers a row asserting comparison, or no row and Block::MissingSymbol. "Missing" and "assessed, no verdict available" are different facts.

So what exists is an AGREEMENT ledger, not a parity ledger: rigorous for the tenth of the corpus where both sides spoke and agreed, silent about divergences, the oracle's limits, and the other ninety percent. D7's "row-per-symbol or it is marketing" turns out to be necessary and not sufficient.

THE TWO THINGS THE SCHEMA MUST LEARN TO SAY, stated as requirements so either option can be judged against them:
1. MEASURED AND UNCALLED. A row whose divergence is observed but whose root cause is deliberately unclassified must read as neither a pass nor a finding. d17i's remaining unclassified rows are exactly this and there is currently no way to write one.
2. LIMITATIONS ON A ROW, NOT ABSENCES FROM IT. The oracle bound (1,425) and the depth-bound inconclusive (kxbj's 65) are facts ABOUT symbols, not missing symbols. Today they can only be absent, which reports them as MissingSymbol - a different and wrong fact.

OPTION A - EXTEND ParityRow. Wire fln-1dxv's existing vocabularies in: OracleVerdict (with its NoAnswer arm), OurVerdict (with its Inconclusive arm), and Scored (Agree / Restrictive / UnsoundlyPermissive / Unscorable). The Parity Ledger predates my use of them and never consumed them; they already model every case above. COST: it changes what every existing refusal MEANS. RootMismatch currently fires on any divergence, which under a per-side-outcome model becomes the normal representation of a finding rather than a defect - so all nine blocking conditions and their mutants need re-derivation, not just re-running. The schema version bumps and every recorded row becomes incomparable. BENEFIT: one schema, one file, continuity of the parts that are right.

OPTION B - SUPERSEDE with a second record. Leave the agreement ledger as-is for what it does well and add a distinct record for non-agreement outcomes. COST: two schemas over one corpus, and the standing risk that a symbol appears in both or neither - which is the completeness problem franken_lean-4l15 exists to prevent, reintroduced one level up. BENEFIT: no existing refusal changes meaning, so nothing already proven has to be re-proven.

WHICH I WOULD PICK: OPTION A. The cost is real but it is a one-time re-derivation of nine refusals I wrote and can re-derive, and it is paid once. Option B's cost is permanent and structural: two records over one corpus is exactly the shape that makes a completeness claim unfalsifiable, and I would rather re-prove nine blocking conditions than defend a cross-record conservation law forever. title: W4 Vellum: Pratt/category parser and exact syntax construction
description:
## Description

Own parser categories, precedences, Pratt tables, parser combinators, expected-token diagnostics, command/term/tactic parsing, antiquotation, ambiguity resolution, full-input accounting, and exact Syntax/SourceInfo construction from lexer tokens.

## Acceptance Criteria

Suites parser_category_inventory, pratt_precedence_model, parse_roundtrip_property, parser_fuzz, parser_corpus_no_mock_e2e cover every category/operator, malformed/truncated input, ambiguity, resource bounds, deterministic diagnostics, and recovery. Named unit/model/property and mutation suites, applicable parser/codec fuzzing, productive 1/8/32 semantic equivalence, typed cancellation/resource/InternalFault nonpublication, real no-mock positive/failure/recovery E2E, canonical semantic NDJSON with separate telemetry, independent validation, and exact cleanup/final state are mandatory.
