comments.author: cc_3
comments.text:
INHERITED OBLIGATION from franken_lean-81oq slice C, from cc_3. Not a note — a constraint this bead has to discharge, and it is cheap to discharge deliberately and expensive to discover late.

crates/fln-syntax/src/recover.rs establishes, by differential over a 20-input corpus, that error recovery may only change what happens to input that was already going to fail; it may never make a previously-rejected file accepted. Both directions are asserted, and three planted defects confirm the test can fail.

WHY IT LANDS ON YOU. That differential currently steps ONE BYTE between trivia runs rather than consuming a token, and I deliberately did NOT wire crates/fln-syntax/src/token.rs::lex_token into it even though slice B had just landed. The reason is a fact about Lean, not a gap in fln-syntax: lexing is parser-driven in places, so there is no total "next token" function to loop. Lean/Parser/Term.lean:91 —

  def docComment := leading_parser ppDedent $ "/--" >> ppSpace >> ... commentBody ... >> ppLine

`/--` is an ordinary table token, but the comment BODY is consumed by commentBody, a dedicated parser the token table knows nothing about. String interpolation is the same shape. So token consumption is driven from YOUR layer, and the acceptance law has to be re-established over whatever drives it.

THE TRAP, stated plainly because it is the kind that passes CI. If you loop lex_token, you refuse the body of every doc comment in the language — and both configurations refuse it identically, so the acceptance differential PASSES and certifies a broken tokenizer. A law only protects the property it states, and this one states acceptance EQUALITY between two configurations, not that either is correct. Re-running the differential is necessary and not sufficient; you also need the positive direction, that real doc comments and interpolated strings are accepted.

WHAT TO DO: re-run recover.rs's differential unchanged over your token consumer. The law is about acceptance, so it does not weaken when the thing between boundaries gets smarter. If it starts failing at that point, your layer has taken acceptance authority it is not allowed to have — treat that as the finding, not as a test to update.

ALSO AVAILABLE TO YOU, already plant-proved, so please consume rather than re-derive: TokenTable with the pin's longest-match (Trie.matchPrefix) and the isToken keyword rule with its >= (not >); the isIdFirst/isIdRest/isLetterLike/isSubScriptAlnum alphabet transcribed with the λ/Π/Σ and ×/÷ exclusions; isIdCont's lookahead; scan_trivia with the tab, isolated-CR and unterminated-block refusals carrying the pin's exact wording; and Attachment/chooseNiceTrailStop for trivia ownership. The lexer emits token extents only and does NOT decide leading/trailing ownership — a second implementation of that rule is a second thing to drift.

comments.author: cc_3
comments.text:
SECOND HANDOFF from franken_lean-81oq (now closed), cc_3. The first comment on this bead carried the acceptance-differential obligation. These are the remaining items 81oq could not reach, with the reason each belongs here rather than in the lexer.

1. ANTIQUOTATIONS. Named in 81oq's scope and deliberately not implemented. tokenAntiquotFn (Lean/Parser/Basic.lean:1777) is a parser-layer function and depends on quotation context — whether we are inside a syntax quotation at all — which the lexer does not and should not have. A lexer-level approximation of it would be a second implementation of a rule the parser owns, and a second implementation is a second thing to drift. That is the same argument that kept the lexer from re-deriving chooseNiceTrailStop's trivia ownership.

2. forbiddenTk?. Parser-context state: a notation forbidding its own leading token to stop left recursion. Modelling it in the lexer would put parser state one layer too low.

3. RE-RUN BOTH DIFFERENTIALS over whatever you use to drive token consumption. This is the important one and it is cheap if done deliberately.
   * crates/fln-syntax/tests/incremental_lex_property.rs asserts that an incremental re-lex equals a full one for every edit, AND that work was actually reused. The second half is not decoration: a relexer that redoes everything satisfies the first perfectly.
   * crates/fln-syntax/src/recover.rs asserts that recovery never changes acceptance, in both directions.
   Both are stated over the driver in crates/fln-syntax/src/run.rs, which is explicitly NOT a faithful Lean tokenizer and says so in its own module docs — Lean's lexing is parser-driven, since docComment := "/--" >> ppSpace >> commentBody >> ppLine consumes its body with a dedicated parser the token table knows nothing about. So there is no total next-token function to loop, and the real driver is yours.

   THE TRAP, restated because it passes CI: if you loop lex_token you refuse the body of every doc comment in the language, and BOTH configurations refuse it identically, so the acceptance differential PASSES and certifies a broken tokenizer. Re-running it is necessary and not sufficient; you also need the positive direction, that real doc comments and interpolated strings are ACCEPTED.

WHAT YOU CAN CONSUME RATHER THAN RE-DERIVE, all plant-proved:
* TokenTable with the pin's longest-match and max_token_len, which is a LOOKAHEAD BOUND and not a convenience accessor — the incremental restart is derived from it, in bytes not characters.
* The isToken keyword rule with its >= rather than >. That one character is the whole rule; written > , every keyword becomes an identifier.
* isIdFirst/isIdRest/isLetterLike/isSubScriptAlnum transcribed with the lambda/Pi/Sigma and multiplication/division-sign exclusions, and isIdCont's lookahead.
* All literal forms including raw strings, with the pin's exact refusal wording.
* scan_trivia with the tab, isolated-CR and unterminated-block refusals.
* lex_run_from, for resuming a run at any trivia event start. lexer_state_model proves resumption is faithful there and — the other direction — that resuming at a token offset is NOT, so the restriction is a constraint and not a convention.
* Attachment and chooseNiceTrailStop for trivia ownership. The lexer emits token extents only and does not decide leading/trailing ownership.
* LexBudget, if you want the same FL-INV-07 story at parser scale: exceeding it is Inconclusive with a ResourceUsage, never a rejection, and Inconclusive::diagnostic stays None on a clean file.

THE INCREMENTAL DAMAGE BOUND, since a parser will want its own version and the lexer's took a differential to get right. Three independent terms, none subsuming another: the longest token in the table (trie walks run past what they emit); overlapped-plus-one (unbounded constructs, whose extent covers what they read); and the earliest refusal at or before the edit (FAILED unbounded scans, which read to end of text and consume almost nothing — an unterminated guillemet at offset 4 scans the whole file and emits a two-byte refusal). Then verify the restart point rather than assuming it: one valid in the old text can sit inside a construct in the new one. Suffix reuse needs no bound — it is sound by the forward-only-reading theorem.

comments.author: cc_3
comments.text:
CLAIMED by cc_3, 2026-07-25. Recording the governing epistemic constraint FIRST, before any code, because it is the one that decides whether this bead's evidence is worth anything.

A DIFFERENTIAL ONLY PROVES AGREEMENT, NEVER CORRECTNESS. If both sides are wrong the same way, you get a green light.

That is not an abstract caution. franken_lean-81oq produced a concrete instance of it, and this bead is where the same trap gets set a second time. A Pratt parser is precisely the place: incremental-vs-from-scratch, one-thread-vs-many, recovery-on-vs-off are all comparisons of my implementation against MY OWN implementation. Every one of them passes when a shared mistake sits underneath.

The 81oq instance, kept because it is specific enough to be useful. Looping lex_token over a file refuses the body of every doc comment in the language, because docComment's body is consumed by a dedicated parser the token table knows nothing about (Lean/Parser/Term.lean:91). Both the recovering and non-recovering configurations refuse it IDENTICALLY, so the acceptance differential passes with a completely broken tokenizer underneath. Re-running that differential here is necessary and not sufficient.

WHAT FOLLOWS FOR THIS BEAD, and I will hold myself to it:
1. Every self-differential (incremental vs from-scratch, 1/8/32, recovery on/off) must be paired with a POSITIVE oracle that is not me. Where the pin defines the shape — precedence, associativity, category boundaries, which constructs are terms versus commands — the assertion goes against the PIN'S OWN behaviour, not against a second run of my parser. A shared mistake cannot then look like success, because the pin does not share it.
2. Every self-differential must also state what it does NOT establish, in its own module docs, so nobody downstream reads "incremental equals from-scratch" as "the parse is right".
3. Where the pin cannot be consulted cheaply, the oracle is the pin's SOURCE as data: precedence numbers and category declarations are extractable, and a table transcribed with citations is a weaker oracle than running the pin but a much stronger one than my own second opinion.

The corollary that bit me in 81oq, worth stating in the same place: an argument is not a substitute for a differential either. I reasoned that a reused literal refusal could not be reached, wrote the reasoning into a code comment, and the property suite found the case within minutes. Both halves of this hold at once — a differential cannot prove correctness, and an argument cannot replace a differential.

TWO CONSTRAINTS INHERITED FROM THE GREEN TREE, carried as constraints and not notes:
* LOSSLESSNESS IS THROUGH THE crlfToLf MAP, not byte-equality with the raw file. The green tree from franken_lean-tkr2 reproduces the file exactly by reconstructing through SourceView, and every position it holds is a VIEW position. Exact syntax construction has to preserve that same recoverability. The specific temptation in a Pratt loop is to REBUILD spans from what a production consumed rather than carry the extents the lexer already produced — and a rebuilt span is where the crlf mapping silently stops being invertible, because the arithmetic is done in whichever coordinate space was nearest to hand.
* EXACTNESS IS WHAT MAKES THE DAMAGE BOUND WORTH ANYTHING. If construction is not exact, incremental reparse cannot be proved equal to a from-scratch parse, and the bound from franken_lean-tkr2 plus the three-term lexical bound from 81oq become decoration. The bound is only load-bearing while the two parses are comparable at all.

comments.author: cc_3
comments.text:
SLICE A LANDED — commit 97c3334, crates/fln-parse/src/state.rs, 12 tests. Plus 4ad4402, the two graph edges fln-parse -> fln-syntax and fln-parse -> fln-core (bookkeeping on the vrmi precedent; the declared ranks 8 -> 7 -> 0 already implied the direction, and cod_2's in-flight ci/ files were untouched because WORKSPACE_GRAPH.txt itself was unmodified).

PIN FACTS, with citations, recorded here so a successor does not re-derive them. All from Lean/Parser/Basic.lean at v4.32.0.

THE THREE PLACES UPSTREAM IS NOT A TEXTBOOK PRATT PARSER, and each is a plausible mistake:
1. Precedence is a property of PARSERS, not tokens (:1953-1965, upstream's own comment). There is no binding-power table keyed by token. Building one is a different algorithm that agrees on simple arithmetic and diverges on anything precedence-restricted.
2. Leading parsers check precedence TOO, not just trailing ones (same comment: "in the original Pratt's algorithm, precedences are only checked before calling trailing parsers. In our implementation, leading *and* trailing parsers check the precedence").
3. An ambiguity is PRESERVED, not resolved. longestMatchFn scores candidates lexicographically as (end position, success-beats-error, priority) at :1418, and on a TIE both are kept under a choiceKind node (longestMatchMkResult, :1439) with lhsPrec set to the MINIMUM of the tied candidates' — upstream's reasoning verbatim: "it is not clear what the precedence of a choice node should be, so we conservatively take the minimum".

Rule 3 is the one to protect. A parser that took the first winner yields a perfectly well-formed tree with the ambiguity silently gone, and the elaborator — which is what resolves ambiguity in this language — never learns a decision existed. Nothing downstream can detect the loss.

OTHER PIN FACTS ALREADY READ, for the slices below:
* checkPrecFn (:160) succeeds if c.prec <= prec, i.e. the CONTEXT precedence is a floor. checkLhsPrecFn (:169) succeeds if s.lhsPrec >= prec. Message for both, verbatim: "unexpected token at this precedence level; consider parenthesizing the term".
* runLongestMatchParser initialises lhsPrec to maxPrec in the LEADING case, because a leading parser has no left-hand side to inherit from.
* mkResult (:1903): a production must leave exactly one node above the mark; a different count is wrapped in nullKind. Upstream's own comment there is "throw error instead?", so this is a place the Reference is unsure and we match its behaviour rather than its doubt.
* leadingParserAux (:1908): when NO parser is applicable it consumes the leading token anyway and flags mkUnexpectedTokenError. So full-input accounting survives an unparseable leading position — it does not stall.
* trailingLoop (:1928-1949) has TWO error-discarding rules and both are load-bearing. Token parse errors from the indexed lookup are discarded and the loop breaks, restoring position, because "the error will be flagged when the next leading position is parsed, unless the token is in fact valid there (e.g. EOI at command level)". And a NON-CONSUMING parse error is discarded with `left` restored, which is "necessary for fallback parsers like app that pretend to be always applicable". A parser that reported either would produce an error for every fallback that declined.
* indexed (:1697) + LeadingIdentBehavior (:1643) — default / symbol / both. This is the controlled punning that lets tactic names be identifiers, so `apply` needs no reserved symbol. behavior=symbol looks up the identifier's own value first and falls back to identKind; behavior=both runs BOTH and concatenates, with a guard against running the same parsers twice when val == identKind.
* categoryParserFn (:1732) and ParserCategory (:1675): a category carries declName, the kinds set, the Pratt tables, and its behavior. prattParser = leadingParser then trailingLoop.

SLICE PLAN, each landing independently green:
* A. DONE — state, precedence, longest_match resolution.
* B. The Pratt loop: leadingParser + trailingLoop, including both error-discarding rules and the consume-and-flag behaviour when nothing is applicable. The trailing loop's error discipline is the part that cannot be guessed.
* C. Categories and the indexed lookup with all three LeadingIdentBehavior variants.
* D. EXACT Syntax construction from lexer tokens, with the round-trip property. The constraint carried in from tkr2: losslessness is through the crlfToLf map, not byte-equality with the raw file, and the temptation in a Pratt loop is to REBUILD spans from what a production consumed rather than carry the extents the lexer already produced. A rebuilt span is where the crlf mapping stops being invertible, because the arithmetic gets done in whichever coordinate space was nearest to hand.
* E. The named suites: parser_category_inventory, pratt_precedence_model, parse_roundtrip_property, parser_fuzz. parser_corpus_no_mock_e2e goes to its own bead like franken_lean-jbru did, since the registration points are cod_2's ci/ domain.

THE ORACLE DISCIPLINE, restated as a commitment for slices B-E: where the pin defines the shape — precedence, associativity, category boundaries, which constructs are terms versus commands — the assertion goes against the pin's own behaviour or its source read as data, NOT against a second run of my parser. Slice A's assertions are all of that kind: every one names the pin rule and line it encodes. No self-differential has been used yet, and when one is (incremental vs from-scratch, 1/8/32) it will be paired with a positive oracle and will say in its own docs what it does not establish.

comments.author: cc_3
comments.text:
SLICE B LANDED — commit 7e07d6d, crates/fln-parse/src/pratt.rs. fln-parse at 22 tests.

THIS COMMENT SORTS EVERY CLAIM IN THE SLICE BY WHAT KIND OF EVIDENCE IT HAS, because "the part that cannot be guessed" is only worth something if a reader can tell which parts were observed and which were read. Three grades:
  (A) OBSERVED — I ran the pinned lean binary at ~/.elan/toolchains/leanprover--lean4---v4.32.0/bin/lean on a probe file and read its diagnostics.
  (B) TRANSCRIBED — read from Lean/Parser/Basic.lean at the pinned tag, with a line number. A reading of source, not a run.
  (C) MINE — reasoned to, not present in the pin. Flagged in the code as a divergence.

=== GRADE A: OBSERVED AGAINST THE RUNNING PIN ===

A1. RULE 1, a token error at a trailing position is discarded and produces no diagnostic.
    Probe: a file containing only `def f : Nat := 1` and a newline.
    Observed: ZERO diagnostics. At the trailing position after `1` the indexed lookup peeks and hits end of input, which is a token error. Were it reported, the file would carry "unexpected end of input". It does not.

A2. RULE 1's stated REASON, that the error resurfaces at the next leading position.
    Probe: `def f : Nat := 1` then a line containing `@@@`.
    Observed: exactly one error — `unexpected token '@'; expected command` at line 2 column 0, which is the next LEADING position, not the trailing position of the previous term. So the discard is not a loss of information; it is a deferral, and the deferral is visible.

A3. RULE 2, a non-consuming trailing failure is discarded and the left operand survives.
    Probe: `#check 1 = 2 = 3`. `=` is infix:50, so its arguments sit at 51; the second `=` runs checkLhsPrec 51 against an lhsPrec of 50, and checkLhsPrec is an epsilon parser, so it fails having consumed nothing.
    Observed: exactly one error — `unexpected token '='; expected command` at column 13, the leftover `=`. So the precedence failure emitted NOTHING of its own, and `1 = 2` was returned intact for the command level to trip over the remainder.
    Reproduced twice more: `#check (1 : Nat) < 2 < 3` gives the same shape at the second `<`, and a user-declared `infix:50 " ## "` with `#check 1 ## 2 ## 3` gives it at the second `##`. Three independent non-associative operators, same behaviour.

A4. leadingParserAux consumes the offending token BEFORE flagging it.
    Probe: `def f : Nat := 1` then `#check @@@`.
    Observed: the error is at end of input, not at the `@`. The `@` was consumed and the scan moved on, which is what keeps accounting total — flagging without consuming means being asked the same position again forever.

A5. The category name appears in the diagnostic, so mkUnexpectedTokenError's argument is the category.
    Observed across probes: `unexpected token '+'; expected term` and `unexpected token '@'; expected command`. Two different categories, same shape.

A6. LeadingIdentBehavior's punning is real, which is evidence for slice C rather than this one.
    Probe: `def apply : Nat := 1` then `#check apply`.
    Observed: no error. A tactic name is usable as an identifier, which is exactly what the behavior field exists to allow.

=== GRADE A-NEGATIVE: OBSERVED ABSENCE, WHICH IS WEAKER ===

A7. I could NOT get checkPrec's message — "unexpected token at this precedence level; consider parenthesizing the term" — to surface in any probe. It appears nowhere in the pin's source except its own definition in Basic.lean. Every non-associativity probe produced the command-level "unexpected token" instead, because rule 2 discards precisely that error.
    I am NOT claiming the message is unreachable. I am recording that I did not observe it reaching a user. That is an absence of evidence, not evidence of absence, and if someone later finds a construct that surfaces it, nothing above needs revising — only this paragraph does.

=== GRADE B: TRANSCRIBED FROM PIN SOURCE, WITH LINES ===

B1. prattParser = leadingParser then, only if no error, trailingLoop (:1969-1975).
B2. leadingParserAux's structure: indexed lookup, propagate a token error, unindexed parsers appended, empty -> consume-and-flag, else longestMatchFn then mkResult (:1908-1921).
B3. trailingLoop's structure and both discard rules with upstream's own comments (:1928-1949). The comments are why I knew what to probe for; the probes are why I believe the code does it.
B4. mkResult wraps a wrong node count in nullKind rather than erroring, and upstream's own comment there is "throw error instead?" — a place the Reference is unsure, so we match its behaviour and not its doubt (:1903).
B5. The trailing loop's restore arithmetic on the non-consuming path: `s.restore (iniSz - 1) iniPos |>.pushSyntax left`, where iniSz was captured BEFORE popping left (:1947).

=== GRADE C: MINE, FLAGGED AS A DIVERGENCE IN THE CODE ===

C1. A no-progress guard in the trailing loop. Upstream's trailingLoop is a `partial def` that recurses unconditionally on success, so a trailing production that succeeded while consuming nothing loops forever there; upstream tolerates it because well-formed grammars do not contain one. I stop the chain instead, on the grounds that a hung parser is a worse failure than a rejected grammar. This converts a hang into a truncated parse, and the test names it as ours rather than the pin's.
C2. The Grammar trait as the seam between the loop and the lookup. Upstream passes PrattParsingTables directly. The trait exists so this slice does not depend on slice C's indexing; it is a structural choice with no behavioural content, but it IS a choice.

SEVEN PLANTS, all killed, and each discard rule planted in BOTH directions — because "discards too much" and "discards nothing" are different defects with different symptoms, and only one of them looks like a missing diagnostic:
  rule 1 not applied -> a diagnostic exists that should not.
  rule 1 over-applied -> the LEADING token error vanishes too. That asymmetry is upstream's and is the whole reason the rule needs stating.
  rule 2 not applied -> the precedence failure becomes user-visible.
  rule 2 over-applied -> consuming failures are swallowed, so malformed input parses.
  rule 2 restoring without pushing left back -> left "nothing", right "atom lhs". The operand silently vanishes from the tree.
  flag without consuming -> the position never advances.
  entering the trailing loop after a leading failure -> the leading error is overwritten.

NO SELF-DIFFERENTIAL IS USED IN THIS SLICE. Every assertion is against grade A or grade B evidence. When incremental-vs-from-scratch and 1/8/32 arrive in slice E they will be paired with a positive oracle and will state in their own docs what they do not establish.

REMAINING: C categories and the indexed lookup with all three LeadingIdentBehavior variants (A6 above is the observation it has to reproduce). D exact Syntax construction and the round-trip. E the named suites, with parser_corpus_no_mock_e2e splitting to its own bead on the franken_lean-jbru boundary — same registration points, same owner, and cod_3 is already paying lane debt on fln-giap.

comments.author: cc_3
comments.text:
SLICE C LANDED — commit f257887, crates/fln-parse/src/category.rs. fln-parse 22 -> 34 tests.

THE POINT OF THIS SLICE, and why the negatives were the whole job. Controlled punning means a keyword-like identifier is legal in some positions and not others. A rule that is TOO PERMISSIVE passes every positive test anyone can write, because permissiveness shows up only as a MISSING rejection — there is nothing to write down that fails. So each variant is pinned by a pair, and five of the six plants are permissiveness defects.

=== GRADE A: OBSERVED AGAINST THE RUNNING PIN ===

The method, which is reusable and worth recording. `declare_syntax_cat` accepts a behaviour on its surface syntax — `declare_syntax_cat foo (behavior := both)` / `(behavior := symbol)` / absent for default (Parser/Syntax.lean:110-112, elaborated at Elab/Syntax.lean:310-318). So I can construct all three variants directly rather than hunting for builtin categories that happen to use each one.

The discriminator: give the ident-indexed and name-indexed productions DIFFERENT SHAPES, so which one matched is visible in whether the file parses. With `syntax (name := X) ident " !" : cat` and `syntax (name := Y) &"pun" : cat`, the input `run pun` parses only if the `pun`-indexed production is available, and is refused with `unexpected end of input; expected '!'` if only identKind is. Reversing which production carries the `!` discriminates the other direction.

C1. Result table, every cell an observation:
      behaviour   production indexed under `pun`   identKind fallback
      default     REFUSED                          available
      symbol      available                        REFUSED
      both        available                        available
    Each REFUSED came from an actual refusal from the pin, not from reasoning. Each is now a test with the word NEGATIVE in its assertion message.

C2. Which behaviour each builtin category registers, read from source and consistent with C1's mechanics: term (Extension.lean:590), command (:595) and level (Level.lean:17) all omit the argument and therefore get default; tactic registers .both explicitly (Term/Basic.lean:33); attr registers .symbol (Attr.lean:20).

C3. `def apply : Nat := 1` then `#check apply` parses with zero errors — a tactic name used as a term identifier, which is default behaviour in the term category doing exactly what the field exists for.

C4. `example (trivial : True) : True := by trivial` parses with zero errors, and so does `example (trivial : True) : True := by exact trivial`. With `trivial` bound as a hypothesis the TACTIC still runs in tactic position, and the identifier still resolves in term position. That is .both offering both sets, observed.

=== GRADE A-NEGATIVE: OBSERVED ABSENCE ===

C5. I could not observe both's DEDUP GUARD. Two identical `ident` productions in one category parse with NO ambiguity error, because a choice node is invisible until something elaborates it and my probe categories have no elaborator. So the guard's presence cannot be confirmed or refuted by this method.

=== GRADE B: TRANSCRIBED, WITH LINES ===

B1. The dedup guard itself: `if val == identKind then (s, as) -- avoid running the same parsers twice` (Basic.lean:1717). Asserted in our tests from the pin's source plus what slice A establishes about ties, and NOT from observation — see C5.
    Its consequence is not obvious and is the reason it matters: without the guard the identKind productions appear TWICE in the candidate list and tie by construction (same position, same success, same priority), so longest_match builds a choice node. The parser manufactures an ambiguity out of a file that has none, and the elaborator then reports a genuine-looking ambiguity error. The plant shows it directly — left ["identProduction","identProduction"], right ["identProduction"].
B2. The trailing lookup passes LeadingIdentBehavior.default EXPLICITLY, whatever the category's behaviour is (Basic.lean:1932). This is a negative for the category rather than for a variant: the field is called *Leading*IdentBehavior and it means it. Punning applies to the position that OPENS a construct, not to positions inside one; a category applying its behaviour to trailing lookups would let a keyword-like identifier act as an operator.
B3. Unindexed productions are appended to the indexed ones and are always offered (`tables.leadingParsers ++ ps`, :1912). They exist because some productions have no first token — upstream's example at :1958 is `syntax term:51 "≤" ident "<" term "|" term : index`, whose first-token set "is any token that can start a term, but this set is always changing".
B4. The branch shapes indexed handles: atom by its symbol, ident by the behaviour, node by its kind, anything else no productions, and a peek failure propagated as an error (:1702-1723).

=== GRADE C: MINE ===

C6. TokenMap is a BTreeMap, so candidate order is deterministic. The resolution rule is order-independent for a WINNER, but the order decides which of two equal candidates is reported first, and determinism is a contract (FL-INV-01). Upstream uses its own TokenMap; this is a container choice with a determinism reason, not a behavioural claim.
C7. Keeping `None` and `Some(empty)` distinguishable in the map. Upstream's `map.get?` already has this distinction; making it explicit in our API is mine, and it is load-bearing because symbol's fallback branches on exactly it.

SIX PLANTS, all killed. Five are permissiveness: default also offering the name-indexed production; symbol also offering identKind (the "be helpful" mistake, and the one I would expect a reimplementation to make); both losing the dedup guard; the trailing lookup honouring the category's behaviour; and symbol never falling back to identKind. The sixth erases slice B's rule 1 by collapsing an unlexable token into an empty lookup.

STILL NO SELF-DIFFERENTIAL ANYWHERE IN THIS BEAD. Every assertion so far is grade A or grade B.

REMAINING: D exact Syntax construction from lexer tokens plus the round-trip property — carrying tkr2's constraint that losslessness is through the crlfToLf map, and that the temptation is to rebuild spans rather than carry the lexer's extents. E the named suites parser_category_inventory, pratt_precedence_model, parse_roundtrip_property and parser_fuzz, with parser_corpus_no_mock_e2e splitting to its own bead on the franken_lean-jbru boundary.

comments.author: cc_3
comments.text:
SLICE D LANDED — commit e493c7d0, crates/fln-parse/src/build.rs. fln-parse 34 -> 45 tests.

THE MEASUREMENT, which is the most useful thing in this slice. I planted the rebuilt-span defect — pos taken from the start of the leading trivia, spans still tiling the file with no gaps — and ran the two relevant tests SEPARATELY:

    the round-trip test           PASSED
    the extent-comparison test    FAILED

So "the round trip cannot see a rebuilt span" is not an argument I am making, it is something I measured. Rebuilt spans are internally consistent, tile the file, and reproduce every byte. They are wrong only in WHERE THE TOKEN IS — which is what a diagnostic underlines. A suite with only the round trip would have been fully green while the caret landed on the whitespace before every token in the language.

This is the same shape as the finding that opened this bead, in a new place: the round trip is a self-consistency check, and a self-consistency check passes whenever the thing it checks is consistently wrong. What pins exactness is comparing each leaf's pos and end_pos against the LEXER's extents — an external reference, not the tree's own account of itself.

WHAT CARRIES RATHER THAN REBUILDS, concretely:
* SourceInfo comes from fln_syntax::attach, whose trivia-ownership rule (chooseNiceTrailStop) was plant-proved under franken_lean-tkr2. There is exactly one implementation of that rule in the program; a production that re-derived it would be a second one, and the two would drift.
* An identifier's raw_val is the lexer's ByteSpan verbatim.
* A literal's atom value is the source SLICE, because upstream's mkNodeToken uses c.extract. A rendering of the literal's value would lose the spelling, and 0x1F and 31 are the same value with different source.
* An interior node stores NO position; its span comes from its arguments. A stored one would be a second place for a span to live and therefore a second place to be wrong.
* leaf_for's only arithmetic is reading fields out of an attachment entry. That is deliberate: there is nowhere for a coordinate-space mistake to happen because no coordinate is computed.

LOSSLESS HELD LITERALLY. The asserted chain is raw -> view -> lex -> attach -> tree -> reconstruct the VIEW -> reconstruct_original -> raw. And in the SAME test, for any file the view actually normalized, the raw comparison is asserted to FAIL. Without that half a round trip written against raw bytes has exactly two futures — it fails on every CRLF file, or it gets quietly relaxed until it passes — and neither one tells a reader that the map is load-bearing. Now the test says so itself.

A second test walks the divergence directly rather than in aggregate: for `g` on the second line of a CRLF file, the leaf's position mapped through to_original lands on the `g` in the RAW bytes, and the UNMAPPED view position lands somewhere else. The two differ by a real number of bytes, and that is the whole reason the map is not optional.

A FIXTURE OF MINE WAS WRONG AND THE ATTACHMENT LAYER CORRECTED IT, recorded in the test itself. I wrote `def    f` and expected `f` to carry four spaces of leading trivia. It carries none: chooseNiceTrailStop attaches same-line whitespace BACKWARD as the previous token's TRAILING trivia, so leading trivia exists only after a newline. The fixture now spans one, and the test discovers which tokens have leading trivia rather than assuming which one does. Worth recording because the wrong intuition here is natural — "the spaces before f belong to f" — and it is exactly backwards.

FIVE PLANTS, all killed. Besides the rebuilt span: a literal rendered from its kind instead of sliced from source; an ident's raw_val rebuilt instead of carried; an interior node storing a position; and descending extents silently sorted rather than refused, since a repaired attachment is the failure mode that reconstructs cleanly and misplaces everything.

EVIDENCE GRADES for this slice. Everything here is grade B (transcribed) or structural, with no grade-A observation, and that is honest rather than a gap: the claims are about OUR representation — which field carries which span, whether a node stores a position — and the pin cannot be observed to settle them because upstream's Syntax stores substrings where ours stores spans, a representation divergence already recorded on fln-syntax's ByteSpan. What the pin DOES settle, and what is cited: mkNodeToken uses c.extract for a literal's value, and Syntax.node carries no position. The exactness assertions are checked against our own lexer's extents, which is an external reference for the construction layer even though it is internal to the program.

REMAINING ON THIS BEAD: E, the named suites parser_category_inventory, pratt_precedence_model, parse_roundtrip_property and parser_fuzz. parser_corpus_no_mock_e2e splits to its own bead on the franken_lean-jbru boundary — same registration points, same owner — and cod_3 is already paying lane debt on fln-giap, so the lane work is landing in the right lanes.

comments.author: cc_3
comments.text:
CLOSING STATEMENT — fln-ffam, cc_3, 2026-07-25. crates/fln-parse at 63 tests across 5 targets. Gates green: fmt, clippy --all-targets -D warnings, cargo test, structure-guard 6/6.

SLICE E LANDED — commit 4747c803. The two suites that carry the weight are both pinned against the pin rather than against my own parser.

PARSER_CATEGORY_INVENTORY is a RE-DERIVATION, not a frozen list, because a completeness claim fails one characteristic way: an inventory that lists what its author thought of is complete with respect to nothing. The suite walks the pin's source at TEST TIME, extracts every category it registers, and fails when the pin has one the inventory does not. The other direction fails too — a stale row claims a category that does not exist — and each category's BEHAVIOUR is checked, since attr=symbol and tactic=both are not guessable from their names.
  Worth recording: the fixture was generated by a Python regex extractor and the suite re-derives with hand-rolled Rust string scanning. Two independent extractors agreeing on 10 builtin and 25 declared categories is evidence, not a tautology. Without the pin the suite SKIPS with a printed reason, because a completeness suite that quietly passes when it cannot see its oracle is publishing evidence it did not gather.
  Three plants killed: a dropped category (missing), an invented one (stale), a wrong behaviour (per-category).

PRATT_PRECEDENCE_MODEL is pinned against SIX VALUES THE PINNED BINARY PRINTED, because this is where the differential-limits law bites hardest — a model wrong in the same direction as the parser built from it produces perfect agreement, and agreement is all a round trip measures.
    2 + 3 * 4              -> 14     (* tighter than +;  else 20)
    2 * 3 + 4              -> 10     (same, other order; else 14)
    2 * 3 ^ 2              -> 18     (^ tighter than *;  else 36)
    2 ^ 3 ^ 2              -> 512    (^ right-assoc;     else 64)
    10 - 3 - 4             -> 3      (- left-assoc;      else 11)
    true || false && false -> true   (&& tighter than ||; else false)
  The model groups, a tiny evaluator computes, the value must equal what the pin printed. EVERY ROW IS PROVED DISCRIMINATING by inverting the table and checking the recorded wrong value actually appears — and one candidate was REJECTED for carrying no information, `true && false || true`, which is true under either grouping. A table of discriminating cases is only as good as its worst row.
  Two declared precedences were not what I would have written from memory, which is the whole argument for citing over recalling: ^ is infixr:80 and not 75, and && and || are infixL and not infixr (Notation.lean:291, 412, 413).

THREE DEFECTS OF MINE THAT SLICE E FOUND rather than confirmed, which is the useful part:
1. The precedence model had only the RIGHT side's requirement, so `1 = 2 = 3` chained happily as ((1=2)=3). The left requirement IS checkLhsPrec, so its absence was slice A's rule 2 — leading AND trailing check precedence — going missing exactly where it is observable. Both sides are now modelled from how the pin desugars a fixity declaration.
2. Flipping only precedence does not produce the wrong value for `2 ^ 3 ^ 2`, because both operators are the same and associativity alone decides. The inverted table flips both now. Caught by my own discriminating-case check, which is the anti-vacuity guard doing its job on the oracle rather than on the subject.
3. PARSER_FUZZ FOUND A REAL DEFECT IN SLICE A. longest_match's AMBIGUOUS path never set the position: restore had put the cursor back and the choice node was pushed without moving it forward. The Pratt loop's no-progress guard would then stop the trailing chain, SILENTLY TRUNCATING THE PARSE on exactly the inputs where the language needs the elaborator to choose. Fixed; the unit test now asserts the position too, with a note that the fuzz suite found it and the unit test did not.

PARSE_ROUNDTRIP_PROPERTY holds tkr2's constraint over 6000 seeded inputs — tree reconstructs the VIEW, view reconstructs the FILE, and for any normalized input the raw comparison is asserted to FAIL. It also carries the exactness assertion deliberately, because slice D MEASURED that the round trip is green for rebuilt spans, and without it the strongest-looking suite in the bead would have been its weakest evidence. Anti-vacuity floors require normalized inputs, inputs with tokens, and at least 50 positions genuinely diverging between view and file so the mapping cannot pass as an identity.

PARSER_FUZZ reuses the lexer suites' seeded splitmix64 rather than inventing a generator. D1 forbids a property-testing crate, and the constraint is right anyway: a fuzz failure nobody can reproduce is a rumour.

=== THE BEAD'S FIVE NAMED SUITES ===
  parser_category_inventory   5 tests   present
  pratt_precedence_model      6 tests   present
  parse_roundtrip_property    3 tests   present
  parser_fuzz                 4 tests   present
  parser_corpus_no_mock_e2e   SPLIT to franken_lean-urd1 (cod_2's ci/ domain)

=== WHAT THIS BEAD ESTABLISHED, BY EVIDENCE GRADE ===
GRADE A, observed by running the pinned binary: both trailing-loop discard rules and rule 1's stated reason; consume-then-flag at a leading position; the category-name in the "expected" diagnostic; a full 3x2 discrimination table for LeadingIdentBehavior's three variants; six precedence/associativity values. Plus one grade-A-NEGATIVE recorded honestly — I could not get checkPrec's message to surface in any probe, and I did not claim it unreachable.
GRADE B, transcribed with line numbers: the resolution law and its score tuple; the choice-node tie rule and its minimum-lhsPrec; mkResult's nullKind; both's dedup guard (probed for and NOT observable, since a spurious choice node is invisible without an elaborator); the trailing lookup's explicit Default.
GRADE C, mine and flagged in the code: the trailing loop's no-progress guard (upstream is a partial def that would loop); the Grammar trait as the seam; TokenMap as a BTreeMap for determinism.

=== 24 PLANTED DEFECTS ACROSS THE BEAD, all confirmed to fail before reverting ===
The ones worth remembering are the plausible ones: scoring priority before position and success before length (both intuitive, both wrong); resolving a tie by taking the first, which discards an ambiguity the elaborator is supposed to resolve and leaves a perfectly well-formed tree; symbol behaviour also offering identKind, the "be helpful" mistake; and rebuilt spans, which round-trip perfectly.

=== HANDED ON ===
franken_lean-urd1 holds the e2e lane, with one lane-specific warning carried onto it: parser_category_inventory READS the pin and skips typed without it, so a lane that reports that skip as a pass would publish evidence it did not gather.
fln-okfb is the dependent — dynamic registration, interleaving, callbacks and the differential join seam — and inherits the differential-limits law that opened this bead, since a join seam is where two implementations get compared and a shared mistake is hardest to see.

title: structure-guard test fixtures are retained unconditionally: 16,370 dirs / 11 GB in /data/tmp, growing ~1.3 GB per hour
description:
AUDIT FINDING, measured not inherited, by cc_3 on 2026-07-26 at HEAD 6ad070b6.
FILED, NOT FIXED: the repair surface is tools/structure-guard/tests/common/mod.rs, which
is cod_2's, and every candidate repair either deletes files or changes fixture identity.
Nothing has been changed and nothing has been removed.

THE FINDING. Every fixture-based structure-guard test leaves its scratch directory in
/data/tmp permanently, on PASS as well as on failure, and nothing ever reclaims it. At
the measurement:

  16,370 directories matching /data/tmp/structure-guard-test-*
  11 GB total, ~0.7 MB each
  oldest 2026-07-24 00:54:44, newest 2026-07-26 16:52:05

Growth is not historical. Per-hour, by directory mtime at 2026-07-26 ~17:00:

  last 0-1h  1884      last 3-4h  1046
  last 1-2h   668      last 4-5h   378
  last 2-3h   167      last 5-6h   173

Roughly 1.3 GB/hour under active swarm use. Disk was at 94% (839G/906G) when measured.
For scale, the orchestrator's parked tally of every agent worktree and scratch target dir
on the box was about 11 GB - this single pile matches all of it, and unlike those it is
still growing.

RETENTION IS UNCONDITIONAL AND DELIBERATE, NOT A LEAK ON THE FAILURE PATH. The tail of
Fixture::materialize() in tools/structure-guard/tests/common/mod.rs is

  eprintln!("retained structure-guard fixture: {}", root.display());

reached on the success path, with no cleanup anywhere in the file and no Drop impl. The
word "retained" says the intent plainly: a fixture is kept so a failing guard run can be
inspected afterwards, which is a genuinely good property and is why this is a design
question and not a bug report. What is missing is any bound - retention applies equally
to the ~99% of runs that pass and are never looked at, and no run ever reclaims an older
one.

WHY IT ACCELERATED. seeded.rs is 61 KB of planted-defect tests and each materializes its
own fixture, so one `cargo test -p structure-guard` costs on the order of a hundred
directories. Multiply by six panes re-running the suite all day. I CONTRIBUTED TO THIS
PILE MYSELF while verifying fln-cross-tree-baked-root-k60n and e7323b51; the finding is
not a complaint about anyone else's habits.

WHY I DID NOT REPAIR IT. Three shapes, all needing a ruling first:
  1. Clean up on success, keep on failure. Smallest and probably right, but it means
     writing deletion code, and RULE 1 plus the standing swarm rule on unauthored
     destructive instructions make that a decision for Jeffrey, not an implementation
     detail I quietly add.
  2. Reuse a stable root per test. Collides with OpenOptions::create_new(true) at
     mod.rs:~147, which exists so a fixture can never silently overwrite - a property
     worth more than the disk.
  3. Cap the pile: keep the newest N. Needs a reaper nobody owns, and reintroduces
     deletion.
A fourth, non-deleting mitigation exists and may be the cheapest honest one: let the root
be overridden by an environment variable so a pane can point its fixtures at a path it is
willing to have reclaimed, leaving today's default untouched.

WHAT THIS BEAD DOES NOT ESTABLISH. I did not measure how often a retained fixture is
actually READ after a failure, so the value side of the trade is unquantified and the
"~99% never looked at" figure above is an inference from pass rates, not an observation.

title: W3: fln check-olean — the Independent Judge CLI and the G1 evidence bundle
description:
Ship fln check-olean — the Independent Judge (§8.6, G1): the standalone auditor that re-checks an entire olean set (all of mathlib in minutes) on a kernel that shares no code, no compiler, and no bignum with the thing it is checking — the program FIRST public artifact, shipped before FrankenLean has elaborated a single file.

Composition: Grimoire read (full-recheck validation level) + Crucible K1/K2 + fln-checker per consensus policy + receipts + optional certificate emission. CLI contract: stable exit codes, --json output (versioned schema), per-declaration verdicts with stable error classes, a summary receipt binding the input set hash, engine build hashes, policy, and totals; --receipts writes the receipt set + transparency-log append. Performance: PG-1 — full mathlib olean set <= 5 min on the 32-core profile, <= 25 min single-thread.

This bead includes the G1 gate evidence assembly: zero acceptance divergence against the Reference toolchain across the full mathlib olean set at the pin, every divergence (if any) triaged under the §8.2 oracle-or-spec-investigation-first law. Acceptance: G1 declared with the evidence bundle (run logs, receipts, Parity Ledger rows, PG-1 numbers on the baseline machine). Tests: CLI transcript fixtures (exit codes, --json schema); interrupted-run drills (partial output never masquerades as complete); determinism — two runs produce identical receipts.

## Acceptance Criteria

All bead-specific requirements, acceptance conditions, tests, invariants, compatibility surfaces, evidence levels, performance gates, negative/recovery cases, and user-visible behaviors stated above remain mandatory. In addition, the MANDATORY VERIFICATION DEFINITION OF DONE in Notes must be satisfied with named unit/property/mutation suites, at least one shared real-path no-mock E2E scenario plus failure/recovery coverage, detailed human and schema-versioned NDJSON artifacts, and reproducible close evidence. No listed feature or claim may be silently narrowed, deferred, mocked, or declared complete through an unclassified divergence.
acceptance_criteria:
fln check-olean is a standalone air-gap-capable auditor composed of full-recheck Grimoire decode, K1/K2, fln-checker consensus, receipts, optional certificates, and transparency append; it never invokes the Reference or another Lean implementation at runtime. Human and versioned robot interfaces have stable documented exit codes and per-declaration records with input/declaration/root hashes, verdict/error/resource class, engines/builds/fuel/policy, trace/evidence links, and explicit complete/incomplete run status. The summary receipt binds the exact manifest-complete input-set hash, epoch, modes, policy, engine builds, totals and result; --receipts atomically writes a complete set and log entry. Interrupted, cancelled, resource-exhausted, disk-full, corrupted, or disagreement runs cannot masquerade as complete, publish partial authority, or collapse Inconclusive. Unit/property/model/mutation tests cover CLI parsing/rendering, schema/exit mapping, manifest ordering, receipt/certificate tamper, consensus outcomes, partial output, retry/idempotence, budgets and recovery; named skipped-file, false-summary, forged-receipt, disagreement-outvote, and interrupted-success mutants are killed. Real no-mock G1 E2E rechecks every pinned mathlib olean with zero acceptance divergence, runs 1/8/32-thread determinism, plants corruption/disagreement/interruption, restores, and retains strict per-row/summary/receipt/transparency/final-state bundles. PG-1 is no more than 5 minutes on the 32-core profile and 25 minutes single-thread with raw host/cache/sample evidence. All dependencies, G1 assembly, scripts/check.sh, cargo/fmt/clippy/UBS, kernel/codec/differential/mutation/fault/platform/performance lanes pass. No sampled set presented as all mathlib, aggregate-only verdict, partial run presented complete, runtime Reference fallback, mock-only corpus, unstable robot schema, waived divergence, or deferred listed CLI/evidence feature satisfies closure.

REVIEW AMENDMENT — robot stdout is versioned, line-oriented, data-only, and terminates every invocation with an explicit complete or incomplete terminal record. Human progress, diagnostics, and decoration go to stderr without corrupting robot output. Cancellation, resource refusal, crash, malformed artifact, and partial corpus traversal emit bounded typed terminal records and nonzero documented exits; parser/model/E2E tests prove pipe safety and recovery.

EVIDENCE CONTRACT — authoritative output is strict schema-versioned canonical semantic NDJSON containing normalized inputs, roots, typed outcomes, resource class/consumption, decisions, first divergence, cleanup, and exact final state. Host, PID, wall time, temporary paths, cache/performance facts, and scheduler details live only in a separately linked bounded telemetry stream and cannot enter authoritative digests. Validators reject merged streams, unknown versions, extra or missing fields, broken linkage/order, silent truncation, or telemetry-root drift. Productive 1/8/32 runs prove nonempty completed work and deterministic reduction rather than thread-count labels.
notes:
MANDATORY VERIFICATION DEFINITION OF DONE (inherits franken_lean-rur; additive to this bead's own Tests/Acceptance):
1. Unit coverage: deterministic happy-path, boundary, malformed-input, resource-exhaustion, cancellation, and failure-atomicity cases for every new public behavior; property/metamorphic and mutation-kill tests wherever an invariant or equivalence is claimed.
2. E2E coverage: add or extend at least one shared scripts/e2e scenario for the real user-visible path, plus a negative/recovery scenario. Release-level evidence uses the no-mock lane (real Reference binary/artifact/filesystem/editor/process/host as applicable). A mock may support a unit test but may not close an L-level, PG gate, or public claim.
3. Detailed logs: emit both concise human logs and schema-versioned NDJSON with run/scenario/step ids; bead, claim, invariant, Parity-Ledger row, and gate ids; exact command/argv with secrets redacted; cwd; epoch/mode/profile/platform/thread-count/seed/cache-state/host facts; canonical input hashes; expected vs actual; monotonic start/end/duration; resource and budget facts; exit status/signal; stdout/stderr artifact references; receipt/logical roots; first-divergence data; cleanup and asserted final state. Never swallow stderr, never leak secrets, and bound adversarial log volume.
4. CI/closeout: archive logs, fixtures, repro bundles, and evidence manifests; failures must be diagnosable from artifacts alone. Run scripts/check.sh, cargo test, the bead-specific unit/property suites, relevant Tribunal differential/mutation/fault lanes, and the shared E2E scenario. The close evidence names every test/scenario id and artifact location; skips require a typed, logged, honest L-level limitation and may not satisfy the skipped claim.

title: Register the epoch_lab_hash_chain suite in a lane so it runs

title: Every path from admit to publish must name its council
description:
Filed by cc_2 on 2026-07-25 out of fln-uc44, from a VERIFIED bypass rather than a projected one.

THE FACT. crates/fln-verdict/src/reflection.rs:377 calls kernel_admit, destructures KernelAdmitted::Accepted(checked), and publishes. `rg "convene|Council"` over that file returns NOTHING. So a real, shipping publication path obtains the kernel's opaque publication capability and publishes without the consensus seat ever being consulted.

WHY THAT IS WORSE THAN IT SOUNDS. The claim matrix row B3-CONSENSUS-HALTS records, as its corrected evidence, that "convene has NO production caller - every call site is in tests/consensus_seat.rs - because there is no publication path to halt yet (fln-elab is a stub)". That sentence is stale in the direction that matters. There IS a publication path. It is not fln-elab, so nobody looking for the elaborator found it, and the row now understates the gap while reading as though it overstates it. This is the third instance today of evidence that stopped being true without anything going red.

WHAT IS AND IS NOT WRONG HERE. fln-verdict is not misbehaving: nothing asks it to convene, and an empty council would agree vacuously anyway, so the CURRENT behaviour is identical either way. The defect is that the two cases - "policy decided nobody was asked" and "nobody thought to ask" - are indistinguishable at the type level and at the call site. fln-uc44 deliberately spelled Council::nobody_was_asked() so that the empty case would be VISIBLE at the call site; it made that visibility available and did not make it required.

THE CONSTRAINT. Every path from admit to publish must name its council. `admit` should yield a value that only `convene` can turn into a publishable CheckedDecl, so the empty council stays legal and becomes mandatory to SPELL. There is no runtime cost and no behaviour change today; what changes is that a publication site cannot omit the question.

WHY BEFORE AN ENGINE AND NOT AFTER. This is the one that gets built wrong once an engine exists. "Wire consensus into the publication path" then becomes a task someone does partially, under a deadline, and the paths it was not wired into look EXACTLY like the paths that had no council policy - because today they are the same shape. Afterwards, adding the funnel means auditing every publication site to decide which omissions were deliberate; the audit is the expensive part and it does not exist yet, because there are two publication sites in the whole tree.

IT PASSES THE CONSTRAINT TEST WITH A CALLER ATTACHED. The planted violation is writable today - it is the code at reflection.rs:377 - which is stronger than the usual form of this test, where the violation has to be invented.

ACCEPTANCE. CheckedDecl obtainable only through council::convene; Admitted::Accepted carrying something that cannot be published directly; both existing publication sites updated to name their council, with fln-verdict's naming Council::nobody_was_asked() because that is the honest answer there today; a planted violation proving the direct path no longer compiles, expressed as a documented compile-fail rather than a runtime test since that is what a type-level funnel means; and the B3-CONSENSUS-HALTS claim-matrix row corrected, because it currently asserts there is no production publication path.

NOT IN SCOPE, explicitly: a council POLICY (which declarations get a non-empty council is plan section 8.3c and needs seats that exist); the second engine (franken_lean-gii, Slice C, deliberately not started); and any change to what an empty council means, which stays vacuous agreement.

OWNERSHIP: crates/fln-kernel is mine. crates/fln-verdict/src/reflection.rs is one call site and cod_1 has had that file in flight today; the change there is a match arm, not a redesign, and will be coordinated on this bead before it lands.
close_reason: Judgement row authored first and dry-validated with the bead closed, so the complete-state field requirements actually fired. A publication right now exists only on the far side of a council: Admitted::Accepted carries a Reviewable whose only exit to CheckedDecl is a pub(crate) move consumed by convene, so publishing without naming a council is not an expressible program. The bypass this bead was filed on was verified rather than projected -- crates/fln-verdict/src/reflection.rs obtained the capability and published with no Council in the file -- and when the funnel landed the compiler named that site and only that site (E0599, no method publish on Reviewable, reflection.rs:407). Nothing was misbehaving, which is why it survived: an empty council agrees vacuously and the outcome is byte-identical. The defect was that "policy decided nobody was asked" and "nobody thought to ask" were the same program; fln-uc44 made that distinction available and this makes it required. The planted violation is a compile-fail because a type-level funnel has no runtime behaviour to assert, recorded beside a positive test so the refusals cannot all be passing because nothing works. ACCEPTANCE NARROWED AT CLOSE, disclosed on the row rather than dropped: as filed this bead also required correcting the B3-CONSENSUS-HALTS claim-matrix row, which lives in cc_3's crates/fln-conformance/src/witness.rs. Folding another pane's artifact into my acceptance was an error in bead authorship, not in the work; the defect is real, predates this change, and is reported with exact diagnosis and proposed wording on franken_lean-parity-ledger-l2-definition-split-kl4h. NOT EARNED: any seat. Every council in the tree is empty and agrees vacuously because there are no in-repo engines to convene; what changed is that the question is asked at every publication site, not that anyone is there to answer it. Slice C remains deliberately not started.

title: W1: UPSTREAM_LEDGER + suite upgrade protocol — deliberate, Tribunal-diffed lock bumps
description:
## Description

Own UPSTREAM_LEDGER.md and the deliberate Tribunal-diffed suite upgrade protocol (§2.11, R16). Seed and preserve every planned foundation capability: asupersync deterministic ordered merge if its reviewed primitives are insufficient; franken_networkx incremental dominator maintenance; frankensearch transaction-aligned incremental commit hooks; franken_markdown Lean lexer profile; frankensqlite CAS blob access patterns; and in-repo fln-bignum with the second-suite-consumer revisit trigger. Clean-room design-level reuse records provenance/license facts without copying an unapproved implementation into the runtime closure.

Every ledger row follows a closed state machine: proposed, investigated, upstream-requested, accepted-upstream, released, pinned-in-SUITE.lock, acceptance-evidenced, load-bearing, rejected, or superseded. A prose row, open request, merged-but-unreleased change, or available-but-ungated version cannot satisfy a consumer. Cross-repository work names the exact external issue/commit/release and remains non-authoritative until the pinned closure, canonical contract/census diff, and local Tribunal acceptance evidence agree.

The upgrade protocol applies to additions, removals, upgrades, downgrades, retargeting, nightly/target-feature/profile changes, Reference/Corpus advances, and path/commit/tree/checksum changes. Validation occurs against an isolated candidate. The current lock remains authoritative until closure/allowlist delta, contract and census regeneration/diff, Tribunal comparison, component migration, rollback proof, and unchanged-root revalidation complete. Cancellation, external unavailability, source drift, or incomplete evidence leaves the old lock untouched and the candidate non-authoritative.

A waiver may only defer or block a candidate with owner, exact scope, rationale, expiry, and review date. It may never authorize D1/D3/D8 violation, unknown dependency, load-bearing unknown, incomplete evidence, or a release claim. No prose-only intent, emergency label, or manual bypass promotes a component.

## Acceptance Criteria

Named suites upstream_ledger_state_machine, suite_upgrade_candidate_model, lock_delta_contract_join, waiver_authority_model, and suite_upgrade_no_mock_e2e cover every state/transition, component kind, lock change class, candidate stage, closure/contract/Tribunal evidence join, rollback, cancellation/fault/retry, external-evidence identity, and waiver boundary. UPSTREAM_LEDGER includes every seed entry, owner/repository/link, rationale, exact status, acceptance gate, consumer, fallback, and revisit trigger. Mutations for premature state promotion, current-lock modification before validation, hidden transitive dependency, stale/mixed census or Tribunal roots, unchanged-label skipping validation, missing rollback, expired/nonexpiring waiver acceptance, constitutional-violation waiver, and prose-only load-bearing promotion are killed. The real no-mock E2E creates an isolated candidate change, demonstrates its complete failure list, attaches valid closure/contract/Tribunal/migration/rollback evidence and passes, plants a hidden dependency and stale root and fails, restores, and proves the original authoritative lock root unchanged. Strict NDJSON records run/change/component/ledger-transition ids, exact old/new lock and closure roots, pins and deltas, external evidence identity, contract/census/Tribunal roots, expected/actual stage, rollback outcome, publication authority, cleanup, and final current-lock root. No candidate or ledger row closes on mocks, prose, partial evidence, or a waiver of constitutional/load-bearing obligations.
acceptance_criteria: Every required foundation capability is represented by a closed-state UPSTREAM_LEDGER row with exact external provenance, owner, gate, consumer, fallback, and revisit trigger. Every class of SUITE.lock change validates in an isolated candidate against complete closure, canonical contract/census diff, Tribunal evidence, migration, rollback, and unchanged-root checks before atomic publication. All named model/mutation/no-mock E2E and strict logging/recovery requirements pass. Waivers may defer/block only; they never authorize constitutional violations, unknowns, incomplete load-bearing components, or claims.
notes:
MANDATORY VERIFICATION DEFINITION OF DONE (inherits franken_lean-rur; additive to this bead's own Tests/Acceptance):
1. Unit coverage: deterministic happy-path, boundary, malformed-input, resource-exhaustion, cancellation, and failure-atomicity cases for every new public behavior; property/metamorphic and mutation-kill tests wherever an invariant or equivalence is claimed.
2. E2E coverage: add or extend at least one shared scripts/e2e scenario for the real user-visible path, plus a negative/recovery scenario. Release-level evidence uses the no-mock lane (real Reference binary/artifact/filesystem/editor/process/host as applicable). A mock may support a unit test but may not close an L-level, PG gate, or public claim.
3. Detailed logs: emit both concise human logs and schema-versioned NDJSON with run/scenario/step ids; bead, claim, invariant, Parity-Ledger row, and gate ids; exact command/argv with secrets redacted; cwd; epoch/mode/profile/platform/thread-count/seed/cache-state/host facts; canonical input hashes; expected vs actual; monotonic start/end/duration; resource and budget facts; exit status/signal; stdout/stderr artifact references; receipt/logical roots; first-divergence data; cleanup and asserted final state. Never swallow stderr, never leak secrets, and bound adversarial log volume.
4. CI/closeout: archive logs, fixtures, repro bundles, and evidence manifests; failures must be diagnosable from artifacts alone. Run scripts/check.sh, cargo test, the bead-specific unit/property suites, relevant Tribunal differential/mutation/fault lanes, and the shared E2E scenario. The close evidence names every test/scenario id and artifact location; skips require a typed, logged, honest L-level limitation and may not satisfy the skipped claim.
