title: Foreign kernel witnesses: leanchecker is reachable at the pin, lean4lean and the export format are not
description:
Filed by cc_2 on 2026-07-25 from franken_lean-bc7. AGENTS.md names lean4checker and lean4lean as foreign witnesses joinable via the export format, and observes that two FOREIGN implementations agreeing is stronger evidence than our verdict agreeing with the Reference. The differential harness in 6f9a6e5 is only the second of those: it is us versus the Reference, one witness, and it should not be read as the full council. This bead records exactly what is reachable today, measured rather than assumed.

leanchecker IS REACHABLE AND DOES REAL WORK. The binary ships in the pinned toolchain at bin/leanchecker. It is not usable as invoked bare: with no LEAN_PATH it resolves through elan to a DIFFERENT installed toolchain (v4.7.0 is also present on this machine) and dies on an incompatible header, which reads like a broken binary and is not. Pointed at the pin it works:

    LEAN_PATH=~/.elan/toolchains/leanprover--lean4---v4.32.0/lib/lean \
      ~/.elan/toolchains/leanprover--lean4---v4.32.0/bin/leanchecker Init.Core

exits 0 silently. That it is doing genuine kernel re-checking rather than a no-op is measurable: over the reachable closure of Init it burns 149s user plus 104s system CPU at about 1170 percent parallelism, 21.6s wall. This is the kernel-level oracle the obligation actually wants, and it is strictly stronger than the lean binary the current harness uses, because lean runs the elaborator and refuses some declarations before the kernel ever sees them.

PACKAGING CAVEAT: leanchecker Init FAILS, and not for a checking reason. Init.olean imports Init.Data.Basic and lib/lean/Init/Data/Basic.olean does not exist in the pin, while 600 other Init oleans and 2433 in total do. Enumerate present oleans rather than walking the import graph.

THE EXPORT FORMAT IS NOT AVAILABLE AT THIS PIN. lean --help at v4.32.0 offers -o for olean, -i for ilean, -c for C and -b for bitcode, and no export flag at all. So the route AGENTS.md describes, joining foreign checkers through the export format, is not reachable with the pinned binary as shipped. Anything depending on it needs either a different pin or a build of the exporter from source, and that is a decision rather than a detail.

lean4lean IS NOT PRESENT. It is a separate project and nothing in the pinned toolchain provides it. Adding it means vendoring or building a third-party Lean implementation, which runs straight into D1's closed dependency universe: the allowlist is std, the pinned nightly, and the Dicklesworthstone suite. A foreign witness is exactly the kind of thing the Oracle-Only Law contemplates living inside the Tribunal rather than the product, but it still needs a deliberate decision and an entry in the dependency ledger, not a quiet cargo add.

WHAT THIS BEAD IS FOR: decide and record how many witnesses the kernel council actually has. Minimum useful step is wiring leanchecker as a second oracle alongside our own verdicts, which needs no new dependency and is available today. lean4lean and the export path are a separate, larger decision. Until then, no document should describe kernel verdicts as multiply witnessed; today it is one foreign implementation and us.

NOT A DEFECT REPORT. Nothing here says the kernel is wrong. It says the evidence is currently one-witness, and names precisely what the second and third would cost.
close_reason: Answered: there is NO foreign kernel witness available at this pin, and the tempting reading of leanchecker is wrong. (1) The export format does not exist at v4.32.0 — no export/dump/emit flag, no export tool in bin, no export olean in lib — so the route AGENTS.md names for joining foreign checkers is unavailable with the shipped binaries. (2) leanchecker is NOT foreign: it ships inside the toolchain and ldd shows it linking libleanshared_1.so and libleanshared_2.so, the same shared Lean kernel as the lean binary, built from a generated LeanChecker.c. It is the Reference kernel re-run, so joining it would add a second execution and not a second opinion — and per B3 a quorum built from copies of one kernel is exactly the shape that could pass a wrong judgment unanimously. (3) It is still useful as an ORACLE UPGRADE rather than a witness: it is kernel-level over compiled artifacts where lean is elaborator-level over source, and that guidance is recorded on fln-lst4. (4) It is not artifact-hardened — measured: 24 flipped bytes in an olean give SIGSEGV, some single-byte flips pass silently — so a crash must be typed as no-verdict and the malformed-input arm cannot use it at all; our own region engine types that same input as a RegionFault and never panics. The council today is the Reference and us: one implementation, one comparison, and no document should describe kernel verdicts as multiply witnessed. lean4lean is the only genuine foreign witness in sight, is absent from the toolchain, and adding it is a D1 closed-dependency decision for a Tribunal owner rather than a kernel one.

comments.author: cc_2
comments.text:
ANSWERED, AND THE ANSWER IS NO: there is no foreign kernel witness available at this pin. I went looking for the stronger evidence the doctrine asks for and it is not there. Recording precisely what is and is not available, because the tempting move here is to call leanchecker a second witness and it is not one.

FINDING 1 — THE EXPORT FORMAT DOES NOT EXIST AT THIS PIN. Checked three ways: lean --help at v4.32.0 has no export, dump or emit flag of any kind; there is no export tool in the toolchain's bin; there is no export-related olean in lib/lean. The route AGENTS.md names for joining foreign checkers — "joinable via the export format" — is simply unavailable with the shipped binaries. Anything built on it needs a different pin or an exporter built from source, and that is a decision, not a detail.

FINDING 2 — leanchecker IS NOT FOREIGN, WHICH IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS. It ships INSIDE the toolchain (bin/leanchecker, with LeanChecker.olean in lib/lean, built from a generated LeanChecker.c), and ldd shows it linking libleanshared_1.so and libleanshared_2.so — the SAME shared Lean runtime and kernel that the lean binary uses. It is upstream's own kernel re-run over compiled artifacts, not an independent implementation of the type theory.

So leanchecker agreeing with lean is one implementation agreeing with itself. Joining it to our differential would produce a number that LOOKS like a council and is not one: it adds a second execution, not a second opinion. B3 is explicit that disagreement halts and never outvotes, and a quorum built from copies of the same kernel is exactly the shape that could pass a wrong judgment unanimously. I am not wiring it in as a witness.

FINDING 3 — IT IS STILL USEFUL, JUST AS SOMETHING ELSE. leanchecker is a KERNEL-level oracle over compiled artifacts, where the lean binary my differential currently uses is an ELABORATOR-level oracle over source. For a kernel differential that is a strictly better oracle: lean refuses some declarations before the kernel ever sees them (unknownIdentifier is elaboration, not kernel), whereas leanchecker re-checks what is actually in the olean. It does real work — 149s user plus 104s system CPU at about 1170 percent parallelism over Init's reachable closure. That belongs on fln-lst4 (the corpus-scale widening) as the oracle to use, and I have noted it there. It is an oracle upgrade, not a witness.

FINDING 4 — leanchecker IS NOT ARTIFACT-HARDENED, so it must never be the oracle for a malformed-input arm. Measured, not assumed. Baseline on a private copy of the Init tree: exit 0. Then:
  * 24 bytes flipped in Init/Core.olean  -> SIGSEGV (exit 139)
  * 1 byte flipped at offset 5000        -> exit 0, corruption undetected
  * 1 byte flipped at offset 200000      -> exit 0, corruption undetected
  * 1 byte flipped at offset 800000      -> exit 1, "while replaying declaration"
Single-byte flips landing in semantically inert bytes passing is fair enough. The SIGSEGV is not: it means the artifact is mapped and trusted rather than validated. Consequences for any harness that uses it: a crash is NO VERDICT and must be typed as such, never read as a rejection — the same rule my reference_differential harness already applies to tagged non-verdict diagnostics — and the corruption arm of a differential cannot use leanchecker at all.

Worth recording the contrast rather than leaving it implicit: FrankenLean's own region engine takes the same class of input and yields a typed RegionFault, never a panic, under FL-INV-07 — and I tightened exactly that path this session when an mpz header extreme could still panic in debug. On artifact robustness we are ahead of the Reference tooling here. That is evidence, not a boast, and it is one of the few places the comparison runs in our favour.

ANTI-RUBBER-STAMP NOTE. I could not run the specific experiment of feeding leanchecker something our kernel accepts and it should reject, because that needs a hand-built olean, and constructing one requires fln-olean's writer — which does not exist yet (the crate is reader-only) and is outside fln-kernel's covenant anyway. What I could falsify, I did: the corruption sweep above establishes that leanchecker is not a rubber stamp on well-formed input and IS unsafe on malformed input. The stronger experiment waits on an olean writer and belongs with fln-lst4.

WHERE THIS LEAVES THE COUNCIL, stated plainly so no document overclaims: today it is the Reference and us. One implementation, one comparison. lean4lean is the only genuine foreign witness in sight and it is not present in the toolchain; adding it means vendoring or building a third-party Lean implementation, which is a D1 closed-dependency-universe decision for the Tribunal rather than something to slip in. Until that happens, no artifact should describe kernel verdicts as multiply witnessed.

Closing this bead: the question it was filed to answer is answered. The actionable residue is on fln-lst4 (use leanchecker as the corpus-scale oracle, treat crashes as no-verdict) and the lean4lean decision, which needs a Tribunal owner rather than a kernel one.

title: W10: native_decide Tier 2 — trace-guided kernel replay discharges ofReduceBool
description:
Implement native_decide Tier 2 — trace-guided kernel replay (§11.6): on certified paths, ofReduceBool is DISCHARGED, not trusted — the Tier 1 replay receipt (function-entry digests over the registered reflection set, branch decisions, literal-arithmetic transcripts) is replayed through Crucible as the DEFAULT for certified profiles, so the compiler and VM leave the trusted base for every evaluation the tier covers.

Scope and honesty rules: the tier holds only where the receipt covers the full evaluation (the registered reflection set; evaluations escaping it remain Tier 1 and are marked so); the trust ledger records per build which tier was achieved, because "we no longer trust the compiler" is a claim with a scope; the cost multiple of replay vs native evaluation is measured and published (an OBSERVED number, per §20.4 — never asserted); Tier 3 (a verified evaluator proven against the Judgment Specification) remains explicitly research and is NOT this bead. Certified --reproducible builds enable Tier 2 by default; standard builds keep Tier 1 sampling policy.

Acceptance: the reflection corpus discharges through kernel replay on certified profiles with zero trust extension to Golem/Iron for covered evaluations; the trust ledger and fln audit --tcb reflect the tier per declaration; the published cost-multiple table lands in the evidence bundle for G6. Tests: e2e certified-build test where a native_decide theorem verifies with the compiler deliberately perturbed (a wrong compiled result MUST be caught by replay — the whole point, proven by mutation); receipt-coverage boundary fixtures (an evaluation outside the registered set must degrade to Tier 1 with the degradation logged and marked, never silently claimed as Tier 2); replay determinism across the certified matrix.

## Acceptance Criteria

All bead-specific requirements, acceptance conditions, tests, invariants, compatibility surfaces, evidence levels, performance gates, negative/recovery cases, and user-visible behaviors stated above remain mandatory. In addition, the MANDATORY VERIFICATION DEFINITION OF DONE in Notes must be satisfied with named unit/property/mutation suites, at least one shared real-path no-mock E2E scenario plus failure/recovery coverage, detailed human and schema-versioned NDJSON artifacts, and reproducible close evidence. No listed feature or claim may be silently narrowed, deferred, mocked, or declared complete through an unclassified divergence.
acceptance_criteria:
1. In certified profiles, Tier 2 is the default for every native_decide evaluation wholly covered by the registered reflection set: the complete Tier 1 receipt is deterministically replayed through Crucible and ofReduceBool is discharged by a kernel-checked artifact, removing Golem/Iron from the trusted base for that evaluation.
2. Coverage is computed per evaluation and provenance-bound. Any escape, unknown operation, incomplete/tampered receipt, replay budget exhaustion, or unsupported version degrades explicitly to Tier 1 with a typed reason and trust-ledger mark; it can never silently inherit Tier 2. Standard builds retain the Tier 1 sampling policy and Tier 3 remains out of scope.
3. fln audit --tcb and the build/declaration trust ledger report achieved tier, covered operations, receipt/proof roots, fallback reason, and evidence. Covered compiler perturbations that change native results are caught by replay before theorem admission.
4. Named unit/property/differential/mutation suites cover full/partial reflection coverage, replay semantics, receipt binding, certified/default policy, explicit degradation, audit aggregation, cancellation/resource exhaustion, and bit-deterministic replay across the certified matrix. Wrong-compiled-result, missing-coverage-edge, silent-Tier1, skip-certified-replay, and false-audit-tier mutants must be killed.
5. A shared no-mock E2E certified build runs real native_decide corpus theorems, deliberately perturbs a compiled result, proves replay rejection, verifies covered theorems with no compiler trust extension, exercises an out-of-set evaluation and its logged Tier 1 degradation, then rebuilds cleanly across certified platforms. Human logs plus schema-versioned NDJSON include run/build/declaration/evaluation/receipt/replay/proof/tier ids, bead/claim/invariant/gate rows, redacted argv/cwd, pin/build/epoch/mode/profile/platform/thread/seed/budget facts, canonical term/environment/reflection/receipt/proof roots, coverage and expected/actual verdicts, cost/timings/resources/status, artifacts, cleanup, and final state.
6. Reproducible evidence publishes replay-to-native cost multiples as observed distributions, not assertions, and archives cross-platform matrices, perturbation mutants, trust ledgers, receipts/proofs, and E2E bundles. Close wording is scoped per covered evaluation and never claims Tier 3 or universal compiler independence.

REVIEW AMENDMENT — unsupported operations may be preclassified Tier 1. Tampered receipts, cancellation, replay-budget exhaustion, malformed artifacts, or incomplete verification are failures or Inconclusive, not automatic successful Tier-1 downgrades. Any G6 cell requiring Tier 2 remains blocked until real Tier-2 evidence passes. Tier transitions are atomic, root-bound, independently validated, and never inferred from absence of a crash.

EVIDENCE CONTRACT — strict canonical semantic NDJSON and separately linked bounded telemetry are mandatory. Semantic records contain normalized ids/inputs/roots, typed outcomes, resource class/consumption, decisions, first divergence, cleanup, and exact final state; host, PID, time, paths, cache and performance stay telemetry-only. Validators reject unknown versions, missing/extra/duplicate fields, broken linkage/order, truncation, merged streams, and telemetry in authoritative roots. Productive 1/8/32 applies where safely parallel; named unit/model/property/mutation/fuzz and real no-mock positive/failure/recovery E2E close claims.
notes:
MANDATORY VERIFICATION DEFINITION OF DONE (inherits franken_lean-rur; additive to this bead's own Tests/Acceptance):
1. Unit coverage: deterministic happy-path, boundary, malformed-input, resource-exhaustion, cancellation, and failure-atomicity cases for every new public behavior; property/metamorphic and mutation-kill tests wherever an invariant or equivalence is claimed.
2. E2E coverage: add or extend at least one shared scripts/e2e scenario for the real user-visible path, plus a negative/recovery scenario. Release-level evidence uses the no-mock lane (real Reference binary/artifact/filesystem/editor/process/host as applicable). A mock may support a unit test but may not close an L-level, PG gate, or public claim.
3. Detailed logs: emit both concise human logs and schema-versioned NDJSON with run/scenario/step ids; bead, claim, invariant, Parity-Ledger row, and gate ids; exact command/argv with secrets redacted; cwd; epoch/mode/profile/platform/thread-count/seed/cache-state/host facts; canonical input hashes; expected vs actual; monotonic start/end/duration; resource and budget facts; exit status/signal; stdout/stderr artifact references; receipt/logical roots; first-divergence data; cleanup and asserted final state. Never swallow stderr, never leak secrets, and bound adversarial log volume.
4. CI/closeout: archive logs, fixtures, repro bundles, and evidence manifests; failures must be diagnosable from artifacts alone. Run scripts/check.sh, cargo test, the bead-specific unit/property suites, relevant Tribunal differential/mutation/fault lanes, and the shared E2E scenario. The close evidence names every test/scenario id and artifact location; skips require a typed, logged, honest L-level limitation and may not satisfy the skipped claim.

title: History rewrites make evidence commit anchors unreachable from main
description:
SYSTEMIC DEFECT. The 2026-07-25 23:59 git filter-branch rewrite changed every commit identity on main while removing four generated census files. Existing beads, immutable comments, and verification coverage rows can therefore cite pre-rewrite commits that are not reachable from current main. Those anchors are not necessarily false; they are unverifiable from main and may disappear entirely after garbage collection. Local refs pre-filter-branch-backup and refs/original/refs/heads/main are temporary forensic aids, never current evidence authority.

REQUIRED BEHAVIOR.
R1. Every measurement re-derived after the rewrite records the full current commit hash and explicitly notes when the superseded anchor predates the rewrite.
R2. Anchor checking distinguishes main-reachable, local-backup-only, and unresolved. Object existence alone is insufficient: current evidence must be reachable from main.
R3. New or mutable evidence surfaces fail closed on an unresolvable or non-main-reachable commit anchor. Mutable surfaces include verification-manifest rows and mutable bead fields; content digests must not be mistaken for commits.
R4. Immutable historical comments are never mass-rewritten. When an old anchor is encountered, the measurement is re-derived and a new immutable comment records current evidence alongside the legacy context.
R5. The mechanism has seeded tests using a temporary rewritten repository: current reachable anchor passes; backup-only anchor is classified legacy; missing anchor refuses; content digest text is ignored; and removing backup refs does not change current-evidence validity.
R6. Scanner inability, ambiguous abbreviation, and repository-state errors are typed inconclusive or refusal, never green.

NON-GOALS. Do not restore the removed generated files, rewrite immutable comment history, bless refs/original as evidence authority, or perform a mass anchor substitution. This bead owns the future mechanism and bounded inventory needed to prevent recurrence, not a bulk cleanup of all historic prose.
close_reason: R1-R6 complete: current anchor inventory remeasured; main-reachability classifier and fail-closed mutable Vellum anchors landed; five-case rewritten-repository fixture and existence-only mutant kill proven; historical comments preserved.

comments.text:
SEVEN ANCHOR TWINS LANDED — on TWO INDEPENDENT DERIVATIONS by different panes, with cc_2 named

Filed by cc_3 (pane 4). Landed at **`da1adcb9`**, with a self-inflicted regression repaired at
**`7046ef59`**. `commit_unreachable` in `artifact_referent_census.rs` reaches **0**.

## THE EVIDENCE IS TWO DERIVATIONS, AND THAT IS THE POINT OF THIS COMMENT

- **cc_3** derived the seven pairs at `c291fd91`, with a negative control taken from the tree:
  `be14ee9b`, the one commit the 2026-07-25 `filter-branch` genuinely altered, refused on
  every identity.
- **cc_2** re-derived all seven independently at `86d87486` — **not** by re-running cc_3's
  script. Its own predicate written from the four content identities, its own shell, and a
  control cc_3 did not have. It then handed the result over as *evidence rather than a
  decision*, because `crates/fln-conformance/` is cc_3's and crossing in to move the constant
  would be the row-ownership violation one layer over. The sequencer ruled that cc_3 lands it.
- **cc_3 (this rotation)** reproduced cc_2's cells at `86d87486` as a landing check: 7/7
  accept, both controls refused, every stable patch-id identical to cc_2's published values.
  **That is a reproduction, not a third derivation, and it is recorded as one.**

Identities, all four required: stable patch-id; byte-identical diff text; touched-path list;
resulting blob per path. Plus the direction check that makes a pair a *recovery* rather than a
coincidence — every OLD must be backup-only and every NEW reachable from `refs/heads/main`.

```
fln-8zsq                                 -> commit:cb014e1b   pid=12502d681b72
fln-kernel-bounded-decl-admission-ukzx   -> commit:419078c6   pid=79ab3aeef0a2
fln-uc44                                 -> commit:104bd8b1   pid=8759d317d3fc
fln-yswb                                 -> commit:dfd77f1f   pid=738699361b07
franken_lean-r0xu                        -> commit:cbffffc6   pid=5a47fbb1ebde
franken_lean-r0xu                        -> commit:18b6d14b   pid=5e9e2554a770
franken_lean-r0xu                        -> commit:e248cfa4   pid=175c461713cc
```

The old shas are deliberately not written here; see the third section.

## WHY CC_2'S CONTROL IS THE ONE THAT MAKES "7 OF 7" MEAN ANYTHING

cc_3's control proves the predicate refuses **known-bad material**. It does not prove the
predicate refuses two **unrelated** commits — a predicate that accepted everything handed to
it would still fail `be14ee9b` for its own reasons and pass all seven. cc_2 cross-paired
`fln-8zsq`'s old anchor with `…-ukzx`'s twin `419078c6`: both rows members of the accepted
set, each with a twin of its own that passes, and the wrong pairing refused on every identity.

> **A negative control drawn from INSIDE the accepted set separates a discriminating
> predicate from a permissive one. One drawn only from known-bad material cannot.**

Also from cc_2, recorded because it nearly cost the confirmation: its first run of this
verification was a **broken scan** — a `for p in $pairs` loop over a space-separated list,
where zsh does not word-split an unquoted parameter, so the loop ran once over the whole
string and took the FIRST sha and the LAST. One row where seven were expected, refused on
every identity, and it read as a genuine finding. What caught it was the **shape**, not the
verdict. Assert the row count before reading any verdict.

## THE TRAP THIS REPAIR CREATED, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH CARRYING

`da1adcb9`'s prose described cc_2's cross-pairing control **by writing the rotted sha into the
sentence**. That sha is backup-only — one of the seven this work had just finished proving
unverifiable from `main`. So the sentence explaining a rot repair minted a fresh instance of
the rot: `commit_anchor_reachability`'s per-file count for `artifact_referent_census.rs` went
1 -> 2 against a ONE-WAY allowance, and `cargo test -p fln-conformance` was red
workspace-wide for six panes between `da1adcb9` and `7046ef59`.

> **A rotted sha is not safe to quote, even in a sentence whose subject is that it is rotted.
> Name the rotted side by its ROW and quote only the reachable twin.**

That is better prose independently of the guard: a reader can act on a bead id and cannot act
on a sha that resolves only through this clone's local backup refs. `be14ee9b` stays quoted
and stays the declared 1 — it is the one commit with no twin, so no row-name substitute would
let a reader find it. **The allowance was not raised**, which was available and would have
gone green; the guard's own words are `Do not raise a number to go green`.

## TWO STRUCTURAL PROPERTIES OF THE GUARD, PAID FOR TODAY

`commit_anchor_reachability` reads **`HEAD`, not the working tree** — deliberately, so five
peers' in-flight edits cannot redden it. The cost side of that trade was not written down:

1. **A repair and the tightening of its own allowance can never be atomic.** The measured fall
   is invisible until the repair is committed, so the tightening always lags by one commit and
   nothing forces the follow-up. Discharged here immediately —
   `ci/VERIFICATION_MANIFEST.jsonl` `17 -> 12` at `7046ef59` — but the general shape is a
   budget that its own repairs refill, arriving in the guard's workflow rather than its data.
2. **A mistake of this shape cannot be caught before it lands.** `da1adcb9` was green on every
   gate available to me and red the instant it existed.

**The fall is 5, not 7, and that gap is a finding.** Two of the seven repaired shas survive
elsewhere in the same file, outside the `artifacts` arrays the census classifies: `a90fadad`
in `…-ukzx`'s `resource` and `…-t0g7`'s `behavior_notes`, and `10c9a2e3` in `fln-uc44`'s
`behavior_notes`. The anchor guard counts distinct anchors per file regardless of field, so
those two still count. Measured two ways that agree: the guard's own probe reports
`declared 1, measured 12`, and an independent sweep of the file's 8-hex tokens classified by
`merge-base --is-ancestor` lists exactly those 12. I predicted 10 from `17 - 7` and was wrong;
the probe corrected it.

Two more live outside the manifest entirely, found by sweeping for the SUBJECT rather than the
count: `10c9a2e3` at `crates/fln-conformance/src/witness.rs:521` and `a873e73c` at
`ci/WORKSPACE_GRAPH.txt:114`. Both real anchors, not hex coincidences — checked by reading the
surrounding text. Disclosed and routed, not repaired: the manifest ones are other panes' rows
and `WORKSPACE_GRAPH.txt` is cod_2's sole authority.

## WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH

**A twin proves two commits carry the same CONTENT; it never proves the sentence citing the
anchor was sound.** That is the harder join and neither derivation touches it. Reachability is
a property of `refs/heads/main` at these commits; local backup refs still make a naive
existence check pass for all seven old shas, which is the whole reason recovery was needed.
Neither pane re-derived cc_3's repository-wide 132/128 sweep, and no per-commit
repository-wide scan exists — a hundred more backup-only anchors in an undeclared file would
still be caught only by the per-file allowance, and one in a *declared* file only if it
exceeded that file's number. One host, class `bounded_model`.

title: W7: Frontier lanes — e-graph saturation + tactic portfolios, shadow-run promotion
description:
Implement the frontier rewrite lanes (§12.3, §12.7): the e-graph equality-saturation lane over simp-set subsets with proof extraction (rewrites recorded as justifications, extracted proofs replayed through the ordinary lemma-application path, kernel-checked like everything else — honestly scoped: conditional rewrites and binder-crossing rules restrict the eligible subset; the lane is an accelerator with a completeness fallback to the faithful core, never a replacement; its win condition is MEASURED via the PG-A profile, not assumed), and speculative tactic portfolios (first-with-work-stealing, deterministic winner selection by registered CGSE policy, losers cancelled through their asupersync regions; snapshot-cheap try trees — the search-side dividend of O(1) environment snapshots, exposed as tactics and through Envoy).

Both lanes promote ONLY by shadow-run (§12.6/§18.9): dual-run on the same demand nodes, products diffed, divergence and latency distributions recorded, promotion per workload/epoch/platform cell with deterministic sampling continuing afterward and auto-demotion on any soundness, fidelity, or tail-latency breach — promotion is a matrix, never a global flag. Frontier features never leak into faithful/sound artifacts (D18).

Acceptance: e-graph lane produces kernel-checked results agreeing with the faithful core on its eligible subset, with the measured win condition published; portfolio winner selection deterministic under the lab at any thread count; shadow-run promotion machinery generic enough for the other promotion consumers (K2 optimizations, Iron tiers, epoch bridges). Tests: extraction-proof replay fixtures; eligibility-boundary fixtures (ineligible rewrites must route to the faithful core); cancellation-correctness under portfolio racing (obligation-leak oracle clean); auto-demotion drill (planted breach must demote and file the incident bundle).

title: env_snapshots: planted-defect kill plus byte-exact recovery for the two identity paths
description:
Split out of fln-amv.12 and fln-amv.1 by PeachBass (cc_1) on 2026-07-25, when both beads' fln-env halves were complete, strictly validated and closed. This bead carries EXACTLY the half that was never built, so nobody reads those closures as evidence that a path-specific planted-defect kill exists.

DOMAIN: scripts/e2e/env_snapshots.sh and scripts/evidence.py (pane cod_3). NOT fln-env. PeachBass has touched none of it.

THE GAP. Both beads' acceptance criteria require their real E2E to prove a planted digest/root defect, typed nonpublication, exact byte restoration, and clean recovery. The lane implements that triple correctly — a source mutation on the retained overlay, a typed kill with an asserted failure signature, byte-exact restoration checked with cmp, then a clean re-run — but only for two OTHER paths: extension_state (the add_decl extension-state clone) and set_union. Neither identity path has one:

  * fln-amv.12, declaration tags. No overlay mutant drops or reorders a tag. The in-process CastAfterSourceReorder and omitted-declaration models ARE strictly validated (source_order_defect_root and omitted_declaration_root must each differ from canonical_root), but they run inside one PASSING test, so no nonpublication and no restoration is ever exercised.
  * fln-amv.1, opaque mutual-block membership. Same shape. The five named defect models (dropped_list, omitted_count, reordered_membership, wrong_domain, failed_root_propagation) are validated per kind, all inside a passing test.

WHAT TO BUILD, two mutant/recovery pairs in the same shape as extension_state_mutant / extension_state_recovery:

1. MEMBERSHIP MUTANT. Seed on the overlay copy of fln-env/src/environment.rs: delete the write_mutual_membership call from the ConstantInfo::Opaque arm of decl_content_digest (currently environment.rs:410) — that is the exact omission this bead's parent was filed against. Target test: environment::tests::mutual_block_membership_changes_the_content_digest, which already exists and already discriminates. Expect the documented mutation-killed contract: classification fail, wrapper exit 1, child exit 101, with a grepped failure signature in BOTH the .out and the .err. Then restore from the pristine copy, cmp for byte-exactness, and re-run for a clean pass.

2. TAG MUTANT. Seed on the same overlay: change definition_safety_tag's DefinitionSafety::Safe arm from 1 to 5. Target: any of the three tests proven to go red on exactly that seed — declaration_identity_tag_policy_is_const_exhaustive_and_cast_free, declaration_identity_tag_is_stable_across_1_8_32_concurrent_complete_builds, or declaration_tag_matrix_e2e_emits_detailed_real_path_evidence. That seed was run and the three failures observed on 2026-07-25 (recorded on fln-amv.12), so the kill is known-good before you write the step.

BOTH SEEDS MUST BE ANCHOR-CHECKED. The existing steps refuse to proceed when the mutation is a no-op (set_final internal_fault ..._mutation_seed_noop). Keep that: a silently non-mutating seed produces a step that passes for the wrong reason, which is worse than no step. The SetUnion step's newer Python-heredoc anchor form ("mutation anchor count is not exactly one") is the stronger version of this and is the one to copy.

WHY NOT A DIFFERENT SEED FOR THE TAG. Do NOT seed a source-order REORDER of the DefinitionSafety or QuotKind enum and expect a failure. The tags bind variant NAMES through an explicit exhaustive match, so a reorder is a no-op by design and nothing should go red; a step asserting otherwise would be asserting the bug. The three-way expectation is: reorder = no digest change, add = compile error, retag = golden failure. Only the retag is a runnable lane mutant.

REGISTRATION, from the lane conventions: every new scenario needs its exact ordered step list in E2E_STEP_ORDERS at the top of scripts/evidence.py, and expected-fail cargo steps use --semantic-failure-exit 101 and must grep BOTH .out and .err, because libtest panics go to stderr under --nocapture.

ALREADY DONE — do not redo. The producers, the strict validators, the E2E_STEP_ORDERS entries and the identity children all exist and pass (fln-amv.14, franken_lean-1umc, commits fe4a825, d6126b9, cd99c43, 8c5e62d). Verified independently on 2026-07-25 by running each child exactly as the lane runs it and calling the same validator with the same arguments: declaration-tag-matrix/1 valid=true records=11 case_count=7 thread_matrix=[1,8,32]; declaration-membership/1 valid=true records=41 matrix_rows=35. The gap is only the two planted-defect/restoration/recovery pairs above.

ONE COUPLING TO KNOW ABOUT, and it is a good one. scripts/evidence.py carries DECLARATION_TAG_GOLDENS, an independent copy of the seven-row tag table with stream bytes, stream hash and digest per case. The validator rejects a case absent from it (unknown), a case seen twice (duplicate), and a case set that does not EQUAL it (missing). fln-env now GENERATES its test matrix from exhaustive successor chains (commit 8ce638d), so adding a DefinitionSafety or QuotKind variant is a compile error there — but it is also a change to this table plus expected_records and the case_count/unique_digest_count/pairwise pins here. Four sites, two of them in this file. That is deliberate: the lane fails loudly rather than passing on a subset.

DO NOT PIN LOGICAL-ROOT HEXES beyond what is already pinned while fln-hash root/canon edits are in flight — the same caution franken_lean-1umc carried.

title: W11 integration: Terminal InfoView + WASM Judge completion join
description:
Completion and release-integration join for the two plan §16.4 products. franken_lean-terminal-infoview-client-9q6 owns fln goals, Lantern RPC parity, terminal rendering, OQ-7 widget behavior, and the real PTY/tmux failure-recovery lane. fln-wasm-judge-browser-kvj owns the integrity-bound offline stock-browser Judge, sealed-capsule verification, native/WASM vectors, accessibility, adversarial browser matrix, and OQ-12 package implementation. Their different code, dependencies, and evidence remain separate.

This join owns only cross-product release coherence: both products are installed and discoverable under the same epoch/release manifest; fln identity/help/docs report their independent versions, support tiers, evidence links, and capability requirements honestly; shared receipt/capsule/snapshot vocabulary does not drift; robot schemas use the common evidence envelope without conflating browser verdicts with live proof-state grades; packaging or failure of either product cannot silently masquerade as success for the other. The front-door bead may integrate fln goals after the terminal child closes and does not wait for browser implementation, while W11 and G6 require this join and therefore both products.

Verification cross-checks release manifests, CLI discovery, schema/version links, support-tier reporting, offline assets, and independent failure isolation. A combined no-mock release smoke runs the installed terminal client against a real daemon and the installed browser package against a real sealed capsule, then exercises one product failing while the other remains correctly reported. It archives concise human logs and bounded schema-versioned NDJSON with both child evidence ids, release/epoch/build hashes, expected versus actual support state, commands/assets, first divergence, cleanup, and final state.

## Acceptance Criteria

Close only when both child beads are closed without narrowed scope and the integrated release exposes both products with correct independent identities, support tiers, schemas, evidence, failure isolation, and combined no-mock release smoke artifacts. The terminal client cannot stand in for the browser Judge; a core-only WASM artifact cannot stand in for the stock-browser package; browser delay cannot block unrelated front-door work; and no child test, negative/recovery lane, logging field, or user-visible feature may be dropped at this join.
design: Decomposition law: terminal RPC/TUI and offline WASM/browser implementation are parallel children because they share neither runtime nor primary user journey. This bead is a join only. franken_lean-eb3 consumes the terminal child directly; the W11 epic consumes this join and therefore retains the complete browser requirement. OQ-7 remains owned by franken_lean-v2p and consumed by the terminal child; OQ-12 remains owned by the packaging contract and consumed by the browser child.
acceptance_criteria:
Both dedicated children are closed with their full unit/property/model/mutation, real no-mock E2E, negative/recovery, resource, determinism, accessibility, and detailed logging contracts. The release manifest and installed surfaces expose terminal and browser products independently with correct epoch/version/support/evidence links and failure isolation. The combined release smoke proves both real paths and one-product-fails behavior. No child substitution, hidden coupling, narrowed scope, or deferred listed feature satisfies closure.

REVIEW AMENDMENT — own pre-release manifest fragments, schema vocabulary, product metadata, and coherence validation only. Final signed/installed release-manifest integration is W12 authority. Fragments bind reproducible semantic/payload roots while signatures, notarization, timestamps, transparency and operational telemetry remain separate envelopes. Consumer absence cannot block fragment production and fragments cannot claim an installed release.

EVIDENCE CONTRACT — strict canonical semantic NDJSON and separately linked bounded telemetry are mandatory. Semantic records contain normalized ids/inputs/roots, typed outcomes, resource class/consumption, decisions, first divergence, cleanup, and exact final state; host, PID, time, paths, cache and performance stay telemetry-only. Validators reject unknown versions, missing/extra/duplicate fields, broken linkage/order, truncation, merged streams, and telemetry in authoritative roots. Productive 1/8/32 applies where safely parallel; named unit/model/property/mutation/fuzz and real no-mock positive/failure/recovery E2E close claims.

title: W5/W10: Iron target/profile contract spike — resolve OQ-4 before FIR freezes
description:
Resolve plan OQ-4 before the FIR pipeline or Iron implementation freezes an expensive backend boundary. This is a contract and feasibility spike, not a substitute for fln-y55 or fln-o0j. It must determine: the supported-target tier beyond x86-64 and aarch64; whether static emission and Iron-JIT share one backend with certified/frontier profiles or require separated implementations; the target-independent FIR/FLBC-to-machine contract; relocation, calling-convention, register-allocation, executable-memory, unwind, and object/executable ownership boundaries; how target features enter cache keys and receipts; and how faithful, sound, frontier, and certified artifacts prevent JIT or host-specific behavior from leaking across modes.

The decision must preserve the closed dependency universe and sovereign-backend goal: no LLVM, Cranelift, system assembler/linker, or hidden C compiler on the Iron path. The optional C backend remains only the D2 parity/exotic-target lane. Use a thin real vertical prototype and measurements to price the alternatives before selecting one; do not ratify from prose alone.

## Acceptance Criteria

A versioned backend contract and decision-log row resolve every OQ-4 branch with evidence, rejected alternatives, migration consequences, safe fallback, and explicit target support tiers. Representative real lowering probes cover closures, calls/tail calls, allocation/RC boundaries, exceptions/effects, literals/bignum calls, relocations, debug/source mapping, and target-feature selection. The selected boundary is consumed by both fln-y55 and fln-o0j; neither may invent a second incompatible machine interface.

Named deterministic unit/property/mutation tests cover IR validation, calling-convention/relocation rules, unsupported features, malformed machine inputs, resource limits, and byte-stability. A real no-mock E2E probe emits and executes supported-host code and validates a non-host target artifact structurally; negative/recovery scenarios prove unsupported targets, unavailable executable memory, invalid relocations, and interrupted publication fail typed and leave no trusted artifact. Human logs and schema-versioned bounded NDJSON record exact inputs, target/profile/features, toolchain/host facts, byte hashes, timings/resources, expected versus actual, first divergence, exit/signal, and artifact references. All prototype claims are labeled at their honest evidence level; no benchmark or target-support claim is promoted from a mock or unmeasured design.
acceptance_criteria:
OQ-4 is resolved before FIR or Iron interfaces freeze by a versioned reviewed backend contract and decision-log row covering support tiers beyond x86-64/aarch64, shared-versus-separated static/JIT architecture, the target-independent FIR/FLBC machine contract, calling conventions, register allocation, relocations, object/executable ownership, executable memory, unwind/debug mapping, target-feature cache/receipt identity, and faithful/sound/frontier/certified isolation. Rejected alternatives, migration consequences, safe fallback, and owner are explicit. A thin real vertical prototype lowers and executes closures, direct/tail calls, allocation/RC, exceptions/effects, literals/bignum calls, feature variants, and relocations on a supported host and structurally validates a non-host artifact without LLVM, Cranelift, system assembler/linker, or hidden cc; the C lane remains D2-only. fln-y55 and fln-o0j consume the identical frozen boundary. Unit/property/model/mutation tests cover IR validation, ABI/relocation rules, deterministic bytes, unsupported/malformed features, budgets, cancellation, executable-memory denial, and publication atomicity; named host-leak, profile-leak, wrong-relocation, nondeterministic-layout, and hidden-tool mutants are killed. The real no-mock E2E includes positive host execution, non-host structural proof, unsupported target, invalid relocation, unavailable executable memory, interruption, exact restoration, and recovery with strict evidence containing target/profile/features/toolchain/host/input/output hashes and resources. All dependencies, scripts/check.sh, cargo/fmt/clippy/UBS, prototype differential/mutation/fault lanes pass. No prose-only decision, mock benchmark, second machine interface, hidden external backend/tool, unmeasured support claim, JIT leakage into certified artifacts, unresolved branch, or deferred listed contract item satisfies closure.

REVIEW AMENDMENT — canonical FLBC remains target-independent. Any target-specific machine IR or legalization belongs after FLBC in W10 and binds an explicit target/profile/features/runtime contract; it cannot contaminate W5 semantic identity. The contract inventories ELF, Mach-O, and PE constraints, platform-runtime allowlists, target-feature identity, W^X lifecycle, and unsupported-target nonpublication. Cross-target tests compare target-neutral roots, never machine bytes.

EVIDENCE CONTRACT — canonical authoritative NDJSON contains normalized semantic inputs, roots, decisions, typed outcomes, resource class/consumption, first divergence, cleanup, and exact final state. Host, PID, time, paths, cache/performance, and scheduler facts are linked bounded telemetry only. Independent validators reject unknown schema, extra/missing fields, broken linkage/order, silent truncation, telemetry in semantic hashes, and final-state mismatch. Productive 1/8/32 evidence proves nonempty completed work and canonical reduction.
notes: MANDATORY VERIFICATION DEFINITION OF DONE (inherits franken_lean-rur; additive to this bead own acceptance): unit/property/mutation coverage must exercise every contract rule, malformed input, boundary, resource, determinism, cancellation, and failure-atomicity case. At least one real no-mock host execution plus one structurally validated non-host artifact and a negative/recovery scenario are required. Emit concise human logs and bounded schema-versioned NDJSON with run/scenario/step, bead/claim/invariant/gate, exact redacted argv and cwd, epoch/mode/profile/target/features/toolchain/host, input and artifact hashes, expected versus actual, monotonic timings, resources/budgets, exit/signal, stdout/stderr references, first divergence, publication and cleanup final state. Archive the decision, rejected alternatives, fixtures, raw measurements, logs, and reproducible commands; skips are typed limitations and cannot satisfy the skipped claim.

title: fln-core: oracle the L1 Parity Ledger rows by extending gen_core_fixtures.lean
description:
Raises every fln-core L1 Parity Ledger row to L2. It is fixture work, not implementation work: the Rust side is written and unit-tested, and the gap is that no Reference-produced value is compared for these symbols.

REQUIRES THE PINNED TOOLCHAIN, which is why this is separate from franken_lean-p8a: the generator runs under ~/.elan/toolchains/leanprover--lean4---v4.32.0/bin/lean (install with elan toolchain install leanprover/lean4:v4.32.0). RCH remote workers do NOT have it — this must run locally. scripts/extract/gen_core_fixtures.sh already locates the binary via elan and verifies its commit against SUITE.lock before trusting a byte of output; --check runs it in CI drift mode.

EXACTLY WHICH CASES TO ADD to scripts/extract/gen_core_fixtures.lean, then regenerate crates/fln-conformance/fixtures/core_observables.txt and extend crates/fln-conformance/tests/core_observables.rs to compare the new records:

* Name ordering and rendering — Name.quickCmp, Name.quickCmpAux, Name.quickLt, Name.toString. Emit the verdict for a matrix of pairs covering: str vs str, num vs num, str vs num both directions, shared prefixes, differing prefixes at varying depths, and the anonymous root. quickCmp orders by prefix first, so pairs that differ only deep in the chain are the interesting ones.
* Name hygiene (landed in 3397b9a, currently unoracled) — Name.hasMacroScopes, eraseMacroScopes, simpMacroScopes, appendCore. Emit hygienic names built as the elaborator builds them: <name>._@.<module>._hyg.<scope>, with one and several numeric scopes, plus a _hyg marker with no _@ separator (which erases to anonymous), plus appendCore over str/num/overflowing-num components.
* Level operations outside the data word — Level.addOffset, toNat, isAlwaysZero, occurs, dec, geq, mkLevelMax', mkLevelIMax'. geq especially: it decides constructor-field universes for KR-604 and until this lands its only evidence is in-repo property tests.
* KVMap — findCore, insertCore, erase, getString, getNat, getInt, getBool, getName, getSyntax, DataValue.sameCtor. Insertion order IS the value upstream, so emit maps built by insert sequences that include a replace-in-place, and read every typed getter including type-mismatch and absent-key defaults.
* FileMap — ofString, toPosition, ofPosition, lineStart, getLastLine, getLine. Positions are UTF-8 byte offsets and are wire-visible through diagnostics and the LSP later, so cover multi-byte characters, CRLF, a file with no trailing newline, and positions at both ends of every line.

ACCEPTANCE: the named rows in ci/PARITY_LEDGER.txt move from L1 to L2 with fixtures cited, the fixture regenerates byte-identically on a second run (the generator is deterministic — no timestamps, no paths), and gen_core_fixtures.sh --check passes in drift mode.
close_reason:
Landed in 64cde78. 28 rows raised L1 to L2, four deliberately left at L1 with the reason recorded in the ledger. crates/fln-core/fixtures/gen_core_ext.lean runs under the pinned binary and emits 533 records; crates/fln-core/tests/pin_ext_observables.rs compares them on every run, checks the fixture's recorded commit against SUITE.lock, and treats an unrecognised label as a failure rather than a skip. Regeneration is byte-identical on a second run.

The oracle found a real divergence on its first run: Level.geq disagreed with the pin on 5 of 196 pairs, all succ^k(imax _ (succ _)). It was a re-derivation rather than a transcription — it recursed back through is_geq (normalizing again each step, and normalize is not idempotent per fln-0uvk) and tested the right-hand imax before the left-hand one. Now transcribed arm for arm from Level.lean:620-638. That function decides KR-604 constructor-field universes and was the same one the p8a audit flagged as having no test and no caller: wrong, unused, and unnoticed.

Still L1: Name.quickCmpAux, KVMap.insertCore, KVMap.getSyntax, FileMap.getLine (our accessor is private; whether it should be public API is a decision, not an oversight). Each rises by adding its cases to gen_core_ext.lean.

The generator lives beside its fixture in crates/fln-core rather than scripts/extract because scripts/ is another pane's domain and this bead's staging was scoped to mine; folding it into scripts/extract alongside gen_core_fixtures.sh is a mechanical move for whoever owns that tree.

title: G0: The Laws of the Machine — pre-construction spike gate (§22.1)
description:
## Description

Gate G0, The Laws of the Machine (§22.1), is the pre-construction decision gate: ten compile-tested spikes retire the load-bearing unknowns before W2-W12 interfaces freeze. The ten exact questions cover ABI/OLEAN resurrection, K1 verdict methodology, Golem ABI-valued execution, Vellum syntax/hygiene fidelity, exact olean re-emission, fuel parity, the defeq tail/K2 design, Native Mirror partition viability, instrumented-oracle traces, and authoritative dependency closure/SUITE.lock.

Each child emits exactly one independently validated G0SpikeDecisionV1. G0DecisionSetV1 joins exactly those ten rows; it is not a green-count dashboard. Outcome is Ratified, Amended, or NoGo, while evidence authority separately records Complete, Inconclusive, or InternalFault. Only a Complete Ratified row, or a Complete Amended row after the exact §25 plan/contracts/dependencies/downstream acceptance changes and full rerun, can satisfy a spike. NoGo, missing/stale evidence, unresolved divergence, resource/cancellation refusal, failed run, or InternalFault blocks.

OQ-1 and OQ-2 must be resolved at G0 by G0-5 and G0-6 respectively; assigning either downstream does not retire its load-bearing unknown. G0-8 must resolve OQ-3’s feasibility boundary, exact Native-Mirror partition law, unsupported-row treatment, and ordered closure plan. W6 may own implementation/promotion of already classified rows but cannot inherit an unpriced partition unknown.

The gate requires a single shared SUITE.lock/Reference/Corpus epoch, canonical ABI/OLEAN/census roots, symbol/rule namespaces, oracle classifications, comparison classes, claim scopes, fixture manifests, resource-accounting ownership, and interface commitments across all ten rows. It rejects aggregate green, hidden exclusions, mock-only evidence, comparison downgrade, double-counted work, semantic/telemetry mixing, fake thread labels, surviving named mutations, and any interface-freeze receipt issued before valid decisions.

## Success Criteria

All ten child beads complete their full unit/property/model/mutation, real no-mock positive/failure/restoration/recovery, resource-boundary, productive thread where applicable, strict semantic log, linked telemetry, and independent bundle-validation obligations. Each decision row binds exact question/outcome/evidence authority, D7 claim type and evidence state, epoch/corpus/platform/mode scope, fixture/contract/implementation/mutation/E2E roots, oracle/comparison, budgets/usage, limitations, interface effects, and reviewed amendments. Cross-spike model and mutation suites plant missing/duplicate/stale rows, root/namespace/oracle/comparison/claim/resource conflicts, mock substitution, NoGo or Inconclusive promotion, incomplete amendment propagation, hidden OQ deferral, fake parallelism, semantic/telemetry merge, and premature freeze; every case fails with exact first divergence and recovery. The final real gate E2E validates child bundles read-only and atomically publishes only a complete consistent decision set. No owner assignment, benchmark, prototype compile, percentage, unpriced unknown, or deferred OQ satisfies G0.
design:
G0DecisionSetV1 is the sole gate join and contains exactly one G0SpikeDecisionV1 for each §22.1 child. Child evidence stays child-owned. Decision outcome is Ratified, Amended, or NoGo; evidence authority is an orthogonal Complete, Inconclusive, or InternalFault field. Complete Ratified and fully propagated/rerun Complete Amended are the only satisfying states. NoGo and non-authoritative evidence remain useful findings but block.

Amended rows bind exact §25 wording, rationale, blast radius, affected contracts/interfaces, stable downstream owners, dependency edits, migration/rollback where relevant, and all amended acceptance results. The validator reads the actual plan and graph identities; prose assertion cannot satisfy propagation.

OQ-1 is closed only by G0-5’s serialization decision, OQ-2 only by G0-6’s fuel decision, and OQ-3 only by G0-8’s feasibility/partition/unsupported-row/closure-plan decision. None can be deferred as an unresolved unknown. Later workstreams may implement a resolved contract only.

The join validates common epoch and canonical contract/census roots, symbol/rule ids, oracle and comparison classes, claim/evidence scopes, platform/mode/profile, fixture manifests, resource ownership, productive-thread evidence, and interface-freeze guards. Canonical semantic records and nondeterministic telemetry are separate. G0 introduces no runtime prototype authority.
acceptance_criteria: G0 closes on exactly ten unique current independently validated G0SpikeDecisionV1 rows and one consistent G0DecisionSetV1. Only Complete Ratified or fully propagated and rerun Complete Amended rows satisfy; NoGo, Inconclusive, InternalFault, stale/missing/mock/root-mismatched/overclaimed evidence blocks. OQ-1, OQ-2, and OQ-3 are resolved at their assigned G0 spikes, not handed downstream unresolved. The join enforces identical authoritative epochs/contracts/namespaces/oracle/comparison/claim/resource identities, complete child test/mutation/no-mock/logging/recovery evidence, and no premature interface freeze. Named gate model/mutation/E2E tests cover every missing/duplicate/conflicting/overpromoted/amendment/OQ/thread/telemetry fault and exact recovery. No aggregate green, owner assignment, benchmark, compile-only prototype, hidden exclusion, or deferred unknown satisfies G0.

This epic/gate may close only when every child deliverable is complete; the verification registry maps every implemented public behavior, FL-INV claim, Parity-Ledger row, Behavior Note, and PG/gate claim to named unit/property/mutation coverage plus a shared no-mock E2E scenario; detailed human + schema-versioned NDJSON artifacts are archived; all divergences and skips are classified; no mock-only evidence is used for a release claim; and the final evidence bundle records exact reproduction commands, environment/epoch/mode/platform/thread/seed/cache facts, input hashes, receipts/logical roots, expected final states, first divergences, and cleanup results.

title: W9: Lantern & Palimpsest — daemon server, snapshots, causal proof graph
description:
Workstream W9 "Lantern & Palimpsest" (§14, §15): the single-daemon server behind the unchanged wire dialect, and the provenance substrate that makes the system explain itself.

Lantern: LSP + $/lean/* byte-compatible (plainGoal, plainTermGoal, rpc/* sessions, waitForDiagnostics, semantic tokens, widget delivery) — vscode-lean4 connects unmodified; one daemon, one shared immutable import heap (kills the ~60s x N-workers x GBs multiplication; PG-4/PG-6); snapshot machinery: immutable DocumentSnapshots with publication generations (stale-diagnostics race structurally impossible), sub-command incrementality from the finest enclosing checkpoint, cancel-correct under typing bursts, stable-identity diagnostics dedup, idempotent precondition-checked code actions, progressive proof-state negotiation, per-root epoch capsules, session replay bundles (server bugs become deterministic objects); the machine session API — fork a proof state, apply a tactic, read goals, O(1) per branch, thousands of branches per daemon (§14.4, the number that embarrasses the 18-735s per-branch literature).

Palimpsest: always-on ring-buffer traces + opt-in archives (frankensqlite); the causal proof graph (Bet B7) with typed edge families and completeness classes — ONLY Complete/Conservative edges may drive invalidation or trust (the welding law); unification forensics (minimal disagreement), instance why-not trees, semantic blame slices; semantic diff levels + semantic merge (blocks silent semantic conflicts Git cannot see; nothing merges around the kernel); fragility signals (advisory, D3); time travel, fln replay, repro bundles; build forensics as SQL.

Exit: gate G5 — vscode-lean4 smoke matrix green, PG-4/5/6/L met, session API live.

## Success Criteria

All scope and outcomes stated above remain mandatory, and every dependency/child deliverable required for this epic or gate must be completed at its honest evidence level. The MANDATORY EPIC/GATE CLOSEOUT CONTRACT in Notes must pass with coverage mapping, no-mock E2E evidence, detailed archived human and schema-versioned NDJSON artifacts, reproducible environment facts, and every skip/divergence classified. No feature, compatibility surface, invariant, performance gate, or release claim may be silently narrowed, dropped, or replaced by a prototype.
design: Stage topology: G5 consumes the concrete Lantern, snapshot/session, and replay/protocol stack needed for the daily-driver editor claim. Full W9 additionally closes Palimpsest, causal proof graph completeness, forensics, semantic diff/merge, why-trusts, time travel, repro bundles, and SQL observability, and therefore blocks G6. W9 consumes the G4-complete toolchain and Ledger core through its component graph, not W8 federation/distribution bookkeeping. Every W9 feature remains mandatory before the final sovereign release.
acceptance_criteria:
W9 closes only when Lantern and Palimpsest share one immutable snapshot/provenance truth. Lantern is byte-compatible with the pinned LSP and $/lean dialect for initialization, document lifecycle, diagnostics, goals, terms, RPC sessions, semantic tokens, completions, code actions, progress, and widgets; unmodified vscode-lean4 passes. One daemon shares one import heap while DocumentSnapshots, publication generations, regions, stable diagnostic identities, preconditioned idempotent actions, progressive goals, epoch capsules, and cancellation prevent stale or cross-document publication. Sub-command incremental processing equals clean processing. ProofStateSnapshot and the machine session API fork O(1), enforce capability/budget/epoch ownership, support thousands of branches, release deterministically, and never treat provisional state as verified. Replay bundles reproduce protocol failures exactly. Palimpsest records typed causal nodes and edges for declarations, instances, simp, macros, elaboration, effects, and kernel verdicts with explicit completeness classes; only Complete or Conservative evidence drives invalidation or trust. It provides minimal unification disagreement, why-not instance trees, blame slices, semantic diff/merge that cannot bypass the kernel, fragility signals, why-trusts, time travel, repro bundles, and bounded SQL forensics. Unit/property/model/metamorphic/mutation/lab tests cover protocol ordering, generation races, cancellation storms, snapshot/session lifecycle, capability denial, replay, causal completeness, welding law, graph queries, merge conflicts, storage crash/corruption, budgets, and recovery; named stale-publication, missing-edge, overclaimed-completeness, and merge-around-kernel mutants are killed. Real no-mock editor, terminal/session, replay, causal-query, semantic-merge, crash/fault, and long-soak E2E lanes emit strict bundles. G5 daily-driver evidence plus full Palimpsest scope, all W9 children, scripts/check.sh, cargo/fmt/clippy/UBS, protocol/editor/lab/thread/platform/performance gates are green before G6. No patched editor, per-file duplicated import heap, mock-only RPC, stale diagnostic, incomplete edge used as complete, advisory signal used as authority, silent semantic merge, unbounded trace/query, or deferred listed W9 feature satisfies closure.

REVIEW AMENDMENT — publish an explicit late-producer handoff matrix. W9 freezes provenance edge schemas, completeness grades, admission rules, and welding laws and proves current producers; a G6-facing downstream join proves real adoption by W11/W12 suggestion, capability-session, branch/merge, migration, and repair producers. Synthetic future edges cannot satisfy production integration, and W9 does not wait on future workstreams.

EVIDENCE CONTRACT — strict canonical semantic NDJSON and separately linked bounded telemetry are mandatory. Semantic records contain normalized ids/inputs/roots, typed outcomes, resource class/consumption, decisions, first divergence, cleanup, and exact final state; host, PID, time, paths, cache and performance stay telemetry-only. Validators reject unknown versions, missing/extra/duplicate fields, broken linkage/order, truncation, merged streams, and telemetry in authoritative roots. Productive 1/8/32 applies where safely parallel; named unit/model/property/mutation/fuzz and real no-mock positive/failure/recovery E2E close claims.

title: W1 Reference baseline: cross-profile report and PG target-ratification join
description:
## Description

Join the complete Linux and Apple-silicon pinned-Reference baseline bundles into the W1 report and produce reviewed PG-1 through PG-M target-ratification proposals. The host lanes remain separate statistical populations; the join compares coverage/methodology and presents both, never merges samples or hides a missing profile. Every row binds exact workload, metric/unit, cache/thread/profile, raw and summary roots, host identity, validity/dispersion/confidence, and D7 claim class.

Classify every PG row by comparator kind: Reference ratio, absolute SLO, zero-tolerance correctness join, first-native baseline, or not Reference-observable. Baseline observations are benchmark claims, variance/repeatability decisions are statistical, and target thresholds are SLOs. A non-observable metric remains TARGETED with an owner and future evidence path; it is neither fabricated nor omitted. Correctness joins cannot be ratified by timing data.

Any target amendment is a reviewed decision proposal containing old and proposed target, both host/data roots, methodology/schema, rationale, affected user promise/gate, uncertainty, owner, and approval state. title: Verification manifest: a complete bead's judgement row is checked for non-emptiness, never for judging that closure
description:
scripts/evidence.py validate_verification_manifest, at the derived_state == "complete"
branch, requires only that the row's required array fields be NON-EMPTY. There is no
comparison against the closure it is supposed to judge: no timestamp relation, no
requirement that the row cite the closing commit or the bead comment that records the
work, nothing that distinguishes a row authored for this closure from one authored weeks
earlier for different work on the same bead.

So the close-plus-judgement-row rule is enforced only in its weakest form: a row must
EXIST and be non-empty. Whether it judges this closure is unchecked.

DEMONSTRATED, not theorised, and by my own mistake. At b2ee77cd fln-lyc8 was closed
(status in_progress -> closed, closed_at 2026-07-26T20:50:06) in a commit that did NOT
carry its updated judgement row. The row present at that commit had been authored earlier
and did not record the closing evidence -- it lacked bead-comment 1335 and the local
workspace-gate result that cod_3 then added by hand in 6ad070b6. Re-running the validator
against the exact tree at b2ee77cd returns valid=true, exit 0. Measured, not inferred.

So nothing mechanical caught an atomicity break that the project treats as
release-relevant. cod_3 caught it by reading. That is AGENTS.md item 7's shape exactly: a
claim (this bead is complete) and its evidence (this row), with the JOIN between them --
does this row judge this closure -- unwatched. Every technique in that section compares a
claim against evidence that still exists; here the evidence exists, is non-empty, and is
about something else.

WHY IT IS REACHABLE ACROSS PANES, which is what makes it more than a discipline problem:
br sync --flush-only exports the ENTIRE beads database, not the caller's bead. Another
pane's close, sitting unflushed in the DB, rides into .beads/issues.jsonl on someone
else's flush and can be committed by an agent who does not own the bead, cannot author its
row, and has no reason to look. Verified for the sibling case: fln-sn0w was absent from
HEAD and reached the working tree only through my flush. The pane that creates the

title: W1 contract extraction: canonical pin/target inventory schema and atomic publication
description:
## Description

Define the single canonical, schema-versioned intermediate consumed by every W1 contract extractor. ContractInventoryV1 separates mechanically observed facts from reviewed policy and joins them bijectively; extraction never invents support policy, and policy never substitutes for a raw fact. Every row binds inventory kind, extractor id/version, exact Reference epoch/commit/tree, authoritative source locator, target and ABI class when applicable, raw evidence hash, canonical row identity, and authority state.

Own the candidate-generation and publication protocol. Generation occurs in a fresh candidate location under fixed locale, timezone, path, and toolchain inputs. Publication is atomic and allowed only after schema validation, row uniqueness, policy bijection, cross-output roots, resource limits, and unchanged pre/post governed-input roots succeed. Cancellation, unavailable extraction authority, source-root change, partial traversal/output, ambiguous target facts, or resource exhaustion produces typed Inconclusive/InternalFault evidence, leaves the previously published generation untouched, and never yields a clean or authoritative inventory.

This task owns the common schema, raw/policy join, deterministic identities, target vocabulary, candidate lifecycle, and publication API. The ABI, OLEAN/ILEAN, and extern/builtin tasks own their domain facts. The terminal integration task owns cross-domain rendering, drift CI, and real handoff verification. No Reference code enters a release/runtime closure.

## Acceptance Criteria

ContractInventoryV1 and its policy join are closed, versioned, deterministic, target-aware, independently validated, and shared by all domain extractors. Candidate publication is failure-atomic and root-bound. Named unit/model/property suites, mutation cases, and a real filesystem candidate/recovery E2E prove complete traversal, deterministic two-run output, invalid/duplicate/stale/missing policy handling, target ambiguity, cancellation/resource refusal, source-root races, interrupted publication, cleanup, and exact restoration. Human logs and strict schema-versioned NDJSON carry run/scenario/step ids, inventory/schema/extractor versions, Reference and SUITE.lock roots, target facts, raw/canonical/policy roots, row totals, unresolved rows, resource facts, publication stage, authority, cleanup, and final published root. No partial, stale, mock-only, cross-target-projected, or unbound inventory can close this task.
acceptance_criteria: ContractInventoryV1 and its policy join are closed, versioned, deterministic, target-aware, independently validated, and shared by all domain extractors. Candidate publication is failure-atomic and root-bound. Named unit/model/property suites, mutation cases, and a real filesystem candidate/recovery E2E prove complete traversal, deterministic two-run output, invalid/duplicate/stale/missing policy handling, target ambiguity, cancellation/resource refusal, source-root races, interrupted publication, cleanup, and exact restoration. Human logs and strict schema-versioned NDJSON carry run/scenario/step ids, inventory/schema/extractor versions, Reference and SUITE.lock roots, target facts, raw/canonical/policy roots, row totals, unresolved rows, resource facts, publication stage, authority, cleanup, and final published root. No partial, stale, mock-only, cross-target-projected, or unbound inventory can close this task.

title: W5: Intrinsic table — the extern census implemented natively, row-per-symbol evidence
description:

title: fln-kernel: migrate the five production add_decl sites onto the bounded declaration admission API
description:
Filed by PeachBass (cc_1) on 2026-07-25 while landing franken_lean-j8h's bounded declaration admission. j8h requires that every PRODUCTION caller use the bounded API and that no unbounded path survive for convenience. Inside fln-env that is already true: after the migration audit, zero non-test uses of Environment::add_decl remain in the crate. Every remaining production caller is in fln-kernel, which is cc_2's domain, so it cannot be done from cc_1.

THE FIVE SITES, verified by grep on 2026-07-25:
  crates/fln-kernel/src/lib.rs:138        env.add_decl(ConstantInfo::Defn(v.clone()))      -- the scratch environment for a definition
  crates/fln-kernel/src/admit.rs:1582     env.add_decl(ConstantInfo::Induct(ind.clone()))
  crates/fln-kernel/src/admit.rs:1597     env.add_decl(ConstantInfo::Ctor(ctor.clone()))
  crates/fln-kernel/src/admit.rs:1628     env.add_decl(ConstantInfo::Induct(ind.clone()))
  crates/fln-kernel/src/admit.rs:1643     env.add_decl(ConstantInfo::Ctor(ctor.clone()))
Test callers in fln-kernel/tests and fln-conformance/tests are NOT in scope: a fixture may use the unbounded helper, which is why it survives.

WHAT TO MIGRATE TO. Environment::plan_add_decl(info, DeclarationBudget, CollisionBudget, Option<&dyn CancellationProbe>) -> Outcome<DeclarationPlan>, then PreparedDeclarationAdmission::commit(&env, cancellation) -> Outcome<DeclarationCommitted>. Landed in e14fe98 with d8720ec and 8180b31. Hashing and insertion are one preflighted transaction: the plan is immutable and non-authoritative, is_cacheable is false, commit revalidates schema, duplicate name, base binding and cancellation, recomputes nothing, and publishes exactly once.

WHY IT IS NOT A MECHANICAL SUBSTITUTION, and the part that needs a kernel decision rather than a kernel edit:

1. THE OUTCOME IS WIDER THAN THE RESULT. add_decl returns Result<Environment, EnvError>: two arms. The bounded path returns Outcome<DeclarationCommitted>: Complete{Published | DuplicateName}, Inconclusive, InternalFault. The kernel must decide what a typed Inconclusive means at ITS boundary. It must NOT collapse to a rejection — that is the FL-INV-07 collapse, and a kernel that records "we ran out of room" as "this declaration is invalid" produces a cached wrong verdict. fln-kernel already has KernelInconclusive and D8's ResourceReason vocabulary, so the arm has a home; the question is which of the kernel's own outcomes each maps to.

2. WHO OWNS THE BUDGET. plan_add_decl takes a DeclarationBudget. The kernel's admission boundary has to decide whether the budget is a kernel option, a caller capability, or UNBOUNDED at these specific sites. UNBOUNDED is a legitimate answer for a scratch environment built from ALREADY-ADMITTED declarations — the input is not untrusted there — but it should be an explicit UNBOUNDED with a one-line reason, not an absence.

3. THE SCRATCH-ENVIRONMENT SITES MAY NOT NEED BOUNDING AT ALL. lib.rs:138 and the admit.rs pairs build temporary environments out of declarations the kernel is itself checking. If the untrusted-input boundary is upstream of them, these are internal and UNBOUNDED is correct. That determination is a kernel-invariant judgement and is exactly why this is not a find-and-replace.

CONSTRAINTS. Do not change any canonical byte, digest, or logical root: this is an authority and resource-reporting change only. The frozen declaration goldens in crates/fln-env/src/environment.rs are the net that proves it — capture them before and after and compare, which is how the fln-env slices were verified (both evidence matrices byte-identical at 11 and 41 records).

DELIBERATELY NOT DEPRECATED. Environment::add_decl carries a prominent NOT AUTHORITATIVE FOR RESOURCE PURPOSES doc block but is not #[deprecated], because that would turn fln-kernel red under -D warnings the moment it landed. Marking a peer's build broken is not a migration. When these five sites are done, deprecating it is a one-line follow-up and should be taken.
close_reason: Delivered in a90fadad. All five production sites migrated; rg '\.add_decl\(' over crates/fln-kernel/src returns zero. The three judgements cc_1 flagged are decided once in admit::scratch_admit: budget explicitly UNBOUNDED with its reason (input already traversed under the kernel's own Budget upstream of these sites), duplicate name stays a rejection, and a non-answer never becomes one - which required Stop::Fault mapping to Outcome::InternalFault, flagged on the bead for review since it widens a TCB surface. 113 kernel tests green, budget 6,334 -> 6,382 of 12,000.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
DONE, EXHAUSTIVELY. cc_2, 2026-07-25, commit a90fadad. 113 kernel tests green, fmt clean, clippy clean over every fln-kernel file, ubs 0 critical.

EXHAUSTIVE, NOT SAMPLED. `rg '\.add_decl\(' crates/fln-kernel/src/` now returns ZERO. Your five sites were exactly the five - I re-grepped before starting rather than trusting the list, and found the same set at slightly drifted line numbers (1599/1614/1645/1660 rather than 1582/1597/1628/1643). No sixth site existed then and none exists now. The unbounded path is gone from production in this crate rather than left alive for convenience; the test callers keep it, which is why Environment::add_decl still exists at all.

THE THREE JUDGEMENTS, decided once in admit::scratch_admit rather than five times at the call sites - which also means a future sixth site inherits the decisions instead of re-litigating them.

1. BUDGET: EXPLICITLY UNBOUNDED, NOT ABSENT. Your point 3 is right and I am taking it. All five sites insert material the kernel has ALREADY traversed under its own Budget during header inference and constructor checking. DeclarationBudget bounds the same row families that traversal just walked, so re-bounding would double-charge the same declaration and could refuse one the kernel had already found structurally sound. The untrusted-input boundary is upstream at check(); these are downstream of it. CollisionBudget is UNBOUNDED for the same reason and is written out rather than left to default() - default() IS UNBOUNDED, and a silent agreement between a default and an intention is exactly what this bead exists to make explicit.

2. DUPLICATE NAME STAYS A REJECTION. A completed determination about the declaration - the name is taken - and it was a rejection before the migration too. No change in meaning.

3. A NON-ANSWER NEVER BECOMES ONE, AND THIS COST A KERNEL CHANGE. Your point 1 is the substantive one. Stop was Reject|Exhausted, so an environment InternalFault could only have been reported as a rejection - the FL-INV-07 collapse you named - or as resource exhaustion, which is a misreport since ExhaustionReason is Steps|Depth and neither happened. I added Stop::Fault(String), mapping to Outcome::InternalFault. One exhaustive match site needed updating. Inconclusive from the environment also routes there rather than to a verdict.

That third arm is the part I would flag for review. It widens the kernel's internal outcome vocabulary, which is a TCB surface, and I chose it over two alternatives I rejected: reusing Stop::Exhausted (misreports a fault as a resource event, and a wrong non-answer is still wrong) and collapsing to AlreadyDeclared (the exact failure the bead forbids). If there is a reason the kernel should not be able to say "my own accounting broke" at this boundary, I would rather hear it than have it discovered later.

BUDGET IMPACT: fln-kernel src 6,334 -> 6,382 of the 12,000-line covenant. The helper is ~65 lines of which most is the reasoning above, recorded where the next person will look rather than only here.

ONE THING I DID NOT DO. Environment::add_decl remains public in fln-env and is still reachable from anywhere. Making it unreachable is not this bead's scope and cannot be done from fln-kernel; as I noted on fln-yswb, a structure-guard rule forbidding non-test callers is probably the right closure since it needs no dependency cycle. Worth its own bead if the raw surface is meant to disappear rather than merely go unused.

NOTE FOR WHOEVER RUNS CLIPPY NEXT: `cargo clippy -p fln-kernel` currently reports two errors in crates/fln-env/src/extensions.rs. That is cc_1's live uncommitted WIP, not from this change and not mine to touch. Every fln-kernel file is clean.
