title: Witness matrix: the kernel LOC covenant's disclosed size came from a foreign counter, and was wrong the day it was written
description:
The Witness claim matrix's ONLY Supported row disclosed a kernel size that never came from the
covenant's own counter. It was wrong on the day it was written, and nothing could see it.

MEASURED. crates/fln-conformance/src/witness.rs, row B3-KERNEL-LOC-COVENANT, read:

  "fln-kernel is 6,535 lines across 5 files, under the 12,000 bound ..."

6,535 is the RAW line count of those files. The covenant's counter is count_loc
(tools/structure-guard/src/checks.rs:840): non-blank lines that do not begin with a comment
marker. At e1623223 -- the commit that authored the row, 2026-07-25, Witness slice 2 -- count_loc
measured 5,416 across those same 5 files. The disclosure was therefore wrong by 1,119 lines
before anyone had a chance to let it rot, and by one file thereafter: council.rs entered the TCB
at 104bd8b1 and the row still said five.

  anchor      covenant lines   raw lines   files
  e1623223         5,416         6,535       5     <- 6,535 is what the row disclosed
  fbb9de1b         6,112         7,870       6     <- 50.9% of the bound, 5,888 headroom

Direction: the error OVERSTATES, which is the safe direction for a ceiling claim -- "under
12,000" held either way. But the headroom a reader would cite is off by 20%, and with the two
predicates swapped the identical defect would have made an over-budget kernel look compliant.
The row's enforcement is Supported, which the matrix defines as "asserted AND supported by
evidence", so this was the strongest state in the matrix resting on an unmeasured number.

WHY NOTHING CAUGHT IT. This is AGENTS.md "Evidence & Census Pins" item 7 exactly: the join
between a claim and its evidence was unwatched. Both artifacts are internally consistent -- the
covenant is genuinely enforced, and the row genuinely cites it -- so no single-artifact review
finds it. It is also the hazard bead
franken_lean-kernel-loc-covenant-not-disclosed-t0g7 predicted in the abstract three commits
earlier: "any claim about kernel size has to be re-derived by reimplementing count_loc, which is
a second copy of the algorithm and can drift from the real one." This is that drift, already in
the tree, in the one row that claimed to be supported.

THE REPAIR, and why only half the number is bound. Bind the FILE cardinality in both directions
(the fln-bench-apparatus-empty-referent-bkw6 move: bind a claim to the cardinality of what it
asserts). Do NOT bind the line count:

  * it moves on every kernel edit, so a pinned figure is a wall that reddens a correct repair
    and gets bypassed -- and this is a six-pane shared tree, where that reddens everyone;
  * re-deriving it inside the test plants a SECOND copy of count_loc's predicate, which is the
    precise drift that caused this defect. A guard must not reproduce the shape it guards.

A file entering or leaving fln-kernel is the opposite kind of event: rare, structural, and
exactly the growth D6 says must be disclosed first rather than noticed later. It has already
happened once unnoticed.

The live line count belongs where it is measured -- the guard's own robot line -- which stays
t0g7, open. This bead claims nothing about that.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT EARN. The covenant itself was never in doubt and this must not be read as
doubting it: FLN-STRUCT-015 enforces it on every structure-guard run, FLN-STRUCT-024 refuses a
larger declared limit, and four branches are planted. What was unbound was the matrix's
DISCLOSURE. And the headroom figure now recorded in the row is one measurement at one commit,
class bounded_model, which nothing rechecks: a kernel that grows four thousand lines without
adding a file leaves the new test green and that sentence stale. That is a deliberate, disclosed
limit, not an oversight.

Found by cc_2 on 2026-07-26 while answering whether the LOC covenant should disclose its measured
value bound to the ceiling. Audit and repair at fbb9de1b.

title: Kernel stack calibration must not be able to go stale silently
description:
Filed by cc_2 on 2026-07-25 out of franken_lean-kxbj and franken_lean-4o3n, from a drift I MEASURED rather than one I inferred.

WHAT IS TRUE TODAY. Budget::MEASURED_STACK_BYTES_PER_DEPTH is 5935, a source constant carrying a doc comment that says to rerun the instrument after any change to the descent. The instrument that produced it, calibrate_stack_bytes_per_depth, is #[ignore]d, so nothing in cargo test ever re-takes it. Its correctness is therefore a convention, enforced by whoever remembers.

WHY THE EXISTING WITNESSES DO NOT COVER THIS, and this is the part most likely to be waved away. The five always-on tests in crates/fln-kernel/tests/depth_stack_calibration.rs prove SURVIVAL AT THE SHIPPED PAIRING - Budget::DEFAULT on a 64 MiB thread returns a typed depth non-answer, for_stack_bytes(2 MiB) does the same on Rust's default spawned stack. That is a different claim from "the shipped number still describes this code". Those tests pass unchanged while the true slope drifts upward, because STACK_SAFETY_FACTOR is 2 and 4096 * 5935 * 2 + 64 KiB was rounded up to 64 MiB: there is roughly 3x of headroom before survival is threatened at all. And when it finally is threatened the test does not FAIL, it ABORTS the test binary with an uncatchable stack overflow. So the detector for a stale calibration is currently "the suite dies", with a silent band beneath it in which the recorded number is simply fiction.

THE DRIFT IS REAL AND WAS OBSERVED TWICE IN ONE AFTERNOON, both recorded on kxbj's judgement row:
  1. The same instrument at the same (profile, arch, os) read 5935.3 bytes/depth on this host and 6553.6 on an RCH remote worker - 10.4% apart, and ExecConfig cannot tell those two configurations apart.
  2. After franken_lean-4o3n widened Budget from 16 bytes to about 144, forall_infer and lam_infer each lost one level of ceiling to fixed entry cost while app_infer kept its. The slope held at 5935.3; the intercept did not.

Neither was caught by anything. Both were caught because a human re-ran an ignored test on a hunch.

THE CONSTRAINT. An always-on tripwire that re-measures the marginal cost cheaply - one shape, one stack size, in the existing contained subprocess - and REFUSES when the observed cost is outside what the shipped constant claims. Tolerance must sit strictly inside STACK_SAFETY_FACTOR so the tripwire fires while the margin is still intact rather than after it is spent. This turns the safety factor from a silent absorber of drift into a margin with a tripwire in it, which is what a margin is supposed to be.

BOTH DIRECTIONS ARE VIOLATIONS. An UNDERSTATED constant is the unsafe direction - the derived MIN_STACK_BYTES then promises less stack than the descent needs, which is the kxbj defect returning. An OVERSTATED one is not merely wasteful: it silently shrinks depth_for_stack_bytes for every caller, so a legitimate deep term becomes a typed non-answer that nobody can distinguish from a real one, and under franken_lean-4o3n that manufactured non-answer is exactly what erodes a consensus seat. Both must fire.

ACCEPTANCE. A test that runs in plain cargo test, costs well under a second, and fails when MEASURED_STACK_BYTES_PER_DEPTH no longer describes the descent. Planted violations in both directions proving it fires - not a re-derivation of the constant inside the test, which would be the same number twice and would prove nothing. The tolerance must be justified against the measured host-to-host spread rather than picked, and must be stated as what it is: a benchmark-class bound (D7) with a margin, not a theorem.

WHY THIS IS BUILDABLE NOW AND MUST NOT WAIT, the same test franken_lean-4o3n records: a planted violation is writable today with no new subsystem, it costs a third of a second while nothing violates it, and it must precede the drift. Once the constant is 30% stale, correcting it moves MIN_STACK_BYTES, the fln-conformance worker stack that is bound to it, and every budget derived from it - all at once, under whatever deadline is current, with a working tree that says the old number.

NOT IN SCOPE. Re-measuring on every target, which the instrument cannot do; making ExecConfig distinguish hosts, which franken_lean-4o3n's row already argues against because it would make every budget Extrapolated the moment it crossed a machine; and Slice C.

OWNERSHIP: crates/fln-kernel only. No ci/ surface, no scripts/ surface, no cross-crate signature change.
close_reason: Judgement row authored first (ci/VERIFICATION_MANIFEST.jsonl, valid=true against the live tracker and dry-validated against a synthetic tracker with this bead closed so the complete-state field requirements actually fired). The tripwire is in: an always-on check that asks the real descent whether Budget::MEASURED_STACK_BYTES_PER_DEPTH and STACK_ENTRY_RESERVE_BYTES still describe it, twelve subprocess probes, no bisection, 0.18s for the whole file including the four pre-existing guards. It brackets rather than re-derives -- it never recomputes the constant and compares the result to itself, which would be the same number twice -- and it takes the claim as a PARAMETER so three planted violations can hand it half the true cost, three times the true cost, and an 8 KiB entry reserve, and require a refusal naming the specific direction. The two directions are quantified differently and that is load-bearing: ABOVE the claim is a property of ANY shape, BELOW it is a property of ALL shapes at once, because the constant is the maximum over four descents and defeq_binder sits 24% below it by design; a per-shape low bound would have parked a permanent tripwire 9 points from a correct value and made this a flake generator. Caught while reading the numbers back, before landing. Tolerances justified rather than picked: 25% high is 2.4x the largest observed host-to-host spread and half the safety factor, so it fires with the margin unspent; 33% low is looser because that direction is not a safety failure, only one that manufactures typed non-answers. Fixed in passing, same defect class one level down: Shape::WITNESS named DefEqBinder as the deepest-per-level descent when the measurement says it is the CHEAPEST of the four and overflows last -- the witness still fired because DEFAULT on 2 MiB overflows on any shape, which is exactly why nobody noticed. WITNESS is now the measured worst. NOT CLAIMED: this re-checks the constant on the machine and profile the suite runs in, which is the configuration that matters and is not every configuration; it remains a benchmark-class bound (D7) with a stated margin, not a theorem, and it does not make ExecConfig able to distinguish two hosts sharing a triple. Gates: fmt clean, clippy -D warnings clean, cargo test -p fln-kernel 149 passed 0 failed, structure-guard real_workspace 7/7, ubs 3 criticals all pre-existing documented false positives (a panic! in the ignored measurement and the deliberate self-re-exec Command).

title: G0-8: Mirror-facade viability spike — census + stubs vs real mathlib tactics
description:
G0-8 Mirror-facade viability spike (§22.1-8, feeds §4.3/§18.2): generate the builtin census and facade stubs for a metaprogram-heavy slice (Lean.Meta core + the tactic-framework entry points); compile a curated set of REAL mathlib tactic files against the facade with native services stubbed at prototype depth; enumerate every API whose semantics resist native backing and assign each an honest L-level.

This is the plan CENTRAL bet (B2) priced before interfaces freeze, and the direct mitigation of Critical risk R1 (Meta-API dependence effectively unbounded — packages compile against Lean.* internals that may expose object identity or allocation order the native facade cannot reproduce). The census partition (toolchain-api native / library-code source-elaborated / user-facing-data) must prove TOTAL on the slice: no unclassified symbol, ever — a symbol the census cannot classify blocks the L-level, never gets guessed.

Acceptance: (a) census extraction runs mechanically over the pinned Init/Std/Lean sources for the slice and emits symbol, signature, telescope, effect class, partition class; (b) generated facade stubs compile against real mathlib tactic code; (c) a written resistance list: every symbol whose observable semantics leak implementation detail, each with equivalence class (bit/obs/perf), honest L-level, and Behavior Note candidate; (d) the ordered closure plan for the facade L-level ratchet (resolves OQ-3). Tests: the slice + tactic files seed the metaprogram-corpus rig (§18.2 Mirror conformance).

## Acceptance Criteria

All bead-specific requirements, acceptance conditions, tests, invariants, compatibility surfaces, evidence levels, performance gates, negative/recovery cases, and user-visible behaviors stated above remain mandatory. In addition, the MANDATORY VERIFICATION DEFINITION OF DONE in Notes must be satisfied with named unit/property/mutation suites, at least one shared real-path no-mock E2E scenario plus failure/recovery coverage, detailed human and schema-versioned NDJSON artifacts, and reproducible close evidence. No listed feature or claim may be silently narrowed, deferred, mocked, or declared complete through an unclassified divergence.
design:
OPEN-QUESTION CLOSEOUT — this G0-8 spike owns the feasibility half of OQ-3. It produces the initial symbol-by-symbol census partition, dependency-closure ordering, generated facade schema, and evidence for real tactic/metaprogram probes. It must identify load-bearing unknown rows and hand a versioned decision artifact to franken_lean-epx; it does not claim the production facade L-level ratchet complete.

MirrorSliceDecisionV1 binds the exact transitive symbol closure rooted at the curated Lean.Meta and tactic entry points, the SUITE.lock epoch, generated-census schema, source/environment extraction inputs, Golem-spike ABI contract, fixture set and decision status. The slice may be smaller than the eventual Mirror, but it is total within that frozen closure: every dependency, generated declaration, instance/attribute registration, intrinsic, opaque constant and user-visible data row is present exactly once or the spike blocks.

Each row distinguishes toolchain-API-native, library-source-elaborated, user-data/opaque and RequiresHandler/unsupported prototype behavior, with exact signature/universes, module/owner, effect/capability/determinism class, ABI conversion, object-identity observables, ordering, resource/cancellation behavior, evidence level and W6 promotion owner. Compile compatibility, load/link compatibility and executed semantic compatibility are separate grades. A stub or typed Unsupported can prove boundary honesty, never semantic success.

The real execution path consumes franken_lean-7xe: upstream-authored tactic source is input data, prototype native services and Golem execute it, and the Reference runs only as Tribunal oracle/fixture producer. No Reference elaborator/runtime is linked, hosted or invoked as a product fallback. If a load-bearing row resists native backing, G0 cannot close by assigning it away; it must amend the boundary/interface. Only a proved non-load-bearing row may be handed to W6 with an explicit typed boundary and freeze guard.

The decision artifact includes an ordered dependency-closure plan, cost/row counts, hard-row blast radii and exact downstream API/schema commitments. W6 consumes the same stable row IDs and cannot silently repartition them.

G0 DECISION INTEGRATION — emit exactly one G0SpikeDecisionV1 whose domain payload is MirrorSliceDecisionV1. Outcome is RatifyNativeMirrorPartition, AmendPartitionOrClosurePlan, or NoGo mapped to Ratified/Amended/NoGo. This decision resolves OQ-3 at G0 by freezing the feasibility boundary, exact toolchain-API/library-code/user-data partition law, treatment and evidence state of every unsupported row, dependency/closure order, and downstream W6 owner plan. W6 may implement and promote classified rows but may not receive an unpriced partition unknown. A stub-linked success, omitted load-bearing row, hidden oracle, unsupported row normalized to success, mock tactic, Inconclusive/InternalFault, or incomplete real tactic closure blocks.
acceptance_criteria:

A reviewed resistance table records every implementation-detail leak or hard semantic row, its bit/observational/performance equivalence, current honest L-level, fixture, Behavior Note candidate, load-bearing unknown, owner, and promotion prerequisite. OQ-3 feasibility closes with a versioned dependency-ordered facade closure plan handed to the production census bead, not a false production-completeness claim. Unit/property/model/mutation tests cover census joins, stub signatures, dependency ordering, unsupported rendering, effect/capability facts, generated declarations, and row promotion; named missing-row, stale-row, wrong-partition, placeholder-success, and hidden-fallback mutants are killed. The real no-mock Mirror-seed E2E compiles and executes representative tactic paths where prototype depth permits, records exact unsupported rows elsewhere, plants census/facade divergences, restores inputs, and retains strict symbol/trace/root/evidence bundles. Dependencies, scripts/check.sh, cargo/fmt/clippy/UBS and census/Mirror lanes pass. No source-regex substitute where environment extraction is required, compile-only success presented as semantic parity, guessed row, fake implementation, overclaimed L-level, unresolved load-bearing row, or deferred listed spike output satisfies closure.

The mechanically extracted slice closure reconciles source, compiled environment and generated declarations one-to-one and proves no missing, duplicate, stale or extra row. Every row's signature, ownership, effect/capability, partition, identity/order observables, resource/cancellation behavior, evidence grade and promotion prerequisite are validated. Exact row/name/depth/dependency/output/work limits and fixed cancellation points yield typed Inconclusive without a partial authoritative census.

Real curated mathlib tactic/metaprogram sources both compile and execute through the prototype facade on the G0-3 Golem path where their rows claim semantic support. Reference runs are oracle-only comparisons. Unsupported rows produce exact typed row-ID diagnostics and cannot be counted in the executed denominator. Productive 1/8/32 fixed-input runs preserve semantic traces, generated names, diagnostics, roots and decision rows.

Unit/property/model/mutation suites cover closure joins, overloads, generated declarations, instances/attributes, effect and capability facts, ABI converters, row ordering, partition transitions and resistance-table completeness. Mutants omit dependencies, classify library source as native, return placeholder success, hide RequiresHandler, call an oracle fallback, change a stable row ID, promote compile-only evidence, or drop an identity/order observable; each is killed by a named assertion.

Strict bundles separate semantic records from timing/host telemetry and include pin/census/Golem/fixture/row/trace/root IDs, exact executed/unsupported status, evidence and claim class, limits/usage, mutation/first divergence, restoration and final state. Validators reject unclassified or load-bearing deferred rows, denominator games, stale generated stubs, hidden fallbacks, cross-pin evidence, fake 1/8/32 work or an OQ-3 handoff without a frozen boundary.

MANDATORY VERIFICATION DEFINITION OF DONE (inherits franken_lean-rur; additive to this bead's own Tests/Acceptance):
1. Unit coverage: deterministic happy-path, boundary, malformed-input, resource-exhaustion, cancellation, and failure-atomicity cases for every new public behavior; property/metamorphic and mutation-kill tests wherever an invariant or equivalence is claimed.

class bounded_model. Landed at the commit whose subject is
"feat(facade): structural class emission closes ratchet step 1".

Increment 9's own artifact named step 1 and priced it at 29 rows plus 20 instance
registrations, all failing on one mechanism: an axiom cannot be a CLASS. The emitter
now rebuilds structures AS structures from the pin's constructor telescope, and the
step is closed by the same rig that priced it, on the same nine curated real mathlib
metaprogram files.

MEASURED, before -> after:
  curated demand available    518 -> 574 of 581
  unresolved                   63 -> 7
  demanded rows emitted       397 -> 427 of 442
  instance registrations kept  61 -> 82   (dropped 20 -> 6)
  per-symbol L0                45 -> 9    (L1 515 -> 551)
  ratchet step 1 members       29 -> 0
144 structural declarations (14 class, 130 structure) generate 697 projections; 25
structures fall back to the axiom form, each carrying the reason it fell back.

THREE FACTS THE STRUCTURAL FORM SURFACED. None is visible to a stub emitter, and two
of them cost real measurement time, so they are recorded rather than summarised.

1. A ONE-MODULE FACADE RE-CREATES A SHADOWING THE REFERENCE NEVER HAS. Lean.Option is
   a structure, so inside a declaration named Lean.Syntax.reprint the printed type's
   "Option String" resolves to Lean.Option and the pin says "Function expected at
   Option". Upstream never hits it: there, Syntax.reprint is elaborated in a module
   that has not yet imported Lean.Option, and module order does the disambiguation for
   free. A facade that declares the whole closure at once has no module order to lean
   on. Every constant occurrence is now root-anchored, driven by the pin's own
   used-constant list for that type so only exact constant tokens are rewritten. 168
   rows. The first symptom was a coverage REGRESSION (397 -> 338) that looked like the
   structural idea failing; it was this, and it was mechanical.

2. CONSTRUCTOR BINDERS ARE THE WRONG SOURCE FOR CLASS PARAMETERS. Lean makes
   constructor parameters implicit, so a class emitted from the ctor telescope reads
   "class Lean.AddMessageContext {m : Type -> Type}" and then "AddMessageContext
   CoreM" is "Function expected at". Parameter binder kinds now come from the
   structure's OWN type telescope. 76 rows, 45 of them demanded.

3. THE FACADE EXPOSES 4 PRIVATE FIELDS AS PUBLIC PROJECTIONS, disclosed rather than
   discovered. The Reference does not export a projection for them (env.find? on the
   derived name returns none, which is why the first structural run refused on
   Lean.Environment.base and its kin); the structural block does. That is a PERMISSIVE
   divergence: a probe can resolve a name the Reference would refuse. It is recorded
   per row and in the module summary, and it is a Behavior-Note candidate the Mirror
   rig must either close or license.

THE COMPILE RIG NOW CHECKS TYPES, NOT ONLY NAMES, and this is the part of increment 9
that was weakest. Each row gets "#check @X" plus an ascription
"noncomputable def flnchk_i.{lvls} : <the pin's printed type> := @X", so the PIN
decides type identity up to defeq rather than a string comparison, which would drown
in universe renaming (the pin prints u,v,w; #check prints u_1,u_2,u_3). For an axiom
row the ascription is TAUTOLOGICAL -- the axiom was declared from that very string --
and the artifact says so in its own summary. For the 697 class projections it is not:
Lean DERIVES those types from the structural block's fields, so this is the only thing
that checks the facade's derived types agree with the Reference's. Result: 0 type
mismatches over 370 of 407 distinct symbols; the other 37 are Init-substrate rows the
facade does not declare and therefore carries no signature for.

GUTTED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, because 0 mismatches is exactly what a dead check reports.
Deleting one axiom from the facade flips exactly one check to unresolved (available
518 -> 517 at the time). Planting one wrong signature in the module manifest yields

control still resolves 37 where the facade resolves 400.

BLOCKER IS INSTANCE SYNTHESIS, NOT DEFAULT EMISSION. 2026-08-20, pin v4.32.0, class
bounded_model. The rejected emitter is NOT in the tree; step 2's action row now
carries the measurement.

THE HYPOTHESIS, and it was a good one. 7 of the 9 residual L0 rows fail on an
optParam whose printed DEFAULT VALUE will not elaborate -- "optParam
Lean.Meta.Context { }", "optParam Lean.Meta.Simp.SimprocsArray (List.toArray
List.nil)". A structure emitted without its field defaults cannot accept "{ }", so
emitting the defaults looked like the fix. The pin hands them over cleanly
(getDefaultFnForField? plus the _default constant's value: "id Bool.false", "id
Option.none", "id { }"), so this was cheap to try.

18 of 146 structures kept their defaults; 41 had them dropped by the repair loop.

WHY IT CANNOT WORK IN THIS FORM, and this is the part worth keeping. The four
structures the residual rows actually need -- Lean.Meta.Context, Lean.Meta.State,
Lean.Elab.Term.Context, Lean.Elab.Term.State -- are ALL in the dropped 41, each with
the pin's own reason: synthInstanceFailed, application type mismatch, overloaded.
Their defaults are "Inhabited.default" and "∅", so elaborating them needs INSTANCE
SYNTHESIS over types the facade holds opaquely. Emitting the default text cannot
conjure the instance. Meanwhile the 18 that did keep defaults broke three rows that

both directions.

SO STEP 2'S PREREQUISITE IS RESTATED FROM EVIDENCE: instance coverage sufficient for
optParam default values to synthesize over facade types -- not field-default

INCREMENT 12 (cc_4, OC-010): STEP 2 CLOSES TO THREE ROWS, AND MY OWN STATED
PREREQUISITE FOR IT WAS WRONG. 2026-08-20, pin v4.32.0, corpus 81a5d257, class
bounded_model.

  curated demand available  574 -> 580 of 581     unresolved 7 -> 1
  per-symbol L0               9 -> 3              L1 551 -> 557
  demanded rows emitted     427 -> 439 of 442     quarantined 59 -> 31
  instance registrations     82 kept / 6 dropped -> 94 kept / 1 dropped
  ratchet step 2 members      9 -> 3

THE RETRACTION FIRST. Increment 11 concluded, and the artifact's step-2 action row
said, that the prerequisite was INSTANCE COVERAGE: optParam defaults like
"optParam Lean.Meta.Context { }" need Inhabited and EmptyCollection synthesised over
facade-opaque types. That is measured false. Printing each type with
pp.structureInstances and pp.notation off renders the same default as a fully
applied constructor term with every instance passed EXPLICITLY, so the synthesis
requirement disappears completely. That third printer tier was implemented, applied
to exactly the 16 failing rows, and rescued ZERO of them. The instances were never
what stood in the way; I had inferred the prerequisite from the shape of the error
rather than from testing it, which is the same move increment 4 made with the census
digests.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY BLOCKING THEM, four mechanisms, each measured and each fixed:

1. REDUCIBLE-ALIAS OPACITY, and this is the one that matters beyond these rows.
   Lean.LMVarId is an ABBREVIATION for Lean.LevelMVarId; Lean.PHashMap for
   Lean.PersistentHashMap. The pin therefore accepts BEq LevelMVarId where
   BEq LMVarId is wanted. Declared as opaque axioms the two become distinct
   constants with no defeq between them, and every row that needs the unfolding
   fails. The facade now emits reducible constants transparently, as a FIXPOINT
   rather than a pass: a transparent value names further abbreviations, and
   PHashMap only surfaced after LMVarId was already fixed. 604 rows, including
   CoreM, MetaM, TermElabM, TacticM and CommandElabM -- the monads every real
   tactic is written in.

2. MONOTONE QUARANTINE. A row that failed an early attempt was never reconsidered,
   even after the dependency that broke it was repaired. Measured: 8 of the 16
   quarantined rows elaborate cleanly against the FINISHED facade. Re-admission
   rounds now clear the quarantine and re-promote the stronger forms; the winning
   round is chosen by demanded-surface coverage, then by residue size, so the
   result does not depend on the order the rounds happened to run in.

3. BLAME BY BARE LOCATION. Any "candidate.lean:<line>:" mention counted as blame --
   including Note: lines and the secondary locations of OTHER errors -- so rows that
   were never the cause were quarantined with an empty reason string. That empty
   reason was the tell. Bare locations are now a fallback used only when no error:
   line named a declaration.

4. STRUCTURE-GENERATED COMPANIONS. A structure block generates casesOn,
   _sizeOf_inst and friends; emitting an axiom for one is a redeclaration, and the
   redeclaration branch filed it as "provided by the Init substrate" -- a FALSE row,
   because Init does not have it and the name disappears entirely if that structure
   later demotes to an axiom. Verified against the pin directly (a bare structure
   does generate both) and against the facade (Lean.ImportM.Context.casesOn
   resolves while the manifest called it unemitted). Companions are now treated as
   provided, and the two senses of "already declared" are distinguished.

DISCLOSED, because the artifact has changed character: 604 of its rows are now
DEFINITIONS carrying the pin's values, not declarations the facade stands behind.
They are exactly the pin's reducible abbreviations, oracle-extracted like every
other row, each carrying form=transparent-abbrev so they can be enumerated and
audited, and the module summary says this in its own words rather than leaving the
coverage number to imply otherwise. A reader who wants the pure-stub number should
read it off the form column, not off the headline.

THE RESIDUE IS THREE ROWS, each with the pin's own diagnostic on its row: two
unresolved on _root_.Lean.PersistentHashMap.mk, one application type mismatch.

GUTTED. A peer added a row-removal control INSIDE the rig while I was working --
it selects a demanded leaf axiom, removes exactly that declaration, and requires the
probe row to go unavailable. It passes on this artifact, so every future run carries
its own missing-row control rather than relying on my hand-run mutant. Planting one
wrong signature in the manifest still yields exactly one type-mismatch (580 -> 579).
The empty-facade control resolves 37 where the facade resolves 406.

UNCHANGED BOUNDS: nothing was executed, so no row exceeds L1 and every equivalence
class stays TARGETED. The curated FILES are still not elaborated against the facade.
One host, one pin, one instant.

COORDINATION: scripts/extract/facade_compile.py now carries another pane's
row-removal control; I did not commit that file, and I verified my working copy of
facade_module.py is a strict superset of their 52db68c8 changes -- no peer line was

INCREMENT 13 (cc_4, WAVE 7): THE LAST THREE RATCHET ROWS WERE ONE BAD BINDER, NOT
THREE SEMANTIC FAULTS. 2026-08-20, pin v4.32.0, corpus 81a5d257, class
bounded_model. Landed at 8d5fc410, scripts/extract/facade_module.py only.

  curated-demand available   580 -> 581 of 581     unresolved 1 -> 0
  per-symbol L0                3 -> 2              L1 557 -> 558
  demanded rows emitted      439 -> 440 of 442     quarantined 31 -> 28
  structural declarations    156 -> 169            transparent 604 -> 653
  type mismatches                                  0 (unchanged)

THE CHAIN. Lean.Meta.MetaM.run, Lean.Meta.simpGoal and Lean.PrettyPrinter.delab all
recorded "Application type mismatch" and read like three independent hard rows. They
were one emission bug three layers down. The structural block for
Lean.PersistentHashMap emitted an instance PARAMETER by name:

  [inst._@.Lean.Data.PersistentHashMap.3696607590._hygCtx._hyg.4 : _root_.BEq α]

That is a PARSE error. A parse error is not local: everything after it in the file
goes undeclared and reports as "unknown identifier", so the repair loop blamed a
dozen innocent rows, demoted PersistentHashMap, which cost InferTypeCache (a
reducible alias for PersistentHashMap ExprConfigCacheKey Expr) its transparent form,
which is why MetaM.run's default value would not typecheck against Cache.mk. The
recorded reasons pointed at the last link every time, which is why three waves of
reasoning about "instance coverage" and then "alias opacity" never reached it.

WHAT I SHOULD HAVE DONE SOONER: read attempt 1's candidate file instead of the
recorded quarantine reasons. The reasons are the pin's message for the row, but a
cascade makes every reason downstream of the real fault. Two minutes with
--max-attempts 1 and maxErrors=6 showed "unexpected token ':'" at the top.

FOUR EMISSION FAULTS FIXED, all of the same class -- they produce PARSE errors and
therefore cascades rather than local failures:

1. INSTANCE BINDER NAMES. The name of an instance binder is never referenced, so an
   unwritable one is dropped: [T] is the same binder. The old test looked only for
   the inaccessible dagger and missed the hygienic form entirely.
2. LEAN KEYWORDS AS FIELD NAMES. Lean.NameGenerator.private and Lean.Lsp.Range.end
   emitted "private : α" and "end : Position". Name components are now escaped with
   French quotes when they are keywords.
3. AN ASCII-ONLY IDENTIFIER TEST. My first writability test was [A-Za-z_]-shaped, so
   it called α unwritable and refused Lean.ToMessageData and Lean.Option, costing
   their projections -- measured as an 8-check regression before I caught it. The
   test is now NEGATIVE: writable unless it carries a character no Lean identifier
   can hold.
4. BINDER KIND RESOLVED AFTER THE RENAME. A structure parameter takes its binder
   kind from the structure's own type rather than the constructor's, so the rename
   must see the kind it will actually be rendered with.

Also landed, from the same investigation: quarantine is no longer a same-pass
action. A row blamed alongside the very dependency that broke it is deferred while
anything else is still being repaired (bounded at two deferrals, then it lands in
the residue); the same victim rule now applies to transparent and structural
demotions; and the defer budget resets per re-admission round instead of being
exhausted globally by early rounds.

THE RESIDUE IS TWO ROWS, and NEITHER is exercised by the curated slice --
used_by_curated is empty for both: Lean.Meta.MetaM.run and Lean.PrettyPrinter.delab,
each carrying the pin's own diagnostic. The curated metaprogram demand is now fully
resolved against the standalone facade.

FOR COD_4, and this is a live blocker on your file, not a complaint. Closing the
demanded quarantine population trips choose_quarantine_control in
scripts/extract/facade_compile.py: it REFUSES when no demanded row is quarantined,
because its control has no member left to observe. That is the repaired-population
shape -- driving a population to zero makes its live guard unkillable, and here it
hard-fails the whole rig. It wants a PLANTED synthetic member rather than a real
casualty, the same way the row-removal control plants its own deletion. I did not
touch your file: the numbers above were measured with a scratch copy that relaxes
only that one guard, so they are reproducible only after you repair it.

SCOPE OF THIS COMMIT: scripts/extract/facade_module.py alone. The artifacts under
contracts/ are NOT regenerated here, so they still describe the 580/581 state; they
will move when the rig can run unrelaxed.

UNCHANGED BOUNDS: nothing was executed, so no row exceeds L1 and every equivalence
class stays TARGETED. The curated FILES are still not elaborated against the facade.
One host, one pin, one instant.

INCREMENT 14 (cc_4, WAVE 13): ALIAS VALUES PRINTED EXPLICITLY — BOTH RESIDUE ROWS
LAND, AND THE SLICE IS L1-TOTAL. 2026-08-20, pin v4.32.0, corpus 81a5d257, class
bounded_model. Landed at 2855076935bb52b6, scripts/extract/facade_module.py only.

  demanded rows emitted    440 -> 442 of 442     quarantined 28 -> 26
  curated-demand available 580 -> 581 of 581     unresolved 1 -> 0
  per-symbol L0              2 -> 0              L1 558 -> 560
  transparent declarations 653 -> 664            of which explicit-value 76
  type mismatches                                0 (unchanged)

THE CAUSE, one more layer of the mechanism increment 12 named. delab's type mentions
Lean.PrettyPrinter.Delaborator.OptionsPerPos, a reducible abbreviation for
Std.TreeMap SubExpr.Pos Options compare. Its transparent form was refused with
"failed to synthesize instance of type class", so it fell back to an opaque axiom,
and EmptyCollection (Std.TreeMap ...) then no longer matched EmptyCollection
OptionsPerPos. Lean.Meta.MetaM.run failed one layer along the same chain.

The refusal was never about the alias. The VALUE was printed in READABLE form, which
leaves instance arguments to be SYNTHESISED, and a facade that holds its classes
opaquely cannot synthesise them. Types already had the explicit-printer ladder;
values did not. Alias values are now probed in an explicit rendering too, and a
transparent row the pin refuses gets that rendering before demotion. 76 of 664
transparent rows need it. The readable form is still tried first on purpose: it is
what a reader can audit, and the ladder spends verbosity only where the pin demands
it.

Note for the record: increment 12 concluded "instance coverage was NOT the blocker"
and that was right about the ROWS it was measuring. It was not right as a general
statement about the facade — here instance synthesis is exactly what blocked the
last two, in a place I had not looked: the value side of a transparent alias rather
than the type side. Both facts stand; the second narrows the first.

A MECHANISM BUILT AND REMOVED IN THE SAME INCREMENT, recorded because the reasoning
failed rather than the code. I first built a TAIL RE-ADMISSION pass on the premise
that both rows elaborate cleanly when appended at the END of the finished module,
where every declaration is already in scope. That premise came from my own
diagnostic printing only the first 2500 characters of the pin's output: the linter
warning block filled it and the error was truncated away, so a failing row read as
clean. Measured properly, both rows fail at the tail as well, and the pass
re-admitted ZERO in both its batch form and its per-row form (28 tried, 0 admitted).
It is NOT in the commit. Inert machinery that costs two minutes a run is worse than
the finding written down, and the finding is: my "elaborates clean" claim in the
first half of this wave was an artifact of a truncating harness, not a measurement.

title: fln-hash: earn the cross-platform vector and multi-host logical-root identity claims on certified CI hosts
description:
Split out of franken_lean-rps by cc_3 on 2026-07-25 when that bead closed on its delivered substance. This is the part of its acceptance that is UNEARNED rather than untested: it needs certified-matrix CI hosts to exist, and no amount of local work can supply them.

## The two claims

1. "hash vectors checked in and stable across platforms". Checked in is done twice over: crates/fln-hash/fixtures/blake3_vectors.txt carries the official upstream BLAKE3 vectors (all three modes plus extended output, the independent ground truth the L2 spec-vectors rows in ci/PARITY_LEDGER.txt point at), and crates/fln-hash/fixtures/domain_vectors.txt freezes all twelve registered domain tags with four digests each, including a chunk-boundary input and a multi-chunk input that exercises the parent/tree path. STABLE ACROSS PLATFORMS is not done: every digest in both files was produced on one host, and the domain-vectors header says so in as many words rather than implying otherwise.

2. The logical-root determinism criterion's "(in CI) different hosts produce identical roots" clause. The thread-count half is done and now genuinely exercises a schedule: three deterministic adversarial accumulation orders plus real concurrency at the project matrix of one, eight and thirty-two threads with arrival order decided by lock contention rather than join order, and the full input closure rendered on mismatch (eb4c674). The different-hosts half is untouched.

## Acceptance Criteria

Both vector fixtures are recomputed on every host of the certified platform matrix and compared byte-for-byte, and a logical root over a fixed declaration and options closure is computed on at least two distinct hosts and compared. A mismatch must fail the run and print the full input closure and the host facts on both sides, so a divergence localizes to a host rather than being reported as a generic difference. The evidence must be reproducible and archived, and the run must be a real no-mock one on real hosts: a single-host run that emulates a second platform does not discharge this. Until it runs, the cross-platform wording in fln-hash's documentation, the parity ledger, and any release note must stay at the level the evidence actually supports.

## Notes

Deliberately scoped to the evidence, not to code: no defect is known or suspected here. The BLAKE3 core is deterministic integer arithmetic with no platform-dependent paths, and the canonical encoders use fixed-width little-endian primitives throughout, so the expectation is that this passes on first run. That expectation is exactly why it must be run — an unearned claim that happens to be true is still unearned, and per D7 a claim's evidence class is not allowed to outrun its evidence.
close_reason:
Closed by cc_3 on 2026-07-25, commit 40de4f6. The deliverable was an honest evidence position, and the two halves of the claim came out differently.

EARNED — MULTI-HOST IDENTITY, and it was reachable from here, which I did not expect when I filed this bead. An RCH remote build worker is a genuinely different physical machine rather than a simulation of one, so a real two-host comparison was available without waiting for a CI matrix. The frozen domain vectors and a LogicalRoot over a fixed closure were recomputed on two distinct machines and agree exactly:

  x86_64-linux-unix-64bit-le|sensedemobox|a24527eb...|17a64c7e...
  x86_64-linux-unix-64bit-le|hetzner2    |a24527eb...|17a64c7e...

fixture_digest is one digest over the whole of domain_vectors.txt, so a single field carries all twelve domain tags and all forty-eight frozen vectors: if any of them were host-dependent, that host's digest would differ. logical_root is built from constants so it depends on nothing but the code.

NOT EARNED — CROSS-PLATFORM IDENTITY, and the reason is the finding rather than a scheduling note. SUITE.lock line 26 declares exactly ONE certified target, x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu. The "certified platform matrix" therefore has a single member, and cross-platform identity is not merely untested but UNDEFINED: there is no second platform to be identical to. No number of runs on the machines above can raise it. That is a stronger and more useful statement than the "pending CI hosts" framing this bead inherited from me when I filed it, and it corrects that framing.

THE LEDGER NOW CARRIES BOTH CLAIMS SEPARATELY. Four rows where there were none, and the absence was the actual problem: the claim existed only in prose, which is precisely the state B8 forbids. Domain.vectors.multi-host-identity and LogicalRoot.multi-host-identity at L2/OBSERVED citing crates/fln-hash/fixtures/host_attestations.txt; the two cross-platform rows at L0/BLOCKED with freshness suite-lock-declares-one-certified-target, so the row states what would raise it rather than implying somebody forgot to run something. L2 is the ceiling on the earned rows for the same reason as the BLAKE3 rows above them: the oracle is our own recorded consensus, not an external specification.

THE TRAP THIS BEAD EXISTS TO CLOSE, handled structurally rather than by good intentions. A cross-platform test that only ever runs on one platform passes trivially and reads as evidence. So the in-crate test asserts only what one host can honestly assert: that THIS host reproduces the recorded consensus, which makes every machine that runs the suite a re-check of host-independence rather than a witness to it; and that the attested platform set has exactly one member. The second assertion is not a limitation dressed up as a check, it is a trigger — the day a genuinely different platform agrees, the suite fails with "that is new evidence, not a failure" and names both platforms, forcing the BLOCKED row to be raised deliberately instead of leaving new evidence unclaimed. A host can only enter the file by actually running there, which is what keeps a single-host run from producing multi-host evidence.

An unreachable host is simply ABSENT from the file rather than recorded as anything, because a host that could not be reached is not a host that agreed.

PROVED BY PLANTING, both directions: drifting the recorded consensus fails with "this host's domain vectors differ from every recorded host's"; adding an aarch64-macos row fails with the platform-set trigger naming both platforms and telling the reader to raise the ledger row.

REPORTED, NOT EDITED — README OVERCLAIM. README.md lines 38, 43 and 308 state bit-identical artifacts and results "across the certified platform matrix" and "across platforms" without qualification. On the evidence above that wording is stronger than the matrix permits, which is exactly what documentation CI is supposed to reject. README is a shared file and outside my staging scope, so it is recorded in the ledger comment block and here for its owner. The honest wording would be multi-host on the certified target, with cross-platform stated as a target rather than a property — the matrix has one member, so "across the certified platform matrix" is currently true only vacuously, which is the worst kind of true.

GATES: cargo test --locked -p fln-hash -p fln-core exit 0 (fln-core 92, fln-hash 50 lib + 18 integration). parity_ledger 2/2, including rows_above_l0_cite_real_evidence which validates that the new L2 rows cite a fixture that exists. fmt clean. clippy -p fln-hash --all-targets -D warnings exit 0. ubs exit 0. Staged crates/fln-hash and the four ledger rows I own.

WHAT REMAINS, and it is not fln-hash's to do: a second target line in SUITE.lock. SUITE.lock is the pin authority and adding a certified target is an epoch-class decision, not a test change. Once it exists, the procedure is one command on the new machine (cargo test -p fln-hash --lib domain::tests::emit_host_attestation -- --nocapture), one pasted row, and raising two ledger rows — the trigger will insist on it.

title: W2: Marrow object model + tri-state RC — the lean_object ABI twin
description:
Implement the Marrow object model + tri-state reference counting (§6.1, §6.1b, §6.2; crates fln-rt + fln-unsafe-abi): the Reference runtime object model, exactly, under the exported lean_* names — object header (RC word, memory-kind/other byte, tag byte), constructor objects with scalar-field packing, arrays/scalar arrays/strings (UTF-8 with byte-length/capacity semantics), closures (arity, fixed args), thunks, tasks, IO.Refs, external objects with class vtables, bignum objects (fln-bignum-backed mpz-shim view), small Nats as odd tagged pointers ((n << 1) | 1). Every layout constant comes from the W1 generated contract tables.

Two heaps, one membrane: CompatHeap (exact ABI, membrane-only allocation, all unsafe confined to fln-unsafe-abi with ledger rows per site) vs NativeHeap (typed asupersync region handles); generated converters with declared ownership and failure semantics; lazy boundary-specific conversion (a metaprogram that never inspects a term never forces its Compat projection — memory-doubling risk R10 is the named gate PG-6, not an accident). Tri-state RC: single-threaded fast path, atomic shared, persistent-never-counted — matching upstream so ABI-crossing borrow/inc/dec behaves identically. Hardened builds: debug ownership shadows (double-release + foreign-pointer misuse detection, quarantine, deterministic replay events).

Structural laws (D3): no fln-unsafe-* crate depends on fln-kernel/fln-checker; no unsafe export launderable into a checked declaration; panic law at the ABI boundary (§6.5). Acceptance: G0-1/G0-3 findings folded; C4 probes pass both directions on the implemented subset. Tests: layout unit tests generated FROM the contract module; RC balance property tests; ownership-shadow mutation tests.

## Acceptance Criteria

All bead-specific requirements, acceptance conditions, tests, invariants, compatibility surfaces, evidence levels, performance gates, negative/recovery cases, and user-visible behaviors stated above remain mandatory. In addition, the MANDATORY VERIFICATION DEFINITION OF DONE in Notes must be satisfied with named unit/property/mutation suites, at least one shared real-path no-mock E2E scenario plus failure/recovery coverage, detailed human and schema-versioned NDJSON artifacts, and reproducible close evidence. No listed feature or claim may be silently narrowed, deferred, mocked, or declared complete through an unclassified divergence.
acceptance_criteria: Marrow implements every generated lean_object layout and exported ownership contract required by the pinned ABI: headers, tags, scalar packing, constructors, arrays/scalar arrays, UTF-8 strings with byte length/capacity, closures and fixed args, thunks, tasks, IO.Refs, external class/vtable objects, bignum views, and odd-tagged small Nats. All offsets/tags/widths come from generated contract rows and compile-time/layout tests. CompatHeap and NativeHeap are type-separated; generated lazy converters are the only membrane and declare ownership, allocation, failure, capability, and no-claim boundaries. Tri-state RC matches single-threaded, atomic-shared, and persistent-never-counted behavior across borrow/inc/dec and concurrent transitions. Every unsafe site lives only in fln-unsafe-abi, has a ledger row and safe fallback, cannot depend on kernel/checker or export a checked-declaration capability, and catches panics at the ABI boundary. Debug ownership shadows detect/quarantine/replay double release, foreign pointers, wrong heap, stale external class, and RC imbalance. Unit/property/model/mutation suites cover every generated layout, tag/packing boundary, object lifecycle, conversion, RC interleaving, external callback, malformed pointer/class, resource limit, and recovery; named drop/retain/tag/layout/converter/unsafe-laundering mutants are killed. Real no-mock C4 E2E loads Reference-built plugins and upstream-generated objects, calls both directions, exercises faults and cleanup, and retains strict ABI/ownership/root/process evidence across certified platforms. G0 findings, dependencies, scripts/check.sh, cargo/fmt/clippy/UBS, unsafe/dependency guards, stage0/plugin/soak/thread/platform lanes pass. No handwritten layout, raw pointer outside membrane, eager whole-world conversion, unchecked foreign object, leak/double-free waiver, hidden upstream runtime, unsafe authority laundering, or deferred listed object family satisfies closure.
notes:
MANDATORY VERIFICATION DEFINITION OF DONE (inherits franken_lean-rur; additive to this bead's own Tests/Acceptance):
1. Unit coverage: deterministic happy-path, boundary, malformed-input, resource-exhaustion, cancellation, and failure-atomicity cases for every new public behavior; property/metamorphic and mutation-kill tests wherever an invariant or equivalence is claimed.
2. E2E coverage: add or extend at least one shared scripts/e2e scenario for the real user-visible path, plus a negative/recovery scenario. Release-level evidence uses the no-mock lane (real Reference binary/artifact/filesystem/editor/process/host as applicable). A mock may support a unit test but may not close an L-level, PG gate, or public claim.
3. Detailed logs: emit both concise human logs and schema-versioned NDJSON with run/scenario/step ids; bead, claim, invariant, Parity-Ledger row, and gate ids; exact command/argv with secrets redacted; cwd; epoch/mode/profile/platform/thread-count/seed/cache-state/host facts; canonical input hashes; expected vs actual; monotonic start/end/duration; resource and budget facts; exit status/signal; stdout/stderr artifact references; receipt/logical roots; first-divergence data; cleanup and asserted final state. Never swallow stderr, never leak secrets, and bound adversarial log volume.
4. CI/closeout: archive logs, fixtures, repro bundles, and evidence manifests; failures must be diagnosable from artifacts alone. Run scripts/check.sh, cargo test, the bead-specific unit/property suites, relevant Tribunal differential/mutation/fault lanes, and the shared E2E scenario. The close evidence names every test/scenario id and artifact location; skips require a typed, logged, honest L-level limitation and may not satisfy the skipped claim.
close_reason: Every acceptance family present with named evidence (census: comment 1772); NativeHeap (51de4533) and the lazy converter membrane (3b34d5c5) landed this session, closing the two-heap architecture; stage0 gauntlet verified 8/8 lanes this session; structure-guard PASS. The asupersync-substrate question is routed as a declared, mechanically-reversible divergence.

MOCK/PLACEHOLDER AUDIT OF crates/fln-unsafe-abi (cc_2, ~6 KLOC, commit 72ce1b8). Could not claim this bead — br refuses, it is blocked by franken_lean-53v, franken_lean-7xe, franken_lean-y24 — so this lands against it without a status change.

ONE DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED: rc::inc_ref_n's ST branch guarded overflow with debug_assert! and then wrapping_add. debug_assert! is compiled out in release, so there was no guard where it counts. m_rc < 0 IS the MT encoding (mark_mt negates in place), so a wrapped count silently reclassifies the object's threading discipline and every later dec takes the atomic path on an unsynchronized object. Now checked_add + expect. Proved by running the new test in BOTH profiles: in debug it passes against the UNFIXED code (the old debug_assert fires with the same message), so only the --release run discriminates — unfixed it failed "test did not panic as expected", fixed it passes. Details in the commit.

Latent today: inc_ref_n is pub(crate) and internal callers all pass n=1, so it needs ~2^31 real references. It stops being latent the moment lean_inc_ref_n is exported, and that row already exists in fln_rt::abi::FUNCTION_CENSUS with a caller-supplied size_t n.

STALE LEDGER EVIDENCE, FIXED: row FLN-UL-0038 claimed the tri-state invariant while naming three tests that never touched overflow. Invariant and evidence fields updated; new row FLN-UL-0180 ledgers the test-only site.

CHECKED AND EXPLICITLY NOT A FINDING, recorded so nobody re-audits it: the other ~20 debug_assert! sites (object.rs ctor_get/ctor_set/array/sarray indexing, membrane sizing, export slot_idx). Those are preconditions on pub(crate) unsafe fns whose # Safety clauses assign the obligation to the caller, and they mirror the pin's own lean_assert, which is likewise compiled out in release. Faithful parity, correct Rust contract, NOT the same shape as the RC bug — that one differed because its # Safety clause said nothing about n and the code deliberately handled overflow by wrapping rather than treating it as a violated precondition. Distinguishing the two is the whole audit.

MECHANICAL JOINS, ALL CLEAN: 169 #[allow(unsafe_code)] sites vs 169 // UNSAFE-LEDGER markers, 1:1. structure-guard reports exactly one workspace finding and it is not in this crate (FLN-STRUCT-032, cod_2's missing contracts/PIN_TARGET_INVENTORY.txt). No unsafe crate names fln-kernel or fln-checker. No public item added, so ci/BOUNDARY_API.txt is untouched.

STATUS FACT WORTH RECORDING, not a defect: the exported surface is 78 #[unsafe(export_name)] sites against 775 AbiFn rows in FUNCTION_CENSUS — roughly a tenth of the ABI is wired. Anyone reading "242 exported lean_* symbols" should know the census is the specification, not the implemented set.

comments.author: cc_2
comments.text:
MARROW CONCURRENCY AUDIT (cc_2, commit 8cd1d3b). Preemptive round over crates/fln-unsafe-abi and crates/fln-rt. Two findings, both fixed and committed; the clean parts are recorded as results rather than omitted.

FINDING 1, FIXED: every m_rc mode probe in the tri-state refcount was a plain ptr::read racing with the atomic read-modify-writes other threads perform on the same address. Six sites. Not theoretical - mt_stress(8, 2000) drives exactly that interleaving 16,000 times per run and an existing test calls it. Proved with a standalone Miri reproduction of the shape, which reported a data race between the non-atomic read and the atomic RMW. All six now use atomic_rc(o).load(Relaxed), which costs nothing on x86-64/aarch64 and is the right strength because a probe deliberately accepts a stale value.

HONEST SEVERITY on that one: no value was ever wrong on a certified platform, since aligned 32-bit loads do not tear and both possible reads select the same branch. It is UB by the memory model rather than an observable misbehaviour. Fixed anyway because this is the crate that promises memory safety across a threading boundary and because a sanitizer would report it on day one.

FINDING 2, FIXED: write_region_file keyed its staging file on the process id alone, so two threads publishing the SAME target shared one temp path. File::create truncates, so T1 could write half its bytes, T2 truncate and write its own, and T1 fsync and rename the mixture into place - a corrupt artifact published through the function whose job is atomic publication. Staging is now per (process, thread, target). Regression test asserts the result equals one input EXACTLY, and fail-first verified at 3 failures out of 3 runs against the old naming.

CLEAN, stated as findings: fln-rt has no concurrency primitives at all - relocate takes &mut [u8], readers take &[u8], crate is forbid(unsafe_code) with no interior mutability, so read-during-relocation is prevented by the borrow checker; the hazard, if any, lives in whoever owns the mapping. The other AtomicPtr fields are correct (whole-value writes before publication, Acquire loads after). LeanRefObject.m_value is a plain pointer in our layout AND the Reference, so its plain access is right. shadow.rs fallbacks all fail toward the operation proceeding, never toward a skipped refcount op. No lock is held across a foreign call and there is no lock ordering to get wrong.

REVERSE HAZARD noted, not fixed: with shadows ENABLED every refcount operation takes one global Mutex, which would serialise the membrane across threads. Fine today - shadows are a test/hardened mode and the disabled path is a single Relaxed load - but a PG-6/PG-7 shape if hardened builds are ever measured for throughput.

ONE BEAD FILED, fln-nhf5 (P1): there is no sanitizer coverage for any of this. TSAN needs -Zbuild-std and therefore rust-src for the PINNED nightly, which is not installed; the miri component is likewise absent for the pin. I proved the race on the other installed nightly with a standalone repro. The MT workload a sanitizer needs already exists and already runs - only the detector is missing, and pointing it at that one existing test would have caught the race just fixed. Toolchain components and SUITE.lock are not my domain, so it needs whoever owns the pin and CI.

title: commit_anchor_reachability: pipe-buffer deadlock hangs the suite at 239 manifest rows
description: The suite's git cat-file --batch-check plumbing deadlocks when the anchor-query volume crosses the pipe buffer: the harness writes all queries before draining responses, so at 239 manifest rows (first crossed 2026-07-30) the git child blocks in anon_pipe_write with its stdout full while the harness waits on a futex, and both sit forever at 0% CPU. Measured live twice independently (pids 70352 ~2h42m and 1201293 ~9h29m, wchan read from /proc for both sides; three idle batch-check children each). Every pane running this suite hangs from today onward — the green is UNAVAILABLE, not red. Repair direction: interleave writes with reads (thread or poll the child's stdout), or chunk queries below the buffer, or use git cat-file --batch-command with per-query flush; add a wall-clock budget so a future hang becomes a typed failure rather than an eternal wait; and pin a regression cell at a row count above the threshold so the fix is measured, not assumed. Found while closing franken_lean-0vf, whose close discloses that this suite's verdict on its row is unmeasured.
close_reason: Repaired at 59d592a5: interleaved chunked batch exchange below the pipe buffer, 120 s wall-clock watchdog with typed timeout, regression cell measured at 600 tokens above the 239 threshold, suite green 9/9 in 2.6 s (hung eternally before). Tenth binary disclosed 9 -> 10 (g05_pilot.olean).

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
JUDGEMENT (close walk) — the deadlock is measured dead, the wait is budgeted, the suite is green.

The harness wrote every `git cat-file --batch-check` query and only then drained
answers; at 239 manifest rows the child's stdout filled while the harness wrote
on, and both pipes parked forever at 0% CPU. The bead measured it live twice;
this session reproduced it: the suite hung past ten minutes at
`the_allowance_carries_no_dead_or_zero_rows` and
`the_backup_only_anchor_population_may_shrink_and_may_not_grow`.

The repair (59d592a5) has three parts, each with its evidence:

1. THE INTERLEAVE. Queries now go out in 64-line chunks and exactly that chunk's
   answers drain before the next chunk is written — a few KB a side per round,
   far below the 64 KiB pipe buffer, so neither pipe can fill against an
   undrained peer. The positional join and its length-conservation law are
   unchanged.
2. THE BUDGET. The exchange runs on a worker thread behind a 120 s wall-clock
   watchdog; a wedged child is killed (handle shared via a poison-tolerant
   Arc<Mutex<Option<Child>>> so the watchdog never deadlocks on the lock) and
   reported typed, never waited on forever — FL-INV-07's posture applied to a
   hang: a timeout is a value, not an eternal wait. The old path's Vec::leak is
   retired with it.
3. THE MEASUREMENT. A regression cell above the measured threshold classifies
   600 tokens with exact control verdicts (HEAD and HEAD~1 reachable, a 64-hex
   zero and a garbage token missing, conservation exact), and the suite that
   hung eternally completes green in 2.6 s — 9/9, including both tests that
   were deadlocked.

Also disclosed in the same commit, because the guard's own law required it in
the same edit: the binary harvest population moved to ten when the G0-5 pilot
crates/fln-olean/fixtures/g05_pilot.olean joined the tree, so the disclosure
moved 9 -> 10 with the new member named.

UBS v5.3.7 class-level triage in comment 1716: +6 panic-family sites, all the
documented class, zero true positives.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH: the watchdog path (a genuinely wedged child) is
not exercised — exercising it needs an injectable child, and classify hardcodes
`git`. The interleave is the fix; the budget is the backstop; the regression
cell proves the interleave, and the timeout's typing is stated, not measured.
And `git cat-file --batch-command` with a per-query flush remains the simpler
alternative not taken: the interleave keeps the existing positional join and
its length law, which the batch-command rewrite would have to re-prove.

title: Log-derived test dispositions cannot carry execution evidence: libtest ok is not a claim that a test ran
description:
THE CLAIM. A verification receipt cannot carry execution evidence for a cargo test suite if its per-test dispositions are DERIVED FROM A RUN LOG. libtest's "ok" means the function returned without panicking; it does not mean the function's assertions ran. Every pin-dependent rig in this workspace declines by early return, so on a host without the pinned Reference it prints exactly the same "ok" line as on a host with it, and the typed skip notice that says otherwise reaches neither capture. A receipt built by log derivation would therefore report those tests as executed and would DISCHARGE the twelve rows fln-rgha holds - re-creating the hollow green inside the mechanism built to end it.

MEASURED, one variable changed, at 6ed65bd3:
  FLN_REFERENCE_LIB=/nonexistent-masked-pin cargo test --locked -p fln-conformance --test kernel_replay prelude_replays_through_the_kernel -- --exact
  exit 0
  stdout: test prelude_replays_through_the_kernel ... ok
  occurrences of the typed skip notice: stdout 0, stderr 0
The rig takes its early return, exits 0, reports ok, and says so to nobody.

CORROBORATED IN A REAL GATE BUNDLE, target/check/check-20260727T004746Z-310405: test.out carries 1679 per-test ok lines, test.err is 18 bytes, and the skip-notice string appears in NO captured stdout or stderr anywhere in the bundle. That run was on a host where the pin IS installed, so those tests genuinely ran. That is the point: the captured bytes are the same either way, so the bundle cannot discriminate in either direction.

WHY THIS IS NOT THE SAME AS THE STDERR PROBLEM fln-rgha ALREADY RECORDS. rgha's finding is that cargo discards a passing test's stderr, so the honest notice is thrown away. This bead is the consequence for the REPAIR: it means the surviving artifact - the per-test ok line - is not merely incomplete, it is not evidence of execution at all. Fixing the capture does not fix this. A rig that returns early produces no output to capture.

SCOPE OF THE DEFECT, stated in both directions so the repair is not overbroad. Log derivation is SOUND for fln.e2e/2 steps: they are separate processes with distinct exit codes, registered step orders in E2E_STEP_ORDERS, and typed reason codes that the runner records. It is UNSOUND for libtest, because a test function's disposition is not observable from outside the process. The distinction is per-artefact, not global, and a repair that banned log derivation everywhere would throw away the half that works.

PROPOSED MECHANISM. Per-test dispositions carry a provenance discriminator, and only one value can discharge a claim.
1. Each pin-dependent or otherwise declining rig EMITS a structured record - rig name, disposition, reason - to a path the gate collects, rather than to captured stderr. This is fln-rgha's own MECHANISM line and it is the part no scan can substitute for.
2. A receipt's per-test disposition records whether it was rig_emitted or log_inferred.
3. execution.authority may be structured_run_log only when every entry in the executed array is rig_emitted; otherwise the receipt is bundle_only.
4. A log_inferred disposition may be RECORDED but may never discharge a coverage row.
5. A tally of zero executed and zero skipped is a broken collector, not a clean tree, and a decoy rig the collector must see is the control that proves it.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLAIM. No receipt exists yet, so nothing has been falsely discharged; this is a constraint on a design under construction, filed before the design lands rather than after. It does not claim any of the twelve rows is false - fln-rgha is explicit that the defect is that the repository cannot tell. It says nothing about whether any rig's assertions are correct. And it is one measurement on one host at one commit, class bounded_model.

RELATIONSHIPS, so this is not read as a fourth guard. franken_lean-verification-receipt-producer-binding-ywmq (cod_2) owns the receipt and its producer binding; this bead is a constraint on that schema and depends on it. franken_lean-ephemeral-manifest-artifact-povo owns referential durability. fln-0rxm owns citations that denote nothing. fln-rgha owns the execution population and the shrink-only allowance. The four are one mechanism with three owners: a citation that denotes a durable record of what executed. My reading of cod_2's join draft is that it is correct in its ownership split and needs exactly this one schema change.

THE PREREQUISITE NOBODY OWNS YET, and it blocks the join. A coverage row cites a FILE. For an integration test, citation to cargo TARGET is already one to one, because cargo binds a target's name to its file stem under tests - that is the rule fln-rgha's guard resolves cargo-test entries on. The gap is INSIDE the target: kernel_replay.rs holds 14 tests, 2 of them ignored and 5 pin-dependent, and the manifest has no way to say which one a row rests on. Until the artifact vocabulary carries a test-function citation kind, a receipt has nothing to join to and this discriminator has nothing to protect. That vocabulary serves povo (durable kinds), fln-0rxm (kinds that denote) and this bead (a kind that denotes an execution), so it should land before the receipt.

NOT THIS BEAD: which paths a lane must govern, and whether a lane's freeze covers the whole repository or a declared subset. That is franken_lean-build-gate-lane-governed-set-98np (cc_1), whose measurement plan already distinguishes three separate drift mechanisms. Deliberately not duplicated here.
close_reason: Rig-emitted records and the verification receipt validator now refuse libtest ok as execution authority while preserving non-discharging bundle-only inventory.

comments.text:

THIS BEAD'S CLAIM SURVIVES, AND NOW BY TWO INDEPENDENT LEVERS. This bead masked the pin with
FLN_REFERENCE_LIB at 6ed65bd3 over ONE test. fln-rgha comment 1484 masked it with HOME at

THE FULL PRICING. Every field a receipt could read out of a libtest run, measured on kernel_replay,
same binary, same cwd, CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR set in both cells, only HOME varied:

  A. the per-test event string ("ok")   IDENTICAL in both cells for all 16 tests. Carries nothing.

--report-time, the four pin-dependent non-ignored tests collapse when the pin is masked:

  admission_fault_matrix_is_typed_and_atomic                 1.567 s     -> 7.023e-05 s
  prelude_replays_through_the_kernel                         2.560 s     -> 4.073e-05 s
  present_olean_corpus_inventory_is_closed_and_honest       38.422 s     -> 3.747e-05 s
  present_olean_import_contexts_accept_reference_extended   76.187 s     -> 4.015e-05 s

while every non-pin-dependent control is stable within about 1.5x (corpus_census_keeps_disclosing_
its_claim_class 0.00754 -> 0.00785; the_thread_matrix_claim_is_scoped_wherever_it_appears 0.00680
-> 0.00671). A ratio of up to 1.9 million looks like a discriminator.

IT IS NOT ONE, AND THE REFUTATION IS IN THE SAME TABLE. The early-returned tests occupy
[3.747e-05, 7.023e-05] seconds. Genuinely executing tests in the pin-VISIBLE cell land inside and
below that band: the_utc_date_derivation_matches_known_calendar_dates at 1.059e-05 is FASTER than
every skip; the_width_comparator_names_the_pair_and_the_unit_that_diverged at 4.163e-05 and
corpus_comparator_preserves_d23_asymmetry_and_no_answer at 4.952e-05 sit squarely within it. Three
of the twelve non-pin tests are at or below the skip band. SO NO GLOBAL THRESHOLD EXISTS. A
duration says a test was fast; fast is what a correct trivial assertion looks like.

Separating them would require comparing each test against ITS OWN prior duration - which is a
durable record of what previous runs did, i.e. exactly the receipt this bead exists to make
soundly. The discriminator presupposes its own conclusion. Two further reasons it cannot discharge
a claim even where it separates: exec_time is absent from default output entirely, so NO existing
gate bundle carries it; and obtaining it requires -Z unstable-options, resting evidence on an
unstable interface. Timing is a SMELL that can prompt an investigation, never a disposition.

WHAT THIS ADDS TO THE PROPOSED MECHANISM. Nothing in it changes; points 1-5 stand as filed. What is
now measured rather than argued is the NEGATIVE that motivates point 1: it is not that log
derivation is merely weaker than a rig-emitted record, it is that NO field of a libtest run - event,
capture, exit code, or duration - carries execution. The rig must emit, because there is nothing to
infer from. That also sharpens point 4: a log_inferred disposition may never discharge a row not
because it is lower quality but because it is not a measurement of the thing named.

AND IT CONFIRMS THE SCOPE SPLIT IN THE DIRECTION THAT PROTECTS THE WORKING HALF. This bead says log
derivation is SOUND for fln.e2e/2 steps and UNSOUND for libtest. The mechanism behind that is now
visible: an e2e step is a separate PROCESS with its own exit code, so its disposition is observable
from outside. A libtest early return is a control-flow event inside one process that produces no
observable at all. The distinction is not a convention, it is a property of the process boundary,
and a repair banning log derivation everywhere would discard the half where the boundary does the
work.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH. No receipt exists, so nothing has been falsely discharged; unchanged.
No row is claimed false, and nothing here says whether any rig's assertions are correct. The
exec_time overlap is measured on ONE binary (kernel_replay, 16 tests) on one host at one commit -
a wider corpus could show a cleaner separation, and it would still not yield a sound threshold,
because the argument against D is structural rather than statistical. Class bounded_model. The
prerequisite this bead names - a test-function citation kind in the artifact vocabulary - is
untouched by this comment and still blocks the join.
