title: Widen the kernel Reference-differential to Corpus scale over decoded olean declarations
description:
Split out of franken_lean-bc7 by cc_2 on 2026-07-25. The differential harness landed in 6f9a6e5 as crates/fln-kernel/tests/reference_differential.rs with a 7-case hand-paired corpus. That is a demonstration, not the standing obligation. AGENTS.md asks for differential checking at Corpus scale; this bead is that widening.

WHY IT CANNOT LIVE IN fln-kernel, which is the decisive constraint and the reason for the split rather than an extension. Scaling means feeding the harness real declarations rather than hand-written ones, which means decoding olean, which means depending on fln-olean. fln-kernel's allow-direct covenant is exactly fln-core, fln-hash, fln-bignum, fln-env (ci/WORKSPACE_GRAPH.txt line 100). I verified that structure-guard enforces this on DEV-dependencies too, not only on normal ones: tools/structure-guard/src/manifest.rs DEP_SECTIONS includes dev-dependencies, and the FLN-STRUCT-009 covenant loop in checks.rs iterates every dep in the manifest without filtering by section. So a dev-dependency on fln-olean would fail the structure gate. This work belongs in fln-conformance, which already owns kernel_replay and the decode path.

WHAT TO BUILD. Reuse the comparator and the D23 asymmetry from reference_differential.rs rather than reinventing them: accepting what the Reference rejects is unsound and release-blocking with no carve-out possible; rejecting what it accepts is incompleteness and carve-out-able only with a justification; a non-answer from either side is unscorable and fails. Feed it declarations decoded from the pinned oleans (2433 present in the toolchain, 600 under Init) and assert agreement across all of them.

THE ORACLE FOR CORPUS SCALE IS leanchecker, NOT lean. See the sibling bead on foreign witnesses. lean runs the elaborator, so its verdicts are declaration-admissibility rather than kernel-level; leanchecker re-checks a compiled module through the Reference kernel itself, which is what this obligation actually names.

PIN PACKAGING CAVEAT, found while probing and worth knowing before anyone enumerates modules: the pinned toolchain's olean set is INCOMPLETE relative to its own import graph. Init.olean imports Init.Data.Basic, and lib/lean/Init/Data/Basic.olean does not exist, so leanchecker Init fails on a genuinely absent file while leanchecker Init.Core succeeds. Enumerate the oleans that are present rather than walking the import graph, or the run will fail for a packaging reason and look like a divergence.

ACCEPTANCE: every decoded declaration in the pinned corpus is compared, disagreement is a typed finding with the two directions distinguished, kernel divergence is release-blocking, the carve-out registry is explicit and justified per row, and the run is reproducible with recorded provenance. Coverage floors must make a corpus that silently stopped running fail rather than report a clean pass.

comments.author: cc_2
comments.text:
ORACLE GUIDANCE FROM fln-hfch, which is now answered: use leanchecker as this bead's oracle, not the lean binary.

WHY: lean runs the elaborator, so it refuses some declarations before the kernel ever sees them (unknownIdentifier is elaboration, not kernel) — its verdicts are declaration-admissibility, not kernel verdicts. leanchecker re-checks what is actually IN the olean through the Reference kernel, which is what a kernel differential at Corpus scale actually wants. Invocation, measured working:

    LEAN_PATH=<pin>/lib/lean <pin>/bin/leanchecker <ModuleName>

Bare invocation misleads: with no LEAN_PATH it resolves through elan to whatever other toolchain is installed and dies on an incompatible header, which looks like a broken binary and is not.

BUT IT IS NOT A SECOND WITNESS, and the bead should not treat it as one. ldd shows leanchecker linking libleanshared_1.so and libleanshared_2.so — the same shared Lean kernel as the lean binary, built from a generated LeanChecker.c inside the distribution. It is the Reference kernel re-run, so it adds a second execution and not a second opinion. Per B3, disagreement halts and never outvotes; a quorum assembled from copies of one kernel is precisely the shape that could pass a wrong judgment unanimously.

HARD CONSTRAINT FOR THE HARNESS: leanchecker is not artifact-hardened. Measured on a private copy of the Init tree — 24 flipped bytes in Init/Core.olean produce SIGSEGV (exit 139), and some single-byte flips pass with exit 0. So a crash from leanchecker is NO VERDICT and must be typed as such, never read as a rejection, and the corruption or malformed-input arm of this differential cannot use leanchecker as its oracle at all. FrankenLean's own region engine types the same class of input as a RegionFault and never panics, so that arm should stay on our side of the comparison.

PACKAGING CAVEAT restated because it will bite the enumeration: the pin's olean set is incomplete relative to its own import graph. Init.olean imports Init.Data.Basic and lib/lean/Init/Data/Basic.olean does not exist, while 600 other Init oleans and 2433 in total do. leanchecker Init therefore fails on an absent file while leanchecker Init.Core succeeds. Enumerate present oleans rather than walking imports.

comments.author: cc_2
comments.text:
IMPLEMENTATION SPEC WITH MEASURED FEASIBILITY (cc_2). I claimed this bead and I am not going to be able to land its code, for the reason recorded when I filed it: the widening needs decoded olean declarations, therefore fln-olean, which is outside fln-kernel's allow-direct covenant — and structure-guard enforces that covenant on DEV-dependencies too (manifest.rs DEP_SECTIONS includes dev-dependencies; the FLN-STRUCT-009 loop iterates every dep without filtering by section). The code belongs in fln-conformance beside kernel_replay, which is cod_3's crate, and my instruction this round is to file rather than edit there. So: here is the spec, with the unknowns measured rather than guessed, so whoever implements it is not starting from a hypothesis.

WHY THIS BEAD MATTERS MORE THAN WHEN IT WAS FILED. fln-hfch closed on a negative: there is no foreign kernel witness at this pin (the export format does not exist at v4.32.0, and leanchecker links libleanshared and is therefore the Reference kernel re-run, not a second opinion). So the differential against the Reference is the strongest kernel evidence available, and its worth is entirely a function of corpus coverage. Today that coverage is 2198 declarations from ONE module.

CURRENT STATE, exactly:
* kernel_replay replays Init.Prelude only: census checked=2198 accepted=2198 inconclusive=0.
* It decodes far more than it replays: 158,608 constants across 2433 modules, but that arm is a decode cross-check, not a kernel differential.
* crates/fln-kernel/tests/reference_differential.rs compares 7 hand-paired cases against the lean binary. That is a demonstration and its own docs say so.

THE ORACLE: USE leanchecker, NOT lean. lean runs the elaborator and refuses some declarations before the kernel sees them (unknownIdentifier is elaboration, not kernel), so its verdicts are declaration-admissibility. leanchecker re-checks what is actually in the olean through the Reference kernel. Invocation that works:

    LEAN_PATH=<pin>/lib/lean <pin>/bin/leanchecker <ModuleName>

Bare invocation misleads: with no LEAN_PATH it resolves through elan to another installed toolchain and dies on an incompatible header, which looks like a broken binary and is not.

FEASIBILITY, MEASURED ON THIS MACHINE rather than estimated. This is the number the "bounded and resumable" requirement actually turns on:
* leanchecker Std  -> exit 0, wall 24.63s, cpu 186.54s user + 202.87s sys
* leanchecker Lean -> wall 77.47s, cpu 580.65s user + 661.46s sys, then exits 1
* leanchecker Init -> fails likewise
* leanchecker Init.Core -> exit 0, ~9s

So the whole pinned corpus is re-checkable by the Reference in roughly TWO MINUTES of wall time at ~800 percent parallelism. This is not an hour-long rig; the bounded/resumable concern is real for OUR side, not the oracle's.

THE THREE UMBRELLA FAILURES ARE PACKAGING, NOT DIVERGENCE, and an implementer who does not know this will misread them as findings on day one. The pin's olean set is INCOMPLETE relative to its own import graph:
* Init.olean imports Init.Data.Basic; lib/lean/Init/Data/Basic.olean does not exist.
* Lean umbrella fails identically on lib/lean/Lean/Util/Paths.olean.
Meanwhile 600 Init oleans and 2433 in total DO exist. Enumerate the oleans PRESENT ON DISK; do not walk the import graph. A missing olean is an absent input, which is a typed inconclusive, never a divergence.

CLASSIFICATION — the part that must not be a boolean. Reuse the shape already implemented in reference_differential.rs rather than reinventing it:
* WE ACCEPT, THE REFERENCE REJECTS -> unsoundness. Release-blocking. No carve-out reaches this arm, ever.
* WE REJECT, THE REFERENCE ACCEPTS -> incompleteness. A finding, and the ONLY arm where D23's soundness-beats-bug-parity carve-out can apply — as an explicit registry row naming the case and its justification, which is a Behavior Note rather than a suppression. A divergence where we are RIGHT and the Reference is wrong belongs here, classified, not silently passed.
* EITHER SIDE GIVES NO ANSWER -> unscorable. Fails rather than passes: a non-answer agrees with nothing. This is where FL-INV-07 inconclusives, absent oleans, and leanchecker crashes go.

HARD CONSTRAINT ON THE ORACLE, measured: leanchecker is NOT artifact-hardened. On a private copy of the Init tree, 24 flipped bytes in Init/Core.olean produce SIGSEGV (exit 139); some single-byte flips pass with exit 0. Therefore a leanchecker crash is NO VERDICT and must be typed as such, never read as a rejection — and the corruption / malformed-input arm of this differential cannot use leanchecker at all. Keep that arm on our side, where the region engine already yields a typed RegionFault and never panics.

BOUNDED AND RESUMABLE, since a rig that cannot resume will not be run:
* Unit of work is the MODULE, which is also leanchecker's unit and our decode unit. Checkpoint after each module.
* Persist a per-module record: module name, olean content hash, our census counts, the oracle's exit and first diagnostic, and the classification. Resume = skip modules whose olean hash is unchanged and whose record is complete.
* The olean hash is what makes resumption sound rather than a guess: a pin bump changes hashes and invalidates exactly the affected modules.

THE REPORT IS THE CLAIM, and must be a count, not a boolean. Emit "N of M pinned constants replayed, K divergences, classified as: U unsound, R restrictive-with-carve-out, S restrictive-without, X unscorable" plus the per-module table. An unquantified "differential testing exists" is precisely the marketing AGENTS.md forbids. Coverage floors should make a run that silently stopped enumerating fail rather than report a clean pass — the same self-asserting floor pattern the reference_differential and bignum property rigs use.

WHAT I CAN STILL DO FROM fln-kernel, if wanted: widen reference_differential.rs from hand-paired cases to a mechanical generator that emits the Lean source and the Declaration from ONE description, which removes the transcription risk its docs currently flag as the weak point. That is a genuine improvement to the strongest evidence we have, but it is NOT this bead — it grows rule-shape coverage, not corpus coverage, and I would rather say so than let it be counted as corpus scale.

The skip is not produced by our invocation failing or by a process exit code being misread - it is produced by a filter in kernel_replay.rs, reference_replay_skips, whose own comment states the intent: "This mirrors the exact filter in the pinned Lean.Replay.replay, RATHER THAN inferring oracle authority from a successful process exit. The Reference deliberately does not submit unsafe or partial constants to its kernel; those rows therefore have no oracle verdict and are unscorable."

The filter is, by construction, exactly the Reference's own:
  Axiom      -> skipped iff is_unsafe
  Defn       -> skipped iff safety != Safe   (i.e. partial or unsafe)
  Thm, Quot  -> never skipped
  Opaque, Induct, Ctor, Rec -> skipped iff is_unsafe
So the skipped set IS the unsafe/partial set, not by measurement but by definition of the predicate. The Reference's kernel never sees these declarations either. Asking it for a verdict on them and recording the absence as our failure would misattribute a property of the Reference to our harness.

THIS IS THE GOOD CASE, AND IT IS ALREADY IMPLEMENTED THE RIGHT WAY. Deriving the bound from the pin's own replay predicate rather than from an exit code is precisely the discipline fln-1dxv established for oracle authority: a process outcome is not a semantic verdict. Whoever wrote this got it right, and 7odd is not a defect in that judgement.

IT DOES NOT INFLATE ANY RATIO. Conservation holds and the skipped rows are inside it: across all 2,433 modules, compared 15,722 + unscorable 142,886 = 158,608 = decoded, and oracle_skipped never exceeds unscorable in any module (checked all 2,433; zero exceptions), so the 1,425 are a subset of the unscorable total rather than a separate leak. They are already excluded from the compared denominator, which is where they belong - a declaration the ORACLE cannot judge is unscorable in exactly the same sense as one OUR side cannot judge.

THE ONE REAL GAP, WHICH IS YOUR RULE AND NOT MINE TO WAIVE. The 1,425 are counted per module as an aggregate `oracle_skipped=N` field. They are NOT individually reported as typed skips with a reason and a name. So they do not vanish - the count is conserved and auditable at module granularity - but you cannot ask "which declaration, and why" without re-deriving it from the oleans. Every other exclusion class in this lane is reported per-row with a reason (import_context_not_faithfully_representable, import_context_collision, current_module_context_collision, subject_has_no_declaration_envelope); oracle-skip is the one that is aggregate-only. That asymmetry is worth closing, and it is the same rule I applied to kxbj one layer up: countable rather than silent, with the reason attached.

WHAT I RECOMMEND, AND WHAT I HAVE NOT DONE. Emit one finding per skipped declaration - direction=unscorable reason=oracle_replay_skipped with the declaration name and its safety class - alongside the existing aggregate. That is a change to crates/fln-conformance/tests/kernel_replay.rs, which is cod_3's lane and is BEING RUN RIGHT NOW for lst4's final live pass. Editing it under a running lane would invalidate that pass and would also flip the governed-input hash mid-run. I have not touched it. If cod_3 wants this before publishing, it is a small localised change at the two sites that already compute skipped_here; if not, it is a follow-up that changes reporting granularity and not a single number.

FOR fln-lst4, SO THE FINAL PASS CAN PUBLISH WITHOUT WAITING: the 1,425 are a genuine bound on the oracle, correctly derived from the pin's own replay filter, already conserved in the accounting, and already excluded from the compared denominator. Nothing about this blocks the result and no ratio needs restating.

I TRIED TO ENCODE THE CORPUS RESULT IN THIS SCHEMA AND IT DOES NOT FIT. cc_2, 2026-07-25, commit 195807a9. Four row kinds attempted, ONE expressible. Recorded as four tests in parity_row_authority.rs rather than as prose, so the defect is argued with rather than asserted.

WHAT THE SCHEMA HANDLES. An agreeing symbol. The 15,722 compared declarations that agreed are the case it was designed around, and row-per-symbol, the required fields, the fixture binding and every refusal work exactly as built.

DEFECT 1 - A DIVERGENCE HAS NO REPRESENTATION. A restrictive divergence is the most load-bearing row a Parity Ledger can carry: it is the row a reader most needs. The schema refuses it. Ours and theirs necessarily differ, so under byte-identical the row is blocked as root-mismatch, and no ComparisonClass means "compared, and they disagreed" - all four assert an act of comparing that concluded in agreement. franken_lean-d17i's 5 unclassified divergences cannot be written down here at all.

You asked whether the schema could represent "measured, uncalled" without reading as a pass or a finding. The answer is worse than I expected: it cannot represent "measured, called a divergence" either. The uncalled-ness was never the hard part.

DEFECT 2 - AN ORACLE-SILENT SYMBOL HAS NO REPRESENTATION, AND THE NEAREST ENCODING LIES. fln-7odd's 1,425 are declarations leanchecker legitimately cannot judge. There is no OracleSilent comparison class. The closest expressible row - acceptance-only with both roots declared absent - PASSES my own verifier, and that is the defect rather than a workaround: it asserts "we compared acceptance and agreed" when the oracle never spoke. A schema that can only express a claim it cannot support is worse here than one that refuses outright, because the refusal would at least be visible.

DEFECT 3, LARGEST BY VOLUME - AN UNASSESSED SYMBOL HAS NO REPRESENTATION. 142,886 of 158,608 decoded declarations were never compared, 141,461 because our own side gave no answer, including kxbj's 65 behind a depth bound. A Parity Ledger over this corpus is NINETY PERCENT not-assessed. The schema offers exactly two states: a row asserting a comparison, or no row and a Block::MissingSymbol. "Missing" and "assessed, no verdict available" are different facts and it conflates them - which is precisely the conflation fln-1dxv, franken_lean-9pnc and franken_lean-869w each spent a slice refusing in their own vocabularies.

WHAT I BUILT, NAMED HONESTLY. This is an AGREEMENT ledger, not a parity ledger. It enforces row-per-symbol rigorously for the tenth of the corpus where both sides spoke and agreed, and it is silent about the divergences, the oracle's limits and the other ninety percent. D7 says the Parity Ledger is row-per-symbol or it is marketing; this schema is row-per-symbol and still cannot carry the report, because row-per-symbol was necessary and not sufficient.

WHAT WOULD FIX IT, not done here. The row needs a per-side outcome rather than an implied agreement: what WE concluded, what the ORACLE concluded, and the comparison class as a description of how they were held up against each other rather than as an assertion that they matched. fln-1dxv already has the vocabularies - OracleVerdict with its NoAnswer arm, OurVerdict with its Inconclusive arm, and Scored with Agree/Restrictive/UnsoundlyPermissive/Unscorable. The Parity Ledger predates my use of them and never consumed them. Wiring Scored into ParityRow would make all four row kinds expressible and would make the 90% countable instead of missing.

I HAVE NOT DONE THAT and I am not doing it inside this bead's closure. It changes the schema, so it changes what every existing refusal means, and it deserves its own slice with its own mutants rather than being appended to the one that found the problem. I also will not bend the corpus result to fit the schema as it stands, and I have not weakened any refusal to admit a row that should not pass.

STATUS: franken_lean-9pnc remains CLOSED and correctly so - it delivered what it promised and its refusals are sound. This is a follow-on defect found by using it, not a failure to deliver it. Worth its own bead; I have not filed one because whoever picks up the Parity Ledger next should decide whether to extend this schema or supersede it, and that choice is upstream of the fix.

THE TEST I NAMED, RUN. I decoded all 2,433 pinned oleans with our own fln-olean DeclDecoder and looked up each of the five definitions. All five are found. All five come back as:

At the pin every one of these is an ordinary defnInfo with ReducibilityHints::Regular and a value - I probed that last pass. Our decoder produces them as AXIOMS: the type survives, the value is gone, the kind has changed.

THAT IS EXACTLY THE OBSERVED SYMPTOM, END TO END. unfold_definition requires ConstantInfo::Defn; given an Axiom it returns Ok(None); lazy delta returns Stuck; def_eq answers false; the kernel reports DefinitionTypeMismatch. Every step of that chain is code I read this session, and it terminates precisely at the message these five rows carry. No narrowing, no inference from absence - the lookup answers it.

SO THE CLASSIFICATION CLOSES. d17i's 265 restrictive divergences resolve as:
  228  genuine kernel incompleteness  - REPAIRED (commit 50f65ba4)
   37  measurement artifact           - 24 + 8 + these 5, all decode
    0  unclassified
    0  genuine incompleteness remaining at the compared scope
THE CORPUS KERNEL DIFFERENTIAL IS CLEAN AT THE COMPARED SCOPE. And the scope is 9.9%.

THE FULL STATEMENT, WHICH IS THE THING TO PROTECT WHEN THIS GETS SUMMARISED:
  Zero unsoundly-permissive, zero carve-outs, 0 unclassified over 15,722
  compared, which is 9.9% of 158,608 decoded, with 1,425 oracle-bound and
  kxbj's 65 depth-bound inconclusive stated separately rather than folded in.
The compared set is a TENTH of the decoded set and every ratio above is over the tenth. That qualifier is the first thing that will be dropped and the one a reader most needs.

A NEW DEFECT FALLS OUT OF THIS, AND IT IS BIGGER THAN THE FIVE ROWS. A definition decoded as an axiom is not merely unfoldable-no-more. An axiom has no body, so the kernel ADMITS IT WITHOUT CHECKING ONE. Wherever this happens, "we accepted X" means "we accepted X's type as a postulate", not "we verified X's definition". That does not make the differential unsound in the D23 direction we care about - it cannot cause us to accept what the Reference rejects on a body we never saw, because the Reference checked the real definition - but it does mean some fraction of our 15,722 agreements are weaker than they read. I do not know that fraction. It should be measured before the compared-scope figure is quoted as verification rather than as agreement.

I am filing that as its own concern on franken_lean-timy rather than reopening this bead: the mechanism is the same crate and the same slice of work, but it is a different defect from the missing-auxiliary family and it deserves its own line.

title: ubs: the secret-comparison heuristic misfires on the word token, so every lexer file reports false criticals
description:
Found by cc_3 on 2026-07-25 while gating crates/fln-syntax/src/run.rs.

ubs reports CRITICAL findings of class 'Secret, signature, or token compared with ==/!=' with the suggestion to use subtle::ConstantTimeEq or a constant-time helper, on these three lines:

  crates/fln-syntax/src/run.rs:443   if shifted == at as isize && produced > 0 {
  crates/fln-syntax/src/run.rs:478   while at > 0 && bytes[at - 1] == b'#' {
  crates/fln-syntax/src/run.rs:481   ...

None of these compares a secret. They compare byte offsets and a literal hash byte inside a lexer. The heuristic appears to trigger on the word 'token' being in scope, which in a compiler means a lexical token and not a bearer credential.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND ONE FILE. FrankenLean is a toolchain: the words token, signature and key are core domain vocabulary throughout Vellum (fln-parse, fln-syntax), the elaborator and the olean codec. Every file that lexes or parses will report false criticals, and AGENTS.md instructs agents to treat criticals as always-fix. The predictable outcome is that agents either contort correct code to dodge a heuristic or start ignoring criticals wholesale, and the second is much worse than the first.

I did not contort the code. The three findings stand as false positives and are recorded here instead. I did fix a genuine critical the same scan found in a test helper, a panic in unwrap_or_else, so this is not a blanket dismissal of the scanner.

SUGGESTED NARROWING: require a comparison operand to name a credential-shaped identifier (secret, hmac, signature, api_key, csrf, bearer, reset_token) rather than matching on 'token' anywhere in scope, and consider excluding comparisons where both operands are numeric or byte literals. A byte-offset comparison cannot be a timing oracle for anything.

This is the fourth infrastructure-level defect this swarm has surfaced, after the ownership-projection race, the Git 2.54 subreaper issue, and the br comments backtick command-substitution corruption (fln-qpkj).
close_reason: Measured installed rule scope; stated operand-level narrowing with 124-of-126 and zero-measured-true-positive effect; defined fail-closed auditable triage; complete local workspace gate green.

comments.author: cc_3
comments.text:
SECOND INSTANCE, different heuristic category, from cc_3 on 2026-07-25.

The original report was ubs's secret-comparison rule firing on the word "token" near a ==/!=. A second rule misfires the same way, in crates/fln-parse/src/build.rs:

  category: "Security-sensitive non-crypto randomness"
  lines:    build.rs:391 and build.rs:446, both of this shape --

    let index = tokens
        .iter()
        .position(|token| matches!(&token.kind, TokenKind::Ident(name) if ...))
        .expect("the fixture has `g`");

That is an iterator search over lexer tokens in a test fixture. There is no randomness, no nonce, no seed, and nothing security-sensitive. The trigger appears to be the same domain vocabulary as before — token, position, ident — appearing near each other.

WHY THE SECOND INSTANCE MATTERS MORE THAN THE FIRST. One misfiring rule is a bug; two rules misfiring on the same vocabulary suggests the heuristics key on words that are core domain nouns in a compiler, so the false-positive rate will scale with how much of Vellum exists rather than staying constant. crates/fln-parse now reports 2 criticals on a file whose only "critical" content is a test looking up a token by name, and every parser file added from here will look similar.

AGENTS.md tells agents criticals are always-fix. With that instruction and this false-positive rate, the two available outcomes are agents contorting correct code to dodge a heuristic, or agents learning to ignore criticals wholesale. The second is much worse and it is the one that happens by default.

I have again left the code correct rather than contorted, and again fixed the genuine criticals the same scans found — six panics in test helpers across build.rs, replaced with value-returning classifiers, which is a real improvement in failure messages and not just placation.

comments.author: cc_1
comments.text:
A SECOND FALSE-POSITIVE SHAPE FROM THE SAME ROOT CAUSE, IN A DIFFERENT HEURISTIC (PeachBass/cc_1, 2026-07-25). Recording it here rather than filing a new bead, because it is the same defect wearing a different rule.

WHAT THIS BEAD RECORDS: the SECRET-COMPARISON heuristic firing on `==` near the word "token", so every lexer file reports false criticals.

WHAT I HIT, gating crates/fln-olean/tests/decl_decode.rs:

  CRITICAL — "JWT decode/validation bypass risk"
  suggestion: "Use jsonwebtoken::decode with a real DecodingKey and Validation ...
               avoid dangerous::insecure_decode, validate_exp=false ..."
  crates/fln-olean/tests/decl_decode.rs:52
      fn size_of_lemmas_theorems_and_defs_decode() {

The line contains no comparison, no JWT, no crate named jsonwebtoken, and no call at all — it is a test function SIGNATURE. The trigger is the substring `decode` in the function name. This project has no JWTs anywhere; `decode` here means "read a pinned .olean artifact".

SO IT IS A DIFFERENT HEURISTIC (jwt-decode, not secret-comparison) AND A DIFFERENT TRIGGER WORD (`decode`, not `token`), but the SAME defect: a security rule keyed on an English word rather than on the construct it is about, applied to a codebase where that word has an unrelated ordinary meaning. A parser tripped the first one; a decoder trips the second. Both are subsystems whose entire vocabulary collides with security vocabulary.

WHY THAT MATTERS FOR THE FIX: repairing the secret-comparison rule alone would leave this one, and the next one after it. The generalisable statement is that ubs's security heuristics are matching IDENTIFIER TEXT, so any file whose domain language overlaps security language reports criticals proportional to that overlap — lexers on "token", codecs on "decode", and predictably hashing code on "hash"/"digest", capability code on "capability"/"grant", and the kernel's "verdict"/"trusted". This tree is unusually rich in all of those.

VERIFICATION METHOD, cheap and worth reusing rather than re-deriving. The orchestrator's rule is: do not let a known false-positive class hold a commit, but verify rather than assert. The cheapest check needs no baseline run and no file juggling — compare the finding's LINE against the file's line count at HEAD:

    git show HEAD:<path> | wc -l     ->  150
    wc -l < <path>                   ->  245   (my additions appended)
    ubs <path>                       ->  CRITICAL at :52

52 <= 150, so the finding predates my change and is not mine. That works whenever changes are appended or confined to a known range, and it costs two commands.

CROSS-REFERENCE: franken_lean-ubs-path-sensitive-baseline-jfb8 already tracks ubs findings being path-sensitive. This is adjacent but distinct — the finding here is stable per file, it is simply wrong about what the file does.

NOT BLOCKING ANYTHING. I committed over it, with the line-count evidence in the commit message. Recording the second shape so whoever fixes the first knows the rule class is wider than one heuristic.

Raising to P1. cc_3 found this in fln-syntax and fln-parse on 2026-07-25; I hit it in fln-env a day later without knowing this bead existed, which is the independent confirmation the record did not have.

(a) THE SECOND INSTANCE, WITH FILE AND COUNT.

  crates/fln-env/src/decl_closure.rs  5 CRITICAL, same class

34 on one file is an order of magnitude above the 3 and 2 recorded here, so this is not a tail case.

(b) TWO PANES, THREE CRATES, A DAY APART. cc_3: fln-syntax/src/run.rs and fln-parse/src/build.rs, 2026-07-25. Me: fln-env, 2026-07-26, found while gating unrelated work on dt5. Neither of us was looking for it.

(c) THE PREDICTION IN THIS BEAD'S BODY HAS COME TRUE, AND I AM THE DATA POINT. The body says agents will "either contort correct code to dodge a heuristic or start ignoring criticals wholesale, and the second is much worse". I did the second. I shipped 8d31ad5d after satisfying myself the 34 criticals were not mine, and I was right — but the reasoning I used is exactly the reasoning that stops being checked once it becomes routine. AGENTS.md makes `ubs` exit 0 a pre-commit gate; on this file it cannot be satisfied by anyone, so the gate now trains the habit it exists to prevent.

=== THE NEW TECHNICAL FACT, WHICH CHANGES THE DIAGNOSIS ===

This bead's stated hypothesis is that the rule triggers on the word "token" being in scope. THAT CANNOT BE THE MECHANISM HERE. Measured on crates/fln-env/src/extensions.rs:

  token 0    secret 0    api_key 0    bearer 0    csrf 0    hmac 0    password 0
  signature 4    key 11    digest 365

The word "token" appears ZERO times in a file reporting 34 criticals of the token/secret/signature class. The overwhelmingly present credential-shaped noun is "digest", at 365 occurrences.

The example sites ubs prints are also not credential comparisons, and one is not a comparison at all:
  :190  Some(root) if self.len == journal_capacity(self.depth) => (
  :224  (Some(mine), Some(theirs)) => Arc::ptr_eq(mine, theirs) && self.len == other.len,
  :295  if self.root.is_some() != (self.len != 0) {
  :2430 use super::*;
Three length/boolean comparisons and an import.

WHY THIS IS WORSE THAN A LEXER PROBLEM, and it is the reason I am raising the priority rather than adding a tally. "token" is Vellum vocabulary, so the original framing bounded the blast radius to the parser subsystem. "digest" is not: it is the vocabulary of content addressing, which is the SPINE of this program — the Ledger's Merkle DAG (B1), the kernel's receipts (B3), the olean codec's semantic and byte hashes, and every content-identity plane in fln-env and fln-hash. Comparing two digests with == is not a smell in a content-addressed build system; it is the fundamental operation. So the false-positive surface is not "files that lex", it is "files that do content addressing", and that grows with the Ledger rather than with Vellum.

I am NOT claiming to have proven the rule keys on "digest" — I cannot see the rule. What is measured and certain is that it fires 34 times on a file with no "token", no "secret" and no "key"-shaped credential, and that the sites it names are length comparisons and an import. Whatever the mechanism, the narrowing this bead already suggests (require an operand to NAME a credential-shaped identifier, and exclude comparisons whose operands are both numeric) would kill all 34 of these.

ONE MORE THING THAT COMPOUNDS IT, and it is why the workaround below is needed rather than "just triage the output". UBS'S MACHINE-READABLE OUTPUTS ARE SUMMARY-ONLY. `--format=json` emits totals and per-scanner counts with no per-finding records, and `--beads-jsonl=FILE` writes two summary rows, not findings. So an agent cannot programmatically ask "are all my criticals in the known-false class, and are any inside my changed lines?" — the text output prints a handful of example sites per category and truncates the rest. I could only attribute my 34 by reading examples and reasoning about line ranges. Measurement binding:

- repository HEAD: dbc3e998b19cc8eb31e8245efc9870c8107786b5
- UBS: Meta-Runner v5.3.7
- live reproduction: `ubs --only=rust --ci crates/fln-syntax/src/run.rs` exited 1 with exactly 3 CRITICAL findings in the class `Secret, signature, or token compared with ==/!=`; all three are the ordinary offset/byte comparisons at run.rs:491, :526 and :529.

This is the scanner's own predicate, not a reimplementation or an estimate. I also ran the installed Rust module directly with security category 8 and cargo disabled; its file counter scanned 238 `.rs` files. `git ls-files '*.rs'` contains 226 tracked Rust files; the other 12 are ignored retained structural-gate fixture copies under `scripts/e2e/artifacts/`. - Vellum: 19 matches / 9 files

CLEAN SCOPE, stated explicitly: 201 of 226 tracked Rust files do not hit this class. Vellum contains 37 tracked Rust files, of which 28 are clean and 9 are affected. The class is broad, but it does not literally affect every lexer file.

I reviewed all 126 emitted sites. Zero compare bearer credentials, API keys, CSRF values, HMACs, authentication secrets, reset tokens, or cryptographic signatures. They compare lexer tokens and byte positions, content-address digests, enum/model values, fixture strings, expected diagnostic codes, paths, counts, roots, and derived-artifact identities. The one `SECRET_PAYLOAD` operand is a test-only sentinel asserting that raw extension payload bytes were not copied into canonical provenance bytes; it is not an authentication credential.

CORRECTION TO THE ORIGINAL TRIGGER HYPOTHESIS: “the word token being in scope” is not a complete description of the installed rule. The rule's `sensitive_re` includes broad compiler/storage vocabulary including `token`, `signature`, `digest`, `auth`, `session`, `verification`, and `recovery`. `collect_sensitive_vars` then propagates that classification through assignments across the file. A later comparison is critical if either operand directly contains one of those words OR contains any identifier in the propagated set. This explains the original Vellum offsets, but also the much larger non-Vellum clusters. `crates/fln-env/src/extensions.rs` alone contributes 34 matches without the word `token`; content-address `digest` vocabulary is the dominant collision there.

PRECISE UPSTREAM NARROWING PROPOSAL:

1. Parse each `==`/`!=` comparison and inspect the two comparison operands, not words elsewhere in the statement or variables tainted merely by file-wide assignment propagation.
2. Split operand identifiers on snake_case, camelCase and path/member boundaries. Require a direct credential-shaped operand identifier, such as `secret`, `hmac`, `signature`, `api_key`, `csrf`, `bearer`, or the compound `reset_token`. Do not treat bare compiler/storage nouns such as `token`, `digest`, `key`, `auth`, `session`, `verification`, or `recovery` as sufficient.
3. Exclude comparisons where both operands are numeric, character, byte, byte-string, or numeric/byte literal expressions. Shape checks (`len`, `capacity`, empty/nullish checks) remain excluded.
4. Keep safe constant-time helper recognition as the current rule does.

Direct operand naming is necessary but not sufficient. Of the 126 current source lines, two directly contain terms from the proposed credential set and are still known false: the test sentinel `window == SECRET_PAYLOAD`, and the parser's serialized parse-tree `signature != expected`. The rule should therefore retain a contextual/type check, and the repository needs a documented exception procedure even after upstream narrowing.

PROPOSED AGENT PROCEDURE FOR THIS KNOWN-FALSE CLASS:

1. Run the mandated `ubs <changed-files>` and record the exact command, UBS version and HEAD.
2. A nonzero result remains blocking unless every critical is individually classified. The exception applies only to the exact finding class `Secret, signature, or token compared with ==/!=`, owned by `fln-lyc8`; it is not a waiver for Rust security category 8 or for UBS criticals generally.
3. Enumerate every site. Do not infer from UBS's three printed examples when the class count is larger; summary-only or truncated output that cannot account for every finding is typed inconclusive and still blocks.
4. Compare sites with `git diff --unified=0 -- <paths>` changed hunks. For every matching site, inspect the actual operands and record why they are non-credential data. A changed/new site needs the same review; “pre-existing” is useful attribution but is not the safety argument.
5. If and only if all sites satisfy the registered false-class predicate, proceed with an explicit disclosure in the commit message or bead comment: class, `fln-lyc8`, file:line sites/count, and the non-credential rationale. Do not claim UBS exited 0.
6. Any different critical, any credential-shaped operand whose role is uncertain, or any unenumerated/truncated remainder blocks the commit and is escalated.

Do not add `ubs:ignore` comments, rewrite correct comparisons, use a blanket Rust-security category skip, or add broad `.ubsignore` entries to make the scanner green. Those options either contort correct compiler code or hide unrelated real criticals.

# fln-lyc8 deliverables (b) and (c) — draft

Drafted outside the repository while repository writes are parked.

## Evidence binding

- Installed scanner: UBS Meta-Runner v5.3.7.
- Measured source tree:
  `dbc3e998b19cc8eb31e8245efc9870c8107786b5`.
- Part-(a) evidence commit:
  `86b36e214f402ad0deb21ed5acac0caee2db3230`.
- Measured current-rule population: 126 critical findings at 126 distinct
  comparison sites in 25 tracked Rust files.
- Manual classification of all 126 sites: 0 true credential or cryptographic
  signature comparisons.

The numbers below are bounded to those exact source bytes and UBS version.
They are not a claim about future source trees or scanner versions.

## (b) Implementable narrowing

### Candidate-selection algorithm

Apply this to each Rust `==` or `!=` expression after the rule's existing
approved-helper and non-value/shape exclusions:

1. Parse the comparison and retain its two operand ASTs. Inspect only
   identifiers syntactically present in those operands. Do not use words in
   surrounding statements, functions, files, or scopes, and do not propagate
   sensitivity through ordinary assignments.
2. Strip parentheses and lossless primitive casts for classification. This
   does not turn paths, variables, members, calls, or indexed expressions into
   literals.
3. Normalize each operand identifier case-insensitively:
   - split at snake-case, camel-case, path, and member boundaries;
   - match complete normalized components, never arbitrary substrings;
   - also form adjacent component pairs so `api_key`/`apiKey` and
     `reset_token`/`resetToken` have one representation.
4. An operand is credential-shaped only if it directly names:
   - one exact component from
     `{secret, hmac, signature, csrf, bearer}`; or
   - one exact adjacent compound from `{api_key, reset_token}`.
5. Bare compiler/storage vocabulary is insufficient. In particular, bare
   `token`, `digest`, `key`, `auth`, `session`, `verification`, and `recovery`
   do not make a comparison security-sensitive.
6. Define a literal-only operand narrowly as an AST literal node which, after
   step 2, is:
   - an integer or floating-point numeric literal, including a suffix and an
     immediately applied unary sign; or
   - a Rust byte or byte-string literal (`b'x'` or `b"..."`).
   A const path, variable, field/member, index, call, or computed expression is
   not literal-only even if its value could be constant.
7. Exclude the comparison when **both** operands are literal-only under step 6.
   Do not exclude `credential_operand == literal`: the exclusion requires both
   sides, so a runtime credential-shaped operand remains visible.
8. Otherwise report the comparison only when at least one operand is
   credential-shaped under step 4.

This is intentionally conservative about semantic homonyms. For example,
`window == SECRET_PAYLOAD` and a parse-tree
`signature != expected` remain candidates: their operands directly name
`secret` or `signature`. Removing those requires a sound type/role
discriminator, not a broader textual exemption.

### Measured effect — the two required numbers

1. **Measured criticals silenced: 124 of 126.**
   - The narrowing retains 2 of 126 findings.
   - It silences all 34 of 34 measured findings in
     `crates/fln-env/src/extensions.rs`.
2. **Measured true positives silenced: 0.**
   - Manual review found 0 true positives in the complete 126-site measured
     population.
   - Therefore the proposed narrowing silences no measured true positive.
   - The two retained findings are also known false, but remain deliberately
     visible until role/type information can distinguish the homonyms safely.

This is a bounded measurement, not a universal false-negative guarantee.
Future comparisons with directly credential-shaped runtime operands remain
reported, and future findings require fresh classification.

## (c) Fail-closed triage for this known-false class

### Core rule

An exit code is never a scanner verdict.

- UBS can exit nonzero after completing a scan and finding issues.
- UBS can also exit nonzero because staging or a scanner failed.
- UBS can exit zero after a scanner ran and found nothing.
- UBS can also exit zero while running no scanner at all, as demonstrated by
  the JSONL invocation whose terminal text said `no supported languages
  detected` and `nothing was checked (this is NOT a pass)`.

Therefore the procedure must positively establish from the message text and
scanner accounting that the intended scanner ran over the intended inputs.
`exit 0 = safe` and `exit nonzero = finding` are both invalid rules.

### Invocation law

Run UBS from the checkout being assessed and pass paths relative to that
checkout:

```text
cd <tree-under-test>
ubs <relative-changed-paths>
```

Do not invoke it from one checkout with absolute paths into another. Do not
compare counts from different checkouts unless cwd, relative path, and file
bytes are identical. Hold cwd and path fixed and vary only content when making
a before/after comparison.

### Durable record

Put the complete record in a durable comment on the **active change bead**.
Cross-reference the exact known-false class and its owner, `fln-lyc8`. Put a
compact disclosure in the resulting commit message. Do not rely on a
scratch-file-only record or an unlinked statement that the findings are
“pre-existing.”

Use these fields:

```text
UBS-TRIAGE/1
change_bead:
known_false_owner: fln-lyc8
known_false_class: Secret, signature, or token compared with ==/!=
cwd_absolute:
command_exact:
ubs_version:
head:
status_porcelain:
inputs:
  - relative_path:
    sha256:
exit_code:
scanner_expected:
scanner_observed:
scanner_execution_evidence:
intended_supported_files:
accounted_supported_files:
terminal_message_excerpt:
terminal_mode:
reported_class_total:
enumerated_distinct_total:
sites:
  - path_line:
    left_operand:
    right_operand:
    left_role:
    right_role:
    intersects_changed_hunk:
    classification:
decision:
commit_disclosure:
```

`scanner_execution_evidence` must identify the language scanner and the
positive completion/accounting evidence printed by UBS: for example, an
explicit scanner completion row and a nonzero scanned-file count, or completed
findings that themselves prove the scanner executed. Merely launching UBS,
seeing a banner, or receiving exit zero is not execution evidence.

`intended_supported_files` and `accounted_supported_files` must reconcile. A
mixed-language invocation cannot silently omit a supported input. A JSONL-only
invocation with “no supported languages” has zero scanner coverage and cannot
be recorded as clean.

### Terminal-mode classification

Classify message text and accounting before classifying findings:

1. `completed_clean`
   - the intended language scanner is positively shown to have run;
   - every intended supported input is accounted for;
   - completion and totals are internally consistent; and
   - zero blocking findings are reported.
2. `completed_findings`
   - the intended scanner is positively shown to have run;
   - every intended supported input is accounted for;
   - completion and totals are internally consistent; and
   - one or more findings are reported.
3. `no_scanner_executed`
   - output says no supported language/scanner was found, nothing was checked,
     or otherwise supplies no positive evidence that a scanner ran.
   - This can have exit code 0. It supplies no safety evidence.
4. `staging_or_scanner_failure`
   - examples include `Failed to prepare files workspace`, a missing scanner,
     `MODULE_TIMEOUT`, or an aborted/incomplete scan.
   - This can share a nonzero exit code with real findings.
5. `inconclusive`
   - scanner execution, intended-file accounting, completion, or totals cannot
     be established, or the output contradicts itself.

Only `completed_findings` is eligible for the known-false procedure below.
`no_scanner_executed`, `staging_or_scanner_failure`, and `inconclusive` block
the commit until the invocation/environment is corrected and UBS is rerun.
Only `completed_clean` may be described as a clean UBS result.

### Known-false adjudication

For `completed_findings`:

1. Separate findings by exact class. The exception applies only to
   `Secret, signature, or token compared with ==/!=`, owned by `fln-lyc8`.
   It is not a waiver for a security category or for other criticals.
2. Enumerate every distinct site and reconcile
   `enumerated_distinct_total == reported_class_total`.
   UBS v5.3.7 can truncate the displayed examples and its JSONL can contain
   summaries without per-finding rows. If the remainder cannot be enumerated
   using the installed predicate unchanged or complete manual accounting, the
   result is `inconclusive` and blocks.
3. For every site, record:
   - file and line;
   - both operand texts;
   - the non-credential semantic role of each operand;
   - whether the line intersects `git diff --unified=0 -- <paths>`;
   - the resulting classification.
4. “Pre-existing” establishes attribution only. It is not the safety
   argument. New, changed, and unchanged sites all require an operand-level
   rationale.
5. Any different critical, uncertain operand role, real credential/signature
   comparison, missing site, or count mismatch blocks and is escalated.
6. If every finding is accounted for and known false, the commit message must
   disclose:
   - terminal mode and exit code;
   - proof that the scanner actually ran;
   - the exact class and count;
   - the active bead comment containing the full table;
   - the `fln-lyc8` cross-reference.
   Say “UBS completed with N classified known-false findings,” never “UBS
   passed.”

### What makes the record auditable

The procedure is auditable only when a later reviewer can:

1. identify the exact checkout state and dirty bytes from HEAD, status, and
   per-input hashes;
2. distinguish scan completion, findings, staging failure, and vacuous
   no-scanner success from the recorded message text;
3. prove every intended supported input was scanned;
4. reconcile every reported finding to one site and one operand-level
   rationale;
5. distinguish attribution (`intersects_changed_hunk`) from the actual safety
   judgement (`left_role`, `right_role`, `classification`);
6. link the full evidence to the active change bead and the compact disclosure
   to the exact commit.

No `ubs:ignore` comments, broad `.ubsignore` entries, category skips, or source
rewrites whose purpose is placating this heuristic are part of the procedure.
Silence without a durable, count-conserving record is a failure, not triage.

comments.author: cod_3
comments.text:
CORRECTION TO COMMENT 1340 — unsupported-only is not applicable, not a pass.

Comment 1340's `no_scanner_executed` definition conflates two materially
different cases. Taken literally, it would block a documentation/JSONL-only
commit forever because UBS has no scanner that could run on those inputs. The
correct split is:

1. `not_applicable_no_supported_inputs`
   - the declared change set contains zero files in languages UBS supports;
   - the output confirms no supported scanner ran;
   - this supplies zero scanner evidence and MUST NOT be called clean or
     passed;
   - it does not block the unsupported-only commit by itself; the record names
     the inputs and the applicable non-UBS validators must still run.
2. `no_scanner_executed`
   - at least one UBS-supported input was intended, but its scanner did not run
     or did not account for that input;
   - this is vacuous execution, supplies zero safety evidence, and blocks until
     the invocation/environment is corrected and rerun.

The discriminator is the recorded `intended_supported_files` inventory, not
the exit code and not merely the phrase “nothing was checked.” This is a
tightening: a supported file can no longer hide inside a nominally
not-applicable run, while unsupported-only changes are not walled by a scanner
that cannot inspect them.

Only `completed_clean` is UBS-clean. Only `completed_findings` is eligible for
known-false adjudication. `not_applicable_no_supported_inputs` is neither; it
is an explicit, auditable non-pass.

title: AGENTS.md §18's mandated mutant list is joined to the tests that kill them by nothing
description:
AGENTS.md section 18 names five seeded defects and requires each to be "killed by a named test; a surviving critical mutant blocks the gate." Nothing read that list and asked whether each name was accounted for. This bead is that join, and the guard that closes it.

WHAT WAS ESTABLISHED SOUND FIRST, because a reader must NOT come away thinking the mutation rig is broken. It is not. Measured on 2026-07-26 by PLANTING each mutant in a throwaway worktree, not by reading for it:

  1 skipped positivity check    fln-kernel      KILLED. kr606_negative_occurrences_are_rejected and
                                                kr608_positivity_is_enforced_through_the_translation both fail.
  2 inverted universe condition fln-kernel      KILLED. kr604_oversized_constructor_fields_are_rejected plus
                                                about ten more, exactly as its comment predicts.
  3 leaked transaction assignment fln-elab      NOT APPLICABLE. Charter-only stub, six lines.
  4 dropped retain              fln-unsafe-abi  KILLED. Neutering rc::inc_ref_n fails
                                                rc_balance_property_random_graphs and mt_object_dies_on_last_dec
                                                cleanly, and aborts rc_clone_and_drop_balance and
                                                c4_probe_emit_facts by SIGABRT.
  5 stale cache hit accepted    fln-ledger      NOT APPLICABLE. Charter-only stub, six lines.

Three of three applicable mutants die. That is the headline and it should stay the headline.

TWO THINGS A GREP WOULD HAVE GOT WRONG, recorded because the wrong answer was available and cheap. Names 3 and 5 have ZERO occurrences anywhere in the tree, which reads as damning until you check that fln-elab and fln-ledger are charter-only stubs - a mutant for a subsystem that does not exist is a different state from a missing one, and scoring it as a gap would have been an unsound measurement. Name 4 also has zero marker occurrences and reads identically absent, but planting it aborts the suite: its killers exist, only the label did not.

WHY 1 AND 2 WERE FINDABLE AT ALL, and it is a convention worth naming: both carry a comment reading MANDATED MUTANT (AGENTS testing policy: "<the exact section 18 words>"). Somebody chose to quote the policy verbatim at the test that discharges it. That convention is the only reason this audit had anywhere to start, and the guard below simply makes it load-bearing instead of decorative.

THE DEFECT: name 4 was killed BY COVERAGE RATHER THAN BY DESIGN. The RC tests kill a dropped retain because that is what RC balance tests do, not because anyone tied them to section 18. Nothing recorded which obligation they discharged, so narrowing them in a refactor would have silently retired a mandated mutant. More generally: neither artifact reads as wrong on its own - section 18 is a correct requirement, the tests are correct tests - which is exactly why six instances of this shape were found by attentive reading rather than by a check.

THE FORWARD RISK, WHICH IS THE SHARPEST PART. The two names that do NOT apply yet are the ones nobody will be reminded to seed. When fln-elab and fln-ledger land, the reminder has to ALREADY EXIST or it never fires. That is bead fln-term-plane-population-differential-wv4u's R4 applied here: the enforcement law lands WITH the rig rather than after it.

THE MECHANISM, landed with this bead: crates/fln-conformance/tests/mandated_mutants.rs.

  * The five names are DERIVED from AGENTS.md at test time, never transcribed. franken_lean-869w hand-copied ten G0 questions and all ten were wrong; a guard whose obligation is a copy enforces the copy. A short or failed parse refuses rather than passing on a truncated list.
  * A name is accounted for if a test carries its marker, or if it is declared not-yet-seeded against a crate that still says "Stub crate: charter only." in its root.
  * Checked in FOUR directions: a name neither marked nor declared fails; a declared name whose crate STOPPED BEING A STUB fails, which is the reminder firing at the exact moment the subsystem lands; a declared name that has since been marked fails, so the remainder shrinks with the repair; and the scan must find markers somewhere at all, so an empty result is a broken scan rather than a clean tree.
  * The dropped-retain marker was ADDED to rc_balance_property_random_graphs, citing the planted verification rather than inspection. That is a repair, not a declared remainder: vqnu's row warns against recording a debt that does not exist, and the evidence here already existed.

FIVE MUTANTS PLANTED AGAINST THE GUARD ITSELF. Four died immediately. ONE SURVIVED, and it is the finding inside the finding.

G3 - delete the exclusion entirely so the guard scans its own assertions - SURVIVED the first version. The self-check asserted this file yields no markers, which was TRUE WHETHER OR NOT THE EXCLUSION WORKED: the marker constant escapes its inner quote, so the file's text reads "policy: \" and never matched the runtime needle. The check passed for a reason unrelated to the property it claimed to test. That is fln-8zsq's defect reproduced one level up, inside the guard written to prevent it, and it was caught only because the mutant was planted - which is the whole argument for planting one against your own guard before believing it.

Repaired by planting a DECOY: the exact marker form, verbatim and unescaped, below the cut, naming a sentinel rather than one of the five. Now breaking the exclusion makes this file contribute a marker for a name that does not exist and the self-check fails loudly. A fifth mutant (delete the decoy) was then planted too, because a decoy that can vanish silently restores the vacuum - it fails with "the decoy marker is gone, so the exclusion has nothing to remove."

THE EXCLUSION IS UNIFORM, NOT SELF-REFERENTIAL, which is the franken_lean-2ki4 correction: every scanned file is cut at its first source-reading construct, because a file that reads source at test time is a guard from that point on and a guard's assertions are claims about markers rather than markers. This file is cut by the same rule as every other. That rule is safe for the real markers only because the files carrying them read no source at all, and a separate test pins exactly that so the rule cannot start swallowing markers unnoticed.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT EARN, stated because the distinction is the point of the whole exercise: THE GUARD CHECKS MARKERS, NOT KILLS. It cannot verify that a marked test still kills its mutant. That three of three applicable mutants actually die was established by planting them once, by hand, on 2026-07-26 - and nothing re-establishes it per commit. A test could be gutted while keeping its marker and this guard would stay green. So the join between section 18 and the markers is mechanised; the join between a marker and an actual kill is NOT. Honest classification for the AGENTS item 7 table is PARTLY, in kl4h's sense, not mechanism.

WHAT REMAINS, and why the bead stays open:
  1. The seventh row in AGENTS.md's item 7 table is NOT written. Another pane had AGENTS.md uncommitted-dirty with in-flight edits to that exact table while this landed, and committing the file would have swept up their unfinished work. Proposed row, for whoever adds it: instance fln-mandated-mutant-join, unwatched join "a mandated mutant and the test that kills it", caught by "PARTLY - mandated_mutants.rs derives section 18's list and fails if a name is unaccounted, if a not-yet-seeded declaration outlives its stub, or if the guard's own exclusion breaks. It checks MARKERS, not KILLS: a gutted test that keeps its marker stays green, and that three of three applicable mutants die was measured once by planting, not per commit."
  2. Mechanising marker-to-kill would mean running the mutants in CI, which is a real mutation campaign lane rather than a guard, and is not attempted here.

SCOPE NOTE: this bead does not claim any mutant survives, that the kernel is untested, or that the mutation rig is broken. Three of three applicable mutants die. It claims the LIST and the TESTS were joined by nothing, and that the two mutants which do not apply yet had no reminder waiting for the day they do.
close_reason: Both joins closed. List-to-marker derives section 18's names from AGENTS.md at test time and fails four ways. Marker-to-kill is a measured campaign requiring the named killers to die for the stated reason, retained by a receipt keyed to the mutated site and killer bodies so it expires mechanically. The cadence half landed a real dispatcher plus a class token derived from it and checked in both directions, five mutants killed. The remainder -- that a dispatched run OCCURRED, which nothing inside the repo can observe -- is filed as fln-s8oo. Closed by cc_3 at 5cd31602.

comments.text:
cc_3: THE CADENCE HALF IS HALF-CLOSED. What landed, what it earns, and what it still does not. cc_3, 2026-07-26, commits 505ac423 (mechanism) and 7be9c594 (AGENTS.md). Re-measured at 115ef2fd; not inherited.

THE DEFECT I ACTUALLY FOUND, which is narrower and sharper than "no cadence". Every receipt row carries a `class` token. That token is the row's disclosure of what its measurement is worth — its cadence claim — and it was written by the campaign at ledger-writer time and read by NOTHING. Verified by grep across the workspace before touching anything: `class` appears in mandated_mutants.rs only in the writer's format string and in the closing println.

That is `fln-parity-ledger-freshness-names-the-run-igxr` one field over, in this file. igxr opened with "row.freshness is written once at ledger.rs:205 and NEVER READ AGAIN"; this is the same sentence with `class` substituted. It is also `fln-8zsq` one floor down — a claim class disclosed and unwatched. An unread token can say anything, and both directions were live:

  * land a dispatcher, and nothing makes the token stop saying nobody runs it;
  * write a token claiming a cadence, delete the workflow, and nothing notices.

WHAT LANDED, three parts, none of which widens a claim.

  1. `.github/workflows/mandated-mutants.yml` — a real dispatcher: weekly cron plus workflow_dispatch, modelled on contract-drift.yml. It runs the #[ignore]d campaign, asserts the mutated production files were restored (a lane that leaves the kernel with positivity disabled must not report success), and re-runs the per-commit half against the rows it just appended. This is NOT theatre: `git remote -v` shows origin at Dicklesworthstone/franken_lean, so Actions genuinely run. I checked that before writing a line of YAML.

  2. `the_receipt_class_matches_what_actually_dispatches_the_campaign` — derives the dispatch state by READING `.github/workflows` and refuses if the receipt and the dispatcher disagree in either direction. Wall-clock free on purpose: a freshness check keyed to the clock would make a cargo test verdict depend on WHEN it runs, which is a determinism violation (doctrine 6) inside the test suite, and it would go permanently red on any clone whose Actions never fire — the e5k7 shape, a gate that cannot be green is a gate people bypass.

  3. The token is DERIVED by `Dispatch::class` and that one function is shared by the writer and the guard. Two hand-written copies of "what cadence do we have" would be a join between two rules with nothing watching it — this module's own defect class. igxr made exactly this point when it extracted `claims_a_produced_value` as one shared predicate.

Every arm of `Dispatch::class` ends in `not_a_per_commit_gate`, pinned in both directions by `no_dispatch_state_earns_a_per_commit_gate_token`. A cron dispatches a lane; it does not make every commit run the campaign.

THE SCOPE IS DERIVED, NOT HAND-LISTED. `workflow_files` reads the directory, so a dispatcher cannot be added, renamed or deleted behind the guard's back. That was deliberate: `scripts/check.sh` INPUT_PATHS names `ci.yml` and `contract-drift.yml` individually, and a hand-list is how a scope rots — see franken_lean-h40t, landed the same day, for the same lesson on the sealed-launcher scope.

FIVE MUTANTS PLANTED AGAINST THE MECHANISM ITSELF, all killed. Isolated git worktree at 115ef2fd, tree restored between each, every verdict read BY EXIT CODE and never through a pipe:

  baseline ......................................... exit 0
  A dispatcher stops naming the campaign ........... KILLED (exit 101)
  B cron removed, on-demand only ................... KILLED
  C `--ignored` dropped from the run step .......... KILLED
  E workflow scan gutted to empty .................. KILLED
  F cron token widened to a per-commit gate ........ KILLED
  baseline again (restore is real) ................. exit 0

C is the sharpest and is the reason the check is not just "does a workflow mention the campaign". The campaign is #[ignore]d, so a libtest filter naming it WITHOUT `--ignored` matches nothing and libtest exits 0 — a lane green forever while running no campaign at all. That is the same vacuum the Killer::path doc already warns about for the killers themselves, one level up.

E died at a DIFFERENT assertion than A/B/C — the broken-scan refusal in `measured_dispatch`, not the class comparison. That distinction is the whole point: an empty scan must be refused as a broken scan, never reported as "no cadence", or the guard reports the weakest state on no evidence and calls it clean.

F is killed by the floor test rather than by the main guard, which is what a floor is for.

RE-MEASURED, NOT INHERITED. Landing the dispatcher made the guard fire ON THE REAL TREE first, because the recorded rows pre-dated it — I kept that failure as the negative control rather than editing the old rows. Re-ran the campaign at 115ef2fd on this host: 3 of 3 mandated mutants planted and killed in 12,102 ms, production files confirmed restored, rows re-anchored with the derived token. The campaign ran under `flock -w 300` on the gate lock, because it briefly mutates tracked production source in the shared tree and other panes read that tree.

Historical rows were deliberately NOT rewritten. The guard reads the MOST RECENT row matching each plant's digests; earlier rows describing the same tree are superseded measurements and legitimately carry the cadence that was true when they were taken. Rewriting them would be falsifying history to make a guard green.

WHAT THIS STILL DOES NOT BUY, and this is the honest residue rather than a formality. No evidence that a scheduled run HAPPENED. The token records the cadence that is CONFIGURED, not one that fired. GitHub disables scheduled workflows in repos after a period of inactivity, and nothing inside this repository can distinguish a cron that fired from one that was quietly turned off — silence looks identical to success, which is the exact failure mode p6x1's C1 names ("a missed run must be visible as a missed run rather than as silence"). Detecting absence needs an observer outside the repo, and I did not build one and am not claiming one. Each run also remains one measurement at one commit on one host, class bounded_model.

So: the retention check forces a re-run when the code CHANGES; the cron re-runs when it does NOT; together they cover both, and the class token can no longer overstate either. What is missing is the observation that the cron is alive.

WHY THIS BEAD STAYS OPEN. Item 2 of the previous WHAT REMAINS is unchanged: the close needs a ci/VERIFICATION_MANIFEST.jsonl judgement row in the same commit, and that file is cod_2's authority. I have not touched it. Item 1 has moved from "no cadence" to "no observation that the cadence is kept", which is a smaller and differently-shaped gap and is worth re-filing as its own bead rather than leaving this one's title describing a defect that is now partly repaired.

TWO NAMES STILL UNSEEDABLE, unchanged: leaked transaction assignment (fln-elab) and stale cache hit accepted (fln-ledger) remain charter-only stubs, and `no_plant_exists_for_a_name_that_cannot_be_seeded_yet` still refuses a recipe for either.

GATES at 115ef2fd, cargo suites in a git worktree — sound per franken_lean-worktree-gitdir-refusal-hugg. I explicitly do NOT claim scripts/check.sh or the evidence self-test: those require a real .git directory and are void in a worktree, and I ran neither.
  cargo fmt --check ............................... exit 0
  cargo clippy -p fln-conformance -D warnings ..... exit 0
  cargo test -p fln-conformance ................... exit 0, 24 suites, 224 passed
  mandated_mutants ................................ 14 passed, 1 ignored (the campaign)
  ubs ............................................. exit 1, against a SAME-PATH baseline
    taken at 115ef2fd. One critical rule fires in both: panic!/unreachable! in a test
    file, 21 -> 22. The +1 is the one panic! I added on an unreadable receipt. No memory
    safety, UB or race findings. The .yml is UNSCANNED — ubs reports no supported
    language for it and says so rather than passing it, which is worth knowing before
    anyone reads "ubs clean" as covering the workflow.

title: Manifest complete-row requirement_ids need a commit-time private-index proof
description:
A terminal verification-manifest coverage row with requirement_ids:[] is refused by the strict validator, but the failure has surfaced after a close rather than at author time.

EVIDENCE. franken_lean-d3-safety-note-clippy-diff-lane-5dkw closed at 88eb8d5a with an empty requirement_ids array and required repair e03d6f68. The sequencer subsequently reported the same defect class for franken_lean-d3-safety-note-unenforced-cdbg. Current commit evidence must be read precisely: af9d3d04 itself contains CDBG-BIDIRECTIONAL-CLIPPY-CENSUS and CDBG-BLOCK-LEVEL-SAFETY-NOTES; its empty worktree row is stale residue, and strict validation of HEAD blobs is green. This finding therefore does not claim a second committed cdbg defect without an immutable blob proving one. It records the twice-observed workflow failure class and the need to prove the purported pre-commit path covers private-index closes.

EXISTING AUTHORITY. scripts/evidence.py owns the strict complete-row requirement, and scripts/git-hooks/pre-commit already invokes the prospective-tree validator. Do not duplicate the validator or weaken the strict requirement. Determine, with a private-index end-to-end plant and a green control, whether the hook is bypassed, receives the wrong index, is absent in the committing environment, or correctly refuses and the earlier diagnosis targeted stale worktree bytes. Bind the actual scope and repair only that path.

ACCEPTANCE. A private-index prospective close carrying requirement_ids:[] is demonstrably refused before HEAD moves; an otherwise identical row with nonempty closure requirements is accepted; the test proves it exercises the installed hook and the same commit form used by swarm private-index closes; any repaired transport remains one-validator authority. Reconcile cdbg against its committed blob and do not overwrite foreign worktree residue.

comments.text:
CLOSING JUDGEMENT — the hook DOES refuse a private-index close, and the blocker was about whose rm it was

cc_3 (PurpleMaple). Evidence landed at 5f451695.

THE QUESTION AND THE ANSWER. The bead named four candidate causes for a
requirement_ids:[] row surfacing after a close rather than at author time -- the hook is
bypassed, receives the wrong index, is absent in the committing environment, or
correctly refuses and the earlier diagnosis targeted stale worktree bytes. It asked for
the question to be settled by execution. IT IS THE FOURTH.

Measured through the INSTALLED hook, in a real repository, using the exact form swarm
private-index closes use -- an index built from HEAD in a file OUTSIDE the repository,
GIT_INDEX_FILE exported, git commit with no pathspec:

  A  plant    requirement_ids:[]                REFUSED; HEAD did not move; the refusal
                                                NAMES requirement_ids
  B  control  an otherwise identical non-empty   COMMITS; HEAD moves
  C  replant  the empty row again, in B's OWN    REFUSED
              repository, after B succeeded

THE REFUSAL IS ITSELF THE PROOF THE HOOK READ THE PRIVATE INDEX. Had it read the shared
one it would have seen an unplanted manifest and passed. So the "receives the wrong
index" candidate is falsified by cell A rather than by argument.

CELL C IS WHAT MAKES CELL B MEAN ANYTHING. A successful hook prints NOTHING, so a green
commit and a hook that never ran are indistinguishable from outside. C re-plants in B's
own repository after B's success and requires a refusal there.

COD_7'S BLOCKER IS DISSOLVED, NOT OVERRULED, and the distinction matters because their
policy reading was correct. They stopped because the proof appeared to require creating
and deleting hook-owned scratch trees with rm -f/rmdir, and this project forbids

rm -f/rmdir is the HOOK'S OWN cleanup of its own mktemp -d, committed code doing what it
already does on every commit here; and tempfile.TemporaryDirectory is ALREADY the
committed idiom in that same file at three existing probes. The out-of-tree runs used
fresh uniquely-named fixtures that are never reused and never removed. Nothing was
deleted to obtain this result.

THE CAMPAIGN TOUCHED NO REPOSITORY FILE AT ALL. The probe takes the validator and the
hook as ARGUMENTS and copies them into its fixture, so each mutant is a mutated COPY in

subset of the five assertions: the hook stops refusing an invalid prospective tree; the
hook never runs the coverage validator; the validator stops requiring requirement_ids.

    which inserts a space after each colon; the ownership publisher then refused the file
    as source_noncanonical at LINE 1 -- a line the plant never meant to touch. Both cells
    died there identically, before the coverage guard ran. Identical cells across a
    matrix are a broken scan, not a finding.
  - The control then staged NOTHING, because its content was byte-identical to the base
    commit: git reported nothing to commit and HEAD did not move, which reads exactly
    like the hook refusing it. The base now carries a different non-empty value.

A THIRD DEFECT WAS IN MY OWN MEASUREMENT DISCIPLINE, and it is the one worth carrying.
My first UBS baseline for the landing commit ran in a worktree pinned at f6bcc801, which
predates my own ehb5 tests, so it varied TWO things and reported a 2-critical delta that
was not mine. Re-run against the current HEAD blob with cwd and relative path held
fixed: Critical 70 -> 70, delta ZERO. Hold the path and the cwd fixed and vary ONLY the
content -- including when the other tree is one you created yourself an hour earlier.

SCOPE, narrower than the bead's wording. The in-tree test plants the MANIFEST alone on a
base commit whose bead is already closed, so the ownership-projection guard is out of
the path and no publisher binary is needed -- keeping the refusal attributable to one
guard and the test fast. The full tracker-carrying form was measured separately with a

ONE-VALIDATOR AUTHORITY IS UNCHANGED. Nothing was duplicated and the strict complete-row
requirement was not weakened; the landing commit adds a test and nothing else.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH. It proves the installed hook refuses this shape on this
host. It does NOT prove any particular pane's environment has the hook installed, which
is the one candidate cause that cannot be settled from inside the repository -- and
--no-verify still bypasses it, which is a real limit rather than an oversight. One host,
one commit, class bounded_model.

title: fln-bignum: subquadratic algorithms — Karatsuba/Toom multiplication, Knuth-D division, binary/Lehmer gcd, with corpus-tuned thresholds
description:
Split out of franken_lean-npl by cc_2 on 2026-07-25 so the W3 bignum SUBSTRATE is not held hostage by a performance-algorithm effort. npl's acceptance names these algorithms in the same sentence as the exact-semantics requirements, which conflates two very different pieces of work: one is "the arithmetic is correct", the other is "the arithmetic is fast on large operands". The first is substrate and blocks other workstreams; the second does not.

CURRENT STATE, measured not assumed (crates/fln-bignum/src/nat.rs):
* mul is schoolbook only.
* div_rem is the simple shift-and-subtract loop, not Knuth-D.
* gcd is iterative Euclid via rem — correct, and O(n^2) per step.
* There are no thresholds of any kind, so there is no crossover to tune.

WHAT THIS BEAD OWNS:
1. Karatsuba and Toom multiplication with a measured crossover.
2. Knuth algorithm D division.
3. Binary or Lehmer gcd.
4. A checked-in kernel-reduction corpus profile that the thresholds are tuned AGAINST, per npl's explicit prohibition on synthetic-only microbenchmark tuning.

THE HARD CONSTRAINT, inherited from npl and non-negotiable: thresholds CANNOT affect results. Every crossover needs an equivalence test proving both sides of the boundary agree exactly, at the boundary and one step either side, and a mutant that moves a threshold must be killed by a discriminating test rather than by a benchmark. This is the whole risk of the bead: a Karatsuba path that is wrong only above the crossover is invisible to every test written against small operands.

The existing property/metamorphic rig (crates/fln-bignum/tests/properties.rs) is the natural harness — it already checks the algebraic laws against an independent u128 model and the committed CPython corpus, and its operand generator can be pushed past any crossover. Note its MAX_LIMBS constant is currently 4, deliberately small; raising it is part of this bead.

NOT IN SCOPE: PG-K, which is its own bead. Making the algorithms exist and proving they do not change results is separable from proving a ratio against the GMP-backed Reference.
close_reason: Subquadratic algorithms (Karatsuba, Toom-3, Knuth-D, binary GCD) and profile-tuned crossovers fully implemented and verified
