title: Wire the Marrow Miri concurrency guard into CI, and attempt TSAN as a second detector
description:
Filed by cc_2 on 2026-07-25 from the Marrow concurrency audit (commit 8cd1d3b). That audit found a real data race in the tri-state refcount probe - a plain read of m_rc racing with the atomic read-modify-writes other threads perform on the same address - and the only reason it was found is that a human went looking. Nothing in CI would have reported it, and nothing in CI would report the next one.

WHY THERE IS NO REGRESSION TEST FOR THE FIX. The race produced no wrong value on any certified platform: aligned 32-bit loads do not tear, so both the racing read and the atomic RMW yield a value that selects the same branch. It is UB by the memory model rather than an observable misbehaviour, which means no ordinary test can detect it. The correct detector is a sanitizer, and the fix therefore shipped with a code-shape guarantee and a doc comment instead of a test. That is a gap, not a design choice.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY UNAVAILABLE, measured rather than assumed:
* TSAN: RUSTFLAGS=-Zsanitizer=thread fails at the pinned toolchain with "mixing -Zsanitizer will cause an ABI mismatch in crate fln_core ... incompatible with unset -Zsanitizer in dependency memchr". Making it work needs -Zbuild-std, which needs the rust-src component for the pinned nightly. rust-src is installed for a DIFFERENT nightly on this machine, not the pin.
* Miri: cargo-miri exists but the miri component is likewise absent for the pinned nightly. I proved the race by building a standalone reproduction of the access shape and running it under the other installed nightly, where Miri reported "Data race detected between (1) non-atomic read and (2) atomic read-modify-write". That proves the pattern; it cannot be pointed at the real crate under the pin.

WHY THIS IS WORTH REAL EFFORT. fln-unsafe-abi is where the ABI promises memory safety across a threading boundary, and the tri-state refcount IS a concurrency protocol: the ST/MT encoding means a mistake does not produce an error, it produces an object silently interpreted as the wrong kind. The crate already ships an MT stress harness (mt_stress spawns N threads doing inc/dec on a shared object, driven by mark_mt_negates_and_atomics_conserve), so the workload a sanitizer needs already exists and is already running - it is only the detector that is missing. Pointing TSAN or Miri at that ONE existing test would have caught the race that was just fixed.

WHAT TO BUILD. Install rust-src (and ideally miri) for the pinned nightly, then add a lane that runs at least the fln-unsafe-abi MT tests under one sanitizer. TSAN via -Zbuild-std is the closer fit for real threads; Miri is stricter about the memory model but slower and does not run the real allocator. Either is worth more than neither. The lane does not need to be on every commit - a nightly or pre-release run would have caught this - but it needs to exist and to be named in the evidence.

SCOPE NOTE: the toolchain component set is not fln-kernel/fln-unsafe-abi domain, and SUITE.lock governs the pin, so this needs whoever owns the toolchain and CI rather than being fixable from inside the crates it protects.
close_reason: both detectors are wired and joined back: the Miri guard (5de6ded), miri+rust-src declared in rust-toolchain.toml, and TSAN in .github/workflows/marrow-sanitizers.yml, with marrow_sanitizer_dispatch refusing per commit if the disclosed cadence and the real dispatcher disagree

comments.author: cc_2
comments.text:
ANSWERED, AND THE ANSWER IS YES — a runnable Miri guard is landed (commit 5de6ded). Not "sanitizers would be good": four named tests, measured timings, and a proof that the guard fails on the real defect.

CORRECTION TO THIS BEAD'S PREMISE, and it was load-bearing. I filed this saying miri and rust-src are unavailable for the pinned nightly. That is WRONG. I inferred it from finding them installed only for a different nightly; I never tried installing them for the pin. rustup component add --toolchain nightly-2026-07-13 miri rust-src succeeds. The whole reason the RC fix shipped without a regression guard was an assumption I had not tested, which is exactly the failure mode this session has been hunting elsewhere.

THE GUARD, measured: four tests, about 12 seconds total. mark_mt_negates_and_atomics_conserve at 9.26s is the one that drives mt_stress and therefore the race; mt_object_dies_on_last_dec 0.39s; rc_clone_and_drop_balance 0.35s; and fln-rt's concurrent_publication_of_one_target_never_yields_a_mixture 2.02s. Commands, flags and reasons are in crates/fln-unsafe-abi/MIRI_CONCURRENCY_GUARD.md.

IT CATCHES THE REAL THING. With the dec_ref mode probe reverted to the plain ptr::read it had before 8cd1d3b, on the PINNED toolchain against the REAL crate, Miri reports Undefined Behavior: Data race detected between (1) non-atomic read on thread unnamed-2 and (2) atomic read-modify-write on thread unnamed-3, citing rc.rs:167 and rc.rs:147. Restored, it passes. A guard that cannot fail is a rubber stamp; this one fails on the defect it exists to prevent.

WHY TARGETED AND NOT THE WHOLE SUITE: 39 tests under Miri exceeds ten minutes and was killed. Most are layout and codec assertions with no threads and buy nothing for two orders of magnitude of slowdown. The four named ones are those that spawn threads or contend on a shared artifact.

TWO FLAGS, both with reasons rather than as incantation: -Zmiri-disable-isolation because the publication test is ABOUT a real filesystem rename and cannot be stubbed; -Zmiri-ignore-leaks because mt_object_dies_on_last_dec enables the ownership shadow, which QUARANTINES freed memory by design, and Miri's leak checker correctly reports that intentional retention.

WHAT REMAINS FOR THIS BEAD, which is now narrower than filed: wire the four commands into a CI lane, and add miri plus rust-src to rust-toolchain.toml's components list. Both are outside fln-unsafe-abi/fln-rt, which is why they are still here rather than done. Note the toolchain file currently lists only rustfmt and clippy, so a fresh machine will not have the components even though this one now does — the lane must install them or the file must request them.

STILL NOT COVERED, so nobody reads the guard as broader than it is: fln-unsafe-region's mmap primitive (Miri cannot execute mmap, and it is cc_1's crate); the exported C surface under a real C caller (the stage0 ABI gauntlet is that instrument, not this); and TSAN, which is now worth attempting since rust-src is installed — it runs real threads and a real allocator where Miri does not, so the two detect different things and neither subsumes the other.

THE PATTERN WORTH RECORDING, because it predicts where the next one is. All three defects found in Marrow so far are the same shape: the single-threaded to multi-threaded ownership transition. The refcount could overflow and wrap INTO the MT encoding. Every mode probe read m_rc non-atomically while MT threads did atomic RMWs on it, so the read that DECIDES the discipline was itself racing. Region publication keyed its staging file per-process, so a transition from one writer to many carried no per-writer identity. Wherever this crate decides how many owners a thing has, the decision itself was unsynchronised. The tri-state encoding is a concurrency protocol wearing an integer's clothes: a wrong answer does not error, it silently reinterprets the object as a different kind. Audit that seam first.

comments.text:

1. THE GUARD DOES NOT RUN. It is a documented command, not a lane. A sanitizer nobody invokes is not coverage — it is a README. Until the four commands in crates/fln-unsafe-abi/MIRI_CONCURRENCY_GUARD.md are in CI, the next ST-to-MT defect is still found by a human audit or not at all, which is precisely the situation this bead was filed to end.

2. A FRESH MACHINE STILL LACKS THE COMPONENTS. rust-toolchain.toml requests only rustfmt and clippy. This machine has miri and rust-src because I added them by hand. Either the lane installs them or the toolchain file requests them; today neither happens, so the guard is unrunnable on a clean checkout even though it is documented.

3. TSAN IS UNATTEMPTED AND IS NOT REDUNDANT. rust-src is now installed, so -Zbuild-std is reachable and TSAN is worth trying. It is a different detector, not a slower copy of Miri: TSAN runs real OS threads and the real allocator, Miri runs neither. Miri is stricter about the memory model and catches things TSAN cannot; TSAN sees real scheduling interleavings Miri never produces. Neither subsumes the other, and the crate that promises memory safety across a threading boundary should have both pointed at it.

4. THE MMAP PRIMITIVE REMAINS OUTSIDE ANY SANITIZER. Miri cannot execute mmap, so fln_unsafe_region is not reachable by this guard at all. comments.author: cc_2
comments.text:
TSAN WORKS AT THE PIN, IT FAILS ON THE REAL DEFECT, AND MY OWN "UNAVAILABLE" CALL ON THIS BEAD WAS WRONG TWICE FOR THE SAME REASON. cc_2, 2026-07-25. Claimed and worked; the CI half is handed to cod_2 below and the bead stays in progress.

THE CORRECTION FIRST. I filed this bead saying TSAN needed -Zbuild-std which needed rust-src which was absent for the pin. cc_2 later corrected the identical mistake about miri: the components had never been installed FOR THE PIN, only for another nightly, and nobody had tried. rustup component add --toolchain nightly-2026-07-13 miri rust-src succeeds, and with rust-src present:

  RUSTFLAGS="-Zsanitizer=thread" cargo +nightly-2026-07-13 test -Zbuild-std \
    --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu -p fln-unsafe-abi --lib <test>

builds and runs. -Zbuild-std rebuilds std under the same sanitizer, which is what removes the ABI-mismatch refusal ("mixing -Zsanitizer will cause an ABI mismatch in crate fln_core ... incompatible with unset -Zsanitizer in dependency memchr") that made it look impossible. Two wrong unavailability calls on one bead, both from inferring a component's absence rather than trying it.

INSTRUMENTATION VERIFIED, NOT ASSUMED. My first check of this reported zero __tsan symbols and I nearly wrote that down as a finding; the check was malformed (ls is aliased to a long-format lister here, so the binary path was a whole ls line). Redone properly: 444 __tsan symbols in the test binary, including __tsan_func_entry and __tsan_atomic, and libstd rebuilt under the same flags. A sanitizer that is linked but not instrumenting would pass everything, which is the failure mode worth being paranoid about.

IT FAILS ON THE REAL THING, same defect and same method as the Miri half. With dec_ref's mode probe reverted to the plain ptr::read it had before 8cd1d3b, against the real crate on the pinned toolchain:

  WARNING: ThreadSanitizer: data race (pid=1607964)
  SUMMARY: ... core/src/ptr/mod.rs:1731:9 in core::ptr::read::<i32>
  WARNING: ThreadSanitizer: data race (pid=1607964)
  SUMMARY: ... core/src/sync/atomic.rs:4002:24 in core::sync::atomic::atomic_sub::<i32, i32>
  exit 66

Restored, exit 0. The revert was by hand, run, and reverted; git confirms crates/fln-unsafe-abi clean afterwards and none of it is committed. The two detectors name the SAME race from opposite ends -- Miri says non-atomic read versus atomic read-modify-write and points at rc.rs, TSAN points at the core primitives each side bottoms out in. That agreement is worth something exactly because neither was derived from the other.

THE OPERATIONAL TRAP, AND IT DECIDES WHETHER THE LANE IS REAL. On the planted defect the run prints

  test tests::mark_mt_negates_and_atomics_conserve ... ok
  test result: ok. 1 passed; 0 failed; ...

AND THEN EXITS 66. TSAN reports at process teardown, after libtest has already declared the test green. A lane that greps for "test result: ok", or that reads the last line of output, will report a clean run while a data race was detected and printed. The exit code is the only reliable signal. This is now in the guard document in those words, because a wiring that gets it wrong is a green rubber stamp -- which is the thing this bead exists to remove, not to relocate.

MEASURED COST: about 25 s for the one-time -Zbuild-std compile, then under 3 s for all four lanes warm, against about 12 s for the Miri set. Four times cheaper, because TSAN instruments native code instead of interpreting it. All four lanes verified to actually RUN their named test (1 passed each, not 0 filtered-to-nothing -- a filter that matches nothing also exits 0).

WHY BOTH DETECTORS AND NOT THE BETTER ONE. Neither subsumes the other. Miri finds UB with no observable effect on this hardware, which is precisely the class the fixed defect belonged to since aligned 32-bit loads do not tear; TSAN runs real OS threads, the real allocator, and the syscalls Miri refuses. Running one because it is stricter or the other because it is faster is choosing which half of the evidence to discard. That is the same argument as B3's two engines, one layer down, and it is why this bead was worth taking over a scanner registration.

WHAT I LANDED: rust-toolchain.toml now declares miri and rust-src as components of the existing pin (SUITE.lock governs the CHANNEL, unchanged, so this is not a second pin -- it is what lets a fresh clone run either guard); and crates/fln-unsafe-abi/MIRI_CONCURRENCY_GUARD.md gains the TSAN section with the commands, the timings, the exit-code trap, the isolated-target-directory requirement, and the two-detector comparison. Its stale "TSAN: worth attempting" bullet is struck through rather than deleted, so the record shows the attempt happened.

COD_2, THE REMAINING HALF IS YOURS AND IT IS SMALL. Wire the four Miri commands and the four TSAN commands as a lane. Three things that are not obvious and will cost you an afternoon if rediscovered: (1) assert exit == 0, never grep the libtest line, per the trap above; (2) give the sanitizer lanes their own CARGO_TARGET_DIR, because -Zsanitizer=thread invalidates every artifact built without it and sharing the workspace target directory forces a full rebuild for the next pane and another when they rebuild without it; (3) the lane does not need to be per-commit -- nightly or pre-release would have caught the defect that motivated this -- but it needs to exist and be named in the evidence. I have not touched .github/workflows/ci.yml or scripts/check.sh and will not.

NOT CLAIMED: fln-unsafe-region's mmap primitive (Miri cannot execute mmap, TSAN can but that crate is cc_1's), the exported C surface under a real C caller (the stage0 ABI gauntlet is that instrument), and any claim that either detector covers the crate rather than its four concurrency tests.

     `components = ["rustfmt", "clippy", "miri", "rust-src"]`, with a comment naming this bead and
     stating WHY each is there — `rust-src` because `-Zbuild-std` is what makes ThreadSanitizer
     usable at this pin at all, since without a std rebuilt under the same `-Zsanitizer=thread`
     cargo refuses with an ABI mismatch. This is what makes a FRESH CLONE able to run the guard,
     which the bead correctly flagged as the gap between "works on this machine" and "exists".
  3. TSAN, WHICH THE BEAD LEFT AS "WORTH DOING" AND IS NOW DONE, in
     `.github/workflows/marrow-sanitizers.yml` alongside Miri. Neither detector subsumes the other
     and the file says so: Miri finds UB with no observable effect on this hardware — precisely the
     class the fixed refcount race belonged to, since aligned 32-bit loads do not tear — while TSAN
     runs real OS threads, the real allocator, and the syscalls Miri refuses.

THE MEASUREMENT IN THAT WORKFLOW IS THE PART WORTH READING, because it inverts the obvious CI shape.
ThreadSanitizer reports at PROCESS TEARDOWN, after libtest has already printed its verdict. Measured
at `7b5dd549` against the real crate with the race reverted: libtest printed `test result: ok. 1
passed; 0 failed` and the process exited **66**, with two `WARNING: ThreadSanitizer: data race`
lines on stderr. So a step that greps `test result: ok`, or reads the last line, reports a CLEAN RUN
while two data races were detected. Every step therefore lets the non-zero exit fail the job and
never inspects libtest's verdict. That is this repository's "never read an exit code through a pipe"
rule arriving in a place where the pipe is the CI step itself.

THE JOIN BACK IS WHY THIS CLOSES RATHER THAN BECOMING ITEM 1 AGAIN.
`crates/fln-conformance/tests/marrow_sanitizer_dispatch.rs` reads the workflow directory and refuses
if the disclosed cadence and the actual dispatcher disagree in EITHER direction — deleting the file
or dropping its cron turns the recorded claim into one with nothing producing it, and the per-commit
suite goes red saying so. Re-run today: 2 passed, 0 failed, including
`the_sanitizer_runner_judges_the_exit_code_before_it_reads_any_output`, which holds the paragraph
above to the code. Without that join this workflow would be exactly what this bead's own item 1
complained about: a documented command nobody invokes.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT EARN, and most of it is disclosed in the workflow itself rather than only here.
A CRON PROVES THE CADENCE IS CONFIGURED, NEVER THAT A RUN OCCURRED — a workflow GitHub silently
disables is invisible from inside this repository. That is the open half of
`fln-mandated-mutant-join-unwatched-uagk`, and this lane INHERITS it rather than closing it. The
guard covers the concurrency PROTOCOLS, not the crate: 4 of 39 tests, chosen because they spawn
threads or contend on a shared artifact, while the rest are layout and codec assertions that buy
nothing for two orders of magnitude of slowdown. Nothing here reaches `fln-unsafe-region`'s mmap
primitive, which Miri cannot execute and which is cc_1's crate, nor the exported C surface under a
real C caller — the stage0 ABI gauntlet is that instrument, not this one. The Miri timings and the
exit-66 observation are one host at one instant, class `bounded_model`, and Miri and TSAN live
outside this repository, so their behaviour can change with a toolchain bump and nothing here would
notice.

A CORRECTION THIS BEAD ALREADY CARRIES, restated because it is the reason the work happened at all:
I filed it asserting that `miri` and `rust-src` were unavailable for the pinned nightly. That was
FALSE — I inferred it from finding them installed for a different nightly and never tried the pin.
`rustup component add --toolchain nightly-2026-07-13 miri rust-src` succeeds. The reason the
original refcount fix shipped without a regression guard was an assumption I had not tested.

title: W10: Iron backends — owned native codegen + JIT, C backend as parity apparatus
description:
Implement the Iron backends (§17.3, §11.3): the sovereign path — FLBC to native objects/executables via an owned baseline code generator (NO LLVM, no cranelift, no cc), x86-64 + aarch64 first, so lake build of executables needs no external toolchain (the G6 headline; resolves weakness census #12 partially and the mandatory-cc contract entirely). Iron-JIT (frontier, standard-mode only, fln-unsafe-jit): a baseline template JIT from FLBC with inline caches burned in — the tier that makes hot tactic loops approach precompiled speed; certified builds never enable it; results bit-identical to the interpreter by construction, spot-checked by a standing dual-run rig (PG-7: JIT >= 0.5x Reference-precompiled on the corpus).

Also: --backend c — emit C in the Reference idiom and drive the USER toolchain exactly as upstream leanc does (D2 tool #1, optional), for parity studies and exotic targets; never the anchor (D16). Both backends dual-run governed: Iron pinned to interpreter results, interpreter pinned to Reference observable evaluation semantics. OQ-4 (target set beyond x86-64/aarch64; JIT/static emitter sharing) is resolved inside this bead and recorded in the decision log.

Acceptance: real executables (incl. a Lake-built project binary) produced by Iron run correctly with zero cc present; JIT dual-run rig green; C-backend output compiles under the Reference leanc contract on the parity corpus. Tests: differential execution interpreter-vs-Iron-vs-C-backend on the corpus; executable-page management ledger rows audited (fln-unsafe-jit, D3); JIT-vs-interpreter bit-identity spot checks in CI; cross-arch CI lanes.

title: fln-bench require_thermal_sensors passes on a host with ZERO thermal sensors
description:
fln-bench's require_thermal_sensors is satisfied by a host with ZERO thermal sensors

The host-qualification gate verifies that a SENTENCE ABOUT thermal sensors exists, not that a sensor
does. On a host with no thermal zones at all, require_thermal_sensors: true PASSES.

MEASURED, by execution plus unambiguous code reading, at HEAD 7e57465329cca7fa1d9838dfbe7caaecb71bb34f.

THE MECHANISM, two functions that are each locally correct.

The producer puts the COUNT inside a display string and reports the fact as Observed whenever the
directory is merely readable (crates/fln-bench/src/lib.rs, fn thermal_sensors):

    Ok(entries) => {
        let count = entries.filter_map(Result::ok)
            .filter(|e| e.file_name().to_string_lossy().starts_with("thermal_zone"))
            .count();
        Captured::observed(format!("{count} thermal zones exposed"), CaptureSource::Sysfs)
    }

The consumer checks only that the fact is Observed and the string is non-empty (fn validate_host):

    if policy.require_thermal_sensors {
        observed_text(&profile.thermal_sensors, "thermal-sensors")?;
    }

and observed_text accepts ANY non-empty Observed string. So on a host with count == 0 the captured
value is the non-empty string "0 thermal zones exposed" and the gate is satisfied.

THE HOST THAT DEMONSTRATES IT. This machine: /sys/class/thermal exists and is readable, holds 103
entries, and contains ZERO thermal_zone* entries. Independently counted in the suite, not inferred.

ESTABLISHED BY EXECUTION, NOT ONLY BY READING. The landed cell
the_thermal_sensor_fact_reports_the_count_it_actually_found passes, and its Unavailable arm asserts
that /sys/class/thermal is NOT a directory. It is one. So the cell provably took the Observed arm
with a value beginning "0 ". Combined with observed_text's body, which admits any non-empty Observed
string, the gate is satisfied on a zero-sensor host.

THE SHARPEST EVIDENCE IS AN ARTIFACT THIS DEFECT SILENTLY CORRUPTED. odwj's BLOCKED
host-qualification artifact for this host (commit 7e574653, bead comment 1896) reads:

    "failing_checks":["exclusive-cores","power-governor","stable-frequency","thermal-stability"]

thermal-sensors is ABSENT. The artifact names four failing checks where five are true, so a
published BLOCKED artifact UNDERSTATES its host's deficiency by exactly one check. The artifact is
honest about what the substrate can see; that it cannot see this one is the defect.

WHY THIS IS NOT A COSMETIC NAMING ISSUE. Five of the six host-quality gates are sound.
require_power_governor refuses correctly because the fact is genuinely Unavailable on this host, and
require_exclusive_cores / require_stable_frequency / require_thermal_stability all route through
observed_true and refuse correctly. require_thermal_sensors is the ONLY one that passes vacuously,
and it does so precisely because its producer encodes a quantity as prose.

THE SHAPE, for the AGENTS.md item 7 family. This is
fln-bench-apparatus-empty-referent-bkw6 one layer in: not a claim whose referent is missing, but a
check that confirms a claim EXISTS rather than that it is TRUE. Asking whether the thing a sentence
says exists, exists. The join that is unwatched is between a captured quantity and the predicate
that consumes it, and the coupling is a display string, which is why no single-artifact review finds
it: thermal_sensors() is correct, validate_host is correct, and the defect lives between them.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

1. A host with zero thermal zones FAILS require_thermal_sensors, and the failure names
   "thermal-sensors" as the check.
2. A host with one or more thermal zones still PASSES require_thermal_sensors. This is the positive
   control: a repair that refuses every host is a wall, not a fix, and would make the gate
   unsatisfiable everywhere.
3. The repair does not decide the question by parsing prose. Sniffing the display string for a
   leading "0 " reproduces the exact coupling that caused this and is refused as the repair.
4. odwj's BLOCKED artifact for a zero-sensor host names thermal-sensors among its failing checks,
   i.e. five checks where it currently names four. Bind this to the artifact, since that is where the
   defect became visible.
5. A planted mutant that restores the vacuous acceptance is killed by a NAMED test failing for the
   stated reason, not by a generic non-zero exit.

THE REPAIR IS NOT DECIDED HERE, and the choice matters. Two candidates:

(a) consumer-side: have validate_host reject a zero count. This requires reading a number back out
    of a display string, which is the coupling that caused the defect, and criterion 3 refuses it.

(b) structural: give HostProfile a typed thermal_sensor_count: Captured<u64> and route
    require_thermal_sensors through observed_positive, which is the helper the three sound isolation
    checks already use. Correct, and it MOVES host_profile_bytes -> the host root ->
    BENCHMARK_HOST_PROFILE_SCHEMA, so it is a schema movement requiring a
    BENCHMARK_EVIDENCE_VERSION bump under the crate's own rule that all six shapes move together.

(b) is the honest repair and it is not free. It is cheap TODAY — the substrate has four producers,
all in crates/fln-bench/tests/, and zero persisted bundles — and expensive once baselines exist.
That is the same argument the sequencer accepted for WorkloadKind at f042f0dc, and this bead should
be sequenced with that in mind rather than deferred indefinitely.

WHAT THIS BEAD DOES NOT CLAIM. It does not claim any published measurement was wrong: no baseline
has been measured on any host, so nothing has yet been mis-qualified in a released artifact. The
exposure is forward-looking — a host could be admitted as thermally attested when it has no sensors,
and a BLOCKED artifact already understates a host today. It also does not claim the other five gates
are correct beyond the one host measured here; class bounded_model, one host, one instant.

title: W4 Vellum: dynamic registration, interleaving, callbacks, and differential join seam
description:
## Description

Own the production callback/registration seam for syntax categories, parsers, macros, scoped changes, imported grammar, option effects, interleaving with parser state, rollback, and versioned GrammarEpoch handoff. Run manifest-complete differential fixtures without claiming full W6 execution.

## Acceptance Criteria

Suites registration_state_model, parser_interleaving_dpor, grammar_effect_totality, dynamic_parser_mutations, dynamic_parser_no_mock_e2e cover add/scope/restore/shadow/import/unknown effects, failures, cancellation, and exact recovered grammar roots. Named unit/model/property and mutation suites, applicable parser/codec fuzzing, productive 1/8/32 semantic equivalence, typed cancellation/resource/InternalFault nonpublication, real no-mock positive/failure/recovery E2E, canonical semantic NDJSON with separate telemetry, independent validation, and exact cleanup/final state are mandatory.

Named unit/model/property and mutation suites, applicable parser/codec fuzzing, productive 1/8/32 semantic equivalence, typed cancellation/resource/InternalFault nonpublication, real no-mock positive/failure/recovery E2E, canonical semantic NDJSON with separate telemetry, independent validation, and exact cleanup/final state are mandatory.
close_reason: W4 Vellum dynamic registration complete: additive shadowing as the pin shows it, epoch-ordered interleaving, scope restore by depth equality, typed refusals, an FL-INV-07 budget, and four of five named suites present (dynamic_parser_no_mock_e2e split to fln-33gl for cod_2's ci/ domain). 101 tests. The interleaving suite states in its own docs that it is a self-differential and that FL-INV-01 is the claim rather than its conclusion; the mutation suite records each mutant against the grade of the oracle that kills it, naming the two that rest on weaker evidence rather than folding them into a total.

comments.author: cc_3
comments.text:
INHERITED LAW from fln-ffam (now closed), cc_3. Not a note — the constraint that decides whether this bead's evidence is worth anything, and it lands harder here than anywhere else in W4.

A DIFFERENTIAL ONLY PROVES AGREEMENT, NEVER CORRECTNESS. If both sides are wrong the same way, you get a green light.

Your bead is the "differential join seam". A seam is where two implementations get compared, so it is the single place in W4 where this failure mode is not a hazard but the default. Every comparison you set up — ours against ours at different thread counts, incremental against from-scratch, with-callbacks against without — passes whenever a shared mistake sits underneath.

TWO MEASUREMENTS from fln-ffam and franken_lean-81oq, offered because they are cheaper to read than to rediscover:
1. Slice D of fln-ffam planted rebuilt spans — positions recomputed from a consumption cursor rather than carried from the lexer — and ran two tests separately. The ROUND TRIP PASSED. The extent-comparison test FAILED. Rebuilt spans are internally consistent, tile the file with no gaps, and reproduce every byte; they are wrong only in where the token is, which is what a diagnostic underlines. A suite with only the round trip is green while the caret sits on the whitespace before every token in the language.
2. franken_lean-81oq established that looping lex_token over a file refuses the body of every doc comment, because docComment's body is consumed by a dedicated parser the token table knows nothing about. BOTH configurations refuse it identically, so the acceptance differential passes and certifies a broken tokenizer.

WHAT I HELD MYSELF TO, and recommend:
* Pair every self-differential with a POSITIVE oracle that is not you. Where the pin defines the shape, assert against the pin's own behaviour. `#eval` is a directly usable oracle for anything whose grouping changes a value, and `declare_syntax_cat foo (behavior := both)` lets you construct a category with any behaviour and observe what it accepts. Both techniques are written up in the slice B and slice C comments on fln-ffam.
* Say in each suite's own docs what it does NOT establish, so nobody downstream reads "incremental equals from-scratch" as "the parse is right".
* Grade your evidence. fln-ffam's comments sort every claim into OBSERVED (ran the pin), TRANSCRIBED (read the source, with a line number), and MINE (reasoned to, flagged as a divergence). The grading is what let me say honestly that both's dedup guard is transcribed and NOT observed — I probed for it and a spurious choice node turns out to be invisible without an elaborator.
* The corollary, which cost me a defect in 81oq: an argument is not a substitute for a differential either. I reasoned in a code comment that a reused literal refusal was unreachable; the property suite found the case within minutes. Both halves hold at once.

WHAT YOU CAN CONSUME rather than re-derive, all plant-proved, in crates/fln-parse:
* state.rs — ParserState with both precedence registers, checkPrec/checkLhsPrec in the pin's direction, and longest_match with the score tuple (end position, success-beats-error, priority) lexicographic. TIES ARE PRESERVED as a choice node with lhs_prec set to the MINIMUM, never resolved by picking one: a parser that took the first winner yields a well-formed tree with the ambiguity silently gone, and the elaborator — which is what resolves ambiguity in this language — never learns a decision existed.
* pratt.rs — the loop, with both trailing-loop discard rules observed against the running pin, and consume-then-flag when nothing is applicable. The no-progress guard in the trailing loop is MINE, not the pin's: upstream is a partial def that would loop.
* category.rs — the indexed lookup and all three LeadingIdentBehavior variants, each pinned by a NEGATIVE case. Note the trailing lookup always behaves as Default whatever the category declares (Basic.lean:1932): punning applies to the position that OPENS a construct, not inside one.
* build.rs — Leaves, which carry the lexer's extents. Do not rebuild spans; see measurement 1 above.
* fixtures/PARSER_CATEGORY_INVENTORY.txt and tests/parser_category_inventory.rs — the inventory RE-DERIVES from the pin at test time, so if you add a category the suite will tell you rather than the inventory quietly agreeing with itself.

ONE DEFECT TO KNOW ABOUT because it is the shape a join seam will hit again: longest_match's ambiguous path originally never set the position. restore had put the cursor back, the choice node was pushed without moving it forward, and the Pratt loop's no-progress guard then stopped the chain — a silently truncated parse on exactly the inputs where an ambiguity exists. parser_fuzz found it; no unit test did. Fixed in commit 4747c803.

comments.author: cc_3
comments.text:
CLAIMED by cc_3, 2026-07-25. ANSWERING THE ORACLE QUESTION FIRST, before any code, because on this bead it decides whether the evidence is worth anything.

WHY A FROM-SCRATCH REPARSE IS NOT AN ORACLE HERE. Dynamic registration means the thing being tested and the thing testing it are assembled from the same parts. A "reparse from scratch" still builds its table with my registration logic, walks it with my lookup, and resolves with my longest_match. If the registry is last-wins where the Reference is additive, both runs agree perfectly and the differential certifies the mistake. That is not a hazard on this bead, it is the default.

So the oracle is the pinned binary, on a corpus that exercises REGISTRATION ORDER. Below is what I got, graded. Every grade-A row is a file I ran through ~/.elan/toolchains/leanprover--lean4---v4.32.0/bin/lean and read the diagnostics from.

=== GRADE A: OBSERVED AGAINST THE RUNNING PIN ===

A1. INTERLEAVING IS REAL AND ORDERED. `syntax "myfoo" : term` plus a macro_rules, then `#check myfoo` -> accepted. The SAME file with `#check myfoo` FIRST -> `error(lean.unknownIdentifier): Unknown identifier 'myfoo'`. A registration takes effect for later commands only, so a parse is against the grammar as of its own position in the file, not the file's final grammar. This is the property a GrammarEpoch has to make explicit.

A2. SHADOWING IS ADDITIVE, NOT LAST-WINS, and this is the finding I would have got wrong. Two `notation "dup"` declarations, then `#eval dup` -> `error: Ambiguous term`. The second declaration does NOT replace the first: both parsers stay registered and the parse becomes genuinely ambiguous. A registry built as a map from syntax to production — which is the obvious shape, and what I would have written — silently drops the first and never reports the ambiguity. Note this is the registration-level confirmation of slice A's choice-node rule: ties are preserved, and here is where the tie comes from.

A3. MACRO_RULES STACK, WHICH IS A DIFFERENT MECHANISM. Two `macro_rules` for the same syntax -> accepted, no ambiguity. So expansion alternatives and parser registrations are not the same thing and must not share a code path: two notations conflict, two macro_rules do not.

A4. SCOPE RESTORE. `local notation "mybar"` inside `section ... end`, used inside -> accepted; used after `end` -> `Unknown identifier 'mybar'`. The scope's registrations are gone at `end`.

A5. NESTED SCOPES RESTORE THE INNER ONE ONLY. Sections A and B nested, `n1` local to A and `n2` local to B: `n1 + n2` inside B -> accepted; `n1` after `end B` -> accepted; `n2` after `end B` -> `Unknown identifier 'n2'`. So `end` pops exactly one scope and does not disturb the enclosing one.

A6. UNKNOWN CATEGORY IS A TYPED REFUSAL. `syntax "zz" : nosuchcategory` -> `error: unknown category 'nosuchcategory'`.

A7. A FAILED COMMAND DOES NOT ROLL BACK EARLIER GRAMMAR. A notation, then a command that errors (`#eval nosuchthing`), then a use of the notation -> only the unknown-identifier error appears; the notation still works. So registration is not transactional across commands, and "rollback" in this bead's scope means scope exit, not error recovery.

=== GRADE B: TRANSCRIBED, WITH LINES ===

B1. CALLBACK ORDER IS REVERSE REGISTRATION ORDER. `registerParserAttributeHook` does `parserAttributeHooks.modify fun hooks => hook::hooks` — a PREPEND (Extension.lean:312-313) — and `runParserAttributeHooks` does `hooks.forM` over the list as-is (:315-317). So the last hook registered runs first.

=== THE HONEST GAP, AND I AM GRADING IT RATHER THAN PAPERING OVER IT ===

CALLBACK ORDERING HAS NO INDEPENDENT ORACLE AVAILABLE TO ME. B1 is a reading of the pin's source, not an observation of its behaviour. I looked for a way to observe it and could not construct one: the hooks are registered by `builtin_initialize` in compiled Lean code, there is no surface syntax for registering two hooks with distinguishable effects from a .lean file, and the two attributes that expose hook running (`run_builtin_parser_attribute_hooks`, `run_parser_attribute_hooks`) run ALL hooks and report nothing about their order.

So for callback ordering my claim is: OBSERVED-BY-READING, NOT PROVED. Concretely that means if my implementation runs hooks in reverse registration order and the Reference does too, I have a citation and not a measurement; and if a future reader finds a way to observe it, the claim should be upgraded rather than assumed correct. I am recording it here so nobody downstream reads the suite's green bar as behavioural evidence.

That is a worse position than slices B through E of fln-ffam had, and it is still better than a differential that certifies both sides. It is also narrow: it applies ONLY to the order hooks fire in. Everything about WHAT registration does — A1 through A7 — has real observations behind it.

=== A HARNESS DEFECT I FOUND AND FIXED, worth recording because it could have corrupted earlier evidence ===

My probe harness grepped for `error: ` and the pin emits some diagnostics as `error(lean.someCode): `. So a file that failed with a coded error was reported as PARSED. I found this while probing A1, where `#check myfoo` before the declaration looked like it succeeded.

I RE-VERIFIED slice C's discrimination table with the corrected harness and it is intact. The distinction slice C relies on is between `unexpected end of input; expected '!'` — a genuine parse refusal — and `elaboration function ... has not been implemented`, which means the parse SUCCEEDED and only the elaborator was missing. My original slice C harness filtered on exactly that and was right. No conclusion changes; the risk was real and the check was cheap.

=== SLICE PLAN ===
* A. The registry and GrammarEpoch: add, scope push/pop, additive shadowing (A2), typed unknown-category refusal (A6), and epoch-ordered lookup (A1). Each law tied to its observation.
* B. registration_state_model: the model of add/scope/restore/shadow as a state machine, checked against the observed corpus.
* C. grammar_effect_totality: every effect answers, typed refusals only, FL-INV-07 nonpublication for resource and cancellation.
* D. parser_interleaving_dpor: schedule independence for concurrent registration, 1/8/32, identical grammar roots.
* E. dynamic_parser_mutations: the mutation suite.
* dynamic_parser_no_mock_e2e splits to its own bead on the franken_lean-jbru / franken_lean-urd1 boundary. Those two stay filed where they are.

comments.author: cc_3
comments.text:
SLICE A LANDED — commit f2190330, crates/fln-parse/src/registry.rs. fln-parse 63 -> 77 tests.

WHAT THE OBSERVATIONS BOUGHT. Every law in the module is tied to a grade-A observation from the previous comment, and one of them overturned what I would have implemented:

SHADOWING IS ADDITIVE. Tables are append-only lists per token, because two `notation "dup"` declarations produce `error: Ambiguous term` at the pin rather than the second silently winning. The obvious registry shape — a map from token to production — is wrong, and wrong in a way nothing downstream can detect: it drops a production and never reports the ambiguity it was supposed to create. This is also where longest_match's choice nodes come from, so slices A and this one now meet: the tie has a source.

EPOCHS ARE THE INTERLEAVING LAW AS A VALUE. A lookup at epoch e sees exactly the registrations with at <= e, which is `#check` before its `syntax` declaration failing and after it succeeding. view_at(category, epoch) reconstructs the grammar a parse actually ran under, which is what makes a replay meaningful rather than a re-run against today's table.

SCOPE EXIT DISCARDS BY DEPTH EQUALITY, and nested scopes are tested separately from single ones because the single-scope test cannot distinguish the two rules — there is nothing enclosing it to damage.

A CLAIM OF MINE THE PLANTS PROVED WRONG, and the way it was found is the useful part. I documented that discarding on "depth >= dying" rather than equality would take the enclosing scope with it. I planted `>=` and IT FAILED TO FAIL. The reason: `>=` discards deeper-or-equal, and a scoped registration can never be deeper than the scope being closed, so on every reachable state `>=` and `==` are the same function. The variant that actually breaks the outer scope is `<=` — discard shallower-or-equal — and that one is now the planted case and is caught (left [], right ["outer"]).

I am recording this because the plant discipline earned its keep in a new way here. Usually a plant confirms that a test can fail. This time a plant that DIDN'T fail exposed a wrong claim in my own documentation — a plausible-sounding statement about which comparison is dangerous, which would have sat there indefinitely being wrong. A plant that fails to fail is information, not a nuisance.

SEVEN PLANTS TOTAL, six killed and one informative-by-not-failing: last-wins registration (left [], right ["first"]); a lookup ignoring the epoch, which loses interleaving entirely; hooks in registration order instead of reverse; a refused registration advancing the epoch; a refused registration firing hooks, which would let an observer act on a grammar change that never happened; and the two scope-discard variants above.

THE GRADE-B CLAIM, isolated so it cannot borrow credibility from the others. Hook ordering is reverse registration order, transcribed from Extension.lean:313 and :315 and NOT observed. Its test exists so the implementation cannot drift from the citation. Both the module doc and the test doc say this in their own words, so a reader of either one learns it without having to find this comment.

A HARNESS DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED, worth recording because it could have corrupted earlier evidence. My pin probe grepped for `error: ` and the pin emits some diagnostics as `error(lean.someCode): ` — so a file that FAILED was reported as PASSED. I found it while probing interleaving, where `#check myfoo` before the declaration looked like it succeeded. I then RE-VERIFIED slice C's discrimination table with the corrected harness and it is intact: the distinction slice C relies on is between `unexpected end of input; expected '!'`, a genuine parse refusal, and `elaboration function ... has not been implemented`, which means the parse SUCCEEDED and only the elaborator was missing. The original slice C harness filtered on exactly that and was right. No conclusion changed; the check was cheap and the alternative was leaving a known hole behind unexamined.

REMAINING ON THIS BEAD:
* B. registration_state_model — the add/scope/restore/shadow state machine as an explicit model, checked over the observed corpus, with the model shown to reject states the registry cannot reach.
* C. grammar_effect_totality — every effect answers, typed refusals only, and FL-INV-07 nonpublication for resource and cancellation. The LexBudget shape from franken_lean-81oq is the precedent: exceeding a bound is Inconclusive with a ResourceUsage, never a rejection, and Inconclusive::diagnostic stays None on clean input.
* D. parser_interleaving_dpor — schedule independence for concurrent registration at 1/8/32, requiring IDENTICAL grammar roots and not merely equivalent ones. Note this is a SELF-differential and will be paired with a positive oracle plus a statement of what it does not establish, per the law on this bead.
* E. dynamic_parser_mutations — the mutation suite.
* dynamic_parser_no_mock_e2e splits to its own bead on the franken_lean-jbru / franken_lean-urd1 boundary when the rest lands. Those two stay filed where they are.

comments.author: cc_3
comments.text:
CLOSING STATEMENT — fln-okfb, cc_3, 2026-07-25. crates/fln-parse at 101 tests across 10 targets. Gates green: fmt, clippy --all-targets -D warnings, cargo test.

SLICES B THROUGH E LANDED — commit 7b788f7d.

=== THE FIVE NAMED SUITES ===
  registration_state_model    5 tests   present
  grammar_effect_totality     7 tests   present
  parser_interleaving_dpor    5 tests   present
  dynamic_parser_mutations    7 tests   present
  dynamic_parser_no_mock_e2e  SPLIT to fln-33gl (cod_2's ci/ domain)

=== WHAT THE ORACLE DISCIPLINE ACTUALLY BOUGHT ON THIS BEAD ===

REGISTRATION_STATE_MODEL is only worth something if the model is independent of the registry, so the suite PROVES the independence rather than asserting it: a last-wins model is shown to disagree with the registry, which means agreement carries information. Every transition cites the pin observation it came from. An exhaustive sweep over every operation sequence up to length five compares the two.

PARSER_INTERLEAVING_DPOR states its limits in its own module docs, at the top, and I want them restated here because the green bar is where the temptation lives. This is a SELF-DIFFERENTIAL. A sweep that finds no interleaving violation is evidence that MY schedule space contains no violation MY OWN MODEL CAN EXPRESS. That is not schedule independence. FL-INV-01 is the claim; this sweep is one piece of support for it, and on its own a weak one:
  * It cannot see a violation that the runner and the canonical order agree on wrongly. If apply_batch's key ordering is wrong, every thread count gives the same wrong root and the suite is green.
  * It explores the arrival orders I generate, not the schedule space the machine has. There is NO DPOR scheduler here — the name is the bead's. What it does is exhaustive permutation of arrival order for a small batch (all 720 of 6!) plus concurrent submission with per-worker rotations at 1/8/32. Calling that DPOR would overstate it, so the module says so.
  * It says nothing about whether the grammar is CORRECT, only that it is the same one every time.

What makes it non-trivial is the positive oracle it is paired with. The pin's observed behaviour is that registration order is SEMANTICALLY SIGNIFICANT — two `notation` declarations under one token give `Ambiguous term` — so the sequence of productions under a token is part of the grammar. Because order matters, locking alone cannot deliver schedule independence: a mutex gives A result, not the SAME result. Independence requires a canonical order, which is the registered tie-break the determinism doctrine asks for. So the suite ALSO asserts the negative: applying on arrival, without canonicalisation, DOES produce different roots. Without that half, the sweep would be equally green for a registry where order never mattered, and it would prove nothing about the mechanism that makes independence true.

DYNAMIC_PARSER_MUTATIONS is built around the criterion that a mutant dying because the oracle and the implementation share an assumption is NOT A KILL. So each of eight mutants carries the GRADE of the assertion that kills it and whether a self-differential could see it:
  FIVE mutants are invisible to the interleaving sweep — they produce the same wrong answer at every thread count and in every arrival order — and all five are killed by PIN OBSERVATIONS: last-wins registration, the epoch filter dropped, the scope discard using <=, a scoped registration treated as global, and an unknown category being auto-created.
  ONE mutant is visible to the sweep and legitimately killed by it: the canonical sort removed.
  TWO are killed only by WEAKER evidence, and they are NAMED in an assertion rather than folded into a total: hook ordering, killed by a reading of Extension.lean:313 and :315; and batch atomicity, which is our own rule with no pin backing — the pin's observed behaviour at COMMAND granularity is in fact the opposite, since a failed command does not roll back earlier grammar.
  That naming is a ratchet. Adding another mutant on weak evidence fails the test and has to be justified rather than absorbed.

GRAMMAR_EFFECT_TOTALITY follows the LexBudget precedent from franken_lean-81oq in both directions: a generous budget produces the identical grammar root, an exceeded one is Inconclusive with a ResourceUsage, publishes no diagnostic on a clean batch, is not a cancellation, and stops ATOMICALLY so a caller can retry with a larger allowance. Totality is checked against unknown categories, an empty token, a 4096-byte token, unicode, a duplicate category, an unopened scope, and lookups at epoch 0 and u64::MAX.

=== WHAT THIS BEAD ESTABLISHED, BY GRADE ===
GRADE A, observed by running the pinned binary: interleaving is real and ordered; shadowing is ADDITIVE and not last-wins; macro_rules stack where notations conflict; scope exit restores; nested `end` pops exactly one scope; an unscoped registration inside a scope outlives it; unknown category is a typed refusal; a failed command does not roll back earlier grammar.
GRADE B, transcribed with lines: hook ordering is reverse registration order (Extension.lean:313, :315).
GRADE C, ours and flagged: GrammarRoot's shape; the canonical key order; batch atomicity; the RegistryBudget units.

THE HONEST GAP, unchanged from the opening comment and worth repeating in the closure so it is not lost: CALLBACK ORDERING HAS NO INDEPENDENT ORACLE AVAILABLE TO ME. Hooks are registered by builtin_initialize in compiled Lean, there is no surface syntax for two hooks with distinguishable effects, and the attributes that expose hook running fire all of them and report nothing about order. The claim is observed-by-reading, not proved. If a future reader finds a way to observe it, the claim should be upgraded rather than assumed correct.

=== 13 PLANTED DEFECTS ACROSS THE BEAD ===
Twelve killed, and ONE INFORMATIVE BY NOT FAILING: I documented that discarding scoped registrations on "depth >= dying" would take the enclosing scope with it, planted `>=`, and it failed to fail — because a registration can never be deeper than the scope being closed, so `>=` and `==` are the same function on every reachable state. The variant that actually breaks the outer scope is `<=`, now planted and caught. A plant that does not fail is information, not a nuisance; this one found a wrong claim in my own documentation that would otherwise have sat there indefinitely.

=== HANDED ON ===
fln-33gl holds dynamic_parser_no_mock_e2e, with two lane-specific notes: the interleaving suite spawns 32 threads, which is the kind of step that trips a process-identity guard; and the suite it wraps is a self-differential that says so in its docs, so a lane publishing its green bar as evidence of FL-INV-01 would be laundering the distinction rather than reporting it.
fln-7li is the dependent epic — W4's Vellum engine — and this closes the last of its parser-side children.

title: fln-olean: lib.rs claims byte-compatible .olean write on line 1 and defers it on line 6
description:
crates/fln-olean/src/lib.rs contradicts itself four lines apart.

Line 1 states the crate is "Grimoire's module codec -- byte-compatible .olean read and write, .ilean, and the olean-next frontier format (plan 7.2-7.4)". Line 6 states "Writing, .ilean, and olean-next arrive with their workstream beads." It names no bead. I looked and could not find one, and neither will the next person. That sentence is where the capability went missing.

This is in-source documentation, not README prose, so the README's present-tense convention does not apply to it at all. It is also the cheapest possible specimen of the defect class that the claim-matrix bead exists to stop: a capability asserted and deferred inside a single doc comment, with the deferral pointing at nothing.

MEASURED SCOPE OF THE ACTUAL GAP. crates/fln-olean/src/ is four files and every one is a read path: region.rs (a working by-value reader for real Reference oleans), decl.rs (decode_expr at line 537 is its only Expr-facing entry point), format.rs (layout constants and Reference source citations), lib.rs. crates/fln-olean/tests/ is three files, all read tests: decl_decode.rs, olean_contract.rs, region_read.rs. A workspace-wide search for any olean write path returns exactly one hit in crates and tools, and it is a comment at format.rs:5 citing the REFERENCE's writer as the source of the layout facts. Separately, there is no round-trippable Expr serializer in any codec: the only Expr-to-bytes family is fln_hash::canon's CanonWriter, a hashing encoder with no inverse.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA. lib.rs states what the crate does TODAY without contradicting itself, and the deferral names the bead that owns the writer.

BLOCKED DOWNSTREAM, so the eventual writer bead can cite them: FL-INV-04 codec fidelity (plan line 189, "Grimoire read-compose-write is identity on the byte level for faithful-mode oleans") is unenforceable without a writer, and AGENTS.md holds that no subsystem ships against an unenforced invariant; AGENTS.md's standing codec rig requires mixed-producer builds in BOTH directions, one of which is FrankenLean producing oleans the Reference consumes; franken_lean-iwu's acceptance requires an olean to olean-next round trip preserving the semantic hash and, on the faithful path, the bytes; and franken_lean-oh1j item 5 requires a codec to round-trip sharing through. The full missing-capability record is on franken_lean-oh1j.
close_reason: Header states read-only reality; deferral names franken_lean-oh1j instead of nothing. Commit 86035037.

title: Parity Ledger: the freshness law is a denylist, so it classifies 0 of 85 produced-value rows and a new source-reading tag passes silently
description:
validate_freshness_names_the_oracle_it_claims refuses a row that claims a produced value
while carrying a freshness tag in SOURCE_READING_FRESHNESS_TAGS. That list is a DENYLIST of
three tags, so ledger.rs:603 reads "if the tag is not on the list, continue" -- an
unrecognised tag is trusted.

Measured on ci/PARITY_LEDGER.txt at 94 rows:
  rows claiming a produced value       85
  distinct freshness tags on those      6
  classified by the denylist            0
  riding on an unclassified tag        85 of 85, which is 100 percent
  pin-census-v4.32.0                    0 rows anywhere in the ledger
  inventory-v4.32.0                     3 rows, none of them produced-value
  unit-suite-v4.32.0                    4 rows, none of them produced-value

So on the real ledger today the law fires on nothing. It is kept exercised by a planted
synthetic row in a_two_field_repair_that_leaves_its_freshness_tag_behind_is_refused, and
the suite deliberately asserts the denylist still contains pin-census-v4.32.0 "so a known
source-reading tag remains denied after the last real row moves off it" -- so the authors
knew the real rows had moved off it. That floor keeps the LIST alive. It does not keep the
COVERAGE alive, and nothing measures the difference.

THE ASYMMETRY IS THE FINDING. The same file guards the adjacent field the safe way.
oracle_kind is an ALLOWLIST -- VALUE_PRODUCING_ORACLES -- so breaks_law is
"level > L1 and NOT in the list", and an oracle-kind nobody has classified FAILS CLOSED and
reddens. freshness is a denylist, so a freshness tag nobody has classified PASSES. Two
fields of the same row, repaired by the same three-field edit, protected in opposite
directions, and only one of them can be defeated by inventing a new string.

This is not hypothetical drift: repairing a row moves three fields, and the whole reason
this law exists is that somebody moved two and left the third. The next such tag will not be
one of the three already enumerated.

WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED. No row in the tree is currently mis-tagged: all six tags in use
name plausible real rigs (core-observables, core-ext-observables, pin-option-defaults,
pin-ctor-inventory, blake3-official-vectors, and a multi-host attestation). This is an
unguarded direction, not an observed false claim. Nothing here shows anyone has exploited
it, and the failure mode requires a new tag to be introduced.

PROPOSED REPAIR, and the trap in it:
Invert to an allowlist, matching oracle_kind one field over: a produced-value row's freshness
tag must be a REGISTERED value-producing run tag, and an unknown tag fails closed.

The trap is that a bare allowlist is a wall -- it reddens the build for anyone adding a
legitimate new evidence run, which is the shrinking-allowance direction problem already
recorded on this bead family, and a gate that cannot go green is one people bypass. So the
registration must be cheap and, better, DERIVED: bind each freshness tag to the rig that
emits it, the way ORACLE_BACKING binds a symbol to the rig that can retire it, so the tag
names something that exists and the binding fails when the rig moves. A tag that no rig
produces is then refusable without anyone maintaining a denylist by memory.

VERIFICATION REQUIRED TO CLOSE:
  - a planted row with a NEWLY INVENTED source-reading tag on a produced-value row must be
    refused; this is the exact case that passes today and is the floor for the whole change;
  - the existing planted two-field repair must still be refused, so the inversion does not
    lose the case the law was built for;
  - a legitimate new value-producing run must be admissible without editing a denylist, or
    the repair has traded a silent hole for a wall;
  - the coverage must be MEASURED and bound to a count, not asserted: the guard should fail
    if the number of produced-value rows it actually classifies drops toward zero again,
    since that is the state it is in today and nothing noticed.

RELATED, AND WORTH FIXING IN THE SAME PASS: the doc comment on
validate_repaired_rows_cite_their_oracle says it is "vacuous today by construction -- all
twelve rows are still in the remainder". Measured: SOURCE_READ_ABOVE_L1_ALLOWANCE is empty
and all twelve ORACLE_BACKING rows are repaired to L2 via pinned-binary, so that law is now
fully live over all twelve and the comment says the opposite. It errs in the safe direction,
understating a guard rather than overstating it, but it would tell an auditor asking whether
the qydn repair completed that it had not.

Found while scoping the qydn open item recorded in cc_2's handoff. Measured at HEAD c15e40a6.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
UBS-unrelated. cc_2, pane 3. The RELATED item at the foot of this bead is repaired at 03e8988b. The CORE finding of this bead is untouched and dy22 stays OPEN.

RE-MEASURED AT efc5e730, unchanged from the 2026-07-26 filing: 94 rows, 85 claiming a produced value, 6 distinct freshness tags on those, 0 classified by the denylist, 85 of 85 riding on an unclassified tag. The denylist direction defect is exactly as filed.

WHAT 03e8988b DID. The doc comment on validate_repaired_rows_cite_their_oracle said the law was "vacuous today by construction - all twelve rows are still in the remainder". Measured false: all twelve have LEFT the remainder, every one L2 on pinned-binary, so the law examines all twelve and admits them on merit, 12/12 citing their rig. parity_ledger.rs carried the same claim and rested its anti-vacuity duty on it.

THE LARGER HALF, which was not in this bead's text. The suite asserted only outcome.is_ok(), a verdict produced identically by the live world and the vacuous one, so the law could be switched off in silence. That the vacuous world returns Ok is not an inference - the sibling test the_successor_law_admits_a_full_repair_and_ignores_an_undeclared_repair asserts that verdict for an unrepaired row.

A THIRD CLAIM, and it bears directly on this bead's proposed repair. SOURCE_READING_FRESHNESS_TAGS gave two reasons for being a denylist and only the second survives. WHY THAT MATTERS HERE. comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
POST-CLOSE JUDGMENT — FAIL-CLOSED PARITY-LEDGER FRESHNESS REGISTRY

`fln-parity-freshness-denylist-direction-dy22` closes at the bounded Parity Ledger integrity boundary implemented in `c6a049b0`. The previous rule only rejected three remembered source-reading tags, so it classified zero of the live 85 produced-value rows and let a newly invented tag pass silently. The implementation replaces that direction with six checked tag-to-rig bindings: every produced-value row must name a registered freshness run and cite that run's rig. An unknown tag is refused; a registered tag whose row omits the rig is refused; a missing rig path or an unused registry entry is refused.

The live population is measured rather than inferred: `VALUE_PRODUCING_FRESHNESS_LIVE_FLOOR` is 85, and the real-ledger cell rejects a clean-looking world in which the registry no longer binds the published produced-value rows. The permanent controls preserve all required directions: `an_invented_tag_is_refused_but_a_registered_new_run_is_admitted` kills the newly invented-tag case and demonstrates the cheap registered path for a legitimate run; `a_two_field_repair_that_leaves_its_freshness_tag_behind_is_refused` retains the historical half-repair refusal; and the source-read/L1 handoff remains explicitly permitted.

Executable evidence: at current descendant `8c89ce02`, warnings-denied `cargo clippy -p fln-conformance --test parity_ledger` passed and `cargo test -p fln-conformance --test parity_ledger -- --nocapture` passed 16/16. The `ci_execution_join` target passed 75/75 after its subsequent citation repairs. The first full `scripts/check.sh` green ran at descendant `0ba1ae3978d3754cc3d08a36f1b70cd9c862735f`, run `check-20260804T082042Z-2338344`, process exit 0; its scratch bundle is deliberately not cited as a durable manifest artifact.

This is not a claim of a Reference/corpus parity result, of the semantic truth of every existing freshness tag beyond its registered rig binding, or of future automatic producer discovery. Registration remains a reviewed tag-to-rig tuple; what is now mechanically enforced is that a produced-value claim cannot invent a tag or omit the rig it names. No deletion, fixture cleanup, or change to non-produced L0/L1 source-reading rows is claimed.

title: Parity Ledger: freshness names the evidence run, is never read, and a two-field repair leaves it stale
description:
The Parity Ledger's freshness field names the evidence run, is the third field encoding a row's provenance, and until this bead nothing ever read it.

MEASURED AT 8aae792a by cc_2. The ledger header (ci/PARITY_LEDGER.txt:5) defines freshness as the evidence freshness; crates/fln-conformance/src/ledger.rs:13 states it plainly: "freshness names the evidence run". The tags bear that out - each names a RUN by prefix and the pin epoch by suffix (core-observables- / pin-census- / core-ext-observables-, all at v4.32.0).

THE MEASUREMENT. Of the 94 rows:

  * Exactly 12 carry pin-census-v4.32.0.
  * Those 12 are SET-IDENTICAL to the 12 non-mixHash entries of SOURCE_READ_ABOVE_L1_ALLOWANCE (verified by sorted diff, not by inspection).
  * pin-census-v4.32.0 appears on no other row. It is a 1:1 marker of the source-reading census crates/fln-core/tests/pin_inventory_census.rs.
  * row.freshness is written once at ledger.rs:205 and NEVER READ AGAIN anywhere in the workspace. All five validators run in the parity_ledger suite; none touched it.

WHY THIS IS THE SAME DEFECT ONE FIELD OVER. The parent bead qydn opened with: "Level and oracle-kind are parsed into typed fields and never compared to each other." That is verbatim true of freshness against oracle-kind, and it stayed true after the oracle law and the successor law both landed.

THE GAP, CONCRETELY. Repairing one of the twelve moves THREE fields: oracle-kind to pinned-binary, fixtures to cite the rig, and freshness to name the rig's run. validate_level_is_supported_by_its_oracle watches the first. validate_repaired_rows_cite_their_oracle watches the second. Nothing watched the third. A row flipped to pinned-binary, citing pin_option_defaults.rs, and still tagged pin-census-v4.32.0 was FULLY GREEN - its stated evidence run naming the source-reading census as the provenance of a binary-produced level. That is our READING of the oracle reported under the name of the oracle, which is exactly what qydn exists to prevent.

Not hypothetical: planted against the real ledger in an isolated worktree (mutant C below) and confirmed green before this change.

WHY IT WAS FILED RATHER THAN JUST FIXED, and this is the argument for the whole bead: the finding's whole point is that reading found it and nothing would catch a recurrence. That IS AGENTS.md item 7. Six of the entries in that table were found by attentive reading rather than by a check, and AGENTS.md says plainly that instances found by reading is not a mechanism, it is luck with good people, and luck does not survive a context restart. Filed three panes into a session in which every cc pane has now been restarted - the argument is not theoretical.

WHAT LANDED, in crates/fln-conformance/{src/ledger.rs, tests/parity_ledger.rs}:

  * SOURCE_READING_FRESHNESS_TAGS - three tags that name a run which only READ the pin. A DENYLIST, not an allowlist, and the direction is forced: both pin rigs are deliberately fixture-less, so the repair needs a tag that does not exist yet, and an allowlist would refuse it. The existing permission test already exercises a tag (rfc-vectors) absent from the real ledger. A new honest tag must pass without asking permission; a known source-reading tag must not.
  * validate_freshness_names_the_oracle_it_claims - read entirely off the ROW, scoped by exactly claims_a_produced_value, so while a row is still at pinned-source the oracle law owns it and this one is silent; the instant it claims a produced value this one takes over. The handoff IS the transition the gap lived in.
  * validate_source_reading_freshness_tags_are_live - the other direction. A declared tag no row carries must be removed, so the remainder shrinks instead of rotting into a permanent hole wearing the costume of a shrinking debt.
  * claims_a_produced_value extracted as one shared predicate. Two hand-written copies of "has this row left the remainder" would be a join between two rules with nothing watching it - this module's own defect class, one floor down. This touches cc_3's validate_repaired_rows_cite_their_oracle body by substitution only, with no change in meaning.

A WALL I BUILT AND THE CAMPAIGN CAUGHT, recorded because it is the exact trap cc_3 documented on this bead and I walked into it anyway. My first draft asserted that the oracle law returns Err on the planted two-field row. True today only because maxErrors is still declared - so the assertion would have gone RED the instant cod_2 landed the correct repair, rewarding the repair with a red build. A planted FULL repair (mutant D) found it. Both preconditions are now allowance-independent: ORACLE_BACKING outlives the repair by design, and "raises no unsupported-level finding" holds in both states.

MUTATION CAMPAIGN, in a git worktree at 8aae792a with only my two files applied, worktree restored between each. ALL BY EXIT CODE:
  baseline .................................................. exit 0, 15 passed
  C  two-field half-repair applied to the REAL ledger ........ KILLED (exit 101)
     oracle-kind flipped, rig cited, allowance shrunk, tag left behind
  D  the FULL three-field repair on the REAL ledger .......... exit 0, 15 passed
     the law is satisfiable and names the path; not a wall
  A  SOURCE_READING_FRESHNESS_TAGS emptied ................... KILLED two ways
  B  the law gutted to a no-op ............................... KILLED by the floor test

D is the one that matters for cod_2: their three-field repair lands green.

THE FLOOR. a_two_field_repair_that_leaves_its_freshness_tag_behind_is_refused is planted permanently rather than verified once by hand. Mutants A and B both die on it. A guard nobody has seen go red is a guard nobody has tested, and a scan returning empty is a broken scan rather than a clean tree.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO. It repairs no row. All thirteen still carry L2 with oracle-kind pinned-source; SOURCE_READ_ABOVE_L1_ALLOWANCE still has 13 entries. Every one of the thirteen still requires an edit to ci/PARITY_LEDGER.txt, which is cod_2's artifact and which I have not touched. This adds a FUTURE obligation to a repair nobody has made yet.

WHAT COD_2 NEEDS TO DECIDE, which is a decision and not a task: the two pin rigs have NO fixture by design (cc_3 avoided creating a capture that could rot). So the twelve need a NEW tag family naming a fixture-less test run. Candidates following the existing convention would be pin-option-defaults-v4.32.0 and pin-ctor-inventory-v4.32.0, but the tag vocabulary is cod_2's and I am not coining one in their artifact.

MIXHASH IS UNAFFECTED and its repair really is one token: its tag is already core-observables-v4.32.0, the correct pair for a fixture-backed pinned-binary row that 38 other rows use. The asymmetry is real - twelve rows need three fields, mixHash needs one.

A SEPARATE OBSERVATION RECORDED WHILE CLASSIFYING, not a defect and not part of this bead: core_observables.txt contains NO mixHash record. The kinds emitted are string, name, level, equiv and expr only. mixHash is pinned COMPOSITIONALLY - mix_hash is the composition primitive for Name (name.rs:83), Level (level.rs:305-333) and Expr (expr.rs:716+), so a wrong mix_hash breaks the binary-produced composite records. cc_3's conclusion that the oracle-kind is the wrong field stands and its L2 is earned; it is earned indirectly. Worth knowing because after repair mixHash is the one row of the thirteen carrying L2/pinned-binary with no direct observation of its own symbol AND the one row ORACLE_BACKING deliberately excludes - each justified alone, but together it is the row with the least mechanism on it.

GATES at 8aae792a: cargo fmt --check exit 0; cargo test -p fln-conformance exit 0, 214 passed 0 failed; cargo clippy -p fln-conformance --all-targets --no-deps -D warnings exit 0; ubs 0 critical. Exit codes read directly, never through a pipe - the first fmt run of this change reported clean through a pipe and was in fact exit 1 on a real violation.

title: Parity Ledger: 13 rows claim L2 with a source-only oracle the ledger's own tier note calls L1
description:
13 Parity Ledger rows claim L2 with an oracle kind the ledger's own tier note defines as L1.

ci/PARITY_LEDGER.txt:41-48 defines its two tiers by ORACLE, not by amount of testing: L2 means "the pinned Reference binary produced the expected value"; L1 means "implemented against the pinned SOURCE semantics with in-repo tests, but no Reference-produced value is compared".

Thirteen rows carry level L2 with oracle-kind pinned-source. By the ledger's own sentence, that combination is L1. Mechanically:

  rg "^row " ci/PARITY_LEDGER.txt | awk -F'|' '{l=$5;o=$7;gsub(/^ +| +$/,"",l);gsub(/^ +| +$/,"",o); if(l=="L2"&&o=="pinned-source") print}'

returns, at HEAD d5e69023:

  meta-api | mixHash                     (fixture: core_observables.txt)
  meta-api | Lean.Expr.ctorInventory      | Lean.Level.ctorInventory
  meta-api | Lean.Name.ctorInventory      | Lean.DataValue.ctorInventory
  meta-api | maxHeartbeats                | maxRecDepth
  meta-api | synthInstance.maxHeartbeats  | synthInstance.maxSize
  meta-api | maxSynthPendingDepth         | maxUniverseOffset
  meta-api | exponentiation.threshold     | maxErrors

Twelve of the thirteen cite crates/fln-core/tests/pin_inventory_census.rs plus a vendored upstream .lean source file. That test reads vendored SOURCE at test time -- real, mechanical, re-checked on every run, and exactly what the ledger calls L1. The thirteenth (mixHash) is a different defect in the same row: its oracle-kind says pinned-source while its fixture is core_observables.txt, which is binary-produced. That row's own two fields disagree about which oracle backed it, so one of the two is wrong and nothing says which.

WHY NOTHING CAUGHT IT. The ledger gate checks two things and neither is this: crates/fln-conformance/tests/parity_ledger.rs:41 asserts rows above L0 cite a non-empty fixture list, and crates/fln-conformance/src/ledger.rs:233 asserts each cited fixture path exists. Level and oracle-kind are parsed into typed fields and never compared to each other. A four-line consistency check over the parsed rows finds all thirteen.

THIS IS A CORRECTION, NOT A RAISE, and that should be said plainly before anyone picks it up: closing it either demotes thirteen published levels or produces the binary-produced evidence that would justify keeping them. The second is cheap and I verified the route -- the stock pinned binary prints its entire registered option table, 661 options with defaults and descriptions, via Lean.getOptionDeclsArray (vendor/lean4-src/src/Lean/Data/Options.lean:127). Probed directly at ~/.elan/toolchains/leanprover--lean4---v4.32.0 on 2026-07-25: maxRecDepth = 512, maxHeartbeats = 200000, maxErrors = 100, table size 661. Extending scripts/extract/gen_core_fixtures.sh to dump that table would move the twelve option and census rows from source-read to binary-produced honestly, and would bring them under that script's existing --check drift lane by construction. The four ctorInventory rows may need a different route; a constructor list has no printed value in the same sense.

A SECOND, DIFFERENT INTEGRITY DEFECT IN THE SAME ARTIFACT, recorded here because it is also "the ledger says something that is not so", though the mechanism is cross-artifact rather than intra-row: the evidence stream's link to the Parity Ledger has no referential integrity. parity_ledger_row is a required field in the evidence schema (scripts/evidence.py:399, :598, :755) whose VALUE is never resolved against ci/PARITY_LEDGER.txt. Two emitted ids resolve to nothing:

  scripts/tribunal/leanchecker_witness.sh:122   emits  kernel.witness.<module>
  scripts/e2e/kernel_replay.sh:317              emits  init-prelude-admission-replay

Neither string appears anywhere in the ledger. A lane can therefore claim to substantiate a row that does not exist, and pass.

WHETHER WITNESS CAUGHT IT: no, and it structurally could not have. The Witness claim matrix (crates/fln-conformance/src/witness.rs) governs prose claim SITES in README.md, AGENTS.md, the plan and one crate header, plus three concept censuses; EVIDENCE_CITATIONS anchors row evidence to facts in files. Nothing in it touches Parity Ledger row ids or the evidence stream, so slice 3's citation mechanism was never pointed at this class. It was found by grep during the 2026-07-25 conformance-harness audit, which is the same way both rows that rotted on 2026-07-25 were found -- by reading, not by a check. That is the freshness gap GOVERNED_SCOPE already names, showing up in a second artifact.

EVIDENCE FRESHNESS: all file:line references and the awk result verified against HEAD d5e69023 on 2026-07-25 by cc_3; the option-table probe was run against the pinned binary the same day. AUDIT SET: filed together with two related findings; ids in the first comment.

comments.text:
cc_3: this is a doctrine fix, not a refactor, and the enforcing law has landed. cc_3, 2026-07-25, commit d5cc084b.

READ THIS PART FIRST, BECAUSE THE CHANGE LOOKS SMALLER THAN IT IS. Someone will see "the test now runs the binary instead of reading the .lean file" and file it as a refactor. It is not.

  Reading upstream's SOURCE tells you what the Reference is WRITTEN to do.
  Asking the pinned BINARY tells you what it DOES.

D8 makes the Reference the differential ORACLE. A rig that reads its source has quietly replaced the oracle with our reading of the oracle -- an assertion about the binary's behaviour wearing the costume of an observation. And the failure is silent by construction: source and built binary agree almost always, so such a row is green right up until the moment they disagree. That moment is exactly the divergence class the Tribunal exists to catch, and it arrives in the one place nothing is watching, because the row that should have caught it is the row that stopped looking.

That is why these thirteen are not a labelling error. A row whose oracle-kind is pinned-source is not a weaker measurement of the same thing; it is a measurement of a different thing -- our reading -- reported under the name of the oracle.

WHAT LANDED IN d5cc084b: the enforcing law, in crates/fln-conformance/src/ledger.rs.

  * validate_level_is_supported_by_its_oracle: above L1, a row's oracle-kind must be one that PRODUCED A VALUE somebody compared against -- pinned-binary, spec-vectors, multi-host-attestation, certified-matrix. pinned-source is deliberately absent and that absence IS the law.
  * The thirteen are a DECLARED REMAINDER, not a grandfather clause. Landing a bare assertion would fail the build until thirteen published levels are re-earned or re-stated, and a gate that cannot be green is a gate people learn to bypass (franken_lean-e5k7). Declared, the FOURTEENTH fails: the class cannot grow while its members are triaged.
  * Checked in BOTH directions. An entry whose row no longer breaks the law is itself a failure, so the allowance shrinks as part of each repair rather than outliving the defect it records. A separate whole-file check refuses an allowance entry that names no row, because the next row to take that symbol would otherwise inherit an exemption nobody granted it.
  * SOURCE_READ_ALLOWANCE_REASON names three different repairs rather than one excuse: the eight option defaults now have a value-producing oracle (dc4e81e6) and need only the row edit; the four ctorInventory rows have no route and I claim none; mixHash is not a level question at all -- its oracle-kind says pinned-source while its cited fixture is binary-produced, so one of its two fields is simply wrong and this law cannot say which.

A DESIGN FLAW MY OWN PLANTED CASE CAUGHT, recorded because it is the argument for always planting the permission half: the first version folded orphan detection into the per-row law, which made the law refuse every SUBSET of the ledger -- including the synthetic ones its own permission test uses. The law is a per-row property that holds on any slice; orphan detection is a whole-file property. Two functions now, two scopes. The failing test was mine and it was right.

WHAT IS LEFT ON THIS BEAD, and it is why it stays open:
  * The eight option rows still SAY pinned-source. ci/PARITY_LEDGER.txt is cod_2's artifact and the edit is theirs; the evidence they need now exists and runs on every cargo test. When they make it, the allowance must shrink in the same change -- the law will tell them so, by name.
  * The four ctorInventory rows have no route. Walking the pin's environment for a constructor list is plausible and untried.
  * mixHash needs someone to decide which of its two fields is wrong.
