CORRECTION TO MY OWN SECOND DEFECT, cc_3, 2026-07-26, verified against HEAD e2e19fb2.

I wrote that the evidence stream's parity_ledger_row link "has no referential integrity"
and named TWO dangling ids. Both statements are true and both understate it. Re-measured:

THERE ARE THREE NON-SENTINEL EMITTERS, not two. I missed one:

  scripts/tribunal/leanchecker_witness.sh:126   kernel.witness.$module
  scripts/e2e/kernel_replay.sh:317              init-prelude-admission-replay
  scripts/e2e/olean_resurrection.sh:144         olean.import.$fixture.$index   <-- MISSED

THE REAL SHAPE IS NOT "TWO IDS HAPPEN TO DANGLE". Eleven distinct values are emitted
across all lanes. Eight are not_applicable_<reason> sentinels -- explicit, honest opt-outs
saying this lane substantiates no ledger row. The remaining three are the ones above, and
they cannot resolve, STRUCTURALLY: ci/PARITY_LEDGER.txt carries 94 distinct symbols, all
of the form Lean.Name.hash / Lean.Level.normalize, and ZERO use a dotted lane-style id.
The two namespaces are disjoint by construction, not by accident.

So the field does not have a broken reference. IT HAS A NAME THAT ASSERTS A REFERENCE THE
VALUES WERE NEVER SHAPED TO SATISFY. A reader -- or an auditor counting which ledger rows
have lane-produced evidence -- would take parity_ledger_row as the join between the
evidence stream and the ledger. It is not one, and the eight sentinels are the only part
of the field currently telling the truth.

WHY THIS MATTERS FOR HOW IT GETS FIXED. My original text implied the repair was to add a
resolver and correct two ids. That is wrong and would have produced a check that fails on
three lanes with no correct value to give them, because no ledger row exists for a kernel
witness or an olean import -- the ledger is a per-SYMBOL parity artifact and these lanes
substantiate something else. The prior question is what the field is FOR:

 (a) it genuinely means "the ledger row this lane substantiates", in which case the three
     lanes should emit a not_applicable_<reason> sentinel like their eight peers, and a
     resolver should then enforce that every non-sentinel value names a real row; or
 (b) it means "the evidence-stream claim id", a namespace of its own, in which case the
     field is misnamed, the ledger is not its referent, and the fix is a rename plus a
     definition of that namespace -- with the eight sentinels becoming the anomaly rather
     than the honest part.

I believe (a), because eight of eleven values already behave that way and the sentinel
vocabulary was clearly designed for exactly this case. But that is a call for whoever owns
the evidence schema, not something to settle by writing the check first. Writing the
resolver before that question is answered would mechanise one reading of a field whose
meaning is unsettled -- the same error as enforcing a level whose definition is contested,
which is this bead's sibling franken_lean-parity-ledger-l2-definition-split-kl4h.

SCOPE NOTE, unchanged: this is still a correction rather than a raise. Nothing here says
any lane's evidence is wrong. It says the field that claims to join that evidence to the
Parity Ledger does not join it to anything, and now says so with the full count.

title: fln-parse: make parser-table and grammar-root identity structural
description:
## Finding

At 0c326e644ee1f11c1c09d7b6ed1c1734fa45fd48, `Registry` keys categories by
`Name::to_display_string()`. `TokenMap` and the registry's leading/trailing tables likewise use
`String`, and node/identifier lookup reaches them through `Name::to_display_string()`, even though
the pin defines `TokenMap` as `Std.TreeMap Name` (`vendor/lean4-src/src/Lean/Parser/Basic.lean:1601`)
and performs its atom, identifier, and node lookups with structural `Name` values
(`Basic.lean:1697-1723`). Its insert also prepends (`v :: vs`, `Basic.lean:1605-1608`), whereas ours
appends. `GrammarRoot` then serializes category names, tokens, and production kinds with unescaped
separators while omitting production priority and scope ownership.

`Name::to_display_string()` is not structural identity: a string component `"1"` and numeric
component `1` both render as `1`, although `Name::Ord` and `Name::Eq` distinguish them. The second
category is therefore refused as a duplicate of the first, and the same collision aliases two
distinct token-table entries.

The grammar projection also has concrete equal-root collisions. One production whose kind renders
as `first,second` produces the same bracket text as two productions `first` and `second`. Two
otherwise identical productions with different priorities also share a root, although priority is
the third component of parser resolution. A scoped and an unscoped registration likewise share a
root even though scope exit treats them differently.

These are false grammar identities beneath FL-INV-01 and the future content-addressed
`GrammarEpoch` contract in `franken_lean-9km`.

## Acceptance

- Key categories by structural `Name`, so equal display projections do not collapse distinct
  category identities.
- Key parser token tables and registration requests by structural `Name`, matching the pin's table
  type and direct identifier/node lookup. Convert atom spellings to simple names only at the lexer
  boundary.
- Offer newer productions first under one token, matching the pin's `TokenMap.insert`.
- Return structural category and production-kind inventories rather than lossy display strings.
- Replace delimiter-dependent root text with a versioned, length-framed projection that embeds the
  established schema-headed canonical `Name` bytes instead of maintaining a private name encoding.
- Bind category behavior, leading/trailing position, structural token name and production kind,
  production priority, registration order, and scope ownership.
- Preserve executable historical views and deterministic iteration.
- Add conventional regressions for structural category/token coexistence, delimiter collision
  separation, priority separation, scope-ownership separation, equal-state stability, and
  historical replay.
- Run focused and all-target `fln-parse` tests, workspace check/clippy, the authoritative main-tree
  workspace test under flock, and a same-path UBS delta.

## Claim boundary

This slice establishes an injective projection for the active parser-table fields it encodes. It
reuses the established `fln-hash` canonical `Name` codec but does not yet content-hash the complete
grammar projection, identify closure callback code/captured state or registered hooks, bind the
current scope-stack depth that governs future mutations, implement memoization, emit typed parser
effects (including `AddsToken`), identify token-parser descriptors, cover options/imported grammar
producers, or close `franken_lean-9km`. Those remain explicit successor work.

No deliberate crash path or new mutation harness is in scope.
close_reason: Structural parser-table identity and framed grammar-root projection implemented and fully validated

title: scripts/evidence.py: the path-object classifier's seven classifications have zero committed coverage
description:
verification_path_object_classification in scripts/evidence.py is committed production code that
returns SEVEN classifications over ELEVEN return sites, and nothing in the committed tree exercises
any of them. This bead exists so that fact survives fln-selftest-symlink-blocks-bundle-4yhd, which
is named after a referent that is empty and will therefore look discardable.

THE REPAIR LANDS IN scripts/, WHICH IS cc_2's DOMAIN. This bead is filed and owned by cc_1 because
cc_1 measured it and because leaving it unfiled loses it entirely; the implementation surface is
scripts/evidence.py and whoever picks this up routes the implementation to cc_2. Stated in the body
rather than left implicit, because a bead whose owner cannot perform its own repair, with nothing
recording why, is exactly the unwatched join this repository keeps rediscovering.

MEASURED by cc_1 at a0c9b1c8, against the COMMITTED blob (git show HEAD:scripts/evidence.py, md5
4f2d151593dbb65e30cd9733a520f798, 25108 lines) and never the working-tree copy, which is an orphan
from a dead pane. Class bounded_model, one host.

THE POPULATION. verification_path_object_classification is defined at scripts/evidence.py:4904 in
that blob. Its return set, derived by two independent extractors that were required to agree:

  directory  ignored  missing  special  symlink  tracked_file  untracked      = 7 classifications
                                                                              = 11 return sites

"symlink" is reachable by two independent branches: an lstat S_ISLNK on any path component, and a
tracked git mode of 120000. "special" is reachable by three.

THE COVERAGE. Zero. git grep verification_path_object_classification over the committed tree
returns exactly two lines -- the definition at 4904 and its single caller at 5067. No test in
scripts/, crates/ or tools/ exercises the function, and no expectation table binds any fixture to
any of the seven outcomes.

WHY THIS IS NOT 4yhd. 4yhd records that the evidence self-test plants a symlink the bundle
publisher forbids, which blocks publication. Its symlink fixture has never been committed in any
commit -- it exists only in cod_2's uncommitted 543-line orphan -- so if that orphan is never
adopted 4yhd evaporates with nothing in HEAD to repair. THIS bead does not evaporate: the
seven-classification function is committed, its coverage is zero today, and that is true whatever
happens to the orphan. The two beads share a cause and have different lifetimes.

WHAT THE ORPHAN ALREADY CONTAINS, recorded so the work is not duplicated. cod_2's uncommitted diff
builds the artifact-classification fixture root and an expectation table binding tracked.log to
tracked_file, untracked.log to untracked, ignored.log to ignored, missing-tracked.log to missing,
directory to directory and symlink.log to symlink -- SIX of the seven. It does not cover "special",
which is the classification with the most return branches. So the orphan is most of this repair,
and adopting it would discharge six sevenths of this bead rather than none of it.

HONEST TYPING OF THE UNCOVERED CASE. "special" is reachable in principle by a fixture: a
non-directory component in the middle of a path, or a final object that is neither a directory nor
a regular file, such as a fifo. Its third branch requires a tracked git mode outside
100644/100755/120000, i.e. a gitlink, and this repository has ZERO -- no .gitmodules and no
mode-160000 entries in git ls-files -s. This is a hole in a test, NOT a bug in production, and it
must not be written up as the latter.

NOT CLAIMED. That any classification is computed incorrectly; the function was read, not tested,
and this bead asserts absence of coverage rather than presence of a defect. That the two sibling
classifiers (verification_artifact_classification, verification_path_lexical_classification) are
uncovered to the same degree -- they were derived for the partition check below but their coverage
was not measured. And a hypothesis that WAS killed: the three classifiers produce 21 distinct
classifications against 19 declared across VERIFICATION_LEGACY_CLASSIFICATIONS and durable_classes,
and the two extras (target_path, unknown_receipt) are NOT a silent gap -- each is refused by name
and the fall-through refuses any non-durable class lacking an exact migration allowance. That
declared set is the migration-ELIGIBLE set, not the possible set. Nothing declared is unproducible.
acceptance_criteria:
The binding is to CARDINALITY PER CLASSIFICATION, not to the existence of a fixture, and it must
fail in BOTH directions. bkw6's rule is to bind a claim to the cardinality of what it asserts when
the far end is empty; k60n's sharpening is that a single aggregate count is a BUDGET that a repair
refills, so bind per member. Here the members are the classifications.

1. A test derives the classification set of verification_path_object_classification from its own
   source at test time -- never a transcribed list -- and asserts that the self-test's expectation
   table covers exactly that set. It fails when a classification gains a return site with no
   expectation row, AND when an expectation row names a classification the function can no longer
   return. One-way membership is refused: a reverse-membership wall reddens a correct repair, and a
   forward-only check lets a deleted classification keep a stale row.

2. The derivation is reconciled against a cheap independent signal and the two must agree, because
   a derived count is exactly as trustworthy as its extractor. This is not ceremony: the extractor
   written while filing this bead was wrong TWICE -- it first missed "missing" because that value
   sits in a ternary else-arm rather than a bare return, then over-collected root, tracked_modes,
   ignored_paths and reachable_commits because it descended into call nodes and read keyword
   argument names as classifications. Both were caught only by a second extractor disagreeing.

3. Anti-vacuity, and it must be reachable from a test rather than only in a healthy tree. A scan
   that returns an empty classification set, or that cannot locate the function, FAILS as a broken
   scan rather than passing as a clean one. Inject the inputs to exercise this floor; with the real
   function present a floor like "at least one classification" can never fire and is decorative.

4. Coverage includes "special", the one classification the existing uncommitted work does not
   reach. A fixture that exercises at least one of its three branches is required -- a non-directory
   mid-path component or a final object that is neither directory nor regular file. The gitlink
   branch may be left uncovered and DECLARED as such, since this repository has no gitlinks; a
   declared remainder is acceptable here and an undeclared one is not.

5. A planted mutant that adds a return site for a new classification without an expectation row is
   killed by a NAMED test failing for the stated reason -- not by a generic nonzero exit and not by
   a compile error. Independently, a mutant that deletes one expectation row is killed at a
   DIFFERENT assertion than the mutant in 3, so the checks are shown not to ride on one another.

6. The bundle-publication contradiction recorded on 4yhd is not reintroduced. If the fixture must
   create a symlink to exercise the symlink classification, the location it writes to and the region
   the publisher tolerates are derived and named at ONE site, so a future scenario adding a
   forbidden artifact kind fails loudly instead of silently disabling publication for every gate run.
   Satisfying this bead must not make 4yhd's defect permanent.

NOT SUFFICIENT FOR CLOSURE: a test that merely calls the function once; an expectation table that
is hand-listed against a hand-listed classification set, since both sides then reconcile by

comments.text:
## The obvious implementation of criterion 1 under-derives by one — `missing` is returned only from a conditional expression, and a literal-only walk cannot see it

Measured at `62892e878b04b0d17d9dac90d032bb9deec151ca`, cc_1.

Criterion 1 requires a test that "derives the classification set of
`verification_path_object_classification` from its own source at test time — never a transcribed
list". Criterion 2 requires that derivation to be "reconciled against a cheap independent signal,
because a derived count is exactly as trustworthy as its extractor."

**This is criterion 2's reconciliation, run now rather than after the test is written — because the
obvious extractor is wrong and the test would have shipped around it.**

### The trap

`scripts/evidence.py:6139`, inside the function's own body:

```python
return "ignored" if path in ignored_paths else "missing"
```

`missing` is returned **from nowhere else**. Every other classification appears at least once as a
bare `return "…"`. So an extractor that reads `ast.Return.value` and keeps it only when it is an
`ast.Constant` — which is the natural first implementation, and is what I wrote first — finds the
returns fine and silently drops one classification:

| extractor | result |
|---|---|
| naive: `Return.value` kept only if `ast.Constant` | **6** — `directory ignored special symlink tracked_file untracked` |
| **what it drops** | **`missing`** |

An expectation table built against that derivation would be **complete in both directions against a
set with a hole in it**, and criterion 1's bidirectional check would pass. The classification with no
coverage would be the one the derivation could not see — which is this bead's own subject, arriving
inside this bead's own repair.

### The reconciliation, both directions agreeing

Two independent extractors, deliberately not sharing a code path:

- **A — AST**: every `ast.Constant` string reachable anywhere under a `Return` subtree, so a
  conditional, a parenthesised expression or a nested call is walked rather than pattern-matched.
  It refuses outright if any return yields no string constant, rather than skipping it — a filter
  that `continue`s is a sampler.
- **B — textual**: over the function's own line span only, matching `return "…"` **and** the
  `… if … else "…"` form as a separate pattern.

```
extractor A : 7 -> directory ignored missing special symlink tracked_file untracked
extractor B : 7 -> directory ignored missing special symlink tracked_file untracked
return sites: AST 10, textual 10
RECONCILED: both extractors agree on 7 classifications over 10 return sites
```

Both the **set** and the **site count** agree, and an empty derivation is refused as a broken scan
rather than reported as a classifier with no outputs.

### What this confirms and what it corrects

**Confirms** comment 2051 exactly: **seven** classifications over **ten** value-carrying return sites,
now at HEAD with the function at lines 6124–6158. The bead body's original "eleven return sites" is
still wrong and 2051's correction to ten still stands, independently re-derived here.

**Corrects nothing in the bead — it corrects the repair I was about to write.** That is the useful
direction: this is the fourth extractor error in this bead's lifetime and the first one caught
*before* it landed rather than after.

### Prescription for criterion 1, so the next author does not re-derive the trap

Walk **all string constants under each `Return` subtree**, never `Return.value` alone. Reconcile
against a textual scan that matches the conditional form explicitly. Refuse a return that yields no
string constant, and refuse an empty derivation. `missing` is the member that tells you whether your
extractor works — if your derivation reports six, it is broken, and it will look exactly like a
classifier with six outputs.

### What this does not earn

**This implements neither criterion.** No test is committed, no expectation table exists, and
coverage is still **zero** — comment 2051's central finding is untouched. This is the derivation and
its reconciliation, which criterion 2 demands and which criterion 1 depends on, landed as a
measurement so the trap is recorded whether or not I am the one who writes the fixtures.

The seven fixtures remain seven-from-nothing: the 543-line orphan that once held six of them is
gone, as 2051 measured.

One host, one commit, class `bounded_model`. The function has already moved once (`:4904` → `:6124`)
and this derivation is keyed to the construct rather than the line, so it survives the next move —
but the *count* does not: a new return site changes it, which is precisely what criterion 1 exists
to catch.

comments.text:
## All seven classifications are REACHABLE by real fixtures — and the run exposes a question criterion 1 does not settle: 7 classifications over 10 return sites

Measured at `d0a602c788b3b1c2c49f43f0e2e4dea68b2aeff5`, cc_1. Follows comment 2088, which derived the
set and found the extractor trap. This is the **precondition** for the expectation table: a
classification no fixture can produce cannot be covered by a real one, and if any member were
unreachable the repair would change shape rather than merely get longer.

### Method

`scripts/evidence.py` is **not edited**. The function is imported and driven against **real
filesystem objects** in a scratch tree — a real symlink, a real directory, a real FIFO, a real
regular file. No mocks: a mocked `lstat` would prove the harness works and nothing about the
classifier.

### Result — every derived classification is reachable, and the two sets are equal

| fixture | → |
|---|---|
| absent, not ignored | `missing` |
| absent, ignored | `ignored` |
| real symlink on disk | `symlink` |
| tracked as `120000` | `symlink` |
| directory | `directory` |
| tracked `100644` | `tracked_file` |
| FIFO — not a regular file | `special` |
| non-directory intermediate component (`notadir.txt/child`) | `special` |
| tracked with mode `160000` | `special` |
| present, untracked, ignored | `ignored` |
| present, untracked, not ignored | `untracked` |

```
derived classifications : 7 -> directory ignored missing special symlink tracked_file untracked
reached by a fixture    : 7 -> directory ignored missing special symlink tracked_file untracked
derived but UNREACHED   : none
reached but UNDERIVED   : none
```

All eleven cases classified as predicted. **The expectation table is buildable**, and these eleven
are its fixtures — measured rather than proposed.

### The question this exposes, which the criterion does not settle

Criterion 1 binds **per classification**. There are **7 classifications over 10 value-carrying return
sites**, so the two cardinalities differ and the criterion picks the smaller one.

Three classifications are multiply-sited:

- `special` — **three** distinct routes: a non-regular final object, a non-directory intermediate
  component, and a tracked mode outside the three recognised ones;
- `symlink` — **two**: an on-disk symlink, and a `120000` tracked mode;
- `ignored` — **two**: absent-and-ignored (the conditional expression from comment 2088), and
  present-untracked-and-ignored.

A table with exactly seven rows satisfies criterion 1 in both directions **while leaving three
return sites covered only by whichever fixture happens to reach them first**. Delete the
non-directory-intermediate branch and a seven-row table stays green, because `special` is still
produced by the FIFO.

That is `k60n`'s lesson one level down, and it is a genuine choice rather than a defect: `k60n`
established that binding to a **population** total is a budget its own repairs refill, and that the
fix is to bind **per member** — but *which* member is the design decision, and here classification
and return site are different members. Eleven fixtures covering all ten sites are already measured
above, so binding per site costs nothing extra in fixtures; it costs a derivation keyed to sites
rather than to values.

**I am not changing the criterion.** It is this bead's own acceptance text, written deliberately,
and the seven-row reading is defensible: the classifier's *contract* is its output vocabulary, not
its branch structure. Recorded so whoever implements criterion 1 chooses knowingly rather than
discovering it afterwards.

### What this does not earn

**Still implements neither criterion.** No test is committed and no expectation table exists;
coverage remains **zero**, which is comment 2051's finding and is untouched. This establishes the
fixtures are constructible and names them.

The eleven cases are sufficient to reach all seven classifications; they are **not** proven minimal,
and I did not check whether some case is redundant. `mkfifo` is POSIX-specific, so the `special`
fixture via a FIFO would need a different object on a platform without one — the other two `special`
routes are portable, so the classification stays reachable either way. One host, one commit, class
`bounded_model`.

title: Process: guard private-index post-commit worktree synchronization
description:
Problem: private-index commits can correctly advance HEAD while leaving the shared worktree copy of the committed file stale. The stale worktree then produces a false validator red for later panes. The required protocol is narrow: after a private-index commit, for each committed file, first prove the worktree copy has zero lines absent from HEAD; only then sync that file from verified HEAD content in the same operation. Never use an unchecked git checkout; preserve any foreign-only worktree lines.

Observed evidence (2026-08-04): (1) the 8g7q/t0g7 private-index closes left DRAFT manifest rows in the worktree after committed finals; the validator refused that stale copy until it was restored from HEAD. (2) a stale worktree manifest deleted the committed fln-wwvr coverage row; the resulting false red blocked 149 validation. (3) the 149 sparse-row private-index landing advanced HEAD while the worktree manifest remained behind HEAD, repeating the same diagnostic hazard.

Acceptance: document and mechanically test a post-private-index sync helper/protocol that computes an exact line-set containment check against HEAD for every target, refuses on foreign-only lines, and only then writes the verified HEAD blob to that one worktree path. Test the three listed cases (draft supersession, missing committed coverage row, and added committed sparse row), including a foreign-line refusal. The implementation must not delete files, must not overwrite foreign WIP, and must route its verified result.

Filing discipline: add a sparse non-terminal verification coverage row and regenerate every tracker projection required by the create/export transaction. This filing makes no claim that the synchronization mechanism has been implemented.

For each deterministic UNSAT fixture, record canonical input identity, generation seed, solver determinism policy/version, and proof schema versions. Tests must solve and emit, compare exact bytes against the frozen fixture, independently read and re-emit with byte identity, and reject unknown outer and inner versions rather than parsing leniently. A deliberate byte-drift mutant must prove the golden comparator fails. The test suite must have no UPDATE_GOLDENS or self-regeneration path: format changes fail until a separately reviewed fixture change is committed. D1 applies: no new crates; generation and comparison remain first-party and deterministic.
close_reason: Delivered byte-exact, provenance-bound Verdict certificate goldens with typed unknown-version and drift refusal; package tests, check, strict clippy, fmt, and UBS pass.

title: W8: Publish compiled rewrite indexes — Ledger CAS + olean-next attachment integration
description:
Integrate W7's deterministic compiled rewrite-index format with the W8 Ledger and Grimoire artifact planes. Publish each per-library discrimination automaton as a typed demand-node product and olean-next attachment keyed by the exact simp-set semantic hash, implementation/schema version, epoch, mode, and CGSE policy; hydrate it through local/remote CAS validation; project it into daemon sessions without rebuilding; and invalidate or reject it structurally whenever any key input changes.

This bead resolves the stage boundary cleanly: W7 implements and proves the faithful simp driver plus deterministic index builder/reader equivalence; W8 owns transactional publication, retention, hydration, invalidation, quarantine, and cache provenance. No W7 component may claim a Ledger-published artifact before this integration exists.

Acceptance: a mathlib slice builds indexes once, publishes atomically, reloads from a fresh process and from a validated remote-cache fixture, and yields candidate sets and simp results identical to a fresh in-memory index; unchanged simp sets reuse byte-identical artifacts; changed rules/options/epoch/schema cannot load stale artifacts; promotion crashes leave no half-published attachment.

Verification: unit schema/key tests, builder-vs-loaded representation equivalence, stale-key and poisoned-cache mutations, kill-at-every-promotion-step drills, and shared no-mock E2E scripts for build -> publish -> hydrate -> simplify with complete CAS keys, manifests, hashes, receipts, expected/final states, and first-divergence logs.

## Acceptance Criteria

All bead-specific requirements, acceptance conditions, tests, invariants, compatibility surfaces, evidence levels, performance gates, negative/recovery cases, and user-visible behaviors stated above remain mandatory. In addition, the MANDATORY VERIFICATION DEFINITION OF DONE in Notes must be satisfied with named unit/property/mutation suites, at least one shared real-path no-mock E2E scenario plus failure/recovery coverage, detailed human and schema-versioned NDJSON artifacts, and reproducible close evidence. No listed feature or claim may be silently narrowed, deferred, mocked, or declared complete through an unclassified divergence.

Publication is atomic and crash-recoverable; retention, quarantine, local/remote hydration, provenance, and validation belong to W8. A fresh process and production daemon can load a valid artifact without rebuilding and obtain candidate sets, ordering, proof terms, and simp results identical to W7 in-memory construction. Unchanged inputs reuse byte-identical artifacts; any rule, attribute, option, epoch, schema, mode, policy, checksum, receipt, or root change structurally prevents stale loading. Remote poison becomes a miss plus security evidence, never acceptance; promotion crashes leave no visible half attachment. Unit/property/model/mutation tests cover key/schema encoding, builder-loaded equivalence, deterministic serialization, retention, quarantine, stale dimensions, poison/truncation, duplicate publication, budgets, and recovery; named omitted-key, stale-hit, unvalidated-remote, half-promotion, and reordered-candidate mutants are killed. title: W6: Unifier/defeq — the approximation ladder, implemented against golden traces
description:
Implement unification + defeq against golden traces (§10.2): transparency-aware whnf/isDefEq mirroring the Reference approximation ladder — syntactic fast paths, first-order approximation, Miller patterns, delayed assignments, postponement, unfolding by reducibility and definitional height, structure-eta awareness. Mathlib DEPENDS on the precise power of the unifier (proofs elaborate because a particular approximation fires); this is where bug-for-bug earns its keep and where Critical risk R2 lives.

Method (the R2 mitigation): implemented AGAINST the instrumented-oracle golden decision traces (G0-9 -> §18.3) — which approximation fired, what postponed, what unfolded, in what order — at Corpus scale, with trace-replay rigs running continuously. Every T3 divergence is triaged with the strong prior that it is a fidelity defect; a persistent divergence class becomes a faithful-mode blocker and a published erratum with quantified Corpus blast radius, never a quiet Behavior Note (the epoch ships R3, not R4, until closed). Failures are recorded as typed constraint cells (HasType, IsDefEq, SynthesizeInstance, Coerce, ResolveName, ElaboratePattern, ProveTermination) with origins, dependencies, attempts, and outcomes — the substrate Palimpsest blame slices are computed from.

Acceptance: trace-replay agreement on the pilot corpus, expanding toward Corpus scale with the divergence ledger empty or fully classified; the G0-7 tail suite green through the production engine; constraint-cell recording complete per the perturbation validator. Tests: golden-trace replay rigs per approximation stage; postponement-order fixtures; defeq differentials vs the oracle on C0-C2.

title: Tribunal epoch lab: append-only revision hash chain with failure-atomic publication (epoch_lab_hash_chain)
description:
First slice carved out of the fln-euo epic by cc_2 on 2026-07-25. The epic is the whole Tribunal bootstrap; this is the load-bearing foundation under it, because every other vocabulary in that epic binds to an epoch revision. Splitting before building, the way lst4 was split out of bc7.

THE GAP, which is the familiar shape. tribunal/epochs/v4.32.0/MANIFEST.txt says in its own header "Immutable once published: revisions are reviewed, hashed regenerations". There is no revision id in the file, no parent link, no chain root, and nothing anywhere that would notice if a published manifest were edited. The immutability is asserted in a comment and enforced by nothing - a claimed invariant with no mechanism, which is exactly the class of thing this session has been converting into guarded rules.

SCOPE OF THIS SLICE:
1. A revision record format: an append-only chain where each revision names its parent's root, the content hash of the manifest it publishes, and its own recomputable root. Domain-separated hashing through fln-hash, matching the ownership-projection precedent.
2. A total verifier: parse is total and typed, every root is recomputed rather than trusted, parent linkage is checked, and the head must bind the manifest actually on disk.
3. Failure-atomic publication: a candidate is written, verified, and atomically renamed. Interruption or invalidity leaves the PRIOR revision authoritative, and a leftover candidate is typed inconclusive rather than consumed - the same discipline cod_2 used for the ownership projection publisher.
4. Genesis revision published for the real v4.32.0 lab, binding the MANIFEST.txt that exists today.

MUTATIONS THAT MUST FAIL, named by the epic and each needing a discriminating test: mutable revision (edit a published revision or the manifest it binds), partial epoch publication (interrupted write, leftover candidate, truncated chain), and root mismatch (a recorded root that does not equal the recomputed one). Each must fail for its intended reason, not merely fail.

WHERE IT LIVES, and why. A nested-workspace crate under tribunal/, following the precedent of tools/structure-guard/kernel-ownership-publisher: its own [workspace] table so it does not add a tooling edge to the product workspace or force unrelated agents to rewrite the root Cargo.lock. The product workspace is members = crates/* plus tools/*, so tribunal/ is not a member, and structure-guard discovers crates only under crates/ and tools/, so this adds no governance rows.

NOT IN THIS SLICE, so the epic is not read as narrowed: C0-C9 schemas, the C1 official-test inventory, oracle authority and precedence, typed normalizers and comparators, the Parity Ledger schema, G0SpikeDecisionV1, the poison boundary and release reachability scan, and the Reference-vs-Reference no-mock E2E. All remain on fln-euo.

CONSEQUENCE TO FILE SEPARATELY: because the crate is a nested workspace it does not run under the workspace cargo test, so the suite needs lane registration - and scripts/ is cod_3's. That follow-up is its own bead rather than a reach across.
close_reason: Landed. The epoch lab's MANIFEST.txt claimed 'Immutable once published' with no revision id, no parent link, no root, and nothing that would notice an edit - a claimed invariant with no mechanism, sitting under every other vocabulary in the fln-euo epic. Now an append-only chain where each revision names its parent's root and its content digest, roots are recomputed on read and never trusted, and appending is the only mutation. Publication is failure-atomic in the order that matters: refuse if a candidate remains, verify the existing chain before extending, re-parse and verify WHAT LANDED rather than what was intended, then atomic rename and dirsync - a crash leaves the prior chain or the prior chain plus a refused candidate, never a half-written authoritative file. All three mutations the epic names are killed by tests pinning their specific ChainError variant: mutable revision (plus the harder variant where an attacker rewrites history AND recomputes roots honestly - defeated by parent linkage), partial epoch publication (planted candidate is deliberately plausible), and root mismatch (checked at every position). Parsing is total over eight hostile inputs. Genesis published for the real v4.32.0 lab, head root 7e554b20907d81a2, and proved on the real lab: flipping one byte of a published executable sha256 makes verify fail with the exact digests; MANIFEST.txt restored byte-identical. Nested-workspace crate under tribunal/ per the kernel-ownership-publisher precedent, so no product-workspace edge, no governance rows, root Cargo.lock untouched. Gates: 10/10 tests, clippy -D warnings clean, rustfmt clean, fln-kernel unaffected. Lane registration filed as fln-giap. Not in this slice and still on the epic: C0-C9 schemas, C1 inventory, oracle authority, normalizers, Parity Ledger schema, G0SpikeDecisionV1, poison boundary, release reachability, Reference-vs-Reference E2E.

title: structure-guard D18: the mode-closure facts are computed and never emitted, so a vacuous scan is indistinguishable from a clean one in the artifact
description:
structure-guard computes D18 mode-closure facts, stores them on RunOutcome, lets tests
read them, and NEVER EMITS THEM. The robot run_end object carries no D18 key of any kind.
A reader of a guard run therefore sees verdict=pass with no findings and has no way to
learn that the D18 check traversed nothing at all.

MEASURED at HEAD 53653a59 by cc_3, 2026-07-26, from a real guard run against this
workspace, not from reading the source. The complete key set of the emitted run_end is:

  authority, authority_count_rule, authority_count_rule_holds, contract_handoff_root,
  duration_ms, event, exit_code, findings, governed_root_after, governed_root_before,
  governed_root_unchanged, schema, traversal, verdict

ModeClosureFacts carries frontier_surfaces, product_roots, closures_scanned,
closure_nodes, nodes and edges. None of the six appears above. grep for mode_closure in
tools/structure-guard/src/main.rs returns nothing; the only reference outside the module
is the pub mod line in lib.rs.

WHY IT MATTERS RATHER THAN BEING A MISSING NICETY. The live D18 scan is VACUOUS: no crate
declares a mode-bound product root, crates/ has no binary targets, so no closure is ever
submitted and ModeClosureFacts::is_vacuous() is true on every run. The module was written
carefully and says so in its own doc - the counts exist precisely so that "the D18 check
ran" can never be read as "a product closure was traversed". That disclosure is correct
and it is unreachable. It lives in a struct that only the test binary observes, while the
artifact everyone else reads says pass.

So the claim is made in one place and the evidence for its scope is produced in another,
with nothing joining them. That is the AGENTS.md item 7 shape applied to an emitted
artifact rather than to prose, and it is the same family as the empty-referent bead
fln-bench-apparatus-empty-referent-bkw6: a green signal whose scope qualifier exists but
is not where the signal is read.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT MEAN, stated first because the title can be misread and the misreading
is expensive:

  * D18 IS ENFORCED AND THE CHECK IS REGISTERED. The chain resolves end to end and was
    verified, not assumed: .github/workflows/ci.yml runs scripts/check.sh; check.sh:1565
    runs the structure-guard binary; checks::run calls mode_closure::audit_with_facts;
    that calls fln_core::mode::scan_mode_closure; and ci/WORKSPACE_GRAPH.txt:94
    acknowledges the structure-guard to fln-core edge. Nobody should read this bead as
    "D18 is unenforced" or as "the check does not run". It runs, on every check.sh.
  * THE SCANNER IS CORRECT AS OF 53653a59. A separate defect - the derivation submitting
    the whole workspace as its closure instead of the reachable subset - was found and
    FIXED in that commit, with a production negative control proving a planted frontier
    contamination makes the registered guard run go red and repair recover. This bead is
    not that defect and does not reopen it.
  * NOTHING IS WRONG WITH ModeClosureFacts. It is well designed. The problem is only that
    its readers are tests and its non-readers are everyone consuming the artifact.
  * NO FINDING IS BEING SUPPRESSED. When D18 refuses, the finding IS emitted through the
    normal findings channel with the core's stable FLN-D18-nnn code. What is invisible is
    the SCOPE of a pass, not the content of a failure.

THE REPAIR IS ADDITIVE and was deliberately not performed by the finder, because it
versions a surface that is not his. Carrying frontier_surfaces, product_roots,
closures_scanned and closure_nodes into run_end makes the vacuity legible at the point the
verdict is read. That touches the structure-guard/3 robot schema, which is a versioned
conformance surface and cod_2's authority. A schema bump may or may not be required for an
additive key; that judgement belongs to its owner. An alternative that avoids the schema
entirely is a separate typed line, but a second artifact reintroduces exactly the join
problem this bead is about, so the additive key is the recommended shape.

ACCEPTANCE. A reader of a single structure-guard run can tell, from the artifact alone,
whether the D18 check traversed a product closure or nothing at all, without reading the
source and without running the test binary. A run whose D18 scan is vacuous must be
distinguishable from one that traversed a closure and found it clean.

ANCHOR NOTE, per franken_lean-history-rewrite-evidence-anchor-reachability-vdi4: every
hash in this bead was recorded against HEAD 53653a59 and re-measured there. At that head
166 of 417 commit anchors cited across the governed artifacts are unreachable from main
after the 2026-07-25 filter-branch, so anchors older than the rewrite in OTHER beads may
not resolve; these do.
close_reason: The D18 mode-closure scope now reaches the terminal run_end record and the human line; the join is bidirectional through evidence.py's exact key set, with eight planted mutants confirmed dead. Landed at 72c4832f.

comments.author: cc_3
comments.text:
CLOSED BY cc_3 AT 72c4832f, 2026-07-26. The finding was re-measured at HEAD 8aae792a on a fresh context before any repair, not inherited: the emitted run_end key set was exactly the fourteen keys this bead lists, with none of ModeClosureFacts' six counts. The repair was then measured against a real guard run at bd13cd96.

WHAT THE ARTIFACT SAYS NOW. The terminal run_end record carries

  "mode_closure":{"scan_class":"vacuous","frontier_surfaces":1,"product_roots":0,"closures_scanned":0,"closure_nodes":0,"nodes":33,"edges":28}

and the human render carries the same facts on its own line, because the human reader had the identical problem. The one frontier surface is fln-unsafe-jit's iron feature. Acceptance is met: a reader of one run can now tell from the artifact alone whether the D18 check traversed a product closure or nothing at all, without reading the source and without running the test binary.

THE PART WORTH REVIEWING IS NOT THE EMISSION. Printing seven more numbers would have satisfied the letter of this bead and left the same defect one level up, because nothing would fail when the emission stopped. What makes it load-bearing is that evidence.py's require_guard_keys compares an EXACT key set: a guard that drops the object fails validate_guard, and a validator that drops the requirement fails against a guard that still emits it. Neither half can go quiet alone.

Presence is the cheap half. validate_guard_mode_closure adds the laws that refuse an object which is present but not derived: scan_class must agree with its own closures_scanned; a mode is scanned only when a product declares a root for it; a scanned closure holds at least its own root and an unscanned one submits nothing; and on a PASSING run the node count equals the crate count. Eight planted mutants, each dying by its intended law, with the clean stream as negative control.

THE PASS-ONLY SCOPING IS DELIBERATE. A failing run may be failing BECAUSE the reviewed graph and the discovered workspace disagree (FLN-STRUCT-005/-006), so demanding the node and crate counts match on a fail would refuse the evidence stream of the very violation the guard exists to report.

SCHEMA structure-guard/3 -> /4. An exact-key-set contract is broken by an added key exactly as by a removed one, so a version that stayed put while its key set moved would claim to describe a shape it no longer describes. Precedent is 65dc97cd, which bumped /2 -> /3 for additive keys. The old-schema mutant now plants /3 rather than /2 - the immediately preceding version - so it proves the version is rejected on its own account, not because its shape happens to be wrong.

SURFACE-OWNERSHIP DISCLOSURE, since this bead itself recorded the repair as cod_2's to make. The orchestrator assigned the structure-guard surface to cc_3 on restart, so cc_3 made the schema call rather than leaving the finding to rot. Nothing else in ci/ was touched: exactly one line of ci/VERIFICATION_MANIFEST.jsonl moved, this bead's own row, under the AGENTS.md one-row exception, and the rewrite asserted byte-identity of every line before and after it.

A LATENT MISCOUNT WAS REPAIRED IN THE FIELD BEING PUBLISHED, and it is the one thing here I would not have found by reading the bead. frontier_surfaces was incremented from the PRE-override classification, so a crate declaring both a frontier feature and a mode-bound product root would have been published as a frontier surface while being SUBMITTED to the core as ModeBound - a disclosed number describing a request the core never received. It is now counted from the final requirement, with a test. No behavioural change today because product_roots is 0 everywhere. Publishing a field I already knew could lie was not an option.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT EARN. The live D18 scan is STILL VACUOUS and nothing here makes it traverse a product closure - there are no products. This bead bought legibility of the vacuity at the point the verdict is read, and nothing about D18 coverage. The parent franken_lean-r2st stays open for the product, sidecar, byte-identity and 1/8/32 halves.

WHY THE LIVE TEST PINS LAWS RATHER THAN NUMBERS. Pinning scan_class vacuous would turn red on whoever lands the first product binary, for doing exactly the right thing. The asserted laws hold in both scopes. The traversed rendering therefore exists only in report::tests, which is what stops the disclosure being a hardcoded constant that a permanently vacuous workspace could never falsify.

GATES at bd13cd96 plus the patch: fmt clean, clippy --all-targets --no-deps -D warnings clean, shellcheck clean on both edited lanes, ubs exit 0 over all eight changed files, cargo test -p structure-guard green in the real tree apart from real_verification_manifest_covers_the_live_tracker, which was failing on another pane's then-uncommitted bead and passes now that 3208f099 landed its coverage row.

title: FL-INV-01: the kernel thread-matrix does not run where the Reference pin is absent
description:
Filed by cc_2 on 2026-07-25 from a concurrency and determinism audit of fln-kernel and fln-env. The code is CORRECT; what is wrong is where its guard runs. Nobody should "fix" anything here -- the work is a decision between widening the guard and narrowing the claim.

THE FACT. crates/fln-conformance/tests/kernel_replay.rs:2961-2967, prelude_replays_through_the_kernel, returns early when the pinned Reference stdlib is absent, printing "SKIP kernel_replay: pinned Reference stdlib not found (set FLN_REFERENCE_LIB or install the pin); typed limitation, not a pass". That test contains the only live FL-INV-01 assertion for the kernel: the same prepared units checked at 1, 8 and 32 workers over a shared racing cursor, with a per-run stream_digest and a byte-identity assertion that emits the first divergence as evidence BEFORE it panics. It is well built. It is also conditional on a property of the host.

AGENTS.md records that RCH remote workers do not have the pin. So on every machine without it the kernel's schedule-independence assertion does not execute at all, and the run is honest about that -- the skip is typed, it is not a silent pass, and I want to be clear that the harness is not lying.

THE GAP IS BETWEEN THE CLAIM CLASS AND THE EVIDENCE CLASS. B4 states, as an invariant, that determinism is "tested at {1, 8, 32} threads on every commit". The evidence is a test that runs on every commit ONLY where a toolchain happens to be installed. An invariant may not rest on conditional evidence (D7: a weaker class may never enforce a stronger one).

THE GENERAL SHAPE, AND IT IS WORTH NAMING BECAUSE IT IS THE FOURTH INSTANCE THIS SESSION.

  ENFORCEMENT SCOPE AND CLAIM SCOPE DIVERGE SILENTLY.

AGENTS.md already carries cc_3's law that evidence must be produced where the claim is made. This is the sharper form of the same thing, and it names a failure the existing law does not catch: the evidence IS produced where the claim is made, and it covers less than the claim says. Nothing goes red, because everything that runs, passes. What is missing never announces itself.

The four instances, all found on 2026-07-25, all in correct code:
  1. fln-glml -- the consensus seat's veto was real and reflection.rs published without ever convening, so the guard covered no production path while the claim said it halted publication.
  2. fln-kx3y -- the stack calibration was measured and correct, and nothing re-took it, so the number could drift arbitrarily while every test stayed green.
  3. franken_lean-h40t -- python3 -I closes the shadowing channels and no trusted call site used it, so the mechanism existed and covered nothing.
  4. this bead -- the thread matrix asserts byte-identity and does not run where the pin is absent.

THE TEST THAT DISTINGUISHES THIS CLASS from an ordinary gap: ask not "is there evidence for this claim" but "what is the evidence's scope, and is it the claim's scope". Both questions have the same answer when a guard is missing, and different answers when a guard is narrow. Only the second question finds these.

WHAT THIS BEAD IS NOT. It is not a request to make the pin mandatory, which would be a real cost on every contributor and a doctrine decision rather than an implementation one. It is not a criticism of the skip, which is correctly typed. The decision is: either the invariant's enforcement is made unconditional, or B4's wording is narrowed to what is actually enforced and the conditional half is stated as a Behavior Note. Either is honest. Silence is not.

ACCEPTANCE. Either (a) an FL-INV-01 thread-matrix assertion for the kernel that executes with no Reference pin present -- the kernel's own fixtures need no oracle, so a pin-free matrix over kernel-authored declarations is buildable today -- or (b) B4's claim narrowed in the plan and the claim matrix to the scope that is actually enforced, with the pin-conditional half recorded as a Behavior Note and a claim-matrix Citation that fails if the enforcement narrows further. Whichever is chosen, a test that proves the chosen scope is the enforced scope.
close_reason: Option (a) of the acceptance taken: the guard is widened, so B4's wording needs no change. crates/fln-kernel/tests/thread_matrix_determinism.rs asserts FL-INV-01 for the kernel at 1, 8 and 32 workers over one shared racing cursor, with NO Reference pin, no oracle and no artifact -- the kernel authority is pure, so a matrix over kernel-authored declarations runs wherever cargo test runs. Byte-identity includes exact consumption, because a matrix comparing only verdicts would pass while the work drifted with the schedule and steps_used/max_depth ride on every Verdict into census rows. All three outcome kinds are in the stream, with an anti-vacuity test asserting the fixture set reaches acceptance, rejection and typed exhaustion, so a later fixture change cannot leave the matrices agreeing over one path. The productivity assertion fired for real during development -- eleven of 32 workers got nothing because the first to wake drained the cursor -- and was repaired by seeding each worker one unit and racing the remaining 224, rather than by widening the assertion, which would have been the first-fire capitulation this class of defect keeps producing. Three runs, no flake, 0.43s. NOT CLOSED BY THIS: the corpus-scale gap, which is franken_lean-2ki4 and is a separate decision; this matrix covers kernel-authored declarations and the conformance matrix covers Reference-authored ones, so neither makes the other redundant.

title: W6: Term elaboration — coercions, match compilation, recursion elaborators, exact generated names

title: br comments add: backticks in an inline -m body are command-substituted, silently corrupting an immutable comment
description:
A bead comment body passed through a double-quoted shell argument is subject to shell expansion before br ever sees it. A markdown backtick pair therefore reads as a COMMAND SUBSTITUTION: the shell runs the enclosed word and splices its output into the text. br stores whatever arrives, so the comment is written already damaged, with no error and nothing in the record indicating anything was lost.

## Observed corruption

2026-07-25, cc_3, writing a design finding onto fln-171x. The body contained a field name wrapped in backticks for markdown emphasis. zsh ran it as a command, printed "Command 'at' not found, but can be installed with: sudo apt install at", substituted empty, and br reported "Comment added to fln-171x". The stored text reads:

    canon's Exhausted carries , the byte offset the decode reached

instead of naming the field. A reader of that comment sees a grammatical sentence with the identifier silently removed. The only reason it was caught is that the substitution happened to name a binary that is not installed, which printed a stray diagnostic; had the word been a real command (date, true, ls, id, w) the substitution would have succeeded and injected its OUTPUT into the durable record with no signal whatsoever.

## Why this is worse than a mutable-field defect

Bead comments and .br_history are EXEMPT from the naming scanner in crates/fln-conformance/src/naming.rs precisely because they are immutable: the scanner polices title, description, acceptance_criteria, design and notes because those can be edited, and exempts comments because they cannot. Immutability is the property that makes a comment usable as a coordination record and as close evidence. So corruption there is strictly worse than in a mutable field: it cannot be repaired, only annotated with a correction comment, and nothing scans it for damage.

This matters most in exactly the situation the project already documents: when Agent Mail is down, bead comments ARE the coordination substrate and the bead assignee IS the soft lock. Findings, handoffs, gate results and cross-domain notes all live there.

## Mitigation, verified working

Write the body to a file, then pass it through a single command substitution:

    br comments add ISSUE --author NAME -m "$(cat /path/to/body.txt)"

The file contents are expanded into the argument once; backticks inside the RESULT of an expansion are not re-parsed, so the text arrives intact. Then read back what actually landed rather than trusting the success line, e.g. by loading the issue out of .beads/issues.jsonl and asserting the expected substring is present. The same hazard applies to dollar-parenthesis, bare dollar-variable references, and history expansion.

## Acceptance Criteria

A documented, enforced convention that bead comment and description bodies are never passed as inline double-quoted shell strings when they may contain backticks, dollar signs, or exclamation marks. The mitigation above is recorded where agents will read it before writing a comment (AGENTS.md beads section). Ideally a guard: either a wrapper that takes a file path, or a check that refuses a body containing an unbalanced or suspicious substitution artifact. Any guard must be demonstrated against a planted body containing a backticked identifier and a dollar-parenthesis, and must be shown to accept a legitimate body that contains backticks when passed correctly, so it is not a blanket refusal of markdown. Verification must include reading the stored record back and comparing it byte-for-byte against the intended text, since the whole defect class is that the write path reports success.

## Notes

Filed by cc_3 on 2026-07-25 at the project owner's direction, after the corruption above. Related findings from the same swarm day, recorded because the pattern is what matters rather than any one instance: the ownership-projection staleness race, and the Git 2.54 subreaper issue. All three are cases where tooling everyone relies on was quietly wrong, and all three surfaced only because someone verified an outcome instead of assuming it. The corrected record and the full description of the mechanism are in the last two comments on fln-171x.
close_reason: Guarded comment and description writes now round-trip complete UTF-8 bytes and are joined to cargo test.

comments.author: cc_2
comments.text:
SECOND AFFECTED SURFACE: git commit -m. Same root cause as this bead, DIFFERENT failure mechanism, DIFFERENT mitigation, and strictly worse repairability. Adding it here rather than filing separately because it is one hazard with one home, and the next agent should find both surfaces in one place. (cc_2, observed 2026-07-25.)

WHAT THIS BEAD ALREADY COVERS: a br comments add -m body, damaged by COMMAND SUBSTITUTION, repaired by --file.

THE SECOND SURFACE: a git commit message, damaged by GLOBBING, repaired by -F.

OBSERVED. Commit 1a980f0. I used the pattern this project uses everywhere:

    git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
    ...body...
    EOF
    )"

Note the QUOTED heredoc delimiter, which is exactly the defence one would expect to work — it does stop the heredoc body from being expanded. The commit succeeded. Two backticked tokens were nevertheless deleted from the stored message: a lone question mark, and a match arm containing Err(stop). The stored text now reads

    short-circuits through  at the point of the trip

and

     companions - 1:1, none missing

with the identifiers gone and the sentences still grammatical — the same signature this bead describes.

THE MECHANISM IS NOT THE ONE THIS BEAD NAMES, WHICH IS WHY IT SURVIVED THE KNOWN MITIGATION. The tell was two stderr lines:

    (eval):1: no matches found: ?
    (eval):1: no matches found: Err(stop)

That is zsh's GLOBBER under NOMATCH, not command substitution. A quoted heredoc protects the heredoc body from expansion, but the resulting argument still passes through filename generation, and a token containing ? or [ or * that matches no file is REMOVED rather than left alone. So "use a quoted heredoc" — the natural reading of this bead's mitigation — is not sufficient for the commit surface. That is the substantive reason this is worth recording as a distinct surface rather than a duplicate sighting.

WHY IT IS WORSE HERE THAN FOR BEAD COMMENTS. This bead argues, correctly, that comment corruption is worse than a mutable-field defect because a comment cannot be edited, only annotated. A commit message is worse still: it cannot even be annotated in place. The only in-place repair is git commit --amend or a rebase, which on a six-agent shared tree is a history rewrite that can strand every agent whose work is parented on it. I did not amend for that reason. The correct response to a corrupted commit message is therefore to leave it corrupted and put the authoritative text somewhere mutable — which is what I did, in the franken_lean-1fxz comment, filed via --file and read back intact.

MITIGATION, PROVEN RATHER THAN ASSUMED:

    printf '%s\n' "line one" "line two" ... > /path/msg.txt
    git commit -F /path/msg.txt

I used exactly this for the follow-up commit c242a6b and then verified with

    git log -1 --format=%B | grep -c "<a token I know I wrote>"

which returned 1. So -F lands intact on the same content that -m damaged. Writing the file with the Write tool instead of printf is equally good and avoids the shell entirely.

THE GENERAL RULE, which covers both surfaces and any future one: never let durable text reach zsh as an argument. Write it to a file with a tool, hand the tool the path (--file for br, -F for git), then READ IT BACK and grep for a token you know you wrote. Both br and git report success on corrupted input, so success is not evidence. And treat any "(eval):1: no matches found: X" on stderr as a deletion notice rather than a warning — it is the only signal you get.

WHERE THIS ULTIMATELY BELONGS. A bead is the right place to track the defect, but the place the next agent actually looks is AGENTS.md — every agent reads it at session start, and both surfaces are one line each. I have not edited it: it is a shared/contested file and this round's commits are restricted to crates/fln-kernel. If whoever owns this bead agrees, the two lines are worth adding to the operational-gotchas section, and I am happy to do it under a reservation.

comments.author: cc_3
comments.text:
SECOND OCCURRENCE, cc_3, 2026-07-25. This defect bit me again, in a different br subcommand, and the second instance is worth more than the first because it shows the fix I adopted was too narrow.

FIRST OCCURRENCE: `br comments add -m "...backticks..."` — the body was command-substituted and silently damaged. My fix at the time was to pass comment bodies via --file.

SECOND OCCURRENCE: `br create --description="...backticks..."`. Same mechanism, different subcommand, and my --file habit did not cover it because br create has no --file option for the description. Two backtick pairs were substituted: one executed the `lean --help` I was documenting and pasted its output into the stored description; the other ran `--json` and substituted empty, leaving only a stray "command not found" on my terminal.

WHY IT IS DANGEROUS RATHER THAN MERELY ANNOYING:
* br stores the damaged field without complaint. There is no validation and no warning.
* The only signal is shell noise that scrolls past. I nearly missed it, and I was looking.
* The damage lands in a field other agents READ as authoritative. My description now contains a fragment of lean's help text presented as if I had written it.
* It is worst for exactly the beads that most need precision — anything documenting a command, a flag, a code snippet, or a shell invocation, which is most infrastructure beads.

WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY FIX IT, in preference order:
1. br reads long text fields from a file or stdin: `br create --description-file <path>`, or `--description -` for stdin. This is the real fix and it is small.
2. Failing that, br rejects or escapes control characters and newlines it did not expect in a field, so damage is loud rather than silent.
3. Failing both, this is a documentation problem and AGENTS.md's beads section should say plainly: never pass backticks to br in a double-quoted shell argument; there is no safe quoting workaround for br create.

I have posted a correction comment on the affected bead (franken_lean-c24a) rather than editing the description, so the damage and its repair are both in the record.

comments.text:
POPULATION MEASURED, AND POST-HOC DETECTION IS LARGELY UNAVAILABLE. Also: ONE PREVIOUSLY
UNRECORDED INSTANCE FOUND.

This bead carried two observed instances and no denominator. Measured at c278127d, reads only,
script at /data/tmp/claude-1000/cc3-scratch/r22_qpkj_population.py. 407 beads, 1502 stored
comments scanned.

BACKTICK PARITY IS NOT THE SIGNAL, which rules out the obvious detector first. Command
substitution deletes the backticks AND their contents together, so the count drops by two and
stays even. What survives is a grammatical scar where the token was: a space stranded before
punctuation, or a doubled space mid-sentence. That is what this scan looks for.

CONTROLS, BOTH DIRECTIONS, RUN BEFORE ANY COUNT WAS BELIEVED.
  * The bead's own recorded damaged string is flagged. A scan that misses it is broken.
  * A legitimate body carrying correctly-passed backticks is NOT flagged -- the acceptance
    criteria forbid a blanket refusal of markdown, so this is a wall the scan must not be.
  * HISTORICAL POSITIVE CONTROL, and it is the one that makes the rest credible: this bead names
    fln-171x as the site of the first instance. The scan finds fln-171x comment 761, and the
    fragment it returns is literally "canon's Exhausted carries , the byte offset the decode
    reached" -- the exact text recorded in this bead's body.

THE HEADLINE, AND IT REDIRECTS THE REPAIR. Two of the four signatures are SATURATED BY THIS
PROJECT'S OWN HOUSE STYLE and are unusable as written:

  169  empty_parens          saturated by Rust call syntax quoted in comments -- git(),
                             completed_exit(), unwrap_or_else(). Every sampled hit legitimate.
  162  double_space_midline  saturated by column-aligned tables inside comments, including
                             several of my own on this very bead. Every sampled hit legitimate.
    4  space_before_comma    tractable
    3  space_before_period   tractable

291 of 1502 comments (19.4%) carry at least one signature, and that figure is NOT a damage
count -- it is dominated by the two saturated signatures and must never be quoted as a
population of corrupted comments. This is fln-ysvo's shape exactly: the predicate that matters is
semantic, the lexical proxy is saturated, and it is saturated BECAUSE the practice is good --
agents quote real code and align real tables in their comments.

THE SEVEN LOW-SATURATION HITS, ADJUDICATED BY HAND. A signature is a candidate, never a verdict.

  fln-171x c761        DAMAGE -- the known instance, the positive control
  fln-171x c763        not damage -- the CORRECTION comment quoting the damaged text
  franken_lean-rur c16 STRONG CANDIDATE, PREVIOUSLY UNRECORDED: "Validator rejected NDJSON
                       line 9 as , then terminal/bundle publication became
                       final_workspace_hash_unava..." -- a backticked value consumed between
                       "as" and the comma, the same signature as the fln-171x instance. NOT
                       repaired by me: the comment is immutable and the bead is not mine.
  fln-ffam c937        AMBIGUOUS: "written > , every keyword becomes an identifier". The '>' is
                       present, so this may be a spacing quirk rather than a loss. Needs its
                       author; I am not guessing.
  fln-8mj c57          false positive -- '--root .' in a shell invocation
  franken_lean-dgxa c1128  false positive -- same
  franken_lean-rur c654    false positive -- same

'--root .' is a systematic false-positive source for space_before_period and should be excluded
by any future scan; it accounts for all three.

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA. The criteria offer two guard shapes: a wrapper that
takes a file path, or a check that refuses a suspicious body. This measurement says the second is
the weaker half and cannot be made both sensitive and non-vacuous on this corpus -- the two
signatures with real recall are saturated by legitimate content. The exact mechanism is the one
criterion 5 already names: WRITE FROM A FILE AND READ THE STORED RECORD BACK, comparing
byte-for-byte. That is not a heuristic and cannot be saturated. Note also that `br comments add`
already accepts `-f <file>`, so the mitigation recorded in this bead's body -- `-m "$(cat file)"`
-- is strictly worse than what the tool offers today, and the documented convention should name
`-f`.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH. The scan detects a scar, not a substitution; a damaged body whose
lost token sat at a place leaving no whitespace artifact is invisible to it, so 1 confirmed + 1
strong candidate + 1 ambiguous is a FLOOR, never a census. The two saturated signatures were not
adjudicated one by one -- 331 sampled hits were checked and every sampled one was legitimate,
which is a sample and not a proof. Nothing was repaired: bead comments are immutable and both
candidate sites belong to other panes' beads. Class bounded_model, one host, one commit.

comments.text:
THE WRITE-PATH GUARD IS BUILT AND DEMONSTRATED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. This comment was written by
it.

`scripts/br_comment.py`, two mechanisms, and the second is what makes it a guard rather than a
convention:

  1. The body never becomes a shell word. It is read from a FILE and handed to `br` through an
     argv LIST, so no expansion of any kind is possible -- not backticks, not `$(...)`, not
     `$VAR`, not history expansion.
  2. The stored record is read BACK and compared to the intended bytes, and a mismatch REFUSES.

Mechanism 1 alone is a convention, and a convention cannot tell you it was followed. Mechanism 2
is exact rather than heuristic and cannot be saturated -- which matters here, because the
post-hoc detector measured in comment 1503 is saturated and unfixable.

THE DEMONSTRATION, four cells against a SCRATCH beads database (`--db` in a lab directory), so
the shared tracker was never written. The acceptance criteria ask for a planted body containing a
backticked identifier AND a dollar-parenthesis, a confirmed refusal, and proof that a legitimate
backticked body is ACCEPTED rather than refused. Decoy body, verbatim:

    The `canon` field must survive, and $(date) must survive verbatim as literal text.

  A  written THROUGH the guard          ACCEPTED, exit 0, byte-identical: 82 chars, 2 backticks,
                                        1 dollar sign, all preserved. Without this cell the guard
                                        could be a blanket refusal of markdown.
  B  the SAME body written the          REFUSED, exit 1. The defect reproduced live: stored 96
     corrupting way -- interpolated      chars, ZERO backticks, ZERO dollar signs. The guard names
     into an inline shell word           the first differing character and prints both sides:
                                          intended: The `canon` field must survive, and $(date)
                                          stored:   The  field must survive, and Mon Jul 27 17:3
                                        `canon` was executed and spliced out; $(date) was replaced
                                        by the actual date. This is precisely the corruption this
                                        bead was filed for, produced on demand.
  C  verify a good comment against      REFUSED, exit 1 -- so the refusal is content-driven and
     the WRONG intended body             not "verify always refuses".
  D  verify the good comment against    ACCEPTED, exit 0 -- the mirror of C.
     its OWN body

Cells C and D are the 2x2's other diagonal. Without them B proves only that something refused.

PRODUCTION-PATH CONTROL, because a scratch database is a fixture and a fixture is not the
production path: `verify` was run against the REAL tracker on comment 1503 of this bead, which I
had written via `-f` earlier -- 4976 chars, 8 backticks, byte-identical, exit 0 -- and the mirror,
the same real comment against a different intended body, exit 1.

AND THIS COMMENT ITSELF was written with `scripts/br_comment.py write`, against the real tracker,
so its own read-back is the last cell.

A TRAP I HIT INSIDE MY OWN HARNESS, recorded because it is this project's documented rule failing
in the hands of the person quoting it: cell C's first run piped the guard's output to `tail -3`
and reported `$?`, which is TAIL's status, not the guard's. It printed EXIT=0 for a cell that had
refused. Caught by reading the output rather than the code. Re-run reading the exit from the
process: exit 1, as it should have said the first time.

WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT SATISFY OF THE ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA. Satisfied: the mitigation is
recorded where agents read it before writing a comment (AGENTS.md's beads section, with the
`git commit -F` second surface named alongside); a guard exists that takes a file path; it is
demonstrated against a planted body carrying both hazards; it is shown to ACCEPT legitimate
backticks; and verification reads the stored record back and compares byte-for-byte. NOT
satisfied: nothing FORCES the tool's use -- plain `br comments add -m` still works and a
corrupting write still succeeds silently. Closing the loop entirely would need a pre-commit check
over `.beads/issues.jsonl`, and comment 1503 measured why that is the weak half: the only
detectable signatures are saturated by this project's own house style.

ALSO CORRECTED IN THE DOCUMENTATION: this bead's body records the mitigation as
`-m "$(cat file)"`. `br comments add` accepts `-f <file>` directly, which is strictly better --
no command substitution occurs at all rather than one that happens to be safe -- so AGENTS.md
names `-f`.

LEFT ALONE DELIBERATELY: franken_lean-rur comment 16, the previously-unrecorded candidate from
comment 1503. Bead comments are immutable, it is another pane's bead, and a discovered instance
is a disclosure to route, never a thing to repair.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH. Cells A-D are one run at one commit on one host, class
bounded_model. The read-back proves THIS write landed intact and says nothing about any other.
`br` lives outside this repository, so its storage behaviour can change with a version and
nothing here would notice -- the guard compares landed bytes against intended bytes precisely so

title: fln-parse: preflight registry batches before publication
description:
## Finding

At 2e59eaaabca5f625c3e87999376c5de571eb05d0, Registry::apply_batch sorts requests and then calls add_leading one at a time with ?. If a canonically later request names an unknown category, every earlier request is already live: epochs advanced, hooks fired, callbacks retained, and the grammar root changed before Err(UnknownCategory). apply_batch_bounded has the same path after resource preflight.

Public Request.key has no uniqueness contract or check. Stable sorting preserves arrival order between equal keys, so distinct same-key requests reach an order-sensitive production list in schedule order. Existing keys are unique, so the current DPOR test misses this case.

Existing atomicity tests cover only pre-mutation budget refusal. The fln-okfb manifest names OKFB-ATOMIC-BATCH, leaving a production hole beneath the existing claim.

## Acceptance

- Canonicalize and validate every request before the first publication side effect.
- Reject duplicate request keys with a deterministic typed error.
- Reject unknown categories before changing the grammar root, epoch, live count, retained storage, or hook observations.
- Preserve bounded-resource precedence: an exceeded budget remains typed Inconclusive before request validation.
- Prove arrival-order independence for invalid batches and prove a corrected retry matches a clean control.
- Run exact-overlay package and workspace gates, main-root cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast under flock, and same-path UBS delta.

## Out of scope

No rollback log, cross-command transaction, parser recovery, macro transaction, content-hashed epoch, serialization, corpus parity, lane expansion, mutation harness, or deliberate crash.
close_reason: Two-phase canonical batch preflight now rejects duplicate keys and unknown categories before publication; retry equivalence, bounded-resource precedence, exact-overlay gates, and the main workspace gate are recorded in comment 1645.
