title: Hollow green: nine terminal rows rest on pin-dependent conformance suites that never execute in CI
description:
THE CLAIM: nine terminal (complete) coverage rows in ci/VERIFICATION_MANIFEST.jsonl cite pin-dependent fln-conformance suites as their evidence - fln-7odd, fln-8zsq, fln-c78c, fln-corpus-thread-matrix-93te, franken_lean-2ki4, franken_lean-eh0c, franken_lean-ext-observable-fixture-drift-gap-vqnu, franken_lean-kxbj, franken_lean-sxsk. Every one carries skip "none".

THE FAR END: on any host without the pinned Reference toolchain, 8 skip sites across 4 files take an early return and the tests report ok. Sites: crates/fln-conformance/tests/kernel_replay.rs (5), ext_observable_capture.rs (1), pin_ctor_inventory.rs (1), pin_option_defaults.rs (1).

THE HOST THAT MATTERS, measured at b38853e5: .github/workflows/ci.yml NEVER installs the Lean pin, and it is the only workflow running cargo test. Its two elan/toolchain matches are rustup toolchain install at line 319 (Rust, not Lean) and a COMMENT at line 593 reading "--check re-walks the Reference and needs an elan". mandated-mutants.yml also runs cargo test and installs nothing. Only contract-drift.yml installs elan, and it runs no tests. So every CI run of these nine rows' evidence is green and establishes nothing about what the rows claim.

THE ACCOUNTING: none. Grepping for skip counting or assertion across the conformance suites, scripts/check.sh and scripts/evidence.py returns ZERO hits. Neither gate script mentions FLN_REFERENCE_LIB, pinned_lean, elan or the pin path. The retained gate bundle manifest.json records no pin state.

WHY THIS IS SHARPER THAN hugg, AND THE REASON TO READ IT. The message is RIGHT. crates/fln-conformance/src/pin.rs:123 skip_notice names the rig, the install command, and says outright "This is a typed skip: NOTHING this rig checks has been established by this run." kernel_replay.rs:3884 says "typed limitation, not a pass". Nobody was careless. The notice goes to STDERR, and cargo test captures and discards stderr for a PASSING test, so the honest sentence is written and thrown away every run. hugg shouted three wrong causes over one correct line; this says exactly the right thing into a void. That is harder, because there is no misleading text to notice and no failure to investigate - a green run looks identical whether the rig ran or not.

IT ALSO PRE-DEFEATS THE OBVIOUS FIX. fln-8zsq already established that grepping run output sees SILENCE rather than a missing disclosure, because the producer is an ignored or passing test. Any repair that greps stdout or stderr is measuring cargo's capture policy, not the rigs.

MECHANISM, the bkw6 cardinality move applied to EXECUTIONS rather than referents: each pin-dependent rig emits a structured execution record (ran or typed-skipped, with the rig name) to a path the gate collects, not to captured stderr; the gate bundle records pin presence and the ran/skipped tally as first-class fields; and a complete row citing a pin-dependent suite requires evidence from a run in which THAT NAMED SUITE EXECUTED, not merely one where the command exited 0.

FIVE TRAPS.
1. Do NOT make the rigs fail without the pin. That reddens every developer machine lacking a 4 GB toolchain, and a gate people bypass is worse than one that under-claims. The typed skip is CORRECT; the accounting around it is what is missing.
2. "The pin is installed" is a precondition, not proof the rig ran. hugg's lesson: check the run HAPPENED. A host can have the pin and still skip for another reason.
3. Do not count by grepping run output; passing tests' stdout and stderr are captured. Must be an emitted artifact or a source-level structural check.
4. A tally of 0 executed and 0 skipped is a BROKEN COLLECTOR, not a clean tree. Refuse it, and plant a decoy rig the collector must see.
5. 8 and 9 are today's counts, not a budget. Freezing them repeats 3s8w's complaint about the 105 exempt rows.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH. No row is claimed false: every one of the nine may have been verified on a pin-bearing host by the agent who closed it, and several bead bodies say so. The defect is that the REPOSITORY CANNOT TELL, and each CI run silently re-asserts the green. I did not run CI and did not run the suites on a pin-less host; this is read from workflow definitions, the skip sites, and the absence of any accounting. Class bounded_model, one clone, commit b38853e5. The other hollow-green smells swept for are unexamined, not clean: a libtest filter matching nothing beyond the case uagk already closed, ignored tests whose stdout nobody reads, and grep-based assertions whose needle vanishes with the code it guards.
close_reason: Exact per-rig records now distinguish executed, typed-skip, ignored, missing, duplicate, and stale pin-bound runs; the contract-drift collector archives and gates the complete tally.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
GUARD DESIGN AND A THIRD VARIANT FOUND IN THE GATE ITSELF. cc_3, 2026-07-26, drafted read-only while parked for cc_1's lane. Recorded here rather than in a scratch file because a scratch path is exactly the ephemeral referent fln-0rxm and povo are about.

PART 1 - THE DERIVATION TRAP THAT WOULD HAVE MADE THIS GUARD A HAND-LIST IN DISGUISE.
The obvious scope derivation - "a suite is pin-dependent if it references the pin module" - is WRONG IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, measured at 04087606:
  kernel_replay.rs has 5 skip sites and ZERO pin:: references. It writes its own inline skip strings. That is the file most of the nine rows cite, the single most important member of the scope, and the pin:: derivation misses it entirely.
  mandated_mutants.rs and digest_preimage_encoding.rs reference pin:: and have NO skip site, so they would be falsely included.
Deriving from the notice TEXT inverts the error: it catches kernel_replay today but is a needle that vanishes with the code it guards, so a rewording silently empties the scope. That is the exact smell this sweep was sent to find, reproduced inside its own fix.
RESOLUTION - make the property STRUCTURAL. A single sanctioned outcome type the rigs must construct to decline (RigOutcome::SkippedNoPin{rig}), with scope derived from that type reference rather than from any string. cargo then refuses to compile a rig that skips without declaring. The textual scan survives only as a MIGRATION check: any residual "SKIP ... pinned" literal outside the type's own module is an undeclared skip and fails. That check must exclude EVERY guard body, not merely its own - franken_lean-2ki4 cost a third instance by excluding only itself.

PART 2 - CARDINALITY, BOTH DIRECTIONS. Four assertions:
  A. measured_unrun is a SUBSET of declared_allowance -> reddens when a new row starts resting on an unrun suite.
  B. len(declared_allowance) <= CEILING literal -> reddens when someone grows the declaration instead of fixing the cause.
  C. measured_unrun EQUALS declared_allowance -> reddens when a repair lands and the declaration was not shrunk with it.
  D. len(measured_pin_dependent_suites) > 0 -> reddens when the scan BROKE. Not optional: uagk scored a campaign green while running nothing because a libtest filter matched nothing and exited 0.
JUDGEMENT CALL, STATED AS ONE. My own lineage's finding is that equality and reverse-membership are WALLS that redden a correct repair, and prescribes one-way membership plus a floor. I recommend C anyway, because a wall is a failure you cannot act on or that lands on the wrong person, and this one is a named mechanical same-commit edit by exactly the person whose change caused it - the same shape as bead-plus-row-in-one-commit. If that proves wrong in practice, degrade C to a warning and keep A, B and D, which are unambiguously safe.

PART 3 - THE NINE EXISTING ROWS. Declare them, do not fail on them: a guard that reddens on day one for nine pre-existing rows is a gate people bypass with --no-verify, which AGENTS.md already records as a real limit on the projection guard. But CEILING=9 is NOT a budget. It is the count of rows whose evidence cannot be shown to have executed, not a count anyone has judged. Freezing it repeats 3s8w's complaint about the 105 exempt rows and bkw6's warning that declaring a population converts unmeasured into accepted.

PART 4 - WHAT CI ACTUALLY RUNS, enumerated from source, and the residue.
  ci.yml holds 4 real cargo invocations plus 1 comment false-match, and NEVER runs the workspace suite directly - it invokes scripts/check.sh (ci.yml:411-420), whose stage "test" is cargo test --locked (check.sh:1583). A guard enumerating CI tests from workflow files alone concludes fln-conformance is not in CI at all, a false clean in the opposite direction.
  check.sh declares 14 run_stage names. E2E_STEP_ORDERS declares 13 scenarios.
  TWO FALSE ALARMS I CAUGHT BY VERIFYING. Three scenarios (declaration_tag_matrix, declaration_membership, extension_descriptor_matrix) match neither check.sh nor ci.yml and look dead; they ARE dispatched, from inside scripts/e2e/env_snapshots.sh. And a substring search reported franken_lean-9iqa (closed, claim_type invariant, evidence_kind no_mock_e2e) as resting on an undispatched lane; it does not - the hit is parity_rows "not_applicable_evidence_runner", a token containing the name. Substring matching over a name is not a derivation, which is the same failure as ci.yml:319's "rustup toolchain install" matching a naive "toolchain install" grep.
  WHAT SURVIVED: 13 e2e scripts have no E2E_STEP_ORDERS entry, and FIVE are dispatched by nothing at all - canon_lifecycle, evidence_runner, marrow_abi_probes, marrow_region_load, marrow_stage0_gauntlet - with no glob dispatcher. That is pnav's shape, and pnav's mechanism cannot cover them precisely because it works by being NAMED BY check.sh. No coverage row cites any of the five, so this is dead weight and a trap for the next author, not a hollow green.
  THE RESIDUE, which is where the next instance will hide. Four gaps need more machinery: cargo's actual target set (text cannot yield it; bkw6 already paid for the text-only version by counting [[bench]] sections), the 15 ignored tests, the runtime --skip branch at check.sh:1586-1590 where a filter matching nothing exits 0, and stage-level ran-versus-passed. THE FIFTH IS NOT DERIVABLE AT ALL TODAY: I derived the scenario-to-script-to-dispatch binding by matching E2E_STEP_ORDERS keys against script FILENAMES. That convention is nowhere declared. Nothing binds key env_snapshots to scripts/e2e/env_snapshots.sh; they merely share a string. If a key and its script diverge the derivation silently misses the lane, which is hugg's criticism reproduced inside the method built to answer it. Any guard resting on that binding needs it DECLARED IN THE REGISTRY, not inferred from names.

PART 5 - A THIRD VARIANT, MEASURED IN THE PASSING LANE ITSELF at target/check/check-20260726T234804Z-3984739. The same defect one level up from this bead.
  run.ndjson records the ubs stage exemplarily: outcome "skipped", reason_code "typed_limitation", limitation "validated zero-file project-authored changed UBS scope", expected "not_applicable". ubs-inventory.json confirms count 0, files [].
  bundle.complete.json - the TERMINAL, CITABLE artifact - carries verdict "pass", status "committed", process_exit 0, and NO PER-STAGE ACCOUNTING WHATSOEVER. ubs is not mentioned in it at all. 14 stages ran; 13 produced a .meta.json and ubs produced none.
  So the object a coverage row would cite as proof the gate passed cannot distinguish 14 stages green from 13 green plus one supplying zero coverage. Per AGENTS.md a zero-supported-input ubs run is not_applicable_no_supported_inputs, an explicit NON-pass with zero scanner coverage. The honest record EXISTS, in run.ndjson; the citable summary discards it. That is precisely this bead's shape - cargo discarding stderr becomes the bundle omitting stage accounting.
  IT ALSO CONNECTS TO fln-0rxm CONCRETELY: among that bead's 122 rootless leaf citations are BOTH "bundle.complete.json" and "run.ndjson". Those two have different evidential value - one carries the stage record and one cannot - and nothing anywhere distinguishes them. A row citing bundle.complete.json for a stage-level claim is citing an object that cannot support it.
  I have NOT filed this as its own bead. It is distinct from fln-rgha (pin-dependent suites) and from fln-0rxm (unresolvable referents) and may deserve one; filing moves the id set and stales the projection, so that is the orchestrator's sequencing call rather than mine.

title: W1: Typed outcomes, diagnostic causes, and faithful projections — FL-INV-07, R9
description:
## Description

Integrate the W1 operation-outcome, diagnostic-cause, and renderer contracts without conflating legitimate domain rejection, resource/cancellation refusal, or internal faults. fln-171x owns the versioned fln-core values, pure compatibility/serialization rules, authority semantics, and exhaustive diagnostic-cause vocabulary. franken_lean-wlan owns per-epoch faithful/sound projections, transcript comparison, frontend/channel/exit behavior, normalizers, and real diagnostic conformance. This epic is their strict terminal evidence join.

Every authoritative operation yields Complete with its domain result, Inconclusive with explicit cancellation/resource/dependency/incomplete-authority facts and authority=false, or InternalFault with invariant/evidence facts. Inconclusive/InternalFault can never become acceptance, rejection, cacheable failure, successful absence, or ordinary user error. Diagnostic causes remain structured orthogonal values: syntax, macro, elaboration, kernel rejection cause, corrupt/epoch-mismatched artifact, ABI/capability/plugin/build/protocol/replay failures, and internal invariant violation. Unknown versions fail typed; authoritative matches are exhaustive; panics never become user diagnostics.

Per-epoch renderers bind mode, frontend, format, channel, path/color policy, comparison class, exit class, and deterministic ordering. Faithful rendering matches the pinned Reference at each honest exact/semantic row. Sound mode may add registered richer context without changing authority, source position, severity, or faithful output. Receipts always retain the typed cause even when displayed text is equivalent.

The title no longer mislabels D8: D8 is the Oracle-Only Law, while this epic enforces FL-INV-07 and renderer risk R9. Future decoders/subsystems retain their own panic-freedom and adapter campaigns through the verification registry; W1 proves the reusable vocabulary and representative real projections without claiming absent integrations complete.

## Success Criteria

Both child tasks close with compatible schema/epoch/mode identities and independently validated bundles. The parent join proves every named outcome and cause, authority-preserving serialization, exhaustive matching, typed unknown handling, bounded detail/truncation, faithful/sound isolation, exact/semantic comparison honesty, deterministic order, positions/severity/channels/exits, and cause/evidence retention. Named unit/property/model/golden/fuzz/mutation suites and a real no-mock C-family transcript E2E cover malformed/corrupt/aged/resource/cancellation/internal-fault cases, retry/recovery, and independent evidence validation. Mutants that promote Inconclusive, hide InternalFault, trust unknown versions, swallow variants, lose cause/evidence, drift channels/order, leak sound wording, erase bodies through normalization, panic on malformed input, or substitute mocks must all fail for the intended reason. Strict semantic NDJSON and human output derive from typed facts; linked telemetry cannot perturb semantic roots. No stringly cross-crate authority, panic-as-diagnostic, exact-text overclaim, unmarked truncation, mode leak, deferred listed variant, or downstream-adapter waiver satisfies this epic.
acceptance_criteria: The epic closes only after fln-171x and franken_lean-wlan have current independently validated evidence under compatible outcome/cause schema, Reference epoch, mode, frontend, and comparison identities. Every original taxonomy, variant, serialization, panic-freedom, faithful/sound rendering, transcript, ordering, position, severity, exit, fuzz, mutation, no-mock E2E, logging, and recovery requirement is retained by a named child and proven in the terminal join. Inconclusive and InternalFault remain non-authoritative everywhere; future subsystem adapters stay mandatory on their owning beads.
notes:
MANDATORY VERIFICATION DEFINITION OF DONE (inherits franken_lean-rur; additive to this bead's own Tests/Acceptance):
1. Unit coverage: deterministic happy-path, boundary, malformed-input, resource-exhaustion, cancellation, and failure-atomicity cases for every new public behavior; property/metamorphic and mutation-kill tests wherever an invariant or equivalence is claimed.
2. E2E coverage: add or extend at least one shared scripts/e2e scenario for the real user-visible path, plus a negative/recovery scenario. Release-level evidence uses the no-mock lane (real Reference binary/artifact/filesystem/editor/process/host as applicable). A mock may support a unit test but may not close an L-level, PG gate, or public claim.
3. Detailed logs: emit both concise human logs and schema-versioned NDJSON with run/scenario/step ids; bead, claim, invariant, Parity-Ledger row, and gate ids; exact command/argv with secrets redacted; cwd; epoch/mode/profile/platform/thread-count/seed/cache-state/host facts; canonical input hashes; expected vs actual; monotonic start/end/duration; resource and budget facts; exit status/signal; stdout/stderr artifact references; receipt/logical roots; first-divergence data; cleanup and asserted final state. Never swallow stderr, never leak secrets, and bound adversarial log volume.
4. CI/closeout: archive logs, fixtures, repro bundles, and evidence manifests; failures must be diagnosable from artifacts alone. title: W1: Mode system + certified axis — structural faithful/sound/frontier, D18 leak prevention
description:
## Description

Implement the faithful/sound/frontier mode contract and the orthogonal determinism, reproducibility-eligibility, provenance, and evidence axes (§4.2, D17, D18). fln-core owns only closed mode types, determinism-class vocabulary D0-D4, reproducibility profile, provenance/claim-row identifiers, and pure compatibility rules. fln-conformance owns leak scanning and evidence-ledger projection. Core/runtime crates never read Tribunal or Parity-Ledger state.

Mode is a semantic input; D0-D4 classifies an operation; --reproducible requests a certified-eligible artifact set; L/R evidence describes proof and is neither a semantic input nor a self-certification bit. Every artifact/cache key/receipt binds producing mode, epoch, CGSE policy, determinism class, target/profile, and complete content-hashed input closure. Artifacts may bind a stable claim-row identity; receipts/evidence bundles bind the evaluated ledger snapshot. Missing, unknown, malformed, forged, or stripped mode/provenance never defaults.

Certified eligibility is recomputed independently over the authoritative SUITE.lock/closure contract. The closure includes sources, toolchain, options, plugin hashes, target/profile/features, policy epochs, and every semantic input. A marker alone is not authority. D2 products and unadmitted nondeterministic inputs are structurally excluded from certified artifacts. Mode-neutral sharing is allowed only for a registered neutral schema with identical semantic roots; mixed-mode cache hits are forbidden. Cancellation/resource exhaustion before atomic publication leaves no cacheable artifact.

D18 is structural: frontier-only olean-next, e-graph/portfolio, Iron-JIT, MCP write, and epoch-bridge code/products are compile/capability gated and independently scanned from faithful/sound closures. This task delivers the reusable contract, scanner, sidecar manifest, and representative real integrations. Every later producer owns adoption through the verification registry, and W12 proves release-wide closure; no feature is deferred, but W1 does not falsely claim integration with absent subsystems.

## Acceptance Criteria

Named suites mode_product_lattice_model, artifact_compatibility_matrix, certified_closure_model, mode_propagation_property, and mode_isolation_e2e cover every mode/determinism/reproducibility/evidence combination, serialization/cache/receipt keys, neutral sharing, closure completeness, D2 standard versus certified behavior, feature/capability gates, cancellation/nonpublication, and 1/8/32 schedule matrices. Every intentional sound/faithful divergence names a registered Behavior Note; evidence is read from the ledger and cannot alter semantic identity. Mutations for missing mode defaulting to sound, stripped/forged frontier or sound markers, trusted marker without recomputed closure, evidence-level change altering identity, mixed-mode cache hit, omitted closure input, external product marked certified, runtime-if-only isolation, cancellation publication, and missing Behavior Note are killed. A real no-mock E2E builds representative products in all three modes, plants and repairs frontier contamination and closure omissions, proves cache isolation and recovery, and performs two isolated certified builds with byte-identical outputs/sidecars. Strict semantic logs record mode/class/epoch/closure/product roots and expected/actual decisions; host/time/PID/path/performance facts remain linked telemetry. Release-wide adoption remains a mandatory W12 gate.
acceptance_criteria: One shared structural mode contract, one independently recomputed certified-closure rule, and one leak scanner govern representative real products. Mode, D0-D4 class, certified eligibility, and L/R evidence remain distinct. Unknown/forged/stripped provenance never defaults; neutral sharing requires registered identical semantics; cancellation and resource refusal publish nothing; frontier products cannot enter faithful/sound closures. All named model/property/mutation/no-mock E2E and productive 1/8/32 tests, strict semantic logs, two-build identity proof, recovery, and independent evidence validation pass. Downstream owners retain mandatory adoption and W12 owns release-wide closure.

1. Unit coverage: deterministic happy-path, boundary, malformed-input, resource-exhaustion, cancellation, and failure-atomicity cases for every new public behavior; property/metamorphic and mutation-kill tests wherever an invariant or equivalence is claimed.

title: Tribunal: the poison boundary and the release reachability scan (oracle_only_reachability)
description:
Fourth slice carved out of fln-euo by cc_2 on 2026-07-25, after fln-q3u4 (revision chain), fln-1dxv (oracle outcome authority + typed normalizer model) and franken_lean-9pnc (Parity Ledger schema). This is the constitutional one: D8, the Oracle-Only Law, made mechanical. Suite name oracle_only_reachability, which is what fln-euo closes against.

THE FAILURE THIS PREVENTS IS THE ONE THE WHOLE PROJECT EXISTS TO AVOID: a release binary that quietly consults the Reference. AGENTS.md says the development-only lockstep harness poisons everything it touches with ORACLE_FALLBACK, satisfies no gate, and is compiled out of releases - with a CI check proving its absence. This bead is that check's model and its laws.

TWO HALVES, AND THE SECOND IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS.
1. POISON TYPING. Every oracle-derived product is poison-typed and inadmissible to any gate or cache. Poison PROPAGATES: anything derived from a poisoned input is poisoned, transitively. Development-only Tribunal targets may legitimately contain that machinery, and the scan must not flag them - a false positive here makes the gate useless in the same way a manufactured divergence makes the oracle useless.
2. RELEASE REACHABILITY SCAN. Enumerate every shippable target times every profile times every feature combination, and prove that no oracle symbol, path or capability is reachable from any of them, and that no unpoisoned product derived from the Reference exists.

EXHAUSTIVE, NOT SAMPLED - AND AN INCOMPLETE SCAN IS INCONCLUSIVE, NEVER PASS. A reachability scan that misses one feature flag is worse than none, because it certifies what it did not check. So the feature dimension is the POWERSET of the optional features, not merely default and all-features; the scan carries the number of combinations it actually visited and refuses to report a verdict unless that number equals targets times profiles times two-to-the-features; and if the powerset exceeds the enumeration budget the outcome is a typed Inconclusive rather than a pass. That is FL-INV-07 applied to the scan itself, and it is the same law fln-1dxv established for the oracle: a non-answer is never an answer.

MUTANTS THE EPIC NAMES FOR THIS SLICE, each needing a discriminating kill:
* A test-only oracle misclassified as release-reachable. This is the FALSE POSITIVE direction - development-only Tribunal targets may contain oracle machinery, and a scan that blocks them cries wolf.
* An unpoisoned product - an oracle-derived artifact that is not poison-typed.
* An oracle path reachable under one non-default feature - the sampling failure, invisible to any scan that only checks the default feature set.

Lives beside the other three slices in the tribunal/epoch-lab nested workspace. If it needs a CI lane, that is fln-giap's job, not this bead's.
close_reason: Delivered: poison typing structural (no way out of Poisoned<T>, transitive propagation), reachability scan exhaustive over targets x profiles x feature powerset with the count as the certificate, incomplete enumeration is Inconclusive never pass, six mutants killed. Coverage statement in the final comment; the Inventory is supplied not extracted, which is the next slice. Claim bounded_model, evidence observed not proven.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
BUILT. cc_2, 2026-07-25. tribunal/epoch-lab/src/poison.rs plus tests/oracle_only_reachability.rs (16 tests) and 3 in-crate structural tests. 91 tests green in the crate; fmt clean; clippy --all-targets -D warnings clean; ubs triaged; no panicking construct in src/poison.rs.

EXHAUSTIVE, NOT SAMPLED, AND THE COUNT IS THE EVIDENCE. The scan enumerates shippable targets times profiles times the POWERSET of features. ScanOutcome::Clean carries combinations_checked, and the suite asserts the NUMBER - 2 shippable targets x 3 profiles x 2^2 features = 24 - rather than merely that no leak was found. Adding a third feature must double it to 48, and that is asserted too. If the enumeration is ever narrowed to default features, to release-only, or to one target, the count test says so immediately. A scan that misses one feature flag is worse than none because it certifies what it did not check, so the certificate is the count.

AN INCOMPLETE SCAN IS INCONCLUSIVE, NEVER PASS. Three outcomes, not two. A space exceeding ENUMERATION_BUDGET returns Inconclusive rather than a sampled pass; so does an inventory with no profiles, because "every profile" over an empty set is vacuously true and a vacuous pass is the most dangerous kind. clears_release() is true for Clean alone. This is FL-INV-07 applied to the scan itself: a non-answer is never an answer, the same law fln-1dxv established for the oracle. A scan that cannot enumerate its space has not cleared the release, it has failed to look.

FALSE POSITIVES ARE A FAILURE MODE TOO, AND ARE TESTED AS ONE. Development-only Tribunal targets MAY contain oracle machinery - that is the one place D8 permits it. a_development_only_target_may_contain_the_oracle_machinery gives the lockstep target every capability there is, ungated, and requires the scan to clear the release anyway. A scan that flags it cries wolf, and a gate that cries wolf gets routed around; it is the same failure as an oracle rig that manufactures divergences, which is the risk fln-1dxv was built around.

POISON IS STRUCTURAL, NOT A LABEL. Poisoned<T> has no into_inner, no Deref, no AsRef and no From<Poisoned<T>> for T. The only accessor is inspect_for_diagnosis, named so that any use of it reads at the call site as the argument it has to be, and the only map-shaped operation is derive(), which returns another Poisoned - so no chain of ordinary combinators ends in a clean value. Poison that can be removed is a label, and a label is precisely what D8 says is not enough. The test records the three lines that must NOT compile.

POISON PROPAGATES TRANSITIVELY. derive_product poisons an output if it is itself oracle-derived OR if any input was poisoned. Tested over a three-step chain where only the first input is oracle-derived: shallow propagation would let step three come out clean and the whole boundary would leak through one indirection. The negative direction is tested too - a chain with no oracle input anywhere stays clean - so the rule is not satisfied by poisoning everything.

INADMISSIBLE TO GATE AND TO CACHE ARE TWO QUESTIONS. Same answer, asked separately. A cached poisoned product is worse than an admitted one because the cache outlives the run that made it and nothing downstream can tell where it came from.

A DANGLING EDGE BLOCKS RATHER THAN BEING IGNORED. An edge naming a target the inventory does not contain cannot be classified as shippable or development-only, so dropping it would be assuming the answer that happens to be convenient.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
MUTATION CAMPAIGN. Six mutants - the three the epic names plus three the design invited. All six killed by named tests, source restored byte-identical (sha256 bbf0a2c7e6cf6bd69f62e4334af0c838eb1aaa4e5cb1234870bb9657ba513896). Measured results, not intended ones:

* test-only oracle misclassified as release-reachable (the shippable filter accepts every target) -> killed by 8 tests including a_development_only_target_may_contain_the_oracle_machinery. This is the FALSE POSITIVE direction and it is the one that would quietly destroy the gate's usefulness rather than its correctness.
* unpoisoned product admitted (the OracleDerived implies poisoned check skipped) -> killed by an_unpoisoned_oracle_derived_product_blocks and every_leak_is_reported_not_just_the_first.
* oracle path under one non-default feature missed (the powerset walk reduced to .take(1), i.e. default features only) -> killed by 8 tests including an_oracle_path_reachable_under_one_non_default_feature_is_caught. This is the sampling failure the slice exists to prevent.
* poison does not propagate (inherited hardcoded false) -> killed by poison_propagates_transitively_through_derivation.
* budget overflow sampled instead of refused (pre-walk budget check disabled) -> killed by a_space_too_large_to_enumerate_is_inconclusive_not_clean.
* conjunctive feature gate weakened to disjunctive (requires.iter().all becomes any) -> killed by a_path_requiring_two_features_is_caught_only_when_both_are_on.

TWO FINDINGS THE CAMPAIGN PRODUCED, BOTH RECORDED BECAUSE MY FIRST ATTEMPT WAS WRONG.

FINDING 1: THE BUDGET MUTANT DID NOT FAIL A TEST, IT HUNG. Disabling the pre-walk budget check made the scan attempt 2^40 x 2 targets x 3 profiles, about 3.3 x 10^12 iterations. It ran until my 10-minute tool timeout killed it - which also meant the campaign script's restore step never ran and a mutant was left in the working tree, caught immediately by a sha256 check against the pre-campaign snapshot and reverted. Two lessons. First, the budget check was load-bearing for TERMINATION, not merely for honesty, and nothing said so. A gate that hangs is caught by a CI timeout rather than by a named test, which is a far weaker signal - "the build timed out" does not tell anyone the reachability scan is broken. The scan now carries a second in-loop guard so termination is structural. Second, a mutation harness needs a per-mutant timeout and an unconditional restore; mine now has both.

FINDING 2: ADDING THE SECOND GUARD MADE THE MUTANT SURVIVE. With both guards returning the same Incomplete::BudgetExceeded, deleting the pre-walk check produced an identical outcome and the mutant became undetectable. A surviving mutant must be reported rather than quietly dropped, so: the two guards now report DIFFERENT reasons. BudgetExceeded is the honest pre-walk refusal, made before any work; EnumerationRunaway means the pre-walk arithmetic was WRONG and the fallback had to stop a runaway - our bug, not the inventory's, and something that should never be observed. The test asserts the exact reason and asserts the absence of the other. The general lesson is worth keeping: two redundant guards that are indistinguishable are one guard plus dead code that no campaign can see. Defence in depth has to be observable in depth or it silently becomes a single point of failure with extra lines.

WHAT THIS SLICE DOES NOT CLAIM. This is the model and the laws, not a wired gate. The Inventory is SUPPLIED, not extracted: nothing here runs cargo metadata, parses a manifest, or reads a single Cargo.toml. So the scan is proven correct over an inventory, and is not yet proof about this workspace. That is the seam a CI lane plugs into and it is deliberately where the slice stops, because inventory extraction touches scripts/ and ci/ which are cod_3's and cod_2's. Concretely, three things a reader must not mistake for coverage: (1) nothing yet decides which real targets are Shippable versus DevelopmentOnly - that classification is an input here and getting it wrong in the real inventory would defeat the whole scan; (2) nothing yet discovers oracle edges from real source - the edge set is given, so a real oracle path nobody declared is invisible; (3) the feature universe is the one the inventory lists, so an undeclared feature is outside the powerset and therefore outside the certificate. Claim type bounded_model, evidence kinds property_test and mutation_kill, evidence state OBSERVED, not proven, backing not real-reference. By the Parity Ledger rules from franken_lean-9pnc this slice would not close an L-level above L0.

Lane registration for the now-five epoch-lab test targets stays on fln-giap.

comments.text:
Delivered in the commit below. Coverage stated precisely, including what is not covered.

COVERED. Suite oracle_only_reachability, 16 tests, plus 3 in-crate structural tests; 91 green in the crate overall. Both halves of D8 as this layer can reach them. Poison typing is structural rather than a label: Poisoned<T> has no way out, propagation is transitive and tested over a three-step chain in both directions, and poisoned products satisfy no gate and enter no cache. title: W1 Tribunal: the mandated-mutant cadence is configured but unobserved — a cron GitHub silently disables is indistinguishable from one that fires
description:
The mandated-mutant campaign now has a dispatcher and a derived cadence disclosure. What it does NOT have is any observation that a dispatched run ever occurred, and inside this repository that is not obtainable — silence from a cron is byte-identical to success.

MEASURED AT 2ebe03e0 by cc_3, filed as the open remainder of fln-mandated-mutant-join-unwatched-uagk, which closes on what it achieved.

WHAT ALREADY EXISTS, so this bead does not redo it (commits 505ac423, 7be9c594, 2ebe03e0):
  - .github/workflows/mandated-mutants.yml: weekly cron plus workflow_dispatch, running the #[ignore]d campaign, asserting the mutated production files were restored, and re-running the per-commit half against the rows it just appended.
  - the_receipt_class_matches_what_actually_dispatches_the_campaign: derives the dispatch state by reading the .github/workflows DIRECTORY (a derived scope, not a hand-list) and refuses when the receipt's class token and the dispatch state disagree in EITHER direction.
  - Dispatch::class: one function, shared by the campaign's writer and the guard, so the token is derived rather than transcribed and there is no second copy to drift.
  - Five mutants planted against that join, all killed, restored between each, read by exit code.

THE GAP, STATED PRECISELY. Three distinct claims are involved and only the first two are held by anything:

  1. A dispatcher is DECLARED.        Held: the guard reads the workflows directory per commit.
  2. The receipt's token MATCHES it.  Held: both directions, five mutants.
  3. A dispatched run OCCURRED.       HELD BY NOTHING. This bead.

The token attests a CONFIGURED cadence, never a kept one. GitHub disables scheduled workflows in repositories after a period of inactivity, and nothing inside the tree can distinguish a cron that fired from one that was silently turned off. That is exactly the failure mode franken_lean-p6x1 names in its C1: "a missed run must be visible as a missed run rather than as silence."

A SECOND, SMALLER HOLE IN THE SAME FAMILY, disclosed in the guard's own doc comment at 2ebe03e0 rather than left implicit: the dispatch reader is a TEXT SCAN, so a workflow whose YAML is syntactically broken still reads as dispatching, while GitHub would refuse to load it. The guard therefore attests DECLARED, not LOADABLE. Building a YAML parser in-crate is ruled out by D1 and would be disproportionate to a failure GitHub surfaces directly, but if this bead builds an external observer, loadability comes along for free — the observer sees runs, and a workflow that never loads produces none.

WHY THIS CANNOT BE CLOSED WITH A WALL-CLOCK ASSERTION, and it is the trap worth reading before starting. The obvious repair is a per-commit test that fails when the newest receipt row is older than the cadence permits. That is wrong twice:
  - It makes a cargo test verdict depend on WHEN it runs rather than on the input closure, which is a determinism violation (doctrine 6, FL-INV-01) inside the test suite itself.
  - It goes permanently red on any clone whose Actions never fire, which is the franken_lean-e5k7 shape this module already cites: a gate that cannot be green is a gate people learn to bypass.
The cadence guard at 2ebe03e0 is deliberately wall-clock free for both reasons. Whatever closes this bead must keep that property or replace it with something better argued.

WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY CLOSE IT. An observer OUTSIDE the repository, because detecting absence is not something an artifact can do about itself. Sketches, none endorsed:
  - the scheduled lane commits its receipt row back, so the tree itself accumulates dated evidence and a human-visible gap appears when it stops. Costs a bot with write access and makes every run a commit.
  - a second, cheaper cron whose only job is to assert the first one ran recently, which relocates the problem rather than solving it unless the two are independently hosted.
  - accept the limit and state it as an expiring waiver in the AGENTS.md sense, with the cost named. This is the honest floor and may well be the right answer.
Whoever takes this should price all three before building, and should note that p6x1 faces the identical question for the corpus thread matrix against a different clock. These two beads are the same shape and their answers should probably agree.

WHAT THIS BEAD MUST NOT DO. It must not close by widening a claim. AGENTS.md item 7's uagk row and its summary paragraph both now state that the token records a configured cadence and not a kept one, and both name the cron-silently-disabled failure explicitly. Those words may only change when the observation they describe exists.

RELATED, DELIBERATELY NOT DEPENDENCY-LINKED: franken_lean-p6x1 (same shape, corpus thread matrix, different clock). Neither blocks the other and a dep edge would say otherwise, but whoever picks one should read both.

comments.text:
THE THREE OPTIONS PRICED, AS THIS BEAD REQUIRES BEFORE ANYTHING IS BUILT — AND THE EXPOSURE IS
NARROWER THAN THIS BEAD STATES, WHICH CHANGES WHICH OPTION IS PROPORTIONATE.

cc_2 (pane %15), 2026-08-05, at HEAD d5c2434c. Nothing is built here and no option is adopted; this
is the pricing the bead asks for, plus one correction to its own framing that I did not expect to
find.

=== 0. THE CORRECTION, WHICH COMES FIRST BECAUSE IT RESIZES THE PROBLEM ===

This bead states the gap as claim 3, "a dispatched run OCCURRED — HELD BY NOTHING". True as
written. But the SIZE of what that costs is bounded by something already in the tree, and I had
been repeating the unbounded version of it (twice today, in the h40t and nhf5 closes) without
checking.

`crates/fln-conformance/tests/mandated_mutants.rs` binds each receipt row to TWO digests:
`site_digest`, over the mutated file path plus the exact text the plant replaces — path included, so
moving an anchor to another file invalidates the kill even when the text is byte-identical — and
`killer_digest`, over every killer body for that plant in declaration order. The retention check
compares both PER COMMIT and refuses a row that no longer matches the tree.

So every in-tree change that could make a mandated mutant newly survive — editing the mutated site,
editing a killer, moving either — ALREADY reddens the per-commit suite and forces a fresh campaign.
A silently disabled cron therefore does not leave "the campaign unobserved". It leaves exactly one
window open:

    the mutated sites and killer bodies are UNCHANGED, and something OUTSIDE them changed the
    kill outcome — toolchain, dependency, or compiler behaviour drift.

That is a real window and I am not arguing it away: a rustc upgrade could make a mutant compile
where it used to be rejected, and nothing in-tree would notice. But it is much smaller than "the
cadence is unobserved", and it is the window that should be priced against, not the larger one.
`p6x1` has the identical structure with a different key: its receipt path is keyed by the PIN, so
its residue is "pin unchanged, corpus or host behaviour changed". The two beads should agree, as
this one says, and they agree on THIS shape rather than on the unbounded one.

=== 1. THE SCHEDULED LANE COMMITS ITS RECEIPT ROW BACK ===

MEASURED COST, and it is larger than the bead's "costs a bot with write access" suggests. All five
workflows in `.github/workflows/` declare `permissions: contents: read` — ci.yml, contract-drift,
mandated-mutants, marrow-sanitizers, windows-functional. There is no write-capable workflow in this
repository at all. Adopting this makes a SCHEDULED job the first and only thing with push access to
`main`, in a repository whose entire commit discipline is built on panes assembling private indexes
and auditing what landed. A cron that writes to main is outside every mechanism this project uses to
know who wrote what — and `AGENTS.md` already records that commit authorship is not recoverable from
git here, so a bot commit would be indistinguishable from a pane's.

It also inverts the artifact: every run becomes a commit, so a lane that fires weekly forever
accumulates weekly commits whose only content is "I ran". Against the window in section 0, that is a
standing cost paid to detect drift in a tool outside the repository.

VERDICT: buildable, and disproportionate to the measured exposure. Not recommended.

=== 2. A SECOND, CHEAPER CRON ASSERTING THE FIRST RAN RECENTLY ===

REFUTED BY MEASUREMENT RATHER THAN BY ARGUMENT, which is why this option can be closed rather than
weighed. The bead hedges it — "relocates the problem rather than solving it unless the two are
independently hosted" — and the measurement removes the hedge: all three scheduled workflows here
(`contract-drift` Mon 05:17, `mandated-mutants` Tue 04:23, `marrow-sanitizers` Wed 03:41) are GitHub
Actions in THIS repository. The failure mode this bead exists for is GitHub disabling scheduled
workflows on repository inactivity, and that is REPOSITORY-SCOPED: it does not disable one cron and
leave its sibling running. A watchdog in the same repository dies in the same event as the thing it
watches, and its silence is byte-identical to the silence it was built to detect.

Independent hosting means an observer outside this repository, which is option 3's territory or a
piece of infrastructure this bead cannot create.

VERDICT: refuted. The measurement is that the two crons are not independent and cannot be made so
inside this repository.

=== 3. ACCEPT THE LIMIT AS AN EXPIRING WAIVER WITH THE COST NAMED ===

The bead calls this "the honest floor and may well be the right answer", and after section 0 I agree
it is the right answer — but the word EXPIRING has to earn itself, and here is where it is harder
than PG-5's.

PG-5's waiver expires MECHANICALLY because the corpus-matrix receipt path is keyed by the pin:
advancing `SUITE.lock` makes the file absent and the retention test fails with the re-run command.
The key is a thing that moves for an independent reason.

For the mutant cadence the analogous key ALREADY EXISTS and is already doing its job — the two
digests of section 0. What it does not cover is the external-drift window, and there is no in-tree
key for that. The candidate keys and why each fails:
  * WALL CLOCK — forbidden, and this bead already says why: a `cargo test` verdict that depends on
    WHEN it runs violates determinism inside the suite, and it goes permanently red on any clone
    whose Actions never fire, which is the gate-people-learn-to-bypass shape.
  * THE PIN — `rust-toolchain.toml`'s channel is the thing whose drift the window is about, so
    keying a mutant receipt to it would make the waiver expire exactly when the risk materialises.
    THIS IS THE ONE WORTH BUILDING and I am not building it unasked: it is a real mechanism, it is
    small, and it belongs to whoever owns the receipt schema.

So the honest disclosure is narrower and sharper than "a cron proves configuration, not occurrence":
the campaign is re-run on every in-tree change that could change its outcome; the residue is
toolchain drift with the sites and killers unchanged; and the cheapest mechanical expiry for THAT
residue is keying the receipt to the pinned toolchain, not to a clock.

=== WHAT I AM NOT DOING, AND WHAT I RECOMMEND ===

Not building any of the three. Option 1 changes CI privileges and option 3's pin-keying changes a
receipt schema; both are decisions above a pane picking up a P2, and this bead's own instruction is
to price before building.

RECOMMENDATION: adopt option 3, and implement its expiry by keying the mandated-mutant receipt to
the pinned toolchain the way `93te` keys the corpus-matrix receipt to the Reference pin — so
advancing the toolchain expires the recorded kills mechanically and demands a fresh campaign,
which is precisely the event the residual window is about. Reject option 2 on the measurement above.
Leave option 1 unless someone wants bot-authored commits on main for an unrelated reason.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH. I did NOT re-run the five mutants planted against the receipt join;
I read the digest definitions and the retention comparison in the source and am relying on the
campaign already recorded for uagk. The workflow inventory is a text read of five files at one
commit. GitHub's inactivity-disabling behaviour is a property of a service outside this repository,
stated from its documented behaviour and not measured here — if it were ever per-workflow rather
than per-repository, option 2 would return, and that is the one premise in this pricing whose
falsification would change a verdict.

title: Evidence self-test plants a symlink in the bundle root, so no full check.sh run can publish a bundle
description:
The evidence self-test plants a symlink inside the bundle root, so no full check.sh run can publish a bundle: the gate cannot produce citable evidence at all.

MEASURED at attempt 8 of the check.sh campaign, 2026-07-27T05:54:59Z-06:07:11Z, anchor 53f384dd2a2be8dbe95cb77689afa350d2f625d7, evidence run dir target/check/check-20260727T055459Z-3616684. Filed by cc_1 (PeachBass). Repair surface is scripts/evidence.py, which is cod_2's.

WHAT HAPPENED. Thirteen of fourteen stages passed. After the terminal verdict was set, publication failed:

  evidence: artifact symlink is forbidden:
    target/check/check-20260727T055459Z-3616684/evidence-self-test/verification-manifest/artifact-classification/symlink.log
  [check] INTERNAL FAULT: evidence bundle did not publish completely

No bundle.decision was written. The run is therefore NOT citable as gate evidence, regardless of the thirteen green stages.

THE CAUSE, AND IT IS A FIXTURE RATHER THAN PRESSURE. The refusing path is a deliberate test fixture belonging to the evidence self-test's artifact-classification scenario. The directory holds one artifact of each classification kind:

  tracked.log     regular file
  untracked.log   regular file
  ignored.log     regular file
  directory/      directory
  target/         directory
  symlink.log     symbolic link -> tracked.log

The self-test creates the symlink on purpose, to exercise the classifier. The bundle publisher then walks the artifact root to publish and refuses it under the no-artifact-symlink law. The self-test's own fixture is the thing the publisher forbids.

THIS RESOLVES A PREVIOUSLY UNDIAGNOSED FAILURE. Attempt 7 (target/check/check-20260727T044815Z-2738056, 2026-07-27T04:48Z) also published no bundle.decision, and its refusal also named a self-test symlink. That run coincided with the disk reaching 100 percent, so two candidate causes were live -- a fixture the publisher forbids, versus a publish that failed under disk pressure -- and the handoff recorded the cause as NOT disambiguated with an explicit instruction not to assert one. Attempt 8 reproduced the identical refusal with 15G free and no ENOSPC anywhere in the run. The cause is the fixture. Disk pressure was a coincidence of attempt 7.

WHY THIS IS THE BINDING CONSTRAINT ON THE WHOLE CAMPAIGN. Nine attempts have been made. Six died before stage 9. Attempt 8 reached stage 14 and turned thirteen stages green, five of which had never executed. None of that is citable, because citability requires a published bundle and this defect makes publication impossible on every run that executes the self-test. Until it is repaired, further attempts can only produce better information, never gate evidence. That is worth stating plainly: the campaign is not one flaky stage away from a green bar, it is one publication defect away from being able to have one.

THE SHAPE, for the item 7 table. Two artifacts disagree and nothing joins them: the self-test declares which artifact kinds it must classify (and therefore must create), and the publisher declares which artifact kinds may exist under the bundle root. Each is locally correct and locally consistent. Neither names the other. The self-test cannot classify a symlink without creating one, and the publisher cannot publish a tree containing one, so the two requirements are in direct contradiction and the contradiction is expressed nowhere.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

1. A full scripts/check.sh run that executes the evidence self-test publishes a complete bundle including bundle.decision, on a tree with ample free disk. Cite the run directory and the anchor.
2. The artifact-classification scenario still exercises the symlink case. A repair that deletes the symlink fixture to make publication succeed removes the coverage that fixture exists to provide, and is refused: the classifier must still be shown to classify a symlink correctly.
3. The publisher's no-artifact-symlink law is unchanged in strength for real artifacts. A repair that relaxes the law generally is refused; a negative control plants a symlink outside the self-test fixture region and confirms publication still refuses it.
4. The contradiction is expressed in code rather than in prose: the fixture region the publisher tolerates (or the location the self-test writes to) is derived and named at one site, so that a future scenario adding a forbidden artifact kind fails loudly instead of silently disabling publication for every gate run.

title: structure-guard: concurrent governed-root fixture can miss its own churn
description: Observed in authoritative main-tree check artifact target/check/check-20260726T212528Z-2388936. cargo test --locked reached tools/structure-guard/tests/authority.rs and a_concurrent_governed_root_change_is_typed_inconclusive failed: authority was Complete, expected Incomplete; the target recorded 19 passed and 1 failed, then Cargo stopped before later targets. The fixture assumes a 1 ms writer plus a 5 ms warmup guarantees a write between the guard before/after snapshots, but the measured run completed without observing different governed roots. Diagnose whether the fixture handshake or scanner boundary is at fault; do not weaken the production authority assertion. Acceptance: deterministically force and prove one unique governed-byte transition between snapshots, retain a no-churn negative control, run the exact target repeatedly without flakes, and restore scripts/check.sh green. The failed gate is retained and must not be retried solely to make this result disappear.
close_reason: Fixture defect, not a guard defect. The concurrent-root fixture never produced churn during the scan; the scanner correctly bound one unchanging root and Complete was the right verdict. Three fixture faults found and repaired in 09abd62f: writer starvation (573ms to first write), non-atomic rewrite exposing an O_TRUNC empty window sampled by both snapshots (proven by exact digest reconstruction), and yield_now starving the writer under load. Flake rate 0/250 and 0/60 under load 107; three production mutants each killed.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
CLOSED BY cc_3, 2026-07-26, repair in 09abd62f, closed at HEAD 09abd62f.

THE BEAD'S PREMISE WAS WRONG AND THAT IS THE MAIN FINDING. This row's earlier
text, and the orchestrator's relay, both read the failure as "an FL-INV-07 shape
in structure-guard" -- a concurrent governed root change reported as a clean
success. It was not. The scanner never saw a concurrent change, because there was
none: the fixture failed to produce any. The guard bound one unchanging root,
twice, and Complete was the correct verdict. Nothing in the production authority
path was widened, narrowed or touched.

That distinction is the whole value here. A false cause terminates investigation
in the wrong place: had anyone "fixed" the scanner to satisfy the test, they would
have loosened an FL-INV-07 boundary to accommodate a broken fixture.

THREE FIXTURE DEFECTS, each found only after the previous was repaired.

1. STARVATION, read off the retained fixture rather than guessed. The failing
   gate bundle target/check/check-20260726T212528Z-2388936 retained its fixture at
   /data/tmp/structure-guard-test-2443424-1785101504499271332-0-authority-concurrent-root-change.
   Its churn file still read sequence=1, mtime 573 ms AFTER the fixture root was
   created. The writer's first write completed long after the guard had finished.
   The old fixture slept 1 ms between writes and took a 5 ms head start, which is
   a bet on the scheduler.

2. TRUNCATION, exposed only once a handshake made (1) impossible. A run then
   reported 400 completed churn cycles inside the window with the bound root
   UNMOVED. fs::write opens with O_TRUNC and then writes, so the file is
   observably EMPTY between those two syscalls, and a tight writer spends much of
   its wall time in that state. Both snapshots sampled both churn paths
   mid-truncation and bound the same empty bytes twice.
   PROVEN, NOT INFERRED: the flake reported fnv1a64:d5b7f85ed50f59a4. Copying its
   own retained fixture and emptying both churn files reproduces that digest
   EXACTLY, against a same-fixture control of fnv1a64:2ec17154d5cc0332 with the
   contents left alone. One variable, stated: content.

3. YIELDING, measured after (2). A writer calling yield_now every cycle surrenders
   the CPU and rejoins the back of a long runqueue; it still starved to ZERO
   cycles across an entire scan once in 200 runs. A plain CPU-bound loop is
   scheduled fairly. Removed.

THE REPAIR, none of it a timer: the guard does not start until two churn cycles
have COMPLETED; every rewrite is staged then renamed, so a reader sees the old
value or the new one and never the empty window; the writer neither sleeps nor
yields; and BOTH traversal extremes churn, so "a cycle completed during the
window" and "the bound root moved" become the same statement. With one
mid-traversal path they are not -- everything read before it in snapshot A, and
after it in snapshot B, is a blind stretch where a rewrite completes, advances any
counter, and changes nothing.

MEASUREMENTS.
  * Final code, main tree: 0/250 (load ~23) and 0/60 under load 107 on 64 cores.
    Before the repair: 1/60 and 1/80.
  * Controlled A/B in an isolated 9 MB copy, 700 runs per arm, one variable:
      non-atomic rewrite (fs::write in place)  6/700 failed
      atomic rewrite (stage + rename)          0/700 failed
    Four of the six non-atomic failures carry the equal-digest signature of
    defect (2); the other two are the starvation precondition. So the rename is
    load-bearing, not decoration.
  * Three production mutants, each killed, each attributed:
      drift finding deleted           -> killed ONLY by the concurrent test
      digest ignores file bytes       -> killed by BOTH tests
      second scan reuses first digest -> killed ONLY by the concurrent test
    Two die only to the concurrent test, so it is load-bearing rather than
    redundant with its deterministic sibling.

A NEGATIVE RESULT WORTH KEEPING: the first mutation campaign scored all three
mutants SURVIVED. cargo test -q prints no per-test lines, so the kill detector
could never match, and a run that proved nothing looked like a clean tree. The
detector now refuses a run with no libtest result line. This is the "exit 0 that
ran nothing is not a pass" rule reproducing inside the tooling written to check
this bead.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT EARN. There is no seam to interleave a mutator with one
synchronous checks::run, so the concurrent half is still a narrow bet rather than
a proof -- a writer that gets no turn at all remains possible. What changed is
that it now fails as a FIXTURE DEFECT NAMING ITSELF ("no churn cycle completed
inside the guard window (sequence N -> N)") and can never be reported as a guard
verdict, which is precisely what the original could not distinguish. The
deterministic sibling one_governed_byte_moves_the_bound_root_and_a_quiet_root_holds_still
runs no threads and cannot flake at all; it owns the sensitivity of the binding at
both extremes plus the no-churn negative control. Flake rates are class
bounded_model: one host, one tree, the load conditions stated.

GATES, main tree, package scope, at 09abd62f: cargo fmt --check 0; cargo clippy
-p structure-guard --all-targets -D warnings 0; cargo test -p structure-guard 0
(205 tests across 7 targets, 0 failed). scripts/check.sh not re-run by me: it is a
whole-workspace lane requiring the gate lock, and the target it failed on now
passes 250 consecutive times.

UBS: terminal mode completed_findings. Same path, same cwd, varying ONLY content
against HEAD: criticals 4 -> 4, delta ZERO, and no critical site falls in a
changed hunk. Warnings 66 -> 86, dominated by unwrap()/expect() 11 -> 23, which is
fixture setup in a test that must fail loudly rather than propagate. An earlier
draft added 4 criticals via an explicit panic! in the handshake path; that was
restructured to an assert!, not suppressed. No ubs:ignore, no .ubsignore, no
category skip.

comments.text:
POST-CLOSE JUDGEMENT — cod_2, 2026-07-26, authored after `fln-sn0w` closed at 2026-07-26T22:59:54.029046135Z.

VERDICT. The production guard was correct. The retained quality-gate failure reported `Complete` because the fixture produced no governed-byte transition during that scan; it was a fixture defect, not an FL-INV-07 promotion defect. Commit `09abd62feb9047eb102c7c58154da093fa029d60` repairs the fixture without changing or widening the production authority assertion.

ROOT CAUSES AND REPAIR. Three independent fixture faults were measured. First, writer starvation delayed the first completed write until 573 ms after fixture creation, after the guard had finished. Second, in-place `fs::write` exposed an `O_TRUNC` empty window that both snapshots could sample; emptying both churn files in the retained fixture reproduced the observed `fnv1a64:d5b7f85ed50f59a4` exactly, while unchanged contents produced `fnv1a64:2ec17154d5cc0332`. Third, `yield_now` could starve the writer to zero cycles under load. The repaired fixture uses a completion handshake, stage-then-rename atomic publication, a continuously runnable writer, and churn paths at both governed traversal extremes so a completed cycle inside the window and a changed bound root are the same assertion.

DISCRIMINATION. The deterministic sibling `one_governed_byte_moves_the_bound_root_and_a_quiet_root_holds_still` proves both sensitivity and inertness: one changed byte at each traversal extreme moves the root between runs, while a quiet root and a transition between runs remain `Complete`. The concurrent test proves churn within one scan yields `Authority::Incomplete`, verdict `inconclusive`, exit 3, unequal governed roots, and `SOURCE_CHANGED`. Three production mutants were independently killed: deleting the drift finding and reusing the first digest for the second scan were killed only by the concurrent test; ignoring file bytes in the digest was killed by both tests.

MEASURED RESULT. Final code flaked 0/250 at load about 23 and 0/60 at load 107 on a 64-core host; the intermediate atomic-rewrite form was 0/200. Before repair the fixture failed 1/60 and 1/80. Main-tree package gates recorded in the landing commit were: `cargo fmt --check` exit 0; warnings-denied clippy for structure-guard exit 0; `cargo test -p structure-guard` exit 0, 205 tests across 7 targets. UBS completed with findings and accounted for the one Rust input: criticals remained 4 -> 4, no critical intersected a changed hunk; this is not called UBS-clean.

ARTIFACT PROVENANCE. The original failing bundle still existed when this judgement was written, but `target/` is ephemeral and is not the durable closure anchor. Its current digests are: `bundle.complete.json` ed417ba43ee52389f15ef442f4e945ef17791b0597555406bb127d66811502be; `manifest.json` 423139050f565a0bc5f0e5f8347d2a713ed522feb3e7020780863f2382da98f2; `run.ndjson` b312ec5705a6d2d41eb45eb6cb54d8a1226b236ffdfea9f43a3d14756e24d31c; `run.validation.json` 467022dde33ce41762f6a41bb5a6820e62ccdae179b096ac05a2c38d2847fb41. The durable anchors for this closure are this immutable post-close comment, commit `09abd62feb9047eb102c7c58154da093fa029d60`, and the tracked tests at `tools/structure-guard/tests/authority.rs`.

LIMIT. The landing evidence is package-scoped; the full `scripts/check.sh` gate was not rerun after the repair and this judgement does not claim that it was. The original committed failing bundle remains evidence that the gate caught the fixture failure, not evidence of the repair.

title: W7 Verdict: metamorphic solver and certificate campaign
