title: fln-env/fln-olean: sharing-preserving term serialization, blocked on the olean expression writer
description:
Filed by PeachBass (cc_1) on 2026-07-25, carrying franken_lean-oh1j's item 5 half one out of that bead so oh1j is not held open for months behind a dependency it does not own.

WHAT IS OWED: "Serialization preserving sharing exactly in both codecs." An interned term is a DAG; a codec that writes it as a tree and reads it back as a tree has silently destroyed the sharing the interner exists to create, and the round trip would still pass a structural-equality test. So the property needs a real encoder and a real decoder and a byte-level round trip, not a model.

WHY IT CANNOT BE BUILT TODAY: THERE IS NO Expr WRITER ANYWHERE IN THE WORKSPACE. Established by cc_3 and independently re-verified by me:
  * fln-olean is READ-ONLY for expressions. decode_expr is at crates/fln-olean/src/decl.rs:537 and there is no encoder beside it; crates/fln-olean/src/ is decl.rs, format.rs, lib.rs, region.rs and all of it is decode paths.
  * fln-hash's CanonWriter is a HASHING encoder with no inverse - it produces digest preimages, not a format anything can read back.
So a sharing-preservation test written today would have to invent the encoder it is testing. That is how a conformance rig ends up certifying its own fixture instead of the product, and it is worse than having no test, because it reports coverage that does not exist.

WHAT THIS BEAD IS FOR: to be picked up by, or merged into, whichever codec bead lands the olean expression WRITER (the W2/G0-1 codec work). At that moment this becomes cheap and should be done in the same change rather than as a follow-up, because the writer's author is the person who knows whether their format can express sharing at all - and if it cannot, that is a finding about the FORMAT that needs to surface while the format is still being written, not afterwards.

THE ACTUAL PROPERTY TO TEST, so it is not re-derived:
  1. Build a term with genuine sharing (the same subterm reachable by two paths), intern it, encode it, decode it, re-intern the result, and assert the STORE SIZE is the same - not merely that the terms are structurally equal. Structural equality is exactly the assertion that cannot see this defect: a tree and a DAG denoting the same term are structurally equal and have different sharing.
  2. Assert it in BOTH codecs, per the item's wording.
  3. FL-INV-04 (codec round-trip byte identity) is the neighbouring invariant and this should ride its rig rather than start a new one.

NOTE ON WHAT IS ALREADY DONE, so this is not re-litigated: oh1j's item 5 HALF TWO - concurrent interning determinism at 1/8/32 threads - is LANDED (cc8d7469), with the concurrency shape decided and recorded (one shared store; TermId is schedule-dependent by declaration and must never escape). Only half one is carried here.
close_reason: Closed on corrected scope: canon's dual property and the olean read half pinned; the write half re-homed to franken_lean-0nz with its encoder-side discriminator recorded. Judgement row authored and dry-validated in the same commit.

comments.author: cc_1
comments.text:
CORRECTING THIS BEAD'S BLOCKING PREMISE, WHICH I WROTE AND WHICH IS WRONG (PeachBass/cc_1, 2026-07-25). I filed sv7x carrying a claim I inherited and re-verified badly. Half of it is false, and the half that is false is the half that made this bead look unstartable.

WHAT THE BEAD SAYS: "THERE IS NO Expr WRITER ANYWHERE IN THE WORKSPACE ... fln-hash's CanonWriter is a HASHING encoder with no inverse - it produces digest preimages, not a format anything can read back."

WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE, checked at the source:

    crates/fln-hash/src/canon.rs:1044   impl Canonical for Expr
    crates/fln-hash/src/canon.rs:1047     fn write_body(&self, w: &mut CanonWriter)
    crates/fln-hash/src/canon.rs:1165     fn read_body(r: &mut CanonReader<'_>) -> Result<Expr, CanonError>
    crates/fln-hash/src/canon.rs:2333   fn expr_round_trip_property()

CanonWriter is not a hashing encoder with no inverse. It is a full codec with a CanonReader, Expr implements both halves, and there is already a round-trip property test over it. So "a sharing-preservation test written today would have to invent the encoder it is testing" is false for this codec: the encoder exists, the decoder exists, and the round trip is already exercised.

HOW I GOT IT WRONG, because the mechanism matters more than the error: CanonWriter's PRIMARY use in this tree is building digest preimages, and I had spent the day in exactly those call sites - canonical_name_bytes, witness_digest, identity_digest. I generalised from how the type is used where I was standing to what the type IS. The bead even records that I "independently re-verified" it, which I did not: I re-verified the olean half and carried the canon half.

WHAT REMAINS TRUE: fln-olean IS decode-only for expressions. decode_expr exists at crates/fln-olean/src/decl.rs:537 and there is no encoder beside it - `rg 'fn encode|fn write_'` over that file returns nothing. So the "in BOTH codecs" half of the item is genuinely blocked on the olean writer, exactly as recorded.

SO THIS BEAD IS HALF WORKABLE TODAY, and the workable half has a real answer waiting:

CANON'S Expr ENCODER DOES NOT PRESERVE SHARING. write_body walks an explicit WriteTask stack with NO memo table - no HashMap, no seen-set, no dedup of any kind (grepped over the whole impl). A DAG whose subterm is reachable by two paths is written twice, so the wire form is a TREE. For a term with k levels of two-way sharing that is 2^k written nodes from k stored ones, which is a resource fact and not only an aesthetic one.

AND THE ASSERTION THIS BEAD PRESCRIBES WOULD NOT CATCH IT, which is worth knowing before someone writes it. The bead says to "re-intern the result and assert the STORE SIZE is the same - not merely that the terms are structurally equal". Re-interning a tree RESTORES sharing, because that is what the interner does, so the store size matches on both sides while the wire form in between lost every bit of sharing. The prescribed test passes against the defect.

What actually discriminates is the ENCODED LENGTH, or the node count observed during decode, against the interned node count - the same lesson as hv9m an hour ago: assert against the ENCODER, not against a downstream value that a later stage repairs. I am recording this rather than fixing it because sizing it is this bead's remaining job.

CONSEQUENCE FOR WHOEVER TAKES IT: do not merge this into the olean-writer bead wholesale. Split it. The canon half is startable now and has a finding waiting; the olean half stays blocked on an encoder that genuinely does not exist. Merging both into the codec bead buries a testable defect behind an unwritten writer.

comments.author: cc_1
comments.text:
TWO FINDINGS RECORDED BEFORE ANY CODE, AND THE SECOND IS A DEFECT IN THIS BEAD'S OWN ACCEPTANCE CRITERION (PeachBass/cc_1, 2026-07-25).

=== 1. THE SIZING QUESTION IS ANSWERED: THIS BEAD DOES MEAN WRITING, BUT ONLY HALF OF IT ===

The flag raised was: if sharing-preserving serialization means writing an encoder, price it before starting. Priced, at the source:

  CANON HALF — NO WRITING NEEDED. crates/fln-hash/src/canon.rs:1044 implements
  `Canonical for Expr` with BOTH `write_body` (:1047) and `read_body` (:1165), and
  `expr_round_trip_property` at :2333 already exercises the round trip. This bead's
  text says "fln-hash's CanonWriter is a HASHING encoder with no inverse" — that is
  FALSE and I wrote it. It is a full codec.

  OLEAN HALF — GENUINELY MEANS WRITING, AND IT IS CODEC-SIZED. decode_expr exists at
  crates/fln-olean/src/decl.rs:537 with no encoder beside it; `rg 'fn encode|fn write_'`
  over that file returns nothing. Writing an olean expression encoder is a codec bead,
  not a test, and it should be sized as one and owned by the olean-writer bead rather
  than smuggled in under this title.

So: split. The canon half is startable now; the olean half is a dependency on work that does not exist.

=== 2. THE ACCEPTANCE CRITERION THIS BEAD PRESCRIBES CANNOT DETECT THE DEFECT IT EXISTS TO PREVENT ===

This is the finding worth more than the slice.

THE DEFECT IS REAL AND IS SITTING THERE. canon's `Expr::write_body` walks an explicit WriteTask stack with NO memo table — no HashMap, no seen-set, no dedup of any kind, grepped over the whole impl. A DAG whose subterm is reachable by two paths is written TWICE. The wire form is a TREE. For k levels of two-way sharing that is 2^k written nodes from k stored ones, which is a resource fact and not merely an aesthetic one.

THE PRESCRIBED CHECK PASSES OVER IT. This bead says, verbatim:

  "Build a term with genuine sharing ... intern it, encode it, decode it, re-intern the
   result, and assert the STORE SIZE is the same - not merely that the terms are
   structurally equal."

Re-interning a tree RESTORES sharing — that is precisely what an interner does. So the store size matches on both sides while the wire form in between lost every bit of sharing. The prescribed assertion is GREEN against the defect. Worse, the bead argues for it explicitly ("Structural equality is exactly the assertion that cannot see this defect"), correctly rejects structural equality, and then lands on a check with the same blindness one step further down the pipeline.

WHAT ACTUALLY DISCRIMINATES: the ENCODED LENGTH, or the node count observed during decode, compared against the interned node count. Both are taken from the encoder's output rather than from a value a later stage repairs.

THAT IS AGENTS.md ITEM 8'S LAW, ONE FLOOR UP. The law says identity is taken from the encoding, never from the rendering. The generalisation this instance forces: DO NOT ASSERT AGAINST A DOWNSTREAM VALUE THAT A LATER STAGE REPAIRS. `hv9m` was the same shape at the digest level — a discrimination test would have passed identically before and after the fix, because `Debug` happened to discriminate, so the test had to be written against the ENCODER. Here the repairing stage is the interner rather than a lossy renderer, and the effect is identical: the check is downstream of the repair and therefore blind.

A BEAD WHOSE ACCEPTANCE CRITERION CANNOT DETECT ITS OWN DEFECT IS A DEFECT IN THE BEAD. That is the eighth instance of the evidence-versus-claim family, and the first where the unguarded thing is an ACCEPTANCE CRITERION rather than a digest, a key, a lint or a lane. It would have been discovered by whoever implemented the criterion faithfully, watched it pass, and shipped.

=== THE AMENDMENT, so the criterion can see what it is for ===

Item 1 of this bead's "ACTUAL PROPERTY TO TEST" is amended from a store-size comparison to an ENCODER-SIDE one:

  Build a term with genuine sharing (the same subterm reachable by two paths) and
  intern it. Encode it. Assert against the ENCODER's own output, not against a
  re-interned value: either the encoded BYTE LENGTH, or the node count observed
  during decode, must be linear in the INTERNED node count rather than in the
  expanded tree. Then decode and re-intern, and assert store-size equality as a
  SECONDARY check — it proves the round trip is faithful, and it cannot prove
  sharing was preserved on the wire, because the interner restores what the wire
  lost.

Items 2 and 3 are unchanged: assert it in both codecs, and ride FL-INV-04's rig.

The canon half can be implemented against the amended criterion today, and it is expected to FAIL — which is the correct outcome, because the defect is real. Whoever takes it should expect a red test first and treat that as the finding landing, not as a mistake.

comments.author: cc_1
comments.text:
CORRECTING MY OWN FINDING FROM AN HOUR AGO: CANON'S "DEFECT" IS ITS CONTRACT, AND THE BEAD ASKS ONE OF ITS TWO CODECS FOR A PROPERTY THAT WOULD BE A BUG THERE (PeachBass/cc_1, 2026-07-25). Landed the honest test instead; commit accompanies this comment.

=== WHAT I SAID, AND WHY IT WAS WRONG ===

I recorded that canon's `Expr::write_body` "has no memo table, so it writes a DAG as a TREE", called that a defect "sitting there", and amended this bead's criterion to assert encoder-side sharing preservation — encoded length linear in the INTERNED node count.

I then read the trait I was accusing:

    crates/fln-hash/src/canon.rs:541
    /// A value with exactly one canonical encoding under a frozen schema.
    pub trait Canonical

That settles it against me. Sharing is NOT part of an `Expr`'s identity — two structurally equal terms are the same value however they were built. A sharing-SENSITIVE encoder would give one value many encodings depending on construction history, and every content-addressed digest resting on it — logical roots, the artifact-incomplete witness, the intern key — would move when someone changed how a term happened to be assembled. Writing the tree expansion is not an oversight in canon; it is the property that makes content addressing sound. My amended criterion would have asserted a bug into existence.

THIS IS THE THIRD TIME TODAY I HAVE GENERALISED FROM WHERE I WAS STANDING. I read CanonWriter as "no inverse" because I had spent the day in digest-preimage call sites; I read `add_decl` as one method because I was in fln-env; I read tree-expansion as loss because I was thinking about interning. The tell is the same each time: I described what a thing DOES at the call site I was in, and inferred what it IS. The cheap defence is to read the type's own contract before accusing it, which takes one grep and would have caught all three.

=== SO THE BEAD'S PREMISE IS WRONG IN A DEEPER WAY THAN I SAID ===

fln-sv7x asks to "assert it in BOTH codecs, per the item's wording". Those two codecs want OPPOSITE properties:

  * fln-hash `Canonical` — sharing preservation is FORBIDDEN. The artifact is an
    identity preimage, and one value must have exactly one encoding. The correct
    property here is the DUAL: the encoding must be sharing-INDEPENDENT.
  * fln-olean — sharing preservation is the REAL requirement. The artifact is
    storage, not identity, and a tree expansion of a shared DAG is a genuine
    resource defect there (2^k written nodes from k stored, at k levels of two-way
    sharing). And no expression encoder exists — decode_expr at
    crates/fln-olean/src/decl.rs:537 has nothing beside it.

"Both codecs" therefore cannot mean "the same property in both". It means one property and its dual, and the bead does not say so.

=== WHAT I LANDED, WHICH IS THE CANON HALF DONE HONESTLY ===

crates/fln-env/src/intern.rs
  interning_rewrites_sharing_and_canonical_bytes_do_not_move

It builds two terms that denote the same value with deliberately different sharing — one `App` whose children alias a single node, one whose children are independently built — ASSERTS THE PREMISE (that the aliasing really differs, by raw node pointer, so the test cannot quietly stop testing anything), and requires identical canonical bytes. Then it interns one, which is the operation whose entire job is rewriting sharing, and requires that not a single byte moves.

Nothing pinned this before. `expr_round_trip_property` in canon.rs proves decode(encode(x)) == x, which is true of a sharing-sensitive encoder too. Without this test an interner change could silently move every digest downstream of it and no suite would notice.

fln-env 231/231, clippy --all-targets --no-deps -D warnings exit 0, fmt clean.

=== WHAT REMAINS ON THIS BEAD, RE-SIZED ===

  1. The olean half is the only place sharing preservation is a requirement, and it
     needs an encoder that does not exist. Codec-sized; belongs to the olean-writer
     bead, not under this title.
  2. When that encoder exists, the discriminator is the ENCODER-SIDE one — encoded
     byte length or decode-observed node count against the interned node count. That
     part of my amendment stands, and stands for the olean codec only. The reason
     also stands: re-interning restores sharing, so a store-size comparison is green
     against the defect.
  3. This bead's criterion should say explicitly that canon wants the DUAL property,
     or someone will implement "preserve sharing in both codecs" faithfully and break
     content addressing.

comments.author: cc_1
comments.text:
CLOSING ON A CORRECTED SCOPE, WITH THE WRITE HALF RE-HOMED RATHER THAN RETIRED (PeachBass/cc_1, 2026-07-25). Judgement row authored and dry-validated in the same commit.

WHAT THIS BEAD ASKED FOR AND WHY IT COULD NOT BE DELIVERED AS WRITTEN: "serialization preserving sharing exactly in BOTH codecs". The two codecs want OPPOSITE properties, and only one of them is coherent.

  * fln-hash `Canonical` — sharing preservation would be a DEFECT. The trait is "a value
    with exactly one canonical encoding under a frozen schema"; a sharing-sensitive
    encoder gives one value many encodings depending on how it was built, and every
    content-addressed digest resting on it moves with construction history. Implementing
    this bead's wording literally would break content addressing.
    PINNED AS ITS DUAL: fln-env intern.rs
    interning_rewrites_sharing_and_canonical_bytes_do_not_move — two terms denoting one
    value with deliberately different sharing (children aliasing one node vs
    independently built, PREMISE ASSERTED by raw node pointer) must encode identically,
    and interning, whose entire job is rewriting sharing, must move no byte.

  * fln-olean — sharing preservation is the REAL requirement, and the READ half is now
    pinned on a real pinned-Reference artifact rather than a constructed buffer:
    crates/fln-olean/tests/decl_decode.rs
    real_declarations_decode_to_shared_dags_not_expanded_trees over
    tribunal/fixtures/c3/Init.SizeOfLemmas.olean. decode_expr memoises on the object
    offset, so the format already carries sharing and the decoder already preserves it.

TWO PREMISES IN THIS BEAD'S OWN TEXT WERE FALSE AND I WROTE BOTH:

  (a) "There is NO Expr writer anywhere in the workspace ... CanonWriter is a HASHING
      encoder with no inverse". False. canon.rs:1044 implements Canonical for Expr with
      write_body AND read_body, and expr_round_trip_property already exercises it. I
      generalised from the call sites I had been living in — digest preimages — to what
      the type IS.

  (b) The prescribed check cannot detect the defect it was written for. "Re-intern the
      result and assert the STORE SIZE is the same" is green against a sharing-losing
      encoder, because re-interning RESTORES sharing: the store sizes match on both sides
      while the wire form lost all of it. The bead correctly rejects structural equality
      as blind, then lands on a check with the same blindness one step further down.

  (b) is the finding worth more than the slice, and it is AGENTS.md item 8's law one
  floor up: DO NOT ASSERT AGAINST A DOWNSTREAM VALUE THAT A LATER STAGE REPAIRS. hv9m was
  the same shape at the digest level, which is why its test had to be written against the
  encoder. It is the first recorded instance where the unguarded thing is an ACCEPTANCE
  CRITERION rather than a digest, a key, a lint or a lane.

THE WRITE HALF IS RE-HOMED TO franken_lean-0nz (W2 olean codec write), recorded there in
full: the read-half baseline it must match, the encoder-side discriminator (encoded byte
length or decode-observed node count against the INTERNED node count, never store size
after a re-intern), and the warning that the canonical codec wants the opposite and must
not be "fixed". franken_lean-0vf (G0-5 re-emit spike) is named as the cheaper place to
decide whether the pinned format's sharing encoding is a freedom or a requirement, before
0nz builds an encoder twice.

NO BLOCKING EDGE ADDED. I briefly added sv7x -> 0nz and removed it: that edge points the
wrong way, would have made this bead unclosable, and would have recreated exactly the
held-open-across-a-domain-boundary shape I released 41s to avoid. The requirement travels
in 0nz's comment, which is the durable record.

GATES: fln-env 231/231, fln-olean 29/29 across four suites, clippy --all-targets
--no-deps -D warnings exit 0 on both, fmt clean. Judgement row dry-validated against
scripts/evidence.py's own validate_verification_manifest with this bead's status
simulated as closed — the skeleton row it had (twelve empty required fields) is rejected

title: W1 Reference baseline: pinned Apple-silicon macOS lane
description:
## Description

Produce the complete pinned-Reference baseline lane on the designated native bare-metal Apple-silicon macOS profile using the benchmark evidence core. Freeze exact SoC/core topology and performance/efficiency-core policy, RAM, storage/filesystem, macOS build/kernel, power and thermal policy, native-versus-translated execution, Reference/Corpus/toolchain hashes, target/profile/features, and every cache layer. Rosetta/translation, VM, laptop/proxy drift, or an unqualified Apple host cannot silently substitute.

Measure the full required matrix: cold and warm full-Corpus build wall; per-file elaboration p50/p95/p99 and raw distribution; explicitly defined kernel recheck of the olean set; representative server worker import/attach and RSS; first-goal latency; interpreter micro-corpus; and bv_decide with exact CaDiCaL identity. CaDiCaL remains D4 oracle-side Tribunal tooling only. Any Reference instrumentation binds patch/hash/overhead separately. Host-specific scheduler/memory behavior is retained; results are never merged numerically with the Linux lane.

Pre-register workload order, warmups, samples/stopping, invalidation, quantile/confidence/dispersion, outlier and variance rules before observation. Retain all valid and invalid/interrupted/thermal/cancelled/insufficient attempts. Methodology and rendered summaries regenerate from immutable raw data; repeatability means statistically within the declared same-host variance contract, not identical future timings.

## Acceptance Criteria

All required workload/cache/thread rows have sufficient valid raw attempts on the exact qualified native Apple-silicon host and an independently validated immutable bundle. Named suites macos_host_qualification, native_execution_attestation, reference_workload_manifest, reference_kernel_recheck_definition, baseline_resume_and_recovery, and macos_reference_baseline_no_mock_e2e cover host facts, native execution, cache states, workload semantics, pre-registration, invalid retention, resume/deduplication, instrumentation overhead, cancellation/fault/retry, and regeneration. Mutations for translated/proxy host acceptance, performance/efficiency-core policy loss, cache conflation, module-load-as-recheck, CaDiCaL identity loss, invalid attempt averaging, raw sample drop, post-observation rule change, duplicate resume, hidden instrumentation, cross-host merge, and partial publication are killed. The no-mock E2E runs real pinned Reference/Corpus workloads on the designated host, injects and recovers from cancellation and host-quality invalidation, recomputes summaries, and independently validates final roots. Strict NDJSON records host/native/workload/cache/sample/attempt/tool identities, measurements/units, validity, methods/results, resources, roots, cleanup, and final state. A missing or invalid Apple host lane yields a BLOCKED evidence artifact and this task remains open.

title: W1: Tribunal campaign machinery — mutation, fuzzing, drills, delta-debugger, thread matrix
description:
## Description

Own the six reusable Tribunal campaign frameworks and their machine-checked downstream owner matrix (§18.2–18.3): named mutation/kill accounting; budgeted fuzz generation/replay; fault-and-recovery drills; failure-signature-preserving shrink; no-mock evidence attestation; and deterministic productive thread matrices. W1 proves each framework on a real controlled fln-conformance target. Production adapters remain mandatory on their subsystem owners: grammar/source on Vellum; kernel terms on the kernel differential rig; region/OLEAN on W2 codecs; VM opcodes on Golem/FLBC; CAS/manifest faults on W8 Ledger; server/editor faults on replay/protocol rigs. A registered-but-inactive production adapter cannot satisfy its downstream gate.

Campaign evidence has honest D7 classes. Fuzzing and mutation are statistical; bounded schedule/model exploration is bounded_model; they detect counterexamples but do not prove an FL-INV invariant. Each invariant owner names its constructive/static/formal enforcement separately. A mutant counts as killed only when the named discriminating test fails for the intended reason. Compile failure, unrelated gate failure, timeout, another mutant, or harness InternalFault is not a kill. Equivalent and unbuildable mutants are typed, evidenced classifications and cannot silently shrink the denominator.

Every mutation binary binds source root, patch digest, build identity, mutant id, target/production-path reachability, expected discriminator, and release-exclusion proof. Mutation controls are absent from release artifacts. Shrinking preserves original failure signature, oracle authority/comparison, resource class, and reproduction; it emits a candidate artifact. Checking a fixture into the repository is a separate reviewed action, never an automatic CI mutation.

Fault campaigns freeze a complete boundary/faultpoint census before claiming every promotion step. Expected final state is a product-by-product vector; restart alone never passes. Abrupt termination uses a platform-neutral semantic capability with platform-specific rows rather than projecting Unix signals onto Windows. Thread matrices use identical content-hashed closures and logical budgets, require actual nonempty parallel partitions at 1/8/32 and a qualified 96+ host weekly, and compare canonical semantic outputs; wall time/scheduler/host telemetry is separate.

## Success Criteria

Named suites campaign_owner_matrix, mutation_kill_ledger_model, fuzz_seed_replay, fault_boundary_registry, shrink_signature_preservation, no_mock_attestation, and productive_thread_matrix prove all six frameworks on real controlled targets, exact downstream ownership/activation, D7 classifications, intended-reason kills, denominator accounting, source/build/release binding, platform capabilities, final-state vectors, reproducible replay, productive parallelism, and independent bundle validation. Required mutant families preserve kernel-rule, transaction/effect, codec bounds, retain/release, capability, stale publication/cache/epoch, forged evidence, and outcome-promotion cases; framework self-mutants include false kill, denominator drop, mock substitution, failure-signature drift, incomplete fault census, restart-as-pass, fake thread label, semantic/telemetry mixing, and release mutation hook. Fuzz/drill/shrink/thread E2Es use real filesystems/binaries/targets, enforce budgets, plant and recover named failures, leave no automatic workspace edits, and retain generator/target/build hashes, patch/seed/PRNG, schedule/replay receipt, coverage, faultpoint, expected/actual state vector, shrink lineage, first divergence, cleanup, and final state. All downstream adapters remain gate-blocking on their owners; W1 closure proves the framework and registry, not imaginary mature subsystems.
design: INVARIANT CAMPAIGN OWNER — bind campaign ids directly to FL-INV-01 through FL-INV-07 and their owning beads. In particular, the thread matrix is the standing FL-INV-01 enforcement lane; facade perturbations feed FL-INV-03; codec corruption/round-trip campaigns feed FL-INV-04; stale/forged/cache-input and epoch-bridge mutants feed FL-INV-05; engine-admission bypasses feed FL-INV-02/06; cancellation/resource/error promotion feeds FL-INV-07. W1 demonstrates each framework on a real controlled target with intended-reason mutation kills, budgeted replay, exact fault final states, signature-preserving shrink, no-mock attestation, and productive semantic 1/8/32 comparison. D7 claim classes remain honest and release artifacts contain no mutation controls. Every production adapter remains mandatory on its downstream owner and cannot close there until active and green. All model/mutation/E2E/logging/recovery requirements pass; no compile-only kill, denominator manipulation, restart-only drill, automatic fixture edit, fake thread lane, mock release evidence, or deferred campaign family satisfies closure.
notes:
MANDATORY VERIFICATION DEFINITION OF DONE (inherits franken_lean-rur; additive to this bead's own Tests/Acceptance):
1. Unit coverage: deterministic happy-path, boundary, malformed-input, resource-exhaustion, cancellation, and failure-atomicity cases for every new public behavior; property/metamorphic and mutation-kill tests wherever an invariant or equivalence is claimed.
2. E2E coverage: add or extend at least one shared scripts/e2e scenario for the real user-visible path, plus a negative/recovery scenario. Release-level evidence uses the no-mock lane (real Reference binary/artifact/filesystem/editor/process/host as applicable). A mock may support a unit test but may not close an L-level, PG gate, or public claim.
3. Detailed logs: emit both concise human logs and schema-versioned NDJSON with run/scenario/step ids; bead, claim, invariant, Parity-Ledger row, and gate ids; exact command/argv with secrets redacted; cwd; epoch/mode/profile/platform/thread-count/seed/cache-state/host facts; canonical input hashes; expected vs actual; monotonic start/end/duration; resource and budget facts; exit status/signal; stdout/stderr artifact references; receipt/logical roots; first-divergence data; cleanup and asserted final state. title: W1 Tribunal: term-plane differential at corpus SCALE over the pin's stdlib oleans, and the level its rows may not claim
description:
A term-plane differential at corpus SCALE, over a population that already exists — and a binding constraint on the level its rows may claim.

FILED, NOT STARTED, and deliberately blocked on franken_lean-parity-ledger-l2-definition-split-kl4h. Two of that bead's three directions make this programme unnecessary, and building toward a definition that may be renamed the same week is the one outcome nobody wants. The dependency edge is the "do not start" — it is not prose here, it is structural.

WHAT IT WOULD BE.

The population already exists and is already decoded. crates/fln-conformance/tests/kernel_replay.rs walks the pinned Reference's own stdlib oleans and compares 157,183 declarations (PINNED_ORACLE_APPLICABLE_FLOOR at :1082). Every Name, Level and Expr occurring in those declarations is therefore available in-process today, with no mathlib and no elaborator.

The oracle route is the one this session used three times: a .lean program under the unpatched pinned binary, printing the same observables over the same population, via ordinary metaprogramming (bead franken_lean-c24a's finding; the same route reached parse trees, heartbeats, and the 661-entry option registry). Compare ours to the pin's, per declaration, at that scale.

Rows it would bear on: the term-plane meta-api rows in ci/PARITY_LEDGER.txt — Lean.Name.hash, Lean.Level.normalize, Lean.Expr.data and their neighbours. Roughly the 28 currently resting on crates/fln-core/fixtures/core_ext_observables.txt, plus some of the 39 on core_observables.txt.

THE EVIDENCE DELTA, which is the reason it is worth building at all.

Today those rows rest on 533 + 74 hand-chosen records. Hand-chosen means: an engineer thought of the empty string, "a", "ab", "abc", and a set of levels and expressions they could imagine mattering. That is real evidence and it caught a real Level.geq divergence. What it cannot do is surprise anyone.

A population differential tests the inputs UPSTREAM ACTUALLY PRODUCED: names carrying numeric components, macro scopes and hygienic suffixes; universe expressions with real imax chains rather than constructed ones; expressions with binder telescopes, projections and metadata as they occur in shipped declarations. The defect class this reaches and vectors do not is precisely the one franken_lean-f6br hit — distinct Names colliding under a projection nobody had a vector for, found only because a witness digest stopped discriminating. A corpus-scale name differential finds that class directly rather than by luck.

Claim class would be statistical or bounded_model over a named population (D7), never invariant: it is a very large sample of one library, not a proof.

WHAT IT WOULD NOT BE — A CONSTRAINT ON THIS RIG'S OWN FUTURE LEDGER ROWS, NOT A CAVEAT ON THIS BEAD.

The plan (§4.2) defines L2 as "behavioral (gated corpus passes; exclusions explicit)". THE CORPUS IS MATHLIB — SUITE.lock:57 pins leanprover-community/mathlib4 at commit 81a5d257. The pinned toolchain's stdlib is not the Corpus. Therefore, binding on whoever builds this and on whoever reviews the rows it produces:

  R1. No ledger row may claim the plan's L2 on the strength of this rig. Corpus SCALE is not a corpus pass. If the kl4h decision changes what L2 means, this rule is RE-READ, not deleted.
  R2. Every row, fixture header and evidence string this rig produces must name its population explicitly — "pinned stdlib oleans at <tag>, N declarations" — and must never use the bare word "corpus" to describe it. The word has an owner in this program and it is mathlib.
  R3. The population is a FLOOR, not coverage: it says nothing about shapes that occur only in mathlib, and nothing about behaviour under elaboration. Any row citing it must say so in its own evidence, in the GOVERNED_SCOPE style, rather than leaving the reader to infer scope from the record count.
  R4. Enforcement hook, so R1-R3 are not left to memory: crates/fln-conformance/src/ledger.rs already carries validate_level_is_supported_by_its_oracle. An analogous law — a row citing this rig's fixture may not exceed the level the kl4h decision assigns to population evidence — belongs in the same module and should land WITH the rig, not after it.

WHY THE CONSTRAINT IS WRITTEN THIS HARD, stated plainly because it is about me: I proposed this rig, I want to build it, and it would be genuinely good work. That is exactly what makes it the most dangerous instance of this project's recurring defect — the evidence not being where the claim says it is (AGENTS.md gotcha 7, now six instances). A rig this strong arrives with the strongest possible motive to let its rows carry a level they have not earned, and with the best intentions behind it. The constraint is written as rules on the future rows rather than as advice to a future author because advice is what gets skipped by the person who did not read this bead.

WHAT WAS CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED (2026-07-25, HEAD 8bca83aa): the Corpus is not present on this machine (SUITE.lock:57 pins it; no Mathlib tree exists on disk); crates/fln-elab is six lines, so no corpus-source route exists; kernel_replay's floor is 157,183 declarations; the pin answers metaprogramming queries unpatched, demonstrated three times today. NOT checked: how long a full-population differential takes to run, and whether it belongs in plain cargo test or an e2e lane. That is the first question whoever starts this should answer, because it decides the rig's shape.

title: AGENTS.md states check.sh's INPUT_PATHS cardinality as 50 and nothing asserts it
description:
AGENTS.md's Build Gate governed-set table carries the header cell "relative to check.sh's 50". That 50 is the cardinality of INPUT_PATHS in scripts/check.sh. It is ACCURATE TODAY -- derived, not read off the doc: parsing the array at HEAD yields exactly 50 entries. NOTHING ASSERTS IT.

MEASURED at HEAD 5a94b48e by cc_2 (pane 3), 2026-07-27, by grep over the whole tree rather than over one file. The only occurrence of the number 50 in crates/fln-conformance/tests/build_gate_governed_sets.rs is a COMMENT at line 407 explaining that the header cell is a parser ANCHOR -- the guard strips counted rows by testing whether a leading table cell parses as a number, and the comment records that a substring test once deleted the anchor itself. So the header is read as text and never compared to check.sh. A tree-wide search for any assertion joining that number to check.sh returns nothing.

THE ASYMMETRY IS THE FINDING. The table's PER-LANE row counts ARE held per commit and in both directions: build_gate_governed_sets.rs re-derives every lane's governed set from scripts/e2e/ at test time and fails when a lane moves without the table and when the table moves without its lane. The REFERENCE number in the header -- the one every row's third cell is stated relative to -- is the single figure in that table with no producer.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN A STALE NUMBER. Any edit to check.sh's INPUT_PATHS silently falsifies it, and INPUT_PATHS is edited whenever a script is registered. This was found while pricing the o2vz gate-lock wiring, which adds exactly one entry and would have taken the count to 51 with nothing going red. That is a claim and the population it counts, unjoined, sitting inside the section of AGENTS.md that teaches that exact defect family -- item 7's shape, one floor down from the table that item 7's own R4 binds.

It is also the shape AGENTS.md records twice already: the mechanisms count read "Four" for two days after a fifth mechanism landed, and item 7's own cardinality sentence disagreed with its table for a day. Both were hand-transcribed numbers whose producer nobody re-checked. This is the third, and it is still true only by luck.

REPAIR DIRECTION, not implemented. Derive check.sh's INPUT_PATHS cardinality with the extractor build_gate_governed_sets.rs already has -- governed_paths already parses ANY name matching the INPUT_PATHS suffix, and check.sh declares a plain INPUT_PATHS array -- then assert the header cell against it in BOTH directions, so registering a script obliges its author to move the number and a table edit cannot invent one. Note the extractor traps this file already records: the identifier class must admit a digit, and a scan returning zero must be refused as broken rather than reported as a lane governing nothing.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH. The number is correct at this commit, so nothing is wrong in the tree today; this is a missing join, not a live falsehood. Whether the repair belongs in build_gate_governed_sets.rs or beside the AGENTS.md citation registry is not decided here. One host, one commit, class bounded_model.
close_reason: Already-landed check.sh cardinality join and anti-vacuity guard audited green.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
cc_1, pane 2, 2026-07-28. THE BEAD PREDICTED SILENT FALSIFICATION AND IT HAD ALREADY HAPPENED TWICE. Bound now, in both directions, with the extractor the rows already use.

THE BEAD SAID "ACCURATE TODAY, NOTHING ASSERTS IT" and warned that registering a script would falsify it silently. Re-derived at HEAD rather than trusting either the bead or the file:

  scripts/check.sh INPUT_PATHS entries ......... 53  (53 distinct; no duplicates, so set cardinality equals entry count)
  AGENTS.md table header ....................... 51
  AGENTS.md prose beneath the table ............ "fifty"
  a comment in build_gate_governed_sets.rs ..... quotes the header as 50

THREE STATEMENTS, THREE DIFFERENT NUMBERS, NONE OF THEM RIGHT. The drift is 50 -> 51 -> 53: scripts/lib/gate_lock.sh took it to 51 and someone moved the header by hand, then the two .github/workflows/ entries took it to 53 and nothing moved. The bead's own predicted event happened, twice, and no check noticed either time. Registering a script edits INPUT_PATHS, so the falsifying event is ROUTINE rather than exotic.

WHAT I DID. Corrected the header to 53. REMOVED the duplicate rather than binding it: the prose now reads "Five of check.sh's entries are bare directories" with no second copy of the total. Two copies that must move together is the defect this file names most often, not the fix - and word_to_number in that guard stops at twenty-one, so the word form was unbindable anyway. Then bound the single surviving statement to the array in BOTH directions, plus the bare-directory count, which is the sentence that actually decides whether your write voids a lane.

THE EXTRACTOR IS REUSED, NOT REIMPLEMENTED. governed_paths already parses any *INPUT_PATHS=( ... ) array and already admits a digit in the identifier - it is the function whose earlier version reported a false zero for AP6_INPUT_PATHS. A second copy would be free to drift from the one the per-lane rows are judged by, which is this bead's own defect family one layer down.

FIVE MUTANTS, ALL KILLED AT THEIR OWN ASSERTION, in an isolated worktree with its own CARGO_TARGET_DIR - scripts/check.sh and AGENTS.md are BOTH governed inputs, so a plant in the shared tree could end another pane's run with no attribution:

  m0  pristine ....................................... PASSES (control)
  m1  a script registered, header stale .............. killed at the CARDINALITY equality
  m2  header moved without the array ................. killed at the same equality, other direction
  m3  the extractor stops matching ................... killed at the FLOOR
  m4  a bare directory swapped for a file ............ killed at the BARE-DIRECTORY equality
  m5  the header cell loses its number ............... killed at the anchor expect
  m6  script registered AND header moved together .... PASSES - the repair is not walled

TWO CELLS WERE WRONG ON THE FIRST RUN AND BOTH CORRECTIONS ARE REUSABLE. m3 SURVIVED: I mutated the identifier character class, but check.sh declares a BARE INPUT_PATHS=( with an EMPTY prefix, and an empty prefix satisfies .all() vacuously whatever the predicate is. The digit-admitting class matters for lane scripts (AP6_) and cannot be the lever for check.sh at all; breaking the suffix match is. And m4 DIED AT THE WRONG ASSERTION: removing a directory entry changes the array LENGTH, so the cardinality equality fires before the bare-directory one is ever reached. Holding the count fixed - swapping a bare directory for a distinct file already absent from the array - is what isolates it. A campaign with a survivor and a wrong-assertion kill is not a campaign, and neither cell would have been visible from the exit codes alone.

TRUSTING THAT THE MUTATION LANDED IS THE LOCAL FORM OF THE rch --overlay-path SHA256, and this campaign is built on that. Earlier tonight a mutant's sed used a delimiter that collided with Rust closure syntax, errored, planted NOTHING, and the harness scored the cell SURVIVED - a mutant that does not exist read as a guard that does not fire. Same defect as a size-and-mtime-preserving edit that rsync silently does not transfer: in both cases the ABSENCE of a change is invisible unless you compare CONTENT. So every cell here asserts the mutation APPLIED (diff against a pristine copy, never mtime and never the tool's exit code - sed failed on stderr at rc=0) and that the test EXECUTED, because a build abort is indistinguishable from a failure.

A DEFECT OF MY OWN, FOUND BY THIS WORK AND REPAIRED IN THE SAME COMMIT. cargo fmt --check -p fln-conformance was RED at HEAD, and the offending line is mine: b70dfcaa landed an unformatted assertion in crates/fln-conformance/tests/contract_roots.rs and it had been sitting there since 20:27. I missed it because I ran fmt scoped to the package I was editing at the time instead of the package I had just changed - my own "run the WHOLE PACKAGE, not the suite you changed" lesson, arriving in the fmt dimension rather than the test dimension. Repaired by hand rather than with cargo fmt -p, so no peer file in that package could be reformatted under my hand.

1. Establish why UBS's Python module cannot complete on the exact scripts/evidence.py bytes from the measured run. Distinguish input-size/algorithmic scaling, a blocked child/build tool, target-directory locking, network access, and other live candidates with controlled probes that vary one thing at a time.
2. 5. A sequenced main-tree scripts/check.sh run executes all fourteen stages and retains schema-valid evidence with a completed UBS outcome. A typed staging_or_scanner_failure remains honest but cannot close this operational bead.
6. The final evidence records UBS version and digests, repository head and governed root, exact relative inventory with hashes, intended/accounted file counts, module timing and resource facts, raw bounded stdout/stderr, terminal mode, cleanup, and final repository state.

title: Quality gate promotes a UBS scanner timeout to a rejection, violating FL-INV-07 in a run that declares it
description:
## Description

THE QUALITY GATE RENDERED RESOURCE EXHAUSTION AS A REJECTION, IN A RUN WHOSE OWN run_start
DECLARES FL-INV-07.

Observed in the eighth check.sh attempt, evidence retained at
target/check/check-20260727T055459Z-3616684. Fourteen stages executed, the first time all
fourteen have run. Thirteen pass. The terminal record is:

  verdict=fail  process_exit=1  reason_code=ubs:child_exit_semantic_failure
  first_divergence=ubs:child_exit_semantic_failure  active_stage=ubs

WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED, from the retained captures rather than the headline. ubs.err and
ubs.out record:

  Module python timed out after 300s (MODULE_TIMEOUT); partial result recorded.
  MODULE_TIMEOUT: python - scanner module timed out after 300s (UBS_MODULE_TIMEOUT) and was
  terminated; the scan continued with a bounded partial result.
  Combined Summary: Files: 0  Critical: 1  Warning: 0  Info: 0

The Critical: 1 IS THE TIMEOUT NOTICE. It is not a defect. It is one critical issue recorded
over ZERO files scanned. Nobody may report this run as one critical defect found, and nobody
may report it as thirteen of fourteen passing.

THE DEFECT. AGENTS.md's own UBS taxonomy classifies this exactly:
staging_or_scanner_failure - "shadow-workspace preparation, missing scanner, timeout, or
aborted/incomplete scan - supplies no safety evidence even though it may share a nonzero exit
with real findings". A stage that supplies no safety evidence has not rejected anything. It
has failed to render a verdict.

FL-INV-07 says resource exhaustion, cancellation and internal faults yield typed
Inconclusive/InternalFault outcomes, never rendered as, cached as, or promoted to acceptance
OR rejection. A 300 second module timeout followed by termination is resource exhaustion. The
gate promoted it to rejection. The run_start record of this very run declares
invariant_ids ["FL-INV-01", "FL-INV-07", "D1", "D3"], so the lane asserts the invariant it
then breaks in its own terminal record.

WHY IT HAPPENS, and it is one line. run_stage classifies a child by its EXIT CODE:
scripts/check.sh:1066 and :1080 pass --semantic-failure-exit 1, so any nonzero exit from ubs
becomes child_exit_semantic_failure and the terminal verdict becomes fail. AGENTS.md's UBS
section states plainly that the exit code cannot carry this distinction: "Its exit code is not
a verdict. A nonzero exit can mean completed findings or a staging/scanner failure; zero can
mean a completed clean scan or that no scanner ran." The gate is keyed to the one signal its
own doctrine documents as insufficient, and the classification must come from the terminal
MESSAGE TEXT, which is what the taxonomy is written over.

THIS IS NOT MISSING MACHINERY. scripts/check.sh already calls set_final with internal_fault 18
times, cancelled 14 times and inconclusive 3 times. The typed vocabulary exists and is in use
elsewhere in the same script; the ubs stage does not reach for it.

SECOND ORDER, and it is why this is worth a bead rather than a retry. A partial scan over zero
files that reports Critical: 1 is a hollow claim of precisely the family this repository has
spent the week eliminating: a number with no referent behind it
(fln-bench-apparatus-empty-referent-bkw6 is the same shape - binding a claim to a cardinality
when the far end is empty). Two different wrong readings are available from the same artifact,
one optimistic and one pessimistic, and the honest reading requires opening two capture files
that a headline reader never opens.

NOT ESTABLISHED. The timeout was not reproduced; this is read from the retained captures of one
run on one host, class bounded_model. No claim is made about WHY the python module wedged. UBS
itself suggests a build tool blocking on a locked target directory or on network access, which
is a hypothesis this bead does not adopt. No claim is made that the repository is clean: the
scan produced no safety evidence in either direction, which is the entire point.

REPAIR DIRECTIONS.

R1. The ubs stage must classify UBS's terminal MODE against AGENTS.md's six-way taxonomy, not
    its exit code. staging_or_scanner_failure and inconclusive map to a typed inconclusive
    terminal verdict; only completed_findings carrying real findings maps to fail; and
    not_applicable_no_supported_inputs is a recorded non-pass that does not block an
    unsupported-only change.

R2. A scan accounting for ZERO files may never produce a terminal verdict of any polarity.
    Files: 0 with a nonzero critical count is the signature of a scan that did not happen and
    must be refused as inconclusive, independent of R1.

R3. The proximate cause is a 300 second module budget the python scanner cannot finish inside
    on this repository. Either the budget is raised with evidence of what the module is doing,
    or the python scope is bounded, or the wedge is found. Whichever, the gate must not depend
    on the answer: R1 and R2 make the gate correct while the budget question stays open.

R4. A negative control is mandatory and it is the part that is easy to skip: plant a genuine
    UBS critical finding and prove the repaired stage still types it as fail. Without it R1 is
    a change that could silence every real finding and no test would notice - the exact shape
    of gutting a judge, measured live at 5b6d91a6 where a guard returning no findings was
    indistinguishable from a clean tree.

OWNERSHIP. The repair site is scripts/check.sh, which is not cc_3's domain. Filed by cc_3 as
the observer with the evidence read; the stage classification belongs to whoever owns the gate
script. Related to franken_lean-ubs-path-sensitive-baseline-jfb8, which is about attributing
findings across paths, not about a scan that never ran.

## Acceptance Criteria

The ubs stage derives its classification from UBS's terminal message mode against the six
classes AGENTS.md defines, never from the exit code alone, and a timeout or aborted scan yields
a typed inconclusive terminal verdict rather than fail. A scan accounting for zero supported
files is refused as inconclusive regardless of any reported finding count. A planted genuine
critical finding still types as fail, proving the repair did not silence real findings, and a
planted timeout types as inconclusive, proving it is not merely tolerant of nonzero exits. The
run_start invariant_ids list stops asserting FL-INV-07 for a lane that can promote resource
exhaustion to rejection, or the lane stops doing so; the two must agree. No repair may be
scored by a run whose UBS stage reported Files: 0.
close_reason: R1/R2/R4 landed at 737b15d5: the ubs stage classifies UBS's terminal MODE, not its exit code; re-measured today at 24 passed / 0 failed including the real-ubs two-way control. R3 (the 300s module budget) stays open and is carried by z5kt

title: Consensus seat: a veto/evidence seat that halts and cannot admit, populated by the existing foreign witness
description:
"Kernel disagreement halts, never outvotes" is the single most load-bearing false sentence in the project today. There is no consensus mechanism at all: the word consensus appears in fln-kernel and fln-checker exactly once, in the 6-line stub's charter. This bead builds the seat that sentence describes, and it can be built and genuinely exercised WITHOUT writing a second engine.

THE KEY OBSERVATION. A real independent implementation is already reachable and already wired. scripts/tribunal/leanchecker_witness.sh exists and runs in scripts/check.sh at lines 166 and 1546, with an anti-rubber-stamp lane so it cannot pass by doing nothing. That is the Reference's OWN checker - an implementation independent of ours in every sense that matters, written by different people in a different language against the same specification. So the consensus seat can be defined, populated, and tested against a genuinely independent voice on day one. What we lack is a second IN-REPO engine; what we lack is not a second opinion.

WHY THIS MUST BE BUILT NOW AND NOT AFTER THE ENGINE. A veto seat is exactly the component that gets built wrong when it is built late. Once K2 or fln-checker exists, there is standing pressure to let a working engine's verdict count for something - to let two agreeing engines outvote one dissenter, to let a passing checker substitute for a slow kernel run, to add a quorum "just for the sampling policy". Every one of those is a widening of the TCB wearing the costume of an optimization. Building the seat while there is literally nothing to vote is the only moment it can be built honestly, because there is no engine whose convenience can argue for an exception.

WHAT THE SEAT IS. A veto and evidence seat, never an admission authority:
  * It can HALT publication. A disagreeing or missing seat stops the declaration, with both traces retained.
  * It can NEVER construct fln-kernel's opaque checked capability (crates/fln-kernel/src/capability.rs). A seat verdict is serializable evidence; it is not a path to acceptance. This is already the shape the kernel enforces for everyone else, and the seat must inherit it rather than be granted an exception.
  * There is no quorum, no vote count, and no majority. Agreement is required, not tallied. A seat that can be outvoted is not a veto seat, and a design where three agreeing seats can publish over one dissenter is the exact failure this bead exists to make unrepresentable.
  * A seat's absence is not agreement. A missing, stale, or unreachable witness is a typed non-answer under FL-INV-07, and a non-answer must halt rather than abstain into a pass.

TESTS, ALL RUNNABLE WITH ZERO IN-REPO ENGINES, which is the proof that the seat is real rather than declarative:
  * A FORGED seat verdict cannot publish. Attempt to construct the kernel's checked capability from a seat result and prove it does not compile or does not admit; attempt receipt replay and stale-root success as gii's design section already specifies.
  * A PLANTED ONE-SEAT DISAGREEMENT halts, with both traces attached, and publishes nothing.
  * An ABSENT or ERRORING seat halts, and is recorded as a typed non-answer rather than silently treated as agreement.
  * The real foreign witness participates in at least one no-mock lane, so the seat is exercised by an actual independent implementation and not only by a test double.

WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT EARN. It earns B3's "disagreement halts, never outvotes" structurally, and it earns it honestly, because the mechanism is real and is exercised against a real independent checker. It does NOT earn "dual-engine" or "second implementation" - fln-checker remains a 6-line stub and there is still no NbE anywhere, which stays franken_lean-gii's and franken_lean-g3k's work. The bead must not be closed with any wording implying a second in-repo engine exists, and the documentation half of that overclaim belongs to franken_lean-claim-matrix-doc-ci-mhew, not here.

NOT FL-INV-02, stated because the confusion is easy and consequential. FL-INV-02 is kernel soundness locality - "no code outside fln-kernel can cause acceptance of a declaration the kernel rejects" (plan line 189). That is the capability boundary, it is implemented in capability.rs and tested in checked_declaration_capability.rs, and it is well supported today. This bead does not rescue FL-INV-02; it builds the defense-in-depth layer that B3 promises on top of it. Do not let a closure here be read as evidence for FL-INV-02, and do not let FL-INV-02's health be read as evidence that this seat exists.

DEPENDS ON the independence-boundary bead: what a seat is allowed to share with the kernel is exactly the question that bead answers, and a seat built before it would have to be revisited.

SCOPE. This builds the seat and its policy, not an engine. Filed under the close-mode exception authorized by the orchestrator on 2026-07-25, from cc_2's structural analysis of the fln-checker gap.
close_reason: Consensus seat landed in 10c9a2e3 and unblocked by r0xu's close. convene() consumes the capability so a halt destroys the publication right; a seat can never construct CheckedDecl (fln-yswb's seal); no quorum, no vote; a non-answer halts. Seven zero-engine tests, mutation-checked by hand. Does NOT claim a second in-repo engine exists - fln-checker is still a charter crate, there is no NbE, and convening is not yet mandatory at any call site.

WHAT LANDED. crates/fln-kernel/src/council.rs plus crates/fln-kernel/tests/consensus_seat.rs.

Property 1, a seat can HALT: convene() consumes the Admitted value from admit(). The publication right IS the CheckedDecl inside it, that value is not Clone, and on a halt convene does not hand it back - it is dropped. Halting is not a flag a caller can ignore. A SeatVerdict is ordinary data anyone may build, which is the design and not a hole: evidence must be freely stateable precisely because stating it grants nothing.

NO VOTE ANYWHERE. No quorum, no majority, no seat count in the module. Three agreeing seats cannot carry one dissenter because nothing counts. A non-answer - absent, errored, cancelled, timed out, never run - halts.

THE MUTATION CHECK IS THE PART I WOULD WANT REVIEWED. Making convene record objections and then ignore them is killed by exactly the two halt tests and by none of the other five. I ran that by hand; it is NOT a standing automated lane, and the row says so rather than listing it under mutation.

WHAT IT DOES NOT CLAIM: no second in-repo engine exists, this does not rescue FL-INV-02 (soundness locality, already supported by capability.rs), and convening is not yet mandatory at call sites - admit() still mints without a council. WHAT THE SEAT DOES NOT EARN. Read this before quoting it. cc_2, 2026-07-25, commit 10c9a2e3.

The seat is real and its tests are real. It is also going to be misread, in a specific and predictable way, so here is the sentence that should stop that:

  A consensus seat exists and halts on disagreement. That is NOT the dual-engine
  claim. There is still NO independent in-repo engine: crates/fln-checker is a
  charter crate with no checking code, and there is no NbE anywhere in the
  workspace. The only genuinely independent implementation the seat has ever been
  exercised against is the REFERENCE's own checker, via the foreign witness -
  which is an oracle we ship tests against, not a second engine we wrote.

So "consensus seat, tested" supports exactly this: the MECHANISM by which a
dissent halts publication is built and cannot be outvoted. It does not support
"dual-engine kernel", "cross-checked continuously", or "an independent second
implementation on its own decoder". Those remain franken_lean-gii (the checker)
and franken_lean-g3k (K2/NbE), both P0 and both open.

Three further limits, stated so nobody has to discover them:

1. CONVENING IS NOT MANDATORY. admit() still mints a capability without a
   council, so today the seat is available, not enforced. Every production
   admission path currently convenes nobody. Making convening unavoidable at
   call sites is real remaining work and it is not done.
2. THE WITNESS IS NOT WIRED IN. fln-kernel is zero-I/O by covenant, so the seat
   takes verdicts as values and cannot read scripts/tribunal/leanchecker_witness.sh's
   NDJSON itself. SeatVerdict is SHAPED to accept that vocabulary - including its
   third case, the witness that did not run - but the adapter that turns witness
   output into seat verdicts belongs to a layer allowed to do I/O and does not
   exist yet. The tests plant verdicts; they do not execute the witness.
3. THE MUTATION EVIDENCE IS MANUAL. I checked by hand that making convene record
   objections and then ignore them is killed by exactly the two halt tests and by
   no others. That is a one-off I ran, not a standing lane, and the coverage row
   leaves the mutation field empty rather than implying otherwise.

WHAT IT DOES EARN, so this is not falsely modest: B3's "disagreement halts, never
outvotes" now has a mechanism with no quorum, no majority and no seat count
anywhere in it; a forged seat cannot manufacture the capability it is supposed to
witness; and a non-answer halts instead of abstaining into a pass. Before this
commit the word "consensus" appeared in fln-kernel and fln-checker exactly once,
in a stub's charter line.

NOTE ON THIS BEAD'S STATE. It is OPEN, not closed, and deliberately so: br refuses
to claim or close it while franken_lean-r0xu blocks it, and r0xu has real
remaining work (exhaustive fln-hash/fln-bignum classification, the fln-bignum
graph-versus-gii contradiction that needs cod_2, and a machine-checked
structure-guard rule). The deliverable is complete and committed; the blocking
bead is not. I would rather this bead sit open with its work done than close a
prerequisite I have not finished.

COVERAGE ROW, schema /2. Note that /2 carries no state field - cod_2's migration
derives lifecycle from .beads/issues.jsonl, which removes the whole class of
stale-row gate failures rather than asking every closer to remember. Every array
is sorted and duplicate-free.
