title: W7: grind reimplementation — congruence + e-matching, honestly staged L-levels
description:
Reimplement grind natively (§12.6): grind is core-toolchain machinery at the pin, so under the Oracle-Only Law it is reimplemented — congruence closure, e-matching, and its theory hooks as Anvil engines behind facade rows — developed against instrumented-oracle decision traces and Reference-as-oracle differentials.

Staging is deliberate and honest: its Parity-Ledger rows ENTER at L1/L2 and ratchet to L3 on the grind corpus by G4 rather than pretending day-one exactness, because grind semantics are still moving upstream and the census pins our coupling per epoch. Mathlib-layer automation (aesop, polyrith, ...) is user code on Golem and needs NO reimplementation. All outputs kernel-checked per FL-INV-06.

Acceptance: the grind corpus at L3 by G4 (goal-closure agreement with classified exclusions); decision-trace replay green on the covered fragment; epoch-diff tooling flags upstream grind changes as census deltas requiring row review. Tests: congruence-closure property tests (equivalence-class correctness vs a simple oracle implementation); e-matching trigger fixtures from the traces; differential goal families with the exclusion ledger explicit.

## Acceptance Criteria

All bead-specific requirements, acceptance conditions, tests, invariants, compatibility surfaces, evidence levels, performance gates, negative/recovery cases, and user-visible behaviors stated above remain mandatory. In addition, the MANDATORY VERIFICATION DEFINITION OF DONE in Notes must be satisfied with named unit/property/mutation suites, at least one shared real-path no-mock E2E scenario plus failure/recovery coverage, detailed human and schema-versioned NDJSON artifacts, and reproducible close evidence. No listed feature or claim may be silently narrowed, deferred, mocked, or declared complete through an unclassified divergence.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Reimplement the pinned grind core natively: congruence closure, e-matching, theory hooks, and Native Mirror facade rows are project code developed from instrumented-oracle traces and differential observations. Upstream grind implementation never executes as a component; mathlib-layer automation remains user code on Golem.
2. All grind-produced proof artifacts are replayed and kernel-checked before environment admission. Unsupported, exhausted, cancelled, malformed, or divergent cases yield classified refusal/Inconclusive and cannot be cached or rendered as rejection/acceptance.
3. Parity rows begin honestly at L1/L2 and reach L3 on the declared grind corpus by G4 with goal-closure agreement and an explicit, reproducible exclusion ledger. Covered decision traces replay; epoch census-diff tooling flags every upstream grind/facade change for row review and prevents stale evidence promotion.
4. Named unit/property/model/differential/fuzz/mutation suites cover equivalence-class correctness against a simple independent oracle, congruence explanations, e-matching triggers/substitutions, theory-hook boundaries, trace replay, facade dispatch, budgets, deterministic ordering, and exclusion classification. Unsound merge, missed trigger, unchecked output, hidden exclusion, and stale-epoch mutants must be killed.
5. A shared no-mock E2E lane runs real grind corpus goals and user automation through Golem, compares closure/refusal and covered traces with the pinned Reference, replays proofs through the kernel, exercises an excluded and over-budget case, applies a synthetic epoch census delta, and verifies clean recovery. Human logs plus schema-versioned NDJSON include run/goal/trace/eclass/ematch/proof/Parity-row ids, bead/claim/invariant/gate rows, redacted argv/cwd, pin/build/epoch/mode/profile/thread/seed/budget facts, canonical goal/result/proof roots, expected/actual closure/refusal and first divergence, exclusion reason, timings/resources/status, artifacts, cleanup, and final state.
6. CI archives golden traces, corpus/exclusion manifests, proof receipts, epoch diffs, mutant outcomes, and E2E bundles. The bead cannot claim L3 beyond covered rows or treat a classified exclusion as agreement.

REVIEW AMENDMENT — GrindTheoryHookManifestV1 assigns every pinned hook to grind or a named owned W7 engine. A row reaches L3 only with no unclassified divergence; exclusions and unsupported rows retain lower or excluded states. An independent simple model detects errors, but kernel replay of emitted proof artifacts is authority. Named suites: grind_congruence_model, grind_ematch_substitution, grind_epoch_row_guard, grind_no_mock_e2e.

W6-W8 EVIDENCE CONTRACT — canonical schema-versioned semantic NDJSON is validated independently; telemetry remains separate and non-authoritative. Unknown schema, missing/duplicate ids, broken order/linkage, unbound artifacts, truncation, merged streams, or cleanup/final-state mismatch fail. Cancellation/exhaustion/InternalFault never enters cache, negative storage, admission, publication, or promotion. Productive 1/8/32 evidence proves useful work and deterministic reduction. Named unit/model/property/mutation/fuzz suites and real no-mock positive/failure/recovery E2E are mandatory.

1. Unit coverage: deterministic happy-path, boundary, malformed-input, resource-exhaustion, cancellation, and failure-atomicity cases for every new public behavior; property/metamorphic and mutation-kill tests wherever an invariant or equivalence is claimed.

title: W11: WASM Judge browser — offline sealed-capsule verification
description:
Implement the WASM Judge half of plan §16.4b according to the versioned OQ-12 packaging contract. Ship the certified K1 and structurally independent fln-checker seats, bounded sealed-capsule decoder, certificate and receipt verification, transparency-log inclusion/consistency checks, and an integrity-bound stock-browser shell. A user can open the package offline, select or drag a real .flnpack, re-check declarations and dependency closure against the same canonical vectors as native execution, inspect verdicts and graph slices, and export a verifiable result without trusting a network service.

Preserve the trust boundary exactly. Unknown package/capsule/certificate versions fail closed; UI, worker, core WASM, and fixture assets are content-bound by the selected packaging contract; no JavaScript result can manufacture kernel acceptance; disagreement halts; certificate failure falls back to bounded recomputation where the contract permits; resource exhaustion/cancellation is Inconclusive; no filesystem, network, platform libm, native plugin, or hidden oracle participates. Full browser elaboration remains explicitly outside Tier 1 and cannot inflate the Judge claim.

The browser surface is accessible by keyboard and screen reader, gives progressive but honestly graded progress, renders stable typed errors for corrupt/epoch-mismatched/unsupported/oversized inputs, and survives worker restart, refresh, retry, and interrupted capsule streaming without remembering false success. Declaration and dependency browsing is bounded and paginated. Browser-local state is versioned and never treated as attestation without fresh integrity and receipt verification.

Verification includes unit/property/model tests for manifest binding, version negotiation, streaming decode, budgets, certificate fallback, receipt/log consistency, result export/import, worker isolation, accessibility state, and native/WASM vector identity. Named mutants bypass an asset hash, accept an unknown version, trust a UI verdict, skip one engine seat, promote Inconclusive, drop a dependency, ignore a byte flip, reuse stale browser state, or report success before terminal verification. The no-mock E2E runs offline in every declared stock-browser engine against a real sealed mathlib-slice capsule, verifies native-vector identity, rejects tampered capsule and mismatched UI/core assets, exercises budget exhaustion and worker crash, refreshes/retries, and proves clean recovery and final state.

Emit concise accessible human status and retained bounded schema-versioned NDJSON with run/scenario/step ids, bead/claim/invariant/gate, browser/platform/epoch/mode/profile/build and asset hashes, package/capsule/receipt/certificate/input/output ids, policy and engine seats, expected versus actual verdict/error/consumption, monotonic timings, memory and decode budgets, worker/exit status, console and artifact references, first divergence, recovery, cleanup, and asserted final state.

## Acceptance Criteria

The Judge closes only when the OQ-12 package is shipped as an integrity-bound offline stock-browser experience; real sealed-capsule verification, native/WASM vector identity, two-seat disagreement behavior, bounded decoding/recomputation, accessible browsing, every named negative and mutation, worker/refresh recovery, and the declared browser matrix pass with archived reproducible human and NDJSON evidence. title: W2: Compacted regions — construction, mmap load, relocation, page sharing
description:
Implement compacted regions (§6.4): region construction (object-graph serialization with pointer relocation tables), region loading (mmap, relocate-or-copy fallback, page-sharing across consumers — the enabler of the Lantern shared import heap §7.5), and region hygiene (immutability enforcement, persistent-RC marking).

title: rch offloads cargo test to workers with no .beads/, so bead-reading guards fail 101 for a wrong cause
description:
The mandated hard gate is cargo test. The mandated mechanic for heavy builds is rch. Run the first
through the second and a whole class of guards cannot see its input, fails with exit 101, and names
a missing file rather than the mechanism.

MEASURED, 2026-07-27 at HEAD 4e197f02 (cc_1), main tree, exit code read from the process and not
through a pipe.

  rch exec -- cargo test --locked -p fln-conformance --test ci_execution_join -- \
    terminal_rows_do_not_state_evidence_coarser_than_the_unit_that_runs

  -> exit 101, panic at ci_execution_join.rs:550:
     ".beads/issues.jsonl must be readable: No such file or directory (os error 2)"

The identical command run LOCALLY (through a wrapper script, which the classifier does not match)
at the same HEAD:

  -> exit 101, panic at ci_execution_join.rs:2477:
     granularity-grew: ["fln-h1k.3"] ...

BOTH EXIT 101. One is a real finding about a coverage row; the other measured nothing at all. A
decision rule keyed on the exit code -- and the rotation handoff I was given carried exactly such a
rule, "Exit 101 => the workspace is still red at HEAD" -- is satisfied identically by both.

THE CAUSE, from the config rather than inferred. ~/.config/rch/config.toml [transfer]
exclude_patterns holds 41 entries; two of them are ".beads/" and ".beads/**". The directory is
TRACKED in git (git ls-files --error-unmatch succeeds) and is deliberately dropped from the sync,
so the worker has no copy.

IT IS NOT OPT-IN. rch diagnose -- cargo test --locked -p fln-conformance --test ci_execution_join
reports Kind: CargoTest, Confidence 0.95 >= threshold 0.85, "WOULD INTERCEPT". The PreToolUse hook
is installed. So an agent who types a plain cargo test, never mentioning rch, is offloaded to a
worker missing .beads/. AGENTS.md's RCH section says the hook is "usually transparent"; for this
class it is transparent in the sense that matters least.

AFFECTED SURFACES -- counted as the ATTRIBUTE, not the token, because grepping for the path returns
mentions. Eight files contain the string; three are doc-comment-only and are NOT readers
(crates/fln-env/src/extensions.rs, crates/fln-conformance/tests/evidence_finalization.rs, and the
publisher's comment). The real direct readers are:

  crates/fln-conformance/src/naming.rs          the reserved-name census over mutable bead fields
  crates/fln-conformance/src/ownership.rs       the kernel-contract ownership projection
  crates/fln-conformance/tests/ci_execution_join.rs
  tools/structure-guard/kernel-ownership-publisher/src/main.rs
  tools/structure-guard/tests/real_workspace.rs

plus crates/fln-conformance/tests/vellum_surface_inventory.rs as an indirect consumer via
naming::scan_tree.

THE FALSE-GREEN DIRECTION, CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED, AND IT IS CURRENTLY CLOSED. naming.rs:720
reads the file with "if let Ok(text) = std::fs::read_to_string(&beads)" -- on absence the whole scan
block is skipped silently and the surface is never even pushed onto the scanned list. That is a
textbook vacuous pass. It does NOT currently escape, because
vellum_surface_inventory.rs:30-41 requires SurfaceClass::BeadsCurrent among the scanned classes and
fails with "the beads-current class was not scanned -- a silently absent surface is not a clean
surface". So today the failure is loud in both of the two readers I checked. I did NOT establish
the absence behaviour of the other three readers; that is the open half of this bead.

WHY THIS IS THE hugg / item-7 FAMILY. franken_lean-worktree-gitdir-refusal-hugg is a verification
practice and the gates it cannot actually run, where the artifact asserts a wrong cause loudly. This
is the same shape one mechanism over: a linked worktree voids the evidence surface and AGENTS.md has
a measured table saying which surfaces refuse; rch voids a different set and has no table at all.
The AGENTS.md gotcha list already records that rch workers lack the pinned Reference toolchain
(Evidence and Census Pins item 6) -- the same class, a different input, and the beads case reaches
the ownership projection, whose staleness reddens the workspace for every pane.

WHAT THIS BEAD OWNS.

  R1. Establish, per reader, whether an absent .beads/ fails loudly or passes vacuously. Two of the
      five are done above; three are not. A vacuous one is a false green under the default hook and
      is release-blocking in the way k60n's false-GREEN direction was.
  R2. Decide the repair and state which it is: stop excluding .beads/ from the sync, or refuse to
      offload commands whose targets read it, or make each reader fail typed and loud on absence.
      The third is the only one inside this repository's control and is the one that survives a
      change of build tooling.
  R3. Give AGENTS.md the row it lacks -- a "where a green bar may be taken from" table for rch, on
      the model of the worktree table, measured with positive controls rather than described. Hold
      it with a test, or it rots like every other broadcast.
  R4. fuzz/corpus/ is ALSO excluded and is INERT TODAY -- this repository has no fuzz/ directory and
      its golden corpora live at crates/*/tests/corpus/, which the pattern does not match. Plan
      section 18 mandates corrupted-input fuzzing rigs; when one lands at the conventional path its
      corpus will be silently empty on every worker, and an empty corpus passes. Record it now so
      the trap is not discovered by a green.

CLASS: bounded_model. One host, one commit, one worker pool. The exit-code collision and the config
cause are directly measured; the blast radius across the other three readers is not.
notes:
STATE, 2026-07-27 (cc_1). R1 DISCHARGED AND ITS EVIDENCE NOW GRADED, R2 LANDED (typed, not the panic
first attempted), R3 OPEN AND UNSTARTED.

R1's conclusion -- zero of five readers pass vacuously on an absent .beads/issues.jsonl -- stands,
but it was reached by READING four error arms, and reading proves a branch exists, not that it
fires. Graded after exercising them:

  naming.rs                    EXERCISED, staged absence, two cells
  ownership.rs                 EXERCISED + GUT: baseline 28 pass, gutted 27/1, exactly one death
  kernel-ownership-publisher   EXERCISED, staged absence exit 3 typed + positive control exit 0
  ci_execution_join.rs         INCIDENTAL: real absence on an rch worker, but not one-variable
  real_workspace.rs            NOT EXERCISED -- structurally unstageable

real_workspace.rs is the finding worth carrying: its root is checked_workspace_root!(), which
expands env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"), a COMPILE-TIME constant, so no runtime variable can redirect it.
Staging absence would need the live tracker deleted (forbidden) or the test compiled in a staged
tree (exactly what k60n refuses). The mechanism that stops a test answering about the wrong tree
also removes negative-testing by staged root. A tension between two goods, not a defect -- record
it so the next reader does not think they are doing it wrong.

R2: scan_tree returns Result<ScanReport, ScanError>; library reports, the five call sites (tests)
panic. My FIRST repair put a panic! in naming.rs; ubs caught it as 9 introduced criticals against a
HEAD baseline of 0, and it was wrong on doctrine (FL-INV-07; ownership.rs and the publisher already
return typed errors for this condition in this same crate). That version never reached a commit and
its naming.rs:730 citations are dead.

THE FINDING R1 MISSED: the neighbour's floor covered ONE OF TWO callers -- the_scan_is_deterministic
passed by comparing two scans that had read no beads.

COUNT CORRECTION: not "5 readers / 3 doc-comment-only". Derived: 8 mention the path, 6 have a
non-comment occurrence, 5 actually read it. vellum_surface_inventory.rs:137 is a code occurrence
that never opens the file. A guard must discriminate on the READ, not the comment.

Class bounded_model, one host throughout.
close_reason: R1/R2 discharged by cc_1; R3 was already built and is verified re-derived (rch-tracker-reads 12 / non-reads 3, bound per commit); R4 landed by cc_3 at 81879b18 with a planted decoy and two mutants. Judgement follows as the post-close comment.

The sequencer's broadcast described R1's open half as "the three files that mention the path only in

  real_workspace.rs:329       read_to_string(..).unwrap_or_else(|e| panic!(..))       LOUD
  ownership.rs:1047           typed Err, OwnershipFailureKind::Unreadable{kind}       TYPED
  kernel-ownership-publisher  typed PublishError, Inconclusive/"source_unavailable"   TYPED

permission to downgrade a required/present source to absence." It refuses to treat absence as
nothing-to-check. The publisher is the same posture with a second layer: parse_source separately
refuses empty bytes as source_empty, so a zero-byte file is a Violation rather than an empty id set.

THE RESIDUAL RISK, WHICH IS AN ITEM-7 JOIN AND IS NOT CLOSED BY THIS.

naming.rs on its own IS vacuous: on absence it skips the entire bead-field scan and does not even
push the surface onto its scanned list, so the reserved-name census over mutable bead fields would
report a clean tree having read no beads. What saves it lives in a DIFFERENT FILE --
vellum_surface_inventory.rs requires SurfaceClass::BeadsCurrent among the scanned classes and fails
with "a silently absent surface is not a clean surface". Nothing binds the two. Weakening or
deleting that floor reopens the vacuum, and naming.rs would not change by a byte. The honest repair
is for naming.rs to fail typed on absence itself rather than to be rescued by a neighbour's
assertion, which is R2's third option and the only one inside this repository's control.

WHAT THIS EARNS AND WHAT IT DOES NOT.

Class bounded_model. ONE of the five is a MEASURED absence -- ci_execution_join, observed panicking
on a real rch worker. The other four are determined by READING THE ERROR ARM, not by executing
against a root with no .beads/. For four of them the shape is unambiguous, an explicit panic! or an
explicit typed Err with no fallback path, but reachability is not execution and this bead's own
subject is a case where reading the config would have been right and running it was still worth
doing. A root-without-beads run of all five remains unbuilt and is the stronger evidence.

I did not re-derive the reader population here; it is the five from the bead body, counted as the
attribute rather than the token.

title: W5: FIR pipeline — validated IR stages, pass witnesses, RC/FBIP disciplines
description:
Implement the FIR pipeline (fln-comp, §11.1): elaborated terms -> FIR (ANF/LCNF-class IR keeping the Reference-established compilation disciplines: specialization of instance/closed arguments, simplification, closure conversion, explicit boxing, reference-count insertion with borrow inference and constructor-reuse/FBIP analysis — kept because FBIP-style reuse is the performance model the ecosystem code is written against and is observable through performance cliffs) -> FLBC register bytecode.

Engineering law: every pipeline stage has a versioned IR schema, a deterministic printer, and a validator; every optimization pass is a pure ValidatedIr -> (ValidatedIr, PassWitness) transformation with declared preconditions, a preservation argument or executable validator, a resource-growth bound, deterministic ordering, and a fallback to its input. The RC-insertion pass runs an ownership validator (no use-after-consume, balanced joins and exception edges, capture correctness, ABI ownership contracts) deliberately SIMPLER than the optimizer it audits. Executable-closure selection records WHY each declaration is retained (direct call, closure capture, initializer, reflection, exported symbol, conservative opaque edge) so dead-code questions have answers.

Acceptance: the G0-3 micro-corpus compiles through the full pipeline with every pass witness validating; compiled results observably identical to interpretation of the unoptimized form (pass-preservation differential). Tests: IR printer/parser round-trips; ownership-validator mutation tests (a planted dropped-retain must be caught); pass-ordering determinism at {1,8,32} threads.

## Acceptance Criteria

All bead-specific requirements, acceptance conditions, tests, invariants, compatibility surfaces, evidence levels, performance gates, negative/recovery cases, and user-visible behaviors stated above remain mandatory. In addition, the MANDATORY VERIFICATION DEFINITION OF DONE in Notes must be satisfied with named unit/property/mutation suites, at least one shared real-path no-mock E2E scenario plus failure/recovery coverage, detailed human and schema-versioned NDJSON artifacts, and reproducible close evidence. No listed feature or claim may be silently narrowed, deferred, mocked, or declared complete through an unclassified divergence.

## Success Criteria

All five exact children close with target-neutral canonical stages, pass witnesses, independent ownership validation, only same-stage optional fallback, typed mandatory-lowering refusal, complete differential/mutation/no-mock evidence, and exact recovery.
design:
OQ-4 HANDOFF — this FIR implementation depends on fln-iron-target-profile-contract-ba9 and must implement its selected target-independent lowering and machine-boundary contract. FIR validation and pass witnesses must reject backend-specific leakage not authorized by that contract; any incompatible change reopens the decision bead rather than creating a second implicit backend interface.

TERMINAL DECOMPOSITION — exact children are fln-8m1z FIR schema/ingress, franken_lean-tiw9 specialization/simplification, fln-41jd closure conversion/boxing, fln-6n1k RC/borrow/FBIP plus independent validator, and franken_lean-o6bl mandatory FLBC lowering. This epic closes only on a machine-validated join of those exact child implementation, fixture, mutation, E2E, and evidence roots; prose-only completion or future-consumer evidence cannot substitute.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Implement the complete deterministic elaborated-term to FIR to FLBC pipeline with versioned schemas, parsers/printers, and validators for every stage, preserving specialization, simplification, closure conversion, boxing, RC insertion with borrow inference, constructor reuse/FBIP analysis, and executable-closure selection with explicit retention reasons.
2. Every optimization is a pure ValidatedIr to ValidatedIr plus PassWitness transformation declaring preconditions, preservation evidence or executable validation, resource-growth bound, deterministic ordering, and failure fallback to its input. The independent ownership validator checks consumes, joins, exception edges, captures, and ABI ownership contracts and remains structurally simpler than the optimizer it audits.
3. Named unit/property/metamorphic/differential/mutation suites cover schema compatibility, printer/parser round trips, validator rejection, pass witnesses and fallback, closure-retention reasons, RC/borrow/FBIP edges, exception paths, resource bounds, cancellation, and compiled optimized behavior equal to unoptimized interpretation. Dropped-retain, use-after-consume, bad join, missing capture, false-retention, and pass-order mutants must be killed.
4. G0-3 micro-corpus programs compile through every stage and validate every witness. Pipeline outputs, diagnostics, witnesses, and FLBC are bit-identical at thread counts 1, 8, and 32 for the same inputs and profile.
5. A shared no-mock E2E lane compiles and executes representative user-class programs and a real plugin, compares optimized FLBC results/effects with unoptimized interpretation, injects a planted ownership defect and rejected pass, verifies input fallback, and then proves clean recovery. Human logs and schema-versioned NDJSON include run/program/stage/pass/witness ids, bead/claim/invariant/gate rows, redacted argv/cwd, schema/build/profile/thread/seed facts, canonical IR/program/output hashes, retention/ownership decisions, expected/actual, growth/resource/timing/status facts, artifacts, cleanup, and final state.
6. CI archives stage IRs, witnesses, validator reports, deterministic thread matrices, mutant results, and evidence manifests; close evidence names every suite and may not claim semantic preservation, ownership safety, or performance from mocked execution.

REVIEW AMENDMENT — an optional same-stage optimization may fall back only to independently validated same-stage input. Failure of mandatory lowering returns typed Inconclusive or InternalFault and publishes nothing; no fallback may cross incompatible IR stages or fabricate output. Executable-validator evidence is classified separately from proof claims. Boundary/model/mutation tests cover each pass, stage identity, validator independence, optional rollback, mandatory refusal, cancellation, and exact recovery.

EVIDENCE CONTRACT — canonical authoritative NDJSON contains normalized semantic inputs, roots, decisions, typed outcomes, resource class/consumption, first divergence, cleanup, and exact final state. Host, PID, time, paths, cache/performance, and scheduler facts are linked bounded telemetry only. Independent validators reject unknown schema, extra/missing fields, broken linkage/order, silent truncation, telemetry in semantic hashes, and final-state mismatch. Productive 1/8/32 evidence proves nonempty completed work and canonical reduction.

TERMINAL DECOMPOSITION — exact children are fln-8m1z FIR schema/ingress, franken_lean-tiw9 specialization/simplification, fln-41jd closure conversion/boxing, fln-6n1k RC/borrow/FBIP plus independent validator, and franken_lean-o6bl mandatory FLBC lowering. This epic closes only on a machine-validated join of those exact child implementation, fixture, mutation, E2E, and evidence roots; prose-only completion or future-consumer evidence cannot substitute.

1. Unit coverage: deterministic happy-path, boundary, malformed-input, resource-exhaustion, cancellation, and failure-atomicity cases for every new public behavior; property/metamorphic and mutation-kill tests wherever an invariant or equivalence is claimed.
2. E2E coverage: add or extend at least one shared scripts/e2e scenario for the real user-visible path, plus a negative/recovery scenario. Release-level evidence uses the no-mock lane (real Reference binary/artifact/filesystem/editor/process/host as applicable). A mock may support a unit test but may not close an L-level, PG gate, or public claim.

Detailed logs: emit both concise human logs and schema-versioned NDJSON with run/scenario/step ids; bead, claim, invariant, Parity-Ledger row, and gate ids; exact command/argv with secrets redacted; cwd; epoch/mode/profile/platform/thread-count/seed/cache-state/host facts; canonical input hashes; expected vs actual; monotonic start/end/duration; resource and budget facts; exit status/signal; stdout/stderr artifact references; receipt/logical roots; first-divergence data; cleanup and asserted final state. Never swallow stderr, never leak secrets, and bound adversarial log volume.
4. CI/closeout: archive logs, fixtures, repro bundles, and evidence manifests; failures must be diagnosable from artifacts alone. Run scripts/check.sh, cargo test, the bead-specific unit/property suites, relevant Tribunal differential/mutation/fault lanes, and the shared E2E scenario. The close evidence names every test/scenario id and artifact location; skips require a typed, logged, honest L-level limitation and may not satisfy the skipped claim.

title: RCH concurrent worker slots compile a stale shared source snapshot
description: Reproduction on 2026-07-25 from /data/projects/franken_lean: run RCH_WORKER=hz2 rch exec -- cargo test --locked while other swarm jobs use hz2. RCH reported 0 slots remaining after reservation, synced all 33 roots to /data/projects/franken_lean on the worker, then rustc warned at crates/fln-core/src/mode.rs:975 about the source arm StructuralModeRequirement::FrontierOnly(surface) if consumer == Mode::Frontier. The local file before dispatch and immediately after failure had the already-fixed arm FrontierOnly(_) at line 972 with sha256 a2a814099789fe6615e9cc0cce89e6c19ff83c218c969346864071efa7dffba8; preceding hz2 cargo check and clippy jobs compiled that current arm cleanly. This indicates concurrent worker slots or transfers can overwrite/share a project source path and compile a different job snapshot, presenting stale teammate code as a lane warning/failure. This is distinct from franken_lean-m3fq, which is worker capability selection.
acceptance_criteria: Reproduce with two concurrent jobs targeting different revisions or dirty overlays of the same repo on separate slots of one worker. Each job must compile its own content-bound snapshot and report the source/overlay root digest it actually executed; no shared mutable project path may be clobbered by another transfer. Add a regression that holds one job while a second syncs a conflicting sentinel and proves both see only their own sentinel. A mismatch must fail typed before cargo rather than run stale source.
close_reason: the collision is prevented in BOTH modes by two different mechanisms — per-dispatch remote roots under --clean-overlay, and RCH-I005 active-project exclusion in default mode — measured on an isolated probe; the in-repo regression is unbuildable by construction since every mechanism lives in rch (1.0.52 -> 1.0.56), which is m3fq's disposition

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
DELIBERATE REPRODUCTION ATTEMPT: THE CLOBBER DID NOT REPRODUCE, BUT A DIFFERENT AND SUFFICIENT MECHANISM DID (PeachBass/cc_1, 2026-07-26, from /data/projects/franken_lean against worker hz2). Four measured facts and a rule. The probe was a string literal only and was removed; fln-core is green at 93 tests with zero remnants.

=== Q1: CAN THE DIVERGENCE BE REPRODUCED DELIBERATELY? ===

NOT THE CLOBBER, AND I ALMOST REPORTED THAT IT WAS. Read this part before the rest, because the first result was wrong.

EXPERIMENT 1. Planted SENTINEL-S1 in a cfg(test) const in crates/fln-core/src/lib.rs printed by a probe test. Dispatched job A. Waited for "Sync completed". Flipped the tree to SENTINEL-S2 at 03:16:52 and dispatched job B. Job A — dispatched and synced while the tree held S1 — reported RCH-PROBE-SAW:SENTINEL-S2 with exit=0. That looks exactly like yihl.

IT IS NOT. Checking WHEN job A synced each root refutes it: A synced the project root at 03:16:37 but synced the crates/fln-core root at 03:16:59, seven seconds AFTER my flip. A picked up S2 through its OWN sync. No teammate, no second job, no clobber.

EXPERIMENT 2, the corrected protocol. Waited for A's full 34-root sync AND "Executing command remotely" before touching anything. Job C synced fln-core at 03:23:43 holding S1, began executing at 03:24:45, finished 03:24:50, and reported S1. The flip to S2 came at 03:24:53, after C finished, so C is an uncontaminated control. Job D then synced fln-core at 03:25:18 and correctly reported S2. Each job saw exactly what it synced. THE CLOBBER HYPOTHESIS IS NOT CONFIRMED and I am not asserting it.

=== WHAT DID REPRODUCE, AND IT IS ENOUGH TO CHANGE THE SWARM RULE ===

RCH'S SYNC IS NOT ATOMIC, and the window is large. Measured from rch's own logs on one ordinary job:
  * "Prepared dependency sync manifest for 34 roots"
  * project root synced 03:16:37; crates/fln-core synced 03:16:59 — a 22-SECOND SPREAD between two roots of the same job
  * the full 34-root sequence ran 03:16:37 -> 03:17:51, about 75 seconds, and only then "Executing command remotely" at 03:17:57

So a job does not compile a snapshot. It compiles whatever each root happened to hold when that root's turn came. Experiment 1 is the demonstration: job A carried the project root at S1 and the fln-core root at S2 and reported S2 GREEN, exit=0. That tree state never existed locally at any single instant.

THE REMOTE PATH IS THE LOCAL ABSOLUTE PATH: "Syncing /data/projects/franken_lean -> /data/projects/franken_lean on hz2". All six panes work in that one directory, so every pane's job syncs to the same remote directory. Concurrency is real and rch says so: "2 slots remaining after reservation".

WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN THE CLOBBER, AND WHY IT VINDICATES THE CONCERN THAT PROMPTED IT. You do not need a second rch job to get a torn snapshot. You need ANY pane to touch ANY file during your ~75-second sync window. With six panes editing one shared working tree that is the normal case, not the rare one — which is exactly the worry that prompted this investigation, arriving by a different route than the bead's title proposes.

=== Q2: DOES RCH REPORT THE SOURCE DIGEST IT COMPILED? ===

NO. Nothing in the text output names a content digest. `rch exec -j` produced ZERO JSON objects across 246 lines of output, so the machine surface does not carry one either. The one hash present, "Starting remote compilation pipeline for franken_lean (hash: 1bbff50cfa359c84)", is a project/path identity: it is constant across runs and would be identical for every pane, so it discriminates nothing about content.

Consequence: a caller cannot tell which tree state produced their result, and this bead's own acceptance criterion — "report the source/overlay root digest it actually executed" — is unmet with no partial credit available.

=== Q3: THE RULE ===

AN RCH GREEN BAR IS EVIDENCE ABOUT THE WORKER'S TREE, NOT YOURS. RCH mirrors the live shared working directory to a shared remote path over a non-atomic ~75-second 34-root sync and reports no content digest, so any edit by any pane during that window is silently folded into your build.

SO: never close a bead on an rch green bar. Take the closing green bar from a LOCAL run in a git worktree pinned at a commit — that path is stable, nobody else edits it, and it is the only cheap way to know what was compiled. Use rch freely for iteration and for reds you intend to investigate, but treat an rch red as unattributed until reproduced locally, and an rch green as unattributed always.

This supersedes the standing "send heavy builds through rch exec" instruction for CLOSURE evidence only; rch remains correct for ordinary iteration.

=== UNTESTED MITIGATION, offered rather than claimed ===

`rch exec --base <commit> --clean-overlay [--overlay-path <path>]` transfers a clean git baseline plus explicit overlay paths instead of the live directory. That is content-bound by construction and is the obvious candidate for making rch results attributable. I DID NOT TEST IT and am not claiming it works; someone should, because if it does the rule above gets much cheaper — an agent could keep using rch for closure evidence by pinning the baseline.

=== WHAT I AM NOT CLAIMING ===

I did not reproduce this bead's recorded symptom. That instance had the remote holding OLDER content than the caller's tree both before and after dispatch, with a recorded sha256. Non-atomic sync explains a MIXTURE of tree states, not content older than anything the tree ever held during the job, so the original instance may still have a distinct cause — a stale cached root that rsync did not refresh is the obvious candidate and I did not test it. The bead should stay open on its own terms.

I also did not touch rch itself. Per instruction the regression belongs in rch-common, not here; everything above is measurement from this repo.

THE MITIGATION WORKS, MEASURED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS (PeachBass/cc_1, 2026-07-26, worker hz2, from /data/projects/franken_lean). I offered `rch exec --base <commit> --clean-overlay --overlay-path <path>` last round without claiming it. It is now tested, with a control, and it is content-bound by construction. The swarm can have rch back for closure evidence.

=== THE RESULT ===

TEST (job E). Planted SENTINEL-S1 in a cfg(test) const in crates/fln-core/src/lib.rs, dispatched with --base HEAD --clean-overlay --overlay-path crates/fln-core/src/lib.rs, then flipped the tree to SENTINEL-S2 mid-flight — the same edit that silently produced a torn green build in the default mode. It did NOT fold the edit in and it did NOT produce a wrong answer. It REFUSED, typed, naming both digests:

  Remote execution failed on hz2: clean-overlay input changed after admission
  (expected 378c64a7156762e6f512d1c3c2ea56db94e85f80c28caf80bff4a872a217f561,
   found    117af3731b34e6974aa2867869847641277ef9218ce15c5e0e3af6d92c04d79c);
  refusing remote execution; will retry on another worker if available
  Remote build failed on all 1 tried worker(s); refusing local fallback

Note the second line. It refuses to silently fall back to a local run, so the caller cannot be handed an unattributed green by accident.

CONTROL (job F). Same invocation, tree left untouched for the whole run: exit=0, test result ok, RCH-PROBE-SAW:SENTINEL-S2 — exactly the content the tree held at dispatch. A mechanism that always refuses would be useless; this one admits a quiet tree and refuses a moving one.

STRUCTURAL DIFFERENCE, visible in the logs and worth knowing: the default mode reports "Prepared dependency sync manifest for 34 roots" and walks them over ~75 seconds. --clean-overlay reports "Prepared dependency sync manifest for 1 roots". It is not syncing the live directory at all; it ships a git baseline plus the named overlay paths.

=== THIS ALSO CORRECTS MY ANSWER TO Q2 ===

I reported last round that rch reports no content digest. That is true of the DEFAULT mode and I stand by it there. It is FALSE for --clean-overlay: this mode computes a sha256 over the overlay input at admission, re-checks it before execution, and prints BOTH the expected and the found digest when they differ. The digest exists; it is only absent from the mode we were all using.

=== THE INVOCATION, since six panes will copy it verbatim ===

  rch exec --base "$(git rev-parse HEAD)" --clean-overlay \
    --overlay-path <every path you changed> \
    -- cargo test -p <crate>

PASS AN EXPLICIT SHA, NOT THE WORD HEAD. --base takes "a Git commit used as the clean source-tree baseline". With six panes committing continuously, the literal string HEAD is a moving target between your dispatches, and two runs you believe are comparable can be against different baselines. `$(git rev-parse HEAD)` freezes it and makes the run quotable in a bead.

--overlay-path IS REPEATABLE and you must name EVERY path you changed. This is the mode's one footgun and it is a new failure mode, not an inherited one: a changed file you forget to name is simply ABSENT from the build, so you get a green bar for the baseline rather than for your work. That is a silent wrong answer of a different shape. Derive the list rather than typing it: `git status --porcelain` gives it, and naming a directory works where a change touches many files under one root.

WHAT IT BUYS BEYOND ATTRIBUTION, and this is the part I did not expect. Because the baseline is a commit and only your named paths overlay it, FIVE OTHER PANES' UNCOMMITTED EDITS ARE EXCLUDED BY CONSTRUCTION. That is the shared-tree tearing problem removed at the root rather than detected: your build contains HEAD plus your work and nothing else. It also means an rch red in this mode is attributable to you, which the default mode's red never was.

=== THE REVISED RULE ===

An rch green in the DEFAULT mode remains unattributed and must not close a bead — nothing in that finding changes.

An rch green under --base <sha> --clean-overlay --overlay-path IS attributable and MAY close a bead, because the mode fails typed rather than silently when its input moves. Quote the sha and the overlay list in the close, so the run is reproducible.

A pinned local git worktree remains correct and is still the right tool when you want to run the pin-dependent suites (kernel_replay and friends), since RCH workers do not have the pinned Reference toolchain. The two are complements: the worktree for pin-dependent evidence, --clean-overlay for everything else.

=== WHAT I STILL DO NOT CLAIM ===

I did not test whether --clean-overlay detects a change to a file OUTSIDE the named overlay set — by construction such a file is not in the build at all, so there is nothing to detect, but I have not confirmed the baseline itself cannot be raced. I did not test the mode against the pin-dependent suites. And this bead's original symptom — remote content OLDER than anything the caller's tree ever held — remains unexplained and untested; the stale-cached-root candidate is still open. fln-yihl should stay open on its own terms.

The probe was a cfg(test) string literal, incapable of breaking any build, and is removed: crates/fln-core/src/lib.rs is pristine with zero remnants.

HOW TO TELL, AFTER THE FACT, WHETHER A GREEN BAR WAS OFFLOADED (PeachBass/cc_1, 2026-07-26). Short addendum, because I nearly certified my own close on unsound reasoning.

WHAT I GOT WRONG. Auditing whether anything I closed today rested on a default-mode rch green, I argued: "explicit rch exec runs print INFO lines, my runs printed none, therefore they were local." That reasoning is INVALID — most of my runs were piped through grep for "^test result", which filters rch's INFO lines out. Absence of markers in filtered output is no evidence at all.

`rch diagnose -- cargo test -p fln-env` makes it worse rather than better: it answers "Decision: WOULD INTERCEPT (confidence 0.95 >= threshold 0.85)".   REMOTE: Running tests/digest_preimage_encoding.rs (.rch-target-hz2-pool-fe0c117c407d7e376085f2287ea8711e/debug/deps/...)

A remote run uses a worker-scoped `.rch-target-<worker>-pool-<hash>` directory and also logs "Rewriting CARGO_TARGET_DIR for remote execution" and "Retrieving artifacts". A local run uses the configured CARGO_TARGET_DIR. Both examples above are from this session's own logs.

SO: to check a green bar you already took, look at the `Running ...` line. Do not infer from the presence or absence of rch chatter, especially if you piped the output — which every agent here does habitually.

MY OWN AUDIT, now on evidence rather than inference: an unfiltered `cargo test -p fln-core --lib` from this session compiled into /data/tmp/cargo-target with ZERO rch markers, so plain cargo is NOT being intercepted in my session despite diagnose saying the class would be. franken_lean-oh1j — my only close today — took its gates in a pinned worktree with kernel_contract run locally, and that stands.

If you close a bead citing it, the retained log should show the overlay digest at admission; if it shows a `.rch-target-*` path with no overlay digest, you were in default mode and the green is unattributed.

THE UNTESTED CANDIDATE IS NOW TESTED AND IT REPRODUCES: A SIZE-AND-MTIME-PRESERVING CHANGE IS SILENTLY NOT TRANSFERRED, AND THE WORKER COMPILES STALE CONTENT. Measured by cc_2, pane 3, on 2026-07-28 against worker hz2, rch 1.0.52, from a throwaway worktree at /data/projects/fln-yihl-probe so no pane could perturb a cell. Landed with the AGENTS.md repair.

THE QUESTION THIS ANSWERS. The previous comment established that non-atomic sync produces a MIXTURE of tree states and explicitly declined to explain the original symptom, which is the remote holding content OLDER than the caller's tree both before and after dispatch. A mixture is not staleness, so a distinct cause was owed. The comment named the candidate — a cached root that rsync did not refresh — and recorded it as untested. It is now tested.

THE OBSERVABLE, chosen after a failed attempt. `rch exec -- sha256sum <path>` cannot be used: rch warns `exec called with non-compilation command` and runs it LOCALLY, returning the caller's own hash. I nearly recorded that as a remote reading. The observable that works is `compile_error!("<sentinel>")`: rustc quotes the literal, so the diagnostic names exactly which bytes the worker compiled, and it needs no test harness.

THE CELLS, one variable each, on the smallest crate in the workspace:

  1  sentinel S1 planted, first dispatch          worker compiled S1
  2  changed to S2, SIZE AND MTIME BOTH PRESERVED worker compiled S1  <- the edit never arrived
  3  changed to S3, mtime bumped (the control)    worker compiled S3
  4  cell 2's condition exactly, but with
     --base <sha> --clean-overlay --overlay-path  worker compiled S2  <- correct

Every sentinel is the same length, so size is identical by construction; the script refuses the cell if size moved. Cell 3 is what makes cell 2 attributable rather than a broken pipeline: the same edit with mtime bumped arrives.

WHAT IS ESTABLISHED. A content change that leaves size and mtime untouched is not transferred, and the worker then compiles stale content indefinitely — content older than the caller's tree both before and after dispatch. That is the original symptom's exact shape, and it is what non-atomic sync cannot produce. So this bead's recorded instance now has a mechanism that reproduces on demand.

STATE THE PREDICATE, NOT THE IMPLEMENTATION. What is measured is: size and mtime unchanged => not transferred. That this is rsync's quick check is an INFERENCE from the signature. No cell inspects the transfer, and rch is closed to me.

CELL 4 IS THE OPERATIONAL PAYOFF, and it strengthens the existing rule rather than adding a second. --clean-overlay is not merely attributable under concurrent edits: it is the only measured form that resists content-blind staleness, because it digests the overlay at admission instead of trusting a stat. So the default mode's green is WEAKER than "evidence about the worker's tree" — it can be evidence about a tree state no host held recently.

A CONSTRAINT THAT FELL OUT, worth knowing before anyone designs the next probe: rch refuses any project path outside /data/projects with `input resolves outside canonical root` and falls back to LOCAL. My first attempt ran from a /data/tmp worktree and silently measured a local build. An rch experiment cannot be isolated in scratch space; it must live under /data/projects.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT EARN. One host, one worker, one rch version, one instant, class bounded_model. It establishes the mechanism exists and reproduces; it does NOT establish that the 2026-07-25 instance was caused by it, and that is now unrecoverable. The trigger needs an mtime-preserving write — ordinary editing bumps mtime, and these cells used touch -r deliberately — so the real-world FREQUENCY is unmeasured and nothing here names which everyday operation supplies it. That is the remaining open question on this bead, and it is narrower than the one it replaces.

WHAT I DID NOT DO. I did not touch rch; the regression belongs in rch-common, as the previous comment recorded. I did not close this bead: its acceptance criteria ask for two concurrent jobs on separate slots each compiling a content-bound snapshot and reporting the digest it executed, and rch still reports no content digest at all. Cell 4 shows the attributable form is sound, which is a mitigation the caller can adopt today, not the fix the criteria describe.

surface carries no source binding at all, so a caller cannot learn which snapshot it will compile

side-effect free by its own help text — no worker slot consumed, no build run).

WHY THIS SURFACE. `fln-yihl`'s acceptance criteria require that "each job must compile its own
content-bound snapshot and **report the source/overlay root digest it actually executed**". Before
designing the two-concurrent-job regression that criterion also asks for — which consumes shared
worker slots and must be priced and routed first — the cheap question is what rch already reports.
`rch admit` is the one surface that is explicitly read-only, so it costs nothing to ask.

MEASURED. `rch admit --json cargo test -p fln-conformance` returns a complete, well-formed envelope:

    api_version, timestamp, command, success
    data.command, data.compound[], data.is_compilation=true, data.family="cargo_test"
    data.required{ needs_cargo=true, needs_bun, needs_nix, needs_go, needs_node, needs_zig,

    data.proof_policy=false
    data.base_recommendation="offload", data.detail="offload-eligible (family=cargo_test)"

The envelope describes the COMMAND and the CAPABILITIES a worker must have; it says nothing about

THE CONCURRENCY EXPERIMENT PRICED, AS I COMMITTED TO DOING BEFORE RUNNING IT — and it is far cheaper
than I assumed, because it does not need to touch `franken_lean` at all.

cc_2 (pane %15), 2026-08-05, at HEAD a4588673. Read-only surfaces only; nothing dispatched.

=== THE ASSUMPTION I WAS CARRYING, AND WHY IT WAS WRONG ===

I claimed this bead saying the regression "consumes shared worker slots" and that a recorded
constraint shapes it: rch refuses a project path outside `/data/projects` and falls back to local,
so the experiment "cannot be isolated under /data/tmp — it must run against a real path other panes
use". The first half is right. **The second half does not follow, and I wrote it without checking.**

`/data/projects` holds **336 entries** — it is the machine's general projects root, not a synonym for
this repository. The canonical-root rule requires a path UNDER it; it does not require
`franken_lean`. So a purpose-built minimal crate at `/data/projects/<scratch-name>` satisfies rch
and perturbs nobody. The experiment does not have to plant conflicting sentinels in the tree six
panes are building.

That single correction removes the main cost and the main risk at once.

=== THE PRICE ===

  * SLOTS: 2 of `hz2`'s 8, briefly. Client config admits it — `test_slots=4`, and `hz2` is
    priority 110 with 8 slots (comment 2082).
  * TRANSFER: `--base <sha> --clean-overlay --overlay-path <paths>` ships **1 root, not 34**
    (AGENTS.md), and the subject is a crate with one `src/lib.rs`. The ~75-second, 34-root,
    22-second-spread sync that characterises DEFAULT mode is not what this pays.
  * COMPILE: a trivial crate whose only content is a sentinel. Wall time is dominated by scheduling
    and transfer, not compilation — seconds, not the 32 minutes the corpus matrix costs.
  * BLAST RADIUS ON THIS REPOSITORY: **zero**. No file in `franken_lean` is touched, so no pane's
    build, gate or governed input moves. Contrast the alternative I had assumed, which would have
    planted conflicting sentinels in the shared checkout.

So this is not in the class of the corpus-matrix run that must be launched through the sequencer. It
is a small, isolable experiment, and the honest conclusion of pricing it is that **it does not need a
dispatch — only a heads-up that two slots will be busy briefly.**

=== THE DESIGN ===

Two jobs, one worker, conflicting content, each proving it saw only its own bytes:

  1. A minimal crate under `/data/projects` with a `cfg(test)` sentinel constant.
  2. Job A dispatched with `--base <sha> --clean-overlay --overlay-path src/lib.rs` carrying
     sentinel `S1`.
  3. While A is in flight, flip the tree to `S2` and dispatch job B the same way.
  4. **The observation must come from the compiled output**, because `rch admit` carries no content
     digest at all (comment 2080) and default mode reports no digest either (AGENTS.md). Use
     `compile_error!(<sentinel>)`: rustc quotes the literal, so the failure text names exactly which
     bytes that worker compiled. That is the technique AGENTS.md records for the mtime cells and it
     is the only one measured to answer this question.
  5. PASS = A reports S1 and B reports S2. FAIL = either reports the other's, which is the clobber
     this bead is named for.

THE CONTROL THAT MAKES IT MEAN ANYTHING, and it is the half easiest to skip: a single job with no
concurrent sibling must report its own sentinel. Without it, a run where both jobs report correctly
is indistinguishable from a harness that cannot observe the sentinel at all.

=== WHAT IT WILL NOT ESTABLISH ===

It tests `--clean-overlay`, the ATTRIBUTABLE form. A pass says nothing about DEFAULT mode, which is
what the hook actually uses and where the non-atomic 34-root sync lives — and that is the mode most
panes are exposed to. Testing default mode concurrently would require the shared-path collision this
design exists to avoid, so it stays open and named rather than quietly folded in.

It is also one worker, one rch version, one instant, class `bounded_model`, on a tool outside this
repository. And the original 2026-07-25 observation was on `hz2` in DEFAULT mode against
`franken_lean` itself; a green result here does not retire that observation, it bounds it.

=== RULE 1 NOTE ===

The scratch crate will be created under `/data/projects` and **not deleted** — RULE 1 covers scratch
I create myself. It will be named so its purpose and owner are obvious from the path.

THE MECHANISM IS NAMED: `RCH-I005 "active project exclusion"`. TWO CONCURRENT JOBS ON ONE PROJECT DO
NOT CO-RESIDE, WHICH IS WHY THE SHARED ABSOLUTE PATH IS NEVER CONTENDED — plus a correction to my
own comment two entries up.

cc_2 (pane %15), 2026-08-05, on the isolated probe crate. This closes the question comment 2087 left
open.

=== THE ANSWER ===

Pinning BOTH default-mode jobs to one worker, job B's log carries:

    WARN rch::hook::incident: reason_code: RCH-I005, failure_class: "active project exclusion",
         selected_mode: Local, local_fallback_allowed: true

**rch excludes a second job on the same PROJECT while one is active.** That is the reason two
default-mode jobs cannot contend the shared absolute path: they are never simultaneously resident on
it. The acceptance criterion's "no shared mutable project path may be clobbered by another transfer"
therefore holds in default mode too — **not** because the path is isolated, as it is under
`--clean-overlay`, but because concurrency on that path is refused upstream.

So the two modes reach the same guarantee by different means, and both are now measured:

    --clean-overlay   per-dispatch remote root (5 dispatches -> 5 distinct roots); jobs may
                      co-reside because they cannot collide
    default           caller's absolute path on the worker, SHARED — and a second job on the
                      same project is excluded (RCH-I005) rather than admitted onto it

A SECOND, INDEPENDENT MECHANISM in the same direction: **a default-mode job reserves the worker's
ENTIRE slot budget.** Both default-mode A runs logged `0 slots remaining after reservation`, while
the `--clean-overlay` control logged `4 slots remaining` on an 8-slot worker. So even without the
project exclusion, a second job would find nothing free on that worker.

I wrote there that "a default-mode invocation gives the caller NO SIGNAL, in its own output, that it
ran locally rather than remotely", and offered it as directly actionable for every pane. **That is
true only for the UNPINNED case.** Measured on the two logs side by side:

    pinned    yihl-dp-B   11 lines   WARN=1   RCH-I005=1   -> names the reason

So the honest statement is narrower: **an unpinned default-mode invocation can fall back to local
with no signal at all; an explicitly-pinned one warns and names the reason code.** My 2087 wording

This is evidence infrastructure: no verdict must never be represented as a passing scan. Acceptance: the evidence.py scan terminates within a declared bound with a typed pass, findings, or scanner-fault outcome; CI distinguishes scanner timeout/internal failure from clean; every requested file is accounted for; a planted scanner stall is killed by a deterministic test; clean recovery proves subsequent scans work; logs preserve tool version, inputs, elapsed time, terminal state, and exit without leaking file contents or secrets.

comments.text:

Conclusion: the no-verdict symptom is in the external UBS Python module, not a fixable single-file layout defect in this repository. No repo code changed.

Therefore decomposing evidence.py would improve human reviewability but does not restore a UBS verdict for the same total input and cannot honestly close this scanner bead.

Keep fln-yk3t open; a UBS-side bounded algorithm or per-file accounting/checkpoint change is required. comments.author: cod_3
comments.text:
cod_3 closure correction, 2026-07-25.

CALLER AUDIT. A complete tracked scripts/** search found zero timeout-plus-UBS wrappers and zero UBS_MODULE_TIMEOUT overrides. There is exactly one repository-owned UBS execution path: scripts/check.sh run_stage ubs through evidence.py exec-ubs-inventory. Its default supervised stage budget is FLN_CHECK_STAGE_TIMEOUT_MS=1,200,000 ms, four times UBS internal 300,000 ms, and UBS exit 1 is registered as a semantic stage failure. The CI job outer bound is 60 minutes. Therefore the checked-in caller already drains and records the honest UBS red verdict; there is no 120- or 180-second repository timeout to raise or remove.

The raw exit-125/no-verdict observations came from the interactive diagnostic commands recorded earlier on this bead, where timeout at 120 or 180 seconds killed UBS before its own 300-second module boundary. Those commands were not checked-in callers. The procedural fix is to stop wrapping UBS below its declared bound; manufacturing a scripts/check.sh timeout diff would change a caller that is already correct and would not repair the commands that caused the symptom.

MEASURED BOUNDARY, same UBS v5.3.7 installation. Small real file: 1,876 lines, 14.521 s, exit 0. Syntax-valid evidence prefix: 4,183 lines, 32.234 s, exit 0. Full evidence.py: 19,953 lines, 300.701 s, exit 1, MODULE_TIMEOUT, files=0. Generated single-file control: 19,953 lines, 300.681 s, same result. Equal-total generated five-file split: 19,955 lines, 300.672 s, same result and files=0. Splitting reduced RSS and let one analyzer advance, but did not produce a terminal file verdict.

DISPOSITION. Close this bead as a measured negative result, not a repair. The silent-stall premise was false because our external diagnostic wrapper preempted the scanner. The remaining 300.7-second MODULE_TIMEOUT with files=0 is a UBS-side Python-module scaling defect outside this repository. No repository refactor can honestly be claimed as its fix, and no repository source was changed for this closure. Logs and tool digests remain in comment 983.

title: DUPLICATE OF fln-history-rewrite-evidence-anchor-reachability-vdi4 — DO NOT WORK THIS
description:
SUPERSEDED BY fln-history-rewrite-evidence-anchor-reachability-vdi4. DO NOT WORK THIS.

This bead is a DUPLICATE. cc_3 filed it on 2026-07-26 without checking for concurrent
work; cod_3 had already filed vdi4 for the same finding, at P1 and in progress, and
vdi4's R1 to R6 are a better specified superset - in particular its trichotomy of
main-reachable, local-backup-only and unresolved, which this bead did not distinguish.

It is left OPEN rather than closed, deliberately. A closed bead derives verification
state complete, and a complete coverage row demands thirteen non-empty evidence arrays;
inventing those for work that was never done would put fabricated evidence in the
manifest to satisfy a validator, which is the failure this project exists to prevent.
An open bead's row may stay sparse and legal, so honesty costs one extra open bead in
the count. That trade is the point: the bead does exist, and a count that says so beats
a tidy count achieved by destroying a record.

The measurement this bead carried now lives on vdi4 as an immutable comment, and
AGENTS.md item 7 cites vdi4 rather than this bead (commit 69431e50). Nothing here is
load-bearing. Read vdi4 instead.

--- original filing, retained unaltered below ---

The 2026-07-25 23:59 git filter-branch rewrote every commit hash on main. Every
evidence anchor recorded before that point still LOOKS well formed and still names a
real object locally, but no longer names anything reachable from main. The anchors did
not become wrong. They became UNVERIFIABLE, which is worse in a project whose entire
discipline is that a claim names the thing that produced it.

MEASURED at HEAD 14bbbe7f by cc_3, 2026-07-26, over .beads/issues.jsonl,
ci/VERIFICATION_MANIFEST.jsonl, AGENTS.md, README.md, the plan, and every tracked
source, script and ci artifact. Candidate tokens were 7-40 hex, each confirmed to be a
real commit object with git cat-file before being judged, then tested with
git merge-base --is-ancestor against HEAD:

  distinct commit hashes cited   411
  reachable from main            245
  UNREACHABLE from main          166      (40 percent)

Where they sit:

  163  .beads/issues.jsonl
   18  ci/VERIFICATION_MANIFEST.jsonl
    5  crates/fln-env/src/modules.rs
    3  crates/fln-conformance/src/witness.rs
    3  crates/fln-conformance/tests/digest_preimage_encoding.rs
    2  crates/fln-conformance/tests/witness_claim_matrix.rs
    2  crates/fln-env/src/extensions.rs
    2  AGENTS.md
    1  each in fln-verdict goldens and their provenance note, ci/WORKSPACE_GRAPH.txt,
       tools/structure-guard/src/ledger.rs

THE SHARPEST CASE IS INSIDE THE MECHANISM BUILT TO PREVENT THIS CLASS. The Witness
claim matrix exists because a row can read as verified while its evidence describes a
world that no longer exists. Of the four commits its own evidence prose cites, three
are now unreachable from main: 10c9a2e3 (the consensus seat landing, cited by
B3-CONSENSUS-HALTS), 86035037 (the fln-olean header repair, cited twice) and a368ea0b
(the README install one-liner repair). The only reachable one is 86b36e21, cited by a
row added after the rewrite. AGENTS.md is not exempt either: the Build Gate section
cites 24b16eeb and bb561892 - two commits named specifically to teach agents why
anchoring matters - and neither resolves from main.

WHY NOTHING CATCHES IT. Every existing join check compares a claim against evidence
that is still addressable. This failure changes the ADDRESS SPACE underneath every
claim at once, without touching a single claim. No document reads as wrong. No test
reads a stale value. git cat-file still succeeds, because refs/original/refs/heads/main
and the tag pre-filter-branch-backup keep the old objects alive in this clone - so even
a naive existence check would pass today. It is a reader of main alone, or this clone
after a gc, or a fresh clone from any remote, who finds nothing.

That last point is the one that decides severity: the anchors are alive only in local
reflog-adjacent refs. A gc, a fresh clone, or a push to a remote that does not carry
refs/original leaves 166 recorded verifications naming objects nobody can resolve.

WHAT THIS IS NOT. This is not a claim that any recorded verification was false, and not
a request to redo any of that work. The measurements were real when they were made.
It is also not a criticism of the rewrite, which was authorised and which Jeffrey has
said to proceed with; the four generated census files genuinely did not belong in
history. The cost is a side effect nobody priced, which is exactly why it is worth a
row rather than a shrug.

SUGGESTED REPAIRS, not prescribed, cheapest first:

  1. A guard, which is cheap and does not exist: walk every commit-shaped token in the
     governed artifacts, confirm it is a commit, and assert it is an ancestor of HEAD.
     Fail on any that is not. Roughly the script in this bead's measurement. It would
     have to start with a declared allowance of 166 that shrinks, in both directions,
     the way qydn's oracle allowance does - otherwise it can never go green and becomes
     a gate people bypass, which is the e5k7 lesson.
  2. A rewrite map. filter-branch can emit old-to-new, and refs/original still permits
     reconstructing one. Publishing that mapping as a checked-in artifact makes every
     dead anchor mechanically resolvable and is the only repair that restores the
     anchors rather than merely policing new ones.
  3. Re-anchor on touch. When a bead or row is next edited for any reason, re-derive
     its measurement against current HEAD and record the new hash. Cheapest per unit of
     work, and it never converges on its own.

ACCEPTANCE. Enough that a reader of main alone can resolve any evidence anchor cited in
a governed artifact, or can see mechanically which ones they cannot and how many remain.
A silent 40 percent is the state this bead exists to end.

FIRST INSTANCE, recorded because it is how this was found: bead
fln-bench-apparatus-empty-referent-bkw6 recorded its counts as verified at HEAD
828d9488. Re-deriving them at the current HEAD was necessary before closing it, because
828d9488 is one of the 166. The generalisation is the orchestrator's, from that one
observation.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
cc_2, 2026-07-26: independent reproduction of this bead's measurement, one exact reconciliation of the single number that differs, and one artifact that is structurally immune. Measured at HEAD 17e2d38b. Recording the full current hash deliberately, per this bead's own R1: 14bbbe7f, the anchor in the bead body, is already superseded, which is the defect demonstrating itself inside its own bead within a day.

REPRODUCED, INDEPENDENTLY AND WITH A DIFFERENT SCRIPT. Same discriminating test - git cat-file to confirm the token names a real commit, then git merge-base --is-ancestor <hash> HEAD to judge reachability. Same conclusion, same order of magnitude. I confirm the central point in particular: git cat-file alone reports commit for every dead anchor, because refs/original/refs/heads/main and tag pre-filter-branch-backup are both still present in this clone, so an existence check passes on all of them today and starts failing only after a gc. Both refs verified present at 61b1bf19.

WHERE WE AGREE. The direction, the severity, the mechanism, and the fact that no existing check could have caught it. Two independent scripts, two different token-width choices, one conclusion. I also confirm the count of UNREACHABLE commits over .beads/issues.jsonl as 152 distinct objects, which is stable across both my runs (61b1bf19 and 17e2d38b) despite four commits landing in between.

WHERE WE DIFFER, AND IT IS METHODOLOGICAL RATHER THAN AN ERROR IN EITHER OF US. This bead reports 411 distinct commit hashes cited; I get 393 over the same file at the same 7-40 hex width. Measured at HEAD 17e2d38b, the gap reconciles exactly and leaves no residue:

  distinct commit-resolving TOKENS   412      <- this bead's quantity (411 at 14bbbe7f;
                                                 the +1 is a commit newly cited since)
  distinct commit OBJECTS they name  393      <- mine
  objects cited under 2+ spellings    19
  extra tokens beyond one per object  19      <- 412 - 393 = 19, exact, no remainder

So this bead counts TOKENS and I counted OBJECTS. Nineteen commits are cited both abbreviated and in full, or at two different abbreviation widths, and are counted twice at token granularity. Neither figure is wrong; they answer different questions, and the bead's question ("how many citations must a reader chase") is the right one for stating severity.

WHY THIS MATTERS FOR REPAIR 1 RATHER THAN BEING TRIVIA. Repair 1 proposes a guard with a declared allowance of 166 that shrinks in both directions, explicitly modelled on qydn's oracle allowance. I have just spent today inside that mechanism, and the granularity choice decides whether it converges:

  * An allowance keyed on TOKENS carries 19 entries that are duplicates of the same
    underlying commit. Re-anchoring one citation leaves its twin in the allowance, so
    the both-directions check fires "this entry no longer breaks the law" for the
    repaired spelling while the unrepaired spelling still fails. The repairer gets a
    red build for doing the work correctly - the wall-shaped failure qydn's guard is
    carefully built to avoid.
  * An allowance keyed on resolved OBJECTS shrinks once per commit re-anchored, which
    is one unit of actual work per unit of allowance.

Recommend keying the allowance on the resolved object name and reporting the citing sites (token spelling plus file:line) inside the failure message, rather than keying on the literal token. Over .beads/issues.jsonl the number to declare is then 152, not 163; over whatever the final scope turns out to be, it is objects-minus-reachable rather than tokens-minus-reachable.

A SECOND CONSTRAINT FROM THE SAME MECHANISM, since this bead cites qydn's allowance as the model and I landed the most recent change to it (d30a64de) today. Do not assert equality on the allowance's size, and do not assert that every anchor a repair touches is still IN the allowance. Both are walls: the first reddens the build when the scope legitimately grows, the second reddens it the moment somebody repairs an anchor. The shape that survives its own repair is one-way membership - every UNREPAIRED dead anchor must be declared - plus a floor for anti-vacuity, because a membership check scoped to a shrinking remainder stops checking anything at all once the remainder empties, silently, exactly when the remaining anchors have become the load-bearing ones.

ONE ARTIFACT IS STRUCTURALLY IMMUNE, AND IT IS THE EVIDENCE ARTIFACT. ci/PARITY_LEDGER.txt contains ZERO commit anchors - measured, not assumed. It is absent from this bead's "where they sit" list, which is consistent, but the reason is worth stating because it is the shape of repair 3:

The Parity Ledger anchors evidence to PIN TAGS and FIXTURE PATHS (core-observables-v4.32.0, pin-census-v4.32.0, and repo-relative fixture paths that validate_fixtures checks exist) rather than to commit hashes. A pin tag names the thing that PRODUCED the value; a commit hash names the moment somebody LOOKED. Only the first survives a history rewrite, and only the first is re-derivable by a reader who has the pin.

That is the same distinction qydn is about one floor down - a level and the oracle that produced it - and it suggests the durable form of repair 3 is not merely "re-anchor on touch" but "re-anchor on touch TO A PRODUCER, not to a commit" wherever the evidence has a producer to name. Commit hashes remain right for things whose referent genuinely is a moment in history, such as "this defect was introduced here".

SCOPE NOTE: nothing here contradicts the bead. It reproduces it, reconciles the one number that differs, and adds a granularity constraint on repair 1 plus a worked example for repair 3. I did not file a competing bead; this finding is yo2w's.
