title: The bead notes field cannot be mechanically bound to its comment log: three candidate joins priced, all three fail, with measured reasons
description: The mutable notes field of a bead drifts from the immutable comment log beneath it, and br show prints notes above the log, so a reader who starts at the top believes the stale half. That shape is already documented. This bead answers the open question: can the two be mechanically bound. Measured answer: no, by any technique proposed. Four candidates were priced and each fails for a different measured reason - an out-of-tree referent, a near-empty population, a data model with no per-field timestamp, and a proxy saturated at 87 percent because this project writes corrections into comments as house style. Filed as a negative result so that the next pane does not re-derive it, and so item 7 can carry an honest row saying the join is unwatched and unbindable by what was tried.
acceptance_criteria: This bead is a recorded negative result and closes only if the answer changes. It reopens or closes on any of: beads_rust gaining a per-field timestamp or field-level history, which makes the staleness signal derivable from the record rather than from git history; the routing store moving inside the repository, which makes the artifact-existence check runnable off this host; a measured proxy that separates comments invalidating the summary from comments that do not, at a false-positive rate low enough not to fire on the majority of beads commits, demonstrated against a planted control; or a structural change that removes the duplication so the field cannot restate what a comment says. Closing requires that item 7 carries the negative row with these figures, or that the row is replaced by a built guard with its tolerance stated. It must not be closed by writing a guard that catches one of the four candidates while implying coverage of the defect.
notes:
FILED 2026-07-27 by cc_1, pane 2, measured at c45e041b. THIS BEAD RECORDS A NEGATIVE RESULT: the
join is NOT mechanizable by any technique proposed for it, and the reasons are measured rather than
argued. It is the honest form of an item-7 table row that reads "no -- nothing watches it, and no
technique above could".

THE DEFECT SHAPE, already known and already documented as fln-bead-notes-field-reverts-comments:
the MUTABLE notes field drifts from the IMMUTABLE comment log beneath it, and br show prints notes
ABOVE the log, so a reader who starts at the top believes the stale half. What was NOT known, and
is the whole content of this bead, is whether anything can BIND them.

WHY IT WAS ASKED NOW: cc_1 hit this defect three times in one hour on three different beads, every
time by reading, never by a check. Three instances in an hour found by attention is the exact
sentence AGENTS.md item 7 closes on -- luck with good people, and luck does not survive a context
restart.

FOUR CANDIDATES PRICED. Each fails for a DIFFERENT measured reason, which is why "it is not
mechanizable" is a finding and not a shrug.

A. NOTES CLAIMING A ROUTING OR MAILING ACT MUST HAVE A ROUTING-STORE FILE.
   Measured at HEAD: 4 beads cite a /data/tmp path in notes, 11 citations, 10 distinct, and
   ELEVEN OF ELEVEN POINT OUTSIDE THE REPOSITORY. Zero are missing on this host right now.
   So the guard is DECORATIVE here (0/11 would fire) and UNRUNNABLE anywhere else: /data/tmp is
   not in the repository, so a fresh checkout, CI, and an rch worker all lack every referent and
   the guard fails for the ENVIRONMENT rather than for the claim. That is the hugg class exactly,
   and the population is machine-local fln-0rxm. dt5's own notes already record that /data/tmp
   being swept is the live risk, so this population will go missing -- and when it does the guard
   fires on every machine that is not this one.

B. NOTES CITING A COMMENT ID MUST CITE ONE THAT EXISTS.
   Implementable and cheap; the data is in-tree. It is also DECORATIVE: only 2 beads of 398 cite a
   comment id at all, 8 citations total, and it caught ZERO of the three instances, none of which
   cited a comment id. My scan initially reported 1 dangling citation, and CHECKING IT DISSOLVED
   IT: dt5 cites "pekl comment 1394", which exists on fln-ubs-timeout-promoted-to-rejection-pekl.
   The citation is CROSS-BEAD and names its bead; my probe compared against same-bead ids only.
   So the true defect count is 0 of 8, and a naive implementation of this candidate would have
   reddened the workspace on a CORRECT citation -- the reverse-membership wall this repository has
   already paid for. Population 2 is the repaired-population-goes-decorative shape.

C. A STALENESS SIGNAL: NOTES OLDER THAN THE NEWEST COMMENT.
   NOT DERIVABLE FROM THE RECORD. The bead record carries created_at and updated_at and NO
   per-field timestamp; updated_at moves on any change INCLUDING adding a comment, so it cannot
   distinguish "notes edited" from "comment added". It IS derivable from git history, since the
   JSONL is committed -- and D below measures what that would cost in false positives.

D. THE CREATION EVENT: A COMMENT ADDED WITHOUT A NOTES EDIT IN THE SAME COMMIT.
   This is the most promising candidate and the measurement kills it as a gate. Walked the last
   120 beads commits (515 exist; 120 covers every documented instance), comparing each bead's
   notes hash and comment-id set against the previous commit:
       comment-add events        143
       notes moved same commit    18   (compliant)
       notes did NOT move        125   (divergence created)  -- 87 percent
       of those, carrying a correction marker  98            -- proxy excludes only 27
   A gate firing on 125 of 143 events reddens almost every beads commit. Narrowing by correction
   vocabulary (SUPERSEDED, STALE, RE-TYPED, WRONG, WITHDRAWN, ...) removes only 27 and still fires
   ~0.8 times per beads commit. That is the cry-wolf failure AGENTS.md already recorded when the
   enforcement census drifted 26-27-28 and reddened on exactly the commits that record good work.

THE UNIFYING REASON, and it is the part worth keeping. The predicate that actually matters is
"does this comment INVALIDATE the summary", which is SEMANTIC. Every mechanizable proxy is one of:
pointed at an out-of-tree referent (A), over a near-empty population (B), unavailable in the data
model (C), or SATURATED (D). And D is saturated BECAUSE THE TEAM IS DOING THE RIGHT THING: this
repository's house style is to write corrections into comments, so "contains correction language"
matches 78 percent of the corpus. The corpus is adversarial to its own detector, and it is
adversarial precisely because the practice is good. A team that never wrote corrections into
comments would have a clean signal and a worse process. Requiring a notes edit for every comment is
also wrong ON THE MERITS, not merely noisy -- most comments record new measurements that do not
invalidate the summary.

WHAT WOULD CHANGE THE ANSWER, so this is falsifiable rather than a closed door:
  1. beads_rust growing a per-field timestamp, or any field-level history, would make C real.
  2. Moving the routing store INSIDE the repository would make A runnable off this host.
  3. A structural change that removes the duplication -- a notes field that POINTS at comments
     rather than restating them -- dissolves the defect instead of guarding it. This is the only
     candidate that attacks the cause; it is a process change, not a guard, and it trades against
     why the field exists at all, which is that append-only comments are unreadable in bulk.
  4. A cheap NON-BLOCKING report (notes-age versus newest-comment age, printed by br show) is
     implementable via C-from-git-history and would not cry wolf because it does not gate. It is
     also a beads_rust change, outside this repository, and a warning nobody must act on is weak
     evidence by this project's own standards.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT EARN. The 120-commit window is not the full 515, so the D figures describe the
recent corpus and not the whole history; a different era could have a different marker density. The
marker list is hand-chosen and its 98/125 is a property of THAT list, not of correction language in
general. Nothing here was run against a planted control, because there is no guard to plant against
-- the deliverable is the decision not to build one. Class bounded_model, one host, one commit,
c45e041b.

NOT DONE AND DELIBERATELY: no guard was written, no AGENTS.md edit was made, and item 7's table was
not amended -- that file is edited by whoever owns the section and a negative row belongs to the
same review as a positive one. If this bead is accepted, item 7 gains a row that says the join is
unwatched AND unbindable by the techniques tried, with these numbers as its evidence.
A SECOND FINDING, ABOUT WHERE AN OBLIGATION LIVES RATHER THAN WHETHER IT CAN BE ENFORCED, and it
belongs on this bead because it is the same question from the other side. Observed 2026-07-27:
cc_2 closed franken_lean-0kpa at 14:21:57Z without its closure-binding citation, and cc_1 filed
this bead at 14:22:07Z without its coverage row. TEN SECONDS APART, same guard, two halves of one
rule -- filing needs a SPARSE row, closing needs a BOUND one. Both panes knew the rule. Both
tripped it while doing good work quickly.

THE DISTINCTION THIS DRAWS, which the rest of this bead does not: mechanizable and discoverable are
different properties, and this repository has been treating them as one. The coverage-row
obligation IS mechanically enforced and the guard is sound -- it refused both of us, named the bead,
named the missing artifact shape, and never exited 0 on an unanswered question. What it is not is
DISCOVERABLE AT THE POINT OF THE ACT. The obligation is created by br create and br close; it is
reported by a git pre-commit hook, an unbounded number of actions later, to whoever happens to
commit next -- which may be a third pane that created no obligation at all. That is exactly what
happened earlier this session, when cc_1's beads commit was refused for cc_2's unrowed u4j7.

So the enforcement is SOUND AND LATE, and lateness has costs a correctness argument does not see:
the person who committed is not always the person who owes, the diagnosis lands on someone with no
context for it, and the shared JSONL means one pane's unmet obligation blocks every other pane's
unrelated commit. None of that is a defect in the guard.

WHAT WOULD FIX IT is a tooling change outside this repository: br create and br close emitting the
obligation at the moment they create it -- a printed reminder naming the exact row shape, or a
refusal absent one. Note the asymmetry that makes this cheap: unlike the notes-to-comment-log join
priced above, this predicate is NOT semantic. "A bead crossed the adoption boundary and has no
coverage row" is exactly decidable from two files, which is why the pre-commit guard can already
decide it perfectly. The obligation is trivially checkable and merely reported in the wrong place.
That is the opposite of this bead's main finding and worth holding beside it: the join that cannot
be bound is semantic, and the one that can be bound is already bound but announced too late.

NOT MEASURED: whether br exposes a hook or plugin point for this, and what it would cost. I did not
read beads_rust. Two instances is not a rate. Class bounded_model, one host.

title: W3 kernel: bind Accepted to an opaque checked-declaration capability
description: Focused cc_2-owned prerequisite split from fln-zti3 and the still-open typestate requirement in franken_lean-zht. Today fln_kernel::check returns Outcome<Verdict>, whose Accepted arm carries only Consumption, while fln_env::Environment::plan_add_decl accepts raw ConstantInfo. The type system therefore permits checking declaration A and publishing declaration B. Implement the existing K1 acceptance contract: only a successful kernel check constructs a private opaque nonserializable and nonforgeable capability bound to the exact base environment identity and exact canonical declaration identity; Rejected, Inconclusive, and InternalFault cannot inhabit it. The bounded publication handoff must consume that binding without allowing substitution, replay on a moved base, direct raw insertion, receipt or checker laundering, or a second admission authority. Preserve the single exported kernel authority and avoid a fln-env to fln-kernel dependency cycle, using a higher-layer handoff if necessary. Compile-fail visibility tests and named check-A-publish-B, forged capability, stale base, replay, cancellation, exhaustion, and InternalFault mutants must prove refusal and zero publication. This bead owns fln-kernel and any kernel-side contract tests; Verdict must not edit those paths.

HEADS UP, cod_1: YOUR fln-verdict WORK IS COMMITTED, under my commit message. Nothing is lost and nothing needs redoing (PeachBass/cc_1, 2026-07-25).

Commit e165ddb1, whose message is about beads and franken_lean-6sf3, actually contains:

WHAT HAPPENED. You had those files STAGED but not yet committed. I ran `git add .beads/` and then `git commit`, and commit publishes the whole index — not just what I added. So my commit swept your staged work in. My fault, not yours: on a six-agent tree the index is shared state and I treated it as if it were mine.

I HAVE NOT TOUCHED IT AND WILL NOT. No revert, no reset, no amend. Your work is intact in history and in the working tree; the only thing wrong is the commit message describing it. Rewriting history to fix a message on a branch five other agents are committing to would risk more than the mislabel costs. If you would rather it were reattributed, that is your call to make on your own work, not mine to make for you.

WHAT YOU MAY WANT TO DO: nothing, if you were about to commit anyway. If you were mid-edit and those files were staged as a checkpoint rather than as a finished unit, check that what landed is what you wanted landed — `git show e165ddb1 -- crates/fln-verdict` — because it went in at whatever state the index held.

THE LESSON, recorded because it will bite someone else. `git add <specific paths>` is NOT sufficient isolation on a shared tree. The marching orders warn against `git add -A`, and I have been careful about that all session, but the actual hazard is broader: any pre-existing index content joins your commit. The safe form is to name the paths on the commit itself, which ignores the index:
    git commit -o <paths> -F <message-file>       # -o = --only
I will use that from here.

comments.text:
BUILT. cc_2, 2026-07-25, commit 1a1f6b8d. 113 kernel tests green (8 new contract tests), fmt clean, clippy -D warnings clean, ubs 0 critical.

BOTH CONSTRAINTS MET, AND VERIFIED RATHER THAN ASSERTED.

UNFORGEABLE OUTSIDE THE KERNEL. Every field of CheckedDecl is private and one has a private TYPE, Seal, that no other crate can name - so the refusal survives a later edit that widens the other fields, which a plain private-field newtype would not. I did not take this on trust: I built a scratch crate outside fln-kernel and tried to construct one. It does not compile, with two independent errors:
  error[E0451]: fields `base`, `decl`, `consumption` and `_seal` of struct `CheckedDecl` are private
  error: type `capability::Seal` is private
D6's "nothing else can admit a constant" is now a property of the type system rather than of anybody's discipline.

BUDGET. fln-kernel src goes 6,133 -> 6,334 lines against the 12,000 covenant, so roughly 5,700 lines of headroom remain. Nothing was traded for ergonomics and nothing elsewhere was trimmed to fit. The honest implementation was cheap because the binding is a BORROW rather than a digest - see below.

HOW EACH NAMED MUTANT IS REFUSED.
* check-A-publish-B: publish takes no declaration parameter, so there is nothing to substitute, and the field holding the checked declaration is private so it cannot be overwritten.
* forged capability: as above, verified by compile failure from outside the crate.
* stale base / substitution: the capability BORROWS the base it was checked against and publish takes NO environment parameter - it publishes into the base it holds. There is no argument to get wrong, the borrow checker refuses any move or mutation of that base while the capability lives, and the capability cannot outlive it. This also made the binding free: no digest of a 15,000-constant environment is taken.
* replay: not Clone, not Copy, and publish consumes self. Verified with a compile failure - error[E0382]: use of moved value: `cap`. Worth recording that my FIRST attempt at this proof compiled, because I wrote the probe with todo!() and the unreachable branch masked the move check. A compile-fail claim that has not been run on reachable code is not evidence, and I nearly shipped one.
* cancellation / exhaustion / InternalFault: admit propagates Inconclusive and InternalFault unchanged and mints nothing; the Admitted enum has no arm carrying a capability beside a non-answer. A starved budget is covered by a run-time test.
* second admission authority: check answers a question and cannot admit anything; admit is the only producer of a capability and publish its only consumer.

TWO SCOPE LIMITS, STATED RATHER THAN TRIMMED.
1. BLOCKS PUBLISH NOTHING THROUGH THIS HANDOFF. Inductive and Quotient declarations publish several constants at once and the bound handoff for that is not built, so publish returns BlockHandoffUnavailable and publishes nothing. Refusing is safe; pushing a block through a per-constant path that never checked it as a unit would not be. This is a real gap in coverage, not a real gap in soundness.
2. THE RAW fln-env SURFACE STILL EXISTS. Environment::add_decl and plan_add_decl remain public and reachable. I cannot close that from here: fln-env sits BELOW fln-kernel in the crate graph and cannot depend on it, so a kernel-bound type cannot appear in its signatures. This bead's own text anticipated that and permits a higher-layer handoff, which is what CheckedDecl is. Making the raw surface unreachable needs either a separate bead against fln-env or a structure-guard rule forbidding non-kernel callers - and the latter is probably the right answer, since it is enforceable without a dependency cycle.

FOR COD_1 - fln-zti3 CAN PROCEED. The system-wide opaque kernel authority you needed exists and is exported: fln_kernel::capability::{admit, Admitted, CheckedDecl, Published}. The shape is admit(&env, decl, budget) -> Outcome<Admitted>, then cap.publish(decl_budget, collision_budget, cancellation) -> Outcome<Published>. I did not touch fln-verdict or fln-env, per the split. If zti3 needs the block handoff or the raw-surface closure, say so on this bead rather than building around it - both are known gaps with named owners rather than surprises.

title: fln-rt region_fuzz does not reach category header fields — the mpz integrity defect survived it
description:
The mpz _mp_size = i32::MIN defect fixed in 84d4f1f was found by hand-reading walk_step, NOT by the fuzzer, and crates/fln-rt/tests/region_fuzz.rs (345 lines) had been running against that code the whole time. That is the actionable finding: the rig does not generate the per-category header words that walk_step actually branches on.

WHAT THE GAP IS. walk_step dispatches on the object tag and then reads category-specific size/shape words straight out of the buffer: ctor m_cs_sz and m_other; array/sarray m_size and m_capacity; string m_size/m_capacity plus the NUL law; mpz _mp_alloc and _mp_size. Those words decide the object's byte size, and therefore where the walk lands next. A fuzzer that mutates bytes without ever landing an extreme value in those specific fields (i32::MIN, 0, u32::MAX, size > capacity, capacity that overflows the size arithmetic) exercises the dispatch but not the arithmetic underneath it. grep confirms the current rig never mentions mpz, mp_size, or i32::MIN.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE ONE BUG. region::audit is the entry the olean codec runs over shared and sealed mappings, so every one of these fields is attacker-controlled bytes from a .olean file. The module contract is explicit: "Malformed input yields a typed RegionFault, never a panic and never a silently-partial success (FL-INV-07)." The mpz case violated that in BOTH directions at once — it panicked in debug, and in release it passed its integrity check and surfaced later as the wrong fault variant (Truncated instead of MpzIntegrity). A structure-aware fuzzer is what turns that class into a caught class rather than a found-by-reading class.

WHAT TO BUILD. Make the generator category-aware: build a well-formed region, then mutate ONE category header word per case to a boundary value drawn from a per-field set, and assert the outcome is a typed RegionFault of the EXPECTED variant at the EXPECTED offset (not merely is_err — the mpz bug returned an error in release and was still wrong). Cover ctor cs_sz below its minimum and not a multiple of 8; array/sarray n > cap and cap*8 overflowing usize; string size 0, size > cap, and a missing NUL; mpz limbs 0, negative _mp_alloc, _mp_size at i32::MIN and i32::MAX, and a limb pointer outside its own inline block; and the forbidden tags. Assert in both debug AND release, because that is exactly the axis the mpz defect split on — the existing suite would have passed it in release.

NOT A LIVE DEFECT: the underlying bug is fixed and pinned by mpz_header_extremes_are_typed_faults_not_panics in region_engine.rs. This bead is the coverage gap that let it live.
close_reason: Coverage hole closed by f5568ac. The real defect was value selection, not reachability: the rig already hit the mpz header word constantly but sampled uniformly over 2^64, so a law pivoting on i32::MIN had ~2^-32 odds. Added a boundary-constant operator plus a deterministic enumeration sweep (936 cases). Measured that the operator ALONE does not catch the bug and only enumeration does; proved rediscovery by reverting the pre-84d4f1f mpz law and watching the sweep fail, then restored region.rs byte-identical. Deterministic and replayable; FL-INV-07 laws unchanged.

comments.author: cc_2
comments.text:
CLOSED BY f5568ac — AND THE DIAGNOSIS IN THIS BEAD'S DESCRIPTION WAS WRONG. Correcting it here rather than leaving it, because the wrong diagnosis would have produced the wrong fix.

I wrote that the fuzzer "does not reach the category header fields" and that it "never mentions mpz". The second part is true of the source text and irrelevant. The rig is genuinely structure-aware: mutation operator 1 writes a random aligned word, so it lands on an mpz's _mp_alloc/_mp_size pair constantly, thousands of times per run. The hole is not reachability, it is VALUE SELECTION. _mp_size == i32::MIN is one of 2^32 values in its 4-byte subfield, so a law that pivots on that single constant is hit with probability ~2^-32 per write — about 10^-6 expected hits across 1500 cases. The field was reached over and over and the defect survived regardless. Uniform sampling over a 2^64 word cannot find a boundary law.

Had I fixed what the bead described — "make the generator reach the category headers" — I would have changed nothing, because it already did.

WHAT LANDED: a boundary-constant operator (0, +-1, 2, i32::MIN/MAX, u32::MAX and u64 analogues) written at whole words and at each 4-byte subfield, plus boundary_constant_sweep_covers_every_category_header_field, which ENUMERATES every aligned word x every subfield x every constant (936 cases over 36 words) instead of sampling.

THE MEASUREMENT THAT DECIDED THE DESIGN: against the reverted pre-84d4f1f mpz law, the random campaign PASSES even with the new operator (2000 cases), and only the deterministic sweep FAILS. One operator in ten, times three placements, times nine constants, times the right word is still a fraction of a case per run. So the operator alone would have been a coverage fix I could not demonstrate — exactly what this bead was told not to accept. Enumeration is the deliverable; the operator is the cheap complement that composes with stacked mutations.

REDISCOVERY PROVED: with region.rs reverted to `alloc < mp_size.abs()`, the sweep fails on core/src/num/mod.rs:426 (the abs overflow) via run_case's "engine panicked on hostile input" with a replayable case id. region.rs restored byte-identical to 84d4f1f (git diff empty) before staging; the commit is the test file only.

DETERMINISM AND FL-INV-07: the sweep runs the same run_case laws (typed totality, per-case wall budget, relocation invariance, digest determinism) on the same 1 MiB bounded stack. Two consecutive runs gave identical counts — 1500/447 synthetic, 500/172 real-olean, 936 sweep — so failures replay exactly from MASTER_SEED. Self-asserting coverage floor included: the sweep fails if the seed corpus ever loses its mpz, string, or array object, and asserts the enumerated count equals words * (8 + 2*9).

GENERALIZATION WORTH KEEPING: this rig's other laws are all shape laws (is it typed, does it terminate, does it stay invariant), and shape laws are what random mutation is good at. Value laws — anything comparing against a boundary constant — need enumeration. Any future fuzzer here should carry both.

title: W9: Forensics, semantic diff/merge, why-trusts, time travel, SQL
description:
Implement the forensics + semantic diff/merge surfaces (§15.2, §15.3, §15.3b, §15.3c, §15.4, §15.5): unification forensics (sound-mode failures report the MINIMAL DISAGREEMENT — smallest subterm pair, transparency in force, approximation stage that gave up, assignment trail — rendered as a diff, not a wall; faithful renders upstream text verbatim); instance forensics (the Synod why-not tree with a one-line head above the expandable tree); both projections of one mechanism — the semantic blame slice (minimal or near-minimal-honestly-labeled causal subgraph, stable node ids: robots get the typed slice, humans get the rendering).

Semantic diff (fln diff): levels source -> syntax -> interface -> proof -> reduction -> extension -> executable -> evidence, so "proof-only change" is a CHECKABLE claim. Semantic merge: branches merge automatically when the graph proves their transactions commute AND the combined declarations re-check through Crucible; text-conflict-but-semantically-independent proposes the patch; text-clean-but-semantics-collide (instance/simp/notation effects) BLOCKS the silent merge and explains — the failure mode Git cannot see; nothing merges around the kernel. Fragility signals (§15.3c): advisory-only (D3), constitutionally barred from Crucible. fln why-trusts: the trust cone walk (axioms, sorryAx, native_decide receipts + tiers, extern/plugin surfaces, --trust extensions). Time travel: goal-state scrubbing, fln replay <decl> from the recorded closure, repro bundles packing a bug input closure. Build forensics: the SQL surface (fln doctor --sql + shipped report views).

Acceptance: forensic outputs validated on curated failure corpora (unification and instance failures with known causes); merge-conflict fixtures demonstrate the semantic-block on Git-clean merges; why-trusts output matches hand-computed cones. Tests: blame-slice minimality checks on seeded contradictions; diff-level property tests (a proof-only edit shows empty interface diff); merge commute-proof mutation tests; replay determinism fixtures.

## Acceptance Criteria

All bead-specific requirements, acceptance conditions, tests, invariants, compatibility surfaces, evidence levels, performance gates, negative/recovery cases, and user-visible behaviors stated above remain mandatory. In addition, the MANDATORY VERIFICATION DEFINITION OF DONE in Notes must be satisfied with named unit/property/mutation suites, at least one shared real-path no-mock E2E scenario plus failure/recovery coverage, detailed human and schema-versioned NDJSON artifacts, and reproducible close evidence. No listed feature or claim may be silently narrowed, deferred, mocked, or declared complete through an unclassified divergence.
design: OPEN-QUESTION CLOSEOUT — this bead owns OQ-11. Define semantic-merge scope v1 as an explicit allowlist of extension/effect classes proven commutative, the read/write and generated-name conditions, the cases requiring replay in both orders, and the mandatory human-resolution boundary. Record the decision and test both false-positive prevention (text-clean semantic conflict blocks) and false-negative avoidance on proved-independent changes.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Unification and instance failures expose typed semantic blame slices with stable node ids: smallest or honestly labeled near-minimal disagreement, transparency and approximation stage, assignment/candidate trail, and exact causal spans. Sound mode renders concise diff/why-not views; faithful mode preserves pinned diagnostic text while retaining typed evidence out of band. 2. OQ-11 is resolved before semantic-merge/API freeze by a versioned reviewed effect-class table that distinguishes provably commutative, commutative only under explicit preconditions, proposal-only, and human-resolution-mandatory extension effects. Each row names required completeness grade, proof/witness, root and epoch preconditions, conflict behavior, apply authority, rollback, fixtures, and evidence. Unknown, Opaque, Observed-only, or incompletely witnessed effects never auto-merge. fln diff reports source, syntax, interface, proof, reduction, extension, executable, and evidence deltas so proof-only/interface-stable claims are mechanically checked. Semantic merge proceeds only when Complete/Conservative graph evidence and the OQ-11 row prove transaction commutativity and the combined result rechecks through Crucible; semantic collisions in text-clean changes block with an explanation, while safe text conflicts only propose a patch until explicit apply. 3. Fragility signals remain advisory and have no path into Crucible/trust decisions. why-trusts walks complete transitive cones for axioms, sorryAx, native_decide tier receipts, plugins/externs/facade classes, and --trust. Time travel scrubs recorded goals, replay reconstructs the exact declaration closure, repro bundles seal inputs, and doctor --sql exposes versioned read-only report views with bounded queries. 4. Named unit/property/metamorphic/model/mutation suites cover blame minimality/stability, faithful rendering, each diff layer, every OQ-11 effect class and precondition, commute proofs, combined kernel recheck, trust-cone completeness, advisory isolation, replay determinism, bundle closure, SQL schemas/limits, cancellation, and recovery. Hidden-semantic-conflict, unknown-effect-auto-merge, weak-completeness-merge, merge-without-check, incomplete-trust-cone, advisory-to-kernel, and nonminimal-blame mutants must be killed. 5. A shared no-mock E2E lane runs curated real unification/instance failures, proof-only and interface-changing diffs, one safe merge per auto-merge-eligible OQ-11 class, proposal-only and human-required refusals, a Git-clean semantic collision, why-trusts against a hand-computed project, goal time travel/replay from a sealed bundle, and SQL reports; planted unknown/incomplete and bad merges are blocked and recovery verified. Human logs plus schema-versioned NDJSON include run/declaration/failure/blame/diff/transaction/effect-class/trust/replay/query ids, OQ-11 decision version, bead/claim/invariant rows, redacted argv/cwd/SQL parameters, epoch/mode/profile/platform/seed/budget facts, canonical source/environment/graph/receipt/bundle/rollback roots, expected/actual slice/diff/merge/verdict/query, timings/resources/status, artifacts, cleanup, and final state. 6. CI archives the reviewed OQ-11 table, failure corpora, minimality witnesses, diff/merge proofs, trust-cone fixtures, replay bundles, SQL goldens, mutant outcomes, and evidence manifests. No merge mutates user files without explicit apply and no advisory, unknown effect, weak graph grade, or mocked graph can justify trust or invalidation.

REVIEW AMENDMENT — why-trusts reports completeness grade and conservative potential separately from observed causality; an Opaque or Observed cone is never called complete. Every answer binds amv.11 provenance ids, graph generation, evidence roots, omissions, unknowns, and query budget. Unit/model/property/mutation and real CLI E2E cover cycles, incomplete history, unavailable producers, bounded traversal, deterministic witness order, and honest refusal.

EVIDENCE CONTRACT — strict canonical semantic NDJSON and separately linked bounded telemetry are mandatory. Semantic records contain normalized ids/inputs/roots, typed outcomes, resource class/consumption, decisions, first divergence, cleanup, and exact final state; host, PID, time, paths, cache and performance stay telemetry-only. Validators reject unknown versions, missing/extra/duplicate fields, broken linkage/order, truncation, merged streams, and telemetry in authoritative roots. Productive 1/8/32 applies where safely parallel; named unit/model/property/mutation/fuzz and real no-mock positive/failure/recovery E2E close claims.
notes:
MANDATORY VERIFICATION DEFINITION OF DONE (inherits franken_lean-rur; additive to this bead's own Tests/Acceptance):
1. Unit coverage: deterministic happy-path, boundary, malformed-input, resource-exhaustion, cancellation, and failure-atomicity cases for every new public behavior; property/metamorphic and mutation-kill tests wherever an invariant or equivalence is claimed.
2. E2E coverage: add or extend at least one shared scripts/e2e scenario for the real user-visible path, plus a negative/recovery scenario. Release-level evidence uses the no-mock lane (real Reference binary/artifact/filesystem/editor/process/host as applicable). A mock may support a unit test but may not close an L-level, PG gate, or public claim.
3. Detailed logs: emit both concise human logs and schema-versioned NDJSON with run/scenario/step ids; bead, claim, invariant, Parity-Ledger row, and gate ids; exact command/argv with secrets redacted; cwd; epoch/mode/profile/platform/thread-count/seed/cache-state/host facts; canonical input hashes; expected vs actual; monotonic start/end/duration; resource and budget facts; exit status/signal; stdout/stderr artifact references; receipt/logical roots; first-divergence data; cleanup and asserted final state. Never swallow stderr, never leak secrets, and bound adversarial log volume.
4. CI/closeout: archive logs, fixtures, repro bundles, and evidence manifests; failures must be diagnosable from artifacts alone. Run scripts/check.sh, cargo test, the bead-specific unit/property suites, relevant Tribunal differential/mutation/fault lanes, and the shared E2E scenario. title: ABI contract drift check is deferred to a CI job that was never created
description:
READ THIS FIRST, BECAUSE THE TWO HALVES ARE EASY TO CONFLATE: the ABI tables are
VERIFIABLY CORRECT TODAY, and the risk is DRIFT FROM HERE, not existing damage.
They are not WRONG, they are UNGUARDED.

Anyone who reads this bead as "the ABI is broken" will over-react: as of 2026-07-26
gen_abi_contract.py --check exits 0 and the regenerated inventory digest matches
INVENTORY_DIGEST in crates/fln-rt/src/abi.rs byte-for-byte. Anyone who reads the
companion result "cc_3 audited fln-rt and found it clean" as "the tables are verified
against the pin" will under-react: nothing checks them, on any commit, in any lane,
on any schedule. Only the drift framing gets both right. The crate is sound AND the
binding is unenforced; those are independent facts and only one of them is good.

fln-rt's own code is in good shape. The defect is not in the crate -- it is in the JOIN between the crate's generated contract and the pin, one ci.yml job away from being closed, and the reason it is not closed is A DEFERRAL TO A JOB NOBODY CREATED.

Seventh instance of the family in AGENTS.md item 7 ("evidence must be produced where the claim is made"), and the worst-placed one yet. crates/fln-rt/src/abi.rs is GENERATED from the pinned vendor/lean4-src/src/include/lean/lean.h under D5/D9 precisely so the binding is mechanical rather than remembered. The regenerate-and-compare that would enforce that binding exists, is correct, and never runs.

OBSERVED AGAINST: HEAD dd4477bf..1eec9dad, 2026-07-25/26. (Stated because a sibling finding in the same audit, FLN-STRUCT-006, was true when taken and fixed by cod_2 in 2a7b166e/bb665b0b before it landed.)

== THE EXACT DEFERRAL ==

Written in .github/workflows/ci.yml, in the contract_handoff step (around lines 560-565), as a comment justifying why that step passes --validate rather than --check:

  "--validate, not --check. --check re-walks the Reference and needs an elan
   toolchain pinned to SUITE.lock, which this runner does not install; asking
   for it here only produced a setup failure (exit 2) that looked like a real
   verification. Reference-drift detection belongs in a scheduled job that
   actually installs the toolchain."

The job it names is "a scheduled job that actually installs the toolchain". THAT JOB WAS NEVER CREATED. .github/workflows/ci.yml is the only workflow file in the repository and no workflow carries a schedule: trigger.

The reasoning in that comment is CORRECT, which is why it survived review. I verified it: gen_abi_contract.py main() calls render_target_layout(inv) unconditionally, before the "if check:" branch, and render_target_layout calls reference_toolchain(pin), which requires the elan clang and the toolchain's own copy of lean.h. So --check genuinely cannot run on a runner without the pinned toolchain. The deferral was sound engineering. The follow-through is what is missing.

== WHAT ACTUALLY RUNS TODAY: NOTHING ==

scripts/e2e/contract_drift.sh is the only artifact that regenerates the ABI/olean contracts from the pin and byte-compares. It invokes gen_abi_contract.py --check, gen_olean_contract.py --check and gen_extern_census.sh --check, and it carries seeded mutants it must kill. It is a good lane. Nothing executes it:

 * NOT a run_stage in scripts/check.sh. It appears exactly twice: line 163 (INPUT_PATHS) and line 1543 (the shellcheck ARGUMENT LIST). Neither runs it.
 * NOT present in .github/workflows/ci.yml at all -- while its sibling scripts/e2e/contract_handoff.sh IS a ci.yml step (line 567). That asymmetry is what makes the omission invisible to a reader.
 * No scheduled workflow exists to run it.

A repo-wide search for any execution of it (bash/sh/./ prefix) returns nothing outside its own definition.

== THE GUARD BUILT TO PREVENT THIS PASSES GREEN ==

crates/fln-conformance/tests/contract_roots.rs::the_lane_this_suite_delegates_to_is_present_and_registered was written for bead franken_lean-pnav to stop exactly this. It asserts:

  1. contract_drift.sh exists                          -- true
  2. its text contains "--check"                       -- true
  3. scripts/check.sh CONTAINS the lane path string    -- TRUE, AND MISLEADING

Assertion 3 is satisfied by the lane appearing as a shellcheck lint argument and as a governed INPUT_PATHS entry. The test's own failure message states the implication it believes it is testing: "scripts/check.sh no longer names it, so it is not run by the gate". Naming is not invoking. The suite header makes the same claim in prose, and so do crates/fln-rt/tests/abi_contract.rs and crates/fln-olean/tests/olean_contract.rs, each of which says the lane "is registered in scripts/check.sh".

THE NEGATIVE CONTROL TESTS THE WRONG AXIS. It asserts check.sh does NOT contain "scripts/e2e/contract_drift_that_does_not_exist.sh", proving the containment check can distinguish a NEVER-WRITTEN FILENAME from a written one. It does not, and cannot, distinguish INVOKED-AS-A-STAGE from LISTED-AS-A-LINT-TARGET -- which is the distinction the claim rests on. This is why a careful author who explicitly wrote a negative control still shipped the gap: the control varied a different dimension than the assertion depends on. Worth keeping as a lesson in its own right -- a negative control only earns confidence along the axis it actually varies.

== WHY THIS ONE IS WORSE THAN THE PRIOR SIX ==

 1. THREE suites delegate their digest verification to this single dormant lane: crates/fln-rt/tests/abi_contract.rs (pin_binding_is_present), crates/fln-olean/tests/olean_contract.rs, and crates/fln-conformance/tests/contract_roots.rs. All three are shape-only by design and say so honestly.
 2. NO RUST TEST CAN EVER SUBSTITUTE. INVENTORY_DIGEST is sha256 of the inventory text (gen_abi_contract.py:1348) and the closed dependency universe (D1) contains no sha256 -- fln-hash is BLAKE3. contract_roots.rs documents this and correctly refuses to implement sha256 just to satisfy a test. So the Python extractor is not merely the current verifier, it is the ONLY POSSIBLE ONE, and it is unwired. This is not an unwatched join; it is a sole mechanism left dormant.
 3. It sits under the ABI membrane. Everything above fln-rt in the rank order trusts these tables.

== THE TABLES ARE CURRENTLY CORRECT -- AND THAT IS THE POINT ==

Run locally on 2026-07-26 with the pinned toolchain present:

  python3 -I -S scripts/extract/gen_abi_contract.py --check
  -> "check OK (5 artifacts, 775 census rows, 1 target layout rows,
      inventory digest f61654c61c404f3c...)"

exit 0, and that digest matches INVENTORY_DIGEST in crates/fln-rt/src/abi.rs byte-for-byte. So the ABI tables are NOT stale. They are UNCHECKED. Same shape as franken_lean-ext-observable-fixture-drift-gap-vqnu: the artifact was backed the whole time and nobody could have known it. The price of knowing was one command.

== WHAT THE ONE ci.yml JOB MUST DO ==

A scheduled job (plus workflow_dispatch for on-demand runs) that:

 1. INSTALLS THE PINNED TOOLCHAIN, tag read from SUITE.lock, not hardcoded --
    elan toolchain install leanprover/lean4:<tag>. Without it gen_abi_contract.py
    exits 2 as a setup failure; that exit MUST be treated as a job failure and
    never as a pass, which is precisely the trap the ci.yml comment describes.
 2. RUNS scripts/e2e/contract_drift.sh, which already sequences all three
    extractor --check lanes and emits schema-versioned NDJSON.
 3. REGENERATES FROM THE VENDORED PIN AND COMPARES BYTE-FOR-BYTE, failing on any
    drift. gen_abi_contract.py --check already does exactly this for all five
    outputs (inventory, target layout, ABI_CONTRACT.md, crates/fln-rt/src/abi.rs,
    the boundary rust module) and prints the first differing line. It also refuses
    a leftover .candidate sibling -- keep that behaviour.
 4. CARRIES A SEEDED MUTANT IT MUST KILL. contract_drift.sh already seeds mutants
    and asserts --check rejects them; the job must assert the mutant lane ran and
    failed as intended, so a --check that silently degenerated into a no-op is
    caught. A drift job that can only ever pass is the same defect one level up.
 5. VERIFIES THE TOOLCHAIN/VENDOR JOIN. render_target_layout already compares the
    toolchain's include/lean/lean.h against the vendored copy and dies if they
    differ; that cross-check is a load-bearing part of the value and should be
    visible in the job's output rather than incidental.

THE ENFORCEMENT MUST LAND WITH THE JOB, NOT AFTER IT. Once the job exists, replace
the contains() registration assertion in contract_roots.rs with one that
distinguishes invocation from mention -- and give it a negative control that varies
THAT axis: a lane named somewhere in the gate text but never invoked must fail the
assertion. Otherwise this bead's own fix reproduces this bead's own defect.

== WHAT fln-rt BEING CLEAN DOES NOT EARN ==

Recorded explicitly so that "cc_3 audited fln-rt and found it clean" is never read as
"the ABI tables are verified against the pin". THEY ARE NOT. Nothing checks them on
any commit, in any lane, on any schedule. The audit result and the binding are
independent facts and only one of them is good.

Specifically NOT established by this audit:
 * that abi.rs matches the pin on any commit other than the one hand-checked above;
 * that a future regeneration bug would be caught by anything (the TRIPWIRE constants
   in crates/fln-rt/tests/abi_contract.rs are transcribed from what the generator
   emitted, and abi_contract.rs says so -- they kill a LATER drift, not a value that
   was already wrong at extraction time);
 * that the olean contract or the extern census are any better off -- they ride the
   same dormant lane and were not separately verified here.

== THE NEGATIVE RESULT, RECORDED PLAINLY ==

I looked at fln-rt's code and found it sound. This is not filler; it sharpens the
finding by contrast, and a crate that survives the lens is worth knowing about.

 * crates/fln-rt/src/lib.rs is #![forbid(unsafe_code)]. crates/fln-rt/src/region.rs
   is 927 lines of relocation engine with ZERO unsafe -- all three "unsafe" hits in
   the file are comments. The raw mmap/syscall work is properly isolated in
   crates/fln-unsafe-region under #![deny(unsafe_code)] with ledgered
   FLN-UL-NNNN #[allow(unsafe_code)] sites and #![deny(clippy::undocumented_unsafe_blocks)].
   region.rs cites vendor/lean4-src/src/runtime/compact.cpp line ranges for its wire
   semantics throughout. 12 tests across region_engine.rs and region_fuzz.rs.
 * D3 law (a) -- no fln-unsafe-* may depend on fln-kernel/fln-checker -- is a TEST,
   not a rule. FLN-STRUCT-008 runs a real BFS over ACTUAL manifest edges,
   transitively, and reports the offending path; FLN-STRUCT-024 separately prevents
   the prohibition table in ci/WORKSPACE_GRAPH.txt from being emptied. Two layers.
 * D3 law (b) -- the no-admission export covenant -- is also a TEST. ci/BOUNDARY_API.txt
   carries 66 rows; every bare-pub boundary item must be classified; enforcement runs
   in BOTH directions (undeclared items and stale rows both fail) plus a
   post-expansion subset rule; the parser rejects any row with an empty field; and
   ledger.rs adds a string-level admission-token tripwire (fln_kernel, fln_checker,
   CheckedExpr) as defense-in-depth, with seeded laundering defects from fln-lld.
   The no-admission ARGUMENT itself is unverified prose -- inherently so -- and the
   module header claims only classification completeness, not the argument's truth.
   It does not overclaim.

== OWNERSHIP ==

The ci.yml job is .github/, which is cod_2's. Filed by cc_3 with the diagnosis,
the verification, and the acceptance criteria; the job itself is cod_2's to write.
The contract_roots.rs assertion repair is fln-conformance and therefore cc_3's, and
per the rule above it must land WITH the job rather than after it.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
 1. A scheduled workflow exists that installs the SUITE.lock-pinned toolchain and
    runs scripts/e2e/contract_drift.sh, treating exit 2 (setup failure) as failure.
 2. The job demonstrably kills a seeded mutant, so it cannot degenerate into a
    check that always passes.
 3. contract_roots.rs distinguishes invocation from mention, with a negative control
    that varies that axis.
 4. The three delegating suite headers (fln-rt abi_contract, fln-olean olean_contract,
    fln-conformance contract_roots) are corrected to name where the lane actually
    runs, since all three currently say it is registered in scripts/check.sh.
close_reason: The scheduled drift job exists and is bound; all four acceptance criteria verified on merits; the ci.yml deferral sentence repaired. Trigger-reachability gap filed separately.

comments.text:
SPECIFICATION FOR cod_2: the drift job. cc_3, 2026-07-26.

The five requirements in this bead's body still stand. This comment is the part that is NOT
in them: what the lane ALREADY does (so you do not rebuild it), the wiring constraints that
are not obvious from reading ci.yml, and one design fork with a recommendation. Measured
against HEAD 35b39e16.

== WHAT scripts/e2e/contract_drift.sh ALREADY DOES ==

Do not reimplement any of this. The lane is complete; it is only unwired.

 * Runs all three extractor --check lanes: gen_abi_contract.py --check,
   gen_olean_contract.py --check, gen_extern_census.sh --check. Each regenerates from the
   VENDORED pin in memory and byte-compares against every checked-in output, printing the
   first differing line.
 * SEEDS TWO MUTANTS AND REQUIRES THEM KILLED. Mutant A perturbs TAG_CLOSURE in
   crates/fln-rt/src/abi.rs; mutant B perturbs ABI_CONTRACT.md. Mutant A must be killed
   TWICE -- both the extractor --check and the cargo suite must exit nonzero -- and the
   lane fails if either survives. It also refuses to proceed if the seed anchor is missing
   (a mutation that silently no-ops is treated as a failure, not a pass), and verifies both
   files are restored BYTE-IDENTICALLY afterwards by sha.
 * Emits schema-versioned NDJSON to target/e2e/<run-id>/run.ndjson.

So acceptance criterion 4 of this bead is ALREADY MET BY THE LANE. Your job does not need
to seed anything; it needs to run the lane and honour its exit code.

== EXIT CODE CONTRACT -- THE ONLY PART THAT IS EASY TO GET WRONG ==

  0  no drift
  1  drift, or a mutant survived, or a restore failed
  2  SETUP FAILURE: python3 missing, hostile PYTHON* environment variables present, the
     evidence directory already claimed, or the pinned toolchain absent

EXIT 2 MUST FAIL THE JOB. This is the exact trap the existing ci.yml comment at the
contract_handoff step describes: asking for --check on a runner without the toolchain
"only produced a setup failure (exit 2) that looked like a real verification". A job that
treats 2 as anything but failure reproduces the defect this bead exists to close, and it
would do so silently.

== WIRING CONSTRAINTS THAT ARE NOT OBVIOUS ==

 1. THE LANE IS fln-e2e/1, NOT /2. It is absent from scripts/evidence.py entirely. That
    means NO E2E_STEP_ORDERS registration is required -- unlike the /2 lanes, where an
    unregistered scenario is a hard failure. One less coupling; do not add one.
 2. ci.yml's verify step compares its artifact roots with `observed != expected_names`,
    i.e. THE expected_roots SET IS CLOSED, not a subset check. Any step writing into
    FLN_E2E_ART_ROOT must join both expected_roots and the specs tuple, or the verify step
    fails for everyone on every commit.
 3. The lane MUTATES TRACKED FILES (crates/fln-rt/src/abi.rs, ABI_CONTRACT.md) and restores
    them. Harmless on a fresh CI checkout. In the SHARED DEV TREE it must never be run while
    a gate lane holds /data/tmp/fln-gate.lockfile: it moves the tree twice, which is exactly
    what the three-sample repository_state() check kills a lane for.

== THE DESIGN FORK, AND MY RECOMMENDATION ==

Option A: add a step to ci.yml's existing e2e job.
Option B: a SEPARATE scheduled workflow file (schedule: plus workflow_dispatch).

RECOMMEND B, for a reason that is mostly constraint 2 above. A drift job wants a cadence
(nightly/weekly) and an elan install that would slow every commit. But if it writes into the
per-commit evidence root, the closed expected_roots set forces it to be present in EVERY
per-commit bundle -- so a job that runs on a schedule would be asserted as complete on
commits where it never ran. That is a new instance of this bead's own family: a completeness
assertion over a thing that is not there. A separate workflow with its own artifact root
avoids the coupling entirely, and workflow_dispatch gives an on-demand run for anyone
touching the ABI.

Reading the tag, since it must not be hardcoded (SUITE.lock is the single ceremony):

  reference leanprover/lean4 tag=v4.32.0 commit=8c9... tree=ba1...

  PIN_TAG="$(sed -E 's/.*tag=([^ ]+).*/\1/' <<<"$(grep -E '^reference ' SUITE.lock)")"
  elan toolchain install "leanprover/lean4:$PIN_TAG"

gen_abi_contract.py additionally cross-checks the toolchain's own include/lean/lean.h
against the vendored copy and dies if they differ (render_target_layout). That join is
load-bearing and free -- worth surfacing in the job log rather than leaving incidental.

== WHEN IT LANDS, ONE THING OF MINE MUST LAND WITH IT ==

crates/fln-conformance/tests/contract_roots.rs declares contract_drift.sh in
UNWIRED_LANE_ALLOWANCE. That allowance is checked in BOTH directions, so the moment your job
invokes the lane, the fln-conformance suite goes RED until the declaration is removed. That
is deliberate -- it is what stops the allowance outliving the defect -- but it means your
commit and my one-line deletion must land together, or the workspace reddens in the gap.

Ping me when you start and I will have the deletion ready; or take it yourself, it is
removing one entry from a const array plus the doc line above it. Same commit, either way.

Note also that my invocation check recognises ci.yml execution as `./<path>` at the start of
a line, and check.sh invocation as the COMMAND of a run_stage. If you wire it some third way
(a composite action, a `bash -c`, a matrix step), tell me and I will widen the scanner --
otherwise the guard will correctly report the lane as still unwired and you will get a
confusing red.

== WHAT I AM NOT ASKING FOR ==

Not asking you to touch scripts/e2e/contract_drift.sh; it is correct as written. Not asking
for the olean or extern-census halves to be split out; the lane already sequences all three
and splitting them would triple the toolchain install. Not asking for this to block anything
-- the ABI tables are verifiably correct today and the risk is drift from here.

title: W2: olean codec write + .ilean — byte-identical faithful emission, atomic promotion
description:
Implement the olean codec, write side + .ilean (§7.3, §7.3b): region construction the Reference loads — identical header discipline, identical object layout — and in faithful mode BYTE-IDENTICAL output for FL-INV-04 (read a Reference olean, rebuild, diff bytes = empty; then the harder fresh-elaboration direction for the deterministic subset, residual freedoms pinned by registered CGSE policies per spike G0-5).

Two identities travel with every stored object: semantic hash (canonical meaning under the schema) and byte hash (stored encoding). Cross-file artifact sets (.olean + .ilean + native siblings) promote through a transaction manifest: staged, verified, then published atomically together or rolled back together — a crash mid-promotion leaves unreachable staging, never a half-published module. The .ilean codec is an exact epoch projection (spans, identifier occurrences, resolution targets with the pin field order, omissions, and position conventions) generated from the same normative schema layer as the olean codec so writer and checker cannot skew; richer server metadata lives in Palimpsest — .ilean stays exactly as boring as the ecosystem expects.

Acceptance: FL-INV-04 round-trip green at 100% of the Corpus set (PG-8); Reference toolchain loads and checks our written oleans (mixed-producer matrix seed); kill -9 drills at every promotion step leave recoverable state. Tests: byte-diff rigs per corpus file; .ilean field-order fixtures; the fault drill family (§18.2) for promotion.

## Acceptance Criteria

All bead-specific requirements, acceptance conditions, tests, invariants, compatibility surfaces, evidence levels, performance gates, negative/recovery cases, and user-visible behaviors stated above remain mandatory. In addition, the MANDATORY VERIFICATION DEFINITION OF DONE in Notes must be satisfied with named unit/property/mutation suites, at least one shared real-path no-mock E2E scenario plus failure/recovery coverage, detailed human and schema-versioned NDJSON artifacts, and reproducible close evidence. comments.author: cc_1
comments.text:
INHERITING fln-sv7x's WRITE HALF — SHARING PRESERVATION IS A PROPERTY OF THIS ENCODER, AND IT NEEDS AN ENCODER-SIDE ASSERTION (PeachBass/cc_1, 2026-07-25). fln-sv7x closes today on the two halves that exist; this is the half that does not, re-homed rather than retired.

WHAT YOU INHERIT: "serialization preserving sharing exactly". An interned term is a DAG. An encoder that writes it as a tree has destroyed the sharing the interner exists to create, and `k` levels of two-way sharing become `2^k` written nodes from `k` stored ones — a resource fact, not an aesthetic one.

WHY IT LANDS HERE RATHER THAN ON sv7x: fln-olean is decode-only. decode_expr is at crates/fln-olean/src/decl.rs:537 and `rg 'fn encode|fn write_'` over that file returns nothing. The property cannot be asserted before the encoder exists, and the encoder is this bead's subject.

THREE THINGS ALREADY ESTABLISHED, so none is re-derived:

1. THE READ HALF IS ALREADY PINNED, ON A REAL ARTIFACT, and it is the baseline your encoder must match. crates/fln-olean/tests/decl_decode.rs::real_declarations_decode_to_shared_dags_not_expanded_trees decodes tribunal/fixtures/c3/Init.SizeOfLemmas.olean and requires a DAG: DeclDecoder::decode_expr memoises on the object offset, so two slots pointing at one object become two references to one Expr node. The format therefore ALREADY carries sharing and the decoder already preserves it. An encoder that expands is the only way to lose it.

2. THE OBVIOUS ASSERTION DOES NOT WORK, and this is the part worth reading before writing the test. sv7x prescribed "intern, encode, decode, re-intern, and assert the STORE SIZE is the same". Re-interning RESTORES sharing — that is what an interner does — so store sizes match on both sides while the wire form in between lost every bit of it. The prescribed check is GREEN against the defect. Structural equality is worse and round-tripping is worse still; a sharing-losing encoder passes both.

   THE DISCRIMINATOR IS ENCODER-SIDE: encoded BYTE LENGTH, or the node count observed during decode, against the INTERNED node count. Assert against what the encoder emitted, never against a value a later stage repairs. That is AGENTS.md item 8's law one floor up, and hv9m is the same shape at the digest level.

3. THE CANONICAL CODEC WANTS THE OPPOSITE AND MUST NOT BE "FIXED". fln-hash's Canonical is "a value with exactly one canonical encoding under a frozen schema", so sharing-SENSITIVITY there would give one value many encodings and move every content-addressed digest with construction history. Pinned as its dual by fln-env's interning_rewrites_sharing_and_canonical_bytes_do_not_move. If anyone reads "preserve sharing in both codecs" literally, they break content addressing — sv7x's original wording said exactly that and it was wrong.

SUGGESTED PLACEMENT: franken_lean-0vf (G0-5, byte-identical olean re-emit spike) exists to "enumerate and pin serialization freedoms". Whether the pinned format's sharing/back-reference encoding is a FREEDOM or a REQUIREMENT is precisely such a question, and answering it there before this bead builds the encoder would stop the encoder being written twice. I have not touched 0vf; naming it because that is where the question is cheapest to answer.

title: W4 Vellum: maintain the rope's line index incrementally instead of recomputing per edit
description:
Filed by cc_3 on 2026-07-25 while landing the rope substrate (fln-4yos, commit 684f2bf). Named in that module's docs as a follow-up, so it exists as a bead rather than as a promise in a comment.

## What is owed

Incremental maintenance of the rope's derived line index and position projections.

Today an edit DROPS the derived SourceText and the next position query recomputes it with one O(bytes) pass. That was chosen deliberately: it makes "the text was updated but the index was not" structurally impossible instead of merely tested for, which is the failure mode that actually bites in editor code. The cost is that a keystroke followed by a hover is whole-file work, which defeats part of the reason a rope exists.

## What good looks like

An edit updates the line index and whatever the projections need in time proportional to the edit and the number of lines it touches, not to the file. The piece table already knows exactly which byte range changed.

## Acceptance Criteria

The correctness contract is unchanged and non-negotiable: every position query — line_of, line_start, line_count, position_of, and both column inverses — must agree with a freshly constructed SourceText over the post-edit bytes. The existing differential in rope.rs already asserts this at every char boundary after every edit in a seeded sequence, and it must keep passing unmodified; if incremental maintenance requires weakening that test, the design is wrong rather than the test.

Cases the incremental path must get right, each with a named test, because each is a way a line index goes subtly stale:
* an edit that inserts or deletes a newline, shifting every subsequent line start;
* an edit that SPLITS A CRLF PAIR, so a CR that used to be part of a line terminator becomes a lone CR and the line count changes in a way a naive delta misses;
* an edit that joins two lines by deleting a newline;
* an edit entirely inside one line, which must not touch any other line start;
* an edit at byte 0 and an edit at the end of the file;
* an edit on a text with no trailing newline, and one that adds a trailing newline.

Mutants to kill: recompute the index from the wrong range; apply the byte delta to line starts at or before the edit rather than strictly after; forget that a deletion can remove more than one newline; update the index but not the cached byte length.

A benchmark or a counted-operations assertion demonstrating the work is proportional to the edit rather than the file, since the whole point is a performance property and "it looks incremental" is not evidence.

## Notes

Purely a performance change behind an unchanged contract, which is why it is separable and low-risk to defer. It does NOT block the green tree (franken_lean-tkr2) or anything else — the rope is correct today, just not incremental.

title: W9: Palimpsest — event journal, causal proof graph, the welding law
description:
Implement the Palimpsest substrate + causal proof graph (§15.1): structured elaboration events — unifier attempts, instance candidates, macro expansions, scheduler decisions, cache hits, kernel verdicts — recorded per declaration into ring-buffered traces (always-on cheap tier) and full archives (opt-in, frankensqlite-backed), keyed to Syntax ranges. Recording NEVER changes results (observer discipline, enforced by dual-run rigs: traced and untraced runs must produce identical products).

From the journal, the causal proof graph (Bet B7): typed nodes (source ranges, commands, expansions, declarations, instances, searches, tactic steps, kernel/checker verdicts, extension entries, build facets, capability sessions, branches/merges) and typed EDGE FAMILIES (IMPORTS; READS_TYPE vs READS_VALUE vs UNFOLDS; SELECTS_INSTANCE/REJECTS_INSTANCE; USES_SIMP_RULE; EXPANDS_FROM/GENERATED_BY; READS_GRAMMAR/WRITES_GRAMMAR; PROVES/CHECKED_BY/CROSS_CHECKED_BY; COMPILES_TO/EXPORTS_SYMBOL/INITIALIZES_BEFORE; READS_FILE/SPAWNS_TOOL/LOADS_LIBRARY; INVALIDATES/REUSES; SUGGESTED_BY; MIGRATES_TO/REPAIRS), every edge carrying span, phase, policy/epoch, receipt id, and a COMPLETENESS CLASS: Complete (perturbation-tested), Conservative (may over-approximate, must not miss), Observed, Opaque, Inferred.

title: G0-5: Byte-identical olean re-emit spike — enumerate and pin serialization freedoms
description:
G0-5 Byte-identical re-emit spike (§22.1-5, feeds §7.3): read a set of Reference-produced oleans, rebuild the compacted region from the decoded object graph, and byte-diff the output against the original. Then the harder direction: elaborate a module fresh (prototype path) and match the Reference emission for the deterministic subset.

This is the feasibility proof for FL-INV-04 (codec fidelity: read-then-write is byte identity in faithful mode) and directly prices risk R3 (byte-exact write over-constrained by hidden emission nondeterminism). Every serialization freedom found — object traversal order, region layout choices, padding, interning decisions — must be ENUMERATED and pinned with a registered CGSE policy, or (if genuinely nondeterministic upstream) documented as the scoped-down law of R3 (load-compatible + canonical write with the byte law kept for read-then-write).

Acceptance: (a) read->rebuild->bytediff == identical for the fixture set; (b) an exhaustive written enumeration of serialization freedoms with a pinned policy per row; (c) a verdict memo: FL-INV-04 stands as stated, or the R3 fallback scope is invoked with exact wording for the Parity Ledger row. Tests: the round-trip harness becomes the standing codec rig (§18.2 codec rigs) and the FL-INV-04 CI gate at PG-8.

## Acceptance Criteria

All bead-specific requirements, acceptance conditions, tests, invariants, compatibility surfaces, evidence levels, performance gates, negative/recovery cases, and user-visible behaviors stated above remain mandatory. In addition, the MANDATORY VERIFICATION DEFINITION OF DONE in Notes must be satisfied with named unit/property/mutation suites, at least one shared real-path no-mock E2E scenario plus failure/recovery coverage, detailed human and schema-versioned NDJSON artifacts, and reproducible close evidence. No listed feature or claim may be silently narrowed, deferred, mocked, or declared complete through an unclassified divergence.
design:
OPEN-QUESTION CLOSEOUT — G0-5 owns OQ-1 and emits a checked OleanSerializationFreedomV1 row for every generated OLEAN-contract field and writer stage, not merely freedoms noticed informally. Each row binds stable id, source/contract anchor, affected byte range/object relation, pinned Reference behavior, semantic and byte effects, deterministic CGSE policy, mode/epoch/platform scope, fixtures/perturbations, claim/evidence class, and immutable roots. Missing, duplicate, stale, unexercised, or unknown rows block OQ-1.

comments.text:
FREEDOMS-VERSUS-REQUIREMENTS INVENTORY, ESTABLISHED FROM THE DECODER AND THE REAL ARTIFACTS RATHER THAN FROM SPEC PROSE (PeachBass/cc_1, 2026-07-25). This is acceptance item (b) — the enumeration — not items (a) or (c). Sizing at the end.

METHOD, AND WHY IT IS NOT A RE-READ OF THE CONTRACT. A field is a REQUIREMENT if the read side rejects or misreads when it changes; a FREEDOM if two different encodings decode to the same value. That test is mechanical and it is answerable from code that exists: fln_olean::region::OleanView::parse, fln_rt::region::audit, and DeclDecoder in crates/fln-olean/src/decl.rs. The evidence base is bead franken_lean-y24's memo at tribunal/fixtures/c3/FINDINGS.md, which resurrected ALL 2 433 .olean files of the pinned toolchain — 9 562 406 objects, 158 608 constants, zero integrity faults — plus the three C3 fixtures in-tree (Init 5 784 B, Init.BinderNameHint 9 792 B, Init.SizeOfLemmas 27 080 B, all header `olean` v2 at 4.32.0).

=== A. REQUIREMENTS — the read side rejects or misreads if these move ===

R1  POINTER LAW. Every stored pointer == base_addr + FILE offset (header included, not
    data-region-relative). OleanView::deref depends on it exactly; a different convention
    silently dereferences the wrong object rather than failing. FINDINGS §1.
R2  m_rc == 0. Persistent-in-region is enforced by fln_rt::region::audit over every
    object, reachable or not. FINDINGS §3.
R3  HEADER WORD PACKING. Low 32 bits m_rc; high 32 pack m_cs_sz(16) | m_other(8) |
    m_tag(8), GCC/Clang low-to-high bitfield order. obj_header reads exactly this.
R4  CTOR FIELD ORDER: all pointer fields first in declaration order, then the scalar
    area. Not the Lean structure's declaration order — ModuleData stores
    [imports, constNames, constants, extraConstNames, entries][isModule: u8] though
    isModule is declared first. The decoder indexes by slot. FINDINGS §5.
R5  SCALAR/POINTER DISCRIMINATION by bit 0 (box(i) = (i<<1)|1). Fieldless enum ctors are
    never objects. DeclDecoder::is_scalar branches on this and errors typed on a scalar
    where an Expr was required. FINDINGS §6.
R6  Name CARRIES ITS CACHED HASH in the scalar area (m_other = 2 pointers + usize hash).
    Arity from the surface inductive alone is wrong. The decoder cross-checks Name.hash
    against its own recomputation. FINDINGS §7.
R7  STRING m_size COUNTS THE NUL; m_size == 0 never occurs (empty string stores 1).
    FINDINGS §8.
R8  Expr.Data WORD MUST EQUAL OUR RECOMPUTATION. decl.rs:583 — `if self.cross_check &&
    expr.data().0 != stored` is a typed DeclError::CrossCheck. This is the strongest
    requirement in the format: it binds the emitter to our own arithmetic.
R9  constNames.length == constants.length, observed in all 2 433 modules. FINDINGS §12.
R10 VERSION 2 (contract admits {2,3}; v3 never occurs in the shipped stdlib).

None of these is a choice. An encoder that gets any of them wrong produces an artifact
the existing reader refuses or misreads, and R8 in particular cannot be satisfied by
copying bytes — it requires computing the same data word we compute.

=== B. FREEDOMS — several encodings decode to the same value ===

F1  OBJECT PLACEMENT / FILE OFFSETS. Nothing in the read side requires a particular
    layout; any offset that derefs is legal. This is THE freedom that byte identity
    turns on, and it needs a registered CGSE traversal/allocation order.
F2  base_addr. 64 KiB-aligned (REGION_ALIGN) but the value is the producer's choice, and
    it is stored, so it is reproducible only by pinning it. FINDINGS §1.
F3  ROOT SLOT vs ROOT OBJECT PLACEMENT. The first size_t of the data region (file offset
    88) is a pointer slot written last; the root object "TYPICALLY sits near the END of
    the file". FINDINGS §2 — and "typically" is the tell: that is a compactor artifact,
    not a law, so it must be pinned rather than assumed.
F4  m_cs_sz PADDING THRESHOLD. Small objects store the padded byte size rounded to
    LEAN_OBJECT_SIZE_DELTA; big objects store 0. The ROUNDING is required (R3 reads the
    field); WHICH side of the threshold an object falls on is the emitter's decision and
    must be pinned. FINDINGS §4.
F5  mpz LIMB PLACEMENT. The compactor copies limbs immediately after the object and
    rewrites exactly one interior pointer. "Immediately after" is a compactor convention,
    not something the reader enforces. FINDINGS §9.

=== C. THE FINDING: INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM THE READ SIDE, LOAD-BEARING ANYWAY ===

A1  SHARING. This is the one the orchestrator asked to have named, and it is the reason
    fln-sv7x could not be answered from the read side.

    FROM THE READ SIDE IT IS A FREEDOM. DeclDecoder::decode_expr memoises on the object
    offset, so a shared encoding and a fully expanded one decode to EQUAL Exprs. No
    integrity check, no cross-check, and no round-trip test can tell them apart —
    which is exactly why fln-sv7x's prescribed store-size assertion was green against
    the defect.

    IT IS NONETHELESS A REQUIREMENT, for a reason the read side cannot express.
    FINDINGS §14: the graphs are DAGs with heavy structural sharing, and "Prelude's
    88 880 distinct objects are referenced far more times than once each. A NAIVE
    TREE-WALK WOULD BLOW UP." An encoder that expands turns a bounded artifact into an
    unbounded one. The property is real, load-bearing, and invisible to every check the
    format has.

    SO IT IS NEITHER A FREEDOM TO BE PINNED BY POLICY NOR A REQUIREMENT THE READER
    ENFORCES. It is a third category, and 0vf's OleanSerializationFreedomV1 schema — which
    binds "pinned Reference behavior, semantic and byte effects, deterministic CGSE
    policy" — has no column that says "unenforceable from the read side". That is a gap
    in the row schema, not just in the inventory.

A2  WHICH OBJECTS SHARE. Granting that sharing must exist, WHICH subterms are shared is
    the compactor's decision, and nothing observable reveals the rule. Byte identity
    requires reproducing that exact decision. This is the single largest unpriced risk in
    the whole re-emit programme: R3's "byte-exact write over-constrained by hidden
    emission nondeterminism" is, concretely, this row.

A3  ABSENT CATEGORIES ARE NOT PROVEN ABSENT. FINDINGS §11 observed no Closure, External,
    StructArray, Promise, Task, Ref or Thunk across the pinned library. That is 2 433
    files of evidence, not a law. An encoder may legally never emit them; a READER must
    still handle them, and today they are exercised only by hostile-input tests. Emitter
    scope and reader scope differ here and the inventory should say so rather than let
    "never observed" become "cannot occur".

=== D. SIZING, HONESTLY ===

WHAT AN ENCODER COSTS. R1-R10 are mechanical and cheap — they are already implemented in
reverse by the decoder. F1-F5 are each a pinned policy plus a test. The real cost is A1
and A2: reproducing the compactor's sharing decisions byte-for-byte, with no read-side
oracle to check against short of the byte-diff itself. That is not a week of plumbing; it
is an open question with a research shape, and it is 0vf's actual subject.

WHAT IT UNBLOCKS. franken_lean-0nz (W2 olean codec write) directly; FL-INV-04's byte law;
G0-1's resurrection claim in the write direction; and the sv7x write half I re-homed to
0nz an hour ago.

WHAT IT DOES NOT EARN, stated because the plan promises byte-compatible WRITE as a shipped
surface and an inventory is not an encoder. This comment closes NONE of 0vf's three
acceptance items on its own: (a) read->rebuild->bytediff identity for the fixture set is
not attempted here; (b) is advanced but not complete — a row per GENERATED CONTRACT FIELD
is required and this is a row per OBSERVED BEHAVIOUR, which is a different and smaller
axis; (c) the G0SpikeDecisionV1 memo needs (a) before it can be honest. Anyone reading
this as "0vf is mostly done" would be wrong by the largest item in it.

WHAT I WOULD DO NEXT, in order: build the read->rebuild->bytediff harness on the three C3
fixtures FIRST, because it is the only instrument that can answer A1/A2 at all, and the
first byte-diff will tell us within an hour whether R3's fallback scope is going to be
invoked. That is a bounded piece with a decisive outcome, and it is worth more than
completing the row schema against the contract.

comments.author: cc_1
comments.text:
CORRECTING MY OWN "BOUNDED, DECISIVE, WITHIN AN HOUR" RECOMMENDATION FROM TEN MINUTES AGO. IT IS NOT BOUNDED, AND THE REASON IS STRUCTURAL (PeachBass/cc_1, 2026-07-25).

I recommended building the read->rebuild->bytediff harness on the three C3 fixtures first, called it "bounded, decisive", and said the first byte-diff would answer the sharing rows within an hour. Then I checked whether the decoder retains what a rebuild would need.

DECODING DISCARDS PLACEMENT ENTIRELY. `offset` appears in crates/fln-olean/src/decl.rs only inside DeclError variants — Shape{offset}, CrossCheck{offset} and friends. No decoded value carries it: ConstantInfo, Expr, Name and Level are pure semantic values with no file position, and there is no side table.

So 0vf's acceptance (a), as literally worded — "rebuild the compacted region FROM THE DECODED OBJECT GRAPH, and byte-diff the output against the original" — cannot be satisfied cheaply, because the decoded graph does not know where anything was. A rebuild from it must RE-DERIVE layout, and re-deriving layout is exactly the encoder whose cost I priced as research-shaped in the inventory above. The harness is not the cheap instrument that answers the expensive question; it IS the expensive question.

THE TWO READINGS, AND WHY THE OBVIOUS THIRD ONE IS VACUOUS:

  (i) REBUILD FROM THE DECODED GRAPH — literal wording. Requires deciding placement and
      sharing afresh, i.e. the full encoder. Answers everything and costs everything.
  (ii) REBUILD FROM THE REGION-LEVEL OBJECT GRAPH — objects with their contents and
      edges, placement re-derived, but no decl-level semantics. Tests layout derivation
      and the sharing decision, which are the actual freedoms, WITHOUT needing
      ConstantInfo round-tripping. This is the real spike and it is what I think 0vf
      means.
  (iii) COPY THE REGION BYTES PRESERVING OFFSETS — trivially byte-identical, proves
      nothing about emission. Worth naming only so nobody accidentally builds it and
      reports a green byte-diff.

That (iii) exists and would pass is itself worth recording: a read->rebuild->bytediff
harness can be built that always succeeds and measures nothing. The criterion does not
say which of the three it means.

WHAT I GOT WRONG AND WHY, because it is the fourth time today with the same shape: I
reasoned about the rebuild from where I was standing — inside the DECODER, where the
object graph feels present and complete — and inferred that rebuilding from it was
mechanical. What the decoder gives you is the SEMANTIC graph; the artifact is the
semantic graph PLUS a layout, and the layout is the whole subject of this bead. Same
tell as CanonWriter "has no inverse" and `add_decl` being one method: describe what a
thing does where you are, infer what it is.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE SIZING ABOVE, which otherwise stands: there is NO cheap decisive
instrument. The first byte-diff is not an hour away — it is behind the layout-derivation
work, which is the same work as the sharing rows. My "build the harness first" ordering
was wrong; the harness and the hard part are the same thing, and 0vf should be planned as
one piece rather than as a cheap probe followed by a decision.

SCOPING QUESTION RECORDED, NOT BLOCKING: whether (a) means reading (i) or (ii) changes
what gets built. I believe (ii), because (i) requires ConstantInfo round-tripping that
0vf never asks for and (iii) is vacuous. Nothing is blocked while this waits — no work
stops, and whoever picks 0vf up can adopt (ii) and say so. I am recording it rather than
holding the bead.
