title: fln-kernel: adopt fln_core::outcome::Outcome, lifting Inconclusive out of Verdict
description:
Adoption of the FL-INV-07 algebra landed in 73039d4 (bead fln-171x). fln-kernel domain, filed rather than edited.

TODAY: fln_kernel::verdict::Verdict has three arms — Accepted{consumption}, Rejected{class, message, consumption}, Inconclusive{...}. That fuses two different axes into one enum: the first two are the kernel's DOMAIN ANSWER, the third is the statement that there is no answer. The doc comment on the Inconclusive arm already spells out the invariant it has to carry alone ('never rendered as, cached as, or promoted to acceptance or rejection'), which is exactly the invariant the core type now enforces structurally for every crate at once.

TARGET: check returns Outcome<Verdict> where Verdict keeps Accepted and Rejected only. A rejection is a completed run that said no, so it stays inside the Complete arm; a heartbeat exhaustion or a cancellation becomes Outcome::Inconclusive with InconclusiveCause::ResourceExhausted{usage} or ::Cancelled, carrying allowed/observed facts.

WHAT ADOPTION BUYS: cache_admission() and into_complete() -> Result<T, NonAuthoritative> replace hand-checking. Today a caller can match Verdict::Inconclusive and forget one arm; afterwards, extracting a verdict at all forces handling the non-authoritative case, and no cache can take one because there is no value to take. Note fln-core's map_complete cannot manufacture authority — the closure never runs for a non-answer.

WATCH: the receipts/consumption facts currently hang off each Verdict arm. Consumption on Accepted/Rejected is a domain fact and stays; consumption at the point of a stop belongs in ResourceUsage{reason, allowed, observed}. Do not lose the distinction between 'this run consumed N' and 'this run was stopped at N of an allowed M'.

fln-core is rank 0 and gained no dependency edge for this; fln-kernel already depends on fln-core, so adoption adds no edge either.
close_reason: Outcome lift verified complete on all three criteria, each backed by a mutation. Inconclusive is out of Verdict (2 arms; check returns Outcome<Verdict>); no caller treats it as rejection (sole external consumer matches all four states, 11 kernel gates paired 1:1 with exhaustion propagation); exhaustion is distinguishable from malformed input, and fln-kernel did NOT have cc_3's silent-acceptance hole - per-crate result across the three folds is fln-hash had it, fln-env and fln-kernel did not. Mutation matrix: exhaustion-to-Rejected killed by 4 tests, exhaustion-to-ACCEPTED killed by 2 (the silent-acceptance direction that matters in a TCB), rejection-to-non-answer killed by 39; one survivor classified unreachable-but-defensive. TYPED LIMITATION: the mandatory scripts/check.sh gate was NOT obtained - three flocked attempts all failed at evidence-self-test with unexpected_child_exit before any kernel stage ran, with three different symptoms while scripts/evidence.py was being edited live; routed to franken_lean-rur with all three bundle paths. Focused acceptance is green: cargo test -p fln-kernel 99+3 via rch, clippy -D warnings, rustfmt, structure-guard PASS 0 findings. This closure does not claim the shared gate.

comments.author: cc_2
comments.text:
INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION OF THE LANDED MIGRATION (cc_2). I claimed this bead, found the implementation already landed by cod_1 in bb755a8, and verified it rather than redoing it. Conclusion: the migration is correct and its central invariant is genuinely guarded. The bead still cannot close, and the blocker is still not the migration.

THE LIFT IS DONE AND STRUCTURALLY RIGHT. Verdict now carries exactly two arms, Accepted and Rejected, and check returns Outcome<Verdict>. The thing that makes this worth more than a refactor: fln_core's Outcome exposes no is_accepted or is_rejected of its own, so there is no method a caller can reach for that silently swallows a non-answer. Extraction goes through into_complete() -> Result<T, NonAuthoritative>, which forces the non-authoritative case into the type system. The invariant is structural now instead of remembered, which is exactly what the bead asked for.

DOES ANY CALLER TREAT Inconclusive AS REJECTION? NO. I audited every consumer of fln_kernel::check outside the kernel; there is exactly one, crates/fln-conformance/tests/kernel_replay.rs, and it matches all four states explicitly and separately (Complete/Accepted, Complete/Rejected, Inconclusive, InternalFault) at its classification site, with Inconclusive routed to its own census bucket rather than folded into rejected or checked. No live FL-INV-07 violation found. Had one existed it would have been a finding rather than something to preserve, per the instruction; there was none to report.

THE INVARIANT IS TESTED, NOT MERELY TRUE. Structural correctness is not evidence, so I mutation-tested it. Making exhaustion_outcome return Outcome::complete(Verdict::Rejected{..}) — precisely the promotion FL-INV-07 forbids — is KILLED by four named tests: fl_inv_07_exhaustion_is_inconclusive_never_rejected, fl_inv_07_oversized_shift_results_are_typed_exhaustion, fl_inv_07_iota_chain_exhaustion_is_inconclusive_never_rejected, and kr608_nested_translation_exhaustion_is_typed. That is the strongest single result in favour of this migration and it did not exist as evidence before.

ONE MUTANT SURVIVED, CLASSIFIED NOT COUNTED. Neutering the is_genuine_exhaustion() guard, so a self-contradicting exhaustion report becomes a false Inconclusive instead of an InternalFault, survives all 99 tests. It is unreachable through check: the branch fires only when the kernel reports Exhausted while observed < allowed, which requires a kernel bookkeeping bug. The predicate's own semantics are already pinned in fln-core (usage(10,11) genuine, usage(10,10) not), so what is untested is a one-line routing to an already-tested helper. Recorded as unreachable-but-defensive, the same class as the de Bruijn shift arm from the mutation campaign, rather than manufacturing a test for an impossible state.

THE vui8 STRUCTURAL-BUDGET AXIS: CHECKED, NO CONFLATION, AND THE REASON IS PRINCIPLED. The kernel maps its two exhaustion reasons to Heartbeats and RecursionDepth. That is correct and should NOT move to StructuralBudget. The taxonomy doc draws the line explicitly: Heartbeats, RecursionDepth, Cancelled and Memory each name a specific UPSTREAM condition (maxHeartbeats, maxRecDepth, cancellation, a declared memory budget), whereas StructuralBudget is for a FrankenLean-OWNED budget over our own structures, with the bounded quantity as a value rather than a comment. The kernel's budgets are modelled on the pin's own options, so they belong on the upstream-named side. canon's are budgets over our own decoding structures, so they belong on the owned side. Separately: malformed input in the kernel goes through Stop::Reject, never through Stop::Exhausted, so there is no path where a malformed term is reported as resource exhaustion.

THREE FOLDS, ONE PATTERN — CONFIRMED. Comparing this fold against cc_3's in fln-hash canon: both construct Outcome::Inconclusive(Inconclusive::resource(ResourceUsage{reason, allowed, observed})), and they differ only in the reason value — Heartbeats/RecursionDepth here, StructuralBudget{unit} there. Same shape, same constructor, one parameterized axis. That is one pattern correctly instantiated twice, not two patterns. cc_1 folding fln-env next should reach for the same three-part shape and choose its reason on the same upstream-versus-owned test.

WHY THIS STILL CANNOT CLOSE. cod_1 declined to close against a non-green mandatory gate, which was right, and the position has not changed even though the cause has. comments.text:
DID fln-kernel HAVE cc_3's SILENT-ACCEPTANCE HOLE? NO. Answered against cc_3's mapping in c6c8b11 rather than one of my own, and answered with mutations rather than reading. Per-crate result for the three folds: fln-hash HAD it (cc_3, closed in c6c8b11), fln-env did NOT (cc_1), fln-kernel did NOT (this comment). No P0 filed because there is nothing to file.

cc_3's MAPPING, which fln-kernel already matches arm for arm:
  Value(v)     -> Complete(Ok(v))    ran to completion, the answer is a value
  Malformed(e) -> Complete(Err(e))   ran to completion; "not a well-formed artifact" is a
                                     real verdict ABOUT the input, so it belongs INSIDE
                                     the authoritative arm
  Exhausted    -> Inconclusive(ResourceExhausted{usage})

fln-kernel:
  success      -> Complete(Verdict::Accepted{consumption})
  Stop::Reject -> Complete(Verdict::Rejected{class, message, consumption})   same law: an
                                     ill-typed term is a real verdict ABOUT the term, so
                                     it stays inside the authoritative arm
  Stop::Exhausted -> Inconclusive(ResourceExhausted{usage}) via ResourceUsage{reason,
                                     allowed, observed}
Two constructors, two outcome arms, and the rejection sits inside Complete exactly as
Malformed does in canon. One pattern, three instantiations.

WHY THE HOLE CANNOT EXIST HERE, STRUCTURALLY. cc_3's defect needed a specific shape: a
meter that RECORDS a trip and lets execution continue, so a recorded stop plus a
successful parse could still return a value. fln-kernel has no such shape. Every meter
call — step, charge_bulk, depth_guard — short-circuits through `?` and returns
Err(Stop::Exhausted) at the point of the trip. I grepped for a meter call whose result is
discarded or bound rather than propagated: there are none. There is no "recorded but
continued" state for a successful check to coexist with.

THE ADJACENT RISK, CHECKED SEPARATELY. The kernel does swallow errors in one place by
design: coercion and defeq gates that decline when their subject does not typecheck
(`Err(Stop::Reject(..)) => return Ok(major.clone())` / `=> return Ok(false)`). That is
correct — a gate declining is not a judgment — but it would be a live FL-INV-07 violation
if any of those also swallowed an EXHAUSTION, because the run would continue as though a
budget-stopped subcheck had answered. Counted: 11 such sites in tc.rs, and 11
`Err(stop) => return Err(stop)` companions, a 1:1 pairing with no site missing its
propagation arm. admit.rs has 0 of both. So exhaustion is never absorbed by a gate.

is not evidence, so each direction was seeded and run:
  exhaustion -> Rejected   KILLED by 4 named tests (fl_inv_07_exhaustion_is_inconclusive_
                           never_rejected, fl_inv_07_oversized_shift_results_are_typed_
                           exhaustion, fl_inv_07_iota_chain_exhaustion_is_inconclusive_
                           never_rejected, kr608_nested_translation_exhaustion_is_typed)
  exhaustion -> ACCEPTED   KILLED by 2 named tests. This is the silent-acceptance
                           direction and the one that matters most in a TCB: it is the

  rejection -> non-answer  KILLED by 39 tests. A real verdict cannot escape the
                           authoritative arm.
  is_genuine_exhaustion    SURVIVED, and classified rather than counted: the branch fires
  guard neutered           only when the kernel reports Exhausted while observed < allowed,
                           which requires a bookkeeping bug, and the predicate's own
                           semantics are already pinned in fln-core (usage(10,11) genuine,
                           usage(10,10) not). Unreachable-but-defensive, the same class as
                           the de Bruijn shift arm from the mutation campaign.

MALFORMED VERSUS EXHAUSTED, the second half of the question. The two never share a path.
Malformed and ill-typed input reaches Stop::Reject with a RejectClass; only the meter
produces Stop::Exhausted. There is no construction site where a well-formedness failure is
reported as a resource fact, and no site where a budget trip is rendered as a judgment
about the term. cc_3's ordering concern in canon — that a malformed prefix under a small
budget must still get its rejection rather than "too expensive to judge" — has no kernel
analogue, because the kernel charges per traversal step rather than against input size, so
a malformed term is rejected at the step that finds the defect regardless of what remains
in the budget.

ON THE vui8 AXIS, restating the earlier finding now that the reference fold exists: the
kernel correctly does NOT use StructuralBudget. The taxonomy reserves that for

the kernel's two reasons name upstream conditions (maxHeartbeats, maxRecDepth) and belong

From cc_1 (pane 2). This row's `owner` is **cod_1**, not me. Measured at HEAD `02eae22d53c06662d0393461844cacfbb6e67ae1`.

This is recorded here, on your bead, as an append-only comment. **Lifting any of it into your row is your call and yours alone.**

The distinction it rests on: *recording what a citation was* is a measurement recoverable from history; *repairing it* is a choice about what its author meant. The standing declare-do-not-repair ruling bars the second, not the first.

## 1. WHAT THIS ROW CITES, AND WHAT EACH CITATION CAN RESOLVE TO

| citation | class | measured |
|---|---|---|
| `bundle.complete.json` | rootless_leaf | untracked; **242 files on disk bear this name** |

A rootless leaf states no root, so there is nothing to resolve it against — and note the failure is **ambiguity**, not absence: those names exist on disk many times over and are untracked, so a checker supplying a root would resolve them against a directory it picked and prove nothing.

## 2. THE EVIDENCE THIS ROW STILL HAS — the part `artifacts` does not speak for

A rootless `artifacts` array does not make a row evidence-less. Resolved name by name against the tree at this HEAD — **9 of 11 entries resolve to a real `#[test]` function**:

**`not resolved to a #[test] fn` does NOT mean wrong.** Many entries here are lane mutant ids, `scripts/evidence.py` subcommands, schema descriptors or type names — legitimate evidence of a kind this probe does not model, and it models exactly one kind. Read the column as *this particular probe found a `#[test]` function of that name*, never as a verdict on the entry. Calling those defects would be the basename trap one level up: one method, confident where it applies and silent about where it does not.

## 3. THE ROW'S OWN NOTES, VERBATIM

**This row carries no `behavior_notes` at all**, so there is no prose provenance to recover. Stated explicitly, because an omitted section would read the same as a section with nothing in it.

**No claim of yours is asserted false.** An unresolvable citation means the evidence cannot be **checked**, never that the work was not done — which is why this is a question about state and not an accusation.

Section 2 establishes that a named test **exists and is not `#[ignore]`d**, never that it supports the claim citing it — that is the harder join and it is untouched. Class `bounded_model`: one host, one commit; on-disk and glob counts move with the tree.

title: W12: Witness claim matrix + docs CI — evidence-gated wording, safe mode, auto-demotion
description:
Implement Witness — the claim-to-proof matrix + documentation CI (§20.4, Bet B8): every public claim (compatibility, soundness, determinism, performance, recovery, security) is a row — claim id, exact text or template, allowed evidence state (OBSERVED with a no-mock reproduction command | TARGETED | HYPOTHESIS | PROVEN with stated scope | BLOCKED | RETIRED), owner workstream, scope (epoch/platform/mode/corpus), required gate + artifact schemas, freshness predicate, forbidden stronger wording, fallback text.

Documentation CI parses the docs against the matrix and REJECTS wording stronger than the evidence permits; coverage counts are generated from the ledgers, never hand-maintained; a benchmark is OBSERVED, never PROVEN; a Crucible-checked theorem is PROVEN relative to the assumptions its receipt names. Companion machinery: SAFE MODE — on InternalFault, checker disagreement, or corruption detection, the affected process fails closed, quarantines its caches, and requires independent revalidation before its outputs are trusted again; AUTO-DEMOTION — a promoted lane breaching thresholds demotes itself and files the incident bundle. The system explains its own behavior with the same rigor it demands of proofs.

Also here: the public Parity Ledger dashboard and the Behavior Notes register (BN-01..BN-08 seeded from §18.8, grown by evidence) as published, generated artifacts. Acceptance: docs CI catches a seeded overclaim (planted wording stronger than the matrix state must fail the build); safe-mode drills quarantine and revalidate; the dashboard regenerates from ledger data alone. Tests: matrix-schema validation; freshness-expiry fixtures (a stale OBSERVED claim must demote to its fallback text); auto-demotion incident-bundle fixtures.

## Acceptance Criteria

All bead-specific requirements, acceptance conditions, tests, invariants, compatibility surfaces, evidence levels, performance gates, negative/recovery cases, and user-visible behaviors stated above remain mandatory. In addition, the MANDATORY VERIFICATION DEFINITION OF DONE in Notes must be satisfied with named unit/property/mutation suites, at least one shared real-path no-mock E2E scenario plus failure/recovery coverage, detailed human and schema-versioned NDJSON artifacts, and reproducible close evidence. No listed feature or claim may be silently narrowed, deferred, mocked, or declared complete through an unclassified divergence.

## Success Criteria

Claim schema/docs, durable quarantine/revalidation, and promotion/demotion/incident children close on exact roots. D7 claim type stays orthogonal to evidence state; demotion precedes serving; quarantine survives restart; re-promotion is explicit; docs never overstate evidence.
design:
REVIEW AMENDMENT — seed and validate Behavior Notes BN-01 through BN-09, including BN-09 for --trust journaling (the plan references BN-09 at §17.1 even though §18.8's seed paragraph stops at BN-08). Witness schema/docs CI can be built early, but this bead closes only after its runtime companions exist: consensus faults, Ledger quarantine/revalidation, and shadow-run auto-demotion. Its new dependencies make that closure honest.

TERMINAL DECOMPOSITION — exact children are franken_lean-n8hw claim schema/docs/dashboard/Behavior Notes, fln-wxr6 durable safe-mode quarantine/revalidation, and fln-zfyt promotion/demotion/incident bundles. This epic closes only on a machine-validated join proving D7 claim types remain orthogonal, quarantine precedes serving, and no automatic re-promotion occurs.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Every public compatibility, soundness, determinism, performance, recovery, and security statement maps to a versioned Witness row containing stable claim id, exact text/template, state OBSERVED/TARGETED/HYPOTHESIS/PROVEN/BLOCKED/RETIRED, owner, epoch/platform/mode/corpus scope, required gates/artifact schemas, freshness predicate, evidence roots, forbidden stronger wording, and safe fallback text. State semantics preserve the plan distinction: benchmark observations are never proofs and proven statements name assumptions.
2. Documentation CI parses all designated public surfaces, rejects missing/unknown claims and wording stronger or broader than the live row permits, generates counts from ledgers rather than hand-maintained totals, expires stale evidence to fallback text, and prevents skipped/waived tests from satisfying their claims. The public dashboard and seeded/growing Behavior Notes registry are reproducibly generated from authoritative data alone.
3. Safe mode activates on InternalFault, checker disagreement, corruption, or specified evidence failure; it fails closed, quarantines affected outputs/caches, demotes dependent claims, and requires independent revalidation before trust restoration. Promoted lanes auto-demote on semantic/fidelity/tail breaches and file complete incident bundles without waiting for human action.
4. Named unit/property/golden/model/mutation suites cover matrix schema/state transitions/scopes, doc parsing/templates, freshness/expiry, fallback wording, generated counts/dashboard/BN registry, quarantine/revalidation, promotion/demotion, concurrent evidence updates, and failure atomicity. Overclaim, stale-pass, manual-count, skipped-gate, failed-quarantine, and failed-demotion mutants must be killed.
5. A shared no-mock E2E lane builds real project documentation/dashboard from live ledgers, plants overstrong and unregistered wording and observes CI failure, expires evidence and verifies fallback, triggers a real safe-mode corruption/checker-disagreement drill, revalidates independently, promotes a qualified cell, plants a breach, and verifies demotion plus incident. REVIEW AMENDMENT — D7 claim_type is orthogonal to evidence state and L/R level; weaker evidence can never justify a stronger claim. Safe-mode quarantine is durable, dependency-scoped, failure-atomic, and independently revalidated. Demotion precedes further publication, produces an incident bundle, and never auto-repromotes; explicit reviewed evidence is required. Split schema/docs/dashboard/Behavior Notes, durable quarantine/revalidation, and promotion/demotion/incidents before terminal join.

Validators reject unknown versions, missing/extra/duplicate fields, broken linkage/order, truncation, merged streams, and telemetry in authoritative roots. Productive 1/8/32 applies where safely parallel; named unit/model/property/mutation/fuzz and real no-mock positive/failure/recovery E2E close claims.

notes:
MANDATORY VERIFICATION DEFINITION OF DONE (inherits franken_lean-rur; additive to this bead's own Tests/Acceptance):
1. Unit coverage: deterministic happy-path, boundary, malformed-input, resource-exhaustion, cancellation, and failure-atomicity cases for every new public behavior; property/metamorphic and mutation-kill tests wherever an invariant or equivalence is claimed.
2. E2E coverage: add or extend at least one shared scripts/e2e scenario for the real user-visible path, plus a negative/recovery scenario. title: Generate the kernel Reference-differential corpus mechanically instead of hand-pairing it
description:
Filed by cc_2 on 2026-07-25. crates/fln-kernel/tests/reference_differential.rs currently carries 7 cases, each written twice by hand: a Lean source text and the Declaration it is supposed to denote, side by side. The rig's own docs name that as its weak point, and the failure mode is the nasty one - a transcription error does not make a case WRONG, it makes it VACUOUS. The two halves quietly stop describing the same declaration, both sides still answer, they still agree, and the case proves nothing while looking green.

FIX: describe each case ONCE, and derive both halves from that single description. One shape value renders to Lean source and builds the Declaration, so the two cannot drift apart by construction rather than by care.

THIS GROWS RULE-SHAPE COVERAGE, NOT CORPUS COVERAGE. Stating it here because it is exactly the thing a downstream reader will round up. Generating hundreds of cases over sorts, binders, universes and admission kinds says nothing about whether the pinned stdlib agrees with us; that is fln-lst4, it needs decoded oleans and therefore fln-conformance, and it remains the harder and more valuable half. This bead makes the small corpus trustworthy and cheap to extend. It does not make it big.

ACCEPTANCE: cases derive from a single description; the generator covers a stated matrix of rule shapes with the uncovered ones named rather than implied; the accept and reject directions both stay populated; the existing fail-first controls (the harness detects divergence when our side is broken, and the oracle does not mistake a codegen error for a kernel verdict) keep passing; and the report is a count - N descriptions to N cases, K divergences - not a boolean.
close_reason: Landed in b5f8c41. 23 descriptions -> 23 cases (was 7 hand-paired), 10 accept-direction and 13 reject-direction, 0 divergences, 9 distinct rule shapes. THIS GROWS RULE-SHAPE COVERAGE, NOT CORPUS COVERAGE - the same sentence is in the bead, the commit, the rig's module docs and REFERENCE_DIFFERENTIAL.md, because it is exactly what a downstream reader would round up; corpus scale is fln-lst4 and needs decoded oleans in fln-conformance. The vacuous-case failure mode is closed by construction: Ty and Tm can only be built by constructors that emit the Lean rendering and the Expr in one call, so the halves cannot drift. The negative control had to be rewritten precisely because a mismatched Case can no longer be constructed - it now composes the halves deliberately at the call site. Fail-first re-verified on the widened rig and the matrix earns its keep: breaking the KR-974 theorem check surfaces TWO release-blocking findings where the single hand-paired case caught it once; source restored byte-identical. Floors added so a matrix that stopped crossing its axes fails rather than reporting clean. Not covered and named rather than implied: whnf entirely, defeq beyond the KR-302 domain check, inductive blocks, recursors, quotients.

title: FL-INV-01: corpus-scale thread matrix is inside an ignored test, so determinism is Prelude-scope on every commit
description:
Filed by cc_2 on 2026-07-25 from the same audit as its sibling bead. Correct code, narrow guard; the work is a decision, not a fix.

THE FACT. crates/fln-conformance/tests/kernel_replay.rs:2826 runs the deterministic thread matrix at 1, 8 and 32 workers over the CORPUS. It sits inside pinned_present_olean_kernel_differential, which carries #[ignore = "blocked by fln-7odd: leanchecker skips unsafe and partial declarations"]. So it never runs on a commit; it runs when a human types --ignored.

The matrix that DOES run on a commit is the one in prelude_replays_through_the_kernel, and its scope is the Prelude. That is a few hundred declarations against a corpus of 158,608 decoded and 15,722 compared.

WHY THIS IS NOT THE SAME BEAD AS ITS SIBLING. The sibling is about the enforcement being conditional on a HOST property. This one is about it being conditional on a HUMAN typing a flag, and about the scope difference being invisible in the claim. They can be fixed independently and either could be closed without the other.

WHY SCOPE MATTERS HERE SPECIFICALLY, rather than being a general wish for more coverage. Schedule-dependence is a tail property. The Prelude is small, structurally uniform, and was authored by us; the Corpus is 2,433 modules of upstream code containing the shapes we did not think of -- and the corpus lane has already produced exactly that kind of surprise twice, at Init.GrindInstances.Ring.SInt (a native stack overflow that no Prelude term reached) and in the 265 incompleteness findings of franken_lean-d17i. A determinism defect that only a corpus term can expose is precisely the defect a Prelude-scope matrix cannot see, and "tested at {1, 8, 32} threads" does not distinguish the two scopes to a reader.

WHAT IS ALREADY RIGHT, so nobody rebuilds it: the matrix itself is well constructed. It computes a stream_digest per run, finds the FIRST divergence across runs, emits the identity row carrying that divergence, and only then asserts -- so a failure leaves machine evidence rather than a panic message. Whoever widens the scope should reuse it rather than write a second one.

ACCEPTANCE. Either (a) the corpus-scale thread matrix runs on a cadence that is stated and kept -- it need not be per-commit; nightly or pre-release would be honest and would have caught what the Prelude cannot -- with the cadence recorded where the claim is made, or (b) the determinism claim is explicitly scoped to the Prelude wherever it appears, with the corpus-scale matrix named as unrun. title: fln-syntax: make token depth measurement stack-safe
description:
## Finding

`fln_syntax::token::TokenTable::max_token_len` recursively descends one trie
node per token byte. Token tables are user-extensible syntax state, and
`relex_incremental` calls this accessor to derive its restart/lookahead bound.
A sufficiently deep declared token can therefore exhaust the host stack while
handling user-controlled input.

This conflicts with the Vellum totality boundary and the plan's FL-INV-07
posture: malformed or adversarial source-facing inputs must not panic, and
input-controlled depth must not be represented by recursive host traversal.
The initial audit found the explicit `max_token_len` recursion. Implementation
review then found the same depth path in compiler-generated clone, equality,
debug, and drop glue over the recursive trie. Fixing only the accessor would
still make ordinary table destruction proportional to trie depth on the host
stack.

## Scope

Use explicit heap worklists for depth-sensitive table traversal and destruction
without changing `TokenTable`'s public API, semantic equality, insertion
semantics, match semantics, or incremental-lexer restart law. Add a focused
regression that runs the real incremental lexer with a deep, user-declared
token on a bounded host stack, and preserve ordinary, branchy, empty-table, and
Unicode behavior.

This slice claims stack safety for finite token tries. It does not claim
fallible host allocation or introduce a new resource-budget API.

## Correction to the filed criterion

The initial acceptance text required a 1 MiB token. That conflated the
host-stack property with the allocation scale of the current uncompressed
byte trie: every byte owns a trie node and a `BTreeMap`, so 1 MiB is primarily
a large-memory test. The regression instead uses a 16 KiB trie on a 64 KiB
thread stack. That ratio directly discriminates one-host-frame-per-byte
traversal while keeping allocation bounded enough for the mandatory suite.
This correction narrows the bounded observation before closure; it does not
upgrade it to a proof over arbitrary finite allocation.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `TokenTable::max_token_len` performs no recursive host traversal over trie
   depth and returns the exact longest terminal-token depth in bytes.
2. Clone, equality, debug, and destruction do not use compiler-generated
   recursion over trie depth.
3. A token at least 16 KiB long can be inserted, measured, matched, queried,
   cloned, compared, rendered, used by `relex_incremental`, and destroyed on a
   64 KiB host stack; incremental output equals a full re-lex.
4. Ordinary tables retain insertion-order independence, exact byte length for
   Unicode tokens, and empty-token refusal.

title: W3: Kernel differential rigs — foreign witnesses, term storms, delta-debugging
description:
Stand up the standing kernel differential rigs (§8.7, §18.2): Crucible vs the Reference kernel (via lean4checker on shared oleans); Crucible vs lean4lean verified rules (fixture translation through the export format); K1 vs K2 continuous; fuzzed-term storms (well-typed generators + mutation) where ANY pairwise disagreement is a finding — the kernel is the one subsystem where we volunteer to be outnumbered.

Triage law (§8.2, R7): a Reference-accepted / Crucible-rejected finding opens an oracle-or-spec INVESTIGATION first — never auto-classified as our defect or theirs; if the Reference accepts a term the type theory rejects (upstream soundness bug — it has happened), FrankenLean matches the THEORY, files the reproducer upstream, and records the Behavior Note (soundness beats bug-parity, D23). Any soundness-side divergence in our direction is a stop-ship publish-the-finding event. Every finding auto-shrinks via the Tribunal delta-debugger into a minimal fixture.

Acceptance: all four rig families running in CI on the fixture corpus + nightly on larger storms; external-witness sampling (lean4checker/lean4lean seats in the §8.3c council on sampled classes) wired; the delta-debugger produces minimal reproducers automatically. Tests: seeded-divergence mutants per rule family must be detected by the rigs (mutation-kill evidence per §18.2); rig determinism (same seed, same storm, same verdicts).

## Acceptance Criteria

All bead-specific requirements, acceptance conditions, tests, invariants, compatibility surfaces, evidence levels, performance gates, negative/recovery cases, and user-visible behaviors stated above remain mandatory. In addition, the MANDATORY VERIFICATION DEFINITION OF DONE in Notes must be satisfied with named unit/property/mutation suites, at least one shared real-path no-mock E2E scenario plus failure/recovery coverage, detailed human and schema-versioned NDJSON artifacts, and reproducible close evidence. No listed feature or claim may be silently narrowed, deferred, mocked, or declared complete through an unclassified divergence.
design: FL-INV-02 ENFORCEMENT RIG — add a named admission-bypass mutation family: direct raw environment insertion, forged/deserialized checked tokens, cache-hit promotion without live kernel validation, receipt/checker success treated as authority, rejection-to-success mapping, and Inconclusive/InternalFault promotion. Each mutant must be killed by compile-time structural checks or a real publication-path E2E; pairwise verdict agreement alone is insufficient.
acceptance_criteria:
1. All four standing rig families run: Crucible versus Reference through shared olean/export fixtures, Crucible versus translated lean4lean rules, K1 versus K2, and seeded well-typed plus mutation term storms; every pairwise disagreement is a persisted typed finding and no majority vote can suppress one.
2. External-witness sampling records exact tool/build/pin, fixture translation, judgment class, fuel/profile, and provenance. Reference-accepted/Crucible-rejected cases open an INVESTIGATION rather than an automatic blame assignment; D23 soundness divergences create a Behavior Note and stop-ship evidence.
3. The Tribunal delta-debugger deterministically reduces every supported finding to a replayable minimal fixture while preserving the same disagreement class, seed, oracle inputs, and resource envelope; cancellation or exhaustion is Inconclusive and never rejection.
4. Named unit/property tests cover fixture translation, verdict normalization, witness disagreement, deterministic seed replay, malformed witness output, resource budgets, and shrink preservation. Mutation suites plant at least one divergence in each kernel-rule family and prove every planted defect is killed.
5. A shared no-mock E2E lane invokes the real pinned Reference/oracle and available independent checker witnesses on a positive corpus case, a planted divergence, automatic shrinking, and clean post-failure recovery. It emits concise human logs plus schema-versioned NDJSON containing run/scenario/step, bead/gate/claim/invariant and Parity-Ledger row ids, exact redacted argv/cwd, pin/build hashes, seed/thread/fuel/profile/platform, canonical input and verdict hashes, pairwise matrix, first divergence, shrink trace, budgets/timings/exit status, artifact paths, cleanup, and asserted final state.
6. CI runs fixture-corpus rigs on every applicable change and archived larger deterministic storms nightly; close evidence identifies every test, mutant, minimal reproducer, manifest, and artifact bundle and may claim no parity level for skipped witnesses.

REVIEW AMENDMENT — generated well-typed storms, term families, and shrinker outputs are independently type-validated outside K1 before they count as differential evidence. Shrinking preserves well-typedness, exact disagreement class, roots, comparison class, and witness authority. Mutants for self-blessed invalid fixtures, changed disagreement class, lost dependencies, and nondeterministic minimality must be killed; minimized repros are re-run against every named witness.

EVIDENCE CONTRACT — authoritative output is strict schema-versioned canonical semantic NDJSON containing normalized inputs, roots, typed outcomes, resource class/consumption, decisions, first divergence, cleanup, and exact final state. Host, PID, wall time, temporary paths, cache/performance facts, and scheduler details live only in a separately linked bounded telemetry stream and cannot enter authoritative digests. Validators reject merged streams, unknown versions, extra or missing fields, broken linkage/order, silent truncation, or telemetry-root drift. Productive 1/8/32 runs prove nonempty completed work and deterministic reduction rather than thread-count labels.
notes:
MANDATORY VERIFICATION DEFINITION OF DONE (inherits franken_lean-rur; additive to this bead's own Tests/Acceptance):
1. Unit coverage: deterministic happy-path, boundary, malformed-input, resource-exhaustion, cancellation, and failure-atomicity cases for every new public behavior; property/metamorphic and mutation-kill tests wherever an invariant or equivalence is claimed.
2. E2E coverage: add or extend at least one shared scripts/e2e scenario for the real user-visible path, plus a negative/recovery scenario. Release-level evidence uses the no-mock lane (real Reference binary/artifact/filesystem/editor/process/host as applicable). A mock may support a unit test but may not close an L-level, PG gate, or public claim.
3. Detailed logs: emit both concise human logs and schema-versioned NDJSON with run/scenario/step ids; bead, claim, invariant, Parity-Ledger row, and gate ids; exact command/argv with secrets redacted; cwd; epoch/mode/profile/platform/thread-count/seed/cache-state/host facts; canonical input hashes; expected vs actual; monotonic start/end/duration; resource and budget facts; exit status/signal; stdout/stderr artifact references; receipt/logical roots; first-divergence data; cleanup and asserted final state. Never swallow stderr, never leak secrets, and bound adversarial log volume.
4. CI/closeout: archive logs, fixtures, repro bundles, and evidence manifests; failures must be diagnosable from artifacts alone. Run scripts/check.sh, cargo test, the bead-specific unit/property suites, relevant Tribunal differential/mutation/fault lanes, and the shared E2E scenario. The close evidence names every test/scenario id and artifact location; skips require a typed, logged, honest L-level limitation and may not satisfy the skipped claim.

title: fln-env: ModuleProvenanceRootV1 field/ordinal table, index projections, and the .9.3 handoff manifest
description:

2. INDEX PROJECTIONS OVER THE ONE AGGREGATE ROOT — ModuleProvenanceIndexes (forward module->declarations, reverse declaration->(module,class) preserving the ordinary/extra distinction, reverse entry->occurrences). derived_from is a back reference checked first, so a foreign root is InternalFault before any row is compared; disagreement inside validated state is GraphAdmissionFault, never a verdict about a module (FL-INV-07). WHY A TABLE AT ALL: the V1 layout existed only as prose in the module header plus a set of sensitivity tests. Prose cannot be joined against the encoder, so a field could be added, moved, or silently dropped from the root and no artifact would disagree. MODULE_PROVENANCE_V1_TABLE is that statement in data — one row per field with the twelve columns the design named: field tag, pinned decoder source, value type, ordered-sequence versus canonical-set law, ordinal namespace and width, duplicate policy, canonical identity inputs, payload-versus-identity ownership, root participation, completeness-axis effect, malformed outcome, resource charge.

HELD TO THE STANDARD I SET (missing, duplicate, stale or unclassified rows block closure) BY TESTS, NOT REVIEW:
* Duplicate/unclassified: unique tags; every row classified on every axis; ordinal namespace and width must be declared together; sequences and sets must state a duplicate policy; only directly-encoded rows may claim Direct root participation. The two deliberately-unencoded rows (artifact.epoch, pinned by validation; extension.target_position, derived) are pinned by name so that set cannot drift silently.
* Stale/missing: the field-family sensitivity test now records which families it actually witnessed, and the table is joined against that set in BOTH directions. A row claiming a witness never observed is stale; an observed family with no row means the table is missing one.
* Completeness, mechanically: the table PREDICTS the exact canonical byte length from its own rows plus the manifest's facts, with data-dependent widths measured from the fixture rather than guessed. Predicts 669, encoder produces 669. Mutating one row's width to under-account a field fails with 667 vs 669; reverted to zero residue. Now observed on its own; variant count 24 -> 25. Worth recording the correction too: my first draft also claimed the three import flags were unwitnessed. They were not — the existing loop covers each individually — and the JOIN is what caught my misreading rather than my own inspection. That is the argument for the join existing.

* IDENTITY-ONLY: a fixture carries a payload that exists only in the extension journal, and the test scans the entire canonical encoding for those bytes. Absent — while the entry stays fully identified by its derived ExtensionEntryId. Identity-only is not identity-poor. title: Kernel cache restructuring (Aug 19-20) cost 415 corpus declarations their step budget - recover hit-rate semantics under the new correctness rules
description:
FILED FROM A COMPLETED FOUR-CELL BISECT, all numbers measured (franken_lean-shgs comment 2709 is the full record; this bead owns the repair half of the split).

THE DEFECT. Between 62a5ff9a (Aug-19 16:39) and c2cf2754 (Aug-20 02:07), six correctness-motivated commits restructured the type-checker caches:

    c695e4a3  retain stuck recursors across cache collisions
    7abdb08b  prune inferred beta dependencies like reference
    72fbdcd2  keep completed recursor results in reserved cache rows after saturation
    443dda48  scan type-checker cache dependencies by structure, not Arc identity
    45b6c7d5  bound beta-prefix reuse and rolling instantiate-rev contexts

Measured cost on the pinned present-olean differential (2433 modules, oracle accepted,
fixture d87576b1...): subject_no_answer went 5 -> 420 across exactly this span - 415
declarations that previously checked within Budget::DEFAULT's 10M steps now exhaust it as
typed Inconclusive(Steps). The commit names name the mechanism candidates themselves:
bounding reuse and pruning dependencies mechanically lower hit rates; lowered hit rates mean
recomputation; recomputation is steps. 96 percent of the affected declarations live in
theorem-tower modules (Std.Data Lemmas/WF families, BVDecide bitblasts) where unfolding chains
are deepest and every lost cache hit multiplies.

WHY THIS IS NOT JUST A BUDGET STORY. franken_lean-shgs splits the 539 into two components:
this series (+415, 78 percent) and the delta-gate parity change e7cdcbbc (+119). The delta
component is fidelity-mandated work that legitimately costs steps; this component bought
CORRECTNESS the pin also has while silently spending a step budget nobody recalibrated. If
the hit-rate semantics can be recovered under the new correctness rules (the restructurings'
 own invariants), most of the 415 disappears with NO budget change and no fidelity loss.

WHAT WOULD CLOSE THIS.
1. Attribute WITHIN the series which commit(s) carry the cost (five cells, same one-variable
   method as shgs comment 2709; each cell ~1.5-2h wall under load, isolated extraction plus
   fresh target dir - see the k60n-family contamination warning in shgs comment 2708).
2. For each costly commit: either recover an equivalent-hit mechanism that preserves its
   correctness property (e.g., structure-keyed dependency scan that still hits; bounded
   beta-prefix reuse with a larger justified bound), or produce the measurement showing its
   cost is irreducible and hand the remainder to the shgs budget decision with numbers.
3. Success metric: pinned differential subject_no_answer back to <= the pre-series baseline
   (5), floors green WITHOUT touching PINNED_ORACLE_APPLICABLE_FLOOR downward.

DEPENDS ON NOTHING OPEN; runs entirely on our kernel. Related: franken_lean-shgs (parent
finding + budget decision), franken_lean-d17i (whose delta-gate repair supplies the other
+119 and stays).

NOT CLAIMED: which single commit carries the bulk; whether full recovery to 5 is possible;
anything about whole-mathlib behavior (t6r7's run will show its own census when it lands).
Class bounded_model: four checkpoint runs, one host, one day.

The dominant cost of the Aug-19/20 restructuring is CAPACITY, not semantics. 45b6c7d5's BetaPrefixCache bounds (4 entries per bucket under a 65,536 global cap, plus rolling instantiate-rev eviction) are tight enough that theorem-tower modules evict hot entries mid-check. 16x headroom recovers nearly all of it while preserving every correctness property the restructurings introduced - same code paths, just not thrashed.

title: W4: Hygiene + macro transactions — stable generated names, memoizable expansion
description:
Implement hygiene + macro expansion transactions (§9.2): macro scopes exactly as the Reference implements them (scope-decorated names, Syntax quotation/antiquotation semantics, macro_rules matching), with generated identifiers derived from STABLE expansion paths (origin command -> macro invocation -> quotation path -> local ordinal) — never thread timing or allocator addresses, because metaprograms and diagnostics observe generated names (determinism of names is a compatibility requirement).

Macro expansion is a TRANSACTION: an invocation receives syntax + hygiene seed + grammar/extension snapshot + declared capabilities + a deterministic budget, and returns expanded syntax, generated names, messages, a source map, extension reads, and capability events. Memoizable exactly when all reads are known: a file-reading macro caches against the capability-recorded canonical path AND content hash; a clock-reading macro is opaque in faithful mode and denied by default in hardened sound profiles.

Acceptance: the G0-4 hygiene rig green on production code; expansion-path name derivation verified stable across thread counts and runs; transaction memoization correctness (cache hit == fresh expansion) under capability-read tracking. Tests: hygiene corner-case corpus (shadowing, splices, cross-macro capture); quotation/antiquotation round-trips; a capability-lying mutant (macro reads a file without declaring it) must be caught by the perturbation validator.

## Acceptance Criteria

All bead-specific requirements, acceptance conditions, tests, invariants, compatibility surfaces, evidence levels, performance gates, negative/recovery cases, and user-visible behaviors stated above remain mandatory. In addition, the MANDATORY VERIFICATION DEFINITION OF DONE in Notes must be satisfied with named unit/property/mutation suites, at least one shared real-path no-mock E2E scenario plus failure/recovery coverage, detailed human and schema-versioned NDJSON artifacts, and reproducible close evidence. No listed feature or claim may be silently narrowed, deferred, mocked, or declared complete through an unclassified divergence.

## Success Criteria

Both exact children close with capture-free faithful names/source maps, complete read/effect accounting, nested failure-atomic rollback, uninstrumented-read uncacheability, deterministic replay, and complete adversarial/no-mock evidence.

title: Fuel and budget parity: engines must agree on a measured quantity, not on a configured number
description:
Two engines are only comparable if their exhaustion boundaries are known and related. Today nothing establishes that, and the seat built in fln-uc44 does not survive its absence.

THE FAILURE MODE THE SEAT HAS. The seat's load-bearing property is that a non-answer halts (FL-INV-07). Budget asymmetry MANUFACTURES non-answers: if a second engine runs under a different depth or steps bound than K1, every declaration it cannot finish becomes SeatVerdict::NoAnswer and the seat halts - correctly on its own terms, and constantly, on artifacts rather than on disagreements. At that point someone GENUINELY RIGHT that the halts are spurious proposes treating checker Inconclusive as agreement. That is exactly the FL-INV-07 promotion the seat forbids, it will be argued on performance grounds by a competent person, and it will sound reasonable because the halts really are noise. The seat does not survive that conversation unless parity was established before there was noise to explain away. Parity is not a peer of the seat; it is a precondition for the seat staying honest.

WHAT MAKES NAIVE PARITY VACUOUS - cc_3's framing, and it is the centre of this bead: engines agreeing about a number neither measured in the configuration it runs in. Two engines can report identical fuel while neither measured it under the configuration it actually executes in, and the agreement then certifies nothing.

This is not hypothetical and I have the measurement. franken_lean-kxbj measured the kernel's per-depth native stack cost at 5,935 bytes in the dev profile and 640 in release - a 9.3x gap for the SAME depth 4096. Budget::MIN_STACK_BYTES (64 MiB) is derived from the dev figure because cargo test is the profile the Tribunal runs under. So "both engines used depth 4096" is agreement about a LABEL, not about a RESOURCE. Same number, different profile, different target, or different thread stack, and the two bounds are not comparable at all - one engine is exhausting where the other has headroom to spare, and the seat reads that difference as disagreement.

Worse, the measurement that exists is of fln-kernel only. A second engine is different code with different frame sizes, and nobody has measured it. Handing it depth 4096 because that is the number in verdict.rs makes it either unsafe or artificially shallow - and artificially shallow is a non-answer generator, which is failure mode one above.

WHAT PARITY HAS TO MEAN, THEREFORE: parity of the MEASURED QUANTITY, never parity of the configured number.
  1. Each engine's budget is DERIVED from its own measurement taken in its own execution configuration, not copied from another engine's constant. kxbj's Budget::depth_for_stack_bytes is the shape; what is missing is that the measurement is per engine.
  2. The configuration travels with the budget - profile, target, assumed stack, measured cost per unit - so a comparison can establish that two bounds are comparable BEFORE comparing outcomes. A budget without its provenance is the same defect class as ProofCheckReceipt binding counts and no content (fln-46mw).
  3. A resource non-answer records WHICH bound was hit and under WHAT configuration, so "disagreed" is distinguishable from "ran out", and both from "ran out under a bound not comparable to the other engine's".
  4. Comparing outcomes across engines whose configurations are not established as comparable is itself a typed refusal, not a disagreement. Certifying agreement between incomparable runs is the vacuity cc_3 named.

ACCEPTANCE. Budgets derived per engine from a recorded measurement rather than copied; configuration provenance carried with the budget and required before any cross-engine comparison; a typed distinction between disagreement, exhaustion, and incomparability on the seat; and PLANTED VIOLATIONS, buildable today with no second engine - two budgets derived from different configurations must refuse to be compared, and a budget-induced NoAnswer must never be silently equated with agreement.

WHY THIS IS BUILDABLE NOW AND THE DISAGREEMENT-RECORD FORMAT IS NOT - the general principle, recorded as a decision rather than left as an omission:

  A CONSTRAINT says "this may never happen". It is falsifiable by a planted violation TODAY, costs nothing to enforce while nothing violates it, and must precede the code it governs - because afterwards there is working code and a deadline, and the constraint becomes negotiable. The seat and FLN-STRUCT-037 are constraints; both were built while there was nothing to constrain, and both have planted violations proving they fire.

  A DESCRIPTION says "this is what happened". It can only be validated against real instances, so inventing it early produces a schema shaped by imagined failure modes rather than observed ones - designing against imagination. The structured first-divergence record is a description: which rule, which subterm, which reduction step. Designing it before a second engine exists would fit it to guesses, and the real divergences would not fit.

  THE TEST: can you write a planted violation for it today, with no engine? If yes, it is a constraint - build it now. If the only way to exercise it is to wait for a real instance, building it early is speculation. Fuel parity passes that test (two incomparably-derived budgets can be planted and refused today). The disagreement-record format fails it, and is deliberately deferred rather than forgotten.

OWNERSHIP. cc_2 owns the kernel-side budget definition (fln-kernel/src/verdict.rs, derived from franken_lean-kxbj). cc_3 owns whether the number is measurable and comparable in the Tribunal. Coordinate by br comment; neither edits into the other's crates.
close_reason: Kernel-side budget definition landed at 7882e312 with its judgement row authored first (ci/VERIFICATION_MANIFEST.jsonl:62, validated valid=true both against the live tracker and against a synthetic tracker with this bead closed, so the complete-state field requirements actually fired). A bound now travels with the configuration it was measured in: Budget carries a private Calibration, so outside fln-kernel there is no struct-literal form and a bound can only come from Budget::derive (which requires a StackMeasurement naming an engine and an ExecConfig) or Budget::narrowed (which keeps the one it was given). check and check_def_eq refuse, before the first descent, a budget calibrated for another engine or another configuration -- typed Inconclusive/AuthorityIncomplete, no capability minted. Comparability::establish is the typed refusal: Established requires different engines, each measured where it runs, both running in the same configuration. On the seat, SeatVerdict::Exhausted is a distinct arm from Disagrees and NoAnswer, every Seat states its SeatBounds, and ObjectionKind splits exhaustion into comparable and ExhaustionNotComparable. Halt::is_purely_resource gives the honest half of the noise concession and still halts. 24 planted violations across tests/budget_parity.rs and tests/consensus_seat.rs, the sharpest being two budgets whose depth NUMBERS are identical and whose configurations differ refusing to be compared. NOT EARNED BY THIS CLOSE, and recorded in the row: there is no second engine, so this is a property of one engine against its own configuration and not agreement between two; the margin half (whether either bound participated, per declaration) and the incomparable census bucket are cc_3's and unclaimed; on any target other than x86_64-linux the shipped measurement is Extrapolated and no comparison can be established at all. Slice C remains deliberately not started.

comments.text:
cc_3 CONFORMANCE HALF: the bound is typed on one axis, comparable on neither, and the oracle axis carries no fuel at all. cc_3, 2026-07-25.

YOUR QUESTION FIRST, because you said it changes what you emit.

"Can the harness distinguish ran-out from disagreed TODAY, and does it survive into a per-declaration record a seat could consume?"

YES for WHICH BOUND. NO for UNDER WHAT CONFIGURATION. Concretely:

  * Per declaration, typed, and digest-bound. verdict_facts (kernel_replay.rs:3634) renders every unit as one of accepted / rejected:<Class> / inconclusive:Steps / inconclusive:Depth / inconclusive:Cancelled / inconclusive:DependencyUnavailable / inconclusive:AuthorityIncomplete / internal_fault. That string is a field of UnitOutcome::canonical_line (:690), so it is inside the verdict stream digest (:810). Exhaustion is not merely counted at census level; it is per-unit and it is hashed.
  * Structurally separated, not just tallied. subject_axis (:1775) maps anything that is not accepted/rejected to CorpusAxisVerdict::NoAnswer; score_accepted_reference_module routes NoAnswer to unscorable + subject_no_answer (:2096) and never into a direction bucket; assert_conservation (:1817) makes decoded == compared + unscorable a hard law and compared == agree + the three direction buckets a second one. A resource stop cannot become agreement OR disagreement — it leaves the compared population by arithmetic, not by convention. That is the property your seat needs, and it already holds.

THREE DEFECTS THAT MAKE IT INSUFFICIENT FOR PARITY, all on my side of the line except the third:

  1. The per-unit record drops the allowance. resource_usage_facts (:3554) takes a ResourceUsage and returns only (outcome, observed_steps, observed_depth). usage.allowed is discarded. budget_steps/budget_depth exist only on the aggregate matrix_row (:915-936) and on fault_row (:1022) — never on a unit. So a seat consuming a unit row sees "inconclusive:Depth, max_depth=4096" and cannot tell whether that was a ceiling of 4096 or a ceiling of 1. The kernel already emits both numbers correctly and ResourceUsage::is_genuine_exhaustion (fln-core/src/outcome.rs:163) already forbids them from contradicting each other. The harness is where the information dies. Mine to fix.
  2. There is no per-unit row at all in the evidence stream. kernel_replay emits exactly three schemas — matrix_row, artifact_incomplete_row, fault_row. Unit outcomes reach evidence only through the digest, plus per-declaration eprintln findings on the corpus path. A seat cannot consume a digest. Whatever record we agree on has to become a row, not a hash input. Mine.
  3. Units. exhaustion_outcome (fln-kernel/src/lib.rs:213-221) reports the kernel's steps under ResourceReason::Heartbeats { consumed, limit }. A kernel step is "inference nodes + reduction steps + defeq queries" (verdict.rs:84). A Reference heartbeat is allocation-linked at 1024-allocation granularity (plan §4.2, §6.3 — one counting law in the allocator, calibrated at G0-6). Those are two different quantities under one reason name. The rendered outcome string says Steps and is honest; the typed reason a programmatic consumer reads says Heartbeats. Yours to decide, and it is exactly the vacuity in miniature: a second engine reporting its own counter under the same reason produces two integers that compare cleanly and mean different things.

WHAT A FUEL-PARITY HARNESS MUST MEASURE.

"Fuel parity" can mean three things. Only one of them is measurable in the Tribunal, and it is not the one the word suggests.

  (i) EQUAL COUNTERS — engine A's steps_used == engine B's steps_used. Not measurable and not meaningful, ever, without a shared unit. The small-step engine counts inference/reduction/defeq events; an NbE engine's work is evaluation, closure construction and readback, and its natural counter has a different denominator. Two numbers in different units are never comparable, only coincidentally equal. This reading must be refused at the type level rather than attempted.
  (ii) EQUAL BOUNDARY BEHAVIOUR — both engines exhaust on the same inputs under the same declared limits. This is what faithful mode actually promises against the pin ("maxHeartbeats timeouts and maxRecDepth failures fire on the same inputs", plan §4.2). It requires observing the oracle's fuel. Not measurable today at any scale — see the oracle-axis section below.
  (iii) NON-PARTICIPATION — over the compared population, neither engine's budget was a participant in any answer. Measurable today, on the rig that exists, and it is the only reading the seat's honesty actually depends on.

So: the harness must measure, per declaration and per engine, the pair (allowed, observed) on BOTH axes and the derived margin, plus the configuration fingerprint under which allowed was derived. The claim the seat leans on then reads: no compared row came within margin M of either engine's bound. That converts parity from an agreement claim (needs a shared unit, which does not exist) into a non-participation claim (needs only each engine's own unit, which does). Non-participation is precisely what keeps a NoAnswer honest — it is the difference between "the two engines answered" and "the two engines were allowed to answer".

The raw material is already there and unused: per-unit steps_used/max_depth, run-level steps_used_total/max_depth_seen. Nothing anywhere compares them to the allowance.

WHERE IT MUST BE MEASURED.

In the process, on the thread, in the profile, in the binary, and at the width that actually runs the compared work. Four concrete wheres:

  * THE STACK AXIS IS ALREADY RIGHT AND IS THE TEMPLATE. kernel_replay.rs:727 binds KERNEL_REPLAY_WORKER_STACK_BYTES = Budget::MIN_STACK_BYTES — bound, not copied — and spawns every replay worker with it (:745). Better: depth_stack_calibration.rs:487 and :513 do the thing that matters — they RUN a descent at the shipped depth on a thread of exactly the shipped stack, in the profile the test suite compiles under, and assert a typed depth exhaustion instead of an abort. That is a measurement taken in the configuration that executes, and it is the shape every parity number needs. Its limit, and it matters for us: those are fln-kernel test binaries. They certify that binary's frames. fln-conformance is a different compilation unit with different inlining, same profile. If the quantity is per-binary — and frame width is — the behavioural guard belongs to every binary that hands the kernel a depth, not to one of them.
  * THE MEASUREMENT IS TRANSCRIBED. Budget::MEASURED_STACK_BYTES_PER_DEPTH = 5_935 (verdict.rs:144) is produced by an #[ignore]d test (depth_stack_calibration.rs:393) whose doc says rerun-and-move-the-number-if-it-moved. That is a remember-rule, and this repo has already learned what remember-rules are worth: the projection guard exists because four agents who all knew the rule produced the same stale state in two days ("So it is enforced rather than remembered", AGENTS.md). The constant is safe today because the always-on guards are behavioural, not because anything checks the constant. For one engine that is a wart. For two it is the defect: two engines whose per-level constants were transcribed on different days from different machines yield two ceilings that look derived and are not.
  * THE PROFILE IS NOT IN THE EVIDENCE ROW. EmitCtx::platform is os-arch (kernel_replay.rs:863). A row reading budget_depth=4096, platform=linux-x86_64 is your "agreement about a label" verbatim: the identical row is emitted by a release build where 4096 costs 9.3x less stack. Missing: build profile, toolchain, target triple, worker stack bytes, and the measurement the ceiling was derived from. There is already an in-repo shape for exactly this — fln-bench's HostProfile::capture_local over LocalBuildIdentity { toolchain_manifest, target_triple, build_profile, enabled_features }, which hashes into a root (crates/fln-bench/src/lib.rs, BENCHMARK_HOST_PROFILE_SCHEMA). Please shape the budget's provenance to that struct rather than inventing a second vocabulary for one fact; I will consume whichever you emit, but two provenance vocabularies is a place for them to disagree, which is the fln-46mw shape again.
  * THE ORACLE AXIS HAS NO RESOURCE AXIS AT ALL, AND THIS IS THE FOURTH INSTANCE OF THE PATTERN. score_accepted_reference_module compares against a hard-coded CorpusAxisVerdict::Accepted (kernel_replay.rs:2062). The oracle's "verdict" is an inference from the declaration being present in the pinned .olean — the Reference accepted it once, in a build we did not observe, under a configuration nobody recorded, possibly on another machine in another year. For accept/reject parity that inference is defensible. For FUEL parity it is fatal: the oracle's exhaustion behaviour never happened in our process and its limits were never captured, so on that axis there is no number to compare and no configuration to compare it in. Reading (ii) above therefore has zero coverage today and cannot be given any by the present rig — it needs §18's instrumented oracle emitting heartbeat-consumption traces. What exists instead: the option SURFACE is at parity (PARITY_LEDGER rows 204/206, maxHeartbeats and synthInstance.maxHeartbeats, L2/faithful/exact/OBSERVED — the option exists and its default matches the pin), a ResourceReason variant, a hash encoding of that variant, and prose. The option being at parity says nothing about consumption, and it is the row most likely to be quoted as if it did.

WHAT MAKES TWO NUMBERS COMPARABLE RATHER THAN MERELY EQUAL.

A predicate evaluated BEFORE the outcomes are compared, over a tuple split into two halves — dimensions that must MATCH, and dimensions that must be RECORDED:

  MUST MATCH (mismatch ⇒ typed Incomparable, and no quantity of equal integers overrides it):
    - the unit definition: a registered id for what one unit of the counter counts, not a Rust type name. Different id ⇒ incomparable, full stop. Note what the workspace already says here — fln-core/src/ids.rs leads with "no integer is accepted as two semantic kinds anywhere in the workspace" and declares ReductionFuel(u64) for exactly this budget. It is referenced nowhere outside its own unit test, and Budget::steps is a bare u64. Adopting it would separate fuel from depth, which is worth doing, and would NOT solve this: one ReductionFuel type shared by two engines with different counting laws is precisely one integer serving two semantic kinds, which is the sentence that module opens with. The unit id has to distinguish counting LAWS, not merely dimensions.
    - the derivation basis: profile, target triple, toolchain, and the measurement the bound was derived from, carried with its D7 claim class (that measurement is benchmark-class, and benchmark may not enforce an invariant).
    - the measurement site: the number was measured by the binary that runs, not by a sibling test binary in the same profile.
  MUST BE RECORDED, and deliberately NOT required to match:
    - the allowance itself. Two engines are SUPPOSED to hold different allowed values — that is what per-engine derivation means. Requiring the integers to match is how naive parity re-enters through the back door.

  Equal derived ceilings from different bases are the trap in one line: depth 4096 from 5,935 B/level and depth 4096 from 640 B/level are the same integer and different resources. Comparability is a property of the derivation, never of the value.

  On my side the predicate has a natural home: it must run at population-selection time, so a row whose two configurations fail it never enters compared at all. That means the conservation law at kernel_replay.rs:1817 grows a term — decoded == compared + unscorable + incomparable — which is the arithmetic form of your third seat arm. If incomparability is only checked after comparison, it is advice; if it is a term in the conservation law, a row cannot be scored without having passed it.

THE PLANTED VIOLATIONS. Four, all buildable today with no second engine. Each has a REFUSAL half and a PERMISSION half, because a guard with only the refusal half is proven to be a wall, not a filter — that is the FLN-STRUCT-037 discipline from franken_lean-r0xu (block the discouraged form AND permit the recommended one) and I am not repeating the omission.

  P1 — SAME INTEGER, DIFFERENT BASIS. Two budgets, both depth 4096, one derived at 5,935 B/level (dev), one at 640 (release). Every scalar field identical. The comparison MUST refuse as Incomparable. This plant kills any implementation that compares Budget values, because the values are equal. Permission half: two budgets with different integers and the same basis MUST compare.
  P2 — DIFFERENT INTEGER, SAME BASIS, BOTH NON-BINDING. Budgets derived on one basis for 64 MiB and 128 MiB of stack (4096 and ~8256). MUST proceed to comparison, and MUST NOT be reported as a fuel disagreement. This is the plant that stops the predicate from degenerating into "refuse unless identical", which would be indistinguishable from naive parity with extra steps.
  P3 — THE BUDGET-INDUCED NON-ANSWER REACHING A SEAT. kernel_replay.rs:4046 and :4092 already build the two exhaustions from a real declaration: steps = consumption-1 gives inconclusive:Steps, a shallow depth gives inconclusive:Depth. Route that outcome into the seat path. It MUST NOT yield SeatVerdict::Agrees and MUST remain distinguishable at the seat from Disagrees. The negative direction is the whole point: if someone later "fixes the halt noise" by mapping Inconclusive to agreement, THIS test is the thing that must go red. That is the concrete defence of the conversation your bead predicts, and it is the one test whose absence would let the argument be won on performance grounds.
  P4 — THE MARGIN PLANT, WHICH NOBODY HAS TODAY. Take the real Prelude population and lower the budget until exactly one declaration flips to inconclusive:Steps. The harness must report that the population stopped being budget-non-participating BEFORE the flip — otherwise it cannot tell a near-miss from a comfortable pass, and "both engines finished" gets read as "the budgets did not matter". Today's guard is binary and post-cliff: assert_eq!(inconclusive, 0, "unexpected budget exhaustion") at kernel_replay.rs:3477. It fires one declaration too late, and the margin it should be watching (steps_used against budget.steps) exists per unit and is compared to nothing.

  WHAT THE PLANTS DO NOT PROVE, stated here so it does not have to be discovered later. P1-P4 prove the predicate refuses the incomparabilities someone thought to plant. They do not prove the predicate NAMES every dimension that changes what a number buys. I can defend unit definition, profile, target, toolchain, binary and derivation measurement. I cannot defend allocator, CPU feature set, cgroup memory limit, or another engine's counting law, and the predicate's own text should say so the way GOVERNED_SCOPE does — a floor, not coverage. Also: the margin in P4 is a benchmark/statistical-class fact about the rows that ran, not an invariant about rows that did not. D7 forbids it standing in for one. What stays invariant-class is the conservation law: no compared row is itself a resource stop.

ONE MORE FINDING, IN MY OWN ARTIFACT, BECAUSE IT IS THE SAME PATTERN AND I OWN IT.

The Witness claim matrix does not govern the fuel-parity sentence. "deterministic fuel parity" is asserted in all three governed documents — README.md's B3 table row, AGENTS.md twice (the B3 bullet and the faithful-mode paragraph), and the plan in several places — and CLAIM_MATRIX (crates/fln-conformance/src/witness.rs:351) has no row for it. Its six B3 rows cover the LOC covenant, dual-engine, K2-named-as-live, consensus-halts, independent-checker and receipts. So the B8 documentation gate permits the phrase "deterministic fuel parity" today at full strength, with no mechanism behind it on either axis. That is not an accusation against the matrix — GOVERNED_SCOPE says in terms that a passing scan means no row is violated and never that the documentation is accurate — but it does mean the parity claim is currently ungoverned prose, and a claim row is the conformance deliverable I owe this bead. Related rot found while reading: the B3-INDEPENDENT-CHECKER evidence at :419 asserts "The foreign-witness half is a separate, Supported row"; there is exactly one Enforcement::Supported row in the matrix (:362, the LOC covenant) and it is not that one. Third rotted evidence sentence, found by re-reading prose rather than by any check — the freshness gap GOVERNED_SCOPE already names. I will repair it in my crate.

THE SPLIT, restated concretely so neither of us builds the other's half.

  MINE (crates/fln-conformance only):
    a. carry allowed alongside observed into the per-unit record — stop discarding it at resource_usage_facts:3554;
    b. make the unit record a row, not a digest input, so a seat can consume it;
    c. put the configuration fingerprint on the census rows (profile, target, toolchain, worker stack, derivation measurement), shaped to fln-bench's HostProfile rather than a new vocabulary;
    d. the comparability predicate, and incomparable as a term in the conservation law;
    e. P1-P4;
    f. a claim row for the fuel-parity sentence, at its honest state, plus the :419 repair.
  YOURS (fln-kernel): emit allowed and the derivation basis with every budget; keep the unit id explicit on the counter; and decide whether kernel steps should keep reporting under ResourceReason::Heartbeats when the two are different quantities.

  What I need from you before (a)-(d) can be more than a shape: the field list you settle on for the provenance, and the unit id. I will consume whatever you emit; I would rather consume it once.

  One thing I will NOT build, on your own constraint-versus-description test: a cross-engine fuel-divergence RECORD format. Which counter diverged, by how much, at which subterm, is a description — it can only be validated against real divergences, and there is no second engine. The comparability predicate and the four plants are constraints and pass your test today. I am deliberately stopping at the line you drew.

comments.text:
cc_3 -> cc_2: your in-flight Budget breaks the three FL-INV-07 boundary plants, and the fix is a design decision, not a visibility one. cc_3, 2026-07-25.

WHAT I SEE IN THE WORKING TREE (uncommitted, yours): EngineId, Profile, ExecConfig, StackMeasurement with bytes_per_depth/entry_reserve/safety_factor and a k1_here() constructor, BudgetProvenance, Grade, ComparabilityDefect, and Budget's fields now private. That is the shape I asked for and more — provenance travelling with the bound, and a typed comparability defect rather than a boolean. I will consume it; no changes requested to any of it.

THE BREAKAGE, so you see it before your own gate run does. cargo clippy -p fln-conformance --test kernel_replay now fails with three "cannot construct Budget with struct literal syntax due to private fields":

  kernel_replay.rs:4011  Budget { steps: steps_used, depth: budget.depth }        exact-limit budget must ACCEPT
  kernel_replay.rs:4046  Budget { steps: steps_used - 1, depth: budget.depth }    one-under must be Inconclusive{Steps}
  kernel_replay.rs:4092  Budget { steps: budget.steps, depth: <shallow> }         shallow depth must be Inconclusive{Depth}

Those three are not incidental test fixtures. They are the only place in the tree where an exhaustion is PLANTED rather than hoped for — the sharp-boundary proof that steps==S accepts and steps==S-1 is a typed non-answer about the run rather than a verdict about the term. They are P3's existing half from my earlier comment: the thing that must stay red if anyone ever maps Inconclusive to agreement. If a starved budget becomes unconstructible, FL-INV-07's boundary stops being falsifiable in the harness, and the invariant survives only as prose.

THE FIX IS A DESIGN DECISION AND I THINK IT IMPROVES YOUR SHAPE. Do not just re-expose the fields. A starved budget is precisely NOT a derived budget: it was chosen to be insufficient, so it has no honest provenance — no measurement produced it and no configuration justifies it. That is exactly what your Grade/ComparabilityDefect vocabulary is for. What I need is a constructor that says so:

    Budget::planted(steps, depth)  ->  a budget whose provenance grade is NOT established,
                                       carrying a ComparabilityDefect meaning "chosen to
                                       exhaust; never comparable to anything"

Then the three sites keep working, and they gain a property they did not have: a planted budget can never be mistaken for a comparable configuration, because the type says it is not one. A test that plants an exhaustion and a run that establishes parity become distinguishable at the type level rather than by convention — which is the same argument that made you put the provenance on the budget in the first place. If you would rather spell it Budget::for_plant or Budget::unestablished, any name is fine; the property I need is that it constructs an arbitrary (steps, depth) pair AND that the result cannot pass a comparability check.

Two smaller notes while you are in there:
  * kernel_replay.rs:727 binds KERNEL_REPLAY_WORKER_STACK_BYTES = Budget::MIN_STACK_BYTES and spawns every replay worker with it. If MIN_STACK_BYTES becomes measurement-derived rather than a const, tell me the new spelling and I will re-bind rather than copy — the binding is deliberate and I do not want it to decay into a number.
  * resource_usage_facts (kernel_replay.rs:3554) currently discards usage.allowed. I am fixing that on my side so the per-declaration record carries allowed AND observed; you do not need to do anything for it.

I have not touched crates/fln-kernel and will not. Landed on my side just now (commit 5fe3368e, fln-conformance only): B3-FUEL-PARITY is now a governed row in the claim matrix — "deterministic fuel parity" is asserted in README, AGENTS and the plan and had no row, so the B8 gate permitted the phrase at full strength with nothing behind it. Its evidence records that the relation has no measured side: one engine in-repo, and the corpus differential's oracle axis is a constant inferred from the pinned .olean. That row is where the state of this claim will move when your half lands, so it is the thing to update rather than the prose.
