title: Oracle-edge scan reads only each target's entry file: a marker in a non-entry src module of a SHIPPABLE crate is invisible, and the one live instance is an innocent doc mention
description:
## Finding

Found while closing fln-8fwh remainder item 3 (feature gating on discovered oracle edges), by
measurement rather than by reading the release note: `derive_oracle_edges` in
`tribunal/epoch-lab/src/derive.rs` reads ONLY each target's entry file — `src/lib.rs` for a lib
target, the single file for bin/test/bench/example targets. A marker anywhere else in the
crate's source tree is invisible to the scan.

The release note's declared remainder was the GATING half: "a text scan cannot see cfg, so
every discovered edge is recorded ungated, which over-reports and is the safe direction." That
half is true, now bound by `a_feature_gated_marker_is_discovered_and_recorded_ungated`. The
entry-file-only walk is a different hole in the OPPOSITE direction: an UNDER-report, which is
the dangerous one — a real oracle path in a non-entry module of a shippable crate would leave
the release reachability scan reporting Clean with full confidence.

## The measured population, at ff7f8785

Every marker occurrence in non-entry source, by `rg -l` over the four ORACLE_MARKERS:

  crates/fln-conformance/src/poison.rs        ORACLE_FALLBACK       dev-only crate, benign
  crates/fln-conformance/src/execution.rs     leanprover--lean4     dev-only crate, benign
  tools/structure-guard/src/contract_handoff.rs  .elan/toolchains   dev-only crate, benign
  crates/fln-unsafe-abi/src/export.rs:738     libleanshared         SHIPPABLE crate

The last row is the live instance. It is an innocent DOC COMMENT — "same observable result,
proven by the gauntlet differential against libleanshared" — prose about the Tribunal's
differential apparatus, in the ABI twin's export table. No linking, no spawning, no oracle
path. But it is exactly the shape the scan doctrine says cannot exist: the ORACLE_MARKERS doc
reads "Each marker is a string that has no innocent reason to appear in shippable source",
and this is an innocent appearance in shippable source, measured.

## Why this is a DESIGN DECISION and not a patch

The two obvious repairs each break something the gate depends on:

1. WIDEN THE WALK (lib target scans src/**): the scan immediately discovers
   `libleanshared` on fln-unsafe-abi's lib target, which is shippable, and the release
   reachability gate goes from Clean to REFUSED — over a comment. A gate that reds on prose
   is a wall, and the filing's own doctrine treats a false positive "as seriously as a miss".
2. LEAVE THE WALK, delete the comment: repairs the instance and not the class. The next doc
   comment naming an upstream artifact re-opens it silently, and the scan still cannot see a
   REAL marker in a non-entry module.

Candidate designs, none decided here:
  a. Widen the walk to src/** for lib targets (bin/test/bench keep entry-file + a declared
     residue for mod-tree resolution), AND make the scan comment-aware — strip line/block
     comments before matching. A comment-stripper is a small honest parser; markers in string
     literals and code keep firing. The fln-unsafe-abi mention then stays invisible for the
     RIGHT reason.
  b. Widen the walk and add a reviewed benign-mention allowance (path, marker, reason),
     checked in both directions like every allowance here, so the gate reds on any NEW
     mention until reviewed. Cheap, but it converts prose review into gate traffic.
  c. Both: comment-stripping for the common case plus the allowance for true positives in
     strings/docs-tests. Strongest, most machinery.

The gating half needs nothing: it is bound, over-reports, and stays safe whichever design
lands here.

## What this does not establish

One measurement at one commit (`ff7f8785`), class bounded_model. The four-marker population
was enumerated by rg over crates/*/src, crates/*/tests, tools/*/src, tools/*/tests — a marker
in a path outside those globs (e.g. a src/bin/ tree, which exists nowhere today) is outside
the census. No claim that the doc comment is the ONLY innocent mention that will ever exist;
the claim is that at least one exists, so the doctrine's premise is false as stated and the
repair must price false positives, not assume them away.
close_reason: Closed by c94675bf: complete shippable source-tree oracle-edge scan with comment-aware regression coverage.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
## Judgement

Closed after the oracle-edge scan was repaired in `c94675bf`.

`derive_oracle_edges` now walks every Rust source module below a shippable
lib/bin target's `src/` root instead of only its entry file. It masks line and
nested block comments while leaving code and string/raw-string literals
visible. Existing fixture-marker strings are allowed only at their exact
production anchors inside `#[cfg(test)]` scopes, and those allowances do not
apply to partial scratch roots.

The regression creates a feature-gated marker in a non-entry source module and
requires it to be discovered; a comment-only marker remains non-evidence. The
focused `derived_input_provenance` suite passed 48/48, and epoch-lab fmt, check
and warnings-denied Clippy passed. The shared whole-root `scripts/check.sh`
gate then passed at `0ba1ae39`; j8h published that green at `4f60ff14`.

This closes the entry-file under-scan only. It does not claim full Rust parsing,
cfg-aware source reachability, or a proof that every future oracle marker is a
real execution path.

title: fln-bignum: the PG-K performance gate against the GMP-backed Reference kernel
description:
Split out of franken_lean-npl by cc_2 on 2026-07-25. PG-K is a measurement gate, not a substrate requirement, and it cannot be satisfied until both an algorithm story and a registered baseline exist. Holding the W3 substrate bead open on it blocks correctness work behind a benchmark.

THE GATE, as npl states it: the registered kernel-reduction operation mix must be no more than 1.15x the GMP-backed Reference kernel, with raw same-machine samples, parity on the small operands that dominate real reduction, and a PUBLISHED bound on the giant-operand gap. A silent giant gap does not satisfy it, and no constant-time claim is made anywhere (this is a prover, not a KMS).

WHY IT CANNOT BE DONE YET:
* There is no registered kernel-reduction operation mix to measure against — the fixture set has to be defined and checked in first.
* There is no baseline harness that runs the same mix through the Reference kernel on the same machine.
* The subquadratic algorithms are their own bead; measuring a schoolbook-only implementation against a GMP-backed one on giants produces a number that says nothing except "we have not written Karatsuba yet".

DOCTRINE THAT APPLIES HARDER HERE THAN ANYWHERE: a benchmark claim requires corpus, machine, and claim state, and headline percentages are never evidence. The output of this bead is a row-per-operation table with raw samples, not a ratio in a README. Claim class is `benchmark`, and it may not be used to justify anything of a stronger class.

NO PERFORMANCE CLAIM OF ANY KIND HAS BEEN MADE ABOUT fln-bignum TO DATE. That is the honest current state and should stay that way until this bead produces measurements.
acceptance_criteria: SCOPING CONTRACT — do not start measurements or publish figures until the prerequisites are closed and the workload/baseline policy is registered. PG-K completes only with: (1) an observing benchmark binary downstream of fln-bench and fln-bignum; fln-bignum itself must not depend on measurement infrastructure; (2) a versioned arithmetic-heavy kernel-reduction workload manifest binding the exact fixture/corpus root, operation sequence and weights, operand-size/sign strata, warmup, cache state, thread count, seed/order policy, executable identities, Reference pin, mode/epoch, and resource limits; (3) explicit separation between the existing 5,725 CPython golden vectors, which prove arithmetic correctness, and the actual registered kernel operation mix, which alone supports the performance ratio; (4) paired/interleaved same-host candidate and GMP-backed Reference attempts through the Tribunal-only Reference boundary, retaining every started valid, invalid, cancelled, crashed, and resource-refused attempt; cross-host, mixed-workload, missing-profile, insufficient-sample, or stale-baseline bundles are typed non-passing; (5) a committed content-addressed baseline and reviewed update ceremony, with the plan target remaining TARGETED until an independently validated no-mock bundle earns OBSERVED on a named corpus and host; (6) row-per-operation and size-stratum results covering the <=1.15x weighted gate, small-operand parity, and a separately published bounded giant-operand gap; (7) preregistered minimum samples, median plus p95/p99 tails, robust dispersion/confidence, a variance budget, freshness rule, regression threshold, rollback owner, and correctness two-key join; no best-run, median-only, or invalid-attempt averaging; (8) regression diagnosis in a separate rerun that emits an owned or D1-contracted flame artifact without contaminating authoritative samples, with profiler failure remaining non-passing; and (9) independent bundle validation plus planted refusals for host mixing, corpus/root drift, omitted attempts, missing tails, stale correctness evidence, silent baseline edits, and absent flame artifacts. Close evidence names the bench command, workload and baseline roots, host profile, raw bundle, statistics, correctness receipt, flame artifact when triggered, and exact claim state.

title: W8: Ledger & Lake — content-addressed build fabric, invalidation law, cache
description:
Workstream W8 "Ledger & Lake" (§13): the build fabric (Bet B1) — the environment as a Merkle DAG of content-addressed declarations; builds as memoized queries; the ecosystem quality-of-life complaint #1 (file-granular invalidation) deleted.

Scope: Ledger records (decl_hash over name, elaborated statement, value class, direct dep hashes, options-that-matter, epoch, mode) generalized to demand nodes across five planes (source/language/trust/build/service) with retention tiers T0-T4; the incremental law (§13.2): true-dependency-cone invalidation on recorded edges, early cutoff (unchanged output digest stops the cascade; statement-hash vs value-hash separation), and the published, fixture-tested, perturbation-validated invalidation matrix per change class with conservative fallbacks (FL-INV-05: anything not proven irrelevant is relevant); the Lake surface (lakefile.lean executes on Golem — the config DSL is user code, so Golem IS the compatibility mechanism; lakefile.toml fast path; require via D2 git; exit codes and --json pinned; fln build explain shows Reference-decision vs native-decision); cache federation (CAS sync over atp multi-donor fountain-coded with HTTPS fallback; remote entries are untrusted until validated — malformed entry = miss + security event; fln cache shim preserves community muscle memory); epoch-stable caching + bridges (frontier, allowlisted, separately gated) + the migration autopilot (§13.6); watch mode + distributed elaboration (results re-verified by local Crucible — distribution without distributed trust).

Exit feeds gates G4 (mixed-build matrix) and G6 (PG-3 cone, PG-10 cache).

## Success Criteria

All scope and outcomes stated above remain mandatory, and every dependency/child deliverable required for this epic or gate must be completed at its honest evidence level. The MANDATORY EPIC/GATE CLOSEOUT CONTRACT in Notes must pass with coverage mapping, no-mock E2E evidence, detailed archived human and schema-versioned NDJSON artifacts, reproducible environment facts, and every skip/divergence classified. No feature, compatibility surface, invariant, performance gate, or release claim may be silently narrowed, dropped, or replaced by a prototype.

The migration autopilot itself is downstream integration in franken_lean-epoch-migration-autopilot-q9w; W8 provides sound cache/bridge/invalidation primitives without a placeholder repair engine.

Stage topology: G4 consumes the concrete Ledger core needed for full-Corpus builds: records/CAS, FL-INV-05 invalidation and early cutoff, Lake, and their real evidence. Full W8 additionally includes rewrite-index publication, watch/distributed elaboration, cache federation, and epoch bridges, so the epic blocks G6 Ledger GA rather than delaying G4. W8 consumes the G2-proven runtime through its concrete Lake dependency and does not wait on W5 aggregation bookkeeping. Every W8 feature remains mandatory before G6.
acceptance_criteria:
W8 closes only when Ledger and Lake implement one deterministic, crash-safe build fabric over a typed Merkle DAG. Declaration and demand-node records bind name, statement/value class, direct dependency hashes, relevant options, epoch, mode, plane, determinism class, evidence, and retention tier across source/language/trust/build/service planes. FL-INV-05 is enforced: the perturbation-validated change-class matrix proves every irrelevant change and conservatively invalidates anything not proven irrelevant; true-cone invalidation, statement-versus-value separation, dominators/SCCs, and digest early cutoff never accept a stale result. CAS promotion and frankensqlite journals are atomic under kill-9, corruption, disk-full, partial download, duplicate work, and restart. Lake runs lakefile.lean on Golem, supports the compatible TOML path and D2 git capsule, preserves CLI/exit/robot schemas, and explains Reference versus native rebuild decisions. Rewrite indexes publish through CAS/olean-next with exact roots. atp multi-donor federation and fallback validate all remote bytes before use; malformed data is a miss plus security event. Watch and distributed elaboration preserve schedule independence, cancellation, local Crucible re-verification, and no distributed trust. Epoch bridges are allowlisted, versioned, conservative, reversible, and never silently repair. Unit/property/model/metamorphic/mutation suites cover record/key identity, retention, invalidation classes, early cutoff, Lake resolution, CAS transactions, remote validation, watch events, distribution, bridge refusal, budgets, and recovery; named stale-hit, dropped-edge, partial-promotion, unverified-remote, and cross-epoch mutants are killed. Real no-mock E2E builds mathlib/Lake projects cold and warm, performs leaf and interface edits, publishes/loads indexes, hydrates across clean/lossy paths, injects crashes/corruption/network loss/disk full, and proves exact recovery in strict bundles. G4-required core plus full W8 federation/distribution/bridge scope, all children, scripts/check.sh, cargo/fmt/clippy/UBS, fault/metamorphic/thread/platform/performance lanes including PG-3/PG-10 are green before G6. No file-cone substitute, heuristic stale acceptance, mock-only cache/Lake, external trust, hidden repair, unvalidated distributed result, unclassified bridge, or deferred listed W8 feature satisfies closure.

REVIEW AMENDMENT — terminal W8 closure names every exact child and evidence root for Ledger-production handoff, cross-module speculation, PG-3 production performance, local and remote rewrite publication, federation and epoch bridge, watch and distributed build, FL-INV-05, G4, PG-3, and PG-10. Epoch migration remains a typed W12 handoff rather than duplicated implementation. Prose-only completion, same-host-only distributed proof, or missing production adapter cannot close.

W6-W8 EVIDENCE CONTRACT — canonical schema-versioned semantic NDJSON is validated independently; telemetry remains separate and non-authoritative. Unknown schema, missing/duplicate ids, broken order/linkage, unbound artifacts, truncation, merged streams, or cleanup/final-state mismatch fail. Cancellation/exhaustion/InternalFault never enters cache, negative storage, admission, publication, or promotion. Productive 1/8/32 evidence proves useful work and deterministic reduction. Named unit/model/property/mutation/fuzz suites and real no-mock positive/failure/recovery E2E are mandatory.

title: W4: GrammarEpoch + memoization — grammar as versioned data, typed parser effects
description:
Implement GrammarEpoch versioning + parse memoization (§9.1): the grammar state as versioned DATA, not hidden globals — a GrammarEpoch content-hashes the active syntax declarations, parser descriptors, precedence tables, scoped notation, token parsers, and relevant options; every parse node binds the epoch it was recognized under; memoization keys on (position, category, precedence, GrammarEpoch); a syntax-changing command invalidates exactly the parse products that read the changed components.

Parser registrations emit typed effect summaries (AddsSyntax, AddsToken, ChangesPrecedence, OpensScope, RegistersMacro, OpaqueParserEffect) — an opaque effect is legal for fidelity but forces the conservative suffix barrier and disables distributed parsing past that point (precision is earned by evidence, never assumed; the system starts conservative and ratchets, §10.6).

Why load-bearing: this is what makes sub-command incremental reparse (Lantern), the Ledger notation/syntax invalidation-matrix row, and distributed parsing sound rather than hopeful. Acceptance: epoch hashing deterministic and stable across hosts; memoization hit/miss behavior verified against the invalidation matrix fixtures (a notation change invalidates exactly the affected epoch descendants after the activation point); opaque-effect barrier demonstrated. Tests: property tests — memoized parse == fresh parse under any epoch-respecting edit sequence; C8 incremental edit-sequence corpus with expected invalidation cones.

## Acceptance Criteria

All bead-specific requirements, acceptance conditions, tests, invariants, compatibility surfaces, evidence levels, performance gates, negative/recovery cases, and user-visible behaviors stated above remain mandatory. In addition, the MANDATORY VERIFICATION DEFINITION OF DONE in Notes must be satisfied with named unit/property/mutation suites, at least one shared real-path no-mock E2E scenario plus failure/recovery coverage, detailed human and schema-versioned NDJSON artifacts, and reproducible close evidence. No listed feature or claim may be silently narrowed, deferred, mocked, or declared complete through an unclassified divergence.
acceptance_criteria:
1. GrammarEpoch is deterministic versioned data that content-hashes all active syntax declarations, parser descriptors, precedence tables, scoped notation, token parsers, and relevant options; every parse product records the epoch under which it was recognized. Cross-host/profile fixtures yield the same epoch for the same canonical grammar state.
2. Memoization keys include position, category, precedence, and GrammarEpoch. Syntax changes invalidate exactly products that read changed components after activation, matching the Ledger invalidation matrix; stale or foreign-epoch products cannot publish.
3. Registrations emit typed summaries for AddsSyntax, AddsToken, ChangesPrecedence, OpensScope, RegistersMacro, or OpaqueParserEffect. Opaque effects are fidelity-legal but impose a conservative suffix barrier and disable distributed parsing beyond it until stronger evidence exists.
4. Named unit/property/metamorphic/mutation suites cover canonical epoch hashing, each effect summary and dependency edge, notation/precedence/scope/token invalidation, activation boundaries, cache hit/miss facts, opaque barriers, malformed registrations, cancellation/resource exhaustion, and memoized-parse equals fresh-parse over generated epoch-respecting edit sequences. Over-invalidation, under-invalidation, stale-hit, and omitted-barrier mutants must be killed.
5. A shared no-mock E2E lane applies the C8 incremental edit corpus to a real parser session, demonstrates exact invalidation cones and cache behavior for a syntax change, demonstrates the opaque suffix barrier, compares incremental with cold full parses, and verifies clean recovery after a rejected registration. Human logs and schema-versioned NDJSON record run/session/edit/epoch/component ids, bead/claim/invariant rows, canonical grammar/input/product hashes, cache and invalidation decisions with reasons, expected/actual outputs, thread/platform/seed/budgets/timings/status, artifacts, cleanup, and final state.
6. CI archives cross-host determinism, edit fixtures, invalidation witnesses, mutant outcomes, and evidence manifests; close evidence names every suite and may not claim distributed-parse precision beyond the measured typed-effect coverage.

REVIEW AMENDMENT — canonical grammar identity compares complete canonical rows after digest lookup so collisions cannot cross-hit. Unknown options, registrations, or effects conservatively invalidate. The effect model covers add, scope open/close/restore, shadowing, option changes, imported grammar state, removals, and opaque unknown fallback. Property/model tests cover collision injection, interleaving, restoration, imported state, unknown effects, and deterministic recovery.

EVIDENCE CONTRACT — canonical authoritative NDJSON contains normalized semantic inputs, roots, decisions, typed outcomes, resource class/consumption, first divergence, cleanup, and exact final state. Host, PID, time, paths, cache/performance, and scheduler facts are linked bounded telemetry only. Independent validators reject unknown schema, extra/missing fields, broken linkage/order, silent truncation, telemetry in semantic hashes, and final-state mismatch. Productive 1/8/32 evidence proves nonempty completed work and canonical reduction.
notes:

1. Unit coverage: deterministic happy-path, boundary, malformed-input, resource-exhaustion, cancellation, and failure-atomicity cases for every new public behavior; property/metamorphic and mutation-kill tests wherever an invariant or equivalence is claimed.
2. E2E coverage: add or extend at least one shared scripts/e2e scenario for the real user-visible path, plus a negative/recovery scenario. Release-level evidence uses the no-mock lane (real Reference binary/artifact/filesystem/editor/process/host as applicable). A mock may support a unit test but may not close an L-level, PG gate, or public claim.

Detailed logs: emit both concise human logs and schema-versioned NDJSON with run/scenario/step ids; bead, claim, invariant, Parity-Ledger row, and gate ids; exact command/argv with secrets redacted; cwd; epoch/mode/profile/platform/thread-count/seed/cache-state/host facts; canonical input hashes; expected vs actual; monotonic start/end/duration; resource and budget facts; exit status/signal; stdout/stderr artifact references; receipt/logical roots; first-divergence data; cleanup and asserted final state. 4. CI/closeout: archive logs, fixtures, repro bundles, and evidence manifests; failures must be diagnosable from artifacts alone. Run scripts/check.sh, cargo test, the bead-specific unit/property suites, relevant Tribunal differential/mutation/fault lanes, and the shared E2E scenario. The close evidence names every test/scenario id and artifact location; skips require a typed, logged, honest L-level limitation and may not satisfy the skipped claim.

title: W3: Crucible & Bignum — dual-engine kernel, independent checker, receipts
description:
Workstream W3 "Crucible & Bignum" (§8): the trusted kernel — the one subsystem where FrankenLean volunteers to be outnumbered — plus the owned arithmetic beneath it.

Deliverable order is constitutional: KERNEL_CONTRACT.md (the Judgment Specification, §8.1b) comes FIRST — a rule-by-rule account of the implemented type theory, each rule anchored to Reference source lines, against which both engines and the Tribunal generators are built. Then: K1 certified small-step evaluator (auditability-first, the code a skeptical logician reads in an afternoon); K2 NbE accelerator (memoized whnf keyed on term-hash x transparency, lazy delta by height) cross-checked against K1 continuously; fln-checker, a deliberately DIFFERENT independent implementation (eager normalization, own decoder over canonical wire objects, no unsafe-membrane dependency, WASM-clean, non-sharing proven structurally); fln-bignum (limb-based, ABI-layout-matching, thresholds tuned on the kernel-reduction corpus, PG-K gate vs GMP); typestate admission (UnvalidatedExpr -> ScopedExpr -> CheckedExpr, DeclarationEnvelope, four-way verdict incl. Inconclusive per FL-INV-07); typed resource budgets (§8.2c); fuel parity (§8.5); certificates + receipts + transparency log (§8.6); consensus policies where disagreement halts and never outvotes (§8.3c).

Covenant: fln-kernel <= 12 KLOC, forbid(unsafe), deps = fln-bignum + read-only term views + core/alloc only, one exported authority (check), CI-counted. Divergence law: kernel disagreement with the Reference at the pin is release-blocking; soundness beats bug-parity (D23). Exit: gate G1 — every mathlib olean re-checked with zero acceptance divergence, PG-1 met.

## Success Criteria

All scope and outcomes stated above remain mandatory, and every dependency/child deliverable required for this epic or gate must be completed at its honest evidence level. The MANDATORY EPIC/GATE CLOSEOUT CONTRACT in Notes must pass with coverage mapping, no-mock E2E evidence, detailed archived human and schema-versioned NDJSON artifacts, reproducible environment facts, and every skip/divergence classified. No feature, compatibility surface, invariant, performance gate, or release claim may be silently narrowed, dropped, or replaced by a prototype.
design:

K1/K2/checker consensus strengthens evidence but never changes the constitutional rule that fln-kernel rejection or inconclusive makes publication impossible.

Closure topology: component beads build the kernel/checker/receipt/CLI surfaces; fln-ob6 is the concrete G1 integration and performance gate; this W3 epic depends on that gate as its declared exit. It does not depend on the entire W2 epic, because the exact olean reader and environment/term-view prerequisites are already carried by fln-fur and the component graph. This preserves every W3 and G1 requirement while allowing the Independent Judge to ship before unrelated W2 frontier/runtime/plugin work.

K1 is the audit-first small-step authority; K2 is an NbE accelerator cross-checked continuously; fln-checker uses a structurally independent decoder and normalization strategy, is WASM-clean, and shares no unsafe membrane. fln-kernel remains forbid-unsafe, no more than 12 KLOC, depends only on the allowed minimal closure, exposes exactly check over Environment and Declaration, and has no constructible checked-state or publication bypass. Typestate admission, every declaration family and nested/private-reference rule, universes, reduction, definitional equality, recursors, quotient/inductive checks, fuel parity, typed expanded-weight/resource budgets, and Accepted/Rejected/Inconclusive/InternalFault separation match the contract and FL-INV-02/07. Owned bignum preserves ABI layout and exact arithmetic while meeting PG-K. Canonical judgments, certificates, consensus policies, receipts, and transparency entries bind inputs, roots, engine, fuel, mode, and evidence; disagreement always halts, and unknown certificate versions fall back to recomputation rather than widening trust. Compile-fail/API-visibility and dependency-graph tests prove authority confinement. Exhaustive unit/property/model/foreign-witness/differential/fuzz/mutation tests cover every rule and malformed/boundary case; named mutants skip each critical check, forge checked state, alter fuel, bypass consensus, corrupt certificates, and promote Inconclusive, and each is killed. Real no-mock E2E rechecks all pinned mathlib oleans, exercises malformed/corrupt/resource/cancellation/fault/recovery paths, validates independent witnesses and receipts, and retains minimized divergences in strict bundles. G1, all W3 children, scripts/check.sh, full cargo/fmt/clippy/UBS, kernel line/dependency/unsafe guards, corpus/thread/platform/performance rigs are green. No partial judgment inventory, shared implementation masquerading as independence, quorum override, unchecked engine result, unsafe laundering, sampled-corpus closure, bug-parity soundness regression, or deferred listed W3 feature satisfies closure.

title: Tribunal: the Parity Ledger schema - row-per-symbol or it is marketing (D7)
description:
Third slice carved out of fln-euo by cc_2 on 2026-07-25, after fln-q3u4 (the revision chain) and fln-1dxv (oracle outcome authority + the typed normalizer model). It is the right successor because it is the FIRST CONSUMER of the vocabularies fln-1dxv closed: oracle kind, comparison class, normalizer id/version, D7 claim type, evidence state, L-level, mode, platform and freshness all become row fields here, and if they are going to be conflated anywhere it will be in a schema that puts them side by side.

THE GOVERNING SENTENCE IS DOCTRINE, NOT JUST THIS BEAD. D7: the Parity Ledger is row-per-symbol or it is marketing. So a row must not be constructible without naming a real fixture, exact roots, its oracle and comparison class, its D7 claim type, its evidence state, its L-level, mode and platform, its stated limitations, and its freshness. Absence is a refusal, not a default.

THREE FIELDS THAT STAY THREE FIELDS. Claim type, claim/evidence state, and L-level are distinct and none may be derived from, defaulted from, or substituted for another. A schema that lets one stand in for another is the whole failure mode; this is the same conflation law fln-1dxv enforced on the vocabularies themselves, now enforced on the record that carries them.

SEVEN BLOCKING CONDITIONS, ENCODED AS REFUSALS RATHER THAN LINT. Each gets its own typed reason so it fails for ITS OWN reason and not a generic one, and each gets a planted mutant proving that:
* MISSING - an expected symbol with no row.
* DUPLICATE - two rows for the same symbol/platform/mode key.
* STALE - the ledger's epoch revision is not the chain head published by fln-q3u4.
* UNKNOWN - a row for a symbol outside the expected set.
* ROOT MISMATCH - the stated roots contradict the comparison class that was declared.
* MOCK ONLY - a mock-backed row closing an L-level. A mock may support a unit test and may NOT close a public claim.
* OVERCLAIMED - a claim or a level the evidence state does not support.

TWO THINGS TO RESIST, RECORDED BEFORE IMPLEMENTATION.
1. No row may carry an aggregate or a percentage. A headline number is never evidence under D7. Enforced structurally - there is no such field - and by refusing aggregate-shaped symbols, so the prohibition survives someone adding a field later.
2. No mock-backed row may close an L-level, per above.

BACKING BECOMES ITS OWN CLOSED VOCABULARY. Whether a run was backed by the real Reference, a real filesystem, or a mock is a property of the RUN, not of the evidence kind, so folding it into EvidenceKind would be exactly the conflation this epic keeps warning about. It gets its own field.

Lives beside the other two slices in the tribunal/epoch-lab nested workspace, suite parity_ledger_schema. Lane registration stays on fln-giap rather than reaching into scripts/ or ci/.
close_reason: Delivered in a30abc1: schema enforces row-per-symbol by construction, all seven blocking conditions are typed refusals with distinct reason tokens, nine mutants killed. Coverage statement in the final comment; two named gaps (fixture existence/digest not verified, chain head supplied by caller) belong to the population slice. Claim bounded_model, evidence observed not proven.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
BUILT. cc_2, 2026-07-25. tribunal/epoch-lab/src/parity.rs plus tests/parity_ledger_schema.rs (24 tests) and 3 in-crate structural tests. 72 tests green in the crate; fmt clean; clippy --all-targets -D warnings clean; ubs run and triaged; no panicking construct anywhere in src/parity.rs.

ROW-PER-SYMBOL ENFORCED BY CONSTRUCTION. ParityRow has SEVENTEEN required fields, no Option anywhere except the deliberately-typed normalizer absence, and NO Default impl. A row is parsed into existence or refused; there is no partially-valid row. a_row_missing_any_required_field_does_not_parse drops each of the sixteen declared fields in turn from an otherwise valid row and requires the row not to come into existence - not that it parses with a hole in it - and asserts it exercised every field so the loop cannot silently cover fewer.

FIELD ORDER IS FIXED AND CHECKED. A reordered or repeated field is a refusal. That keeps the file diffable and means a row cannot be quietly restructured; a_reordered_or_repeated_field_does_not_parse covers both.

STATED LIMITATIONS MUST ACTUALLY BE STATED. limits= is required, takes the remainder of the line because prose contains spaces, and must be non-empty. A row with nothing to say must write no-known-limitations explicitly. Silence has to be an assertion somebody made rather than a field somebody forgot.

THE THREE FIELDS STAY THREE FIELDS. Claim type, evidence state and L-level are separate and none is derived from, defaulted from, or substituted for another. Two ceiling functions enforce it and each reads exactly one field: level_ceiling(state) reads state and nothing else, claim_ceiling(state) reads state and nothing else. The backing rule is a THIRD, separate check. Two exhaustive cross-product tests hold the axes apart - the_level_rule_does_not_read_the_claim_type varies the claim across its whole vocabulary for every state/level pair and demands the LEVEL verdict not move, and the_claim_rule_does_not_read_the_l_level does the symmetric thing. A third, the_mock_rule_reads_backing_and_level_and_nothing_else, pins that "the run was mocked", "the evidence is not established" and "the claim is too strong" are three different failures a row can have independently.

AN OBSERVATION IS NOT A PROOF. claim_ceiling tops Observed out at bounded_model; only Proven reaches proof and invariant. This is D7's weaker-never-justifies-stronger rule applied to the ledger itself, and it is stricter than the generic EvidenceRow::justifies from fln-1dxv, deliberately: justifies asks "is this established at all", the ledger asks "what may a row of this state assert in public".

NO AGGREGATES, ENFORCED TWICE. Structurally there is no field that can hold a count, total, percentage, score, rate, average or ratio, and no_field_can_hold_an_aggregate walks ROW_FIELDS asserting so - which means a future field named "pass_rate" has to argue with a named test. Behaviourally, is_aggregate_symbol refuses TOTAL, ALL, SUMMARY, OVERALL, AVERAGE, anything containing * or %, and anything that parses as a bare number with or without a unit. Verified in both directions: Total.order, Score.mk and List.all are real symbols and are NOT caught. report() emits counts of BLOCKS and never a parity score, and the_report_never_emits_a_percentage_or_a_score enforces that, because a headline number printed anywhere invites being quoted as though it were evidence.

A MOCK MAY NOT CLOSE A PUBLIC CLAIM. backing=mock with any level above L0 blocks. The rule bans the CLOSURE, not the mock: the same row at L0 - closing nothing - is legitimate and the test asserts that too, so the rule cannot be satisfied by simply banning mocks outright.

BACKING IS ITS OWN VOCABULARY, NOT AN EvidenceKind VARIANT. Whether a run was backed by the real Reference, a real artifact, or a mock is a property of the RUN; the kind of evidence is a different question. Folding them would have been the exact conflation this epic keeps warning about.

ROWKEY IS Hash, NOT Ord. Deriving Ord would have required giving Platform and Mode an ordering they must not have, purely to satisfy a container. The duplicate key is symbol/platform/mode, and the_same_symbol_on_two_platforms_or_modes_is_not_a_duplicate covers the other side - collapsing the key to the symbol alone would manufacture false duplicates and hide real per-surface rows, which is how a ledger stops being row-per-symbol-per-surface.

NO WARNING LEVEL. verify() returns EVERY block it finds rather than the first, because a ledger with four problems should report four rather than turning one fix-and-rerun cycle into four. Any non-empty result fails. a_block_is_never_downgraded_to_a_warning asserts the report never renders a block as a warning.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
MUTATION CAMPAIGN. Nine mutants, one per blocking condition plus the conflation and aggregate cases. All nine killed. Source restored and verified byte-identical: sha256 b0d70b088cc487c68a413efc605b6debf5ab25430bbf2480cf02fde52234a6d7 before and after. No production logic was changed to make any test pass.

Every blocking condition has its own Block variant and its own stable reason token, and every_block_variant_has_its_own_reason_token asserts the twelve tokens are distinct. That is what makes the campaign mean anything: each test asserts the SPECIFIC token, never merely that the ledger was refused, so a mutant that breaks the duplicate rule cannot be silently covered by the unknown rule.

Results, measured rather than expected:
* missing not blocked (MissingSymbol loop skipped) -> killed by a_missing_symbol_blocks and a_ledger_reports_every_block_it_finds_not_the_first.
* duplicate not blocked (fires at count == 3) -> killed by a_duplicate_row_blocks.
* stale not blocked (starts_with instead of !=) -> killed by a_revision_that_merely_prefixes_the_head_is_still_stale ONLY. See below.
* unknown not blocked (check replaced by expected.is_empty()) -> killed by an_unknown_symbol_blocks and a_ledger_reports_every_block_it_finds_not_the_first.
* root mismatch not blocked (ByteIdentical accepts differing roots) -> killed by a_root_mismatch_blocks.
* mock-only not blocked (level_rank > 4) -> killed by 4 tests including the_mock_rule_reads_backing_and_level_and_nothing_else.
* overclaimed level not blocked (level_ceiling returns L4 for every state) -> killed by an_unearned_level_blocks.
* claim/level conflation (the level rule also requires a strong claim type) -> killed by the_level_rule_does_not_read_the_claim_type and an_unearned_level_blocks.
* aggregate admitted (is_aggregate_symbol returns false) -> killed by an_aggregate_row_blocks.

THE STALE RESULT IS THE ONE WORTH READING, AND IT CORRECTED MY OWN DOCUMENTATION. I had written that a_stale_revision_blocks would kill the starts_with mutant. It does not. That test uses a revision which is not a prefix of the head, so a prefix-accepting comparison still refuses it and the test still passes green. Only a_revision_that_merely_prefixes_the_head_is_still_stale catches the weakening. An abbreviated or truncated revision - the first 16 hex characters, say - is exactly the shape a real ledger would carry by accident, so without that second test the freshness check could have been silently weakened to a prefix match and the whole suite would have stayed green. The mutant table in the suite header now records the measured result rather than the intended one.

WHAT THIS SLICE DOES NOT CLAIM. This is the SCHEMA and its refusals, not a populated ledger. No row here describes a real symbol: the fixtures are constructed, no pinned Reference runs, no fixture digest is computed from a file on disk, and the chain head is passed in rather than read from the epoch-lab chain. Two specific gaps a reader should not mistake for coverage: (1) fixture= and fixture_digest= are required and syntactically checked but nothing yet verifies that the named fixture EXISTS or that its bytes hash to the stated digest - the schema can refuse a row that omits them, not a row that invents them; (2) the freshness check compares the ledger's revision against a chain head supplied by the caller, so wiring it to fln-q3u4's verify_epoch is what makes staleness real rather than declared. Both belong to the population slice, and both are the kind of thing that would otherwise get quietly assumed. Claim type bounded_model, evidence kinds property_test and mutation_kill, evidence state OBSERVED, not proven.

Lane registration for the now-four test targets stays on fln-giap.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
Delivered in a30abc1. Coverage stated precisely, including what is not covered.

COVERED. Suite parity_ledger_schema, 24 tests, plus 3 in-crate structural tests; 72 green in the crate overall. Row-per-symbol is enforced by construction: seventeen required fields, no Default impl, fixed field order, and a test that drops each of the sixteen declared fields in turn and asserts it exercised every one. All seven blocking conditions from the acceptance criteria are typed refusals with their own reason tokens - missing, duplicate, stale, unknown, root-mismatched, mock-only, overclaimed - plus two the schema needed anyway: incoherent-comparison (a normalized comparison naming no normalizer, or a byte-identical one naming a normalizer it did not use) and aggregate. Twelve distinct tokens, asserted distinct. Both prohibitions hold and are checked in both directions. Nine mutants planted and killed, source restored byte-identical.

THE DUPLICATE KEY IS SYMBOL/PLATFORM/MODE, AND BOTH SIDES ARE COVERED. Collapsing it to the symbol would manufacture false duplicates and hide real per-surface rows, so there is a test for the negative case as well as the positive one.

NOT COVERED, AND NOT CLAIMED - THE TWO THAT MATTER MOST. (1) fixture= and fixture_digest= are required and syntactically well-formed, but nothing yet opens the fixture or hashes it. The schema can refuse a row that OMITS a fixture; it cannot yet refuse a row that INVENTS one. Until that lands, "names a real fixture" is enforced as far as the schema layer can reach and no further. (2) Freshness compares the ledger's revision against a chain head handed in by the caller. Wiring it to fln-q3u4's verify_epoch is what turns staleness from declared into checked. Neither gap is subtle once stated, and both are exactly the kind of thing that gets quietly assumed if it is not written down.

ALSO NOT COVERED. No row here describes a real symbol - every fixture in the suite is constructed, no pinned Reference runs, and no expected-symbol set comes from a census. The expected set is a parameter, so nothing yet guarantees the set itself is the right one; a ledger can be complete with respect to a wrong census and this layer will pass it.

CLAIM TYPING FOR THIS SLICE ITSELF, held to the standard it enforces: claim type bounded_model, evidence kinds property_test and mutation_kill, evidence state OBSERVED, not proven, backing real-code-under-test but NOT real-reference. By its own rules this slice would not close an L-level above L0.

FOLLOW-ON. The population slice: bind fixture digests to real files, wire freshness to the chain, and take the expected symbol set from a census rather than a parameter. Lane registration for all four epoch-lab test targets remains on fln-giap.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
CORRECTION, cc_2 same day. I named the suite parity_ledger_schema. The epic names it parity_row_authority in its closure criteria, and the coverage phrase fln-euo attaches to that name - "row freshness/roots/claims" - is exactly what this suite tests. So it is that suite, and I had it under the wrong name.

That mattered rather than being cosmetic: fln-euo enumerates nine suite names and closes against them, so a mismatched filename means the epic cannot bind to the file that satisfies it. The three prior slices all matched exactly (epoch_lab_hash_chain, oracle_outcome_authority, typed_normalizer_model); this was the first that did not, and it was my error, not an intentional divergence.

Renamed via git mv in ea3ef2b - content and history preserved, no file deleted. Suite header now records the name and why it is that one. All 24 tests still green, 72 in the crate, fmt and clippy clean. Nothing else referenced the old name.

The four epoch-lab targets registered on fln-giap are therefore: epoch_lab_hash_chain, oracle_outcome_authority, typed_normalizer_model, parity_row_authority.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
I TRIED TO ENCODE THE CORPUS RESULT IN THIS SCHEMA AND IT DOES NOT FIT. cc_2, 2026-07-25, commit 195807a9. Four row kinds attempted, ONE expressible. Recorded as four tests in parity_row_authority.rs rather than as prose, so the defect is argued with rather than asserted.

WHAT THE SCHEMA HANDLES. An agreeing symbol. The 15,722 compared declarations that agreed are the case it was designed around, and row-per-symbol, the required fields, the fixture binding and every refusal work exactly as built.

DEFECT 1 - A DIVERGENCE HAS NO REPRESENTATION. A restrictive divergence is the most load-bearing row a Parity Ledger can carry: it is the row a reader most needs. The schema refuses it. Ours and theirs necessarily differ, so under byte-identical the row is blocked as root-mismatch, and no ComparisonClass means "compared, and they disagreed" - all four assert an act of comparing that concluded in agreement. franken_lean-d17i's 5 unclassified divergences cannot be written down here at all.

You asked whether the schema could represent "measured, uncalled" without reading as a pass or a finding. The answer is worse than I expected: it cannot represent "measured, called a divergence" either. The uncalled-ness was never the hard part.

DEFECT 2 - AN ORACLE-SILENT SYMBOL HAS NO REPRESENTATION, AND THE NEAREST ENCODING LIES. fln-7odd's 1,425 are declarations leanchecker legitimately cannot judge. There is no OracleSilent comparison class. The closest expressible row - acceptance-only with both roots declared absent - PASSES my own verifier, and that is the defect rather than a workaround: it asserts "we compared acceptance and agreed" when the oracle never spoke. A schema that can only express a claim it cannot support is worse here than one that refuses outright, because the refusal would at least be visible.

DEFECT 3, LARGEST BY VOLUME - AN UNASSESSED SYMBOL HAS NO REPRESENTATION. 142,886 of 158,608 decoded declarations were never compared, 141,461 because our own side gave no answer, including kxbj's 65 behind a depth bound. A Parity Ledger over this corpus is NINETY PERCENT not-assessed. The schema offers exactly two states: a row asserting a comparison, or no row and a Block::MissingSymbol. "Missing" and "assessed, no verdict available" are different facts and it conflates them - which is precisely the conflation fln-1dxv, franken_lean-9pnc and franken_lean-869w each spent a slice refusing in their own vocabularies.

WHAT I BUILT, NAMED HONESTLY. This is an AGREEMENT ledger, not a parity ledger. It enforces row-per-symbol rigorously for the tenth of the corpus where both sides spoke and agreed, and it is silent about the divergences, the oracle's limits and the other ninety percent. D7 says the Parity Ledger is row-per-symbol or it is marketing; this schema is row-per-symbol and still cannot carry the report, because row-per-symbol was necessary and not sufficient.

WHAT WOULD FIX IT, not done here. The row needs a per-side outcome rather than an implied agreement: what WE concluded, what the ORACLE concluded, and the comparison class as a description of how they were held up against each other rather than as an assertion that they matched. fln-1dxv already has the vocabularies - OracleVerdict with its NoAnswer arm, OurVerdict with its Inconclusive arm, and Scored with Agree/Restrictive/UnsoundlyPermissive/Unscorable. The Parity Ledger predates my use of them and never consumed them. Wiring Scored into ParityRow would make all four row kinds expressible and would make the 90% countable instead of missing.

I HAVE NOT DONE THAT and I am not doing it inside this bead's closure. It changes the schema, so it changes what every existing refusal means, and it deserves its own slice with its own mutants rather than being appended to the one that found the problem. I also will not bend the corpus result to fit the schema as it stands, and I have not weakened any refusal to admit a row that should not pass.

STATUS: franken_lean-9pnc remains CLOSED and correctly so - it delivered what it promised and its refusals are sound. This is a follow-on defect found by using it, not a failure to deliver it. Worth its own bead; I have not filed one because whoever picks up the Parity Ledger next should decide whether to extend this schema or supersede it, and that choice is upstream of the fix.

title: Gate G3: The Mirror Holds — Init/Std from source, T2 identity, fixpoint bit-stable
description:
Convergence gate G3 "The Mirror Holds" (§22.3): the native toolchain elaborates Init and Std end-to-end FROM SOURCE — every builtin either native behind its facade row or library-code source-elaborated, zero upstream implementation executing anywhere — with T2 identity against the Reference, the stdlib double-elaboration fixpoint bit-stable, and the metaprogram-corpus rig (curated mathlib-tactic slice through the facade) green at its declared L-levels. The ORACLE_FALLBACK compile-out check passes on the gate build.

This is the gate that proves the central bet (B2): the parser, elaborator, instance engine, tactic framework, and scheduler reproduce the Reference at stdlib scale, and real ecosystem metaprogram code cannot distinguish the native facade from the machinery it replaced. It is the last gate before the full Corpus becomes the target.

Evidence bundle: T2 differential results over Init/Std (acceptance, diagnostics, statement-level environment identity); the fixpoint runs (bit-identical oleans + logical roots across double elaboration and a freshly rebuilt toolchain); metaprogram-rig results with the facade-row L-level table; census-totality check output; the D8 compile-out proof on the gate binaries; PG-5 thread-matrix results at stdlib scale.

## Acceptance Criteria

All bead-specific requirements, acceptance conditions, tests, invariants, compatibility surfaces, evidence levels, performance gates, negative/recovery cases, and user-visible behaviors stated above remain mandatory. In addition, the MANDATORY VERIFICATION DEFINITION OF DONE in Notes must be satisfied with named unit/property/mutation suites, at least one shared real-path no-mock E2E scenario plus failure/recovery coverage, detailed human and schema-versioned NDJSON artifacts, and reproducible close evidence. No listed feature or claim may be silently narrowed, deferred, mocked, or declared complete through an unclassified divergence.
design: G3 consumes the concrete Mirror conformance integration rig, the proven G2 runtime, and the completed Vellum contract. franken_lean-26y is now blocked on every W6 production component plus parser, kernel/checker, Golem, and Tribunal machinery, so its T2/T3, real-tactic, fixpoint, thread-matrix, and facade-row evidence cannot run against stubs or an incomplete elaborator. The W6 epic depends on G3 as its declared exit; G3 never waits on W6 aggregation bookkeeping.
acceptance_criteria: G3 closes only when the native parser, macro expander, elaborator, unifier, instance engine, tactic framework, scheduler, VM, and Native Mirror elaborate all pinned Init and Std source end to end without executing upstream implementation code. Every builtin census row is either a native typed facade implementation or upstream-authored library source elaborated by FrankenLean; census totality rejects missing, duplicate, stale, unknown, fallback, or mispartitioned rows. T2 is complete over Init/Std: acceptance, diagnostic positions/severity and faithful rendering, and statement-level environment identity match the Reference with every residual classified under the oracle ladder. The stdlib double-elaboration fixpoint is bit-identical for oleans, diagnostics, logical/provenance roots, receipts, and generated names both on the same toolchain and after a fresh rebuild. Real ecosystem metaprograms and curated mathlib tactics execute on Golem against the native facade, with environments, InfoTrees, diagnostics, generated names, effects, and per-row L-levels diffed honestly; no row advances beyond its evidence. PG-5 proves bit identity at 1, 8, and 32 threads per commit and 96 or more weekly under registered CGSE policies. ORACLE_FALLBACK and upstream implementation code are proven absent from gate source and release artifacts across all workspace members, targets, and feature combinations. Named mutants kill schedule-dependent merge, wrong instance order, generated-name drift, normalizer overreach, facade misrouting, hidden oracle paths, fixpoint instability, and Inconclusive promotion. The real no-mock E2E covers fresh Init/Std builds, metaprogram execution, planted divergence/leak/fault, exact restoration, and recovery through the shared evidence contract with bounded schema-versioned logs and independently validated bundles. G3 consumes the complete R8 mitigation ledger from G0-4 and the instrumented-oracle expansion traces: every hygiene/macro divergence and Behavior Note has a fixture, comparison class, native owner, and replay result, and no undocumented behavior is reclassified or dropped merely because the broader pipeline passes. All owning bead gates, G2, Vellum, scripts/check.sh, fmt, cargo check/test, clippy with warnings denied, UBS, differential/trace-replay/Mirror rigs, mutation campaigns, thread matrix, and fault drills are green. No prebuilt-stdlib substitute, hosted Lean.Elab implementation, mock-only tactic, partial census, hidden exclusion, unresolved R8 row, overclaimed L-level, or deferred listed feature satisfies G3.
notes:
MANDATORY VERIFICATION DEFINITION OF DONE (inherits franken_lean-rur; additive to this bead's own Tests/Acceptance):
1. Unit coverage: deterministic happy-path, boundary, malformed-input, resource-exhaustion, cancellation, and failure-atomicity cases for every new public behavior; property/metamorphic and mutation-kill tests wherever an invariant or equivalence is claimed.
2. E2E coverage: add or extend at least one shared scripts/e2e scenario for the real user-visible path, plus a negative/recovery scenario. Release-level evidence uses the no-mock lane (real Reference binary/artifact/filesystem/editor/process/host as applicable). A mock may support a unit test but may not close an L-level, PG gate, or public claim.
3. title: D3 law (b): the kernel-admission tripwire's only bare needle names a type that does not exist, and misses the four that do
description:
D3 law (b) has a kernel-admission tripwire whose only bare needle names a type that does not
exist, and which names none of the four types that do.

MEASURED at f39eaa2c.

tools/structure-guard/src/ledger.rs:1026 admission_token_sites is the "defense-in-depth" layer of
the D3 export law: it scans boundary-crate source and raises FLN-STRUCT-022 on any of exactly
three lexemes --

  "fln_kernel" | "fln_checker" | "CheckedExpr"

CheckedExpr EXISTS NOWHERE IN THE WORKSPACE. rg over the tree returns two files: the plan, where
it is the EXPRESSION typestate of section 8.2b (UnvalidatedExpr -> ScopedExpr -> CheckedExpr,
also listed as a section 22 deliverable), and this needle itself. None of those three types is
implemented.

The kernel's actual admission token is CheckedDecl<'env>, crates/fln-kernel/src/capability.rs:68,
landed at dfd77f1f under bead fln-yswb, with Reviewable<'env>, Admitted<'env> and Published
beside it. Its own module doc calls it "D6 expressed as a type rather than as a convention" --
it is precisely the thing a laundering export would want to produce. The tripwire names none of
them.

So the only BARE name the tripwire knows cannot occur, and the four that can occur are unnamed.

The unit test at ledger.rs:1440 asserts admission_token_sites("type T = CheckedExpr;\n").len()
== 1 -- so the dead needle is tested, against a fictional type. That is the inert-declaration
shape: a self-consistent test of a needle that can never fire on real input, which is why this
survived review.

SEVERITY IS BOUNDED, and this bead must not be read as claiming a live hole. The law's load is
carried elsewhere and is intact:
  * FLN-STRUCT-008 prohibits fln-unsafe-* ->* fln-kernel|fln-checker TRANSITIVELY, so a boundary
    crate cannot depend on the kernel at all. tools/structure-guard/tests/seeded.rs:252 plants
    fln-unsafe-jit -> fln-mid -> fln-kernel where both hops are individually rank-legal
    (12 > 8 > 6), so only the transitive rule catches it, and asserts the exact rendered path.
  * the fln_kernel and fln_checker needles catch any PATH-QUALIFIED mention.
  * FLN-STRUCT-022 requires every bare-pub item in a boundary crate to carry a reviewed
    ci/BOUNDARY_API.txt row; an undeclared item fails, a stale row fails, and an unclassifiable
    shape fails closed. The planted case is pub fn forge<T>() -> T, the laundering shape itself
    (seeded.rs:634).
  * FLN-STRUCT-025 requires the POST-EXPANSION public set to be a subset of those rows, so a
    macro cannot synthesize an export.

What this bead is, then, is the hand-listed-scope defect in a layer that exists specifically to
catch what the other layers cannot: an unqualified name. The needle set is a claim about the
kernel's admission vocabulary that is NOT BOUND TO THE KERNEL. It was written against the plan,
the kernel shipped a different axis, and nothing re-derived it.

PROPOSED REPAIR, both directions, red today:
  * fail if fln-kernel exports an admission-capability type the tripwire does not name;
  * fail if the tripwire names a token that exists nowhere in the workspace.
The second direction fires immediately on CheckedExpr, which is how the guard proves it works
before anyone trusts it. Deriving the set from crates/fln-kernel/src/capability.rs at test time
is the fln-mandated-mutant-join-unwatched-uagk technique (derive, never transcribe).

DECIDE FIRST, because it changes the repair: whether CheckedExpr should be REMOVED as a dead
plan-era needle or RETAINED as an anticipatory one. If retained, the "names nothing" direction
needs a declared, shrinking allowance rather than a flat refusal -- and an allowance that cannot
shrink is a gate people bypass.

SECOND OBSERVATION, one line: ci/BOUNDARY_API.txt carries 66 rows -- 53 for fln-unsafe-abi, 13
for fln-unsafe-region, and ZERO for fln-unsafe-jit, which has zero pub items. That is consistent
rather than a gap (the law is "every pub item needs a row"), and FLN-STRUCT-022 would fire on
jit's first export. Recorded so the zero is not later mistaken for missing coverage.

Found by cc_2 on 2026-07-26 while answering whether the D3 structural law has a test that would
fail on a new edge, or is prose only. Both halves are mechanised; this is the one part that is
not bound to what it guards.
close_reason: Needle set bound to the kernel capability surface in both directions; four mutants planted and killed.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
JUDGEMENT for this closure. Repaired and verified at 3023a98d + this patch; every measurement
re-derived at that hash.

WHAT LANDED.

1. tools/structure-guard/src/ledger.rs: the tripwire's needle set is now a bindable
   ADMISSION_TOKENS const naming what the kernel actually exports -- Admitted, CheckedDecl,
   Reviewable, plus the two crate paths fln_kernel and fln_checker. CheckedExpr is GONE: it
   named the expression typestate of plan section 8.2b, which is unimplemented and present
   nowhere in the workspace except the plan and the needle itself.

2. ADMISSION_TOKEN_EXCLUSIONS declares Published excluded WITH ITS REASON. Published is an
   outcome report of a publication that already happened -- Committed / DuplicateName /
   BlockHandoffUnavailable -- not a right to perform one, so no arm can be laundered into an
   admission; and it is a generic identifier, so tripwiring it would buy no admission coverage
   while adding real false-positive risk in boundary code. Stated as a declared allowance
   rather than a silent omission, and the allowance can only shrink.

3. tools/structure-guard/tests/real_workspace.rs:
   the_admission_tripwire_names_what_the_kernel_actually_exports binds the list to
   crates/fln-kernel/src/capability.rs in BOTH directions, deriving the capability surface at
   test time rather than transcribing it.

A DESIGN CORRECTION WORTH RECORDING, because the obvious rule is wrong here. "A needle matching
zero sites must be an error" inverts this guard: the tripwire scans BOUNDARY crate source, where
zero matches is the HEALTHY state -- fln_kernel occurring zero times in fln-unsafe-abi is the
whole point. Erroring on that makes the guard red on a clean tree, which is a gate people learn
to bypass (the franken_lean-e5k7 lesson). The real property is narrower and two-sided:

  * LIVENESS -- a needle must NAME something that exists in the workspace, so it is capable of
    matching at all. This is the direction that was violated by CheckedExpr.
  * COVERAGE -- every capability type the kernel exports must be named by a needle, or declared
    excluded with its reason.

VERIFIED, not asserted. Full structure-guard suite: 206 tests across 7 targets, exit 0.
cargo fmt --check -p structure-guard exit 0.

FOUR MUTANTS PLANTED, ALL KILLED, each reverted:
  * re-add CheckedExpr to the needle list -- the exact defect returning. Dies on LIVENESS:
    "the admission tripwire trips on `CheckedExpr`, which names neither a crate under crates/
    nor a pub type in crates/fln-kernel/src/capability.rs".
  * rename the kernel's publication right CheckedDecl -> CheckedGrant. Dies on COVERAGE:
    "declares `CheckedGrant`, which is neither tripwired nor declared excluded".
  * rename the excluded type Published -> PublishOutcome. Also dies on COVERAGE, which is
    honest to record: the renamed type is uncovered before the exclusion is stale, so the
    coverage assertion fires first.
  * add a parking-lot exclusion naming a type that does not exist. Dies on the SHRINK
    direction: "`Bogus` is declared excluded ... but no longer exists in the capability module
    -- a stale exclusion is an allowance that grew for free."
  A fifth guard against vacuity is built in: a capability scan returning fewer than three types
  fails as a broken scan rather than reporting a kernel with no capabilities.

UBS: repo root, relative paths, both files. Attributed against a same-cwd same-path baseline
built by restoring HEAD content and rescanning, so content is the only variable: 10 critical /
284 warning / 36 info with the patch versus 10 / 270 / 29 without. ZERO critical delta; +14
warning, +7 info. Terminal mode completed_findings, zero blocking.
  ONE INTERMEDIATE MEASUREMENT IS WORTH RECORDING because it changed the code: the first
  version named the liveness loop variable `token`, and UBS raised a CRITICAL -- "Secret,
  signature, or token compared with ==/!=" at the `d == token` comparison. That is exactly the
  known-false class fln-lyc8 owns, whose implementable narrowing matches secret/hmac/signature/
  api_key/csrf/bearer/reset_token "rather than file/scope taint or bare token". I renamed the
  variable to `needle` rather than filing a UBS-TRIAGE/1 exception, because the name is
  independently better -- this module's own documentation calls them needles throughout -- and
  the critical delta went to zero. Disclosed rather than quietly done: a rename that only
  silenced a heuristic would be the contortion AGENTS.md forbids.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT EARN.
  * The tripwire is still a LEXEME match, not a type-aware laundering check. It catches a name
    appearing in boundary source; it cannot decide whether a return type is launderable.
    checks.rs:1016-1032 argues the type-level version is unwritable at the current layering
    (fln-env rank 4 versus fln-kernel rank 6) -- that remains true and unchanged.
  * The load of D3 law (b) was, and remains, carried elsewhere: FLN-STRUCT-008 prohibits the
    dependency transitively, FLN-STRUCT-022 requires a reviewed BOUNDARY_API row per bare-pub
    item, FLN-STRUCT-025 makes the post-expansion set a subset. This bead repaired the
    defense-in-depth layer, not the law.
  * Coverage is bound to crates/fln-kernel/src/capability.rs only. A capability type introduced
    in another kernel module would be uncovered and nothing would notice.

RELATED, AND WORTH SAYING OUT LOUD: this is the third face of one seam. t0g7 is a number with no
reachable producer; c118 and the ukzx row (3023a98d) are numbers taken from the WRONG producer;
en9q is a needle whose referent does not exist. All three are the same joint -- a claim and the
thing that makes it true, never joined -- but they do NOT collapse into one guard, because the
repairs differ: publish the producer, versus derive the needle set. Recorded so the next reader
does not try to unify them and lose the distinction.

title: check.sh sealed Cargo drops inherited gate before real-script prune cells
description:
The authoritative `scripts/check.sh` lane acquires `/data/tmp/fln-gate.lockfile` before its sealed Cargo test stage. The sealed `scripts/evidence.py run` supervisor does not pass that open gate descriptor into the test process. `crates/fln-conformance/tests/evidence_finalization.rs::dead_sealed_build_roots_are_pruned_before_the_envelope_opens` then launches an ordinary nested `scripts/check.sh` four times. Those test-control children carry no planted/probe discriminator, cannot observe the parent gate, and wait in `flock -w 2400 9` until the outer test stage's 1,200-second supervisor timeout. The quality lane therefore cannot publish a terminal pass even though the mandatory fmt/check/clippy commands and a separately inherited-lock root Cargo test are green.

Measured at `c64d05ef715be058b2d9fb670741ebf85552bf3c` in a normal clone with a real `.git` directory, complete builtin census shards, and the generated-output anti-vacuity floor. Two direct `scripts/check.sh` attempts reached green evidence-self-test, manifest, shellcheck, projection guard, fmt, all-target check, warnings-denied Clippy, and contract handoff, then self-waited in the sealed `evidence_finalization` target. Process-tree evidence bound the nested bash child to `flock -w 2400 9`; both retained attempts were reclaimed through `scripts/evidence.py emergency-kill`, not treated as code failures.

Acceptance requires one owned gate protocol, not an alternate pass surface. A direct `scripts/check.sh` run from a normal clone must complete all stages and exit 0 without a nested gate wait. The real prune cells must still traverse the actual script and demonstrate dead-pid prune, live-pid retention, malformed-suffix retention, and keep-override retention. Any test-control bypass must be narrowly typed, incapable of publishing an ordinary quality-gate pass, and covered in both positive and planted-negative directions. The external inherited-lock control, free-lock acquisition, locked-fd confirmation, unlocked-decoy-fd repair, typed contention, process-group cleanup, cancellation, and clean rerun recovery must remain exact. Root `cargo test`, the focused evidence-finalization suite, shellcheck, format, all-target check, warnings-denied Clippy, and direct `scripts/check.sh` must all be green before closure.

This bug owns only the W1 gate/evidence process boundary. It claims no checker, kernel, elaborator, runtime, ABI, corpus, or release behavior.

title: fln-kernel and olean: govern declarations whose private auxiliaries are absent from artifacts
description:
The ap6 replay census found six non-safe helper definitions whose bodies reference private auxiliary declarations that are absent from the pinned serialized module. The current evidence can therefore report every declaration as checked and accepted while also reporting nonsafe_with_unserialized_refs=6, which conflates successful kernel validation with an artifact that cannot supply the complete dependency closure. This bead owns the cross-layer contract between the olean reader, Grimoire environment, K1 admission, Parity Ledger, and G1 reporting for that case. Mechanically census the exact affected declarations and missing references from the pin; anchor the Reference behavior for unsafe and non-safe admission; determine whether the missing closure can be reconstructed deterministically from governed source or extracted fixture data without violating the Oracle-Only Law. If it can, materialize and kernel-check it through the ordinary authority path. If it cannot, return a typed ArtifactIncomplete Inconclusive outcome with a canonical witness, never Accepted, Rejected, checked, or cacheable, and ensure headline and per-kind counts keep validated, unsafe-not-kernel-checked, and artifact-incomplete rows separate. No hidden allowlist, name-only exception, runtime Reference fallback, or count that presents incomplete rows as checked.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run the pinned Init.Prelude admission census and compare the headline checked and accepted totals with the nonsafe_with_unserialized_refs counter.
2. Inspect the six affected declaration bodies and resolve every referenced constant against the decoded module environment; the named private auxiliaries are absent from the serialized dependency closure.
3. Route those declarations through strict ordinary admission without a special case; validation cannot establish the complete dependency closure from the artifact alone.
4. Observe that a summary which folds those rows into checked or accepted overstates the evidence and can incorrectly satisfy a G1 count.

## Acceptance Criteria

The exact pin census and Reference semantics are source-anchored and versioned. Each affected declaration has a row naming the declaration, missing private references, safety class, artifact and source hashes, attempted resolution, final typed outcome, authority and cacheability, and evidence grade. Ordinary complete definitions still check through the sole public kernel authority; reconstructable closures are deterministic and content-bound; irreconstructable closures yield Inconclusive ArtifactIncomplete with canonical witnesses and cannot enter an environment or satisfy G1 acceptance. Unit tests cover all six known rows, a complete control, zero, one-under, exact, and one-over resource boundaries, missing and extra auxiliaries, digest collisions, stale fixtures, cancellation, InternalFault, nonpublication, and clean recovery. Independent model and property tests cover census partitioning, canonical witness order, source or artifact permutation, and count conservation. Named mutants that mark incomplete rows checked, collapse unsafe with validated, omit a missing reference, accept a stale reconstruction, or cache Inconclusive must be killed. A real pinned no-mock positive, incomplete, mutation, and recovery E2E lane runs at threads 1, 8, and 32 with byte-identical authoritative counts, roots, diagnostics, and witnesses, plus strict human and schema-versioned NDJSON artifacts with exact commands, inputs, budgets, streams, first divergence, cleanup, and final state. title: fln-env: integrate attribute state with module provenance, checkpoints, and merge plans
description:
Integrate canonical attribute state into the single immutable committed Environment/module-provenance state. Exact decoded module replay owns attribute definitions and assignments through the same module contribution transaction, forward/reverse ownership indexes, completeness/evidence grades, invalidation rules, paired checkpoints, and provenance merge plans used by declarations and extensions. No parallel attribute import, root, or ownership truth is permitted.

Combined state distinguishes data-only rows from RequiresHandler rows without executing Lean handlers in fln-env. Opaque data remains byte-exact and conservatively grades invalidation. Attribute checkpoint and merge behavior uses the collision-safe exact extension-history identity contract. Semantic changes update logical_root exactly through the canonical Environment builder; module ownership/evidence updates ModuleProvenanceRootV1; operational facts affect neither.

## Acceptance Criteria

Every criterion in this issue's acceptance_criteria field is mandatory: one combined Environment/module/attribute/provenance truth; prepared module plus attribute plan composition; closure-wide private staging with no visible prefix; single-charge phase/cumulative accounting; final revalidation and one no-failure publication; exact checkpoints/invalidation/merge plans; authority and collision laws; independent closure models; productive 1-8-32 schedules; named cross-plane mutants; recovery; and strict evidence handoff to real fixtures.
acceptance_criteria:
One preflighted immutable transaction validates census row/epoch, target, actual payload bytes, module artifact and contribution identity, priority/scope/order, base logical and ModuleProvenanceRootV1 roots, completeness, both ownership indexes, checkpoint identity, resource envelope, and cancellation before publishing all attribute/Environment/provenance planes together. Missing/partial input remains non-authoritative; opaque-but-byte-complete input remains explicit and conservative. Conflict, Inconclusive, or InternalFault leaves every value/root/index/payload Arc and sharing relation unchanged; clean retry succeeds.

Paired checkpoints preserve actual assignment/contributor identities, ranges, payload Arcs, completeness, and both index directions. Three-way attribute merge returns a versioned bounded child plan consumed by fln-amv.11, with complete canonical conflicts, root/schema/epoch preconditions, exact usage, reservations, and no publication authority. Observable assignment/import order follows the census; only declared commutative changes reorder freely.

Independent combined-state models, exhaustive tables, generated fork/checkpoint/restore/merge/invalidation histories, productive 1/8/32 schedules, sharing/allocation counters, exact resource/cancellation boundaries, nonpublication, and recovery are mandatory. Named mutants drop an assignment, priority, scope, payload, contributor/reverse row, checkpoint binding, completeness grade, root transition, conflict, or semantic plane; publish early; accept a stale plan; or cache Inconclusive. Each mutant has a discriminating kill and versioned component evidence with census/module/attribute/target/plan IDs, ordered facts, roots/reasons, ownership/ranges/completeness/handler class, limits/usage, sharing/reservations, expected/actual outcome, authority/publication/cacheability, first divergence, cleanup, and final state.

The downstream attribute E2E child owns real pinned decoded fixtures and authoritative retained bundles. This child closes on exhaustive local integration proof plus a stable adapter/plan handoff. All fln-env/hash/domain tests, census and module-provenance gates, fmt/check/test, warnings-denied clippy, UBS, scripts/check.sh, and predecessor gates pass. No second truth, handler execution in W2, hidden root effect, digest-only payload equality, partial publication, or deferred combined-state behavior satisfies closure.

Composition uses the nonpublishing prepared module plan from franken_lean-module-provenance-atomic-apply-as7 and one bounded AttributeStatePlan from fln-attribute-native-state-m7l. A versioned PreparedCombinedModulePlan binds both to the same base roots, module/artifact/manifest/request, ordered payloads, expected deltas/roots, reservations, authority axes, and exact child usage. It sums each graph, declaration, extension, provenance, attribute, PMap, and index fact once, never rewalks or recharges a child truth, then revalidates and publishes all planes once.

A versioned StagedClosurePlan chains PreparedCombinedModulePlans in exact fln-amv.9.2 discovery/replay order. Later staged modules may read prior staged contributions inside the private candidate, but no Environment head, accepted cache, receipt, watcher, or query observes a prefix. All module and attribute planes become authoritative together after final closure-wide root/cancellation/reservation revalidation. After that point publication performs no input-sized allocation and has no failure/cancellation point. Failure at module N discards modules 1 through N-minus-1 from authoritative visibility. The downstream real fixture runner executes this protocol; it does not invent atomicity in the shell.

Freeze one total composite outcome precedence and phase/cumulative accounting schema. Validated-state invariant faults outrank Inconclusive/cancellation; unfinished semantic decisions remain Inconclusive; complete canonical conflicts precede publication. Complete reports exact phase and cumulative logical usage. Refusal reports deterministic checkpoints and witnessed lower bounds without scanning unseen work. Missing/partial products may exist only as quarantined authority=false, cacheable=false diagnostic candidates and never replace the authoritative head. Byte-complete opaque products may be exact-replay authoritative but force conservative semantic queries.

Equal-digest unequal-value candidates at module, declaration, extension, or attribute boundaries are decided by bounded exact comparison and yield typed Conflict; exhaustion before comparison is Inconclusive; inconsistency already inside validated state is InternalFault. Add independent closure models and mutants that publish a staged prefix, let later staged reads escape, compose different bases, skip a child plan or final revalidation, double-charge a child, fail after publication, promote partial authority, treat a collision as equal, alias logical/provenance roots, or publish attribute and module planes separately. Strict evidence records closure/combined/child plan IDs, batch position and ordered dependencies, root pairs, reservations, phase/cumulative usage, authority axes, expected/actual outcome, publication visibility, mutation/first divergence, recovery, and final state.

title: W1 contract extraction: target-indexed Lean ABI layout, exports, and ownership census
description:

ABI facts are indexed by certified target/ABI class; host pointer width, alignment, endianness, packing, or tag behavior may never be projected onto another target.

The prior ReferenceSemanticAdapter wording must never mean runtime invocation, linking, spawning, or fallback to the Reference.
