title: fln-kernel K1: soundness-boundary + inference test coverage (zht follow-up)
description:
Verification child for franken_lean-zht. Maintain the finite coverage audit for every K1 judgment, reduction, definitional-equality, resource, and admission rule that is actually implemented in fln-kernel. This bead owns evidence, not production semantics: it must never add a test-only acceptance path, weaken a rule, or stand in for an unimplemented kernel slice.

Maintain a rule matrix keyed by KERNEL_CONTRACT identifier with implementation location, public-surface fixture, positive case, discriminating rejection or near-miss, boundary/resource case where applicable, determinism status, mutation or defense-in-depth evidence, and no-mock replay coverage. Every implemented branch must have a named test through the public kernel authority. Rules not yet implemented remain explicitly assigned to their production slice, including franken_lean-5p2 for KR-205/KR-316/KR-317/KR-955, and become mandatory rows here as soon as that slice lands. The matrix must distinguish implemented-and-covered, implemented-but-uncovered, not-yet-implemented, structurally enforced, and externally replayed; an unimplemented row can never be reported as passing.

For each rule family, cover the successful judgment and the closest unsound or false-accepting alternative, not just malformed syntax. Required families include typing and inference, beta/zeta/projection/delta and recursor reductions, universe equivalence, proof irrelevance boundaries, application and binder congruence, eta laws, declaration safety and authority transitions, fuel/cancellation/FL-INV-07 outcomes, and schedule-independent verdict plus consumption. Use single-defect mutation kills where one site owns the property. Where redundant checks deliberately provide defense in depth, document and test the minimal multi-site mutant needed to remove the property rather than overclaiming a single-site kill.

The shared real-path no-mock E2E is the pinned real-olean kernel replay seeded by franken_lean-z6c and extended as K1 grows. It must record before/after accepted, rejected by stable family, inconclusive, and internal-fault counts; cross-check selected accepted modules with the pinned foreign witness; exercise a deliberately perturbed or invalid declaration that must not be accepted; and finish with a clean recovery replay proving later valid work is unaffected. Future full differential rigs in franken_lean-3j8 are additive and do not replace this closure evidence.

Emit concise human output and retained schema-versioned NDJSON. Each record includes run/scenario/step and rule ids, bead and invariant, epoch/reference/fixture identity, canonical module/declaration/input hashes, expected and actual verdict/error/consumption, budget/cancellation facts, engine/build and thread/seed facts, mutant or defense-in-depth id when applicable, witness result, exit status, first divergence, artifact references, authority/cacheability, cleanup, and asserted final state. Bound diagnostic volume and preserve stderr artifacts.

Do not close until a mechanical comparison of the implemented K1 rule inventory against this matrix reports zero implemented-but-uncovered rows, every production follow-up has contributed its boundary tests, all named mutations are killed or honestly classified as structural/defense-in-depth checks, the no-mock negative/recovery replay is green, and fln-kernel plus applicable Tribunal quality gates pass.
acceptance_criteria:
The implemented K1 inventory has zero uncovered rows and every row is backed by named public-authority unit/boundary evidence, discriminating negative coverage, and mutation or structural enforcement evidence. Production slices such as franken_lean-5p2 contribute their rule rows when they land. Deterministic verdict/consumption and FL-INV-07 resource/cancellation behavior are covered. The pinned real-olean no-mock replay includes foreign-witness sampling, an invalid or perturbed negative case, clean recovery, retained human and schema-versioned NDJSON logs, and exact before/after counts. No test-only authority path, unimplemented-as-passing row, silent coverage deferral, or undocumented surviving critical mutant satisfies closure.

REVIEW AMENDMENT — this terminal gate mechanically joins the final KERNEL_CONTRACT inventory, every production K1/K2/checker slice, private-reference and nested-inductive rows, witness coverage, mutation-kill records, and exact evidence roots. Zero uncovered rows is asserted here, not on upstream producers. The join rejects duplicate, stale, provisional, unsupported-without-policy, mock-only, root-mismatched, or unbound rows and emits a manifest-complete first-divergence report.

EVIDENCE CONTRACT — authoritative output is strict schema-versioned canonical semantic NDJSON containing normalized inputs, roots, typed outcomes, resource class/consumption, decisions, first divergence, cleanup, and exact final state. Host, PID, wall time, temporary paths, cache/performance facts, and scheduler details live only in a separately linked bounded telemetry stream and cannot enter authoritative digests. Validators reject merged streams, unknown versions, extra or missing fields, broken linkage/order, silent truncation, or telemetry-root drift. Productive 1/8/32 runs prove nonempty completed work and deterministic reduction rather than thread-count labels.

* the occurs-in-result-args check (drop the negation on the contains test)

These are not decoration: tc.rs computes the major premise position as num_params + num_motives + num_minors + num_indices at tc.rs:703, 749 and 768, so a decoded recursor that lies about either field makes iota reduce against the WRONG argument while the recursor's own type still checks out. Killed by kr950_quotient_init_checks_the_eq_constructor_not_only_the_eq_type, which carries a CONTROL arm asserting the correct refl gets PAST this check and fails later on the absent quotient declarations; without that arm the test would pass on any rejection whatsoever.

THE HEURISTIC THAT FOUND THEM, worth reusing. Count named tests per KR family and compare against the number of rules in that family, then seed where the ratio is worst. It predicted all three rounds before any mutant confirmed it. The census at round 2: KR-608 had 24 named tests; KR-800..803 had ZERO and did not appear in the test-name census at all; KR-950..954 had 3 for 5 rules; KR-30x had 8 across a dozen defeq rules. * SURVIVOR: KR-302 binder congruence never compared DOMAINS. The body comparison still succeeds, so "B -> A" is accepted where "A -> A" was declared, for arbitrary unrelated A and B: function types become defeq up to their argument types. Every pre-existing binder case (KR-312 eta, KR-202 beta, lambda congruence) used matching domains. Now killed by kr302_binder_congruence_compares_the_domain_not_only_the_body.
* KR-316 structure-eta gate deleted -> killed by kr310_projection_congruence_on_stuck_scrutinees AND kr316_iota_is_stuck_without_a_constructor_major_or_full_arity.

KR-800..803 recursor regeneration — 2 mutants, 2 survived. This family had ZERO named tests before the campaign; it did not appear in the test-name census at all.
* SURVIVORS: num_motives and num_minors each deleted from the decoded-versus-regenerated observables comparison, independently. tc.rs locates the major premise as num_params + num_motives + num_minors + num_indices (tc.rs:703, 749, 768), so a decoded recursor lying about either field makes iota reduce against the WRONG argument while its own type still checks. The adjacent type comparison cannot catch it — these are separate decoded fields that can disagree with a well-formed type. kr607 pinned the decoded FLAGS; nothing pinned the arities. Now killed by kr802_decoded_recursor_arity_observables_are_cross_checked.

KR-950..954 quotient init — 1 mutant, 1 survived.
* SURVIVOR: the Eq.refl CONSTRUCTOR check deleted. The only pre-existing KR-95x case removes Eq from the environment entirely and returns at the first guard, never reaching the constructor. Quot.sound is stated in terms of this Eq, so an Eq.refl of the wrong type is a different equality wearing the right name. Now killed by kr950_quotient_init_checks_the_eq_constructor_not_only_the_eq_type, which plants a coherent worst case (a refl over two DIFFERENT values, proving everything equal) and carries a control arm.

KR-200..205 whnf, iota and K conversion — 2 mutants, 1 survived. THE WORST FINDING OF THE CAMPAIGN.
* SURVIVOR: KR-317's K-conversion defeq gate deleted. Unlike the de Bruijn arm below, this branch is LIVE — a planted panic there fires in an existing test — so it was reached constantly and simply never discriminated on. kr317_k_like_recursor_reduces_an_opaque_proof covers the direction where K must FIRE; nothing covered the direction where it must NOT. With an Eq-shaped E and an opaque h : E x y, the nullary constructor at those parameters is E.refl x : E x x, not defeq to E x y. Without the gate the kernel rewrites h into E.refl x and iota-reduces, so a recursor application at index y computes as though it were at x: a proof of x = y for arbitrary distinct x and y. Now killed by kr317_k_conversion_refuses_a_major_whose_index_does_not_match_the_constructor, with a control proving K still fires at the matching index.

KR-970..974 admission — 3 mutants, 1 survived.
* KR-971 duplicate level params, off-by-one in the scan window -> killed by kr971_duplicate_level_params_are_rejected.
* SURVIVOR: KR-972, the refusal of a declaration whose TYPE is not a sort. kr104_kr972 covers the direction where it is; nothing declared something whose type is not a type. Admitting it would put a constant in the environment whose type is not a type at all. Now killed by kr972_a_declaration_type_that_is_not_a_sort_is_rejected, with a control.

KR-100..112 typing — 1 mutant, 1 survived, CLASSIFIED SEPARATELY.
* Dropping the decrement in instantiate's shift arm (the de Bruijn off-by-one) survived, but a planted panic proved the branch is never reached by any test AND cannot be through the public surface: KR-100 rejects loose bvars, so in a closed term every bvar reached at depth k has index at most k. Defensive code inside the TCB resting on an unstated precondition, one pub(crate) caller from being live, where a wrong shift silently rebinds a variable to a different binder and still typechecks. Pinned directly, in-crate, by instantiate_shifts_loose_bvars_down_past_the_consumed_binder. Recorded as unreachable-but-defensive rather than counted as an unguarded rule, because "mutant survived" and "rule is unguarded" are different claims.

THE PATTERN, SEEN IN EVERY SINGLE SURVIVOR. The guard one level ABOVE the rule is tested; the rule itself is not. Two-constructor elimination was tested, single-constructor was not. K firing was tested, K refusing was not. The Eq type was tested, its constructor was not. Type-is-a-sort acceptance was tested, refusal was not. Matching binder domains were tested, disagreeing ones were not. In each case the suite was green while a kernel judgment went unchecked, which is exactly the distinction between coverage and evidence.

THE HEURISTIC, which predicted every round before the mutants confirmed it. Count named tests per KR family, compare against the number of rules in that family, seed where the ratio is worst. At the start: KR-608 had 24 named tests, KR-800..803 had ZERO, KR-950..954 had 3 for 5 rules, KR-30x had 8 across a dozen defeq rules, KR-700..702 had 2. Every survivor came out of a thin spot. Cheap to run: grep the test names, bucket by family, sort ascending. Worth doing first on any future campaign in this crate.

NOT SEEDED, stated so this closure is not read as more than it is. KR-101/102/103 (metavariables, fvar typing), KR-106..111 individually beyond the app/binder/let cases already covered by existing tests, KR-112 projection typing, KR-200/201/203/204 individually (beta, mdata, zeta, proj) beyond the KR-316/317 recursor paths, KR-303 sort defeq, KR-313's Nat-literal acceleration and KR-314's String expansion, KR-955 quotient computation, KR-973 safety gating, and the KR-800..803 generation internals beyond the observables cross-check. A future round should start there.

AGENTS.md CLASSES: "skipped positivity check" and "inverted universe condition" were both seeded and are both now guarded. "Leaked transaction assignment", "dropped retain" and "stale cache hit accepted" have no seat in this crate — there is no cache in tc.rs, no transaction seam in admit.rs, and no refcounting anywhere in the kernel — and belong to fln-env or fln-unsafe-abi. That is a gap in the mutation obligation, not in this crate, and it is worth a bead against whichever crate owns those seams.

DISCIPLINE HELD THROUGHOUT. Source restored byte-identical after all 14 mutants, verified with git diff every time. Every new test was run against unmutated source BEFORE being allowed to count as evidence — which caught one bad test of my own (the KR-302 draft asserted the wrong reject class; the kernel was right and the test was wrong). Every new test was then re-run against its mutant to prove it discriminates, and the survivors that shared a rule were each re-applied separately rather than assumed equivalent.

GATES AT CLOSURE: cargo test -p fln-kernel via rch, 99 integration + 3 lib, 0 failed; clippy --all-targets -D warnings exit 0; rustfmt clean; structure-guard PASS 0 findings including the kernel LOC and macro covenants.

comments.author: cc_2
comments.text:
bc7 CANNOT CLOSE, AND THE BLOCKER IS REAL. Recording rather than forcing, and rather than removing an edge.

br refuses ordinary closure: bc7 is blocked by franken_lean-79k (KERNEL_CONTRACT.md, the rule-by-rule Judgment Specification) and by franken_lean-artifact-incomplete-private-refs-sgt. I checked whether 79k is a spurious workstream-adjacency edge, the way h5z1 -> npl was earlier today. It is not. It is the correct dependency, and this campaign is evidence FOR it rather than against it.

WHY, CONCRETELY. bc7 asks for soundness-boundary and inference test COVERAGE. Coverage is a ratio, and the denominator is the rule inventory. There is no KERNEL_CONTRACT.md, so to run this campaign I had to reconstruct the denominator by grepping `KR-[0-9]+` out of source comments in tc.rs and admit.rs and bucketing the hits by family. That worked well enough to find seven unguarded rules — but it means my coverage statement is measured against what the CODE CLAIMS its rules are, not against an independent specification of what they SHOULD be.

That is exactly the inversion 79k exists to fix: "the Reference specification is its C++; FrankenLean specification is a document the C++ is CHECKED AGAINST". My denominator came from the implementation. A rule that was never implemented, and therefore never commented with a KR id, is invisible to the method I used, and no amount of mutation testing against the source can surface it. A missing rule cannot have a surviving mutant.

So the honest position is: the campaign is complete against the implemented inventory, and cannot be complete against the specified one until 79k lands. The coverage statement in the preceding comment stands on its own and should be treated as the deliverable; the bead stays open for the part that genuinely is not done.

WHAT SHOULD HAPPEN WHEN 79k LANDS: re-run this campaign with the document's rule list as the denominator instead of the grep, and diff the two inventories. Any rule in KERNEL_CONTRACT.md with no KR id in the source is either unimplemented or unlabelled, and both are findings that this round structurally could not produce. The thin-family heuristic (count named tests per family, seed where the ratio is worst) transfers directly and should be run against the document's families.

I am not removing either edge and not force-closing. bc7's remaining scope is the coverage claim measured against a specification that does not exist yet.

comments.author: cc_2
comments.text:
DIFFERENTIAL HARNESS LANDED against the pinned Reference kernel (cc_2, commit above).

AGENTS.md names this as a standing Tribunal obligation and my round-3 coverage statement listed it as the least-covered one. Every other test in fln-kernel asserts what I believe a rule says; this is the only one that asks the pin.

WHAT IT IS. tests/reference_differential.rs runs real Lean source through the pinned lean binary, reads the verdict off the process, constructs the same declaration as an fln_kernel Declaration, and compares. No Reference expectation is hard-coded anywhere - an expectation I wrote would just be my belief about the pin restated, and my belief is the thing under test.

THE D23 ASYMMETRY IS ENCODED STRUCTURALLY. Accepting what the Reference rejects is unsoundness and is release-blocking, and the classifier has no path that excuses it. Rejecting what it accepts is incompleteness, a finding unless an explicit carve-out row justifies it - the one shape D23 permits. A non-answer from either side is unscorable and fails rather than passing. The carve-out registry is empty and a row in it is a public statement that we knowingly disagree with the pin.

PROVED BY BREAKING THE REAL KERNEL. With the KR-974 theorem-must-be-a-Prop check disabled in src/lib.rs, the harness reported REF-REJ-001 as UnsoundlyPermissive and failed with the release-blocking text; source restored byte-identical afterwards. A differential that cannot detect divergence is worse than none, because it converts an untested claim into a false one - the same mistake as a green suite over an unguarded rule, one level up.

IT CAUGHT TWO DEFECTS IN ITS OWN ORACLE FIRST, both of which would have inverted it silently. Exit status is not a verdict: a well-typed def over an axiom exits non-zero on a CODEGEN error, and reading that as a rejection would have scored a clean acceptance as a refusal and then agreed with a broken kernel for the wrong reason. My first fix was also wrong - treating any tagged error as a non-verdict swallowed error(lean.unknownIdentifier), which IS a refusal - and the corpus caught it by reporting a case as unscorable. Both are now pinned by tests.

CORPUS: 7 cases, all agreeing. Accept direction KR-972 and KR-974 twice; reject direction KR-974 theorem-not-Prop, KR-974 body mismatch, KR-105 unknown constant, KR-107 binder domain not a type. Self-asserting floors check the case count and that both directions are non-empty.

HONEST LIMITS, recorded in tests/REFERENCE_DIFFERENTIAL.md with the provenance and the empty carve-out registry: the corpus is hand-paired, which is the weak point, since a transcription error makes a case vacuous rather than wrong. Scaling past that needs decoded olean declarations and therefore fln-olean, which is outside this crate's allow-direct covenant, so it belongs in fln-conformance next to kernel_replay. leanchecker ships in the pin and would give kernel-only verdicts over olean input - the natural next step, needing the same olean path. And lean runs the elaborator, so this compares at declaration-admissibility level rather than strictly at the kernel boundary; unknownIdentifier is elaboration, not kernel.

PLACEMENT NOTE for whoever owns the Tribunal: D8 puts the Reference-as-differential-oracle inside the Tribunal, and this file lives in fln-kernel because that was the round's scope. The crate itself gains no dependency - only its test invokes the pin - but if you would rather the differential live in fln-conformance, moving it is cheap and I have no objection.

Gates, all LOCAL since the pin cannot run on rch workers: cargo test --locked -p fln-kernel, 99 judgments + 3 differential + 3 lib, 0 failed; clippy --all-targets -D warnings exit 0; rustfmt clean; structure-guard PASS 0 findings; UBS 0 criticals.

comments.text:
SCOPED, NOT LEFT HALF-DONE. Two follow-ons filed; bc7 itself still cannot close, for the reason recorded earlier rather than a new one.

fln-lst4 (P1): widen the differential to Corpus scale over decoded olean declarations. This is a SPLIT rather than an extension because of a hard constraint I verified rather than assumed: scaling needs fln-olean, and fln-kernel's allow-direct covenant is fln-core, fln-hash, fln-bignum, fln-env. structure-guard enforces that on DEV-dependencies too - manifest.rs DEP_SECTIONS includes dev-dependencies and the FLN-STRUCT-009 loop iterates every dep without filtering by section - so a dev-dependency on fln-olean would fail the structure gate. The work belongs in fln-conformance, which already owns kernel_replay and the decode path. The comparator and the D23 asymmetry are reusable as-is.

fln-hfch (P2): the foreign-witness question, answered by measurement. leanchecker IS reachable at the pin and does real kernel-level work - LEAN_PATH pointed at the pin, leanchecker Init.Core exits 0, and over Init's reachable closure it burns 149s user plus 104s system CPU at about 1170 percent parallelism. It is strictly stronger than the lean binary my harness uses today, because lean runs the elaborator and refuses some declarations before the kernel sees them. Bare invocation misleads: with no LEAN_PATH it resolves through elan to the v4.7.0 toolchain also installed here and dies on an incompatible header, which looks like a broken binary and is not.

WHAT IS NOT REACHABLE, recorded so nobody reads the current harness as the full council: the export format does not exist at this pin - lean --help at v4.32.0 offers -o, -i, -c and -b and no export flag - so the route AGENTS.md describes for joining foreign checkers is unavailable with the shipped binary. lean4lean is not present at all and adding it runs into D1's closed dependency universe, which makes it a decision rather than a detail. Today the kernel council is ONE foreign implementation and us, and no document should say otherwise.

PIN PACKAGING FACT worth knowing before anyone enumerates modules: the pin's olean set is incomplete relative to its own import graph. Init.olean imports Init.Data.Basic and lib/lean/Init/Data/Basic.olean does not exist, while 600 other Init oleans and 2433 in total do. So leanchecker Init fails on an absent file while leanchecker Init.Core succeeds. Enumerate present oleans rather than walking imports, or a packaging gap will look like a divergence.

bc7 STAYS OPEN, unchanged from my earlier assessment: it is blocked by franken_lean-79k (KERNEL_CONTRACT.md) and franken_lean-artifact-incomplete-private-refs-sgt, and I argued at the time that the 79k edge is genuine rather than spurious. The differential harness does not change that and if anything reinforces it - its 7 cases were chosen by me, from the same implementation-derived rule inventory, so the coverage denominator is still the code rather than a specification. Closing bc7 now would assert a coverage claim measured against nothing.

comments.author: cc_2
comments.text:
CONSTRAINT ON WHAT MAY BE CLAIMED ABOUT KERNEL WITNESSES (cc_2, from fln-hfch which is now closed). Registering this here so a later reader does not assume the council exists, because the differential harness landing in 6f9a6e5 makes it easy to assume exactly that.

THE FINDING, restated in claim terms: at the pinned toolchain there is NO foreign kernel witness, and the B3 standard of two implementations that share no code CANNOT be met at v4.32.0.

* The export format does not exist at the pin. lean --help at v4.32.0 has no export, dump or emit flag; there is no export tool in bin; there is no export olean in lib.
* leanchecker is not foreign. It ships inside the toolchain and ldd shows it linking libleanshared_1.so and libleanshared_2.so — the same shared Lean kernel the lean binary uses, built from a generated LeanChecker.c. It is the Reference kernel re-run over compiled artifacts: a second EXECUTION, not a second OPINION.
* lean4lean is absent from the toolchain entirely.

WHY THIS IS A CLAIM CONSTRAINT AND NOT JUST A BEAD OUTCOME. The stronger reading is not "foreign witnesses are unimplemented" — that would be ordinary and expected at this stage. It is that the MECHANISM the plan names is unavailable as described at this pin. AGENTS.md's Tribunal section states the obligation as "Kernel verdicts diffed against the Reference kernel, lean4checker, and lean4lean", and README describes "foreign witnesses (lean4checker, lean4lean-class checkers via the export format) as optional council members". Both name a route — the export format — that the pinned binaries do not provide, and one witness — lean4checker — that on inspection is the Reference kernel itself.

WHAT THAT MEANS FOR ROWS AND DOCS, concretely:
1. No Parity Ledger row may cite foreign-witness or multi-implementation corroboration for a kernel verdict. I checked: no row does today, so this is a guard against a future one rather than a correction.
2. Any doc sentence implying the council is assembled is currently unearned. README is explicitly a spec written in the present tense rather than a status report, so those sentences are not defects — but the export-format clause specifically should be marked as pin-dependent, because it is not a matter of building something, it is unavailable at v4.32.0.
3. The differential harness in crates/fln-kernel/tests/reference_differential.rs IS the strongest kernel evidence currently available, and its own docs already say it compares us against one implementation. That framing should not drift upward as the corpus grows.

WHAT WOULD CHANGE IT: lean4lean, vendored or built, is the only genuine second opinion in sight. That is a D1 closed-dependency-universe decision for a Tribunal owner, not something to add quietly. Alternatively a pin that ships an exporter would reopen the route the plan actually names.

NOT MY FILE: ci/PARITY_LEDGER.txt and README.md are outside crates/fln-kernel. This is recorded here so whoever owns them has the fact and the reasoning; I am not editing either.

title: W1 tooling: make Beads workspace durability and doctor results truthful
description:
## Problem

`br doctor --json` reports a healthy SQLite/JSONL store with matching record counts and no reliability anomalies, but still exits nonzero for three distinct classes: `.beads/.gitignore` does not ignore `.write.lock`; `.beads/.write.lock` has a stale mtime and appears orphaned; and `beads.base.jsonl` is absent after a recorded successful flush. It also labels fulfilled closed blocking prerequisites as dead dependencies even though those edges are intentional implementation/evidence provenance and do not block readiness. Leaving real durability warnings mixed with a false-positive graph heuristic makes operators either ignore doctor or remove valuable history.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run `br doctor --json` from the repository root and retain the complete machine output and exit code.
2. Confirm the reliability audit, SQLite integrity, JSONL parse, count parity, and sync metadata are healthy while the gitignore, stale-lock, missing-post-flush-anchor, and closed-prerequisite findings remain.
3. Run `br sync --flush-only`, then rerun `br doctor --json`; observe that the export timestamp advances while the merge-anchor finding can remain.
4. Compare `br ready --json` and `br dep cycles --json` with the doctor edge list; fulfilled closed prerequisites do not block readiness and the graph remains acyclic, while a genuinely missing blocker must still be diagnosed.

## Scope

Reproduce each finding against the exact pinned `br` version and determine whether it is repository configuration/state, a supported repair workflow, or an upstream beads_rust defect. Repair the real lock/ignore/merge-anchor conditions through documented supported operations. Preserve every valid closed-prerequisite edge. If the doctor heuristic or base-anchor behavior is upstream, record the exact version/finding id/reproducer, obtain or pin a corrected release when available, and document a narrow expiring classification until then; never blanket-ignore doctor failure.

## Constraints

No direct SQLite editing, JSONL rewriting, deletion, lock removal, or moving any file without the user’s explicit written permission required by AGENTS.md. First prove no live writer owns a lock. Do not remove closed dependency edges merely to silence `dep.dead_closed_blocking_edges`; they encode sequencing and closure evidence. Do not weaken `br doctor`, bypass nonzero status globally, or hide unknown/new findings. All Beads issue/status/dependency changes use `br` only.

## Acceptance Criteria

The machine acceptance field is authoritative and additive to this scope.
acceptance_criteria: 1. On the exact installed/pinned br version, deterministic repro fixtures independently cover incomplete inner gitignore, a genuinely live lock, an orphan/stale lock, successful flush with merge anchor, missing/stale anchor, healthy SQLite/JSONL parity, intentional open-to-closed prerequisite edges, a truly missing blocker, and a genuinely stale/unready issue. Every case produces the correct stable finding_id, severity, message, and exit class; the fix must distinguish real durability failures from graph-history false positives. 2. Before any lock action, a read-only ownership check proves whether a live writer exists. No file is deleted, moved, overwritten, or manually rewritten without the exact user approval required by AGENTS.md; no SQLite or JSONL surgery is allowed. Supported br operations or a reviewed upstream fix create/refresh the merge anchor and leave DB/JSONL hashes and counts synchronized. 3. Intentional closed-prerequisite edges remain present and continue to prove implementation/evidence ordering. Doctor must stop calling fulfilled blockers dead, or a version-bound, finding-id-specific, exact-edge-set classification with owner and expiry must fail closed on any changed/new edge or finding; no blanket exit-code suppression. 4. Named unit/model tests in the owning repair surface cover lock ownership/age boundaries, atomic anchor creation and interruption points, flush idempotence, concurrent writers, closed/missing blocker classification, malformed metadata, permissions, and recovery. Named mutants that ignore a live lock, accept a missing anchor, misclassify a missing blocker as fulfilled, remove closed provenance, or swallow an unknown warning are each killed. 5. A no-mock E2E runs real br commands in isolated retained workspaces for healthy create/update/dependency/flush/doctor, live-lock refusal, orphan-lock diagnosis, interrupted/missing-anchor failure, exact approved repair, concurrent flushes, intentional closed-edge acceptance, genuine missing-edge failure, and clean recovery. It never mutates or cleans the production .beads tree during the test. 6. Human logs and strict schema-versioned NDJSON record br version/build, workspace identity, command/argv/cwd, DB/JSONL/anchor/lock paths and hashes without private contents, writer facts, finding ids/severities, exact edge ids and states, expected/actual exit, separate bounded stdout/stderr artifacts, approved action if any, artifact manifest, cleanup/retention, and final state. Validator self-tests reject missing/extra/stale/swapped/merged-stream/wrong-finding/unknown-warning evidence, and retained bundles validate independently. 7. Final production verification shows SQLite integrity and reliability healthy, DB/JSONL counts and hashes synchronized, lock/ignore/anchor findings truthful, all intentional dependencies preserved, br lint and cycles clean, bv alerts clean, and any remaining upstream limitation explicitly version-bound and non-silent. Applicable format/test/ShellCheck/UBS gates for any repository-owned conformance surface and the upstream br test suite for any upstream fix are green.
notes: cod_3 / MistyBluff conclusion, 2026-07-24: the defect is owned and already fixed upstream in `/data/projects/beads_rust`, not in FrankenLean scripts or fln-conformance. Installed `br --version` is 0.2.16. On the healthy FrankenLean workspace, `RUST_LOG=error br doctor --json` exited 1 despite workspace_health=healthy, reliability_audit.health=healthy with anomaly_count=0, SQLite integrity OK, and synchronized DB/JSONL counts of 233; stdout is `/tmp/franken_lean-cod_3-br-doctor-20260724T2248Z.stdout.json`, sha256 dd27e5e64171256ac28e027a1c85c7797bda3e8a49311892d5b3e03f92d0e74d. `RUST_LOG=error br sync --flush-only` succeeded but the missing merge anchor warning survived; post-flush stdout is `/tmp/franken_lean-cod_3-br-doctor-post-flush-20260724T2249Z.stdout.json`, sha256 37a811b0df83168e41571b5062d6c784ff2afac2fe631ac98cfa50947c995624. Upstream commit 480a412df250c04da1b5120b59203569e4514c49 (`fix(sync+doctor): materialize the merge anchor from clean flushes (#378); name real skip reasons on close (#380)`) makes no-op and real flush-only runs maintain `beads.base.jsonl` and makes doctor warn only on real drift; upstream commit c2cd87dd464e86bda67aa097f3b797806d47f068 (`fix(doctor): keep fresh workspaces health-clean`) fixes the fresh-workspace `.write.lock` and expected FrankenSQLite WAL-only diagnostics. Current upstream is 0.2.19. Named regression proof: from `/data/projects/beads_rust`, `rch exec -- cargo test --locked e2e_flush_only_maintains_merge_anchor_and_doctor_agrees -- --nocapture` exited 0; `tests/e2e_sync_status_health.rs::e2e_flush_only_maintains_merge_anchor_and_doctor_agrees` passed 1/1. title: check.sh sealed build roots are never pruned: 284G of one-day accumulation under target/sealed filled the disk twice
description:
check.sh gives every run a private sealed build root — `SEALED_BUILD_ROOT="${FLN_CHECK_SEALED_BUILD_ROOT:-$REPO/target/sealed}/$RUN_ID"` (scripts/check.sh:114, introduced under `fln-evidence-runner-bootstrap-btk`, whose own comment promises "never the user's ambient CARGO_HOME or target directory") — and every cargo-invoking stage runs sealed (`--sealed-cargo --sealed-build-root`, scripts/check.sh:1152-1153). `prepare_sealed_cargo` then creates `<root>/cargo-home` and `<root>/target` and points CARGO_TARGET_DIR into them (scripts/evidence.py:4512-4535). The sealing itself is correct: hermetic admission must not trust ambient caches.

What is missing is any retention policy. `rmtree` appears nowhere in scripts/evidence.py; check.sh never removes SEALED_BUILD_ROOT — no trap, no startup prune, no bound. Each run therefore pays a cold full-workspace build into a directory nothing will ever read again, and leaves it on disk forever.

MEASURED 2026-08-02T03:45Z at d0560fc9 by BeigeMarsh, one host, class bounded_model:

- /data/projects/franken_lean/target = 285G by st_blocks (dust -b), of which **target/sealed = 284G**.
- target/sealed holds **37 roots** named `check-20260801T*Z-<pid>` — ALL dated 2026-08-01 (08:27Z through ~21:40 local). Mean ~7.7G per root. So the leak rate at that day's check.sh cadence is roughly **284G/day**.
- Disk at measurement: 906G total, **598M free**, stable across two df samples 20s apart. The 2026-08-01 ~22:00 ENOSPC event that took every pane's harness down (route-CobaltLantern-to-sequencer-DISK-holder-named-...) and the standing shortage now are both this mechanism: the observed "recovery to 3.3G" was then consumed by subsequent sealed runs.
- The sibling per-run trees are NOT the problem: target/check 162M, target/e2e 433M, target/evidence-self-test 17M, target/structure-guard-expand 59M, and the `diagnostic-projection-no-mock-*` scratch dirs (crates/fln-conformance/tests/diag_render.rs `scratch_dir()`, deliberately retained) are ~40K each.

Repair shape, for the owner to decide:

1. **Immediate, not an agent action** (Rule 1 / break-glass): the user authorizes removal of the accumulated roots under target/sealed. No run ever reuses a root — the next run's cold build is paid regardless — so deletion costs nothing.
2. **Durable**: end-of-run cleanup of the run's own SEALED_BUILD_ROOT (trap on exit), plus a startup prune as a backstop for SIGKILLed runs. RUN_ID embeds `$$`, so a prune can skip any root whose pid is still alive and never race a concurrent run. Bounded retention-on-failure is an option ONLY if bundles reference the build root — NOT VERIFIED either way; check whether anything under ART_DIR cites SEALED_BUILD_ROOT paths before choosing.
3. **Optional, separate decision**: a warm sealed cache keyed by (toolchain identity, SUITE.lock digest, Cargo.lock digest) would cut both the ~8G/run disk cost and the cold-build wall time, but it converts per-attempt isolation into keyed reuse — a hermeticity trade needing its own argument, never a rider on the leak fix.

NOT ESTABLISHED: per-root sizes (284G/37 is a mean; variance unmeasured); the rate is one day on one host; whether any evidence bundle references its run's build root; and whether FLN_CHECK_SEALED_BUILD_ROOT is set by any caller anywhere (a caller pointing it elsewhere relocates the leak rather than curing it).

title: Build Gate: the stated freeze mechanism does not predict which mid-lane writes actually void a lane
description:
The Build Gate section states one rule -- while a lane holds the lock, write nothing inside
the repository -- and justifies it with one mechanism: scripts/evidence.py samples
repository_state() three times and requires the WHOLE repository to be byte-identical, so it
is not a path list. That justification is now known to be incomplete, and the gap was found
by an accident rather than by a check.

THE OBSERVATION, 2026-07-27, measured at fbb9de1b (cc_1). cc_3 created
crates/fln-conformance/src/execution.rs at 00:17:09Z and modified lib.rs at 00:17:12Z, 33
seconds into a held lock, while scripts/e2e/env_snapshots.sh was running. THE LANE PASSED:
terminal verdict=pass reason=all_obligations_passed process_exit=0, 44 step records all
assertion=pass, and input_root identical across all 44 records. A mid-lane write to a tracked
source file did not void the lane.

WHY, AND IT IS STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN LUCKY. There are TWO different checks and the doctrine
describes only one of them.

  1. The three-sample path-agnostic freeze lives in verify_vendor_binding and is reached by
     every hash-tree --vendor-path call, which the lane makes at every step boundary via
     hash_governed(). It compares three samples taken BACK TO BACK inside a single call. It
     therefore catches the repository MOVING DURING one call's sample window -- microseconds
     -- and does NOT compare against the state at lane start. A write that lands between two
     calls, and then holds still, passes it.

  2. The governed-input check is a PATH LIST and differs per lane.
     scripts/e2e/env_snapshots.sh INPUT_PATHS covers Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, SUITE.lock,
     rust-toolchain.toml, crates/fln-core, crates/fln-hash, crates/fln-env, vendor/NOTICE,
     four scripts and the CI workflow. It does NOT cover crates/fln-conformance.
     scripts/check.sh INPUT_PATHS covers bare "crates", bare "ci", bare "tools",
     .beads/issues.jsonl, contracts, and much more.

So env_snapshots was insensitive to that write BY CONSTRUCTION. A write into crates/fln-env
would have voided it. check.sh, whose list contains bare "crates", would have seen the same
write.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY WRONG HERE. The doctrine's stated mechanism ("it asserts that the whole
repository held still") is the strict reading, and the strict rule it produces is correct and
should stand. But the mechanism as described does not predict the behaviour observed above,
which means the section teaches a model that a reader can falsify in one afternoon. A rule
whose stated justification is falsifiable gets re-derived into a weaker one by the next
person who notices -- which is exactly the failure mode the section already documents three
times ("three people derived three wrong rules"). This is a fourth, waiting.

WHAT THIS BEAD OWNS. Produce the measurement that lets the section state a rule that is both
correct and true to the mechanism, then hold it with a check.

  R1. For each lane script under scripts/e2e/ plus scripts/check.sh, DERIVE its governed path
      set from the script rather than transcribing it, and record where the two checks
      differ. Derivation, not a hand list -- a hand-listed scope is the defect one floor up.
  R2. Measure, do not infer: for at least env_snapshots and check.sh, plant a write in each
      of {a path inside that lane's own governed set, a tracked path outside it, an untracked
      new file outside it, .beads/issues.jsonl, AGENTS.md} and record for each whether the
      lane voids, with the exact refusal text. Twelve evidence surfaces already refuse for
      reasons that name something else, so capture the message, not just the exit code.
  R3. Correct the Build Gate section so its stated mechanism matches what was measured,
      keeping the conservative rule as the operating instruction. The rule is not what is in
      question; its justification is.
  R4. A guard that fails when a lane's governed set changes without the section being
      updated. Without R4 this bead buys one afternoon's accuracy and rots like the anchors
      in item 7.

TRAP, STATED FIRST BECAUSE IT IS THE WHOLE RISK. This must NOT become permission to write
during a lane. One observation that two lane types differ is not a licence, and the
conservative rule stands unchanged until R1-R4 land. Anyone reading this bead as "writes
outside a lane's INPUT_PATHS are safe" has read it exactly backwards: the measurement exists
to make the strict rule defensible, or to replace it with a precise one, never to relax it on
the strength of one lucky run. Three lanes died unsequenced on 2026-07-26 and the one that
had a park in place is the one that passed.

A SECOND, SMALLER DEFECT FOUND IN THE SAME SECTION AND NOT YET REPAIRED. The Build Gate text
cites scripts/evidence.py:10296-10307 for the three-sample freeze. At fbb9de1b those lines
are sealed-interpreter shape checks; the freeze is at 11959-11969 inside
verify_vendor_binding. The anchor rotted without anything noticing -- item 7's vdi4 family
landing on the doctrine that teaches anchoring. Repairing the line numbers by hand recreates
the same rot on the next refactor, so the citation should name the FUNCTION, or a test should
hold the section to the code the way
the_evidence_surface_refuses_a_gitdir_pointer_root already holds the green-bar table.

WHAT THIS BEAD DOES NOT CLAIM. That any lane result recorded to date is wrong -- the
env_snapshots run above is valid on its own terms and its governed inputs were provably
static. That the freeze is weak: it does what it says, the doctrine just describes it as
something stronger. And no claim about lanes other than env_snapshots and check.sh, which are
the only two observed; the other e2e scripts are unmeasured and must not be assumed similar.

comments.text:
# 98np measurement plan — which lane hashes what, and the experiment that settles it

cc_1 (PeachBass), drafted read-only during cod_3's park. **Derived at HEAD `974fcc5a`**
(scripts read at that HEAD; the retained bundle evidence is from earlier runs and is
anchored inline). Nothing here is committed. Harness:
`/data/tmp/claude-1000/cc1-98np-derive.py`, output `cc1-98np-derived.json`.

## 0. The headline: the doctrine blames the wrong mechanism for its own worked example

AGENTS.md's Build Gate section explains what ends a lane with **one** mechanism —
`repository_state()` sampled three times, path-agnostic, "not hashing a list of paths" — and
says getting it wrong "has cost two lanes".

**Measured: the 23:16 run did not die of that.** Its retained bundle
`target/check/check-20260726T231630Z-3650592/run.ndjson` `run_end` record says:

```
reason_code     : final_workspace_changed
first_divergence: final_workspace_changed
active_stage    : complete
verdict         : inconclusive     process_exit: 3
input_root : sha256:8bd4af684addac4201632a61f01af95046098d62cade2780b662ddd92a29172c
final_state: sha256:b7902448f41d52617773f768bb0eca93ddc2ef00c3b683b37d5396b64cabbdc0
```

`final_workspace_changed` is raised at **`scripts/check.sh:741`**, comparing the **governed
path-list root** at start against the same list at end. It is not `repository_state()`. And
`active_stage: complete` says every stage ran; the drift was caught only at finalization.

So the section's mechanism paragraph and its own casualty do not match. This is the same
shape AGENTS.md item 7 documents under `hugg` — *the artifact asserts the wrong cause* —
landing on the Build Gate text itself.

## 1. There are THREE mechanisms, not one

| # | mechanism | where | scope | what it can catch |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| M1 | three-sample `repository_state()` | `evidence.py:11959-11969`, inside `verify_vendor_binding`; reached by every `hash-tree --vendor-path` and by `vendor-binding` | **path-agnostic, whole repo** | only motion **within one call's three back-to-back samples** (microseconds). A write that lands between two calls and then holds still passes it. |
| M2 | governed root, **start vs end** | `check.sh:741` → `final_workspace_changed` | that lane's `INPUT_PATHS` | persistent drift in a governed path, detected **only at finalization**, after every stage has run |
| M3 | governed root, **at every step boundary vs run-start root** | `env_snapshots.sh:798-805` `require_unchanged` → `governed_inputs_changed`, `exit 3` | that lane's `INPUT_PATHS` | persistent drift in a governed path, detected **within one step** |

M3 is strictly stronger than M2: `require_unchanged` compares `GLOBAL_BEFORE` *and*
`GLOBAL_AFTER` against `INPUT_ROOT`, not merely against each other, so any persistent drift
aborts at the next step boundary rather than at the end.

**Why my 2026-07-27 observation is consistent with all three and contradicts none.** A write
to `crates/fln-conformance` during `env_snapshots` is outside that lane's `INPUT_PATHS`, so
M2/M3 cannot see it; and it did not land inside a sample window, so M1 did not see it. The
lane was insensitive **by construction**. Nothing about the freeze is weak — it does exactly
what it says, and the doctrine describes it as something stronger.

## 2. Derived coverage over all 21 e2e lanes + check.sh (R1)

**A correction to this section, kept because it is the most instructive thing here.** My
first pass keyed on the `INPUT_PATHS=(` idiom and the literal string
`governed_inputs_changed`, and reported "8 lanes declare a governed set, 13 declare none,
`kernel_replay` and `contract_handoff` are unenforced anomalies". **That was wrong in both
anomalies.** `contract_handoff` enforces at `:231` (M2) and `:421-422` (M3-shaped);
`kernel_replay` carries a full governed set under different variable names
(`AP6_GOVERNED_ARGS`, `AP6_INPUT_ROOT`) and compares at `:255` and `:627`. I searched for one
*spelling* and called the misses defects — a hand-listed scope wearing a derived scan's
clothes, which is precisely what this bead exists to stop. Second pass keys on semantic
markers (`--governed-path` usage, comparisons against any `*INPUT_ROOT` variable, and the
reason strings): `/data/tmp/claude-1000/cc1-98np-derive2.py`.

**Nine lanes carry a drift mechanism; which mechanisms differ per lane:**

| lane | M1 freeze | M2 end | M3 per-step |
|---|:--:|:--:|:--:|
| `closure_audit`, `env_snapshots`, `structure_gate`, `vellum_naming_no_mock_e2e`, `verdict_schema` | yes | yes | yes |
| `contract_handoff` | yes | yes | — |
| **`check.sh`** | yes | yes | **—** |
| `kernel_replay` | yes | — | yes |
| `unsafe_note_clippy` | **—** | — | yes |

**Thirteen lanes show no detected drift mechanism at all:** `bignum_vectors`,
`canon_lifecycle`, `contract_drift`, `core_observables`, `diag_goldens`, `evidence_runner`,
`hash_identity`, `kernel_contract_ownership`, `marrow_abi_probes`, `marrow_region_load`,
`marrow_stage0_gauntlet`, `olean_resurrection`, `structural_gate`.

**Three findings that fall out of this, all needing confirmation before use:**

1. **`check.sh` has no per-step check.** It is M1 + M2 only — the *loosest* of the nine
   enforcing lanes on persistent drift, and it is the one the doctrine holds up as the
   strictest. `env_snapshots`, which the doctrine treats as the weaker case, is strictly
   tighter: M3 aborts at the next step boundary, M2 only at finalization.
2. **`unsafe_note_clippy` never reaches M1** — zero `--vendor-path` calls. It has M3 alone.
3. **13 lanes appear unprotected.** Before calling that a defect, check whether they run
   under the gate at all; a lane that never holds the lock needs no freeze. That check is not
   done and must not be skipped — it is the same charitable-reading error as above, inverted.

**Standing limit on this table:** M2 detection is *still* keyed to the string
`final_workspace_changed`. `kernel_replay:627` does compare a final root against its input
root without that label, so the M2 column understates by at least one. Treat the table as a
probe list, not an inventory, until R1 parses the comparisons structurally.

`.beads/issues.jsonl` is in **`check.sh`'s** list and **not** in `env_snapshots`'. That single
fact explains the first `env_snapshots` casualty recorded in AGENTS.md ("filing a bead is a
write") being attributed to the wrong list.

## 3. The experiment that settles it (R2)

One lane run per cell is too expensive (`env_snapshots` ≈ 9 min, `check.sh` ≈ 7 min). So the
design measures the **mechanisms** directly and uses full lanes only as controls.

**Cheap tier — decides M1 and M2/M3 semantics without running a lane.** For each mechanism,
drive its function directly against a scratch repo clone:

- **M1 probe.** Call `evidence.py hash-tree --root R --vendor-path V` while a helper mutates
  `R` in a tight loop; and again with a mutation that lands strictly between two calls.
  Expect: raises `Reference repository state changed during verification` only in the first.
  *This is the load-bearing claim of the whole doctrine and it has never been tested.*
- **M2/M3 probe.** Compute the governed root over a lane's derived `INPUT_PATHS`, mutate one
  path inside the set and one outside, recompute. Expect: root moves only for the inside-set
  mutation.

**Expensive tier — 4 real lane runs, not 40.** Two lanes × two cells, chosen because they are
the only two cells the cheap tier cannot decide (they test *when* detection happens, not
*whether*):

| lane | write | expected | settles |
|---|---|---|---|
| `env_snapshots` | tracked file **inside** its `INPUT_PATHS` (`crates/fln-env/src/extensions.rs`), mid-run | `governed_inputs_changed`, exit 3, **at the next step boundary** | M3 timing |
| `env_snapshots` | tracked file **outside** it (`crates/fln-conformance/src/lib.rs`), mid-run | **pass** | reproduces 2026-07-27 deliberately rather than by accident |
| `check.sh` | tracked file inside its set, mid-run | `final_workspace_changed`, exit 3, **`active_stage: complete`** | M2 timing — confirms all stages still run |
| `check.sh` | write then **revert before finalization** | **pass** — M2 is start-vs-end, so a reverted write is invisible | the sharpest cell; if it passes, M2 provably cannot see transient drift |

**Capture the message, never the exit code.** Twelve evidence surfaces already refuse with
text naming something else (AGENTS.md item 7, `hugg`). Record `reason_code`,
`first_divergence`, `active_stage`, `input_root` and `final_state` from the `run_end` record,
as extracted above — that is where the truth was, and the human summary line was not.

## 4. Traps this plan must not fall into

1. **Do not let this become permission.** Every cell above is designed to make the strict
   rule *defensible*, or to replace it with a precise one. The conservative rule — while any
   lane holds the lock, write nothing inside the repository — stands until R3/R4 land. The
   "outside the set → pass" cells exist to be *documented*, not exploited.
2. **Do not re-derive the governed sets by hand.** They are in the scripts; parse them (R1).
   The moment this table is transcribed it starts rotting, which is R4's whole point.
3. **A scan finding zero differences between lanes is a broken scan**, not a uniform fleet —
   13 lanes provably have no `INPUT_PATHS`.
4. **Do not run these probes in a linked worktree.** Every path here goes through
   `run_git`/`verify_vendor_binding`, which refuse on a gitdir-pointer root; the refusal
   blames something else.
5. **Anchor every number to the commit it was measured at.** This document's derivations are
   at `974fcc5a`; the bundle evidence is from `check-20260726T231630Z-3650592`.

## 5. What R3/R4 should then say

- **R3** — rewrite the Build Gate mechanism paragraph to name all three mechanisms and
  attribute its two casualties correctly. The *rule* does not change; its justification does.
  Fix the rotted anchor by naming `verify_vendor_binding` rather than a line range.
- **R4** — a test that derives each lane's governed set and fails when it moves without the
  doctrine changing, in **both directions** (a lane gaining or losing a governed path), with
  a planted decoy proving the scan is not vacuous. Model:
  `the_evidence_surface_refuses_a_gitdir_pointer_root`, which already holds the green-bar
  table to the code.

## 6. What this does not establish

The `env_snapshots` run at `fbb9de1b` is valid on its own terms — its governed inputs were
provably static (`input_root == final_state`, one value across all 44 step records). No claim
that any recorded lane result is wrong. No claim about the 19 lanes not probed here. The
`contract_handoff` anomaly is **unexplained, not diagnosed** — I did not find its finalizer,
and `check.sh` proves that looking like "declared and unenforced" is not the same as being it.

=== PART 1. THE CONTAINMENT QUESTION THIS BEAD LEFT OPEN ===

R1 established the derivation harness and reported "5 of 8 lanes contained in check.sh's set, 3 not" under prefix semantics. What was not established was whether containment is a NARROWING that buys anything, or a near-equality that buys nothing. For scripts/e2e/env_snapshots.sh it is a real narrowing, re-derived directly at this anchor rather than inherited from the r1-derived.json run:

  env_snapshots INPUT_PATHS (scripts/e2e/env_snapshots.sh:85):   13 paths
  check.sh      INPUT_PATHS (scripts/check.sh:149-171):          50 paths
  contained, prefix semantics:                                   13 of 13
  dropped:                                                       37

Prefix semantics, not literal string comparison: check.sh governs the directory "crates" while the lane governs "crates/fln-core", "crates/fln-hash", "crates/fln-env". A literal comparison scores those three as NOT contained and inverts the result. This is the same trap R1 recorded; restating it because the number above is wrong under the other reading.

The 37 dropped paths are, specifically, the other panes' work surfaces:

  .beads/issues.jsonl        <- the path that killed check.sh attempt 6 (a bead close)
  ci                         <- entire directory

So the lane governs its own subject (crates/fln-env), that subject's two dependencies, the shared runner, and the config pins — and nothing any other pane is likely to be holding.

M1's HEAD half is repo-wide: a commit by anyone in the sample window kills this lane exactly as it kills check.sh. Concretely: a peer's "br close" WITHOUT a commit cannot touch this lane; the same close WITH a commit still can. Parking the swarm is therefore still required for an e2e lane — it only has to hold for minutes rather than for a full 13-stage run. Anyone quoting the 13-vs-50 ratio as "the lane is safe from peers" has dropped M1 and is wrong.

Measured for env_snapshots only. The other seven lanes are not re-derived here.

=== PART 2. THE STATICNESS INSTRUMENT — a blindness worth recording next to the M-table ===

The Build Gate section says a static dirty tree is fine and a changing one is not, so before requesting a lane the operative question is "is the tree static". Tonight I certified it static across three samples (05:13Z, 05:14Z, 05:15:57Z) using HEAD plus a porcelain digest:

  git rev-parse HEAD                        -> ad2b9207... (all three)
  git status --porcelain | sort | sha256sum -> 747588f2... (all three)

  05:13  mtime=1785127264  size=988379  sha256=fcc7677d...
  05:22  mtime=1785129460  size=989798  sha256=86d16fc8...

and the porcelain digest 747588f2... did NOT move — across the entire window, including after both edits. It cannot: the file was ALREADY in the dirty set, so its status letter stayed " M" and the digest is a function of the status lines, not of content.

scripts/evidence.py is in env_snapshots' governed set twice (INPUT_PATHS at :85, COLLISION_INPUT_PATHS at :1596). Had a lane been sequenced at 05:15 on my certification, it would have died to a peer's WIP — the seventh such death tonight, and this bead exists because of exactly that failure family.

THE RULE: a porcelain-based staticness probe is sound only for files that are CLEAN. For a file already dirty — which is precisely the interesting case, since that is the file someone is working on — it is blind by construction. Certify staticness with the instrument the mechanism uses: size and mtime (M4), or a content hash. Not "git status".

Corollary for whoever writes R4: this is a fifth-mechanism-shaped hazard from the other side. It is not a missing mechanism; it is a missing instrument on the OPERATOR's side of the same table. The M-table tells you what voids a lane; nothing tells you how to check the precondition, so people reach for git status because it is the obvious tool, and it is the wrong one.

comments.text:
M4 SURVIVES ATTACK; THE OPERATOR-SIDE FINGERPRINT DOES NOT. Per-field attribution, and the one field that cannot be forged.

cc_1 (PeachBass), 2026-07-27T05:3xZ, measured at HEAD eb6c0ac2. Probe ran entirely under /data/tmp; nothing in the repository was written or touched. Follow-up to comment 1377 Part 2.

=== WHAT M4 ACTUALLY COMPARES, read from the code rather than the doc ===

scripts/evidence.py stable_file_facts (committed blob at HEAD, lines 1455-1497):

  before = os.fstat(descriptor)
  ... read the whole file through that same descriptor ...
  after  = os.fstat(descriptor)
  stable_fields = ("st_dev", "st_ino", "st_size", "st_mtime_ns", "st_ctime_ns")
  if any(before.F != after.F for F in stable_fields): raise "file changed while being read"

FIVE fields, not two. AGENTS.md's Build Gate section names only st_mtime_ns and st_ctime_ns; the code also carries st_dev, st_ino and st_size. Both stats are os.fstat on the SAME HELD DESCRIPTOR, not os.stat on the path -- that distinction is what the probe below was built to attack.

=== THE ATTACK, three vectors, each designed to evade ===

A file is opened and read; a mutation lands while the descriptor is open; before/after are compared. Vectors 2 and 3 are constructed specifically to defeat a size-and-mtime instrument -- vector 2 restores mtime with os.utime after a byte-identical rewrite (the cp -p / rsync -t shape), vector 3 writes a replacement, forges its mtime to match, and os.replace()s it over the original (the atomic-save shape used by many editors, and the shape this repo itself sanctions for the ownership projection's .candidate sibling).

  vector                          M4 (fstat, held fd)   path stat, 5 fields   mtime+size only
  in_place_append                 CAUGHT                CAUGHT                CAUGHT
  identical_rewrite_mtime_kept    CAUGHT                CAUGHT                BLIND
  atomic_replace_rename           CAUGHT                CAUGHT                BLIND

PER-FIELD ATTRIBUTION, which is the part worth keeping:

  identical_rewrite_mtime_kept   fd fields moved: [st_ctime_ns]
                                 path fields moved: [st_ctime_ns]
  atomic_replace_rename          fd fields moved: [st_ctime_ns]
                                 path fields moved: [st_ino, st_ctime_ns]

=== FINDING 1: M4 IS SOUND. I FAILED TO BREAK IT, AND THE REASON IS NON-OBVIOUS ===

I predicted M4 would be BLIND to atomic_replace_rename, reasoning that the held descriptor still refers to the old inode, so an fstat of it cannot see a new file appear at the path. The prediction was wrong and the mechanism is right. Unlinking an inode updates that inode's ctime, because ctime tracks inode metadata including link count. So os.replace() bumps st_ctime_ns on the very inode M4 is holding open, and M4 refuses. Recorded as a wrong prediction rather than quietly dropped: the M-table's M4 row survived a deliberate attempt to evade it, which is worth more to this bead than another unchallenged reading of the source.

Note also that M4 refuses rather than publishing stale bytes. Under atomic_replace_rename the descriptor read the pre-replace content (sha d53eda7a...) while the path then held different content (sha c422e707...). M4 raises instead of returning that stale snapshot as the governed content.

=== FINDING 2: st_ctime_ns IS THE ONLY FIELD THAT CATCHES EITHER SUBTLE VECTOR, AND IT IS THE ONLY ONE A WRITER CANNOT FORGE ===

In BOTH evasion vectors, st_ctime_ns is the single field that moved on the held descriptor. Not size, not mtime, not inode. That is not a coincidence: os.utime can restore atime and mtime to any value, but the utime call itself bumps ctime, and there is no syscall that sets ctime backwards. mtime is attacker-controlled; ctime is not.

CONSEQUENCE FOR ANY OPERATOR-SIDE STATICNESS PROBE. A fingerprint over size and mtime is blind to two of the three vectors above -- including the byte-identical rewrite that AGENTS.md already documents as killing a lane 7 trials out of 8. Adding size and mtime to a content digest therefore does NOT close the byte-identical hole in the general case; it closes it only when the writer happens to let mtime float. The field to add is st_ctime_ns. Adding st_ino as well is worth it at the path level, since it is what distinguishes an atomic replace from an in-place write and it is free.

Recommended operator instrument, matching the mechanism exactly: stat each governed path and hash (st_dev, st_ino, st_size, st_mtime_ns, st_ctime_ns). Anything less than ctime is weaker than M4 and will certify static a tree that M4 will refuse.

=== WHAT THIS DOES NOT EARN ===

Three vectors on one filesystem (ext4-class, /data/tmp, same device as the repo), one host, one run each, class bounded_model. Not a proof that no fourth vector evades M4; a hardlink-swap, an overlayfs copy-up, a different filesystem's ctime granularity, or a same-nanosecond race are all untested. The claim is bounded: for these three vectors M4 caught all three and a size-plus-mtime probe caught one.

This closes nothing on 98np's open list. R4 remains unwritten; whether a FIFTH mechanism exists remains unestablished -- and note that this comment did not look for one, it attacked an existing row. contract_handoff's finalizer remains unexplained and not diagnosed.

comments.text:
TWO OF THIS BEAD'S FOUR OPEN ITEMS ARE NOW MEASURED. One of them falsifies the M-table's completeness; the other shows the probe everyone trusts answers a question about a file no lane touches.

cc_1 (PeachBass), 2026-07-27T06:3xZ, measured at HEAD 5f102102. Source read from the COMMITTED blob at HEAD; the runtime probes ran entirely under /data/tmp against synthetic roots. Nothing in the repository was written or touched.

=== ITEM: "whether the 13 zero-governed-set lanes take the lock at all" — ANSWERED, AND THE QUESTION WAS TOO NARROW ===

NO LANE TAKES THE GATE LOCK. Not the thirteen, not any of them.

A repo-wide search over tracked .sh, .py, .rs, .yml and .toml surfaces (excluding target/ and vendor/) for the string fln-gate.lockfile returns ZERO hits. The only flock in any tracked script is:

  scripts/extract/gen_extern_census.sh:  flock -w 2400 200
  scripts/extract/census_materialize.sh: flock -w 2400 200

which is $PUBLICATION_LOCK on fd 200 -- the census publication lock, a different lock for a different purpose. This confirms and sharpens comment 1367's finding (ii) that the gate lock is convention-only: it is not merely absent from the lane scripts, it is absent from every tracked executable surface in the repository.

WHAT THAT MEANS OPERATIONALLY, and it is worse than "convention". The lock is acquired only by whoever WRAPS the invocation, e.g. flock -w 2400 /data/tmp/fln-gate.lockfile bash scripts/check.sh. A lane launched WITHOUT that wrapper is fully functional and takes no lock at all. It does not warn, it does not fail, it runs. And every other pane's flock -n probe then reports FREE.

So the probe this project relies on -- flock -n /data/tmp/fln-gate.lockfile -c true, exit 1 = HELD -- returns FREE in two different worlds: nothing is running, AND a lane is running unwrapped. AGENTS.md already records that a FREE probe can be stale because the lane acquires with a waiting flock -w 2400. This is a second and independent way FREE can be wrong, and unlike the first one no amount of re-probing detects it, because there is nothing to detect: the running lane never touched the file.

The honest repair is for the lane scripts to acquire the gate lock themselves, at which point FREE means free. Until then, "the lock said free" is evidence about an operator's habit, not about the repository.

=== ITEM: "whether a FIFTH mechanism exists (M1-M4 found by reading, exhaustiveness never established)" — ANSWERED: THE TABLE IS INCOMPLETE ===

M4's row in AGENTS.md reads: "stable_file_facts fstats each governed file before and after reading it". That describes ONE of two functions. The governed-tree hash DISPATCHES ON PATH TYPE (scripts/evidence.py at HEAD, the hashing walk):

  full_mode = path.lstat().st_mode
  mode = full_mode & 0o7777
  if stat.S_ISLNK(full_mode):
      _data, file_size, file_digest_hex = stable_symlink_facts(path)
      kind = b"L"
  else:
      _data, file_size, file_digest_hex = stable_file_facts(path)
      kind = b"F"

A governed path that is a SYMLINK is guarded by stable_symlink_facts, which differs from stable_file_facts in every dimension that matters:

  dimension            stable_file_facts            stable_symlink_facts
  syscall              fstat on a HELD descriptor   lstat on the PATH, twice
  subject hashed       file contents                the link TARGET STRING
  kind marker          b"F"                         b"L"
  refusals             "file changed while being    "symlink changed while being read"
                       read", "file size changed    AND "canonical link changed type"
                       while being read"

The type-change refusal has NO analogue in stable_file_facts. It fires when a path stops being a symlink between the walk's lstat and the guard's -- a state transition M4's row does not describe and nobody reading that row would anticipate.

MEASURED, NOT DERIVED. Probes under /data/tmp against synthetic roots, using the committed evidence.py blob, one variable per probe:

  A  baseline, sub/ = {real.txt "hello", link.txt -> real.txt}   sha256:46810e2443ce7bb6...
  B  real.txt content changed                                     sha256:2ea4060d90c0d15e...  (differs: contents contribute)
  C  real.txt restored                                            sha256:46810e2443ce7bb6...  (== A, deterministic)
  D  link RETARGETED, no file content edited                      sha256:b4dedf17313c9af5...  (differs: the TARGET STRING contributes)

  CONTROL, fresh directory, tree rebuilt identical to A           sha256:46810e2443ce7bb6...  (== A; path-independent)
  ONE VARIABLE, same tree but link.txt a REGULAR FILE whose
  bytes are exactly "real.txt"                                    sha256:2868649fda2c15d8...  (differs from A)

The last pair is the discriminator: identical byte content at an identical path, differing ONLY in whether the entry is a symlink or a regular file, produces different governed roots. The kind marker is load-bearing, so the two paths are genuinely distinct mechanisms rather than one mechanism with a cosmetic branch.

DISCLOSED: an intermediate probe appeared to show a restored symlink not returning to the baseline digest. That was an experimental artifact -- a file created during the retarget step remained in the tree -- and the fresh-directory control above accounts for it entirely. Recorded rather than dropped, because an unexplained non-reproduction is exactly the kind of thing that gets rationalised away.

WHAT THIS EARNS. The claim "the freeze is four mechanisms" is FALSE as an exhaustiveness claim. M4 is two mechanisms with different syscalls, different subjects and a refusal the table does not name. Whether to number it M5 or to restate M4 as covering both is a presentation choice; what matters is that the table was found incomplete by DERIVATION (dispatch on S_ISLNK at the hashing walk) after being complete-looking to three separate careful readings, which is precisely the failure mode this bead's R4 exists to mechanise.

NOTE THE COINCIDENCE, WITHOUT OVERREADING IT. Attempts 7 and 8 both failed to publish a bundle because of a SYMLINK in the artifact tree (fln-selftest-symlink-blocks-bundle-4yhd). That is a different code path -- the publisher's artifact walk, not the governed hash -- and this is NOT a claim that the two share a defect. What they share is a blind spot in the DOCTRINE: symlinks are handled by separate code under separate rules in more than one place, and no prose in AGENTS.md says so anywhere.

title: W4 Vellum: conformance harness against the pin's own parse trees (oracle is reachable without Tribunal instrumentation)
description:
Filed by cc_3 on 2026-07-25 with the enabling finding, NOT started — I was at my context limit and a half-built harness is worse than none.

THE FINDING, which changes what is possible here. The pinned Reference will print its own Syntax tree from a plain .lean file, with no patching and no instrumented-oracle build:

    import Lean.Elab.Command
    open Lean in
    run_cmd do
      let stx <- `(term| 1 + 2 * 3)
      Lean.logInfo (toString stx)

prints

    (``term_+_'' (num "1") "+" (``term_*_'' (num "2") "*" (num "3")))

That is node kinds and grouping, i.e. the parse STRUCTURE, obtained through the Reference's ordinary metaprogramming surface. Note what it is not: it is not a patched Reference and not a build-time trace dump, so it does not require the §18 instrumented oracle. Lean (version 4.7.0, x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, commit 6fce8f7d5cd1, Release)
Miscellaneous:
  --help -h          display this message
  --features -f      display features compiler provides (eg. LLVM support)
  --version -v       display version number
  --githash          display the git commit hash number used to build this binary
  --run              call the 'main' definition in a file with the remaining arguments
  --o=oname -o       create olean file
  --i=iname -i       create ilean file
  --c=fname -c       name of the C output file
  --bc=fname -b      name of the LLVM bitcode file
  --stdin            take input from stdin
  --root=dir         set package root directory from which the module name of the input file is calculated
                     (default: current working directory)
  --trust=num -t     trust level (default: max) 0 means do not trust any macro,
                     and type check all imported modules
  --quiet -q         do not print verbose messages
  --memory=num -M    maximum amount of memory that should be used by Lean
                     (in megabytes)
  --timeout=num -T   maximum number of memory allocations per task
                     this is a deterministic way of interrupting long running tasks
  --threads=num -j   number of threads used to process lean files
  --tstack=num -s    thread stack size in Kb
  --server           start lean in server mode
  --worker           start lean in server-worker mode
  --plugin=file      load and initialize Lean shared library for registering linters etc.
  --load-dynlib=file load shared library to make its symbols available to the interpreter
  --deps             just print dependencies of a Lean input
  --print-prefix     print the installation prefix for Lean and exit
  --print-libdir     print the installation directory for Lean's built-in libraries and exit
  --profile          display elaboration/type checking time for each definition/theorem
  --stats            display environment statistics
  -D name=value      set a configuration option (see set_option command) has no AST flag and  emits only messages, so this is the route.

WHY THIS MATTERS. Every Vellum suite today tests the parser against itself or against fixed cases. pratt_precedence_model gets fidelity from six values the pin PRINTED via #eval, which is real but indirect — it infers grouping from an evaluated result. The route above gives the grouping DIRECTLY, and it generalises to constructs that have no evaluable value at all: commands, tactics, binders, patterns, doc comments.

It is also strictly stronger evidence for the gap documented in crates/fln-syntax/TESTING_COMPOSITION.md. That gap is a change which is uniform enough to be metamorphically invisible AND only observable outside the 8 golden rows. A structural comparison against the pin closes it directly, because the oracle does not share our rule.

SCOPE JUDGEMENT, stated so the next person does not have to relitigate it. A harness of a few dozen hand-chosen constructs is legitimately fln-syntax/fln-parse work: it is a .lean file, a captured stdout, and a comparison. A harness at CORPUS scale — mathlib, thousands of files, per-file diffing with tiers — is the Tribunal's differential rig (§18) and belongs there, not here. The boundary is scale and infrastructure, not the oracle: the oracle turns out to be available on both sides of it.

WHAT A FIRST SLICE SHOULD DO:
1. A fixture set of Lean source snippets covering the constructs Vellum claims to parse — mixed-precedence terms, right- and left-associative chains, non-associative operators, binders with and without types, dotted and escaped identifiers, every literal form including raw strings, doc comments, nested block comments.
2. For each, capture the pin's printed Syntax once and freeze it, with per-artifact provenance on the shape crates/fln-syntax/tests/corpus/VELLUM_GOLDENS_PROVENANCE.md uses. Same rule: no update mode.
3. A translation from our green tree to the pin's rendering, or from the pin's rendering to a shape our tree can be compared against. THIS IS THE HARD PART and it is where the design judgement lives — the two representations differ (upstream stores substrings where we store spans, and its node kinds are Names we do not yet mint identically), so a naive string comparison will fail for uninteresting reasons. Decide explicitly what is being compared: node kind sequence, grouping shape, or both, and say what is deliberately NOT compared.
4. A typed SKIP when the pin is absent, matching parser_category_inventory — and per the lane spec on franken_lean-jbru/urd1/fln-33gl, any lane wrapping this must assert the skip did NOT happen.

WATCH: the pin invocation above took roughly a minute on first run because it imports Lean.Elab.Command. That is fine for a frozen-fixture generator run by hand; it is NOT fine inside a per-commit gate. Freeze the pin's output rather than calling the pin from the test.
close_reason: Reference parse-tree differential slice delivered and package evidence green

  The pinned lean binary has no AST or syntax-dump flag. Its --json option reports messages as

  metaprogram route shown above is the only way to obtain the Reference's own Syntax, and it does
