title: W1: Convergence governance — R15 WIP caps and earliest-failing-gate routing
description:
Implement the program-control mitigation required by risk R15 so a large multi-agent effort converges on R4 instead of maximizing simultaneous subsystem starts. Define a versioned, reviewable policy over the live br dependency graph and evidence registry: distinguish workstreams, gate/contract prerequisites, active incidents/security fixes, verification lanes, and additive leapfrog work; cap active implementation workstreams; route capacity first to the earliest failing convergence gate and its transitive blockers; reserve bounded capacity for independent critical bugs and verification; and freeze additive work when convergence evidence regresses. Freeze means retain every bead and feature in the backlog with reasons and resume conditions, never delete or silently descope it.

Expose a robot-safe command/report suitable for CI and agents. It reads stable br JSON plus evidence/gate state, never launches a TUI, never mutates bead status implicitly, and emits both a concise recommendation and schema-versioned NDJSON containing graph/evidence hashes, active-workstream classification, WIP budget, critical path, earliest failing gate, selected/held work, reason codes, exception owner/expiry, starvation age, and exact next unblocking actions. The policy must handle stale/missing/cyclic/inconsistent graph or evidence inputs as typed inconclusive/internal outcomes, not as permission to start more work.

## Acceptance Criteria

The decision log freezes the initial numeric WIP budget, reserved verification/incident capacity, workstream classification law, priority order, exception authority, expiry/review cadence, fairness/starvation rule, and resume criteria. Configuration changes are reviewed, versioned, and evidenced; agents cannot bypass the cap by splitting or relabeling equivalent work. CI rejects unauthorized over-cap in-progress states and expired exceptions while providing actionable reasons; emergency/security work can proceed under a logged bounded exception without erasing the main critical path. The policy treats bv metrics as advisory evidence and validates semantic dependencies, so keyword similarity or a transient PageRank score cannot rewrite the plan automatically.

Named deterministic unit/property/mutation tests cover empty/single/many-track graphs, ties, multiple failing gates, incidents, verification reservation, starvation, blocked and deferred beads, closed/reopened work, stale evidence, missing owners, cycles, duplicate labels, malicious metadata, expired exceptions, and stable output under reordered JSONL. A real no-mock E2E uses a temporary br project plus real br and bv robot output to exercise claim, over-cap rejection, gate regression freeze, incident exception, expiry, close/unblock, and clean recovery without mutating the production project. Detailed bounded human and schema-versioned NDJSON logs record tool/schema versions, exact redacted commands/cwd, graph/evidence/config hashes, selected/held ids and reasons, monotonic timings/resources, exit status, stderr/stdout artifacts, expected versus actual, and final bead states. A mock-only planner, hidden auto-mutation, feature deletion, or unlogged exception cannot close this bead.
design:
REVIEW AMENDMENT — classification authority is a canonical versioned workstream/gate registry keyed by stable bead ids. Labels, titles, keyword similarity, PageRank, and bv recommendations are advisory only and cannot assign WIP class, rewrite dependencies, or start/hold work. Unknown or unclassified beads consume no free implementation capacity and cannot move to in_progress until reviewed.

The policy distinguishes passed, failed, dependency_blocked, not_yet_runnable, stale, Inconclusive, and InternalFault. It derives dependency blocking from the authoritative br graph rather than the bead status field and routes to the nearest ready transitive blockers of the earliest non-passed convergence gate. Read graph, evidence, config, exception, and adoption snapshots under one consistency protocol; pre/post hash drift yields Inconclusive and no admission recommendation. Missing bv metrics alone does not: bv is optional advisory input.

Do not overclaim race-free atomic admission unless the tracker exposes an atomic policy claim. Concurrent agents may transiently oversubscribe after identical reports; the honest contract is deterministic detection, an ordered newcomer hold rule, and no further admission until the cap drains. A one-time adoption snapshot classifies already-active work and issues a bounded drain plan—no silent perpetual grandfathering and no destructive cancellation.

Priority is explicit: bounded incident/security exception; evidence-integrity repair; nearest ready blockers of the earliest gate; reserved independent verification; fairness within the same eligible class. Starvation never ages additive work above a frozen earlier gate. Exceptions have exact scope/owner/expiry/review and cannot erase features or evidence obligations.

D7 claims remain separate: deterministic conformance to the frozen policy is an invariant; WIP-cap compliance at a specific snapshot is observed; the assertion that the policy improves convergence is HYPOTHESIS/statistical and never proof. Archive the complete normalized graph/evidence/config/exception/adoption inputs, not only their hashes, with each recommendation.
acceptance_criteria: A frozen id-keyed registry and reviewed policy define numeric caps/reservations, state vocabulary, graph-derived blocking, priority, consistency protocol, anti-evasion, adoption/drain, exception, fairness, freeze/resume, and honest claim classes. Robot output is deterministic, read-only, and stable under JSONL reordering; bv remains advisory. Named governance_policy_model, earliest_gate_routing, snapshot_consistency, concurrent_admission_detection, adoption_drain_model, exception_state_machine, and governance_no_mock_e2e suites cover empty/many-track graphs, ties, dependency blocking, all outcome states, graph/evidence drift, bv timeout/absence, simultaneous claims, unknown beads, initial over-cap state, incidents, verification reservation, starvation, reopened work, and exception expiry/renewal. Mutants for status-only blocking, keyword/PageRank authority, auto-mutation, stale-snapshot admission, missing-bv Inconclusive, race-free overclaim, silent grandfathering, unknown-bead capacity, feature deletion, evergreen exception, and hypothesis-as-proof are killed. The real temporary-project E2E consumes real br and robot bv, preserves production state, exercises admission/over-cap/freeze/exception/expiry/close/unblock/recovery, and archives normalized inputs plus strict semantic decisions/final states. No hidden mutation, permissive failure, destructive drain, or feature loss satisfies closure.
notes: MANDATORY VERIFICATION DEFINITION OF DONE (inherits franken_lean-rur; additive to this governance bead): unit/property/mutation coverage must exercise policy classification, ordering, WIP arithmetic, failure states, exceptions, fairness, determinism, and non-mutation. Real no-mock temporary-project E2E coverage must use br changes and bv robot diagnostics for normal, over-cap, regression, incident, expiry, and recovery scenarios without touching production statuses. Emit concise human and bounded schema-versioned NDJSON with run/scenario/step, policy/schema/tool versions, exact redacted argv/cwd, graph/evidence/config hashes, active/selected/held beads and reason codes, budgets/exceptions/starvation, expected versus actual, monotonic timing/resources, exit status, stderr/stdout artifacts, and final states. Archive configs, fixtures, logs, and reproduction commands; a skip, mock-only result, hidden mutation, or lost feature cannot satisfy the claim.

comments.text:
CLASSIFICATION. cc_2, 2026-07-25. All 265 rows parsed from the retained log and clustered by MECHANISM rather than by reject family. Headline: 228 genuine kernel incompleteness, 24 measurement artifacts, 13 unclassified. K is left nonzero deliberately.

FIRST, TWO REFRAMINGS THAT CHANGE WHAT THE NUMBER MEANS.

The 265 rows are not 265 findings. The 228 BlockMismatch rows come from exactly 76 distinct recursors, three rows each - the inductive, its .mk and its .rec - because one recursor regeneration failure rejects the whole block. So 228 rows are 76 root causes, and as shown below those 76 share ONE root cause.

The three families split into two disjoint populations. All 24 UnknownConstant and all 13 DefinitionTypeMismatch rows are _private declarations of the equation-compiler family (eq_N, eq_def, match_N, _proof_N): 37 of 37, 100%. Zero of the 228 BlockMismatch rows are private or equation-family. The families are not three symptoms of one problem.

N = 228 ROWS / 76 ROOT CAUSES: GENUINE KERNEL INCOMPLETENESS, ROOT CAUSE NAMED.

Evidence chain. The reject message said only that recursor level parameters "diverge from regeneration" without saying how - a name difference, an order difference and a missing motive universe all read identically, which is why this was hard to classify. I extended the message to print both lists and re-ran the live lane. It reports, for every affected block: generated [u,v,w], decoded [u_1,u,v,w]. We emit NO motive universe; the pin prepends one.

Cross-checked against the pin directly: for all 76 of the affected inductives, the Reference's recursor carries exactly one MORE level parameter than the inductive itself - 76/76, zero exceptions. So the pin permits large elimination for all 76 and we permit it for none.

Root cause, confirmed by execution rather than reading: fln-kernel/src/admit.rs, elim_only_at_universe_zero. It classifies a constructor field as "a Prop" by testing the field's inferred sort with Level::is_zero(), which is purely structural - matches!(self.node(), Node::Zero). A field whose sort is Sort (imax u 0) is semantically Prop but is not structurally Node::Zero. I verified against fln-core: imax(u,0).is_zero() = false, imax(u,0).normalize().is_zero() = true, and the nested imax(u+1, imax(u,0)) behaves the same way under normalize_fixpoint. So such a field is pushed to to_check, is not found among the result's arguments, and the inductive is wrongly restricted to Prop-only elimination. init_elim_level then sets elim_level to Level::zero() rather than a fresh u-family parameter, rec_lparams returns the inductive's own lparams unchanged, and the regenerated recursor's level-parameter list is one shorter than the decoded one. Every declaration in the block is then rejected.

Named fix, NOT applied in this pass: normalise the inferred field sort before the zero test. This is genuine incompleteness in our kernel in the D23 restrictive direction - we refuse large elimination the Reference permits - so it is safe, non-release-blocking on its own, and CARVE-OUT-ELIGIBLE in principle. I do not think a carve-out is the right disposition: it is a one-line-shaped defect with a known fix, and carving out 76 subsingleton types would permanently weaken elimination for a large part of the Prop hierarchy. It should be repaired, not excused.

M = 24 ROWS: MEASUREMENT ARTIFACT, NOT A CARVE-OUT.

Every one of the 24 UnknownConstant rows is a _private equation lemma whose missing dependency is also a _private auxiliary - 21 distinct constants, all of them match_N, _proof_N or .loop auxiliaries generated by the equation compiler. Two decisive checks. First, ZERO of the 24 name a constant we rejected earlier, so this is not a cascade from the 228. Second, each missing constant appears in the entire retained log exactly ONCE, and that occurrence is the unknown-constant error itself - our decode never produced them at all. Several are referenced across module boundaries, e.g. Init.Meta.Defs referencing _private.Init.Prelude.0.Lean.Name.beq.match_1, and Init.Prelude was decoded first with 2,204 declarations.

The Reference had these constants; our decode never handed them to the checker. That is the user's second category exactly - a decode path that never supplied what the kernel needed - and per D23 it is NOT a carve-out, because there is no kernel judgement to carve out. It is a bug in the measurement, and it means these 24 rows say nothing whatever about our kernel's completeness. They should be removed from the divergence count once decode covers the equation-compiler auxiliary family, and until then the honest reading of the corpus result is 241 comparable divergences, not 265.

K = 13 ROWS: UNCLASSIFIED, DELIBERATELY.

All 13 DefinitionTypeMismatch rows are _private equation lemmas, and their messages show the body's type beginning with a universe binder - body has (Sort<u> -> ..., (Sort<u_1+1> -> ..., (Sort<w+1> -> ... - against a declared type that does not. THE 13 UNCLASSIFIED, TAKEN EXHAUSTIVELY. cc_2, 2026-07-25. Result: 8 attributable to the decode gap, 5 remaining as the only candidates for genuine kernel incompleteness in the entire corpus run. K goes 13 -> 5, and the 5 are named.

WHAT THEY ALL ARE. All 13 are equation lemmas f.eq_N, and in every one the body's inferred type carries `f args` on BOTH sides of the Eq while the declared type carries the reduced right-hand side. That is the shape of an rfl-style proof: the body proves `f args = f args` and the declared type says `f args = rhs`, so admission requires defeq to delta-unfold f. The check that rejects them is def_eq_public, full defeq rather than a structural comparison, so these are genuine reduction failures rather than a too-strict equality test. 13 rows over 9 distinct definitions.

8 ROWS / 4 DEFINITIONS: SAME ROOT CAUSE AS THE 24, NOW MOVED TO THE ARTIFACT BUCKET. Four of the nine definitions appear in BOTH families - Lean.Name.beq, List.toArrayAux, Std.DHashMap.Internal.AssocList.contains, Std.Iterators.Types.Attach.Monadic.modifyStep - and for three of them I can name the exact missing auxiliary that blocks the unfolding:
  Lean.Name.beq        <- MISSING _private.Init.Prelude.0.Lean.Name.beq.match_1
  List.toArrayAux      <- MISSING _private.Init.Data.List.ToArrayImpl.0.List.toArrayAux.match_1
  modifyStep           <- MISSING ._proof_1 and ._proof_3
The mechanism is one root cause with two symptoms: when the un-decoded auxiliary appears directly in a declaration's own type or body we report UnknownConstant; when it appears only on the unfolding path defeq needs, we report DefinitionTypeMismatch. Lean.Name.beq shows both at once - eq_4 and eq_def failed as UnknownConstant while eq_1, eq_2 and eq_3 failed as DefinitionTypeMismatch. These 8 rows say nothing about kernel completeness and belong with franken_lean-timy.

5 ROWS / 5 DEFINITIONS: THE ONLY REMAINING CANDIDATES FOR GENUINE INCOMPLETENESS. Lean.Arrow, Option.choice, WellFounded.fixFC, Array.insertIdxIfInBounds, Std.PRange.UpwardEnumerable.least - one row each. I probed the pin for all five: NONE of their definition bodies uses a match_, a _proof_ or a WellFounded auxiliary. Their unfolding is pure delta and needs no auxiliary constant at all, so the decode gap cannot explain them. Lean.Arrow is the sharpest of the five and the best place to start: Lean.Arrow a b is definitionally (a -> b), so `Lean.Arrow a b = (a -> b)` should close in a single delta step, and our defeq does not close it.

I AM NOT CALLING THESE 5 GENUINE YET, AND HERE IS THE EXACT TEST THAT WOULD SETTLE IT. Ruling out the auxiliary gap is not the same as ruling out decode. A definition decoded WITHOUT its value, or with a reducibility hint that suppresses delta, would produce this symptom with no missing constant anywhere. The discriminating check is to confirm that our decoded environment carries these five definitions with their values and with delta permitted. If it does, the 5 are genuine kernel incompleteness in defeq and are the most important finding in the subsystem; if it does not, the corpus-scale kernel differential is CLEAN and every one of the original 265 was either a repaired elimination-rule defect or a measurement gap. Those are very different conclusions and I am not guessing between them.

THE 5, NARROWED SHARPLY — AND MY EARLIER REASONING WAS PARTLY WRONG. cc_2, 2026-07-25. Still uncalled, deliberately, but the settling test is now one cheap check rather than an open question.

WHAT I RULED OUT THIS PASS, all three by reading the code or probing the pin rather than guessing.

1. THE PIN PERMITS UNFOLDING ALL FIVE. Probed Lean.Arrow, Option.choice, WellFounded.fixFC, Array.insertIdxIfInBounds and Std.PRange.UpwardEnumerable.least in the pin's environment: every one is an ordinary defnInfo with ReducibilityHints::Regular - regular(1), (3), (5), (11), (3) respectively. None is opaque, none is an axiom, all carry values. So there is no upstream reason they should not unfold.

2. OUR UNFOLDER IS NOT GATED. tc::unfold_definition finds the Defn, checks only that safety is Safe, takes the value and instantiates level parameters. There is no hints gate, no reducibility filter, nothing that would refuse a Regular definition.

3. OUR LAZY-DELTA DOES NOT GET STUCK ON A MISMATCHED HEAD. I suspected the failure was comparing `f args` against a term with no constant head - a Pi, in Lean.Arrow's case - and that our delta only unfolds when BOTH sides have a height. It does not: the (Some(_), None) and (None, Some(_)) arms each unfold the side that has one. That hypothesis is dead.

THE CORRECTION, WHICH MATTERS MORE THAN ANY OF THE ABOVE. I previously argued the decode gap could not explain these five because none of their bodies uses a match_, _proof_ or WellFounded auxiliary. That argument rules out ONE mechanism - a missing auxiliary INSIDE the definition's body - and I treated it as ruling out decode entirely. It does not. It says nothing about whether the definition ITSELF is present in our environment.

And here is the part I got wrong. I reasoned that Lean.Arrow must be in our environment because the reject message prints `Lean.Arrow.{u,v} #1 #0` on both sides. That does not follow: rendering an expression does not consult the environment. A Const node prints its own name whether or not the environment can resolve it.

Worse, the symptom is consistent with absence. If the constant is missing, env.find returns None, unfold_definition returns Ok(None), lazy delta returns Stuck, defeq answers false, and the kernel reports DefinitionTypeMismatch - NOT UnknownConstant, because UnknownConstant is raised by a different check over the declaration's own references. So a definition missing from our environment produces exactly the message these five produce.

THE SETTLING TEST, NOW ONE CHECK. For each of the five, determine whether the definition is present as a ConstantInfo::Defn WITH ITS VALUE in the environment at the moment its equation lemma is checked. If absent, all five join the decode bucket and the corpus differential is clean at the compared scope. If present with a value, the five are genuine defeq incompleteness and are the most important finding in the subsystem. The check needs the replay to report the resolved environment for a failing row, or a targeted harness that decodes the module and looks the name up - neither of which I have context left to build properly.

I AM NOT CALLING THEM. The probability has moved substantially toward artifact - three independent mechanisms eliminated, and the one surviving hypothesis is the same decode gap that already explains 32 other rows - but "the evidence now points the other way" is not a classification, and I have twice this session revised a conclusion I reached by narrowing rather than by testing. They stay uncalled until the lookup says otherwise.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT CHANGE. Zero unsoundly-permissive and zero carve-outs still hold. The compared-scope figure remains 5 unclassified over 15,722 compared, which is 9.9% of 158,608 decoded, with 1,425 outside the oracle's reach and kxbj's 65 inconclusive behind a depth bound - all stated separately, none folded into the number.

Every step of that chain is code I read this session, and it terminates precisely at the message these five rows carry. No narrowing, no inference from absence - the lookup answers it.

A NEW DEFECT FALLS OUT OF THIS, AND IT IS BIGGER THAN THE FIVE ROWS. A definition decoded as an axiom is not merely unfoldable-no-more. An axiom has no body, so the kernel ADMITS IT WITHOUT CHECKING ONE. Wherever this happens, "we accepted X" means "we accepted X's type as a postulate", not "we verified X's definition". That does not make the differential unsound in the D23 direction we care about - it cannot cause us to accept what the Reference rejects on a body we never saw, because the Reference checked the real definition - but it does mean some fraction of our 15,722 agreements are weaker than they read. I do not know that fraction. It should be measured before the compared-scope figure is quoted as verification rather than as agreement.

I am filing that as its own concern on franken_lean-timy rather than reopening this bead: the mechanism is the same crate and the same slice of work, but it is a different defect from the missing-auxiliary family and it deserves its own line.

WHAT I DID NOT DO. I did not confirm WHY fln-olean emits these as axioms - whether the value is elided in the olean for a class of definitions, or dropped in our decode path. That is the fix, and it belongs to fln-olean's owner. The settling test only had to answer artifact-or-genuine, and it did.

METHOD. The 15,722 compared declarations live in exactly 210 modules (192 fully compared, 18 partial), which decode to 15,881 constants. I decoded those 210 oleans with our own fln-olean DeclDecoder and counted ConstantInfo kinds. The counts below are over 15,881 rather than 15,722 - a 159-declaration overhang, about 1%, because 18 modules were only partly compared. Every figure is therefore accurate to within 159 and I am not rounding it away.

THE TWO COUNTS, as asked, not a percentage:

  COMPARED WITH A BODY OR STRUCTURE THE KERNEL ACTUALLY CHECKED   ~8,874
      Defn   6,604   (value present, body typechecked)
      Thm      788   (proof checked)
      other  1,482   (inductives, constructors, recursors, quotients - each
                      admitted under its own K1 rules rather than postulated)

  COMPARED AS AXIOMS, WHERE BOTH SIDES ONLY AGREED ON A POSTULATED TYPE  ~7,007

THESE ARE NOT REAL AXIOMS. That is the whole discriminator and it is unambiguous. The 7,007 carry 6,998 DISTINCT NAMES. Lean's genuine axiom set is about four constants - propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound, sorryAx. What is actually in the set: Acc.brecOn, Acc.inv, Acc.recC, Acc.recC._unary, Acc.rec_eq_recC, Acc.wfRel._proof_1, Add.add_eq_hAdd. Those are definitions and theorems. Our decoder is producing them with their types intact and their values stripped, exactly as it did for d17i's five.

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE CLAIM. Roughly 44 of every 100 declarations in the compared set were compared as postulates. For those, "we agreed with leanchecker" means both sides accepted a TYPE that neither of us derived from a body - our side because it had no body to check, the Reference because it checked the real definition and we then compared against a stripped copy. That is agreement, not verification, and only the first survives being called a differential result.

THE HONEST HEADLINE, REPLACING THE ONE NOW IN COMMIT MESSAGES AND BEAD COMMENTS:

  Zero unsoundly-permissive, zero carve-outs, 0 unclassified over 15,722
  compared - which is 9.9% of 158,608 decoded - and of that compared set
  roughly 8,874 were checked with a body or structure while roughly 7,007
  were compared as axioms whose bodies our decoder had stripped. 1,425 are
  outside the oracle's reach and kxbj's 65 are inconclusive on a depth bound,
  both stated separately.

So the strong form - "our kernel verifies what the Reference verifies" - holds for about 8,874 declarations, not 15,722. The weaker form - "our kernel and the Reference agree that this was asserted" - covers the rest. I would have quoted the total as verification if I had not measured this, and it is already sitting in commit messages where someone would have.

WHAT DOES NOT CHANGE. Zero unsoundly-permissive and zero carve-outs still hold, and the D23 direction is still safe: a stripped body cannot make us accept something the Reference rejected, because the Reference checked the real definition. The 228 elimination-rule repairs are real and still repaired. This narrows what the number MEANS; it does not reverse anything.

FRANKEN_LEAN-KXBJ. Diagnosis complete, fix not started, split by owner.
  - Does NOT reproduce today: the module is excluded upstream as import_context_not_faithfully_representable (65 declarations, subject_no_answer=65). It never reaches the checker, so the overflow is MASKED, not fixed. Closing on "cannot reproduce" would be wrong.
  - It is deep-but-finite, not runaway recursion. TypeChecker::step charges and checks depth before every descent in whnf_core/reduce_recursor/infer, and Expr::drop is already iterative. Both obvious hazards are ruled out.
  - Root cause: Budget::DEFAULT.depth = 4096 was never calibrated against the stack it runs on. kernel_replay checks inside scope.spawn workers; `rg stack_size` over crates/ and tools/ finds nothing, so they inherit Rust's 2 MiB default, not the main thread's 8 MiB.
  - A stack overflow ABORTS and cannot be caught, so the fix must be a depth ceiling provably below the stack floor, never a recovery.
  - Two halves, two owners: an explicit stack_size on the harness threads (cod_3's lane, cheap); and a kernel depth default justified against a documented minimum stack (fln-kernel, needs a measured worst-case frame — do not just pick a smaller round number, that relocates the uncalibrated bound rather than calibrating it).

K1 RUNAWAY RECURSOR REPAIR LANDED: 1461e4a8.

POSITIVE OBSERVABLE. The real pinned declaration ite_not in Init.PropLemmas previously consumed the entire default accounting budget and returned typed Steps exhaustion at 10,000,001 charged steps. On final source, selected_real_module_resource_probe accepts it in 1,968 steps at max depth 22, with a 52-module closure, 9,845 decoded declarations, and zero collisions. The adjacent dite_not control remains accepted at its prior 5,163 steps and max depth 24.

ROOT CAUSE AND FIX. A nested Finish frame in whnf_recursor_chain returned None when its major was stuck, restored frame.original, and failed to publish the identity WHNF. An outer Retry then reopened the same safe definition, rebuilt the same stuck recursor, and repeated until budget exhaustion. The fix records stuck -> stuck in both epoch-scoped WHNF caches before the outer retry. This is a termination/cache-completeness repair; it does not admit a declaration or change a rejection into acceptance by bypass.

REGRESSION AND NEGATIVE CONTROL. k1_judgments now constructs the pin-independent shape: a safe definition exposes a stuck inner E.rec that becomes the major of an outer E.rec. Repaired source returns ordinary NotDefEq under 512 steps. Removing only the two cache insertions makes that same test fail at observed 513 versus allowed 512 with Inconclusive(ResourceExhausted ExecutionSteps); restoring them returns green.

FINAL-SOURCE EVIDENCE. cargo test -p fln-kernel --no-fail-fast exited 0 with 197 executed tests, 0 failed, and 1 explicitly ignored calibration test; this includes the new regression, the three pinned-reference differential tests, and the 1/8/32 thread matrix. cargo fmt --check, cargo check --all-targets, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, checker charter citations, and the final real ite_not probe all exited 0. A diagnostic-only whole Init.PropLemmas run on the same production repair observed 414 of 414 declarations accepted, zero rejected, and zero inconclusive; that run preceded relocation of the regression test only, with production tc.rs unchanged.

NON-GREEN / NO-CLAIM. The repository-wide scripts/check.sh is not green in this shared main tree: evidence-self-test stops on the pre-existing ignored .cargo/config.toml ambient rustflags file, and structure-guard independently reports only FLN-STRUCT-016 for that file after the regression was moved out of crate source. I did not alter or delete the file because deletion lacks user authorization. UBS over the two changed files exited 1 on inherited file-wide test panic-macro heuristics; its embedded fmt, clippy, check, test-build, unsafe, advisory, and dependency scans were green. This commit closes the ite_not runaway mechanism only. It does not close d17i, widen the corpus denominator, or repair the fln-olean body/private-auxiliary gaps tracked by franken_lean-timy and fln-20n.

SOURCE VERIFICATION OF THE 228 REPAIR, AND THE 13 CLASSIFIED. cc_2, 2026-08-20.

Code-first rotation: no lane run, no check.sh, no gate lock. Everything below is read from source at
HEAD or from a cargo check, and I say which. Nothing here is a re-measurement.

1. THE 228 / REPAIR A IS LIVE AT HEAD AND MECHANICALLY DOES WHAT IT CLAIMS.

A landed repair can be refactored away by someone who never knew what it was for, so I verified the
construct rather than trusting 50f65ba4's commit message.

elim_only_at_universe_zero in crates/fln-kernel/src/admit.rs still computes is_prop as
level.normalize_fixpoint().is_zero() before deciding whether to push the field onto to_check. I then
traced the normalization end to end in crates/fln-core/src/level.rs rather than assuming it:
is_zero is purely structural (matches on Node::Zero); is_already_normalized_cheap is false for an
IMax node, so imax(u,0) actually enters the walk instead of being returned unchanged; its second
child is Zero so is_never_zero() is false, which routes it to mk_imax_aux; and mk_imax_aux's FIRST
branch returns u2 when u2.is_zero() -- imax _ 0 = 0. So normalize_fixpoint(imax(u,0)).is_zero() is
true, and the repair is not merely present but load-bearing.

It is also guarded, which the bead record does not say. crates/fln-kernel/tests/large_elimination_imax.rs
(landed 5d420354) is still in the tree, has grown to seven cases, and includes
imax_field_permits_large_elimination and recursive_imax_field_permits_large_elimination.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH: I did not re-run the lane. This says the repair is present, correct in
mechanism, and guarded. It does not say the corpus count is still zero.

2. THE 13 DEFINITIONTYPEMISMATCH ROWS: ZERO ARE K1.

I re-derived the chain at HEAD instead of taking it from the record, because the record's own author
revised this classification twice by narrowing before settling it by execution.

  - unfold_definition (crates/fln-kernel/src/tc.rs) binds Some(ConstantInfo::Defn(defn)) and returns
    Ok(None) for every other kind. Its only other refusal is safety != Safe. There is no
    reducibility gate and no hints filter, so a Regular definition with a value is never refused.
  - definition_height returns None for every non-Defn kind AND for an absent name.
  - lazy_delta's (None, None) arm returns Stuck immediately. The (Some, None) and (None, Some) arms
    each unfold the side that HAS a height, so the old "mismatched head gets stuck" hypothesis stays
    dead at HEAD -- I re-checked it rather than inheriting the refutation.
  - The KR-974 body check in crates/fln-kernel/src/lib.rs turns a false def_eq_public between the
    inferred body type and the declared type into RejectClass::DefinitionTypeMismatch.

An Axiom therefore yields (None, None), immediate Stuck, false defeq, DefinitionTypeMismatch -- the
exact class these 13 rows carried. Both mechanisms behind them (a missing private auxiliary on the
unfolding path for the 8, a stripped definition body for the 5) are decode. 0 of 13 are K1, so I
changed no kernel behaviour and wrote no kernel residual. That was the condition I was given and it
was not met.

3. WHAT I ADDED: e4e41aea, crates/fln-kernel/tests/definition_body_stripping.rs.

The classification above is the load-bearing fact of a P0 bead and no test asserted it -- nothing in
the suite failed if either end of that chain changed. Three pin-independent cases, shaped like the
sharpest of the five rows (Lean.Arrow, definitionally (a -> b), one delta step):

  definition present WITH its value    -> Accepted
  same definition stripped to an axiom -> Rejected DefinitionTypeMismatch
  same definition absent entirely      -> Rejected UnknownConstant

The first makes the second a finding rather than a limitation: the kernel admits this shape when
handed a body, so the rejection is attributable to the stripped value and nothing else. The third is
the anti-vacuity control -- if absence produced the same class, the second case would be satisfied
by any unresolvable name and the two decode symptoms this bead separated (24 UnknownConstant against
13 DefinitionTypeMismatch) would not be separable by class at all.

NOT EXECUTED. Per the rotation I ran cargo check -p fln-kernel --all-targets, clippy --all-targets
-D warnings, and cargo fmt -p fln-kernel --check; all three exit 0. The file is genuinely in the
check -- I planted a decoy that errored, then removed it, because a remote-intercepted check on an
untracked file is otherwise indistinguishable from one that never saw it. The three assertions
encode my source reading; if the reading is wrong the batch run will say so, and I would rather that
be visible than smoothed over.

4. THE DECODE SIDE IS STRUCTURALLY REPAIRED -- BY SOMEONE ELSE, AND I DID NOT RE-MEASURE IT.

37ee8d81 and 1391adcf load complete server/private companion chains, and kernel_replay's
decode_corpus_module now decodes the .olean.private part rather than the public file alone. The test
module_system_private_part_restores_bodies_and_private_auxiliaries binds BOTH mechanisms directly:
the private level carries _private.Init.Data.List.ToArrayImpl.0.List.toArrayAux.match_1, and
List.toArrayAux comes back as a Defn rather than a weakened axiom. That is one named constant from
this bead's own log.

5. ONE NAMED RESIDUAL RISK, RAISED NOT CLAIMED, AND NOT MINE TO EDIT.

decode_corpus_module returns ONLY the private part's constant array. Nothing asserts that array is a
SUPERSET of the public part's -- the existing assertion is private_infos.len() > public_infos.len(),
and a count is not a containment. If the private array were ever not a superset for some module, the
repair would trade the old omission for a new one and every decoded count would still have gone UP,
so the symptom that caught the first defect could not catch the second. Cheap to close: assert set
containment per module instead of a length inequality. That is fln-olean and the conformance lane --
cc_1's area on franken_lean-timy -- so I am naming it rather than reaching across.

Related and also unchecked by me: 2 of the 2,433 pin oleans have no .olean.private (LeanChecker.olean
and Leanc.olean). decode_corpus_module branches on is_module and read_corpus_module_part errors when
a companion is missing, so it fails closed rather than silently omitting; I did not confirm those two
are non-module artifacts.

6. THIS BEAD STAYS OPEN. Its acceptance is a lane re-run at zero restrictive-without-carve-out and I
ran no lane. I closed nothing and weakened no gate.

THE FIVE, SETTLED BY NAME. AND A CORRECTION TO HOW THIS BEAD DESCRIBES THE DEFECT. cc_2, 2026-08-20.

OC-010 rotation, code-first: no lst4 lane, no cargo test. This is a zero-build measurement over the
pinned oleans plus source reading. Artifacts retained:
  /data/tmp/fln-d17i-constantinfo-kind-probe.py
    SHA-256 5f66f96e121df9a3f23f2770649eec7389c30e93493ed0c46f36c91181e7e7fe
  /data/tmp/fln-d17i-kind-probe-20260820.log
    SHA-256 11e299ca629791ad249c7ae705e9c640b8a9f9d5c04f4dec8ec33b6f002dc34b

1. THE SETTLING TEST THIS BEAD NAMED ON 2026-07-25, RUN BY NAME.

Comment 1064 asked for exactly one check: are these five present as a Defn WITH a value at the
moment their equation lemma is checked. It was answered in aggregate (all five Axiom), never by name
after the companion wiring landed. Now it is, for the exported part against the private part of the
same pinned module chain:

  declaration                          module                                    exported  private
  Lean.Arrow                           Init/SimpLemmas                              Axiom     Defn
  Option.choice                        Init/Data/Option/Lemmas                      Axiom     Defn
  WellFounded.fixFC                    Init/WFComputable                            Axiom     Defn
  Array.insertIdxIfInBounds            Init/Data/Array/Basic                        Axiom     Defn
  Std.PRange.UpwardEnumerable.least    Init/Data/Range/Polymorphic/UpwardEnumerable Axiom     Defn

Five of five. The exported column reproduces this bead's own 2026-07-25 finding exactly, which is
what makes the private column a repair rather than a different measurement.

The other half, the auxiliaries behind the 24 UnknownConstant and the 8:
  _private.Init.Data.List.ToArrayImpl.0.List.toArrayAux.match_1   ABSENT -> Defn
  _private.Init.Prelude.0.Lean.Name.beq.match_1                   ABSENT -> Defn
  _private.Init.Prelude.0.Lean.Name.hash._proof_1                 ABSENT -> Thm
  _private.Init.Prelude.0.Lean.Syntax.getHeadInfo?.match_1        ABSENT -> Defn
  _private.Init.Prelude.0.Lean.Syntax.getTailPos?.loop.match_1    ABSENT -> Defn

And the row that started it: _private.Init.SimpLemmas.0.Lean.Arrow.eq_1 is a Thm present in BOTH
parts. So that row never failed because the LEMMA was missing -- it failed because Lean.Arrow, on
the unfolding path defeq needed, was an Axiom. That is the mechanism this bead inferred, now
observed on both ends at once.

2. A CORRECTION, AND IT CHANGES WHERE THE NEXT PERSON LOOKS.

Comment 1066 says "Our decoder is producing them with their types intact and their values stripped"
and comment 1064 says "the value is gone, the kind has changed". Read literally that names a
decoder defect -- something in decode_constant_info dropping a value -- and someone will go looking
for it.

There is no such defect. The EXPORTED .olean genuinely contains axiomInfo for these declarations.
Lean's module system writes non-exposed bodies to the .olean.private part; the exported part stores
the postulated type on purpose. Our decoder was FAITHFUL to the bytes it was given. The defect was
PART SELECTION -- reading the exported part alone -- which is what 37ee8d81 and 1391adcf fixed.

This does not change the classification (still 0 K1, still measurement artifact) and it does not
reduce the severity of what was measured. It relocates the cause from decode_constant_info, where
there is nothing to find, to which file the decoder was pointed at.

3. FOUR CONTROLS, BECAUSE A KIND PROBE THAT ALWAYS SAYS Defn WOULD PRINT THE SAME TABLE.

  C1 real axioms stay Axiom: Classical.choice and sorryAx read Axiom in BOTH parts; Nat reads
     Induct, Nat.succ reads Ctor. The probe discriminates kinds rather than asserting one.
  C2 cross-check against an assertion I did not write: kernel_replay's
     module_system_private_part_restores_bodies_and_private_auxiliaries pins the ToArrayImpl
     exported census at exactly 5. The probe independently reads 5 exported, 6 private, with the
     named auxiliary as the sixth and List.toArrayAux going Axiom -> Defn. Two different readers,
     same numbers.
  C3 the auxiliary table above.
  C4 containment, measured rather than assumed: over the six modules, exported 3,377 names against
     private 3,706, with ZERO names lost in either direction and 1,089 changing kind. Init.Prelude
     is 2,204 -> 2,314 with 0 lost and 246 kind-changed, which also reproduces this bead's 2,204.

C2 earned its place. My first run reported the ToArrayImpl auxiliary ABSENT from the private part,
which would have been a finding. It was my own probe rendering numeric Name components as a
placeholder, so no _private.<Module>.0.<name> could ever match. The private count of 6 against
exported 5 is what exposed it -- the constant was plainly there and my reader could not name it. A
probe with only the five-row table would have shipped that as a result.

4. WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT ESTABLISH.

DOES: every constant this bead ever named as missing or stripped is present in the pinned private
part with an ordinary ConstantInfo, and the exported/private containment holds with zero losses on
the six modules measured. Combined with the source chain in comment 2155, all 13
DefinitionTypeMismatch rows and all 24 UnknownConstant rows are accounted for as part selection,
with zero kernel residual.

DOES NOT: this is six modules, not 2,433. I did not run the lane and I am not restating the corpus
counts. C4's containment is a measured floor over a sample chosen because this bead names it, not a
corpus property -- cc_1 reports the same containment over all 600 Init modules from an independent
reader, which is corroboration, not proof at corpus scale. Nothing here is a G1 claim.

5. BEAD STAYS OPEN. Acceptance is a lane re-run at zero restrictive-without-carve-out. I ran no
lane, closed nothing, and weakened no gate. The kernel-side guard from comment 2155 (e4e41aea)
remains unexecuted pending the batch run.

THE THREE KERNEL CASES RAN AND PASSED. AND A VACUOUS GREEN I ALMOST SHIPPED. cc_2, 2026-08-20.

1. EXECUTED, NOT READ. The three cases from e4e41aea ran under
cargo test -p fln-kernel --test definition_body_stripping, 3 passed 0 failed:

  a_definition_with_its_value_admits_the_declaration_that_needs_one_delta_step   ok
  the_same_definition_stripped_to_an_axiom_is_rejected_as_definition_type_mismatch ok
  the_same_definition_absent_entirely_is_rejected_as_unknown_constant            ok

So the chain this bead's classification rests on is now an executed fact rather than a source
reading: a definition handed a body admits in one delta step; the same definition stripped to an
axiom is rejected DefinitionTypeMismatch; the same definition absent is rejected UnknownConstant.
The first case is what makes the second a finding rather than a kernel limitation, and the third is
what stops the second being satisfied by any unresolvable name. These are pin-independent and read
no .beads and no git, so the remote worker is a sound host for them.

2. THE PART I WOULD RATHER NOT HAVE FOUND THIS WAY. I also wrote a pin-dependent lane and ran
cargo test -p fln-conformance --test d17i_constantinfo_kinds. It reported:

    running 3 tests ... test result: ok. 3 passed; 0 failed

Every one of those three had SKIPPED. The run was offloaded to a worker with no ~/.elan, all three
took the pin-absent path, and libtest swallows a passing test's stderr, so the skip notice was
invisible. Only re-running with -- --nocapture showed three SKIP lines above three oks. I had the
output in hand and read it as a pass.

That is this repository's fln-rgha hazard exactly, and the registry exists because of it. Worth
stating plainly for whoever hits it next: for a pin-dependent lane, "N passed" is not evidence that
anything ran. Check --nocapture, or check the registry, before citing it.

3. COMMITTED: ee0b1d52, crates/fln-conformance/tests/d17i_constantinfo_kinds.rs. It pins by name
what comment 2166 measured with a throwaway reader:

  Lean.Arrow, Option.choice, WellFounded.fixFC, Array.insertIdxIfInBounds,
  Std.PRange.UpwardEnumerable.least        exported Axiom -> private Defn
  the five named auxiliaries                exported ABSENT -> private Defn/Thm
  _private.Init.SimpLemmas.0.Lean.Arrow.eq_1   Thm in BOTH parts

The exported expectations are load-bearing rather than decorative: they are what fails if both reads
are ever pointed at the same part, and they reproduce this bead's own 2026-07-25 observation. The
file also carries the correction from comment 2166 in its header, so the next reader does not go
hunting a value-stripping bug in decode_constant_info that does not exist.

VERIFIED FOR IT: cargo check -p fln-conformance --test d17i_constantinfo_kinds and
cargo fmt -p fln-conformance --check, both exit 0. NOT VERIFIED: its three cases have not executed
against a real pin — see item 2 for why the run I have does not count. Batch-test pending.

4. A GAP I AM FILING RATHER THAN CLOSING. That new lane uses a bare typed skip and is NOT a member
of PinRig::ALL, so fln-rgha's rig-execution registry does not govern it and any pin-absent
environment reports it green. This matches existing practice — kernel_replay's
module_system_private_part_restores_bodies_and_private_auxiliaries is pin-dependent and unregistered
too — so it is not a new shape, but the registry's own governed surface is derived from PinRig::ALL
rather than from a source scan, which means an unregistered pin-dependent lane is invisible to it
rather than caught by it. Registering mine needs a PinRig variant, an identity citation, and a CI
job that installs the pin for the new target; that is shared-governance surgery I am not doing
inside a code-first rotation, and doing it badly would redden every pane.

5. BEAD STAYS OPEN. Acceptance is a lane re-run at zero restrictive-without-carve-out. I ran no
lst4 lane, closed nothing, weakened no gate.

THE STRIPPED-AXIOM POPULATION, CLASSIFIED AND MEASURED. DECODE, RESOLVED, ZERO K1. cc_2, 2026-08-20.

WAVE 2, code-first: cargo check only, no cargo test, no lst4 lane. The census below is a zero-build
read of the pinned oleans, not a lane run. Commit aa6e4593. Kernel LOC changed: 0.

WHAT WAS STILL OPEN. Comment 1066 measured that roughly 7,007 of 15,881 compared declarations -
about 44 in 100 - were compared as axioms whose bodies our decoder had not supplied, and said the
honest reading for those was agreement on a postulated type rather than a verified body. That was
the largest unretired claim on this bead, larger than the 13 or the 5, and it was never remeasured
after the companion chain landed.

THE CENSUS, over all 600 Init modules that carry a complete three-part chain:

  exported part      32,150 Axiom
  private part           15 Axiom
  transitions        Axiom -> Thm 28,555    Axiom -> Defn 3,283    Axiom -> Opaque 297
  names lost              0
  names added        13,898
  decode failures         0   (600 of 600 modules decoded both ways)

32,135 of 32,150 postulates come back with a checked body or structure. The residue is 15.

THE 15, AND WHY EACH IS CORRECT. I pinned them by NAME rather than by count, because the question is
WHICH declarations the kernel still takes on trust and any fifteen survivors would satisfy a count.
Every one is declared axiom in the vendored pin source, checked at its declaration site:

  propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound, sorryAx     Lean's four genuine axioms
  lcAny lcCast lcErased lcProof lcUnreachable lcVoid unsafe axiom, compiler primitives
  isScalarObj, Quot.lcInv                            unsafe axiom, compiler primitives
  Lean.trustCompiler, Lean.ofReduceBool,             axiom, the native_decide trust surface

(+138, crates/fln-conformance/tests/d17i_constantinfo_kinds.rs only). Kernel LOC 0.

Residual chosen by derivation rather than by guess: I listed every stored field on every
ConstantInfo variant against what this file names, and all of them are covered. The
uncovered surface is inside Expr. Three ExprNode variants are walked past with { .. } at
all four of this file's walkers and asserted nowhere -- BVar's index, FVar, MVar -- which
is the gap the projection cell's own comment already disclosed and nobody had taken.

It is the right one to take next. A de Bruijn index is the one part of a decoded
expression whose corruption is invisible to every other cell in this file: an off-by-one
in binder nesting still yields a well-typed Expr, still resolves every constant
reference, still matches every stored arity, still round-trips through the census. It
surfaces only as an index that escapes its binders.

Measured over Init/Prelude at private level, across EVERY stored expression -- 2,314
types, 1,887 values, 160 recursor rule right-hand sides; 4,361 roots, 191k node/depth
pairs:

  zero loose indices: every BVar i sits under at least i + 1 binders
  zero FVar and zero MVar (elaboration-time nodes; no stored declaration may carry one)
  deepest binder nesting 53, largest index 47

Non-vacuity is a tightness argument, not a count. 10,454 occurrences sit exactly at
idx == depth - 1, so idx < depth cannot be narrowed to idx < depth - 1 without failing.
That is asserted, so the relation cannot quietly go weak.

THE DEDUP IS THE PART THAT COULD HAVE GONE WRONG SILENTLY. The four existing walkers key
their seen-set on allocation_identity() alone, and that is correct for them: a reference
set does not depend on where a subterm sits. It is WRONG for a depth-sensitive walk. A
shared subterm is reachable at more than one depth, and skipping its shallower occurrence
discards precisely the visit where an index would be loose -- so reusing the existing
idiom would have produced a clean run over a corrupted artifact, in the one direction
that hides the defect the cell exists to catch. seen is keyed on (identity, depth).

Same discipline applied to what gets pinned exactly. Depth and index maxima are exact
because they do not depend on how the decoder shares subterms -- a node at depth d is
visited iff reachable at depth d, whatever the sharing. The visited-pair count DOES
depend on sharing, so it is asserted as a floor only. Pinning it exactly would have been
a row that reddens on a decode change that is not a defect.

Two probe slips en route, both caught by the reader rather than by a plausible answer:
ci+8 is the Val, not the ConstantVal, so the first walk dereferenced a hints word as an

WAVE 107 (cc_2). Name component structure pinned at fa40b0a9 (+166,
crates/fln-conformance/tests/d17i_constantinfo_kinds.rs only). Kernel LOC 0.

A Name is a tree of str and num components. Every cell in this file has read them through
to_display_string, which renders a num component as bare digits and therefore cannot be
inverted. ALL the name matching in the file rests on that projection: _private. prefixes,
.splitter suffixes, .rec delegates, _impl correspondences, the whole auxiliary census.
Nothing checked the projection was faithful. It is the same shape as the import-row key
landed at 0acc4cd6 one wave ago -- a projection used as an identity -- and this time the
projection is one the file itself depends on everywhere.

THE ASSUMPTION HOLDS, AND THE REASON IS MEASURED RATHER THAN STRUCTURAL. Across
Init.Prelude, Init.Meta.Defs and Init.Data.List.Basic there is no str component
consisting of digits, so no str component can collide with a num one, so display strings
are injective over each module's declarations. A single declaration named with a
digit-only string component would break that, and nothing in the olean format forbids
one. Both facts are asserted -- the injectivity itself, and the absence of the collision
material that explains it -- because asserting only the first would leave a green that
says nothing about why.

The rest is an EXACT BICONDITIONAL, which I want on the record after three consecutive
one-way results on this bead (2290, 2325, 2345):

  a name carries a num component IFF its first component is _private
  there is exactly one such component, its value is always 0, nothing overflows
  it sits at index 1 + <components in the owning module name> -- 3, 4, 5 for the three
    modules, and the row's field is compared against the DERIVED value rather than
    carried as an independent constant

So the private-name shape the earlier scope cell reads off a string is stored
structurally, and the num component's POSITION encodes the owning module's own component
count. Scoped populations 113 / 156 / 73, each asserted a proper subset.

is currently RED on the kernel_replay target: expect_err on a Result<OleanInventory, _>
whose Ok type has no Debug. Attribution, measured rather than assumed: kernel_replay.rs is

WAVE 109 (cc_2). Rule-list ORDER and MULTIPLICITY pinned at b5c4cd4f (+139,
crates/fln-conformance/tests/d17i_constantinfo_kinds.rs only). Kernel LOC 0.

I started to write this as a new law and the COMPILER stopped me: my constant collided
with NESTED_AUXILIARY_RECURSORS, already defined at line 1540. Reading that cell showed
the block-relations test ALREADY compares a recursor's rule constructors against its
block's constructors and finds them equal. It compares them as BTreeSets. So the honest
cell is not the correspondence -- it is the delta a set comparison cannot see, and the
commit claims only that. The set equality is not re-derived.

A BTreeSet discards exactly the two properties the kernel depends on. A second rule for
one constructor collapses into the same set. Any permutation produces the same set.

BOTH MATTER, AND ON THIS BEAD'S OWN FAILURE CLASS. tc.rs:3209 resolves a rule by SEARCHING
the list for the constructor's name rather than indexing it. A duplicate rule is therefore
not an error: the search takes the first and the second is unreachable, silently. A
MISSING rule does not fail to decode and does not fail to resolve either -- the recursor
simply never reduces, which is a restrictive divergence of exactly the kind d17i collects.

Measured over Init/Prelude at private level, 129 recursors:

  127 have rules equal to the concatenated ctors of their block IN ORDER
  ZERO have the right constructors in the WRONG order -- so the stronger sequence law
    holds everywhere the set law does, which is worth recording rather than assuming
  0 have two rules for one constructor
  the 2 departures are the nested auxiliaries the block cell already names

NEW FACT: num_minors is a property of the BLOCK, not of the recursor. It agrees with the
rule count for 126, and the three exceptions are exactly the Lean.Syntax nested family --
each stores num_minors == 7 and num_motives == 3, the totals for the whole family, while
their own rule lists partition those seven as 4 + 1 + 2. That is only visible where a
block holds more than one recursor, which in this module happens exactly once.

TWO SURFACES I RULED OUT BEFORE THIS ONE, so nobody re-chases them:

1. The Expr/Level/Name cached data words are NOT a residual. DeclDecoder sets
   cross_check: true by default (decl.rs:191) and compares the stored word against its own
   recomputation at decl.rs:384 (name hash), 530 (level data) and 827 (expr data). Every
   decode in this file already validates them; a cell asserting agreement would be vacuous
   because the decode errors first. What is NOT covered is that the check itself could go
   inert if the flag were flipped -- that is fln-olean's concern and needs a corrupted
   fixture, not a pin read.

2. A probe slip worth recording because it produced a WELL-FORMED WRONG ANSWER rather than
   a crash: InductiveVal's numParams and numIndices occupy POINTER slots holding boxed
   scalars, so ctors is slot 4 and all is slot 3 -- not 2 and 1. Reading slot 2 gave an
   empty constructor list for every inductive, which surfaced as "126 of 129 recursors
   mismatched" with a plausible-looking 3-vs-126 split. Had the split been less lopsided I
   might have written it up. The fix was to dump one InductiveVal's slots and read the
   layout instead of inferring it from field order -- the same correction as RecursorVal's
   rules at slot 6 two waves ago.

comparisons instead of looking for unread fields, and the extension cell is the remaining
one: it maps every block to its NAME and compares the two levels as name sets. entries is
the last unread field in the module header, and a duplicate block name would collapse
into the same set unnoticed.

READING IT PRODUCES A RELATION WORTH MORE THAN THE FIELD. The block exportedAxiomsExt is
written by CollectAxioms -- a different part of the pipeline from the one that fills
constNames -- and its entry count equals the module's EXPORTED declaration count exactly.
It STAYS at the exported figure when the module is read at PRIVATE level, where constNames
is larger:

  Init.Prelude            constNames 2204 / 2314   witness 2204 at both levels
  Init.Meta.Defs          constNames  379 /  530   witness  379
  Init.Data.List.Basic    constNames  791 /  805   witness  791
  Init.Data.Array.Lemmas  constNames 1018 / 1297   witness 1018

So the artifact carries an INDEPENDENT witness of the exported/private distinction this
whole bead turns on, in an array nothing here had read. If part selection were wrong again
-- the original d17i defect -- the constant array and this witness would disagree. That
makes it a cross-check rather than a census row.

The presence rule is an exact biconditional, measured over all 600 Init modules and
recorded as provenance rather than asserted: the block occurs IFF the module exports at
least one declaration. 517 carry it and every count matches, zero violations; 83 lack it
and ALL 83 have an empty exported constant array; none carries it with an empty one.
Init.Control (0 exported, 0 private, 4 blocks, no witness) is the zero-export row in the
cell, so both sides of the biconditional are exercised by what actually runs.

The rows are written so the equality DISCRIMINATES: for every module carrying the witness
the cell asserts the private array is strictly larger. Without that, "the witness equals
the exported count" would also be satisfied by a module where the two counts coincide, and
the interesting half -- that it does not follow the private count -- would go unchecked.

Three smaller facts, two of which the name-set comparison cannot see: no block name
repeats within a module; no stored block is empty; and no shared block's entry count
SHRINKS between the levels, which extends the "the private part adds and never removes"
result from block presence to block contents.

crates/fln-conformance/tests/d17i_constantinfo_kinds.rs only). Kernel LOC 0.

A module ships THREE parts and this file has read two. Every cell here hands
.olean.server to parse_with_dependencies as a byte buffer and then never examines it. On a
bead whose entire repair was part SELECTION, what the middle of the chain contains was an
open question nobody had asked.

Measured over Init/Prelude, Init/Meta/Defs and Init/Data/List/Basic, and the answer is
uniform:

  constNames at server equals the exported array as a SEQUENCE, not merely in length --
    2,204 / 379 / 791, the same names in the same order
  extraConstNames likewise, and the import array is identical at all three levels
  extension names NEST, exported subset server subset private, strictly at each step:
    56 < 60 < 62 for Init/Prelude, 40 < 44 < 50, 43 < 47 < 51
  what the server adds is the SAME FOUR blocks in every module, and all four are
    documentation extensions: declRangeExt, docStringExt, inheritDocStringExt,
    moduleDocExt

SO READING THE SERVER PART INSTEAD OF THE PRIVATE ONE WOULD HAVE RECOVERED ZERO of the
declarations this bead is about. The private part is the only one that adds any. That is
the fact the whole part-selection repair rests on, and it was assumed rather than checked
from the middle part's own bytes.

IT ALSO DECOMPOSES A FACT ALREADY RECORDED IN THIS FILE, which is the part worth flagging.
The extension cell lists six blocks as private-only and describes them as "the
documentation and compiler-cache extensions". That is true against the EXPORTED part, but
it attributes all six to the private level. Four of the six are contributed by the SERVER
part; only the two compiler-cache ones are genuinely private. The two statements are
consistent -- the parts nest, so everything the server adds is also absent from the
exported part -- but only the new one says which part supplies what. The cell asserts that
nothing the server supplies can be counted again as a private addition, so the
decomposition cannot silently re-merge.

Method note, since this is the second wave running on it: I picked this by continuing the
lossy-comparison sweep from 2354 and finding there were no lossy comparisons left, then
asking what INPUT the file accepts without reading. The server part was being passed to
every decode in the file and inspected by none of them. "What does the code take in and
never look at" turns out to be a second question of the same kind as "what does this
comparison discard", and it found a whole part rather than a field.

WAVE 116 (cc_2). Cross-level type preservation pinned at 1044cec8 (+111,
crates/fln-conformance/tests/d17i_constantinfo_kinds.rs only). Kernel LOC 0.

THIS IS THE SOUNDNESS CONTENT OF THE PART-SELECTION REPAIR, AND IT WAS NEVER ASSERTED.
The kind cell establishes that the private read does not rewrite kinds wholesale and that
no name is lost. Both are about the NAME set and the kind TAG. Neither says anything about
a declaration's TYPE -- and the type is the whole of what a declaration asserts. A part
selection that silently altered types would satisfy every cell in this file, and it would
be a SOUNDNESS defect rather than a restrictive one: the opposite direction from
everything else d17i collects, and the direction that actually matters. Every other cell
on this bead guards against rejecting too much. This one guards against accepting
something different.

Measured over Init.Prelude, Init.Meta.Defs and Init.Data.List.Basic -- 3,374 declarations
present in BOTH parts:

  ZERO have a different type_, compared structurally rather than by hash
  ZERO have different level_params
  671 change kind, and EVERY ONE of them is from Axiom. Not a single declaration
    changes between two kinds that both carry a value

So the exported part postulates and the private part supplies, and that is the only thing
that ever differs between the two readings of a module.

  Init.Prelude            2204 shared, 246 changed:  86 Defn / 148 Thm / 12 Opaque
  Init.Meta.Defs           379 shared, 197 changed: 165 Defn /  16 Thm / 16 Opaque
  Init.Data.List.Basic     791 shared, 228 changed:  20 Defn / 208 Thm /  0 Opaque

The proportions differ sharply per module, which is why the row carries all three numbers
rather than a total. The ZERO in the List.Basic row is asserted AS a zero, so a decode
that started producing opaques there fails rather than passing quietly.

Non-vacuity is the unchanged majority: 2,703 of the 3,374 shared declarations keep their
kind, and their types go through the same equality. "Zero retyped" is therefore not a
consequence of a small or empty comparison -- most of the population being compared never
changed at all, which is exactly the part a kind-focused cell would skip.

Method note, third wave on the same approach. "What does this comparison discard" was
exhausted at 2354; "what input does the file accept and never read" found the server part
at 2357; this one came from "what does the file DERIVE but never cross-check against an
independent reading". The file decodes each module twice, at two levels, in several cells
-- and never compares the two decodings field by field. The two readings were always
sitting next to each other.

0acc4cd6 line 5566 collects any edge whose name is not in `present` and asserts the

looking a name up in the set that init_modules produces -- and nothing checks that
projection is a KEY. init_modules strips the final extension and replaces / with a dot. A
file named Init/Foo.Bar.olean projects onto Init.Foo.Bar and collides with
Init/Foo/Bar.olean, because stripping the final extension leaves the interior dot in

  NO .olean basename contains a dot -- the only collision material there is, and nothing

    for every member: a premise several cells rest on and none of them states

names, because a duplicate would already have been lost by the time those names exist --
counting distinct names and finding 600 proves nothing on its own. Non-vacuity: the
deepest module has at least five components, so the separator replacement is exercised on

WAVE 142 (cc_2). Decode-helper agreement and determinism pinned at aebe775d (+69,
crates/fln-conformance/tests/d17i_constantinfo_kinds.rs only). Kernel LOC 0.

ABSENCE CONFIRMED, and the hole is in the file's own scaffolding rather than in the
artifact. Init/Prelude at private level is decoded through TWO different helpers.
decode_prelude_private opens the three parts and decodes. decode_at first parses the
exported part standalone to read its imports, then parses the chain and decodes. They are
separate code paths, 31 cells use the first and 12 the second, and nothing asserted they
produce the same thing. If they drifted, this file's claims would silently split into two
populations while every cell went on saying "Init/Prelude at private level".

Three identities, none previously stated:

  the two helpers agree element for element AND IN ORDER, so a cell can be moved between
    them without changing what it asserts
  decoding the same bytes twice through the same helper gives the same result. The
    decoder caches names, levels and expressions in HashMaps; a HashMap iterated anywhere
    on the output path leaks its order into the answer, which is a nondeterminism this
    project's doctrine rules out and which NO SINGLE DECODE CAN REVEAL
  the decoded count equals the constants field read from the header by module_view -- a
    different reader over the same bytes

Non-vacuity: 2,314 declarations spanning all EIGHT ConstantInfo kinds, so it is not
agreement over a short or uniform list. The element-wise comparison reports the first
disagreeing NAME rather than only failing, so a future drift is diagnosable from the
message instead of requiring a bisect.

HOW I GOT HERE, since the wave list of exclusions is now long. I swept the file's
hand-listed constant tables looking for another carve-out that could be DERIVED from a
stored property, the way is_module derived last wave's LeanChecker/Leanc list. The best
candidate was UNADJUDICATED_HEIGHT_ROWS, and I measured it: three of the four are
structure-instance definitions storing Regular(1) over much taller bodies
(Lean.Name.instBEq 1 over Lean.Name.beq 11; Lean.instHashableName 1 over Lean.Name.hash 7;
Lean.Macro.instInhabitedState 1 over its own .default 2), while the fourth,
Lean.Name.append, stores 12 over Lean.extractMacroScopes at 14. Three share a property and
the fourth does not, so no single derived rule replaces the list, and the discriminating
check that WOULD settle it still needs the pinned Lean binary. THE DISCLOSURE STANDS
UNCHANGED and I did not weaken it to manufacture a cell. Recording the measurement here so
the next person starts from the characterisation rather than from the four bare names.

crates/fln-conformance/tests/d17i_constantinfo_kinds.rs only). Kernel LOC 0.

ABSENCE CONFIRMED, and this is the assumption underneath every number in the file. Every
count here is stated against "the pin": 2,204 and 2,314 declarations, 600 modules, 3,153
import edges, 35,225 level nodes, 3,374 shared declarations. All of it rests on
reference_lib, which returns FLN_REFERENCE_LIB when set and checks ONLY that the path is a
DIRECTORY. Point that variable at a different toolchain and every cell goes on asserting
the pin's numbers against something else -- failing with count mismatches that read as
decode defects, or, for a toolchain whose numbers happened to line up, PASSING while
describing the wrong artifact. Nothing established which toolchain was actually opened.
Forty-odd cells, one unchecked premise.

The header answers it from the bytes rather than from the path:

  all 600 Init modules carry ONE header identity -- lean_version 4.32.0, githash
    8c9756b28d64dab099da31a4c09229a9e6a2ef35 -- and the whole 2,433-file library carries
    the same one
  the three parts of a chain share that identity and have THREE DISTINCT base addresses,
    which is exactly why the companion chain has to be pointer-linked across regions
    rather than read as one file

The constancy is asserted because region.rs CLAIMS it in a comment -- lean_version and
githash are "properties of the TOOLCHAIN, identical across every module" -- and nothing
tested it. Same shape as the is_module prose two waves ago: a stated property with no cell
behind it. The distinct base addresses are asserted because they are the mechanism this
bead's repair depends on: three parts, three regions, one pointer graph.

TWO SLIPS EN ROUTE, both caught rather than shipped, and the first is the dangerous kind.

I first read the header with guessed offsets and got lean_version = '' for all 600
modules. That is a well-formed WRONG answer that reads as a finding -- "the pin stores no
version string" -- and I nearly had it. The cause: read_str("lean_version", 33) passes a
LENGTH, not an offset. The real layout is magic(5) + version(1) + flags(1) +
lean_version(33) + githash(40) + base_addr(8) = 88, which the field sizes verify against
each other: 7+33 = 40 and 40+40 = 80. The githash read happened to be correct at 40 and
matched the pin sha I already knew, which is what made the empty version string look like
a fact about the artifact rather than about my reader.

Second: OleanView::header is a FIELD, not a method -- the pub fn header I found by grep
belongs to a different type. Compile error, fixed, no consequence.

comments.text:
WAVE 146 (cc_2). Name identity pinned at edffc1ad (+141,
crates/fln-conformance/tests/d17i_constantinfo_kinds.rs only). Kernel LOC 0.

THE NAMED CANDIDATE WAS REFUTED, AND I DID NOT COMMIT IT. The wave asked for the header
flags byte vs filename-inferred part role, conditional on flags actually distinguishing
the three parts. Measured across 600 modules x 3 parts, 1,800 files: every one carries
(version 2, flags 1). Flags do NOT distinguish the parts. A part's role is not
self-describing anywhere in the fixed header, so the FILENAME is the only thing that says
which part a file is -- which is itself worth knowing, but "flags is constant" is a census
and not a law, so there is no cell here. Recording the measurement so nobody re-runs it.

WHAT I COMMITTED INSTEAD is the general question under an existing single-example cell.
The scope cell proves, for ONE named declaration, that a _private prefix names the privacy
SCOPE rather than the storing module, and lists two modules that store it. One example
establishes that the exception exists. It says nothing about how common it is, and nothing
at all about the question underneath: does a name identify a declaration across the
library?

Measured over all 600 Init modules at private level, 65,273 distinct declared names:

  92 names are declared by MORE THAN ONE module -- up to SEVEN for InvImage.eq_1
    (multiplicity histogram 2:69, 3:13, 4:7, 5:1, 6:1, 7:1). The name is not a key for
    the pair (module, declaration)
  every one of the 92 is an equation-compiler auxiliary by tail -- eq_1 x36,
    congr_simp x24, eq_2 x9, eq_def x9, induct_unfolding x6, eq_3 x4 -- which is exactly
    the family this bead exists to recover
  16,189 declarations are _private-scoped; 16,155 carry a scope prefix equal to their
    declaring module and 34 do not. Those 34 are the POPULATION behind the scope cell's
    single example, which appears among them twice, once per storing module

THE LOAD-BEARING HALF IS THAT THE DUPLICATION IS BENIGN. The seven declarations of
InvImage.eq_1 agree on KIND and on TYPE. The environment the kernel builds is keyed by
name, so a name declared twice with different content would be either a conflict or a
silent shadowing -- and the codebase already has an OleanCheckError::ConflictingModuleDeclaration
variant for the first case. Measured, it is neither: same kind, same type, seven times.

Cost was the design constraint and is worth stating. The census comes from the HEADER name
arrays (600 header reads, same profile as the import-graph cell). The kind/type agreement
is checked by decoding only the SEVEN modules carrying the worst case. Decoding all 600
modules' declarations -- which is what my Python sweep did to establish the 92 agree
everywhere -- would cost more than every other cell in this file put together, so that
part is provenance rather than assertion.

One compile slip, no consequence: Expr is PartialEq but not Ord, so a BTreeSet cannot hold
it; the agreement check compares pairwise against the first element instead.

ABSENCE CONFIRMED, and the requested cell was genuinely open. edffc1ad checks kind and
type agreement for ONE of the 92 duplicated names -- the seven-module worst case -- and
leaves 91 unchecked. I had justified that scoping by saying a 600-module decode would cost
more than the rest of the file put together. THAT JUSTIFICATION WAS WRONG, and measuring
it is what unblocked this wave: only 90 modules declare a duplicated name, ~18,600
declarations, which is roughly what decoding Init/Prelude eight times costs -- and this
file already decodes Prelude thirty-one times. I had estimated the cost of the sweep I
happened to run in Python (all 600) rather than the cost of the check that was actually
needed (the 90 that matter). Worth remembering: a cost objection to a check should be
priced against the check, not against the exploration that found it.

Measured over all 223 declaration sites:

  every one of the 92 is a THEOREM. No definition is ever multiply declared
  kind, type and universe parameters agree in EVERY module, zero exceptions
  values do NOT always agree -- 11 of the 92 carry a DIFFERENT PROOF in different modules

THE TEMPTING STATEMENT IS "ALL 92 AGREE", AND IT IS FALSE. This is the fourth time on this
bead that the clean-sounding universal turned out to have a measured exception, after
Prop-vs-motive-universe (2290), Prop-vs-noConfusion (2325) and importAll-vs-isExported
(2345). Here the exception is in a different field from the one the previous cell sampled,
so sampling one name out of 92 could never have found it.

What makes the disagreement harmless is exactly that all 92 are theorems: a theorem's
value is a proof, two proofs of the same proposition are interchangeable under proof
irrelevance, and the kernel never unfolds one to decide a conversion it could not decide
without it. Had even ONE of the 11 been a Defn, a differing value would change
definitional unfolding and be a real conflict rather than a benign regeneration. So the
"all 92 are theorems" assertion is load-bearing rather than descriptive, and it is
asserted first for that reason.

The count 11 is asserted as a NON-ZERO, not tolerated. A decode that lost the difference
-- by returning a constant value, or by resolving the name once and reusing the result
across modules -- would report perfect agreement and sail through a cell that only looked
for disagreement in the fields that matter.

WAVE 150 (cc_2). Flag-respecting import closure pinned at 7912e5c7 (+119,
crates/fln-conformance/tests/d17i_constantinfo_kinds.rs only). Kernel LOC 0.

ABSENCE CONFIRMED BY READING THE HELPER, and what I found is that an existing GREEN cell
was proving its result against the wrong environment. closure_declared walks the transitive
imports and decodes EVERY member at the requested level. At Level::Private that reads every
closure member's private part -- and a real environment does not get one. An ordinary
import supplies a module's exported declarations; only `import all` supplies its private
ones. The helper CANNOT respect that distinction, because decode_at hands back imports as a
bare Vec<String> with the flags discarded before the helper ever sees them.

So "Init.Meta.Defs is reference-closed at private level" was true, and was proved against
an environment LARGER than Lean would build. Not a false claim -- an under-constrained one,
which is the harder kind to notice because it is green.

Measured, correcting the closure to: the module itself at private, its import_all targets
at private, every other transitive member at EXPORTED only.

  permissive closure 9,217 names -> flag-respecting closure 8,744, which is 473 fewer
  all 898 referenced constants still resolve, ZERO unresolved
  EXACTLY ONE resolves only because of the import_all private part, and it is
    _private.Init.Prelude.0.Lean.Name.beq.match_1

THAT LAST NUMBER IS THE WHOLE POINT AND IT IS THIS BEAD'S OWN OBSERVATION. The reference
d17i names as crossing an import edge is the UNIQUE reference in Init.Meta.Defs that the
import_all flag is required for; the other 897 resolve from exported parts alone. So
import_all is load-bearing for one name in 898, and a decoder that ignored the flag
entirely would look correct on 897 of them. That is exactly the ratio that lets a
part-selection defect hide.

Non-vacuity has two halves, both asserted. The flag-respecting closure must be STRICTLY
smaller than the permissive one, or the two are the same computation under another name.
And the one-name result is asserted BY NAME rather than as a count, so a different
reference becoming the load-bearing one fails here instead of passing as "still exactly
one".

Method note: this came from the same question as the server part two waves ago -- what does
the file take in and never look at. decode_at receives ModuleImport rows carrying three
flags and returns only the module names; every closure built on it is therefore
flag-blind by construction. Three cells use closure_declared.

MY CELL AT 90221754 ASSERTED A FALSE UNIVERSAL. It claimed every one of the aggregator's
43 edges is a plain re-export -- import_all false, is_exported true, is_meta false. The
third conjunct is false. Measured, all three flags this time:

  42 edges are (import_all 0, is_exported 1, is_meta 0)
   1 edge  is  (import_all 0, is_exported 1, is_meta 1), and it is Init.Try

CAUSE, AND IT IS THE SECOND FALSE UNIVERSAL IN THREE WAVES BY A DIFFERENT ROUTE. Last time
(2383) I read a truncated histogram as a complete decomposition. This time my measurement
printed a Counter over a TWO-element tuple -- (import_all, is_exported) -- which reported
{(0,1): 43} and looked exhaustive. is_meta was never in the tuple. I then asserted a
THREE-flag universal from a TWO-flag measurement, and the missing dimension is invisible in
the output because a Counter over a projection never mentions what it projected away. The
general form: a measurement's shape silently bounds what it can refute, and an assertion
wider than the measurement's shape is unfalsified rather than verified. Both instances
would have been caught by the same discipline -- read the assertion back against the
measurement field by field before committing.

edges here would accept them anywhere, and is_meta is precisely the flag that says a
dependency is compile-time only -- the one distinction worth not blurring in an aggregator
whose whole job is re-export.

AND THE EXCEPTION EXPLAINS THE OTHER ODDITY INSTEAD OF SITTING BESIDE IT. The 43 edges
carry only 42 distinct names; the repeated one is Init.Try, imported once plainly and once
as meta. My original cell reported those as two separate facts -- "42 distinct" and "all
plain" -- and the second was false precisely because of the first. The cell now asserts the
LINK: the meta edge's module must also appear as a plain edge. So the duplicate row and the
meta flag are pinned as one fact, and a future artifact that separated them fails.

aggregator, 43 edges over 42 distinct names, no census module importing it, transitive
reach of all 600.

  FIFTEEN axiom declarations carrying fifteen distinct names. No axiom is declared twice,
    which is worth asserting precisely because 92 other names are (2381)
  they live in exactly TWO modules: Init.Prelude with ten, Init.Core with five. The other
    598 postulate NOTHING
  eight unsafe, seven safe -- so is_unsafe is not constant over the set

  safe:   Classical.choice, Lean.ofReduceBool, Lean.ofReduceNat, Lean.trustCompiler,
          Quot.sound, propext, sorryAx
