declarations, and is the heaviest cell in the file -- comparable to the thirty-one

claim. Two waves ago I refused a similar cost and was right, because there the check
needed only the 90 modules that mattered; here the population IS the claim. The rule I am
using: pay for a corpus pass when the negative half of the statement is the point.

than I measured -- a truncated histogram (2383) and a Counter over a two-field projection
while the assertion named three fields (2390). For this cell I measured name, module AND
is_unsafe for all fifteen rows, and the assertion names exactly those three fields and

measurement field by field, and refuse any conjunct the measurement did not print.

WAVE 162 (cc_2). is_exported transitive gating pinned at 4117f8d3 (+125,
crates/fln-conformance/tests/d17i_constantinfo_kinds.rs only). Kernel LOC 0.

THIS RETIRES A DISCLOSURE I HAVE CARRIED FOR THREE WAVES (2389, 2394). The import_all
closure cell tightened the closure in one dimension and said so; it was still loose in a
second, and I said that twice without landing it because the intervening waves excluded
re-opening that surface. This wave did not, so it goes in. A disclosed defect that survives
three waves is on its way to becoming permanent -- nothing fails while it sits there, which
is exactly why it needed taking the moment the exclusion lifted.

is_exported on an edge M -> Y says whether a module importing M also receives Y. It
therefore does NOT restrict what M itself sees -- a module always has its own direct
imports -- but it DOES restrict what M inherits through them. Over half the corpus edges
carry it false, 1,612 of 3,153, and the previous closure followed every one.

Measured for Init.Meta.Defs, 898 referenced constants, three closures:

  everything at private          9,217 names   0 unresolved
  respecting import_all          8,744 names   0 unresolved   46 modules
  also respecting is_exported    8,628 names   0 unresolved   44 modules

Each step strictly shrinks and resolution survives both.

THE NEW CONCEPT, and it is worth naming: REACHABILITY IS NOT VISIBILITY. Init.Control.State
and Init.Data.Nat.Div.Basic are reachable from Init.Meta.Defs in the raw import graph -- the
graph the import-graph cell walks and calls closed and acyclic -- and are NOT visible to it,
because the only edges reaching them are not re-exported. Both are pinned by name. Any cell
that treats the import graph as a proxy for an environment is off by at least these two
modules and 116 names.

The direct/transitive asymmetry is the part that had to be got right, and it is easy to get
wrong in the tightening direction: the walk seeds UNCONDITIONALLY from the module's own
seven edges and applies the flag only to edges discovered later. Filtering the direct edges
too would drop Init.Data.Array.GetLit, Init.Data.Char.Basic, Init.MetaTypes and
Init.WFTactics -- modules Init.Meta.Defs plainly imports, three of whose edges carry
is_exported=0. Over-tightening would have produced a smaller closure that still resolved,
and would have looked like a better result.

Anti-vacuity is asserted in both dimensions: strictly fewer names than the permissive
closure, AND a non-empty reachable-but-not-visible set. A flag respected vacuously fails.

crates/fln-conformance/tests/d17i_constantinfo_kinds.rs only). Kernel LOC 0.

FIRST, THE WAVE'S OWN SUGGESTION IS ALREADY LANDED. The reachable-but-not-visible pair is
a test assertion at 4117f8d3: REACHABLE_BUT_NOT_VISIBLE is compared with assert_eq!, so
Init.Control.State and Init.Data.Nat.Div.Basic already fail the cell if either stops being
invisible. The 116-name delta is not pinned as a standalone count, but pinning it would be
a one-line addition to the is_exported cell, which this wave excludes. So I took the "one
new visibility/closure property" branch.

WHAT I FOUND. The import-row cell counts repeated names -- 102 modules carry one. A count
says a duplicate EXISTS; it does not say what the rows DIFFER in, and the difference is the
whole of what a dedup would destroy.

Measured over all 600 modules: 128 groups of a module importing the same module more than
once, 126 of size two and 2 of size three, spanning exactly SIX row-sets summing to 128:

  115  import X re-exported, plus import all X NOT re-exported
    5  plain, plus the same module as meta
    3  differing only in is_exported
    2  three rows: plain, non-re-exported, and import all
    2  genuinely identical rows, collapsing to one row-set
    1  plain, plus a non-re-exported meta

117 OF THE 128 GROUPS CARRY ROWS THAT DIFFER IN import_all. A decoder that deduplicates
imports by module name -- the natural thing to write, and precisely what decode_at already
does by returning bare names -- drops a private-part license in 117 groups unless it takes
the UNION of the flags. import all is what licenses reading a private part, so this is the
bead's own mechanism being discarded by a plausible optimisation. The dominant shape (115)
shows Lean emitting `import X` and `import all X` as two rows with complementary flags,
which is why the pair is never interchangeable.

THE DECOMPOSITION IS ASSERTED AS A DECOMPOSITION -- the six counts are summed and compared
against the group total. Both reworks on this bead came from a partial view read as a
complete one (a truncated histogram, a two-field projection), and a table that does not add
up to its own total is the shape both had. This is the first cell where that check is in
the code rather than in my head.

AND ONE CLAIM I DECLINED TO MAKE. I went looking at is_meta first, and found that
Init.Meta.Defs's meta edge is closure-redundant: removing it changes nothing, 8,628 names
over 44 modules either way. But the reason is degenerate -- Init.MetaTypes is ALSO imported
by a plain edge, so the module is reached regardless. "Meta imports contribute nothing to
the closure" does not follow, and the artifact cannot settle it, because the only meta edge
available is shadowed. Recorded in the cell's doc so nobody reads the redundancy as the
general law.

WAVE 166 (cc_2). Structure projections pinned at b890d1eb (+140,
crates/fln-conformance/tests/d17i_constantinfo_kinds.rs only). Kernel LOC 0.

ABSENCE CONFIRMED. The eliminator cell covers casesOn, recOn, noConfusion, below and
brecOn. FIELD PROJECTIONS are a different generator with a different rule and nothing in
this file read them -- a second generated family, disjoint from the first.

The rule is not a naming convention that has to be guessed. For a structure-shaped
inductive (one constructor, no indices), the projection for field i is named after the
CONSTRUCTOR'S OWN BINDER at position num_params + i. So the family is derived from three
stored fields this file already reads separately -- num_params, num_fields, and the
constructor's binder names -- and had never related.

Measured over Init/Prelude at private level, 103 structure-shaped inductives with at least
one field:

  95 carry a DEFINITION named <Inductive>.<binder> for every field
  8 do not, in two measured shapes: three are Prop-valued (And, ByteArray.IsValidUTF8,
    Nonempty) and carry ZERO projections; five are not Props (Char, Fin, Lean.Macro.State,
    String, Subtype) and are short by EXACTLY ONE

All eight are pinned by name with field and projection counts, so a ninth fails and so does
a change in how short any of the five is.

WHAT I DECLINED TO CLAIM, and it is the interesting part. Char, Fin, String and Subtype
each carry a PROOF as their last field, so "the missing projection is the proof field" is
the obvious explanation and is probably right. Deciding whether a field's type is a
proposition requires TYPE INFERENCE, which this file does not have and the artifact does
not store -- a Sort's level is stored, but the level of an arbitrary field type is not.
So the counts are measured and the mechanism is not asserted. Lean.Macro.State is the case
that would test it: three fields, two projections, and I do not know which one is missing
or why.

Two measurement slips, both caught before they reached an assertion. First I counted
"plausible projections" as any X.<single-component> name outside a hand-listed generated
set, which counted ByteArray.IsValidUTF8.intro -- a CONSTRUCTOR -- as a field projection
and reported 1 of 2 present instead of 0. Second, that same heuristic would have made the
Prop class look like "short by one" rather than "zero", collapsing the two shapes into one
false rule. The fix was to stop pattern-matching names and read the constructor's binder
list at the stored offsets, which is the same correction this file has needed repeatedly:
a name shape is not a stored relation.

suffix attached to a known inductive in Init/Prelude and looked for families no cell reads.
That surfaced ctorIdx -- 103 declarations, all definitions, the same order of magnitude as

    the same one-way shape as noConfusion (2325)
  the converse is FALSE: 14 non-Props lack it too, pinned by name

the part worth recording. "ctorIdx exists iff the inductive has >= 2 constructors and is

WAVE 172 (cc_2). The ctorElim family pinned at a5e2edc1 (+117,
crates/fln-conformance/tests/d17i_constantinfo_kinds.rs only). Kernel LOC 0.

Found by re-running last wave's suffix census and reading the TOP of the histogram, which
I had never seen -- the first run scrolled it off and I only looked at the tail. ctorElim
and ctorElimType sit at 12 each, directly under the families this file already pins
(casesOn 127, rec 127, recOn 125, noConfusionType 115, noConfusion 115, ctorIdx 103, mk 89,
then ctorElim/ctorElimType 12). Writing the census output to a FILE instead of piping it
through tail is what made the top visible; the same truncation habit produced the rework at
2383.

They are paired the way noConfusion and noConfusionType are: neither ever occurs without
the other, zero one-sided across 127 inductives.

THE PRESENCE RULE IS AN EXACT BICONDITIONAL, no counterexample over the module:

  X.ctorElim exists  IFF  X has at least two constructors AND X carries a ctorIdx

Both conjuncts are load-bearing and the artifact witnesses each. Seventeen inductives have
two or more constructors; only twelve carry a ctorIdx; exactly those twelve carry a
ctorElim. The five that do not -- Decidable, Lean.Name._impl, Nat.le, Nat.le.below, Or --
are pinned, because without them the rule is indistinguishable from "two or more
constructors" alone, which is measurably weaker.

I tested the biconditional before writing, not after. The first hypothesis I formed while
reading the table was "ctorElim iff >= 2 constructors", and the five witnesses are exactly
what refutes it. Last wave the analogous guess for ctorIdx failed with 93 counterexamples;
this time the guess was nearly right, which is the more dangerous case, and only the
explicit test separated them.

THIS IS THE FIRST FAMILY WHOSE PRESENCE COMPOSES out of things already pinned rather than
needing its own carve-out list. The ctorIdx cell (2411) records fourteen non-Prop
inductives with no ctorIdx and explicitly declines to explain them. Five of those fourteen
now do explanatory work: they are precisely why this family has twelve members and not
seventeen. A remainder I could not explain last wave turns out to be the mechanism this
wave -- worth remembering before deleting an unexplained remainder as noise.

Non-vacuity: both sides populated, and the twelve span constructor counts 2 to 13 rather
than one shape repeated.

WAVE 174 (cc_2). Auxiliary numbering pinned at 1f8df77a (+117,
crates/fln-conformance/tests/d17i_constantinfo_kinds.rs only). Kernel LOC 0.

THIS IS THE MOST ON-THREAD CELL IN A WHILE. match_N and _proof_N are the equation-compiler
auxiliaries this bead and franken_lean-timy exist to recover. Nothing here had read their
NUMBERING -- and the numbering is exactly what an enumerator relies on.

Measured over Init/Prelude at private level:

  _proof_N covers 25 base names and every one is contiguous from 1
  match_N covers 72 base names and THREE are not:
      List.hasDecEq       1, 3, 5
      String.decEq        1, 3
      instDecidableEqRaw  1, 3

THE CONSEQUENCE IS THE POINT. Code that recovers a declaration's match auxiliaries by
walking match_1, match_2, ... until one is absent STOPS AT THE FIRST GAP. It finds one of
three for List.hasDecEq and one of two for the other two, and reports success. That is a
decode gap which looks like a complete answer -- the same shape as the part-selection
defect this bead started from, where reading the exported part alone returned five
declarations and looked complete. The cell asserts the consequence directly rather than
just the gap: for each gapped base, a walk from 1 recovers strictly fewer auxiliaries than
exist.

THE TWO FAMILIES DIFFERING is what makes this worth having as a pair. Observing only
_proof_N would invite "auxiliary indices are contiguous" as a general rule, and that rule
is FALSE. Had I measured _proof_N first and stopped, I would have written exactly that
generalisation -- the same failure as the two reworks, avoided here only because I
enumerated both families in one pass.

How I found it: the decEq family was my intended subject this wave (9 members, paired 9/9
with instDecidableEq* instances, converse false with four named instances lacking a decEq).
While listing those instances I noticed instDecidableEqRaw carried match_1 and match_3 with
no match_2. The decEq cell would have been fine and thin; the gap was the better finding
and it was visible only because I printed the full instance list rather than a count.

NOT CLAIMED: why the three are gapped. All three are decidable-equality functions, which
looks like a rule and is three cases with a shared shape -- I cannot distinguish that from
coincidence, and the artifact does not record why an index is skipped.

Non-vacuity: the contiguous majority is asserted at 69, so "three are gapped" is not a
statement about a tiny population, and at least one family must have more than two members
or contiguity is trivially satisfied.

WAVE 176 (cc_2). Instance-name non-injectivity pinned at 7f7aeb31 (+126,
crates/fln-conformance/tests/d17i_constantinfo_kinds.rs only). Kernel LOC 0.

Lean names a derived instance after the type it is for -- instDecidableEqNat,
instDecidableEqBool. The name embeds the type's LAST component, not its full name, so the
mapping from inductive to instance name is a PROJECTION. This file has found projections
used as identities that turned out non-injective four times now (import rows, path->module
census, Name display, ctorIdx naming). This one is non-injective too, and it is Lean's own
convention rather than our code.

Measured over Init/Prelude's 127 inductives:

  126 distinct last components -- the projection collides EXACTLY once: Raw is the last
    component of both String.Pos.Raw and Substring.Raw
  13 instDecidableEq* instances; 12 resolve to exactly one inductive by last component,
    and instDecidableEqRaw resolves to TWO

So the instance's NAME does not determine its subject. Anything recovering "which type is
this an instance for" from the name gets a unique answer twelve times and an ambiguous one
on the thirteenth -- and would most plausibly take the first match, being right by luck or
wrong silently. A 12-of-13 success rate is exactly the ratio at which a defect survives
review.

THE ENDING IS WHAT MAKES THIS WORTH A CELL RATHER THAN A COMPLAINT. The artifact still
carries the answer: instDecidableEqRaw's stored TYPE references String.Pos.Raw and does not
reference Substring.Raw. The relation the name loses is recoverable from the declaration
itself, and the cell asserts that resolution. Every previous non-injectivity finding on
this bead ended with "key on the stored relation, not the name shape" as advice; this is
the first one where the correct key is DEMONSTRATED on the case that needs it.

How I got here: last wave I set the decEq family aside as "fine and thin" -- 9 members,
paired 9/9 with instances, converse false with four instances lacking a decEq -- and took
the match_N gap instead. Coming back to it this wave, the thin part was the pairing; the
sharp part was a name I had noticed and not chased, instDecidableEqRaw, whose base is not
a top-level inductive. Following the odd name rather than the tidy census is what produced
a law.

Non-vacuity: both colliding inductives are asserted present and distinct, and the twelve
unique resolutions show the ambiguity is specific rather than universal.

comments.text:
WAVE 178 (cc_2). Derived-equality shapes pinned at 298ae49e (+132,
crates/fln-conformance/tests/d17i_constantinfo_kinds.rs only). Kernel LOC 0.

This is the decEq cell I flagged as available at 2419 -- but not the cell I would have
written then. Two waves ago I had it as a NAME pairing: nine X.decEq, nine matching
instDecidableEq* names, four instances without one. That version would have passed and
would have proved nothing about the artifact, because a name match is not a relation. After
7f7aeb31 established that an instance name is not a key, the honest form was to derive the
pairing from the instance's stored VALUE.

Done that way it says considerably more:

  each of the nine X.decEq is referenced by exactly one instance, and it is the instance
    whose name embeds X's last component. Here the name-derived and reference-derived
    pairings AGREE nine times out of nine -- the opposite outcome to last wave, where the
    name resolved to two inductives and only the type settled it. Agreement is worth
    recording precisely because the previous cell found disagreement
  the remaining four reference NO X.decEq at all. Three delegate to another INSTANCE --
    Char to UInt32, Fin and Raw to Nat -- and instDecidableEqList delegates to no
    instance, using List.hasDecEq, a decidable-equality function that simply is not named
    decEq

LIST.HASDECEQ IS THE INTERESTING ONE and it links two cells. It is also one of the three
bases whose match_N auxiliaries are not contiguous (1f8df77a). So a tool enumerating
derived equality by the .decEq suffix misses it entirely, and a tool enumerating its match
auxiliaries by counting from 1 finds one of three. The same declaration defeats two
different name-shaped assumptions, independently. That is the strongest single argument on
this bead for keying on stored relations.

The delegating instances bottom out in generated ones -- UInt32 and Nat are both among the
nine -- so the two shapes compose rather than being disjoint worlds. Asserted, because a
delegation chain ending nowhere would be a different fact.

Method note: the value of holding a thin cell rather than shipping it. I set decEq aside at
2417 as "fine and thin", took the match_N gap instead, and came back to it twice. Each
return added something the earlier version could not have had -- the instance-name
non-injectivity at 7f7aeb31, then the reference-derived pairing here. A cell deferred is
not a cell lost, and the deferral is what let the later findings inform it.

comments.text:
WAVE 180 (cc_2). Private-only population shape pinned at dc6edd6f (+140,
crates/fln-conformance/tests/d17i_constantinfo_kinds.rs only). Kernel LOC 0.

ABSENCE CONFIRMED, and this is the missing half of a cell already here. The retyping cell
(1044cec8) covers declarations present in BOTH parts and shows the private read never
changes a type. It says nothing about the declarations the private part INTRODUCES -- 110
in Init/Prelude, 151 in Init.Meta.Defs -- which are precisely what this bead exists to
recover, and whose shape nothing had characterised. Shared declarations: covered. Added
declarations: not.

Two decompositions, each asserted to SUM to its population:

  by kind: every private-only declaration is value-carrying -- Defn, Thm or Opaque.
    Prelude 103/5/2, Meta.Defs 123/10/18. Not one is an Axiom, and not one is an Induct,
    Ctor or Rec
  by name: every one is either privacy-scoped or an indexed auxiliary (match_N, _proof_N,
    eq_N). Prelude 82/25/3/0, Meta.Defs 95/50/2/4. ZERO fall outside

THE KIND LAW IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS. Reading the private part can only give a declaration
a body it did not have, or add an auxiliary that has one. It cannot enlarge the type
universe and it cannot enlarge the trusted base. That is the same guarantee the postulate
cell (f01ba978) establishes globally, arrived at from the other direction and per module --
and the two together say the part-selection repair could not have changed what the library
means, only what it can compute.

ANTI-VACUITY IS THE PART I NEARLY GOT WRONG. "No Axiom is ever added" is worthless if the
module has no axioms to add. So the cell asserts that the EXPORTED part of each module does
declare axioms, inductives, constructors and recursors -- their absence from the added set
is then a property of what gets added, not of what the module contains. Both modules
qualify.

ALSO TRIED AND ABANDONED, recorded so nobody repeats it. I spent the first half of this
wave on the idea that a composite lemma name encodes its statement -- X.down_up should
reference X.down and X.up. Only THREE theorems in Init/Prelude have both name parts as
sibling definitions, and none references both: Lean's lemma names use notation words like
mod and lt, not the underlying constant names, so Nat.mod_lt references HMod.hMod rather
than Nat.mod. Refuted at a scale too small to be worth a cell in either direction. The
general lesson is the file's own recurring one from the opposite side: a name shape does
not encode a stored relation, and that holds for lemma statements too.

WAVE 180b (cc_2). Gapped match auxiliaries named at ee3f25c1 (+125,
crates/fln-conformance/tests/d17i_constantinfo_kinds.rs only). Kernel LOC 0.

ABSENCE CONFIRMED AGAINST MY OWN EARLIER CELL, and the delta is real. 1f8df77a derives
which bases are gapped and pins their index SETS. It does not name the stored declarations,
and -- the part that matters -- it never asserts the missing indices are ABSENT. A decoder
that INVENTED List.hasDecEq.match_2 would produce the contiguous set 1..5 and satisfy that
cell by ceasing to be a counterexample. Pinning "which families are gapped" does not pin
"these declarations do not exist".

Eleven declarations are now named, each present one confirmed as a decoded Defn in the
private companion so the names are read back from the artifact rather than spelled from a
pattern:

  List.hasDecEq       match_1, match_3, match_5   missing match_2, match_4
  String.decEq        match_1, match_3            missing match_2
  instDecidableEqRaw  match_1, match_3            missing match_2

THE ABSENCES HOLD AT BOTH LEVELS, and this is the fact that belongs on THIS bead
specifically. List.hasDecEq.match_2 is missing from the exported part AND from the private
companion. The obvious guess when a numbered auxiliary is absent is that it is one of the
bodies the private part restores -- which is exactly what d17i and timy recovered for other
auxiliaries, so it is the guess a reader of this bead is primed to make. It is WRONG here.
Reading the companion chain does not fill these gaps, because the indices were never
generated. Anyone chasing match_2 as a decode defect would be chasing a declaration Lean
never emitted.

The mutant is a simulation rather than a description: a walk asking for match_1, then
match_2, stopping at the first absence recovers exactly ONE auxiliary for each of the three
bases -- one of three for List.hasDecEq, one of two for the others. The number 1 is
asserted, not just "fewer than all".

Non-vacuity has a specific shape: one base must skip MORE than a single index, or the
mutant is only ever killed by an off-by-one, and List.hasDecEq missing both 2 and 4 is what
supplies that. The eleven names are also asserted to be every declaration the cell reasons
about, so the table cannot silently shrink.

WAVE 181 (cc_2). Gapped bases placed on the decidable-equality path by reference, at
04192a6a (+112, crates/fln-conformance/tests/d17i_constantinfo_kinds.rs only). Kernel LOC 0.

ABSENCE CONFIRMED, and the gap was between MY OWN PROSE AND MY OWN CODE. The
derived-equality cell (298ae49e) says in its doc that instDecidableEqList uses
List.hasDecEq. Its assertion says only that the instance delegates to no other INSTANCE --
a different and weaker claim. The reference the doc describes was never checked, and a
decoder that dropped it would have satisfied that cell completely. This is the same defect
class I have flagged twice in cells I did not write: a stated property with nothing behind
it. Worth recording that I produced one too, in a cell whose whole point was that the
stored relation beats the name.

The numbering cell (1f8df77a) observes that all three gapped bases are decidable-equality
functions and explicitly DECLINES to claim it, because a shared name shape is not a
relation. That refusal was right and it left the observation unusable. The reference graph
settles it without reading any name:

  List.hasDecEq       used by exactly ONE declaration, instDecidableEqList
  String.decEq        used by exactly ONE, instDecidableEqString
  instDecidableEqRaw  used by NONE, because it is itself the instance

Two implementations behind one instance each, and one instance. All three on the same path,
argued without a decEq substring anywhere in the reasoning.

"EXACTLY ONE" IS THE LOAD-BEARING PART. A decode that lost the reference gives zero users;
one that duplicated the declaration gives two. Both are caught, where "is used somewhere"
would catch neither. A declaration's own auxiliaries are excluded from its user set, since
the question is who USES it, not which of its generated pieces mention it.

NEAR MISS WORTH RECORDING, about concurrent formatting. I checked git status for the
package, saw only my file dirty, and ran cargo fmt -p fln-conformance. Between those two
steps cc_3 wrote kernel_replay.rs, which is in the same package -- so the fmt ran with
their file dirty, exactly the situation I have been avoiding for several waves by applying
rustfmt suggestions by hand. No harm done, and the evidence is specific rather than
hopeful: their diff is 69 insertions and ZERO DELETIONS, a pure addition of a doc block and
a test section. A reformat shows deletions. So nothing of theirs was altered.

The lesson is that checking status immediately before the write is NOT sufficient when
peers write concurrently -- the window is real and I lost that race without noticing. The
durable check is the deletion count on the peer's path afterwards, which is what I should
run every time rather than trusting the pre-check.

WAVE 183 (cc_2). Declaration reference-graph acyclicity pinned at 804c29d0 (+141,
crates/fln-conformance/tests/d17i_constantinfo_kinds.rs only). Kernel LOC 0.

ABSENCE CONFIRMED. The import-graph cell (c4f9a970) establishes acyclicity between MODULES.
Between DECLARATIONS nothing had asked, and it is the sharper question: a cycle in the
reference graph means no order exists in which the kernel could admit the declarations,
since each would need the other already present.

Measured over Init/Prelude at private level, 2,314 declarations, walking every stored
expression for the constants it names:

  the full graph HAS cycles -- 32 of them, 32 distinct participants
  every participant is a definition whose DefinitionSafety is NOT Safe, and all 32 share
    the same non-safe variant
  removing the non-safe definitions leaves 2,271 declarations and ZERO cycles, so an
    admission order exists for everything the kernel would accept

BEING NON-SAFE IS NECESSARY BUT NOT SUFFICIENT: 43 definitions are not Safe and only 32
are in a cycle. The other eleven are non-safe and perfectly well-founded. Asserted,
because "the cycles are the unsafe ones" invites the converse and the converse is false --
the fifth one-way implication on this bead.

A WELL-FORMED WRONG ANSWER I ALMOST BUILT THE CELL ON. My first probe read the safety
scalar at the wrong byte offset and reported ALL 1,720 definitions as unsafe. With that
reading the law "the safe subgraph is acyclic" would have been vacuous -- an empty safe
set is trivially acyclic -- and the cell would have passed while asserting nothing. The
tell was the distribution itself: a Prelude in which every definition is unsafe is not a
Prelude. Re-probed against known cases (Nat.add and List.append safe, Nat.sub._unsafe_rec
not) and found DefinitionSafety is byte 0 at the scalar base, giving 1,677 / 32 / 11.

The repair is not just the corrected offset. The cell now DERIVES the safety variant from
the decoded declarations instead of naming one, so a test that hardcoded which variant the
recursive implementations carry cannot pass while the decoder maps the byte differently.
That is the same defence the instance-name cell needed: do not let the assertion depend on
a mapping the measurement guessed.

REWORK (cc_2). Repaired at 1f9cca00 (+111 -47,
crates/fln-conformance/tests/d17i_constantinfo_kinds.rs only). Kernel LOC 0.

MY CELL ASSERTED 32 CYCLE PARTICIPANTS. The isolated run measured 41, and 41 is right.

CAUSE, and it is a new variant of an old mistake. My probe built each declaration's edges
from its type and, for value-carrying kinds, its value. The CELL uses
declaration_expressions, which for a RECURSOR also yields the iota rule right-hand sides.
Those edges are real and my probe did not have them. So the probe was under-covering and I
asserted the probe's number in a cell whose walk was strictly wider. Previous reworks came
from measuring less than I asserted (a truncated histogram, a two-field projection); this
one came from measuring a DIFFERENT GRAPH than the one the cell walks. The general form is
the same and the specific check is new: when a cell reuses a file helper, the probe must
reproduce that helper's inputs exactly, not a reasonable approximation of them.

Re-derived with the file's own expression set:

  41 participants, splitting exactly into 32 DEFINITIONS and 9 RECURSORS, and the two
    counts are asserted to account for all 41
  all 32 definitions are non-Safe and share one safety variant -- the recursive
    implementations that call themselves rather than going through a recursor
  the 9 recursors are EXACTLY the recursors whose block head carries is_rec: a
    biconditional over all 129 recursors, no counterexample. A recursor's iota rule for a
    recursive constructor names the recursor ITSELF, because that is how recursion is
    written down. Seven recursive inductives yield nine recursors because the nested
    Lean.Syntax block contributes three

SO THE ORIGINAL CLAIM WAS FALSE, not merely mis-counted. "Remove the non-safe definitions
and the graph is acyclic" leaves the nine recursors. Removing those as well leaves 2,262
declarations and zero cycles. Both numbers are now asserted and each exclusion is derived
from a stored field rather than from a name.

THE FAILURE IMPROVED THE CELL. The nine recursors were invisible to my probe, and they
carry the sharper of the two relations -- a biconditional against is_rec, where the
definitions only give a one-way non-safety implication. Had the cell passed at 32 it would
have recorded the weaker half and hidden the stronger one.

Kept unchanged: non-safe is necessary but not sufficient (43 non-safe definitions, 32 on a
cycle), and the safety variant is still derived from the decoded declarations rather than
written down.

WAVE 187 (cc_2). Recursor self-reference levels pinned at 6b341982 (+157,
crates/fln-conformance/tests/d17i_constantinfo_kinds.rs only). Kernel LOC 0.

ABSENCE CONFIRMED, and this refines the cell I repaired last wave rather than repeating it.
1f9cca00 establishes that exactly the recursors of recursive blocks sit on a cycle -- nine
of them. It does not distinguish HOW, and the two mechanisms are different:

  SEVEN reference themselves directly in an iota rule
  TWO do not, and reach a cycle only through their siblings: Lean.Syntax.rec and
    Lean.Syntax.rec_1. The nested block's three recursors form a directed THREE-CYCLE --
    rec to rec_1 to rec_2 and back -- with rec_2 also naming itself

That three-cycle is the only mutual recursion among recursors in the module and it is
INVISIBLE to a cell that counts cycle participants. Nine was right; nine as a single
population was not the whole shape.

THE LEVELS ARE THE SUBSTANTIVE HALF. Iota reduction replaces a recursor application by its
rule's right-hand side, so a self-reference inside that right-hand side IS the recursive
call. If it carried different universe arguments the reduct would be ill-typed at the
instantiation it came from. Measured: every self-reference carries exactly the recursor's
own level parameters, as Params, in the DECLARED ORDER -- no exception across every
occurrence, and Lean.ParserDescr.rec alone has seven of them.

The existing level-arity cell checks that a Const reference carries the right NUMBER of
levels. This checks WHICH ones, for the references where being wrong breaks REDUCTION
rather than resolution -- a decode that permuted the level arguments would satisfy the
arity cell completely and produce ill-typed reducts corpus-wide.

ORDER IS DISTINGUISHABLE FROM SET HERE, which is what makes "in order" worth asserting
rather than decorative: List.rec declares [u_1, u], NOT alphabetically sorted, so a check
comparing sets or sorted lists would pass on a permutation. Two of the seven declare no
parameters at all, so the claim is exercised at zero, one and two.

WAVE 187b (cc_2). num_motives formula pinned at d4ab921f (+105,
crates/fln-conformance/tests/d17i_constantinfo_kinds.rs only). Kernel LOC 0. The wave
instruction arrived twice; 6b341982 answered the first, this is the next residual.

ABSENCE CONFIRMED, AND IT WAS HIDING BEHIND A CARVE-OUT. The block-relations cell compares
a recursor's num_motives against the number of inductives in its block and CARVES OUT the
nested ones, because there the equality fails. The carve-out is correct and it conceals a
formula: a nested block generates one motive per nesting CONTAINER on top of the one per
inductive, so

  num_motives == all.len() + num_nested

holds for every one of the 129 recursors, nested included, with no exception. Only two
shapes occur: 126 at (1 inductive, 0 nested, 1 motive) and 3 at (1, 2, 3). The three are
the Lean.Syntax family -- the same three that form the recursor three-cycle at 6b341982 --
and that identity is asserted rather than remarked on.

This is the fourth time on this bead that a hand-written exception turned out to be a
derivable rule: is_module predicting the companion chain, ctorIdx explaining ctorElim's
count, the recursive-block predicate explaining which recursors are cyclic, and now
num_nested explaining the motive carve-out. The pattern is worth naming: WHEN A CELL CARVES
SOMETHING OUT BY NAME, THE CARVE-OUT IS USUALLY A FORMULA NOBODY WROTE DOWN.

WHAT THIS CELL CANNOT CHECK, and I asserted the limitation rather than leaving it in prose.
The formula has two terms and only ONE varies at the pin: every recursor here has
all.len() == 1, because Init/Prelude has no mutual inductive block and neither does the
corpus -- a standing disclosure on this bead since early on. So what is actually under test
is 1 + num_nested, and a two-term rule exercised on one term is unfalsified rather than
verified, which is precisely the failure mode behind two of my reworks. The cell therefore
REQUIRES every block size to be 1. The day a mutual inductive block appears that assertion
fails, and whoever sees it re-derives the formula instead of trusting it.

WAVE 190 (cc_2). Indexed inductives pinned at c988c79a (+121,
crates/fln-conformance/tests/d17i_constantinfo_kinds.rs only). Kernel LOC 0.

ABSENCE CONFIRMED: num_indices appears in this file only inside arity formulas, never as
the subject of a relation.

FOUR CELLS compute a telescope from num_params + num_motives + num_minors + num_indices +
1 and check it against a binder count. Each is a five-term formula and nothing said how
much of it the pin exercises. It exercises the index term FOUR TIMES:

  exactly 4 of 127 inductives have num_indices > 0 -- Eq and Nat.le with one, HEq and
    Nat.le.below with two
  all four are Prop-valued, and NO non-Prop inductive carries an index
  the converse fails: six Props carry none, and they are named

So num_indices is ZERO for 123 of 127, and every arity formula here is checked against a
term that vanishes almost everywhere. That is not a defect in those cells -- the formula is
right -- but it is the difference between a five-term identity VERIFIED and one verified at
four points, and it was nowhere recorded. Both widths occur, so a formula with the term
dropped would agree on 123 inductives and disagree on four, two by one and two by two.

This is the second wave running where the cell's real content is a COVERAGE statement about
existing cells rather than a new artifact law: last wave I asserted that num_motives'
block-size term never varies, this wave that the index term is nonzero four times. Both
came from the same question -- which parts of a multi-term formula does the pin actually
move? -- and it is a question worth asking of every formula in the file, because an
unexercised term is unfalsified rather than verified. That framing is the durable part.

HOW I GOT HERE, including the dead end. I started by trying to derive the 14 non-Props
without ctorIdx, since four previous carve-outs turned out to be formulas. Two sub-classes
ARE derivable -- zero constructors (Empty, PEmpty) and a result sort that is a bare
universe parameter, which cannot support a Nat-valued eliminator because the type may be
instantiated at Prop -- but that accounts for 4 of 14 and the remaining 10 are separated by
no stored field I can read. I stopped rather than forcing a rule that fits two thirds of a
population. The index observation fell out of the same feature table, which is the one
useful thing the dead end produced.

comments.text:
WAVE 192 (cc_2). Two commits, both crates/fln-conformance/tests/d17i_constantinfo_kinds.rs
only, kernel LOC 0.

  e00ddbcb (+21 -8)  REWORK of c988c79a -- compare the indexed tables by name
  29e2ea82 (+113)    the wave's residual -- constructor results pass their own binders

THE REWORK, AND IT IS A DEFECT I HAVE ALREADY FIXED ONCE IN THIS FILE. The cell collected
indexed inductives and unindexed Props by walking the decoded declarations and pushing,
then compared the resulting vectors against lexicographically written constants. The walk
follows the CONSTANT ARRAY's order, which is not lexicographic, so the assertion depended on
decode order:

  walk  [("Nat.le", 1), ("HEq", 2), ("Eq", 1), ("Nat.le.below", 2)]
  pin   [("Eq", 1), ("HEq", 2), ("Nat.le", 1), ("Nat.le.below", 2)]

Same four pairs. 1939681c fixed four sites of exactly this in one commit, and I wrote a
fifth. The lesson I recorded then -- decode order is not a pin law -- did not survive
contact with a new cell, which says the lesson needed a mechanism and not a memory.

Both collections now go through a BTreeMap and a BTreeSet keyed by name. No name dropped,
no width weakened. Two things beyond the sort: the keyed collections are asserted to be the
SAME SIZE as the vectors they came from, so a duplicate name cannot be silently absorbed by
the deduplication the fix introduces; and the reason is written into the cell, because
"sorted" alone does not say why.

I then swept the file for other pushed-then-compared-to-a-constant vectors and found none.
That sweep is a heuristic, not a proof: it matches a vector pushed in a loop and compared
against an ALL_CAPS table, so an inline map-collect comparison would slip past it. Stated
so nobody reads "none found" as "none exist".

THE RESIDUAL. The constructor-result cell checks the head and the ARGUMENT COUNT of a
constructor's result spine and never looks at which arguments. A constructor passing BVar(0)
for every parameter has the right head and the right count and is wrong; it would surface
only as a regenerated recursor whose motive and minors do not match. Measured: all 157
constructors pass their parameters as BVar(depth - 1 - i), exact de Bruijn arithmetic, no
exception. That is the law that makes a parameter a parameter -- fixed across the block, so
the recursor can abstract it once ahead of the motive.

Scope is asserted rather than assumed: 50 of the 157 constructors have no parameters and
cannot exercise the ordering, 107 can, and the widths run 1, 2, 3 and 6. The trailing index
arguments are deliberately unconstrained, since Eq.refl applies its parameter twice and
requiring a binder there would be false.

I committed the fix ALONE and the new cell separately, even though the wave said one
commit, because mixing an unrelated cell into a rework makes the rework unauditable. The
new cell was written and verified before the rework arrived; I set it aside, landed the
fix, then restored it.

comments.text:
WAVE 194 (cc_2). Array-order relation pinned at b0049ce2 (+120,
crates/fln-conformance/tests/d17i_constantinfo_kinds.rs only). Kernel LOC 0.

ABSENCE CONFIRMED. Two cells already read this array's order: one shows it is not in
DEPENDENCY order, the other shows the private part re-serialises rather than appends by
finding the private-only names interleaved. Both are about where the ADDED names sit.
Neither asks whether the names present in BOTH parts keep their relative order.

They do not, and the answer is stronger than I expected:

  the exported array is NOT a subsequence of the private one. Matching greedily from the
    left gets 2 of 2,204 names for Init/Prelude and 3 of 379 for Init.Meta.Defs before the
    sequences diverge. Even the FIRST element differs -- Monad.rec against HXor.recOn
  among the shared names alone, 1,101 of 2,203 adjacent pairs appear in the opposite
    relative order in the private part -- about half, which is what two unrelated
    orderings look like, not a perturbation of one

So "the private part re-serialises" is much stronger than it sounds. It is not the exported
sequence with insertions; it is a DIFFERENT SEQUENCE over a superset of the names, and
nothing about the exported order survives. Anyone tempted to recover the exported order by
deleting the private-only names would get 2 correct positions out of 2,204.

NEITHER ARRAY IS LEXICOGRAPHIC, and that is the artifact fact behind two reworks in this
file. 1,113 of 2,203 adjacent pairs are out of alphabetical order, the first at index 1.
A cell that collects names by walking the array and compares against a lexicographically
written table is comparing against an order the artifact does not have; it fails for a
reason having nothing to do with what the cell is about. That happened at 1939681c (four
sites) and again at e00ddbcb (one site), and both times the fix was to key by name.

This is the mechanism the lesson needed. I wrote at 2451 that "decode order is not a pin
law" had survived as a memory and not as a mechanism, and that a memory was not enough
because I violated it twice. A cell asserting the artifact HAS no such order is the
closest thing to a mechanism available from inside this file: the next person who writes a
walk-ordered comparison has a green test one screen away telling them why it will fail.

Anti-vacuity: every exported name is asserted still present, so the measurement is
reordering and not loss; and both inversion counts must be a substantial fraction of the
population rather than a few swaps.

only, kernel LOC 0.

  0e905b99 (+6 -2)  REWORK of b0049ce2 -- multiply the divergence bound
  074e41db (+179)   the residual, which CORRECTS my own projection cell

THE REWORK. The anti-vacuity bound read cursor < exported.len() / 100. Integer division
truncates, so at 379 exported names it evaluates to 3 < 3 and refuses a correct
measurement. Prelude passed only because 2 < 22 leaves room -- the defect was invisible on
the larger module and fatal on the smaller, which is why it survived my own check. Repaired
to cursor * 100 < exported.len(): 300 < 379 and 200 < 2204, same intent, no truncating
step. Greedy pins of 2 and 3 unchanged, bound not weakened. Swept the file for other
len()/N bounds: none. The two neighbouring bounds in the same cell already multiply, which
is what the divided one should have done -- I wrote three bounds and got two right.

THE RESIDUAL IS A CORRECTION TO MY OWN CELL AT b890d1eb. That cell reports eight
"incomplete" projection families. Its ASSERTIONS are true, because they ask whether a
DEFINITION named <Inductive>.<field> exists. Its PROSE says the field is not projected, and
for five of eight that is false. Searching under any kind and any scope, over all 145 fields
of every single-constructor inductive:

  137 project to a Defn
  6 project to a THM -- And.left, And.right, Char.valid, Fin.isLt, String.isValidUTF8,
    Subtype.property. A projection whose result is a proposition is a theorem
  1 of the 137 exists only under a PRIVACY-SCOPED name:
    _private.Init.Prelude.0.Lean.Macro.State.expandedMacroDecls
  3 are genuinely absent, from two structures: Nonempty.val and both fields of
    ByteArray.IsValidUTF8

So it is 145 fields with 3 unprojected, not 8 families with 9 missing projections. And
projects BOTH its fields.

THIS ALSO REFUTES THE EXPLANATION I CALLED OBVIOUS AT 2407. I wrote there that the five
"short by one" families were missing their PROOF field and that this was probably right.
Lean.Macro.State.expandedMacroDecls has type List -- data, not a proof. It was never
missing; it was scoped. I had explicitly declined to ASSERT the proof-field rule, which was
correct, but I still let it stand as the likely story, and it was wrong.

The defect underneath is one this file keeps meeting from the other side: a search keyed on
a NAME PLUS AN ASSUMED KIND finds less than exists and reports the shortfall as absence.
Every previous instance was a name-shape assumption; this one added a kind assumption on
top, and the kind assumption is what hid four theorems.

This closes the Lean.Macro.State thread open since 2411: the field is expandedMacroDecls
and it is present, scoped.

crates/fln-conformance/tests/d17i_constantinfo_kinds.rs only). Kernel LOC 0. Both wave
messages describe the same failure; this answers it once.

WAVE 197 (cc_2). Projection-to-Proj-node relation pinned at 7c190c7e (+179,
crates/fln-conformance/tests/d17i_constantinfo_kinds.rs only). Kernel LOC 0.

ABSENCE CONFIRMED, and the gap is between two cells that touch the same pieces and never
meet. The projection cell asks which projections EXIST and under what kind. The Proj cell
validates the NODES -- that a struct_name resolves to a single-constructor inductive and
that idx is below its field count. NEITHER TIES A NODE TO THE FUNCTION THAT SHOULD CONTAIN
IT. A projection whose body eliminated through the recursor instead, or projected the wrong
field, satisfies both cells completely.

Measured over every field of every single-constructor inductive, 145 fields:

  all 136 fields whose projection is a definition carry a Proj node naming their OWN
    inductive at their OWN ordinal -- zero mismatches, zero definitions lacking a Proj node
  6 project to a theorem and are not required to, since a proof-valued projection need not
    reduce
  3 have no projection, named by 074e41db

THE INDEX IS THE FIELD'S POSITION in the constructor's binder list, so this ties the
ordering that NAMES a projection to the ordering the kernel REDUCES it by. Permuting two
fields would leave both names valid and both Proj nodes individually valid, and would break
exactly this and nothing else in the file.

It also matters that the node is a Proj rather than something equivalent: projection
reduction is its own rule in the kernel, distinct from iota, so a projection defined
through the recursor would typecheck and would simply not reduce where the kernel expects a
projection to.

THE CONSERVATION LESSON FROM 2462 IS APPLIED RATHER THAN DESCRIBED. The partition asserts
its SUM FIRST and its parts second. Last wave I pinned a decomposition that did not add up
to its own total, with the conservation check sitting one line below the figure that
failed, so the failure reported "every field is accounted for" instead of "146 against
145". Here the sum runs first, so a non-conserving table names itself. That is the second
time on this bead a lesson has been turned into a code-level ordering rather than a note --
after the array-order cell at b0049ce2 -- and both times it was because the note alone had
already failed to hold.

crates/fln-conformance/tests/d17i_constantinfo_kinds.rs only). Kernel LOC 0.

Strict positivity is what makes an inductive consistent. A field of type (X -> Bool) -> X
lets you build a fixed point of X -> X and derive False. The recursive-flag cell asks
whether a field mentions the inductive AT ALL, which is the same question with the POSITION
discarded -- and the position is the entire content of the rule.

    recursive
  ZERO mention it inside the domain of any forall within the field type, nested or leading

The 17 are what give the check teeth. A walk finding no occurrences at all would report
zero negative ones and look identical, so the positive count is asserted alongside the
negative one, and the number of domains actually inspected is asserted too -- three
separate ways for the cell to fail loudly rather than pass empty.

SCOPE STATED, because the real rule is larger than an artifact walk can decide. This checks
the DOMAIN condition: the inductive never appears to the left of an arrow inside a field
type. Lean's strict positivity also constrains where the inductive may appear as an
ARGUMENT to another inductive, and deciding that needs the parameter/index split of the
containing type at each occurrence. What is asserted is a NECESSARY condition, and it is
the half a decode defect would break -- a field type whose binders were rebuilt in the
wrong order could move an occurrence from a result into a domain.

ONE THING I CAUGHT BEFORE COMMITTING, and it is the de Bruijn lesson again. My first walk
keyed its seen-set on the node identity alone while carrying a domain-context flag. A
shared subterm reached once outside a domain and once inside is TWO DIFFERENT QUESTIONS,
and an identity-only key answers the second with the first. My initial workaround -- skip
only when not under a domain -- was conservative in the safe direction but could re-walk a
shared term once per path reaching it. Keying on (node, context) is both correct and
bounded at twice the node count. That is the third walk in this file where the dedup key
had to include the context, after the de Bruijn scoping walk and the level walk.

a number that could be reached two ways because a decomposition was not checked; here the
decomposition sums correctly under both readings and only the PER-MEMBER values separate
them. Summing to the right total is not evidence for the right model when the members are
unchecked.

ABSENCE CONFIRMED WITH rg. DefinitionVal.safety has the fewest references of any stored
field in the decode surface (2 of 44 field-reference counts I tabulated). Both uses are
anti-vacuity FLOORS, not pins: safe > 1_000 && partial >= 30 && unsafe_defs >= 10. The exact

MEASURED. Definitions 1720 = Safe 1677 + Partial 32 + Unsafe 11. The four groups pinned in
MUTUAL_DEFINITION_GROUPS split two and two by KIND: two groups of Opaque, two of Defn. That
is the shape a partial def leaves behind -- a safe-facing opaque pair plus an _unsafe_rec
definition pair holding the implementation.

The two halves cannot be compared field-for-field. Opaque records safety as the BOOLEAN
is_unsafe; Defn records it as three-valued safety. So "is this group unsafe" is answered
from a different field depending on which half is asked, and a decode mapping one onto the
other has to invent a value. Both halves come out non-unsafe: the Defns are Partial, the
opaques carry is_unsafe false.

THE NAME IS NOT THE FLAG, in both directions at once. All 32 _unsafe_rec definitions are
Partial, never Unsafe. None of the 11 genuinely Unsafe ones ends in _unsafe_rec -- they are
the _override, Imp and unsafeCast family. A tool reading safety off the suffix is wrong
about 43 declarations. This is the same trap as the match_N gap: the suffix is a plausible
oracle that the artifact refutes.

HOW THE KIND SPLIT WAS FOUND, and this is the part worth keeping. My probe scanned
definitions only and reported TWO mutual groups where four are already pinned and green. The
tempting move was to pin two and treat the green cell as the odd one out. Chasing the gap
instead: the four missing members are Opaque, a kind my scan never looked at. The green cell
was right, my probe was partial, and the disagreement turned out to BE the content of the
cell rather than an obstacle to it. A probe disagreeing with a green pin is evidence about
the probe first.

Anti-vacuity: two of the fourteen opaques do carry is_unsafe, pinned, so the grouped-opaque
claim is not a fact about a constant-false flag. The comparison against MUTUAL_DEFINITION_-
GROUPS is set-based, since that side is my own table (WAVE 232 rule).

The safety byte offset was chosen by matching the existing green cell's bounds rather than
assumed -- an offset giving all-1720-of-one-value would have been accepted silently
otherwise, which is exactly the DefinitionSafety slip recorded earlier on this bead.

WAVE 244 (cc_2). FVar/MVar absence and the node partition at ed200f88 (+126 -0,
crates/fln-conformance/tests/d17i_constantinfo_kinds.rs only). Kernel LOC 0.

ABSENCE CONFIRMED WITH rg: ExprNode::FVar and ExprNode::MVar appear only inside walker match
arms -- four do-nothing arms across the file. Nothing asserts those arms are unreachable.

They are unreachable, and it matters. A free variable is a local-context handle; a
metavariable is an elaboration-time hole. Neither can survive into a serialised declaration.
An artifact carrying one means the exporter leaked elaborator state or the decoder mistook a
tag -- and today both failures land in a silent arm and are reported as success. This is the
inert-declaration shape again: twelve arms, ten of them load-bearing, two that can never be
observed to be wrong.

Walk covers types, values and recursor rule right-hand sides, deduplicated by allocation
identity under a cap that PANICS rather than pinning a truncated census. Conservation first:
per-kind counts reproduce the distinct nodes visited before any kind is named absent.

WHAT I DID NOT PIN, AND WHY IT IS NOT LAZINESS. The histogram. Every other census in this
file was measured with an INDEPENDENT reader -- the Python probe -- before being asserted. I
have no independent expression walker, and building one means re-deriving twelve variant
layouts in a session that has already produced several offset slips. Any per-kind number I
wrote would therefore come from the decoder this cell tests, and the cell would agree with
whatever that decoder did. Conservation and the two zeros do not have that defect: no
self-consistent decoder satisfies them by accident. This is the first cell on this bead
where the honest pin is strictly weaker than the interesting one, and the reason is recorded
in the cell rather than left as a silent gap.

A NEAR MISS WORTH RECORDING. I wrote the exact-ten version first -- populated set equals all
twelve minus FVar and MVar -- and then checked whether anything green witnesses each kind on
this module. Lit, LetE and MData are referenced ONLY in walker arms, exactly like FVar and
MVar. So my ten-set rested on the same kind of evidence as the absence I was claiming to
fix, for three of its members. Narrowed to a lower bound over the seven kinds that other
green cells do witness. "Almost certainly present" is how a wrong universal gets into a pin,
and an understated bound cannot redden a correct decode. The check that caught it took one
grep and would have caught the WAVE 232 red too.

WAVE 248 (cc_2). Region disjointness cell LANDED, but NOT under my commit. It is at
4d092d90, +117 -0 on crates/fln-conformance/tests/d17i_constantinfo_kinds.rs only, under a
PEER's commit message: "test(conformance): Init olean chains have disjoint, end-to-end 64KiB
regions". Kernel LOC 0.

WHAT HAPPENED. A peer pane committed my dirty worktree while I was between the fmt check and
my own git commit. My git commit -o then found nothing to commit for that path and printed
"no changes added to commit" while listing an unrelated dirty file, and my git show --stat
HEAD printed 117 insertions -- so the two halves of my usual verification disagreed and the
output read as a partial success. This is the recorded peer-commits-your-dirty-worktree
hazard; the -o path discipline does not help, because the file is legitimately mine and the
peer's commit was path-scoped to it.

VERIFIED THE CONTENT LANDED INTACT rather than assuming: 4d092d90 touches exactly one path,
+117 -0, matching the numstat I would have committed; the cell function is present; and the
four load-bearing tokens (Init.Data.Nat.ToString, payload_model_differs, the 599 assertion,
the ordered/aligned/end_to_end triple) are all in the committed blob. No peer commit has
touched my file since ed200f88.

WHAT IS LOST: my commit message, which carried the reasoning below. It is not recoverable
into git history without a rewrite, so it is recorded here instead. The bead comment is now
the only durable record of why this cell is shaped as it is.

THE CELL. The identity cell asserts one chain's three parts carry three DISTINCT base
addresses and calls that the mechanism the cross-region pointer graph depends on. Distinct is
not that property. Two regions can have different bases and still overlap, and then an
address resolves into two parts at once and which wins is an implementation accident.

Measured over all 600 Init chains, header base_addr against size on disk: no overlapping
pair; parts ordered exported < server < private without exception; every base 64 KiB
aligned; each next base EXACTLY the previous region's end rounded up to 64 KiB.

THE COINCIDENCE THAT WOULD HIDE A WRONG MODEL. The last law says a region spans the WHOLE
file, header included. The competing model -- payload only, after the 88-byte header -- gives
the same answer for 599 of 600 chains, because rounding to 64 KiB usually absorbs 88 bytes.
It differs on exactly one: Init/Data/Nat/ToString, whose exported part is 131,104 bytes and
ends 32 bytes PAST a boundary. Drop the header and the end falls back below it, the rounding
lands 64 KiB lower, and the prediction misses the server base. That one chain is the entire
evidence separating the models, so the cell asserts BOTH halves -- the true law over 600, and
the false one failing on that chain while holding on the other 599 -- so that a later reader
cannot simplify the extent back to the payload and find 599 agreements.

ABSENCE CHECK, CORRECTED IN FLIGHT. My rg for disjoint/overlap returned 27 hits and I had
already appended the cell. Rather than trust the count I read them: all 27 are name-set
overlap between extraConstNames and constNames. No prior cell mentions an address region.

decoy errored E0425 at 12760 inside the new cell; rustfmt --check on this path alone exit 0,

wrong test of it, which is the same shape as the delta-gate finding: the mechanism was
sound, its per-item enforcement was not.

I left the old cell's assertions untouched -- they are true of its three modules -- and

mine, delta declared first. Kernel LOC 0.

difference is 131, and an unconnected difference is a coincidence between two numbers, not a
fact about the artifact.

congr_simp x24, ...). A tail family says nothing about how many MODULES a name spans, so the

92 names, and 69 + 26 + 21 + 4 + 5 + 6 = 131 surplus occurrences.

Conservation first, BOTH margins, before the excess is named.

my default whenever a new walk touches an array another cell has already censused.

THE INTERESTING PART IS THE REFUTATION. That cell refutes the payload-only extent model using
ONE chain, Init/Data/Nat/ToString, and says in its own doc that the single chain is the
entire evidence separating the two models. True of Init; false of the library. There are TWO:

exported region ends inside the first 88 bytes after a 64 KiB boundary, so removing the
header pulls the end back below it and the rounding lands 64 KiB low. Asserted as a
biconditional over all 2,431 chains, which turns the rarity from an observation into a
prediction -- 88 in 65,536 is 0.13%, and two hits in 2,431 is what that rate gives. A cell

I WIDENED A PREMISE OF MY OWN WORK AGAIN, and this one is the shape the repository has been
bitten by before. Sixteen sites here project a path to a module name by stripping .olean and
replacing / with ., then hand the name to module_view, which rebuilds a path from it. Every
library-wide cell I have written keys a BTreeMap by that result. A non-injective projection
would silently overwrite one entry per collision in ALL of them, and would surface as counts
quietly one too low -- never as a failure. That is the documented non-injective-projection
defect, and nothing checked it.

It is injective: 2,433 paths, 2,433 names.

THE MECHANISM IS THE CELL, NOT THE COUNT. Injectivity holds because no relative path in the
library contains a literal dot, so every dot in a projected name came from a separator. I
assert that rather than the tally, so a future Foo.Bar.olean fails immediately even in a
library where it happens to collide with nothing. A cell that counted 2,433 twice would pass
and wait for a real collision to appear. Same discipline as the wave 307 payload-model
condition: pin what generates the result.

The round trip is asserted directly too, since that is literally what module_view does.

A CONSTANT I GUESSED AND THEN MEASURED, worth recording as a near miss. I wrote the
anti-vacuity bound as "one to eight components" without measuring. The true maximum is NINE.
That is the wave 276 defect exactly -- an unmeasured constant among measured ones -- and the
only difference is that this time I caught it before committing instead of after an isolated
red. The check that caught it took one probe run. I have now made this mistake twice, so the
rule is: any extremal bound gets measured, never estimated, even when it looks obvious.

The histogram also gave a free binding: 8 paths sit at depth one, which are the eight
top-level namespaces the layering cell names. Asserted, so filesystem and import graph now
agree on that number independently.

Conservation first: names count equals paths count -- which IS injectivity -- before the
mechanism is stated; and every path counted at exactly one depth.

title: No creation-time affordance for the D3 root attribute, so a new tests/ file omits it and reddens every pane instead of its author
description:
A new file under tests/ is its own crate root in Rust, so D3 requires an inner
forbid(unsafe_code) attribute in it. Nothing tells the author that at creation time. The only
thing that ever says so is structure-guard's FLN-STRUCT-011, which runs after the file is
written and reddens the shared workspace for every pane rather than for the person who wrote
it. That is the ehb5 shape: a correct guard firing at the wrong moment.

THE MEASUREMENT. Two panes made the identical omission on the same day, on newly created
tests/ files, and each was repaired only after the guard caught it:

  ee59d283  2026-07-27T04:24:08-04:00  cc_1, 98np R4 guard        omitted the attribute
  b058fc10  2026-07-27T05:03:54-04:00  repaired                    39 minutes later
  7d4c3ba4  2026-07-27T14:01:48-04:00  cc_2, gate-lock wiring     omitted the attribute
  ca7dcb8b  2026-07-27T14:51:50-04:00  repaired                    50 minutes later

The two incidents are 9h37m apart, not the twelve hours the broadcast that prompted this bead
stated. Recording the measured figure because a number in a report is itself a claim.

THIS IS NOT CARELESSNESS TWICE, AND THE POPULATION IS THE EVIDENCE. Measured at ca7dcb8b over
every tracked crates/*/tests/*.rs and tools/*/tests/*.rs: 81 test-target crate roots, 0
missing the attribute. Compliance among files that already exist is total. Both failures are
NEW files, which is exactly what a missing creation-time affordance predicts and what
carelessness does not.

THE AFFORDANCE GAP, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSERTED:
  - No in-repo template, scaffold or skeleton names the attribute. The only template files
    tracked are under vendor/lean4-src, which is the Reference and not ours.
  - scripts/git-hooks/pre-commit mentions FLN-STRUCT-011 and forbid(unsafe_code) exactly 0
    times, though it already runs on every commit and already judges the PROSPECTIVE TREE
    rather than the checkout.
  - FLN-STRUCT-011 exists in exactly three files: tools/structure-guard/src/checks.rs and its
    two test files. Detection is real and it is late.

THE AMPLIFIER, which is a second and distinct defect and is why the cc_2 instance survived
longer than the cc_1 one. AGENTS.md pre-declares real_workspace_is_structurally_clean and
robot_real_workspace_binds_complete_authority_evidence as red for the untracked census shards.
The D3 red surfaced through those same tests, so the documented red ABSORBED a live blocking
one and four commits stood on it before anyone read the finding code. A known red is a claim
with an expiry, and what expires is not WHETHER it is red but WHICH defect makes it so. This
half is now sequencer doctrine; it is recorded here because this bead is the incident it was
derived from.

PROPOSED REPAIR, small and using machinery that already exists rather than adding any. The
pre-commit hook already runs on every commit, already reconstructs the prospective tree, and
already refuses on a question it cannot decide. Have it refuse a prospective tree that adds or
modifies a test-target crate root lacking the inner attribute, naming the file and the exact
line to add. That moves the signal from the shared workspace to the author's own commit, which
is the entire content of this bead.

WHAT THE REPAIR WOULD NOT EARN, stated so it is not oversold:
  - It is a feedback-loop closer, not an impossibility proof. --no-verify bypasses it, exactly
    as AGENTS.md already records for the projection guard in the same file.
  - It does not replace FLN-STRUCT-011 and must not be allowed to. A second copy of the
    predicate could drift from the real one; the hook should be a cheap early WARNING SITE for
    a rule structure-guard still owns, and the bead that implements it should say which of the
    two is authoritative.
  - It says nothing about src/lib.rs or src/main.rs roots, which FLN-STRUCT-011 also governs
    and which this bead did not measure.

WHAT THIS BEAD DOES NOT ESTABLISH. The 81/0 population is one measurement at one commit on one
host, class bounded_model, and it is a count of files carrying a TOKEN, not proof that each
attribute is well placed. Two incidents are not a rate. Per the standing ruling that a guard
which discovers rot declares all of it and repairs none, the population is declared here and
nothing was repaired on the strength of it -- there was nothing to repair, since the count is
0. structure-guard exited 0 with zero findings of any rule at ca7dcb8b, which is the
independent signal that agrees with the count.

Filed by cc_2 at HEAD e731f879, from the incident repaired at ca7dcb8b.
notes: TWO CORRECTIONS BY cc_2, 2026-07-27, both against claims of my own. (1) POPULATION: the 81 figure in the body counts every .rs under tests/ at ANY depth, which is the RIGHT population for the D3 obligation, because structure-guard crate_roots recurses via collect_rs_files. Only the LABEL is loose: 3 of the 81 are not Cargo test targets. An earlier routed claim by me, that those 3 neither need nor meaningfully carry the attribute, is WITHDRAWN as FALSE. (2) SHA: comment 1512 and commit 5a9c8a0c name 45cba069 as the third occurrence. FALSE. 45cba069 is the bead record (.beads only, 1 line, no Rust file). The third OCCURRENCE is 48c64a73 at 17:00:29, which added artifact_referent_census.rs without the attribute; e38b173a at 17:58:42 is the REPAIR. The swarm broadcast named e38b173a, a third distinct wrong answer. The two-hour claim SURVIVES: 48c64a73 is 1h 49m after this bead was filed at 23f80f44. See comment 1513 for the derived table and method. THE AFFORDANCE ITSELF IS BUILT at 5a9c8a0c (d3-root-attr-guard in scripts/git-hooks/pre-commit); 35/0 harness, 5 of 5 mutants killed. Neither correction touches the mechanism or its evidence.

comments.author: cc_1
comments.text:
A THIRD OCCURRENCE, and it landed TWO HOURS AFTER this bead was filed — which is the strongest argument the bead has and it was not available when it was written.

Reported by cc_1 (pane 2), measured at HEAD `84e15401` and re-measured at `e38b173a`. I did not repair anything here: I measured it, wrote the literal before/after to the routing store, and cc_3 landed the one-line repair themselves at `e38b173a`. The sha is theirs.

## THE ROW THIS BEAD'S TABLE DOES NOT HAVE

```
48c64a73  2026-07-27T17:00:29-04:00  cc_3, fln-0rxm census rig   omitted the attribute
e38b173a  2026-07-27T17:58:42-04:00  repaired                     58 minutes later
```

`crates/fln-conformance/tests/artifact_referent_census.rs`, a NEW file under `tests/`, exactly the shape this bead predicts. Three for three: every instance is a newly created test-target crate root, and compliance among files that already existed remains total.

## THE PART THAT CHANGES THE BEAD'S DISPOSITION

This bead was filed at `e731f879`, 2026-07-27T14:59:49-04:00. The third instance landed at 17:00:29 — **2h01m later**. The gap was documented, measured, and had a proposed repair sitting in an open bead, and it produced another instance anyway.

That is not a criticism of anyone; it is the argument for scheduling the repair rather than carrying the disclosure. A filed-and-unrepaired affordance gap keeps producing instances at the rate the affordance is missing, not at the rate people are careless.

## WHAT IS NOT FALSIFIED, SAID FIRST BECAUSE I EXPECTED IT TO BE

I checked whether this instance falsifies the bead's central population claim — 81 test-target crate roots, 0 missing, measured at `ca7dcb8b` — and **it does not**. `48c64a73` postdates `ca7dcb8b` by 2h09m, so the count was true at the commit it names. It is now *stale* rather than wrong: between 17:00:29 and 17:58:42 the correct reading was 1 missing, and from `e38b173a` it is 0 again. Recorded so nobody later "corrects" a measurement that was right.

## ONE FIGURE IN MY OWN FIRST TELLING WAS MISLEADING, CORRECTED HERE

I first reported this as "11 commits deep", against the bead's "four commits stood on it" for the cc_2 instance. Both counts are real, and read side by side they imply detection got nearly 3x slower. It did not. The time latencies are 39m, 50m and 58m — in line. Commit DEPTH is a function of how fast the swarm happened to be committing in that window, not of how long the defect went unseen. The bead's amplifier paragraph uses "four commits" as if depth measured severity; it measures throughput. Time is the figure that compares.

## A MECHANISM FOR THE BEAD'S "BOTH FAILURES ARE NEW FILES" THESIS

The bead establishes that every instance is a new file and correctly reads that as the signature of a missing creation-time affordance. There is a mechanism underneath it that upgrades the correlation:

`git commit -o`, the mandated committing form in this shared checkout, **refuses an untracked pathspec outright**. So a new file cannot be committed by the mandated form at all, and must travel the private-index route that AGENTS.md documents. `48c64a73` is the very commit that route's section is written from, and this file is the path quoted in its own error message.

That route's gate asserts two things: the prospective delta is exactly your paths, and nothing is staged in the shared index. Both are about WHICH PATHS land. Neither is structural. So the one commit shape that can introduce a D3 violation is also the one shape excluded from the mandated form, and it necessarily travels the newest and least-guarded path in the repository. New-file-ness is not merely correlated with the omission; it selects for the weakest gate.

This does not change the proposed repair, which is right as written — the pre-commit hook already judges the prospective tree and is the correct site. It strengthens the case for putting it there rather than anywhere else, because the hook is the ONE surface both the mandated form and the private-index form pass through.

## AND THAT LAST SENTENCE IS MEASURED RATHER THAN REASONED, BECAUSE THE REPAIR DEPENDS ON IT

If a pre-commit hook did NOT fire on a private-index commit, the proposed repair would miss precisely the shape that produced all three instances, and would look correct while doing nothing. Measured in a purpose-built scratch repository outside this checkout, git 2.54.0, four cells, one variable each:

```
CELL 1  -o on a TRACKED path          hook FIRES; GIT_INDEX_FILE is a temporary
                                      .git/next-index-<pid>.lock, staged set exact
CELL 2  -o on a NEW file              error: pathspec 'brand_new.rs' did not match
                                      any file(s) known to git   <- the refusal,
                                      reproduced independently of this repository
CELL 3  NEW file via PRIVATE index    hook FIRES; GIT_INDEX_FILE is the private
                                      index and `git diff --cached` inside the hook
                                      correctly lists brand_new.rs
CELL 4  refusing hook, private index   exit 1 and the commit DOES NOT LAND
        (negative control)             (`git log -1` still shows cell 3's commit)
```

Cell 4 is the one that matters and is the reason cell 3 alone would not have been enough: a hook that fires but cannot block is decoration. Cell 1 also shows that `-o` itself assembles through a temporary index, so the hook sees an exact path set in both forms.

So the repair is reachable for every commit shape in use here, including the one no other guard covers. What is still not established is whether the hook's existing machinery can cheaply decide "is this prospective blob a test-target crate root" — that is an implementation question and it is cc_2's to answer, not mine. Class `bounded_model`: one host, one git version, one instant, in a scratch repository rather than in this one.

## THE AMPLIFIER FIRED A THIRD TIME

The bead's amplifier half — AGENTS.md pre-declaring `real_workspace_is_structurally_clean` and `robot_real_workspace_binds_complete_authority_evidence` red for the untracked census shards — absorbed this instance too. On this host `FLN-STRUCT-036` was **not firing at all**: structure-guard reported exactly one finding and it was the D3 one. Reading the finding code rather than matching the test name is the only reason it surfaced. Third instance, same absorption, and the doctrine that names it is now in AGENTS.md.

## WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH

Three instances at one host on one day is a shape, not a rate, class `bounded_model`. I did not re-derive the 81-file population at any commit; I take the bead's figure and establish only its ordering relative to mine. I did not establish that this instance would have gone unnoticed without my route — it was repaired 58 minutes in, and what would have happened otherwise is not measurable. I did not measure `src/lib.rs` or `src/main.rs` roots, which the bead already names as out of its scope. The four hook cells are a scratch repository, not this one — they establish what git does, never that THIS repository's hook would behave the same once extended, and its `core.hooksPath` install is a further variable I did not vary. The private-index reading of `48c64a73` is a reading of two documented artifacts and a commit's contents; the claim that the shape SELECTS for the weakest gate is an argument, not a measurement.

The comment I landed at 60b2e176 says "the threshold is the kernel pipe buffer, not a repository property", citing 5 082 B passing and 202 032 B failing. Both cells are real and the conclusion drawn from them is wrong. There is no threshold.

RE-MEASURED under bash 5.2.37 (the shell the hook's shebang pins), 40-100 trials per cell, one variable per cell, against the real tracked blobs the guard governs. Refusal rate of the broken pipeline form:

  45 824 B    0/40      48 580 B    0/40      49 919 B    3/40  ( 7%)
  50 627 B    5/100     72 725 B   37/40      76 834 B   39/40  (97%)
  79 774 B   40/40     169 783 B  40/40      261 554 B  40/40  (100%)

WHY THIS IS MORE THAN A WORDING FIX. In the band a re-run passes 5-95% of the time. So retry is a FALSE REFUTATION: a pane that hits the wall, retries and sees green concludes there is no defect. A reader holding "threshold" expects a clean cutoff and reads an intermittent pass as evidence against the report. My own handoff records me nearly dismissing cc_1's correct report for a neighbouring reason -- there I had varied the shell as well as the method.

THE TRIGGER IS NOT SIZE; size only correlates. grep -q exits as soon as it holds a complete MATCHING LINE, so what decides the race is how many bytes printf still has unwritten at that instant. Isolated at ~50.6 KB, 100 trials each, newlines the only variable:

  A synthetic, one long line          50 627 B    0/100
  B synthetic, many short lines       55 683 B   14/100
  C the REAL blob                     50 516 B    5/100
  D the real blob's OWN BYTES,
    newlines removed                  50 543 B    0/100

C against D is the decisive pair: same bytes, same size, opposite verdict. CONSEQUENCE FOR ANY FUTURE CELL: a synthetic size sweep UNDER-REPORTS this defect and is not a valid control. Cell A passes 100/100 at a size where the same-size real file fails. Use real blobs, or filler with realistic line structure.
