title: D3 SAFETY-note enforcement needs a clippy-diff CI lane: the shrink direction is unobtainable in-source
description:
FOR COD_2 (scripts/ and .github/). Filed by cc_3 from franken_lean-d3-safety-note-unenforced-cdbg. All measurements below were made and are not to be re-derived.

WHAT IS ALREADY TRUE, so nothing here is rebuilt:
  * The unsafe-ledger ROW half is enforced both ways (FLN-STRUCT-013/014), 180 rows against 180 sites, structure-guard PASS.
  * Both D3 structural laws are walked; FLN-STRUCT-024 requires the prohibitions be declared.
  * FLN-STRUCT-040 now checks EVERY target root, not just src/lib.rs (commit 99291ba6), after it was found reporting fln-unsafe-region as ENFORCED while an undocumented block sat in examples/, uncovered.
  * The evidence remainder is counted (commit 0effc5b2): 1 lane-cited, 59 symbol-resolved, 120 prose, 71 resolving tokens, all pinned in both directions.

THE REMAINING GAP. fln-unsafe-abi has 28 unsafe blocks clippy reports as undocumented, and carries a UNSAFE-NOTE-WAIVER naming cdbg. While that waiver stands, a TWENTY-NINTH undocumented block in that crate does not fail anything. Per-crate counts measured at HEAD 3847fb04: fln-unsafe-abi 28, fln-unsafe-region 1 (now fixed), fln-unsafe-jit 0.

WHY THIS CANNOT BE FIXED IN-SOURCE, TESTED RATHER THAN ARGUED. The obvious move is qydn's declared-allowance idiom: turn the lint on at the root and declare the 28 sites, so the 29th fails and the allowance shrinks with each repair. I built and measured it.

  FORWARD DIRECTION WORKS: root deny plus per-site #[expect(clippy::undocumented_unsafe_blocks)] gives 28 sites, one expect planted, 27 errors remaining; all 28 planted, clippy exits 0. A 29th undocumented block fails immediately.

  SHRINK DIRECTION DOES NOT: with all 28 declared and the crate compiling clean, I documented one site and left its #[expect] in place. Clippy reported nothing, exit 0, including on a forced rebuild. A CONTROLLED COMPARISON isolates the cause: #[expect(unused_variables)] on a function with no unused variable DOES report "this lint expectation is unfulfilled" in this toolchain. The mechanism exists and works for rustc lints; it does not fire for clippy's own lints here.

So a per-site expect ROTS: someone writes the note, forgets the attribute, and nothing ever says so. Landing the forward half alone gives a list that grows correctly and never shrinks — a permanent hole wearing the costume of a shrinking debt, which is the inverse of what qydn's row records. It was deliberately not landed.

WHAT WOULD WORK, and why it is yours. Run clippy in a lane and diff its reported site set against a declared list, in BOTH directions:
  * a site clippy reports that is not in the declared list FAILS (the 29th-site property);
  * a declared site clippy no longer reports FAILS (forces the shrink in the same change as the repair).
This keeps clippy as the SOLE decider of whether a block is documented — no second implementation of that property, which is the constraint FLN-STRUCT-040 was explicitly built to respect — and it obtains the shrink direction that in-source attributes cannot. It is a CI lane plus a declared artifact, so it is scripts/ and .github/.

SUGGESTED SHAPE, not prescribed: model on scripts/e2e/closure_audit.sh; the declared list is a checked-in artifact (path plus line-independent identifier if you can manage it, since line numbers churn); register in scripts/check.sh INPUT_PATHS and the shellcheck stage and as a ci.yml step joining expected_roots and specs. Expected-fail steps use --semantic-failure-exit 101 and must grep BOTH .out and .err.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLAIM: no assertion that any of the 28 blocks is unsound. cdbg's own triage found the first one examined was FULLY DOCUMENTED in a doc comment, just not where clippy reads — so "29 undocumented" means 29 whose justification a mechanical reader cannot see, not 29 unjustified blocks. Writing the 28 notes is a separate and much larger judgement, deliberately declined: a wrong SAFETY note at the TCB boundary is worse than a missing one, because the missing one is visibly absent and the wrong one is silently trusted.

title: D3 SAFETY-note requirement is unenforced: 29 undocumented unsafe blocks in the boundary crates
description:
D3 requires a SAFETY note at every unsafe site; 29 unsafe blocks in the boundary crates have none, and nothing checks.

WHAT WAS TESTED AND FOUND SOUND FIRST, so this bead is not read as an indictment of the boundary crates' discipline, which is mostly excellent:

  * The no-admission export covenant (D3 law b) is NOT a rule without a guard. It is enforced in THREE layers: a textual scan (tools/structure-guard/src/checks.rs:1912-1999, refusing forbidden export shapes and treating an unreadable file as INCONCLUSIVE rather than clean), a type-aware layer over every bare-pub item with its own row grammar (tools/structure-guard/src/boundary_api.rs), and a C-ABI layer over every Linkage::Export (tools/structure-guard/src/export_status.rs). This was the hypothesis worth checking and it is negative.
  * The ledger's ID join reconciles EXACTLY: 180 rows against 180 `#[allow(unsafe_code)]` attribute sites across nine files. A crude grep suggests 183; the extra three are doc-comment mentions of the policy in the three crate roots, each of which correctly carries `#![deny(unsafe_code)]`.

WHAT IS NOT GUARDED. AGENTS.md (D3) requires each allow site to carry "a `// SAFETY:` note and a ledger row". The ledger row half is mechanised in both directions. The SAFETY note half is not mechanised at all, and clippy has the lint built for exactly this:

  cargo clippy -p fln-unsafe-abi -p fln-unsafe-region --all-targets -- -W clippy::undocumented_unsafe_blocks

reports 29 unsafe blocks missing a safety comment. `undocumented_unsafe_blocks` appears nowhere in the workspace -- not in a Cargo.toml lint table, not in a crate root, not in ci.yml -- so the requirement is held by care alone. Care has held it well; 29 out of 412 unsafe occurrences is a good ratio for a rule nothing enforces. It is still the difference between a discipline and a guarantee, in the only crates where project-authored unsafe exists.

THE 29, by file:
  15  crates/fln-unsafe-abi/src/tests.rs
  11  crates/fln-unsafe-abi/src/object.rs
   1  crates/fln-unsafe-abi/src/membrane.rs
   1  crates/fln-unsafe-abi/src/export.rs
   1  crates/fln-unsafe-region/examples/region_trap_probe.rs

NOT ALL OF THEM ARE MISSING PROSE. Some have a note that is not positioned where the lint -- or a reader scanning for it -- expects. crates/fln-unsafe-abi/src/export.rs:246 is inside mk_string_from_bytes_impl, which DOES carry "// SAFETY: caller (C contract) vouches for sz readable bytes" at :242, attached to the enclosing `let` rather than to the `unsafe` block. That is a real distinction and it cuts both ways: the invariant IS stated, and a mechanical reader cannot tell it apart from a block with no justification at all. Whoever takes this should triage the 29 rather than assume they are uniformly undocumented.

WHY IT MATTERS HERE MORE THAN ELSEWHERE. This is the same shape as the other findings in this session's audit -- a claim whose evidence nothing joins -- but the claim is a safety invariant in the TCB's membrane, and the reader who most needs the note is the next person to modify the block. The ledger row records why the SITE is admissible; the SAFETY note records why the OPERATION is sound. They are different statements and only one of them is enforced.

SUGGESTED SHAPE, not prescribed: enable the lint at the three boundary crate roots (not workspace-wide -- ordinary crates are `forbid(unsafe_code)` and would never trip it, so a workspace-wide setting would be noise that says nothing), triage the 29 into "note exists but is misplaced" and "no note", and fix both classes. Enabling the lint and fixing the sites must land TOGETHER or the lint will be turned off by the next person who meets it red.

SCOPE NOTE: this bead does not claim any of the 29 blocks is unsound. It claims the requirement is unenforced and that 29 sites cannot be distinguished, mechanically, from sites that were never justified.

Filed by cc_3 on 2026-07-25 from the boundary-crate audit; measured against HEAD f4c22a2d.

CONSTRAINT 1 DISCHARGED: the list below is routed to whoever owns Marrow. I am not writing these notes. Each one asserts an invariant about code I did not write, in the only crates where a wrong assertion is a soundness claim rather than a documentation defect.

  crates/fln-unsafe-abi/src/tests.rs:1434:5
  crates/fln-unsafe-region/examples/region_trap_probe.rs:39:5

A CORRECTION I OWE THIS BEAD, because I nearly built the guard on it. I first tried to enforce the rule at the granularity AGENTS.md states it -- "each `#[allow(unsafe_code)]` site carrying a `// SAFETY:` note" -- by scanning the comment block attached to each attribute. That reported 101 of 180 sites non-compliant. The number is an ARTIFACT of my heuristic, not a finding.

The convention in these crates is the correct Rust one: the doc comment above the attribute describes the pin symbol, the UNSAFE-LEDGER marker authorises the site, and the SAFETY note sits at the unsafe OPERATION inside the body, where the person changing that operation will read it. crates/fln-unsafe-abi/src/export.rs:311-315 is typical -- doc, marker, attribute, then `// SAFETY: p was minted by the small heap per the ABI contract.` immediately above the unsafe use.

So the enforceable granularity is the BLOCK, not the allow site, and 29 is the real number. That was my fourth unsound measurement of the day and the only one that would have shipped as a guard, which is the argument for the recommendation below.

WHY I AM NOT HAND-ROLLING A STRUCTURE-GUARD SCANNER FOR THIS. A bespoke comment-position scanner would be a SECOND implementation of a property clippy already decides with a real parser -- and mine would have to handle unsafe fn bodies, nested blocks, unsafe impl, macro expansion and attribute ordering. I have now been wrong about exactly this property once today. Two implementations of one property is how they disagree, and the one nobody trusts is the one that gets disabled.

THE GUARD THAT IS RIGHT, and it does not fit in this bead's current state:
  1. `#![deny(clippy::undocumented_unsafe_blocks)]` at the three boundary crate roots -- not workspace-wide, since ordinary crates are forbid(unsafe_code) and would never trip it, so a global setting would be noise that says nothing.
  2. A structure-guard rule asserting that attribute IS PRESENT at each boundary root, with a planted violation (remove it, the guard fails). That is the FLN-STRUCT-037 move applied here: enforce that the enforcement exists, rather than reimplementing what it enforces.

It cannot land green today: step 1 fails on these 29 the moment it is added. Which is the sequencing question the orchestrator told me to raise before landing rather than after.

MY RECOMMENDATION: notes first, then lint and guard in ONE commit. The alternative -- landing the lint with the 29 carved out as per-site allow attributes -- writes 29 new bypasses into the crates whose entire purpose is that unsafe cannot be bypassed silently, and the e5k7 lesson is that a gate people must route around is a gate they learn to route around.

WHAT IS ALREADY MECHANISED, so nobody rebuilds it: the ledger ID join is total in both directions (180 rows against 180 allow sites, exactly), and the no-admission covenant has three layers (textual, type-aware, C-ABI). Only the note is unguarded.

cc_3, 2026-07-26: the count is CONFIRMED at 29, the enforcement is much further along than this bead's body says, and the declared-allowance approach DOES NOT FIT for the 28. One real gap found and closed. Verified at HEAD 3847fb04 and landed on top of it.

THE COUNT, RE-MEASURED RATHER THAN INHERITED. 29, and the same per-file split as the body, about nineteen commits after the original measurement. fln-unsafe-abi 28 (tests.rs 15, object.rs 11, membrane.rs 1, export.rs 1); fln-unsafe-region 1 (examples/region_trap_probe.rs); fln-unsafe-jit 0. The zero is new information: the body's clippy invocation named only abi and region, so jit had never been measured. It is clean.

WHAT IS ALREADY ENFORCED, and this materially corrects the body, which was written before FLN-STRUCT-040 landed in 5416810c:
  * The LEDGER ROW half is enforced in both directions, by FLN-STRUCT-013 (unledgered site) and FLN-STRUCT-014 (stale or mismatched row). 180 rows against 180 sites, and structure-guard reports PASS with 0 findings on the real tree right now. AGENTS.md's sentence "CI rejects an unledgered site" is TRUE.
  * BOTH D3 structural laws are walked. Law (a) is not merely true in fact, it is declared as prohibit fln-unsafe-* ->* fln-kernel and ->* fln-checker in ci/WORKSPACE_GRAPH.txt:98-99 and enforced by a transitive BFS over the REAL edge set derived from the Cargo.tomls, which reports the offending path. Law (b) has three layers as the body already recorded.
  * THE PROHIBITION IS LOAD-BEARING, NOT REDUNDANT, and this is the part worth knowing: fln-unsafe-jit is rank 12 and fln-kernel is rank 6, so FLN-STRUCT-007's strict-downward layering rule would PERMIT a jit-to-kernel edge. For rank-2 abi and region the rank rule happens to coincide with the prohibition; for jit it does not, and only the explicit prohibit line forbids it. Deleting those two lines as "already implied by layering" would silently unguard the one crate that sits above the kernel.
  * The SAFETY-note half is unenforced in fln-unsafe-abi, but it is no longer SILENT: FLN-STRUCT-040 requires every boundary root to enable the lint or carry a UNSAFE-NOTE-WAIVER naming a bead, and abi carries one naming this bead.

So the missing piece is the note and only the note, and the answer to "is AGENTS.md describing a mechanism or an intention" is: a mechanism for the ledger row and both structural laws, and a mechanically-declared intention for the note.

THE NEW GAP, FOUND AND CLOSED IN THIS CHANGE. FLN-STRUCT-040 read src/lib.rs and nothing else. A cargo target is its own crate root, so a library-root deny reaches neither examples/ nor tests/ nor benches/ nor src/bin/. fln-unsafe-region has the deny at src/lib.rs:21 and no waiver, so it READ AS ENFORCED - while its one undocumented block sat in examples/region_trap_probe.rs, covered by nothing. Verified by execution rather than by reading: cargo clippy -p fln-unsafe-region --all-targets -- -D warnings exited 0 with the block present. The posture check, whose whole purpose is to make the enforcement state visible, was itself producing a false clean.

Closed by extending FLN-STRUCT-040 to walk EVERY target root, and by making that example genuinely clean. Two planted violations, both killed: removing the deny from the example root now fires FLN-STRUCT-040 naming that exact file (previously nothing looked there), and deleting the note with the deny in place fails clippy.

AND THAT BLOCK WAS NEVER UNJUSTIFIED. It carried a full, careful note in a doc comment - "SAFETY: none claimed, this site deliberately breaks the sealed-region immutability invariant to prove the hardware trap" - just not where clippy reads. I relocated the AUTHOR'S OWN WORDS into block position and left the doc comment intact. I did not author a safety claim. This is exactly the case the body predicted when it said whoever takes this should triage the 29 rather than assume they are uniformly undocumented: the first one triaged was documented all along. The honest reading of "29" is 29 blocks whose justification a mechanical reader cannot see, not 29 unjustified blocks.

WHY THE DECLARED-ALLOWANCE SHAPE DOES NOT FIT THE REMAINING 28, tested rather than argued. The proposal was qydn's idiom: declare the sites so the twenty-ninth fails, and check the allowance in BOTH directions so it shrinks with each repair. The only mechanism that can decide "is this block documented" at site granularity without a second implementation of the lint is clippy itself, via #[expect].

  FORWARD DIRECTION WORKS. Root deny plus per-site #[expect] was measured: 28 sites, one expect planted, 27 errors remain; all 28 planted, clippy exits 0. A twenty-ninth undocumented block fails immediately.

  SHRINK DIRECTION DOES NOT. With all 28 declared and the crate compiling clean, I documented one site and left its #[expect] in place. Clippy reported nothing and exited 0. Forced rebuild, same result. A CONTROLLED COMPARISON isolates it: #[expect(unused_variables)] on a function with no unused variable DOES report "this lint expectation is unfulfilled" in this toolchain, so the mechanism exists and works - it simply does not fire for clippy's own lints here. So a per-site expect can rot: someone writes the note, forgets the attribute, and nothing ever says so.

Landing the forward half alone would have produced a list that grows correctly and never shrinks - a permanent hole wearing the costume of a shrinking debt, which is the opposite of what qydn's row records. I am not landing that and calling it both directions.

WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY WORK, for whoever takes it: run clippy in a lane and diff its reported site set against a declared list, in both directions - a site clippy reports that is not declared fails, and a declared site clippy no longer reports fails. That keeps clippy as the sole decider and gets both directions, but it is a CI lane rather than a structure-guard rule, so it belongs to whoever owns scripts/ and .github/.

WHAT THIS CHANGE DOES NOT ESTABLISH, stated plainly so the commit cannot be read as closing D3:
  * The 28 sites in fln-unsafe-abi REMAIN UNDOCUMENTED. Nothing here makes them safe and nothing here documents them.
  * A NEW undocumented block in fln-unsafe-abi still does not fail, because that crate's waiver is still in force. The twenty-ninth-site property exists today only for fln-unsafe-region and fln-unsafe-jit.
  * D3's SAFETY-note requirement is therefore still not enforced in full. What improved is that the enforcement state is now correctly reported for every target rather than only for library roots.

I am still not writing the 28 notes, for my predecessor's reason and the orchestrator's: a wrong SAFETY note at the TCB boundary is worse than a missing one, because the missing one is visibly absent and the wrong one is silently trusted.

BEAD STAYS OPEN. Gates in an isolated worktree at HEAD with only these two files: fmt clean, clippy --all-targets --no-deps -D warnings clean, cargo test --workspace exit 0 with ZERO skips, structure-guard's own 79 tests pass, structure-guard PASS 0 findings. ubs 0 critical. All runs local, not through rch.

title: fln-conformance: derive the corpus schema descriptors from SCHEMA_REGISTRY (Appendix B, corpus half)
description:
Split out of franken_lean-rps by cc_3 on 2026-07-25 when that bead closed on its delivered substance. This is the half of requirement (b) that fln-hash structurally cannot reach.

## What already exists

fln_hash::canon::SCHEMA_REGISTRY is the program's inventory of durable formats: eleven rows across fln-hash, fln-env and fln-verdict, each naming the format, its owning crate, and what it serializes (landed in f5a3944). It is enforced, not asserted: names unique and shaped, fln-hash's own rows joined against the real constants at compile time, and every owner's declaration file scanned and joined in BOTH directions, so an unregistered format fails and a row whose codec vanished fails. Plant-proved by removing a row and watching the cross-crate join fail with actionable instructions.

That satisfies the CODEC half of Appendix B: "every durable format specified once, generated into both the codecs and the conformance corpus".

## What is owed

The CONFORMANCE CORPUS half. Nothing in crates/fln-conformance derives its schema descriptors from SCHEMA_REGISTRY, so the corpus is not a projection of the registry — the two can disagree about which durable formats exist, what version each is at, and who owns them, and no artifact would notice. Appendix B wants one specification feeding both.

fln-hash cannot do this. The crate map (§21) points dependency edges strictly downward and fln-hash sits below fln-conformance, so it can never import upward to check or to generate. The work belongs to the Tribunal crate's owner. Note the direction that IS available and already used: the registry join reads other crates' SOURCE textually, because reading down-graph source is the only direction the layering allows.

## Acceptance Criteria

The conformance corpus's schema descriptors are derived from SCHEMA_REGISTRY rather than restated beside it, and a join proves it in both directions: a registry row with no corpus coverage fails, and a corpus descriptor naming no registry row fails. Version drift on either side fails. The derivation must be demonstrated against a planted mismatch in each direction, and must be shown to accept the clean tree, so it is not a blanket refusal. If the corpus legitimately covers only a subset of registered formats, that subset must be declared and justified per row rather than left implicit, since a silent partial projection reads as full coverage.

## Notes

Related and deliberately NOT folded in here: the cross-platform and multi-host identity claims, which are their own bead; and the second half of §7.3's two identities per stored object (semantic hash and byte hash), which franken_lean-iwu already owns through its acceptance that an olean to olean-next round trip preserves the semantic hash and, on the faithful path, the bytes.
close_reason: Delivered in c49909b3 and green: the conformance corpus is a projection of SCHEMA_REGISTRY, joined in both directions with planted mismatches each way, version drift failing from either side, and total coverage with no declared-exclusion variant. Judgement row authored in the same commit.

comments.author: cc_3
comments.text:
IMPLEMENTATION COMPLETE AND GREEN, UNCOMMITTED, HELD BY THE WRITE FREEZE. cc_3, 2026-07-25.

The orchestrator declared a write freeze so cod_2 can take the exclusive gate and run the full 13-stage scripts/check.sh after clearing the e5k7 backlog at 2cba4c79. My work for this bead is finished and passing, and it is sitting in the working tree UNCOMMITTED by instruction. I am not committing, not running cargo fmt, and not writing to any governed path until the orchestrator broadcasts GATE RELEASED. This comment is the durable record in the meantime.

WHAT IS IN THE TREE, five paths, all inside my domain except the lock:
  crates/fln-conformance/src/corpus.rs                     NEW, the projection
  crates/fln-conformance/tests/corpus_schema_projection.rs NEW, nine named suites
  crates/fln-conformance/src/lib.rs                        one pub mod line + one doc bullet
  crates/fln-conformance/Cargo.toml                        one new path dependency, fln-verdict
  Cargo.lock                                               exactly that one edge, nothing else

THE DESIGN, against this bead's acceptance criteria clause by clause.

"Derived rather than restated beside it." A CorpusDescriptor BORROWS its SchemaRow. Name, version, owner and the covers line exist only in fln-hash's registry. A CorpusCoverage has no owner field and no covers field at all, so there is nowhere in the corpus for either to be restated and drift. The only thing the corpus spells out is the join key, and the join is what makes that safe. This is a property of the types, not of a test, which is why the suite states it rather than tries to enforce it.

"A join proves it in both directions." project() reports Uncovered for a registry row nothing covers, Unregistered for a claim naming no row, and it reports EVERY disagreement at once, sorted and deduped, rather than stopping at the first. A one-at-a-time gate turns one edit into N runs; the message is meant to be the thing someone repairs the tree from.

"Version drift on either side fails." VersionDrift is its own fault, reported AS drift and not as the Uncovered plus Unregistered pair a name-only join would produce, because the two situations call for opposite repairs: one means re-verify the exercise against the new encoding, the other means add or delete a row. Both directions are planted.

"Demonstrated against a planted mismatch in each direction, and shown to accept the clean tree." Every plant drives the PRODUCTION join over perturbed copies of the real tables; the checked-in tables are never modified. That is the lesson already recorded in fln-hash's own suite - a mutation harness that re-implements the thing it mutates can report a false green - and it applies here unchanged.

"If the corpus legitimately covers only a subset, declare and justify per row." It does not cover a subset. All eleven registered formats have a runnable exercise and there is NO declared-exclusion variant, deliberately: section 21 puts fln-conformance last in the crate map, so an uncoverable row would be a layering claim that is not true. Covering fln-verdict's three wire formats costs one path dependency pointing downward like every other edge in this crate. I would rather the conditional in the acceptance criteria be satisfied vacuously than have a justified-exclusion mechanism that reads as an escape hatch the moment a format is inconvenient.

ONE THING I ADDED BEYOND THE ASK, because the bead's own fear demands it. The bead says a silent partial projection reads as full coverage. A coverage table whose rows are SENTENCES has the same defect one level up: it can claim anything and the name join still passes. So CorpusCoverage::run is a function pointer, not prose - to claim the corpus covers a format you must supply the exercise, and the suite runs all eleven. Each exercise is handed the row it is registered under and binds itself to that row's identity FIRST, against the type's own Canonical::SCHEMA for the term plane and against the owning crate's declared constant elsewhere. Without that a copy-pasted entry could cover one format twice while another went untested, and both directions of the name join would still pass. an_exercise_registered_under_the_wrong_row_is_refused is that guard, and it drives every descriptor against its neighbour's row.

projection_root() digests the whole descriptor set under Domain::CanonicalSchema - the domain already documented as "a canonical-serialization schema descriptor (self-describing corpora)", which had no consumer in the tree until now. Length-prefixed per field, and the suite plants a name/version/owner/covers/exercise change plus a field-boundary-ambiguity case and requires each to move the root.

IT CAUGHT A REAL DRIFT ON ITS FIRST RUN, which is the part worth keeping. I hand-wrote version 1 for all eleven rows. fln.canon.diag is at version 2 - bumped when the structural-budget resource tag was added, precisely so two artifacts labelled fln.canon.diag/1 could not both exist. The join refused with the drift message. The row is now at 2 AND the exercise gained a second case covering the KernelInconclusive value carrying that very tag, so the corpus witnesses what the bump was about rather than merely agreeing with the number. Moving the number alone is the failure my own error text warns against, and I was one edit away from it.

GATES, all run against the tree as of 12:49-12:52 EDT, all before the freeze:
  cargo fmt --check          clean, and the only file it touched was my own corpus.rs
  cargo check --all-targets  clean, workspace-wide, after the new dependency edge
  clippy -D warnings         clean on fln-conformance, --no-deps, run locally
  cargo test -p fln-conformance   green, EVERY suite in the crate, run locally
  cargo test --test corpus_schema_projection   9 passed
  ubs                        exit 0, 0 critical

ONE HONEST LIMIT ON THAT GREEN. My full-crate cargo test finished at about 12:49. At 12:52:36 another pane modified crates/fln-conformance/tests/kernel_replay.rs - binding KERNEL_REPLAY_WORKER_STACK_BYTES to Budget::MIN_STACK_BYTES, which is substantive work and not mine. So my whole-crate green predates that edit and does not cover it. My own two files are unaffected: the change is in a different test binary and touches nothing my suites read. I did not write that file, and my cargo fmt did not reformat it - the diff is seven insertions and three deletions, all semantic, no formatting hunks.

EXACT DIFF TO APPLY WHEN THE FREEZE LIFTS: none. The code is final and the message is written. The only remaining action is one command, which I will run only on GATE RELEASED:
  git commit -o crates/fln-conformance/src/corpus.rs crates/fln-conformance/tests/corpus_schema_projection.rs crates/fln-conformance/src/lib.rs crates/fln-conformance/Cargo.toml Cargo.lock
It carries no .beads path, so the voz4 projection guard has nothing to judge. The beads export is a separate commit and moves no bead ID, only this bead's status and comments, so the projection stays valid there too.

comments.text:
FOR cod_2: ONE LINE NEEDED IN ci/WORKSPACE_GRAPH.txt. cc_3, 2026-07-25, after the gate run at check-20260725T165436Z-3195200.

THE FINDING IS MINE AND IT IS REAL. structure-guard --test real_workspace raises FLN-STRUCT-005 on crates/fln-conformance/Cargo.toml: the dependency edge fln-conformance -> fln-verdict is not acknowledged. That edge comes from my uncommitted work for this bead. It is not in HEAD.

THE EXACT LINE, matching the file's grammar and the comment style of its neighbours. It belongs in the "acknowledged dependency edges" block, directly after the existing `edge fln-conformance -> fln-hash` line, which is where the other fln-conformance edges already cluster:

edge fln-conformance -> fln-verdict # corpus schema projection exercises the CNF/model/proof wire formats (franken_lean-dgxa)

I HAVE NOT COMMITTED, AND WILL NOT UNTIL THAT LINE LANDS, so HEAD never contains an unacknowledged edge. My working copy keeps structure-guard red in the meantime; that is the cost of sequencing it this way and I would rather pay it than push the red into HEAD.

WHY THE EDGE IS RIGHT, decided before asking rather than after, because the orchestrator's instruction was explicitly not to add an edge just to silence a finding.

1. IT POINTS STRICTLY DOWNWARD, which is the layering law the ranks exist to encode. fln-conformance is rank 22, fln-verdict is rank 13. 22 > 13.

2. IT IS A SHORTER REACH THAN EDGES ALREADY ACKNOWLEDGED. fln-conformance already declares edges to fln-core (rank 0), fln-hash (1), fln-env (4), fln-olean (5) and fln-kernel (6). An edge to rank 13 reaches LESS far down than five of the six edges this crate already has. If reaching into Verdict were a layering mistake, reaching into the kernel would be a worse one, and that edge is acknowledged with a bead citation.

3. NO PROHIBITION TOUCHES IT. All seven prohibit rules have fln-unsafe-*, fln-kernel or fln-checker as their source. fln-conformance is none of those, and it is kind=ordinary, not unsafe-boundary. Adding this edge creates no new transitive path that any rule forbids: fln-verdict depends on fln-core, fln-env and fln-kernel, and fln-conformance already depends on all three directly.

4. NO COVENANT TOUCHES IT. allow-direct binds exactly two crates, fln-kernel and fln-checker, and exists to keep the trust base's dependency closure on one page. fln-conformance is not in the trust base; it observes it.

5. IT IS WHAT THE CRATE MAP MEANS. AGENTS.md's §21 note is "Palimpsest and Tribunal observe everything and control nothing", and fln-conformance is placed LAST at rank 22 precisely so it can observe every subsystem without any subsystem observing it. Nothing in the workspace depends on fln-conformance (checked: it appears in no other crate's Cargo.toml), so this edge cannot pull Verdict into anyone's closure but the Tribunal's own.

WHY THE ALTERNATIVE — "move the shared type down" — IS THE WRONG REPAIR HERE, which I checked rather than assumed. What I need from fln-verdict is Cnf, SatModel and UnsatProof with their to_canonical_bytes/from_canonical_bytes pairs, plus the three SchemaId constants. Those ARE Verdict's durable wire formats. Relocating them downward would contradict a decision the architecture has already made and written down, in crates/fln-hash/src/canon.rs beside SCHEMA_REGISTRY itself:

  "Formats live in the crate that encodes them - the registry does not centralize the CODECS, only the IDENTITIES. That is forced by the crate map (§21): dependency edges point strictly downward and fln-hash sits below fln-env and fln-verdict, so this crate cannot import their constants even to compare them."

The registry is deliberately a table of identities precisely BECAUSE the codecs cannot be moved down. Moving Verdict's codec into the term plane to spare the Tribunal one edge would invert that, and it would put a rank-13 subsystem's wire formats below rank 4.

THE ONLY REAL ALTERNATIVE, stated so the choice is visible rather than implied: drop the three fln.verdict.* rows from the corpus and mark them as a declared, justified exclusion. That is explicitly permitted by this bead's acceptance criteria. I rejected it, and I want the reason on the record because it is a judgment and not a fact: an exclusion mechanism that exists gets used, and the first thing it would be used for is the format that is inconvenient to reach. The bead's own fear is that a silent partial projection reads as a full one; a DECLARED partial projection is better than a silent one, but a total projection with no escape hatch at all is better than both, and it costs exactly one acknowledged edge that the layering already permits. Eleven of eleven registered formats now have a runnable exercise.

WHAT I NEED, concretely: cod_2 applies the one line above. I commit immediately after and re-run structure-guard to confirm FLN-STRUCT-005 clears. If cod_2 judges the edge wrong, say so on this bead and I will convert the three verdict rows to a declared exclusion with per-row justification instead, drop the dependency from Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock, and the bead still closes against its acceptance criteria - just weaker. That call is cod_2's to make on ci/'s behalf and I will take it either way.

title: scripts/check.sh cannot pass: 87 beads owe VERIFICATION_MANIFEST coverage rows, and the gate stops at stage 2 of 13
description:
MEASURED, not inferred, by PeachBass on 2026-07-25 from a full gate run someone else launched: target/check/check-20260725T145840Z-2329904, bundle verdict fail, process_exit 1.

WHAT HAPPENS. The check.sh stage verification-manifest raises:
  ci/VERIFICATION_MANIFEST.jsonl: beads crossed the adoption boundary without coverage rows: [87 ids]
check.sh stops on the first failure, so ELEVEN of the thirteen stages then record not_run: shellcheck, fmt, check, clippy, test, tribunal-manifest-inventory, epoch-lab-test, epoch-lab-live-verify, structure-guard, vendor-tree, ubs. The gate is failing at stage 2 of 13 and has not reached a compiler, a test, or the structural guard.

THE RULE, read from scripts/evidence.py rather than guessed. VERIFICATION_ADOPTION_AUTHORITY_HASH (evidence.py line 55) freezes a grandfathered adoption set. The validator then computes:
  required_coverage = current_ids - adopted
  required_coverage += every adopted bead that was OPEN at adoption time and is no longer open
  missing_coverage = required_coverage - coverage_rows_present
So EVERY bead created after the freeze owes a row in ci/VERIFICATION_MANIFEST.jsonl, and every grandfathered-open bead owes one the moment it moves. The manifest currently holds 20 records. 87 ids are missing.

WHY IT REACHED 87 RATHER THAN BEING CAUGHT AT 1. Same structural shape as franken_lean-projection-republish-mechanical-voz4, one level worse. The obligation attaches at bead creation; nothing at bead creation mentions it; and unlike the ownership projection - whose staleness surfaces in cargo test, which everyone runs constantly - this one surfaces ONLY in a full check.sh, which is expensive, needs the exclusive gate slot, and is therefore run rarely. So it accumulated silently. The missing ids include beads closed on 2026-07-24, which dates the failure to at least then.

SCOPE OF THE EVIDENCE, stated so nobody over-reads it. I did not run check.sh; I read the bundle of a run that another pane launched at 14:58:40Z. I have not established WHEN the gate last passed, and I have not established that the eleven not_run stages would pass if reached - only that they did not run. Nobody should read this bead as either a claim that the rest of the gate is green or a claim that it is not.

AND YES, FILING THIS MAKES IT 88. That is not a joke at the bead's expense, it is the finding: an obligation that grows with every bead anyone files, enforced only by a gate too expensive to run often, converges on always-failing. The two questions are separable and should be answered separately:
  1. THE BACKLOG. 87 rows across many owners and workstreams. Not one agent's job, and the rows are not mechanical - a coverage row names claim type, evidence kind, scenarios, invariants and gate ids, which is a judgment about what the bead actually verified.
  2. THE MECHANISM. Whatever the backlog answer, the same accumulation restarts tomorrow unless coverage is demanded at a moment someone is present. Options in the shape voz4 settled: refuse at bead creation (needs a br wrapper), refuse at commit (the pre-commit guard from voz4 already exists and could carry this check too, at the cost of making every bead-creating commit owe a hand-written coverage row), or run the validator in the cheap cargo-test lane rather than only in check.sh so staleness surfaces in minutes rather than days. My read: the third, first - it is the smallest change that converts a silent multi-day accumulation into an immediate one, and it does not require deciding the backlog question first.

I am not claiming either question. I found this while verifying my own work did not break the gate; it did not, and the failure predates it.

DESIGN DECISION: serialized close-with-coverage wrapper; no time-based grace.

The first post-enforcement gate caught fln-zti3 within ten minutes, and the
next publication attempt then caught franken_lean-c24a closing concurrently.
That proves both halves of the diagnosis: early enforcement is working, and a
human cod_2 handoff on every close is an unacceptable serialization point.

I am choosing the required-argument wrapper shape. The bead owner supplies:

1. the bead id;
2. the close reason through a file;
3. one canonical fln.verification-manifest/1 complete coverage row through a
   file.

The wrapper will take one repository-local publication lock, verify that the
row names exactly the bead being closed, construct and validate the prospective
closed tracker plus manifest before mutation, call br close and br sync, then
publish the canonically sorted manifest through a candidate plus atomic rename.
Peers will not hand-edit ci/VERIFICATION_MANIFEST.jsonl; the checked-in wrapper
is its mechanical writer. The existing prospective-tree pre-commit guard stays
as defense in depth and catches direct br close or a wrapper failure before the
debt reaches HEAD.

Why this option:

- evidence judgment remains with the bead owner who has the implementation and
  terminal evidence;
- serialization is a short machine critical section, not cod_2 inbox latency;
- the close and its obligation are presented together rather than repaired
  later;
- a grace period would make correctness depend on wall-clock or session state
  and would recreate the silent backlog in a softer form;
- per-bead fragments followed by a later merge still leave the canonical
  publication stale unless the validator grows a second source of truth.

The immediate zti3/c24a backlog will be cleared first and the full gate rerun
before this mechanism is expanded, preserving the established backlog-first,
enforcement-second ordering.

title: fln-env: effective_imports substitutes an empty first-discovery witness path instead of faulting
description:
Found by a mock-code / placeholder audit of crates/fln-env (PeachBass, pane cc_1, 2026-07-24). Category: silently-ignored error path.

DEFECT: crates/fln-env/src/effective_imports.rs:884

    let first_path = route_witness.paths.first().cloned().unwrap_or_default();

If a ComponentWitness ever carries an empty paths list, this substitutes a DEFAULT (empty) ImportWitnessPath and publishes it as the module's first_discovery witness. An empty path is a plausible-looking value that says "discovered via no import path at all", which is not true of any discovered module.

CONFIDENCE AND SEVERITY: this is P3 because the empty case appears unreachable today. ComponentWitness::root() seeds paths with exactly one ImportWitnessPath and append extends an existing witness, so paths is non-empty by construction along every path I traced. I did NOT prove the invariant holds under every future edit, and I did not find a way to reach it now — so this is a latent robustness defect, not a live bug. It is filed rather than dropped because the substitution is silent: if the invariant ever breaks, the closure reports a confident-looking wrong witness instead of failing.

WHY IT IS INCONSISTENT WITH THE SURROUNDING CODE: this module already models exactly this situation as a typed fault. ClosureInternalFault has a MissingComponentWitness variant (component, source, direct_row_index) used elsewhere for precisely "a witness component that should exist does not". Per FL-INV-07 an internal invariant failure must surface as a typed InternalFault, never as a fabricated value.

FIX: replace the unwrap_or_default with the existing typed fault path — return ClosureStatus::InternalFault with ClosureInternalFault::MissingComponentWitness naming the component, source, and direct row index — so a broken invariant is reported rather than papered over. Alternatively, if the invariant is genuinely structural, encode it in the type (a NonEmpty witness, or a first_path field on ComponentWitness populated at construction) so the empty case becomes unrepresentable and the unwrap disappears.

TESTS TO ADD: a unit test constructing a ComponentWitness with an empty paths list and asserting the closure reports InternalFault rather than a witness with an empty first_discovery path. If the type-level route is taken instead, the test becomes a compile-fail or is unnecessary, and that should be recorded in the closing note.

SCOPE: entirely inside crates/fln-env. No pin, census, or scripts change.
close_reason:
FIXED and CLOSED in commit 0f8ded4. Found by my own mock-code audit of crates/fln-env; nothing owed, no residual, no split.

THE DEFECT: propagate_candidate ended with route_witness.paths.first().cloned().unwrap_or_default(), so an absent route path became ImportWitnessPath::default() — an empty path published as the module's FIRST DISCOVERY, asserting it was reached by no import at all. Same substitute-a-plausible-default class as the f6br witness collision, and worse than a loud failure because nothing downstream can distinguish "discovered via no path" from "we lost the path".

THE FIX: ok_or_else(|| fault(WitnessComponent::FirstDiscovery))?. The enclosing function already returns Result<_, ClosureInternalFault> and already carried a `fault` closure for exactly this situation, so the fix uses the seam the module already had rather than inventing one. Under FL-INV-07 an invariant failure is an InternalFault, never a fabricated result.

WitnessComponent gained a FirstDiscovery arm rather than borrowing Data's. A missing route witness is a different failure from a missing data or import-all witness and reporting it as one would have been a smaller version of the same dishonesty. The enum is only ever constructed, never matched exhaustively, so the arm is additive and breaks nothing.

REACHED HONESTLY, NOT BY A BACKDOOR: the state is unreachable in normal operation — ComponentWitness::root seeds one path and append only extends — which is exactly why it must fault rather than default. The test drives the real production path: with every component witness absent the route is parent.route_witness.append(..), and append maps over paths, so an empty parent route stays empty. GlobalOLeanLevel::Server requests IR globally so the candidate is not short-circuited as uninteresting before the route witness is built.

MUTATION EVIDENCE: restoring unwrap_or_default() fails the new test, and the failure output IS the defect — first_discovery: ImportWitnessPath { steps: [] } returned inside a successful Some(Candidate { .. }). Reverted to zero residue. The test also asserts the non-blanket half: the identical request with a seeded route witness still yields a candidate whose first-discovery witness has exactly one real step and is distinguishable from the default, so the fault is about missing evidence and not about the request.

GATES: rch exec -- cargo test --locked -p fln-env 137/137 (136 before); fmt clean; clippy -p fln-env --all-targets -D warnings exit 0; UBS on effective_imports.rs exits 0 with 0 CRITICALS and 0 panics, HEAD and working identical. That is a genuinely clean UBS read rather than the usual two false-positive classes, because this file contains no enum-equality or panic patterns.

title: W12: Front doors — lean/leanc/lake personalities + the fln multiplexer verbs
description:
Implement the toolchain front doors (§17.1, fln-cli): the binaries lean, leanc (the C-driver personality: flag-compatible, driving the D2 cc when present, explaining its absence via capability errors when not), lake, and the fln multiplexer exposing the new verbs — check-olean, audit (--tcb), replay, doctor (--sql), cache, olean, goals, serve-mcp, why-trusts, diff, build explain, server replay, verify-capsule, identity.

Contract: flags, exit codes, env vars (LEAN_PATH, LEAN_SYSROOT), and --json shapes pinned to the Reference at the pin (CLI transcript corpus, C-family fixtures); --trust levels ACCEPTED with upstream semantics but journaled into receipts and surfaced by fln audit rather than silently honored (BN-09); new flags live under --fln-* only; the version line stays parse-compatible (Reference version/commit fields preserved) with a separate machine-readable implementation field — compatibility never becomes deception, and an exact-reference transcript mode exists for conformance harnesses only. Robot-mode discipline per AGENTS.md: stable versioned schemas, deterministic where possible, explicit exit codes, line-oriented output, no human decoration mixed into machine streams.

Acceptance: the CLI transcript corpus diffs clean against the Reference for the shared surface; each fln verb has a --json schema contract test against a frozen fixture; elan invokes the binaries transparently via the release layout (verified in W12). Tests: golden transcripts per verb (human and JSON modes) with detailed logging of any drift; exit-code matrix fixtures; --trust journaling fixtures; capability-error fixtures for missing cc/git naming the alternative.

## Acceptance Criteria

All bead-specific requirements, acceptance conditions, tests, invariants, compatibility surfaces, evidence levels, performance gates, negative/recovery cases, and user-visible behaviors stated above remain mandatory. In addition, the MANDATORY VERIFICATION DEFINITION OF DONE in Notes must be satisfied with named unit/property/mutation suites, at least one shared real-path no-mock E2E scenario plus failure/recovery coverage, detailed human and schema-versioned NDJSON artifacts, and reproducible close evidence. No listed feature or claim may be silently narrowed, deferred, mocked, or declared complete through an unclassified divergence.
design: REVIEW AMENDMENT — this is the final front-door integration, not an early flag parser. Every advertised verb must route to its real owning subsystem and the fln library API: check-olean, audit/why-trusts/diff/replay/doctor, Lake/build-explain, cache, olean/capsules, goals, serve-mcp, server replay, and identity/Witness facts. title: Six scratch producers outside structure-guard still retain every root: 15,894 dirs / 350 MiB, blocked on where the shared reclaimer lives
description:
## Finding

`franken_lean-s2sn` routed every `tools/structure-guard` scratch producer through one
reclaimer and measured 49 retained directories per suite run before, 0 after. It repaired
89.2% of the live leak and named the rest. This bead carries the rest, with the census
already made so nobody re-derives it.

Six producers still retain every scratch root they create, on the passing path as well as
the failing one, with nothing ever reclaiming them. Measured at 2026-07-28 16:19 local
against `/data/tmp`, allocated bytes via `st_blocks * 512`:

  producer                                                    dirs   allocMiB
  crates/fln-conformance/src/ownership.rs:2329                13919      258.3
  crates/fln-conformance/tests/evidence_finalization.rs:3326   1727       68.7
  crates/fln-syntax/tests/golden_vellum.rs:782                   98       20.4
  crates/fln-conformance/tests/gate_lock_discriminator.rs:54     65        1.5
  tribunal/epoch-lab/tests/epoch_lab_hash_chain.rs:23            40        0.5
  tribunal/epoch-lab/tests/derived_input_provenance.rs:294       20        0.5
  crates/fln-kernel/tests/reference_differential.rs:130          25        0.2
  TOTAL                                                       15894      350.1

Still growing at the census: five of the seven had roots less than three hours old.
Independently confirmed after `s2sn` landed — one full `cargo test --workspace` on the
patched tree with a private `TMPDIR` left 99 directories, ZERO of them from any
structure-guard family and every one of them from this list.

## The decision this bead exists to force, stated without pre-judging it

The reclaimer landed in `tools/structure-guard/src/scratch.rs`, a `kind=tool` crate. None of
the crates above can reach it, and the two obvious repairs are both real choices rather than
implementation details:

OPTION A — give `fln-conformance` its own copy. Cheapest by far, and it covers 328.5 of the
350.1 MiB, since three of the seven producers live there and would need no graph change at
all. It plants a SECOND COPY OF THE FENCE, which is
`franken_lean-evidence-python-config-rule-drift-imuu`'s defect exactly: two unbound copies of
one rule, free to drift, with nothing joining them. `s2sn` declined this on purpose.

OPTION B — move the reclaimer somewhere both `tools/*` and `crates/*` can reach. `fln-core` is
rank 0 and every affected crate already sits above it, so no new edge is needed for the
`crates/*` members; `tools/structure-guard` is `kind=tool` and exempt from layering by
`FLN-STRUCT-007`, so it can depend downward freely. This keeps one fence. It puts test-support
code in a product crate, which is a judgement about what `fln-core` is for.

OPTION C — leave them. Defensible for `fln-kernel` (25 dirs, 0.2 MiB) and arguably for
`gate_lock_discriminator` (65, 1.5 MiB); indefensible for `ownership.rs`, which is 13,919
directories and the largest producer by COUNT in the entire workspace.

The graph is not this bead's to change. Whoever owns it should pick, and the picking is the
work — the mechanical part is a two-line change per producer once the address is settled.

## Scope

Route every producer above through ONE reclamation predicate, whichever address the decision
lands on, preserving retention on the failing path exactly as `s2sn` did: `Drop` checks
`std::thread::panicking()`, a failing test keeps its root and still prints a retention line,
only the passing path reclaims. Prove both directions per producer family — a passing root
asserted GONE and a failing one asserted STILL PRESENT under `catch_unwind`, because
`panicking()` is only true during an unwind and a cell that merely ASKS cannot observe it.

`tribunal/epoch-lab` is a NESTED workspace with its own `Cargo.lock`. `cargo test --workspace`
never walks it, which is why its two producers are absent from the post-`s2sn` workspace
measurement — absence there is the glob's boundary and not evidence of a repair. It carries
the same manifest constraint `kernel-ownership-publisher` does and may end up a declared
remainder for the same reason; if so, declare it with the reason rather than omitting it.

REMOVE NOTHING. The 33,928 directories already on disk are
`fln-fixture-retention-unbounded-evit` item 1, parked with the repository owner. This is
growth-bounding only, under the orchestrator's recorded 2026-07-26 ruling that a harness
reclaiming its own scratch directory is ordinary hygiene rather than an agent deleting files.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Every producer in the table either routes through a single shared reclamation predicate or
   is a declared remainder carrying its own reason, with conservation checked in both
   directions so the remainder cannot be emptied by deleting a row instead of routing a
   producer.
2. Exactly one copy of the fence and one `Drop` body exists across the whole workspace after
   this lands. If the decision is Option A, this criterion is knowingly waived and the waiver
   must say so in those words.
3. Retention on failure is preserved for every converted producer, proved in BOTH directions
   rather than inferred from the passing cell.
4. A before/after directory count over one full `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` with a
   private `TMPDIR` on both sides, measured on ALLOCATED blocks. The expected after-count is 0
   for every converted family and unchanged for any declared remainder.
5. The four mandated gates pass, run locally rather than through the RCH hook, and the exact
   changed Rust files receive a completed UBS scan with a same-path baseline.

## Evidence class and limits

Claim class `bounded_model` for the census: one host, one instant, one `/data/tmp`. The
absolute figures are properties of this box under this swarm's load on this day and must not
be carried forward — re-measure before acting on any of them, and record the commit you
measured at.

WHAT THE CENSUS DOES NOT COVER, stated so this bead is not read as the whole population. The
scan is `std::env::temp_dir()` ONLY. A harness writing scratch state anywhere else is
invisible to it, and at least one such site already exists INSIDE the repository —
`crates/fln-conformance/target/fln-worker-refusal-*`, produced by
`crates/fln-conformance/tests/evidence_finalization.rs:1531`, which is a different site in the
same file as the `fln-rch-` producer above. It is untouched, uncounted, and named here rather
than left to be discovered. Anything behind an `#[ignore]` or a feature gate is likewise
outside both the census and the workspace-run confirmation.

The value side of retention remains unpriced, exactly as `evit` left it: nobody has measured
how often a retained fixture is actually READ after a failure. Retention on the failing path
is preserved BECAUSE that price is unknown, not because it has been shown to be worth it.

Remainders declared: publisher, epoch-lab x2.

title: W7: Engine-backed tactic facade integration — simp, norm_num, omega, bv_decide, grind
description:
Complete the engine-backed core-tactic surface after the W6 native tactic framework and W7 engines exist. Wire the stable facade/dispatch contracts to the faithful simp core, norm_num and omega certificate producers, Verdict bv_decide, and native grind; execute both direct core invocations and real Golem-hosted user tactics through CoreM/MetaM/TermElabM/TacticM; require every produced declaration to pass Crucible and the configured consensus policy (FL-INV-02/06).

This bead removes a stage-order contradiction: W6 owns goal/state/backtracking/InfoTree semantics and the bootstrap-safe primitive tactic set; W7 owns these engine-backed rows. Until this bead lands, the corresponding census rows remain at their honest L0/L1 state and return precise typed Unsupported results where invoked — no fake implementation, compatibility shim, or hidden oracle.

Acceptance: the metaprogram corpus exercises each engine-backed row through the production facade; environments, InfoTrees, diagnostics, generated names, tactic state/backtracking, and goal-closure behavior match the Reference at each row's declared comparison class; simp/grind decision traces replay; norm_num/omega/Verdict certificates replay through Crucible; unsupported markers for the completed rows disappear only when their evidence rows promote.

Verification: per-row unit and negative tests, backtracking/failure-atomicity properties, bogus-certificate and direct-admission mutation tests, budget/cancellation scenarios, and shared no-mock E2E scripts running real tactic files on Golem with detailed step, trace, receipt, and first-divergence logging.

## Acceptance Criteria

All bead-specific requirements, acceptance conditions, tests, invariants, compatibility surfaces, evidence levels, performance gates, negative/recovery cases, and user-visible behaviors stated above remain mandatory. In addition, the MANDATORY VERIFICATION DEFINITION OF DONE in Notes must be satisfied with named unit/property/mutation suites, at least one shared real-path no-mock E2E scenario plus failure/recovery coverage, detailed human and schema-versioned NDJSON artifacts, and reproducible close evidence. No listed feature or claim may be silently narrowed, deferred, mocked, or declared complete through an unclassified divergence.

Every completed engine-backed facade row for simp, norm_num, omega, bv_decide, and grind dispatches through the production Native Mirror and real Golem-hosted CoreM/MetaM/TermElabM/TacticM path as well as direct core APIs; W6 goal/state/backtracking/InfoTree semantics are preserved. Simp/grind traces, environments, diagnostics, generated names, goals and comparison classes match the Reference at each row declared evidence level. norm_num/omega/Verdict certificates are versioned, resource-bounded, replayed by Crucible, and subject to configured consensus before any declaration publishes under FL-INV-02/06. Rows promote from precise typed Unsupported only after their exact fixtures and Parity Ledger evidence pass; no placeholder or hidden oracle. Per-row unit/property/model tests cover success, failure, backtracking, state rollback, diagnostic/InfoTree shape, budgets, cancellation, malformed input, and recovery; named bogus-certificate, direct-admission, skipped-kernel-check, wrong-dispatch, state-leak, and false-promotion mutants are killed. A real no-mock E2E runs representative tactic files on Golem for every row, plants trace/certificate/budget/cancellation failures, restores exact inputs, and emits strictly validated detailed bundles with row, trace, receipt, roots, first divergence, cleanup, and final state. No direct-API-only proof, fake success, unchecked engine output, unsupported row silently swallowed, mock-only tactic, overclaimed L-level, or deferred listed behavior satisfies closure.

Verify both direct engine calls and the real Golem façade path. Unsupported, cancellation, resource, malformed artifact, or engine failure rolls tactic state and evidence publication back exactly. Named suites: engine_row_promotion_model, engine_tactic_state_rollback, engine_facade_no_mock_e2e.

W6-W8 EVIDENCE CONTRACT — canonical schema-versioned semantic NDJSON is validated independently; telemetry remains separate and non-authoritative. Unknown schema, missing/duplicate ids, broken order/linkage, unbound artifacts, truncation, merged streams, or cleanup/final-state mismatch fail. Cancellation/exhaustion/InternalFault never enters cache, negative storage, admission, publication, or promotion. Productive 1/8/32 evidence proves useful work and deterministic reduction. MANDATORY VERIFICATION DEFINITION OF DONE (inherits franken_lean-rur; additive to this bead's own Tests/Acceptance):
1. Unit coverage: deterministic happy-path, boundary, malformed-input, resource-exhaustion, cancellation, and failure-atomicity cases for every new public behavior; property/metamorphic and mutation-kill tests wherever an invariant or equivalence is claimed.

title: Verification manifest accepts evidence paths after their referents are pruned
description:
## Finding

The verification manifest accepts ephemeral filesystem paths as durable evidence citations, so a row remains green after a janitor removes the object it cites.

Measured on 2026-07-26:

- `fln-sn0w` cited `target/check/check-20260726T212528Z-2388936`. The directory still existed when this finding was filed, approximately 95 minutes after production, only because the orchestrator prune had not yet reached it.
- `franken_lean-lu5` cited `target/check/check-20260725T190953Z-814126/bundle.complete.json`. That file was already absent.
- `validate-verification-manifest` did not distinguish the live path from the dead path and remained green at HEAD. The manifest checks array shape and closure timing, not artifact durability.
- The destroying tool was the orchestrator tick, which pruned `target/check` at 180 and 360 minutes. Both prunes have been removed, stopping further damage but not restoring the lost lu5 referent.

This is the empty-referent defect family: a claim and citation remain while the far end disappears without changing either governed input. An existence check alone is insufficient because it only moves the race to validation time; a path that exists during validation can still be pruned one minute later, and a fresh clone never contains ignored `target/` state.

## Repair decision

Terminal manifest evidence must not cite `target/` or another ignored/untracked path. The validator should classify artifact strings and enforce:

1. Structured durable references such as `bead-comment:<bead>:<id>` are checked by their owning authority.
2. A repository path citation must normalize inside the repository, be a regular non-symlink file, and be Git-tracked. Existence without tracked durability does not count.
3. A transient run may be cited only after publishing a compact, revalidatable receipt into a tracked durable evidence namespace; the manifest cites that tracked receipt, not the transient run directory. Copying to another untracked directory is not publication.
4. Commit-anchor reachability is orthogonal and remains owned by the history-anchor bead; this repair must not claim that any resolvable object is reachable from `main`.
5. Existing dead citations are repaired honestly. In particular, the missing lu5 bundle cannot be recreated by changing its path string: its owner must supply extant durable evidence, downgrade the row, or record the loss.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `validate-verification-manifest` rejects a `target/` citation even when the target currently exists, proving the rule is durability-based rather than a time-of-check existence probe.
- It rejects missing, absolute, escaping, symlinked, directory, ignored, and untracked path citations with typed reasons that name the row and artifact.
- It accepts tracked regular-file citations and supported structured references without requiring transient build output.
- Seeded controls cover both a currently present transient path and an already absent one; neither can score as durable.
- **SUPERSEDED 2026-07-27 — TIGHTENED, not weakened. The original is quoted verbatim here so a replaced criterion is never indistinguishable from one that was never met.** ORIGINAL: "The live manifest contains zero `target/` artifact citations." REPLACEMENT: **the live manifest contains zero UNTRACKED path citations.** FALSIFYING MEASUREMENT, at `9b6a7dfa`, manifest sha256 `d5715feb3ca3bff3`, over 584 artifact entries in 189 coverage rows: **18** repo-relative path citations do not resolve, of which **only 3** are under `target/`, so the original read literally leaves **15 dangling**. Both directions, so this cannot be misread: the original catches **3 of 18**, tracked-ness catches **18 of 18**. It is a tightening because every citation the original rejects the replacement also rejects — `.gitignore` line 2 is `/target`, so a `target/` path is never git-tracked — and it additionally rejects the 15 the original admits. The measurement is recorded immutably in this bead's comment log. Every migrated terminal row retains an honest evidence class and cites only evidence that still exists; unrecoverable evidence is disclosed rather than synthesized.
- The three shapes are separated rather than counted together, because a single check treating them alike is wrong three ways. (a) **Referent PRODUCED AND THEN REMOVED** — 3 citations at `9b6a7dfa`, all under `target/`, two of them created after this bead was filed. That is this bead. (b) **Referent NEVER EXISTED IN ANY COMMIT** — 6 citations naming 5 paths, each with zero commits under `git log --all`; the sharpest is `crates/fln-syntax/src/syntax.rs`, cited by two rows, when the real file is and always was `crates/fln-syntax/src/tree.rs`. Those never denoted anything and did not rot, so they belong to `fln-0rxm`. (c) **Rootless run-directory fragments** — 9 citations, classified by shape only; whose bead they are is a judgement about intent nobody has made, and it is left open rather than absorbed here.
- A compact receipt publication format, if introduced, binds the producer run id, verdict, input/final roots, bundle/manifest/run-log digests, producing commit, and evidence class, with a validator that rejects missing or mismatched fields. Full bundles are not copied into Git without an explicit size/retention policy.
- The verification-manifest self-test and conformance coverage plant deletion, present-but-ephemeral, untracked-copy, symlink, traversal, and tracked-receipt mutants; each is killed for its stated reason.
- The ownership projection, sparse coverage row, beads export, validator changes, migrated rows, and any durable receipt are committed atomically where their contracts require it.
notes:
STATE 2026-07-28. POVO DOES NOT CLOSE, CRITERION 5 BLOCKS, AND THE BLOCKER IS ADOPTION RATHER
THAN IMPLEMENTATION. This bead is BLOCKED ON A DECISION, NOT ON WORK. Decision-holder: cod_2
(ci/ is their sole authority). Read comment 1555, then 1554; 1554 corrects 1550.

NOTHING ON THIS BEAD IS PICKABLE. Do not take it from br ready expecting work: the half that
could be built without the decision is built and green (fa9729d8, bad6c5bd). Every remaining

WHY NOTES AND NOT ONLY A COMMENT. br show prints this mutable field ABOVE the immutable log, so
a reader who starts at the top meets this and may never reach the comments. A correction filed
only as a comment is effectively reverted by the summary standing over it -- this project has a
recorded case. So a correction goes in BOTH: the immutable record in the log, the pointer here.

THE DECISION (cod_2): mint ci/VERIFICATION_EVIDENCE_RECEIPTS.jsonl via a frozen migration --
adoption_projection_hash, a legacy-authority hash bound to a named migration_commit,
record_count, target_artifact_ceiling == 0, every legacy-artifact row content-addressed by
pair_id and refused unless its pair was present at migration. A second decision follows it:
whether the Rust debt table survives adoption or is deleted in favour of the registry.

THE WORK (five other owners): the 7 citations enumerated in comment 1554 must be repaired or
withdrawn first, because target_path raises BEFORE the legacy allowance is consulted. None is
mine to touch.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE, and it is not what comment 1550 says:
  - scripts/evidence.py ALREADY implements this bead's repair decision, COMMITTED at HEAD, with
    the same (bead, artifact) keying I built in Rust. Criteria 1, 2, 3 and 7 are IMPLEMENTED.
  - It validates NOTHING: the registry has never been minted, so validate-verification-manifest
    reports not_adopted_registry_absent, scans 608 pairs, validates 0, and exits 0. Measured
    from the committed copy and the h4o1 working copy separately; identical, so the orphan is
    NOT the cause. The orphan holds criteria 4 and 8 -- 510 uncommitted self-test lines.
  - VERIFICATION_LEGACY_TRACKING_BEAD names THIS bead in their code, so povo is the designated
    owner of the legacy debt and cannot close while it exists.

THE OPERATIVE NUMBER IS 7, NOT 150: 143 of the 150 untracked citations are adoptable as frozen
legacy rows; 7 must be repaired or withdrawn (the 3 on non-terminal beads are a SUBSET of those
7). Those 7 are exactly the pruned ephemeral run directories this bead was FILED for.

CRITERIA: 1,2,3,7 implemented-and-inert | 4,8 written-and-uncommitted (h4o1) | 5 UNMET, 150 live
-- THE BLOCKER | 6 met | 9 not reached.

THE 322c40e0 MISCLASSIFICATION WAS TRACKED-NESS — the same predicate this bead's amended criterion turns on, which makes it evidence for the criterion rather than a neighbouring curiosity

Filed by cc_3 (pane 4) on the sequencer's observation. Recorded here rather than only on
`fln-0rxm`, because the shared predicate is the point.

## THE FACT

`fln-0rxm`'s census classified an artifact citation by **shape first** — no `/`, therefore no
root, therefore nothing to resolve against — and tested **tracked-ness second**. So a citation
naming a tracked file at the repository root scored as *never-denoted*: `AGENTS.md` fourteen
times, `README.md` four, plus `Cargo.lock`, `rust-toolchain.toml`, `ABI_CONTRACT.md`,
`OLEAN_CONTRACT.md` — **22 citations across 14 rows**, every one denoting exactly one file.
Repaired at `322c40e0` by testing tracked-ness first; `rootless_leaf` 121 -> 99.

## WHY IT BELONGS ON THIS BEAD

povo's repair decision (criterion 2) is that a repository path citation must "normalize inside
the repository, be a regular non-symlink file, and be **Git-tracked**. Existence without
tracked durability does not count." That is the same predicate, and `322c40e0` is now direct
evidence for two properties of it that were previously only asserted:

1. **Tracked-ness is a total, unambiguous discriminator and shape is not.** `AGENTS.md`
   resolves to exactly one file with no root supplied by the checker, because `git ls-files`
   contains the string verbatim. Any classifier that reasons about the *form* of the string
   before consulting the tracked set will get this class wrong — which is exactly what
   happened, silently, for the whole life of that census.
2. **Order matters, and the wrong order fails in the over-reporting direction.** The census
   over-stated its own defect population by 22 and was never at risk of hiding one. povo's
   criterion inherits that safety only if it, too, consults the tracked set before any
   shape-based reasoning about `target/`, globs or rootless leaves.

**Concretely, for povo's own numbers:** this bead's population script has always tested
`a in tracked` first and has therefore always reported `rootless_leaf 99` — the correct figure
— while the census reported 120. The two disagreed for the whole time both existed and nobody
compared them, because they report different TOTALS (150 untracked vs 178 unresolvable) and
there was no reason to line up a sub-class. **A second implementation earns its cost precisely
where the first is confidently wrong, and the comparison that finds it is a CLASS, not a
total.** Whoever builds povo's enforcement should therefore keep the population script as an
independent second reading rather than folding it into the validator, and reconcile them
per-class.

## THE PATTERN THE SEQUENCER NAMED, WITH ITS LIMIT

Three populations turned out **smaller** than their first measurement today — 786 of a true
1880 denominator, 150 naive against a real 3, and 121 -> 99 — and every one was found by
**re-deriving**, never by re-reading. That is worth carrying as a habit and NOT as a law:

- The three have different causes — a filter that `continue`d, a naive count over the wrong
  predicate, and a classifier ordering bug — so "populations shrink on re-derivation" is a
  coincidence of three instances, not a mechanism. Nothing here predicts the direction of the
  next one, and treating shrinkage as expected is how an over-count would be waved through.
- Two of the three were found because a **second** artifact disagreed, not because anyone
  re-read the first more carefully. That is the transferable half.

## WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH

`tracked_exists` means the citation **resolves**, never that it **supports** the claim citing
it. `AGENTS.md` as evidence for fourteen separate beads is a weak citation in exactly the way
tracked-ness cannot see. povo's criterion 3 — that a transient run may be cited only via a
tracked, revalidatable receipt — is untouched by any of this and remains unbuilt. One host,
class `bounded_model`.

## WHAT LANDED

`crates/fln-conformance/tests/artifact_referent_census.rs`, beside `fln-0rxm`'s census, because
the classifier is there and a second copy of it is the defect family both beads sit inside.
`UNTRACKED_PATH_CITATION_DEBT` declares all 150 live untracked citations across 48 rows, keyed
`(bead, entry)`. Two tests:

* `an_undeclared_untracked_path_citation_is_refused_and_a_foreign_member_cannot_borrow_a_slot`
* `repairing_a_declared_citation_without_touching_the_debt_does_not_redden`

## WHY THIS IS NOT WHAT THE CENSUS ALREADY DOES — the half that is easy to miss

`UNRESOLVABLE_CENSUS` pins each class by equality in both directions, so the population cannot
GROW. It is still an AGGREGATE. `fln-cross-tree-baked-root-k60n` measured what that costs over
70 commits: one repair took a total 44 to 38 and four new unprotected rigs then landed in four
separate commits, in four different crates, under a guard that was green the whole time,
because the total never came back to 46. Repair one rootless_leaf citation here and the class
count frees a slot ANY OTHER row may take — the census reads 99 either way.

The two laws are load-bearing TOGETHER and neither is sufficient: equality on the class stops
the population growing and cannot see a repair funding a swap; one-way membership per member
sees the swap and permits the total to fall.

## THE DIRECTION, AND THE TEST THAT PROVES IT IS NOT A WALL

One-way: every MEASURED untracked citation must be declared; a DECLARED entry that no longer
denotes one is NOT a failure. Reverse membership reddens the commit doing the repair, which is
a wall this repository has already paid for. Reviewing the law's direction is not enough,
because a precondition inside its own test inherits the same question — so the repair is
SIMULATED IN MEMORY (one declared row loses every untracked citation, the table untouched, the
verdict must not gain an entry). Nothing writes to the manifest: it is a shared file and a
transient edit is a governed-input mutation that can end another pane's lane.

The cost is stated rather than hidden: the table is an UPPER BOUND on the live debt, never a
count of it.

## THREE PLANTS, ONE UNION, ONE ASSERTION

A "real tree is clean" test plus a separate "a plant is refused" test leaves the live assertion
decorative the day the debt reaches zero. Judged as a union instead:

* A — a citation declared for NOBODY: must be refused.
* B — a citation the table declares FOR A DIFFERENT BEAD: must be refused. The ONLY cell that
  separates this law from an artifact-keyed one. Its entry is DERIVED from the table, so it
  cannot rot into naming something no longer declared.
* C — a commit-anchor citation: must NOT be refused. Without C the exclusion is INERT, since
  `commit_unreachable` measures 0 today, so deleting it changes no verdict and no test fails.
  C's kind is supplied rather than classified deliberately: `classify` would need a real 40-hex
  sha in a tracked source file, and that MINTS a fresh commit-anchor citation — the exact
  mistake made at `7046ef59`, where prose about a rotted anchor created one.

## CAMPAIGN: 6 mutants, 6 killed

Pristine GREEN before and after every cell, the file md5-verified on each restore, each cell's
killers asserted BY NAME so a mutant riding a neighbour's assertion is visible:

    M1 one declared entry deleted             -> the law
    M2 keyed on the entry, not (bead, entry)  -> the law   [plant B is the only killer]
    M3 commit-anchor exclusion deleted        -> the law   [plant C is the only killer]
    M4 the law governs nothing                -> the law AND the wall check
    M5 plant B not planted                    -> the law
    M6 law made reverse-membership            -> the wall check, ALONE

M4 dies at two cells because it guts the predicate both laws share; that is recorded as the
EXPECTATION rather than scored a wrong-cell kill. M1's first spelling was scored VOID rather
than surviving — rustfmt had reflowed its anchor, so the cell was "not planted" and was never
reported as a guard that does not fire.

## THE TABLE IS DERIVED BY A SECOND IMPLEMENTATION AND RECONCILED PER CLASS

`povo_population.py` has tested tracked-ness first since before the Rust classifier did. The
two now agree 99 / 20 / 15 / 9 / 7 / 0 across every untracked class. A total that agrees is
worth much less: these two agreed on no total for their whole co-existence while disagreeing
by 22 INSIDE one class, which is how `322c40e0` was found. Derived at `84f35ea6` and checked
against HEAD's manifest and the worktree separately — a peer's in-flight row added 8 citations
in that window, all tracked or structured, so the untracked population is identical in both and
the table does not rest on anyone's uncommitted work.

## WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH

* It refuses a new untracked citation; it repairs none, and 150 remain.
* It says nothing about whether a citation SUPPORTS the claim citing it. Tracked-ness cannot
  see that, and `AGENTS.md` as evidence for fourteen beads is weak in exactly that way.
* Criterion 3 — a transient run cited only via a tracked, revalidatable receipt — is untouched
  and unbuilt. So is criterion 1's structured-reference authority check.
* The validator (`validate-verification-manifest`) still accepts these citations. This law
  lives in `cargo test`, not in the validator, because the validator is `scripts/evidence.py`
  and that file is an h4o1 orphan nobody may touch. Whether the predicate should ALSO live
  there once the orphan lands is a decision, not an omission.
* The campaign is one run at one commit on one host, class `bounded_model`. What runs per
  commit is the binding, never the campaign.

## VERIFIED

Locally through an `exec cargo "$@"` wrapper so the RCH hook could not offload it onto a worker
with no `.git`; exit codes read from the process, never through a pipe.

    cargo test -p fln-conformance --no-fail-fast : 31 targets, 30 ok, 1 red

    cargo clippy -p fln-conformance --all-targets -- -D warnings : exit 0
    rustfmt --edition 2024 --check, the one changed file          : exit 0

uncommitted `crates/fln-syntax/tests/golden_vellum.rs`. It is not mine, it is present with
these changes absent, and no full-gate verdict is obtainable while that orphan stands.
