title: W12: Epoch migration autopilot integration — audited repair, explicit apply, rollback
description:
Integrate the §13.6 migration autopilot at the stage where all of its real prerequisites exist: the W12 epoch ratchet and machine-diffed censuses, W8 epoch bridges/cache identities, W9 semantic diff and blame slices, and W11 Bloodhound's verified proof-repair engine. Audit an unchanged downstream project against the new epoch; locate the earliest failed constraints and affected surfaces; propose minimal source/config/import/termination/instance/simp repairs; run lockstep old/new builds; validate every candidate through Athanor, Crucible, and the configured consensus policy; and emit an explicit apply transaction with a sealed rollback bundle. It never edits a project without an explicit apply.

Issue-tracker integration must respect D2: shipped FrankenLean tooling never spawns br or any third external tool. The ratchet emits a deterministic, schema-versioned migration-issue manifest with one row per moved symbol/divergence and exact br import/apply instructions for the repository-maintenance harness or human operator; applying that manifest is outside release-binary execution and is separately receipted.

All bead-specific requirements, acceptance conditions, tests, invariants, compatibility surfaces, evidence levels, performance gates, negative/recovery cases, and user-visible behaviors stated above remain mandatory. Validators reject unknown versions, missing/duplicate ids, broken step order, unbound artifacts, silent truncation, merged streams, and cleanup/final-state mismatch. title: W2: Marrow & Grimoire — ABI twin, object model, environment, olean codec
description:
Workstream W2 "Marrow & Grimoire" (§6, §7): the runtime/ABI twin and the environment/module codec — the load-bearing act of drop-in compatibility and the spine of gate G1.

Marrow: the Reference object model implemented exactly in Rust under the lean_* exported names (header packing, tag bytes, scalar-field packing, odd-tagged-pointer small Nats, tri-state RC discipline), with layout constants compiled from the GENERATED contract tables of §6.5 — never transcribed. Two heaps, one membrane (§6.1b): CompatHeap (exact ABI layouts, membrane-only allocation, unsafe confined to fln-unsafe-abi) vs NativeHeap (typed asupersync region handles for toolchain-internal structures); values cross only through generated converters; no raw Compat pointer ever enters the kernel (D22). Owned size-classed allocator with the heartbeat hook (fuel parity lives here). Compacted regions: construction, mmap-load, relocation — deliberately the SAME code path the olean codec uses.

Grimoire: the environment as persistent HAMT-style maps with O(1) snapshots and logical roots (§7.1); total contractual interning with alpha-canonical digest lane (§7.1b); olean codec read (three validation levels) and faithful byte-identical write (FL-INV-04); .ilean codec; olean-next frontier lane; import-at-daemon-scale shared heap (§7.5). Effects ride asupersync behind Reference IO/Task semantics (§6.7). fln-libm owned deterministic transcendentals (§6.8). Exit: G1 spine ready — real mathlib oleans resurrect, re-emit byte-identically, and load into the Reference.

## Success Criteria

All scope and outcomes stated above remain mandatory, and every dependency/child deliverable required for this epic or gate must be completed at its honest evidence level. The MANDATORY EPIC/GATE CLOSEOUT CONTRACT in Notes must pass with coverage mapping, no-mock E2E evidence, detailed archived human and schema-versioned NDJSON artifacts, reproducible environment facts, and every skip/divergence classified. No feature, compatibility surface, invariant, performance gate, or release claim may be silently narrowed, dropped, or replaced by a prototype.
acceptance_criteria: W2 closes only when Marrow and Grimoire form one proven compatibility spine across the generated ABI and OLEAN contracts. CompatHeap implements exact lean_object headers, tags, scalar packing, small-Nat encoding, tri-state RC, allocation classes, heartbeat charging, and every exported ownership convention; NativeHeap uses typed region handles; generated converters are the only membrane, and no raw Compat pointer or unsafe boundary can enter the kernel or checked declarations. Persistent environments, extension registries, module/provenance graphs, term interning, collision handling, logical/provenance roots, and O(1) snapshots preserve exact semantics, deterministic canonical identity, structural sharing, typed budgets, FL-INV-05 conservatism, and failure atomicity. One compacted-region construction/load/relocation path serves mmap and codec use. Olean read validates structural, semantic, and paranoid levels; faithful write and ilean emission are byte-identical and atomically promoted; corrupt/truncated/future artifacts are bounded typed outcomes; olean-next remains frontier-isolated. Reference IO/Task effects ride asupersync with capability receipts, fln-libm is bit-locked across platforms, D2 subprocess capsules are the sole optional cc/git path, and real inbound plugins plus the upstream stage0 ABI gauntlet pass without fallback. Exhaustive unit/property/model tests and named mutations cover every ABI field/tag/retain-release transition, allocator boundary, membrane conversion, PMap/term/store operation, root and snapshot law, relocation/codec field, effect outcome, libm vector, subprocess policy, and plugin failure. Real no-mock E2E spans mathlib olean load/re-emit/mixed consumption, upstream generated C, plugin execution, IO/Task, mmap sharing, corruption/resource/cancellation/crash/disk-full refusal, exact restoration, and clean recovery with strict evidence bundles. G1-spine evidence plus all W2 child gates, scripts/check.sh, full cargo/fmt/clippy/UBS, codec/mutation/fuzz/fault/thread/platform rigs are green. No handwritten layout, raw-pointer laundering, vector-sized snapshots, hidden oracle, external-runtime substitute, silent artifact repair, timing-only resource claim, optional tool on reproducible paths, or deferred listed W2 feature satisfies closure.
notes:
MANDATORY EPIC/GATE CLOSEOUT CONTRACT:
This epic/gate may close only when every child deliverable is complete; the verification registry maps every implemented public behavior, FL-INV claim, Parity-Ledger row, Behavior Note, and PG/gate claim to named unit/property/mutation coverage plus a shared no-mock E2E scenario; detailed human + schema-versioned NDJSON artifacts are archived; all divergences and skips are classified; no mock-only evidence is used for a release claim; and the final evidence bundle records exact reproduction commands, environment/epoch/mode/platform/thread/seed/cache facts, input hashes, receipts/logical roots, expected final states, first divergences, and cleanup results.

title: the twelve evidence fields of a coverage row are never resolved against a function
description:
THE FINDING. A coverage row in ci/VERIFICATION_MANIFEST.jsonl carries twelve evidence
fields -- unit, boundary, error, property, metamorphic, mutation, negative_recovery,
failure_atomicity, resource, fault, fuzz, cancellation. Nothing in this repository ever
resolves one of them against a real function. A row may name a test that was renamed,
deleted or #[ignore]d, and no gate anywhere goes red.

THE PRODUCER, read at HEAD b6ead16e rather than inherited. Seventeen tracked files name
VERIFICATION_MANIFEST, and the mention is not the read. FOUR of the seventeen name the twelve
evidence fields, and not one of the four resolves a citation:

  scripts/evidence.py -- all twelve, in VERIFICATION_COVERAGE_ARRAY_FIELDS, consumed only by
  require_manifest_string_array(..., nonempty=False), which establishes that the value is a
  list of non-empty strings, sorted and duplicate-free. That is the whole of it: a structural
  check, never a resolution.
  ci/VERIFICATION_MANIFEST.jsonl -- all twelve; it is the data.
  scripts/git-hooks/test_projection_guard.sh -- all twelve, inside a synthetic planned_row
  fixture with every array empty, built to exercise the pre-commit hook; it reads nothing.
  .beads/issues.jsonl -- one occurrence of metamorphic, in bead prose.

The other thirteen name none of the twelve. The only citation-resolving path in the tree is
crates/fln-conformance/tests/ci_execution_join.rs, which feeds record_field(line, "artifacts")
to test_function_citation: artifacts only.

CORRECTED, and the correction is disclosed rather than quietly applied. The first version of
this description and commit 8d7c2caf's immutable message both read "Zero of the other fifteen
manifest-naming files name any of the twelve fields at all" -- a claim about fifteen files
built from ten hand-tested ones. test_projection_guard.sh is a SCRIPT naming all twelve, which
is exactly the shape that would have falsified this bead had it resolved them. It does not, so
the finding stands unchanged; the claim underneath it did not. See the immutable correction
comment on this bead.

THE MEASUREMENT, re-derived at b6ead16e and unchanged from the 7e1765cd anchor: 786
citation-shaped entries across the manifest, 765 resolve to a test that exists and runs.

THE NON-RESOLVING FIGURE IS 20 ENTRIES ACROSS 8 ROWS AND 15 DISTINCT CITATIONS, NOT 21/9/16,
and the correction is mine and cuts against the finding. The scan's 21st entry,
9m74's boundary citation crates/fln-env/src/extensions.rs:ExtensionState::merge, DENOTES:
impl ExtensionState is at extensions.rs:2019 and pub fn merge at 2666. It is an
implementation reference, not a test citation, and the scan mis-buckets it because its
left-hand side is a file path rather than a package or member directory, so it exits before
reaching the scan's own Type::method classifier. One row, fln-env-merge-resource-envelope-9m74,
leaves the population.

THE FIFTEEN WERE CONFIRMED BY AN INDEPENDENT PATH, not by re-running the scan. A plain
grep -F for "fn <name>(" over all 232 tracked .rs files finds no definition of any of them
anywhere in the repository -- not merely absent from the package the citation names, absent
from the tree. The grep carries a four-name positive control that fires:
real_workspace_is_structurally_clean, the_evidence_surface_refuses_a_gitdir_pointer_root, and
the two renamed forms below. The eight rows: fln-k5rr, fln-q3u4,
franken_lean-claim-matrix-doc-ci-mhew, franken_lean-l84f, franken_lean-pnav, franken_lean-rps,
franken_lean-tkr2 (8 entries, wholly rotted), franken_lean-vrmi.

THE INSTANCE THAT DECIDES ITS PRIORITY IS SELF-INCRIMINATING. mhew is a row cc_3 repaired and
landed at cc7edf63. It has rot in two fields that repair did not touch: its mutation cites
witness_claim_matrix::a_partial_repair_cannot_pass and its negative_recovery cites
witness_claim_matrix::the_matrix_is_clean_against_the_real_tree, both renames of tests that
now read a_partial_repair_within_one_document_cannot_pass and
the_matrix_and_the_censuses_are_clean_against_the_real_tree. Both new names are present in
crates/fln-conformance/tests/witness_claim_matrix.rs and both old names are absent from the
tree. The checked field was repaired and the unchecked ones were left rotted because nothing
told the author they were there.

THE FIRST PASS WAS WRONG IN THE DIRECTION THAT MANUFACTURES FINDINGS, and it is recorded here
because that is the more dangerous failure. It reported 55 non-resolving across 18 rows. Its
package map was a depth-2 */*/Cargo.toml glob, blind to tribunal/epoch-lab (a nested
workspace) and to tools/structure-guard/kernel-ownership-publisher (depth 3), and it could not
resolve a unit test living in a binary target's mod tests. Thirty-four findings evaporated when
the scope widened. A scope too narrow reports absence as rot, loudly, on other panes' rows.

THE ADJACENT STAGE IS INERT, which is why a citation to a file absent from all of history
validates. validate-verification-manifest returns artifact_reference_validation =
not_adopted_registry_absent: 577 artifact pairs scanned, none classified, durable_artifact_pairs
and legacy_artifact_pairs both null, zero legacy rows. Confirmed at b6ead16e.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH. That any resolving citation is TRUE: resolution proves the named
function exists, runs and is not #[ignore]d, never that it tests what the row claims. The
figures are one host, one commit, class bounded_model; any test rename or #[ignore] moves them.
The grep control proves the fifteen names define no function in tracked Rust source; it does not
prove they never existed. And the seventeen-file mention population is a property of the string
VERIFICATION_MANIFEST, so a reader that opens the file by some other spelling would be missed.

NO REPAIR IS PROPOSED IN THIS BEAD. A guard design exists and is routed to whoever sequences
the swarm for a ruling; this bead is the finding, which does not wait on that decision. Filed
deliberately as a finding with a producer, a measurement and a HEAD anchor rather than held
hostage to a design ruling -- the disclosed-unknowns-rot shape this repository has filed
against repeatedly.

whole denominator is the pkg_colon_dcolon citations carrying NO prose tail. It drops 32 citations
of the kind it does model, purely because a trailing clause follows the citation
("crates/fln-env/src/extensions.rs:the_ancestry_budget_spans_both_branch_walks asserts the typed
dimension..."). Those 32 have never been resolved by anything. Classify by the HEAD token; a
citation followed by prose is still a citation.

SO THE NEVER-RESOLVED CITATION-SHAPED POPULATION IS 298, not zero and not 21: 1249 classified minus
165 not_applicable leaves 1084 citation-shaped, of which the standing measurement reaches 786. The
other 298 are 32 prose-tailed members of the modelled kind plus 266 members of six kinds nothing
models. fln-46mw's six are in pkg_dcolon_colon, which is why a grammar splitting on the first colon
manufactured six false accusations against a row that is not rotted.

THE CONTROLS ARE THE POINT, AND THEY CAUGHT THREE DEFECTS IN THIS CLASSIFIER BEFORE IT WAS
BELIEVED. C1 conservation, sum of kinds plus residual equals total, so no entry is silently
dropped. C2 disjointness, every entry evaluated against ALL predicates and required to match at
most one - it failed first, on evidence.py:<contract>::<case> matching both pkg_colon_dcolon and
script_multipart, repaired by excluding a .py/.sh lhs from the package kind. C3 decoys, one planted
entry per kind plus a planted prose sentence that must land in residual. C3 failed on
bare_module_path, whose predicate read "':' not in h and '::' in h" - UNSATISFIABLE, since '::'
contains ':'. It held zero members, so every deletion mutant scored it KILLED vacuously and the
kind read as a legitimate absence. Only the planted decoy could find it, and repairing it moved 48
real entries out of residual. That is the inert-declaration shape: a set that cannot be satisfied
is unkillable by mutation. The same trap then recurred in this script's own REPORTING, where a
zero-member kind scored KILLED because moved == expect == 0; the two genuinely empty kinds now
report DECLARED, ZERO MEMBERS instead.

Deletion mutants: all eight populated kinds KILLED, each moving exactly its own members to residual
and none absorbed by a neighbour.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH. Nothing is resolved here and no row is accused: this establishes the
DENOMINATOR and the kind inventory, which is what the ruling at 3ac7dfaf requires before anything
is called rot. Ten kinds is a FLOOR on the kinds in use, never a census - the 631 residual is
classified as prose by the absence of a matching head, and any citation form nobody thought of sits
in there looking exactly like a sentence. Head-token classification is itself a modelling choice: a
citation with a leading prose clause is invisible to it. This is one host, one commit, class
bounded_model, and it moves with any manifest edit. The script is at
/data/tmp/claude-1000/cc3-scratch/kind_partition.py, OUTSIDE the tree deliberately - a file in
tests/ runs the instant it exists and reddens six panes.

RE-DERIVATION: THE GOVERNING FIGURE WAS A SAMPLE. 2056 resolvable, not 786; 39 non-resolving, not 20.

cc_2 (pane %15), 2026-08-04, HEAD 5c143a8b. This is a measurement, not a repair. It does not
overturn the bead's finding -- it enlarges it, and it corrects the number every downstream
decision has been resting on, including the f2t9 widening ruling that named this bead as its
precondition.

=== WHAT THE OLD FIGURE MEASURED ===

The description's governing line reads "786 citation-shaped entries across the manifest, 765
resolve to a test that exists and runs", corrected later to 20 non-resolving across 8 rows and 15
distinct citations. Those figures are internally consistent and were produced carefully. What they
are not is the population.

Re-derived with EVERY entry assigned to exactly one bucket and the buckets required to sum to the
total -- because a scan that skips what it cannot parse silently redefines its own denominator:

    total entries across the twelve fields   3792
      1866  citation, pkg-or-memberdir : target :: fn
      1116  prose (contains whitespace; not a citation)
       265  typed not_applicable_*
       190  citation, `test:` artifacts grammar
       170  unclassified (disclosed below, not skipped)
        94  script reference
        52  bead: reference
        35  citation naming a TARGET but no function
         4  implementation reference (file.rs:Type::method)
      3792  SUM -- accounted

    FUNCTION-RESOLVABLE POPULATION   2056
    NON-RESOLVING                    39 entries, 14 rows, 28 distinct citations

So the prior scan covered 786 of 2056, about 38%, and reported the non-resolving count of that
sample. The finding is unchanged and the exposure is roughly double what the bead records.

=== MY OWN FIRST PASS WAS ALSO A SAMPLER, BY 105, AND MY OWN RULE CAUGHT IT ===

Recorded because it is the same defect one layer down. My first run classified only left-hand
sides matching a package NAME, so all 105 `tribunal/epoch-lab:target::fn` citations -- whose left
side is a member DIRECTORY PATH -- fell into "unclassified" and left the resolvable population.
That run reported 33 non-resolving across 11 rows and, worse, LOST two rows the bead already
knew about (fln-q3u4 and franken_lean-claim-matrix-doc-ci-mhew), which is what made the error
visible. Nothing but the bucket-sum discipline and the bead's own known-bad list separated a
smaller number from a better one. Accepting a left-hand side that is either a package name or a
member directory restores them and yields the 39.

=== THE FOURTEEN ROWS ===

Eight are the ones this bead already names: fln-k5rr, fln-q3u4,
franken_lean-claim-matrix-doc-ci-mhew, franken_lean-l84f, franken_lean-pnav, franken_lean-rps,
franken_lean-tkr2, franken_lean-vrmi.

SIX ARE NEW AND WERE OUTSIDE THE SAMPLE:

    franken_lean-contract-pin-tree-unestablished-monc   2 entries (unit, negative_recovery)
    franken_lean-gii.1                                  4 entries, one citation in all four
    franken_lean-gii.7                                  2 entries (unit, fault)
    franken_lean-gii.11                                 1 entry  (unit)
    franken_lean-y24                                    4 entries, 2 distinct
    franken_lean-z6c                                    6 entries, 6 distinct

z6c is the widest: six distinct citations across error, fault, fuzz, metamorphic and resource,
naming functions in fln-conformance:kernel_replay, fln-olean:region_read, fln-kernel:budget_parity
and fln-kernel:depth_stack_calibration, none of which define the cited name anywhere in tracked
Rust source.

=== CONTROLS, because a scan that finds nothing and a clean tree are the same green ===

  * a_partial_repair_cannot_pass                        absent   (expected absent -- the rename
                                                                  this bead documents)
  * a_partial_repair_within_one_document_cannot_pass    present  (expected present -- its new name)
  * real_workspace_is_structurally_clean                present  (expected present)

All three as expected. The derivation refuses outright if it finds fewer than 20 packages or 500
test functions, so a broken walk reports a refusal rather than a clean tree. Measured: 35 packages,
35 member directories, 360 tracked Rust files, 2878 test functions, 6 of them #[ignore]d.

=== WHAT I AM NOT CLAIMING ===

Resolution proves the named function EXISTS in tracked Rust source; it does not prove the function
tests what the row claims, and this scan does not check which package the function lives in -- a
citation naming the right function under the wrong package resolves here. Both are deliberate:
this pass measures the population the guard must cover, not the guard's final predicate.

The 170 unclassified entries are disclosed, not skipped: 83 are `pkg:target` with no function at
all (target-granular, unresolvable to a function by construction, counted separately at 35 after
the fix plus these), 59 are bare tokens naming types rather than tests (ExpandedWeight, InputBytes,
ProducedNodes), and the rest are single-colon forms. None of them is silently folded into the
resolvable count.

#[ignore] detection reads three lines either side of the `#[test]` attribute; only 6 ignored test
functions were found workspace-wide, which is low enough that I would not rely on that half without
re-measuring it.

One host, one commit, class bounded_model. Every figure moves with any rename.

=== CONSEQUENCE FOR THE GUARD, AND WHY I HAVE NOT BUILT IT YET ===

The bead says no repair is proposed and that a guard design was routed for a ruling. That ruling
should now be taken against 39/14/28, not 20/8/15: an allowance declared at the old size would be
wrong by nineteen entries and six rows on the day it landed, and the six new rows include four
belonging to the gii.* family, which is another pane's area. I am routing the corrected measurement
rather than authoring an allowance over other panes' rows unilaterally.

crates/fln-conformance/tests/evidence_field_citations.rs, 9 tests, plain cargo test. This is the
mechanism half of bs5o.

wrote it, ran its gates, and then PARKED it untracked and static at 02:04:50 for the sequencer's

describes the work accurately. I did not write that commit and am not claiming it; I am recording

tested are both sha256 11dc716974c4351e4dd9e4161aaf886e2ab63e29999bdc04c1187d6442afd611, and the
file's mtime never moved from 02:04:50, so nothing was edited between the 9/9 run and the landing.

CONSEQUENCE WORTH CARRYING, because "park your WIP static" does not cover it: an untracked
tests/*.rs file is NOT invisible to cargo, which auto-discovers integration targets from disk. A
parked, uncommitted test participates in every other pane's gate run. Mine was green so nothing
came of it, but a half-written parked test would redden somebody else's gate while looking clean
in git status.

The bead's own scope said no repair was proposed and that a design was routed for a ruling; what
needed the ruling was authoring an ALLOWANCE OVER OTHER PANES' MANIFEST ROWS. This guard does not
do that: the declaration lives in a test file in my own lane's crate, it edits nobody's row, and
it judges nobody's evidence. The open question -- who repairs the 39 -- is still routed and still
open.

=== WHAT IT DOES ===

Reads ci/VERIFICATION_MANIFEST.jsonl, derives the workspace (packages, member directories, every
#[test] function in tracked Rust source), and resolves every citation in the twelve fields against
that set. Measured at the landing commit: 3810 entries, 2071 function-resolvable, 39 non-resolving
across 14 rows and 28 distinct citations.

EVERY ENTRY LANDS IN EXACTLY ONE BUCKET AND THE BUCKETS MUST SUM TO THE TOTAL. That is the rule
that makes the number a population rather than a sample, and it is in the guard rather than in a
scratch script because it is the rule both prior scans broke -- the bead's, which covered 786 of
2071, and my own first pass, which lost 105 tribunal/epoch-lab citations by requiring the left-hand
side to be a package NAME rather than a member DIRECTORY.

=== THE DIRECTION, WHICH IS THE DESIGN DECISION WORTH READING ===

NONRESOLVING_ALLOWANCE is CEILING plus ONE-WAY MEMBERSHIP, never an equality:

  * an undeclared non-resolving citation FAILS -- that is silent growth, the defect;
  * the declared set may SHRINK FREELY. A repair by any pane must never redden this guard. An
    equality, or a "declared but no longer measured" rule, converts one pane's correct repair into
    another pane's red. The 28 span several panes' rows, four of them gii.*, so that is not a
    hypothetical cross-pane wall.
  * the measured COUNT is separately capped at 39, because membership alone cannot stop the same
    declared citation spreading to more rows -- a mutant proves exactly that.

THE PRICE IS STATED IN THE MODULE HEADER RATHER THAN HIDDEN: the allowance can accumulate dead
entries, because nothing forces it to shrink. That is accepted as the cheaper of two failures.

=== PROVEN TO FIRE, NOT MERELY TO PASS ===

The live cell was decoy-tested in a PRIVATE worktree -- never the shared tree, where this manifest
is committed every few minutes. Baseline passes; with one planted citation naming a function that
exists nowhere, the cell FAILS and the failure names the finding code, the planted citation, and
the row carrying it. Worktree manifest restored and verified clean.

Six further cells are injected-input mutants: an undeclared citation is refused; a declared one is
permitted AND its repair stays green (the cross-pane rule, asserted rather than described); the
ceiling refuses creep when every citation is declared; a scan whose buckets do not reconcile is
refused as a sampler; an empty walk is refused rather than reported clean -- it satisfies
membership and the ceiling vacuously, and only the floors catch it; and the citation splitter
accepts a member directory, rejects a stranger, and rejects a target with no function.

=== WHAT THIS DOES NOT EARN ===

Resolution proves the named function EXISTS in tracked Rust source, never that it tests what the
row claims. It does not check the function lives in the package the citation names -- I measured
that dimension separately and it is EMPTY: 0 mismatches across 1827 citations, with a planted
control (real_workspace_is_structurally_clean attributed to fln-anvil) proving the detector fires,
silent on the truth, and silent on names that exist nowhere. A guard on an empty population is
decorative unless exercised by a planted member, so it is deliberately NOT built rather than added
and sold as coverage. #[ignore] detection is not attempted: six ignored test functions exist
workspace-wide, too few to rest a rule on.

Gates, taken before the park: evidence_field_citations 9/9; fmt --check clean; clippy -p
fln-conformance --all-targets -D warnings clean; UBS on the new file 0 critical / 42 warning / 19
info, and being a NEW file every finding is attributable to me -- there is no baseline to subtract.

RE-VERIFIED AFTER LANDING, and this is the check that matters once a guard is in the tree rather
than in a branch: it now runs inside every pane's cargo test, including the j8h gate runs, so a
stale allowance would make MY guard the thing blocking somebody else's gate. Re-derived at four
successive HEADs across the freeze chain -- 2b06e27b, 891306d0, and 84b4cb9b -- with the
allowance, ceiling and every floor PARSED OUT OF THE LANDED FILE rather than retyped, against both
HEAD's manifest and the live worktree:

  total=3810  resolvable=2071 (floor 1500)  non-resolving=39  distinct=28  undeclared=0  ceiling OK
  test functions 2893 (floor 500)  packages 35 (floor 20)

GREEN on every one. The manifest grew from 3792 to 3810 entries between drafting the allowance and
the landing, which is exactly the window in which a transcribed ceiling arrives already above the
tree -- the check exists because that hazard is real, not because the number looked doubtful.

NEVER GOT ANSWERED IS ANSWERED BY THIS PROJECT'S OWN STANDING SHAPE.

under plain `cargo test`. It resolves every citation in all twelve fields against the tracked Rust
sources, refuses an undeclared non-resolving citation by name, refuses a declared one that has
started resolving (so a repair must shrink the declaration), refuses an empty walk as a broken scan
rather than a clean tree, and refuses a scan whose buckets do not reconcile — the sampler defect
this bead's own history contains.

on its green path:

    evidence-field-citations: entries=4162 resolvable=2253 non-resolving=41 declared=31 ceiling=51

That print landed an hour before this close and exists BECAUSE of this close: the three numbers had
lived only inside the panic message, so the sole way to read the population was to break the guard,

should not be closed on a number from a tree that no longer exists.

=== THE QUESTION I ROUTED, AND WHY I AM NOW ANSWERING IT ===

I routed "who repairs the non-resolving citations" to the sequencer and it was never ruled on. I am
not closing this by declaring my own question moot; I am closing it because the project answered the
question in practice and in doctrine while I waited.

DOCTRINE: a declared remainder under a ceiling, one-way, is the shape this repository already uses
for every population it cannot empty today — the UBS `class-level` allowance, the file-granular
evidence allowance, the ignored-producer allowance, the k60n raw-site residue. Each shrinks when its
subject is repaired and forces an author to raise a number under review when it grows. This guard
has exactly that shape and has had it since it landed.

PRACTICE: on 2026-08-05 three panes repaired their own rows' citations without any ruling —
`f123b674` retracting a residual across four rows, `1377d539` repairing four dangling citations,
`e868fde4` and `8e577ccd` correcting rows the guard named. The owner of a row repairs its citations.
That is the answer, and it was demonstrated rather than decided.

So the honest state is: the ABSENCE this bead was filed for is gone; what remains is a declared,
ceiling-bound, per-owner queue, which is a normal condition of this repository rather than an open
defect.

The guard resolves EXISTENCE and RUNNABILITY, never that a named test carries the row's claim. That
is a semantic question no count answers and this guard never reads a row's prose.

It reads the WORKTREE, and that is deliberate and opposite its sibling `closure_binding_population`,
which judges HEAD. A non-resolving citation is introduced BY the commit that adds it, so a
HEAD-reading guard would notice one commit late; the cost is that it can be red for a peer's

The 41 non-resolving entries are NOT repaired by this bead and are not claimed to be. Note that 41

title: Evidence runner: producer and strict validator hold two unbound copies of the Python configuration rule
description:
scripts/evidence.py classifies interpreter-configuration channels in exactly one place --
overridden_python_environment, which admits a name in PYTHON_CONFIGURATION_ENV_EXACT or
matching PYTHON_CONFIGURATION_ENV_PREFIXES -- and records the resulting names in
effective_interpreter_identity.overridden_env. The strict NDJSON run-record validator then
re-derives that same rule INDEPENDENTLY as a hardcoded name.startswith("PYTHON"). Nothing
binds the two.

Measured at 5b6158ad by loading the real module and varying one constant: widening the
producer tuple to ("PYTHON", "PY_", "PYVENV") makes it emit PY_HOSTILE and PYVENV_LAUNCHER,
which the validator then refuses with "sealed-interpreter environment names are malformed".
The runner rejects a record it had just produced.

Latent today, because nobody has widened the tuple, and it fails in the safe direction --
a false refusal, not a false pass. It is filed because the whole point of the classification
is that the family can be extended when CPython adds a channel, and today extending it
breaks the runner. This is AGENTS.md item 7's shape: two artifacts, a join between them,
nothing naming the join, and each artifact locally consistent so no single-artifact review
finds it.

Found while landing franken_lean-h40t's classification guard (commits 29cf8a8e, 6b94c8d5).

SCOPE / PROPOSED REPAIR (drafted and verified against a copy, not yet applied):
Extract one predicate beside the constants and point both call sites at it:

  def is_python_configuration_name(name: str) -> bool:
      return name in PYTHON_CONFIGURATION_ENV_EXACT or any(
          name.startswith(prefix) for prefix in PYTHON_CONFIGURATION_ENV_PREFIXES
      )

Three anchored replacements, each verified to occur exactly once: the constants block, the
producer body, and the validator's hardcoded literal. Verified on a scratchpad copy under
the pinned CPython 3.13.7: the patched file compiles; as shipped the classification is
byte-identical (8 names, no regression); the validator no longer carries its own copy; and
with the tuple widened the original rejects two names while the patched rejects none. The
negative control -- that the ORIGINAL genuinely drifts -- is asserted, so the verification
cannot pass vacuously.

VERIFICATION REQUIRED TO CLOSE, and the guard here MUST be structural -- stated explicitly
because my first draft of this bead demanded a behavioural one, which is impossible:

Once both sites call one predicate, a behavioural test that "the validator accepts what the
producer emits" compares f to f. It cannot fail, for the same reason the widening probe
CAN fail today: the drift is observable only while two copies exist, and the repair is
precisely what removes the observation. Unifying the rule converts the property from
behavioural to structural, and a rig that kept asserting it behaviourally would be green
forever while proving nothing.

That is the same shape as this bead's parent finding on franken_lean-h40t -- cod_3's
checklist asked for a mutant-kill against an inert constant, and no such test existed -- so
it is written down rather than rediscovered.

The guard must therefore assert, over the source of scripts/evidence.py:
  - the shared predicate exists, and the producer routes through it;
  - the validator's acceptance test routes through it and does not re-derive the rule;
  - NO other hand-rolled test of the interpreter-configuration family exists outside the
    predicate, so a third copy written a third way is refused rather than tolerated -- the
    grep-for-the-deleted-literal version passes the moment someone rephrases it;
  - and the scan refuses loudly if it matches nothing, since a broken scan and a clean tree
    are otherwise indistinguishable.
It must say in its own doc comment that it is structural and earns nothing about runtime.
No self-exclusion problem arises here: the guard is Rust scanning Python, so its own text
is outside the search space -- unlike fln-8zsq, where it was not.

The BEHAVIOURAL half that remains meaningful is the one already landed in 29cf8a8e: that
every required channel is actually classified, with controls. That does not become vacuous,
because it tests the predicate against reality rather than against its own twin.

BLOCKED ON, and this is a working-tree fact rather than a dependency:
scripts/evidence.py carries cod_2's uncommitted census work (524 lines, live in the tree,
re-applied from stash@{0} onto current HEAD). A git commit -o of that path would sweep it
under another agent's message. This slice needs that file quiet and committed first. The

NOTE ON FILING: creating this bead stales ci/KERNEL_CONTRACT_OWNERSHIP.jsonl and must be
committed with a regenerated projection in the same commit.

landed VERBATIM and I verified that rather than assuming it: scripts/evidence.py at HEAD is
byte-identical to my parked copy, md5 e3216ff7fb23da35ca37d1cc6be989ba on both, diff empty, and the
Rust file is a single appended hunk at @@ -4675,3 +4675,207 @@ containing my two guards and nothing
else. No complaint attached. This is exactly what I did to cod_8 at 70b8a97c and disclosed
afterwards; static WIP in a shared tree is adoptable by whoever commits the path.

WHAT THE REPAIR IS. is_python_configuration_name is the one place the interpreter-configuration
family is decided in Python. The producer overridden_python_environment and the strict NDJSON
run-record validator both route through it. Before, the producer read the two constants and the
validator independently hardcoded name.startswith("PYTHON"), and widening the prefix tuple -- the
entire reason the tuple exists -- made the runner emit names its own validator refused as malformed.
It rejected a record it had just produced.

THE EVIDENCE, WITH THE NEGATIVE CONTROL THAT STOPS IT PASSING VACUOUSLY. Measured by loading HEAD's
blob and the patched file as two modules and varying exactly one thing, the prefix tuple:

  as shipped, HEAD classifies 9 / patched classifies 9  -> IDENTICAL, no regression
  widened, HEAD    emits 11, its validator REFUSES 2: PYVENV_LAUNCHER, PY_HOSTILE
  widened, patched emits 11, its validator REFUSES 0

The middle line is the control. Without it the third line would be a function agreeing with itself.

THREE MUTANTS, EACH KILLED AT A DISTINCT ASSERTION, file restored and md5 re-verified after each:

  A  the validator re-derives the rule (the original defect, restored)
     -> dies at the literal rule, "hardcodes a startswith test ... outside the predicate"
  B  the producer re-derives it in REPHRASED form
     -> dies at the constant-count rule. This is the one that matters: a guard greping for the
        deleted literal passes the moment somebody rephrases the copy, which the bead's own
        acceptance criteria warned about. Keying on the CONSTANTS rather than the literal is what
        catches B.
  C  a shell copy leaves the population
     -> dies at the named-population rule

WHY THE GUARD IS STRUCTURAL, AND THAT IS A CONSEQUENCE RATHER THAN A WEAKENING. Once both sites call
one predicate, "the validator accepts what the producer emits" compares f to f and can never fail.
The disagreement was observable only while two copies existed, and the repair is precisely what
removes the observation. The guard says so in its own doc comment and claims nothing about runtime.
No self-exclusion problem: it is Rust scanning Python, so its own text is outside its search space.

=== TWO FINDINGS THE BEAD DID NOT CONTAIN ===

FINDING A. PYTHON_CONFIGURATION_ENV_EXACT IS INERT, AND IT IS THE MECHANISM BEHIND THE BEAD. All
seven of its names begin with PYTHON, so the prefix tuple already matches every one; emptying the
frozenset changes no classification (8 -> 8, measured). So the two copies did not "agree on all 8
names" by luck as the bead says -- they were EXTENSIONALLY EQUAL, and the drift was latent BECAUSE
of the subsumption. The first exact name that does not begin with PYTHON ends the latency. Recorded
in the predicate's docstring rather than left for the next reader to rediscover, and the frozenset
is kept rather than deleted: it states which channels are known by name and stops being inert the
moment the family grows sideways rather than longer.

FINDING B. THERE IS A THIRD COPY, IN SHELL, IN TWENTY FILES: scripts/check.sh, seventeen
scripts/e2e/ scripts, scripts/tribunal/ref_vs_ref.sh and scripts/verify_vendor_tree.sh, each
hand-writing [[ "$environment_name" == PYTHON* ]]. Prefix-only, no shared definition. So the family
is decided in three places across two languages, and this bead's own closing requirement -- that no
other hand-rolled test of the family exists outside the predicate -- is violated twenty times TODAY
and could not be discharged by unifying the two Python sites.

The two findings compose into the risk neither states alone: the shell copy is safe ONLY because
EXACT is inert. Add one non-PYTHON-prefixed exact name and one edit yields two failures at once --
twenty shell surfaces stop refusing that channel at the door, and the validator refuses a record the
producer legitimately emitted.

I DID NOT UNIFY THE SHELL COPIES, DELIBERATELY. Twenty governed inputs across seventeen e2e scripts,
check.sh and two others is a separate change with its own freeze cost, and folding it in would make
this bead unreviewable. the_shell_copies_of_the_interpreter_configuration_rule_are_a_named_population
binds the exact set instead, in both directions, so a fourth copy cannot appear silently and a copy
that disappears forces the list to shrink. That test asserts a DEFECT, not a repair, and says so.

=== THREE THINGS I GOT WRONG, EACH CAUGHT BY A MECHANISM RATHER THAN BY CARE ===

1. I PUBLISHED THE SHELL POPULATION AS NINETEEN AND IT IS TWENTY. A recursive rg walk missed
   scripts/verify_vendor_tree.sh that a git ls-files walk found, at the same commit, with the needle
   provably in the file at both -- I confirmed the file was not newly changed rather than assuming
   the population had moved. Worse, my first count WAS twenty and I "corrected" it downward on the
   strength of the lossy scan. My own guard caught it within minutes of being written. Derive
   populations from the index, not from a recursive walk.

2. MY GUARD REFUSED MY OWN EXPLANATION. Its first form counted startswith("PYTHON") over the whole
   file, and the predicate's docstring QUOTES the deleted literal while explaining what it replaced.
   The gate matched the token instead of the claim and fired on its own correction. Now scoped
   outside the predicate.

3. MY OWN EDIT ROTTED TWO CITATIONS. Inserting the predicate shifted every line after :267 by 19,
   invalidating scripts/evidence.py:2089 and :17640 in AGENTS.md and reddening
   every_agents_line_citation_points_at_the_construct_it_names. Both were re-derived FROM THE
   CONSTRUCT rather than patched by +19, and both halves -- the prose citation and its cite row --
   moved together, as that test demands. Had I parked one minute earlier I would have left a red in
   cod_2's tree caused by my own edit.

=== WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH ===

Nothing here is reachable in a shipped run: no configuration widens the tuple, and both halves fail
in the SAFE direction -- a false refusal, never a false pass. This remains a latent extensibility
failure, and the bead was right to type it that way. The guard is structural and says nothing about
what the predicate computes; the behavioural half that stays meaningful is the one landed at
29cf8a8e, which tests the predicate against reality rather than against its twin. I did not run
scripts/check.sh. One host, one commit, one CPython, class bounded_model.

title: W7 Verdict: deterministic decoder and certificate boundary fuzzing
description: Add a dependency-free deterministic seeded fuzz campaign inside crates/fln-verdict for the two trust boundaries. Target canonical CNF byte decoding plus the public DIMACS literal decoder with malformed, truncated, nested-count, and pathologically-large bounded inputs; no malformed input may panic. Target the independent streaming certificate checker with structurally and semantically invalid hostile mutations, explicitly including unknown versions; no invalid certificate may be accepted, no refusal may carry a receipt or verdict, and the recovery path must recompute a newly checked artifact. Keep checker work bounded and demonstrate certificate checking is cheaper than solver recomputation using existing resource facts where comparable. Use only a hand-rolled seeded PRNG, no new crate or dependency, and make every failure replayable by rerunning its recorded seed. Report campaign seed count, total inputs, panics, invalid-certificate acceptances, and every reproducing seed. Convert any finding into a permanent regression before close.
close_reason: Seed-replayable parser and proof-checker negative-path campaign delivered in aa5d344; 5,120 inputs, zero panics or invalid proof acceptances; cost defect split to franken_lean-r4m8.

title: Parity Ledger: the 533-record ext observable capture backing 28 L2 rows is never re-derived from the pin
description:
28 Parity Ledger rows rest on a 533-record oracle capture that nothing re-derives from the pin.

crates/fln-core/fixtures/core_ext_observables.txt holds 533 Reference-produced records and backs 28 rows in ci/PARITY_LEDGER.txt at L2. The ledger's definition of that level (ci/PARITY_LEDGER.txt:41-46) is "the pinned Reference binary produced the expected value, and ... compares ours to it on every run", and the second half is true: crates/fln-core/tests/pin_ext_observables.rs runs the comparison on every test run. What is not re-validated is the CAPTURE.

THE ASYMMETRY, which is what makes this cheap to fix and easy to miss. Two oracle fixtures exist and they are treated differently:

  crates/fln-conformance/fixtures/core_observables.txt      74 lines,  39 rows
    Generated by scripts/extract/gen_core_fixtures.sh, which has a --check mode
    (:11, :64-67) that regenerates to a scratch file and diffs against the
    checked-in copy. scripts/e2e/core_observables.sh:39 runs that --check against
    the LIVE pinned binary on every lane run, and :74-98 plants a seeded corruption
    to prove the diff detects change. The oracle is re-consulted. This is the model.

  crates/fln-core/fixtures/core_ext_observables.txt        533 records, 28 rows
    Generated by crates/fln-core/fixtures/gen_core_ext.lean, run BY HAND per its own
    header (:8 documents the manual command line). gen_core_fixtures.sh:18 covers
    only its sibling. No --check mode, no lane, no regeneration anywhere:
    rg gen_core_ext across the tree finds only the file itself, its consumer, and
    prose.

WHAT ACTUALLY GUARDS IT TODAY, and why that is not enough: crates/fln-core/tests/pin_ext_observables.rs:172-184 extracts the commit string from the fixture header and asserts SUITE.lock contains it. That catches one failure mode -- the pin moving out from under a fixture generated at an older commit. It cannot catch a stale capture at the same commit, a hand edit, a partial regeneration, or a fixture that was correct when written and has since been touched, because the check is a string comparison against a header the same edit could preserve. The file says GENERATED at :111 and nothing enforces that it still is.

CONSEQUENCE, stated at the strength the evidence supports: this is not a claim that the 533 records are wrong. It caught a real divergence in Level.geq when it was introduced (recorded in the ledger's own header note), and there is no reason to think it has rotted. It is a claim that if it rotted, nothing here would say so, and 28 rows would go on reporting L2 against it. That is the same shape as the fixture whose sibling IS re-derived, which is what makes it worth closing rather than arguing about.

THIS IS A CORRECTION, NOT A RAISE. Closing it does not move a single row up a level; it makes 28 rows' already-claimed evidence continuously true instead of true-as-of-one-manual-run. The work is small and the pattern is already in the repo: give gen_core_ext.lean a shell wrapper with the same --check contract as gen_core_fixtures.sh, and add it to the existing scripts/e2e/core_observables.sh lane rather than writing a new lane. Note the operational constraint if a new lane is attempted anyway: every --wait-ms for the process-identity guards is capped at 30000, and the scenario must be registered with its exact ordered step list in E2E_STEP_ORDERS at the top of scripts/evidence.py, in scripts/check.sh INPUT_PATHS, and in the ci.yml verify-step expected_roots set. Extending the existing lane avoids all of that.

ONE THING TO CHECK WHILE IN THERE: the ext generator is a .lean file run under the pinned binary, so the wrapper needs the same typed SKIP behaviour the other pin-dependent lanes have when the toolchain is absent (scripts/tribunal/leanchecker_witness.sh:59-62 is the pattern -- emit a typed limitation, never a silent pass). RCH remote workers do not have the pinned toolchain, so this must run locally or skip typed.

EVIDENCE FRESHNESS: all file:line references verified against HEAD d5e69023 on 2026-07-25 by cc_3. AUDIT SET: filed together with two related findings; ids in the first comment.
close_reason: The capture is now re-derived from the pin on every run (commit above). Measured: it was byte-identical, so the 28 rows were backed all along; what was missing was any way to find out. No row declared or re-levelled -- they do not outrun their evidence.

title: fln-env: witness_digest binds a lossy display projection of Name, so distinct finding sets share a witness
description:
Found by a mock-code / placeholder audit of crates/fln-env (PeachBass, pane cc_1, 2026-07-24). Category: code that LOOKS complete but is semantically a stub — a digest that omits identity it claims to bind.

DEFECT: fln_env::decl_closure::witness_digest (crates/fln-env/src/decl_closure.rs:175-197) hashes each Name via to_display_string() rather than the canonical Name::write_body used everywhere else in the crate. to_display_string (crates/fln-core/src/name.rs:151) joins components with '.' WITHOUT escaping, and renders Repr::Num and Repr::Str identically. The projection is therefore not injective, and the length prefixes do not help because the lossy strings are already equal before prefixing.

PROVEN, not inferred. A temporary probe run against the real function reported:
  Name::str(anon, "a.b")  vs  Name::str(Name::str(anon,"a"), "b")  -> same witness (declaration position)
  the same pair inside the finding's missing list                  -> same witness
  Name::str(anon, "1")    vs  Name::num(anon, 1)                   -> same witness
All three printed digest_equal = true. The probe was reverted and the tree left clean.

WHY IT MATTERS: the witness is the identity of an ArtifactIncomplete finding set. Two materially different missing-closure situations — different declarations, or different missing constants — can produce the same witness, so the witness cannot do the one job it has: distinguishing the evidence it binds. It is also pinned as KERNEL_ADMISSION_ARTIFACT_WITNESS in scripts/evidence.py and recomputed by consumers, so the ambiguity is baked into the census contract.

SEVERITY IS P1, NOT P0, and the reason is worth recording. ArtifactIncomplete is an FL-INV-07 inconclusive-family outcome: never Accepted, never Rejected, never counted checked, never cacheable, never entering an Environment. A colliding witness therefore CANNOT corrupt an Environment or a cache key; it degrades evidence identity only. If that barrier ever weakens, re-rank to P0 immediately.

FIX: encode the declaration Name and every entry of the missing list with the canonical Name::write_body — as environment.rs decl_content_digest and provenance.rs write_contribution_record already do — instead of to_display_string. Keep the existing length prefixes, WITNESS_TAG, and domain.

THIS IS A PIN MOVE, NOT A SILENT FIX. Changing the encoding changes every witness digest, so the census v2 pins must move together: KERNEL_ADMISSION_ARTIFACT_WITNESS in scripts/evidence.py, the expected-rows array in crates/fln-conformance/tests/kernel_replay.rs, and the census needles in scripts/e2e/kernel_replay.sh. Those live outside crates/fln-env, so this needs the fln-env owner and the scripts owner to land together, or the fln-env change staged behind the pin move.

TESTS TO ADD: a regression asserting witness_digest differs for each of the three proven pairs, plus a property test that distinct Name sets always yield distinct witnesses over generated multi-component, dotted-component, and numeric-component names.

RECURRENCE GUARD: every other to_display_string call in fln-env is inside a Display impl and is fine, so a review rule of "no to_display_string inside a hasher" is sufficient and cheap.
close_reason:
FIXED in commit 61a1839, pin moved in the same commit, lane verified green end to end.

THE FIX: witness_digest now binds the structural Name via Name::write_body — the same canonical encoding Environment::decl_content_digest and the provenance manifest already commit to, tagging each component's kind and length. Reusing that encoder rather than writing a private one here is deliberate: a second name encoding is precisely how the two would drift apart again. Tag bumped fln.artifact-incomplete-witness/1 -> /2, because an encoding that changes silently under an unchanged version is indistinguishable from corruption to a consumer that recomputes.

THE TEST CAME FIRST AND FAILED FIRST. the_witness_binds_name_structure_not_its_display_form asserts for each pair BOTH that the names are structurally distinct AND that they render identically, so the test proves something even if Name changes later. Against the old code it failed immediately on the first pair with "two distinct declarations share a witness". It covers all three loss channels (declaration position, missing-list position, numeric-vs-string component), plus separator forgery (x.y.z as three components vs one), plus a determinism check so discrimination was not bought with instability.

WORTH RECORDING: the numeric-component case is NOT hypothetical. Lean's private mangling puts a genuine Num component inside real pin data such as _private.Init.Prelude.0.Lean.Name.hash._proof_1, so the ambiguity was reachable from the very census this witness binds — not just from synthetic names.

PIN MOVE, old -> new:
  d690ccada7f5151a88c1a06062328cf5b13f3f507074ccd489f59c576ebcc96a
  c7fa135fc4f85a21488bfc2393cbe4f7fa81b13205dbf18023ced322b829e015
Sites updated: KERNEL_ADMISSION_ARTIFACT_WITNESS in scripts/evidence.py, the census needle in scripts/e2e/kernel_replay.sh, and the tag references in evidence.py's comment and AGENTS.md.

A DOC CORRECTION FELL OUT: AGENTS.md listed crates/fln-conformance/tests/kernel_replay.rs among the pins that "move together" for the witness. That is true of the census ROWS but not of the witness HEX — that file recomputes the witness via decl_closure::witness_digest (line 384) rather than hardcoding it, so it followed automatically and needed no edit. AGENTS.md now says so, which should save the next person a wasted search.

BLAST RADIUS CHECKED, NOT ASSUMED. The same local conformance run reports checked=2198 accepted=2198 inconclusive=0 artifact_incomplete=6 nested_partial_blocks=0 nested_full_blocks=1, verdict_stream_digest 91ac64a1..., final_logical_root bdd5f7b0... — every one identical to the committed pins. Only the witness field moved, which is exactly the blast radius a witness-encoding fix should have.

VERIFICATION: rch exec -- cargo test --locked -p fln-env 134/134 (133 before, +1 regression). cargo test -p fln-conformance --test kernel_replay run LOCALLY against the pinned v4.32.0 toolchain, 2/2. The full scripts/e2e/kernel_replay.sh lane under the fln-gate flock exits 0, all lanes green — that lane is where evidence.py's witness comparison at :5739 and :5823 actually executes, so it is the end-to-end proof the pin move is complete rather than merely plausible. fmt clean; clippy -p fln-env --all-targets -D warnings exit 0 (it caught a needless clone in my test, fixed). UBS on decl_closure.rs exits 1 with 5 criticals, all pre-existing panic!-in-test-module findings; the count is identical in HEAD and this change adds zero panic/unwrap/expect sites.

TEAMMATE WORK PRESERVED: scripts/evidence.py also carried MistyBluff's active 83pz work. I staged only my own hunk with git apply --cached; their 1386 insertions remain intact and uncommitted in the working tree. This is the same hazard that hit me in bcd7b44, so I was not going to repeat it in the other direction.

title: W6: Deterministic dataflow scheduler — speculative parallelism, canonical merge, perturbation-validated effects
description:
Implement the deterministic dataflow scheduler (Bet B4, §10.6): declarations as dataflow nodes — parse yields a conservative dependency pre-scan; elaboration proceeds speculatively in parallel asupersync regions against O(1) environment snapshots; a declaration that reads a not-yet-committed name suspends on its true dependency or aborts-and-retries; commits merge in CANONICAL ORDER (source order per module; module order per Ledger topology) so the resulting environment, diagnostics, and InfoTrees are those of sequential elaboration — bit-for-bit, at any thread count (FL-INV-01 by construction, the invariant upstream Elab.async demonstrably lacks).

Mechanics: optimistic concurrency — transactions get source-order IDs; commit-time read-set validation against the latest committed predecessor either commits in canonical order or discards/rebases; no last-writer-wins anywhere; conflicting extension mutations serialize. Side-effecting commands are ordering barriers detected conservatively: unknown effects serialize; known-commutative registered effects parallelize. Command effect summaries (ReadsDecl(name, Type|Value|Attributes), ReadsInstances(head), ReadsSimpSet, ReadsGrammar, ReadsOption, WritesDecl, WritesInstance, WritesGrammar, WritesEnvExtension, UsesCapability, Opaque(reason)) are captured dynamically and validated BY PERTURBATION: mutate an allegedly-unread input, require the product unchanged; a failing perturbation demotes the producer to Opaque and opens a Parity-Ledger bead. Cross-module speculation rides Ledger hashes-in-flight; mis-speculation costs a retry, never a wrong answer.

Acceptance: PG-5 thread-matrix {1,8,32} bit-identical environments/diagnostics/artifacts per commit on the corpus; speculation win measured against the sequential baseline; perturbation validator running in CI. Tests: DPOR-bounded schedule exploration of the merge protocol under the asupersync lab; abort/retry storm fixtures; seeded effect-summary lies must be demoted.

## Acceptance Criteria

All bead-specific requirements, acceptance conditions, tests, invariants, compatibility surfaces, evidence levels, performance gates, negative/recovery cases, and user-visible behaviors stated above remain mandatory. In addition, the MANDATORY VERIFICATION DEFINITION OF DONE in Notes must be satisfied with named unit/property/mutation suites, at least one shared real-path no-mock E2E scenario plus failure/recovery coverage, detailed human and schema-versioned NDJSON artifacts, and reproducible close evidence. No listed feature or claim may be silently narrowed, deferred, mocked, or declared complete through an unclassified divergence.
acceptance_criteria:
Declarations execute as asupersync regions against O(1) snapshots using conservative dependency pre-scan and dynamic read/effect sets. Source-order transaction ids, predecessor validation and canonical source/module commit order make environment, diagnostics, InfoTrees, artifacts, roots and receipts byte-identical to sequential elaboration at every thread count; no last-writer-wins exists. Missing committed dependencies suspend or retry, and conflicting extension writes serialize. Typed effect summaries cover declaration type/value/attributes, instances, simp, grammar, options, extensions and capabilities; unknown effects are barriers. Perturbation mutates every allegedly unread input, requires identical products, and atomically demotes lying producers to Opaque with evidence and follow-up. Cross-module speculation binds Ledger hashes-in-flight and wrong speculation only retries. Unit/property/model/metamorphic/DPOR/mutation tests cover commit/rebase/abort, dependency discovery, retry storms, barriers, conflict sets, cancellation/resources, failure atomicity, fairness and recovery; named read-set lie, out-of-order commit, last-writer, dropped-diagnostic, effect misclassification and nondeterministic-seed mutants are killed. Real no-mock corpus E2E runs 1/8/32 threads per commit and 96 or more weekly, injects schedule/effect/cancellation faults, restores, and retains strict schedule/read/effect/root/first-divergence bundles. PG-5 is bit-identical across the certified matrix; speculation performance is reported separately from correctness. All dependencies, scripts/check.sh, cargo/fmt/clippy/UBS, lab/perturbation/thread/mutation/fault lanes pass. title: The fmt gate cannot separate an absent rustfmt component from a real finding, so an environment fault is reported as a code defect (FL-INV-07)
description:
The fmt stage of scripts/check.sh registers --semantic-failure-exit 1, and "cargo fmt --check"
exits 1 BOTH for a real formatting finding AND for a missing rustfmt component. The two are
therefore indistinguishable to the gate, so an environment fault is reported as a code defect.
That is an FL-INV-07 violation in the toolchain layer: an inconclusive outcome rendered as a
verdict about the code.

MEASURED, and the measurement is what makes this filable rather than suspected. A 2x2 was run
against a scratch crate with a real local toolchain lacking both components (recorded on
franken_lean-m3fq, re-measured at rch 1.0.52 on 2026-07-27):

  gate                                   real finding   component absent   check.sh registers   separable
  cargo clippy --all-targets -D warnings      101              1                  101              yes
  cargo fmt --check                             1              1                    1              no

The clippy stage is already FL-INV-07-correct, and by a margin nobody had written down: an absent
component exits outside its declared semantic set, so it types internal_fault rather than a stage
failure. That registration is now pinned per commit precisely so the 101 is not "simplified" to 1,
which would convert every environment fault on the clippy stage into a reported code defect. The
fmt stage has no such margin, and this bead is that gap.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN IT LOOKS. rust-toolchain.toml declares
components = ["rustfmt", "clippy", "miri", "rust-src"]. Those are components OF THE PIN, so a
machine on the right nightly WITHOUT rustfmt does not have this repository's toolchain. Nothing
verifies them: parse_rust_lock in scripts/evidence.py is the sealed-cargo path's toolchain check
and reads that file for channel only. Locally rustup installs the components from the same file,
which is why this has never been felt on a developer machine -- and is exactly why the remote case
went four reproductions without a rule. rch workers are the live exposure: the capability surface
reports a Rust VERSION rather than the pinned toolchain and does not inventory rustfmt or clippy,
and the fleet is now 11 workers where this was filed on 2. cod_1 reproduced selection of a worker
without cargo-clippy four times on 2026-07-25, each time after the full sync had already been paid.

WHY IT WAS NOT FILED UNTIL NOW, recorded so the gap in the record is itself legible. cc_2 measured
it on 2026-07-27 while working m3fq and deliberately did not file it, because creating a bead moves
the id set and forces a ci/KERNEL_CONTRACT_OWNERSHIP.jsonl regeneration in the same commit. It was
disclosed in AGENTS.md under a guard instead, so it could not vanish silently, but it had no
tracker entry and so appeared in no triage and no br ready. The sequencer priced the trade and
authorised the filing on 2026-07-27.

WHAT A REPAIR REQUIRES, and why this is not a five-minute fix. The repair changes the fmt stage's
control flow: the gate must distinguish the absent-component case before consuming the exit code,
which means either probing the component's presence first or registering an exit outside the
semantic set the way clippy does. Both are real edits to scripts/check.sh. NO FULL-GATE check.sh
VERDICT IS OBTAINABLE while the two orphaned working-tree files stand (franken_lean-h4o1), because
check.sh runs cargo test at workspace scope on both branches and one orphan reddens it. So a repair
landed today could only carry package-scope evidence for a change to the gate itself, which is the
wrong shape of evidence for this particular change.

PRIORITY. Filed P2 deliberately, not because the defect is small. The repair is blocked on evidence
that cannot be obtained until 2026-08-01 or an authorised adoption, and a P1 that no pane may
action misleads the next rotation into thinking it is claimable. Raise it when h4o1 resolves.

WHAT IS ALREADY HELD PER COMMIT, so nobody rebuilds it. the_pin_declares_components_and_the_gates_
that_cannot_separate_them_are_disclosed derives the component list from rust-toolchain.toml rather
than transcribing it, and fails if the pin's components move without the AGENTS.md section, if the
clippy stage stops registering an exit outside the environment-fault code, or if the disclosure of
the non-separable gate disappears. What is NOT held: nothing verifies a component is PRESENT before
a gate consumes its verdict. That is this bead.

CLAIM CLASS. The 2x2 is bounded_model -- one host, one instant, a scratch crate. The rch figures
are outside this repository and no test here can hold them; re-measure and record the version.
notes:
BLOCK RE-TESTED AND FALSE -- cc_2, 2026-07-27, at HEAD 5a94b48e. Full measurement in comment 1468.

The description below still says the repair is blocked until 2026-08-01 or an authorised adoption, and that the dependency on franken_lean-h4o1 governs it. That is FALSE and the dependency has been REMOVED. This note exists because a correction filed only as a comment prints BELOW the description, so a reader starting at the top believes the stale half.

WHY IT IS FALSE: the block conflated two surfaces. Verifying the end-to-end gate does need a full check.sh run and is still unavailable. Verifying the CLASSIFICATION -- which exit each stage registers as semantic, the half that decides whether the repair is correct -- is already per-commit at PACKAGE scope via pin_component_findings and registered_semantic_exit in crates/fln-conformance/tests/evidence_finalization.rs. That helper takes the stage as an ARGUMENT and already parses check.sh; re-running its algorithm against HEAD returns fmt=1, clippy=101. So the fmt half needs no new machinery and no orphan, no adoption and no lane.

STILL TRUE AND UNCHANGED: this bead is OPEN and UNFIXED, no guard exists, and the repair is undesigned beyond a candidate (a preflight component check; post-classifying rustup stderr text is REJECTED as an out-of-repo referent). Priority stays P2 -- it is now actionable rather than parked, which is the only thing that moved.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
THE RECORDED BLOCK IS FALSE. RE-TESTED AT HEAD 5a94b48e BY cc_2 (pane 3), 2026-07-27.

This bead was filed blocked on franken_lean-h4o1, and AGENTS.md states the reason in the m3fq
section: "recorded rather than repaired here because repairing it changes the gate's control flow
and no full-gate check.sh verdict is obtainable while the two orphaned working-tree files stand".

I re-tested that before waiting on it, which is this repository's own rule, and it does not hold.
Nothing here is inferred from the call graph; every figure below is derived from the files at HEAD.

=== WHAT THE BLOCK ASSUMES, AND WHY IT IS WRONG ===

It conflates two different verification surfaces:

  (A) THE CLASSIFICATION -- which exit each stage registers as SEMANTIC, and therefore whether an
      absent component types as FL-INV-07 internal_fault or as a code finding.
  (B) THE END-TO-END GATE -- does a real check.sh run refuse correctly with rustfmt absent.

(B) does need a full-gate verdict and is genuinely unavailable while the orphans stand. (A) is the
half that decides whether the repair is correct, and it is ALREADY verified per commit at PACKAGE
SCOPE, today, by the mechanism m3fq itself built.

=== THE MECHANISM ALREADY EXISTS AND IS ALREADY PARAMETERISED BY STAGE ===

crates/fln-conformance/tests/evidence_finalization.rs:

  registered_semantic_exit(check_sh, stage)  -- finds the case arm "|<stage>|" in scripts/check.sh,
      then the next --semantic-failure-exit, then PARSES the digits. It is a parser, not a substring
      match, and it takes the stage as an ARGUMENT.
  pin_component_findings(manifest, check_sh, agents)  -- consumes it, and already refuses when the
      clippy stage registers COMPONENT_ABSENT_EXIT ("1"), and already refuses if AGENTS.md stops
      disclosing that the fmt gate is the non-separable one.
  the_pin_declares_components_and_the_gates_that_cannot_separate_them_are_disclosed  -- the #[test].

That suite runs at PACKAGE SCOPE. I ran it this session: evidence_finalization is 46 passed / 1
failed, the single failure being the h4o1 orphan's rch-tracker test, unrelated to this. No workspace
build, no check.sh, no e2e lane, no Reference pin.

MEASURED -- the parser's own algorithm re-implemented in python against scripts/check.sh at HEAD and
run, rather than reasoned about:

  registered_semantic_exit(check_sh, 'fmt')       = '1'
  registered_semantic_exit(check_sh, 'clippy')    = '101'
  registered_semantic_exit(check_sh, 'test')      = '101'
  registered_semantic_exit(check_sh, 'shellcheck')= '1'

So the fmt half needs NO NEW MACHINERY. The one call that states this bead's defect as a per-commit
finding is registered_semantic_exit(check_sh, "fmt") == COMPONENT_ABSENT_EXIT, in a function that
already takes the argument. The needle exists: check.sh:1077 carries "shellcheck|fmt|" and
check.sh:1082 carries "check|clippy|test".

=== WHAT THE BLOCK IS TRUE OF, STATED IN THE DIRECTION AGAINST MY OWN FINDING ===

A full check.sh run would confirm the repaired gate end to end, and that is unavailable. But it is
not REQUIRED to land a correct repair, and the standard is one this session already met twice: the
o2vz gate-lock library at 5a94b48e was verified by an isolated probe of the function plus per-commit
guards, with the end-to-end rollout explicitly deferred and disclosed. Same shape here. What may not
be claimed afterwards is that the gate was proven end to end.

=== THE REPAIR, AND WHY THE OBVIOUS ONE IS WRONG ===

cargo fmt --check exits 1 for BOTH a real formatting finding and an absent rustfmt, so no choice of
--semantic-failure-exit can separate them. The separation has to come from somewhere else:

  REJECTED -- post-classify on the stderr text. The message is rustup's, lives outside this
  repository, and changes on a version bump with nothing here noticing. That is exactly the
  UBS/rch class this repository already has three instances of.

  CANDIDATE -- a PREFLIGHT: verify the component is present before the stage runs, and emit a typed
  inconclusive if it is not. Then exit 1 from the fmt stage means a finding unambiguously, and the
  registration stays 1 legitimately rather than by accident. It is testable in isolation with a
  manipulated PATH, the same way gate_lock.sh was, and it generalises to every component the pin
  declares rather than to rustfmt alone.

NOT IMPLEMENTED, NOT PRICED IN FULL. I have not measured what a preflight costs per run, nor whether
it belongs in check.sh or in evidence.py's sealed-cargo path where parse_rust_lock already reads
rust-toolchain.toml for channel and ignores the components array.

=== A SECOND FINDING, IN THE EXISTING GUARD, FOUND WHILE VERIFYING THE FIRST ===

registered_semantic_exit is POSITION-DEPENDENT: it takes the FIRST "|<stage>|" and then the NEXT
--semantic-failure-exit anywhere after it. Today that lands correctly because run_stage's
classification case (1077/1082) precedes the sealed-cargo case (1092) and the self_test registration
(1297). Reorder those blocks -- a plausible refactor -- and "clippy" would resolve through
check.sh:1092's "fmt|check|clippy|..." to the NEXT registration it finds, which is
"--semantic-failure-exit 1" at 1297, producing a FALSE gate-conflates finding.

The direction is right (it fails loudly rather than silently) but the message would blame the gate
for a defect of the parser, which is hugg's misdirection shape. Nothing anchors the parser to the
classification block. Recorded here rather than repaired, and deliberately NOT folded into this
bead's scope -- it is a defect of m3fq's guard, not of the fmt gate.

=== WHAT THIS DOES NOT EARN ===

Re-testing a block establishes that the stated reason does not hold. It does not establish that the
repair is easy, correct, or scheduled. This bead stays OPEN and stays unfixed; what changes is that
it is no longer blocked on h4o1, so it does not need adoption, the orphans, or a lane to proceed.
One host, one commit, class bounded_model.
