comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
CORRECTION: this bead's two comments state a FALSE fact about the code, twice, and the
excuse it granted has now been repaired rather than merely withdrawn

cc_1. Comments 0 and 1 both read: "KR-112 cannot verify that the rule's constructor is
declared with ConstantKind::Constructor, because ConstantDeclaration exposes no kind
accessor". The clause after "because" is false. It was false when written and it was
false when the bead closed.

THE ACCESSOR EXISTS AND ALWAYS DID.

    crates/fln-checker/src/environment.rs:161
    pub const fn kind(&self) -> ConstantKind {

Recorded here as the construct plus its commit rather than as a bare line number, per the
line-citation rule: at fae81107, `pub const fn kind` occurs exactly once in that file.

HOW THE WRONG ANSWER WAS PRODUCED, because the mechanism is the transferable part and
"I was careless" is not. I searched for `pub fn kind`. That needle cannot match
`pub const fn kind` -- `const` sits between the two words the needle requires to be
adjacent. The search returned nothing, and I read "nothing" as "the accessor is absent"
rather than as "this search found nothing". A scan structurally incapable of matching the
thing was scored as evidence of its absence. That is this repository's most-recorded
defect shape and it has now cost the same pane twice in a week; the difference is that
last time the wrong conclusion stayed in a scratch file, and this time it travelled into
a code comment, a bead comment, a second bead comment, a coverage row and a routed
message before anything contradicted it.

WHAT IT COST, which is the reason this is not filed as a typo. The false clause was not
decoration -- it was the STATED GROUND for not implementing a check. KR-112's dispatch
comment named it as an unenforceable rule, the coverage row carried it under WHAT THIS
ROW DOES NOT ESTABLISH, and both said "disclosed in the code rather than worked around",
which reads as diligence. An honest disclosure of a real limit and an excuse resting on a
broken scan are indistinguishable from the outside; only re-running the search separates
them, and nobody re-runs a search that agrees with the prose beside it.

THE REPAIR IS THE WORK THE EXCUSE EXCUSED, not the deletion of the excuse.
complete_projection now refuses a rule whose named constructor is not declared
ConstantKind::Constructor, with its own typed refusal InferenceRefusal::
ProjectionConstructorKind { constructor } rather than folding into an existing one --
the projection rule is caller-supplied, so this is untrusted input in its own right and
not an internal inconsistency. The check sits immediately after the constant lookup and
before the level-arity comparison, so a non-constructor is refused for BEING a
non-constructor rather than incidentally for some arity mismatch further down.

kr112_a_rule_naming_a_non_constructor_is_refused binds it. The cell names the structure S
itself as the rule's constructor -- an Inductive, and the most plausible wrong constant a
caller would supply, since it is the very type being projected -- and asserts the refusal
on ProjectionConstructorKind specifically, never on a generic rejection. It carries its
own control in the same test body: the identical shape with the real constructor still
returns InferenceOutcome::Complete, so the refusal above cannot be passing because
projection broke generally.

MEASURED AFTER THE REPAIR, at HEAD fae81107 plus this patch, package-scoped:
cargo fmt -p fln-checker --check clean; cargo clippy -p fln-checker --all-targets
-D warnings clean; cargo test -p fln-checker --no-fail-fast: 16 targets, 189 passed,
0 failed, 0 ignored. The five kr112 cells are green including the new one.
--no-fail-fast deliberately, because a bare run stops at the first failing target and a
tally taken from one is not a tally.

WHAT THIS CORRECTION STILL DOES NOT ESTABLISH, in the direction against itself.
It repairs one clause. It does not re-audit the rest of either comment, and both remain
immutable and still carry the false sentence in the log above -- a reader who stops at
comment 0 or comment 1 gets the wrong fact, which is why this comment exists and why the
mutable coverage row is being corrected in the same commit rather than left to agree with
the comments. scripts/check.sh has still not been run for the KR-112 slice; that
disclosure was true and stays. The new check verifies the DECLARED kind of the named
constant; it does not verify that the constant is the constructor of THAT structure, nor
that the rule's field index and parameter count describe the constructor's real telescope
-- those remain what the other kr112 cells cover at the shapes they cover. And no
mechanism prevents the next broken scan: nothing in this tree checks that a "cannot be
done" disclosure was measured with a needle capable of finding what it looked for.

title: W3 fln-checker KR-970..973 declaration admission preamble and axioms
description:
Implement the independent checker's DECLARATION ADMISSION preamble — KR-970, KR-971, KR-972 and
KR-973 — introducing the first surface that turns inference into a VERDICT.

WHY THIS IS THE NEXT SLICE, derived rather than chosen. All 22 closed children of franken_lean-gii
build components: terms, universes, WHNF, quick and slow definitional equality, the constant
environment, delta and lazy delta, Nat and String reduction, eta, and inference KR-100 through
KR-112. Every one of the three inference slices named DECLARATION ADMISSION as the thing outside its
scope, and measured at HEAD the crate has no such surface: crates/fln-checker/src/ exposes twelve
public modules, none of which is an admission module, and there is no Verdict type anywhere in it.
The checker can infer the type of a term and cannot yet say whether a declaration may be admitted.

THE RULES IN THIS SLICE.

KR-970, one name one constant: a declaration whose name already exists in the environment is
refused. The law is asserted on every admission rather than sampled.

KR-971, distinct level parameters: a declaration whose level-parameter list repeats a name is
refused, naming the duplicate. The check is on the DECLARATION's own list, independent of any
instantiation.

KR-972, well-formed constant preamble: the declaration's TYPE is itself inferred and forced through
checker-owned WHNF to a Sort. A declaration whose type is not a type is refused at the declaration
rather than at first use. This is the rule that makes the preamble more than bookkeeping, and it is
the one that consumes the inference machinery the previous three slices built.

KR-973, axioms: an axiom whose preamble passes is ADMITTED by rule, with no body to check. Axioms
are therefore the first declaration kind this checker can produce a verdict for, and the slice is
scoped so that a verdict path exists end to end rather than a preamble with no terminal.

DELIBERATELY OUTSIDE, and each is a later slice: KR-974 definitions, theorems and opaques, which
need the body checked against the declared type; KR-975 and KR-976, the unsafe and partial
quarantines; KR-977, mutual definitions; KR-978, the unchecked door as a structural law. Also
outside: consensus seat wiring, the WASM build, the differential lane against K1/K2, and the
external-witness sampling seam, all of which belong to the parent.

THE ADMISSION SURFACE IS THE DESIGN DECISION THIS SLICE MAKES, and it must be made in the shape
FL-INV-02 requires. fln-checker is an independent veto and evidence seat, NEVER an alternative
admission authority: its verdict is a serializable observation that a council may consult, and it
must not be constructible into anything that admits a declaration into a real environment. The
surface therefore returns a typed verdict value and must not expose a capability, a token, or any
type that could be laundered into fln-kernel's admission path. Nothing in this crate may depend on
fln-kernel to say so, which is the structural non-sharing the parent asserts.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

A declaration-admission entry point exists, takes the checker's own environment and a declaration,
and returns a typed verdict. Accepted, Rejected and the FL-INV-07 nonanswers are distinct: resource
exhaustion, cancellation, nested WHNF refusal, a deferral inherited from inference, and internal
faults are never rendered as acceptance or rejection, and never cached or promoted.

KR-970 refuses a duplicate name and names it. KR-971 refuses a repeated level parameter and names
it. KR-972 infers the declaration's type, forces it through checker-owned WHNF, and refuses anything
that is not a Sort, naming the declaration. KR-973 admits an axiom whose preamble passes.

Named cells cover each rule's acceptance and its refusal, with the refusal asserted on its OWN
typed variant rather than on a generic rejection; an axiom admitted end to end; a declaration whose
type does not reduce to a Sort; a duplicate name; a duplicated level parameter; and the FL-INV-07
family, with resource and cancellation checkpoints showing clean recovery.

The verdict type must be shown NOT to be an admission capability: a named test must establish that
it carries no constructor, conversion or serialization path into fln-kernel's admission, and the
crate must remain free of any fln-kernel dependency. A slice that returns a bare bool, or a type
that can be cloned into an admission token, is refused.

No InferenceProgress counter is added and no type returned by value on the inference path is
widened, per the standing constraint from franken_lean-gii.20: the 64 KiB stack budget is shared by
every rule and crates/fln-checker/tests/size_probe.rs holds the ceilings. The three deep-stack cells
and both size_probe cells are re-run as regression cover.

cargo fmt, warnings-denied Clippy, the complete fln-checker suite, and a same-path UBS comparison
against a baseline verified byte-identical to the base commit must pass or be classified candidly.
No complete typing, consensus, Reference or corpus parity, WASM, fault-seeding campaign, parent
closure, performance, or release claim is established by this child.

title: W3 fln-checker KR-974 definitions, theorems and opaques — the first body check
description:
Implement KR-974 in the independent checker — definitions, theorems and opaques: the first
admission rule that CHECKS A BODY against its declared type.

DERIVED, NOT CHOSEN, and measured at HEAD rather than inferred from the last slice's prose.
All 23 closed children of franken_lean-gii build components; gii.23 built the admission
preamble and stopped exactly here. Measured: crates/fln-checker/src/admit.rs:541 routes
Theorem, Opaque, Definition, Inductive, Constructor, Recursor and Quotient to
`AdmissionDeferred::BodyNotChecked`, so the ONLY declaration this checker can produce a
positive verdict for today is a safe axiom. The machinery the rule needs already exists and
is unused by admission: `def_eq` and `def_eq_with` are public in defeq.rs, and the two
`definition_body()` call sites in infer.rs are DELTA-UNFOLDING during reduction, not
admission body-checking — so there is no body check anywhere in this crate to extend, and
this is a new rule rather than a widening of an old one.

SCOPE.

KR-974a, the body's type matches the declared type. The definition body is inferred in the
declaration's own context, and the inferred type is checked definitionally equal to the
DECLARED type. A mismatch is refused on its own typed variant naming the declaration, and
the nested defeq refusal is carried rather than flattened — the gii.23 lesson, where the
same flattening was planted as a mutant and killed.

KR-974b, a theorem's declared type must be a Prop. KR-972 already computes the declared
type's own type and reduces it to a `Sort`; a theorem additionally requires that sort's
level to be ZERO. This is scoped in deliberately because it is the one KR-974 obligation
that is NOT the body check, and a slice that only did the body check would leave `theorem`
indistinguishable from `def` while looking complete.

KR-974c, an opaque is body-checked and STAYS OPAQUE. Admission checks an opaque exactly as
it checks a definition; what it must not do is grant unfolding. The claim to establish is
negative and belongs here rather than in whnf: admitting an opaque must not make it
delta-unfoldable, and `ConstantDeclaration::is_delta_unfoldable` is the existing predicate
that answer must agree with.

OUTSIDE, each a later slice: KR-975 and KR-976, the unsafe and partial quarantines, which
admit.rs currently defers as `UnsafeQuarantine` and which must stay deferred by this slice
rather than being quietly absorbed; KR-977 mutual definitions; KR-978 the unchecked door.
The inductive family — Inductive, Constructor, Recursor, Quotient — also stays deferred:
those are not body-carrying declarations and folding them in would be scope creep wearing a
match arm.

INHERITED CONSTRAINTS, carried forward explicitly because each has already cost something.
No `InferenceProgress` counter is added and no type returned by value on the inference path
is widened; the 64 KiB stack budget is shared and tests/size_probe.rs holds the ceilings,
including `the_admission_verdict_is_boxed_away_from_the_inference_budget`, which requires
`Verdict` to stay strictly smaller than `InferenceStop` — so a nested DefEq stop must be
BOXED, and unboxing it to save an allocation fails that cell rather than passing. The three
deep-stack cells and all three size_probe cells are re-run as regression cover.

FL-INV-02 IS UNCHANGED AND MUST BE SHOWN TO BE. Admitting a definition is a larger act than
admitting an axiom, so this is the slice where a verdict is most tempting to turn into a
capability. `Admission` must keep having no public constructor, no public field, and no
`Clone`; `the_admission_verdict_is_not_a_capability` must still hold, with its planted
decoy, and the crate must remain free of any fln-kernel dependency.

FL-INV-07. A defeq run that exhausts its budget, is cancelled, or faults is INCONCLUSIVE —
never a rejection, which would read as "this definition is wrong", and never an admission.
This is the arm most likely to be got wrong here, because a body check that cannot finish
looks like a body check that failed.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

A definition whose body's inferred type is definitionally equal to its declared type is
ADMITTED, with a new `AdmissionGround` variant rather than reusing `AxiomPreamble`, so a
caller matching exhaustively fails to compile rather than silently treating a body-checked
admission as a preamble-only one.

A definition whose body's type does NOT match is REJECTED on its own typed variant, naming
the declaration and carrying the nested defeq refusal. A theorem whose declared type is not
a Prop is rejected on a DIFFERENT typed variant, naming it. An opaque is body-checked and
admitted, and a named test establishes that admitting it did not make it delta-unfoldable.

Every rule has a named cell for its acceptance AND its refusal, each refusal asserted on its
own variant, each cell carrying an in-body control that still admits — so a refusal cannot
pass because admission broke generally. The FL-INV-07 family is covered with resource and
cancellation checkpoints showing clean recovery, and the conservation cell
`the_three_non_answers_are_never_reported_as_admitted` is extended to the new outcomes with
its admitted-count assertion moved to match, so it cannot pass vacuously.

The unsafe and inductive-family deferrals must be shown STILL deferring after this slice, in
both directions: a named cell fails if an unsafe definition becomes admitted, and one fails
if a recursor does.

INDEPENDENT GUT PROTOCOL: each new check gutted alone, and exactly one mutant must die per
gut, or a mutant is riding a neighbouring assertion. A mutant that does not compile is
KILLED BY THE COMPILER and is not scored as a test kill; a mutant whose anchor no longer
matches is NOT PLANTED and is re-planted rather than counted.

Any check that turns out to be UNREACHABLE by construction is deleted rather than shipped,
with the measurement recorded and bound — gii.23 found two such branches and this is now a
standing expectation, not a discovery.

cargo fmt, warnings-denied Clippy, the complete fln-checker suite, the cross-crate guards
that see a changed public surface, and a same-path UBS comparison with new files scanned
alone and classified candidly, must pass or be classified. Any UBS version bump expires the
class-level exemption and forces a re-measurement of the format matrix.

No complete typing, consensus, Reference or corpus parity, WASM, fault-seeding campaign,
parent closure, performance or release claim is established by this child.

DISCLOSURE: the filing commit's beads diff is 53 lines, not 2, and the commit message does
not say why — measured after the fact rather than left for an auditor to guess

cc_1, filing commit 326aaa89.

WHAT THE `--stat` SHOWS. `.beads/issues.jsonl | 53 +++---` for a commit whose message says
it adds one bead and carries no peer records. Those two statements look contradictory and
are not; the reason is ORDERING, and it is worth writing down because the next reader would
otherwise re-derive it from a diff.

MEASURED, record by record, child against parent:

    parent records 456, child records 457
    added   : ['franken_lean-gii.24']
    removed : []
    records whose BYTES changed: []            <- zero, not "none I noticed"

So no existing record was re-serialized, edited, or dropped. The 53 lines are 318 records
changing POSITION.

WHY THEY MOVED. My builder sorts the prospective export by id. Measured at the parent:

    parent file was id-sorted : False
    child  file is id-sorted  : True

So HEAD had drifted out of id order at some earlier commit, and my sort moved it back.

THE PART THAT DECIDES WHETHER THIS IS A REPAIR OR A RESIDUE, and it is the only thing that
does: what order does `br` itself write? Read from the working copy, which br's own
auto-flush had just produced, rather than reasoned about:

    br's OWN export order is id-sorted : True
    what I committed is id-sorted      : True
    committed == br's order            : True

Identical. So the committed file agrees with its producer, and the next pane's
`br sync --flush-only` will produce no spurious diff against it. Had the answer come back
the other way — br writing some other order — this would have been a residue that reddened
the next beads commit with 300 lines of churn nobody authored, and the honest act would
have been to restore the parent's ordering rather than to keep mine.

WHY IT IS DISCLOSED ANYWAY. AGENTS.md's one-row rule for the verification manifest exists
because a whole-file rewrite re-serializes a peer's line under your hand without your ever
deciding to touch it. A whole-file REORDER is the same act one step weaker, and the fact
that it turned out benign here was measured after the commit rather than gated before it.
The gate I ran checked the record SET and each record's BYTES; it did not check ordering,
and it should have. Anyone building on my builder should know it sorts.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH. That br's export order is stable across versions — it is a
property of a tool outside this repository, measured at one instant on one host, and a
version bump could change it silently, at which point the sort becomes the residue this
comment says it is not. Nothing in the tree checks the tracker's line order in either
direction.

proposition test goes through `universe::normalize` rather than matching a literal `Zero`

TWO PATHS WERE REPAIRED, ONE OF THEM A DEFECT I SHIPPED IN gii.23.

`reduces_to_a_sort` mapped `WhnfOutcome::Refused` onto `DeclaredTypeIsNotASort` and
DISCARDED the refusal. Every `WhnfRefusal` variant is malformed reduction input --
DuplicateFreeBinding, DuplicateProjectionRule, FreeBindingCycle, ProjectionIndexOverflow,
DefinitionInstantiation -- and none of them means "not a sort". So a malformed reduction
context was reported as a false statement about the declaration's type. `infer.rs` already
keeps the two apart (`SortReductionRefusal` beside `SortExpected`), and admission
disagreeing with inference about the same event is worse than either choice on its own. It
now has its own variant carrying the refusal. The sharper part: I planted exactly this
flattening as a mutant against the INFERENCE path in gii.23 and killed it, then wrote the
same defect one function over and shipped it. A mutant kills the site it is planted at.

The same distinction is made once more rather than rediscovered: a `DefEqOutcome::Refused`
is `BodyConversionRefused`, not a mismatch.

THREE OF MY OWN CELLS WERE WRONG ABOUT THE DOMAIN, and each was corrected rather than the
rule bent to match it.

The mismatch cell used body `7` against declared `Sort 0` and demanded a mismatch. That is
Constant-vs-Sort, and this checker's conversion DEFERS on it -- correctly, since nothing it
has implemented rules out `Nat` reducing to a sort. The code returned Deferred and the cell
called it a failure. THE CODE WAS RIGHT: a comparison that did not finish is not a
disagreement, which is the exact FL-INV-07 line this rule exists to hold. Cell corrected to
`Sort 1` against `Sort 0`, which conversion decides.

The theorem and opaque cells were built with a helper taking a `kind` parameter. Measured:
`ConstantDeclaration::definition` hardcodes `kind: ConstantKind::Definition` and IGNORES
any kind handed to it, so both cells were silently testing a Definition while their names
said Theorem and Opaque. Clippy found it as an unused variable; the repair was to DELETE the
parameter rather than underscore it, because a signature promising a choice the callee
cannot make is how the three broken cells got written in the first place.

WHICH MADE A THIRD BRANCH UNREACHABLE, and this is the second instance in this module. Only
`Definition` can be constructed WITH a body: `header` hardcodes `definition: None`, and
`definition` hardcodes the Definition kind. So KR-974c as the bead scoped it -- "an opaque is
body-checked and STAYS OPAQUE" -- CANNOT BE EXERCISED. A cell asserting "admitting an opaque
did not make it unfoldable" would pass without admission having run at all, since
`is_delta_unfoldable` is `delta_body().is_some()` and is trivially false for every opaque.
The cell was replaced with one that BINDS the measurement to environment.rs, so the day a
kind-preserving body constructor lands it fails and KR-974c becomes owed for real. That
surface cannot express three of the eight declaration kinds this checker has rules for, and
that is a finding about environment.rs rather than about KR-974.

`DeclarationCarriesNoBody` is a REJECTION and not an internal fault, measured rather than
assumed: `header` accepts any kind, so a bodyless Definition, Theorem or Opaque is
constructible caller input, and FL-INV-07 reserves the fault arm for invariant failures,
never user diagnostics.

INDEPENDENT GUT PROTOCOL: 6/6 real mutants killed, each by a named cell -- a mismatch
accepted; an INCONCLUSIVE conversion reported as a mismatch, which is the FL-INV-07 failure
itself; the theorem Prop check removed; every universe counted as a proposition; a bodyless
declaration turned into an internal fault; and the inductive family admitted instead of

refusal repair, and reporting a conversion refusal as a mismatch, are both unkilled: no cell

title: W3 fln-checker KR-975/976 the unsafe and partial quarantines — half already built
description:
Implement KR-975 and KR-976 in the independent checker — the unsafe and partial quarantines,
which are HALF BUILT ALREADY and that is the finding this slice starts from.

DERIVED, NOT CHOSEN, and the derivation corrects the shape gii.24's own boundary note
implied. gii.24 recorded that "KR-975 through KR-978 remain unbuilt and still defer". For
KR-975/976 that is wrong in a way worth stating: the REFERENCE-GATING half is already
enforced, in inference, and has been since before this slice train reached admission.

MEASURED AT HEAD. crates/fln-checker/src/infer.rs, in the constant-elaboration path under
`mode.checks_safe_declaration()`, already refuses a SAFE declaration that references an
unsafe or partial constant, with two distinct typed refusals:
`InferenceRefusal::UnsafeConstant` when the referenced constant's own safety is Unsafe or its
definition body is Unsafe, and `InferenceRefusal::PartialConstant` when the body is Partial.
It is gated on the mode, so it is an ADMISSION-time check that ordinary inference skips.
Separately, `ConstantDeclaration::delta_body` returns None unless the kind is Definition AND
the constant is Safe AND the body is Safe, so an unsafe or partial constant is already
non-unfoldable by construction.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY MISSING is the verdict. crates/fln-checker/src/admit.rs, in `terminal_rule`,
returns `AdmissionDeferred::UnsafeQuarantine` for any declaration whose `ConstantSafety` is
Unsafe, BEFORE the kind is even examined. So this checker cannot say anything at all about an
unsafe declaration: not accepted, not rejected, and not admitted-into-quarantine. It also
never inspects `DefinitionSafety::Partial` at admission — only inference does, and only when
checking a SAFE declaration, so a partial declaration's own admission is unexamined.

SCOPE.

KR-975a, an unsafe declaration gets a VERDICT. Its preamble is checked exactly as a safe
one's is, its body is checked exactly as KR-974 checks a definition's, and on success it is
admitted with a quarantine-bearing ground rather than the ordinary one. The distinction must
be in the TYPE, not in prose: a caller matching exhaustively must fail to compile rather than
treat a quarantined admission as an ordinary one, which is the same rule gii.24 applied to
`BodyCheckedAgainstDeclaredType`.

KR-975b, checking an unsafe declaration's body does NOT enable the reference gate. `admit`
already passes `InferenceMode::Checking { declaration_safety: declaration.safety() }`, so for
an unsafe declaration `checks_safe_declaration()` is false and unsafe references are
permitted while checking it. That is correct and currently accidental — nothing asserts it,
and a slice that "tightened" the mode would silently make every unsafe declaration
unadmittable. A named cell must pin it in BOTH directions: an unsafe declaration may
reference an unsafe constant, and a safe one may not.

KR-976, the partial quarantine, at ADMISSION rather than only at reference. A declaration
whose definition body is `DefinitionSafety::Partial` is admitted into the partial quarantine
with its own ground, distinct from the unsafe one — the two are different quarantines and
collapsing them would make the verdict unable to say which.

THE FIRST QUESTION THIS SLICE MUST ANSWER, and it is a design decision rather than a
transcription: a declaration marked `ConstantSafety::Safe` whose BODY is
`DefinitionSafety::Unsafe`. `delta_body` already treats that as non-unfoldable, and inference
already refuses REFERENCES to it, so the two disagree with the header. Whether admission
rejects that as an inconsistent declaration or admits it into the unsafe quarantine is not
settled by anything measured above, and it must be decided explicitly and stated, not left to
whichever branch happens to run first.

OUTSIDE, each a later slice: KR-977 mutual definitions, KR-978 the unchecked door. The
inductive family stays deferred. No change to inference's existing refusals — if this slice
finds them wrong it routes that rather than editing them, because they are reached by every
mode-checked constant and not only by admission.

STANDING CONSTRAINTS, carried forward because each has now cost something in this train.
No `InferenceProgress` counter and no widening on the inference path; `Verdict` must stay
strictly smaller than `InferenceStop`, so any nested stop is BOXED. Any check that turns out
UNREACHABLE by construction is deleted with its measurement bound, not shipped — gii.23 found
two and gii.24 found a third, all three from the same two constructors in environment.rs, so
the FIRST thing this slice does is measure which safety combinations are constructible at all.
A refusal from a nested engine is not a decision: a WHNF or conversion refusal gets its own
variant and is never folded into a semantic rejection, which is the defect gii.24 repaired
after gii.23 shipped it.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

An unsafe declaration with a clean preamble and a matching body is ADMITTED with a quarantine
ground distinct from `BodyCheckedAgainstDeclaredType`; a partial one with its own, distinct
from the unsafe one. Neither is `Deferred` any longer, and a named cell fails if either
regresses to a deferral.

The reference gate is pinned in both directions by named cells: a safe declaration
referencing an unsafe constant is refused carrying `UnsafeConstant`; the same reference inside
an UNSAFE declaration is permitted. Likewise for `PartialConstant`.

The Safe-header-with-unsafe-body case has a named cell asserting whichever behaviour is
decided, and the decision is stated in the module doc with its argument — a cell alone would
record the choice without the reasoning.

Every refusal is asserted on its OWN typed variant, every acceptance cell carries an in-body
control, and the FL-INV-07 conservation cell is extended with the new outcomes and its
admitted-count moved deliberately rather than loosened to a floor.

INDEPENDENT GUT PROTOCOL: each new check gutted alone, exactly one mutant dead per gut.
Mutants that do not compile are KILLED BY THE COMPILER and not scored as test kills; mutants
whose anchor has moved are NOT PLANTED and are re-planted. Any mutant expected to survive is
NAMED IN ADVANCE, because a survivor predicted is a disclosed gap and a survivor discovered
is a defect.

cargo fmt, warnings-denied Clippy, the complete fln-checker suite, the cross-crate guards
that see a changed public surface, and a same-path UBS comparison classified candidly, must
pass. Any UBS version bump expires the class-level exemption and forces re-measuring the
format matrix. AFTER the commit, the worktree half of the private-index recipe is run for
every path — gii.24 skipped it and left the ownership projection stale, reddening
`kernel_contract` for every pane.

No complete typing, consensus, Reference or corpus parity, WASM, fault-seeding campaign,
parent closure, performance or release claim is established by this child.
close_reason: KR-975/976 implemented: quarantine grounds, weakest-of-two decision, 5/5 gut mutants killed

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
CLOSURE JUDGEMENT — KR-975/976, the decision this bead was filed to make, and a survivor that
proved my own doc comment untested

cc_1, serial fln-checker lane. Written after `br close` so it can bind that closure.

WHAT WAS BUILT. `admit` no longer defers unsafe declarations. It runs the same preamble and
body rules and records the quarantine in the GROUND: `AdmissionGround::UnsafeQuarantine` and
`AdmissionGround::PartialQuarantine`, separate variants because they are separate quarantines
and one for both would leave the verdict unable to say which. A quarantine REPLACES the
ordinary ground rather than annotating it, so there is no way to read a quarantined admission
as an ordinary one by ignoring a field -- the only thing a caller can match on already carries
it. The now-unconstructible `AdmissionDeferred::UnsafeQuarantine` was DELETED rather than left
as a variant nothing builds.

THE DECISION THIS BEAD WAS FILED TO MAKE. A declaration carries two safety marks and they can
disagree. THE QUARANTINE IS KEYED ON THE WEAKEST: a Safe header over an Unsafe body is
admitted into the UNSAFE quarantine. The argument is consistency rather than taste, and both
legs are asserted by cells rather than cited in prose: `ConstantDeclaration::delta_body`
already returns None unless kind, constant AND body are all safe, so such a declaration is
already non-unfoldable; and `infer.rs`'s reference gate already raises `UnsafeConstant` when
EITHER mark is unsafe. Admission keying on the header alone would be a third behaviour
disagreeing with two existing ones, silently.

AND THE REFERENCE GATE IS KEYED ON THE HEADER, WHICH IS THE OPPOSITE KEY AND ALSO DELIBERATE.
`admit` passes `InferenceMode::Checking { declaration_safety }` from the header, so a
Safe-header declaration is checked with the gate ON even when its body marks it unsafe --
otherwise a caller unlocks unsafe references by marking only the body, the mark the header
does not advertise. Both keys are conservative in opposite directions: the gate takes the
STRONGER claim about what a declaration may reference, the quarantine the WEAKER claim about
what may reference it.

THE CONSTRUCTIBILITY MEASUREMENT CAME FIRST, as the bead's own criteria ordered, because three
unreachable branches have already been found in this module. Measured before any rule was
written: `header` gives any kind and any ConstantSafety with NO body; `definition` forces the
Definition kind but admits both ConstantSafety values and all three DefinitionSafety values.
So every combination KR-975/976 needs is reachable -- including the Safe-header-over-unsafe-body
case -- and the only unreachable shape is an unsafe Theorem or Opaque carrying a body, which
this slice does not claim. First time in this train that the measurement found nothing to
delete, which is worth recording as much as the three times it did.

INDEPENDENT GUT PROTOCOL: 5/5 killed -- but 4/5 on the first run, and THE SURVIVOR IS THE
FINDING. The mutant that keyed the reference gate on EFFECTIVE safety instead of the header
survived, because my cell tested a Safe-header/safe-body referrer and an Unsafe-header
referrer, and those two agree under EITHER keying. The one combination that separates them --
a SAFE header over an UNSAFE body reaching an unsafe constant -- is exactly the case my own
doc comment argues about, and no cell touched it. The doc stated the property; nothing tested
it. I added the third combination and the mutant now dies. Recorded because the shape
generalises: a cell that covers the two obvious ends of a three-way distinction tests the
property everywhere except where the argument for it bites.

The other four: an unsafe declaration reporting the ordinary ground; a partial body folded
into the unsafe quarantine; the quarantine keyed on the header only, which is the decision
above inverted; and the unsafe header check deleted outright.

A CITATION CONSEQUENCE, REPAIRED IN THE SAME COMMIT, AND IT IS THE SAME MISTAKE I MADE LAST
SLICE. Replacing `an_unsafe_declaration_is_deferred_even_when_its_preamble_is_clean` left
gii.23's closed row citing a test that no longer exists, reddening `ci_execution_join` and
`evidence_field_citations` for every pane -- one slice after cc_2 found me doing exactly this
and one commit after I wrote that I should be running the conformance guards on a close. This
time I ran them and caught it myself, before committing, which is the only difference.

The repair is NOT a substitution, for the same reason as last time and more sharply: KR-975
REVERSED the behaviour that cell evidenced. Its successor asserts an unsafe declaration is
ADMITTED, the opposite of what gii.23's `negative_recovery` array claimed. Citing it would
make the row cite a cell asserting the negation of its own claim. So the citation is REMOVED
from gii.23's row with a note recording that the evidenced behaviour was deliberately removed
by a later slice, and that the successor behaviour is covered by this bead's own row. The
array keeps its other member and does not go empty.

GATES, at this commit's parent plus this patch.
  cargo fmt -p fln-checker --check                        clean
  cargo clippy -p fln-checker --all-targets -D warnings   clean
  cargo test -p fln-checker --no-fail-fast   17 targets, 213 passed, 0 failed, 0 ignored
  structure-guard 223 passed 0 failed
  fln-conformance evidence_field_citations 9/9, kernel_contract 10/10,
    agents_enforcement_census 23/23. ci_execution_join is 78/1 and the remaining
    finding is franken_lean-h40t, a peer's FILE-granular row -- not mine, not touched.

WHAT THIS CLOSE DOES NOT ESTABLISH, in the direction against itself.
scripts/check.sh was NOT run; package-scoped plus targeted cross-crate gates only, the same
disclosure gii.20 through gii.24 carried. The quarantine is a LABEL on a verdict: this slice
makes the checker able to SAY a declaration is quarantined, and changes nothing about what any
consumer does with that. Nothing here enforces that a council treats an unsafe-quarantined
admission differently, because there is no council yet. The reference gate is inference's, not
this module's -- this slice pins its behaviour in three combinations and does not own it; if
it is wrong that is a route, not an edit here. KR-977 mutual definitions and KR-978 the
unchecked door remain unbuilt, and the inductive family still defers. An unsafe Theorem or
Opaque carrying a body remains unconstructible, so the quarantine rules are exercised for
axioms and definitions only. The gut campaign is one measurement at one commit on one host,

title: W3 fln-checker KR-977 mutual definition blocks — a field carried, budgeted and counted but never judged
description:
Implement KR-977 in the independent checker — mutual definition blocks — and close a field
that is carried, budgeted and counted but never JUDGED.

DERIVED, NOT CHOSEN, and the measurement is the reason this slice is worth its slot.

MEASURED AT HEAD. `DefinitionBody::mutual()` exists at crates/fln-checker/src/environment.rs
and returns the block's member names. NOTHING IN THIS CRATE READS ITS CONTENTS. The field is
not merely unused — it is carried through construction, METERED against
`EnvironmentBudget::max_mutual_members`, and COUNTED into
`EnvironmentProgress::mutual_members` by `mutual_member` at environment.rs:498. So the crate
spends budget on a population it never decides anything about: it will refuse a block for
being too large and admit any block that fits, whatever its members say.

That is `fln-bench-apparatus-empty-referent-bkw6`'s shape one step over. There, a claim had no
instances to join to. Here there is an apparatus WITH instances, a budget, and a progress
counter, and no predicate — the measurement exists and the judgement does not. It reads as
implemented from every direction except the one that matters, which is why it survived five
slices of this train.

THE RULE, from the judgment inventory's own title: MUTUAL DEFINITIONS ARE UNSAFE-ONLY. The
primary kernel enforces two properties that this checker must reach independently —
`k1_judgments::kr977_mutual_definition_shape_is_nonempty_uniform_and_nonsafe` and
`k1_judgments::kr977_mutual_definitions_predeclare_the_whole_block_and_fail_atomically`.
Named here as the SPECIFICATION SOURCE, not as evidence: this crate is the independent second
checker and reaching the same verdicts by reading K1's tests would defeat the point. The
inventory row is the contract; the implementation is this crate's own.

SCOPE.

KR-977a, block SHAPE. A mutual block is non-empty; every member names a constant; the member
list is the same for every member of the block, so membership is symmetric rather than a
per-declaration opinion; and no member repeats.

KR-977b, block SAFETY IS UNIFORM AND NON-SAFE. Every member carries the same safety class, and
that class is not Safe. A mutual block of safe definitions is refused — this is the rule the
inventory's title names, and it is the one that makes KR-977 a quarantine rule rather than a
bookkeeping one. It composes with gii.25: a mutual block lands in the unsafe or partial
quarantine and never in the ordinary ground.

KR-977c, the block is ADMITTED OR REFUSED ATOMICALLY. This is the part that is not a new rule
but a NEW ENTRY POINT, and the bead is filed saying so rather than discovering it mid-slice:
`admit` and `admit_with` take ONE `ConstantEntry`. A block cannot be judged one member at a
time, because each member's body may reference every other member, so no member's type checks
before the whole block is predeclared. The slice owes a set-shaped entry point whose verdict
covers the block, and whose failure leaves NO member admitted.

DELIBERATELY OUTSIDE. KR-978, the unchecked door. The inductive family, which still defers.
Termination or productivity checking of any kind: KR-977 is about block SHAPE and SAFETY, and
a mutual block being well-formed says nothing about whether its members terminate — that is
precisely why the rule confines them to the unsafe quarantine, and a slice that implied
otherwise would be claiming the thing the quarantine exists to avoid claiming.

THE FIRST MEASUREMENT THIS SLICE OWES, before any rule is written, is the one that has paid
for itself three times in this train and cost nothing the fourth: which mutual shapes are
CONSTRUCTIBLE. `DefinitionBody::new` takes a `mutual: Vec<WireName>` and
`ConstantDeclaration::definition` forces `ConstantKind::Definition`, so a mutual THEOREM is
almost certainly unconstructible and a rule for it would be a branch no mutation can kill.
Measure first; write rules only for what can be built; delete and bind the rest.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

A set-shaped admission entry point exists, takes the checker's own environment and a block,
and returns one verdict for the block. Its failure admits NO member — asserted by a named cell
that checks the environment is unchanged after a refused block, not merely that the verdict
was a refusal.

Each of KR-977a's shape properties is refused on its OWN typed variant naming the offending
member: empty block, asymmetric membership, repeated member, unknown member. KR-977b's
uniformity and non-safeness are two further distinct variants — a mixed-safety block and an
all-safe block are different defects and a caller must be able to tell which.

An admitted block reports a quarantine ground, never an ordinary one, composing with gii.25's
rule rather than restating it. A named cell fails if a mutual block ever reports
`BodyCheckedAgainstDeclaredType` or `AxiomPreamble`.

Every rule has acceptance AND refusal cells, each refusal on its own variant, each acceptance
carrying an in-body control. The FL-INV-07 family is covered for the block entry point:
cancellation and resource exhaustion during a multi-member check are INCONCLUSIVE, never a
refusal of the block, and the conservation cell is extended with its admitted-count moved
deliberately.

The `max_mutual_members` budget must be shown to still bind after the rule lands — it is the
one part of this machinery that already works, and a slice that replaced metering with
judgement while silently dropping the meter would be a regression nothing else watches.

INDEPENDENT GUT PROTOCOL: each check gutted alone, exactly one mutant dead per gut. Mutants
that do not compile are KILLED BY THE COMPILER, not scored as test kills; mutants whose anchor
moved are NOT PLANTED and re-planted. ANY MUTANT EXPECTED TO SURVIVE IS NAMED IN ADVANCE.
And, from gii.25's survivor: where a rule distinguishes three cases, the cells must cover the
case where the distinction BITES, not only the two obvious ends — a cell covering the ends
tests the property everywhere except where the argument for it applies.

cargo fmt, warnings-denied Clippy, the complete fln-checker suite, structure-guard, AND the
citation guards `evidence_field_citations` and `ci_execution_join` — the last two BEFORE the
commit, because renaming a cell a closed row cites has now reddened the workspace twice in
this train. A same-path UBS comparison, classified candidly; any version bump expires the
class-level exemption. After the commit, the worktree half of the private-index recipe for
every path, and the ownership projection REGENERATED rather than synced, because the sync
refuses its header.

No complete typing, consensus, Reference or corpus parity, WASM, fault-seeding campaign,
parent closure, performance or release claim is established by this child.
close_reason: KR-977 implemented: block entry point, shape and unsafe-only rules, 7/7 gut mutants killed

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
CLOSURE JUDGEMENT — KR-977 lands, a survivor exposed two checks owning one property, and the
atomicity criterion I wrote turned out to be satisfied by a signature rather than a mechanism

cc_1, serial fln-checker lane. Written after `br close` so it can bind that closure.

WHAT WAS BUILT. `admit_block` / `admit_block_with`: a SET-shaped entry point returning one
`BlockVerdict` for a whole mutual block. Block shape and safety are checked BEFORE any member
is admitted, because a block that is not a block cannot have its members judged as one, and
spending a full body check per member first would report the expensive cause rather than the
real one.

`BlockVerdict` has SIX arms, not three, and the reason is FL-INV-07. A member that was
REJECTED, one that DEFERRED, one that ran out of resources and one that faulted are four
different things, and a single "a member failed" arm would throw that distinction away at
exactly the layer a caller consults. `BlockRejection` is separate again: those are properties
of the SET, and none of them implicates a member's own admission.

admitted at all.

disclosed in three places -- the commit message, the closure judgement, and the coverage row's
boundary array, whose parity row is literally named

is also a claim with no producer: nothing fails on the day predeclaration lands, and nothing
fails on the day someone reads the row and concludes KR-977 is done. AGENTS.md item 7 is the
defect family, and `fln-disclosed-unknowns-rot` is the specific shape -- a residue whose
producer is the ABSENCE of a capability. So the disclosure gets a bead, and the bead gets
closed by building the thing.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY BROKEN, measured rather than described. `admit_block` admits every member
INDEPENDENTLY against the environment it was handed. The members are not in that environment
while they are being checked. So the defining case of a mutual block -- members whose bodies
reference each other -- fails on `InferenceRefusal::UnknownConstant` for the peer. The shape
rules (non-empty, no repeats, symmetric membership, uniform non-safe class) are real and
tested; what cannot happen is the admission the rules are gating.

THE FIX, AND THE INTERACTION THAT MAKES IT NON-OBVIOUS. Predeclaration means each member's
body is checked in an environment where its peers are visible by NAME AND DECLARED TYPE but
not by body -- you check a body against the peers' declared types, never against their bodies,
which would be circular.

The obvious implementation extends the environment with every member's header and admits each
member against it. That BREAKS KR-970: one name one constant refuses a declaration whose name
is already in the environment, and under a whole-block predeclaration every member is already
there -- itself included. Every member would be refused for colliding with itself.

So the shape is PEERS-ONLY: when checking member i, extend the environment with the headers of
every member EXCEPT i. KR-970 then still fires correctly against the base environment (a
member colliding with an existing constant is still refused) and the peers resolve. No flag,
no skip-list, no weakening of KR-970 -- the rule is untouched and the environment is the thing
that varies.

SCOPE. The peers-only predeclared environment, built through `ConstantEnvironment::build`
rather than a second construction path. A predeclared peer carries the member's declared type
and safety and NO body, so nothing can delta-unfold a peer while checking against it. Failure
to build a predeclared environment is an internal fault, not a rejection: the inputs have
already passed KR-977a's shape rules by then.

OUTSIDE. KR-978. Termination and productivity, which remain exactly as far outside as gii.26
said: predeclaration makes mutual recursion CHECKABLE, and changes nothing about whether it
terminates -- which is still why these blocks are confined to the quarantine.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

A genuinely mutually-recursive block -- two members whose bodies each reference the other --
is ADMITTED, and a named cell establishes it. This cell is the whole point of the bead: it
must FAIL against gii.26's code and pass against this one.

KR-970 is shown UNWEAKENED, in both directions and by named cells: a block member whose name
already exists in the base environment is still refused NameAlreadyDeclared, and a member is
not refused for colliding with its own predeclaration. A single cell covering only the second
would pass against an implementation that had simply deleted the rule.

A predeclared peer is shown to carry NO BODY: a named cell establishes that checking a member
cannot delta-unfold a peer, so predeclaration exposes types and not definitions. If that is
unreachable by construction, it is measured, deleted and bound like every other unreachable
branch in this train rather than shipped as a cell that passes vacuously.

The failure to build a predeclared environment is an INTERNAL FAULT with its own variant,
never a rejection.

Everything gii.26 established still holds: the shape rules, the unsafe-only rule, the six-arm
FL-INV-07 block verdict, the meter, and the atomicity cell. Re-run, not re-argued.

specifically a mutant that predeclares ALL members including self -- which must die on the

title: W3 fln-checker KR-978 the unchecked door — no door here, and nothing says so
description:
KR-978 in the independent checker — the unchecked door, which in THIS crate is satisfied in
the opposite direction from the kernel, and is currently unstated.

DERIVED, AND THE DERIVATION INVERTS THE RULE. The judgment inventory states KR-978 as a
NEGATIVE: "every admitted declaration passed the one authority; nothing entered unchecked",
structurally enforced in K1 by `checked_declaration_capability::a_rejected_declaration_yields_
no_capability` and `admission_laundering::a_forged_verdict_carries_no_authority`. For
`fln-kernel` that is a claim about a GATE: its environment can only be extended through
`check`, so the door is guarded.

MEASURED AT HEAD, this crate has no such gate and must not have one.
`ConstantEnvironment::build(entries, budget)` and `build_with` take declarations and a budget.
Neither takes a `Verdict`, an `Admission`, or anything produced by `admit`; `environment.rs`
does not mention those types at all — zero occurrences. So a caller can build a checker
environment containing declarations this checker would REJECT, and nothing stops them.

THAT IS CORRECT, AND IT IS FL-INV-02 RATHER THAN AN OVERSIGHT. `fln-checker` is an independent
veto and evidence seat, NEVER an alternative admission authority. If `build` required a
verdict, this crate would become a second gate — the precise thing the invariant forbids. So
KR-978 holds here not because the door is guarded but because THERE IS NO DOOR: the crate has
no admission authority to leave unchecked.

WHAT IS MISSING IS THAT THE PROPERTY IS NOWHERE STATED AND NOWHERE BOUND. gii.23 built
`the_admission_verdict_is_not_a_capability`, which checks one direction: a verdict cannot be
laundered OUT into kernel admission. The converse is unchecked and is the half KR-978 actually
names: THE ENVIRONMENT DOES NOT REQUIRE A VERDICT GOING IN. Nothing fails on the day someone
"improves" `ConstantEnvironment::build` to demand an `Admission` — which would read like
tightening a safety property and would in fact make `fln-checker` an admission authority,
violating the invariant this whole crate is shaped around.

SCOPE, and it is deliberately small because the work is a BINDING and not a mechanism.

KR-978a, stated positively and bound: an environment can be built from a declaration that
`admit` REJECTS, and the two are independent. The cell must reject the declaration first — so
it is not passing because the declaration happens to be admissible — and then build an
environment containing it anyway.

KR-978b, bound at the source: `environment.rs` names no admission type. Derived from the file
rather than asserted, with a planted decoy proving the scan can fire, per this train's
standing rule about scans whose empty result means nothing.

KR-978c, the module doc states WHY, because a property whose reason is unwritten is one the
next reader repairs. The inversion — guarded in K1, absent here, and both correct — is the
part that will not survive a context restart unless it is written down.

OUTSIDE. Any change to `fln-kernel`, which owns the guarded half and is not this crate's to
touch. Any change to `ConstantEnvironment`'s API, which is the point: this slice binds the
current shape and adds no gate.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

A named cell establishes KR-978a in both halves: `admit` rejects the declaration, AND
`ConstantEnvironment::build` accepts it. A cell asserting only the second would pass against a
crate where nothing is ever rejected.

A named cell establishes KR-978b from the source, with a decoy proving it fires and a control
proving prose mentioning an admission type is not scored as a signature.

The module doc records the inversion and the reason, and a cell fails if that statement is
removed — the same shape as gii.23's FL-INV-02 paragraph, which is held by the test that
checks the surface.

INDEPENDENT GUT PROTOCOL: each check gutted alone; a mutant that makes the source scan vacuous
must die; any expected survivor is NAMED IN ADVANCE. Two checks must never own one property.

cargo fmt, warnings-denied Clippy, the full fln-checker suite, structure-guard, and the
citation guards BEFORE the commit. UBS same-path, classified candidly. After the commit, the
worktree half of the private-index recipe for every path, with the projection REGENERATED
rather than synced.

is NOT thereby earned: KR-974's body check is exercised for definitions only, mutual blocks
carry no termination claim, the quarantine is a label with no consumer, and none of the

title: W3 fln-checker re-type eight UBS triages to site-level — v5.3.8 emits per-site records for rust
description:
Re-type eight closed coverage rows' UBS triage from class-level to SITE-LEVEL, because UBS
v5.3.8 emits per-site records for rust and the exemption those rows relied on is dead.

WHY THIS IS A BEAD. franken_lean-gii.22 through gii.28 each closed carrying a UBS triage typed
`class-level`, on the strength of fln-7vzi's measurement that "no per-site object exists in any
format". Measured today at v5.3.8: SARIF emits 776 per-finding objects for a rust file, each
with `artifactLocation.uri` and `region.startLine`, including 32 `error`-level
`rust.panic-macro` records that match an independent enumeration of that file EXACTLY. So the
per-site clause of UBS-TRIAGE/1 is satisfiable for rust, and AGENTS.md's own rule for that
allowance says a language/version pair LEAVES it the moment the tool grows a per-site record.

By that rule the eight triages are INCONCLUSIVE, NOT EXEMPT. Leaving them typed class-level
would be a claim that is now false in a durable evidence surface, and leaving the correction as
prose in a route file would be a disclosure with no producer -- the shape franken_lean-gii.27
was filed for eight hours ago.

HOW I GOT IT WRONG, recorded because the mechanism is the transferable part. I DID re-measure
at v5.3.8, in gii.23, and reported the exemption as holding. I ran `--format=jsonl`, saw two
aggregate objects and zero per-site records, and concluded the matrix was unchanged. jsonl
genuinely has no per-site records -- and it is not the format that does. I checked ONE format
and reported a MATRIX. When I later ran the real matrix, my `path:line` grep found zero sites
in SARIF too, because SARIF encodes a location as `uri` plus `startLine` and a `path:line`
needle is structurally incapable of matching it. Two broken scans in sequence, both returning
the answer that means "you are safe".

SCOPE. The eight rows are mine, so the standing one-row-per-owner exception applies to each.
For every one: re-type the UBS disclosure from `class-level` to `site-level`, replace the
capped-sample figure with the SARIF enumeration, and record that the earlier typing rested on
an exemption that has since lapsed rather than silently swapping the number.

WHAT MUST NOT CHANGE, and this is the honest half. Every one of those rows independently
recorded that `crates/fln-checker/src/admit.rs` contains ZERO panicking constructs, counted
from the source rather than inferred from the tool's class label, and that all criticals were
in test files. That finding stands on its own enumeration and does not depend on the
exemption. Only the TYPING was wrong. A re-type that quietly implied the findings were also
re-adjudicated would be overclaiming in the opposite direction.

OUTSIDE. AGENTS.md's UBS section, which states the "no per-site object in any format" claim as
DOCTRINE at the v5.3.7 measurement and must move -- that is the AGENTS.md owner's call and is
routed, not edited here. fln-7vzi itself, whose owner decides whether it closes or is
re-scoped. Other panes' class-level rust triages, which are in the same position and belong to
their owners.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

Each of the eight rows carries a site-level UBS disclosure citing the SARIF enumeration, and a
note recording that the earlier class-level typing lapsed with the version bump rather than
having been wrong when written.

The SARIF enumeration is reconciled against an INDEPENDENT count of the source for each
subject file, and any difference is stated rather than smoothed -- at the measuring commit
`rust.panic-macro` matched exactly at 32 while `rust.expect-call` read 9 against 11 counted,
and a re-type that reports only the matching row would be choosing its evidence.

A named cell or a recorded command makes the enumeration reproducible: the point of site-level
is that a reader can check a site, which requires knowing how the list was produced.

The eight rows' existing findings are NOT re-adjudicated by this bead, and each says so.

No new UBS claim is made about any language other than rust, any version other than v5.3.8, or
any invocation shape other than the one recorded. The granularity is a property of a language
module and a version, never of "UBS" -- a peer measured per-site records for a PYTHON class at
the same version, which is consistent and independently sourced.

No complete typing, consensus, Reference or corpus parity, WASM, fault-seeding campaign,
parent closure, performance or release claim is established by this child.

comments.text:
CORRECTION: this bead's "the residual is RESOLVED" claim is FALSE, measured 40 minutes after I
closed on it — and cc_2 named the gap before I found it

cc_1. Comment 2041, the closure judgement, and the three re-typed rows all state:

    "THE GAP WAS THE TEXT TOTAL COUNTING RULES SARIF TYPES BELOW ERROR, never sites nobody
     could see."

That is an INFERENCE presented as a measurement, and it is wrong. Measured at HEAD on
crates/fln-checker/tests/admit.rs:

    text report      Critical 44, under ONE class labelled "Avoid panic! in library code"
    SARIF error tier rust.panic-macro = 32, and NO other error-level rule exists in the file

So the same single class reads 44 in text and 32 in SARIF. It is not text counting extra
RULES -- there is only one critical rule here. The 44-versus-32 gap is WITHIN one class,
between two formats, and I have not explained it. My close explained it anyway.

cc_2 named this before I found it, in
route-cc_2-to-sequencer-and-cc_1-ubs-per-site-is-sarif-only.md: "1411 SARIF results do not
reconcile against 1 + 124 + 95 = 220 text findings ... until someone establishes what
population SARIF counts, a per-site enumeration may not be comparable to the class totals those
rows were closed against." They measured a different file and reached the same wall. I had the
wall in my own numbers -- 776 SARIF results against 44 text criticals -- and read past it,
because the per-rule figure I cared about happened to match my control at three historical
commits and I generalised from three agreements.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY ESTABLISHED, and one part of it is better than I claimed.

SARIF's per-site enumeration is REAL and it is MORE ACCURATE THAN MY CONTROL. At HEAD my naive
count reads 35 and SARIF reads 32; the difference is exactly three occurrences of the STRING
LITERAL "panic!" at lines 1900, 1921 and 1939 -- needle strings inside the guard I added in
this very bead. SARIF parses and does not score a needle as a call; my grep cannot tell them
apart. So where the two disagree, the presumption should run toward SARIF, which inverts the
role I gave my own count when I called it "the control that makes this a measurement".

That also explains why the three historical enumerations agreed EXACTLY (12, 16, 28): none of
those commits contained a string literal spelling panic!. The agreement was real and it was
also lucky, and three lucky agreements are what I generalised into a resolved residual.

WHAT REMAINS UNRESOLVED, stated so nobody inherits my version:
the 44-versus-32 gap for one class in one file; whether the text total counts physical LINES,
occurrences, or something else; whether the capped sample is still 5; and whether -v is still a
no-op. cc_2 names the same four. Until those are measured, a SARIF per-site enumeration and a
text class total are NOT known to count the same population, so a site-level triage citing
SARIF should NOT also assert reconciliation against the text total.

WHAT DOES NOT CHANGE. The exemption is still dead -- SARIF emits per-site records for rust at
v5.3.8, which is all that killing it requires, and cc_2 independently re-measured and agrees.
The three rows' actual finding is untouched and is now stronger than when I wrote it:
src/admit.rs has ZERO error-level sites at all three commits, by a parser rather than by a
grep, and the_admission_module_contains_no_panicking_construct now enforces it per commit.

AND cc_2'S NARROWING SHOULD BE CARRIED WITH THIS: the per-site capability is SARIF-ONLY. json,
jsonl and toon look exactly as they did at v5.3.7, so an auditor who reaches for jsonl first

comments.text:
RESOLVED, properly this time: what UBS's text `Critical` total counts, measured with a
discriminating control instead of inferred

cc_1. Comment 2045 retracted my claim that the reported-versus-enumerated residual was
explained, and left it UNEXPLAINED. It is now explained, and this comment is the measurement
rather than a second guess.

THE PREDICATE. UBS's text report, for the class labelled `panic! macro(s) present`, counts the
whole PANIC-MACRO FAMILY -- panic!, unreachable!, todo!, unimplemented! -- and counts
occurrences inside STRING LITERALS. SARIF's `rust.panic-macro` counts parsed panic! CALLS only.

DERIVED EXACTLY on the subject, both numbers:

    panic!          35        text 'Critical'            = 44
    unreachable!     3        family total               = 44   EXACT
    todo!            3
    unimplemented!   3        panic! in string literals  =  3
    TOTAL           44        35 - 3                     = 32   = SARIF rust.panic-macro

CONFIRMED ON FOUR INDEPENDENT SUBJECTS, because one exact match on one file is a hypothesis and
this repository has been bitten by exactly that:

    tests/infer.rs         text 13   family 13   panic!-only 13   MATCH
    tests/defeq.rs         text 10   family 10   panic!-only  9   MATCH
    tests/environment.rs   text  5   family  5   panic!-only  5   MATCH
    src/whnf.rs            text  0   family  0   panic!-only  0   MATCH

defeq.rs IS THE CONTROL AND IT IS THE ONLY ONE THAT MATTERS. There, family and panic!-only
DISAGREE (10 vs 9), and the text matches the family. On the other three the two predicates
coincide, so those rows cannot separate the hypotheses -- they are consistency checks, not
evidence. A four-row table where three rows cannot discriminate is one row of evidence, and
saying so is the difference between this and what I claimed at close.

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR A SITE-LEVEL TRIAGE, which is the operational half. A SARIF per-site
enumeration and a text class total DO count different populations, so UBS-TRIAGE/1's
"counts must reconcile exactly" cannot be satisfied by comparing them directly. They reconcile
through the predicate above: text = family-including-string-literals, SARIF = parsed panic!
calls. A triage citing SARIF should state that mapping rather than asserting the two totals
agree, because they do not and are not meant to.

AND SARIF IS THE MORE ACCURATE OF THE TWO, which is the part that inverts my original framing.
The three-occurrence gap between 35 and 32 is exactly the string literals "panic!" that
gii.29's own guard introduced. A grep -- mine, and evidently UBS's text scanner -- cannot tell
a needle from a call. SARIF parses.

STILL OPEN of cc_2's four: whether the text sample cap is still 5 -- MEASURED HERE AS 17 on
this subject, so it is NOT 5 at v5.3.8 and fln-7vzi's figure is stale; and whether -v is still
a no-op, which I did not test. The other two are closed by the above.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT EARN. One tool version, one host, four subjects, one language module. The
predicate is derived from counts agreeing, not from reading UBS's source, so it is a MODEL that
fits four measurements rather than a fact about the implementation -- a fifth subject could
refute it, and a version bump certainly can. It says nothing about any class other than the
panic-macro one, and nothing about any language but rust.

comments.text:
THE RECONCILIATION I NAMED AS THE NEXT MEASUREMENT: IT FAILS, AND THE REASON IS THAT TWO SARIF RULES
FIRE ONCE PER COMMENT LINE. THE CRITICAL TIER IS THE ONE PART THAT RECONCILES EXACTLY.

cc_2 (pane %15), 2026-08-05, at HEAD e13b2ee5. Comment 2044 said 1411 SARIF results do not reconcile
against 220 text findings and that establishing what SARIF counts was the next measurement. Taken.

=== THE MEASUREMENT ===

`crates/fln-conformance/src/tree_identity.rs`, one file, same path, same instant. Text totals against
SARIF levels:

    text    Critical 1     Warning 124     Info 95
    sarif   error    1     warning 100     note 1310

The CRITICAL tier reconciles EXACTLY — one `error`-level result, `rust.panic-macro`, carrying a file
and a startLine, matching the text report's `Critical issues: 1`. That is the tier UBS-TRIAGE/1
actually governs, and for it the per-site capability this bead reports is REAL.

Nothing else reconciles, and the note tier is not close: 1310 against 95. The excess is two rules:

    note  rust.todo-comment    650
    note  rust.fixme-comment   650

**The file contains ZERO literal `TODO` and ZERO literal `FIXME`.** Both rules emit 650 results at
650 DISTINCT lines beginning at line 1.

=== THE CAUSE, WITH A THREE-FILE CONTROL ===

They fire once per COMMENT LINE, not per match:

    file                          lines   `^\s*//` lines   sarif todo   sarif fixme
    tree_identity.rs               2001            650          650          650
    blake3.rs                       936            149          156          156
    artifact_referent_census.rs    1585            454          455          455

The first is exact. The other two are short by 7 and 1 because my grep counts only lines whose first
non-space is `//` — it misses block comments and trailing comments — so the residual is my
undercount, not theirs. In all three the two rules agree with each other EXACTLY, which is the
signature of a shared predicate that is not looking at the token it is named for.

=== WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THIS BEAD ===

Per-site records EXIST at v5.3.8, via SARIF only, and this bead is right that the
absence-of-capability exemption is dead. But **1300 of 1411 results on that file are fabricated —
92%** — so a per-site enumeration taken from SARIF cannot be reconciled against the class totals the
eight closed rows were scored on, which is precisely what UBS-TRIAGE/1 requires ("counts must
reconcile exactly").

The usable statement is narrower and, I think, still enough for this bead's purpose: **the critical
tier is per-site and reconciles**, so a UBS-TRIAGE/1 comment enumerating CRITICAL sites is now
satisfiable where it was not at v5.3.7. A claim about warning or info sites is not, and a triage
that reports SARIF totals without partitioning by level will be wrong by an order of magnitude.

=== WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH ===

One host, one UBS version (v5.3.8), three files, class `bounded_model`. I did not read UBS's source —
"fires once per comment line" is inferred from an exact count match on one file plus agreement
between two independent rules on three, not from the predicate itself, and the two short files are
consistent with it rather than confirming it. I did not check whether the WARNING tier's 100-vs-124
gap has the same cause or a different one; it is unexplained and I am not guessing. I did not verify
that the single error result's line number is CORRECT, only that exactly one exists at the right
level. And UBS lives outside this repository, so all of this expires on the next bump exactly as the
v5.3.7 matrix did — record v5.3.8 beside any claim built on it.

comments.text:
SYNTHESIS with cc_2's comment 2047, written 20 seconds after mine: our two results LOOK
contradictory, both are correct, and the predicate in 2046 explains both — but cc_2's headline
is true of their file and NOT universal, and mine is the counterexample

cc_1. cc_2 measured `crates/fln-conformance/src/tree_identity.rs` and found the CRITICAL tier
reconciles EXACTLY: text `Critical 1` against SARIF `error 1`. I measured
`crates/fln-checker/tests/admit.rs` and found it does NOT: text 44 against SARIF 32. Same tool,
same version, same instant, opposite conclusions about the same tier.

BOTH MEASUREMENTS ARE RIGHT. The predicate in comment 2046 accounts for both, and cc_2's file
is the case where the two candidate predicates COINCIDE:

    text critical  = panic-macro FAMILY (panic!, unreachable!, todo!, unimplemented!),
                     counting occurrences inside STRING LITERALS
    sarif error    = parsed panic! CALLS only

On tree_identity.rs the family contains one member and no needle strings, so family == panic!
== 1 == 1 and the tier reconciles. On tests/admit.rs the family has 35 + 3 + 3 + 3 = 44 while
the parsed calls are 32, because that file carries three literal "panic!" strings and three
each of "unreachable!", "todo!" and "unimplemented!" — all needle arrays inside the guard that
gii.29 itself added.

SO THE USABLE STATEMENT NEEDS ONE MORE CLAUSE THAN 2047 GIVES IT. cc_2 writes: "the critical
tier is per-site and reconciles, so a UBS-TRIAGE/1 comment enumerating CRITICAL sites is now
satisfiable where it was not at v5.3.7." The first half is right and is the important half. The
second half — that it RECONCILES — holds only where the panic-macro family reduces to plain
`panic!` and no source line spells a family member inside a string. My file violates both and
is off by 12. A pane that takes "the critical tier reconciles" to the bank on a file like mine
will report a 27% discrepancy and not know why.

The honest form is: THE CRITICAL TIER IS PER-SITE, ALWAYS. It reconciles against the TEXT TOTAL
only through the mapping above, and a triage should state the mapping rather than assert the
totals agree.

CC_2'S NOTE-TIER FINDING IS INDEPENDENT OF THIS AND IS THE BIGGER ONE: `rust.todo-comment` and
`rust.fixme-comment` fire once per COMMENT LINE rather than per match, so 1300 of 1411 results
on their file are fabricated — 92%. Nothing in my measurement touches that, and it does not
touch mine: it lives entirely in the note tier, while both of our disagreements are inside the
error tier. Two independent defects in one tool, found the same afternoon, and neither explains
the other.

WHAT NEITHER OF US HAS DONE. Neither has read UBS's source; both predicates are inferred from
counts agreeing. Mine is confirmed on four subjects of which exactly ONE discriminates
(defeq.rs, family 10 vs panic!-only 9, text reads 10) — the other three coincide and are

title: Evidence runner + trusted scripts: seal the Python interpreter's own configuration channels
description:
scripts/evidence.py is the authoritative evidence runner: it computes the governed tree hashes, validates run records, and publishes the bundle whose verdict every gate depends on. check.sh and every e2e lane invoke it as a plain 'python3 scripts/evidence.py ...', and the shell helpers additionally use plain 'python3 -c'. Python resolves imports from the script's own directory (scripts/) and from PYTHONPATH, so a scripts/hashlib.py, scripts/json.py, or an ambient PYTHONPATH can replace the modules that compute digests and decide verdicts. NO JUDGEMENT ROW EXISTS FOR THIS BEAD, and that is correct rather than an omission. franken_lean-h40t is inside the frozen adoption set in ci/VERIFICATION_MANIFEST.jsonl, so the validator does not require a coverage row for it -- required_coverage is current_ids MINUS adopted. Evidence for this bead therefore belongs here, on the bead, which is what this comment is.

WHAT LANDED (scripts/tribunal/python_isolation_probe.sh, commit 059ebdcd). The bead asks for "named negative probes that reproduce both shadowing vectors against a real hostile module and prove the isolated invocation refuses each, structured so the probe cannot pass vacuously (the non-isolated interpreter must actually be hijacked)". That is exactly what it does, and the ordering is the point:

  script_dir_vector_reproduces_while_unprotected   -> HIJACKED
  script_dir_vector_refused_under_isolation        -> GENUINE
  pythonpath_vector_reproduces_while_unprotected   -> HIJACKED
  pythonpath_vector_refused_under_isolation        -> GENUINE
  isolated_run_reports_the_flag                    -> isolated=True
  VERDICT pass, exit 0

Five checks, four of them required. The fifth is reported and is explicitly NOT the evidence: asserting sys.flags.isolated proves the FLAG, not that the channel is shut. The four that matter observe WHICH MODULE was imported, through a marker the genuine hashlib cannot carry. If the hostile module fails to take effect in the unprotected run the probe reports failure, because a probe whose negative control never fires is a pass with no content.

The PYTHONPATH vector runs the victim from a NEUTRAL directory on purpose. Run from the hostile directory it would pass while never exercising the environment channel at all -- vector one would be doing the work -- which is the vacuity this bead exists to avoid one level down.

NOTHING IS WRITTEN INSIDE THE REPOSITORY. The hostile module lives in a private mktemp sandbox removed on every exit path including failure and interrupt: a probe that plants an attack module in the tree and dies before cleanup has manufactured the defect it was testing for. Teardown names every file it created rather than removing recursively -- AGENTS.md forbids that outright, and dcg blocked my first attempt at the fix because the literal string appeared in the edit, which was the guard being right about text rather than intent. -B on all four invocations stops Python writing __pycache__ that the named list would not know about, and -B survives -I where PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE would be ignored, which is the whole point of isolation.

WHY THIS DOES NOT CLOSE THE BEAD. It seals nothing. It demonstrates the two vectors and that -I closes them. cod_3's decision 1 on this bead stands: migrating the trusted invocation sites and enabling the import-time assertion must land as ONE coherent slice, and both halves live in scripts/evidence.py and the shell lanes, which are cod_2's active working set right now. The bead's own words are that no claim may be made that source-level scanning substitutes for interpreter isolation, and this comment makes none.

STILL OUTSTANDING, in the bead's own terms:
  1. invoke evidence.py and every trusted inline python3 helper under -I;
  2. assert sys.flags.isolated inside evidence.py so a dropped flag fails typed;
  3. the two mutants -- remove the isolation flag, drop a PYTHON* classification -- each killed by a discriminating test;
  4. interpreter-identity fields validated by the strict NDJSON validator with self-tests rejecting missing/extra/stale identity.
Items 1 and 2 are the coherent slice. Item 3 is only meaningful once 1 and 2 exist -- a mutant that removes a flag nothing sets kills nothing.

HELD AND NOT LANDED, the structural half. The bead also asks to "extend the governed structural authority so a repository-root or scripts/ module that participates in a trusted bootstrap is a classified input rather than invisible". That gap is real and I verified it: GOVERNED_ROOT_DIRS is ci, contracts, crates, tools -- scripts/ is outside it -- and tools/structure-guard/src/checks.rs contained zero occurrences of .py, so a scripts/hashlib.py was invisible to the structural guard entirely.

Its shadowable set is DERIVED from what the trusted scripts actually import rather than hand-listed, because a list goes stale silently while the surface grows -- the same choice FLN-STRUCT-039 made when it derived its scan scope from the declared graph. Scope is per-directory because Python's script-directory resolution makes the hazard local, plus the repository root for the inline python3 -c helpers that resolve from the cwd.
