THE PROBE THAT PROVES THE ISOLATION WORKS WAS RUN BY NOTHING. Measured read-only at
94fa9e7e, re-anchored at 5f7e44ad (unchanged between them), repaired in this commit.

THE FINDING. every_python_launch_under_scripts_is_sealed ends its doc comment with:
"it does not observe a single interpreter actually start: that is
scripts/tribunal/python_isolation_probe.sh's job, and asserting -I is set is not
evidence that -I works." That job was delegated to a script no surface executed.
git grep over scripts/ and .github/ returns nothing. The probe is named in exactly
four places: .beads/issues.jsonl, ci/VERIFICATION_MANIFEST.jsonl, this bead's own
coverage row, and evidence_finalization.rs's UNSEALED_LAUNCH_ALLOWANCE -- which
declares an exemption FOR it rather than running it.

So the per-commit half checked the FLAG and the half that checks the CHANNEL never
ran. This bead's coverage row cites four probe outcomes across boundary and error
(script_dir and pythonpath, each reproduced-while-unprotected and refused-under-
isolation). All four were one hand-run, recorded once. Nothing would have noticed if
-I stopped shutting the channel, if the hostile module stopped taking effect so the
negative control went vacuous, or if the probe stopped executing altogether.

That is pnav's row in AGENTS.md item 7 -- an assertion and the lane it delegates to --
reproduced inside the guard whose own doc comment states the delegation. And it is
hugg's lesson in general form: where a claim rests on a run, check that the run
HAPPENED, not that the command exists and the exit code looked right.

THE CLASS IS BOUNDED, AND I MEASURED IT RATHER THAN ASSUMING. Of 16 distinct .sh paths
cited by coverage rows, 14 are named by a runnable surface. TWO are not:
python_isolation_probe.sh (this bead) and marrow_sanitizer_guard.sh (fln-nhf5, whose
own row already discloses that registration remains and is cod_2 surface). So this is
two instances, one of them already disclosed by its owner -- not systemic rot. Note the
census counts scripts/ and .github/ as runnable surfaces only; after this commit the
probe is run by a cargo test, which that definition does not see. Re-deriving the
number without adjusting for that yields a false positive on this very bead.

WHAT LANDED.
1. The probe gains ONE stdout line: the absolute path of its artifact directory,
   printed the instant the directory claim succeeds so a caller holds the address even
   when the probe later fails or is interrupted. stdout was previously unused; this
   makes it data-only per the Agent Ergonomics rule and is what lets a caller read the
   run record rather than scrape narration.
2. the_interpreter_isolation_probe_runs_and_produces_every_outcome_cited_for_it runs
   the real probe under plain cargo test and binds it to the manifest in BOTH
   directions: every outcome any coverage row attributes to the probe must be one this
   run produced, and every load-bearing outcome produced must be cited. Scope is
   derived from the manifest, so a row that starts citing the probe is bound without
   anyone remembering to add it.
3. the_interpreter_isolation_binding_kills_each_mutation_it_claims_to -- 10 mutants,
   each required to die for its own reason token, over a base forged from the
   manifest's own citations so it cannot drift from the population the real test
   judges. Two of the ten are the same violation from opposite sides (an outcome
   nobody cites; a citation removed from the row) and both are kept, because that is
   what equality in both directions means and a one-sided check passes one of them.
   Plus a parser mutation over an IN-MEMORY copy of the manifest, proving the cited set
   comes from the file rather than from a constant -- ci/VERIFICATION_MANIFEST.jsonl is
   a governed input and writing one during a lane ends that lane.

THE CONTROL THAT MATTERS, on the production path. Forged mutants prove the judgement
discriminates; they prove nothing about this repository. So the real probe was broken
by one variable -- python3 -IB changed to python3 -B on the script-directory vector --
and the real test went red at the named check:
  probe-check-failed:script_dir_vector_refused_under_isolation
  verdict="fail" exit=Some(1)
  produced=[... ("script_dir_vector_refused_under_isolation", false) ...]
The probe was restored and sha256-verified byte-identical. Without that cell the repair
would rest on a check that demonstrably fires and no evidence anything was ever open.

ORDERING IS LOAD-BEARING, and it is the arm I got wrong first. A per-check failure is
reported BEFORE the run-level verdict. Reading the verdict first makes a broken
negative control and a broken refusal both die at probe-verdict:fail -- indistinguishable,
and a rig accepting any failure would score both killed by an arm that had stopped
testing either property.

FL-INV-07: a setup that could not be established is refused as
probe-setup-inconclusive:<reason>, never rendered as a refutation of the isolation,
which is a claim no failed setup can support. An empty outcome set is refused as a
broken probe rather than reported as a clean sweep.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT EARN.
  * The probe is a bounded model: two vectors, one host, one CPython. Running it per
    commit does not widen it. An opaque PYTHONHOME, a sitecustomize, or a shadow module
    reached by some path neither vector plants are all outside it, and -I closing those
    is untested here. Class bounded_model, unchanged.
  * It says nothing about whether scripts/evidence.py is LAUNCHED sealed. That is the
    line scanner above it, and the two halves share no code deliberately.
  * A future third vector must be added to BOTH the probe and a citation or the
    equality refuses it. That is intended -- the alternative is a probe that grows
    silently -- but it is friction, and the next person to add a vector should be told
    rather than discover it.
  * Nothing here touches the still-open h40t remainder: the interpreter-identity
    self-tests and the fln.supervisor/4-to-/5 schema wiring, both of which live in
    scripts/evidence.py and are still contended by another pane's census work.

COST, disclosed because the last guard in this file to write per-run artifacts put
4.3 MB a run into a machine-wide shared target directory before anyone measured it:
0.16 s and 5.1 KB per run, under the gitignored target/e2e/. Three orders of magnitude
below that precedent, and reclaimed by cargo clean.

GATES. cargo fmt --check clean on the two changed files. cargo clippy -p fln-conformance
--all-targets -D warnings clean. cargo test -p fln-conformance: 25 suites, 0 failed

    = 30 "panic! macro(s) present" + 6 "Secret, signature, or token compared with ==/!="

It is triggered here by file-scope taint on the word "token" (3 added occurrences, all

CLOSING JUDGEMENT: EVERY SCOPE ITEM IS LANDED AND MECHANISED PER COMMIT — AND MY OWN RE-VERIFICATION
OF IT WAS WRONG FOUR TIMES BEFORE IT WAS RIGHT.

cc_2 (pane %15), 2026-08-05, at HEAD 650ea628. Written after `br close` so it binds this closure.

=== THE SCOPE, ITEM BY ITEM, AUDITED RATHER THAN ASSUMED ===

  1. ISOLATED INVOCATION of evidence.py and the trusted shell helpers. Measured across all 34
     trusted shell surfaces (`scripts/check.sh` plus the 33 in `scripts/e2e/`): 25 build a sealed
     interpreter, 9 invoke python3 nowhere in command text, and **0 invoke it unsealed**. Buckets
     reconcile, 25 + 0 + 9 = 34.
  2. `sys.flags.isolated` ASSERTED INSIDE evidence.py, so a dropped flag fails typed rather than
     silently reopening the channel: `sealed_interpreter_unsealed_startup`, which refuses on
     `isolated`/`no_site`. I hit this refusal repeatedly today from my own scratch tooling, which is
     the cheapest possible proof that it is live rather than declared.
  3. THE `PYTHON*` FAMILY CLASSIFIED, not left unclassified: `PYTHON_CONFIGURATION_ENV_EXACT` and
     `PYTHON_CONFIGURATION_ENV_PREFIXES = ("PYTHON",)`. Its author has already disclosed, in the
     source, that the EXACT set is presently INERT because the prefix subsumes every member — the
     inert-declaration shape, named where it lives rather than left for a reader to discover.
  4. INTERPRETER IDENTITY IN THE RUN RECORD: `effective_interpreter_identity`, recording executable,
     version, isolation flags and resolved prefix beside the existing compiler identity.
  5. GOVERNED STRUCTURAL AUTHORITY extended to bootstrap modules: `tools/structure-guard/src/checks.rs`
     reasons explicitly about `scripts/hashlib.py` and a repository-root `tomllib.py`, the exact
     shadow-module vector this bead was filed on.
  6. THE PROBES AND MUTANTS EXIST AND RUN, which is the half a scope list usually leaves as prose:
     `the_interpreter_isolation_probe_runs_and_produces_every_outcome_cited_for_it`,
     `the_interpreter_isolation_binding_kills_each_mutation_it_claims_to`,
     `every_python_launch_under_scripts_is_sealed`,
     `every_supervisor_launcher_seals_python_configuration_before_imports`,
     `every_workflow_python_launch_is_sealed_or_declared`,
     `the_python_interpreter_configuration_rule_has_exactly_one_definition`, and
     `the_shell_copies_of_the_interpreter_configuration_rule_are_a_named_population`. None is
     `#[ignore]`d; `evidence_finalization` ran 63 passed / 0 failed at this HEAD.

=== THE PART WORTH MORE THAN THE CLOSE: I MEASURED ITEM 1 BY HAND AND GOT IT WRONG FOUR TIMES ===

Every attempt returned a WELL-FORMED, PLAUSIBLE, WRONG answer, and all four erred toward "unsafe":

  attempt 1  `grep -c 'python3 -I -S' scripts/check.sh` -> **0**. False. check.sh builds
             `PYTHON=("$PYTHON_BIN" -I -S)` once, at line 38, and calls `"${PYTHON[@]}"` everywhere.
             A COUNT GREP CANNOT SEE A DECOMPOSITION.
  attempt 2  classify a `python3` token not followed by `-I` as unsealed -> **24 of 34 unsealed**.
             False. Every single hit was an ERROR MESSAGE: `echo "... python3 is required"`. A
             SCANNER WHOSE SEARCH SPACE INCLUDES PROSE REPORTS PROSE.
  attempt 3  strip comments and quoted strings first, then classify -> the array detection broke,
             because `PYTHON=("$PYTHON_BIN" -I -S)` becomes `PYTHON=("" -I -S)` after the strings
             are removed. The apparatus destroyed the evidence it was built to read.
  attempt 4  count sites inside sealed scripts that are not literally `-I -S` -> **27 unsealed
             sites**. False. The needle `python3?` matches the BARE WORD `python`, so it fired on
             `"python": platform.python_version()` inside JSON payloads and on the artifact name
             `hostile-python-configuration`.

The correct answer needed the digit made mandatory and sealed-array lines excluded, reconciled
against a second independent needle, with the bucket sum required to equal the population. **And
the whole exercise was unnecessary**: `every_python_launch_under_scripts_is_sealed` already derives
this population per commit and had been green the entire time. The lesson is not "be careful with
grep" — it is that AN AD-HOC SCAN IS NOT A SECOND OPINION ABOUT A MECHANISED POPULATION; it is a
fifth thing that can be wrong, and here it was wrong four times while the guard was right once.

=== WHAT THIS CLOSE DOES NOT ESTABLISH ===

The `PYTHON_CONFIGURATION_ENV_EXACT` set remains INERT, subsumed by its own prefix rule, so no
mutation can kill it and it earns nothing today — it is retained as a declaration of intent and its
author says so in the source. My item-1 figure is a property of THIS tree at THIS commit: a new
lane that invokes python3 unsealed would not be caught by anything I ran, only by
`every_python_launch_under_scripts_is_sealed`, which is the actual producer and the reason this can
close. I did not re-run the hostile-shadow-module probes myself; I established that they exist, are
not ignored, and pass in a suite that ran green at this HEAD. CPython lives outside this repository,
so `-I`'s semantics are a property of a tool no test here holds. One host, one commit, class
`bounded_model`.

title: Two orphaned working-tree files from panes that are out until 2026-08-01, one of which reddens the tree
description:
Two files are uncommitted in the shared working tree and their authors cannot finish them. This
bead exists because an undocumented condition in a shared tree rots: without it, every pane that
runs the full fln-conformance suite rediscovers the same red independently, and each rediscovery
costs a build.

THE ORPHANS, measured at 42a227ad..9d86aac2 on 2026-07-27:

  crates/fln-syntax/tests/golden_vellum.rs  -- author cod_3, pane 7
  scripts/evidence.py                       -- author cod_2, pane 6 (543 insertions, 1 deletion)

Both panes hit a hard codex usage limit at approximately 10:20Z with a stated reset of
2026-08-01, so neither author can complete the edit during this session. All three cod panes
(5, 6, 7) are out.

THE RED, and it has exactly one cause. golden_vellum.rs names the beads tracker path TWICE in the
working tree and ZERO times at HEAD. That alone fails
evidence_finalization::the_rch_tracker_exclusion_row_matches_the_measured_population, whose guard
requires every tracked crates/** or tools/** Rust file naming the tracker to be declared in either
rch-tracker-reads or rch-tracker-non-reads in AGENTS.md. Measured twice, independently: the
sequencer ran it filtered and observed exit 101 from the process with 1 failed and 28 filtered
out; cc_2 ran the whole target and observed 28 passed, 1 failed. The failure output mentions
VERIFICATION_MANIFEST zero times, which is the discriminator that keeps it from being mistaken for
collateral from any ci/ change. So the working tree carries a red that NO LIVE PANE CAUSED and
that will not clear on its own.

THE DECISION, which is the durable part of this bead:

  The files are NOT reverted, NOT stashed, and NOT committed.

  Not reverted or stashed, because AGENTS.md forbids overwriting another agent's work, and the
  author's absence does not create an exception -- it REMOVES THE ONLY PERSON who could say what
  half-finished state a revert would destroy. Not committed, because that lands someone else's
  unfinished edit under a name that never read it, and for golden_vellum.rs it lands the red.

  No guard is needed to hold this. git commit -o <paths> builds a commit from the paths named and
  consults neither the working tree's other files nor the shared index, so an orphan cannot ride
  along. That is the second time in one hour that -o was the only thing preventing a bad commit;
  the first was 1e4bce00, where an index-based commit took a peer's files instead of the author's.

WHAT WOULD RESOLVE IT -- two routes, and only these:

  1. The author returns after 2026-08-01 and finishes the edit.
  2. Someone deliberately ADOPTS the file: reads it IN FULL, adds it to rch-tracker-reads or
     rch-tracker-non-reads in AGENTS.md as the guard's message directs, moves the mentions= and
     matching counts, and lands it UNDER THEIR OWN NAME.

  An adoption is NOT authorised as of this filing. The sequencer has the question with the user.
  Nobody adopts golden_vellum.rs without the sequencer's say-so.

THE IRONY, MEASURED RATHER THAN NOTED. scripts/evidence.py is itself one of the two orphans, and
it is the file that validate-verification-manifest runs from -- so the validator used to check
this bead's own coverage row is the absent author's uncommitted copy. Checked rather than assumed:
the validate_verification_manifest body is BYTE-IDENTICAL between the worktree copy and HEAD, and
both copies return valid=true with the same sha256 21cd1191dd72179f and coverage_rows=179 on the
same inputs. The orphan's 543 added lines do touch code that references
validate_verification_manifest, so the two copies are not interchangeable in general -- they are
merely indistinguishable for THIS invocation, which is why it was measured here instead of
assumed. Anyone validating while this orphan persists should re-run the control:
git show HEAD:scripts/evidence.py > /tmp/control.py and compare.

SCOPE. This bead tracks the CONDITION and the decision, not a repair. It should be closed by
whichever of the two routes above actually happens, and the closing judgement must say which.
close_reason: Resolved by explicit route-2 adoption: scripts/evidence.py landed under audited QYDN ownership and golden_vellum.rs was read in full, wired non-decoratively, integrated, and verified through the green full workspace gate.

title: W5: Initialization + capability-scoped effects — ordering, --pure-elab, receipts
description:
Implement initialization + capability-scoped effects (§11.5): initialize / builtin_initialize ordering, import-time extension replay interleaving, and real-world IO effects exactly as upstream — under asupersync capabilities, so a --pure-elab audit mode can DENY ambient filesystem/network/clock to metaprograms and report exactly which declarations demanded them.

The posture: capability-scoped metaprogramming is a sound-mode observability win and a frontier-mode sandbox, NEVER a semantic change to compliant code (faithful mode default ambient authority approximates an ordinary Lean process — drop-in means unchanged packages just run, with effects OBSERVED into provenance). Initialization DAG receipts (from the plugin door, §6.6) unify with this: cycles, duplicate initializers, and late capability requests are explainable. This bead also covers the interaction with Golem-hosted lakefile execution (Ledger, §13.3) — lakefiles are user code with declared effect surfaces.

Acceptance: initializer-ordering fixtures match Reference-observable behavior incl. interleaving with extension replay; --pure-elab on a corpus with known effectful metaprograms reports exactly the offender set; capability events land in Palimpsest with correct spans. Tests: ordering property tests over generated init DAGs; denial fixtures (a denied capability yields typed CapabilityDenied naming the alternative, never silent substitution — D2 discipline); provenance-completeness checks against the perturbation validator.

All bead-specific requirements, acceptance conditions, tests, invariants, compatibility surfaces, evidence levels, performance gates, negative/recovery cases, and user-visible behaviors stated above remain mandatory. No listed feature or claim may be silently narrowed, deferred, mocked, or declared complete through an unclassified divergence.

title: W10: Backends & ABI doors — Iron native backend, JIT, C parity, outbound plugins
description:
Workstream W10 "Backends & ABI doors" (§17.3, §17.4, §11.3): the sovereign compilation path and the bidirectional plugin promise.

Scope: Iron static backend — FLBC to native objects/executables (x86-64, aarch64 first) with NO LLVM, no cranelift, no cc: the owned baseline emitter grown a static mode; lake build of executables with zero external toolchain (the G6 headline). Iron-JIT (frontier, standard-mode only, fln-unsafe-jit): baseline template JIT with inline caches burned in; results bit-identical to the interpreter by construction, spot-checked by a standing dual-run rig; certified builds never enable it. --backend c parity generator: emit C in the Reference idiom and drive the USER toolchain exactly as upstream leanc does (D2 optional tool #1) — parity apparatus and exotic-target escape hatch, never the anchor. Both backends dual-run governed: Iron pinned to interpreter results, interpreter pinned to Reference observable evaluation semantics on the differential corpus. ABI door outbound (§17.4, the harder direction, staged to G5): FrankenLean-built plugins loading into the Reference host, per-platform Tribunal matrix; inbound (Reference plugins into FrankenLean) lands earlier under W2/G2. Risk R5 honesty: outbound tiers per platform in the Parity Ledger rather than blocking G5.

WHAT ITEM 1 ASKS FOR, verbatim: "Expressions, levels and names hash-consed CONTRACTUALLY, not opportunistically: one node per full structural identity INCLUDING binder names and mdata, because metaprograms observe them and faithful Expr behaviour demands exact round-trip."

WHAT EXISTS: crates/fln-env/src/intern.rs interns EXPRESSIONS. There is no Level store and no Name store. A Level or a Name appearing in two different Const nodes is shared only TRANSITIVELY - when the two Const nodes are themselves structurally identical and therefore intern to one node. Two distinct Consts that happen to share a Level do not share that Level's allocation, and two distinct declarations that share a Name component do not share it either.

WHY THIS IS BEING FILED RATHER THAN QUIETLY NARROWED. cc_3's handback on oh1j lists item 1 as landed, and it IS landed for expressions, which is the large majority of the value. But oh1j exists BECAUSE fln-49c closed on a subset of its own title and someone had to notice afterwards. Doing the same thing one level down - letting "expressions, levels and names" close on expressions - would be the same failure with the excuse that it was mostly done. Whoever closes oh1j should either implement the other two interners or amend item 1 to say expressions-only and record why; both are fine, silently doing the second is not.

WHAT IS ALREADY TRUE AND MAKES THIS CHEAPER THAN IT SOUNDS:
  * Name is ALREADY Arc-backed with structural sharing by construction (crates/fln-core/src/name.rs: a name is its parent plus one component, each node behind an Arc), and it already carries a cached O(1) hash. So a Name interner is not about making Name cheap to clone - it already is - it is about collapsing two independently-built EQUAL names onto one allocation. The value is memory and pointer-equality, not clone cost.
  * intern.rs's existing machinery generalises: the post-order worklist, the bucket-plus-full-equality confirmation, the ProducedNodes budget and the SharingStats accounting are all type-agnostic in shape. A Level or Name interner is the same algorithm over a different node type, not a new design.

WHAT TO DECIDE FIRST, because it is the question that makes this real rather than mechanical: WHAT OBSERVES IT? Expression interning earns its keep because Expr::equal collapses to a pointer compare and kernel defeq caches key on identity pairs (oh1j item 2). Before building Level and Name stores, name the caller that benefits. If the honest answer is "nothing yet", then amending item 1 to expressions-only and filing the other two against the caller that eventually wants them is the BETTER outcome, and this bead should close that way rather than by building two stores nobody consults. A hash-cons with no consumer is memory overhead plus a maintenance surface.

RELATED, and the reason not to just do it: crates/fln-env/src/intern.rs currently has NO production callers at all. The expression interner itself is not yet consulted by anything. Building two more stores beneath an unconsumed one would be speculative work on speculative work.
close_reason: Amended oh1j item 1 to expressions-only with measured evidence (zero production callers of the expression interner); judgement row authored and dry-validated before close. Audit found the fourth instance of the discrimination-failure family and fixed it.

comments.text:
DECIDED: AMEND, NOT BUILD. And the audit this bead asked for found a FOURTH instance of the discrimination-failure family, which is worth more than the decision (PeachBass/cc_1, 2026-07-25).

=== THE DECISION, AND THE ONE FACT THAT MAKES IT ===

This bead's own text names the question that makes it real rather than mechanical: WHAT OBSERVES IT? Measured rather than assumed:

    rg 'fln_env::intern|crate::intern' over crates/, excluding intern.rs itself
      -> exactly ONE hit, and it is a DOC COMMENT (decl_closure.rs:195)

So the EXPRESSION interner has zero production callers. Not "few" - none. Building a Level store and a Name store beneath an unconsumed store would be speculative work founded on speculative work, and a hash-cons with no consumer is memory overhead plus a maintenance surface plus two more identity encodings to keep correct.

The second fact points the same way: Name is ALREADY Arc-backed with structural sharing by construction and carries a cached O(1) hash. A Name interner would not make Name cheap to clone - it already is. It would buy pointer-equality and the collapse of two independently-built EQUAL names onto one allocation. Real value, but only to a caller that compares or stores names at volume, and there is no such caller.

So oh1j item 1 is AMENDED to expressions-only, in the bead's description field, with the reasoning inline rather than by reference. The amendment was applied as a single verified substitution: the replacement was asserted to be the only change (reversing it byte-reproduces the original), and the write-back was read back and compared. When a consumer appears, file the two stores AGAINST THAT CONSUMER - that is strictly better than a bead that says "build two stores because the title mentions three things".

I want to be explicit that this is the outcome the bead pre-authorised, not a narrowing I invented: "If the honest answer is 'nothing yet', then amending item 1 to expressions-only and filing the other two against the caller that eventually wants them is the BETTER outcome, and this bead should close that way."

=== THE FOURTH INSTANCE, FOUND IN intern.rs WHILE AUDITING FOR IT ===

THE LEDGER, so the count stays single-valued: f6br (census witness), bf9ef450 (intern key), franken_lean-oof9 (a build-gate rule keyed on a method name), and now this. fln-extension-history-checkpoint-identity-41s was audited and is CLEAN; it is not an instance and must not be re-audited.

WHAT IT IS. identity_digest fed `format!("{:?}")` - a Debug RENDERING - into the digest preimage at three sites: Sort's level, Const's level list, and the FVar/MVar ids. bf9ef450 fixed the NAME half of this very function, replacing to_display_string with the structural canonical encoding, and left the level and id halves on Debug. The correct encoder was already reachable and already used one line away: `Canonical for Level` has existed in fln-hash all along, tagged per variant and iterative for stack safety.

That is the sharpest instance yet, because the fix was incomplete IN ITS OWN FUNCTION, with the right tool already imported.

SEVERITY, STATED HONESTLY AND NOT INFLATED - IT WAS LATENT, NOT ACTIVE. Level's Debug is a hand-written stack-safe copy of the DERIVED rendering, so it is structural and tagged, and Name's Debug is structural too. FVarId/MVarId/LMVarId are newtypes over Name with derived Debug, so they inherit that. I checked rather than assumed: no two distinct levels collide under it today. Nothing was broken, no digest was wrong, and unlike f6br there is no demonstrable collision to exhibit.

WHAT WAS ACTUALLY WRONG is that the correctness rested on an ACCIDENT that nothing pinned, inside a function whose entire subject is identity:
  * Level's own doc says its Debug is "byte-identical to the derived rendering". A field added, renamed or reordered in Level or its Node silently moves every digest preimage. Nothing would catch it - the digest is a bucket hint confirmed by full Expr equality, so every test stays green while bucket_misses quietly changes meaning. That is the same blinded-instrument consequence bf9ef450 recorded.
  * The rendering includes Level's packed `data` word - a CACHED hash seed, depth and flags - so the identity preimage depended on a cache rather than on the level's structure alone.

THE TEST IS WRITTEN AGAINST THE ENCODER, NOT AGAINST DISCRIMINATION, and that choice is the interesting part. Because Debug does discriminate today, a discrimination test would pass identically before and after the fix - it would prove nothing and would quietly certify the defect. So the test independently recomputes the preimage (Domain::DeclContent, the intern tag, the Sort discriminant, then the length-prefixed Canonical bytes) and requires identity_digest to agree. KILLED RATHER THAN ASSUMED: reverting the Sort site to format!("{level:?}") fails it, verified by doing exactly that and restoring.

THE GENERALISATION THIS ADDS. The rule recorded on 41s is about SERIALISATION - every variable-length field self-delimiting, every sum type tagged - with the diagnostic "can two different values produce the same bytes?". That diagnostic returns NO here, because Debug is injective, and would have passed this file. The widened rule from ccde957f is what finds it: ANY PROJECTION USED AS AN IDENTITY. The follow-up question is not only "can two values collide?" but ALSO "is this projection a CONTRACT, or is it a rendering that happens to be injective today?" A renderer that discriminates by luck is a defect waiting for a refactor, and no collision test can see it.

=== SCOPE NOTE ===

Fixing intern.rs was not in this bead's title. I did it here because the audit this bead asked for is what found it, the fix is eight lines in a file with zero production consumers, and filing it would have cost three governed artifacts to track work smaller than the bead describing it. Recorded rather than silent.

title: A coverage row may cite a test CI never runs, and the granularity guard scored that a repair
description:
A COVERAGE ROW MAY CITE A TEST CI NEVER RUNS, AND THE GRANULARITY GUARD SCORED THAT A REPAIR.

Item 7's twelfth instance, found exactly where the guard's own residue list said the next one
would hide, and opened by that guard's own repair.

WHAT THE RESIDUE ITEM SAID. `crates/fln-conformance/tests/ci_execution_join.rs` residue item 4,
"The five #[ignore]d tests":

  "A cited surface can be run by CI while the test inside it that produces the evidence never
   executes. Artifact citations are file-granular, so the manifest cannot express which test a
   row rests on and this guard cannot check it."

True when written. FALSE from f24b6670, which added the `test:<pkg>::<target>::<path>` citation
kind so a row could finally name the function that carries it. The obstacle the residue item
gave as its reason for being residue was removed by the same pane four commits later, and
nobody re-read the residue list. The premise stayed on the page; the exposure it described
became reachable.

THE DEFECT. `judge_granularity` resolves a `test:` citation by asking whether the function
EXISTS in the target's function list (`d.target_tests`) or the package's lib-test list
(`d.lib_tests`). It never asks whether that function is one CI executes. `d.ignored` - every
#[ignore]d test in the workspace, as (surface, function) - is a field of the SAME `Derivation`
value, populated forty lines above, and is consulted only by `judge_ignored`. The join is one
containment test and it was not made.

So a row migrates from a file citation to `test:fln-conformance::kernel_replay::<an ignored fn>`
and three things happen at once: the row leaves FILE_GRANULAR_EVIDENCE_ALLOWANCE, the ceiling
drops by one, and the change is recorded as a repair - for a row that now rests on exactly one
test, and that test is one cargo compiles and libtest never runs. Before the migration the row
rested on the surface's tests collectively and the ignored fraction was 2/14; after it, 0/1.
The file-granular defence does not survive the repair for file granularity.

MEASURED, not read. At 5f7e44ad, four mutants planted against the intact guard: a citation
naming an ignored integration test, a citation naming an ignored lib unit test, a coarse
citation of a surface whose every test is ignored, and an emptied ignore scan. All four FAILED
- the guard was green on every one - while the other 44 tests passed. That is the before
measurement; the after is 48/48.

THE EXPOSURE IS NOT IN THE TAIL. Ten terminal coverage rows cite one of the four
ignored-producer surfaces (fln-7odd, fln-8zsq, fln-c78c, fln-corpus-thread-matrix-93te,
franken_lean-2ki4, franken_lean-kxbj on kernel_replay.rs; fln-mandated-mutant-join-unwatched-uagk
on mandated_mutants.rs; fln-kx3y and franken_lean-kxbj on depth_stack_calibration.rs;
franken_lean-ome7 on golden_vellum.rs). ALL TEN are declared debts in
FILE_GRANULAR_EVIDENCE_ALLOWANCE, whose one sanctioned repair is that migration. For two of
them the ignored function is the only honest answer to "which test carries this row": the
#[ignore] reason on pinned_present_olean_kernel_differential names fln-7odd, and the one on
present_olean_corpus_thread_matrix_compares_stream_digests names 93te. The correct answer to
the guard's question was a function CI does not run.

A SECOND CLAIM, TRANSCRIBED AND UNCHECKED. IGNORED_PRODUCER_ALLOWANCE's doc comment defended
the ten rows with a measurement: "the ignored fraction is 2/14, 1/15, 1/10 and 1/9, and no
surface has every test ignored". The last clause is the load-bearing one and it was a number
typed into a doc comment at 974fcc5a with nothing rechecking it - AGENTS.md's own "a
measurement written down, not a derived one". Derived now. The four fractions are deliberately
NOT pinned: they move whenever a test is added, so pinning them buys churn while the clause
that matters is the property, not the arithmetic.

THE REPAIR, landed with this bead.

  - granularity-ignored, in BOTH citation shapes. Integration: the (target_path, function) pair
    is looked up in d.ignored at the point the citation resolves. Lib: no lib unit test is
    #[ignore]d today, so that half has no live instance and is exercised by a planted one -
    an unfalsifiable half is bkw6's empty referent, and a population with no members is where
    the next instance lands.
  - granularity-hollow-surface: a coarse-cited file whose every #[test] is #[ignore]d. This is
    the derived form of the transcribed clause above, and it is not redundant with the
    file-granular population: that population is a debt about EXPRESSIVENESS, this is a fact
    about EXECUTION.
  - granularity-ignored-scan: an empty d.ignored makes both checks vacuous and every citation
    resolve clean regardless of whether CI runs it. Refuse loudly - the producing scan
    breaking must not read as a tree in which every test now runs.

FOUR MUTANTS, EACH GUT-TESTED INDEPENDENTLY. cc_3's own handoff rule: eight mutants each
killed at the assertion they name is NOT sufficient, because gutting judge_lane_binding failed
all eight while leaving the negative control green. So each of the four checks was disabled on
its own, one variable per run, at 5f7e44ad: each gut killed EXACTLY the mutant that names it
and no other (47 passed / 1 failed, four times, four different names). No check is dead weight
and no mutant rides on a neighbour's assertion. The file was restored byte-identical after the
last gut and re-verified 48/48.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT EARN.

  - A file-granular row citing a surface where SOME tests are ignored still cannot say which
    test it rests on. That is the 67-row debt, untouched by this join.
  - #[ignore] is only one way a compiled test does not run. #[cfg] gating and an early return
    are not modelled; --skip is residue item 5.
  - The lib half has one planted instance and zero real ones. It is a mechanism with no
    measured population, disclosed as such.
  - This is a per-commit check over the real tree, class bounded_model for the mutant runs
    themselves: four guts at one commit on one host.

THE GENERAL LESSON, which is why this is filed rather than quietly fixed. A DISCLOSED UNKNOWN
IS A CLAIM, AND IT ROTS LIKE ONE. Residue item 4 was written honestly and reviewed repeatedly;
what invalidated it was not a mistake in it but a REPAIR ELSEWHERE that removed its premise -
landed by the same pane, in the same file, four commits later. Item 7 says every claim must
name the thing that produces it and fail when that thing changes; a residue list is a claim
whose producer is the absence of a capability, and nothing failed when the capability arrived.
Every "we cannot check X because Y" in this repository should be re-read the day Y is repaired,
and no mechanism does that today.
close_reason: Repair landed by cc_3 at 5f7e44ad; re-derived green at HEAD b0ef355e by cc_2 (75/75 ci_execution_join, ceiling 57 == allowance 57, residue ceiling 2). Credit for the repair is cc_3 s.

comments.text:
THE MECHANISM THIS BEAD SAID DID NOT EXIST NOW EXISTS, for this file's own residue list.

The bead body closes on: "Every 'we cannot check X because Y' in this repository should be
re-read the day Y is repaired, and no mechanism does that today." That is now false for
crates/fln-conformance/tests/ci_execution_join.rs, which is the file the defect was found in.

WHAT LANDED. RESIDUE_PREMISES binds every numbered residue item in the module header to the
thing that must stay true for its stated reason to hold. judge_residue evaluates the derived
ones every run and binds the cardinality in both directions.

  item 1  Undecidable - runtime dispatch cannot be observed from inside the repository at all
          (uagk's cron limit: a workflow naming a script is not a run of it)
  item 2  Derived  layout-derived-target-set-is-exact
                   -> d.granularity_preconditions.is_empty()
  item 3  Derived  submode-jobs-also-invoke-the-plain-gate
                   -> every job naming --self-test or --tribunal-manifest-inventory also
                      carries a bare check.sh invocation. Measured: the only such job is
                      `gate`, and it does.
  item 4  Undecidable - the remaining non-execution reasons (#[cfg] gating, an early return)
          are properties of a RUN, not of the source layout; the #[ignore] half is derived
  item 5  Derived  skip-filters-names-not-targets
                   -> every --skip in check.sh sits on an invocation carrying no -p, --test
                      or --manifest-path. Measured: one site, `run_stage test cargo test
                      --locked -- "${census_test_args[@]}"`, narrowed by nothing.

RESIDUE_UNDECIDABLE_CEILING = 2, by EQUALITY. One-way-plus-floor is wrong here for the inverse
of FILE_GRANULAR_EVIDENCE_CEILING's reason: this counts disclosures nothing watches, so it is
a debt, and a debt that can grow silently is 0ad34e9c's shape - a single ceiling is a budget
every repair refills. Converting an Undecidable to a Derived premise must lower the number in
the same commit.

THE DIRECTION A NAIVE CHECK MISSES. Item 5's premise fails BOTH ways. A --skip appearing on a
narrowed invocation flips it, and so does the --skip site VANISHING - because the item would
then name a site that is not there, which is the transcribed-anchor rot the item's own line
number ("scripts/check.sh:1586-1590", already off by three) is an instance of. A "does a --skip
exist" check would pass on the first and a "is any --skip narrowed" check would pass on the
second.

WHAT A PREMISE IS NOT. It is a NECESSARY condition for the item's stated reason, never a
sufficient one. Item 2's derivation can be exact while its prose is wrong about something else.
This catches a reason evaporating; it does not check that an item is well written.

SCAN REGION, and it is load-bearing rather than tidy. residue_items reads only the module doc
between the residue heading and #![forbid(unsafe_code)], so every guard body below - including
residue_items itself, which necessarily spells the marker it searches for - is outside the
search space BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by an exclusion someone must maintain. fln-8zsq's
first version asserted its needle appeared SOMEWHERE IN THE FILE and a mutant that gutted the
real site survived; franken_lean-2ki4 then paid again when one guard's assertion text satisfied
another guard's probe. Scope to the SITE, and prefer a region bound to an exclusion list.

THIRTEEN TESTS, TEN INDEPENDENT GUTS, measured at 729bcd0f. Every check disabled on its own,
one variable per cell, restored and sha256-verified between cells (intact
a3957a05e57250887029abc84fe7f42564716683f38457bd7a73396cf553df87 before and after all ten).

  gut  1 residue-scan refusal          -> 1 killed  (collapsed doc scan)
  gut  2 residue-unbound               -> 1 killed  (new item, no premise)
  gut  3 residue-stale                 -> 1 killed  (premise for a deleted item)
  gut  4 residue-ceiling               -> 1 killed  (grown declaration)
  gut  5 residue-vacuous               -> 1 killed  (blank Undecidable reason)
  gut  6 residue-unknown-premise       -> 1 killed  (judge-level unknown id)
  gut  7 residue-premise-flipped       -> 4 killed  (all four flip mutants share this ONE
                                          reporting site by design - recorded as 4, not
                                          dressed up as 1:1)
  gut  8 premise item 2 forced true    -> 1 killed
  gut  9 premise item 3 forced true    -> 1 killed
  gut 10 premise item 5 forced true    -> 2 killed  (the two DIRECTIONS of one predicate)

THE PROTOCOL EARNED ITS KEEP TWICE IN ONE SESSION, before any gut ran. Enumerating the checks
to gut them found (a) residue-ceiling and residue-vacuous had NO mutant at all, and (b) the
unknown-premise mutant asserted on premise_holds DIRECTLY, so gutting the judge's own arm would
have left it green - a mutant that cannot see the code path it is named for. Both were repaired
before the campaign; gut 6 confirms the judge-level twin dies and the direct assertion survives,
which is exactly the failure mode the protocol exists to expose. This is the generalisation of
this pane's earlier finding that gutting judge_lane_binding failed all eight of its mutants
while leaving the negative control green: EIGHT MUTANTS EACH DYING AT THE ASSERTION THEY NAME
IS NOT EVIDENCE THE CHECKS ARE INDEPENDENT.

Where a gut kills more than one mutant it is recorded as such rather than reported as one-to-one.
A gut killing SEVERAL means those mutants share an assertion; a gut killing NONE means the check
is dead weight. Both are answers, and only the second is a defect.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT EARN. Five residue items in ONE file. Nothing extends this to hugg's
hand-listed surface set, to the "what this does not earn" paragraphs across the verification
manifest, or to AGENTS.md's own disclosed limitations - all of which are the same population
and all of which remain unwatched. The bead stays OPEN on that, and on the residue already
recorded in its coverage row.

No coverage-row edit accompanies this: ci/VERIFICATION_MANIFEST.jsonl is cod_2's, and the
one-row exception covers a row in the same commit as its own bead's CLOSE, which this is not.
The row filed with a7351122 is unchanged and still accurate; this comment is the durable record.

title: Ignored producers are compensated one by one, but nothing binds the class
description:
THE CLAIM. Five tests in this workspace carry the #[ignore] attribute, so cargo compiles them and never runs them. All five are already compensated - but by five bespoke mechanisms, written by four different people, each invisible from the ignore site. NOTHING BINDS an ignored producer to a compensating mechanism. A sixth #[ignore] added tomorrow gets no scrutiny at all.

This is AGENTS.md item 7's own sentence turned on a class it had not been turned on: instances found by attentive reading are not a mechanism, they are luck with good people, and luck does not survive a context restart.

MEASURED at 974fcc5a, attribute-counted:
  kernel_replay.rs            pinned_present_olean_kernel_differential (blocked by fln-7odd)
  kernel_replay.rs            present_olean_corpus_thread_matrix_compares_stream_digests (cost)
  mandated_mutants.rs         the_mandated_mutants_are_planted_and_their_killers_die (edits tracked source)
  depth_stack_calibration.rs  calibrate_stack_bytes_per_depth (spawns hundreds of subprocesses)
  golden_vellum.rs            emit_corpus_for_review (regeneration ceremony, only prints)

WHAT EACH IS COMPENSATED BY, since that is the part nobody can see from the ignore:
fln-8zsq made its census guard SOURCE-level precisely because its producer is ignored - a lane grepping stdout observes silence rather than a missing disclosure. fln-corpus-thread-matrix-93te carries AGENTS.md's public PG-5 waiver, which expires MECHANICALLY because the receipt path is keyed by pin. fln-mandated-mutant-join-unwatched-uagk has a per-commit retention receipt, a weekly dispatcher, and a class token DERIVED from what dispatches it. franken_lean-4o3n has the private Calibration field, so no bound can exist without the provenance of the configuration it was measured in. golden_vellum's is not evidence for anything - it only prints rows for a human to paste.

WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED. No coverage row is hollow on this ground and I checked specifically. Ten terminal rows cite one of these four surfaces, but the ignored fraction is 2 of 14, 1 of 15, 1 of 10 and 1 of 9, so a citing row most likely rests on a test that does run; and ZERO surfaces have every test ignored, which is the strictly stronger condition. The instances are fine. The class is what is unguarded.

ROOT CAUSE, SHARED WITH fln-rgha. Artifact citations in ci/VERIFICATION_MANIFEST.jsonl are FILE-granular; cargo executes per TEST FUNCTION. So the manifest structurally cannot say which test a row rests on. That is the same reason the rgha guard cannot check pin-dependence per function either. One root cause, two symptoms - and worth joining with cod_2's povo argument rather than treated as a third mechanism.

THE MEASUREMENT ERROR THIS BEAD IS ALSO A RECORD OF, because it happened inside the guard written about exactly this defect. Counting the same construct three ways gives three answers: rg -c on the token returns 22, because kernel_replay.rs is full of module docs, doc comments, an assertion message and one guard's own NEEDLE that all mention it; a #[test]-with-#[ignore]-within-six-lines window returns 6; the attribute at a line start returns 5. My predecessor's handoff said 15 and I committed "fifteen" into the rgha guard's module documentation at 974fcc5a without measuring it. This is the mentions-versus-construct error fln-bench-apparatus-empty-referent-bkw6 already paid for by counting [[bench]] sections while cargo auto-discovered the rest. Corrected in the same commit that files this bead.

MECHANISM DELIVERED WITH THIS BEAD. IGNORED_PRODUCER_ALLOWANCE in crates/fln-conformance/tests/ci_execution_join.rs declares each ignored test with the mechanism that compensates for it, bound by cardinality in both directions: an undeclared ignore reddens, a declaration that outlived its ignore reddens and names the entry to delete, the ceiling is an equality so a shrink must lower it in the same edit, an empty scan refuses rather than agreeing with every declaration, and a blank mechanism is refused as a declaration that says nothing. The derivation is fln_conformance::execution::ignored_tests, which requires the line to BEGIN with the attribute - that is what separates a declaration from a discussion of one.

FIVE MUTANTS, each asserting WHICH finding fires rather than that something went red. The decisive one is mutant_discussing_the_attribute_must_not_change_the_count: it injects all five shapes of mention that kernel_replay.rs actually contains - module doc, doc comment, a contains() needle, an assertion message - and requires the count NOT to move, then adds one real attribute and requires it to move by exactly one. That mutant is the one that would have caught the wrong number above.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT EARN. It does not observe a run happening, and it does not establish that any declared mechanism actually works - only that a claim to have one exists and is non-empty. Reading whether a compensating mechanism is real remains a human judgement, and a declaration whose prose is wrong passes this guard. The honest next step is not more scanning: it is making an artifact citation able to name a test function, which would close this and the rgha residue together.
close_reason: Mechanism delivered and green: IGNORED_PRODUCER_ALLOWANCE binds the class by cardinality in both directions, five mutants each assert which finding fires, and the follow-on this bead named -- an artifact citation that can name a test function -- landed at f24b6670.

title: W1 contract extraction: exact OLEAN and ILEAN format inventory
description:
## Description

Mechanically extract the pinned .olean and .ilean contracts into the shared canonical ContractInventory schema. Preserve header and epoch fields, constructor and field ordering, scalar encodings, relocation tables, compact encodings, sharing/back-reference behavior, ModuleData inventory, extension-entry encoding, validation-level semantics, and Lean.Server.Ilean fields. Every fact binds its authoritative pinned source locator and raw evidence; generated Markdown, constants, fixtures, and validators may only consume the canonical rows.

The extractor must distinguish absent, unsupported, corrupt, epoch-mismatched, and genuinely unknown facts. It must not infer host-specific layout into another target, normalize away format-significant ordering or sharing, use source comments as authority when executable/environment evidence is required, or silently accept a newer unknown field/version. Load-bearing ambiguity blocks publication with typed non-authoritative evidence.

This task owns exact format fact extraction and domain validation. It does not implement the production decoder/writer; those downstream codec beads consume this contract and retain their complete round-trip, corruption, resource, and mixed-producer obligations.

Attested evidence objects may carry RaptorQ repair sidecars via the asupersync coder; repair reconstructs to staging, re-verifies the canonical hash and a full schema decode, publishes without changing identity, and journals the corruption/repair event — repair is a durability feature, NEVER a trust shortcut. title: W12: Epoch ratchet — mechanical pin advances, census diffs, migration beads
description:

title: fln-env: bound declaration content hashing and admission with typed atomic resource refusals
description:
Problem: Environment::decl_content_digest currently traverses and buffers input-sized declaration state into an unbounded CanonWriter and returns a bare Digest, while Environment::add_decl performs an unbounded persistent-map insert and can refuse only duplicate names. No current API can truthfully report typed declaration byte/work exhaustion, cancellation, or atomic over-budget refusal. Runner-level time/output limits and PMap collision limits are orthogonal and must not be cited as this contract. Scope: design and implement first-class declaration-identity/admission limits and exact work facts for every ConstantInfo field family, including canonical output bytes, name/level/expression structure and depth, mutual-member rows, constructor rows, recursor rules, and persistent-map admission work. Limit and cancellation observation points must be deterministic; exhaustion/cancellation is typed Inconclusive rather than rejection, acceptance, panic, or partial publication (FL-INV-07). Hashing and admission must be one preflighted atomic operation: failure leaves the original Environment root, contents, and sharing unchanged; a later adequate-budget retry succeeds with the same digest/root as the unlimited mathematical model. Do not preserve an unbounded internal compatibility path merely for convenience; migrate callers to the capability/limit-aware API and keep any explicitly trusted test helper visibly non-authoritative. Avoid double traversal where a bounded canonical sink and checked counters can establish the same facts. Preserve exact Domain::DeclContent bytes for admitted declarations, one-name/one-constant semantics, insertion-order independence, snapshot sharing, and all existing variant identity. Verification must include independent byte/work models; exact-boundary and one-over refusal for every dimension; deep/wide/adversarial declarations; cancellation at every fixed observation point; schedule matrices; failure atomicity and clean recovery; named missing-check, late-check, partial-insert, wrong-actual, cancellation-as-rejection, and digest-drift mutants; comprehensive unit/property/model tests; and a no-mock environment E2E negative/recovery lane with versioned detailed logs and retained independently validated artifacts. This is the explicit home for the resource functionality previously impossible to prove inside fln-amv.12; fln-amv.12 remains responsible only for the finite one-byte enum-tag projection.

## Acceptance Criteria

Every acceptance criterion in the structured field is mandatory, including exact reproducible logical usage; immutable declaration-admission plans; typed Complete/Invalid/Conflict/Inconclusive/InternalFault precedence; no arbitrary allocator-abort recovery claim; exact retry and nonpublication; .13 PMap accounting consumed once; exhaustive boundaries, models, productive 1-8-32 schedules, named mutants, real recovery coverage, and strict independently valid evidence.
acceptance_criteria:
A reviewed declaration-identity/admission contract defines explicit versioned limits and exact usage facts for canonical encoded bytes, name/level/expression nodes and depth, mutual-member rows, constructor rows, recursor rules, declaration count, and persistent-map admission work; unsupported dimensions cannot fall through to an unbounded path. Outcomes keep Complete, typed Inconclusive resource exhaustion/cancellation, duplicate-name refusal, and InternalFault structurally distinct under FL-INV-07. Limit and cancellation observation points and actual-count semantics are frozen and schedule-independent. Declaration hashing plus insertion is one preflighted immutable transaction: no digest/root/environment is published on refusal, the original environment remains value-, root-, and sharing-identical, and a later adequate-budget retry produces the exact existing Domain::DeclContent bytes, digest, and logical root. Every production caller uses the bounded API; no hidden unlimited wrapper, timing-only limit, partial insert, double-counted work, or runner-only substitute is accepted. Unit/property/model tests cover every ConstantInfo variant and field, empty/exact/one-over/large/deep boundaries, checked arithmetic, malformed internal shapes, cancellation at each fixed point, 1/8/32 schedules, snapshot sharing, failure atomicity, and clean retry against independent byte/work models. Named missing-check, late-check, wrong-resource, wrong-actual, overflow, partial-publication, cancellation-as-rejection, and digest-drift mutants are killed. A shared real environment E2E exercises admitted, every resource refusal, cancellation/inconclusive, exact restoration, and later recovery with strict schema-versioned NDJSON containing run/scenario/step ids, bead/claim/invariant rows, governed input hashes, limits/usage, expected/actual outcome, authority/publication flags, exact digest/root values, process/resource facts, separate bounded streams, cleanup, and final state; validators reject missing, duplicate, stale, contradictory, reordered, or extra evidence and retained manifests revalidate independently. cargo fmt --check, all fln-env and relevant fln-hash tests, check/clippy with warnings denied, UBS, scripts/check.sh, the authoritative environment runner, mutation/fault lanes, and parent W2 gates pass. No panic, silent truncation, unbounded bypass, mock-only closure, process budget substituted for in-process refusal, or changed canonical bytes satisfies closure.

Plan-space precision addendum: usage facts are logical, reproducible units: canonical bytes emitted, Name/Level/Expr node occurrences visited, maximum logical depth, mutual/constructor/recursor row occurrences, PMap comparison/path/fresh-node work, and explicitly reserved capacity. They do not claim unique Arc-node counts, CPU instructions, allocator-resident bytes, or globally available memory. Complete reports exact full totals. A refusal reports exact consumption through the deterministic refusal checkpoint, the triggering dimension, and a witnessed lower bound on remaining required work, normally limit plus one; it never scans an unobserved suffix merely to claim an exact total.

A versioned total precedence table covers malformed/internally inconsistent input, duplicate-name observation, checked-arithmetic overflow, cancellation, and simultaneous resource breaches. A duplicate/conflict is authoritative only after its required bounded lookup completes; an unfinished lookup is Inconclusive. For simultaneous resource dimensions at one checkpoint, one frozen dimension order selects the primary reason while all observed facts remain available. Pairwise tie tests prove identical outcome, checkpoint, usage, authority, publication, and cacheability across schedules.

Hashing/preflight produces an immutable non-authoritative DeclarationAdmissionPlan binding schema/epoch, the exact canonical declaration input and provisional digest/bytes, source Environment logical root/revision, duplicate-name observation, usage, and the canonical collision/PMap admission plan. A provisional digest computed before a later refusal is never returned, logged, or cached as authoritative. Commit revalidates declaration, base root, cancellation, and plan integrity, consumes collision/PMap facts exactly once, performs genuinely fallible input-sized reservations where supported, then publishes one immutable Environment. It does not recompute canonical bytes, digest, collision order, or PMap work. Stale, substituted, cross-base, replayed, or internally inconsistent plans are typed under the same precedence table and confer no authority.

Typed memory refusal is limited to configured budgets, checked arithmetic, and demonstrably fallible reservation calls. No in-process claim promises recovery from arbitrary Arc/Box/global allocator abort unless every allocating path is proved fallible. All claimed reservations precede publication; the final phase uses reserved storage, immutable moves, and non-failing bookkeeping. The existing dependency path through fln-amv.14 and fln-amv.13 supplies the bounded PMap contract; no second resource truth or double charge is permitted.

j8h owns the exhaustive per-declaration matrix: every ConstantInfo field and logical usage dimension, zero/one-under/exact/one-over, each cancellation checkpoint, plan substitution/staleness, nonpublication, and retry. Productive 1/8/32 workers process distinct declarations/interleavings with fixed reported seeds and replayable minimized counterexamples; a sequential loop merely labeled with thread counts is insufficient. Additional named mutants double-charge PMap work, omit one usage dimension, expose a provisional digest, accept a stale/cross-base plan, reserve after publication, or treat unfinished duplicate lookup as conflict. fln-amv.11 owns only cross-plane composition; fln-amv.14 owns the authoritative lifecycle/envelope mechanism. Evidence references each independently validated child bundle once.

THE PRECISE GAP, sharper than the problem statement.

  a. try_add_decl_with_budget takes expanded_weight AS A CALLER-SUPPLIED u64. The boundary trusts a number instead of measuring it. That is the concrete form of "no current API can truthfully report byte/work exhaustion": the one resource number crossing this boundary today is an unverified input.
  b. decl_content_digest is entirely unbounded and uncancellable, and it is the input-sized half.
  c. Hashing and admission are two separate calls, so there is no atomic hash-plus-admit transaction and no plan.
  d. DeclAdmission::Rejected(EnvError) collapses duplicate-name with any future invalid input; this bead wants Complete/Invalid/Conflict/Inconclusive/InternalFault distinct under a frozen precedence table.

MIGRATION IS SMALL, which was worth checking before designing. Environment::decl_content_digest has exactly ONE production caller in the whole workspace: logical_root at environment.rs:462. Every other use is a test. (crates/fln-hash/src/root.rs has a same-named function over raw bytes — unrelated, do not confuse them.) So "migrate the callers, keep no unbounded path" is a small, tractable change rather than a sweep.

THE BLOCKING CONSTRAINT, and it is cross-domain. The canonical-bytes dimension — the FIRST dimension this bead names — cannot be bounded from inside fln-env:
  * CanonWriter (crates/fln-hash/src/canon.rs:219) is a concrete struct wrapping Vec<u8>. It exposes new, into_bytes, and the typed writers. There is NO length accessor, so the byte count cannot even be OBSERVED mid-stream — only by into_bytes(), which consumes, and only after the whole unbounded write already happened. That is exactly the defect this bead describes.
  * Canonical::write_body(&self, w: &mut CanonWriter) takes the CONCRETE type, so a budgeted sink cannot be substituted from fln-env.
  * The asymmetry is striking and makes the ask precise: the READ direction is already fully budgeted in that same file — CanonReader::with_budget, DecodeBudget, r.charge_node()?, Exhausted, into_inconclusive(). The write direction has none of it. What this bead needs is the writer counterpart of machinery that already exists twenty lines away.
fln-hash and fln-core are cc_3's domain. I have touched neither and will not.

THE DESIGN THAT DOES NOT NEED THAT CHANGE, and is better anyway on the refusal path.

Because the encoding is deterministic and length-prefixed, the exact canonical byte total is a FUNCTION OF THE STRUCTURE. So: one bounded structural pre-pass over the ConstantInfo with checked counters and cancellation checkpoints, computing every usage fact INCLUDING the exact canonical byte count, refusing before a single byte is buffered; the real write happens only for declarations that already passed. Consequences worth stating:
  * On refusal NOTHING is allocated, which is stronger than a bounded sink that fills to the limit and then stops.
  * It is a single traversal, not the double traversal this bead forbids — the write is not a second measuring pass, it is the publication of an already-decided result.
  * The byte model must stay exactly in step with the encoder. That is not a new liability: this bead ALREADY REQUIRES an "independent byte/work model" as verification. Using the mandated model as the preflight makes the requirement load-bearing instead of decorative, and it is pinned by evidence that landed today — the frozen golden_stream_bytes per tag case (286 for definitions, 157 for quotients) and the 35 membership rows, which fail loudly if model and encoder ever diverge.
If cc_3 later lands a budgeted writer, the byte dimension can move onto it without changing this contract; the pre-pass stays useful for the structural dimensions regardless.

PLANNED SHAPE, twinning modules.rs deliberately rather than inventing names:
  DeclarationResource { CanonicalBytes, Nodes, Depth, MutualRows, ConstructorRows, RecursorRules, PMapWork }
  DeclarationBudget { per-dimension limits, plus an UNBOUNDED const, exactly as CollisionBudget does }
  DeclarationUsage { exact totals on Complete; exact consumption through the refusal checkpoint otherwise }
  DeclarationCheckpoint { the fixed observation points, frozen and schedule-independent }
  DeclarationInconclusive { ResourceLimitExceeded{resource,limit,actual,witnessed_lower_bound,checkpoint}, Cancelled{checkpoint}, PlanSuperseded{expected_root,actual_root} }
  DeclarationOutcome<T> { Complete, Invalid, Conflict, Inconclusive, InternalFault }
  PreparedDeclarationAdmission { is_cacheable() -> false; commit() revalidates base root, cancellation and plan integrity, consumes the amv.13 PMap facts ONCE, publishes one immutable Environment, recomputes nothing }
Per the bead: a provisional digest computed before a later refusal is never returned, logged, or cached. That falls out of the design — the digest is not computed at all until preflight has passed.

TWO TRAPS THIS BEAD FLAGS, restated because they are easy to violate by accident: runner-level time/output limits and PMap collision limits are ORTHOGONAL and must not be cited as this contract; and no unbounded internal path may survive "for convenience" — logical_root moves onto the bounded API and any trusted test helper is named so it reads as non-authoritative.

SEQUENCING. Slice 1 is the bounded measurement core plus the typed vocabulary, verified byte-identical against today's digests at unbounded budget — the goldens above are the regression net. Slice 2 is the plan/commit transaction, the precedence table and caller migration. Slice 3 is the E2E negative/recovery lane, which lands after fln-identity-path-mutant-recovery-mbco so it uses that lane's mutant/restore shape rather than a fourth one.

DESIGN CORRECTION BEFORE ANY CODE: do NOT invent a DeclarationOutcome/DeclarationInconclusive pair. The shared FL-INV-07 taxonomy already exists and its own documentation forbids what I sketched an hour ago (PeachBass/cc_1, 2026-07-25). Correcting my own previous comment rather than leaving both readings on the bead.

WHAT I FOUND after surveying further. Two more pieces of this bead already exist:

1. crates/fln-env/src/terms.rs::expanded_weight(root: &Expr, budget: &WeightBudget) -> Outcome<WeightReport> is already a BOUNDED, ITERATIVE (explicit stack, so a deep term is a measurement rather than a stack overflow), typed-inconclusive traversal of an Expr DAG. It reports exact facts (expanded_weight, distinct_nodes, edges) and — note — already implements this bead's "witnessed lower bound, normally limit plus one" rule, via observed.max(allowed.saturating_add(1)) with the comment "a stop must report spending past its allowance or it is not a stop". So the hardest dimension is done; j8h consumes it rather than rebuilding it.

2. The authority vocabulary is fln_core::outcome: Outcome<T>, Inconclusive { cause, diagnostic, progress }, InconclusiveCause { Cancelled{at}, ResourceExhausted{usage}, DependencyUnavailable, AuthorityIncomplete }, ResourceUsage, and fln_core::diag::{ResourceReason, StructuralUnit}.

WHY MY EARLIER SKETCH WAS WRONG. Inconclusive's own doc records decision fln-um4a, dated 2026-07-25 — today — declining to add a payload parameter, with the reasoning that a domain payload on the non-answer arm is "the FL-INV-07 footgun this module exists to remove", and naming fln-env specifically as a crate that appeared to need one and did not. It prescribes the alternative verbatim: "a caller with genuine partial progress keeps its own report type and folds only the authority field, e.g. Report { work, status: Outcome<Verdict>, facts }", with the constraint that the partial work must be unreachable without consulting the status. modules.rs having its own ModuleGraphOutcome is the older pattern; the shared one is the intended home now. A fourth parallel taxonomy in this crate is exactly the f6br-class collision the naming and tagging conventions exist to prevent.

CORRECTED SHAPE:

    pub struct DeclarationAdmissionReport {
        usage: DeclarationUsage,                             // exact per-dimension facts, present on EVERY path
        status: Outcome<PreparedDeclarationAdmission>,        // the authority, folded not hand-rolled
    }

with usage private and reachable only through an accessor that the status gates, per the doc's constraint. Duplicate-name stays a completed verdict inside Outcome::Complete (the doc is explicit that a completed traversal reporting "invalid" belongs in Complete, exactly as a decoder's "malformed" is a verdict about bytes) — NOT a fifth arm. Exhaustion and cancellation are Outcome::Inconclusive with InconclusiveCause::ResourceExhausted / Cancelled. That satisfies this bead's Complete/Invalid/Conflict/Inconclusive/InternalFault precedence requirement without a new enum: the distinctions live in the Complete payload and the shared cause, which is where the taxonomy already puts them.

THE ONE GENUINELY CROSS-DOMAIN QUESTION, for cc_3 (fln-core is theirs, and StructuralUnit is a CLOSED taxonomy whose doc says adding a variant "is a reviewed taxonomy revision that breaks every consumer until handled").

  StructuralUnit today is { InputBytes = "bytes consumed from a serialized input", ProducedNodes = "values materialized from it", ExpandedWeight = "the denoted tree size" }.

  This bead's first dimension is canonical bytes EMITTED by the encoder. That is neither consumed input nor a materialized value. The unit's own stated bar for a new variant is "not 'it is a different number' but 'a caller has to react differently'", and a caller does react differently: an encoded-output bound is reduced by shrinking the declaration, whereas InputBytes describes what you were handed. So the question is whether canonical output bytes should widen InputBytes' meaning or get a reviewed fourth unit. I am NOT deciding this in fln-env and I have not touched fln-core.

  The other dimensions do NOT need new units, which was the pressure worth removing: mutual rows, constructor rows, recursor rules and declaration count are all ProducedNodes; depth is ResourceReason::RecursionDepth, which already exists; expanded weight is ExpandedWeight. Per-dimension exactness lives on DeclarationUsage, and the frozen dimension order picks which one names the primary reason. That is this bead's "one frozen dimension order selects the primary reason while all observed facts remain available", discharged by the report type rather than by growing a closed taxonomy.

ONE EXISTING INCONSISTENCY WORTH RECORDING, not mine to fix here: pmap.rs's bounded insert (fln-amv.13) refuses with its own CollisionExhausted { resource, limit, attempted, collision_hash } as a std::error::Error, NOT through Outcome/Inconclusive. So the PMap dimension currently sits outside the shared FL-INV-07 taxonomy while every other bounded path in the crate is inside it. This bead must consume those facts exactly once and must not double-charge them; whoever unifies that should do it as its own change, because it touches amv.13's published contract.

ALSO CONFIRMED: fln-hash has no budgeted writer and no bead asking for one. CanonWriter is a bare Vec<u8> with no length accessor while CanonReader in the same file has with_budget, DecodeBudget, charge_node and Exhausted. My design routes around the gap by computing the exact byte total in the bounded structural pre-pass and refusing before anything is buffered, so this is not a blocker — but the asymmetry is real and is recorded here because the next person to bound a write path will hit it.

STATE: nothing written to fln-env yet, deliberately. The survey changed the design twice, and a 400-line diff started before the second correction would have been a fourth taxonomy on a shared tree. Next pane: implement DeclarationUsage plus the bounded pre-pass consuming terms::expanded_weight, fold authority through Outcome, and verify byte-identity at unbounded budget against the frozen goldens (golden_stream_bytes 286/157 per tag case, plus the 35 membership rows) — those are the regression net that proves canonical bytes did not move.

comments.text:
FOUR FORGE SEAMS, ALL ALREADY PROVEN DISCRIMINATING IN-PROCESS — inherit these seeds rather than deriving them (PeachBass/cc_1, 2026-07-25).

This bead was filed for j8h's declaration-admission seeds. fln-extension-history-checkpoint-identity-41s needs the same treatment through the same run_identity_path_mutant_recovery helper, and its seeds are already written and already known to kill. Recording them here so both sets live in one place and cod_3 is not re-deriving what fln-env tests have already established.

THE SEAMS, all #[cfg(test)] in crates/fln-env/src/extensions.rs, none reachable from a production path, each with a test that proves it discriminates:

1. forge_recorded_base_digests(history, state)
   Forges only the checkpoint's two RECORDED base digests, leaving the retained base handle intact, so every fast path accepts and only the exact comparison can refuse.
   Proven by: extensions::tests::equal_length_and_equal_digest_unequal_histories_are_refused — refuses at divergence 0 and, separately, at divergence 2 for a late-diverging pair. The unforged checkpoint still restores, so the seam is discriminating rather than universally breaking.
   Lane seed suggestion: checkpoint_base_digest_collision.

2. forge_journal_facts(digest, payload_bytes)
   Forges a BASE's own journal digest and byte count, which is the capture-side counterpart — capture compares the base's own digest against a prefix digest computed from the target, so it needs a different seam from (1). That the two defects need two seams is the clearest evidence they are two defects.
   Proven by: extensions::tests::capture_refuses_a_base_that_only_matches_the_prefix_digest — refuses at entry 2; the honest base still captures at base lengths 0 through 3.
   Lane seed suggestion: checkpoint_prefix_digest_collision.

3. forge_schema_version(v)
   Proven by: extensions::tests::full_journal_binding_omissions_each_die_for_their_own_typed_reason — CheckpointError::UnsupportedVersion, never guessed compatible.
   Lane seed suggestion: checkpoint_schema_omission.

4. forge_cumulative_facts(captured_entries)
   Makes the declared cumulative facts disagree with the journal they describe.
   Proven by: the same test — CheckpointError::MalformedCheckpoint.
   Lane seed suggestion: checkpoint_cumulative_facts_omission.

WHY THIS IS A STRONG HANDOFF AND NOT A WISHLIST. A lane mutant is only worth writing if the target test is known to go red for the RIGHT reason. All four above already do, in-process, with the typed error variant asserted rather than a generic failure — so whoever writes the lane steps starts from a known-good kill and only has to supply the overlay mutation and the two grep signatures. That is the same position the three mbco seeds were in when this bead's parent framing was written, and it is why that one went smoothly.

ONE CAVEAT WORTH KNOWING BEFORE WRITING THE STEPS. The four seams are test-only, so an OVERLAY source mutation cannot call them — the lane's mutation has to edit production code to produce the same observable defect. For (3) and (4) that is easy: change the schema constant, or change the captured-entries arithmetic. For (1) and (2) the production-equivalent mutation is to DELETE the exact-comparison call, so the digest accelerator becomes the only check — which is exactly the pre-fix behaviour and exactly what the target tests refuse. That mutation is single-site and anchor-checkable in both places.

j8h's three seeds are unchanged and are in this bead's description. Same helper, same step shape, seven seeds total across the two beads if both are taken together.

**`not resolved to a #[test] fn` does NOT mean wrong.** Many entries here are lane mutant ids, `scripts/evidence.py` subcommands, schema descriptors or type names — legitimate evidence of a kind this probe does not model, and it models exactly one kind. Read the column as *this particular probe found a `#[test]` function of that name*, never as a verdict on the entry. Calling those defects would be the basename trap one level up: one method, confident where it applies and silent about where it does not.

## 3. THE ROW'S OWN NOTES, VERBATIM

Reproduced in full and unfiltered — this is what withdrawal would destroy, since a wrong citation still records what its author rested the claim on:

- The five checkpoint-history seams exercised by the same helper are claimed independently by fln-extension-history-checkpoint-identity-41s.
- This row claims the four j8h production-equivalent overlay mutants and their byte-exact recoveries only; it does not claim the parent j8h positive declaration-admission producer or full epic closure.

## 4. WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT ESTABLISH

**No claim of yours is asserted false.** An unresolvable citation means the evidence cannot be **checked**, never that the work was not done — which is why this is a question about state and not an accusation.

Every figure is DERIVED by the script that wrote this comment (`/data/tmp/claude-1000/cc1-r20/recover14b.py`); none is hand-transcribed, because a copied number in fourteen documents is fourteen chances to drift. **Its v1 had a defect worth carrying:** it selected provenance notes by keyword and kept 0 of the 9 these rows carry, emitting every body with no notes section — an absence indistinguishable from nothing-to-recover. v2 takes notes verbatim and asserts the drop is zero. Its classifier is checked against `artifact_referent_census.rs`'s declared census class by class before any body is written, and the `#[test]` index is floored so a broken walk refuses instead of reporting a clean tree.

Section 2 establishes that a named test **exists and is not `#[ignore]`d**, never that it supports the claim citing it — that is the harder join and it is untouched. Class `bounded_model`: one host, one commit; on-disk and glob counts move with the tree.
