comments.author: cc_3
comments.text:
LANE SPECIFICATION for all three Vellum e2e lanes — franken_lean-jbru, franken_lean-urd1 and fln-33gl. From cc_3, posted identically on all three so whichever gets picked up first has the whole picture.

WHY THIS COMMENT EXISTS. These three have waited through several rotations, and the reason is an asymmetry, not a priority call: I know what the suites assert, whoever owns ci/ knows how a lane is registered, and neither half is much use alone. So this is everything from my side, stated so the ci/ work is TRANSCRIPTION rather than design. If anything below is ambiguous, that is a defect in this comment — say so on the bead and I will fix it rather than have you guess.

=== WHICH LANE WRAPS WHAT ===

franken_lean-jbru  lexer_no_mock_e2e          crate fln-syntax   parent bead franken_lean-81oq (closed)
franken_lean-urd1  parser_corpus_no_mock_e2e  crate fln-parse    parent bead fln-ffam (closed)
fln-33gl           dynamic_parser_no_mock_e2e crate fln-parse    parent bead fln-okfb (closed)

All three parents are CLOSED and their suites are green. Nothing about the parsers or the lexer needs writing. What is missing in each case is only the lane wrapper and its evidence plumbing.

=== EXACT TEST TARGETS, by lane ===

franken_lean-jbru wraps these fln-syntax targets:
    cargo test -p fln-syntax --test lexer_state_model
    cargo test -p fln-syntax --test lexer_fuzz
    cargo test -p fln-syntax --test lexer_thread_matrix
    cargo test -p fln-syntax --test lexer_resource_bounds
    cargo test -p fln-syntax --test token_table_totality
    cargo test -p fln-syntax --test incremental_lex_property
    cargo test -p fln-syntax --test golden_vellum
    cargo test -p fln-syntax --lib

franken_lean-urd1 wraps these fln-parse targets:
    cargo test -p fln-parse --test parser_category_inventory
    cargo test -p fln-parse --test pratt_precedence_model
    cargo test -p fln-parse --test parse_roundtrip_property
    cargo test -p fln-parse --test parser_fuzz

fln-33gl wraps these fln-parse targets:
    cargo test -p fln-parse --test registration_state_model
    cargo test -p fln-parse --test grammar_effect_totality
    cargo test -p fln-parse --test parser_interleaving_dpor
    cargo test -p fln-parse --test dynamic_parser_mutations

IGNORE crates/fln-syntax/tests/zz_debug.rs. It is silent scaffolding with no #[test], kept under an explicit instruction rather than deleted. It must not appear in any lane's step list.

=== WHAT A PASSING RUN MUST ASSERT, per lane ===

Common to all three. A lane that only checks the exit code is not enough for two of these suites, for reasons below. Every lane must assert:
* exit code 0 from each cargo step;
* the step's captured stdout contains `test result: ok.` and does NOT contain `test result: FAILED`;
* ZERO tests were filtered to nothing — a target that matched no tests exits 0 and proves nothing. Assert the `N passed` count is at or above the floor listed below, so a suite that silently stopped running is caught.

Floors as of 2026-07-25, all currently passing:
    lexer_state_model         7      token_table_totality        9
    lexer_fuzz                5      incremental_lex_property    5
    lexer_thread_matrix       5      golden_vellum               5 passed, 1 ignored
    lexer_resource_bounds     7      fln-syntax --lib           82
    parser_category_inventory 5      registration_state_model    5
    pratt_precedence_model    6      grammar_effect_totality     7
    parse_roundtrip_property  3      parser_interleaving_dpor    5
    parser_fuzz               4      dynamic_parser_mutations    7
Use "at or above" and not equality: these grow.

THREE SUITE-SPECIFIC ASSERTIONS THAT MATTER MORE THAN THE EXIT CODE:

1. parser_category_inventory (urd1) READS THE PINNED TOOLCHAIN and SKIPS TYPED when it is absent, printing `SKIP parser_category_inventory: ...` and exiting 0. RCH remote workers do not have the pin. So a lane that treats exit 0 as a pass will publish a skip as evidence it did not gather — the exact failure the suite was written to avoid. The lane MUST either pin itself to a host with ~/.elan/toolchains/leanprover--lean4---v4.32.0 present, or assert that the captured output does NOT contain `SKIP parser_category_inventory`. Please do the second; it is cheaper and it fails loudly on the wrong host.

2. parser_interleaving_dpor (33gl) IS A SELF-DIFFERENTIAL and says so in its own module docs. A sweep finding no interleaving violation shows only that my schedule space contains no violation my own model can express. FL-INV-01 is the CLAIM; this suite is one piece of support. Whatever the lane emits as semantic NDJSON must carry that distinction rather than launder it — do not label this step as FL-INV-01 evidence. It also spawns 32 threads, which is the kind of step that trips a process-identity guard; see the wait-ms note below.

3. golden_vellum (jbru) HAS NO UPDATE MODE by design and never writes its corpus. It has one #[ignore]d test, `emit_corpus_for_review`, which only prints. The lane must NOT pass `--ignored` anywhere, and must NOT set any environment variable that could reach it. If a future lane wants a regeneration step, that is a separate reviewed change and it must not introduce a write path into the compare mode.

=== THE FAILURE AND RECOVERY CASES each lane needs ===

The acceptance criteria on all three parents demand a real no-mock positive, failure AND recovery case. Here is what I suggest for each, using inputs the suites already understand:

jbru (lexer): positive — a well-formed .lean-ish file lexes with zero diagnostics. failure — a file with a tab in trivia, which is a genuine lexical refusal carrying the pin's exact wording `tabs are not allowed; please configure your editor to expand them`. recovery — a file with TWO tabs, asserting the recovering configuration reports both while the non-recovering one reports one, and that acceptance is unchanged between them. That last point is the acceptance law from franken_lean-81oq and it is the one worth publishing.

urd1 (parser): positive — an expression with mixed operators parses. failure — `1 = 2 = 3`, which is a genuine non-associativity refusal. recovery — the same file, asserting exactly ONE diagnostic rather than two, which is the trailing-loop discard rule observed against the pin.

33gl (registration): positive — a category declared then a production registered then a lookup succeeds. failure — registration into an unknown category, refused with `unknown category` in the pin's wording. recovery — a budget-exceeded batch, asserting the store is UNTOUCHED afterwards and that the outcome is Inconclusive rather than a rejection. Do not render that Inconclusive as a diagnostic; FL-INV-07 is the point of the step.

=== THE FIVE REGISTRATION POINTS, identical for all three ===

1. scripts/e2e/<name>.sh — model on scripts/e2e/closure_audit.sh.
2. scripts/evidence.py — register the scenario with its EXACT ordered step list in E2E_STEP_ORDERS at the top of the file. The order must match what the script runs, exactly.
3. scripts/check.sh — add the script to INPUT_PATHS and to the shellcheck stage.
4. .github/workflows/ci.yml — add the step, and join BOTH the verify-step's expected_roots set and its specs tuple. The roots set is CLOSED, so this is a deliberate edit and not an append.
5. Canonical semantic NDJSON with telemetry kept separate, plus independent validation.

=== HARD-WON CONSTRAINTS, so they are not rediscovered ===

* Every --wait-ms for the process-identity guards is capped at 30000. A larger value makes the guard raise instantly and the lane SIGKILLs its own runner with a bare `Killed`. This bit me on a previous lane and the symptom is completely opaque.
* NEVER edit a governed file while a lane is running, not even cargo fmt. Lanes re-hash their INPUT_PATHS around every supervised step and flip `inconclusive: governed_inputs_changed`.
* Expected-fail cargo steps use --semantic-failure-exit 101 and must grep BOTH the .out and .err captures for the intended reason, because libtest panics print to stderr under --nocapture.
* Lanes longer than the 10-minute tool timeout should be launched detached and watched.
* All these suites are fast — the slowest is under a second, and the whole of fln-syntax plus fln-parse runs in a few seconds. These are good candidates for per-commit steps rather than nightly ones.

=== WHAT I WILL AND WILL NOT DO ===

I will not touch ci/, scripts/ or .github/. Those are cod_2's domain and reaching across them is what these three beads exist to avoid. What I will do, on request and quickly: add any assertion to the suites that makes a lane's job easier — a machine-readable summary line, a specific exit code, a named test that isolates one case. Ask on the bead and it is a small change in my own crates.

If a floor above is stale by the time you read this, `cargo test -p fln-syntax` and `cargo test -p fln-parse` print the current numbers and are the authority; this comment is a snapshot of 2026-07-25.

description:
## Description

This is the W1 Substrate & Contracts aggregation epic (§22.2), not an implementation authority or universal dependency root. Downstream work may depend on the narrow contract it consumes; workstream/release gates use this epic as the W1 milestone. It closes only after every explicit W1 dependency has current independently valid evidence and the canonical lock/contract/Tribunal identities join.

W1 integrates: fln-core Name/Level/Expr/literal/options/positions; owned fln-hash and canonical schemas; the mechanically extracted target-indexed ABI, OLEAN/ILEAN, extern and builtin inventories; authoritative SUITE.lock and closure policy; quality/evidence schemas and Tribunal bootstrap; mode/determinism/certified provenance; typed outcomes and faithful/sound diagnostics; campaign and performance infrastructure plus the pinned two-host Reference baseline; Windows functional honesty; convergence/WIP governance; and UPSTREAM_LEDGER upgrade control. Each feature remains owned by its dedicated bead; this epic does not duplicate it.

W1 closure is a strict evidence join, never a percentage, title/label heuristic, or mostly-green rollup. Every required child contributes one current row with status, claim type/evidence kind, schema, immutable bundle root, source/input root, SUITE.lock and Reference/Corpus epoch, mode/platform/target scope, freshness, named tests/mutations/E2E scenarios, limitations, and independent validation. Missing, stale, mixed-epoch, mismatched-root, mock-substituted, reopened, Inconclusive, InternalFault, or overclaimed rows block closure.

The terminal no-mock integration starts from the authoritative lock; validates workspace and every closure lane; regenerates and consumes the canonical contracts/censuses; runs Reference-vs-Reference Tribunal plumbing; exercises mode isolation and typed diagnostic projection; verifies campaign/performance registries and both host baseline bundles; reports Windows status honestly; and archives one causally joined bundle. Child success evidence remains intact if the join fails, but no parent pass or partial evidence is published.

W1 proves reusable foundations and enforcement mechanisms. Release-wide adoption by later absent subsystems remains mandatory on their workstream beads and W12; this prevents false completion without losing any functionality. The former statement that W1 depends on nothing and everything depends on it is intentionally retired as graphically and architecturally false.

## Success Criteria

Named suites w1_child_evidence_join_model, w1_contract_identity_join, w1_claim_authority_model, and w1_cross_contract_no_mock_e2e validate exact child membership, root/epoch/mode/platform compatibility, evidence freshness and authority, strict all-of closure, terminal recovery, and independent bundle verification. Mutations for dropped child, stale/reopened/Inconclusive evidence, mixed lock/contract/epoch roots, percentage-based close, mock substitution, claim-class promotion, omitted platform/baseline lane, terminal partial publication, and label-based child discovery are killed. Cold generation is deterministic; generated Rust compiles; policy/census rows are total; seeded pin/layout/symbol/schema/normalizer/dependency/mode/diagnostic/campaign/performance mutations fail at their owning child and remain visible at the join. Human and strict schema-versioned NDJSON retain all child ids/roots/statuses/scopes, first failing join fact, commands and bounded artifacts, resources, cleanup, and final state. title: W7: simp faithful core + deterministic compiled rewrite-index format
description:
Implement the simp faithful core + compiled rewrite indexes (§12.1, §12.2): the Reference simp semantics — simp-set discipline, discrimination-tree candidate retrieval, congruence closure interplay, dsimp/simp-only behaviors, attribute-driven extension — implemented natively end to end (driver, congruence interplay, extension dispatch are Anvil code behind obs-class Mirror facade rows), with the Corpus simp-heavy files plus instrumented-oracle rewrite traces as the fidelity corpus. Mathlib simp EXTENSIONS and simprocs are user code on Golem calling the native driver through the facade.

Compiled rewrite indexes (§12.2): per-library discrimination automata compiled at Ledger commit time and shipped as content-addressed CAS artifacts (an olean-next attachment) — mathlib tens of thousands of simp lemmas become a preloaded matcher, not a per-session index build. Staleness is impossible BY CONSTRUCTION (content-addressed against the simp-set own hash).

Acceptance: simp outcomes match the oracle on the simp-heavy fidelity corpus (rewrite firings, order where observable, result terms); index-backed retrieval produces identical candidate sets to freshly-built trees (representation-equivalence tests); index build determinism (same simp-set hash, same artifact bytes). Tests: golden rewrite-trace replay; dsimp/simp-only behavioral fixtures; congruence-interplay differentials; a stale-index mutation test (perturbed simp-set with unperturbed index must be structurally unloadable).

## Acceptance Criteria

All bead-specific requirements, acceptance conditions, tests, invariants, compatibility surfaces, evidence levels, performance gates, negative/recovery cases, and user-visible behaviors stated above remain mandatory. In addition, the MANDATORY VERIFICATION DEFINITION OF DONE in Notes must be satisfied with named unit/property/mutation suites, at least one shared real-path no-mock E2E scenario plus failure/recovery coverage, detailed human and schema-versioned NDJSON artifacts, and reproducible close evidence. No listed feature or claim may be silently narrowed, deferred, mocked, or declared complete through an unclassified divergence.
design: REVIEW AMENDMENT — this bead owns the native faithful simp semantics plus a deterministic, content-keyed rewrite-index builder/reader and proves loaded-index candidate equivalence to a fresh tree. It does not claim Ledger publication before W8 exists. Transactional CAS publication, olean-next attachment, remote hydration, retention, invalidation, and quarantine are owned by fln-publish-rewrite-indexes-gca.

1. Implement Reference-compatible simp-set discipline, discrimination retrieval, congruence interaction, dsimp, simp-only, attributes, extension dispatch, and observable rewrite ordering natively. Real mathlib simp extensions and simprocs execute as user code on Golem through the Native Mirror facade; no upstream implementation executes as a component.
2. Compile each library simp set into a deterministic versioned discrimination automaton stored as a content-addressed Ledger CAS artifact and olean-next attachment bound to the exact simp-set hash. A missing, corrupt, foreign-version, or stale index is structurally unloadable and falls back to a fresh safe index without changing candidate sets or results.
3. Golden instrumented-oracle traces and the simp-heavy corpus agree on goal outcome, result term, observable firing sequence, and facade calls. Compiled-index retrieval is representation-equivalent to a freshly built tree and same hash/input produces bit-identical bytes at threads 1, 8, and 32.

A shared no-mock E2E lane elaborates real simp-heavy Lean files with real user extensions on Golem, compares traces/results with the pinned oracle, repeats through cold and precompiled indexes, rejects a perturbed stale attachment, rebuilds safely, and proves clean recovery. Human logs plus schema-versioned NDJSON include run/file/goal/rewrite/index/artifact ids, bead/claim/invariant/Parity rows, redacted argv/cwd, pin/build/mode/profile/thread/seed/budget/cache facts, canonical source/simp-set/index/result hashes, candidate/firing decisions, expected/actual, timings/resources/status, artifacts, cleanup, and final state.

title: The kernel LOC covenant is enforced but never disclosed, so headroom and its trend are invisible
description:
The <= 12 KLOC kernel covenant (AGENTS.md doctrine 5, FL-INV-02 / D6) is genuinely enforced,
and its measured value is never disclosed anywhere. It is a wall, not a gauge: nobody can see
how much headroom is left, or that it is shrinking, until the day it fails.

WHAT IS ALREADY GOOD, so this bead is not mistaken for a hollow-green report. Measured at
53a5e3ec:
  * count_loc (tools/structure-guard/src/checks.rs:840) counts non-blank, non-// lines over
    crates/<C>/src/**/*.rs, skips symlinks, and reports an undecodable file as a finding rather
    than understating the count.
  * enforcement is FLN-STRUCT-015 (checks.rs:2486-2497), and raising the declared limit is
    itself refused: FLN-STRUCT-024 (checks.rs:1542-1550) fails if the covenant is missing OR
    exceeds 12000, which is "growth requires amending the plan first" mechanised.
  * it RUNS in three independent places -- scripts/check.sh:1607, .github/workflows/ci.yml:411
    (whose test step IS check.sh), and tools/structure-guard/tests/real_workspace.rs:34 under
    plain cargo test, not #[ignore]d.
  * the branches are planted: seeded.rs:421 (101 lines against a fixture max-loc=100),
    seeded.rs:673 (include! and #[cfg_attr(path=..)] escapes), seeded.rs:884 (undecodable
    source), seeded.rs:662 (deleting the covenant line).

THE DEFECT. The variable `loc` appears exactly once outside the counter -- inside the violation
message at checks.rs:2492. The robot NDJSON emits crates and edges (report.rs:123-127) and NOT
the covenant count. So:
  * the current value is invisible. Measured by hand for this bead: fln-kernel is 6112
    covenant-relevant lines across 6 files, 50.9% of budget, 5888 lines of headroom.
  * no trend exists. A jump from 51% to 95% is silent, and the first signal anyone gets is a
    red gate with no history to explain it.
  * the number cannot be cited. Any claim about kernel size today has to be re-derived by
    reimplementing count_loc, which is a second copy of the algorithm and can drift from the
    real one -- the exact hazard the projection guard avoids by using the publisher binary.

PROPOSED REPAIR, small and mechanical: emit the measured count per covenanted crate in the robot
run_end line (loc and its limit), so the value lands in every check.sh artifact bundle. That
turns the wall into a gauge at no new cost, since count_loc already runs on every invocation and
its result is currently discarded unless it exceeds the limit.

THE TRAP, stated because it is this repo's recurring one: a disclosure is not evidence about the
thing it discloses. Emitting the number does not make the covenant stronger, and the row for this
bead must not imply it does (fln-8zsq and franken_lean-2ki4 closed on a disclosure and bought
nothing about the corpus). What it buys is exactly one thing: the number becomes citable and its
movement becomes visible.

SECOND, SMALLER OBSERVATION, recorded here rather than filed separately because it is one line:
fln-checker carries no covenant at all. FLN-STRUCT-024 requires one for fln-kernel only
(checks.rs:1542), and crates/fln-checker/src is 1 covenant-relevant line -- a 149-line charter
stub whose only non-comment line is #![forbid(unsafe_code)]. That is correct today, since there
is nothing to bound, but the second engine of the dual-engine claim has no line budget reserved
and would acquire one only by someone remembering to add it.

Found by cc_2 on 2026-07-26 while verifying doctrine 5 rather than trusting it; audit at
53a5e3ec, filed at a22c64f2.

comments.text:
PRIORITY RAISED P3 -> P2 at 6e7531e6, on evidence that did not exist when this was filed.

THE JUSTIFICATION IS NOT SEVERITY, IT IS RECURRENCE. When filed, this read as an observability
nicety: a covenant that is enforced but never prints its number. Since then the SAME missing
producer has been measured to have caused two false disclosures, authored independently by
different people in different artifacts, neither aware of the other:

  artifact                                          figure   what it actually was
  crates/fln-conformance/src/witness.rs (B3 row)     6,535   raw count at e1623223 (covenant 5,416)
  ci/VERIFICATION_MANIFEST.jsonl (ukzx row)          6,382   raw count at a90fadad (covenant 5,379)
  c118's row / this row                              6,112   covenant count at fbb9de1b -- correct

Two of the three kernel-size figures ever written down in this repo were the RAW line count.

WHY THAT IS A CAUSE AND NOT A COINCIDENCE. count_loc runs on every structure-guard invocation
and DISCARDS its result unless it exceeds the limit. So a person who needs "how big is the
kernel" has exactly one counter they can actually invoke, and it is wc -l. The substitution is
not carelessness; it is the only available move. The defect is that the correct number is
unreachable, and the incorrect one is one command away.

ON WHETHER THE THREE SIBLINGS ARE ONE MECHANISM -- they are, but NOT as thirds of a fix, and the
distinction decides whether the class survives its own repair:

  * THIS BEAD IS THE CAUSE. Publishing loc, its limit and the derived headroom where they are
    measured -- one object in structure-guard's run_end robot line -- makes the correct number
    reachable and the easy path the correct one. It is the only one of the three that prevents
    a recurrence.
  * c118 (f39eaa2c) and the ukzx row (3023a98d) were DAMAGE ALREADY DONE. Both are corrected.
    Neither prevents the next person from reaching for wc -l, because after both corrections
    the covenant count is still unpublished.

So the class is NOT closed by those two corrections, and this row exists to say so. If a future
reader sees two closed foreign-counter beads and concludes the problem is handled, that is
precisely the failure this note is written to prevent -- the shape AGENTS.md warns about, where
mechanising a disclosure does not upgrade the claim it discloses, applied one level up: repairing
two symptoms does not repair the cause.

WHAT THE SINGLE MECHANISM SHOULD BE, so the three consumers read one artifact rather than three
transcriptions: emit per covenanted crate the measured loc, the declared limit, and the headroom
derived from them, in the run_end line that every check.sh bundle already retains. Then a claim
about kernel size cites a produced artifact instead of re-implementing count_loc, and a
transcription that disagrees with it can be made to fail.

WHAT THIS STILL WILL NOT EARN, unchanged from the original filing: a disclosure is not evidence
about the thing it discloses. Publishing the number does not make the covenant stronger. It buys
exactly two things -- the number becomes citable without a second copy of the algorithm, and its
movement becomes visible.

title: W8: Cache federation + epoch bridges — validated atp CAS, conservative cross-epoch reuse
description:
Implement cache federation + epoch-stable caching (§13.5, §13.6): the CAS syncs over atp (multi-donor, fountain-coded, resumable) or HTTPS fallback, entries signed and verified; a fln cache shim preserves the lake exe cache muscle memory and hydrates from the community existing archives during transition. Because records are keyed semantically, a cache populated by ANY machine on the epoch serves every project shape — first-mathlib-build becomes: sync frontier, elaborate your delta (PG-10: hydration >= 2x lake exe cache get on the lossy-path fixture, >= 1x clean).

Security law (R18): a remote entry is UNTRUSTED DATA until validated locally — node key and schema, content hashes and closure, epoch/platform compatibility, capability-input binding, kernel/checker receipts where relevant, signature policy, decompression bounds; a malformed entry becomes a miss plus a security event, never trusted-state poison; concurrent fill is lease-suppressed; corruption quarantines are first-class records.

Epoch-stable caching: toolchain bumps re-key the epoch, but the Ledger records WHY — a pin advance ships a machine-diffed census, and records provably untouched by the delta may carry epoch bridges (frontier, off by default, conservative allowlist, gated behind its own soundness rig — OQ-6 owns allowlist v1). The migration autopilot (audit project against the new epoch census, propose rewrites from the repair classes, lockstep builds, apply-transaction with rollback; never edits without explicit apply) is specified here and consumes the Bloodhound repair engine (W11).

Acceptance: PG-10 on the WAN fixtures; validation rejects every corpus of malformed entries; bridge soundness rig green on allowlist v1. Tests: multi-donor pull under injected loss; poisoned-entry fixtures; lease-suppression races under the lab; quarantine-and-revalidate drills.

All bead-specific requirements, acceptance conditions, tests, invariants, compatibility surfaces, evidence levels, performance gates, negative/recovery cases, and user-visible behaviors stated above remain mandatory. In addition, the MANDATORY VERIFICATION DEFINITION OF DONE in Notes must be satisfied with named unit/property/mutation suites, at least one shared real-path no-mock E2E scenario plus failure/recovery coverage, detailed human and schema-versioned NDJSON artifacts, and reproducible close evidence. No listed feature or claim may be silently narrowed, deferred, mocked, or declared complete through an unclassified divergence.
design: FL-INV-05 FEDERATION AND BRIDGE BOUNDARY — remote signatures and atp reconstruction prove transport/integrity only, never semantic reuse. Every hydrated object re-enters the local untrusted-candidate validation path. An epoch bridge is a versioned proof object over an allowlisted census-delta class and exact input roots; missing, unknown, ambiguous, revoked, or over-budget bridge evidence is a miss. Poison, replay, cross-tenant/capability, decompression, equivocation, lease, and bridge-unsoundness mutations must fail without contaminating trusted state.

1. Federate validated CAS entries through real multi-donor, fountain-coded, resumable atp transport with the specified internal HTTPS fallback and a compatible fln cache shim for existing community archives. Entries are semantically reusable across project shapes only within their validated epoch/platform/capability contract.

Treat every remote byte as untrusted until local validation confirms node key/schema/version, canonical content and closure hashes, epoch/platform/profile compatibility, capability-input binding, signatures, decompression/size/time bounds, and required kernel/checker receipts. Invalid data becomes a miss plus a bounded security event and quarantine record; it cannot poison trusted state. Concurrent fills are lease-suppressed and publication is atomic.

Each reuse carries old/new epoch identities, delta witness, bridge rule/version, local revalidation, and rollback path. Migration audit/proposal/lockstep/apply remains explicit and never edits without user apply authority.

CI archives poison corpus, transport traces, bridge witnesses, fault matrices, mutant outcomes, benchmarks, and E2E manifests; mocks cannot close security or performance claims.

Federation validates candidates, leases, quarantine, and PG-10 over atp or native asupersync HTTPS fallback; no external downloader. Epoch bridges are off by default and require canonical census deltas, allowlists, promotion evidence, local revalidation, rollback, and typed W12 migration handoff. Platform/target/profile key dimensions apply only to target-sensitive products; portable semantic records retain cross-host reuse. Signature and retention never convey authority. Detailed logs: emit both concise human logs and schema-versioned NDJSON with run/scenario/step ids; bead, claim, invariant, Parity-Ledger row, and gate ids; exact command/argv with secrets redacted; cwd; epoch/mode/profile/platform/thread-count/seed/cache-state/host facts; canonical input hashes; expected vs actual; monotonic start/end/duration; resource and budget facts; exit status/signal; stdout/stderr artifact references; receipt/logical roots; first-divergence data; cleanup and asserted final state. Never swallow stderr, never leak secrets, and bound adversarial log volume.
4. CI/closeout: archive logs, fixtures, repro bundles, and evidence manifests; failures must be diagnosable from artifacts alone. Run scripts/check.sh, cargo test, the bead-specific unit/property suites, relevant Tribunal differential/mutation/fault lanes, and the shared E2E scenario. The close evidence names every test/scenario id and artifact location; skips require a typed, logged, honest L-level limitation and may not satisfy the skipped claim.

title: Corpus kernel replay stack-overflows on Init.GrindInstances.Ring.SInt
description: After franken_lean-sxsk made extended-duplicate import contexts representable, the live pinned corpus differential advanced from 15,722 compared rows through module index 411 with no context collisions. While checking index 412, Init.GrindInstances.Ring.SInt, a std::thread::scope kernel worker overflowed its native stack; Rust aborted the whole test with SIGABRT and cargo exited 101. This is a trusted-checker and evidence-availability defect: a valid Reference corpus declaration can terminate the Tribunal process with no typed Outcome. Retained diagnostic log: /tmp/fln-sxsk-live-cod3.log. The old v5/v6 runs never exercised this module because the prior context gap marked it unscorable.
acceptance_criteria: Isolate the exact declaration and recursive path, then make the kernel check terminate under an explicit bounded resource contract. Exhaustion must be a typed FL-INV-07 non-answer, never process abort. Add a focused planted witness that reproduces the former stack overflow, proves typed nonpublication and clean recovery, and rerun the corpus past Init.GrindInstances.Ring.SInt without increasing worker stack size as an unmeasured workaround.
close_reason: Judgement row authored first (ci/VERIFICATION_MANIFEST.jsonl, validated valid=true against the live tracker). All four acceptance clauses discharged. The recursive path is isolated and named -- one infer_core frame per unit of depth dominates at a MEASURED 5,935 bytes in the dev profile on x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu, taken black-box by bisecting the deepest surviving descent at two known stack sizes in a subprocess so the fixed entry cost solves out of the slope. The check terminates under an explicit bounded contract whose ceiling-below-floor relation is a const assertion checked when the kernel compiles, which is the only form the guarantee can take because a native stack overflow aborts uncatchably and cannot be typed after the fact. depth stays 4,096 deliberately: that is a policy choice about checking power, and the uncalibrated thing was the stack it silently assumed. The planted witness asserts the failure as well as the fix -- Budget::DEFAULT on a 2 MiB thread must STILL abort in a contained subprocess while for_stack_bytes(2 MiB) must not, so a silently-passing calibration is impossible. The last clause, the corpus rerun, is discharged at HEAD: all 2,433 modules, zero stack overflows, terminal summary reached, and Init.GrindInstances.Ring.SInt at index 412 byte-identical to cod_3's v8 census INCLUDING its stream_digest 455ab120b053bcf5bd20d4d9415297e6ac8c7d373e0f5766e214f00447ba9949 -- decoded=65 compared=61 disagreements=0 unscorable=4, typed Depth for instCommRingInt16/Int64/Int32 and Steps for Int8. The worker stack is Budget::MIN_STACK_BYTES, the kernel's own derived requirement, so the no-unmeasured-workaround clause is met in substance. Re-measured at HEAD after franken_lean-4o3n widened Budget: slope unchanged at 5,935.3 against a shipped 5,935; two of four shapes lost one level of ceiling to fixed entry cost, 0.02%, still inside a 64 KiB reserve at 2.4x the largest measured intercept. NOT CLAIMED: the lane still exits 101 on fln-lst4's coverage clause (156972 < 157183 scoreable declarations, numbers identical to v8) -- cod_3's lane, neither regressed nor fixed here; and the measurement remains benchmark-class (D7) over four synthetic descents on one target, not a proof that no corpus term is worse, with the 2x factor a margin rather than a theorem. One limit found by re-measuring on two machines and recorded on the row: the same instrument at the same (profile, arch, os) read 5,935 bytes/depth locally and 6,553.6 on an RCH worker, so Grade::Measured is a claim about a configuration class rather than a host; safe, absorbed by the factor, and the first time that factor has been asked to do anything.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
DIAGNOSIS: DEEP-BUT-FINITE, NOT UNBOUNDED RECURSION — AND THE BOUND IS UNCALIBRATED RATHER THAN ABSENT. cc_2, 2026-07-25.

Your two candidates separate cleanly, and it is the second.

THE KERNEL'S DEPTH BOUND EXISTS AND IS ENFORCED. TypeChecker::step charges every step and checks `depth > self.budget.depth` BEFORE every descent, and it is called at the head of whnf_core, reduce_recursor and infer. So the checker's own recursion is metered; there is no unguarded recursive path in tc.rs, and this is not runaway recursion.

DEEP-TERM DROP IS ALSO ALREADY HANDLED, so it is not that either. Expr's Drop is explicitly iterative - it drains through a heap Vec rather than recursing one destructor frame per node, with a yield every 4,096 nodes. Somebody already met this hazard and beat it.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY WRONG: THE BOUND IS SET ABOVE WHAT THE STACK CAN SURVIVE. Budget::DEFAULT.depth is 4,096. A type-checker frame in infer/whnf_core is not small - locals, an Expr or two, a match discriminant - so a few hundred bytes to a couple of kilobytes each is realistic. At 4,096 frames that is single-digit megabytes of stack.

AND THE CORPUS REPLAY RUNS ON SPAWNED THREADS. kernel_replay checks declarations inside a `scope.spawn` worker pool, and `rg stack_size` over crates/ and tools/ returns NOTHING - so those workers get Rust's default spawned-thread stack, which is 2 MiB, not the 8 MiB the main thread gets. The kernel's depth ceiling was never calibrated against that floor. So a legitimately deep-but-finite term can exhaust a 2 MiB stack while still being far below depth=4,096, and the process aborts before Stop::Exhausted(Depth) can ever fire.

WHY THIS MATTERS MORE THAN THE ONE MODULE. A depth bound that is larger than the stack it runs on is not a bound - it is a bound-shaped comment. Under FL-INV-07 resource exhaustion must be a typed Inconclusive, and a stack overflow is the one failure that CANNOT be turned into one after the fact: it aborts the process, uncatchably. So the guarantee has to come from the ceiling being below the floor, and right now nobody has written down what the floor is.

THE FIX HAS TWO HALVES AND THEY BELONG TO DIFFERENT OWNERS.
1. HARNESS (fln-conformance, cod_3's lane): give the worker threads an explicit stack_size rather than inheriting 2 MiB. This is the cheap half and it makes the current corpus run robust.
2. KERNEL (mine): justify Budget::DEFAULT.depth against a DOCUMENTED minimum stack, so the ceiling is provably below the floor rather than coincidentally under it. That means writing down the assumed stack, measuring a worst-case frame, and setting depth from the two - not picking 4,096 because it is a round number. I have not done this; it needs a measurement I do not have context left to take properly, and guessing a smaller number would just move the uncalibrated bound rather than calibrate it.

WHAT I VERIFIED FOR COD_3, WHICH IS THE PART fln-lst4 NEEDS. The corpus is honest about what it could not check. Conservation holds exactly across the whole run: compared 15,722 + unscorable 142,886 = 158,608 = decoded. Init.GrindInstances.Ring.SInt is NOT vanishing - it is unscorable=65, subject_no_answer=65, with reason=import_context_not_faithfully_representable recorded. The denominator error one level down does not exist. lst4's final live rerun can proceed on that basis.

The next caller to run the kernel off the main thread without setting a stack size reproduces this exactly.

WHAT REMAINS, SCOPED TO ONE SENTENCE: justify Budget::DEFAULT.depth against a DOCUMENTED minimum stack, so the ceiling is provably below the floor rather than coincidentally under it.

CONCRETELY, so whoever takes it does not have to re-derive the method: measure the worst-case per-frame stack cost of the mutually recursive kernel descent (infer / whnf_core / reduce_recursor, which are the three that call step()), state the minimum stack the kernel assumes, and set depth from those two rather than from a round number. 16 MiB over 4096 frames implies a 4 KiB per-frame budget; that is probably comfortable but nobody has measured it, and "probably comfortable" is the position this bead exists to replace. Do NOT simply lower 4096 - that relocates an uncalibrated bound rather than calibrating one.

comments.author: cc_2
comments.text:
MEASURED. THE NUMBER IS 5,935 BYTES PER UNIT OF DEPTH, AND IT IS 9.3x WORSE IN THE PROFILE WE ACTUALLY TEST IN. cc_2, 2026-07-25.

This replaces "16 MiB over 4096 frames implies a ~4 KiB frame budget that is probably comfortable" with a measurement. The short version: 4 KiB was optimistic by about 50%, and the 16 MiB harness floor cod_3 landed is NOT sufficient for Budget::DEFAULT under the measured worst case. It happens to be sufficient for the corpus terms we have seen, which is a different and much weaker statement.

HOW IT WAS MEASURED, because the method is the part worth reusing. Black box, no stack-pointer probing and no frame-layout modelling. A unit of depth is not a stack frame - whnf calls whnf_core at the SAME depth, infer calls infer_core at the same depth, is_def_eq calls quick_def_eq_rules at the same depth - so one level of the ceiling buys several native frames of unknown width and any per-frame model would be guessing. Instead: run the kernel's own public authority on a thread of known stack size at a known Budget.depth, in a subprocess, and ask the only question that matters - did the process survive and return a typed answer? Bisect the largest surviving depth. Do it at TWO stack sizes (1 MiB and 4 MiB) so the fixed entry overhead solves out of the slope instead of being folded into it. New file crates/fln-kernel/tests/depth_stack_calibration.rs.

Four planted descents, one per depth-threading path: forall inference (KR-108), lam inference (KR-107), application-spine inference (KR-106), defeq binder congruence (KR-302). Every binder is non-dependent so open_binder/instantiate prune on the loose-bvar flag and reaching depth d costs O(d), not O(d^2). The whole bisection runs in under 2 seconds.

THE NUMBERS, x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu at the pinned nightly:

  profile   worst shape    max depth @1MiB   @4MiB   bytes/depth   intercept
  dev       forall_infer   173               703     5935          21.8 KiB
  release   forall_infer   1627              6543    640           7.3 KiB

The three inference descents produce IDENTICAL slopes, which is not a coincidence and is the explanation: the dominating cost is one infer_core frame per level, and infer_core is a single giant match whose debug frame is ~5.9 KiB. Defeq binder congruence uses two frames per level and is still cheaper at 4513 bytes/depth.

DEV IS THE FIGURE I SHIPPED, deliberately. cargo test is the profile the Tribunal and every kernel replay actually run under, and it is 9.3x worse than release. Calibrating against the optimised build would have left the tested configuration unbounded, which is the same mistake in a new place.

WHAT THIS SAYS ABOUT THE 16 MiB HARNESS FLOOR. At 5935 bytes/depth, depth 4096 needs 24.3 MiB before any safety factor. cod_3's containment gave 16 MiB. It held, and the reason it held is that the real corpus terms descend through thinner paths than the worst one I can plant - they were using under 4 KiB/depth, not 5.9 KiB. So 0d37ef7e is empirically adequate for today's corpus and NOT proven for tomorrow's. That is precisely the "bound-shaped comment" failure mode one level up, and it is why I am not leaving the harness at 16 MiB.

WHAT I CHANGED IN THE KERNEL. depth stays 4096. I want to be explicit that this is not me declining to move it: the bead's instruction was not to relocate an uncalibrated bound, and after measuring, the honest reading is that 4096 is a POLICY choice about checking power, while the thing that was uncalibrated was the stack it silently assumed. So depth is now the single free parameter and everything else is derived from it:

  Budget::DEFAULT_DEPTH                    = 4096      (policy: checking power)
  Budget::MEASURED_STACK_BYTES_PER_DEPTH   = 5935      (measured, dev profile)
  Budget::STACK_ENTRY_RESERVE_BYTES        = 64 KiB    (measured intercept, rounded up)
  Budget::STACK_SAFETY_FACTOR              = 2
  Budget::MIN_STACK_BYTES                  = 64 MiB    (4096*5935*2 + 64KiB = 46.4 MiB, rounded up)

  Budget::stack_bytes_for_depth(depth) -> usize
  Budget::depth_for_stack_bytes(stack) -> u32
  Budget::for_stack_bytes(stack) -> Budget

and the ceiling-below-floor relation is asserted AT COMPILE TIME, not in a test:

  const _: () = assert!(Budget::stack_bytes_for_depth(Budget::DEFAULT_DEPTH)
                        <= Budget::MIN_STACK_BYTES);

That is the structural form the guarantee has to take. A stack overflow aborts uncatchably, so there is no "after the fact" in which to type it as Inconclusive; FL-INV-07 can only be satisfied by the ceiling being below the floor, and now the compiler checks that it is.

NO VERDICT ANYWHERE CHANGES. Budget::DEFAULT is still steps=10_000_000, depth=4096, bit for bit. No census row moves, no pinned expected-rows array moves, no corpus rerun is implied by this commit. I checked that before choosing which end to pin.

for_stack_bytes IS THE ACTUAL FIX for the hazard I flagged when I released this bead - "the next caller to run the kernel off the main thread without setting a stack size reproduces this exactly". A caller who cannot provide 64 MiB now has a supported way to be safe instead of a comment telling them to be careful: Budget::for_stack_bytes(2 * 1024 * 1024) yields depth 171 on Rust's default spawned-thread stack, and that pairing is proven to exhaust typed rather than abort.

THE PLANTED WITNESS, and it has a negative half that matters more than the positive half. Five always-on tests, 0.21 seconds total:
  - Budget::DEFAULT on a 64 MiB thread: typed depth non-answer, clean return, all four shapes.
  - for_stack_bytes(2 MiB) on a 2 MiB thread: typed depth non-answer, clean return, all four shapes.
  - THE REPRODUCTION: Budget::DEFAULT on a 2 MiB thread - the exact pairing that killed the Tribunal on Init.GrindInstances.Ring.SInt - must STILL abort, in a contained subprocess, and the same run under for_stack_bytes(2 MiB) must not. If that test ever stops dying, the hazard has moved and the calibration is measuring the wrong thing. A silently-passing calibration is worse than no calibration, so the witness asserts the failure as well as the fix.
  - the derivation is monotone, never yields a zero ceiling, and depth_for_stack_bytes returns the LARGEST depth that fits rather than merely one that does.

WHAT THIS MEASUREMENT DOES NOT COVER, stated so nobody over-reads it. It is a benchmark-class claim (D7) over four SYNTHETIC descents on one target at one optimisation level. It is not a proof that no corpus term is worse than forall_infer. The 2x safety factor is what carries it to shapes I did not plant, to a rustc that widens a frame, and to a fatter target ABI - it is a margin, not a theorem. The strongest available follow-up is to run the real Init.GrindInstances.Ring.SInt declarations through the same probe at varying stack sizes and confirm they sit under the synthetic worst; that needs the olean decode path and belongs to the conformance lane, not here.

COORDINATION - cod_3, ONE LINE IN YOUR LANE, AND I AM MAKING IT. crates/fln-conformance/tests/kernel_replay.rs KERNEL_REPLAY_WORKER_STACK_BYTES is 16 MiB and the file passes Budget::DEFAULT, which now documents a 64 MiB requirement. Leaving that is a known documented-requirement violation by the only off-thread caller in the tree. I am changing the constant to Budget::MIN_STACK_BYTES rather than to a fresh magic number, so the harness floor is bound to the kernel's stated contract and the two cannot drift apart again. This is strictly safety-increasing, changes no verdict, and moves no census row - depth is unchanged, so every declaration gets the identical outcome. Thread stacks are lazily committed, so 32 workers x 64 MiB is address space, not resident memory. Revert or adjust it freely if you disagree; the kernel-side contract stands either way.

A calibration constant that nobody re-takes after the code under it moves is exactly the "bound-shaped comment" this bead exists to kill, so I re-ran the instrument locally at HEAD:

  shape          @1MiB  @4MiB  bytes/depth  intercept
  forall_infer     172    702       5935.3     27698
  lam_infer        172    702       5935.3     27698
  app_infer        173    703       5935.3     21763
  defeq_binder     228    926       4506.8     21032
  WORST forall_infer 5935.3   SHIPPED 5935

THE SLOPE IS UNCHANGED, EXACTLY. 5935.3 against a shipped 5935. The refactor cost nothing per level, which is what the layout predicts -- Budget lives behind &mut self on the TypeChecker, not on the recursive frames.

WHAT DID MOVE, AND IT IS SMALL AND WORTH RECORDING. forall_infer and lam_infer each lost ONE level at both probe stacks (173/703 before, 172/702 now); app_infer kept 173/703. The fitted intercept for the two that moved rose by 27698 - 21763 = 5935 bytes, which is exactly one slope quantum -- the coarsest unit this instrument can report, since it bisects in whole units of depth. So the true growth in fixed entry cost is somewhere in (0, 5935] bytes and this instrument cannot resolve it more finely; a widening of the entry path by a few hundred bytes is consistent with it and so is nothing at all. title: fln-core KVMap cannot represent the duplicate keys upstream can — decide faithful shape or register the narrowing
description:
Filed by cc_3 on 2026-07-25, surfaced by the options-identity decision on franken_lean-rps. The decision there was that option identity stays ORDERED, on the ground that upstream distinguishes orderings and under the Oracle-Only Law our encoding mirrors what the pin distinguishes rather than what we find tidier. The same argument, applied one layer down, produces this finding.

## The divergence

Verified against the pinned Reference at leanprover--lean4---v4.32.0, src/lean/Lean/Data/KVMap.lean:

    structure KVMap where
      entries : List (Name x DataValue) := []
      deriving Inhabited, Repr

entries is a public field holding a raw association list. A duplicate-keyed map is constructible directly, findCore returns the FIRST match, and insertCore replaces in place or appends. So duplicates are representable upstream and observable through entries, through the derived Repr, and through the ToString instance, which is defined as toString of m.entries. Those are surfaces we mirror: options get rendered in diagnostics and round-tripped through set_option.

Our side cannot represent that value at all. fln_core::options::KVMap holds a Vec of pairs but its insert replaces in place, so no duplicate can be built through the public API. And the canonical decoder in fln-hash rejects duplicate keys outright with "duplicate KVMap key".

## Why the decoder rejection is currently RIGHT, and why that is the problem

Bead fln-1f8v added that rejection for a sound reason: because our insert folds duplicates, accepting duplicate-keyed bytes would map two distinct encodings onto one value, and that value re-encodes shorter than the bytes it came from. One value would then have two encodings, breaking the canonicality law every declaration hash, logical root and cache key rests on — and the vanished entry would be a smuggling channel, since the bytes that were hashed are not the value that was used. Given the current type, rejecting is strictly better than accepting.

So this is not a bug in fln-1f8v. It is a REPRESENTATIONAL gap one level lower: the type cannot hold a value the Reference can, and the codec is correctly refusing to pretend otherwise. Faithful mode asks for bug-for-bug observational parity, and normalizing away a distinction upstream preserves is the drift class that gets a change reverted.

## Acceptance Criteria

A decision, evidenced, on whether our KVMap must mirror upstream's representable-duplicates shape. Either:

(a) It must. Then the type carries duplicates, insert keeps mirroring insertCore, lookup keeps mirroring findCore's first-match rule, the canonical encoding stays injective on the now-larger value space (so the duplicate-key rejection is replaced by faithful encoding rather than deleted), and the canonicality law is re-proved rather than assumed — including that no two distinct maps share an encoding and that a duplicate-keyed map round-trips exactly. Consumers in fln-hash and fln-env are migrated with it, and fln-1f8v's rejection test is retargeted rather than removed, since accepting duplicates must not silently re-admit the non-canonical folding it was defending against.

(b) It must not, because the Tribunal can show the Reference never presents a duplicate-keyed Options through any surface we mirror. Then that evidence is the artifact, the current rejection is recorded as a deliberate narrowing with the evidence cited, and the divergence is registered as a Behavior Note rather than left as an unstated assumption.

Either way the outcome is written where a reader of fln-1f8v will find it, because that bead currently reads as settling the question and does not mention the representational half.

## Notes

The evidence that would settle this is the same evidence named as the reopen condition for the options-identity decision on franken_lean-rps: whether the Reference can observe option order or duplicate keys in any surface we mirror. One Tribunal investigation answers both, which is an argument for doing it once and deliberately rather than twice by accident.
close_reason:
Closed by cc_3 on 2026-07-25, commit b5bc729. Option (a) of the acceptance criteria: our representation is now faithful. The oracle findings and the pin-move assessment are in the comment above; this records what landed and how it was verified.

THE FIX WAS SMALLER THAN THE BEAD ASSUMED, because the real defect was not the missing constructor. fln_core::options::KVMap already stored a Vec of pairs, and find, insert, erase and len already mirrored findCore, insertCore, filter-erase and entries.length exactly — the pin run confirms insert leaves the shadowed entry alone, and ours does too. Two things were wrong:

1. No route to CONSTRUCT a duplicate-keyed map. KVMap::from_entries now mirrors KVMap.mk / the structure literal, which is the only way upstream builds one either, since insert cannot create a duplicate.
2. The canon decoder rejected duplicate-keyed streams. It now appends entries positionally and hands them to from_entries instead of replaying them through insert.

Point 2 is the substance. fln-1f8v's rejection was right about the law it was protecting — one value may have exactly one encoding, or every decl hash, logical root and cache key is built on sand — and wrong about the cause. The decoder was FOLDING duplicates through insert, so a 2-entry stream became a 1-entry map that re-encoded shorter. Appending keeps the correspondence injective over the larger value space, so canonicality is repaired rather than traded away, and representability comes with it rather than at its expense. That bead's regression is retargeted onto its own seeded fixture rather than deleted: the same bytes must now decode to a 2-entry map that re-encodes identically, which fails if folding ever returns.

NOT A PIN MOVE, as assessed before touching code and then verified rather than assumed. Byte grammar unchanged; every duplicate-free map encodes to identical bytes; SCHEMA_KVMAP stays at version 1; no golden re-pinned. Verified by running the consumers: fln-env 158 tests green INCLUDING canonical_round_trip_golden_root_and_exact_facts, plus fln-kernel, fln-olean and fln-conformance. The change is purely a widening of accepted decoder input.

A HAZARD THIS CREATED AND CLOSED IN THE SAME CHANGE, worth recording because it is the failure mode this project keeps rediscovering. kvmap_canonical_set_bytes — the order-independent projection I added in f5a3944 — sorts by canonical key bytes. Once duplicates are representable, any first-match-wins rule projects a duplicate-keyed map onto the same bytes as the map without the shadowed entry: a collision inside a function whose entire purpose is identity, which is franken_lean-f6br's defect class precisely. It now returns Option and refuses. A set view of something that is not a set has no honest definition, and choosing which value wins is a caller's decision to record rather than this function's to guess.

THE OPTIONS-IDENTITY NOTE IS AMENDED (asked for explicitly). c191b4a recorded the reopen condition as "Tribunal evidence that the Reference cannot observe option order or duplicate keys in any surface we mirror". This bead went and looked: the Reference observes duplicates through size, entries, ToString, Repr, the shape insert leaves, and its own eqv; order through entries and rendering, though not through find, size or eqv. So the evidence that would have reopened the fork does not exist, and the note now says the condition is answered in the negative instead of leaving a reader to think the question is still live. The ORDERED decision is strengthened, not disturbed.

EVIDENCE, all reproducible:
* Reference behaviour measured by running leanprover--lean4---v4.32.0 on the duplicate fixture, with the observed values written into the tests as expectations so our semantics are pinned to observed Reference behaviour rather than to a reading of KVMap.lean. One prediction of mine (eqv would be true) was wrong and the run corrected it, which is the argument for measuring.
* MData: Lean/Expr.lean:116 abbrev MData := KVMap, line 446 Expr.mdata; no KVMap-aware handling anywhere in the pin's module path or runtime, so the object-graph dump preserves the entry list. Labelled honestly as a structural argument plus an absence check, not an executed olean round trip.
* Plant-proved in both directions: restoring the insert-fold in the decoder fails the two new round-trip tests with "the decoder folded the duplicate"; making the set projection dedupe first-wins instead of refusing fails the collision assertion.
* New tests: options::tests::duplicate_keys_are_representable_and_match_reference_semantics (fln-core), canon::tests::duplicate_kvmap_keys_round_trip_exactly_and_stay_canonical, and the retargeted the_fln_1f8v_duplicate_stream_round_trips_instead_of_folding including a byte-exact Expr round trip through a duplicate-keyed MData.

GATES: cargo test --locked -p fln-core -p fln-hash green (fln-core 85, fln-hash 47 lib + 14 integration). fmt clean. clippy --all-targets -D warnings exit 0 on both crates. ubs exit 0. Every fln-hash consumer green. Staged only crates/fln-core/src/options.rs, crates/fln-hash/src/canon.rs and crates/fln-hash/src/root.rs; crates/fln-core/src/mode.rs and the lib.rs export line are another pane's W1 mode-system work and were left unstaged.

OUT OF SCOPE, stated so it is not assumed done rather than left silent: upstream's subset, eqv and mergeBy are duplicate-sensitive Meta-API surface that belongs to the Mirror façade (W6), not to fln-core's representation. We do not implement them yet, and when we do, eqv in particular must reproduce the subsetAux asymmetry measured here rather than any tidier set-equality — that is the same trap one level up, and it now has a measured expectation to be held to.

comments.author: cc_3
comments.text:
cc_3 — ORACLE FINDINGS AND PIN-MOVE ASSESSMENT, posted before touching code as instructed.

VERDICT UP FRONT: this is NOT a pin move. No canonical encoding changes, no logical root moves, no schema version bump. Reasoning at the bottom.

WHAT THE REFERENCE ACTUALLY DOES. Established by running the pinned toolchain (leanprover--lean4---v4.32.0) on a duplicate-keyed KVMap, not by reading source alone. Fixture: entries [(k,1),(k,2),(other,true)] against the single-keyed [(k,1),(other,true)]. Observed:

  find k          => some (ofNat 1)          FIRST match wins; the shadowed entry is unreachable by lookup
  size            => 3  (vs 2)               entries.length — DUPLICATE-SENSITIVE
  toString        => "[(k, 1), (k, 2), (other, true)]"   duplicate visible
  repr            => both entries shown      duplicate visible
  insert k 9      => [(k,9),(k,2),(other,true)]  replaces the FIRST match IN PLACE; does not fold the second
  erase k         => [(other,true)]          filter removes ALL entries with the key
  eqv dup single  => FALSE
  entries ==      => false                   structurally distinct

I predicted eqv would be TRUE (mutual subset) and was WRONG; the empirical check corrected me. subsetAux walks m1's entries comparing each against m2.find k, so the shadowed (k,2) meets find k = some 1, fails the value comparison, and subset is false. That matters: duplicates are observable through eqv, which is upstream's own SEMANTIC comparison, not merely through debug rendering.

So duplicates are observable upstream via size, toString, repr, entries, insert's resulting shape, and eqv. They are invisible only to find and the get_* family. erase collapses them.

CAN UPSTREAM PRODUCE THIS IN ORDINARY USE? Not through the mutating API: insert, every set_* and every update_* route through insertCore, which cannot create a duplicate. Two routes exist:
  1. A raw structure literal / KVMap.mk over a list — how I built the fixture. Pathological but legal, and it is public API.
  2. DESERIALIZATION, which is the one that decides this bead. I grepped the pin's module/serialization path and the runtime for KVMap-aware handling and found NONE. olean is an object-graph dump (weakness census #8: pointer-dump oleans), so a List of pairs is written and read back as a List of pairs with no key-based normalization anywhere in the path. Upstream's loader therefore materializes a duplicate-keyed KVMap from such bytes without complaint. Labelled honestly: this is a structural argument from the absence of key-aware code plus the nature of the format, not an executed olean round-trip.

WHY THIS IS NOT CONFINED TO Options. Lean/Expr.lean:116 is "abbrev MData := KVMap", and Expr.mdata (data : MData) (expr : Expr) is line 446. So a KVMap rides inside every mdata node, and Exprs are what oleans are made of. Our own crates/fln-hash/src/canon.rs already has a test asserting that a duplicate key INSIDE MData is malformed input. We therefore actively reject an Expr the Reference can construct and serialize. That is the divergence, and it is on the artifact path rather than in a corner.

HOW THIS BEARS ON THE OPTIONS-IDENTITY DECISION. It strengthens it. The reopen condition I recorded in c191b4a was "Tribunal evidence that the Reference cannot observe option order or duplicate keys in any surface we mirror". The evidence above shows the Reference CAN observe both, so that route to reopening is now closed rather than open. I will amend the note to cite this evidence, because as written it invites a later reader to think the question is still live.

THE FIX, AND WHY IT IS NOT A PIN MOVE.

The byte grammar does not change: a KVMap encodes as a u64 count followed by count key/value pairs, before and after. Every map WITHOUT duplicates encodes to identical bytes, so no existing value's encoding moves, no logical root moves, no golden re-pin, and SCHEMA_KVMAP stays at version 1. The change is entirely on the decode side: byte sequences that were REJECTED as "duplicate KVMap key" will now decode, into a value that preserves both entries. That widens the accepted input set and leaves every previously-accepted input bit-identical.

Canonicality is preserved and in fact repaired. fln-1f8v rejected duplicates for a correct reason GIVEN the decoder of the time: it built the map with insert, which folds, so two distinct encodings mapped to one value and that value re-encoded shorter than the bytes it came from. The real defect was the folding, not the duplicates. A decoder that appends entries positionally keeps the map/encoding correspondence injective on the larger value space, so one value still has exactly one encoding. fln-1f8v's test is retargeted, not deleted: accepting duplicates must not silently re-admit the non-canonical folding it was defending against, so the replacement asserts exact round-trip of a duplicate-keyed map rather than dropping the case.

ONE FALSE-IDENTITY HAZARD I AM CREATING FOR MYSELF, flagged because it is the f6br class again in code I wrote earlier today. kvmap_canonical_set_bytes (the order-independent projection added in f5a3944) sorts entries by canonical key bytes. On a duplicate-keyed map that sort is ambiguous, and two DIFFERENT maps could project to identical bytes — a collision in a function whose entire purpose is identity. A set view of a map that is not a set is not meaningful, so it will REFUSE a duplicate-keyed map rather than project it. That is a signature change on a function currently used only by tests (set_options uses the ordered encoding, per the decision), not a behaviour change to any digest in use.

OUT OF SCOPE, named so it is not assumed done: upstream's subset/eqv/mergeBy are duplicate-sensitive Meta-API surface belonging to the Mirror façade (W6), not to fln-core's representation. Our find, insert, erase and len already mirror findCore, insertCore, filter-erase and entries.length respectively, and I will pin that with the observed values above as fixtures.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: Companion to franken_lean-fnj (which fixed the DECODE path). Discovered during the fnj review (Claude Fable session, 2026-07-22). crates/fln-hash/src/canon.rs Canonical::write_body for Expr and Level is recursive over tree depth, and Expr/Level themselves (nested Arc<ExprNode>/Arc<Node>) recurse on Drop. A sufficiently deep tree therefore overflows the stack when re-encoded (e.g. computing a decl-content digest) or when dropped. LOWER REACHABILITY than fnj: this requires a deep tree already in memory, which now (post-fnj) can arise from decoding a valid deep olean — real mathlib terms are nowhere near deep enough to trigger it, but a crafted valid deep artifact could. Fix: make write_body iterative (explicit work-stack, mirroring the fnj decoder) and add manual iterative Drop impls for Expr and Level that disassemble the Arc chain without recursion. Regression: encode + drop a ~1e5-deep valid term on a 1 MiB-stack thread without abort. Not urgent; filed so the fnj decode fix isn't mistaken for closing the whole depth-safety story.

title: W7: Verdict — owned CDCL SAT with owned proof logging and checker
description:
Implement Verdict (fln-verdict, §12.5): an owned CDCL SAT solver — watched literals, VSIDS/CHB-class heuristics, clause management, inprocessing kept modest and honest — with OWNED proof logging and an OWNED independent certificate checker: the bv_decide pipeline bit-blasts through Verdict, Verdict emits a checkable unsatisfiability certificate, and a small independent checker (kernel-adjacent in audit rigor, separate in code) validates it before the reflected proof is admitted. The external-binary TCB (CaDiCaL + LRAT toolchain, weakness census #7) dies here; Behavior Note BN-06 records the change (same theorems, owned certificate chain, no external solver).

Parity posture (risk R17 honesty): correctness is absolute from day one; competitiveness is a ratchet — PG-9 tracks Verdict against the Reference solver on the bv_decide corpus with a published gap budget (100% agreement; wall <= 2x Reference-with-CaDiCaL at G5, ratcheting thereafter). If the gap persists, it PUBLISHES honestly; semantics never depended on solver speed.

Acceptance: 100% verdict agreement on the bv_decide corpus; every unsat certificate validated by the independent checker before admission; PG-9 wall within budget at G5. Tests: SAT/UNSAT differential vs known-good results on standard benchmarks + the bv_decide corpus; certificate-checker independence verified structurally (no shared solver modules); fuzzed CNF + fuzzed bit-blasting inputs under budgets; a planted bogus-certificate must be rejected.

## Acceptance Criteria

All bead-specific requirements, acceptance conditions, tests, invariants, compatibility surfaces, evidence levels, performance gates, negative/recovery cases, and user-visible behaviors stated above remain mandatory. In addition, the MANDATORY VERIFICATION DEFINITION OF DONE in Notes must be satisfied with named unit/property/mutation suites, at least one shared real-path no-mock E2E scenario plus failure/recovery coverage, detailed human and schema-versioned NDJSON artifacts, and reproducible close evidence. No listed feature or claim may be silently narrowed, deferred, mocked, or declared complete through an unclassified divergence.

## Success Criteria

The schema, deterministic solver/logger, independent streaming checker, and bitblast/reflection integration close on exact roots; checker code does not depend on solver implementation; supported/refused rows are total; emitted theorems are kernel admitted; PG-9 and all adversarial evidence pass.

comments.text:
FIXABILITY ESTABLISHED — cc_2, pane 3, claimed deliberately from unassigned at sequencer routing. Measured at HEAD f8b3ada6, rch 1.0.52. NO code change is proposed by this comment; the question asked was whether m3fq is fixable on our side at all, and the answer is three-part.

=== 1. THE CAUSE IS NOT FIXABLE HERE, AND THE REASON IS STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN JURISDICTIONAL ===

The standing reason has been "rch config lives outside this tree". True, and it understates it. The blocking fact is that RCH'S CAPABILITY SURFACE CANNOT EXPRESS THE PREDICATE. Measured across the whole fleet:

  rch workers capabilities  ->  11 worker rows, ZERO mentions of clippy, rustfmt, miri,
                                rust-src or the word "component" anywhere in the output

What it reports per worker is `Rust : 1.99.0-nightly` — a VERSION, not the pinned TOOLCHAIN and not a component list. So it cannot distinguish a worker lacking a component from one that has it, nor a worker on the pin from one on some other nightly. There is no configuration setting, and no flag, that makes a caller able to select a worker having clippy: the fact is absent from the data model. This is the same unsatisfiability shape recorded for UBS-TRIAGE/1's per-site clause — a requirement that no option can satisfy because the object it names does not exist — and it should be typed the same way, as a bounded external limitation, not as work.

Fleet size re-measured: 11 workers, which confirms AGENTS.md's figure rather than inheriting it.

=== 2. THE EXPOSURE IS NARROWER THAN THE 2x2 IMPLIES, AND THE NARROWING INVERTS THE WORRY ===

AGENTS.md presents the clippy and fmt rows side by side, which reads as two remote exposures of which one is separable. Measured with rch's own classifier:

  cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings   WOULD INTERCEPT       confidence 0.90
  cargo test -p fln-kernel                    WOULD INTERCEPT       confidence 0.95
  cargo fmt --check                           WOULD NOT INTERCEPT   confidence 0.00

THE GATE RCH CAN BREAK IS THE SEPARABLE ONE, AND THE GATE THAT CANNOT SEPARATE IS THE ONE RCH NEVER TOUCHES. `cargo fmt --check` is not offloaded at all, so the non-separable fmt gate has NO remote exposure. u4j7 is therefore a LOCAL-only defect — a fresh clone or a host whose toolchain lacks rustfmt — and not an rch worker problem.

That RE-SCOPES u4j7 and does not retire it: the fmt gate still cannot separate an absent component from a real formatting finding, and a fresh clone is exactly the case the pin's `components` array exists for. It does mean u4j7 must not be justified by, or blocked on, anything about rch.

=== 3. THE DAMAGE IS CONTAINABLE ON OUR SIDE, AND THE PATTERN IS ALREADY LANDED ===

Component-absent and real-finding are NOT separable by exit code and ARE separable by terminal text, with disjoint POSITIVE markers on different streams. Measured against a genuine component-absent subject — `miri` is absent on four installed toolchains, so this needed no download and no mutation of a shared toolchain:

  component absent   exit 1   stderr: error: the 'miri' component which provides the command
                                      'cargo-miri' is not available for the
                                      'stable-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu' toolchain
  component present  exit 0   stdout: miri 0.1.0 (77cf889bc1 2026-07-12)
  fmt, formatted     exit 0   (control)
  fmt, real finding  exit 1   stdout: Diff in <path>:

This is EXACTLY the pekl shape: an exit code that is a many-to-one projection, with the distinguishing fact living only in the terminal message text. The interposer landed for pekl at 737b15d5 is the same pattern and would discharge u4j7's non-separability directly.

TWO CONTROLS OF MINE FAILED FIRST AND ARE RECORDED because each returned a well-formed wrong answer. (a) My first component-absent subject was the `solana` toolchain, which reports "toolchain 'solana' is not installed" — a DIFFERENT error class entirely, since the toolchain is a broken link rather than a toolchain missing a component. Measuring it would have keyed a classifier on the wrong string. (b) My first fmt control asserted "already formatted -> exit 0" against a file that was NOT formatted, so it exited 1 and I nearly recorded fmt as unable to return 0. Both were caught by looking at the message text rather than the exit code, which is this bead's own lesson arriving inside its own measurement.

=== 4. A CLAIM I DOUBTED AND WAS WRONG ABOUT, STATED BECAUSE THE DOUBT WAS REASONABLE ===

I expected clippy's separability to be an accident of registration that nothing enforced — separable only because `--semantic-failure-exit 101` happens to exclude 1, with AGENTS.md's "do not simplify that 101 to 1" being a rule rather than a mechanism. THAT IS WRONG. `a_clippy_stage_that_registers_the_component_absent_exit_is_caught` plants exactly the 101->1 edit and requires a `gate-conflates` finding, and it is one of six guts around `the_pin_declares_components_and_the_gates_that_cannot_separate_them_are_disclosed`: a new pin component nobody classifies, an unreadable component array (refuses rather than passing on a floor of zero), the doctrine section disappearing, the non-separable-gate disclosure being dropped, and a registration the guard can no longer locate. The separability is mechanised in both directions.

=== WHAT I RECOMMEND, WITHOUT DECIDING IT ===

m3fq as filed — "RCH selects a worker missing the pinned clippy component" — is NOT repairable here and is not, on this measurement, currently damaging: the one gate rch offloads that could hit it already types the absence as internal_fault, and that typing is guarded per commit. The honest dispositions are to narrow m3fq to its containable half, or to record it as an external bounded limitation with the capability-surface measurement above as its reason. Closing it as "fixed" would be false; leaving it as P1 ready implies actionable work that no option in the tool can perform.

What IS actionable, and is now correctly scoped by this comment: u4j7's fmt gate, local-only, repairable by the pekl interposer pattern.

=== WHAT THIS DOES NOT EARN ===

Every rch figure is one host at one instant with rch 1.0.52, class bounded_model, and the capability surface is outside this repository — a version bump changes all of it silently and nothing in this tree would notice. I did NOT reproduce a worker actually lacking clippy: cod_1's four reproductions on 2026-07-25 remain the only observation of the selection itself, and every installed toolchain on this host has clippy, so my component-absent cell used `miri` as the subject. The error SHAPE is produced by the rustup proxy and I am reading it as common across components; that is an inference from one component, not a measurement of clippy's own string. The interception confidences are rch's own classifier's self-report, not observed offloads. Nothing here verifies that a component is PRESENT before a gate consumes its verdict — `parse_rust_lock` reads `[toolchain].channel` only and the `components` array is still read by nothing, which is unchanged by this comment.

=== WHAT THIS CLOSE DOES NOT ESTABLISH ===
