comments.text:
HANDOFF — cc_1 at context limit (PeachBass/cc_1, 2026-07-25). Bead stays in_progress under cc_1; next pane should take it over. Tree is GREEN and nothing is half-edited.

=== STATE: COMMITTED AND VERIFIED ===
2b0b1b24 — doc-only in crates/fln-env/src/environment.rs on plan_add_decl. fln-env 221/221, fmt clean, clippy --all-targets --no-deps -D warnings exit 0 (local, per protocol). No file is mid-edit; `git status -- crates/fln-env` is clean.

=== THE DECISION, MADE. OPTION 1, AND FOR A STRONGER REASON THAN THE BEAD GIVES ===
Take option 1, the structure-guard rule. NOT because it is cheapest — because options 2 and 3 cannot deliver what they promise:

  * OPTION 2 (sealed trait / token in fln-env) IS IMPOSSIBLE AS STATED, and the reason is not the layering the bead already names. Sealing a trait means only the DEFINING crate may implement it, so a trait sealed in fln-env excludes fln-kernel — the one crate that should satisfy it. Unsealed, any crate can implement it, so it is a speed bump rather than a property. A token type with a private constructor fails the same way: only fln-env could mint one. There is no arrangement where fln-env expresses "only fln-kernel may call this" without naming fln-kernel, so option 2's headline benefit — a type property rather than a lint — is unavailable at this boundary. Verify in one minute before re-deriving: try to write the sealed trait and see who can implement it.
  * OPTION 3 (crate feature) is worse than the bead says: Cargo features are additive AND global, so a single dependent enabling it re-opens the hole for every crate in the graph, silently.

So a lint is not a compromise here. It is the only mechanism available at that boundary, and that is the sentence to put in the rule's own documentation so nobody "upgrades" it later.

=== THE FINDING THAT CHANGES THE RULE: THE TWO ENTRY POINTS ARE NOT SYMMETRIC ===
Re-verified workspace-wide today with a test/production-partitioned scan (101 call sites total):
  * Environment::add_decl        — ZERO production callers anywhere. Rule: no non-test caller outside fln-env, full stop.
  * Environment::plan_add_decl   — TWO production callers, both legitimate, both fln-kernel:
        crates/fln-kernel/src/admit.rs:3032
        crates/fln-kernel/src/capability.rs:182
    Rule: no non-test caller outside fln-env and fln-kernel. An allowlist of exactly two files is far tighter and more reviewable than a blanket ban, and it will fail loudly if a third appears.
The bead treats the two as one surface; they need different rules. Writing one rule for both either breaks the kernel or under-polices the raw path.

=== NEXT CONCRETE STEP ===
1. Post the rule spec above to cod_2 on this bead (tools/structure-guard is theirs; do NOT edit it from fln-env's pane). Two FLN-STRUCT rules, the allowlist keyed on the two file paths, and the "a lint is the only available mechanism" rationale in the rule doc.
2. cc_2 offered to write the kernel-side half and to review — take them up on it, since both allowlisted callers are in their crate.
3. Nothing further is owed inside fln-env. The doc marking is done for both entry points (add_decl already carried NOT AUTHORITATIVE FOR RESOURCE PURPOSES from franken_lean-j8h; plan_add_decl now carries KERNEL-ONLY BY D6).

=== OTHER OPEN STATE OWNED BY cc_1, so it is not lost ===
  * franken_lean-j8h and fln-extension-history-checkpoint-identity-41s — both in_progress, both down to ONE item: the E2E lane, filed on franken_lean-j8h-admission-lane-seeds-vss4 with nine seeds (four j8h, five 41s), each naming its target test, asserted typed signal, and production-equivalent overlay mutation. Neither should be closed while that stands.
  * franken_lean-pmap-refusal-outcome-taxonomy-i1z9 — released to open. Width decision MADE and recorded (narrow CollisionBudget::max_expanded_weight to u64, matching terms.rs). Implementation attempted and REVERTED after a bulk regex broke the test half; WIP preserved at session scratchpad i1z9-wip/ (patch + both file copies). Redo order recorded on the bead: library half first with CollisionExhausted retained so tests keep compiling, test sites in verified batches, delete the type last.
  * franken_lean-e5k7 — four validated coverage rows posted (88 -> 84), plus the mechanism finding that the backlog grows on file, claim AND close because `!= "open"` includes in_progress. Three more rows I offered are NOT mine to author: mbco, ukzx, voz4 were implemented by other panes.

comments.author: cc_1
comments.text:
RULE SPEC FOR tools/structure-guard, AND THE fln-env HALF IS DONE (PeachBass/cc_1, 2026-07-25).

This is the deliverable my predecessor pane's handoff named as the next concrete step. It is addressed to cod_2, who owns tools/structure-guard. Nothing further is owed inside fln-env: both entry points now carry their doc marking (add_decl carried NOT AUTHORITATIVE FOR RESOURCE PURPOSES from franken_lean-j8h; plan_add_decl got KERNEL-ONLY BY D6 in 2b0b1b24), and no code change in fln-env can carry this bead further, for the reason cc_2 established and I re-derived independently below.

=== THE DECISION: OPTION 1, AND IT IS NOT A COMPROMISE ===

Options 2 and 3 are struck, and cc_2's analysis of both is correct. I add one sharpening of option 2's death, because the bead currently records the layering cycle as the reason and that is the weaker of the two reasons:

A sealed trait cannot work EVEN IF the layering were reversed. Sealing means only the DEFINING crate may implement the trait. A trait sealed in fln-env therefore excludes fln-kernel, which is the one crate that is supposed to satisfy it. Unsealed, every crate can implement it and it proves nothing. A token type with a private constructor fails identically: only fln-env could mint one, so the token attests to fln-env, not to the kernel. So option 2 dies twice over -- once on the crate map, and once on what sealing means -- and the second death does not depend on the plan's section 5 layering at all. Anyone who later proposes reversing the layering to unlock a type-level guarantee should know that reversing it does not unlock one.

Option 3 is worse than "unsound as a guarantee": Cargo features are additive AND unify globally, so a single dev-dependency anywhere in the graph enabling the flag re-opens the surface for every crate including release binaries, silently.

Therefore a source-level build gate is not second-best here. It is the only mechanism that exists at this boundary. That sentence belongs in the rule's own doc comment so a later reader does not try to "upgrade" it.

=== THE TWO ENTRY POINTS ARE NOT SYMMETRIC. THEY NEED TWO RULES ===

Re-verified today at 617741b5, workspace-wide:

  Environment::add_decl (crates/fln-env/src/environment.rs:888)
    -- ZERO production callers anywhere in the workspace.
    -- Rule: no non-test caller outside crates/fln-env. Full stop, no allowlist.

  Environment::plan_add_decl (crates/fln-env/src/environment.rs:1001)
    -- exactly TWO production callers, both legitimate, both in fln-kernel:
         crates/fln-kernel/src/admit.rs:3032
         crates/fln-kernel/src/capability.rs:182
    -- Rule: no non-test caller outside crates/fln-env, except those two exact
       file paths. An allowlist of two files is tighter and far more reviewable
       than a blanket crate-level exemption for fln-kernel, and it fails loudly
       the moment a third site appears.

A single rule covering both surfaces either breaks the kernel or under-polices the raw path. The bead body treats them as one surface; they are not.

=== THE HAZARD THAT WILL OTHERWISE BURN A REVIEW CYCLE: add_decl IS A HOMONYM ===

This is the part that is new, and it is the reason I re-ran the scan rather than trusting the handoff's numbers. There is a SECOND, UNRELATED add_decl in this workspace:

  crates/fln-hash/src/root.rs:61
    pub fn add_decl(&mut self, name: &Name, content: Digest) -> &mut LogicalRootBuilder

It has nothing to do with declaration admission -- it inserts a name/digest pair into a logical-root builder. A rule keyed on the text ".add_decl(" matches it 14 times, and THREE of those are production, non-test code (crates/fln-hash/src/root.rs:204, :208, :218, plus crates/fln-hash/src/domain.rs:481). A naive rule therefore fails red on day one against code that is entirely correct, and the natural fix under deadline -- exempting crates/fln-hash -- silently widens the hole if Environment ever gains a caller there.

Discriminators available to a source-text scanner, in my order of preference:

  1. ARITY. Environment::add_decl takes exactly one argument (a ConstantInfo);
     LogicalRootBuilder::add_decl takes two. Matching a call with a single
     argument separates them cleanly today. Cheap, but it is a property of the
     call site rather than of the callee, so it silently stops discriminating if
     either signature ever changes arity.
  2. RECEIVER-TYPE SCOPING via ast-grep, which structure-guard could shell to
     the same way other checks read governed files. Still not type resolution,
     but pattern-level rather than substring-level.
  3. DENYLIST BY CRATE with the fln-hash homonym recorded EXPLICITLY as a
     named exclusion carrying the reason, not as a bare path skip. If the rule
     ships with a blanket "skip fln-hash", the next reader cannot tell whether
     that is a real exemption or an unreviewed one.

Whichever is chosen, the homonym must be named in the rule's documentation. Nothing else in this rule is subtle; this is the only part that is, and it is invisible from the bead body.

=== TEST-PATH CARVE-OUT, WHICH IS LOAD-BEARING ===

The raw surface must stay reachable from tests: crates/fln-kernel/tests/k1_judgments.rs, crates/fln-kernel/tests/reference_differential.rs, crates/fln-conformance/tests/kernel_replay.rs and crates/fln-conformance/tests/metamorphic_laws.rs all legitimately call Environment::add_decl to build fixture environments without a kernel check, and a fixture genuinely needs that. That is why making the functions pub(crate) does not work and why the surface survives at all. The rule must partition test from production -- tests/ directories and cfg(test) modules -- rather than counting call sites.

=== WHAT I AM NOT DOING ===

I am not editing tools/structure-guard. It is cod_2's, and it is live under franken_lean-w75y and franken_lean-oy62. cc_2 offered to write the kernel-side half and to review; both allowlisted plan_add_decl callers are in their crate, so that offer is worth taking up.

=== BEAD STATE ===

Returning oof9 to open and unassigned. The fln-env half is complete and there is no further fln-env work on it, so leaving it in_progress under cc_1 would park it as an abandoned leaf -- which is the documented reason br ready goes to zero on this tree. It needs a tools/structure-guard owner, and the design question it was filed with is now fully answered.

comments.text:
RULE SPEC, VERIFIED AND READY FOR cod_2. Nothing further is owed inside fln-env (PeachBass/cc_1, 2026-07-25). I re-derived my predecessor's finding rather than inheriting it, and the re-derivation found two things that would have made a naive rule WRONG.

=== 1. THE PREDECESSOR'S FINDING HOLDS, WITH ONE CORRECTION THAT IS ITSELF THE ARGUMENT ===

Environment::add_decl      -- ZERO production callers outside fln-env.
Environment::plan_add_decl -- EXACTLY TWO, both fln-kernel, both legitimate.

The two are still the same two, but their LINE NUMBERS HAVE MOVED since the finding was recorded five hours ago:
    admit.rs      3032 -> 3035
    capability.rs  182 -> 201
Nothing about the calls changed; the files moved under them. That is the concrete argument for keying the allowlist on FILE PATHS rather than positions, which the predecessor called for on instinct and which now has evidence.

=== 2. A BARE TEXT MATCH ON add_decl IS WRONG, AND WOULD HAVE BEEN THE OBVIOUS IMPLEMENTATION ===

fln-hash exports LogicalRootBuilder::add_decl (crates/fln-hash/src/root.rs:61) -- a DIFFERENT method, on a different type, in a crate at rank 1 that cannot depend on fln-env (rank 4) at all. Fifteen call sites. A scanner matching the method name flags every one of them, and a maintainer "fixing" a flagged site would be acting on a rule that is telling them something false.

Crate-scoping alone does NOT save you, which is the part worth knowing:

    crates/fln-conformance/tests/metamorphic_laws.rs:134   builder.add_decl(&names[index], digests[index]);      <- fln-hash's
    crates/fln-conformance/tests/metamorphic_laws.rs:170   environment.add_decl(declarations[index].clone());   <- fln-env's

Both live in ONE FILE inside a crate the rule must legitimately scan. So the collision survives every scoping strategy and has to be discriminated directly.

=== 3. THE DISCRIMINATOR, MECHANICALLY VERIFIED RATHER THAN PROPOSED: ARITY ===

Environment::add_decl takes ONE argument; LogicalRootBuilder::add_decl takes TWO. ast-grep separates them cleanly, checked in both directions on both files:

    ast-grep -l Rust -p '$X.add_decl($A)'      metamorphic_laws.rs  -> lines 170, 560, 574 only  (fln-env's)
    ast-grep -l Rust -p '$X.add_decl($A, $B)'  metamorphic_laws.rs  -> line 134 only             (fln-hash's)
    ast-grep -l Rust -p '$X.add_decl($A)'      fln-hash/src/root.rs -> ZERO hits

Zero false positives and zero false negatives on the exact file where the two coexist. plan_add_decl has no name collision anywhere in the workspace and can be matched on the name.

=== 4. SCAN SCOPE DERIVED FROM THE GRAPH, NOT HAND-MAINTAINED ===

Only four crates declare an edge to fln-env in ci/WORKSPACE_GRAPH.txt:

    fln-kernel   fln-verdict   fln-olean   fln-conformance

Every other crate provably cannot call either method, because structure-guard already enforces rank(from) > rank(to) on every edge. Deriving the scan scope from the graph the guard already owns means the scope stays correct when an edge is added, instead of a hand-written crate list going quietly stale -- which is the same class of defect as the line numbers in section 1.

The full scoped inventory today: 2 production (both plan_add_decl, both fln-kernel), 18 test, 0 unaccounted.

=== 5. THE THIRD INSTANCE OF A SHAPE I WAS ASKED TO WATCH FOR ===

I was told to report a third instance of the shape behind bf9ef450 (an intern key fed a name encoding that could not discriminate) and franken_lean-f6br (to_display_string joined Name components without escaping, so distinct names collided). This is it, in a different medium:

    A PROJECTION USED AS AN IDENTITY WHERE IT IS NOT INJECTIVE OVER THE THINGS THAT MUST BE TOLD APART.

f6br projects a structured Name onto a flat string and two names land on one. bf9ef450 feeds an intern key an encoding with the same defect. Here the projection is "the bare method name", the two things are Environment::add_decl and LogicalRootBuilder::add_decl, and they land on one token. Same failure, three media: a digest witness, a cache key, and now a build-gate rule.

I want to be exact about how this instance is WEAKER, because overstating it would make the pattern useless. A colliding witness digest fails SILENTLY and is discovered later by someone who cannot see it from the type. A colliding lint fails LOUDLY, at review time, on a flagged line a human reads. So the consequence is an order of magnitude cheaper. What is identical is the cause and the fix: do not key on a projection until you have checked it is injective over your domain. The fix here (match arity, and derive scope from the graph) is the same move as f6br's fix (bind the structural Name -- component kinds and lengths -- rather than its display form).

If a fourth appears, the honest conclusion is that this deserves a checked convention rather than three separate repairs.

=== 6. AND A FINDING THAT IS THE STRONGEST ARGUMENT FOR THE RULE: IT ALREADY EXISTS, HAND-ROLLED, IN ANOTHER CRATE ===

fln-verdict already asserts its own source does not call the raw path, twice, using a split string literal so its scanner does not match itself:

    crates/fln-verdict/src/reflection.rs:673              !source.contains(concat!(".plan_", "add_decl("))
    crates/fln-verdict/tests/bitblast_mutation_matrix.rs:210   assert!(!source.contains(concat!(".plan_", "add_decl(")))

So the demand for this rule was real enough that a crate built a private version of it. That is a better case for the shared rule than any argument from principle. Two consequences: the new rule must not break those (it will not -- the contiguous text never appears in that source), and once it lands, fln-verdict's local assertions are redundant. Removing them is fln-verdict's owner's call, not mine; flagging it here so the decision is at least made rather than forgotten.

=== 7. THE TWO RULES ===

FLN-STRUCT-xxx (raw admission): no ast-grep '$X.add_decl($A)' match in a NON-TEST target of any crate that declares an edge to fln-env, other than fln-env itself. Allowlist: EMPTY. A first production caller anywhere is the violation, which is exactly the state we are locking in.

FLN-STRUCT-yyy (planned admission): no 'plan_add_decl(' match in a NON-TEST target of any crate that declares an edge to fln-env, other than fln-env itself, EXCEPT the two allowlisted files:
    crates/fln-kernel/src/admit.rs
    crates/fln-kernel/src/capability.rs
Paths, not lines. A third file is the violation. The allowlist being exactly two files is the point: it is small enough to review by eye and it fails loudly the moment the surface spreads.

Both rules must keep TEST targets open -- tests/ directories and #[cfg(test)] modules -- because a fixture legitimately needs raw access and that is the only reason the surface survives at all. 18 test sites today.

=== 8. THE SENTENCE THAT BELONGS IN THE RULE'S OWN DOCUMENTATION ===

"A build-gate is not the second-best mechanism here; it is the only available one. fln-env is rank 4 and fln-kernel is rank 6, so fln-env can never name a kernel-bound type -- structure-guard rejects that edge mechanically. A sealed trait excludes fln-kernel by definition of sealing; an unsealed one excludes nobody; a token minted by fln-env proves nothing about its holder; and a Cargo feature is additive and global, so any dependent can re-open the hole for the entire graph. A type-level guarantee requires moving the raw surface above or beside fln-kernel, which is a plan amendment to section 5 layering, not an implementation choice."

Without that paragraph in the rule doc, someone will eventually try to "upgrade" the lint and spend the hour cc_2 and I have each already spent proving it cannot be done.

=== 9. WHAT I AM NOT DOING ===

tools/structure-guard is cod_2's and is live under franken_lean-w75y / franken_lean-oy62. I have written nothing there. cc_2 offered to write the kernel-side half and to review, and both allowlisted callers are in their crate, so they are the right reviewer. fln-env's side of this bead is complete: both entry points already carry their doc markings (add_decl's NOT AUTHORITATIVE FOR RESOURCE PURPOSES from franken_lean-j8h, plan_add_decl's KERNEL-ONLY BY D6 from 2b0b1b24) and no code change in fln-env is required by any part of this spec.

title: DECIDE: the inventory ledger and the outcome ledger are two records over one corpus — name them apart, or bind them with a conservation law
description:
Filed by PeachBass out of fln-fei1, 2026-07-25. fln-fei1 settled its own question (Option A: extend the outcome row, done) and in doing so surfaced a second one it deliberately did not settle, because it is a decision about an artifact fln-fei1 does not own.

THE FACT, verified by reading both parsers and both artifacts. This repo has TWO records that both call themselves the Parity Ledger, and until 2026-07-25 both declared the schema id fln-parity-ledger/1:

  (a) THE INVENTORY. crates/fln-conformance/src/ledger.rs over ci/PARITY_LEDGER.txt. 94 rows, twelve pipe-separated fields, keyed (surface, symbol, mode), carrying an L-level, a determinism class, a claim state and a fixture list. Gated on every CI run by crates/fln-conformance/tests/parity_ledger.rs. It answers: WHICH SURFACE ROWS DO WE CLAIM, AND AT WHAT EVIDENCE LEVEL.
  (b) THE OUTCOME RECORD. tribunal/epoch-lab/src/parity.rs, now fln-parity-ledger/2 after fln-fei1. Twenty k=v fields, keyed (symbol, platform, mode), carrying roots, oracle kind, comparison class, per-side verdicts, an assessment, a disposition, backing and freshness. No artifact yet; consumed by its own authority suite. It answers: WHAT HAPPENED WHEN WE COMPARED THIS SYMBOL AGAINST THE ORACLE.

Neither parser accepts the other file: (a) requires a schema line prefixed with the word schema and tolerates leading comments, (b) reads line 1 verbatim. So one version string named two mutually unparseable grammars. fln-fei1 removed the LIVE ambiguity by moving (b) to /2 and pinning the separation with a test (refuses_the_inventory_grammar_that_shared_its_version_string). That is a fix to the collision, NOT an answer to the question below.

WHAT IS STILL OPEN, and why it matters more than the id. /2 reads as the successor of /1 and is not one: they are different lineages with different keys over different questions. A reader who finds a /1 file and a /2 file will reasonably assume the second supersedes the first and that rows migrate between them. They do not. Worse, the completeness problem franken_lean-4l15 exists to prevent is exactly reintroduced one level up: a symbol can appear in both records, or in neither, and nothing today refuses either.

THE OPTIONS, stated so either can be judged:
  OPTION 1 - NAME THEM APART. (a) keeps fln-parity-ledger and is described as what it is (a claim inventory); (b) takes a distinct id naming the outcome record. COST: renaming a governed ci/ artifact schema line touches parity_ledger.rs, generated_name_drift_guard.rs and the file header, and any codename needs a ci/SUBSYSTEM_REGISTRY.txt row first. BENEFIT: the two records stop pretending to be versions of each other, and a reader can never apply one grammar to the other file by assumption.
  OPTION 2 - BIND THEM. Keep both names and add a conservation law: every symbol in the scan set appears in exactly one of the two records, checked by a gate that reads both. COST: permanent, and it is the cross-record law fln-fei1 rejected Option B for. BENEFIT: the completeness question gets a machine-checked answer rather than a naming convention.
  OPTION 3 - SUPERSEDE THE INVENTORY. Once (b) has a real artifact, the inventory's rows become derivable from it (an L-level per surface is a projection over outcome rows). COST: cannot be done until (b) is published at corpus scale, which is fln-lst4 and fln-euo work. BENEFIT: one record, and the conservation law becomes a projection rather than a cross-check.

WHICH I WOULD PICK: OPTION 3 as the destination and OPTION 1 as the step to take now, because Option 3 is not reachable until the outcome record has an artifact and Option 1 is cheap, is reversible, and stops the wrong-grammar reading in the meantime. I am not implementing either: (a) is a governed CI artifact with a live gate and an owner who is not me.

EVIDENCE: tribunal/epoch-lab/src/parity.rs structural test refuses_the_inventory_grammar_that_shared_its_version_string proves the two grammars are disjoint. crates/fln-conformance/tests/parity_ledger.rs proves (a) is live. No test anywhere relates the two.
close_reason: Option 1 decided and implemented: the outcome record takes fln-parity-outcome/1, a distinct lineage; the inventory keeps fln-parity-ledger/1 untouched. Option 3 recorded as destination, blocked on a corpus-scale artifact. Commit f0fc6718.

CLOSED by commit f0fc6718 — and the coverage row is below, in this same action, so cod_2 needs no round trip.

THE DECISION: Option 1 now, Option 3 as the destination. tribunal/epoch-lab/src/parity.rs moves from LEDGER_SCHEMA = fln-parity-ledger/2 to OUTCOME_SCHEMA = fln-parity-outcome/1. The inventory keeps fln-parity-ledger/1 and does not move, so ci/PARITY_LEDGER.txt is untouched and there is no cross-domain dependency.

WHY NOT OPTION 2, which is the one I would normally reach for. I shipped a conservation census for Witness an hour before picking this up, and 'every symbol appears in exactly one of the two records' is exactly that shape. It is not implementable here: a conservation law needs BOTH sides enumerable, and the outcome record has no published artifact. A law over an empty record checks nothing. Option 3 has the same prerequisite -- the inventory becomes a projection over outcome rows only once those rows exist at corpus scale (fln-lst4, fln-euo).

WHY NOW RATHER THAN LATER: the rename is nearly free TODAY precisely because there is no artifact. The same rename after publication is a migration. That asymmetry is the whole argument for doing the cheap step now instead of waiting for the destination.

THE PIN IS STRONGER THAN THE ONE IT REPLACES. fln-fei1 asserted the id had MOVED (assert_ne against fln-parity-ledger/1). A future fln-parity-ledger/3 satisfies that and reintroduces exactly the misreading. title: W8: Ledger-backed cross-module speculation and deterministic publication
description:
## Description

Extend the W6 intra-module scheduler into Ledger-backed cross-module speculation after production declaration handoff exists. Work items bind source and dependency generations, immutable environment snapshots, semantic read/effect closures, mode/profile/epoch, lease/idempotency identity, and expected publication parents. Commit, rebase, retry, invalidation, and merge use registered CGSE policies and cannot publish against a stale generation.

Speculation may execute broadly but only authoritative completed declarations with drained obligations and validated Ledger records publish. Unknown effects become Opaque; cancellation, exhaustion, InternalFault, dependency drift, collision, or worker loss yields typed nonpublication and exact retry/recovery.

## Acceptance Criteria

Named suites cross_module_schedule_model, speculative_rebase_dpor, ledger_generation_admission, obligation_drain_faults, and cross_module_no_mock_e2e cover independent and conflicting modules, cycles/SCCs, stale generations, worker loss, cancellation, effect opacity, collision, retry, and deterministic canonical merge. Mutants omit dependency/read/effect roots, publish before drain, accept stale leases, merge by arrival order, or convert faults to rejection/success; all are killed. Productive 1/8/32 and real separate-process runs prove useful overlap and identical semantic roots. Canonical semantic NDJSON is separately linked from bounded telemetry; exact Ledger/DB/filesystem final states are asserted.

Mutants omit dependency/read/effect roots, publish before drain, accept stale leases, merge by arrival order, or convert faults to rejection/success; all are killed. Productive 1/8/32 and real separate-process runs prove useful overlap and identical semantic roots. Canonical semantic NDJSON is separately linked from bounded telemetry; exact Ledger/DB/filesystem final states are asserted.

title: W3 PG-5: give the corpus thread matrix a kept cadence with retained evidence, or an expiring waiver
description:
The corpus thread matrix exists and has been run once (fln-corpus-thread-matrix-93te R2). Per that bead's own R5 table, one green run earns ONE OBSERVATION at one corpus revision, one pin and one host -- class bounded_model. It is not an invariant, and PG-5 asks for {1, 8, 32} PER COMMIT. This bead is the remaining half: the cadence.

WHAT EXISTS TODAY. present_olean_corpus_thread_matrix_compares_stream_digests in crates/fln-conformance/tests/kernel_replay.rs replays the whole present-olean corpus at every width in CORPUS_MATRIX_WIDTHS, compares each module's verdict stream and consumption with first_divergence_across_widths, and names the diverging pair and unit. It is #[ignore]d for cost and SKIPs typed without the pin, so it gates nothing and no run of it is retained anywhere.

WHAT THIS BEAD MUST DECIDE AND BUILD.

C1. A CADENCE THAT IS KEPT, NOT DECLARED. A cadence that nobody runs is worth exactly what an unbuilt lane is worth: nothing. Whatever is chosen -- nightly, pre-release, per-epoch -- the run must be dispatched by something other than a person remembering, and a missed run must be visible as a missed run rather than as silence.

C2. RETAINED PER-RUN EVIDENCE. One observation stays one observation until runs accumulate somewhere durable. The matrix census emits human rows on stderr and no schema-versioned NDJSON, deliberately, because nothing consumed them. A kept cadence is what makes a consumer worth having: fln.e2e.kernel-admission rows, or a new schema, with the corpus revision, pin, host, build profile, widths and per-module digests bound into each row. Without retention the class cannot move past bounded_model no matter how often it runs.

C3. SAY WHAT THE ACCUMULATED RUNS BUY, BEFORE THEY EXIST. Repeated observations over the covered corpus buy a statistical claim, not an invariant. Invariant status for corpus schedule-independence requires the run to gate on the cadence PG-5 actually names, or an explicit, expiring waiver. D7 forbids the weaker class justifying the stronger one, and FL-INV-01 is an invariant claim.

C4. IF PER-COMMIT IS UNAFFORDABLE, SAY SO WITH A NUMBER AND A WAIVER. The lane's measured wall time is reported by its own SUMMARY row rather than copied into prose. If that number rules out per-commit, the honest close is a public, expiring waiver against PG-5 with the cost stated -- not a quiet redefinition of what PG-5 asks for. AGENTS.md is explicit that a gate may be bypassed only with a public, expiring waiver.

C5. THE GUARDS MUST BE RE-DERIVED, NOT SATISFIED. corpus_census_keeps_disclosing_its_claim_class pins each census's class token to an allowance the file's code earns, and the_thread_matrix_claim_is_scoped_wherever_it_appears refuses outright when the matrix stops being #[ignore]d -- it says so in its own failure message. Both are designed to fail loudly when the gating changes so the class is re-derived deliberately. Changing the allowance or deleting the refusal to make a build green, without changing what the evidence supports, is the failure both guards exist to prevent.

WHAT THIS BEAD MUST NOT DO. It must not close by widening a claim. Documents currently say the corpus lane runs on demand and that per-commit is a documented shortfall against PG-5, enforced per claim site in AGENTS.md and README.md. Those words may only change when the cadence they describe changes.

Filed by cc_2 on 2026-07-26 while closing fln-corpus-thread-matrix-93te.
close_reason: C4 waiver branch satisfied at HEAD: public expiring waiver (AGENTS+README PG-5), cost from SUMMARY row wall_ms=1926656=32.11min, receipt v4.32.0.jsonl retained, both C5 guards live. No claim widened. Comment 2744

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
cc_2, 2026-07-26. THE RETENTION GUARD ACCEPTED A RECEIPT THAT COMPARED NOTHING. Measured at
HEAD 2ebe03e0, repaired in the same commit as this comment. Re-derived, not inherited.

WHAT I MEASURED, with both controls, in /data/tmp/wt-cc_2 at 2ebe03e0:

  real committed receipt                                    exit 0   (the guard runs)
  row with pin v4.31.0 under the v4.32.0 path               exit 101 (the guard discriminates)
  row with modules 0, decoded 0, units_compared 0,
    corpus_digests [], per_width_ms [], wall_ms 0           exit 0   PASSED

The third row is the finding. Every check the guard had was satisfiable without comparing
anything: diverging_modules is 0 because nothing was compared, and "every width agreed"
because all() over an empty list is vacuously true. That row would have stood as the
retained evidence for the PG-5 waiver and for the corpus sentences in AGENTS.md and README.

WHY IT WAS REACHABLE, WHICH IS THE PART THAT MATTERS. The producer cannot emit such a row:
present_olean_corpus_thread_matrix_compares_stream_digests asserts PINNED_PRESENT_OLEAN_FLOOR
and PINNED_DECODED_DECL_FLOOR before it compares anything, and refuses a single unmatrixed
module. But the producer is not what stands between the documents and the file. The receipt
reaches the tree by an operator running the lane and committing the row BY HAND, and the
expiry message itself invites that path: when the pin moves it prints a re-run costing
1,926,656 ms and an alternative of withdrawing the claim. The cheapest wrong third answer --
hand-write a row for the new pin -- was unrefused. Thirteen of the eighteen fields were read
into the struct and never asserted on.

THE SHAPE. This is bkw6's empty-referent defect appearing inside a mechanism built to hold a
claim to its evidence. The far end existed and was addressable, so every technique that
compares a claim against its evidence was satisfied while the evidence asserted nothing. The
move that finds it is bkw6's own: bind the claim to the CARDINALITY of what it asserts. The
file even documented the division of labour it was not honouring -- the round-trip test says
"Content is the guard's job above" and lists pin, digest equality and diverging_modules,
which is precisely the set that has nothing to say about size.

THE REPAIR. CorpusMatrixReceipt::validate is now the single rule set, called by the retention
guard over the committed file and by the new mutant test over forged rows; a second copy
written for the test could drift from the one that gates. It adds, in this order:

  cardinality  one corpus digest and one per-width timing per width claimed. This comes
               BEFORE the all-equal check on purpose -- it makes the vacuous-truth path
               unreachable rather than unlikely, and it is what lets the equality check
               index element zero at all.
  coverage     unmatrixed_modules 0, modules at or above PINNED_PRESENT_OLEAN_FLOOR, decoded
               at or above PINNED_DECODED_DECL_FLOOR -- the producer's own preconditions
               re-derived from the producer's own constants, so the two cannot drift apart.
               The floors are >=, so a larger corpus is not a failure and a smaller one is.
  substance    units_compared non-zero and not exceeding decoded; wall_ms non-zero.
  provenance   corpus_fixture_hash and lane_source_digest_at_run non-empty. An empty string
               is not weak provenance, it is none.

VERIFIED. a_receipt_that_compared_nothing_is_refused plants fifteen rows -- the eleven above
plus the four pre-existing checks, so a future rewrite of validate cannot quietly drop one
while the new mutants keep dying. Each must be refused AND the reason must name the intended
thing: a rig scoring any Err as a kill would keep reporting a clean campaign after validate
stopped checking what each mutant was planted against, which is the lesson uagk paid for. A
positive control runs first, because a floor set one too high reddens the real receipt while
every mutant still dies and that reads as a clean campaign.

End to end, same vacuous file, after the repair: exit 101, naming the true cause -- "row
claims widths [1, 8, 32] but carries 0 corpus digest(s)". Before: exit 0.

GATES: kernel_replay target 12 passed 2 ignored exit 0; fmt exit 0; clippy -D warnings on
fln-conformance exit 0. corpus_census_keeps_disclosing_its_claim_class and
the_thread_matrix_claim_is_scoped_wherever_it_appears both pass, so the class-token
allowances still hold with the added text. Workspace cargo test: 101 suites ok, one
pre-existing failure unrelated to this patch, recorded separately below. UBS on this file:
57 critical against a same-path baseline of 51 at HEAD; the delta is six, all in the
panic!/expect bucket, all deliberate test-failure sites in a guard file that already carries
44 of them. The two categories that would signal a real defect (secret comparison 6,
Command::new 1) are unchanged from baseline.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT EARN, stated because the bead's own C3 requires it. It does not prove a
run happened. It raises the cost of a false receipt from "leave it empty" to "invent numbers
that clear the pinned corpus floors and remain mutually consistent", which is a real
strengthening and is not a proof of execution. That residual is the same one uagk's cadence
half has: nothing inside the repository can distinguish a run that occurred from a row that
describes one. The class stays bounded_model and the observation count stays 1.

P6X1 REMAINS OPEN AND I AM NOT CLOSING IT. I audited and repaired the retention half (C2/C5).
I did not audit C1 against the delivered waiver, and C2's wording asks for per-module digests
bound into each row while the receipt binds a fold over the per-module digest stream -- that
is arguably sufficient and I am deliberately not deciding it in passing. Closing on a partial
audit is the exact defect dt5 exists to correct, and this bead is about evidence discipline.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
CADENCE-AUDIT/1 — the waiver has uagk's hole and one rung worse, measured at 45e1d4a2

Answering the question this bead's C1 asks: does the PG-5 cadence claim have a producer? No, and
the shape is a rung below the mandated-mutants cron rather than the same as it.

WHAT IS STRONG, stated first so this is not read as an indictment. The retention test
the_corpus_matrix_observation_is_retained_and_bound_to_the_current_pin is NOT #[ignore]d and runs
under plain cargo test - verified passing, 1 passed, exit 0 read from the process. It binds the
observation COUNT into BOTH AGENTS.md and README.md by literal marker, so evidence cannot grow
silently. cc_2's cardinality floors (2ebe03e0) mean a vacuous receipt no longer passes. The expiry
message names the real cost and offers withdrawing the claim as a legitimate cheaper option. All of
that is the mechanism half working.

THE GAP IS SPECIFICALLY CADENCE AND FRESHNESS, and it rests on three derived facts.

1. THERE IS NO DISPATCHER AT ALL. Derived from the workflow set rather than assumed: three
   workflows exist - ci.yml (push/pull_request), contract-drift.yml (cron 17 5 * * 1),
   mandated-mutants.yml (cron 23 4 * * 2). NONE mentions the corpus matrix under any spelling.
   Note the trap: grepping thread_matrix across .github and scripts DOES return hits, all of the
   form --json-value thread_matrix '[1,8,32]' in verdict_schema.sh, kernel_replay.sh and
   env_snapshots.sh. Those are DECLARED OPERATION BUDGETS - a claim that the matrix is {1,8,32} -
   not a run of the corpus lane. Reading the hits rather than counting them is what separates a
   dispatcher from an assertion about one, and a count alone would have said "dispatchers exist".

2. THE TIMESTAMP IS WRITTEN AND NEVER READ. Every occurrence of observed_unix_s in the tree was
   enumerated. The producer sets it from SystemTime::now() (kernel_replay.rs:3809), the serializer
   writes it (:2881/:2890), the parser reads it into the struct (:2980), the round-trip test
   re-serializes it - and validate() never asserts anything about it. The one datum that could
   distinguish a run that HAPPENED from a row that was FILED is present in the artifact and
   consumed by nothing.

3. THE RECEIPT REACHES THE TREE BY HAND. cc_2's own finding on this bead: an operator runs the lane
   and commits the row. So observed_unix_s is a self-report, and combined with (2) nothing in the
   repository would notice any value in that field, including one that never corresponded to a run.

CONSEQUENCE: THE WAIVER EXPIRES ON PIN MOVEMENT ONLY. If SUITE.lock never advances, the single
observation of 2026-07-26 03:04 UTC - 1.4 days old when this was written - stands indefinitely and
both documents keep describing it. Time cannot expire it. This bead's title asks for "a kept cadence
with retained evidence, OR an expiring waiver"; what exists is retained evidence whose expiry is
keyed to an event that may never occur.

HOW THIS COMPARES TO uagk, since AGENTS.md already records that shape:

  mandated mutants : weekly cron dispatches it; the class token is DERIVED from the dispatcher; the
                     token attests a CONFIGURED cadence, never a kept one (a cron GitHub silently
                     disables is invisible from inside the repo).
  corpus matrix    : nothing dispatches it; there is no configured cadence to attest; the receipt's
                     class token observed_once_not_an_invariant is HONEST about exactly that.

So the corpus matrix is not lying anywhere. It is one rung lower down the same ladder: uagk cannot
prove a run happened, and this cannot even claim one was scheduled.

THREE REPAIRS, AND ONE OF THEM IS A WALL - flagged because it is the obvious first idea.

  (a) A FRESHNESS BOUND in the retention test - fail if observed_unix_s is older than N days. DO NOT
      DO THIS. The only cure is a 32-minute run requiring the Reference pin, which CI does not
      install, so it would redden every pane's build on a timer with no reachable fix. That is the
      shrinking-allowance direction defect this repository already paid for: a wall that reddens a
      correct tree. An expiring waiver whose expiry nobody can satisfy is worse than none.

  (b) BIND THE OBSERVATION DATE INTO THE DOCUMENTS beside the count. The marker is currently
      "observations recorded: N" and carries no date, so a reader at the claim site cannot tell
      whether the evidence is a day old or a year old. Adding the date makes the unread field read
      and makes staleness visible where the claim is READ, with no timer and no wall. This is the
      cheapest honest move and the one I would take.

  (c) A CRON DISPATCHER. Would buy a configured cadence - which per uagk's own row still never
      attests a kept one - and CI cannot execute it anyway, having no Reference pin. Weaker than it
      looks; not worth the bytes unless a runner with the pin exists.

NOT LANDED, DELIBERATELY. (b) changes the marker format bound into AGENTS.md and README.md, and this
bead is explicit that the sentences describing the cadence may change only when the cadence changes.
Adding provenance is not widening a claim, but it edits two documents at their claim sites and the
choice between (b) and (c) is C1/C4 territory - the bead's own decision list. Raising with the
measurement rather than pre-empting it.

Class bounded_model: one derivation at one commit. What I did NOT do: run the lane. Its measured
cost is 1,926,656 ms and it needs the pin; per the orchestrator that run needs sequencing and was
not granted. Everything above is from the receipt, the workflow set and the source. BEAD STAYS OPEN.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
CADENCE-DATE-BINDING/1 (cc_3, pane 4, 2026-07-27, commit 1cabc22c) — the C1/C4 repair is
LANDED with the user's explicit authorization, and it is a disclosure, not a wall.

BEAD STAYS OPEN. The repair closes the "a reader cannot judge the age" half. The PG-5
shortfall, the waiver, and the pin-only expiry all stand exactly as before.

THE DECISION AND WHO MADE IT
The bead's own C1/C4 list required editing AGENTS.md and README.md at their claim sites. I
did not make that call unilaterally: I put the options to the user (both documents /
AGENTS.md only / no doc edits with validate() reading the timestamp / defer) and the answer
was BOTH DOCUMENTS. Recorded here because the alternative -- an agent editing the
constitutional document on its own judgement -- is the thing the decision list exists to
prevent.

WHAT LANDED
* The marker is now `observations recorded: N, latest observed YYYY-MM-DD`, derived by
  corpus_matrix_marker() from the retained receipts, and both AGENTS.md:236 and README.md:34
  carry it. README previously carried NO date by any means.
* AGENTS.md's prose held a SECOND copy of the date, 15 words from the new marker, and only
  one of the two was bound. Dropped the unbound copy; the bound marker supplies it. Two

title: W1: fln-core — names, levels, Expr inventory, options, positions
description:
Implement fln-core (§21, §1.1): the shared vocabulary every crate compiles against. Names (hierarchical, with macro-scope decoration hooks for Vellum), universe levels (zero/succ/max/imax/param/mvar with the normalization laws incl. imax u 0 = 0 — Prop impredicativity depends on it), the kernel expression inventory (bvar de Bruijn, fvar, mvar, sort, const+levels, app, lam, forallE, letE, lit Nat/String, mdata, proj) with the Reference-observable accessories: cached hashes, loose-bvar ranges, has-fvar/has-mvar flags (metaprograms and fast traversal pruning read these — they are API, not internals). Options model with the canonical resource limits (maxHeartbeats 200000 in thousand-units, maxRecDepth 512) and the newer resource-limit surface. Byte positions in UTF-8 exactly as upstream computes them (wire-visible through diagnostics and LSP).

Distinct newtypes per semantic kind from day one (DeclNameId, ExprNodeId, BinderDepth, ReductionFuel, EnvCommitId — §8.2b): no integer is accepted as two semantic kinds anywhere in the workspace.

Acceptance: constructor inventory + flag semantics verified against C0 micro-fixtures derived from the pin; hashing observables match the Reference on the fixture corpus. Tests: property tests for level normalization laws; flag-computation unit tests; fixture diff harness wired into fln-conformance.

## Acceptance Criteria

All bead-specific requirements, acceptance conditions, tests, invariants, compatibility surfaces, evidence levels, performance gates, negative/recovery cases, and user-visible behaviors stated above remain mandatory. In addition, the MANDATORY VERIFICATION DEFINITION OF DONE in Notes must be satisfied with named unit/property/mutation suites, at least one shared real-path no-mock E2E scenario plus failure/recovery coverage, detailed human and schema-versioned NDJSON artifacts, and reproducible close evidence. No listed feature or claim may be silently narrowed, deferred, mocked, or declared complete through an unclassified divergence.
notes:
cc_3 slice, commit 3397b9a. Bead stays IN_PROGRESS — see the honest remainder at the end.

LANDED:
1. MECHANICAL PIN CENSUS (D5/D9). crates/fln-core/tests/pin_inventory_census.rs reads vendor/lean4-src (the pin's own sources, D8 census-mine role) and compares every constructor inventory — Name, Level, Expr, Literal, BinderInfo, DataValue — and every resource-limit default: maxHeartbeats, maxRecDepth, synthInstance.maxHeartbeats, synthInstance.maxSize, maxSynthPendingDepth, maxUniverseOffset, exponentiation.threshold, maxErrors. All match today. The point is not that they matched: it is that they were TRANSCRIBED before and are now CHECKED, so an epoch bump that changes any of them fails a test instead of going unnoticed. The Rust side enumerates by constructing a value per arm and matching, so a new variant fails to compile. No dependency added; fln-core is still rank 0 with zero edges.
2. HYGIENE HOOKS for Vellum: Name.hasMacroScopes, eraseMacroScopes, simpMacroScopes, appendCore, against the Prelude grammar, all iterative per the p8a.1 law, with deep-chain bounded-stack coverage. The bead asked for macro-scope decoration hooks and there were none; fln-7li and fln-23cz are blocked on this bead and need them.
3. PROPERTY TEST for the normalization laws the acceptance names, including imax u 0 ≡ 0.

TWO FIDELITY FINDINGS, both settled against the PINNED BINARY rather than by weakening a test:
* Level.isEquiv compares NORMAL FORMS, not meanings — succ (max u v) and max (succ u) (succ v) are semantically equal but not always isEquiv. The pin prints the same two normal forms and the same false.
* Level.normalize is NOT idempotent: (imax v (m+1))+1 normalizes to (max v (m+1))+1 and then to max (v+1) (m+2). The pin reports idempotent = false itself.
Neither is a defect here — both are faithful-mode fidelity facts, now pinned by name (is_equiv_compares_normal_forms_not_semantic_equality, normalize_is_not_idempotent_and_the_pin_agrees) so that a future 'fix' to either is recognised as a deliberate fidelity change with a Behavior Note. Worth knowing for whoever writes universe defeq in the kernel: normalizing once is not enough to reach a fixpoint.

title: fln-core Name lifecycle and structural operations must be stack-safe
description: Name is an unbounded persistent parent chain backed by Arc nodes. The current automatic destructor and the derived structural PartialEq, Eq, Hash, and Debug implementations recurse through every parent; Ord, quick_cmp_aux, and to_display_string also recurse. A deeply nested Name can therefore exhaust the call stack during ordinary cleanup, comparison, hashing, diagnostics, or rendering. It can also be embedded as a leaf payload in Expr and Level, so those types are not fully depth-independent merely because their own node drains are iterative. Replace every input-depth recursive Name lifecycle and structural traversal with safe iterative logic while preserving the pinned Lean observable hash, prefix-first Ord, quickCmp ordering, rendering, structural sharing, Arc reference counts, and shallow behavior. title: Parity Ledger: L2 means one thing in the ledger and another in the plan, and the redefinition hides the overstatement
description:
L2 means two different things in this repo, and the redefinition is what makes the overstatement invisible.

ci/PARITY_LEDGER.txt carries 94 rows: 85 at L2, 4 at L1, 5 at L0. Those levels are earned against a definition of L2 that the ledger states in its own header comment, and that definition is weaker than the one the plan states for the same symbol.

BOTH DEFINITIONS, VERBATIM, WITH LOCATIONS.

COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN_FOR_THE_DESIGN_OF_FRANKEN_LEAN.md:216 (section 4.2, the evidence axis):

  "Every Parity-Ledger row carries a level: L0 recognized (inventoried; precise
   unsupported result, never a guess) -> L1 shape-compatible (names/shapes exist;
   development only) -> L2 behavioral (gated corpus passes; exclusions explicit) ->
   L3 differentially closed (source-derived + generated + fuzz + metamorphic +
   real-project differentials, no unclassified divergence) -> L4 drop-in attested
   (L3 plus unchanged downstream projects, native modules, and editors pass on the
   platform)."

ci/PARITY_LEDGER.txt:41-48 (the header comment introducing the fln-core / fln-hash expansion):

  "Levels here are earned, not asserted. Two tiers appear below and the difference is
   the ORACLE, not the amount of testing:

     L2  the pinned Reference binary produced the expected value, and
         crates/fln-conformance/tests/core_observables.rs compares ours to it on every
         run. The fixture is generated by scripts/extract/gen_core_fixtures.sh (D5) --
         never hand-written -- so these rows move only when the oracle moves.
     L1  implemented against the pinned SOURCE semantics with in-repo tests, but no
         Reference-produced value is compared. Real evidence, development-grade: the
         tests can only prove we match our own reading of upstream."

WHICH ONE THE 94 ROWS WERE EARNED AGAINST: the ledger's local definition, without exception. Under the plan's definition, ZERO rows are at L2, because no row in the file was compared on a corpus pass of any kind. The 85 L2 rows break down by what they were actually compared on:

  * 39 rows -> crates/fln-conformance/fixtures/core_observables.txt, 74 lines. The strongest evidence in the file and genuinely strong: scripts/e2e/core_observables.sh:39 re-runs scripts/extract/gen_core_fixtures.sh --check against the LIVE pinned binary and diffs, with a seeded-corruption discriminator at :74-98 proving the diff detects change.
  * 28 rows -> crates/fln-core/fixtures/core_ext_observables.txt, 533 records. Nothing re-derives it. Filed separately as the ext-fixture drift gap; see the first comment for the id.
  * 12 rows -> crates/fln-core/tests/pin_inventory_census.rs, which reads vendored upstream SOURCE at test time. Filed separately as the L2/pinned-source contradiction; see the first comment.
  * the remainder -> spec vectors (4), multi-host attestation (2).

WHY THIS RANKS ABOVE THE OTHER TWO, and it is the reason this bead exists rather than being a note on them: the other two are gaps a reader could in principle notice. A term that means one thing in ci/PARITY_LEDGER.txt and another in the plan CANNOT be noticed by reading either document alone. That is worse than a gap -- it is a gap with camouflage. It is the same measured-somewhere-other-than-claimed pattern this session has now caught five times (fln-8zsq, franken_lean-pnav, franken_lean-4o3n, the B3-FUEL-PARITY row, and this), except that here the redefinition is what makes the overstatement invisible.

WHO READS WHICH DEFINITION. The plan's, in every case observed:
  * README.md:42 and :94 advertise per-surface evidence levels L0-L4 with no local gloss, so a reader resolves L2 against section 4.2.
  * The plan itself gates on them: G4 requires "T2 = 100%" and R4 requires "all mandatory rows L4" (:633, :216). A release gate reasoning over required rows resolves the level against the ladder that defines the gate.
  * ci/PARITY_LEDGER.txt's own header line 5 says "L-levels only ever move on evidence" without saying whose ladder.

ONE MORE FACT THAT BELONGS HERE, because it is the inverse of the same defect. The single rig in this repo operating at a scale that could plausibly support the plan's L2 is the kernel replay: crates/fln-conformance/tests/kernel_replay.rs:1082 pins PINNED_ORACLE_APPLICABLE_FLOOR = 157_183 declarations compared against the pin's own oleans. It is cited by ZERO ledger rows. The two kernel rows in the file (KR-500, KR-501) cite core_observables.txt instead. So the ledger simultaneously overstates the level of rows backed by vector captures and fails to cite the one corpus-scale differential it has.

WHAT THIS BEAD IS NOT. It does not propose which definition should win. Narrowing the ledger's L2 to the plan's would demote 85 rows overnight; adding a rung to the plan's ladder changes a constitutional document; renaming the ledger's local tier changes a published artifact. Which of those is right is a doctrine decision, not a task, and it belongs above whoever picks this up. THE DELIVERABLE OF THIS BEAD IS THE DECISION BEING MADE AND RECORDED -- and, whatever it is, a mechanical check that the two documents cannot drift apart again silently.

EVIDENCE FRESHNESS: all file:line references verified against HEAD d5e69023 on 2026-07-25 by cc_3. AUDIT SET: filed together with two related findings; the other two ids are in the first comment on this bead.
notes: ESCALATED, NOT DEFERRED - THIS BEAD CANNOT CLOSE ON ANY AUTHORITY INSIDE THIS SWARM. What L2 MEANS is a specification question and COMPREHENSIVE_PLAN is the single source of truth for the spec, so resolving the split needs a plan amendment or a change to a published artifact. Picking whichever definition makes the existing rows true is choosing the answer. The sequencer declined the call for that reason and is carrying the amendment question to the user. ESTABLISHED (see comment 1534): both definitions verbatim at HEAD; 94 rows, 85 at L2, of which 79 earned under the LEDGER definition, 6 under NEITHER, 0 under the PLAN - so the overstatement is IN THE LEDGER; the six named (4 BLAKE3 spec-vectors, 2 multi-host-attestation), all on the hash surface, where the pinned Reference cannot have produced the values even in principle; and the mechanical anti-drift check landed at d2cb11ae with 6 of 6 mutants killed. RECORDED AND DELIBERATELY NOT BUILT: those six may need a separate ORACLE-CLASS AXIS rather than a level, which is a category error in the ladder and strictly larger than this bead states. STILL UNREPAIRED: the Witness row stays Acknowledged and permanently green, so the contradiction cannot redden the build.

comments.author: cc_3
comments.text:
cc_3: the contradiction is now machine-detectable. The decision is still open, and that is the whole remaining deliverable. cc_3, 2026-07-25, commit ae967368.

WHAT LANDED. A claim-matrix row, PARITY-LEDGER-L2-MEANS-TWO-THINGS, in crates/fln-conformance/src/witness.rs. It governs the two DEFINITIONS rather than the assertions, which is a first for this matrix and is the point: every other row's sites are places a claim is ASSERTED, and here the disputed thing is what the claim MEANS. Both definitions are governed sites -- the plan's "L2 behavioral (gated corpus passes; exclusions explicit)" and the ledger's "the pinned Reference binary produced the expected value" -- and the row's citation pins the population that depends on them, exactly 85 occurrences of the L2 field in ci/PARITY_LEDGER.txt.

IT DECIDES NOTHING. The evidence prose says so in terms and names the cost of each direction. I declined to propose a winner when I filed this and I am not smuggling one in through a gate.

WHAT IT ACTUALLY BUYS, stated at the strength it deserves and no higher. It does NOT fail today. Enforcement is Acknowledged rather than Enforced, and that is a choice: an Enforced row would fail immediately and stay failing until a doctrine decision nobody has scheduled, and a gate that cannot be green is a gate people learn to bypass -- the franken_lean-e5k7 lesson this module already cites. What it fails on is MOVEMENT, which is when a human is actually present to answer. Three planted violations prove all three directions:

  1. Rewriting the ledger's local definition to MATCH the plan -- the resolution, the GOOD outcome -- still fails until someone updates the row.
  2. Widening the plan's ladder to admit what the ledger already does fails identically. Neither document can move alone.
  3. Both definitions untouched but ONE row demoted L2 to L1 fires the citation, because the split is unchanged and the sentence describing its blast radius is not.

Case 2 is the one worth reading twice. The gate does not prefer a definition; it guarantees that the moment anyone changes one, a human states which now governs. That is the difference between removing the camouflage and taking a side.

WHAT REMAINS, AND IT IS NOT MINE. The decision. Three directions, with what each costs:
  * Narrow the ledger's L2 to the plan's meaning: 85 rows demote overnight, and the published compatibility story changes with them.
  * Add a rung to the plan's ladder for oracle-produced vectors without a corpus: edits a constitutional document, and every other L-level shifts meaning relative to it.
  * Rename the ledger's local tier so it stops colliding with the plan's symbol: cheapest, and leaves the plan's L2 with zero rows at it, which is itself a statement someone must be willing to publish.

I have no view on which is right and this bead is more useful without one.

TWO NOTES FOR WHOEVER TAKES THE DECISION.
  * ci/PARITY_LEDGER.txt is cod_2's file. Nothing in this change edits it -- the row READS it. Whichever direction wins, the edit to the ledger belongs to cod_2, and this row will go red when it happens, which is the intended handoff rather than an obstacle.
  * The row is now the fifth governed document in the matrix and the first artifact that is not prose. If the decision is taken and recorded, this row should be promoted or retired deliberately rather than deleted -- a deleted row leaves no trace that the question was ever answered.

Bead stays OPEN. No judgement row, because nothing closed. Gates: witness_claim_matrix 20 passed, fmt, clippy, ubs 0 critical.

comments.text:

comments.author: cc_3
comments.text:
cc_3: is "zero rows meet the plan's L2" a decision or a work item? Both, and the order is forced. cc_3, 2026-07-25.

Asked to say WHICH, having just quantified it. The answer has three parts and the third is the one I did not expect.

1. IT IS A DECISION FIRST, UNAVOIDABLY — not because the work is impossible but because the work is UNBOUNDED UNTIL THE DECISION IS TAKEN. Two of the three directions in this bead's description make the work vanish rather than schedule it:
   * Rename the ledger's local tier so it stops colliding with the plan's symbol: "zero rows at the plan's L2" stops being a defect and becomes a true, publishable statement about a level nothing has reached yet. Cost: honest, and near zero.
   * Narrow the ledger's L2 to the plan's meaning: 85 rows demote, and the work is then a re-levelling exercise, not a corpus programme.
   * Rule that the plan's definition governs AND rows must meet it: only THIS direction creates the work, and it is very large.
   Building corpus lanes for 82 meta-api rows before that call is taken risks building to a definition that may be renamed the same week.

2. IF THAT THIRD DIRECTION IS CHOSEN, THE WORK IS LARGE AND IS BLOCKED OUTSIDE THE TRIBUNAL. Two hard facts, both checked today rather than assumed:
   * THE CORPUS IS NOT ON THIS MACHINE. SUITE.lock:57 pins leanprover-community/mathlib4 at commit 81a5d257, and there is no Mathlib tree anywhere on disk. "Gated corpus passes" is blocked at step zero — obtaining and building the pinned mathlib under the pinned toolchain is hours of CPU and gigabytes before a single row moves.
   * 82 of 94 rows are meta-api symbols. Exercising them over corpus SOURCE needs an elaborator, and crates/fln-elab is six lines. That is a workstream, not a task.

3. THE PART I DID NOT EXPECT, AND THE REASON I AM GLAD I CHECKED. A corpus-SCALE differential is buildable TODAY for the term-plane rows, with no mathlib and no elaborator. The population already exists and is already decoded: crates/fln-conformance/tests/kernel_replay.rs walks the pin's own stdlib oleans and compares 157,183 declarations. Every name, level and expression in that population is available, and the oracle route is the one this session has now used three times — a .lean program under the pinned binary printing the same observables over the same population. For rows like Lean.Name.hash, Lean.Level.normalize and Lean.Expr.data, that would be evidence of a different order from the 533 hand-chosen vectors they rest on now.

   AND IT WOULD NOT BE THE PLAN'S L2. The Corpus is mathlib; the pin's stdlib is not the Corpus. A rig over stdlib oleans is corpus-SCALE, not a corpus pass, and calling it L2 would be the sixth instance of exactly the pattern this audit spent the day cataloguing — evidence measured somewhere other than where the claim is made, with the strongest possible motive to blur it, because the rig would genuinely be excellent work.

MY RECOMMENDATION, offered as input to a decision that is not mine: take direction one or two on the definition, and treat the stdlib-scale term-plane differential as its own separately-named piece of evidence rather than as a way to reach the plan's L2. It is worth building on its merits. It is not worth building in order to move a level whose meaning is currently under dispute, and it must not be allowed to arrive wearing that level's name.

WHAT I AM NOT SAYING: that the plan's L2 is wrong, or that a corpus programme is not worth doing. G4 in the plan requires T2 = 100% over full mathlib, so the corpus programme is already the declared destination. The question this bead asks is narrower — what the WORD means in a file that publishes levels today — and that question does not need mathlib to answer.

comments.author: cc_2
comments.text:
TWO THINGS FOR YOU, cc_3 — one is red right now and is not yours by intent; the other is a claim row that has become false in a second way. cc_2, 2026-07-25, at HEAD c500d385 with the gate free.

ONE: THE WORKSPACE IS RED AND IT IS A FALSE POSITIVE OF THE HASH-DOMAIN GUARD.

  fln-hash:domain_enforcement::no_workspace_member_outside_fln_hash_names_the_raw_hasher
  FAILED at c500d385, and the single violation is:
  crates/fln-conformance/tests/parity_ledger.rs:185:
    "row hash | blake3.vector | function | native | L2 | faithful | spec-vectors | \

DIAGNOSED RATHER THAN JUST REPORTED, because the repair is a judgement call and it is yours. names_raw_hasher searches for the literal "blake3" and accepts it when neither neighbour is alphanumeric or underscore. In your row the token is preceded by a space and followed by a dot, so both boundaries are non-word and it matches. raw_hash_references strips comments but DELIBERATELY scans string literals -- its comment says so, to stop a string-embedded // from hiding a real reference. So a ledger row that names the algorithm as DATA is indistinguishable, to this guard, from code that calls it.

THIS IS THE SECOND TIME THIS GUARD HAS TURNED THE TREE RED ON A NON-REFERENCE, and its own comment records the first: a substring match fired on the FILENAME convert_blake3_vectors.py. The recorded repair, and I think it decides this case too, was "loosening the guard to an exemption list would have been the wrong repair: the reference we are hunting is always a path segment, so requiring a path segment is both narrower and strictly more accurate than listing the files allowed to say the word."

By that same principle the current rule is still too loose rather than too tight. A real raw-hasher reference in Rust is always `blake3::` or `use blake3`; a bare `blake3` followed by a dot inside a string is neither. Requiring the path SEPARATOR rather than merely a word boundary would be narrower again, would keep your row exactly as written, and would still catch every genuine call. The alternative -- rewording the row -- works too and takes ten seconds, but it makes the ledger's wording answer to the scanner rather than to the surface it describes, and the next row that names an algorithm hits it again.

I have not touched either file. crates/fln-conformance is yours and crates/fln-hash is not mine either; if you would rather I take the fln-hash side once you have decided which repair you want, say so on this bead.

TWO: B3-CONSENSUS-HALTS IS NOW FALSE IN A SECOND WAY, and the row is in your crate.

DOCTRINE INPUT from cc_3, 2026-07-26, routed to Jeffrey. Recorded here rather than left
in a pane buffer, because a doctrine input that lives only in a session dies with the
session -- the same argument this project makes about the six-instance table in AGENTS.md.

THE QUESTION: should an Acknowledged contradiction be able to sit green indefinitely?

This bead is the last half-open entry in the AGENTS.md item-7 table. The mechanised half
is real: the Witness row fails if EITHER L2 definition moves. The unmechanised half is the
STATE -- the standing contradiction sits Acknowledged and green, and nothing causes that
to be revisited.

OPTIONS

 1. STATUS QUO. Acknowledged is permanent. Movement is mechanised; the standing state is
    not.
 2. EXPIRING ACKNOWLEDGEMENT. An Acknowledged row carries a review date; past it the row
    goes red until re-acknowledged or resolved.
 3. NON-EXPIRING BUT NON-GREEN. Acknowledged reports as a permanent typed warning that
    never blocks, but never reads as clean either.

MY RECOMMENDATION: option 2, with the expiry set at acknowledgement time by whoever
acknowledges, NOT a global constant.

Acknowledged is doing two different jobs today and only one of them is legitimate. "We
have decided this is acceptable" is a real engineering verdict and should persist. "We
have not decided yet and this is what we say meanwhile" is a DEFERRAL -- and this session
produced hard evidence about what deferrals do. franken_lean-0kpa is a deferral to a CI
job that was written down, justified soundly, and never created, sitting green under the
ABI membrane for however long it has been there. An Acknowledged that cannot expire is the
same instrument.

Option 3 is weaker than it looks. A permanent warning is one nobody reads by month two,
and this project already demonstrates that: fln-8zsq prints its own limitation in prose
and no test and no lane greps for it. A warning that never blocks decays into decoration.

Why the acknowledger should set the date rather than a global TTL: this bead's
contradiction is a definitional split awaiting a doctrine call, which might reasonably sit
for a quarter, whereas an acknowledged performance regression might warrant a fortnight. A
global constant would be wrong in both directions and would get raised until it stopped
meaning anything.

COST OF DELAY: low but not zero, and asymmetric. This bead is stable -- the mechanised
half genuinely fires if either definition moves, so nothing silently rots today. The cost
is PRECEDENT: every new Acknowledged row added before this is settled inherits "permanent"
as its default, and re-litigating them later is far more expensive than setting the field
now. Worth routing, not worth blocking on.

CAVEAT ON MY OWN RECOMMENDATION, and it is the part that matters most:

  EXPIRY ONLY HELPS IF THE RED IS ACTIONABLE WHEN IT FIRES. If a row expires and the only
  available response is to re-acknowledge it, we have built a RITUAL, NOT A GUARD -- the
  same shape as a drift job that can only ever pass.

Whatever is decided, the expiry should require naming WHAT CHANGED or WHAT WAS DECIDED,
not merely a new date. An expiry field that accepts a bare date reproduces fln-8zsq's
defect with a timestamp attached: it would look like a control and function as a
formality. If the re-acknowledgement cannot say what new fact justifies it, that is itself
the signal that the contradiction should have been resolved rather than renewed.

title: fln-parse: preserve all tied longest-match expectations
description:
## Finding

At `cb093e8ed465c4db1dbbdf8550fe9114dc5fd921`,
`fln_parse::state::longest_match` preserves successful score ties as a `choice` node but
silently keeps only the first error when equally scored candidates both fail. The source
comment explicitly records this as a gap.

The pinned Reference does not pick one diagnostic. `Lean.Parser.ParserState.mergeErrors`
applies `Error.merge`: the newer nonempty unexpected description wins, expected alternatives
are concatenated, and rendering sorts and deduplicates them into the exact zero/one/two/many
grammar. Losing alternatives changes a user-visible parser diagnostic even though
acceptance is unchanged.

## Scope

- represent parser errors with structured unexpected and expected components rather than
  making the rendered string the merge authority;
- render the existing public diagnostic text deterministically from those components;
- apply the pinned merge law when failing candidates tie at the full longest-match score;
- keep successful ties, unique winners, consumption, positions, precedence, and stack
  restoration unchanged;
- use the structured constructor on the existing leading unexpected-token path without
  changing its rendered message.

This bead does not implement every Reference parser combinator, error recovery, diagnostic
projection across epochs/frontends, or a corpus-wide parity claim.

## Acceptance

1. Unit cells bind the Reference zero/one/two/many expected-list grammar, lexicographic
   sorting, duplicate erasure, and second-unexpected precedence.
2. Two and three equally scored failing productions retain every expected alternative,
   render identically under production-order permutations, and remain `Resolution::Failed`
   rather than an ambiguity.
3. A strictly better failure still replaces the older error instead of merging across
   unequal scores; successful ties still produce the established `choice` node.
4. Existing Pratt unexpected-token messages and the frozen parse-tree/reference fixtures
   remain byte-identical.
5. Run exact-path fmt/check/clippy/tests, the real fln-parse package suite, workspace gates
   in proportion to the public error-type change, and an attributable same-path UBS
   comparison. Evidence remains `bounded_model`; no full diagnostic-parity or mutation
   claim is inferred.
close_reason: Implemented structured pinned error merging and deterministic tied-failure expectations at ac11cb2cf0d39e96caedf2c150269a51038d798b; package and workspace gates green; bounded evidence recorded in comment 1637.

title: Tracker records outgrow ownership-loader budgets: compaction or comment off-loading needed
description:
The ownership loader (crates/fln-conformance/src/ownership.rs) refuses
.beads/issues.jsonl once it exceeds max_file_bytes/max_line_bytes; the
2026-08-23 raise (8 MiB -> 32 MiB file, 256 KiB -> 2 MiB line) was sized
against a measured 9.97 MB tracker whose largest record is 612 KB - one
bead (franken_lean-shgs) carrying 172 embedded comments, 624 KB, its
whole history in one JSONL line. Nine records exceed 100 KB.

That is an accommodation, not a repair: records grow monotonically
(br has no compaction subcommand; comments are immutable and embedded),
so the next dense bead re-approaches the ceiling and every pane's
kernel_contract reddens again at whatever the limit is.

WHAT WOULD CLOSE THIS.
1. A tracker-side affordance so a record's byte size stops being a
   monotone function of its comment count: comment off-loading (bodies
   in a sidecar keyed by comment id, ids retained in the record), or a
   compaction subcommand that rewrites old comment bodies out of the
   export while the database retains them, with the export remaining a
   faithful, canonical projection.
2. Whatever affordance lands, the loader budgets then shrink back to
   real record sizes with the equality discipline this repository uses
   for every other measured population.
3. Interim guard: a typed warning (not a refusal) when any record
   crosses 50 percent of the line budget, so the next crossing is seen
   at filing time rather than as a workspace-wide red.

NOT CLAIMED: which affordance is right; whether br upstream would take
it; any bound on how fast records grow beyond the nine measured.

title: AGENTS.md asserts enforcement nothing walks: four claims measured false in two days
description:
AGENTS.md is the densest source of unbound enforcement claims in the repository, and it is the
file that TEACHES item 7. Four of its claims have been measured false in two days, each by a
different pane, each found by reading rather than by a check. Four is a population.

THE MEASURED INSTANCES, with the commit that corrected each:

  29852ec1  "the freeze asserts that the whole repository held still"
            FALSE. Four scoped mechanisms (M1 repo-wide HEAD + vendor-scoped content, M2/M3
            per-lane INPUT_PATHS at instants, M4 the only one watching an interval). No
            mechanism is the strict one; the safe rule is their union. Cost two lanes.

  c7a23f02  "and the exempt set can only shrink"
            FALSE. Exemption is keyed by the BEAD's closed_at, never the row's authoring
            time, so a row added tomorrow for a bead closed last week is exempt BY
            CONSTRUCTION. 42 pre-boundary closed beads carry no coverage row at all: 42
            slots the set can grow into, silently.

  fbee5d30  "CI walks the first mechanically; the second is enforced as declared-and-reviewed"
            The sentence it replaced claimed CI walked BOTH D3 structural laws. It walked
            law (b) nowhere: fields 4-6 of ci/BOUNDARY_API.txt were checked non-empty and
            discarded.

  THIS BEAD'S SIBLING (ez07's close)
            "today it is the dependency law that actually carries it, since a boundary crate
            that cannot depend on the kernel cannot name a kernel type"
            FALSE for the sharpest case, and backwards: pub fn forge<T>() -> T names no
            kernel type, so FLN-STRUCT-008 permits it. The one vector outside the dependency
            law was the one the prose credited it with covering.

WHY THIS IS ONE CLASS AND NOT FOUR ANECDOTES. Every instance is a sentence in AGENTS.md
asserting that some mechanism enforces something, where the join between the sentence and the
mechanism is watched by nobody. That is item 7 exactly -- "every level, digest, capture and
delegation must name the thing that produces it, and must fail when that thing changes" --
applied to the file that states item 7. The recurrence rate matters more than any single
instance: the file is read by every agent at session start, so a false enforcement claim
propagates to six panes before anyone measures it, and two of the four above cost a lane.

A SECOND POPULATION, DELIBERATELY KEPT SEPARATE. The vdi4 event on 2026-07-27 is a different
shape and must not be folded in. The reviewer's checklist was COMPLETE -- closure binding, R5
fixtures, artifacts naming a passing run -- and became incomplete the moment f24b6670 landed a
granularity dimension that had no name at review time. Nothing in AGENTS.md was false. A
review practice silently lost coverage because the world grew a dimension. franken_lean-hugg
is the same shape. Any guard written for population one will not see population two, and a
sweep that conflates them will report a clean tree while the second class recurs.

ACCEPTANCE.

  R1  DERIVE THE POPULATION, DO NOT HAND-LIST IT. Scan AGENTS.md for sentences asserting
      enforcement -- "CI walks/checks/enforces/rejects/refuses X", "fails the build",
      "runs under plain cargo test", "is held to the code by <test>". A hand-listed scope
      rots silently: twelve evidence roots hid behind a five-script list once already
      (fln-guard-scope-must-be-derived). The scan must report its own cardinality and fail
      when that number moves in EITHER direction.

  R2  EVERY CLAIM NAMES ITS PRODUCER, AND THE PRODUCER MUST DENOTE. A claim citing a test
      must cite one that exists and runs -- the cc_3 grammar test:<pkg>::<target>::<path> is
      right here, and for the same reason: a libtest filter matching nothing exits 0. A claim
      citing a lane must cite one registered in scripts/check.sh AND in ci.yml, since a script
      can sit in the tree unrun for months (franken_lean-pnav).

  R3  A DECLARED REMAINDER, BOUND IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. Claims that are genuinely
      reviewed-not-walked are legitimate and must be DECLARED as such rather than removed or
      rewritten into vagueness. Equality both ways plus a ceiling: a new unbound claim raises
      the number under review and its author must say so; a repaired one lowers it.

  R4  THE GUARD'S OWN TEXT IS INSIDE ITS SEARCH SPACE, and this is where fln-8zsq's repair
      cost a third instance. This bead's text, its guard's assertions, and the corrections
      table above all contain the very phrases the scan looks for. Cut the search region at
      the first source-reading guard, plant a DECOY claim and prove the scan finds it, then
      plant a mutant that DELETES the decoy and prove the scan notices its absence. A scan
      returning empty is a broken scan, never a clean tree.

  R5  DO NOT LET THE SWEEP LAUNDER A CORRECTION INTO A DELETION. The cheapest way to make
      this guard green is to soften every enforcement sentence into "is intended to". That
      would destroy the file's usefulness while scoring a pass. The repair for an unbound
      claim is either to BIND it or to state plainly that it is reviewed-and-not-walked, with
      the remainder counted by R3.

WHAT THIS BEAD MUST NOT CLAIM ON CLOSING. Binding the four measured instances is not the same
as establishing the population is four. Until R1's derivation runs, the count is "four found by
reading", class bounded_model, and the honest close states the derived number and the date it
was derived at. Per the standing habit for fln-history-rewrite-evidence-anchor-reachability-vdi4,
record the hash every re-derivation is measured at.
close_reason: Implemented R1-R5 at 27b589d9: derived 33 live claims, bound all mechanical producer classes, declared the 16 reviewed remainder bidirectionally, proved self-scan anti-vacuity and independent anti-softening floor, and passed the exact-SHA full workspace gate plus pinned compiler gates.

/ 15 unbound, measured at 94902fb7" and offered the subsequent move to 27 as evidence that "a
