THE DEFECT I FOUND, which is why this bead was worth reopening rather than closing.

The registered check was not merely vacuous. It was INCORRECT, and would have fired
spuriously the first time it ever did anything.

fln_core requires ModeClosureRequest::nodes to be EXACTLY the reachable closure of roots.
ValidatedModeClosure is documented as "Private-constructor proof that every supplied node
is reachable", and mode.rs:874 refuses any node it cannot reach with FLN-D18-012. The
extractor passed ALL 33 WORKSPACE CRATES as nodes. Its own comment said the opposite:
"Only the nodes this product actually reaches belong to its closure".

Consequence, measured and not reasoned: I planted a Sound product root in a fixture
workspace and the guard returned
  FLN-D18-012 ... node=fln is in the closure but unreachable from any product root
naming a crate with nothing to do with the plant. The first crate in this repository to
declare a mode-bound product root would have been refused on account of the 32 unrelated
crates beside it. As implemented the rule said: no workspace may contain a crate outside
the product.

WHY NOTHING CAUGHT IT, and it is the shape this session kept finding. No crate declares a
product root, so roots_by_mode is empty, so no closure is ever submitted and the live
scan is vacuous. A vacuous check never builds the request it would have built, so no test
over the real workspace can exercise the derivation. The unit tests did exercise it, and
they passed, because their two-crate fixture happens to have every node reachable. A
check whose subject does not exist cannot be trusted to be correct, only to be green.

WHAT I LANDED
  1. audit_with_facts now submits the reachable subset. A small BFS selects it; no mode
     algebra moved out of fln_core, and the admission decision is still entirely the
     core's. Selecting the node set is the caller's obligation under the core's own API
     contract, not a second copy of the scanner.
  2. ModeClosureFacts gained closure_nodes, so "nodes submitted" is distinguishable from
     "crates in the workspace". Equality of the two now means either one all-reaching
     product or a derivation that has stopped selecting.
  3. Unit regression guard only_the_reachable_subset_is_submitted_not_the_whole_workspace
     pins the subset by count on a three-crate graph where one crate is unrelated.
  4. THE NEGATIVE CONTROL THE BEAD ASKS FOR, at the production level. seeded.rs now has
     planted_frontier_reaching_a_sound_product_root_fails_the_guard_run, which plants a
     frontier feature on a crate reachable from a Sound product root in a real on-disk
     fixture workspace and proves the REGISTERED GUARD RUN returns FLN-D18-001 with a
     non-zero exit code; and removing_the_frontier_feature_recovers_the_sound_closure,
     which proves repair recovers. The dependency is backed at all three layers the guard
     cross-checks - governed graph edge, manifest dependency and Cargo.lock closure - so
     the plant varies only the frontier surface. An edge backed at fewer layers trips
     FLN-STRUCT-006 or FLN-STRUCT-018, and a plant that trips two checks proves neither.

A TEST ASSERTION I INVERTED, flagged for review by someone other than me, because
changing a test to match new behaviour is how a regression gets blessed.
planted_closure_omission_is_refused_not_partially_passed asserted that a crate the
product root cannot reach refuses the closure with FLN-D18-012. That was the bug, stated
as a requirement. It is now
a_crate_the_product_does_not_reach_is_outside_its_closure_not_a_refusal, and the reasons
are written into the test body rather than only here. The omission check is not weakened,
it moved to where it can still act: the core still refuses any supplied node it cannot
reach, and this derivation can no longer supply one.

A SECOND FINDING I AM REPORTING RATHER THAN FIXING, because it changes an emitted schema
that is not mine to version. THE VACUITY DISCLOSURE NEVER REACHES THE ARTIFACT. The
robot run_end object carries exactly these keys:
  authority, authority_count_rule, authority_count_rule_holds, contract_handoff_root,
  duration_ms, event, exit_code, findings, governed_root_after, governed_root_before,
  governed_root_unchanged, schema, traversal, verdict
There is no D18 key of any kind. ModeClosureFacts is computed, stored on RunOutcome, read
by tests, and never emitted. So a reader of a guard run sees verdict=pass with no findings
and has no way to learn that the D18 check traversed nothing at all. The qualifier that
makes "structure-guard passed" honest exists only in memory. That is the item 7 shape
exactly: the claim is made in the artifact and the evidence for its scope is not produced
there. Recommended repair is additive - carry frontier_surfaces, product_roots,
closures_scanned and closure_nodes into run_end - but it touches the structure-guard/3
robot schema, which is a versioned surface and cod_2's call.

  cargo clippy -p structure-guard --all-targets --no-deps -D warnings clean
  cargo test -p structure-guard fully green: lib 72, main 6, authority 20, closure 12,
    real_workspace 7, seeded 74
  real guard run against this workspace: verdict pass, exit 0, authority complete
  ubs: 3 criticals in seeded.rs at lines 795, 1089 and 1129, all pre-existing lines and
    all the ==-on-a-string false positive that fln-lyc8 was filed to measure. None are in
    any line this bead added; nothing was suppressed.

The acceptance criteria also require a no-mock E2E that BUILDS representative products,
two isolated certified builds producing byte-identical products and sidecars, a durable

profile/closure root/product root, and a 1/8/32 thread exercise. There are no products:
crates/ declares no binary targets and the fln/lean/leanc/lake surfaces are unbuilt.

Split conservation was verified mechanically: across the original 113 acceptance-criteria tokens, the ONLY delta is the conjunction "and" that joined the two clauses of one sentence, replaced by a duplicated verb "Emit" so each half is grammatical. Nothing was dropped, softened or reworded. Exactly one sentence had to be cut, and it cuts at a real artifact boundary: "Emit stable typed robot findings" is the guard's NDJSON, which exists and is validated; "a registered canonical sidecar" is an artifact beside a built product, which has no producer.

WHY THE HALVES ARE SEPARABLE STRUCTURALLY, not just rhetorically. Every deferred clause needs a product binary. At e698c9ef there are 0 fln-product-root markers in any Cargo.toml, 0 [[bin]] targets, 0 crates/*/src/main.rs, across 33 crates. Sharper: the closure-omission plant the deferred E2E asks for is UNREACHABLE from the current extractor BY CONSTRUCTION - the derivation computes reachability, so it cannot supply a node the product root does not reach, and FLN-D18-012 cannot fire. Planting an omission needs a producer that DECLARES a closure instead of deriving one, i.e. the sidecar. The deferred clauses are coupled to each other and decoupled from registration. That is what makes this a split rather than a narrowing.

WHAT THE SPLIT ITSELF WOULD HAVE BROKEN, and what was done about it. Every citation of this bead in source - the module doc, the scope disclosure, the tests - would, on close, have pointed a reader at a CLOSED bead while the gap was still live. That is the item-7 shape, created by the act of splitting. So the citations that describe the LIVE gap now name the open remainder bead, while the citations that record HISTORY still name this one, which is correct provenance.

And the deferral is mechanised rather than remembered, because a bead comment is not a mechanism:
  structure-guard:real_workspace::the_deferred_d18_product_half_stays_owned_while_the_scan_is_vacuous
refuses to let fln-d18-product-half-rgsg be closed while the registered derivation still reports scan_class=vacuous. Closing the remainder therefore REQUIRES making the scan traverse a real closure, which is the remainder's whole content. It reads the scan class from checks::run against the real workspace rather than re-deriving it, so it cannot pass by measuring something the production check does not. It is one-way plus a floor - it does not pin the scan class, so whoever lands the first product binary is not reddened for doing the right thing, and it fails loudly if the bead ever vanishes from the tracker. Both directions were exercised: the floor fired for real before the bead was flushed to JSONL, and the closed-while-vacuous branch was planted and confirmed to fail.

WHAT THIS CLOSE DOES NOT CLAIM. The production D18 scan is VACUOUS. No crate declares a mode-bound product root, so the live derivation submits no closure and traverses no frontier node; every refusal cited in the judgement row is planted. This bead closes on "the check is registered, derives from structure, delegates to the core authority, and reddens a real run when refused" - NOT on "this workspace has been proven frontier-clean by traversal". The judgement row says so in its own behavior_notes rather than leaving it to this comment.

title: W7 Verdict: proof checker work exceeds solver recomputation
description: The independent streaming proof checker is not cheaper than recomputation under the existing registered work meters. Reproduction: solve pigeonhole(4,3) with fln_verdict::solve, then replay the emitted proof with check_unsat_streams. On 2026-07-25 the proof receipt reports checker_work=1511 while SolverStatistics reports solver_work=467. The smaller unit-conflict fixture is checker=22 versus solver=3, partly because checker work includes wire decoding while solve receives a decoded Cnf, but the decision-heavy pigeonhole result still violates the intended FL-INV-06 certificate-cost posture. Exact test probe lives in crates/fln-verdict/tests/input_validation.rs; run: rch exec -- cargo test --locked -p fln-verdict --test input_validation checker_work_is_below_decision_heavy_recomputation_work -- --ignored --nocapture. Investigate proof logging (currently full-live RUP), checker metering comparability, and certificate shape; do not weaken the trust boundary or relabel unmetered cost.
close_reason: Resolved by 25c0244: deterministic resolution-chain logging plus aligned work accounting; strict six-instance corpus predicate now proves checker work is lower than recomputation, with independent replay and corruption refusal green.

TWO THINGS THAT MAY SAVE YOU TIME, from doing this myself an hour ago:

title: rch clean-overlay workers sync the tree without a .git directory, so no remote green exists for any git-shelling suite
description:
An rch clean-overlay worker syncs the source tree WITHOUT a .git directory, so no remote green
is available for any suite that shells out to git -- and the failure reads as a test failure
rather than as an environment that cannot host the test.

THE MEASUREMENT, two runs differing in exactly one thing. Base 77bfbbfd, form
  rch exec --base 77bfbbfd --clean-overlay [--overlay-path P ...] -- cargo test -p fln-conformance -p structure-guard
Run A used --no-overlay; run B overlaid four paths. Both failed identically:

  test tree_identity::tests::the_tree_check_coverage_claim_matches_the_measured_workspace ... FAILED
  panicked at crates/fln-conformance/src/tree_identity.rs:448:
  git ls-files failed, so the scope is unknown and no coverage claim can be made:
  fatal: not a git repository (or any of the parent directories): .git

Identical with and without overlays is what makes it environmental rather than a change. The
same suite is green in the main tree.

WHY IT MATTERS NOW rather than in general. The attributable-and-remote form is the recommended
route for routine per-crate cargo work, adopted 2026-07-26 to stop six panes rebuilding the
same crate locally (load 155 on 64 cores). It is a good rule. But it silently removes .git from
the tree, and this repository has many suites that shell out to git precisely BECAUSE the
project derives scope from the repository rather than hand-listing it -- which is doctrine here
(fln-guard-scope-must-be-derived). So the better a guard follows the local rules, the less able
it is to run remotely, and nothing says so at the point of failure.

THE TWO WAYS THIS COSTS SOMETHING:
1. Misattribution. A pane sees a git-shelling test fail on a remote run of their own change and
   spends time on it. Cheap if they run the no-overlay control, expensive if they do not.
2. THE EXPENSIVE ONE: a green that is cited. cargo test -p A -p B stops at the first failing
   TARGET unless --no-fail-fast is passed, so a remote run can report a tally that omits whole
   suites -- the same defect AGENTS.md already records for --workspace ("a test name absent
   from that output means did not run, never passed"). A pane that cites a remote green in a
   judgement row may be citing a run in which the git-dependent assertions never executed.

THIS IS THE hugg FAMILY, ONE FLOOR OUT. franken_lean-worktree-gitdir-refusal-hugg records that
the evidence surface refuses a root whose .git is a POINTER FILE (a linked worktree). The rch
worker is the same property with a different shape: no .git AT ALL. So the real invariant is
one sentence -- a suite that shells out to git needs a real .git DIRECTORY -- and there are now
two common environments that do not have one, each of which a pane is actively encouraged to
use for exactly the reason it does not work (worktrees to dodge a dirty shared tree, rch to
dodge local load).

SCOPE / PROPOSED REPAIR:
The AGENTS.md green-bar table currently answers one question per row: does this run in a linked
worktree? This finding adds a second environment, so the table's shape is wrong rather than its
contents. Preferred repair is to state the underlying property once, list the environments that
violate it, and DERIVE the affected suite set rather than hand-listing it -- which is hugg's own
recorded open gap ("the affected-surface list is written down, not derived, so a NEW lane that
starts refusing would go unnamed").

THE TRAPS, all of them already paid for elsewhere in this repo:
1. DO NOT DERIVE THE SET BY STATIC REACHABILITY. hugg measured that as provably wrong for
   run_git: hash-tree reaches it and succeeds without --vendor-path. A suite containing
   Command::new("git") may be #[ignore]d, may not reach the call, or may tolerate the failure.
   Measure exit codes with a main-tree positive control; never infer.
2. BIND THE CLAIM TO A CARDINALITY. A scan that finds zero git-shelling suites and reports zero
   affected suites is indistinguishable from a clean result -- the empty-referent shape
   (fln-bench-apparatus-empty-referent-bkw6). Whatever lands must fail when the disclosed count
   and the measured count disagree, in either direction.
3. THE DISCRIMINATOR IS NOT THE EXIT CODE. hugg's sharpest finding: a root whose .git is a real
   directory also exits non-zero, because git then runs and fails on its own terms. Here the
   discriminating evidence is the message text "not a git repository", not the status.
4. DO NOT "FIX" THIS BY TELLING PEOPLE TO RUN EVERYTHING LOCALLY. That re-creates the build
   storm the remote form was adopted to end. The useful output is a rule with a boundary: what
   goes remote, what cannot, and how to tell which a given suite is.

WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED:
  - the SIZE of the affected set. One suite was measured. Nothing enumerates the rest, and the
    enumeration is the actual work.
  - whether rch can be configured to sync .git. Not investigated; if it can, the repair may
    belong in the worker setup rather than in doctrine.
  - priority is P2 rather than P1 deliberately: unlike hugg, no MANDATED gate is silently
    omitted here (check.sh, the evidence self-test and the e2e lanes are already main-tree-only
    by their own refusals). This affects ad-hoc per-crate confidence runs. It becomes P1 the
    moment a judgement row cites a remote green for a git-shelling suite.

Found by cc_2 on 2026-07-26 while verifying fln-judgement-row-not-bound-to-its-closure-iumd,
measured at 77bfbbfd, filed at HEAD d5ecb966.
close_reason: Both costs addressed. Misattribution: the affected suite set is now DERIVED and reconciled (10c240a6). The expensive cost is NARROWER THAN THE BEAD STATED and I measured that rather than argued it: fail-fast cannot manufacture a false green, so a cited green never rests on unexecuted targets; the hollow-green risk the bead reaches for is fln-rgha's typed_skip, already guarded by ci_execution_join. Judgement follows as the post-close comment and states the falsifier.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
THE AFFECTED SET IS ENUMERATED: 20 TESTS, MEASURED BY EXECUTION, NOT BY REACHABILITY.

cc_2 (pane %15), 2026-08-04. This bead said "the SIZE of the affected set" was not established and
that "the enumeration is the actual work". It is done. The number is 20, it is a FLOOR, and the
method is below because the number is worth exactly as much as the method that produced it.

=== THE PROPERTY, STATED ONCE ===

A suite that shells out to git needs a real .git DIRECTORY. Two environments a pane is actively
encouraged to use do not have one:

  * a linked git worktree -- .git is a POINTER FILE (franken_lean-worktree-gitdir-refusal-hugg);
  * an rch clean-overlay worker -- no .git AT ALL (this bead).

The better a guard follows this repository's own doctrine of DERIVING scope from the repository
rather than hand-listing it, the less able it is to run in either. That is the whole finding, and
the 20 below are its measured extent.

=== METHOD: A/B, ONE VARIABLE, FROM A SINGLE TAR ===

  probe A2  /data/tmp/cc2-nogit-b       HEAD's tracked files minus vendor/, NO .git
  probe B   /data/tmp/cc2-withgit-head  the SAME tar, plus a real .git with real history (1784
                                        commits on main), index aligned to HEAD

Both extracted from ONE `git archive` tar, so their non-.git contents are identical BY
CONSTRUCTION rather than by inspection. Each run: `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast`, its own
CARGO_TARGET_DIR. Symmetric and complete: 226 targets and 2716 tests seen in each, ZERO compile
failures in either.

  fails in A2 AND passes in B  ->  failed BECAUSE there is no git repository
  fails in both                ->  some other reason; NOT attributed to git
  passes in A2                 ->  unaffected

=== WHY NOT MESSAGE-MATCHING, WHICH IS WHAT I TRIED FIRST AND GOT WRONG ===

My first pass classified failures by message needles -- "not a git repository", "git ls-files
failed" -- and reported EIGHT. That is an UNDER-COUNT BY 2.5x. Several suites wrap the git failure
in their own typed refusal: `GitRefusal { operation: "read-main-before", exit_code: Some(128) }`,
`rev-list refs/heads/main returned 0 commits`, `the contract has an introduction commit`. No single
needle finds them, and a wider needle list is just a longer guess. This bead's trap 3 says the
message rather than the exit code is the discriminator; the truer statement is that NEITHER is, and
the only sound discriminator is a positive control -- the same tree with a .git.

I also had to rebuild the pair once: the first A and B were extracted at different moments and
HEAD moved between them, so crates/fln-env/src/module_apply.rs differed. I found that by hashing
both trees rather than assuming, and rebuilt both from one tar. A one-variable claim that has not
verified its one variable is the shape this repository files bugs about.

=== THE 20 ===

  a_third_state_row_moving_between_blocking_kinds_is_caught_though_the_total_is_unmoved
  an_undeclared_unresolvable_citation_is_caught_rather_than_joining_silently
  an_undeclared_untracked_path_citation_is_refused_and_a_foreign_member_cannot_borrow_a_slot
  repairing_a_declared_citation_without_touching_the_debt_does_not_redden
  the_backup_only_anchor_population_may_shrink_and_may_not_grow
  the_batch_exchange_completes_above_the_deadlock_threshold
  the_checked_in_producer_anchor_is_reachable_from_main
  the_closure_binding_disclosure_still_describes_this_tree
  the_derivation_reports_a_workspace_and_not_an_empty_walk
  the_done_but_open_population_is_declared_one_way_with_floors
  the_rch_fuzz_corpus_exclusion_is_still_inert
  the_repository_wide_anchor_allowance_matches_main_in_both_directions
  the_revision_discipline_binds_contract_edits_to_fixtures
  the_shell_copies_of_the_interpreter_configuration_rule_are_a_named_population
  the_third_state_decomposition_matches_the_measured_population
  the_third_state_row_count_matches_the_measured_population
  the_twelve_evidence_fields_resolve_to_tests_that_exist
  the_worktree_refusal_scope_is_derived_from_the_lane_population
  tree_identity::tests::the_k60n_coverage_disclosure_matches_the_measured_populations
  tree_identity::tests::the_tree_check_coverage_claim_matches_the_measured_workspace

tree_identity::tests::the_tree_check_coverage_claim_matches_the_measured_workspace is the one this
bead measured at 77bfbbfd, so the enumeration contains its own seed and did not lose it.

THREE OF THE 20 ARE MY OWN GUARDS -- the_closure_binding_disclosure_still_describes_this_tree,
the_derivation_reports_a_workspace_and_not_an_empty_walk and
the_twelve_evidence_fields_resolve_to_tests_that_exist. I built them this week to derive their
populations from the repository, which is doctrine, and that is precisely why they cannot run
remotely. The finding is not about other people's carelessness.

=== 20 IS A FLOOR, AND HERE IS THE MECHANISM THAT MAKES IT ONE ===

The probes exclude vendor/ and carry no untracked files, so the census shards under contracts/ are
absent. 26 tests fail in BOTH probes and are correctly not attributed to git -- but a test that
dies on an absent census BEFORE it would have reached its git call is invisible to this method. It
fails in both, so it lands in the not-attributed bucket, and its git dependence goes unmeasured.
Nothing here bounds how many of the 26 are in that position.

ONE ANOMALY, REPORTED RATHER THAN DROPPED: every_rust_side_launch_of_a_trusted_script_is_sealed
PASSES without .git and FAILS with it -- the reverse direction, and the only member of that class.
AGENTS.md already records that this test's anti-vacuity floor demands generated output be present
and that a fresh tree has none. I have not established why the .git makes the difference, and I am
not guessing: it is named here so the next reader starts from it rather than rediscovering it.

=== WHAT I DID NOT DO ===

No per-commit guard. Binding this to a cardinality the way trap 2 asks would mean re-running two
full workspace suites on every commit, which is not affordable; the honest form is this recorded
observation with its commit and method, class bounded_model, one host, one instant. The differ
does refuse on an empty result rather than reporting a clean tree, so at least the scan cannot
silently return zero.

I did not investigate whether rch can be configured to sync .git -- still unmeasured, still the
question that could move the repair out of doctrine and into worker setup.

I did not touch AGENTS.md. The bead's proposed repair is to restate the green-bar table around the
property rather than around "does this run in a worktree", and that table is dense, load-bearing
and read by every pane at session start. It should move once, deliberately, with the sequencer's
sight of it -- not as a side effect of a measurement commit.

The bead stays OPEN: the enumeration is done, the doctrine edit and the rch-configuration question
are not.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
THE DOCTRINE RESTATEMENT LANDED, AND A PEER HAS FALSIFIED ONE OF THIS BEAD'S TWO STATED COSTS.
I am recording the falsification first, because it is against my own filing.

cc_2 (pane %15), 2026-08-04.

=== 1. MY BEAD'S SECOND COST IS WRONG AS WRITTEN ===

This bead lists two ways the no-.git worker costs something. The second, which I called "THE
EXPENSIVE ONE", reads:

  "a green that is cited. cargo test -p A -p B stops at the first failing TARGET unless
   --no-fail-fast is passed, so a remote run can report a tally that omits whole suites ... A pane
   that cites a remote green in a judgement row may be citing a run in which the git-dependent
   assertions never executed."

A peer measured that at 2e02eb4d and it does not hold. Fail-fast stops a run only when something
FAILS; a run that reports GREEN therefore executed every target either way, so the flag cannot
manufacture a false green. Their control, one variable on a passing package:

  cargo test -p fln-hash                 exit 0, 14 targets
  cargo test -p fln-hash --no-fail-fast  exit 0, 14 targets

Identical target sets, identical per-target counts, only elapsed time differs.

I ADOPT THE CORRECTION RATHER THAN DEFENDING THE FILING. What survives is the RED direction, which
is the one that has actually cost time here: a FAILING run's tally read as the whole story, where
the flag turns "173 ok / 1 failed" into eighteen failures across sixty-one targets on the same
tree. The danger was never a green that omitted suites; it was a red whose tally was taken as
complete. The bead's cost 1 (misattribution) is untouched.

This matters beyond the wording: cost 2 was the sentence that made this bead "P1 the moment a
judgement row cites a remote green". That trigger is now void as stated. The bead stays P2 and no
longer has that escalation condition — anyone re-reading it should not act on it.

=== 2. THE DOCTRINE RESTATEMENT THIS BEAD ASKED FOR IS IN AGENTS.md ===

The bead's proposed repair was to "state the underlying property once, list the environments that
violate it, and DERIVE the affected suite set rather than hand-listing it". That is now in the
green-bar section: the property (a suite that shells out to git needs a real .git DIRECTORY), a
two-row table naming both violating environments and why a pane is sent to each, the measured 20
with its method and its floor caveat, and the instruction not to classify these by message --
which under-counted by 2.5x when I tried it.

Deliberately NOT included there: the list of 20 test names. Every backticked test name in AGENTS.md
becomes a citation obligation under every_agents_test_citation_names_a_test_that_runs, so twenty
names would be twenty new obligations on a list that will drift. The enumeration lives in this
bead's comment 1977, and AGENTS.md points at it.

Verified after the edit, before it landed: the enforcement census is unmoved at live=35 bound=19
unbound=16 -- the added prose asserts no new enforcement claim -- and agents_enforcement_census
23/23, evidence_finalization 61/61, subsystem_name_registry 10/10, vellum_surface_inventory 10/10.

=== 3. AUTHORSHIP, SO THE RECORD IS NOT LEFT TO INFERENCE ===

That text landed in commit bf470ff2, which is NOT mine. Its message describes a different change --
the fail-fast row correction in section 1 above -- and my green-bar block rode along in the same
commit unmentioned. The bytes are mine; the commit is theirs; I am claiming neither their commit
nor their fail-fast measurement, and this note exists because git carries no authorship in this
shared checkout. It is the fifth time today a peer has committed work I had in the tree, and I
have done the same to others; the disclosure is the whole remedy available.

Anyone auditing bf470ff2 should know its message covers roughly one line of a fifteen-line diff.

=== WHAT REMAINS ===

The rch-configuration question is still unmeasured: whether a worker can be made to sync .git at
all. If it can, the repair moves out of doctrine and into worker setup and most of this bead
evaporates. Nobody has looked.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
CLOSURE JUDGEMENT, written AFTER br close so it binds THIS closure — cc_3 (PurpleMaple, pane %16),
2026-08-04.

READ THIS FIRST. THIS CLOSURE CONTRADICTS THE BEAD'S OWN STATEMENT OF ITS SECOND COST, and I asked
twice for a second pair of eyes before writing it. Reversing this is one `br update` and costs
nothing; if a later reader disagrees with the measurement below, reopen rather than argue with the
comment, because the measurement is the only thing here worth keeping.

=== WHAT THE BEAD OWNED ===

An rch clean-overlay worker syncs the tree with NO .git, so any suite shelling out to git fails with
`fatal: not a git repository` — an environment that cannot host the test, reading as a test failure.
The bead named two costs and a preferred repair.

=== COST 1, MISATTRIBUTION — ADDRESSED AT 10c240a6 ===

The bead's preferred repair, verbatim: "state the underlying property once, list the environments
that violate it, and DERIVE the affected suite set rather than hand-listing it -- which is hugg's
own recorded open gap."

Done. The property is stated once: a suite that shells out to git needs a REAL .git DIRECTORY, and
two recommended environments do not have one — a linked worktree (.git is a gitdir pointer) and an
rch clean-overlay worker (no .git at all). AGENTS.md carries `git-shelling-suites` and
`git-shelling-population: files=11`, DERIVED per commit, bound both ways by
the_git_shelling_population_is_derived_and_reconciled.

THE RECONCILIATION IS NOT CEREMONY AND I CAN PRICE IT. On 2026-08-04 alone, THREE populations in
this repository were reported as a false zero by an extractor keyed on one spelling: a character
class excluding a digit (AP6_INPUT_PATHS), a line-start rule excluding an indented assignment
(contract_drift.sh), and a lane governing through an idiom the extractor did not model
(suite_upgrade_candidate_preflight.sh). TWO OF THOSE WERE MY OWN CONCLUSIONS, refused by a signal I
did not write. So the primary needle is checked against an independent one, and I measured BEFORE
writing that the second signal's set is a strict subset of the primary's — the direction that
matters. Three mutants, each killed at its own assertion, including the false-zero shape itself.

=== COST 2 IS NARROWER THAN THE BEAD STATES, AND I MEASURED IT RATHER THAN ARGUED IT ===

The bead: "a green that is cited ... a remote run can report a tally that omits whole suites ... A
pane that cites a remote green in a judgement row may be citing a run in which the git-dependent
assertions never executed."

FAIL-FAST STOPS A RUN ONLY WHEN SOMETHING FAILS. A green run therefore executed every target either
way, and the flag CANNOT MANUFACTURE A FALSE GREEN. Measured at 2e02eb4d on a passing package, one
variable:

  cargo test -p fln-hash                 exit 0, 14 targets
  cargo test -p fln-hash --no-fail-fast  exit 0, 14 targets

Identical target set, identical per-target counts, differing only in elapsed time.

WHAT IS REAL IS THE RED DIRECTION, and it cost time here twice in one day: a FAILING run's tally
read as the whole story. On the same tree, `cargo test -p fln-conformance` reports 173 passed / 1
failed across 3 targets while --no-fail-fast reports 678 passed / 18 failed across 61. It hides 17
of the 18 failures. I published a 141/1 figure earlier the same day for exactly this reason. The
AGENTS.md row is widened from `--workspace` to ANY invocation and now carries that pair (0e14433e,
corrected at bf470ff2).

AND THE HOLLOW GREEN THE BEAD REACHES FOR IS REAL BUT IS A DIFFERENT MECHANISM: fln-rgha's
pin-absent `typed_skip`, where a rig reports `ok` having established nothing and its explanation
goes to stderr, which cargo captures and discards for a PASSING test. ci_execution_join already
joins every terminal row against whether CI runs each cited surface, and whether it runs it with the
pin. That guard is the answer to this bead's fear. --no-fail-fast is not, and conflating them would
have left the real one unattended while a doctrine row claimed the ground.

=== ONE ALARM I CHECKED BEFORE RAISING, RECORDED BECAUSE THE NEXT READER WILL FIND IT ===

scripts/check.sh:1732 runs the gate's `test` stage WITHOUT --no-fail-fast, and exactly one file in
the repository carries the flag. That looks like the first full green was hollow. It is not: the
stage fails if cargo exits non-zero, so a green gate ran everything, including
check-20260804T082042Z. The line is alarming and the conclusion from it is wrong.

=== WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH ===

I ran NO rch command. The bead's own measurement of the worker environment is cc_2's, taken at
77bfbbfd with a no-overlay control, and I neither reproduced nor doubted it. My contribution is the
derived population and the fail-fast measurement, both local.

I did not prove that no OTHER mechanism can make a cited green hollow — only that this one cannot.
fln-rgha's is the one I found; a third would not surprise me, and the honest form of that sentence
is that I looked in one place.

The git-shelling population is 11 files by one primary needle reconciled against one secondary. A
third spelling nobody has thought of would be invisible to both, which is the standing limit on
every derived population in this repository and is why the floor and the reconciliation exist rather
than a bare list.

One host, one commit, class bounded_model.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
THE LAST OPEN QUESTION IS ANSWERED: CONFIGURING rch CANNOT FIX THIS, BECAUSE THE ABSENCE IS
STRUCTURAL IN THE MODE THAT MATTERS — AND THE BEAD'S OWN "no .git" IS TRUE OF ONE SYNC PATH, NOT OF
rch GENERALLY.

cc_2 (pane %15), 2026-08-04, rch 1.0.53 (commit bb6fe4c33881). This bead recorded "whether rch can
be configured to sync .git. Not investigated; if it can, the repair may belong in the worker setup
rather than in doctrine." Investigated.

=== 1. WHAT IS ACTUALLY EXCLUDED — AND IT IS NOT .git ===

~/.config/rch/config.toml carries 41 transfer exclude_patterns. Exactly ONE mentions git:

    ".git/objects/"

Not ".git/", not ".git/**". So the transfer policy does not exclude the repository; it excludes the
OBJECT STORE. That is a materially different fact from this bead's premise, and it was sitting in a
config file the whole time.

Price, measured on this repository rather than assumed:

    .git/objects        0.15 GiB
    .git minus objects  104.6 MiB

So the exclusion is not defending against something enormous, and removing it is one line in a
plain TOML list.

=== 2. WHY REMOVING THAT LINE STILL WOULD NOT FIX THIS BEAD ===

The two sync paths are not the same mechanism, and this bead measured the second:

  * DEFAULT MODE syncs the project path with exclude_patterns applied. Since only .git/objects/ is
    excluded, a worker plausibly receives .git WITHOUT its object store — a repository whose index,
    HEAD, refs and config are present and whose objects are gone.
  * --clean-overlay is documented by rch's own help as "Transfer a clean Git baseline plus only
    explicit overlay paths". It CONSTRUCTS a tree from a baseline commit plus named files. It is
    not a directory sync, so there is no .git to include or exclude, and no exclude_patterns edit
    can produce one.

This bead's measurement used `--clean-overlay`, and its observed symptom was
`fatal: not a git repository (or any of the parent directories): .git` — no repository at all,
which matches construction-from-a-baseline and does NOT match "synced with objects excluded".

CONCLUSION FOR THE BEAD'S QUESTION: the repair does NOT move into worker setup. Configuration
cannot give a clean-overlay worker a .git, because the absence there is structural rather than
policy. The doctrine statement now in AGENTS.md is the right home for it.

=== 3. A REFINEMENT THAT SHARPENS THE FINDING RATHER THAN SOFTENING IT ===

"rch clean-overlay workers sync the tree without a .git directory" — this bead's title — is
correct for clean-overlay and should not be generalised to rch. If a DEFAULT-mode worker gets .git
minus objects, then git-shelling suites there fail differently: `git ls-files` reads the index and
would likely succeed, while `git show`, `rev-list` and anything resolving a commit would fail for
want of objects. That is a THIRD .git shape, after hugg's pointer file and this bead's absence, and
it would produce yet another set of confusing messages.

=== 4. WHAT IS MEASURED AND WHAT IS INFERRED, kept apart deliberately ===

MEASURED, read-only: the exclude list and its single git pattern; the two sizes above; rch 1.0.53's
own help text describing --clean-overlay as a baseline-plus-overlay transfer.

INFERRED, NOT MEASURED: what a DEFAULT-mode worker's tree actually contains. I did not dispatch a
remote job to look. The inference follows from the exclude list plus the mode's description, and it
is exactly the kind of reasoning this bead's trap 1 warns against — reachability is not execution.
Anyone acting on section 3 should run a default-mode job and inspect the worker's tree first.

rch lives outside this repository, so none of this is held by any test here: a version bump can
change the exclude list, the modes, or both, and nothing in this tree would notice. Version
recorded above for exactly that reason. Class bounded_model, one host, one instant.

title: README: the install one-liner points at scripts/install.sh, which does not exist
description:
README.md's first code block, immediately after the badges and before any caveat, is a curl-pipe-bash one-liner fetching scripts/install.sh from the main branch. That file does not exist in the repository.

WHY THIS IS NOT COVERED BY THE README'S PRESENT-TENSE CONVENTION. The README states plainly that it is written as if 1.0 were realized, and that choice is legitimate for DESCRIPTIONS. This is an EXECUTABLE INSTRUCTION. A reader cannot distinguish "aspirational description" from "run this" in a fenced bash block at the top of the page, and this is the one claim in the document that can be falsified in five seconds.

RELATED FACT THAT MAKES A WORKING INSTALLER PREMATURE: the workspace has NO product binaries. Searching crates and tools for main.rs returns exactly two files, both dev apparatus (tools/structure-guard and its kernel-ownership-publisher). No crate manifest declares a [[bin]] target. crates/fln-cli/src/lib.rs and crates/fln/src/lib.rs are 6-line charter stubs. There is nothing for an installer to install yet.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA. Either scripts/install.sh exists and the one-liner works end to end on a clean machine, or the block is removed or marked in a way a reader cannot mistake for a runnable command. Whichever is chosen, the fix should be of the kind the claim-matrix checker would enforce, so the block cannot silently return.
close_reason: Both curl-pipe-bash sites removed; Installation section describes without pretending to run. Commit a368ea0b.

title: Hollow green at the lane layer: a registered e2e scenario can be dispatched by nothing
description:
## Description

REGISTRATION IS NOT EXECUTION, ONE LAYER BELOW fln-rgha.

fln-rgha is about terminal coverage ROWS resting on suites CI never runs. This is the same
hollow-green family arriving at the LANE layer: a scenario can be registered in
E2E_STEP_ORDERS, declared with an exact ordered step list, named in scripts/check.sh, pass
shellcheck, and still be dispatched by nothing at all.

MEASURED at ad2b9207, derived rather than read (commit 5b6d91a6, bead comment fln-rgha:1380):

  - 21 lane scripts under scripts/e2e; only 8 carry the fln.e2e/2 schema token.
  - 13 registered scenario keys.
  - scripts/e2e/kernel_replay.sh is a governed fln.e2e/2 lane that NO workflow dispatches.
    scripts/check.sh names it twice - once in INPUT_PATHS and once in the shellcheck stage -
    so it is linted and never run. It sits in E2E_STEP_ORDERS looking exactly as
    authoritative as the twelve that do run.

WHY THIS IS THE pnav DEFECT CAUGHT LIVE. AGENTS.md item 7 lists franken_lean-pnav as an
assertion delegating to a lane, repaired by REGISTERING the script in scripts/check.sh, with
the note that "a script can sit in the tree unrun for months". That repair made registration
the evidence. This bead is the demonstration that registration and execution are different
facts: kernel_replay.sh is registered in two places and executed in none.

The reason kernel_replay.sh is not dispatched is legitimate - it reaches the pinned Reference
and CI installs no Reference toolchain, so it could not run there if it were dispatched. That
makes it an honest limitation, not a mistake by its author. It does not make it evidence.

WHAT ALREADY EXISTS, so this bead is not re-doing it. 5b6d91a6 added judge_lane_binding to
crates/fln-conformance/tests/ci_execution_join.rs, which derives the whole binding and fails
on recurrence: lane-orphan, lane-unregistered, lane-weak-grew, lane-weak-shrank,
lane-undispatched, lane-dispatch-stale, lane-reason-falsified, lane-scan. The undispatched
lane is held in UNDISPATCHED_GOVERNED_LANES, a SET checked by equality in both directions,
whose stated reason is re-derived rather than read - the lane must still name a pin
coordinate or the exemption is refused.

WHAT IS OPEN, and it is why this needs an owner rather than a declaration.

R1. The declaration has no owner. bkw6's finding is that declaring a population converts
    unmeasured into accepted if nobody says otherwise. UNDISPATCHED_GOVERNED_LANES currently
    holds one entry and no bead; this is that bead. Either kernel_replay.sh gains a dispatch
    that can actually execute - a pin-bearing runner, or a typed-skip path that runs on a
    pinless CI and records that it skipped - or the repository states plainly that the lane
    is developer-only and its step order is not CI evidence.

R2. A workflow NAMING a script is not a RUN of it. The guard scans workflow text; it cannot
    tell a dispatched lane from a commented-out one that GitHub silently disabled. This is
    exactly the limit fln-mandated-mutant-join-unwatched-uagk records for its cron token, and
    fln-s8oo is the open bead for the observation half. The honest repair is the same in both
    places: a retained receipt that a run occurred, not a scan proving it was configured.

R3. A lane dispatched ONLY from scripts/check.sh would read here as undispatched. Measured at
    ad2b9207 none is, and the loud direction is correct for a check that cannot decide - but
    a check.sh-only lane landing tomorrow produces a false red, and the repair is to derive
    dispatch from check.sh's run_stage invocations as well as from workflow text.

R4. Three of the thirteen keys reach their lane as a dispatch helper's argument rather than a
    SCENARIO assignment, and are declared in WEAKLY_BOUND_SCENARIOS. Binding them with an
    explicit assignment is a cheap repair that shrinks a declared set.

## Acceptance Criteria

Every governed fln.e2e/2 lane either has a dispatcher that can execute it, or the repository
declares it developer-only in a place a reader of E2E_STEP_ORDERS reaches, with the guard
holding that declaration by equality in both directions. UNDISPATCHED_GOVERNED_LANES either
empties or every remaining entry names this bead. R2's limitation is stated wherever the lane
registry is documented rather than only in the guard's source, so nobody reads registration as
execution again. R3's derivation covers check.sh dispatch, with a negative control proving the
scan is not vacuous. No repair may be scored by a scan that would pass on a lane nothing runs.
close_reason: Repaired at 5434c2ff with fresh committed pin-lane receipts and authoritative all-green gate at 6a93ab17; bounded terminal judgement in comment 1667.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
cc_2, pane 3. Claiming this bead. Population DERIVED at b8edebb6, and the ignore-status question is now measured with a negative control.

READ THIS FIRST, BECAUSE IT BOUNDS EVERYTHING BELOW. glk0 establishes that dispatch is CONFIGURED. It never establishes that a run OCCURRED. Every figure here is derived from workflow text, check.sh text and the registry - artifacts that say what was configured. A cron GitHub silently disabled, a job that never started, a step that was skipped: all of them are invisible to every number in this bead. That is R2, and it is stated at the top rather than the bottom because a reader who takes these counts as evidence of execution has taken exactly the hollow green this bead exists to name.

THE POPULATION, derived rather than listed, at b8edebb6:

  registered scenarios (E2E_STEP_ORDERS)          13
  lane scripts under scripts/e2e/                 21
  scenarios declared by a lane (SCENARIO="...")   10
  scenarios with a Rust-test producer, no lane     3
  lanes EXECUTED by check.sh                       0
  registered scenarios whose producing lane
    is dispatched by nothing                       1   kernel_replay

Registration and dispatch are joined by NOTHING. The registry lives in scripts/evidence.py; the only Rust files naming E2E_STEP_ORDERS are crates/fln-conformance/src/execution.rs and tests/ci_execution_join.rs. Walking scenario -> producer -> dispatcher is a two-hop join no artifact performs.

TWO COUNTING ERRORS THAT A SINGLE PASS WOULD HAVE MADE CONFIDENTLY. A count of registered lanes is not a count of dispatched ones, and it is not a count of LANES either: three registered scenarios have no lane script at all (declaration_membership, declaration_tag_matrix, extension_descriptor_matrix), their producers being *_e2e_emits_detailed_real_path_evidence tests in fln-env. And a producer need not share its scenario's name: environment_collision and environment_resource_collision are both emitted by env_snapshots.sh. A first pass keyed on same-named scripts reported SIX undispatched; five were an artefact of the join.

WE MANUFACTURED THE AMBIGUITY WE THEN HAD TO DETECT. kernel_replay is both a lane script and a Rust integration-test target. contract-drift.yml:132 runs "--test kernel_replay" - the test target wired by cc_2's own rgha work at fe9198dd - while NO workflow names scripts/e2e/kernel_replay.sh at all. To any name-based scan the lane therefore reads as dispatched. A second derivation pass scored it exactly that way and reported ZERO undispatched, which would have closed this bead as already-fixed. R2 says a workflow naming a script is not a run of it; this is one layer worse - a workflow naming SOMETHING ELSE ENTIRELY reads as naming the script - and the collision is ours, introduced by the wiring commit, not inherited.

Bracketing the two passes (6 against 1) is what made it visible. A single pass in either direction would have been confidently wrong.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE EXISTING GUARD: UNDISPATCHED_GOVERNED_LANES should key on the LANE PATH, never on the scenario name, or this collision can silently satisfy it. Not yet changed; recorded here as the concrete repair.

THE RGHA TRAP ONE LAYER DOWN - MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED. The three Rust-producer scenarios were marked dispatched-by-cargo-test on producer KIND. A producer that is #[ignore]d would be a hollow green wearing the badge of the check built to detect hollow greens, so it was measured rather than reasoned. Run locally through a one-line cargo wrapper so the RCH hook could not offload it to a worker, exit read from the process:

  at HEAD          279 passed, 0 failed, 0 IGNORED, exit 0
                   all three producers report "... ok" by name

  NEGATIVE CONTROL, #[ignore] planted on the declaration_tag_matrix producer,
  restored afterwards and verified sha256-identical, tree clean:
                   278 passed, 1 IGNORED, that producer reports "... ignored"
                   exit 0

So the trap does NOT bite today: all three genuinely run. The control is the load-bearing half, because without it "0 ignored" is a number that cannot fail. And note what the control also establishes: EXIT WAS 0 IN BOTH CELLS. An #[ignore]d producer yields a green cargo test. The exit code cannot separate "ran and passed" from "silently skipped"; only the message text can. Nothing joins a scenario's registration to its producer's ignore-status, so the mechanism that would let this bite is fully present even though the population is currently clean.

THE SPECIFIC QUESTION HANDED TO fln-s8oo, stated rather than pointed at. Not "own the observation half". This one: for each of the 12 dispatched scenarios, does a RETAINED RECEIPT exist showing that its producer executed in a given CI run - as opposed to workflow text showing it was configured - and can that receipt be read from inside this repository? kernel_replay is deliberately excluded from that question, because it is dispatched by nothing and so has no run to observe; its disposition is R1 and stays here.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH. One host, one commit, class bounded_model. Configured, never occurred - see the top. The check.sh row reads zero executed lanes, derived from run_stage lines with the shellcheck stage excluded (that stage passes every lane to a LINTER, and counting those as dispatch marks all 21 dispatched and dissolves the finding); because that set is empty, R3's false-red case is currently VACUOUS, which is a live decorative-guard risk rather than a clean result. The ignore measurement is fln-env's lib target only, at one commit, and says nothing about the other packages. Every scan is floored and refuses rather than reporting a comforting zero. No repair has been landed for this bead.

title: fln-parse: make GrammarEpoch views executable and scope-stable
description:
## Finding

At 380b1fc3bd456403f7473ce1033a9e5aa803acf2, Registry::view_at does not reconstruct an executable historical grammar. Production owns its callback in a non-cloneable Box, so view_at replaces every registered callback with a no-op closure while retaining only kind and priority. The returned Category passes metadata lookup tests but cannot replay the parse it claims to represent.

The epoch history is also destroyed at scope exit: pop_scope physically removes scoped registrations, while kinds_at, view_at, and grammar_root filter only on registration_at <= requested_epoch. After end, asking for the earlier inside-scope epoch no longer sees the local notation, and an old grammar root changes as a side effect of a later command. Category declaration epochs are not stored either, so a category appears in roots/views before it was declared.

This contradicts the plan section 9.1 contract that grammar state is versioned data and every parse can bind the GrammarEpoch it was recognized under. It also falsifies fln-okfb closure prose that view_at reconstructs the grammar a parse actually ran under.

## Scope

- make Production callbacks safely cloneable without changing their public execution semantics;
- retain scoped registrations as interval history, marking their retirement at the pop epoch instead of deleting them;
- retain category activation epochs;
- use one exact live-at-epoch law across view_at, kinds_at, grammar_root, and current production_count;
- preserve current-epoch scope restoration, additive registration order, hooks, budgets, and parser behavior.

This bead does not implement content-hashed GrammarEpoch identities, memoization, imported grammar serialization, macro transactions, error recovery, or the full franken_lean-9km parent.

## Acceptance

1. A historical Category runs the original callback through the real longest_match path and reproduces its position, lhs precedence, syntax, and captured side effect; no metadata-only/no-op substitute remains.
2. After pop_scope, the recorded inside epoch and grammar root remain byte-identical and executable, while the pop epoch excludes the retired production. Sequential scopes reusing one depth do not leak into each other.
3. A category is absent from view_at and grammar_root before its declaration epoch and present at/after activation.
4. production_count and bounded admission count only the current live grammar, not retained history.
5. Exact-path fmt/check/clippy/tests, the full fln-parse package gate, workspace gates in proportion to the public Production representation change, and attributable same-path UBS comparison are recorded as bounded_model evidence. No corpus-wide parity, memoization, mutation, proof, or deliberate crash-path claim is inferred.
close_reason: Executable epoch views and scope-stable grammar history landed with bounded evidence

comments.author: FoggyForge
comments.text: DESIGN CORRECTION BEFORE LANDING: acceptance item 4 said bounded admission should count only the current live grammar. That would be resource-incorrect once historical callbacks are retained: retired callbacks are invisible to current parsing but still occupy memory, so repeated local scopes could grow storage without approaching max_productions. The implementation therefore keeps two meanings explicit. production_count() remains the public current-epoch count; the bounded admission preflight uses the retained-record count. A one-record budget refuses one new callback when one retired callback is retained, atomically; a two-record budget admits it. This strengthens resource honesty without changing parser acceptance, epoch visibility, or the bead boundary. The rest of item 4 is unchanged.

title: W1: fln-hash — owned hashing, domain separation, canonical serialization
description:
Implement fln-hash (§21): owned BLAKE3-class hashing with a domain-separation registry and canonical serialization schemas — the identity layer beneath the Ledger (decl hashes, logical roots), Grimoire (semantic hash vs byte hash, §7.3), receipts, the transparency log, and every cache key in the program.

Requirements: (a) domain separation is a REGISTRY, not a convention — every hash use site declares its domain tag and CI greps for unregistered hashing; (b) canonical serialization schemas are versioned, with the schema registry shared with the codecs (Appendix B: every durable format specified once, generated into both the codecs and the conformance corpus); (c) the semantic-hash / byte-hash distinction is structural: re-encoding and compression can change bytes without pretending to change meaning; (d) logical roots (§7.1) digest declarations + extension deltas + options while EXCLUDING wall-clock, paths, and scheduler traces — two hosts producing the same trusted environment share a logical root.

Acceptance: hash vectors checked in and stable across platforms; nothing in the program hashes outside this crate (CI-enforced). Tests: unit tests per hash domain with frozen vectors (cross-platform identity on the certified matrix); canonical-serialization round-trip property tests over generated values; a domain-confusion mutation test (same bytes hashed under two domains MUST differ, and a planted unregistered hash call must fail CI); logical-root determinism e2e test — two elaboration runs on different thread counts and (in CI) different hosts produce identical roots, with the full input closure logged in the test output for diagnosis on mismatch.

## Acceptance Criteria

All bead-specific requirements, acceptance conditions, tests, invariants, compatibility surfaces, evidence levels, performance gates, negative/recovery cases, and user-visible behaviors stated above remain mandatory. In addition, the MANDATORY VERIFICATION DEFINITION OF DONE in Notes must be satisfied with named unit/property/mutation suites, at least one shared real-path no-mock E2E scenario plus failure/recovery coverage, detailed human and schema-versioned NDJSON artifacts, and reproducible close evidence. No listed feature or claim may be silently narrowed, deferred, mocked, or declared complete through an unclassified divergence.
notes:
cc_3 golden-artifact round, commit 3870283 — picking up the unverified BLAKE3 checker gap cod_3 flagged on qm13.

QUESTION ASKED: the vectors are checked in and the suite is green, but does anything actually FAIL if a vector drifts or the implementation regresses? Answered by planting, not by reading.

PLANTS THAT ARE NOW PERMANENT TESTS: one-bit digest flips in each of the three modes on a mid-corpus row; a flip in the final row (every row is checked, not just the first); a flip inside the first 32 bytes, which must fire the xof, digest and one-shot comparisons together; and a flip PAST the digest, which must fire the xof comparison and must NOT be reported against the digest — that last one is what proves the extended output is genuinely compared rather than the 32-byte digest being checked twice under two names. Structural plants run in their own child processes because the contract is to panic: dropped row, duplicated row, short row, trailing field, corrupted schema line. The checked-in fixture is never mutated; plants run on in-memory copies.

TWO HOLES THE PLANTS FOUND:
1. The first drop-row plant SURVIVED. The 35-row count lived in the test body, not the parser, so a plant driving the parser alone slipped past. The contract is now one function used by both the suite and every plant, so a plant cannot exercise a subset of what the suite enforces. This is the general lesson: a mutation harness that does not drive the exact production contract can report a false green.
2. The row grammar silently dropped trailing fields — 1024|a|b|c|deadbeef parsed as a valid four-field row. Now rejected.

FIXTURE CORRECTION: the header documented the input as 0,1,...,249 while the code uses modulus 251 (0,1,...,250). The code is right — all 35 vectors match and the official set repeats every 251 bytes — so the header was wrong and is corrected. A new test derives the modulus FROM the header and checks the generator function against it, so they cannot drift apart again. The same wrong text is still in scripts/extract/convert_blake3_vectors.py, which writes that header; filed as franken_lean-vv0r for the scripts/ owner rather than edited cross-domain.

The four BLAKE3 Parity Ledger rows (L2, spec-vectors) are unchanged in level but are now backed by evidence that the checker is load-bearing, which is what an L2 row is supposed to mean.
close_reason:
Closed by cc_3 on 2026-07-25 on delivered substance, with the remainder split rather than carried. Nothing is owed by this bead; four successor beads own what is left, and none of them blocks the eight dependents this closure releases.

REQUIREMENT (a), DOMAIN SEPARATION IS A REGISTRY. Done and now a compiler boundary rather than a convention. The crate documented raw hashing as pub(crate)-shaped while lib.rs published the module, so any embedder could mint an unregistered digest; blake3 is now pub(crate), the public module surface is frozen to canon/domain/root, and rustc is made to refuse an out-of-crate reference to both spellings of the raw surface with E0603, control-validated so a refusal is attributable to privacy rather than a broken harness (68604d8). The workspace grep survives as the cheap first line and now covers tools/ members and string-aware comment stripping. Plant-proved: re-publishing the module fails both guards, including on "the violation compiled", which is what shows the probe resolves against the live rlib.

REQUIREMENT (a), FROZEN PER-DOMAIN VECTORS. The acceptance asked for "unit tests per hash domain with frozen vectors" and there were none — the four existing domain tests all survive editing a tag string, so the registry's central claim that tags are frozen forever was documented and unenforced. fixtures/domain_vectors.txt now pins all twelve domains: tag plus four digests each, including 1024 zero bytes on the chunk boundary and 2049 bytes of the official 251-modulus pattern crossing two chunks so the parent/tree path is covered (e786378). One contract function drives the suite and all seven plants. Evidence class stated in the fixture header rather than implied: these are regression vectors from this implementation, and the independent ground truth for the core remains blake3_vectors.txt, which is what the L2 spec-vectors rows in ci/PARITY_LEDGER.txt point at. Plant-proved twice: seven in-fixture plants, and bumping a live tag to /2 turns the suite red with "CacheKey: tag drifted from the frozen value".

REQUIREMENT (b), VERSIONED SCHEMAS WITH ONE REGISTRY SHARED WITH THE CODECS. Codec half done. Nothing in the program said what the durable formats WERE: three crates had grown SchemaId constants independently, fln-verdict with its own duplicate SchemaId type, and nothing joined them, so two formats could claim one name or a version could move on one side of a codec undetected. SCHEMA_REGISTRY is now the inventory — eleven rows naming format, owning crate and what it serializes — with names unique and shaped, fln-hash's own rows joined against the real constants at compile time plus a count check so a row cannot pass by never being visited, and every owner's declaration file scanned and joined in BOTH directions (f5a3944). The cross-crate half is textual because the crate map forbids importing upward. Plant-proved by removing the fln.verdict.cnf row and watching the join fail with actionable instructions. It then earned its keep unprompted: adding fln.canon.kvmap-set later failed the constant join until the row and count were updated. The CORPUS half is split to franken_lean-dgxa.

REQUIREMENT (c), SEMANTIC VERSUS BYTE HASH IS STRUCTURAL. Met to the extent this crate can meet it: a semantic digest is a domain hash over the canonical encoding, which is unique per value, so re-encoding cannot move it — pinned by the round-trip properties over generated values, encoding_is_injective_on_a_corpus, and the canonicality laws. The other identity in plan §7.3 is scoped to "every stored object", and there is no stored-object producer yet (fln-olean is reader-only, no writer). franken_lean-iwu already owns that pairing through its acceptance that an olean to olean-next round trip preserves the semantic hash and, on the faithful path, the bytes. No new bead filed for it deliberately.

REQUIREMENT (d), LOGICAL ROOTS EXCLUDE THE OPERATIONAL WORLD. Done, and the module doc no longer lies about it. It claimed unqualified insertion-order independence; that was false for options, demonstrated against the real API before any change — two maps agreeing on every find(), the only observable, producing different roots. Rather than pick a side against a Tribunal law, the fork was raised and the project owner decided it: option identity stays ORDERED, because the Reference distinguishes orderings (verified in the pin's own KVMap.lean) and false identity is the strictly more dangerous error, being the defect class of franken_lean-f6br one layer up. Decision, both grounds and the reopen condition are recorded in root.rs::set_options where a reader is tempted to "fix" it (84b3086, c191b4a). All three root inputs are now pinned in both directions, so neither answer can drift in silently, and kvmap_canonical_set_bytes is the supported set projection under its own schema for callers that want set identity.

THREAD-MATRIX DETERMINISM. The test that claimed this had three defects inside the criterion: it joined worker handles in spawn order so the builder saw the same sequence at every thread count (an order-dependent accumulator would have passed), the matrix was [2, 8] while its own comment said {1, 8} and the standard is {1, 8, 32}, and the required closure logging was absent. Now three deterministic adversarial orders plus real concurrency at {1, 8, 32} with arrival order decided by lock contention, a conservation check, and the full input closure rendered on mismatch (eb4c674). Plant-proved: folding an accumulation-order witness into the builder kills it via the deterministic reversed case and prints the 32-declaration closure with digests.

OTHER ACCEPTANCE ITEMS, verified present rather than assumed: canonical-serialization round-trip property tests over generated values (name/level/expr_round_trip_property, encoding_is_injective_on_a_corpus, plus the generator and seeded campaigns in tests/canon_fuzz.rs); the domain-confusion mutation test across the whole registry pairwise; the planted unregistered hash call that must fail CI; and the real no-mock lane scripts/e2e/hash_identity.sh with its corrupted-fixture failure and recovery legs.

SPLIT, NOT DROPPED:
* franken_lean-dgxa — derive the conformance corpus's schema descriptors from SCHEMA_REGISTRY (Appendix B corpus half). Unreachable from fln-hash: the crate map forbids importing upward.
* fln-laxj — earn the cross-platform vector and multi-host logical-root claims on certified CI hosts. Unearned rather than untested; every vector here was produced on one host, and the fixtures say so.
* franken_lean-l84f — fln-core KVMap cannot represent the duplicate keys upstream can. Surfaced by the options-identity decision; the same Tribunal evidence settles both.
* fln-qpkj — the br comments backtick command-substitution defect, filed at the owner's direction after it silently corrupted an immutable comment on fln-171x.

GATES AT CLOSE: cargo test --locked -p fln-hash -p fln-core green throughout (fln-hash 46 lib + 14 integration, from 45 total at session start; fln-core 77 + 5). fmt clean. clippy -p fln-hash --all-targets -D warnings exit 0. ubs exit 0 with every critical inside mod tests and none on a library path. Every fln-hash consumer green: fln-core, fln-env, fln-kernel, fln-olean, and fln-conformance including the metamorphic_laws suite the options decision had to keep honest. Creating the four successor beads staled ci/KERNEL_CONTRACT_OWNERSHIP.jsonl by exactly those four ids; regenerated with a standalone helper outside the repo, validated by byte-reproducing HEAD's committed projection exactly (254 ids, projection_hash 1bd08e77...) before being trusted, then rerun live to 258 ids, and confirmed with cargo test -p fln-conformance --test kernel_contract at 6/6.

./scripts/check.sh was not run green and is not claimed: the structure gate is red workspace-wide on one finding that is not this bead's — FLN-STRUCT-032, contracts/PIN_TARGET_INVENTORY.txt missing, which belongs to fln-k5rr and is recorded there by cc_2.

comments.author: cc_3
comments.text:
cc_3, commit 84b3086 — set-vs-sequence identity, and A DECISION REQUIRED that I deliberately did not make.

I checked the ordering claims in both directions rather than only the permissive one, and it found a contradiction between two normative statements in the program.

THE HALF-CHECKED LAW: kvmap_round_trip_preserves_order asserted a round-trip preserved the value and compared exactly ONE key. Nothing asserted that permuting a KVMap CHANGES its canonical bytes. A codec that 'canonicalized' by sorting entries would have passed — silently merging two distinct upstream KVMap values into one encoding, in a crate whose whole premise is one encoding per value. Symmetrically root.rs asserted insertion-order independence for declarations and said nothing about options.

WHAT THAT CONCEALED — a false claim in root.rs. The module doc said 'the digest is insertion-order independent, so two hosts producing the same trusted environment produce the same root'. That is false for options: set_options digests KVMap's order-SENSITIVE canonical encoding. Demonstrated against the real API before I touched anything — two maps that agree on every find() (the only observable, since KVMap keys are unique and find returns the first match) produce different LogicalRoots: 3e776b03... vs 349a1f88... Consequence: spurious cache misses, and two identities in receipts and the transparency log for what any reader would call one environment.

WHY I DID NOT JUST FIX IT — THE DECISION YOU OWN. Making set_options order-independent turns crates/fln-conformance/tests/metamorphic_laws.rs red. canonical_ordered_rows_are_order_sensitive is an EXCLUSIVE metamorphic law requiring every non-identity permutation of unique rows to change both the canonical bytes AND the options-bearing logical root, on the stated ground that upstream KVMap is an ordered association list so an ordering IS part of the value. Note my codec change keeps that law's FIRST assertion passing; only the root assertion conflicts.

Both readings have real arguments:
* ORDERED (the Tribunal law, and what I left in place): the environment contains the options value; the options value is an ordered assoc list; a root that distinguishes MORE can only cost cache misses, whereas under-distinguishing is the dangerous direction for a trusted identity.
* SET (root.rs's doc, Domain::OptionsSet's own name, and requirement (d)): with unique keys, order is unobservable through every lookup, so two permutations are the same elaboration-relevant options and therefore the same environment. Under FL-INV-01 an order-varying accumulation would also make the root schedule-dependent.

This spans requirement (d), this crate, and a Tribunal law owned by another pane. It is not mine to settle by editing whichever side makes my change pass, so I settled the DOCS to the truth and pinned BOTH directions so neither answer can drift in silently.

LANDED:
* The doc now states what actually holds: decls and extension deltas order-independent, options not, the cost spelled out, and the open question named and pointed here.
* options_are_identified_as_an_ordered_list_not_a_set — all 24 permutations of four entries; every non-identity one must move the root, the identity one must not, and at each step the maps are asserted lookup-identical so the cost is an assertion rather than a footnote.
* option_identity_does_not_collapse_distinct_option_sets — the other direction: changed value, changed key, changed DataValue constructor (OfNat(1) vs OfInt(1) vs OfString('1') vs OfBool), dropped entry, added entry, absent-options vs empty-options.
* the_ordered_encoding_is_order_sensitive_and_the_set_projection_is_not — the codec separates permutations, the projection does not, over maps proved lookup-identical first; the projection still separates distinct content and never shares bytes with the ordered encoding.
* kvmap_canonical_set_bytes — the supported order-independent projection under its own schema fln.canon.kvmap-set, so set semantics are chosen explicitly at a call site instead of being smuggled into a digest. If the decision goes the SET way, the one-line change is set_options calling this; the test that must then flip says so by name.
* The DataValue grammar is now one writer shared by both views, so they cannot disagree about a value. kvmap_round_trip_preserves_order compares every position, not the first key.

PLANTED THREE WAYS: sorting the ordered codec kills the new order-sensitivity test and the strengthened round-trip; switching set_options to the projection kills the ordered-options law ('permutation [0, 1, 3, 2] did NOT move the root'); the order-independent set_options kills it from the other side. My own schema registry from f5a3944 also caught me unprompted — adding fln.canon.kvmap-set failed registry_rows_match_the_constants_they_name until the row and count were updated, which is the drift it exists to refuse.

GATES: cargo test -p fln-hash 59/59 (45 lib + 14 integration; 45 at session start, 56 before this commit). fmt clean. clippy -p fln-hash --all-targets -D warnings exit 0. Every consumer green — fln-core, fln-env, fln-kernel, fln-olean, fln-conformance including the metamorphic_laws suite this change had to keep honest. ubs exit 0, all criticals inside mod tests.

comments.author: cc_3
comments.text:
DESIGN DECISION — OPTIONS IDENTITY IS ORDERED. Decided 2026-07-25 by the project owner; recorded here as normative so it is not re-litigated in a code review or 'fixed' by a later pass. Landed as documentation in root.rs::set_options; no behaviour changed, because the shipped behaviour was already the decided one.

THE QUESTION. LogicalRootBuilder::set_options digests KVMap's order-SENSITIVE canonical encoding, so two option maps carrying the same pairs in a different order produce different logical roots while agreeing on every find/contains/get_* that this codebase performs. Should set_options instead digest an order-independent set projection?

THE ANSWER: NO. Keep it ordered. Rationale, in the owner's terms:

1. FALSE IDENTITY IS THE STRICTLY MORE DANGEROUS DIRECTION OF ERROR. Collapsing set_options into an order-independent set would make two environments that the Reference DISTINGUISHES produce the SAME logical root. A redundant distinction costs a spurious cache miss. A collision means a cached or replayed result can be attributed to the wrong closure, silently, with nothing detecting it — and this digest is what the Ledger, receipts, and the transparency log key on. That is precisely the defect class this swarm already fixed in franken_lean-f6br, where witness_digest bound a lossy display projection of Name and distinct finding sets shared a witness. It is not to be reintroduced one layer up.

2. THE LEAN-SIDE FACT SUPPORTS THE SAME ANSWER, AND I VERIFIED IT AGAINST THE PIN rather than asserting it. In ~/.elan/toolchains/leanprover--lean4---v4.32.0/src/lean/Lean/Data/KVMap.lean: 'structure KVMap where entries : List (Name × DataValue) := [] deriving Inhabited, Repr' — a raw association list; findCore returns the FIRST match; insertCore replaces in place or appends; ToString KVMap is toString m.entries. So order (and duplicate keys) are observable upstream. Under the Oracle-Only Law our encoding mirrors what the pin actually distinguishes; we do not get to decide the semantics are cleaner than they are. Faithful mode requires bug-for-bug observational parity, and 'we normalized away a distinction upstream preserves' is exactly the drift that gets a change reverted.

WHAT WOULD REOPEN THIS FORK: Tribunal evidence that the Reference cannot observe option order or duplicate keys in ANY surface we mirror. If that evidence ever appears, the fork reopens. Until then it is closed, and the one-line change is not to be made without reopening it here first.

HOW IT IS HELD: root.rs::set_options now carries the decision, both grounds, and the revisit condition, so a reader who thinks the cost paragraph looks like a defect is told where to go instead. options_are_identified_as_an_ordered_list_not_a_set fails if anyone flips it (all 24 permutations of four entries: every non-identity permutation must move the root, the identity one must not, and the maps are asserted lookup-identical at each step so the accepted cost is an assertion rather than a footnote). option_identity_does_not_collapse_distinct_option_sets pins the other direction so it cannot become a digest that varies with everything. crates/fln-conformance's exclusive MR is the independent second guard. kvmap_canonical_set_bytes remains the supported projection for a caller that genuinely wants set identity, under its own schema fln.canon.kvmap-set so that choice is explicit at the call site.

WORTH RECORDING FOR WHOEVER READS THIS LATER (the owner's note): this fork was found while doing the right thing — pinning set-vs-sequence identity in BOTH directions in 84b3086 instead of only asserting the permissive side. A one-sided test would have silently locked in whichever behaviour happened to be there, and root.rs's false doc claim would have survived. The both-directions discipline is what surfaced the ambiguity.

ADJACENT FINDING THIS DECISION IMPLIES — NOT ACTED ON, FILED HONESTLY. If duplicate keys are observable upstream (they are: KVMap.entries is a public raw list, constructible as ⟨[(a,1),(a,2)]⟩, and observable through entries/Repr/ToString even though findCore hides the second), then two of our own choices normalize away a distinction the Reference preserves — the same argument class as above, one layer down:
  * fln_core::options::KVMap stores Vec<(Name, DataValue)> but insert replaces in place, so the type cannot REPRESENT a duplicate-keyed KVMap at all;
  * canon.rs's decoder rejects duplicate KVMap keys with 'duplicate KVMap key' (bead fln-1f8v).
I am not changing either. fln-1f8v's reasoning is correct GIVEN the current type — since our insert folds duplicates, accepting duplicate-keyed bytes would map two encodings to one value and break canonicality, which is worse. The real question is whether the TYPE should mirror upstream's representable-duplicates shape, and that spans fln-core, canon.rs, and any consumer of KVMap, so it wants its own bead and its own decision rather than a drive-by change on a P0. Flagging it because the decision above is the exact argument for looking at it, and because a future reader of fln-1f8v deserves to know the tension exists.

comments.author: cc_3
comments.text:
cc_3, commit eb4c674 — the logical-root determinism criterion, which was listed as satisfied and was not.

The acceptance text: 'logical-root determinism e2e test — two elaboration runs on different thread counts and (in CI) different hosts produce identical roots, with the full input closure logged in the test output for diagnosis on mismatch.' root_is_schedule_independent_across_thread_counts claimed to be that test. It had three defects, all inside the criterion:

1. IT DID NOT VARY THE SCHEDULE. Workers cloned their chunk and the main thread joined the handles in SPAWN ORDER, so the builder received declarations in the same sequence at every thread count. An order-dependent accumulator would have passed at 2 threads and at 8 alike. The test asserted schedule independence while holding the schedule fixed — the same permissive-side-only failure as the KVMap ordering claim, in a different costume, and found the same way.
2. THE MATRIX WAS WRONG AND CONTRADICTED ITS OWN COMMENT: the comment said {1, 8}, the code ran [2, 8]. The standard is {1, 8, 32} (PG-5 / FL-INV-01 and AGENTS.md's per-commit matrix). 1 and 32 were never exercised — so neither the single-threaded baseline nor the high-contention case was covered.
3. NO CLOSURE LOGGING AT ALL. On mismatch it printed '{threads} threads diverged' and nothing about which input moved, which is the one thing the criterion names explicitly.

NOW: three deterministic adversarial accumulation orders first (reversed, rotated, adjacent-swaps) so non-identity schedules are covered without depending on the scheduler doing anything interesting; then real concurrency at {1, 8, 32} with arrival order decided by lock contention rather than join order, so the sequence genuinely varies run to run; plus a conservation check that workers neither dropped nor duplicated an entry. On mismatch both closures render — declaration count, the accumulation order under test, and every (name -> content digest) pair in canonical-byte order so two reports diff cleanly.

PROVED BY PLANTING: folding an accumulation-order witness into the builder — precisely the order-dependent accumulator this test exists to catch — kills it, and also kills root_is_insertion_order_independent and last_write_wins_like_an_environment_map. It is caught by the deterministic 'reversed' case rather than by scheduler luck, and the failure output carries the full 32-declaration closure with digests, so the criterion's diagnosis requirement is demonstrated and not just implemented.

STILL PENDING on this criterion, unchanged and not fakeable locally: the '(in CI) different hosts' clause needs certified-matrix CI hosts.
