title: W1: Quality gates — scripts/check.sh, CI pipeline, e2e smoke harness with detailed logging
description:
## Description

Own the W1 verification contract and scenario-activation registry: scripts/check.sh runs fmt, check, clippy -D warnings, and test in order with observable short-circuit semantics; CI invokes that script rather than duplicating stages; changed-file UBS integrates through the same manifest; one typed event stream renders both human logs and strict schema-versioned NDJSON. This bead consumes the existing evidence-runner supervision, sealed-build, and durable-bundle contract; it tests typed results and does not create a second runner/publication authority.

The verification manifest is keyed by stable bead/requirement/claim/invariant/Parity/Behavior-Note/workstream/gate ids. It records D7 claim_type and evidence_kind separately, deterministic unit/boundary/error/resource/cancel/failure-atomicity coverage, applicable property/metamorphic/fuzz/mutation/fault coverage, real user-path and negative/recovery E2E scenarios, owner/activation state, and closing artifacts. Evidence class must be strong enough for the claim; benchmark/fuzz/mock evidence cannot close an invariant or PROVEN claim.

At migration, freeze a versioned hash of the then-governed Beads set and require a complete manifest row before any governed bead moves to in_progress or closed. New open planning beads may carry explicit planned rows, but must become complete before implementation. This replaces the unbounded phrase every existing task bead with a reproducible adoption boundary while preserving total future coverage.

RUR closes on check/CI stage semantics, manifest/event/log schemas and validators, registry/activation machinery, self-tests, and the currently runnable real workspace smoke. Future scenarios are preserved through explicit owner rows: contracts-regenerate belongs to franken_lean-53v; tribunal-smoke to fln-euo; judge-smoke to fln-fur; parity/T2 smoke to its integration owner, ultimately franken_lean-26y/G4. A planned BLOCKED row cannot satisfy that owner’s gate; execution becomes mandatory when its owner is runnable. This removes the prior semantic cycle where RUR required Tribunal/Judge/T2 execution before their implementations could depend on RUR.

Semantic records contain canonical inputs, expected/actual outcomes, claim/comparison classes, logical budgets, roots, stage decision, cleanup, and final state. Host/timestamp/duration/PID/absolute-path/performance facts are bounded linked telemetry and cannot alter logical roots. After the first failed stage every later stage emits explicit not_run with causal reason. Closed-schema validation rejects duplicate/extra keys, malformed UTF-8, truncated lines, multiple/missing terminals, human/machine inconsistency, escaped artifacts, swallowed stderr, missing final state, or telemetry in semantic identity.

## Acceptance Criteria

Named suites verification_manifest_model, claim_evidence_authority, stage_short_circuit_model, scenario_activation_registry, event_render_equivalence, strict_ndjson_validator, and workspace_smoke_no_mock_e2e cover migration-set hashing, planned-to-active transitions, owner/gate enforcement, all stage outcomes/not_run records, semantic/telemetry separation, malformed/adversarial logs, failure/recovery, and independent bundle validation. Mutants include absent coverage, mock-only release claim, benchmark/fuzz closing an invariant, unclassified skip, swallowed stderr, omitted not_run or final state, extra/duplicate/truncated log fields, human/machine divergence, escaped path, dynamic-unbounded migration set, planned scenario counted passed, and Tribunal/Judge/T2 execution required before its owner exists; all are killed. scripts/check.sh and the real current workspace smoke pass locally/CI with a planted stage failure diagnosable from retained artifacts and a clean recovery. All existing evidence-runner boundary, finalization, setup-envelope, sealed compiler-environment, durability, and hostile-environment acceptance requirements recorded in Design remain binding and are not modified or claimed implemented by this plan correction.
design:
REVIEW AMENDMENT — this bead is the mandatory verification contract and scenario registry, not only a convenience script.

In addition to the existing scope, define a machine-checked verification manifest schema keyed by bead id, requirement/claim id, FL-INV id, Parity-Ledger row, Behavior Note, workstream, and convergence/performance gate. Every implementation bead must register: deterministic unit tests for success/boundary/error/resource/cancel/failure-atomicity behavior; applicable property, metamorphic, fuzz, mutation-kill, and fault-drill coverage; at least one real user-path E2E scenario and one negative/recovery scenario; and the evidence artifacts that close the requirement. CI fails on an implemented row with no registered coverage, an orphan scenario, a release claim backed only by mocks, an unclassified skip, or a scenario that does not assert its final state.

The shared E2E runner must produce paired human and schema-versioned NDJSON logs containing run/scenario/step correlation ids, bead/claim/invariant/row/gate ids, redacted command argv, cwd, toolchain epoch, mode/profile, platform, thread count, seed, cache state, host facts, canonical input hashes, expected/actual values, monotonic timing, resource/budget facts, exit/signal, stdout/stderr artifact references, receipt/logical roots, first-divergence records, and cleanup/final-state assertions. Logs are bounded and secret-redacted, stderr is never swallowed, and CI archives everything needed to diagnose a failure without rerunning it.

REVIEW AMENDMENT — process supervision and evidence publication are part of the trusted test-result boundary. Every launched stage must be causally contained before target exec: establish the guardian/subreaper, session/process-group identity, start ticks, and pidfd handles behind a bounded child gate, publish readiness only after those bindings exist, then release exec. Never signal a raw numeric PID after an asynchronous gap. Setup/readiness has its own bounded timeout; execution timeout starts only after child-authored readiness. Fast leader exit, detached descendants, PID churn/reuse, pidfd exhaustion, cancellation storms, and every supported signal are mandatory typed cases; successful, semantic-nonzero, unexpected-nonzero, and signalled immediate-exit commands run as a repeated stress matrix with zero false internal faults and zero survivors.

Finalization installs one common HUP/INT/TERM handler atomically before doing work and uses a durable write-once decision protocol. `validate-bundle` remains read-only; a distinct `adopt-bundle` operation may recover a valid decision by O_EXCL marker publication, fsync of marker plus every parent through the artifact root, and full post-adoption revalidation. Relative/absolute artifact arguments are normalized and containment-checked once; parent walks detect fixed points and every finalizer has a bounded termination budget. Concurrent adopters are idempotent, cancellation cannot be adopted as pass, mismatched decision/marker fails closed, and crash points from decision through directory fsync have named recovery tests. Quality runs use a per-attempt isolated Cargo target (or prove cache identity cryptographically), bind UBS inventory to the final governed source, and never promote inconclusive/internal-fault evidence.

REVIEW AMENDMENT — the evidence envelope begins before fallible setup. Once a fresh artifact directory exists, UBS inventory, vendor binding, governed-root hashing, host/argv fact capture, initial event publication, snapshot construction, and every other setup step execute under the same finalization state machine as ordinary stages. Setup failure, concurrent governed-source drift, cancellation, or internal fault must still yield exactly one typed terminal record and a durable independently validatable bundle; the pre-envelope may do only argument validation and atomic creation/refusal of the artifact directory. No run may strand an ambiguous partial directory containing setup artifacts but no verdict.

REVIEW AMENDMENT — authoritative builds run inside a sealed compiler environment. Resolve the exact SUITE.lock toolchain before repository-controlled compilation, invoke cargo and rustc through that explicit rustup channel, and exclude or fail closed on ambient RUSTFLAGS, CARGO_ENCODED_RUSTFLAGS, RUSTC and Cargo rustc-wrapper overrides, RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN, target-specific rustflags, Cargo-home configuration, and ancestor .cargo configuration. Use per-attempt isolated Cargo home and target directories without deleting or mutating user caches, and record the admitted environment plus compiler path/version/commit in the initial evidence envelope. This is required because pinned rustc accepts deny(unsafe_code) and forbid(unsafe_code) crates containing unsafe when cap-lints allow is injected; source posture and environment isolation are independent defenses.
acceptance_criteria: RUR closes on the shared check/CI contract, versioned verification-manifest adoption set, claim/evidence authority, typed event plus strict human/NDJSON rendering, scenario owner/activation registry, self-tests, and the currently runnable real workspace smoke. Contracts, Tribunal, Judge, and T2 scenarios remain mandatory on their named downstream owners and cannot count passed while planned/BLOCKED. All named model/mutation/no-mock/recovery/log-validator tests pass; later stages after failure are explicit not_run. Existing Design requirements for the evidence-runner boundary, setup/finalization/durability, sealed compiler environment, and hostile-environment tests remain fully mandatory. This bead does not duplicate that implementation authority.
notes:
MANDATORY VERIFICATION DEFINITION OF DONE (inherits franken_lean-rur; additive to this bead's own Tests/Acceptance):
1. Unit coverage: deterministic happy-path, boundary, malformed-input, resource-exhaustion, cancellation, and failure-atomicity cases for every new public behavior; property/metamorphic and mutation-kill tests wherever an invariant or equivalence is claimed.
2. E2E coverage: add or extend at least one shared scripts/e2e scenario for the real user-visible path, plus a negative/recovery scenario. Release-level evidence uses the no-mock lane (real Reference binary/artifact/filesystem/editor/process/host as applicable). A mock may support a unit test but may not close an L-level, PG gate, or public claim.
3. Detailed logs: emit both concise human logs and schema-versioned NDJSON with run/scenario/step ids; bead, claim, invariant, Parity-Ledger row, and gate ids; exact command/argv with secrets redacted; cwd; epoch/mode/profile/platform/thread-count/seed/cache-state/host facts; canonical input hashes; expected vs actual; monotonic start/end/duration; resource and budget facts; exit status/signal; stdout/stderr artifact references; receipt/logical roots; first-divergence data; cleanup and asserted final state. Never swallow stderr, never leak secrets, and bound adversarial log volume.

(1) Do not publish/release merely because pidfd binding succeeded: Popen can return and the parent can bind while the helper is still runnable, before it executes SIGSTOP. An early SIGCONT is then lost and the helper later stops forever. Require child-authored gate readiness or a repeated identity-bound /proc state proof of T/t before release. (2) run_supervised currently computes deadline_ns from started_ns before Popen; time spent awaiting/releasing the stopped child would consume execution budget. Record a separate bounded setup/readiness duration and start the execution deadline only after confirmed release. Seed delayed-stop, early-CONT/lost-wakeup, never-stops, and stop-then-dies cases in addition to the 100x4 immediate matrix.

comments.author: CopperHare
comments.text: Concrete wiring bug in the current stopped-finalizer diff (wrapper hashes/mtimes 12:50 EDT): process-start-ticks gained --stopped and resume-bound-process correctly rejects a non-T/t process, but all three run_finalizer_command call sites invoke process-start-ticks with --session-leader only. The binder can therefore return before cmd_stopped_exec reaches SIGSTOP; resume then rejects and the wrapper kills a valid finalizer as resume_failed. Pass --stopped at all three binding sites and keep the post-bind T/t recheck in resume. Add a tight immediate-finalizer stress case; do not weaken resume to accept runnable state.

comments.author: cc_2
comments.text:
TOOLING HAZARD, WIDER THAN cc_3 FOUND IT: the backtick corruption also eats GIT COMMIT MESSAGES, not just br comment bodies (cc_2, observed 2026-07-25).

cc_3's finding was that backticks in a br comments add -m body get command-substituted and silently damage an immutable bead record; the fix was to pass the body via --file. I hit the same class from a different direction and it is worth widening the warning, because every agent here writes commit messages the same way.

WHAT HAPPENED. I committed with the usual pattern:
    git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
    ...body...
    EOF
    )"
with a QUOTED heredoc delimiter, which is supposed to protect the body. The commit succeeded. Two backticked tokens were nevertheless deleted from the stored message: a lone question mark in backticks, and a backticked match arm containing Err(stop). The stored text now reads "short-circuits through  at the point of the trip" and " companions - 1:1, none missing", with the identifiers simply gone.

THE ONLY TELL was two lines on stderr that are easy to read as noise:
    (eval):1: no matches found: ?
    (eval):1: no matches found: Err(stop)
That is zsh's globber, not command substitution: a quoted heredoc protects the heredoc body, but the tokens still pass through globbing on the way into the argument and NOMATCH removes them. So the failure mode is slightly different from cc_3's (glob rather than substitution) while the outcome is identical - an immutable record that looks complete and is not.

WHY THIS IS WORSE THAN THE BEAD CASE. A bead comment can be repaired by appending a correction. A commit message cannot, short of rewriting history, which on a six-agent shared tree is not an acceptable repair for a typo. I did not amend for exactly that reason; the uncorrupted text lives in the franken_lean-1fxz bead comment, which was filed via --file and read back intact.

PRACTICAL RULES, for anyone writing durable text from the shell here:
1. Prefer prose without backticks in commit messages, or use git commit -F <file>.
2. For beads, br comments add supports --file. Use it.
3. After writing any immutable record, read it back and grep for a token you know you wrote. "Comment added" and a successful commit both report success on corrupted input.
4. Treat any "(eval):1: no matches found: X" on stderr as a deletion notice, not a warning.

Filing here rather than opening a bead because it is a workflow hazard for the quality-gate surface rather than a defect in a crate, and because rur is where the gate/tooling findings are already collected. If you would rather it be a bead, say so and I will file one.

title: structure-guard harnesses retain every scratch root: 23,017 dirs / 3.2 GiB live across ten producers, still growing
description:
## Finding

`fln-fixture-retention-unbounded-evit` repaired one harness and closed with an explicit
unmeasured remainder: "Only structure-guard was fixed. Other harnesses may retain scratch
state the same way and I have not looked. That is the obvious next measurement."

That measurement is made here. Other harnesses do retain unconditionally, the pile is still
growing, and the largest still-unfixed producer is not the one that was repaired.

Derived from the source rather than from the directory names: every `std::env::temp_dir()`
call site under `crates/`, `tools/` and `tribunal/` was read and classified by whether it
creates a scratch root and whether anything ever reclaims it. Disk side measured at
2026-07-28 16:19 local (America/New_York), one pass over `/data/tmp`, at HEAD abf81db8.

  family                        n   apparentMiB  allocMiB   newest       producer
  structure-guard-test-     10911         600.2    7248.8   07-28 09:51  tools/structure-guard/tests/common/mod.rs:153  (FIXED at b0a52442)
  structure-guard-closure-   3776         207.1    2486.9   07-28 13:51  tools/structure-guard/tests/closure.rs:33
  contract-handoff-          2080       92763.8     321.7   07-28 13:51  tools/structure-guard/src/contract_handoff.rs:1323
  fln-ownership-            13919           5.4     258.3   07-28 13:47  crates/fln-conformance/src/ownership.rs:2329
  fln-contract-inventory-    1267          40.7      76.4   07-28 13:51  tools/structure-guard/src/contract_inventory.rs:3244
  fln-rch-                   1727           0.2      68.7   07-28 13:47  crates/fln-conformance/tests/evidence_finalization.rs:3326
  fln-vdi4-                    98           2.8      20.4   07-28 13:50  crates/fln-syntax/tests/golden_vellum.rs:782
  fln-gate-discriminator-      65           0.4       1.5   07-28 13:49  crates/fln-conformance/tests/gate_lock_discriminator.rs:54
  fln-epoch-lab-               40           0.0       0.5   07-27 18:49  tribunal/epoch-lab/tests/epoch_lab_hash_chain.rs:23
  fln-derive-                  20           0.0       0.5   07-27 18:49  tribunal/epoch-lab/tests/derived_input_provenance.rs:294
  fln-refdiff-                 25           0.0       0.2   07-25 06:22  crates/fln-kernel/tests/reference_differential.rs:130
  TOTAL                     33928       93620.7   10483.8

Live, still-unfixed leak: 3,235.0 MiB allocated across 23,017 directories from ten producers,
the newest about two and a half hours old at measurement. `df /data` read 79 G free of 906 G.

A separate 146 entries under `/data/tmp` carry an `fln-` or `structure-guard` prefix and match
no harness family. Those are one-off per-bead probe artifacts (`fln-2tcr-*`, `fln-33gl-*`,
`fln-46mw-*` and so on), not harness output, and this bead makes no claim about them.

## The measurement note, which outranks the numbers

Apparent size is wrong in BOTH directions here, and neither error is small. The first pass of
this census used `st_size` and was misleading twice over:

  * `contract-handoff-` reads 92,763.8 MiB apparent against 321.7 MiB allocated, a 288x
    overstatement. 181 of those roots hold a deliberately SPARSE 512 MiB file planted by the
    `resource-exhaustion` cell; the entire 181-directory set costs 20.5 MiB of real disk.
    Published unchecked, that number reads as a 90 GiB emergency. It is not one.
  * `structure-guard-test-` reads 600.2 MiB apparent against 7,248.8 MiB allocated, a 12x
    UNDERstatement, because 10,911 directories of small files each round up to a 4 KiB block
    and every directory inode costs too. That figure reads as "not worth fixing", and it is
    the largest single pile on this box.

So the rule is `st_blocks * 512`, never `st_size`. And never `du -sh` in this shell: `du` is
aliased to `dust`, which on `-sh` prints its own help text, which reads like an error rather
than like the wrong tool having answered. cc_3's original "11 GB across 16,370 directories" is
correct on the allocated measure; anyone re-deriving it from apparent size concludes cc_3 was
wrong and stops.

## Scope

This bead repairs `tools/structure-guard` only: `tests/closure.rs`, `src/contract_handoff.rs`,
`src/contract_inventory.rs`, and `kernel-ownership-publisher/src/main.rs`. That is 2,885.0 MiB
of the 3,235.0 MiB live leak (89.2%) inside one crate with one owner, and the crate already
contains the reclaimer cc_3 proved at `b0a52442`. The repair therefore GENERALISES one
predicate to a caller-supplied prefix and routes every producer through it. It does not plant a
second copy of the predicate, which is `franken_lean-evidence-python-config-rule-drift-imuu`'s
defect family and is not going to be reproduced inside a repair.

Deliberately out of scope, named so nobody reads this bead as covering them:
`crates/fln-conformance` (`ownership.rs`, `evidence_finalization.rs`,
`gate_lock_discriminator.rs`), `crates/fln-syntax` (`golden_vellum.rs`), `crates/fln-kernel`
(`reference_differential.rs`), and `tribunal/epoch-lab` — together 350.0 MiB across 15,829
directories. Those crates cannot reach a helper living in a `kind=tool` crate without a
dependency edge that is the graph owner's decision, and `crates/fln-syntax` currently carries
another pane's uncommitted `franken_lean-36di` work. The measurement above is the handoff.

NOTHING IS REMOVED. Not one of the 33,928 existing directories. This bounds future growth only,
exactly as `b0a52442` did, under the orchestrator's recorded 2026-07-26 ruling that harness
cleanup is an ordinary repair rather than a deletion (RULE 1 forbids an agent deleting files;
a harness reclaiming the scratch directory it created seconds earlier is ordinary hygiene).
`evit` item 1, the pre-existing pile, stays parked with Jeffrey and is untouched.

## Acceptance criteria

1. One reclamation predicate exists in `tools/structure-guard`, parameterised by the caller's
   prefix, and all four structure-guard scratch producers route through it. No second copy of
   the fence or of the `Drop` body exists in the crate.
2. Retention on failure is preserved byte-for-byte in behaviour: a panicking test still leaves
   its root on disk and still prints a retention line naming it.
3. The fence refuses any root whose parent is not exactly the harness temp dir or whose final
   component lacks the caller's declared prefix, and says so rather than guessing. `Drop` never
   panics.
4. Proved in BOTH directions, because a reclaimer that never fires is indistinguishable from
   one with nothing to do: a passing fixture is asserted GONE and a failing one asserted still
   PRESENT, with the failing cell driven under `catch_unwind` because `std::thread::panicking()`
   is only true during an unwind. The probe reclaims the root it deliberately retained, so the
   proof is not itself a new leak.
5. A before/after directory count over one full `cargo test -p structure-guard --no-fail-fast`
   shows delta 0 for the three live families, measured on allocated blocks.
6. `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo check --all-targets`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`
   and `cargo test` pass; the exact changed Rust files receive a completed UBS scan. Any
   unrelated failure is reported with truthful provenance and not promoted to this bead.

## Evidence class and limits

Claim class `bounded_model` for the census and the before/after delta: one host, one instant,
one `/data/tmp`, and the growth rates are properties of this box under this swarm's load on this
day and must never be carried forward. The reclamation behaviour itself is exercised per commit
by the in-both-directions cells, which is stronger, but they demonstrate the named finite cases
on one implementation and host.

What this does NOT establish. It does not measure how often a retained fixture is actually READ
after a failure, so the value side of the retention trade remains unquantified exactly as `evit`
left it — retention is preserved on the failing path precisely because that price is unknown.
It says nothing about the six out-of-scope producers beyond the census row each one carries. It
cannot see scratch state written anywhere other than the system temp dir, so a harness writing
under `target/` or under a crate directory is outside this scan entirely, and at least one such
site exists (`crates/fln-conformance/target/fln-worker-refusal-*`, inside the repository rather
than in `/data/tmp`), which is recorded here and not repaired.

retention would happen cannot observe it. The probe then reclaims the directory it
deliberately retained, so the proof is not itself a new leak.
`the_fence_refuses_everything_outside_the_harness_namespace` covers a foreign name, a

findings. A "the producer must never inline the literal" rule refused `tests/common/mod.rs`
for writing `structure-guard-test-1-2-3-tag` as legitimate fence TEST INPUT. A "must name the
constant" rule refused `kernel-ownership-publisher`, which cannot import the constant at all —
that is the very condition being disclosed, so requiring the constant of it was a wall against
the disclosure. Both are now bound at the CALL SITE instead: a routed producer must contain
`ScratchRoot::create(<its constant>`, which is the thing that could actually drift, and the
remainder must carry its literal and must NOT construct a guard. Recorded because a guard that
refuses a correct file is this repository's most expensive recurring shape and I built two of
them in one afternoon.

GATES, with truthful provenance. All run LOCALLY through a one-line wrapper, because the RCH
PreToolUse hook classifies on the command text and a bare `cargo test` is offloaded to a worker
whose tree is not this one:
  cargo fmt -p structure-guard --check      clean (scoped with -p: a bare `cargo fmt` writes
                                            workspace-wide and would reformat a peer's file)
  cargo clippy -p structure-guard --all-targets -- -D warnings   clean
  cargo test -p structure-guard --no-fail-fast                   222 pass, 0 fail

UBS, with a same-path baseline because a count without one is not attributable. Baseline taken

  before  5 files  21 criticals = 2 `panic!` + 19 `Secret/token compared with ==`
  after   6 files  22 criticals = 3 `panic!` + 19 `Secret/token compared with ==`

DELTA IS EXACTLY +1, and it is `scratch.rs:318` — the deliberate `panic!` that IS the
retention mechanism, since `panicking()` cannot be observed without an unwind. Its twin at
`tests/common/mod.rs:551` is cc_3's identical probe and sits in the baseline. The 19
`Secret/token` findings are unmoved and are `fln-lyc8`'s documented false-positive class

WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH.

1. The value side of retention is STILL unpriced. Nobody has measured how often a retained

   Retention on the failing path is preserved precisely BECAUSE that price is unknown.
2. Six producers outside `tools/structure-guard` still retain unconditionally: 350.0 MiB

WORKING TREE; this one reads the INDEX, and the difference between them is exactly one
`git commit`. A pre-commit green cannot cover it, and no amount of care before the commit
would have.

  `cargo test -p fln-conformance --lib` takes seconds. The pre-commit workspace green does not

`fln_conformance::checked_manifest_dir!()`, which `tools/structure-guard` can reach because it

comment describing the fix WAS the finding. `fln-8zsq`'s lesson arriving inside a later repair

alongside the two above with "no churn cycle completed inside the guard window (sequence

title: check.sh sealed Cargo hides br from mandatory convergence governance test
description:
`scripts/check.sh` cannot currently reach a terminal pass after the live R15 convergence test landed.

Measured independently at committed HEAD `23259b30117f35dfcb54be612c490fb10fe05e69` in a clean clone with a real `.git` directory and the required untracked census inputs. The governed lane passed its evidence self-test, manifest, shellcheck, UBS classifier, projection harness, workspace format/check/Clippy, and census-availability stages. Its hard `cargo test` stage then failed only in `fln-conformance --test convergence_governance`: `real_workspace_policy_report_is_complete_and_read_only` launched `scripts/convergence_governance.py`, whose live mode invokes bare `br`, while the sealed Cargo environment rebuilds `PATH` as the pinned Rust toolchain plus `/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin`. This host installs `br` at `/home/ubuntu/.local/bin/br`, so the policy judge returns typed `command-unavailable` and the gate exits 1. A direct current-tree run of the same test passed 2/2, separating policy behavior from the gate-environment join.

This is a W1 evidence/test-process boundary defect. It owns neither thermal qualification (`fln-odva`) nor the remaining R15 policy work on `franken_lean-convergence-wip-governance-149`. It repairs only the impossible join between the compiler-sealed Cargo stage and the live tracker test.

Acceptance criteria:

1. The mandatory live convergence test executes the exact resolved `br` binary when run inside the sealed Cargo test stage; it must not widen the sealed `PATH` to an ambient directory.
2. The same test still passes under ordinary direct `cargo test`, and the production policy command still defaults to ordinary `br` discovery for interactive callers.
3. An absent, relative, non-file, or non-executable explicit `br` path is refused before a tracker command runs, with a typed diagnostic that names the invalid authority rather than a generic policy result.
4. The exact executable path is used for both sides of the live double snapshot. No fallback after the first snapshot may silently switch tracker binaries.
5. A planted mutant that discards the explicit path and restores bare `br` is killed under a sealed-PATH control for the stated reason; a positive control using the same real binary succeeds.
6. The repair does not parse `.beads/issues.jsonl` as a substitute for the live tracker database, does not turn the test into an ignored/typed-skip hollow green, and does not weaken the compiler seal.
7. Focused tests, format, strict Clippy, the relevant evidence/manifest validators, and a complete current-HEAD `scripts/check.sh` run must exit 0 before closure. A partial gate or a direct-only green does not close this bead.

What this filing does not establish: no current gate pass exists; the installed `br` binary is not a SUITE.lock-pinned product dependency; no R15 policy correctness, product behavior, Reference parity, or release claim follows. Claim class is `bounded_model`, one host and one observed sealed environment.

title: br accepts a status the verification validator refuses, so one pane's blocked bead stops every pane's export
description:
br accepts a bead status the verification validator refuses, so a single pane setting a bead to
blocked stops EVERY pane from committing a beads export until that record is changed or excluded.

MEASURED THREE TIMES ON 2026-08-04 by cc_1, each time while trying to land unrelated work.

  scripts/evidence.py, the validator the pre-commit hook runs, accepts exactly four statuses:
  open, in_progress, closed, tombstone. Its refusal reads

    verification-manifest: .beads/issues.jsonl:<line>: bead '<id>' has unsupported status 'blocked'

  br accepts blocked and writes it to the shared export. Nothing between the two says so.

THE INSTANCES, and they are three separate beads set by more than one pane:

  1. fln-census-out-of-git-2ya9 and fln-ubs-stage-no-complete-verdict-z5kt, both at blocked,
     refused a gii.19 close commit that carried them incidentally. Pinning those two records to
     their HEAD versions was the only way to land unrelated work.
  2. The same pair refused again during the gii.20 close.
  3. fln-manifest-complete-row-preflight-gap-77xh, at blocked, is refusing right now. It was
     surfaced by scripts/br_obligation.py on its first live run, which reported it VERBATIM as a
     non-obligation refusal rather than mislabelling it.

WHY THIS IS WORSE THAN AN ORDINARY VALIDATION ERROR, and the reason it deserves its own tracker
entry rather than a paragraph in a handoff. The export is SHARED. A status is set by one pane, on
one bead, for good reasons; the refusal then lands on a different pane, at commit time, for a record
it did not touch and has no context for. That is exactly franken_lean-xjjr's shape -- an obligation
announced to the wrong pane, an unbounded number of actions late -- but with a harder edge: xjjr's
obligation can be met by the pane that owes it, while this one cannot be met at all by the pane that
hits it. Its only options are to pin the offending record out of its own commit, which is what I did
twice, or to change another pane's bead status, which it must not.

WHAT IS NOT WRONG. The validator is not wrong to refuse a status it does not model; a validator that
silently accepted an unmodelled lifecycle value would be worse. br is not obviously wrong to offer
blocked either -- a dependency-aware tracker having a blocked state is unremarkable. The defect is
the DISAGREEMENT, and that nothing joins the two vocabularies or fails when they diverge.

THREE CANDIDATE REPAIRS, NOT CHOSEN HERE because the choice is a decision about lifecycle semantics
rather than a bug fix:

  1. The validator models blocked, deriving whatever coverage state is correct for it. Cheapest to
     state, but it commits the project to a fifth lifecycle state in the coverage projection, and
     every derived-state count and closure-binding rule would need re-deriving against it.
  2. The swarm stops using blocked, and something REFUSES it at the point of setting -- br cannot be
     changed from here, but scripts/br_obligation.py already wraps br create and br close and could
     wrap br update, reporting the mismatch at the moment of the act. Same producer, no second copy
     of the predicate.
  3. The two vocabularies are bound explicitly, so that br growing or losing a status, or the
     validator's supported set changing, fails a named test rather than surfacing as a refused
     commit for a third party. This is the only candidate that survives a version bump on either
     side, and it does not by itself decide (1) or (2).

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA. Any ONE of the following closes this, and a measured negative closes it as
legitimately as a repair:

  1. The validator's supported status set and br's are bound by a named test that fails in BOTH
     directions -- a status br can write that the validator refuses, and a status the validator
     models that br cannot produce -- with the br version recorded, since br lives outside this
     repository and a version bump changes the answer silently.
  2. blocked is refused at the point of setting, by the existing wrapper calling the existing
     validator, with a before/after measurement showing the refusal reaching the pane that set it
     rather than the pane that commits next.
  3. The validator models blocked, with the derived coverage state for it stated and its effect on
     the closure-binding counts re-derived and disclosed.

It must NOT be closed by hand-editing the offending records, which is what I did twice under time
pressure and which fixes one commit rather than the defect. It must also NOT be closed by a second
copy of either vocabulary inside this repository: both must be read from their producers.

IT MASKS THE ANNOUNCEMENT MEANT TO REPLACE IT, observed while filing this very bead. The validator
stops at its FIRST error. fln-manifest-complete-row-preflight-gap-77xh sits at line 139 with status
blocked, so when scripts/br_obligation.py ran after the br create that filed this bead, it reported
the blocked refusal and never reached the adoption-boundary check for the new bead. The wrapper
behaved correctly -- it repeated its producer verbatim and refused to mislabel -- but the coverage
obligation it exists to announce was invisible behind an unrelated early refusal. So this defect does
not merely block commits: while any record sits at blocked, the obligation announcements
franken_lean-xjjr's repair provides are suppressed for every pane.

NOT MEASURED, deliberately: whether br's status vocabulary is configurable or fixed, and what other
statuses it accepts beyond the five now observed. beads_rust's source was not read. Class
bounded_model, one host, br 0.2.19, one day.
close_reason: criterion 2: blocked refused at point of setting by the existing wrapper calling the existing validator; re-measured at HEAD 502e3ab3 under br 0.3.2

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
MEASURED: br HAS NO STATUS VOCABULARY TO BIND TO. CRITERION 1 OF THIS BEAD IS IMPOSSIBLE AS WRITTEN,
AND I WROTE IT.

This bead's criterion 1 asks that "the validator's supported status set and br's are bound by a named
test that fails in BOTH directions". That presumes br HAS a set. Measured at br 0.2.19, in a scratch
workspace created with br init so no real bead was touched, it does not.

THE PROBE. A throwaway bead was created in the scratch workspace and br update --status was invoked
with ten candidate values. Classified by reading the STORED status back rather than by grepping the
command's own output, because a text classifier over exit messages is exactly the well-formed wrong
answer this repository keeps recording:

  open          ACCEPTED
  in_progress   ACCEPTED
  blocked       ACCEPTED
  deferred      ACCEPTED
  wontfix       ACCEPTED
  review        ACCEPTED
  done          ACCEPTED
  nonsense      ACCEPTED
  closed        REFUSED -- terminal, and br update says so: use br close, so close-policy and
                dependency rewiring are enforced (beads_rust#301)
  tombstone     REFUSED -- terminal, same reason, use br delete

And the decisive cell, which I set up as a POSITIVE CONTROL expecting a refusal and which instead
produced the finding: br update --status=zzzz-not-a-status was ACCEPTED. br show renders
[P2 - ZZZZ-NOT-A-STATUS] and br sync --flush-only exports "status": "zzzz-not-a-status" verbatim.

SO THE DEFECT IS NOT THE ONE THIS BEAD DESCRIBES. I filed it as a two-vocabulary DISAGREEMENT --
br has a fifth state the validator does not model. It is not that. br's --status is an UNVALIDATED
FREE-TEXT FIELD on one side, and a closed four-element set on the other. blocked is not a fifth
state; it is one arbitrary string among infinitely many, and it happens to be the one panes reach
for.

THREE CONSEQUENCES, each sharper than the original framing.

  1. Criterion 1 cannot be satisfied. There is no enumerable br vocabulary to read from its producer
     and compare, so "fails in both directions" has no second direction. A test could only pin the
     validator's set against a HAND-LISTED set of strings someone believes br accepts -- which is
     the hand-listed-scope defect this repository has found in three separate places, and which this
     bead's own criteria forbid.
  2. Any TYPO is a swarm-wide export blocker. Not just blocked: a mistyped status on any bead, by
     any pane, refuses every other pane's beads commit until it is changed or pinned out. The blast
     radius is the whole swarm and the trigger is a keystroke.
  3. Criterion 3 -- the validator models blocked -- is a partial repair at best. Modelling one extra
     string leaves the other infinity unmodelled, and the next typo reproduces the outage exactly.

WHAT THIS LEAVES. Criterion 2 is the only tractable option and it is now clearly the right one
rather than one of three: refuse the value at the POINT OF SETTING, by wrapping br update in
scripts/br_obligation.py and checking the requested status against the validator's supported set --
read from the validator, which is its producer, so no second copy of either vocabulary exists. That

cc_2 (pane %15), 2026-08-04. I filed franken_lean-px33 for the same defect within the same hour,

sighting, and the "announced to the wrong pane and cannot be met by the pane that hits it" framing

close yours.

=== 1. THE COLLISION: `blocked` ALREADY MEANS SOMETHING ELSE ON THE VALIDATOR'S SIDE ===

This bead says the defect is "the DISAGREEMENT, and that nothing joins the two vocabularies". True,
and there is a sharper edge under it that changes what a repair may do:

`blocked` is ALREADY a word on the validator's side, meaning something different. It is a DERIVED
COVERAGE STATE computed from the coverage ROW's `skip` field — scripts/evidence.py's
derived_verification_coverage_state returns "blocked" when skip == "blocked", and the row validator
requires skip=blocked for any row whose derived state is blocked. So the validator already has a
`blocked` describing a ROW's evidence disposition, while br's `blocked` describes a BEAD's work
state.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE OBVIOUS FIX: adding "blocked" to the accepted-status set literal is a one-word
edit that silently puts one word on two concepts inside one validator. That is why the repair below
is marked provisional in the source rather than presented as a fix.

=== 2. THE REPAIR IS LANDED, PROVISIONALLY, AT 4d954f9f ===

scripts/evidence.py now accepts `blocked` as a bead status, and maps it EXACTLY as `open`:

    if bead_status in {"open", "blocked"}:
        return "blocked" if skip == "blocked" else "planned"

A blocked bead therefore cannot reach `complete` — which would owe evidence and invoke the
closure-binding law — and escapes nothing an open bead owes. Conservative by construction: it adds
no obligation and removes none.

THE CONTROL, which is why it was safe to take while both cod_2 (this surface's owner) and cod_7
(the assignee here) were quota-blocked: old code and new code run against IDENTICAL committed blobs
produce identical derived-state counts {active 32, blocked 1, complete 232, planned 17} and an
identical report sha256 3c489337a02571a5. Provably inert for everything committed; only beads at
status `blocked` are affected and HEAD had none. evidence.py self-test PASS at 107 cases;
evidence_finalization 62/0; closure_binding_population 13/0; evidence_field_citations 9/0; and no
test anywhere pins the accepted status set.

So this bead's operational symptom — a pane's export refused for another pane's bead — should stop
occurring. What remains open is the vocabulary decision in section 1, which is why the patch is
reversible and says so.

=== 3. WHAT UNBLOCKING IT REVEALED, so the next red is not mis-attributed ===

The validator STOPS AT THE FIRST OFFENDING RECORD. With the four blocked beads accepted it
progresses and now stops at ci/VERIFICATION_MANIFEST.jsonl:120, "requirement_ids must not be empty",
on fln-yihl — an entirely sparse row whose bead was closed in the WORKING TREE by cod_7 at
13:19:09Z with no post-close comment, so it would fail the closure-binding law even with all twelve
fields filled. That defect was there all along, behind the earlier refusal, and 4d954f9f did not
cause it. Every repair to this validator exposes the next one behind it.

=== 4. WHAT I AM NOT CLAIMING ===

I did not measure whether any br status other than `blocked` is reachable in practice. br lives
outside this repository, so no test here holds its accepted set and a version bump could change it
silently. The three instances in this bead's body are cc_1's measurements, not mine, and I have not
re-derived them. One host, one instant, class bounded_model.

comments.text:
## Re-tested at br 0.2.20 / schema 17: the finding SURVIVES — and br's validation hook turns out to exist, which sharpens the repair

Measured at `707efc513878456fad3f41be7536261e97d0850f`, cc_1. **This bead is cod_7's; this is a
measurement routed to its owner, not a claim on it.**

### Why re-test now

This bead's core finding — *`br` accepts a status the verification validator refuses* — was measured
by me at **br 0.2.19**, against **schema 16**. Both have since moved: `abedbcf3` applied the
**16 → 17** migration, and the installed tool is now **br 0.2.20**.

This repository's own doctrine, which I have applied to UBS and rch all week, is that **a version
bump expires every claim measured against that tool**. It applies to my own measurements too, and
that is the whole reason to run this: the cheapest outcome of re-testing a block is learning it still
holds, so it is the run nobody has a reason to make.

### Safety, because the defect is the experiment

Writing an invalid status into the shared tracker **is** the outage this bead describes — it blocks
every pane's export. So every cell ran inside a throwaway database under `/data/tmp`, and
`/data/projects/franken_lean/.beads` was never the target.

### Result: unchanged, and measured twice over

| cell | | |
|---|---|---|
| positive control — `in_progress` | **exit 0** | the probe can see a success |
| `zzzz-not-a-status` | **exit 0**, stored `'zzzz-not-a-status'` | accepted verbatim |
| `banana-42` | **exit 0**, stored `'banana-42'` | accepted verbatim |

Two *different* arbitrary values, deliberately, so the result reads **"accepts anything"** rather
than "accepts that one" — a single arbitrary value cannot separate those.

**The finding survives the version bump and the schema migration.** `shlw` stays open on its own
terms.

### The new fact, and it changes what the repair looks like

`br` **does** validate the status field. It refuses two values, with specific policy messages:

```
--status closed    -> refusing to close via `br update --status closed`: terminal-state transitions
                      must go through `br close` so close-policy (close-reason / AC / attribution)
                      is enforced … See …/beads_rust/issues/301.
--status tombstone -> refusing to tombstone via `br update --status tombstone`: use `br delete <id>`
                      instead so dependency rewiring and tombstone metadata are applied correctly.
```

So this is **not** "br has no status validation". There is a validation hook on exactly this field,
it fires, and it carries reasoned messages. What it validates is **transitions** — which terminal
states must go through a dedicated verb — and **not the vocabulary**.

That is a sharper statement of the bead than the one I originally supplied, and it matters for the
repair: whoever fixes this does not have to build validation from nothing and does not have to touch
the validator's side. There is a hook at the right place, and the gap is that its predicate is about
*how* a state is reached rather than *whether the value is a state at all*.

**It does not weaken the bead.** The validator's four accepted values and br's free-text field still
disagree, nothing between them says so, and one typo still blocks every pane's export.

### Disclosed: my first probe was broken and measured nothing

The first attempt regexed the bead id out of `br create`'s human output and got a token that was not
a bead, so three cells returned `Issue not found` at exit 3. **Three cells failing identically is a
broken scan, not a finding**, and reporting those exits as "br refused" would have inverted this
bead's conclusion. Re-run taking the id from `br list --json`, with the positive control placed
*first* so a probe that cannot write anything is caught before the interesting cells run.

### What this does not earn

`br` lives outside this repository, so this is one host, one version, one instant, class
`bounded_model` — and it expires again on the next bump, exactly as the 0.2.19 measurement did. The
version is recorded here so the next reader can tell whether it still describes their machine.

I did not test the whole value space, only two arbitrary strings plus the two refused ones; the
refusal set may be larger than `{closed, tombstone}` and I have not enumerated it. And I did **not**
re-test the other half of the bead — that the validator refuses what br accepts — because that half
is in-repo and was not touched by a `br` bump.

title: Gate G5: The Daemon — vscode-lean4 unmodified, PG-4/5/6/L, Verdict PG-9
description:
Convergence gate G5 "The Daemon" (§22.3): Lantern serves vscode-lean4 unmodified across the smoke matrix; PG-4 (attach), PG-5 (determinism), PG-6 (memory), PG-L (interactive latency ladder) met; the machine session API live; Verdict at PG-9; FrankenLean-built plugins load in the Reference (ABI door, outbound — or honestly tiered per platform per the R5 fallback).

This is the gate at which FrankenLean becomes a daily-driver: the editor experience (the ecosystem most-felt surface) is proven at wire fidelity and at interactive latency, the single-daemon shared-heap architecture delivers its promised arithmetic (once-per-daemon import replacing the per-worker multiplication), and the decision-procedure stack stands on owned components end to end.

Evidence bundle: the editor smoke matrix transcripts (open/edit/hover/goals/completion/widgets across representative projects incl. a mathlib slice); PG-4/5/6/L measurements with claim states and tail distributions; session-API load results (thousands of concurrent branches); PG-9 corpus agreement + wall numbers; outbound C4 matrix results or the per-platform tier table; 4-hour soak with zero leaks.

## Acceptance Criteria

All bead-specific requirements, acceptance conditions, tests, invariants, compatibility surfaces, evidence levels, performance gates, negative/recovery cases, and user-visible behaviors stated above remain mandatory. In addition, the MANDATORY VERIFICATION DEFINITION OF DONE in Notes must be satisfied with named unit/property/mutation suites, at least one shared real-path no-mock E2E scenario plus failure/recovery coverage, detailed human and schema-versioned NDJSON artifacts, and reproducible close evidence. No listed feature or claim may be silently narrowed, deferred, mocked, or declared complete through an unclassified divergence.
design: G5 is the concrete daily-driver daemon gate. It consumes G4, Lantern wire/topology, immutable snapshots and machine-session API, the replay/protocol/editor smoke rig, Verdict PG-9, and the outbound plugin matrix. Those beads collectively own PG-4/5/6/L, vscode-lean4 compatibility, cancellation/fault recovery, branch-load evidence, and retained transcripts. G5 does not wait for the entire W9 forensics and semantic-analysis catalog. Full W9 remains mandatory at G6, so no causal graph, semantic merge, time-travel, why-trusts, or SQL feature is lost.
acceptance_criteria:
G5 closes only when unmodified vscode-lean4 connects to Lantern and passes the registered real-editor smoke matrix across representative standalone, Std, and mathlib projects: initialize/open/change/save/close, diagnostics, hover, completion, goals, InfoView widgets, requests/cancellation, stale-response suppression, reconnect, and crash recovery all preserve pinned wire behavior and typed $/lean extensions. One daemon shares one immutable import heap while per-document regions and publication generations isolate failure; thousands of concurrent ProofStateSnapshot branches remain O(1) to fork, capability-scoped, deterministic, bounded, cancellable, and leak-free. Replay bundles reproduce every protocol failure. PG-4 meets warm attach at no more than 2 seconds p50 and cold first attach at no more than 1.2 times Reference import; PG-5 is bit-identical across 1, 8, and 32 threads per commit, 96 or more weekly, and the certified reproducible matrix; PG-6 holds daemon RSS for at least 8 open mathlib files at no more than 1.3 times one Reference worker, zero leaks over 4 hours, and per-declaration peak no more than Reference p95. PG-L meets edit-ack plus stale-cancel at 25 ms p95, exact syntax diagnostics at 60 ms p95, and verified first goal at 100 ms p50, 150 ms p95, 400 ms p99, with progressive impact reporting for large cones. Verdict has 100 percent bv_decide corpus agreement and wall no more than 2 times Reference-with-CaDiCaL; every certificate is independently checked. FrankenLean-built outbound plugins load in the Reference on each certified C4 platform or carry an explicit non-R5 tier without weakening other platforms. Unit/property/model and named mutation suites cover protocol ordering, generation races, cancellation, capability denial, branch isolation, cache/root staleness, plugin ABI drift, certificate bypass, and fault recovery. title: W2: Inbound plugin door — dlopen Reference-built plugins, revocation-first, receipts
description:
Implement the inbound plugin door (§6.6): Reference-built shared libraries (precompileModules artifacts, user @[extern] libraries) dlopen into FrankenLean, lean_* imports resolved against Marrow exports, initializers run under Golem initialization ordering (§11.5).

Posture: a plugin is native code and is trusted as such; FrankenLean adds PROVENANCE (hash + origin in the build record), the --no-plugins audit mode (plugin-dependent declarations flagged), and revocation-first loading in sound mode (hash + trust-card check BEFORE dlopen, never after). Each load emits an initialization-DAG receipt so cycles, duplicate initializers, and late capability requests are explainable rather than opaque loader failures. The panic law holds at every exported boundary: no Rust panic crosses the ABI; wrappers catch, convert only what the epoch contract maps, and never fabricate a successful Lean result after an internal panic (§6.5).

Acceptance: real Reference-built mathlib-adjacent plugins load and run (G2 requirement, inbound half); --no-plugins elaboration flags exactly the dependent declarations; a deliberately crashing plugin isolates with a typed PluginCrashed error and a receipt, not process death in the daemon. Tests: the C4 cross-load matrix inbound lanes per platform; initializer-ordering fixtures; revocation-first denial fixtures (tampered hash never reaches dlopen).

## Acceptance Criteria

All bead-specific requirements, acceptance conditions, tests, invariants, compatibility surfaces, evidence levels, performance gates, negative/recovery cases, and user-visible behaviors stated above remain mandatory. title: fln-syntax: make deep Syntax tree lifecycle and leaf walks stack-safe
description:
## Finding

At `0d0cd3217402d4de442a56a594dcc917ef3c6824`, `fln_syntax::tree::Syntax`
still maps user-controlled tree depth onto native call-stack depth in ordinary operations:

- compiler-derived `Clone`, `PartialEq`, and `Debug` recurse through `Node.args`;
- compiler-generated destruction recursively drops the same `Vec<Syntax>` chain;
- `Syntax::collect_leaves` recursively walks every nested node.

`Syntax` is built from parsed source and exposed to user macro code, so its nesting is not a
trusted implementation constant. A sufficiently deep but finite tree can therefore abort the
process instead of producing a value or typed refusal. This is also an uncovered requirement of
closed bead `fln-23cz`, whose acceptance explicitly named deep and wide trees.

## Scope

Make the existing `Syntax` value stack-safe as one lifecycle unit:

- explicit heap worklists for clone, structural equality, debug rendering, and leaf traversal;
- iterative draining destruction;
- preserve all four public variants and their fields, source-order leaves, structural identity,
  compact and alternate debug shapes, and reconstruction behavior.

This bead does not redesign parser recursion, add a new allocation API, or claim arbitrary-depth
or allocation-failure totality. It closes native call-stack growth for finite in-memory `Syntax`
values only.

## Acceptance

1. A bounded regression constructs a 16 Ki-deep unary `Syntax` tree on a 64 KiB thread stack and
   completes clone, equality, compact debug, source-order leaf collection, and destruction.
2. The bounded-stack cell runs in an isolated child process and requires a completion marker, so
   an unexpected process abort or an accidentally empty test filter cannot be reported green.
3. Shallow fixtures cover every variant and verify that manual clone/equality/debug behavior
   retains every field and the established derived formatting shape.
4. Existing lossless reconstruction, parser, lexer, golden, fuzz, property, and thread suites
   remain green. Run exact-path fmt/check/clippy/tests plus `ubs` with an attributable baseline.
5. Evidence remains `bounded_model`: no arbitrary-depth proof, fallible allocation guarantee,
   parser-recursion claim, Reference-parity promotion, or deliberate crash-inducing test is
   inferred from the bounded cell.
close_reason: Delivered by 4d1d0c0fa15e182e6fb97e5b80bec8f6f1c9bfbb with bounded-stack and workspace-gate evidence in comment 1634.

title: Whole-mathlib-corpus kernel differential lane: extend the chosen-set closure machinery to a full standing rig over the provisioned corpus
description:
Filed by MistyEagle 2026-07-29 out of the z6c close (comment 1705, limitations).

## Context

The G0-2 chosen-set driver (crates/fln-conformance/tests/kernel_replay.rs,

THE GAP. validate_retained_receipts splits on newlines and treats each piece as a row. If any field
could carry a RAW newline, one receipt would arrive as TWO fragments, with the split falling
wherever the hostile content put it. A forged second "row" could be smuggled inside a legitimate
one, and every count on either side of the break would belong to neither receipt.

The property does hold - json_string escapes newlines, returns, tabs, quotes, backslashes and
control bytes - but it held by the ESCAPER'S GOOD BEHAVIOUR ALONE, and that escaper is SHARED with
several other row formats in this file. A change made for one of those would silently break the
retention file's framing here and no test would notice. That is the recurring shape from a new
angle: not an unexercised guard, but a property with no guard at all, resting on a helper that
belongs to somebody else's format.

TWO DIFFERENT PROPERTIES, BOTH ASSERTED, and separating them is the point. Surviving as one line is
FRAMING. Being rejected by the reader is CONTENT. A hostile row that stayed on its own line but was
ACCEPTED would corrupt nothing structurally and everything semantically; a row that was rejected but
split its own line would corrupt its neighbours regardless. So the test requires all three: the row
is one line, a two-receipt file splits into exactly two rows rather than three, and the reader
refuses the hostile one BY INDEX - blaming row 1 rather than its innocent neighbour.

The fixture uses every character the escaper special-cases plus a bare control byte, and I mirrored
the escaper to confirm the encoding carries no raw break before asserting on it.

A MIRROR REPLACED BY A SPECIFICATION. 3eb168dc. cc_3, 2026-08-21, WAVE 66. Code-first; compiled and
format-checked at HEAD in an isolated worktree, NOT run. Test file only. Corpus NOT provisioned.
cc_2's file dirty, untouched, not reverted. Bead open.

FIXING THE WEAKNESS I FOUND LAST WAVE AND LEFT. The stub-resistance pass turned up one test that
survived only by accident: the parallel-vectors test recomputed each expected module name by calling
module_name_from_path - the very function whose output it was checking. That is a MIRROR. Replace
the projection with a stub returning a constant and both sides change together, so the assertion
holds while the projection is wrong. It survived only because the injectivity rule inside the walk
fails first on all-equal names: protection by a NEIGHBOUR rather than by the check itself. I
reported it and did not fix it; this fixes it.

Reporting a weakness and leaving it is only acceptable for one wave. The finding was mine, the fix
was cheap, and the reason it survived - a different rule happening to fire - is exactly the kind of
accident that stops holding when the fixture changes.

THE EXPECTED NAME IS NOW COMPUTED FROM THE SPECIFICATION: a module name is its path below the
library root, with the trailing `.olean` removed and the components joined by dots, under the
namespace. The test states that directly and uses NONE of the projection's machinery - in particular
not Path::with_extension, so a change to what counts as "the extension" becomes a DISAGREEMENT
between the two rather than a change both follow.

DELIBERATE DUPLICATION, same pattern as the corpus root path written once as a constant and once as
a literal: one side is the implementation, the other is what the implementation is supposed to MEAN.
Reusing the implementation to describe its own meaning is what made the original assertion empty. A
second implementation is usually a smell; in a test it is often the only thing that makes the
assertion say something.

I checked the two agree on every entry of the fixture before committing, including the
dotted-directory case where the final-extension rule and the trailing-suffix rule could plausibly
have diverged: Mid.dotted/Leaf.olean is Fixture.Mid.dotted.Leaf under both.

THE SCHEMA NAME'S VALUE WAS PINNED NOWHERE. b72fab57. cc_3, 2026-08-21, WAVE 70. Code-first;
compiled and format-checked, NOT run. Test file only. Corpus NOT provisioned. cc_2's file clean and
untouched. Bead open.

THE FINDING. to_row writes WHOLE_MATHLIB_RECEIPT_SCHEMA and from_row compares against it, so
producer and reader both read the same constant and its VALUE is unconstrained. Change it and both
move together: every test still passes, and every receipt already retained under the old name
becomes unreadable. The value appears exactly ONCE in the file - its own definition. The round-trip
cell that mutates receipt/1 into receipt/2 tests that the CHECK works; it says nothing about which
name the check is for.

THE FAILURE IS LOUD BUT WRONG, WHICH IS ITS OWN HAZARD - and it is the mirror image of last wave's.
A changed DIRECTORY makes the guard report nothing retained: a silence. A changed SCHEMA makes it
REFUSE every retained row, with a message blaming the ROW rather than the rename. Whoever reads it
is looking at evidence that was valid when written and is now being called malformed. Silence sends
you nowhere; misdirection sends you somewhere wrong, and costs more.

THE NAME IS NOW A LITERAL IN THE TEST. One side is the constant the code uses, the other is the name
retained rows were filed under. Changing the format becomes deliberate: advance the version suffix
and decide what happens to rows carrying the old one, rather than a rename that passes CI and
quietly invalidates an archive. The suffix is pinned too - without it there is nothing to tell an
old row from a malformed one.

AND A REAL ROW MUST CARRY IT, FIRST. Checking the constant alone would leave a producer that wrote
some other name, or put the schema in the middle, entirely unexamined; a reader scanning a mixed
NDJSON file identifies a row by what it leads with.

VERIFICATION NOTE. My first grep for the format head matched the OTHER receipt's to_row in this file
- it also leads with schema but diverges two fields later - so the answer looked right for the wrong
object. I re-ran it scoped to the impl block before asserting on the leading substring. Two files'
worth of similar formats in one file is a standing trap for exactly this.

71. Code-first; compiled and format-checked, NOT run. Test file only. Corpus NOT provisioned. cc_2's

THE CENSUS TAXONOMY WAS PROSE. b5293822. cc_3, 2026-08-21, WAVE 72. Code-first; compiled and
format-checked, NOT run. Test file only. Corpus NOT provisioned. cc_2's file clean and untouched.
Bead open.

THE FINDING. check_family_token's own documentation says the two context families carry a `context:`
prefix "so a reader can tell a kernel outcome token from a context-construction reason". That is the
ENTIRE interpretability of the TRIAGE line the driver publishes: rejected: is a D23 finding,
inconclusive: an exhaustion, internal_fault a bug in us, context: a module our side could not build
an environment for. Nothing enforced it. Rename either constant to something unprefixed and every
test still passes - the grammar rule only requires a non-answer NOT to start with rejected: - while
the census gains a family a reader cannot place.

CLOSED, NOT MERELY PREFIXED. The stronger property is that those four shapes are ALL of them. A new
emitter adding a fifth would put an unclassifiable family into a published census while the triage
line still looked complete. So the population is assembled from every source a run can draw on - the
kernel's rejection classes read from its own source, the resource causes through the production
formatter, the two context constants, the internal-fault token - and each must land in one of the
four. A token belonging to none fails with a message telling the author to give it a prefix that
says what KIND of thing it is, or to widen the taxonomy deliberately.

ALL FOUR MUST ACTUALLY OCCUR, and that assertion is the one I would have skipped a month ago: a
taxonomy checked against three of four shapes says nothing about the fourth, and the population is
assembled rather than fixed, so a source drying up would silently narrow it.

This also pins the two constants' VALUES as literals - the smaller finding that led here, and the
same shape as the schema name and the floors: producer and tests both read the constant, so a rename
moves everything together and nothing disagrees. Three waves, three constants, one defect class.

A RESULT THAT PANICS IS NOT A RESULT. a43b9c2a. cc_3, 2026-08-21, WAVE 73. Code-first; compiled and
format-checked, NOT run. Test file only. Corpus NOT provisioned. cc_2's file clean and untouched.
Bead open.

THE FINDING. validate promises to REFUSE a bad row and returns a Result to say so. Its conservation
rules added retained-row counts with a plain `+`, and so did family_total's accumulator - six
unchecked additions in total. Two fields near u64::MAX overflow that, and in a DEBUG build, which is
how these tests run, an overflow ABORTS. The guard would die with "attempt to add with overflow"
rather than saying the row does not conserve: a panic where a refusal was promised, and a diagnosis
pointing at arithmetic instead of at the row.

WHY THIS ONE STINGS. The retained file is append-only and hand-editable - that is precisely why the
reader already refuses duplicate keys, unknown fields, hostile control characters, and rows that
split their own line. I built all of that on the premise that the file is hostile, then fed the same
file's NUMBERS into unchecked arithmetic. The premise was applied to the shape of the row and not to
its contents. Worth stating because it is not a missing test - it is an inconsistency between two
decisions I made about the same input.

ALL SIX ARE NOW CHECKED, through one helper carrying a LABEL so the refusal says which sum
overflowed. Several of them add attacker-supplied numbers, so "overflows a u64" alone would not
identify the rule - the same expectation-collision rule that has governed every cell on this bead.

I traced validate's ORDER before choosing the two cells' inputs: the population sum is reached
before the buckets sum, so the first needs compared and unscorable large while the second needs
agree and unsoundly_permissive. Had I used the same shape twice, both would have tripped the first
rule and one cell would have proved nothing.

A BYTE SLICE AT THE MIDPOINT IS A LATENT PANIC. 65a939a7. cc_3, 2026-08-21, WAVE 74 (and the same
ask arrived as WAVE 99; this answers both). Code-first; compiled and format-checked, NOT run. Test
file only. Corpus NOT provisioned. cc_2's file clean and untouched. Bead open.

THE SAME HOSTILE-INPUT LENS AS LAST WAVE, ON SLICING RATHER THAN ARITHMETIC. &row[..row.len() / 2]
slices by BYTE index and Rust aborts on an index inside a character. The truncation cell is safe
today only because the sample receipt happens to be pure ASCII - a property of the fixture's current
CONTENTS, not of the format, and one nothing asserts. A row legitimately carries whatever a corpus
path, a bead name or a family token contains, and the hostile-field test already proves those are
ESCAPED rather than rejected. If the cut itself panicked, the cell meant to test the reader's
response to a truncated row would fail with a complaint about indices and say nothing about the
reader.

I CHECKED THE HAZARD RATHER THAN ASSERTING IT, AND THE CHECKING MATTERED. My first demonstration
picked a plausible multi-byte row whose midpoint WAS a boundary, so nothing would have gone wrong -
"contains non-ASCII" is not sufficient to trigger this. I constructed one that does: "aé a" is five
bytes and byte two lands inside the é. Had I not gone looking for a concrete case I would have
written a commit message claiming a hazard I had not produced.

AND I NEARLY SHIPPED A VACUOUS ASSERTION IN THE FIX ITSELF. My first control asserted the truncation
round-trips as valid UTF-8 - which a String passes BY CONSTRUCTION, and which could never have run
anyway, since the slice would panic before producing one. It now asserts where the cut LANDS.
Writing a guard is no protection against writing a vacuous guard; that is the lesson this bead keeps
re-teaching me, and the third time it has been my own new code in the same session.

comments.text:
A PARENT MODULE MAKES PATH ORDER DISAGREE WITH MODULE-NAME ORDER. 82385f30. cc_3, 2026-08-21, WAVE 103.
Code-first; compiled and format-checked at HEAD a1bdd6d4 in an isolated worktree, NOT run. Test file
only. Corpus NOT provisioned. Three peer files dirty in the shared tree, untouched. Bead open.

THE NEIGHBOURING TEST ASSERTED THAT THE MODULE NAMES COME BACK SORTED, AND THAT IS FALSE OF THE WALK.
Path orders COMPONENT BY COMPONENT, not byte by byte, so a component that ends sorts before any
longer one sharing its bytes: the directory `Algebra` precedes the file `Algebra.olean`, and the
CHILD module is enumerated before its PARENT. The projection joins components with `.` and runs
straight past that boundary, so by name the parent comes first. One tree, opposite orders.

THE SHAPE IS THE ORDINARY LEAN LIBRARY LAYOUT, not an edge case: wherever a module has submodules it
is a file `X.olean` sitting beside a directory `X/`. Neither existing inventory fixture holds one -
the sorted fixture's `Nested/` has no `Nested.olean`, the parallel fixture's `Mid.dotted/` has no
`Mid.dotted.olean`. The claim stood because the fixtures omitted the most characteristic shape of the
thing they model, which is a realism gap, not a sorting bug.

I MEASURED BEFORE WRITING THE ASSERTIONS, AND MY FIRST FIXTURE WAS WRONG. I reasoned from raw bytes -
`.` is 46, `/` is 47, so a dotted file stem beside a sibling directory should invert - wrote the
fixture, the test and a paragraph of confident prose explaining the mechanism, and it compiled. A
standalone rustc probe over `Vec<PathBuf>::sort` then showed that pair AGREES: Path's Ord is
component-wise and the byte story does not apply to it at all. Compiling is not evidence about an
ordering, and the wrong version would have passed - it asserted a disagreement I would have had to
observe to notice was absent. The tree in this commit is the one the measurement produced.

SPLIT, NOT DELETED. The sortedness assertion still fires on its own fixture and now states the
premise it rests on: no entry is a parent module, checked mechanically, so adding `Nested.olean`
reddens it with a message naming that cause instead of sending the reader after a sorting bug.

THE UNSORTED ORDER IS THE RIGHT ANSWER, WHICH IS WHY IT IS PINNED RATHER THAN REPAIRED. modules[i]
must be the projection of oleans[i] - the struct hands a caller two vectors side by side and a
neighbouring test pins that they may be zipped - and path order is what preserves that. Sorting the
NAMES is the obvious-looking tidy that would break it. The correspondence is re-checked here on the
parent-module tree, against the independent specification rather than the projection itself.

host and a skip earns nothing: no G1, no PG-1, no whole-corpus acceptance.

THE EMPTY-COMPONENT GUARD INSPECTED THE PATH, NOT THE NAME. 48268485. cc_3, 2026-08-21, WAVE 106.
Code-first; compiled and format-checked at HEAD 0bf8e750 in an isolated worktree, NOT run. Test file
only. Corpus NOT provisioned. Bead open.

THE PATH'S COMPONENTS ARE NOT THE NAME'S SEGMENTS. module_name_from_path refuses a component that
is_empty(), which reads like the right rule and can never fire: a Component::Normal produced by the
parser is never empty. The JOIN is where an empty segment comes from. `x..olean` has extension
`olean` and stem `x.`, so `Dotted/x..olean` projected to `Dotted.x.` - a trailing segment with no
characters - straight past both guards, because every component along the way was non-empty and
normal. The guard names the real hazard and looks for it in the one place it cannot appear. That is
a third instance of the shape this bead keeps turning up: a check whose subject is one step away
from the thing it is written about.

MEASURED, NOT REASONED. A standalone rustc probe over Path::extension, with_extension and Components
established that `x..olean` IS collected by the exact-extension filter, that it projects to
`Dotted.x.`, and that the neighbouring `..olean` takes a DIFFERENT branch - it strips to `..`, which
Components reports as ParentDir. Two dotted names one character apart, two different refusals; a cell
asserting only "refused" would pass on either, so each asserts on the words unique to its branch.

THE COST IS SILENCE, WHICH IS WHY NOTHING FOUND IT. A name with an empty segment matches no import
recorded in any olean, so the module joins the census, adds one to every count taken from it, and
resolves against nothing. Downstream that reads as a corpus with unresolved imports - a
corpus-integrity problem - rather than as a file that should never have been named.

NO EXISTING FIXTURE MOVES, and this was checked rather than hoped. All 33 fixture entries in the file
were run through the new predicate with the same probe: 5 are not collected at all, 27 project
cleanly, only the new `Dotted/x..olean` is refused. `Nested.olean/Inner.olean` and
`Mid.dotted/Leaf.olean` stay accepted, which is the green control - the rule is about empty segments,
not about dots. That is the regression evidence I can produce without running the suite, and it is
not a substitute for the batch run.

AND A MISCOUNT IN THE PROSE BESIDE IT. The refusal test's doc opened "four of these five messages
share `module path`"; three of them contain that phrase. The tally is now stated per fragment,
against the checked list it sits two lines above, with the old sentence recorded so nobody re-derives
it.

comments.text:
A FIXTURE ENTRY COULD LEAVE THE FIXTURE TREE. 07366a09. cc_3, 2026-08-21, WAVE 109.
Code-first; compiled and format-checked at HEAD a020f3e3 in an isolated worktree, NOT run. Test file
only. Corpus NOT provisioned. Bead open.

THE PARAMETER IS CALLED relative_files AND NOTHING MADE IT SO. Path::join follows the caller:
base.join("/x/y.olean") IS "/x/y.olean" - the base is discarded and the write lands outside
CARGO_TARGET_TMPDIR altogether - while base.join("../sibling/x.olean") climbs into whatever tree sits
beside this one. Both were reachable from any caller, and the writer creates parent directories on
the way, so neither needed its target to exist first. Measured with a standalone rustc probe over
join/starts_with/components, not inferred from the docs.

IT IS THE HAZARD THE NAME REGISTRY EXISTS FOR, BY A ROUTE THE REGISTRY CANNOT SEE. That guard catches
two tests claiming one NAME. This is two tests sharing one FILE while holding different names, which
the registry reads as two unrelated fixtures. Same symptom, harder to trace: a count moves in a test
whose own fixture list never mentions the file.

THE OBVIOUS GUARD IS VACUOUS, WHICH IS WHY THE CHECK IS ON COMPONENTS.
base.join("../sibling").starts_with(base) returns TRUE - `..` is an ordinary component to a lexical
prefix test and nothing on that path resolves it - so a containment check written the natural way
passes on the one input it exists to catch. The test asserts that rather than describing it, so a
future Rust that resolved `..` would tell us the fix can be simplified instead of leaving a stale
justification behind.

ON COMPONENTS, NOT ON THE SUBSTRING. `Dotted/x..olean` is a real entry in this file, added two waves
ago for the empty-segment work, and both of its components are Normal. A substring test for `..`
would refuse a tree the walk is supposed to accept; it is the green control here for that reason.

NOTHING MAY LAND, WHICH IS THE PART A MESSAGE ASSERTION CANNOT SHOW. A refusal arriving AFTER the
write would still panic and still carry the right words. Both escape targets are named before the
calls and asserted absent afterwards. The absolute entry points inside target/ on purpose: it is
outside the fixture tree, which is all the cell is about, and a regression then strays somewhere
harmless rather than into /tmp.
