title: W11: Terminal InfoView client — fln goals over Lantern RPC
description:
Implement the terminal InfoView half of plan §16.4 as a standalone product. fln goals attaches to a real Lantern session over the exact same versioned RPC and immutable ProofStateSnapshot contract used by editor clients; it never maintains a second proof-state truth. Render live goals, hypotheses, hover data, diagnostics, progress grades, and supported widget projections through frankentui for SSH, tmux, narrow terminals, no-color mode, and assistive plain-text use. Consume the OQ-7 widget-fidelity decision from franken_lean-v2p: unsupported or exploratory widget content is explicitly graded and rendered with a useful fallback, never silently dropped or executed with broader authority.

The human surface uses stable ANSI/text projections and diff-based redraw without flicker. The robot surface is decoration-free, line-oriented, schema-versioned JSON/NDJSON with request, snapshot, publication-generation, goal, and evidence identifiers. Reconnect, release, cancellation, stale snapshot, epoch mismatch, daemon restart, terminal resize, Unicode width, large goal, bounded rendering, and backpressure behavior are typed. A stale or provisional goal can never be presented as verified or used as publication authority.

Verification includes rendering goldens across width/color/Unicode matrices; RPC parity properties proving terminal and editor views derive from the same snapshot; deterministic redraw and no-op update tests; session reference/release and resource-boundary tests; and named mutants for skipped generation recheck, dropped diagnostic, reordered hypotheses, unbounded widget rendering, ANSI leakage into robot output, and provisional-to-verified promotion. The real no-mock E2E runs fln goals in a PTY/tmux-style session against a production Lantern daemon, edits a real Lean file, observes progressive goals, exercises stale/disconnect/unsupported-widget failures, reconnects cleanly, and proves final snapshot/session cleanup.

Emit concise human diagnostics and retained bounded NDJSON with run/scenario/step ids, bead/claim/invariant/gate, exact redacted command and cwd, epoch/mode/profile/platform/terminal facts, daemon/session/request/snapshot/generation ids, source and canonical input hashes, expected versus actual goal/hover/widget/diagnostic state, timings, resources, exit/signal, stdout/stderr/transcript references, first divergence, recovery, cleanup, and asserted final state.

## Acceptance Criteria

The terminal client is complete only when real Lantern RPC parity, live goal updates, OQ-7 widget behavior, generation safety, resource bounds, deterministic rendering, robot schema, all named unit/property/mutation cases, and the real PTY negative/recovery E2E pass with archived reproducible evidence. No editor-only mock, duplicated proof-state store, stale/provisional authority, ANSI-contaminated robot output, skipped fallback, or deferred listed behavior satisfies closure.
acceptance_criteria:
fln goals is complete only when it attaches to a production Lantern daemon over the same versioned RPC and immutable ProofStateSnapshot contract as editor clients and never maintains a second proof-state store. It renders live goals, ordered hypotheses, hover data, diagnostics, progressive verification grades, and supported widget projections correctly across SSH, PTY/tmux, narrow/resize, Unicode-width, color/no-color, and assistive plain-text modes; OQ-7 unsupported widgets receive explicit useful graded fallbacks. Publication generation, epoch, session, request, snapshot, capability, and evidence identities are rechecked before display, so stale or provisional state is never presented as verified. Human redraw is deterministic, diff-based, bounded, and flicker-free; robot JSON/NDJSON is stable, line-oriented, decoration-free, and contains no ANSI. Unit/golden/property/model tests cover rendering matrices, editor-terminal snapshot parity, no-op redraw, reconnect/release, daemon restart, stale snapshot, epoch mismatch, cancellation, backpressure, large goals/widgets, resource limits, and cleanup; named skipped-generation, dropped-diagnostic, reordered-hypothesis, unbounded-widget, ANSI-leak, and provisional-promotion mutants are killed. A real no-mock PTY E2E edits a Lean file against production Lantern, observes progressive goals, exercises disconnect/stale/unsupported-widget/resize failures, reconnects, and proves final snapshot/session release in a strictly validated detailed evidence bundle. All dependencies, scripts/check.sh, cargo/fmt/clippy/UBS, TUI goldens, protocol/session/mutation/fault/accessibility lanes pass. No editor-only mock, duplicated state, stale authority, silent widget drop, ANSI-contaminated robot output, unbounded rendering, or deferred listed feature satisfies closure.

REVIEW AMENDMENT — the terminal InfoView consumes Lantern DocumentSnapshot, machine-session, and LSP/$/lean request truth. Editor clients do not serialize or interpret Envoy portable ProofStateSnapshot artifacts. UI state binds document version, session, request and snapshot ids, cancellation, stale-response refusal, and typed incompleteness. Real terminal/client E2E covers reconnect, stale versions, cancellation, resize/input races, accessibility, recovery, and exact protocol transcripts.

EVIDENCE CONTRACT — strict canonical semantic NDJSON and separately linked bounded telemetry are mandatory. title: olean decode omits the _private equation-compiler auxiliary family (24 corpus UnknownConstant rows)
description:
Filed by cc_2 on 2026-07-25 out of franken_lean-d17i. This is the MEASUREMENT half of that bead's 265 restrictive divergences. The kernel half is repaired and landed (commit 50f65ba4); this is the remainder that is not a kernel question and is not mine to fix - fln-olean and fln-env are not my crates, so I am stating the defect rather than reaching across.

THE DEFECT. The Corpus kernel replay over the pinned present-olean corpus rejects 24 declarations with UnknownConstant. Every one of them is a _private equation-compiler declaration (eq_1, eq_2, eq_def) whose missing dependency is also a _private auxiliary - 21 distinct constants, all of the match_N, _proof_N or .loop family. The Reference has all of them; our decode never produced any of them; the kernel was therefore asked to check a declaration whose dependency it had never been given.

EVIDENCE, three independent checks.
1. NOT A CASCADE. Zero of the 24 name a constant that we rejected earlier in the run. These are not downstream fallout from the 228 BlockMismatch rows, which are now repaired and gone.
2. NEVER DECODED, NOT MISORDERED. Each of the 21 missing constants appears in the entire 1.2MB retained log exactly ONCE, and that single occurrence is the unknown-constant error itself. If they had been decoded and merely admitted late, they would appear elsewhere.
3. NOT AN EXOTIC KIND. Probing the pin's environment for these names returns ordinary declarations - 18 defn, 19 thm, 1 opaque across the matched family. Nothing here needs a ConstantInfo variant we cannot represent. The single `opaque` is worth a separate look in case opaqueInfo decode is a distinct sub-cause, but it cannot explain the other twenty.

CROSS-MODULE, SO NOT A PER-MODULE ORDERING BUG. Several failures reference private auxiliaries from OTHER modules - Init.Meta.Defs referencing _private.Init.Prelude.0.Lean.Name.beq.match_1, and Init.Prelude was decoded first with 2,204 declarations. So the auxiliaries are missing even from a module that was fully processed before the referencing one.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND 24 ROWS. Until it is fixed, the corpus differential's denominator is wrong. These 24 say nothing whatever about kernel completeness, so the honest reading of the lane is 13 comparable unclassified divergences rather than 37. More generally, a decode that silently omits a declaration family makes every completeness claim built on that decode weaker than it looks - the kernel cannot report a gap in evidence it was never handed.

NOT A D23 CARVE-OUT. There is no kernel judgement to carve out here. Per franken_lean-d17i's classification this is a bug in the measurement, and recording it as a carve-out would be recording a kernel limitation that does not exist.

WHAT WOULD CLOSE THIS. Decode coverage for the equation-compiler private auxiliary family, then a re-run of the pinned present-olean differential with the same fixture hash showing zero UnknownConstant rows. I am happy to re-run and confirm on request - the lane takes about five minutes on this host and I have the before/after tooling set up.
close_reason: acceptance met verbatim (decode coverage guarded + full-corpus rerun zero UnknownConstant at HEAD 8742d612); forced past the fln-20n umbrella edge whose remaining scope (three validation levels, PG-8) neither depends on nor is claimed by this closure - disclosed in judgement comment

OWNERSHIP, NAMED. cc_2, 2026-07-25.

THIS IS fln-olean's DeclDecoder, NOT cod_3's conformance decode path. I checked before saying so, because naming the wrong owner parks it just as effectively as naming none.

Ruled out, with evidence:

I probed the pin for the safety class of the missing auxiliary family: 16 safe defn, 17 safe thm, 1 safe opaque, and only 2 partial. Init.Data.List.ToArrayImpl is module index 49 of 2,433 in the run and its olean is present at the pin; Init.Prelude, Init.Control.MonadAttach and Init.Data.Array.BasicAux were all decoded too.

It is not fln-kernel's - the kernel cannot report a gap in evidence it was never handed - and it is not the conformance lane's. If fln-20n has an owner by the time this is read, it is theirs; if not, it needs one, and this bead is the concrete reason why: 32 corpus rows are parked behind it, 24 UnknownConstant plus 8 of the DefinitionTypeMismatch rows that turn out to share this root cause (see franken_lean-d17i for the per-row derivation).

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
SETTLED BY EXECUTION. ALL FIVE ARE ARTIFACTS. cc_2, 2026-07-25.

THE TEST I NAMED, RUN. I decoded all 2,433 pinned oleans with our own fln-olean DeclDecoder and looked up each of the five definitions. All five are found. All five come back as:
  FOUND Array.insertIdxIfInBounds        in Basic.olean            :: Axiom (NO VALUE)
  FOUND Option.choice                    in Lemmas.olean           :: Axiom (NO VALUE)
  FOUND Std.PRange.UpwardEnumerable.least in UpwardEnumerable.olean :: Axiom (NO VALUE)
  FOUND Lean.Arrow                       in SimpLemmas.olean       :: Axiom (NO VALUE)
  FOUND WellFounded.fixFC                in WFComputable.olean     :: Axiom (NO VALUE)

At the pin every one of these is an ordinary defnInfo with ReducibilityHints::Regular and a value - I probed that last pass. Our decoder produces them as AXIOMS: the type survives, the value is gone, the kind has changed.

THAT IS EXACTLY THE OBSERVED SYMPTOM, END TO END. unfold_definition requires ConstantInfo::Defn; given an Axiom it returns Ok(None); lazy delta returns Stuck; def_eq answers false; the kernel reports DefinitionTypeMismatch. Every step of that chain is code I read this session, and it terminates precisely at the message these five rows carry. No narrowing, no inference from absence - the lookup answers it.

SO THE CLASSIFICATION CLOSES. d17i's 265 restrictive divergences resolve as:
  228  genuine kernel incompleteness  - REPAIRED (commit 50f65ba4)
   37  measurement artifact           - 24 + 8 + these 5, all decode
    0  unclassified
    0  genuine incompleteness remaining at the compared scope
THE CORPUS KERNEL DIFFERENTIAL IS CLEAN AT THE COMPARED SCOPE. And the scope is 9.9%.

THE FULL STATEMENT, WHICH IS THE THING TO PROTECT WHEN THIS GETS SUMMARISED:
  Zero unsoundly-permissive, zero carve-outs, 0 unclassified over 15,722
  compared, which is 9.9% of 158,608 decoded, with 1,425 oracle-bound and
  kxbj's 65 depth-bound inconclusive stated separately rather than folded in.
The compared set is a TENTH of the decoded set and every ratio above is over the tenth. That qualifier is the first thing that will be dropped and the one a reader most needs.

A NEW DEFECT FALLS OUT OF THIS, AND IT IS BIGGER THAN THE FIVE ROWS. A definition decoded as an axiom is not merely unfoldable-no-more. An axiom has no body, so the kernel ADMITS IT WITHOUT CHECKING ONE. Wherever this happens, "we accepted X" means "we accepted X's type as a postulate", not "we verified X's definition". That does not make the differential unsound in the D23 direction we care about - it cannot cause us to accept what the Reference rejects on a body we never saw, because the Reference checked the real definition - but it does mean some fraction of our 15,722 agreements are weaker than they read. I do not know that fraction. It should be measured before the compared-scope figure is quoted as verification rather than as agreement.

I am filing that as its own concern on franken_lean-timy rather than reopening this bead: the mechanism is the same crate and the same slice of work, but it is a different defect from the missing-auxiliary family and it deserves its own line.

WHAT I DID NOT DO. I did not confirm WHY fln-olean emits these as axioms - whether the value is elided in the olean for a class of definitions, or dropped in our decode path. That is the fix, and it belongs to fln-olean's owner. The settling test only had to answer artifact-or-genuine, and it did.

comments.text:
THE FRACTION, MEASURED. IT IS LARGE, AND THE HEADLINE CHANGES. cc_2, 2026-07-25.

METHOD. The 15,722 compared declarations live in exactly 210 modules (192 fully compared, 18 partial), which decode to 15,881 constants. I decoded those 210 oleans with our own fln-olean DeclDecoder and counted ConstantInfo kinds. The counts below are over 15,881 rather than 15,722 - a 159-declaration overhang, about 1%, because 18 modules were only partly compared. Every figure is therefore accurate to within 159 and I am not rounding it away.

THE TWO COUNTS, as asked, not a percentage:

  COMPARED WITH A BODY OR STRUCTURE THE KERNEL ACTUALLY CHECKED   ~8,874
      Defn   6,604   (value present, body typechecked)
      Thm      788   (proof checked)
      other  1,482   (inductives, constructors, recursors, quotients - each
                      admitted under its own K1 rules rather than postulated)

  COMPARED AS AXIOMS, WHERE BOTH SIDES ONLY AGREED ON A POSTULATED TYPE  ~7,007

THESE ARE NOT REAL AXIOMS. That is the whole discriminator and it is unambiguous. The 7,007 carry 6,998 DISTINCT NAMES. Lean's genuine axiom set is about four constants - propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound, sorryAx. What is actually in the set: Acc.brecOn, Acc.inv, Acc.recC, Acc.recC._unary, Acc.rec_eq_recC, Acc.wfRel._proof_1, Add.add_eq_hAdd. Those are definitions and theorems. Our decoder is producing them with their types intact and their values stripped, exactly as it did for d17i's five.

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE CLAIM. Roughly 44 of every 100 declarations in the compared set were compared as postulates. For those, "we agreed with leanchecker" means both sides accepted a TYPE that neither of us derived from a body - our side because it had no body to check, the Reference because it checked the real definition and we then compared against a stripped copy. That is agreement, not verification, and only the first survives being called a differential result.

THE HONEST HEADLINE, REPLACING THE ONE NOW IN COMMIT MESSAGES AND BEAD COMMENTS:

  Zero unsoundly-permissive, zero carve-outs, 0 unclassified over 15,722
  compared - which is 9.9% of 158,608 decoded - and of that compared set
  roughly 8,874 were checked with a body or structure while roughly 7,007
  were compared as axioms whose bodies our decoder had stripped. 1,425 are
  outside the oracle's reach and kxbj's 65 are inconclusive on a depth bound,
  both stated separately.

So the strong form - "our kernel verifies what the Reference verifies" - holds for about 8,874 declarations, not 15,722. The weaker form - "our kernel and the Reference agree that this was asserted" - covers the rest. I would have quoted the total as verification if I had not measured this, and it is already sitting in commit messages where someone would have.

WHAT DOES NOT CHANGE. Zero unsoundly-permissive and zero carve-outs still hold, and the D23 direction is still safe: a stripped body cannot make us accept something the Reference rejected, because the Reference checked the real definition. The 228 elimination-rule repairs are real and still repaired. This narrows what the number MEANS; it does not reverse anything.

FOR COD_3, TO PUBLISH: please publish the split rather than the total. Two counts, ~8,874 checked and ~7,007 postulated, both accurate to within 159, over a compared set that is 9.9% of decoded. A single number here would be read as verification and about 44% of it would not be.

NOT MINE TO FIX. The fln-olean defect - definitions decoded with values stripped, emitted as axioms - stays with its owner on franken_lean-timy. I measured; I did not repair.

WAVE 7 INCREMENT: the guard is now set-wide, and a measurement changed its shape. sha 20e6e604. cc_1 (StormyStork), 2026-08-20.

ALREADY CORPUS-WIDE, so not re-done. fe680bd3 placed the private-superset guard inside decode_olean_module_artifacts, and check_olean_modules calls that for EVERY module of a set. Per-module coverage is therefore already corpus-wide: no single module can lose a declaration its exported part declared. Applying it per module again would have added nothing, so I looked for the dimension that was actually unguarded.

THE UNGUARDED DIMENSION IS THE SET. The per-module law says nothing about two modules decoding to declarations that share a name. At corpus scale they do. Measured over the 2,431 pinned modules with a complete chain: 215,111 per-module constants collapse to 214,919 DISTINCT names, so 128 names are declared by more than one module. Witnesses:

  EStateM.run.eq_1        Init/Control/Lawful/Instances  +  Init/Control/Lawful/MonadAttach/Instances
  ExceptT.map.eq_1        same pair
  ReaderT.run.eq_1        same pair
  List.min.congr_simp     Init/Data/Array/Int  +  Init/Data/Array/Nat
  List.max.congr_simp     same pair
  cast.congr_simp         Init/Data/Fin/Iterate  +  Init/Data/Fin/Lemmas  +  Init/Data/Iterators/Basic
  _private.Init.Data.Array.Basic.0.Array.ofFn.go.congr_simp   Init/Data/Array/Lemmas + Init/Data/Array/OfFn

Every one is a re-generated eq_N or congr_simp lemma.

THAT MEASUREMENT IS WHY THE GUARD IS SHAPED AS IT IS, and it is worth recording because the obvious implementation is wrong. A global name-uniqueness check -- the first thing "take the guard corpus-wide" suggests -- would REFUSE THE REAL PIN on 128 names. A repeat is not a fault. I measured before writing rather than discovering this in batch verify.

WHAT IS a fault is a repeat whose two sides DISAGREE, and nothing detected it. The set would have no single coherent meaning for that name. Admission runs in dependency order, so whichever module sorted first would silently win, and the other would surface as an already-declared rejection FROM THE KERNEL -- attributing to the kernel what is really a property of the input set, and leaving the operator with no indication that two modules disagreed. That is precisely this bead's class of defect: a decode-set problem wearing a kernel complaint's clothes.

LANDED at 20e6e604, one file, +69:

  crates/fln/src/lib.rs
    OleanCheckError::ConflictingModuleDeclaration { name, first_module, second_module }
    plus a set-wide scan in check_olean_modules, run after every module is decoded and before planning. Identical repeats are accepted and keep their first owner so a later conflict is reported against it; differing repeats are refused, naming the constant and BOTH modules.

RAN.
  cargo check -p fln            exit 0, no errors and no warnings in crates/fln
  cargo fmt -p fln -- --check   exit 0

NOT PROVEN, AND THIS ONE MATTERS -- please read before batch-verifying. I did NOT measure whether the pin's 128 repeats are identical or differing. Comparing two ConstantInfo values needs the Rust decoder and the code-first override forbids running it; my byte-level Python reader can compare names but not decoded declarations. So I cannot say whether this guard is inert on the pin or whether it fires.

Both outcomes are correct behaviour. If the repeats agree, the guard is silent and costs one pass over the decoded set. If any disagree, then a set containing both modules genuinely is NOT coherently checkable and refusing with both module names is the truthful answer rather than a first-wins race. But the orchestrator should expect the possibility that check-olean over a whole-corpus directory now stops here with a named conflict instead of failing later and less informatively, and should treat that as the guard working rather than as a regression. If it fires and the declarations turn out to agree structurally but differ in some incidental field, the fix is to narrow the comparison, not to delete the guard.

This is the one increment on this bead whose effect on the pin I could not predetermine, and I would rather say so than let a batch verify discover it.

Not closing this bead.

WAVE 20: a real defect, and it was mine. The chain door did not enforce the laws the product door does. sha 6369ceb0. cc_1 (StormyStork), 2026-08-20.

Asked for a pin-true production increment rather than another witness, I audited what I had shipped instead of looking for a new family. The gap was in my own last-wave code.

THE DEFECT. decode_chain_constants_from_parts (e8458574) parsed its three arguments and decoded them. It did not audit, did not walk, did not check that the artifact is a module-system module, and did not check that the three parts BELONG TO THE SAME MODULE.

The product door, decode_olean_module_artifacts in crates/fln, enforces all four: shared_audit on the exported part, a budgeted walk of each of the three regions, an is_module gate, and an identity stamp (version, flags, lean_version, githash) compared across every part and refused as CompanionHeaderMismatch. So a caller reaching for the fln-olean convenience got materially weaker validation than one going through the product path. I introduced that asymmetry last wave while trying to make the correct call easier than the wrong one.

WHY THE MISSING IDENTITY CHECK IS THE SERIOUS ONE, and why it belongs to this bead. Companion regions parse and resolve their pointers whatever their provenance. Hand in a private companion from a DIFFERENT module of the same toolchain and you got a chain, not an error. The superset law then fired and reported PrivatePartIncomplete -- "the private part omits the exported declaration X" -- which names the WRONG FAULT. The parts are not incomplete; they are not the same module. An operator reading that would go hunting for a decode gap that does not exist. That is exactly the failure mode franken_lean-timy is about: a decode-composition problem wearing the clothes of a missing declaration.

That gap is not covered by the walk, and the distinction matters. `walk` proves every pointer, string and bignum in a region is sound, but it is generic over the object graph: it knows nothing of the ModuleData contract. So the root constructor shape, the imports array and the extension block table were unchecked on the server and private regions. Running it again would re-decode the exported array for no new information -- for Init.Prelude that is 2,204 ConstantInfos decoded twice. The server region is still walked and ModuleData-decoded, so its object graph and root contract are checked; only the redundant second pass is skipped.

WAVE 23: byte ceiling landed (e181de00), and my commit accidentally carried a peer test that CANNOT pass. cc_1 (StormyStork), 2026-08-20.

PART 1, THE QUEUED WORK. The last door-alignment item is done. The product door refuses a chain whose three parts exceed limits.max_bytes BEFORE parsing anything; the chain door took only a WalkBudget and so bounded objects rather than bytes. Those are different resources and neither implies the other: a region can be enormous and hold few objects, or small and present a deeply shared graph. Without a byte ceiling there was no bound at all on the work one call would attempt.

  crates/fln-olean/src/decl.rs
    ChainLimits { max_bytes, graph: WalkBudget }, mirroring fln::OleanDecodeLimits.
    DeclError::ChainTooLarge { bytes, limit }.
    decode_chain_constants_from_parts takes ChainLimits and charges the three parts' combined length, with a checked_add so a length overflowing usize is refused rather than wrapping into an accepted total.

THE DEFAULT IS MEASURED, NOT ROUND. The largest chain the pin ships is Init/Data/BitVec/Lemmas at 14,418,208 bytes across its three parts; next is Std/Data/DTreeMap/Internal/Lemmas at 12,288,976. ChainLimits::default() is 64 MiB -- over four times the real maximum, so every pinned chain passes with wide headroom while an input that could only be hostile or corrupt is refused. The doc records the measurement and says callers holding larger artifacts should state their own ceiling rather than raise the default.

SIGNATURE CHANGE, SCOPE CHECKED. All six callers are inside fln-olean and all six are updated. I grepped the whole workspace to confirm no other crate names this function or ChainLimits, which matters because the override lets me check only this package.

TEST: a_chain_over_its_byte_ceiling_is_refused_before_parsing. A positive control first -- the same input under a ceiling that admits it gets past the charge and fails later on the module-system gate, so the refusal is demonstrably the ceiling and not the fixture -- then a ceiling one byte under the exact total, asserting ChainTooLarge with both the observed size and the limit.

  private_eq_n_auxiliary_requires_the_companion_and_keeps_its_real_kind

It does:

WAVE 31: my companion guard was comparing TOOLCHAINS, not modules. Two of my own tests would have failed on first execution. sha 4b09c5a4. cc_1 (StormyStork), 2026-08-20.

THE DEFECT, and it is mine. same_chain_identity (6369ceb0, extended to the view door at 1927b4db) compared version, flags, lean_version and githash and called the result a module identity. IT IS NOT. Those four fields identify the TOOLCHAIN: measured across all 2,431 chained modules of the pin they take exactly ONE distinct value. The comparison therefore returns true for ANY two artifacts this Lean built. It rejects a companion from a different toolchain, which is not a substitution that happens, and admits a companion from any other module of the same one, which is the substitution the guard exists for.

WHAT THAT MEANT FOR MY TESTS, stated plainly because two of them were wrong and I did not catch it for two waves.

  the_view_door_refuses_a_private_part_from_another_module (WAVE 25) supplies a foreign private part parsed against ITS OWN chain, so the view is well formed and only identity can separate it. With the stamp passing, decode continued to verify_private_superset and produced PrivatePartIncomplete -- exactly the error the test asserts it must NOT be. It would have failed.

  the_extra_const_names_union_refuses_a_foreign_private_part (WAVE 29) is worse: the union has no superset requirement, so with the stamp passing there is no error at all and its expect_err would panic.

  a_chain_assembled_from_two_modules_is_refused_by_identity (WAVE 20) would still have passed, but for an unrelated reason: it parses the foreign bytes against the WRONG regions, so the pointers fail to resolve long before any identity check runs. Its green was never evidence that the guard worked. That is the uncomfortable part -- the one test that could have run green was the one proving nothing.

Batch verify has reported these suites green, which I now read as those cells not having executed against a present pin rather than as confirmation.

THE REAL BOND IS STRUCTURAL. A companion is parsed against the earlier regions and stores their compacted addresses, and base_addr is distinct per module: 2,431 distinct values across 2,431 exported parts.

LANDED at 4b09c5a4, two files, +104 -14:

  crates/fln-olean/src/region.rs
    OleanView::is_chained_to(&other) -- is other's region among the dependency regions this view was parsed against.

  crates/fln-olean/src/decl.rs
    same_chain_identity replaced by is_companion_of(companion, exported), which keeps the header comparison as a cheap toolchain gate and then requires the structural bond. Both doors updated. The doc states which field answers which question, so the two are not conflated again.

THE NON-VACUITY TEST, which is the one that matters:
  the_toolchain_stamp_does_not_identify_a_module_but_the_chaining_does
It asserts the four header fields are EQUAL across two different modules -- i.e. that the cheap check ADMITS the foreign part -- and that is_chained_to is true for the module's own private part and false for the other's. Without it, is_companion_of could regress to a header comparison and every refusal test in this crate would still pass: one for the wrong reason, the rest by accident. The githash assertion carries a note that if it ever differs between two modules of one build, the test has stopped witnessing anything.

INERT ON CORRECT USAGE. Every legitimate caller parses the private view with the exported region among its dependencies, so is_chained_to holds. The pin cannot trip this.

RAN.
  cargo check -p fln-olean --tests    exit 0, no errors, no warnings
  cargo fmt -p fln-olean -- --check   clean for both files I touched; the crate is red on tests/private_companion_decode.rs from a peer's commit, which is theirs to land.

STILL UNPROVEN. Nothing executed; the code-first override forbids cargo test. The one-distinct-stamp and 2,431-distinct-base_addr measurements come from an independent byte-level reader.

THE GENERAL LESSON, since this is the second time this rotation the same shape has bitten. A guard whose PASS condition is satisfied by almost every input is indistinguishable from no guard, and a refusal test can go green because the input failed for some unrelated reason upstream. Both of my broken tests looked like evidence. The fix in each case was to assert that the CHEAP check admits the bad input, so that only the real check can be doing the work.

Reversed, a private part offering an axiom where the exported part had a body would hand the kernel a postulate in place of a definition, and the kernel would AGREE with it rather than check it. WAVE 38b: the "_unary decoded as axiom" failure is the decoder being FAITHFUL, and the crate lacked the API to say so. sha 968b1615. cc_1 (StormyStork), 2026-08-20.

THE REPORTED FAILURE IS NOT A DECODER BUG. unary_family_keeps_concrete_members_on_both_chain_origins reports that exported _unary Array.zipWithMAux._unary decoded only as an axiom. Read straight from the ConstantInfo constructor tag in the bytes:

  Init/Data/Array/Basic, Array.zipWithMAux._unary
    exported part : Axiom
    private part  : Defn

The exported bytes hold an AxiomVal. Decoding them to an axiom is correct. A decoder that returned a definition there would be INVENTING a body, which is the one direction that is genuinely unsound: it would hand the kernel a declaration the artifact does not contain, and the kernel would accept a type nobody derived. I did not write that, and I would not.

This is not a special case, and the scale is the point. Across the 2,431 chained modules, 84,590 of the 158,583 declarations named by BOTH arrays are an axiom in the exported part and a real declaration in the private one -- 60,640 theorems, 22,177 definitions, 1,773 opaques -- and NOT ONE runs the other way. One Shape reason with a return site and no mutant: "List cons". A list cell is cons and nothing else; a different constructor would be read with cons's head/tail layout, so a declaration's universe parameters or mutual-block names would be taken from an object of the wrong type.

SHADOWING CHECKED FIRST. The list decoder has no size bind at all, so none of the object-size rules I added across waves 47-57 can fire ahead of it, and the constructor check is the first thing it does with the header. The plant moves only the tag and the cell asserts the arity and size are unchanged afterwards.

IT NEEDED A NON-EMPTY LIST, the recurring trap in its sixth form. List.nil is fieldless and therefore scalar-boxed, so a fixture whose levelParams and all are empty contains NO cons cell and this rule is unreachable from it -- axiom_module and definition_module are both like that. param_level_module, added at cb87680c for the Level arity mutant, declares one universe parameter, so its ConstantVal.levelParams is a real cons.

That is the second time an earlier fixture has paid off rather than a new one being needed, and both times it was a fixture added for an unrelated rule. Worth noting for whoever works this file next: the fixture set is now varied enough (axiom, definition with abbrev hint, definition with regular hint, succ level, nested succ level, universe param, forall expr) that checking it BEFORE writing a new one is usually cheaper than adding another.

The cell asserts the slot is a POINTER before dereferencing it, so if the fixture ever loses its universe parameter the test fails loudly instead of silently exercising nothing. That guard is the direct product of the five earlier waves where a fixture would have exercised nothing.

WAVE 64: scalar-list mutant killed — the list pair is now complete. sha 8cb55e5e. cc_1 (StormyStork), 2026-08-21.

One Shape reason with a return site and no mutant: "scalar List not nil".

THIS COMPLETES THE LIST PAIR. The list decode has exactly two rules -- a scalar must be nil, a heap cell must be cons -- because nil is fieldless and therefore boxed while cons is an object. The cons half got its mutant last wave at 233a306d; this is the other. Same reasoning as the ReducibilityHints pair at 14e130f7 and 02c0cfbc: a type with two rules and one mutant reads as covered from the outside, which is a worse state than obviously uncovered.

Unchecked, a boxed value other than nil would be silently accepted AS the empty list, so a declaration's universe parameters or mutual-block names would come back EMPTY rather than wrong. That is a quiet loss rather than a visible corruption, and quiet losses are the failure class this whole bead started from.

THE FIXTURE PROBLEM FLIPS ROUND HERE, which is worth recording after six waves of the opposite. Every previous cell needed a fixture RICHER than the default, because the fieldless case is scalar-boxed and offers no object to plant on. This rule IS the fieldless case, so it needs the EMPTY list, and axiom_module -- the plainest fixture in the file -- is exactly right. param_level_module, which was the answer last wave, would not work here at all. So the rule for this file is not "prefer the richer fixture"; it is that the fieldless/heap split decides which fixture can reach a given rule, in whichever direction.

SHADOWING CHECKED FIRST. The plant writes a slot inside the ConstantVal, so that object's header is untouched and its arity and size rules cannot fire; the cell re-reads that header as (0, 3, 32) after planting to prove it.

WAVE 65: ConstantInfo wrapper arity mutant killed, and a shadowed group identified. sha c36e4ca5. cc_1 (StormyStork), 2026-08-21.

ONE PREMISE CORRECTION FIRST, per the block-expiry rule, which says to verify an instruction's premise before acting on it. The wave order says w64 asked for one Shape reason with a return site and no mutant and that I "completed the list-nil pair instead". Those were the same thing: "scalar List not nil" IS a Shape reason with a return site and no mutant, and it was the only one I landed that wave. Completing the pair was the reason I chose that particular reason, not a substitution for the ask. Nothing needs redoing.

THIS WAVE'S REASON: "ConstantInfo arity". The wrapper is one pointer -- the payload -- and nothing else; a second claimed pointer would make every later slot index address the wrong word.

SHADOWING CHECKED FIRST, and the answer is why I chose this one. "ConstantInfo arity" is the FIRST check decode_constant_info makes, ahead of the payload deref and therefore ahead of the payload size (1b53cb09) and padding (e9348f58) binds I added later. The wrapper's own cs_sz is bound by nothing, so the plant leaves it at 16 while claiming two pointers, and only the arity rule can object.

A SHADOWED GROUP, FOUND WHILE CHECKING, and I am recording it rather than leaving it for someone to rediscover. The PER-VARIANT arities -- "AxiomVal arity", "DefinitionVal arity", "OpaqueVal arity", "QuotVal arity", "InductiveVal arity", "ConstructorVal arity" -- all sit BEHIND my size and padding binds inside the same function. A bare arity plant on any of them trips the size rule first, because expected_cs_sz is computed from the arity being planted. Co-planting the size does not rescue it either: with a larger claimed size the padding read runs past the real object's end into whatever follows, so the padding rule fires on foreign bytes instead. So that whole group needs either a fixture whose payload really has the larger arity, or the same ordering cleanup I did for Level at f193516d -- moving the size and padding checks after the per-variant arity match. The second is the honest fix and it is not a one-liner, because the size check needs the tag to know the scalar count while the arity checks live inside the tag match.

That is the third time one of my own binds has shadowed a pre-existing rule (Level arity at f193516d, checked-and-clear for Name at c7a0733c, and now this group). The pattern is consistent enough to state: every size bind I added in waves 47-57 should be assumed to shadow whatever arity rule follows it until checked.

TEST: a_constant_info_wrapper_claiming_the_wrong_arity_is_refused. Positive control; assert the wrapper really is the axiom variant with one pointer and 16 bytes; claim two pointers in the header word alone; re-read to assert only the arity moved, as (0, 2, 16); assert the specific refusal. Every constant read back from the fixture rather than hard-coded.

WAVE 66: scalar-Expr-child mutant killed. sha 62de766d. cc_1 (StormyStork), 2026-08-21.

One Shape reason with a return site and no mutant: "scalar Expr child".

WHY IT MATTERS. Expressions are heap objects. A boxed scalar in a child slot is not a small expression -- it is a slot holding something that is not an expression at all. Unchecked, the post-order walk would SKIP it, because that walk only pushes non-scalar children, and the node would then be built from a child that was never decoded. That is a silent-substitution failure rather than a crash, which is the class this bead has been closing throughout.

SHADOWING CHECKED FIRST, per the pattern that has now caught three of my own binds. Within decode_expr the order is constructor, then arity, then this child loop, and only afterwards the size bind I added at 269b4671 -- so neither that bind nor the padding rules can fire ahead of it. The plant writes a SLOT rather than the header, so arity and size are untouched, and the cell re-asserts the header as (7, 3, 48) after planting to prove it.

TEST: a_scalar_in_an_expr_child_slot_is_refused. Positive control; assert the object really is the forallE shape AND that expr_child_slots(7) is [1, 2], so the table the loop iterates and the slot the cell plants into are pinned to EACH OTHER rather than one being assumed from the other; assert slot 1 currently holds a heap expression, so the plant is a change and not a no-op; box a scalar in its place; assert the header unchanged; assert the specific refusal.

That table-and-object pinning is the same shape I used for expr_slots at b32e0720. It is worth doing consistently: these cells depend on two things agreeing, and asserting only one of them leaves the cell passing if the other drifts.

The sibling reason "scalar Expr" -- a scalar reaching the decoder as a ROOT rather than as a child -- is a separate site and is left for its own wave, one mutant per commit as before.

WAVE 67: scalar-Expr-root mutant killed — the scalar-Expr pair is complete. sha a7095365. cc_1 (StormyStork), 2026-08-21.

The sibling of last wave's child-slot rule, and a genuinely separate SITE rather than a second way to reach the same one.

WHY IT NEEDED ITS OWN MUTANT, which is the part worth recording because it is not obvious from reading the two rules side by side. The child loop rejects a scalar BEFORE it can ever be pushed onto the decode stack, so no child plant can reach the top-of-loop guard. The only way a scalar arrives there is as the ROOT the decoder was handed -- a slot whose owner believed it held an expression. ConstantVal.type_ is such a slot, so a boxed scalar there is the one shape that exercises it.

That also means the two rules cannot be collapsed into one: they catch the same bad value arriving by two different routes, and only one of the routes is reachable from a child. A reviewer looking for redundancy would plausibly try to merge them.

SHADOWING CHECKED FIRST. decode_constant_val validates its own header -- arity, then the size bind from f820d9b1 -- before touching any slot, and the plant leaves that header alone. The two slots decoded AHEAD of the type, name and levelParams, are untouched too, so neither the Name rules nor the list rules can fire first. That last check mattered here more than usual: this cell plants inside an object whose other slots feed four rules I have already mutated, so "nothing else fires first" needed three exclusions rather than one. The cell asserts the owning header is still (0, 3, 32) after planting.

TEST: a_scalar_reaching_the_expression_decoder_as_a_root_is_refused. Positive control; assert the type slot currently holds a heap expression, so the plant is a change and not a no-op; box a scalar in its place; assert the owning header unchanged; assert the "scalar Expr" refusal specifically. The assertion message says "rather than the child-slot one", because the two reasons are adjacent and a cell that accepted either would not distinguish them.

THIS COMPLETES THE Shape RULES FOR Expr, as 80dc4134 did for Level. The arity (b32e0720), the object size (269b4671), the post-order law (bc2d8630), the scalar child and scalar root (62de766d, a7095365) and the binder byte (49b72dcf) all have mutants; the constructor was the last without one. Expr and Level are now the two types in this decoder whose Shape rules are fully mutated.

SHADOWING CHECKED FIRST. expr_slots is consulted immediately after the header, ahead of the arity check and well ahead of the size bind, so an unknown tag is rejected before either can look at it.

THE SHARPER HALF IS WORTH RECORDING BESIDE THE LEVEL CASE, because it is a different failure mode. The size bind would NOT have caught this on its own: expr_scalar_bytes falls back to zero for an unrecognised tag, so tag 12 carrying this object's arity and size is arithmetically CONSISTENT to the size law. Had the ordering been the other way round -- as decode_level's was before f193516d -- the plant would not have been reported as a size fault. It would have sailed PAST the size check with the fallback's blessing and been caught later or not at all.

So the two orderings fail differently. In Level, an early size bind SHADOWED a later rule and produced the wrong diagnosis. In Expr, an early size bind would have produced NO diagnosis, because its table has a permissive default for exactly the input the constructor rule exists to reject. A guard placed after a fallback can be reached with the fallback having already approved the object, and that is a quieter failure than shadowing.

THIS COMPLETES Literal, whose decode has exactly ONE rule, the way 80dc4134 and ebfd2d85 completed Level and Expr. A one-rule type with no mutant is the easiest kind to lose quietly: the rule here is the catch-all arm of a match, and a refactor that turned that arm into a permissive fallback would look like a simplification and go unnoticed. That is nonsense as Lean -- a type is not a numeral -- and deliberately so: this exercises a decode shape, not an elaboration, and the encoder does not care. So the fixture-reachability question has two distinct causes now, boxing and simple absence, and both have to be checked rather than assumed.

SHADOWING CHECKED FIRST. decode_literal has no size bind of its own, so none of the object-size rules from waves 47-57 reach it, and the constructor match is the first thing it does with the header. The enclosing Expr.lit object is untouched by the plant, so the Expr constructor, arity and size rules cannot fire either; the cell asserts that header afterwards as well as the literal's.

WAVE 72: DataValue.ofBool arity mutant killed. sha 466d162b. cc_1 (StormyStork), 2026-08-21.

First of the DataValue group, reachable because 27f2ce93's mdata_expr_module put a real DataValue in the region. First wave in three that needed NO new fixture.

WHY THIS ONE FIRST, ahead of the group's catch-all. ofBool carries a single scalar byte and NO pointers, so the decoder reads that byte at a fixed off + 8. A claimed pointer field puts a whole WORD where the byte is, and the value then read as the flag is the LOW BYTE OF A POINTER -- a plausible 0 or 1 either way. So the fault does not announce itself: the decode succeeds and the option is silently true or false depending on an address. That is the quiet-substitution shape this bead keeps turning up, and it is a better first target than a rule whose failure is an obvious refusal.

SHADOWING CHECKED FIRST, and this cell has the deepest nesting so far: the DataValue sits inside a pair, inside a list cell, inside an Expr.mdata. FOUR rule sets could plausibly fire ahead of it, where earlier cells had one. decode_data_value has no size bind, and its scalar guard passes because ofBool is a heap object -- asserted rather than assumed, since a fieldless constructor would have been boxed and unreachable, which is the trap from waves 60-64. The plant leaves the pair, the cell and the mdata object untouched, so the KVMap pair rule (27f2ce93), the list rules (233a306d, 8cb55e5e) and the Expr rules cannot fire; all three headers are re-asserted after planting alongside the value's own.

Positive control; assert the value really is ofBool with zero pointer fields; assert the flag byte reads 1 AT THE OFFSET THE RULE PROTECTS, so the cell demonstrates what the arity is guarding rather than only that a number changed; claim one pointer field in the header word alone; assert only the arity moved and all three enclosing objects are unchanged; assert the specific refusal.

That flag-byte assertion is a small addition to the pattern and I think worth keeping: until now these cells proved the mutant was refused, but not what the rule was protecting. Reading the guarded byte in the positive case says why the arity matters.

WAVE 73: QuotKind byte mutant killed — on the pin's thinnest-covered constructor. sha 6c8d6724. cc_1 (StormyStork), 2026-08-21.

One Shape reason with a return site and no mutant: "QuotKind byte". The four kinds are Type, Ctor, Lift and Ind, and they say which axiom of the quotient a declaration IS. A fifth value has no meaning, and silently folding it onto one of the four would misidentify a quotient primitive -- a semantic fault like the definition safety byte (95c98cbd), not a layout one.

THIS IS THE THINNEST-COVERED CONSTRUCTOR IN THE PIN, and that is the specific reason to reach it from a fixture rather than trust corpus traffic. While binding the payload sizes at 1b53cb09 I counted the whole corpus by variant -- 215,111 ConstantInfo payloads across all 2,431 chained modules:

  Defn 110,102   Thm 90,536   Ctor 4,977   Rec 3,199
  Opaque 3,142   Induct 3,071   Axiom 80   Quot 4

Four. The corpus exercises this path four times in total, so a rule about its scalar cannot be called covered by corpus traffic in any meaningful sense, and the ratio to Defn is about 1 in 27,000. quot_module is the first fixture in this file to build one, and I would suggest the same reasoning applies to anything else that touches Quot: the pin will not find your bug.

SHADOWING CHECKED FIRST. The kind is the FIRST scalar of the payload, at voff + 8 + 8*other, so the plant leaves the header alone and the payload size bind (1b53cb09) cannot fire; and the byte is not inside the padding the padding bind (e9348f58) guards. THE FIXTURE HAD THE SAME DEFECT AS LAST WAVE'S. recursor_module set k and isUnsafe both to false. That is the second vacuity of exactly this shape in a fixture I wrote two waves ago: equal values in indexed sibling fields. The counts were 0/0/0/0 and the flags were false/false. The rhs is the half of a computation rule the kernel REDUCES with. ctor and nfields say WHEN a rule applies; the rhs says WHAT it produces. The arity/order pin from 191a5783 compares rules as (ctor, nfields) pairs, so it is satisfied by two rules whose right-hand sides have been swapped - each rule is still well-formed, each still points at a well-formed name and expression, and the recursor still computes the wrong thing.

THE FIXTURE WAS NOT SUFFICIENT, AND THAT IS THE FINDING. Both rules carried Sort 0. The property was untestable by construction: identical expressions cannot reveal a swap, and any assertion distinguishing rule 0's rhs from rule 1's would have been vacuous - it would have passed on a decoder that had crossed them. This is the fifth instance in this one fixture of a value chosen for convenience rather than for distinguishability, after the telescope counts, the flags, the level parameters and the mutual block, and like all four it was invisible until someone tried to pin the field. I recorded in comment 2346 that recursor_module had no placeholder defaults left; that was true of EMPTY and ZERO defaults and false of DUPLICATE ones, which is a category I had not been checking for. The second rule now carries Sort 1.

SUCCESSIVE SORTS RATHER THAN TWO ARBITRARY EXPRESSIONS, and the choice is load-bearing rather than cosmetic. Sort 0 holds a scalar-boxed Level.zero in its slot; Sort 1 holds a POINTER to a Level.succ object. So the two are distinguishable on the wire without decoding anything, and they are distinct heap objects - which is what lets the cell check the ASSOCIATION between rule and rhs rather than only the two values.

Asserting that literal from layout reasoning alone (8 header + 2 pointers) is exactly the unmeasured-size mistake recorded in comments 2285 and 2286, where I asserted forallE cs_sz == 40 with a message whose own arithmetic said 48. The measurement this needs: count List.cons objects reachable from the pin's constant arrays and confirm every one is cs_sz == 24, the same shape as the Name measurement already in decode_name. cidx, numParams and numFields are three Nats at ADJACENT payload slots 2, 3 and 4, all read by the same decode_nat_u32. Nothing about their shapes distinguishes them: a decoder crossing any two produces three well-formed naturals, and no arity, size or constructor rule can object. THE ROUND-TRIP FIXTURE HAD EXACTLY THAT: cidx and numFields BOTH held u32::MAX, so slots 2 and 4 were indistinguishable and a swap decoded identically.

THIS IS A THIRD SHAPE OF VACUITY AND IT IS WHY THE PREVIOUS TWELVE WAVES WALKED PAST IT. The campaign has been clearing two shapes: EMPTY/ZERO placeholders (the recursor telescope 0/0/0/0, the empty all, the empty levelParams) and SINGLE-ELEMENT lists with no order (recursor rules, inductive all/ctors, constructor levelParams). Both are recognisable as defaults - nobody chose them, they were what you write when the field does not matter.

u32::MAX is not that. It is a DELIBERATE boundary value: it exercises the u32::try_from edge in decode_nat_u32, which is a real thing to test and the reason someone wrote it. Being deliberate is precisely what stopped anyone reading it as a default, including me, across every scan I have run over this fixture. The rule the previous waves arrived at - "vacuous 0 is not a pin" - does not catch it, because 0 is not the problem.

THE ACTUAL RULE IS ABOUT NEIGHBOURS, NOT ABOUT VALUES. A value chosen for a good reason is still a vacuity if a NEIGHBOURING field of the same type was chosen for the SAME good reason. Two fields that both deserve the boundary value must not both get it, because their adjacency is what a decoder can get wrong and their equality is what hides it. I did not have this rule before this wave; I had "not a default", which is a property of one field read alone, and this defect is only visible reading two.

REPAIR KEEPS BOTH PROPERTIES. cidx is now 7 and numFields keeps u32::MAX, so the three are pairwise distinct AND the try_from boundary is still exercised. Dropping the boundary to get distinctness would have traded one real test for another.

cidx IS THE SHARPEST OF THE THREE, because it is the constructor's POSITION in its inductive's constructor list. But more than that: a single witness is weak in a way I did not see until I had the second one. Read alone, c48c0813 says "malformed input produces an error" - which is what a decoder is supposed to do, and a reader could close the bead on it. If the planted cell were caught by the Name ctor shape rule instead, this cell would still pass while proving the OPPOSITE of what it says - that the two shapes are distinguishable without consulting the size. So it asserts the message is the SIZE rule's, and separately that the planted cell really carries the colliding tag and arity and a size other than 32, so there is something for that rule to refuse. That is the shadowing check applied to a refusal message rather than to a mutant: an earlier rule firing first would make the later one untestable, exactly as my Level size bind shadowed the arity rule before f193516d.

The offset is asserted for the same reason as in the sibling: refusing at the planted cell rather than one hop later is precisely the behaviour list_ptrs lacks, and asserting only "an error occurred" would keep passing against either.

The cell decodes the module first, asserts the pinned 16-constant SizeOfLemmas census this file already fixes, and then selects a ConstantVal by DECODING its slot-0 name and requiring that name to be one the module actually declares. The plant therefore lands in a real declaration and the failure messages name it. No declaration string is hard-coded, so there is nothing here to rot when the fixture is regenerated.

WAVE 140: the cons cell's stored size recorded, by DERIVING it rather than writing it down. sha ac97cb3a. cc_1 (StormyStork), 2026-08-21.

c48c0813 established that a name link and a cons cell differ in cs_sz, which is what makes the list_ptrs repair possible. It deliberately did not write the cons cell's number: that was the one value I had reasoned to and not measured, and comments 2285/2286 record what writing such a literal costs.

THE DEFECT IN MY OWN PREVIOUS WAVE, NAMED PLAINLY. That left the measurement EXISTING and the number UNRECORDED. A passing test prints nothing. So the cell has been computing the cons size on every run and telling nobody, and I reported the src repair as blocked on a value that was already being computed three commits earlier. The blocker was real but its description was wrong: the missing thing was never the measurement, it was a channel for the measurement to arrive on. That is worth writing down because "we lack the measurement" and "the measurement has nowhere to go" look identical from the outside and have completely different repairs.

THE WAY OUT IS NOT TO GUESS BETTER, IT IS TO DERIVE. Every Lean object's size is its header, plus one word per declared pointer field, plus whatever scalar area the constructor stores after them. `other` is on the wire. So the SCALAR AREA WIDTH is measurable per object as cs_sz - (8 + 8 * other) - and it is that WIDTH, not the total, that actually separates the two shapes: a cons cell stores nothing after its two pointers, a name link stores the Name.hash word. decode_name's own comment states the same arithmetic for its side, as 8 + 8*2 + 8.

This also answers the order's caution about not inventing a discriminator. I did not invent one. The width is read from each object's own header, and the rule it yields is the one decode_name already applies, expressed in the form that makes it apply to cons cells too.

THE LITERAL IS ENTAILED, NOT ASSERTED. The cell proves from the bytes that the cons scalar width is zero, that the name width is eight, and that every cons cell declares two pointer fields - and only then records what that makes the size, 24. ORDER MATTERS for the reason f193516d had to correct in decode_level: a literal checked before the rule that explains it teaches the reader nothing when it fires. If the corpus disagrees, the derivation fails first and names the real width, so the failure is a finding rather than a puzzle.

SCALE. The cell scans the three C3 fixtures and, where the pin is installed, Init/Prelude.olean as well - so a host with the Reference measures at corpus scale while a host without it still measures. It refuses to report below 100 objects of each kind, because a measurement over nothing reports whatever it likes.

WHAT THIS IS NOT. It is not the repair and it does not make one; list_ptrs still reads no size, and src/ is untouched per the order. What it removes is the last stated blocker: the src change now has a derived width rule and a recorded number to apply, rather than my arithmetic.

The recorded size is what this cell WILL establish on its first run, not something I have observed. If 24 is wrong, the derivation assertion above it fires first and prints the true width - which is the outcome this cell is built to produce, not a failure of it.

WAVE 141: the measured cons cells bound to the ones the decoder actually walked. sha c4cbf83c. cc_1 (StormyStork), 2026-08-21.

CONFIRMED ABSENT BEFORE WRITING, as the order asked. I grepped decl_decode.rs for any existing tie between a measured cell and a decoded list length and found none.

WHAT THE ABSENCE ACTUALLY WAS, and it is a hole in my own three previous commits rather than a missing nicety. c48c0813's collision measurement, 35efc748's two witnesses and ac97cb3a's derived width all classify objects by walking bytes from the ROOT WORD. Not one of them establishes that the objects so measured are the objects list_ptrs traverses. I had been treating "reachable from the root" and "walked by the list decoder" as the same set without ever saying so, let alone checking it.

THE GAP IS INVISIBLE WHILE THE NUMBERS AGREE AND FATAL IF THEY DO NOT. A width measured over cells the decoder never visits would license a size rule for a population the rule will not be applied to, and the src repair would rest on a measurement of the wrong set. Nothing in those three commits would have said so - they would all still be green, and the recorded 24 would still look like a measurement. This is the denominator defect again: a scan whose population is quietly not the one it names. I have now hit that shape three times on this bead (the filter-continue sampler, the vacuous classifier, and this), each time in a different layer, which is the argument for checking the population every time rather than recognising the pattern.

THE BINDING IS A COUNT, PER DECLARATION. For each ConstantVal on the wire the cell walks its levelParams chain and counts cells; for each decoded constant it takes level_params.len(); and it requires the two to be equal for that declaration BY NAME. Equality in both directions is what makes the two populations one: no cell the decoder skipped, and no name it invented. Width and size are then asserted on the cells that count bound, not on everything shaped like a cons cell - which is the whole difference from ac97cb3a.

THE ANTI-VACUITY GUARD IS THE TOTAL, and it is load-bearing. Every equality here is satisfied as 0 == 0 by a corpus of universe-monomorphic declarations, so the cell would pass over an empty population and report a binding it never made. It requires the bound total to be positive and prints it with the declaration count.

PERFORMANCE, since a test that hangs is a test nobody runs: the object map is indexed once per module rather than scanned per chain hop. Prelude carries enough objects that the naive find-in-vector form would have made this cell quadratic, and I caught that in review rather than at run time - which I mention because I could not have caught it at run time, the override forbidding cargo test.

REWORK of WAVE 141: my decode-binding cell was itself the defect it looks for. sha 57da74fe. cc_1 (StormyStork), 2026-08-21.

w113 RED: the_measured_cons_cells_are_the_ones_the_decoder_walked panicked on Init/Prelude.olean with (246, 0) != (1, 2).

THE CELL TREATED A HEADER SHAPE AS AN IDENTITY. It selected candidates by (tag, other, cs_sz) == (0, 3, 32), called them ConstantVals, and asserted that every hop of such an object's slot-1 chain was a cons cell. That shape is ConstantVal's AND also other three-field structures'. Tag 246 is TAG_ARRAY, so on Prelude one of those structures holds an array where a levelParams list would be, and my assertion fired on it.

THE PART WORTH RECORDING IS THE TIMING, NOT THE BUG. This is a projection keyed as an identity without checking injectivity - the defect my own memory names as recurring, that a build gate exists for elsewhere in this repo, and that the surrounding cells in this very file were written to catch. I committed it one commit after writing in comment 2371 that I keep hitting the population-mismatch shape in a new layer each time and that the lesson is to check the population every single time rather than trust myself to recognise the pattern. I then did not check my own. Knowing the shape did not help; only the corpus did.

WHY IT LOOKED FINE: the three C3 fixtures are too small to contain a collision, so the filter was injective on everything I could reach under the code-first override and stopped being injective at Prelude scale. A discriminator validated only on the small corpus is a discriminator validated nowhere, and the previous cells in this file share the C3-only exposure - what saves them is that they classify by an independent structural discriminator rather than by a header shape.

THE REPAIR IS NOT A LOOSER ASSERTION, and the order explicitly allowed one. Skipping non-cons hops would have made the cell pass while silently measuring whatever it stumbled into, which is the outcome the whole campaign is about avoiding. Instead: a candidate must also NAME a declaration the module declares; a candidate whose slot 1 is not a cons chain is DROPPED rather than asserted against, because a mismatch there is evidence the object is something else and not evidence the corpus is malformed; and the binding then requires some candidate to carry a chain of EXACTLY the decoded length, with widths and sizes measured on that chain.

THAT IS STRICTLY STRONGER THAN WHAT w113 KILLED. The old version did `insert` into a name-keyed map, so two same-named candidates silently overwrote each other and the binding could have been built from a lookalike's bytes with no assertion firing. The red exposed a second defect I was not looking for.

The walk is now capped at 4096 hops. The post-order law forbids cycles and hostile_input.rs tests that, but a test that hangs is worse than one that fails, and this cell should not depend on a law it is not itself checking.

The four cells that passed - both planted witnesses, the collision measurement and the scalar-area derivation - are untouched. Verified: the diff is three hunks, all inside the failing cell and its doc comment, and zero lines of the other four cells' bodies are in it.

WAVE 144: the whole (1,2) population bounded, not the part my classifier could name. sha 2493b77b. cc_1 (StormyStork), 2026-08-21.

EVERYTHING MEASURED SO FAR WAS THE WRONG HALF. A cons cell is 24, a name link is 32, so a size rule can tell those two apart - that is SUFFICIENCY. But adding cs_sz != 24 to list_ptrs makes it REFUSE, and a refusal rule is safe only if nothing legitimate carries a size it rejects, and useful only if nothing illegitimate carries a size it accepts. Neither direction follows from measuring the two shapes we already knew about. I have been recommending a one-line fix for four commits on evidence that does not reach the property the fix needs.

AND MY EARLIER MEASUREMENT COULD NOT HAVE SEEN IT. c48c0813's classifier ends in `_ => {}`. A (1,2) object whose second field is neither a string, nor boxed nil, nor another (1,2) object is silently dropped. So its populations are a FILTERED SUBSET and its "every cons cell is 24" is a claim about what it chose to look at, not about the corpus. That is the filter-that-continues-is-a-sampler defect, in my own code, undetected through three subsequent commits that cited it as the measurement.

The cell is not WRONG about what it measured. It never bounded the remainder, and the remainder is exactly where a refusal rule gets hurt. Those are different failures and only the second one matters here, which is why this commit adds a cell rather than editing that one.

WHAT THE NEW CELL ASSERTS. It partitions the same population exhaustively: every (1,2) object of size 24 really is cons-shaped, so the rule accepts nothing it should reject; every one of size 32 really is a name link, so it rejects nothing it should accept; and no third size occurs at (1,2) at all. The partition is checked by ARITHMETIC - the two classes must sum to the population - so a shape falling outside both is a failure rather than a silent omission. That arithmetic check is the specific thing c48c0813 lacked, and it is cheap; the reason it was missing is that a match with a fallthrough arm looks exhaustive.

A FAILURE HERE IS A FINDING THAT BLOCKS THE REPAIR, not a broken test, and the assertion messages say so. If a third size appears, or a 24-byte (1,2) object is not a cons cell, then cs_sz does not identify these shapes and the fix is wrong. That is exactly what (0,3,32) did to the binding cell at w113: one header triple, two different structures. The same thing happening at (1,2) is not a remote possibility - it is the thing that has already happened once in this file, one commit ago, to me.

COMPLIANCE WITH THE ORDER: no (1,2) assertion is made on an even pointer reached by walking a chain. This cell enumerates objects that already carry that header and asks what their sizes mean, so the w113 failure mode is structurally absent rather than avoided by care. The four passing cells are untouched; the commit is +146 -0.

WAVE 146 (resumes 145): the all and ctors chains bound to the decoder, not just levelParams. sha e7485ba4. cc_1 (StormyStork), 2026-08-21.

CONFIRMED ABSENT FIRST, as ordered, and the confirmation mattered: decl_decode.rs was clean against HEAD 58ee4942 and the cell name appeared zero times.

THE GAP. the_measured_cons_cells_are_the_ones_the_decoder_walked is green at w114 - and it walks levelParams and nothing else. decode_name_list has SEVEN call sites: levelParams, `all` on five different payloads, and `ctors`. So "the cells list_ptrs walks" has meant "the cells ONE of its seven callers walks", while the size rule the repair adds would apply to all of them. That is the denominator question one level up: not which OBJECTS were measured, but which CALLERS produced the objects that were measured. I have now had to ask that question at three different levels on this bead, and each time the previous answer read as complete.

MATCHED BY CONTENT, NOT BY SLOT INDEX, and that is forced rather than stylistic. `all` sits at payload slot 3 for a definition, 2 for a theorem and an opaque, 3 for an inductive, 1 for a recursor, and `ctors` at 4 - six layout constants. A cell keyed on those numbers would mean nothing the moment one moved. This scans every pointer slot of the payload, tries to read a cons chain of names from each, and accepts the slot whose decoded members EQUAL the list the decoder returned. A layout change moves which slot matches; it cannot make a wrong slot match.

IDENTIFIED BY REFERENCE, NOT BY HEADER. A ConstantVal is trusted only when its slot-0 name is one the module declares; the payload is then whatever object POINTS AT that ConstantVal in its own slot 0, base being slot 0 in all eight variants. No (tag, other, cs_sz) triple is treated as an identity anywhere in this cell, because (0,3,32) already proved they are not. That is the w113 lesson applied structurally rather than remembered.

A candidate slot that is not a cons chain is SKIPPED rather than asserted against. The claim is carried by REQUIRING a matching chain to exist, not by rejecting the ones that do not. No assertion in this cell says an even pointer must be (1,2), per the order.

WHY WAVE 145 DID NOT LAND, and it is worth recording as a mechanism rather than as an excuse. The heredoc that wrote the patch script ran as the disk filled, so the script was created ZERO BYTES. Python exits 0 on an empty file: it prints nothing, changes nothing, and returns success. The cause was only findable by stat-ing the script. REWORK of WAVE 144: a third shape shares the cons cell header. The size rule is BLOCKED. sha daaaabe2. cc_1 (StormyStork), 2026-08-21.

THE FINDING IS AGAINST MY OWN RECOMMENDATION, and it is the most important thing on this bead in ten waves.

w115 measured 7,591 objects at (tag, other) == (1, 2). NINETY-NINE of them are 24 bytes with a tail that is neither a cons cell nor boxed nil, the first at Init/Prelude.olean offset 0x32e7d0. So cs_sz == 24 does NOT identify a cons cell, and the one-line list_ptrs fix I recommended across five commits - bad3bd20, c48c0813, 35efc748, ac97cb3a, 2493b77b - is wrong as stated. A refusal keyed on the size would accept those 99 as list cells.

I HAD BEEN CALLING IT UNBLOCKED. Comment 2368 said the repair was "unblocked pending one green run". Comment 2374 corrected that to two greens and said sufficiency had been measured while safety had not. The second correction was right about the shape of the gap and still understated it: safety is not merely unmeasured, it FAILS. The measurement I asked for is the one that killed the recommendation.

WHAT SURVIVES, stated precisely so nobody over-corrects. Size still separates a NAME LINK from a cons cell. Both planted witnesses stand, decode_name's 32-byte rule is untouched, and the Name/cons collision is still real and still one-directional. What does not survive is the inference from "size separates these two shapes" to "size identifies a cons cell". Separating two known shapes is not identifying one, and identifying one is what list_ptrs needs.

NOTE WHICH ASSERTION PASSED, because it locates the defect and it is the reusable lesson. The partition BY SIZE is still exhaustive: every (1,2) object is 24 or 32, and there is no third SIZE. The third shape hides INSIDE 24. A cell that had only counted sizes would still be green and still be wrong. The four earlier measurement cells all counted sizes. This one looked at what the TAIL POINTS AT, and that single extra question is the entire difference between a green that means something and a green that does not.

WHAT THE 99 ARE IS NOT KNOWN AND IS NOT GUESSED. The cell now splits the 24-byte population into cons-shaped and this third tail, PINS the remainder at 99 so the blocker cannot quietly disappear, and captures a characterisation of the tails - object tag and arity, boxed scalar value, or unresolvable pointer - into the failure message. I deliberately did not write a hypothesis into the test. Identifying them is the next piece of work and it is now the critical path.

Per the order: misfits.is_empty() is gone; the anti-vacuity floor of 100 and the requirement that both 24 and 32 be witnessed are kept; the pinned count is asserted only where Init/Prelude.olean was actually loaded, since that is the corpus it was measured over.

THE PIN IS TWO-DIRECTIONAL ON PURPOSE. If the remainder grows, the corpus changed. If it falls to zero, the blocker is gone and the size rule is back on the table. Either way somebody must look, which is what a disclosed remainder has to do to be worth more than a comment.

RENAMED: no_third_shape_shares_the_cons_cell_header_and_the_sizes_identify_the_two is now a_third_shape_shares_the_cons_cell_header_and_bounds_the_size_rule. The old name asserts what the corpus disproved. Isolated runs tracking the old name should follow the new one.

comments.text:
WAVE 149: the 99 identified — they are not lists at all, and no size rule can rescue list_ptrs. sha 2ea2447b. cc_1 (StormyStork), 2026-08-21.

MEASURED, NOT GUESSED, and the method matters. I did not write an expected histogram and let an isolated red print the real one. That would be using CI as a print statement, and it is the lazy version of what w115 did honestly. Instead I computed the histogram over the same four modules with an independent walker - a standalone parser, not cargo test, so the code-first override is respected - and that walker reproduced w115's two published numbers EXACTLY: 7,591 objects at (1,2), 99 third tails, first at Init/Prelude.olean 0x32e7d0. Two implementations agreeing on the population is the reason this pin is a record rather than a hypothesis.

THE HISTOGRAM OF WHAT THE 99 TAILS POINT AT:
  tag 0 arity 2      71
  tag 4 arity 2      11
  boxed scalar 1     6
  boxed scalar 2     4
  boxed scalar 3     2
  boxed scalar 4     2
  boxed scalar 5     2
  boxed scalar 6     1
                     --- 99

THE BOXED SCALARS SETTLE IT, and this is the finding. A List tail is either a pointer to another cell or the boxed nil - and nil is boxed ZERO, because List has exactly ONE nullary constructor. Seventeen of the 99 carry a boxed tail of 1 through 6. An object whose second field holds boxed 1..6 belongs to a type with SEVERAL nullary constructors. It is not a list, and no walk of it as a list can be correct at any step.

The other 82 point at two-field structures, tag 0 and tag 4. Those are CONSISTENT with the same reading and do not establish it on their own, which is why the seventeen carry their own assertion instead of being left inside the histogram where an edit could quietly drop them.

SO THE 99 ARE CONSTRUCTORS OF OTHER INDUCTIVES that coincide with List.cons on tag, arity AND size. That sharpens daaaabe2 from "the size rule is blocked" to something stronger and worse: NO REFINEMENT OF THE SIZE CAN SEPARATE THEM, because the size is identical. The one-line repair I recommended across five commits is not merely out of scope for some population - it cannot be made to work by choosing a better constant. I have now argued for that fix, found it blocked, and found the block unfixable-in-kind, across three consecutive waves.

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE BEAD, stated plainly because I have been wrong about it twice. list_ptrs cannot be repaired by reading cs_sz. If it is to be repaired at all, the discriminator has to come from CONTEXT - what the caller expects at that slot - not from the object header, because the header is genuinely ambiguous in this corpus. I am not proposing that design here; the honest state is that the cheap fix is dead and the expensive one is unscoped.

WHAT IS STILL NOT KNOWN: which inductives these are, and whether any of them is reachable from the constants array as opposed to only from ModuleData's entries payload. I wrote a reachability cell for exactly that question this wave and did not land it, because the re-sent order asked for the histogram and one cell. The reachability split is the obvious next increment and would settle whether list_ptrs can ever be HANDED one of these, which is a different question from whether they exist.

Per the order: misfits.is_empty() is asserted nowhere; the remainder count stays pinned two-way; the population floor of 100 is kept and re-checked in this cell so the two cannot drift apart about which population they describe. Without the pin the cell asserts the third shape does NOT occur in the C3 fixtures rather than skipping silently, so finding one there would be a new fact rather than a no-op.
