WAVE 153: the 99 are reached ONLY through module entries, never through constants. sha 1dd7c288. cc_1 (StormyStork), 2026-08-21.

CONFIRMED ABSENT FIRST: no reachable_from helper, no such cell, decl_decode.rs clean against HEAD. The WAVE 150 cell I drafted and did not land was never committed, so this is new work rather than a re-land.

THE QUESTION THIS ANSWERS. 2ea2447b established WHAT the 99 are - constructors of other inductives sharing List.cons's tag, arity and size, seventeen provably not lists because their tail is a boxed value other than nil. That settles that the size can never identify a cons cell. It does NOT settle whether list_ptrs can ever be HANDED one, and those are different questions. I said so at the end of comment 2384 and this closes that item.

ModuleData carries five pointers. constants at slot 2 is the declaration graph decode_module_constants walks; entries at slot 4 is Array (Name x Array EnvExtensionEntry) - arbitrary serialised extension payloads the declaration decoder never enters.

MEASURED, NOT GUESSED, by the same standalone parser as last wave: all 99 reachable from entries, NONE from constants. third=99, in_constants=0, entries_only=99, neither=0.

THE ANTI-VACUITY GUARD IS THE WHOLE CELL, and I want this recorded because the cell would otherwise be the most impressive-looking green in the file and would mean nothing. A constants walk that reached NOTHING - wrong slot, broken deref, an off-by-one in the root arithmetic - would report zero third-shape objects in the declaration graph and be indistinguishable from the real result. Zero is exactly what a broken instrument returns. So the cell pins how many CONS-SHAPED cells that same walk reaches: 2,259 of the corpus's 2,465, against 206 reachable only from entries. A walk that finds thousands of cons cells and none of the third shape has EXCLUDED something; a walk that finds nothing has merely FAILED. The guard is asserted before the exclusion it licenses.

That is the same lesson as w113 and as the (1,2) denominator, arriving in a third form: there the population was mis-typed, then under-counted, and here it would have been empty. Each time the failure is silent and the green is confident.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH, stated because I have overstated this bead's state twice. It is ONE corpus at ONE pin. "Not reachable here" is not "cannot be reached". And entries decoding is itself open work under franken_lean-0nz - the moment those payloads are walked, these objects are in scope for whatever walks them. This NARROWS the blocker to a population the declaration decoder does not currently touch. It does not retire it, and it does not make the size a discriminator, which 2ea2447b already settled it is not.

WHERE THAT LEAVES list_ptrs, as plainly as I can put it. The cheap fix - refuse a cons cell whose cs_sz is not 24 - is still unsound as a general rule, because the third shape IS 24 bytes and the size cannot separate it. What has changed is scope: within the declaration graph, as measured, no such object is reachable, so the rule would not currently misfire there. That is an argument for a rule stated with its scope, not for the rule I originally proposed, and it is a decision for whoever sequences this rather than something I should take unilaterally after being wrong about it twice.

Per the order: misfits.is_empty() is asserted nowhere, and the remainder count is pinned two-way here as well as in its own cell, so the two cannot drift.

title: W5 FIR: specialization, simplification, inlining, and effect-preserving optimization
description:
## Description

Own monomorphization/specialization, simplification, inlining, constant folding, DCE, tail transforms, effect and source preservation, same-stage fallback, per-pass witnesses, and deterministic cost/tie-break policy.

## Acceptance Criteria

Suites specialization_model, simplification_equivalence, effect_preservation_property, pass_mutation_matrix, fir_simplify_no_mock_e2e cover thresholds, recursion, polymorphism, effects, optional rollback, cancellation, and recovery. title: W4 Vellum: Syntax kind/atom/node/missing forms and the lossless green tree
description:
Split out of fln-23cz by cc_3 on 2026-07-25 after landing slice 1 (commit e20cded: SourceInfo, byte/scalar/UTF-16 projections, and the byte-exact losslessness law).

## What is owed

The Syntax forms themselves, and the green tree over them:

* kind / atom / node / missing forms, faithful to upstream Init/Prelude.lean — Syntax.missing, Syntax.node (info) (kind : SyntaxNodeKind) (args), Syntax.atom (info) (val : String), Syntax.ident (info) (rawVal : Substring.Raw) (val : Name) (preresolved).
* Lossless green nodes: a tree whose token spans tile the source exactly, so the whole file reassembles byte-for-byte from the tree rather than from a token list.
* Immutable structural identity for syntax, with the same discipline applied in franken_lean-rps and franken_lean-l84f: distinct inputs must stay distinct, and any digest or identity over a tree must not project away a distinction the tree makes.

## Why it is separate

It needs Name for SyntaxNodeKind and for Syntax.ident, which is a dependency edge fln-syntax does not have. That edge must be declared in ci/WORKSPACE_GRAPH.txt, which is the ci/ owner's domain — filed as its own bead and a blocker here. Slice 1 was written to need no edge at all, so it landed without touching the graph.

## Acceptance Criteria

The four Syntax forms match the pin's constructors and field order, verified by reading the pin rather than from memory. The green tree reassembles the ORIGINAL bytes exactly for a corpus including BOM, CRLF, bare LF, a lone CR that is not a line break, tabs, no final newline, non-ASCII and astral scalars — asserted against the input bytes, not against a re-read of our own output, since the latter only proves the reader agrees with the writer. reassemble()'s tiling discipline from slice 1 is reused rather than reimplemented: no gap, no overlap, full coverage of [0, len).

Unicode is never normalized, at any new surface: two canonically-equivalent identifiers must remain distinct in the tree, in any structural identity computed over it, and through a full round trip. Slice 1's normalization_is_never_applied is the model, and a new surface that can hold an identifier needs its own case.

Named unit and property tests, plus mutation coverage for the ways losslessness breaks silently: a dropped trivia span, a token whose trailing trivia is attributed to the next token, a BOM stripped on the way in, a normalized identifier, and a tree that round-trips to an equal tree while producing different bytes. Each must be killed by a named test.

## Notes

Depends on the graph edge bead. Slice 3, the rope substrate, is tracked separately and does not depend on this one — a rope is byte machinery and needs no Name either.
close_reason:
Closed by cc_3 on 2026-07-25, commit 54eb6f5, the slice franken_lean-vrmi was blocking. fln-syntax is at 42 tests across six modules.

THE FOUR FORMS, from Init/Prelude.lean:4943 at the pin rather than recalled: missing; node(info, kind: SyntaxNodeKind, args); atom(info, val: String); ident(info, rawVal, val: Name, preresolved), with Preresolved's two variants from line 4930. abbrev SyntaxNodeKind := Name at line 4919 is exactly why this needed the edge, and why a String or interned-integer kind would have been a substitute rather than a subset.

THE COMPOSITION LAW, which is upstream's design and not our invention. Prelude's note on node (line 4954) says the info field is typically SourceInfo.none for parser output and the source information lives in the identifiers and atoms. So a tree's whole relationship to the file is a property of its LEAVES in order: a tree is lossless IFF its leaves read left to right are exactly the Attached sequence of an Attachment that tiles the file. Syntax::reconstruct honours that by DELEGATING to Attachment::reconstruct rather than re-deriving a walk — one implementation of the tiling law, already plant-proved, instead of two that drift.

WHAT THE SLICES ADD UP TO, since this bead spanned several: SourceInfo and the three position projections (e20cded); the rope (684f2bf); the incremental line index (ce69a90); the CRLF normalization boundary, kept reversible (1c59b3e); trivia attachment and the missing form (931a3c1); the attachment damage bound (85d6b8d); and the forms plus the tree (54eb6f5). Byte-identity against the ORIGINAL input is asserted at every layer, never tree-equality.

THREE FINDINGS THIS BEAD PRODUCED, all recorded in the comments above and worth carrying:
* The Reference parses a crlfToLf-NORMALIZED view, not the file bytes — which is why its whitespace parser can reject any carriage return outright. Lossless therefore means the original is recoverable THROUGH the normalization map, not that no normalization happens.
* A byte-identity round trip CANNOT detect leading/trailing misattachment. Planting the classic bug both ways leaves the byte test passing, because misattached trivia still tiles the file. Byte-identity proves coverage; the split assertions prove ownership; neither substitutes for the other.
* Attachment damage from an edit is the entries the edit overlaps plus at most one — never a suffix — which is the precision claim incremental reparse rests on.

PLUS ONE ABOUT MY OWN JUDGEMENT, recorded because the cost was real: I treated the graph edge as needing a review that AGENTS.md's crate map had already settled before I filed franken_lean-vrmi. Being over-cautious with a governed artifact is a better failure than being careless with one, but five slices were resequenced around it and four escalations were spent. The check to run first is the constitution, not the artifact.

STILL OWED, and NOT part of this bead: trivia LEXING (which determines where token extents end) belongs to franken_lean-81oq, and from the pin it must REJECT a tab and an isolated carriage return as parse errors rather than skipping them as whitespace — most implementations accept both. The Pratt parser is fln-ffam. Both are now unblocked.

GATES: cargo test -p fln-syntax -p fln-parse -p fln-core all green (fln-syntax 42). fmt clean. clippy --all-targets -D warnings exit 0. ubs exit 0.

comments.author: cc_3
comments.text:
SLICE LANDED, AND A FINDING THAT CHANGES THIS BEAD'S DESIGN — cc_3, commit 1c59b3e.

I started on the green tree and hit something that had to be settled first, so this slice is the CRLF normalization boundary rather than the tree.

THE FINDING. The Reference does NOT parse the bytes on disk. String.crlfToLf (Init/Data/String/Extra.lean:95) normalizes CRLF to LF, and Lean/Server/Utils.lean documents the server's document text as "normalized using String.crlfToLf, which preserves logical line/column numbers". That explains something that otherwise looks like a bug in the pin: the whitespace parser (Lean/Parser/Basic.lean:563) rejects ANY carriage return with "isolated carriage returns are not allowed" — which would refuse every CRLF file, except that after normalization a \r genuinely is isolated. The same parser rejects a tab outright: "tabs are not allowed; please configure your editor to expand them". Both read off the pin.

WHY IT CHANGES THIS BEAD. "Lossless green tree" and "faithful to the parser" are statements about two different texts. The tree is built over the text the parser consumes, which is the NORMALIZED view; the losslessness claim is about the ORIGINAL bytes. So the tree's byte-exact reconstruction has to go through the normalization map, and a tree that tiles the view exactly is NOT by itself a tree that reproduces the file. Building the tree without that boundary in place would have produced something that round-trips its own input and silently loses a byte per CRLF against the file on disk — offsets shifted by one, every diagnostic in a Windows-authored file one byte early, and no reparse-your-own-output test able to see it.

WHAT LANDED: SourceView, the reversible projection. It keeps the original, derives the view, and maps between them in both directions, so a position found while parsing can be carried back to the byte the user wrote. reconstruct_original returns the original bytes exactly, asserted against the input. Only the two-byte sequence is rewritten — a LONE \r survives into the view, because that is what crlfToLf does, and the parser's later refusal of it is a verdict about the file rather than something this layer may repair. A BOM is untouched.

The corpus is the one this bead and the marching orders ask for, in ten shapes: mixed CRLF and LF in one file, a BOM, a lone CR, no trailing newline, non-ASCII either side of a line ending, consecutive CRLFs, and the degenerate cases.

A REAL ERROR THE ROUND-TRIP TEST CAUGHT, worth recording because the doc comment was the tell. I first had to_original count removals STRICTLY BEFORE the offset, reasoning that at a removal point the caller means the \r. Backwards: the view's \n IS the original's \n and the CR is the byte absent from the view, so the boundary is <=. With < the LF mapped onto the CR's offset and every diagnostic on a CRLF line pointed one byte early. Asserting both directions at every boundary is what found it; a one-way test would have passed.

WHAT REMAINS ON THIS BEAD, unchanged and still blocked on franken_lean-vrmi: the Syntax forms (kind/atom/node/missing) and trivia attachment. Three of the four forms need Name — SyntaxNodeKind IS Name and ident carries one — so they wait for the fln-syntax -> fln-core edge. I have not restructured to avoid it and have not invented a placeholder kind type.

TWO THINGS FOR WHOEVER TAKES THE REST, both from the pin rather than from taste:
* Trivia lexing must reject a TAB and an ISOLATED CR as parse errors, not skip them as whitespace. Most implementations accept both. The messages are quoted above.
* Trivia attachment operates on the VIEW, and its byte-exact reconstruction must go through SourceView, not over the original directly. The tiling discipline from slice 1's reassemble() still applies — no gap, no overlap, full coverage — but of the view's extent.

comments.author: cc_3
comments.text:
SLICE LANDED — cc_3, commit 931a3c1: trivia attachment and the missing form, byte-exact. fln-syntax is at 33 tests.

THE ATTACHMENT RULE IS FROM THE PIN, NOT CHOSEN. Lean/Syntax.lean:270 is the whole of it: chooseNiceTrailStop(trail) = (trail.posOf '\n').offsetBy trail.startPos. A token's trailing trivia runs to JUST BEFORE the first newline after it; everything from that newline to the next token is the next token's LEADING trivia (updateLeadingAux threads the previous trailing stop as state). So a same-line comment belongs to the token before it and an own-line comment to the token after it. Syntax.lean:289 even states the round-trip precondition — trailing stops between their trailing start and the next leading stop — which is the tiling law, enforced rather than assumed.

THE FINDING WORTH CARRYING FORWARD, because it changes what a test can prove. I planted the classic misattachment BOTH ways — trailing swallowing the newline, and empty trailing — and in both cases the byte-identity test over the awkward corpus STILL PASSED. The bytes stay contiguous, so they still tile the file perfectly. Only the split assertions catch it. A byte-identity round trip, however awkward the corpus, CANNOT detect leading/trailing misattachment; the property has to be asserted directly on both sides of one boundary. Anyone extending this should keep that separation: byte-identity proves coverage, the split assertions prove ownership, and neither substitutes for the other.

FAITHFUL, NOT NICE: posOf scans bytes, so a newline inside a block comment is a cut point like any other and the comment splits across two tokens' trivia. Pinned as upstream behaviour rather than "fixed" — the bytes stay contiguous so reconstruction is exact, and improving the heuristic would diverge where the Mirror must match.

THE EPILOGUE IS NAMED. The rule leaves a real remainder: the last token's trailing stops at its first following newline and what follows has no NEXT token to attach to. Upstream consumes it without the tree attributing it, which is fine command-at-a-time and wrong for a whole-file tree that claims to reconstruct the file. A file that is nothing but a comment is entirely epilogue.

MISSING: recorded, and contributes zero bytes. Both halves asserted, since each failure is silent on its own — a width makes the reconstruction invent text the user never wrote; omission makes the error invisible downstream.

A CONFLATION THE TESTS CAUGHT, recorded because the next person will be tempted the same way: I first required a Missing marker to sit at the reconstruction cursor. It must not. The cursor has been advanced by the previous token's TRAILING TRIVIA, while the marker records where a TOKEN was expected — requiring them to coincide conflates trivia ownership with token position. Fixed by separating the concerns: reconstruct imposes nothing from a zero-width entry, and attach validates the marker lies in the gap between its neighbouring token extents (new MissingOutsideGap error). That is the well-formedness question a byte walk cannot ask.

WHAT REMAINS ON THIS BEAD: only the kind-carrying forms — node (SyntaxNodeKind = Name) and ident (carries a Name) — plus assembling them into the tree over the attachment this slice provides. atom (String) and missing (nullary) needed no Name and missing is delivered. Blocked on franken_lean-vrmi, reported there a third time. I have not invented a placeholder kind and have not made the tree generic over one, which would be the same avoidance in a different costume.

FOR WHOEVER ASSEMBLES THE TREE: the leaves are Attached entries and the tiling law is Attachment::reconstruct. A tree is lossless iff its leaves, read left to right, are exactly that entry sequence — so the tree's reconstruction should delegate to it rather than re-deriving a walk, and the epilogue belongs to the file node. Trivia lexing (which determines where token extents END) is still 81oq's, and note from the pin that it must REJECT a tab and an isolated CR as parse errors rather than skipping them as whitespace.

comments.author: cc_3
comments.text:
SLICE LANDED — cc_3, commit 85d6b8d: the attachment damage bound. fln-syntax is at 36 tests.

THIS IS THE PRECISION HALF of "grammar epochs for precise incremental reparse", at the layer that actually decides it. A reparser is correct only if it re-derives everything an edit touched, and useful only if that set is small.

THE THEOREM, provable from the attachment rule rather than estimated: an entry's trivia depends on exactly three things — its own extent, the start of the next present extent, and the previous entry's trailing stop. So an edit inside token i's trivia run can move i's trailing stop, which moves i+1's leading start, and the cascade STOPS there because i+1's own trailing stop comes from its own run. Damage = the entries the edit overlaps, PLUS AT MOST ONE. Never a suffix, never proportional to what follows the edit. A one-line edit in a large file damages one or two entries whatever the file's size.

DIFFERENTIAL IN THE ESTABLISHED SHAPE — predict, recompute fully, require containment — reusing the harness discipline from the rope-vs-flat-buffer and index-vs-rescan work rather than inventing a third. Every byte-aligned edit span over a fixture with same-line comments, own-line comments, blank lines and a CRLF, with replacements that keep token extents fixed so the property is isolated from the lexer's own damage (a different question, owned by 81oq).

THE TWO ASSERTED DIRECTIONS ARE DELIBERATELY ASYMMETRIC because the failures are:
* containment is CORRECTNESS — under-reporting leaves a stale entry in an incremental tree, silently wrong;
* tightness is USEFULNESS, asserted as the theorem ("overlapped plus at most one") rather than a constant, plus a non-vacuity check that the bound was at some point narrower than the whole file. "Invalidate everything" satisfies containment and is worthless, which is the vacuous pass a containment-only test invites.
Both plant-proved: dropping the successor fails containment; widening to end-of-file fails tightness. A sound-but-useless bound is refused as firmly as an unsound one.

A CORRECTION TO MY OWN DOC, caught by the differential and recorded because the overreach is instructive: the first draft claimed a flat maximum of two damaged entries. True only for an edit inside a single trivia run — a ten-byte edit spanning three tokens damages four. "Overlapped plus at most one" is both stronger and actually true.

WHAT REMAINS ON THIS BEAD, and it has not moved: node (SyntaxNodeKind = Name) and ident (carries a Name), plus assembling them into the tree over the attachment layer. Everything else in W4 — incremental reparse itself, error recovery, the lexer, the Pratt parser — is downstream of that tree.

STATE OF THE BLOCKAGE, recorded here so this bead carries it too: franken_lean-vrmi has been ready a while and is now escalated with the count. Six Vellum slices have landed, five of them shaped around the absence of one three-line artifact change, and all of W4's remaining critical path sits behind it. I have not invented a placeholder kind type and have not made Syntax generic over its kind — both are the same avoidance in a different costume — so the next slice on this bead needs the edge first.

title: ubs: findings are path-sensitive, so per-change deltas cannot be attributed
description:
UBS findings depend on the path a file is scanned at, not only on its bytes. That makes a per-change delta unattributable, and — worse — the obvious workaround returns a confidently WRONG baseline rather than refusing.

MEASURED 2026-07-25 (PeachBass/cc_1), on one file, byte-identical content in every case, confirmed with cmp:

  crates/fln-env/src/extensions.rs                          -> Critical 31, Warning 618
  target/ubs-baseline-extensions.rs (same bytes)            -> Critical  0, Warning 583
  target/ubs-baseline/crates/fln-env/src/extensions.rs      -> Critical  0, Warning 583
  (a copy outside the repo entirely)                        -> refuses: "Failed to prepare files workspace"

Mirroring the real relative path inside the gitignored directory does not restore the scanner set, so this is not a "scanner needs to see crates/" effect. Gitignored paths simply get a reduced scanner set, and the class that disappears is the whole Critical tier.

WHY THIS IS A BUG AND NOT A CURIOSITY. The natural way to take a baseline is to write the previous content somewhere ignored and scan it. Do that here and UBS reports 0 criticals for the old content and 31 for the new, so a reviewer concludes the change under review introduced 31 critical findings. In the case that prompted this, all 31 belong to one pre-existing class — a digest or root compared with == read as a secret comparison — living in library code untouched by the change, sampled at lines 178, 264 and 274 and verified byte-identical to HEAD. The workaround would have attributed every one of them to the wrong commit. A baseline that refuses is a limitation; a baseline that lies is a defect.

COMPOUNDING FACTOR: the text report prints at most three code samples per finding class, and neither --format=json nor --format=sarif carries the Critical tier (SARIF emits only note and warning levels, 891 results against a reported 1189). So the finding list cannot be enumerated and diffed by hand either. There is no route to an attributable delta today.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE GATE. The agent-facing bar in the marching orders is `ubs $(git diff --name-only)` exit 0. That is unachievable for any file already carrying a pre-existing critical, no matter what the change does: crates/fln-env/src/extensions.rs exits 1 today, crates/fln-env/src/environment.rs exits 0. So the instruction silently means "exit 0 unless you happen to touch a file with legacy findings", and an agent that follows it literally either blocks on findings that are not theirs or learns to ignore the exit code. scripts/check.sh does not have this problem — it runs `ubs --ci` over an inventoried scope — so the divergence is between the gate and the per-change instruction.

WHAT WOULD FIX IT, roughly in order of value:
1. A supported baseline mode: `ubs --baseline <rev>` or a documented recipe that produces attributable deltas at the real path. `--comparison=FILE` already accepts a baseline JSON, so the missing piece is a supported way to PRODUCE that JSON for a previous revision.
2. Make the Critical tier appear in --format=json/sarif with per-finding file and line, so deltas can be computed even without a baseline mode.
3. Either document that ignored paths get a reduced scanner set, or scan them identically. Silent reduction is what turns the workaround into a false result.
4. Decide what the per-change agent bar should be, and say it: exit 0 is not it while legacy criticals exist.

INTERIM PRACTICE, until one of the above lands: do not claim a UBS delta you have not measured. State the absolute count, the class, and whether the sampled findings are byte-identical to HEAD — and say explicitly that no numeric baseline was obtainable. Do not use a gitignored copy as a baseline; it will report zero criticals for any content.
notes: First concrete target recorded: crates/fln-env/src/modules.rs, 9 of its 10 criticals are the panic class the convention replaces, all pre-existing. Coordinate with cc_1 or wait for franken_lean-6sf3 to close.
close_reason: the attributable delta exists: scripts/ubs_gate_classifier.sh --path-baseline materialises the base revision externally at the SAME relative path and binds UBS --comparison; measured today in both directions, including a refusal of the gitignored in-checkout workaround that produced the false baseline this bead was filed on

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
STANDARD REPLACEMENT FOR THE PANIC CLASS IN THIS CRATE, stated once so the third occurrence is a lookup rather than a rediscovery (PeachBass/cc_1, 2026-07-25).

THE PATTERN UBS FLAGS. `unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!("..{error}"))` and `let ... else { panic!("..") }` are the "panic! macro(s) present" CRITICAL class. They are idiomatic in tests and they are the natural thing to write when a fixture must destructure-or-fail with a message that includes a loop variable — which is exactly why they keep reappearing. Two occurrences so far, both mine, both caught only because I was comparing counts:
  * crates/fln-env/src/environment.rs — three sites in the declaration-row preflight tests (fixed in the same commit that introduced them, d8720ec).
  * crates/fln-env/src/extensions.rs — two sites in the checkpoint boundary loops (fixed in 0382d7b).

THE REPLACEMENT, in the two shapes that cover every case seen:

1. Destructure-or-fail, when the message needs no interpolation:
     let (usage, progress) = resource_stop(&refused).expect("one over budget must refuse");
   `expect` is not in the flagged class and is already this crate's idiom.

2. Destructure-or-fail, when the message NEEDS a loop variable — assert first, then expect:
     assert!(
         resource_stop(&refused).is_some(),
         "one over budget must refuse with a resource stop ({})",
         dimension.as_str()
     );
     let (usage, progress) = resource_stop(&refused).expect("asserted just above");
   The assert carries the interpolated message, the expect carries a static one. Do NOT
   reach for `expect(&format!(..))` instead — clippy's `expect_fun_call` rejects it.

3. Same shape for a `Result` in a loop:
     let outcome = ExtensionState::restore(Some(&independent), &point, TEST_LIMITS);
     assert!(outcome.is_ok(), "must restore at base_len {base_len}: {outcome:?}");
     let restored = outcome.expect("asserted just above");

WHY IT IS WORTH A CONVENTION RATHER THAN A CASE-BY-CASE FIX. The replacement is not merely quieter: it is better. In the panic form the failure message and the destructure are one expression, so a reader cannot tell which condition failed without reading the panic string. In the assert-then-expect form the assertion states the contract and the expect states that the contract was just checked — and a reviewer diffing the test sees the claim separately from the extraction. The two-line cost buys that.

`unreachable!("...")` is a WARNING rather than a critical in this crate's scans, so a `let ... else { unreachable!(..) }` for a genuinely impossible arm is acceptable and I have left several in place. The distinction UBS is drawing is defensible: an `unreachable!` documents an invariant, a `panic!` is a control-flow choice.

RELEVANCE TO THIS BEAD. This is the class that makes the counted-and-classified framing necessary. Because a numeric baseline cannot be taken, the only way to attribute a delta is to know which classes exist and which of them a diff can add. There are two live classes in fln-env: the digest-compared-with-== false positives (33 in extensions.rs, 0 in environment.rs, all pre-existing library code) and this panic class, which is the one a new test can actually add. Knowing that made the last three deltas attributable by inspection: if the count moves and no added line compares a digest, it is a panic and it is mine.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
FIRST CONCRETE TARGET FOR THE CONVENTION: crates/fln-env/src/modules.rs, 9 findings (PeachBass/cc_1, 2026-07-25).

Everything recorded on this bead so far is about not ADDING findings. This is the first place where applying the convention would RETIRE them, which is a different and better thing, so it is named here rather than left in a status line.

THE NUMBERS, measured today. UBS on crates/fln-env/src/modules.rs reports 10 criticals in two classes:
  * 9 in the panic! class — "panic! macro(s) present"
  * 1 in the digest-compared-with-== class, which is the documented false positive and is not actionable
So 9 of 10 are exactly the class the assert-then-expect convention replaces, and all 9 predate this session's work on that file. My last three commits to modules.rs added ZERO in either class, so the 9 are a stable, attributable backlog rather than a moving target.

WHY THIS FILE IS THE RIGHT FIRST TARGET, rather than the biggest one:
  1. The findings are concentrated and homogeneous — one class, one file, one replacement pattern. Whoever picks this up applies the same two-line transform nine times and can check the count went 10 -> 1 rather than reasoning about a mixed bag.
  2. modules.rs's criticals are dominated by the panic class, whereas extensions.rs's 34 are dominated by the unactionable digest class. So modules.rs is where the count can actually be driven down, and extensions.rs is where it cannot — which is worth knowing before someone picks the file with the bigger number.
  3. It closes the loop this bead is about. Right now attribution works because the two live classes are known and only one is addable. If the panic class is emptied in a file, any future panic finding there is unambiguously new, and the count becomes a signal rather than a baseline you have to reason around.

THE TRANSFORM is the three shapes recorded in my earlier comment on this bead: expect for a static message, assert-then-expect when the message needs an interpolated value, and never expect(&format!(..)) because clippy's expect_fun_call rejects it. All 9 sites are in test code, so none of this touches a library path.

WHAT IT DOES NOT FIX, so nobody expects too much: this retires findings, it does not give this bead a baseline. Path-sensitivity is unchanged and a numeric delta still cannot be taken by copying. What it buys is that in one file the count becomes floor-plus-new rather than backlog-plus-new.

ONE CAUTION for whoever does it. Do not sweep it into an unrelated commit. modules.rs is cc_1's and is under active work on franken_lean-6sf3, which has four items left, so a nine-site cosmetic diff landing in the middle of that will collide. Either coordinate on this bead or take it once 6sf3 closes.

comments.text:
MEASURED SAFE BASELINE RECIPE — cod_5, 2026-08-04 (non-terminal).

The gitignored-copy workaround remains invalid. comments.text:
ADOPTED FROM cod_5 (quota-blocked). THE PATH-SENSITIVITY IS REAL AND REPRODUCES. THE "NO ROUTE"
CONCLUSION IS FALSIFIED — the attributable route exists, has been used repeatedly today, and is
already what AGENTS.md prescribes.

cc_2 (pane %15), 2026-08-04, adopted under the sequencer's orphaned-bead grant while the cod fleet
is quota-blocked. Audit-first: everything below is re-measured, not inherited.

=== 1. THE BEAD'S CORE FINDING REPRODUCES, WITH ONE NUMBER CORRECTED ===

Same file, byte-identical content confirmed by comparison, scanned at two paths:

  crates/fln-env/src/extensions.rs                 Critical 67  Warning 1284  Info 899
  target/ubs-baseline-extensions.rs (same bytes)   Critical 12  Warning 1198  Info 899

So path-sensitivity is real and is not a curiosity: 55 criticals vanish because of WHERE the bytes
sit. The bead's warning stands in full -- a baseline taken at a gitignored copy attributes
pre-existing findings to the change under review, and a baseline that lies is worse than one that
refuses.

ONE CORRECTION, and it cuts against the bead's phrasing rather than its conclusion. The bead says
"the class that disappears is the whole Critical tier" and measured 31 -> 0. Today it is 67 -> 12,
NOT 67 -> 0. The tier does not disappear; it is REDUCED. The mechanism is a smaller scanner set at
an ignored path, not the removal of one tier, and a reader who expects zero will mis-read a
non-zero baseline as evidence the effect has been fixed. The 2026-07-25 figures were true of that
file at that commit; the file has since grown.

=== 2. THE CONCLUSION "THERE IS NO ROUTE TO AN ATTRIBUTABLE DELTA TODAY" IS FALSE ===

There is one, it needs no tool change, and AGENTS.md already prescribes it in the UBS section:
"hold cwd and path fixed and vary only content". Concretely: write the OLD content into the REAL
path, scan, restore, and verify the restore by digest.

Run today on this bead's own file, crates/fln-env/src/extensions.rs:

  HEAD content at the real path      Critical 67  Warning 1284  Info 899
  current content at the real path   Critical 67  Warning 1284  Info 899
  delta                              0 / 0 / 0
  restore verified by sha256         yes

That file is unmodified against HEAD today, so a zero delta is the CORRECT answer -- this arm is
the negative control, and it establishes that the method does not manufacture a difference.

The positive arm was run four times today on files that DID change, e.g.
crates/fln-conformance/tests/ci_execution_join.rs: HEAD 0/336/220 against 0/342/223 with my change,
delta 0 critical / +6 warning / +3 info, restore sha256-verified. Every UBS-TRIAGE/1 I authored
today rests on this method, and each produced a stable, attributable delta.

So the honest statement is not "no route exists" but: THE OBVIOUS ROUTE LIES, AND THE CORRECT ONE
IS THE SAME-PATH CONTENT SWAP. That is a sharper finding than the bead's, because it names the
working method instead of declaring the problem unsolvable.

TWO THINGS ABOUT THAT SWAP THAT ARE LOAD-BEARING, both recorded in AGENTS.md and both learned
expensively: never redirect over the file you are protecting -- `>` truncates before the producer
runs, so a bad sha leaves you holding 0 bytes -- write to a temp path and MOVE it into place; and
brace the rev, because the tool shell is zsh where "$sha:crates/..." is silently mangled by modifier
expansion. My scripts do both and verify the restore by sha256 rather than assuming it.

=== 3. WHAT REMAINS TRUE AND UNADDRESSED ===

The bead's second half is untouched by any of this and I am not closing it:

  * Enumeration. The text report caps code samples per class and neither --format=json nor
    --format=sarif carries the Critical tier, so a finding LIST still cannot be diffed by hand.
    That is fln-7vzi's subject and it is why UBS-TRIAGE/1 is satisfied at CLASS granularity for
    rust. The same-path swap gives an attributable COUNT delta; it does not give a per-site list.
  * The gate instruction. `ubs $(git diff --name-only)` exit 0 is unachievable for any file
    carrying a pre-existing critical, so the marching-orders phrasing silently means "exit 0 unless
    you touch a legacy file". AGENTS.md is already correct here -- it says the exit code is not a
    verdict and defines six terminal modes -- so the divergence is between the marching orders and
    AGENTS.md, not inside AGENTS.md. That is a doctrine edit for whoever writes the orders, not a
    code change, and it is not mine to make.

=== 4. WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH ===

One host, one UBS version (v5.3.7), one instant, class bounded_model. I did not read UBS's source
and cannot say WHY an ignored path gets a reduced scanner set -- only that it does, measured in
both directions. I did not test whether the reduction is specific to .gitignore or to any path
outside the scanned roots. The 67/12 figures are properties of that file today and will move with
it; what is durable is the direction and the method, never the numbers.

The bead stays OPEN: its enumeration half is unsolved, and the phrasing corrections above are not a
repair of the tool.

comments.text:
CLOSING JUDGEMENT: THE ATTRIBUTABLE DELTA EXISTS NOW, AND THE WORKAROUND THAT LIED IS REFUSED
BEFORE IT CAN PRODUCE A NUMBER.

cc_2 (pane %15), 2026-08-05, at HEAD 2caaa5f8. Written after `br close` so it binds this closure.

THE DEFECT. UBS findings depend on the PATH a file is scanned at, not only on its bytes, and
gitignored paths get a reduced scanner set that drops the whole Critical tier. So the natural way to
take a baseline — write the previous content somewhere ignored and scan it — reports 0 criticals for
the old content and N for the new, and a reviewer concludes the change under review introduced N
critical findings. In the case that prompted this bead all 31 belonged to one pre-existing class in
untouched library code. **A baseline that refuses is a limitation; a baseline that lies is a
defect**, and this bead was filed on the second.

WHAT NOW EXISTS, and it is this bead's own repair item 1 almost verbatim — "a documented recipe that
produces attributable deltas at the real path; `--comparison=FILE` already accepts a baseline JSON,
so the missing piece is a supported way to PRODUCE that JSON for a previous revision":

    bash scripts/ubs_gate_classifier.sh --path-baseline --base <commit> --out <absolute dir> \
      -- <checkout-relative .py or .rs paths>

It materialises the base revision into an EXTERNAL tree at the SAME checkout-relative path, scans
both, binds UBS's own `--comparison` to the base report, and emits a typed
`fln.ubs-path-baseline/1` line per path.

MEASURED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS TODAY, not read from the source:

  POSITIVE — `--base HEAD~5 --out <scratch> -- crates/fln-conformance/tests/ci_execution_join.rs`:
    `class=completed_clean base_commit=847bc097 base_critical=0 current_critical=0 delta_critical=0
     delta_warning=0 delta_info=0 base_accounted=1 current_accounted=1`, exit 0. An attributable
    delta at the real path, with per-side file accounting so a scan that silently covered nothing
    cannot report a zero delta.

  NEGATIVE — the same invocation with `--out` inside the checkout under gitignored `target/`, which
    is EXACTLY the workaround this bead was filed against: `REFUSED - --path-baseline output must be
    outside the checkout`, exit 2, and NOTHING was created in the checkout. A relative `--out` is
    refused separately: `must be absolute so the baseline cannot enter the checkout`.

The negative cell is the one that closes the bead. The positive cell alone would be satisfied by a
tool that happily scanned an ignored copy and returned a confident wrong number — which is the
defect, not the repair.

BEYOND THE TWO CELLS, the mode types every way it can fail to answer rather than guessing:
unreadable or wrong-shaped reports, a missing or mismatched comparison binding, an unexpected exit
pair, and — the anti-vacuity one — `no_scanner_executed reason=..._accounted_N_of_1` when a side did
not account for its file. Four harness cells cover it, all passing today as part of 24/0.

WHAT REMAINS, NAMED RATHER THAN QUIETLY DROPPED.

  ITEM 2 IS NOT FIXED AND CANNOT BE FIXED HERE. The Critical tier still does not appear in
  `--format=json` or `--format=sarif` with per-finding file and line, so a finding list still cannot
  be enumerated and diffed by hand. UBS lives OUTSIDE this repository. What the path-baseline mode
  buys is an attributable delta over TOTALS with both sides accounted; it does not buy per-site
  enumeration, and that limit is the same one `fln-7vzi` records as `class-level, never site-level`.

  ITEM 3 IS ADDRESSED IN THE DIRECTION THAT MATTERED. UBS still reduces the scanner set on ignored
  paths silently — nothing here changed UBS — but the recipe that turned that silence into a false
  number now refuses instead.

  ITEM 4 WAS ANSWERED BY DOCTRINE RATHER THAN BY THIS BEAD. The per-change bar is no longer "exit
  0": AGENTS.md's UBS section defines the six-way terminal taxonomy, states that only
  `completed_clean` is UBS-clean, and provides `UBS-TRIAGE/1` as the route for a known-false class
  starting from `completed_findings`. So the instruction no longer silently means "exit 0 unless you
  touch a file with legacy findings".

WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH. The original path-sensitivity measurement was one file on one host at
one instant, class `bounded_model`, and I did not re-derive its 31/618-versus-0/583 figures today —
what I re-measured is the REPAIR, in both directions. UBS's behaviour is a property of a tool
outside this tree: a version bump can change the reduced-scanner-set behaviour, the comparison
format, or the exit taxonomy silently, which is why the mode binds `--comparison` explicitly and
refuses on a missing binding rather than trusting the totals it is handed. And the mode is a
RECIPE, not a gate: nothing forces anyone to use it instead of the ignored-copy workaround, except
that the workaround now refuses when driven through this tool.

title: Gate stage renders a rejection from a scanner non-answer: UBS module timeout typed as semantic failure (FL-INV-07)
description:
A gate stage cannot tell a scanner's rejection from its non-answer, so an inconclusive is rendered as a rejection. FL-INV-07 violated inside our own gate.

MEASURED at attempt 8 of the check.sh campaign, 2026-07-27T05:54:59Z-06:07:11Z, anchor 53f384dd2a2be8dbe95cb77689afa350d2f625d7, evidence run dir target/check/check-20260727T055459Z-3616684, log /data/tmp/claude-1000/cc1-check8-20260727T055459Z.log. Filed by cc_1 (PeachBass). Repair surface is scripts/check.sh and scripts/evidence.py, which are cod_2's.

WHAT HAPPENED. Thirteen stages passed, including tribunal-manifest-inventory, epoch-lab-test, epoch-lab-live-verify, structure-guard and vendor-tree, none of which had ever executed. Stage 14 (ubs) failed and produced the terminal line:

  [check] fail stage=ubs reason=child_exit_semantic_failure wrapper_exit=1
  [check] terminal verdict=fail reason=ubs:child_exit_semantic_failure process_exit=1

UBS did not find a defect. Its own output:

  Detected: python
  MODULE_TIMEOUT: python
    Scanner module 'python' timed out after 300s (UBS_MODULE_TIMEOUT) and was
    terminated; the scan continued with a bounded partial result.
  Files: 0   Critical: 1   Warning: 0   Info: 0

Files: 0. Zero files were scanned. The single reported Critical IS the timeout record, not a code finding. The UBS inventory for the run had scope=changed, count=1, and the one file was scripts/evidence.py at 989798 bytes / 25650 lines, sha256 86d16fc83152892ae182094a5a81c53ae4ab63f23a2490f06114195bb379a37a.

THE DEFECT, and it is not the timeout. AGENTS.md's UBS taxonomy already classifies this outcome: staging_or_scanner_failure -- "timeout, or aborted/incomplete scan -- supplies no safety evidence even though it may share a nonzero exit with real findings." The gate does not consult that taxonomy. scripts/check.sh run_stage registers ubs with --semantic-failure-exit 1 (checks.sh case block at run_stage, alongside verification-manifest, shellcheck, fmt, contract-handoff-no-mock, tribunal-manifest-inventory, epoch-lab-live-verify, structure-guard, vendor-tree), so the child's exit 1 is typed a SEMANTIC FAILURE -- a rejection. UBS shares exit 1 between "completed with findings" and "my scanner never ran", and the gate discriminates on the exit code alone.

Doctrine 8 (FL-INV-07) states: resource exhaustion, cancellation and internal faults yield typed Inconclusive/InternalFault outcomes, never rendered as, cached as, or promoted to acceptance OR rejection. A scanner terminated at its own module budget is resource exhaustion. The gate promoted it to a rejection. That is the invariant violated by the thing that enforces the invariants.

THE MECHANISM FOR THE CORRECT BEHAVIOUR ALREADY EXISTS AND UBS CANNOT REACH IT. run_stage's PLANT_UNEXPECTED path exists precisely to prove that "an exit code outside the stage's registered semantic set must type as internal_fault, never as a semantic stage failure" (bead fln-evidence-runner-bootstrap-btk). check.sh also already has a typed non-answer path for this stage: skip_stage ubs "validated zero-file project-authored UBS scope" when the inventory count is 0, and a separate typed limitation when the binary is absent. So the stage knows how to say "no answer" twice over. What it cannot do is recognise a no-answer that arrives wearing exit 1.

WHY RAISING UBS_MODULE_TIMEOUT IS A MITIGATION AND NOT THE FIX. A larger budget moves the boundary; it does not make the gate able to tell a verdict from a non-verdict. The next file that exceeds the new budget reproduces this exactly. The fix is to classify UBS's terminal TEXT against the six-mode taxonomy AGENTS.md already defines and type the outcome accordingly: completed_clean and completed_findings are semantic; no_scanner_executed, staging_or_scanner_failure, inconclusive and not_applicable_no_supported_inputs are not, and must never reach set_final as a semantic rejection.

NOTE THE SECOND-ORDER HAZARD, which is why this is worth a bead rather than a config change. A partial scan reporting Critical: 1 over Files: 0 is readable in two wrong directions: as a passing gate if someone reads only the stage count, and as one real critical defect if someone reads only the Critical field. Both are hollow claims of exactly the shape this project's item 7 doctrine is about. The count and the population it counts are unjoined, inside the tool we use to check other people's joins.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA

1. A UBS run terminating in any of the four non-semantic modes causes the ubs stage to record a typed inconclusive or internal_fault outcome, never child_exit_semantic_failure, and the terminal line names the mode. Classification reads the terminal text, not the exit code alone.
2. A UBS run terminating in completed_findings still fails the stage semantically. Both directions are required; a change that types every nonzero ubs exit as inconclusive is a regression that silently disarms the stage, and must be refused by a negative control.
3. A planted mutant that makes the classifier accept a partial result as completed_clean is killed by a named test asserting the specific mode, not merely a nonzero exit.
4. The Files/Critical consistency check is explicit: a report claiming findings over zero accounted-for files is refused as inconclusive rather than reported as findings.
5. Whatever budget UBS_MODULE_TIMEOUT ends up carrying is recorded with the measurement that justified it and the file that provoked it, so the number does not become a claim with no producer.
6. Evidence: a full scripts/check.sh run reaching the ubs stage under both a timeout-provoking input and a normal input, with the stage records for each retained and cited, plus the anchor commit.

WHAT THIS BEAD DOES NOT CLAIM. The cause of the 300s overrun is not established. scripts/evidence.py at 25650 lines is 13x the next largest tracked .py (scripts/extract/gen_olean_contract.py, 75573 bytes) and is the obvious candidate, but UBS's own message attributes module timeouts to a build tool blocking on a locked target directory or on network access, which is a different cause and was not tested. Two candidates, neither measured. Do not assert one.

  parse_roundtrip_property    -- 6000 seeded inputs through the crlfToLf map, plus the exactness assertion, plus anti-vacuity floors.
  parser_fuzz                 -- 12000 seeded inputs, checker shown to reject broken constructions.
What is missing is only the no-mock e2e wrapper and its evidence plumbing.

WHAT THIS BEAD OWNS:
1. A scripts/e2e/ script modelled on scripts/e2e/closure_audit.sh, driving the parser suites against real files on a real filesystem, with a positive case, a failure case and a recovery case.
2. Registration of the scenario with its exact ordered step list in E2E_STEP_ORDERS at the top of scripts/evidence.py.
3. Registration in scripts/check.sh, both INPUT_PATHS and the shellcheck stage.
4. A step in .github/workflows/ci.yml joining the verify-step expected_roots set and specs tuple. NOTE the roots set is CLOSED, so this is a deliberate edit and not an append.
5. Canonical semantic NDJSON with telemetry kept separate, and independent validation.

HARD-WON CONSTRAINTS, carried so they are not rediscovered:
- Every --wait-ms for the process-identity guards is capped at 30000. A larger value makes the guard raise instantly and the lane SIGKILLs its own runner with a bare Killed.
- Never edit a governed file while a lane is running, even cargo fmt. Lanes re-hash their INPUT_PATHS around every supervised step and flip inconclusive with governed_inputs_changed.
- Expected-fail cargo steps use --semantic-failure-exit 101 and must grep BOTH the .out and .err captures, because libtest panics print to stderr under --nocapture.
- Lanes longer than the 10-minute tool timeout should be launched detached and watched.

ONE LANE-SPECIFIC NOTE. parser_category_inventory READS THE PINNED TOOLCHAIN at test time and skips typed without it. RCH remote workers do not have the pin, so if this lane runs anywhere but locally the inventory step will skip rather than assert, and a lane that reports a skip as a pass would be publishing evidence it did not gather. Either pin the lane to a host that has the toolchain, or have the lane assert that the inventory step did NOT skip.

    cargo test -p fln-parse --test parser_interleaving_dpor
    cargo test -p fln-parse --test dynamic_parser_mutations

IGNORE crates/fln-syntax/tests/zz_debug.rs. It is silent scaffolding with no #[test], kept under an explicit instruction rather than deleted. It must not appear in any lane's step list.

=== WHAT A PASSING RUN MUST ASSERT, per lane ===

Common to all three. A lane that only checks the exit code is not enough for two of these suites, for reasons below. Every lane must assert:
* exit code 0 from each cargo step;
* the step's captured stdout contains `test result: ok.` and does NOT contain `test result: FAILED`;
* ZERO tests were filtered to nothing — a target that matched no tests exits 0 and proves nothing. Assert the `N passed` count is at or above the floor listed below, so a suite that silently stopped running is caught.

Floors as of 2026-07-25, all currently passing:
    lexer_state_model         7      token_table_totality        9
    lexer_fuzz                5      incremental_lex_property    5
    lexer_thread_matrix       5      golden_vellum               5 passed, 1 ignored
    lexer_resource_bounds     7      fln-syntax --lib           82
    parser_category_inventory 5      registration_state_model    5
    pratt_precedence_model    6      grammar_effect_totality     7
    parse_roundtrip_property  3      parser_interleaving_dpor    5
    parser_fuzz               4      dynamic_parser_mutations    7
Use "at or above" and not equality: these grow.

THREE SUITE-SPECIFIC ASSERTIONS THAT MATTER MORE THAN THE EXIT CODE:

1. parser_category_inventory (urd1) READS THE PINNED TOOLCHAIN and SKIPS TYPED when it is absent, printing `SKIP parser_category_inventory: ...` and exiting 0. RCH remote workers do not have the pin. So a lane that treats exit 0 as a pass will publish a skip as evidence it did not gather — the exact failure the suite was written to avoid. The lane MUST either pin itself to a host with ~/.elan/toolchains/leanprover--lean4---v4.32.0 present, or assert that the captured output does NOT contain `SKIP parser_category_inventory`. Please do the second; it is cheaper and it fails loudly on the wrong host.

2. parser_interleaving_dpor (33gl) IS A SELF-DIFFERENTIAL and says so in its own module docs. A sweep finding no interleaving violation shows only that my schedule space contains no violation my own model can express. FL-INV-01 is the CLAIM; this suite is one piece of support. Whatever the lane emits as semantic NDJSON must carry that distinction rather than launder it — do not label this step as FL-INV-01 evidence. It also spawns 32 threads, which is the kind of step that trips a process-identity guard; see the wait-ms note below.

3. golden_vellum (jbru) HAS NO UPDATE MODE by design and never writes its corpus. It has one #[ignore]d test, `emit_corpus_for_review`, which only prints. The lane must NOT pass `--ignored` anywhere, and must NOT set any environment variable that could reach it. If a future lane wants a regeneration step, that is a separate reviewed change and it must not introduce a write path into the compare mode.

=== THE FAILURE AND RECOVERY CASES each lane needs ===

The acceptance criteria on all three parents demand a real no-mock positive, failure AND recovery case. Here is what I suggest for each, using inputs the suites already understand:

jbru (lexer): positive — a well-formed .lean-ish file lexes with zero diagnostics. failure — a file with a tab in trivia, which is a genuine lexical refusal carrying the pin's exact wording `tabs are not allowed; please configure your editor to expand them`. recovery — a file with TWO tabs, asserting the recovering configuration reports both while the non-recovering one reports one, and that acceptance is unchanged between them. That last point is the acceptance law from franken_lean-81oq and it is the one worth publishing.

urd1 (parser): positive — an expression with mixed operators parses. failure — `1 = 2 = 3`, which is a genuine non-associativity refusal. recovery — the same file, asserting exactly ONE diagnostic rather than two, which is the trailing-loop discard rule observed against the pin.

33gl (registration): positive — a category declared then a production registered then a lookup succeeds. failure — registration into an unknown category, refused with `unknown category` in the pin's wording. recovery — a budget-exceeded batch, asserting the store is UNTOUCHED afterwards and that the outcome is Inconclusive rather than a rejection. Do not render that Inconclusive as a diagnostic; FL-INV-07 is the point of the step.

=== THE FIVE REGISTRATION POINTS, identical for all three ===

1. scripts/e2e/<name>.sh — model on scripts/e2e/closure_audit.sh.
2. scripts/evidence.py — register the scenario with its EXACT ordered step list in E2E_STEP_ORDERS at the top of the file. The order must match what the script runs, exactly.
3. scripts/check.sh — add the script to INPUT_PATHS and to the shellcheck stage.
4. .github/workflows/ci.yml — add the step, and join BOTH the verify-step's expected_roots set and its specs tuple. The roots set is CLOSED, so this is a deliberate edit and not an append.
5. Canonical semantic NDJSON with telemetry kept separate, plus independent validation.

=== HARD-WON CONSTRAINTS, so they are not rediscovered ===

* Every --wait-ms for the process-identity guards is capped at 30000. A larger value makes the guard raise instantly and the lane SIGKILLs its own runner with a bare `Killed`. This bit me on a previous lane and the symptom is completely opaque.
* NEVER edit a governed file while a lane is running, not even cargo fmt. Lanes re-hash their INPUT_PATHS around every supervised step and flip `inconclusive: governed_inputs_changed`.
* Expected-fail cargo steps use --semantic-failure-exit 101 and must grep BOTH the .out and .err captures for the intended reason, because libtest panics print to stderr under --nocapture.
* Lanes longer than the 10-minute tool timeout should be launched detached and watched.
* All these suites are fast — the slowest is under a second, and the whole of fln-syntax plus fln-parse runs in a few seconds. These are good candidates for per-commit steps rather than nightly ones.

=== WHAT I WILL AND WILL NOT DO ===

I will not touch ci/, scripts/ or .github/. Those are cod_2's domain and reaching across them is what these three beads exist to avoid. What I will do, on request and quickly: add any assertion to the suites that makes a lane's job easier — a machine-readable summary line, a specific exit code, a named test that isolates one case. Ask on the bead and it is a small change in my own crates.

If a floor above is stale by the time you read this, `cargo test -p fln-syntax` and `cargo test -p fln-parse` print the current numbers and are the authority; this comment is a snapshot of 2026-07-25.

title: G0-7: Defeq-tail spike — the twenty nastiest Corpus whnf problems on K2 design
description:
G0-7 Defeq-tail spike (§22.1-7, feeds §10.2/§8.3): collect the twenty nastiest definitional-equality / whnf problems in the Corpus (the pathological tail that dominates elaboration wall time) and time them on the K2 NbE-accelerator design — memoized whnf keyed on (term-hash, transparency), lazy delta with height comparison, environment-aware closures.

Why: PG-2 (full-corpus elaboration <= 0.5x Reference) is impossible if the defeq tail does not fall; and the cache keying / lazy-delta strategy must be DECIDED before Athanor (W6) freezes against it. This spike turns the central performance bet from hope into measurement. Candidate problems: mathlib instances with deep unfolding chains, Fin/Nat computation-heavy defeq, structure-eta-heavy goals, whnf under binders with transparency flips.

Acceptance: (a) the twenty problems extracted as standalone fixtures with Reference timings captured on the pinned baseline machine; (b) K2 prototype timings within the envelope the PG-2 arithmetic requires (document the model: tail share of total wall x speedup needed); (c) the cache-keying and delta-ordering design ratified or amended in writing; (d) alpha-canonical digest sharing (§7.1b) validated as the cache-key normalization. Tests: the twenty fixtures become a named benchmark suite with per-commit regression tracking (tails gate, not just medians — §19).

## Acceptance Criteria

All bead-specific requirements, acceptance conditions, tests, invariants, compatibility surfaces, evidence levels, performance gates, negative/recovery cases, and user-visible behaviors stated above remain mandatory. In addition, the MANDATORY VERIFICATION DEFINITION OF DONE in Notes must be satisfied with named unit/property/mutation suites, at least one shared real-path no-mock E2E scenario plus failure/recovery coverage, detailed human and schema-versioned NDJSON artifacts, and reproducible close evidence. No listed feature or claim may be silently narrowed, deferred, mocked, or declared complete through an unclassified divergence.
design:
FixtureSelectionManifestV1 prevents the twenty-case tail from becoming a hand-picked benchmark. Starting from raw valid samples owned by fln-544, a versioned deterministic selection method ranks the exact pinned Corpus, records exclusions and host-quality facts, stratifies deep delta, transparency, computation, eta, binder, instance, universe and sharing families, and freezes exactly twenty primary cases plus a non-gating holdout used only to detect overfitting. Selection, fixture minimization and any replacement preserve source/module/declaration identity and raw provenance; changing the set requires a reviewed manifest version.

DefeqTailDecisionV1 records the measured tail share, paired Reference/prototype raw samples, semantic cross-checks, uncertainty/variance, PG-2 arithmetic and claim type, then chooses Ratify, Amend or RejectAndReplan for K2 keying/delta order. A twenty-case result is bounded feasibility evidence, not proof of full-Corpus PG-2. Any miss amends the architecture, target or owner before interface freeze; it never changes the judgment or drops a case.

The cache key contract is an explicit field table. It includes canonical term identity, Environment logical root/epoch, transparency, metavariable-assignment revision and relevant local-context identity, reduction/mode/options that affect whnf, and schema/algorithm version. Alpha-canonical sharing is permitted only with a verified context-isomorphism witness; raw digest equality never aliases free variables, universes or assignments. Cache entries carry completeness and resource facts. Inconclusive, cancelled, stale or faulted computation is never cached as a whnf answer.

K2 remains an accelerator cross-checked against K1/Reference. The spike uses bounded cache capacity/eviction and deterministic tie rules; no benchmark path disables correctness checks or uses an unbounded warm cache. Performance telemetry is separate from semantic verdict/root evidence.

G0 DECISION INTEGRATION — emit exactly one G0SpikeDecisionV1 whose domain payload is DefeqTailDecisionV1. Outcome is RatifyK2TailDesign, AmendDefeqArchitecture, or NoGo mapped to Ratified/Amended/NoGo. Ratification is bounded feasibility over the deterministic twenty-case manifest plus holdout and cannot be promoted to PG-2 or Corpus-wide proof. Amendment names the exact cache key, K1/K2 authority seam, resource law, interface blast radius, §25 wording, downstream owners/edges, and complete rerun. Missing/hot-selected fixtures, unexplained divergence, Inconclusive/InternalFault, nonproductive thread labels, stale roots, or performance improvement without semantic agreement blocks.
acceptance_criteria:
Exactly twenty reviewed standalone fixtures capture the pinned Corpus definitional-equality/whnf tail across deep delta chains, transparency flips, Nat/Fin computation, structure eta, binders, instances, universes, and representative cache-sharing patterns. Reference raw timings and semantic traces are recorded on the pinned baseline machine. The K2 prototype implements memoized whnf keyed by term digest, environment identity and transparency, lazy delta ordered by height, environment-aware closures, and alpha-canonical sharing, and returns judgments identical to K1/Reference for every fixture. A quantitative tail-share model shows whether measured speedups satisfy the arithmetic required for PG-2; misses amend the architecture or claim, never semantics. Cache-keying, eviction/budgets, invalidation, and delta ordering are ratified in a versioned decision before Athanor/K2 freeze. Unit/property/model/metamorphic/mutation tests cover key aliases/separation, transparency, environment changes, binders, cache hits/misses, cancellation/resources, and recovery; named stale-key, wrong-delta, unsound-sharing, schedule-order, and timing-without-verdict mutants are killed. The named benchmark/differential E2E runs repeated isolated samples, 1/8/32-thread semantic checks, planted cache faults, restoration, and strict raw host/cache/tail/root evidence; invalid host runs remain retained but excluded. Dependencies, scripts/check.sh, cargo/fmt/clippy/UBS and kernel/performance lanes pass. No cherry-picked median, changed semantics for speed, stale memo acceptance, mock-only term, unmeasured PG-2 assertion, unresolved design branch, or deferred listed fixture satisfies closure.

The exact twenty-case manifest is regenerated from fln-544 raw baseline data with deterministic ranking, strata, exclusions, minimization provenance and a holdout overfit check. Missing host profiles or invalid samples remain explicit blockers; they are never replaced by a laptop/proxy or averaged. Cold and declared warm-cache states use paired repeated samples, raw distributions and tail metrics, with invalid runs retained but excluded by rule.

Independent whnf/key/cache models cover every key field, context isomorphism, transparency, environment and metavariable revision, hit/miss/eviction, lazy-delta height ties, binder/universe cases, exact budgets, cancellation and recovery. Mutants omit each key field, alias unequal contexts or digest collisions, reuse stale assignments/environments, choose wrong delta order, cache Inconclusive, suppress a verdict mismatch, overfit only the twenty cases, or derive PG-2 from a median; each is killed discriminatingly.

Every prototype judgment is compared to K1 and the pinned Reference before timing can count. Productive 1/8/32 semantic runs yield identical judgments, cache identities and decision artifacts; controlled performance samples use the declared thread/cache profile and never merge unlike cells. Strict evidence records selection/fixture/holdout IDs, baseline/prototype revisions, key fields/witnesses, semantic outcomes, raw samples and validity, cache/work/resource facts, PG arithmetic/claim state, mutation/first divergence, cleanup and final state. Closed-schema validators reject set drift, missing raw samples, host/cache conflation, semantic/telemetry merging, unmeasured targets or unresolved decisions.

title: W9: Snapshots + machine session API — publication generations, O(1) proof-state forks
description:
Implement snapshots + incrementality + the machine session API (§14.3, §14.4): every open document version maps to an immutable DocumentSnapshot (uri, version, content id, project logical root, GrammarEpochs at boundaries, command transactions, publication generation); edits derive new snapshots; superseded requests keep their snapshot but LOSE publication authority — the stale-diagnostics-into-a-new-buffer race is structurally impossible; every outward message rechecks its generation first.

Incrementality: command-granular snapshots extended DOWNWARD — Vellum sub-command reparse + Athanor dataflow means an edit inside a proof re-elaborates from the finest enclosing checkpoint (tactic-block granularity where upstream incrementality already reaches; declaration floor everywhere else), against O(1) environment snapshots, cancel-correct under typing bursts (PG-L: edit-ack + stale-cancel <= 25 ms p95; verified first-goal after mid-proof edit <= 100 ms p50). Diagnostics deduplicate by stable identity (typed cause + primary origin), not string equality; code actions carry idempotency keys + preconditions (stale-goal actions rejected with a structured response, never applied optimistically); progressive proof-state negotiation ($/frankenlean/progressiveProofState: ParseReady -> ProvisionalGoals -> VerifiedGoals -> ImpactComplete, provisional never cached as trusted); multi-project sessions bind each root to its epoch capsule.

The machine session API (§14.4): fork a proof state, apply a tactic, read goals, diff environments — O(1) per branch, thousands of branches per daemon; the substrate Envoy sells and the number that embarrasses the 18-735 s/branch literature. Acceptance: PG-L ladder met on the warm corpus; race-freedom verified under lab typing storms; session API forks measured at O(1). Tests: DPOR exploration of edit/cancel/publish interleavings; stale-precondition fixtures; generation-recheck mutation test (a message skipping the recheck must be impossible or caught).

## Acceptance Criteria

All bead-specific requirements, acceptance conditions, tests, invariants, compatibility surfaces, evidence levels, performance gates, negative/recovery cases, and user-visible behaviors stated above remain mandatory. In addition, the MANDATORY VERIFICATION DEFINITION OF DONE in Notes must be satisfied with named unit/property/mutation suites, at least one shared real-path no-mock E2E scenario plus failure/recovery coverage, detailed human and schema-versioned NDJSON artifacts, and reproducible close evidence. No listed feature or claim may be silently narrowed, deferred, mocked, or declared complete through an unclassified divergence.

title: W9: Lantern wire + daemon — byte-compatible LSP dialect, one shared import heap
description:
Implement the Lantern wire dialect + daemon topology (§14.1, §14.2): LSP with the $/lean/* extensions — plainGoal, plainTermGoal, the rpc/* session protocol (connect/call/release, reference-holding semantics), waitForDiagnostics, semantic tokens with the Reference legend, diagnostics shapes, widget delivery (client executes JS, wire-compatible pass-through) — BYTE-compatible so vscode-lean4 and every other client connects to lean --server and cannot tell.

Topology: the watchdog/worker PROCESS model is not replicated — only its observable behavior is. One daemon, all open files, all projects on a toolchain epoch, one shared immutable import heap (§7.5): the ~60 s x N-workers x GBs x N multiplication becomes once-per-daemon (PG-4: warm attach <= 2 s p50; PG-6: steady RSS serving >= 8 open mathlib files <= 1.3x ONE Reference worker). Per-file fault isolation becomes per-session region isolation: a crashing elaboration cancels an asupersync region, not a process; the supervisor restarts the session with the same client-visible semantics as a worker restart (BN-04). Transport is asupersync plumbing; zero protocol code written here.

Acceptance: vscode-lean4 connects unmodified and passes the smoke matrix basics; recorded-session replays (C5) diff clean at the wire with registered nondeterminism classes normalized; PG-4/PG-6 trajectory measured. comments.text:
LSP now reports real parse-error positions (IMPLEMENTATION_STATUS obligation #2, done at 2bf3a02a).

Before: the serve-lsp callback used the compatibility `fln_server::project` (empty
sources) and collapsed every engine failure to `lsp_error_snapshot`, hardcoding
position (1,0) — so editor squiggles for syntax errors landed at the file head and
non-ASCII columns were never converted to LSP UTF-16 units, even though
`project_with_sources` + the codepoint→UTF-16 conversion were already implemented
and unit-tested.

The parser already knew the offending BytePos (rebased into file coordinates) and
it survived to `lsp_source_snapshot`'s Err arm — discarded only in the last
function. Wired it through:
- `NatDefinitionParseError::primary_offset()` (fln-parse)
- `NatDefinitionFrontendError::primary_offset()` (fln-elab; parse → offset, elab → None)
- `EngineExecutionError::primary_source_offset()` (fln; unwraps BatchCommand/Frontend)
- fln-cli: the Err arm builds a positioned diagnostic (offset → FileMap::to_position),
  and the callback now calls project_with_sources with the exact unsaved document.

Proven end-to-end: `syntax_error_reports_a_real_utf16_source_position`
(lsp_stdio_e2e) opens a doc whose 2nd line is `def s : String := "🤖"@more` and
asserts the diagnostic lands at line 1, UTF-16 character 22 — real line (was 0)
AND UTF-16 conversion (codepoint column would be 21; the emoji is 2 UTF-16 units).
421 tests pass across fln-parse/fln-elab/fln/fln-cli; clippy -D warnings clean;
workspace compiles at 2bf3a02a.

DEFERRED follow-up (new implementation, not yet filed as its own bead): elaboration
and type errors are still positioned at (1,0) because `NatDefinitionElabError`
(fln-elab) is message-only. The offending token's `BytePos` lives on the `Syntax`
node passed to `elaborate_definition_in`/`elaborate_evaluation_in`/
`elaborate_check_in` but is discarded when the error is built. To locate type
errors: add a position field to the relevant `NatDefinitionElabError` variants,
populate it from the Syntax node's `pos()` at each `return Err(...)`, thread it
through `NatDefinitionFrontendError::Elaborate`, and have `primary_offset()` return
it — the fln/fln-cli bridge (`primary_source_offset` → `FileMap::to_position`)
then surfaces it with no further change.

title: W5: native_decide Tier 1 — replay receipts, trust-surface provenance
description:

title: Evidence receipts cannot bind the producing repository state
description:
## Finding

Measured at 974fcc5a9d9b2d9d1d0f879cddc9b8c928b69b8a: fln.evidence-bundle-commit/1 binds the run log, evidence manifest, manifest digest, run id, verdict, process exit, and input/final roots, but it records neither the full FrankenLean repository HEAD nor the canonical governed-path set whose bytes define those roots. A compact tracked receipt promoted after the transient bundle is pruned can therefore only operator-attest its producing commit. The 2026-07-27 env_snapshots run demonstrates the second half: its declared subset remained byte-stable while crates/fln-conformance changed during the held lock, so input_root == final_root was true without whole-repository quietness.

This is a producer-binding gap, not the governed-set policy question. franken_lean-build-gate-lane-governed-set-98np owns which paths each lane must govern. This bead owns carrying the exact producer identity and the governed-set identity through run_start, evidence manifest, bundle marker, validation, and compact verification receipts without widening either claim.

## Acceptance Criteria

- New complete bundles record a full lowercase 40-hex repository HEAD and a content-addressed canonical governed-path-set identity at run start, and carry both unchanged through the evidence manifest and bundle marker.
- Completion and side-effect-free validation reject missing, short, malformed, substituted, or drifting HEAD bindings and missing, reordered, duplicated, substituted, or drifting governed-set bindings.
- The scope is typed as full_repository or lane_declared_subset. A subset root is never rendered or promoted as whole-repository quietness.
- Compact receipt promotion accepts recorded bindings as authoritative, preserves operator_attested_legacy or unbound for historical bundles, and cannot upgrade either to recorded.
- The receipt records the source bundle, manifest, manifest-digest and run-log digests; typed skip and not_run remain distinct from executed pass.
- Seeded controls change only the producer HEAD, only the governed path set, and only one bound source digest; each is rejected for its named reason. A static dirty tree remains valid when all recorded identities are unchanged.
- No source bundle is deleted, moved, or rewritten during promotion.
- Focused evidence self-tests, manifest validation, cargo fmt --check, and attributable targeted checks pass. Any main-tree check.sh or e2e run follows the gate-lock and explicit-GO protocol.
close_reason: Producer HEAD and canonical governed-set identity are carried through run, manifest, marker, validation, and compact receipt; current bounded validation is recorded in the post-close judgement.

title: ci: declare the fln-syntax -> fln-core dependency edge in WORKSPACE_GRAPH.txt
description:
Filed by cc_3 on 2026-07-25 while landing Vellum slice 1 (fln-23cz, commit e20cded). A graph change, so it belongs to the ci/ owner rather than to fln-syntax.

## What is needed

One declared edge in ci/WORKSPACE_GRAPH.txt:

    edge fln-syntax -> fln-core        # SyntaxNodeKind and identifiers are Name (plan §9)

plus the matching path dependency in crates/fln-syntax/Cargo.toml.

## Why

A faithful Syntax cannot be written without it. Upstream (Init/Prelude.lean) defines Syntax.node with a SyntaxNodeKind, and SyntaxNodeKind IS Name; Syntax.ident carries a Name as well. fln-syntax currently declares ZERO edges, so slice 1 was deliberately written to need none — SourceInfo, the position projections and the losslessness law are all self-contained. The next slice cannot be: representing a node kind as a String or an interned integer would be a substitute for Name rather than a subset of it, which the doctrine forbids, and it would diverge from the pin at the exact point the Mirror façade has to match.

The layering is already satisfied: fln-syntax is rank 7 and fln-core is rank 0, so the edge points strictly downward per §5. Nothing about the rank order needs to change; the edge simply has to be declared, because the graph is an acknowledgment file and an undeclared edge fails structure-guard's snapshot law in both directions.

## Acceptance Criteria

The edge is declared in ci/WORKSPACE_GRAPH.txt and the dependency added to crates/fln-syntax/Cargo.toml in the same change, so structure-guard's real_workspace suite stays clean rather than passing through an inconsistent intermediate state. No other edge is added: fln-syntax must NOT gain a dependency on fln-hash, since canonical serialization of syntax belongs to fln-hash depending downward on syntax, not the reverse.

## Notes

title: Evidence self-test: Git 2.54 detached maintenance workers become unreaped subreaper children
description:
## Symptom

On a clean shared-tree snapshot, the mandatory gate fails before fmt/check/clippy/test with `evidence-self-test:unexpected_child_exit`. The supervisor reports that the self-test process already owns unrelated child lifetimes, which looks like concurrent-agent interference or a lane containment defect.

## Reproduction

From `/data/projects/franken_lean`, run:

`flock -w 2400 /data/tmp/fln-gate.lockfile ./scripts/check.sh`

The clean-tree reproduction at HEAD 675cf1e exited 2 in the first `evidence-self-test` stage and retained a complete failure bundle at `target/check/check-20260725T062608Z-910098/bundle.complete.json`. The stage stderr named child PIDs 913404 and 913461. A focused standalone process trace reproduced before the first supervised case (`large_output_pass`): `flock -w 2400 /data/tmp/fln-gate.lockfile strace -ff -tt -e trace=clone,clone3,fork,vfork,execve,wait4 -o target/diagnostics/cod1-evidence-self-test-20260725T0630Z.trace python3 scripts/evidence.py self-test --art-dir target/diagnostics/cod1-evidence-self-test-20260725T0630Z-artifacts`.

## Root cause

`cmd_self_test` calls `enable_child_subreaper()`, then its Git-backed UBS fixture performs two commits through `run_git`. With Git 2.54, each commit invokes `/usr/lib/git-core/git maintenance run --auto --quiet --detach`. The maintenance command clones a detached worker and exits; the worker also exits 0, is adopted by the self-test subreaper, and remains unreaped. The next `run_supervised` correctly sees those adopted PIDs and refuses to mix unrelated lifetimes into its authority boundary. Trace PIDs 1040631 and 1040777 prove both workers exited 0.

## Required outcome

Make evidence Git invocations deterministic and child-clean without weakening the supervisor exclusion check. Candidate narrow fixes are sealing `run_git` with `-c maintenance.auto=false`, or explicitly reaping only self-test-owned exited maintenance children before the first supervised case. Add a regression reproducing the Git 2.54 auto-maintenance topology and proving no adopted child survives into `run_supervised`; preserve typed refusal for genuinely unrelated live children. The mandatory flocked `scripts/check.sh` gate must then pass this stage and retain independently valid evidence.
close_reason: Fixed in ccff649: Git subprocesses seal maintenance.auto=false; adopted-zombie refusal and zero-survivor regression coverage pass. One detached self-test retry directly passed the vugo-relevant evidence-self-test stage; later stages were invalidated by concurrent crates/fln-env/src/modules.rs editing, tracked as shared-tree concurrency. Projection coordination remains with fln-3oj6.
