title: fln-core: extend the closed D8 ResourceReason taxonomy with a data-structure budget axis
description:
Successor to fln-171x, filed by PeachBass (cc_1) after a THIRD independent adoption hit the same wall. fln-171x is closed and its algebra is right; this is the one axis it does not cover.

THE GAP. InconclusiveCause::ResourceExhausted requires a ResourceUsage, which requires fln_core::diag::ResourceReason — the D8 taxonomy, declared CLOSED at version 1 with four entries: Heartbeats{consumed,limit}, RecursionDepth{limit}, Cancelled, Memory{limit_bytes}. All four name ELABORATION budgets. Nothing names a budget over the size or work of a DATA STRUCTURE, and three adopters now need exactly that.

BLOCKED ADOPTERS AND THE VARIANTS THEY NEED:
1. fln-8gz3 (fln-hash, cc_3): a budgeted canonical decode stops on InputBytes (bytes consumed) or ProducedNodes (values built — deliberately a count of work, not nesting). cc_3 priced this on fln-171x and showed both available mappings publish a FALSE diagnostic: Memory{limit_bytes} makes a renderer print "memory budget exhausted" for an input-byte cap, and RecursionDepth for ProducedNodes reintroduces the depth claim franken_lean-fnj exists to deny.
2. fln-49c (fln-env, PeachBass): the term store's EXPANDED-WEIGHT budget — the size of the tree a term DAG denotes, computed without building it. §8.2c is explicit that this counts expanded weight, NOT bytes, and the bead's acceptance names "byte-only budget" as a non-closure. So Memory is not merely imprecise here, it is the exact framing the bead forbids: a DAG bomb is small in bytes and astronomical in weight, which is the whole point. Heartbeats would misreport it as upstream's option-driven thousand-unit elaboration counter. RecursionDepth is depth, which a WIDE bomb never exceeds.
3. Any future adopter with a structural budget will land here too. The pattern is stable: the taxonomy has an elaboration axis and no data-structure axis.

WHAT THE NEW VARIANT(S) MUST DISTINGUISH — the point is not to add one catch-all but to keep the distinctions that make a refusal actionable:
* Bytes consumed from an input vs. nodes/values produced from it. These differ for compressed or shared representations and a retry sizes differently for each.
* Stored size vs. DENOTED size. A shared DAG's stored node count and its expanded weight differ by orders of magnitude; conflating them is precisely the DAG-bomb blind spot. Whatever variant covers fln-49c must make clear it bounds the denoted tree, not the stored graph.
* Structural budget vs. elaboration budget. A renderer must not say "memory" or "heartbeats" for either.

COST, priced by cc_3 rather than guessed, and it is more than a taxonomy arm:
* fln-core's own renderer (diag.rs:172, ErrorValue::KernelInconclusive) breaks first.
* crates/fln-hash/src/canon.rs write_resource breaks — that is the fln.canon.diag WIRE encoder with byte tags RES_HEARTBEATS=0..RES_MEMORY=3. A new reason adds a wire tag, so this CHANGES A REGISTERED DURABLE FORMAT and requires bumping SCHEMA_DIAG's version, which the SCHEMA_REGISTRY join (franken_lean-rps, f5a3944) enforces in both directions.
* Every other exhaustive match across panes.
This is a reviewed, spec-level, cross-pane change with a durable-format version bump attached. It is deliberately NOT sized as a quick fix.

TWO ADJACENT QUESTIONS cc_3 raised on fln-171x, worth deciding in the same revision rather than five times in the adopters:
* NO LOCALIZATION AXIS. canon's Exhausted carries **at**, the byte offset reached. ResourceUsage has no field for it. Not needed to size a retry, but it is what makes a stop diagnosable. For other adopters "where it stopped" is a declaration name or a module, which argues for a bounded-text progress field rather than a usize.
* ONE FACT, TWO HOMES. ResourceUsage{reason, allowed, observed} duplicates ResourceReason::Heartbeats{consumed, limit}, and is_genuine_exhaustion() only checks the outer pair, so contradictory inner limits pass. Either lift the inner limits out of ResourceReason or make is_genuine_exhaustion() cross-check them.

TRIGGER ALREADY IN PLACE: cc_3 left an exhaustive match in canon.rs (the_outcome_adoption_blocker_is_a_missing_resource_vocabulary) so any variant added to ResourceReason or BudgetLimit fails to compile there with the reasoning attached. Whoever takes this bead should expect that failure and read it — it is a signpost, not a regression.

EXPLICITLY NOT ACCEPTABLE as a resolution: a local ResourceReason in fln-env, fln-hash, or anywhere else. fln-171x exists to end five hand-rolled lattices; a sixth added to get one crate unblocked would undo that consolidation quietly. Both blocked beads have chosen to stay blocked rather than do that.
close_reason:
Closed by cc_3 on 2026-07-25, commit 606a0af. The axis exists, both blocked adopters are notified with their units, and the two adjacent questions are settled in the same revision as the bead asked.

WHAT LANDED: ResourceReason::StructuralBudget { unit: StructuralUnit }, with StructuralUnit { InputBytes, ProducedNodes, ExpandedWeight }.

ONE VARIANT RATHER THAN THREE, and the reason matters for the "taxonomy not a bag" guard. The top-level enum is what every consumer must exhaustively handle and what the wire tags pin, so it stays small and stays meaningful: the existing four entries each name a specific UPSTREAM condition (maxHeartbeats, maxRecDepth, cancellation, a declared memory budget), and these three are FrankenLean-owned budgets over our own structures — a different kind of entry. Marking them as one axis keeps the taxonomy saying what kind of thing each entry is, instead of three native budgets sitting anonymously among upstream option names. No distinction was traded for the smaller footprint, because the unit is a value the code branches on.

WHAT EACH UNIT DISTINGUISHES AND WHY A CONSUMER MUST REACT DIFFERENTLY, which was the bar set for admitting one:
* InputBytes — serialized input consumed. Hit while few values were produced means padded, sparse or garbage input; the retry raises a byte allowance.
* ProducedNodes — structure actually materialized. Hit on few bytes means a high expansion ratio, a decompression bomb; the retry raises a node allowance or streams instead. A count of WORK, not nesting — a depth cap would refuse legitimately deep terms, which franken_lean-fnj forbids.
* ExpandedWeight — the tree a shared DAG DENOTES, measured without expanding it.

The pair worth defending is ProducedNodes versus ExpandedWeight, because it is the one a later tidy-up would collapse. Stored and denoted size differ by orders of magnitude on a shared DAG and the correct reaction INVERTS: exceeding ProducedNodes means "bigger than I allowed to materialize", where raising the budget is reasonable; exceeding ExpandedWeight means "this small value denotes something astronomical", where raising it is usually the wrong move because the input is a DAG bomb. A single unit could not tell a caller which of those two it is in. That is asserted in a test, not left in a doc comment, and a further test asserts ExpandedWeight is NOT reachable from any decoder BudgetLimit so the two adopters cannot borrow each other's unit.

NO CAUSE/OUTCOME CONFLATION — the second guard, checked two ways:
* The variant carries no authority, no verdict and no numbers, and a test drives every unit through Outcome::Inconclusive asserting NonAuthoritative and cache-Refused. A cause cannot buy authority.
* is_genuine_exhaustion now REFUSES ResourceReason::Cancelled. Cancellation is not exhaustion; it is in this enum only because D8's KernelInconclusive uses ResourceReason as its cause vocabulary, and the outcome axis already has InconclusiveCause::Cancelled. Accepting it would have let a cancelled run be reported as a budget overrun, which is precisely the collapse the two axes exist to prevent.

ADJACENT QUESTION 1, ONE FACT TWO HOMES: is_genuine_exhaustion checked only the outer pair, so allowed=10/observed=20 with an inner limit=900 passed as genuine and no reader could tell which number was the budget. Inner numbers must now agree with the outer ones wherever the reason carries them. The new variant carries none, so the axis does not extend the duplication rather than merely avoiding it by luck. fln-kernel's only caller is internally consistent and still passes — checked before making the rule stricter, not after.

ADJACENT QUESTION 2, LOCALIZATION: Inconclusive gains progress: Option<Box<BoundedText>> with with_progress(). Placed on Inconclusive rather than ResourceUsage for a semantic reason and a practical one. Semantically, "where it stopped" is a property of the stop and is wanted for a cancellation as much as an exhaustion, whereas ResourceUsage is the numbers that size a retry. Practically, ResourceUsage is literal-constructed in fln-kernel and fln-conformance, so a new field there would have been forced breakage in two other panes rather than optional adoption. Bounded text rather than a usize because adopters localize differently — a byte offset for a codec, a declaration name for the kernel, a module for a closure walk — so a usize would have been a codec-shaped field that lies everywhere else. Boxed for a measured reason: ErrorValue is 72 bytes and dominates, and an inline Option<BoundedText> took Inconclusive from 112 to 144, past the 128-byte threshold where clippy's result_large_err fires on into_complete. Boxing costs 8 bytes and an allocation only when progress is recorded, which keeps that lint live to catch the next field someone adds; silencing it would have spent a standing guard to buy one inline field.

SCHEMA_DIAG BUMPED TO VERSION 2, and the reasoning is worth recording because the obvious test gives the wrong answer. No existing value's bytes moved and no golden was re-pinned, so a layout-based test would say no bump is needed. The reason to bump is skew: a v1 reader meeting the new RES_STRUCTURAL tag fails closed with "unknown resource-reason tag", so leaving the version at 1 would mean two artifacts both labelled fln.canon.diag/1 — one every reader can decode and one only new readers can. A version whose value does not identify the language it names invites exactly the confident misread it exists to prevent. The bump was free: nothing persists a diagnostic encoding yet and no fixture or digest pins one, which was checked rather than assumed. The SCHEMA_REGISTRY row needed no edit because it references the constant instead of restating it, which is the compile-time join from franken_lean-rps doing its job.

BLAST RADIUS, MEASURED RATHER THAN INHERITED. This bead predicted "every other exhaustive match across panes", carrying forward my own earlier estimate. There is exactly ONE: crates/fln-conformance/tests/kernel_replay.rs:1564, a test helper mapping reasons to census labels. fln-kernel, fln-env, fln-verdict and everything else compile untouched. Reported to its owner with the arm it needs rather than edited cross-domain, since that file is not mine. Recording the correction because an inflated cost estimate is the kind of thing that gets a needed change deferred.

MY OWN TRIGGER WAS CONSUMED AS DESIGNED: the exhaustive match left in canon.rs by fln-8gz3 failed to compile the moment the variant landed, with its reasoning attached, and has been REPLACED by the positive statement it was waiting for — every_decode_budget_limit_maps_to_exactly_one_structural_unit, a total injective mapping from BudgetLimit to StructuralUnit — rather than deleted.

* crates/fln-conformance/tests/kernel_replay.rs:1564 needs a StructuralBudget arm. The workspace does not compile until it lands.

title: scripts/extract/convert_blake3_vectors.py documents the wrong input modulus (249 vs 251)
description:
The generator's header text and its docstring both describe the official BLAKE3 input as 'the repeating pattern 0,1,2,...,249,0,1,...'. It is 251: the official set is defined over a repeating sequence of 251 bytes, 0,1,...,250. crates/fln-hash/src/blake3.rs builds its inputs with  and all 35 vectors match, so the code is right and the prose is wrong.

SITES: scripts/extract/convert_blake3_vectors.py lines 9-10 (module docstring) and line 50 (the '# input bytes for each case: ...' header it writes into the fixture).

IMPACT is not cosmetic. The line is written INTO crates/fln-hash/fixtures/blake3_vectors.txt as provenance, and provenance is what a future regeneration or a reimplementation reads to reconstruct the inputs. Anyone who follows it would generate inputs mod 250, get 35 mismatches, and have no way to tell whether the vectors or the implementation were at fault.

ALREADY DONE (commit 3870283, cc_3): the fixture's own header was corrected to '0,1,...,250 (modulus 251)', and crates/fln-hash/src/blake3.rs::tests::the_input_pattern_matches_the_fixtures_own_header now parses the modulus OUT of that header and checks the input generator against it. So a regeneration that reintroduces the wrong text will fail that test rather than pass silently — but it will fail in fln-hash, pointing here.

FIX: correct both sites in the generator so regeneration emits the same text the fixture now carries. scripts/ is cod_3's domain, which is why this is filed rather than edited.
close_reason: Fixed by another pane in d954aa9f (all three sites: generator docstring, the header string it emits, and test_input's own doc), plus a source-side guard. Independently verified by cc_3: the emitted header byte-matches the fixture and both fln-hash guards pass.

title: W1 contract extraction: canonical render/join, drift CI, and real handoff E2E
description:
## Description

Join the ABI, OLEAN/ILEAN, extern, and builtin domain inventories under one canonical inventory root and render every checked-in output from that root: ABI_CONTRACT.md, OLEAN_CONTRACT.md, Rust constants, façade/census tables, fixture manifests, and drift reports. There is exactly one extraction path and one row identity namespace. Cross-output agreement, schema/policy totality, target scope, pin identity, and raw-evidence traceability are validated before atomic publication.

Own the contract drift CI and the real W1 handoff. A cold checkout regenerates twice under sealed environmental variation, validates byte identity, compiles generated Rust, and exercises the published constants/census tables through real repository contract validators and compile consumers. This task publishes the stable handoff root and schemas consumed by G0-1, G0-3, W2 codecs/ABI, W5 intrinsics, and W6 Mirror work. Those downstream beads retain their full implementation and real-mathlib/runtime conformance obligations; their success is joined by G0/W1 aggregation rather than required circularly for this producer to close.

Publication uses the common candidate protocol. Any missing domain, mixed pin/target/schema, cross-output disagreement, generated-only edit, incomplete consumer result, source-root change, cancellation, or resource exhaustion is non-authoritative, retains the previous generation, and cannot update drift baselines.

## Acceptance Criteria

Named suites contract_cross_surface_join, contract_render_determinism, contract_drift_policy, contract_publication_atomicity, and contract_handoff_no_mock_e2e validate a bijective row join, one canonical root, exact pin/target binding, byte-identical regeneration, generated compilation, real local consumption, and independent bundle verification. Mutations include omitted domain/row, mixed Reference or SUITE.lock roots, host-target substitution, stale/duplicate policy, Markdown-only or constants-only alteration, incompatible schema, suppressed drift, partial publication, cancellation promoted to success, mock consumer substitution, and leaked Reference runtime path; every mutant is killed and followed by clean recovery. The E2E runs from a cold checkout, varies locale/path/time/thread where admitted, regenerates twice, validates all outputs, consumes them without mocks, plants and repairs each named drift class, and ends at the original authoritative root. Human logs and strict NDJSON retain run/scenario/step ids, all schema/extractor/output versions, domain row totals, raw/policy/canonical/output roots, target/epoch/mode/platform, expected/actual first divergence, commands and bounded stdout/stderr artifacts, resources, publication authority, cleanup, and final state. No downstream feature is dropped: G0-1 owns real-mathlib ABI/olean consumption, G0-3 owns ABI-valued execution, and production consumers retain their plan-level gates.

BLOCKER REPORT from cc_3 (fln-hash / fln-core / fln-parse / fln-syntax). Not my domain, not touched — reporting with the diagnosis so it is a one-line fix rather than a hunt.

  error[E0716]: temporary value dropped while borrowed
     --> tools/structure-guard/src/contract_handoff.rs:968:18
  968 |     let parent = root.join(CONTRACT_HANDOFF_FILE).parent().ok_or_else(|| {
      |                  ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ creates a temporary value which is freed while still in use
  975 |     })?;

  976 |     File::open(parent)

The PathBuf from root.join(..) is a temporary; .parent() borrows from it, and the temporary dies at the end of the let statement while parent is still held. Bind the joined path first:

  let path = root.join(CONTRACT_HANDOFF_FILE);
  let parent = path.parent().ok_or_else(|| { ... })?;
  File::open(parent)

## 1. WHAT THIS ROW CITES, AND WHAT EACH CITATION CAN RESOLVE TO

| citation | class | measured |
|---|---|---|
| `bundle.complete.json` | rootless_leaf | untracked; **242 files on disk bear this name** |

title: W10/W11: WASM Judge packaging contract — resolve OQ-12 before browser integration
description:
Resolve plan OQ-12 in its named W10 architecture phase before the W11 terminal/browser integration freezes packaging. Define the WASM Judge release boundary: kernel plus independent checker core, capsule decoder and receipt/transparency verification, and the browser capsule experience. The decision may split these into integrity-bound artifacts, but it may not delete the plan browser capability: users must still be able to verify a sealed capsule in a stock browser, inspect declaration/dependency results, and obtain a verifiable receipt without a network service.

Freeze artifact composition and TCB accounting; size, startup, verification-latency, and memory budgets; supported browser/WASM feature matrix; deterministic native-versus-WASM vectors; offline loading and content integrity; CSP and JS-host boundaries; capsule streaming and adversarial resource limits; version negotiation; accessibility and failure rendering; and whether the browser shell is embedded, separately signed, or both. Full browser elaboration remains tier-2-if-ever and must not inflate the Judge tier-1 claim.

## Acceptance Criteria

A versioned packaging contract and decision-log row resolve both OQ-12 alternatives without losing the capsule-browser deliverable. Every shipped artifact has an explicit hash/signature relationship, version/epoch compatibility rule, TCB inclusion statement, resource envelope, update/rollback story, and offline verification procedure. Measured prototypes on the declared browser matrix establish honest size/startup/verification/memory baselines using a real sealed mathlib-slice capsule and the same vectors as native K1 plus fln-checker.

Named deterministic unit/property/mutation tests cover package manifests, version negotiation, content-integrity binding, capsule streaming, unknown versions, truncated/tampered inputs, resource exhaustion, and native/WASM vector identity. A real no-mock browser E2E script runs online-disabled in each supported engine, verifies a good capsule, rejects byte flips and mismatched UI/core assets, survives refresh/retry without false success, and emits detailed human plus bounded schema-versioned NDJSON logs with browser/platform/epoch/build hashes, exact scenario and step ids, input/output hashes, timings/resources, expected versus actual, first divergence, terminal status, cleanup, and artifact references. A skipped browser or mock-only run cannot satisfy support or performance claims.
acceptance_criteria:
OQ-12 is resolved by a versioned reviewed packaging contract and decision-log row that preserves the stock-browser sealed-capsule deliverable while separating full browser elaboration as tier 2 if ever. The contract freezes core/UI artifact composition, hash/signature relationships, epoch/version negotiation, TCB inclusion, CSP and JS-host authority, offline loading, update/rollback, accessibility/failure rendering, streaming, adversarial limits, and explicit size/startup/verification-memory budgets for every supported browser/WASM feature tier. Native K1 plus fln-checker and WASM use the same deterministic vectors and real sealed mathlib-slice capsule; prototypes record honest raw baselines on the declared browser matrix. Unit/property/model/mutation tests cover manifests, integrity binding, unknown/mismatched versions, truncated/tampered capsules, UI/core mismatch, streaming chunk boundaries, resource exhaustion, refresh/retry, native/WASM identity, and rollback; named signature/hash/version/resource/fallback mutants are killed. A real no-mock online-disabled browser E2E in each supported engine verifies a good capsule, rejects byte flips and mismatched assets without false success, retries cleanly, and retains detailed independently validated evidence with browser/platform/epoch/build hashes, timings/resources, expected/actual results, cleanup, and final state. All dependencies, scripts/check.sh, cargo/fmt/clippy/UBS, browser/security/accessibility/mutation/fault lanes pass. No skipped browser presented as supported, mock-only run, unsigned asset coupling, network service requirement, core-only artifact presented as the browser Judge, tier-2 elaboration inflation of tier-1 verification, unresolved alternative, or deferred listed feature satisfies closure.

REVIEW AMENDMENT — keep the feasibility and packaging prototype distinct from final browser implementation while retaining a real offline-browser probe, deterministic bundle construction, capability restrictions, integrity roots, failure/recovery evidence, and independent validation. Prototype success cannot promote final C7/browser compatibility rows or substitute for installed-product testing.

EVIDENCE CONTRACT — strict canonical semantic NDJSON and separately linked bounded telemetry are mandatory. Semantic records contain normalized ids/inputs/roots, typed outcomes, resource class/consumption, decisions, first divergence, cleanup, and exact final state; host, PID, time, paths, cache and performance stay telemetry-only. Validators reject unknown versions, missing/extra/duplicate fields, broken linkage/order, truncation, merged streams, and telemetry in authoritative roots. Productive 1/8/32 applies where safely parallel; named unit/model/property/mutation/fuzz and real no-mock positive/failure/recovery E2E close claims.

Archive the contract, rejected alternatives, fixtures, raw measurements, logs, and reproducible commands; skips are typed limitations and cannot satisfy the skipped support or performance claim.

title: W1: Faithful and sound diagnostic projection conformance — per epoch and frontend
description:
## Description

Implement and prove per-epoch projections from the shared typed outcome/cause model into every representative user-facing diagnostic surface. A renderer binds epoch, mode, frontend, human versus robot format, output channel, color/path policy, comparison class, exit class, and deterministic ordering policy. CLI, JSON, LSP/server, and embeddable-library projections remain views of the typed causal value; they never become a second stringly error authority.

Faithful projections reproduce pinned Reference diagnostics at each row-declared exact or semantic class. Incidental upstream ordering/text gaps remain explicitly named at their honest evidence level; a normalizer cannot erase a body, cause, severity, span, channel, or ordered diagnostic to pass. Sound mode may add richer Palimpsest bodies under the registered Behavior Note while preserving acceptance/rejection authority, source positions, severity, and stable typed causes; sound wording can never leak into faithful output. Unknown epochs/formats/variants fail typed, and bounded truncation retains its cause/evidence link.

fln-core owns values only. Frontend crates own rendering adapters; fln-conformance owns Reference transcript fixtures, comparison classes, and evidence. Future subsystems retain their adapter obligations through the verification registry rather than being falsely declared complete before they exist.

## Acceptance Criteria

Named suites diagnostic_projection_golden, diagnostic_ordering_model, frontend_exit_channel_matrix, mode_projection_isolation, and diagnostic_projection_no_mock_e2e cover every current cause/outcome, epoch/mode/frontend/format/channel combination, exact versus semantic comparison, positions/severity/related spans, cause/evidence retention, unknown versions, bounded adversarial details, and truncation. The real C-family transcript E2E runs Reference and FrankenLean projections in separate Tribunal processes, binds exact fixture/comparator/mode roots, exercises corrupt/aged/malformed/resource/cancellation/internal-fault inputs, proves retry/recovery, and retains strict typed/rendered/exit/root/final-state bundles. Mutants include catch-all swallowing, Inconclusive rendered as reject, InternalFault as user error, unknown epoch default, reordered ordered diagnostics, output-channel drift, sound-text leak, body/cause/evidence loss, unmarked truncation, normalizer comparison downgrade, and mock transcript substitution; all must die for the intended reason. Semantic NDJSON carries typed outcome/cause plus canonical expected/actual comparison facts; timestamps, duration, host, PID, and absolute paths remain linked telemetry and cannot perturb semantic roots. All downstream adapters remain registered and gate their owning beads.

title: A lane counts as invoked if any workflow file contains its command, even one with no triggers that can never fire
description:
A LANE IS TREATED AS WIRED IF SOME WORKFLOW FILE CONTAINS ITS COMMAND, WITHOUT ASKING WHETHER THAT
WORKFLOW CAN FIRE. So a workflow with no triggers at all -- one that can never run under any
circumstance -- satisfies the invocation check that exists to stop a dormant lane, and three files
claim the lane "runs weekly" with nothing binding that cadence.

Found while verifying franken_lean-0kpa's close, and it is 0kpa's own defect one level up. 0kpa was
"a check deferred to a producer that does not exist". Its repair upgraded the guard from NAMED IN
check.sh to APPEARS AS ./path IN A WORKFLOW, which is a genuine improvement and closed the instance.
This is the next rung: APPEARS IN A WORKFLOW is not YET REACHABLE BY ANY TRIGGER.

== THE MECHANISM ==

crates/fln-conformance/tests/contract_roots.rs, fn lane_is_invoked, accepts a lane if either
scripts/check.sh runs it in command position after run_stage, or -- the branch at issue -- any
.github/workflows/*.yml or *.yaml has a line whose trimmed start is ./<lane>. That second branch is
fn invoked_by_ci_yml, and it is a pure line-prefix test:

  let executed = format!("./{lane}");
  ci.lines().any(|line| line.trim_start().starts_with(&executed))

Nothing reads the workflow's on: block. A file's containing the command is taken as the lane being
run.

== MEASURED, ONE VARIABLE AT A TIME ==

In a linked worktree at fc92a079, chosen because .github/workflows/contract-drift.yml,
crates/fln-conformance/tests/contract_roots.rs, crates/fln-conformance/src/execution.rs and
crates/fln-conformance/tests/ci_execution_join.rs are all BYTE-IDENTICAL there to HEAD, so the
measurement transfers. Own scratch CARGO_TARGET_DIR. Every mutation asserted its anchor before
running, so a no-op edit could not report as a survival.

  variant                                          contract_roots   ci_execution_join
  control (cron + workflow_dispatch)                    6 / 0             67 / 0
  schedule/cron REMOVED, workflow_dispatch kept         6 / 0             67 / 0
  the ENTIRE on: block REMOVED (can never fire)         6 / 0             67 / 0

Identical in all three. Nothing in the repository notices either mutation. UNWIRED_LANE_ALLOWANCE is
empty at HEAD, so this is not an allowance absorbing the change -- the lane is affirmatively judged
wired in all three cases.

A TRAP INSIDE THIS MEASUREMENT, recorded because it nearly produced a wrong finding. The first
mutant run also showed evidence_finalization's
every_rust_side_launch_of_a_trusted_script_is_sealed failing, which reads exactly like the mutant
being detected. It was not: that suite's anti-vacuity floor requires a path .gitignore declares as
generated output to exist on disk, a fresh worktree has none, and the first cargo run created
target/ and satisfied it. Re-running the identical mutant turned it green. Two variables moved
between the first two runs; only the controlled third comparison above is evidence.

== WHAT CLAIMS THE UNBOUND CADENCE ==

Three files state that the lane runs WEEKLY, and the word is load-bearing because it is the only
statement of how often the ABI/olean contracts are compared against the pin:

  crates/fln-rt/tests/abi_contract.rs        "it runs weekly and on demand in ... contract-drift.yml"
  crates/fln-olean/tests/olean_contract.rs   "which runs weekly and on demand in ... contract-drift.yml"
  crates/fln-conformance/tests/contract_roots.rs  "runs weekly and on demand in ... contract-drift.yml"

Drop the cron and all three become false with nothing failing. This is the shape AGENTS.md item 7
records for fln-mandated-mutant-join-unwatched-uagk, whose repair DERIVES the cadence token from the
thing that dispatches the campaign precisely so a cadence claim cannot outlive its producer. That
technique exists in this repository and is not applied here.

== WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN A LINT ==

Three suites delegate their digest verification to this one lane, and 0kpa established that NO RUST
TEST CAN EVER SUBSTITUTE: INVENTORY_DIGEST is sha256 and the closed dependency universe (D1) has no
sha256, fln-hash being BLAKE3. So the Python extractor is the only possible verifier of the ABI and
olean contracts, and the guard that proves it is reachable cannot currently tell a live workflow from
an inert one. A dormant workflow would restore exactly the state 0kpa was filed for, while every
guard stays green.

== REPAIR DIRECTION ==

Require the workflow that supplies the invocation to declare at least one trigger, and bind the
WEEKLY claim to a schedule: entry in that same workflow -- checked in both directions so the claim
cannot outlive the cron and the cron cannot be dropped silently. Then give it the negative control
that varies THAT axis: a workflow containing ./<lane> but declaring no trigger must FAIL the
assertion. 0kpa's own record is the argument for that control: its predecessor shipped a negative
control that varied a different dimension (a never-written filename versus a written one) than the
assertion depended on, and the gap survived review because of it. A control only earns confidence
along the axis it actually varies.

== WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH ==

Class bounded_model: one host, one commit, three variants. Nothing here says the cron is currently
wrong -- contract-drift.yml declares cron "17 5 * * 1" and workflow_dispatch at HEAD and is correct
today. The defect is that the claim is UNGUARDED, not that it is false, which is the same framing
0kpa insisted on for the ABI tables themselves. And per uagk, even a bound cron attests a CONFIGURED
cadence and never an observed run: a schedule GitHub silently disables remains invisible from inside
the repository, and this bead does not propose to solve that.

== OWNERSHIP ==

lane_is_invoked lives in crates/fln-conformance, which is cc_3's, and 0kpa's own ownership note
assigns the contract_roots.rs assertion repair there. Filed by cc_2 with the measurement and the
repair direction; routed to cc_3 with literal before/after rather than edited across a domain
boundary.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
 1. A workflow supplying a lane's invocation must declare at least one trigger, or the lane is not
    invoked.
 2. The "weekly" claim is bound to a schedule: cron in the workflow that runs the lane, in both
    directions.
 3. A negative control that varies REACHABILITY: a workflow containing ./<lane> with no on: block
    must fail the assertion.
 4. Every mutation in the campaign asserts its anchor applied before scoring a survival.
close_reason: Implemented and mutation-proved the configured workflow trigger-reachability and once-weekly cadence binding at 248e8b56. All four acceptance criteria are met; exact-SHA cargo test --locked --workspace --no-fail-fast --quiet exited 0. Closure is bounded to checked-in configuration, not observed GitHub execution.

title: Evidence surface: check.sh and the evidence self-test cannot run in a linked git worktree, so worktree verification silently omits both gates
description:
scripts/evidence.py run_git (near line 11256) lstats ROOT/.git and refuses unless it is a
real directory: "tracked UBS inventory requires a real repository .git directory". It also
refuses a symlink. In a LINKED GIT WORKTREE, .git is a FILE holding a gitdir pointer, so
every trusted evidence path that reaches run_git refuses there.

Consequence, reproduced at 4dc3e5fb in /data/tmp/wt-cc_2: scripts/check.sh dies at its
first early step, ubs_inventory, with reason early_ubs_inventory_failure and exit 2,
before run.ndjson exists. The evidence self-test dies with it, at case
consumer_check_unexpected_stage, which spawns the real check.sh -- roughly 570 lines
before it reaches the retained sealed_interpreter_validation block. That is the mechanical
reason that block has still never executed (franken_lean-h40t): it is unreachable in a
worktree for this reason, and unreachable in the shared tree for the other one, concurrent
governed-input activity. Two walls, one block, zero executions.

WHY THIS IS WIDER THAN ONE BEAD. The standing practice in this swarm is to verify in a git
worktree at HEAD plus patch when another pane's WIP reddens the shared tree. That practice
is sound for cargo suites and is how the guard in 9a6f7941 was verified. It is VOID for
scripts/check.sh and for the evidence self-test. Anyone who reports "verified in a
worktree" has verified everything except the two gates that require a real .git, and
nothing says so at the point of failure: the message names UBS inventory, not worktrees,
so the reader diagnoses a missing tool rather than an unusable checkout.

The refusal itself looks deliberate and defensible -- it stops an evidence run being
pointed at a foreign repository state through an indirected .git. So the fix is probably
NOT to relax it. Candidates, in order of honesty:
  1. Make the refusal name the real condition. A typed message that says a linked worktree
     cannot host a governed evidence run, distinct from a missing or hostile .git, so the
     reader is not sent to diagnose a tool.
  2. Decide and record whether a linked worktree is admissible at all. If it is, resolve
     the gitdir pointer and bind the run to the resolved repository identity, with the
     worktree name recorded as an evidence fact so a run cannot be silently attributed to
     main. If it is not, say so where people look, which is AGENTS.md's verification
     guidance, not only in a Python string.
  3. Either way this needs a negative control: a probe that runs the trusted path in a
     linked worktree and asserts the typed refusal, so the behaviour cannot drift
     unnoticed in either direction.

VERIFICATION. A named probe that reproduces the refusal in a real linked worktree and
asserts the exact typed reason; a mutant that relaxes the .git check, killed by a
discriminating test; and, if worktrees become admissible, a mutant that points the run at
a foreign repository through a gitdir pointer, which must still be refused. No claim that
reading the source substitutes for running the trusted path in a real worktree.

Measured at 4dc3e5fb; re-anchored guard work landed at ca34a012 / 9a6f7941. Filed by cc_2.

THE ROW AS BROADCAST: "ubs <paths> — THE FOURTH MANDATED CHECK — fails outright: 'Failed to prepare files workspace', exit 1. Same file, same command, in the main tree: exit 0." Conclusion drawn: "RUN ubs IN THE MAIN TREE. Always."

WHAT I MEASURED. A 2x2 over (working directory) x (argument form), same file, same ubs, back to back:

  cwd = main repo,  arg = relative, inside cwd ............ WORKS, Critical: 28
  cwd = WORKTREE,   arg = relative, inside cwd ............ WORKS, Critical: 28
  cwd = main repo,  arg = ABSOLUTE, outside cwd ........... Failed to prepare files workspace
  cwd = WORKTREE,   arg = ABSOLUTE, into the main repo .... Failed to prepare files workspace

The worktree is confirmed linked in the run that WORKED: its .git is a 62-byte FILE, not a directory, so it is the same checkout shape that defeats evidence.py run_git.

CONCLUSION: the variable is whether the path argument resolves INSIDE the current working directory. It is not the worktree. ubs prepares a shadow workspace rooted at cwd and cannot stage a file that lies outside it, which is also why my very first attempt failed — I passed an absolute scratchpad path while sitting in the repo, and read that as a worktree problem because the broadcast had primed me to.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND THE ROW, and it is uncomfortable: this is the exact pattern this bead identifies, reproduced inside the correction. "Every one of these failures blames something else... the diagnostics actively point away from the cause." Failed to prepare files workspace names neither worktrees nor cwd. The confound is easy to hit, because reaching for a worktree and reaching for an absolute path tend to happen in the same breath — you go to the worktree to get a clean measurement, then point ubs at the file you actually care about, which is in the main tree.

THE RULE I WOULD SUGGEST INSTEAD, and it is narrower and cheaper than always returning to the main tree: run ubs with cwd at the root of the tree that CONTAINS the files, and pass paths relative to that root. Then a worktree is fine. "Always run ubs in the main tree" is not wrong as a safe default, but it costs a real capability — a per-file ubs delta taken in a worktree at a pinned commit is the cleanest attributable baseline available while the shared tree is dirty, and this rule would have retired it for no reason.

I did not test check.sh, the evidence self-test, or closure_audit.sh in a worktree, and I make no claim about them — the run_git mechanism you documented is specific and I have no reason to doubt it. title: beads: the coverage-row obligation is announced to the wrong pane, an unbounded number of actions late
description:
The coverage-row obligation is created by br create and br close, and reported by a git pre-commit
hook an unbounded number of actions later, to whoever commits next -- who may be a third pane that
created no obligation at all. The enforcement is SOUND AND LATE, and lateness has costs a
correctness argument does not see.

SPLIT FROM fln-ysvo, which closed 2026-07-27 on its main finding. That bead asked whether a bead's
mutable summary can be mechanically bound to its immutable comment log and measured the answer NO,
by four priced candidates each failing differently. This is its SECOND finding, and it is the exact
opposite in kind, which is why it needs its own tracker entry rather than a paragraph inside a
closed bead: ysvo's join is SEMANTIC and therefore unbindable, while this one is EXACTLY DECIDABLE
and already bound -- it is merely announced in the wrong place. Filed separately because a closed
bead is out of br ready and every triage, and a guarded disclosure is not a substitute for a
tracker entry (the u4j7 lesson, recorded in AGENTS.md).

WHAT IS NOT WRONG, stated first because this bead must not be read as an indictment of the guard.
The verification-coverage guard and the projection guard both behave exactly as designed. Measured
2026-07-27: each refused a real violation, named the bead, named the missing artifact shape,
printed the exact validator command to check the obligation, and neither ever exited 0 on an
unanswered question. The closure-binding law also fired correctly on a genuine post-boundary close.
NOTHING HERE PROPOSES WEAKENING ANY OF THEM. The predicate is not the problem; its delivery point
is.

THE MEASURED INSTANCES, two, which is not a rate.

  1. 2026-07-27T14:21:57Z and 14:22:07Z, TEN SECONDS APART: cc_2 closed franken_lean-0kpa without
     its closure-binding citation, and cc_1 filed fln-ysvo without a coverage row. Same guard, two
     halves of one rule -- filing needs a SPARSE row, closing needs a BOUND one. Both panes knew
     the rule. Both tripped it while doing good work quickly.
  2. Earlier the same session, cc_1's beads commit was refused for cc_2's unrowed u4j7. The person
     who committed was not the person who owed, and the diagnosis landed on someone with no context
     for it.

THE THREE COSTS, none of which is a defect in the guard:
  a. The person who commits is not always the person who owes.
  b. The diagnosis lands on someone with no context for the obligation.
  c. The shared JSONL means one pane's unmet obligation blocks every other pane's unrelated commit,
     which in a six-pane swarm is a cross-pane stall for a single-pane omission.

WHY THIS IS CHEAP WHERE ysvo's MAIN FINDING WAS IMPOSSIBLE. "A bead crossed the adoption boundary
and has no coverage row" is exactly decidable from two files, which is precisely why the pre-commit
guard already decides it perfectly. There is no semantic predicate, no saturated proxy, no
out-of-tree referent. The obligation is trivially checkable AT THE MOMENT IT IS CREATED and is
merely checked somewhere else.

THE REPAIR SURFACE IS OUTSIDE THIS REPOSITORY, and that is the whole difficulty. It is beads_rust:

title: W8: Remote rewrite-index hydration, validation, quarantine, and recovery
description:
## Description

Consume locally published rewrite-index products and the federation authority to hydrate indexes from a remote candidate. Verify RewriteIndexKeyV1, complete canonical semantic manifest, builder/schema/epoch compatibility, owning theorem and environment roots, payload bytes, signatures when present, retention policy, and local authority before atomic installation. Remote identity, signature, or digest never grants proof authority.

Malformed, stale, unsupported, cross-mode, collision-mismatched, partial, poisoned, cancelled, or unavailable candidates are quarantined with bounded evidence and fall back to safe local rebuild where policy permits. Installation is crash-safe and idempotent.

## Acceptance Criteria

Named suites remote_index_candidate_model, canonical_manifest_collision_guard, hydration_transaction_recovery, quarantine_lease_dpor, and remote_index_no_mock_e2e cover real remote transport, cache miss/hit, corruption, wrong roots/versions/modes, collision, interruption at every phase, quarantine, local rebuild, and retry. Mutants trust digest/signature alone, omit theorem order/options, expose before validation, reuse stale leases, or suppress remote failure; each is killed. Canonical semantic NDJSON is separate from telemetry and exact CAS/index/filesystem final states are asserted.

title: W11: Bloodhound — verified search, premise retrieval, proof repair, counterfactuals
description:
Implement Bloodhound (fln-hound, §16.1): the candidate-production system under one law — every candidate is untrusted text/terms until Athanor elaborates and Crucible accepts it (ranking is UX, proofs are proofs; determinism class D3, never touching the trust story).

Scope: in-toolchain hybrid search (frankensearch two-tier: lexical + semantic, bundled embedder, no network/Python/service) over statements, names, docstrings, simp/instance membership, indexed INCREMENTALLY at Ledger commit; exact?/apply?-class premise retrieval as a candidate generator verified by actual elaboration; Loogle-style structural patterns on a type-shape fingerprint lane; CandidateCards (source/term, provenance + retrieval channels, required imports/instances, rank components, elaboration outcome, kernel outcome, fragility signals, replay identity) in three grades — initial (low-latency lexical/type-head/local-context), refined (structural unification, graph ranking over Palimpsest cones, prior-use paths, optional learned rerank), verified (kernel-accepted under the exact snapshot); a failed refinement never withdraws a valid initial result.

Proof repair (the migration autopilot engine): diff old/new environment + extension graphs, find the earliest failed constraint cell, re-elaborate with holes around the blame slice, search replacements (renames, binder-order shifts, bridge lemmas, instance-priority shifts, simp-set drift, termination adjustments via TerminationCards, import moves), validate each minimal patch through the FULL pipeline, rank by semantic change size + fragility delta, emit a patch transaction with rollback. Counterfactual analysis (replay under altered policy on branch-local snapshots) and minimization (declared objective vectors, trade-offs shown). Learned components (frankentorch tier): local-first, identity on every card, candidates-only, removal leaves a complete deterministic baseline.

Acceptance: search quality measured on a query corpus; repair success rate measured on a broken-proof corpus derived from real mathlib migrations; every repair kernel-validated. Tests: index incrementality (commit -> queryable within the latency budget); candidate-grade monotonicity fixtures; repair rollback drills; learned-tier removal leaves baseline green.

## Acceptance Criteria

All bead-specific requirements, acceptance conditions, tests, invariants, compatibility surfaces, evidence levels, performance gates, negative/recovery cases, and user-visible behaviors stated above remain mandatory. In addition, the MANDATORY VERIFICATION DEFINITION OF DONE in Notes must be satisfied with named unit/property/mutation suites, at least one shared real-path no-mock E2E scenario plus failure/recovery coverage, detailed human and schema-versioned NDJSON artifacts, and reproducible close evidence. No listed feature or claim may be silently narrowed, deferred, mocked, or declared complete through an unclassified divergence.

1. Incrementally index Ledger commits with local-only frankensearch lexical and bundled-semantic lanes over statements, names, docstrings, simp/instance membership, type-shape fingerprints, contexts, and provenance. No Python, network service, or learned component is required for a complete deterministic baseline.
2. CandidateCards carry source/term, retrieval channels and rank components, required imports/instances, snapshot/epoch/provenance, elaboration and kernel outcomes, fragility signals, replay identity, and initial/refined/verified grade. Refinement may improve/rerank but never withdraw a valid initial result; verified means elaborated and kernel-accepted under the exact snapshot. Rankings remain untrusted UX data.
3. exact?/apply?-class retrieval, structural search, and optional learned reranking only propose candidates. Removing the learned tier leaves baseline results valid. Counterfactuals execute on branch-local snapshots with declared policy changes and minimization reports objective vectors/tradeoffs rather than a hidden scalar.
4. Proof repair finds the earliest failed constraint/blame slice, searches every plan-listed repair class, validates minimal patch transactions through the full elaboration/kernel pipeline, ranks semantic-size and fragility deltas, and carries explicit preconditions plus rollback. It never edits without explicit apply authority.

Named unit/property/metamorphic/differential/mutation suites cover commit-to-query incrementality, deletion/epoch invalidation, rank determinism, grade monotonicity, candidate replay, learned-tier removal, counterfactual isolation, each repair class, kernel validation, minimization, rollback, cancellation/resource exhaustion, and failure atomicity. Unverified-label, stale-index, withdrawn-initial, learned-required, and unchecked-repair mutants must be killed.

A shared no-mock E2E lane indexes a real mathlib slice, runs the declared query corpus, verifies candidates in exact snapshots, commits an edit and measures query visibility, disables learned ranking, repairs real migration-derived broken proofs with rollback and explicit apply, runs a counterfactual, plants a bogus repair, and confirms rejection/recovery. 7. Reproducible evidence publishes retrieval metrics/latency on the named query corpus and repair success/quality on the real broken-proof corpus with distributions and exclusions. title: W4: Vellum — parser, Syntax/SourceInfo, hygiene, macro transactions
description:
Workstream W4 "Vellum" (§9): the parser and macro engine — the reimplementation graveyard, visited early with flowers (spike G0-4).

Scope: token tables + Pratt-precedence engine with the Reference category/leading/trailing model; Syntax trees with identical node kinds, atom/ident/node structure, SourceInfo discipline (original vs synthetic, whitespace attachment, UTF-8 byte positions — wire-visible, therefore conformance surface); the full extensibility contract (parsing interleaves with elaboration; commands install syntax/macros visible immediately; precedence interactions match). Internals: lossless rope + persistent green tree with red views; origin sets per node projected to the single-primary-span convention at the wire; GrammarEpoch content-hashing of the active grammar state with memoization keyed on (position, category, precedence, epoch); typed parser-registration effect summaries (an OpaqueParserEffect forces the conservative suffix barrier). Hygiene: macro scopes exactly as the Reference implements them; generated identifiers derive from stable expansion paths, never thread timing; macro expansion as a memoizable transaction with declared capability reads (§9.2). Sound-mode improvements (§9.3): specified error recovery (recovery may add diagnostics, never change acceptance; RecoveredSyntax law), sub-command incremental relex/reparse, provenance into Palimpsest.

Exit: hygiene fidelity rig green on the macro-heavy corpus; syntax trees, positions, and hygiene observables byte-agree with the Reference across C0-C2 fixtures.

All scope and outcomes stated above remain mandatory, and every dependency/child deliverable required for this epic or gate must be completed at its honest evidence level. The MANDATORY EPIC/GATE CLOSEOUT CONTRACT in Notes must pass with coverage mapping, no-mock E2E evidence, detailed archived human and schema-versioned NDJSON artifacts, reproducible environment facts, and every skip/divergence classified. No feature, compatibility surface, invariant, performance gate, or release claim may be silently narrowed, dropped, or replaced by a prototype.

title: G0-10: Dependency-closure audit + authoritative SUITE.lock
description:
## Description

Own the authoritative SUITE.lock, the complete governed dependency-closure model, reviewed allowlists, lock-only build enforcement, and closure-policy evidence for D1/R16. This bead does not own ABI/OLEAN/ILEAN/extern/builtin extraction or drift generation; franken_lean-53v owns that feature. G0/W1 joins both evidence bundles, so no second extractor or contradictory drift path exists.

Compute separate runtime, build, dev, test, bench, fuzz, proc-macro-host, and tool closures across every certified or functionally supported host/target triple and reviewed feature/profile combination. Cargo.lock membership is necessary but insufficient: resolved features, target predicates, host/target split, build scripts, proc macros, native links, checksums/source/tree, suite package-to-repository mapping, canonical path, exact commit, license, unsafe review, reason, owner, and upgrade policy must all agree bidirectionally with manifests, pinned trees, WORKSPACE_GRAPH, and SUITE.lock.

SUITE.lock binds exact FrankenSuite commits/trees/checksums, the Rust nightly and target-feature sets, Reference epoch/commit/tree, and Corpus commit in one ceremony. --locked alone is not authority. A build is lock-authoritative only after an independent verifier succeeds under the exact toolchain, host/target, feature/profile, suite-path, and closure configuration. Sources are admitted only by the closed D1 allowlist; source syntax alone is not the policy decision.

Malformed or policy-violating complete inputs produce a typed complete violation. Missing checkouts or unverifiable metadata produce Inconclusive. Partial traversal, cancellation, resource exhaustion, graph/root drift, ambiguous identity, or stale evidence can never yield compliant. Candidate lock/allowlist changes validate in isolation and cannot replace the current authority before complete evidence.

## Acceptance Criteria

Named suites closure_policy_model, target_feature_closure_matrix, suite_path_bijection, cargo_lock_v4_parser, and suite_lock_candidate_e2e cover all closure lanes, host/target splits, feature/profile resolution, manifests and lock grammar, canonical paths/symlinks, exact suite mappings and pins, every policy field, complete/inconclusive outcomes, candidate atomicity, and recovery. The closure inventory and allowlist are bijective over every reachable package/target/source; unlisted or stale rows and policy violations fail with stable exact codes. Mutations for omitted target-only or proc-macro-host edges, suppressed features, stale suite checkout, mismatched package/repo path, path alias/symlink escape, checksum/tree/source/license/policy drift, partial scan promoted to compliant, evidence root detached from candidate lock, malformed/non-v4/duplicate/unterminated lock structures, and reviewless allowlist change are killed. The real no-mock E2E validates a cold authoritative closure, plants each named failure in an isolated candidate, proves typed refusal and unchanged current lock, restores, and independently validates the final bundle. Strict NDJSON records closure lane, host/target, feature/profile set, package source/version/tree/checksum, suite mapping, policy facts, pre/post graph and lock roots, completeness/authority, first divergence, resources, cleanup, and final state. CI runs the audit permanently. No Cargo.lock-only inference, syntax-only source ban, unverifiable pass, hidden transitive dependency, or duplicated extraction path satisfies G0-10.

title: W8: Ledger records + CAS — demand nodes, five planes, retention tiers
description:
Implement Ledger records + the CAS store (§13.1): every declaration commit produces a record — decl_hash = H(name, elaborated statement, elaborated value/body class, direct dep hashes, options-that-matter, toolchain epoch, mode) — stored content-addressed (frankensqlite metadata + CAS blobs) with dependency edges as first-class rows. The environment at any point is a Merkle frontier keyed by logical roots; a module is a view; a build is a query.

The record generalizes to a demand node — kind, implementation version, epoch, semantic inputs, declared reads/effects (the §10.6 vocabulary), capability inputs, output schema, determinism class D0-D4 — spanning five interlocking planes with separate retention: source, language, trust (kernel/checker receipts), build (facets, codegen, links), service (LSP products, indexes). An LSP hover can be evicted without touching the checked declaration beneath it; retention tiers T0 (trusted roots, never sole-copy-evicted) -> T4 (observational, sampled) with eviction weighing recomputation cost, fan-out, and pressure.

Acceptance: record creation + retrieval on real elaboration output; plane separation demonstrated (service-plane eviction leaves trust plane intact); logical-root stability across hosts. Tests: hash-input completeness property tests (any semantic input change changes the hash; any excluded input does not); retention-tier eviction policy fixtures; frankensqlite crash-recovery drills on the metadata store (WAL semantics honest under kill -9).

## Acceptance Criteria

All bead-specific requirements, acceptance conditions, tests, invariants, compatibility surfaces, evidence levels, performance gates, negative/recovery cases, and user-visible behaviors stated above remain mandatory. In addition, the MANDATORY VERIFICATION DEFINITION OF DONE in Notes must be satisfied with named unit/property/mutation suites, at least one shared real-path no-mock E2E scenario plus failure/recovery coverage, detailed human and schema-versioned NDJSON artifacts, and reproducible close evidence. No listed feature or claim may be silently narrowed, deferred, mocked, or declared complete through an unclassified divergence.
design: FL-INV-05 STORAGE BOUNDARY — CAS presence, signature, receipt presence, or matching key yields only an untrusted candidate, never a semantically admitted cache hit. Record schemas bind every semantic/capability/determinism input and separate byte identity from logical identity; publication is atomic and generation-bound. Only the validated reuse path owned by franken_lean-5h8 may promote a candidate, and its proof/recompute evidence is linked in the record. Seeded omissions of each hash-input class and stale-generation publication must be killed.
acceptance_criteria:
1. Persist declaration records content-addressed by canonical name, elaborated statement, value/body class, direct dependency hashes, semantic options, toolchain epoch, and mode; dependency edges are first-class rows and the environment is a Merkle frontier addressed by stable logical roots. Real elaboration records retrieve identically across certified hosts.
2. Generalize records to versioned demand nodes carrying kind, implementation version, epoch, semantic inputs, declared reads/effects, capability inputs, output schema, determinism class D0-D4, output roots, and evidence links across separate source, language, trust, build, and service planes.
3. Enforce T0-T4 retention: trusted roots are never sole-copy evicted; lower planes may be evicted by declared recomputation cost/fanout/pressure without invalidating stronger planes. Service-plane eviction demonstrably leaves language/trust records, receipts, roots, and rebuild validity intact.
4. Named unit/property/metamorphic/model/mutation suites prove hash-input completeness and exclusions, canonical serialization, cross-host logical-root stability, dependency traversal, plane isolation, tier policy, concurrent readers/promotions, cancellation/resource exhaustion, and failure atomicity. Omitted-semantic-input, included-observational-input, cross-plane-eviction, stale-root, and premature-promotion mutants must be killed.
5. A shared no-mock E2E lane elaborates real declarations into frankensqlite metadata plus CAS blobs, retrieves and rebuilds them, evicts service data under pressure, and performs kill-9/crash drills at every metadata/blob promotion boundary before restart and exact state verification. Human logs and schema-versioned NDJSON include run/record/demand/plane/tier/transaction ids, bead/claim/invariant/gate rows, exact redacted argv/cwd, epoch/mode/profile/platform/thread/seed/cache/disk facts, canonical input/dependency/output/logical/receipt roots, eviction/promotion decisions, expected/actual state, timings/resources/status, artifact/WAL references, cleanup, and final state.
6. CI archives hash witnesses, host matrix, retention model traces, crash/fault matrix, mutant outcomes, database/CAS manifests, and named test/E2E bundles. No durability, retention, or root-stability claim closes from in-memory or mocked storage.

The language-plane Ledger persists ModuleProvenanceRootV1 with exact canonical manifest bytes, schema/epoch, capture/transparency/authority axes, and collision-aware references to every required declaration and extension payload object. Root equality alone is insufficient on restart: canonical manifest bytes and every actual payload binding are revalidated before authority is restored. Forward/reverse provenance indexes are rebuilt deterministically from primary records or, if cached, treated as discardable derived data and validated for complete bidirectional coverage. Missing, stale, substituted, or equal-digest unequal-byte objects remain untrusted candidates and cannot produce a cache hit.

The W2 handoff is explicitly in-memory and contains the canonical manifest/root, payload requirements, evidence facts, and index-rebuild recipe. This W8 bead owns durable encoding, atomic persistence, restart rehydration, collision-aware retrieval, and exact recovery evidence. Tests and retained records distinguish candidate lookup from validated promotion; include index-cache deletion/rebuild, stale/missing/substituted/equal-digest-unequal-byte objects, partial payload availability, evidence-axis preservation, deterministic reconstruction, typed Inconclusive resource/cancellation, zero-authority recovery candidates, and a later successful rehydration. Mutants trust root equality alone, skip one payload binding, promote a cached index as truth, restore unjustified authority, or let W2 Arc/address identity leak into durable bytes; each is killed discriminatingly.

REVIEW AMENDMENT — declaration identity binds the full canonical payload, truth-bearing metadata, and semantic read/effect manifest, not a vague statement or value class. Retention tier is orthogonal to authority. SQLite metadata and CAS blobs use a journaled visibility generation: stage, validate, publish one marker atomically, replay idempotently, and recover unreachable staging; no cross-store atomicity is implied. Hash, root, signature, or tier alone cannot promote. Preserve ModuleProvenanceRootV1 collision-aware handoff. Named suites: ledger_record_identity_model, plane_authority_separation, cas_visibility_recovery_model, ledger_storage_no_mock_e2e.

W6-W8 EVIDENCE CONTRACT — canonical schema-versioned semantic NDJSON is validated independently; telemetry remains separate and non-authoritative. Unknown schema, missing/duplicate ids, broken order/linkage, unbound artifacts, truncation, merged streams, or cleanup/final-state mismatch fail. Cancellation/exhaustion/InternalFault never enters cache, negative storage, admission, publication, or promotion. Productive 1/8/32 evidence proves useful work and deterministic reduction. Named unit/model/property/mutation/fuzz suites and real no-mock positive/failure/recovery E2E are mandatory.

title: W2: fln-libm — owned deterministic transcendentals, bit-locked across platforms
description:
Implement fln-libm (§6.8): owned, fixed-implementation Float transcendentals — sin, cos, tan, exp, log, pow, atan2, hypot (and the rest of the family the extern census enumerates) — with documented accuracy (<= 1 ulp target, per-function error tables published) and IDENTICAL BITS on every certified target, locked by cross-platform vectors in CI. No platform libm is linked, period (D21).

Why: Float arithmetic is hardware IEEE-754 binary64 (portable), but upstream defers transcendentals to platform libm, so compiled evaluation, #eval, and native_decide-class computation drift across glibc/macOS/Windows in the last ulps — the Reference cannot promise ITSELF cross-platform bit-stability (§1.6b). Kernel judgments never consume floats (Float ops are opaque to the kernel), so the soundness surface is untouched; the evaluation surface gains bit-stability recorded as a Behavior Note (platforms disagree with each other; we pick one correct answer and keep it everywhere).

Acceptance: cross-platform vector suite green on the certified matrix (identical bits linux-x86-64 / linux-aarch64 / macos-aarch64); error tables generated and published per function; a CI symbol-scan proves no libm import in any release binary. Tests: ulp-error measurement harness against high-precision references; boundary cases (subnormals, infinities, NaN payloads, huge args for range reduction); Float printing/parsing round-trip fixtures matching the Reference conventions.

comments.text:
FINDING (BeigeMarsh, unsolicited but load-bearing — fln-libm is COMPLETE AND INERT, and the fix is a known legal edge, not more algorithm work). Reported, not adopted: this bead is unassigned and I do not own it; the route asking to adopt it went unanswered, so this is evidence offered to whoever does.

MEASURED STATE (this box, 2026-08-09, crate cold since 2026-08-04):
- crates/fln-libm implements EVERY transcendental the bead enumerates: sin cos tan asin acos atan atan2 exp exp2 expm1 log log2 log10 log1p sinh cosh tanh asinh acosh atanh cbrt pow hypot sqrt frexp scalbn + the rounding family. 34 unit tests, all green.
- It exports ZERO C symbols: no #[export_name], no #[no_mangle] anywhere in lib.rs.
- It is depended on by NOTHING: absent from every crate's Cargo.toml except its own; the only references outside the crate are the structure-guard rank table (rank 1) and the census extractor.
- So the whole yzd workstream currently ships ZERO product behavior. Float.sin is @[extern "sin"] (Init/Data/Float.lean:307) — compiled Lean links the BARE C symbol `sin`, which today can only resolve to glibc libm, the exact thing D21 says must never be linked. fln-libm's deterministic `sin` is never in that link path.

THE FIX IS A NAMED LEGAL EDGE, not algorithm work. fln-libm is rank 1; fln-unsafe-abi (the C-ABI export crate) is rank 2. So `fln-unsafe-abi -> fln-libm` is a DOWNWARD, cycle-free edge — identical in shape to the existing `fln-unsafe-abi -> fln-bignum` (2 -> 1) edge. The transcendentals then export from fln-unsafe-abi under their bare `@[extern]` names, delegating to fln-libm's algorithms — exactly the pattern the float plane used (lean_float_* exports over the object/bignum cores). The edge needs WORKSPACE_GRAPH.txt updated (cod_2's ci/ authority).

WHY I DID NOT JUST WIRE IT. Two honest blockers, both about VERIFICATION not capability: (1) everything this session was byte-differential against the Reference (glibc); fln-libm DELIBERATELY diverges from glibc in the last ulps (the bead's entire point), so the gauntlet's byte-differential is INAPPLICABLE by construction — exporting `sin` and diffing against glibc would fail by design. (2) The bead's real acceptance is cross-platform bit-identity on the certified matrix (linux-x86-64 / linux-aarch64 / macos-aarch64) plus ulp error tables; I have ONE platform, so I can prove connection/round-trip/self-consistency and measure ulp-vs-glibc divergence here, but NOT the cross-platform bit-identity that is the bead's core claim. Wiring it under a verification regime I can only half-run, on a crate I don't own, spanning the build-system link-resolution question (how does the final leanc/lake link resolve `@[extern "sin"]` to fln-libm instead of glibc?), is an architecture decision — the same shape as the process seam (comment 2130), and not one pane's unilateral call.

WHAT THIS EARNS. The bead is closer to done than it looks: the algorithms are complete and green. What remains is not more math — it is (a) the fln-unsafe-abi -> fln-libm export edge (legal, priced), (b) the build-system link-resolution decision that makes `@[extern "sin"]` bind our symbol, and (c) the cross-platform matrix run for the bit-identity claim. Whoever owns yzd can take the export edge immediately; I will implement it the moment it is assigned or the edge is sanctioned. Class bounded_model, one host, this commit.

- 14 functions at <=1 ulp distance: sin (incl. 1e6 range reduction), cos, atan, exp, exp2, expm1, log, log2, log10, asinh, acosh, cbrt, sqrt.

Localized: atanh = 0.5*log1p(2x/(1-x)); as x->1 the reduction feeds log1p a LARGE argument (~1900 at the worst input -0.99895), and log1p — accurate for SMALL args by construction — is the wrong callee there. The accurate fix is a reduction that routes the large-argument regime through log directly, or a large-arg-correct log1p; it touches shared numerics and wants the true-ulp oracle to validate no regression, so it is the owner's call with this harness now in hand, not a blind rewrite.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
CORRECTION (BeigeMarsh, retracting my own comments 2131 and 2132 on their central accuracy claim). Those comments called atanh's 220-ulp table row "the crate's one unambiguous accuracy DEFECT". THAT IS FALSE, found on a fresh-eyes review of my own harness (commit eec4a67f corrects it). The root cause, measured against 80-digit decimal truth rather than assumed:

At atanh(-0.99895005000000003381...) (bits 0xbfeff7661862cd55) the correctly-rounded answer is 0xc00e34dfc0f3d6e1. fln-libm::atanh returns EXACTLY that — 0 ulp from truth, correctly rounded. Rust's std::f64::atanh returns 0xc00e34dfc0f3d7bd — 220 ulp WRONG (confirmed at runtime under black_box, so not a compile-time const-fold artifact; and glibc's atanh via Python IS correct, so Rust std here is not glibc). So the 220 was the REFERENCE's error, and my harness mislabeled the oracle: I documented std as "~1-ulp glibc", which it is not for atanh.

WHAT ACTUALLY HOLDS about fln-libm's accuracy, now verified oracle-independently (golden_correctly_rounded, embedding correctly-rounded 80-digit truth as bit patterns): fln-libm is within 1 ulp of correctly-rounded truth at every curated hard point tested — atanh (both signs), log at a moderate arg, exp, sin, tanh. fln-libm's transcendentals look GOOD, not defective. The "2-3 ulp band" and "pow 33" I reported were also distances-from-an-unreliable-oracle, not attributed fln-libm errors; the distance tables are now demoted to informational regression tripwires and make NO accuracy claim about fln-libm.

TWO harness bugs fixed in the same commit: (1) the log/exp/sqrt sweeps used a LINEAR grid over [1e-300, 1e300] (step ~1e295), sampling only the extreme tail — now Geometric + a mid-range partition; (2) the oracle mischaracterization above. The standing lesson for the next reader: a distance-from-libm harness cannot attribute blame; only a correctly-rounded golden can, and Rust std f64 methods are NOT a safe golden. What still needs the platform matrix (cross-platform bit-identity) is unchanged. Net: acceptance criterion 2 (error tables) now rests on the golden test, and fln-libm passes it. Class bounded_model, one host, commit eec4a67f.

title: W8: Watch mode + distributed elaboration — local re-verification, no distributed trust

title: W5: FLBC interpreter — ABI-valued registers, inline caches, PG-7 floor
description:
Implement the FLBC interpreter (fln-vm, §11.2): threaded dispatch, inline caches on constructor tags and closure arities, direct-call fast paths for the intrinsic table, allocation through Marrow (heartbeats count identically to native paths — fuel parity crosses the VM boundary), and the Reference semantics for panics, partial non-termination, stack depth, and checkSystem interruption polls.

The design masterstroke to preserve at all costs: FLBC values ARE Marrow ABI objects, so calls cross between interpreted code, Iron-compiled code, Reference-built plugins, and the Mirror native facade with ZERO conversion — one calling convention for the whole membrane (validated by spike G0-3). Performance floor PG-7: >= 3x the Reference interpreter on the tactic micro-corpus — deliberately conservative because the interpreter is the default vehicle for the long tail of user tactics (the interpreter tax is weakness census #5).

Acceptance: #eval/IO/Task parity corpus green (G2 requirement); PG-7 met on the micro-corpus against the W1 baseline; interruption polling honors the checkSystem contract (latency fixtures). Tests: opcode-level unit tests; VM opcode fuzzing under budgets (§18.2); inline-cache correctness under polymorphic call sites (cache hit == cache miss result); cross-boundary call matrix (interpreted <-> intrinsic <-> plugin) with RC-balance assertions.

## Acceptance Criteria
